title: Transferring End-to-End Visuomotor Control from Simulation to Real World for a Multi-Stage Task

claims.claim: Domain randomization applied to simulated training images enabled a CNN trained purely in simulation to transfer to real-world image-to-velocity control without any real images
claims.direction: favors domain randomization / synthetic-only training for sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: sim-trained, real robot eval, multi-stage pick-and-place task

claims.claim: The learned policy generalized to novel real-world environments including dynamic lighting conditions, distractor objects, and moving objects (including the target basket) despite training only in simulation
claims.direction: supports robustness to lighting/distractor/object-motion shift via domain randomization
claims.conditions: real robot, zero real images used for training, multi-stage cube-pick-and-drop task

title: Benchmark for Skill Learning from Demonstration: Impact of User Experience, Task Complexity, and Start Configuration on Performance

claims.claim: Task performance of learning-from-demonstration approaches depended on task complexity, demonstrator expertise, and robot start configuration, based on 9 participants, 4 tasks, 180 trained task models and 720 physical-robot reproductions
claims.direction: demo quality/diversity (user expertise, start configuration) affects downstream policy performance, not just count
claims.conditions: real robot, 9 human demonstrators, 4 manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Four different motion-based LfD approaches were compared head-to-head on the same tasks and demonstrations
claims.direction: comparative benchmark of LfD methods (no single winner stated in abstract)
claims.conditions: real robot, benchmark study

title: Generative predecessor models for sample-efficient imitation learning

claims.claim: GPRIL (generative-model-based imitation learning) outperforms or matches a state-of-the-art imitation learning method on two simulated manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors generative-model-based imitation learning over baseline IL method
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation tasks + real robot demonstration, comparison vs one SOTA IL baseline

claims.claim: Learns robust policies from only a small number of expert demonstrations plus self-supervised environment interaction, with significantly higher sample efficiency than baseline, demonstrated on a real robot
claims.direction: supports feasibility with few demos when combined with self-supervised interaction
claims.conditions: real robot, small number of expert demos (exact count not given in abstract)

title: Self-Supervised Correspondence in Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Training the visual encoder with self-supervised dense visual correspondence outperforms autoencoding and end-to-end policy optimization for generalization performance and sample efficiency in visuomotor imitation learning
claims.direction: favors self-supervised correspondence pretraining of vision encoder over autoencoding/end-to-end training
claims.conditions: real robot hardware, imitation learning, simulated ablation also reported

claims.claim: Extensive hardware validation on challenging manipulation tasks with as few as 50 demonstrations
claims.direction: supports that ~50 demos suffice given the right visual representation
claims.conditions: real robot, closed-loop real-time vision-based policies

claims.claim: Learned policies generalize across classes of objects, react to deformable object configurations, and manipulate textureless symmetrical objects in a variety of backgrounds
claims.direction: supports representation choice driving generalization to novel objects/backgrounds
claims.conditions: real robot, closed-loop vision-based control

why_deep_read: Directly analogous setup (real robot, ~50 demos, closed-loop vision policy) with controlled comparison of vision representation training methods (correspondence vs autoencoding vs end-to-end) -- full ablation tables would clarify which encoder pretraining to pick for our low-data SO-101 setup (Q03) and how much of the generalization benefit (Q14) transfers to lighting/camera-shift conditions relevant to our failure modes.

title: SQUIRL: Robust and Efficient Learning from Video Demonstration of Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Bootstrapping a task-conditioned policy with behavioral cloning then refining via a learned Q-function (bypassing reward learning) performs more robustly (90%+ success) than behavioral cloning alone on new long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors BC-bootstrap + Q-function refinement over pure BC for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: real robot and simulation, vision-based pick-pour-place / pick-carry-drop tasks

claims.claim: Algorithm performs a new but related long-horizon manipulation task robustly given only a single video demonstration
claims.direction: supports feasibility of extremely low demo counts (single demo) when combined with online experience
claims.conditions: real-robot, single video demo of new task, meta-IRL/BC hybrid

title: Using Human Gaze to Improve Robustness Against Irrelevant Objects in Robot Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Deep imitation learning from raw pixels overfits to training images and is easily distracted by task-irrelevant objects; a gaze-predicting mixture density network that crops images around predicted gaze locations is robust to task-irrelevant objects and improves manipulation performance especially in multi-object handling, evaluated on four manipulation tasks designed to test distractor robustness
claims.direction: favors gaze-guided cropping/attention over raw full-image behavior cloning for distractor robustness
claims.conditions: real robot(s), four manipulation tasks, head-mounted eye tracking used only at training time

claims.claim: Cropping images around predicted gaze positions before computing the action removes visual distractions from irrelevant objects
claims.direction: favors gaze-informed cropping as an inductive bias / preprocessing augmentation
claims.conditions: real robot, behavior cloning with mixture density network

title: Ex-DoF: Expansion of Action Degree-of-Freedom with Virtual Camera Rotation for Omnidirectional Image

claims.claim: Virtual rotation of an omnidirectional robot camera image enables data augmentation that supports transferring a vision-based control policy from a lower-DoF robot (3-DoF wheeled) to train a higher-DoF (6-DoF arm) robot
claims.direction: favors virtual-viewpoint augmentation for cross-embodiment/viewpoint data transfer
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF arm robot, dataset originally collected on a 3-DoF wheeled robot, omnidirectional camera

claims.claim: A control system using multiple policies with different fields of view enables object reaching with a 6-DoF arm robot
claims.direction: suggests multi-viewpoint policy composition can substitute for a single fixed camera viewpoint
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF arm robot, omnidirectional camera setup (not a standard fixed RGB camera)

title: Reinforcement Learning Control for Robot Arm Grasping Based on Improved DDPG

claims.claim: Adding a batch of teaching (demonstration) data to the experience replay pool of DDPG raised the grasping success rate from 36% (unimproved DDPG) to 70%, under the same number of training episodes
claims.direction: favors seeding learning with demonstration data to improve sample efficiency/success rate
claims.conditions: simulation only, 6-DOF manipulator with gripper in ROS, low-cost/inexpensive arm framing

title: Sim-to-Real Visual Grasping via State Representation Learning Based on Combining Pixel-Level and Feature-Level Domain Adaptation

claims.claim: Combining pixel-level and feature-level domain adaptation for sim-to-real visual grasping achieves a substantial improvement over using only pixel-level or only feature-level domain adaptation alone
claims.direction: favors combining multiple domain-adaptation/augmentation strategies over a single one
claims.conditions: real-world visual grasping of unseen objects, off-policy actor-critic RL, small amount of real-world data

claims.claim: State representation learning (SRL) as a preprocessing module (shared between simulated and real/adapted images) makes actor-critic RL from raw images feasible/stable for visual grasping
claims.direction: favors a learned state-representation encoder over training directly on raw pixels for RL stability
claims.conditions: real + simulated grasping, off-policy actor-critic RL

title: Learning robot anomaly recovery skills from multiple time-driven demonstrations

claims.claim: A method (mean-prior GPR) for learning anomaly/recovery skills from multiple demonstrations by modulating a learned trajectory to safe via-points was compared against Gaussian mixture regression, probabilistic movement primitives, and kernelized movement primitives on benchmark reaching/pushing/writing/pressing tasks plus a real-time bin-picking task
claims.direction: favors incorporating demonstration variability explicitly for recovery-skill learning over baseline probabilistic LfD methods
claims.conditions: real robot bin-picking plus benchmark tasks; classical (non-deep) probabilistic trajectory models, not deep action heads

claims.claim: Fair comparison of several probabilistic movement-encoding methods (GMR, ProMP, KMP, proposed MP-GPR) for path accuracy and variability
claims.direction: comparative but abstract does not state a single clear winner across all metrics
claims.conditions: classical probabilistic trajectory models, real + benchmark tasks

title: LILA: Language-Informed Latent Actions

claims.claim: LILA models, which use language to modulate a low-dimensional latent action space, are more sample efficient and performant than imitation learning and end-effector control baselines, and are qualitatively preferred by users in real-world studies
claims.direction: favors language-conditioned latent action spaces over plain imitation learning / direct end-effector control baselines for language-guided manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot (7-DoF Franka Emika Panda), real-world user studies, shared-autonomy/teleop setting (human still provides low-dim joystick input plus language)

claims.claim: Learning a latent action space conditioned on language instructions outperforms directly learning end-effector control policies from demonstrations
claims.direction: favors latent/learned action representations over raw end-effector action regression
claims.conditions: real robot, shared-autonomy teleoperation, complex multi-step manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Real-robot, user-study comparison of language-conditioned latent-action control vs plain imitation learning and end-effector baselines is directly relevant to our Q08 decision (whether/how to add language conditioning for a second object); the full paper's sample-efficiency numbers and task set would clarify how much benefit language conditioning gives at low demo counts, though note this is a shared-autonomy (human-in-the-loop) setting rather than a fully autonomous policy, so applicability should be checked.

title: End-to-end training of deep visuomotor policies

claims.claim: Jointly training perception (CNN) and control end-to-end outperforms hand-engineered/separately trained perception and control on real-world manipulation tasks requiring vision-control coordination
claims.direction: favors end-to-end joint training over hand-engineered separate perception
claims.conditions: real robot arm, real-world tasks (e.g. screwing a bottle cap), small CNN with 92,000 parameters, guided policy search

claims.claim: A small CNN policy (92,000 parameters) trained end-to-end from images to torques achieves strong performance on contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.direction: small models can suffice
claims.conditions: real robot, guided policy search transforms policy search into supervised learning

title: Robot eye-hand coordination learning by watching human demonstrations: a task function approximation approach

claims.claim: Learned visual task function combined with uncalibrated visual servoing adapts to changes in target position, background, illumination, and occlusion without retraining
claims.direction: favors learned reward/task-function + classical visual servoing for robustness to environmental shift
claims.conditions: real robot, per-task Jacobian estimation ~4-7s, learned from raw video demonstrations, qualitative claim (no numeric robustness data given)

title: Robotic Grasping using Deep Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A multi-view camera setup increases grasping accuracy compared to a single-view model
claims.direction: favors multi-view over single-view cameras
claims.conditions: Baxter robot, Gazebo simulation + real robot experiments, double deep Q-learning (GraspQ-Network), RL not imitation learning

title: Learning to Generalize Across Long-Horizon Tasks from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A two-stage offline imitation learning algorithm (GTI) trains from a small number of human demonstrations by exploiting intersecting trajectory structure across multi-task demos to compose novel behaviors
claims.direction: favors leveraging structure in modest demo sets over larger unstructured demo collection
claims.conditions: real robot, long-horizon multi-stage manipulation; exact demo count not given in abstract

claims.claim: Goal-directed policy trained via GTI generalizes to unseen start and goal state combinations not contained in demonstrations
claims.direction: favors goal-conditioned imitation for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon manipulation domain plus simulated domains

title: Translating Natural Language Instructions to Computer Programs for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Translating a language instruction into an executable program (querying an object detector, using a constraint solver) to control the robot performs better than training a neural network to directly predict robot actions from image+instruction
claims.direction: favors modular/programmatic language grounding over end-to-end language-conditioned action-prediction networks
claims.conditions: comparison against direct neural action-prediction baseline; real/sim setting not clearly specified in abstract

title: DexPoint: Generalizable Point Cloud Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Training a dexterous manipulation policy on point cloud inputs (with imagined hand point clouds as augmented input) enables generalization to new objects of the same category in sim-to-real transfer, described as the first policy-learning framework to achieve this with dexterous hands
claims.direction: favors point cloud over other (e.g. RGB) representations for cross-object sim2real generalization
claims.conditions: Allegro Hand, simulation + real-world evaluation, RL (not imitation learning), dexterous multi-finger grasping

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Multi-Object Keypoints for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Self-supervised image keypoints learned via a Dense Correspondence pretext task, extended to multi-object scenes for scale-invariance and occlusion handling, are compared against other visual representation learning approaches and shown effective for sample-efficient policy learning
claims.direction: favors self-supervised keypoint/dense-correspondence pretraining over alternative visual representations for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world robot manipulation tasks, multi-object scenes, comparison across visual representation learning methods (specific baselines/numbers not given in abstract)

title: Masked World Models for Visual Control

claims.claim: Decoupling visual representation learning (masked autoencoder with reward-prediction auxiliary objective) from latent dynamics learning achieves 81.7% success rate across 50 visual manipulation tasks from Meta-world, versus 67.9% for an end-to-end baseline that trains representation and dynamics jointly
claims.direction: favors decoupled representation+dynamics learning with masked-autoencoding and auxiliary reward prediction over end-to-end joint training
claims.conditions: simulation only (Meta-world, RLBench), visual model-based RL, convolutional+ViT autoencoder

title: Instruction-driven history-aware policies for robotic manipulations

claims.claim: A transformer that keeps track of the full history of observations and actions (not just current observation) improves manipulation precision over history-less baselines
claims.direction: favors observation/action history over memoryless (reactive) policies
claims.conditions: RLBench benchmark (74 diverse tasks) plus real-world robot; transformer architecture with multi-view input

claims.claim: Integrating multi-view scene observations improves manipulation precision compared to single-view
claims.direction: favors multi-view over single-view observation
claims.conditions: RLBench benchmark and real-world robot

claims.claim: Unified transformer conditioning on natural language instructions generalizes well to previously unseen instruction-conditioned task variations and scales to 74 diverse tasks, outperforming prior state of the art
claims.direction: favors transformer-based joint language+history+multi-view conditioning
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation benchmark and real-world robot

why_deep_read: Full paper ablations on how much history length and number of camera views actually contribute (vs. language conditioning alone) would directly settle our Q07 (history/memory) and Q11 (multi-view) design choices, and whether a full-history transformer is affordable at our small model-size/compute budget.

title: Leveraging Haptic Feedback to Improve Data Quality and Quantity for Deep Imitation Learning Models

claims.claim: Adding real-time haptic feedback to human teleoperators during data collection improved data throughput by 6%, and an image-based deep imitation learning policy trained on data collected with haptic feedback performed on average 11% better than an equivalent policy trained on data collected without haptic feedback
claims.direction: favors improving demonstration-collection quality (via feedback to the teleoperator) as a lever on downstream policy performance, complementary to increasing demo count
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator robot, door-opening task with latch handles, teleoperated data collection, image-based deep imitation learning models, controlled with/without-haptic-feedback comparison across six trained models

title: Analysis of Randomization Effects on Sim2Real Transfer in Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Comparing four randomization strategies (three randomized parameters) in simulation and on a real robot reach-and-balance task: more randomization helps sim2real transfer robustness, but too much randomization can harm the ability of the algorithm to find a good policy in simulation; fully randomized simulation plus fine-tuning transfers best to the real robot among the approaches tested
claims.direction: favors substantial (but not unlimited) domain randomization/augmentation, combined with fine-tuning, for robustness under transfer
claims.conditions: real robot manipulator, controlled comparison of 4 randomization strategies, RL (not imitation), reach-and-balance benchmark task

title: Task-grasping from human demonstration

claims.claim: A grasping skill trained via deep RL with contact-web rewards and domain randomization of approach direction, learned from human demonstration hints (Learning-from-Observation), is shown to be robust to errors in object pose and to uncertainty in object shape
claims.direction: favors domain randomization + demonstration-guided reward shaping for pose/shape robustness
claims.conditions: real robot, qualitative robustness claim (no specific numbers given in abstract)

title: Learning Hybrid Actor-Critic Maps for 6D Non-Prehensile Manipulation

claims.claim: A point-cloud-based, temporally-abstracted, spatially-grounded object-centric action representation (selecting a contact location from the point cloud plus motion parameters) achieves an 89% success rate on unseen object categories in simulation and 50% zero-shot success in the real world for 6D non-prehensile manipulation, more than 3x higher success than the best alternative action representation baseline
claims.direction: favors point-cloud object-centric/hybrid discrete-continuous action representations over alternative (implicitly non-point-cloud or non-object-centric) representations
claims.conditions: 6D pose alignment task, randomized initial poses and goals, diverse object categories, simulation + real-world zero-shot transfer, RL not imitation learning, non-prehensile (pushing) manipulation not pick-and-place

title: Train Offline, Test Online: A Real Robot Learning Benchmark

claims.claim: TOTO benchmark compares five pretrained visual representations across institutions on a shared real-robot manipulation task suite requiring generalization to unseen objects, positions, and lighting
claims.direction: provides controlled cross-lab comparative data on which pretrained visual representation generalizes best (rankings not given in abstract)
claims.conditions: real shared robot hardware, remote multi-institution evaluation, manipulation task requiring generalization to unseen objects/positions/lighting

claims.claim: TOTO benchmark compares four offline policy learning baselines on the same real-robot task suite
claims.direction: provides controlled comparative data on offline policy learning approaches (specific ranking not given in abstract)
claims.conditions: real robot, offline training, online real-robot evaluation

why_deep_read: This is a controlled, cross-institution real-robot benchmark explicitly testing generalization to unseen objects/positions/lighting -- exactly our Q14 failure modes -- and reports which pretrained visual representations (Q03) and offline policy-learning methods (Q01) perform best; the full paper's tables would give concrete rankings directly transferable to our design choices.

title: Understanding Multi-Modal Perception Using Behavioral Cloning for Peg-In-a-Hole Insertion Tasks

claims.claim: Combining vision, force/torque sensing, and proprioception for behavioral cloning improves robustness to target-hole location uncertainty vs single modality
claims.direction: multi-modal fusion favored over vision-only
claims.conditions: real manipulator, peg-in-hole insertion, LfD/behavioral cloning

claims.claim: A proposed multi-step-ahead loss function improves behavioral cloning performance over standard one-step BC loss
claims.direction: multi-step-ahead loss favored
claims.conditions: real robot assembly (PiH) task

title: Robust Policies via Mid-Level Visual Representations: An Experimental Study in Manipulation and Navigation

claims.claim: Using mid-level visual representations (features learned asynchronously for traditional computer vision objectives) as perceptual state in end-to-end RL aids generalization, improves sample complexity, and leads to higher final performance compared to training end-to-end from scratch
claims.direction: pretrained/frozen mid-level visual features favored over learning vision from scratch
claims.conditions: manipulation and navigation tasks; includes zero-shot sim-to-real experiments on real robots

claims.claim: Mid-level representations scale better to harder problems and larger domain shifts than domain randomization; in some cases domain randomization and learning-from-scratch failed where mid-level representations succeeded
claims.direction: pretrained mid-level features favored over domain randomization for robustness to domain shift
claims.conditions: manipulation + navigation, zero-shot sim-to-real on real robots

why_deep_read: Controlled comparison of vision encoder choice (mid-level pretrained features vs scratch vs domain randomization) on generalization/robustness with real-robot sim-to-real results directly informs Q03/Q14 encoder choice for our small-data, shifting-lighting/camera setup.

title: Guided Imitation of Task and Motion Planning

claims.claim: A feed-forward policy trained via imitation of a TAMP solver's output solves a 4-object pick-place task 88% of the time from object pose observations, and a 9-goal benchmark 79% of the time (averaged) from RGB images
claims.direction: imitation-learned feed-forward policy viable substitute for expensive TAMP at inference time
claims.conditions: simulation (RoboSuite / RoboDesk benchmarks), 7-DoF joint control, hierarchical policy architecture

title: Multiscale Sensor Fusion and Continuous Control with Neural CDEs

claims.claim: A continuous-time policy (InFuser, using Neural Controlled Differential Equations) that integrates and fuses asynchronous multi-frequency sensory observations (e.g. 30Hz video, 100Hz proprioception, 500Hz force-torque) notably outperforms several baselines that batch observations into fixed-time windows, especially when one modality arrives much sparser than others
claims.direction: continuous-time fusion favored over fixed-window discrete-time batching for multi-rate sensors
claims.conditions: behavior cloning, dynamic manipulation tasks (e.g. swinging a ball into a cup)

title: Visual Backtracking Teleoperation: A Data Collection Protocol for Offline Image-Based Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Deliberately collecting visually similar failures and recoveries alongside successes (Visual Backtracking Teleoperation) and training offline RL on this data outperforms standard behavior cloning on successful-demonstration-only data by 13%, given equal-sized datasets (60 minutes of real-robot data)
claims.direction: failure/recovery demos + offline RL favored over success-only behavior cloning under matched data budget
claims.conditions: real robot, image-based, deformable manipulation (T-shirt grasping), small dataset (60 min)

why_deep_read: Directly quantifies the value of collecting failure/recovery demonstrations vs success-only demos under a matched small real-robot data budget -- central to our Q13 decision on how to spend our 50-100 demo budget.

title: DFBVS: Deep Feature-Based Visual Servo

claims.claim: Using deep-learned visual features (matched automatically) for visual servoing, rather than comparing raw target/current images directly or handcrafted features, enables generalization to unseen objects/scenes while remaining robust to background distraction
claims.direction: learned deep features favored over both handcrafted features and whole-image comparison
claims.conditions: real robotic grasping task, camera-based servoing

title: Learning to Fold Real Garments with One Arm: A Case Study in Cloud-Based Robotics Research

claims.claim: Systematic real-robot comparison of 8 algorithms (4 learning-based modeling expert actions, keypoints, reward functions, dynamic motions; 4 learning-free/inverse-dynamics) for fabric folding found a new algorithm combining imitation learning with analytic methods achieves human-level performance on flattening and 93% of human-level performance on folding
claims.direction: hybrid imitation-learning + analytic method favored over pure learning-based or pure learning-free baselines
claims.conditions: real robot (single arm), fabric/garment manipulation, cloud-based remote benchmarking

why_deep_read: One of few controlled multi-algorithm real-robot comparisons of action-generation approaches (Q01); the ablation/comparison table would clarify which specific design choices (keypoints vs reward-model vs dynamic-motion modeling) transfer to our low-cost-arm, few-demo setting.

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Language Instructions

claims.claim: A meta-RL algorithm that uses language instructions to shape task interpretation significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in training and testing task success rates on the Meta-World manipulation benchmark
claims.direction: language-conditioned meta-RL favored over non-language-conditioned baselines
claims.conditions: simulation (Meta-World benchmark), multiple manipulation tasks, RL not imitation learning

title: ToolFlowNet: Robotic Manipulation with Tools via Predicting Tool Flow from Point Clouds

claims.claim: A policy that predicts dense per-point flow on a tool from point-cloud input, then derives the robot transformation from that flow, significantly improves performance over baselines that do not use point-cloud flow; real-robot experiments (50 physical scooping trials) attain 82% success
claims.direction: point-cloud/flow-based representation favored over non-flow (implicitly image-based) baselines
claims.conditions: real robot, imitation learning, deformable-object tool manipulation (scooping, pouring)

why_deep_read: Direct real-robot comparative evidence for 3D point-cloud representation over baseline (non-flow) approaches with a quantified success rate — core to our Q04 RGB-vs-depth/point-cloud decision.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Corrective Demonstrations and a Low-Cost Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Corrective demonstrations considerably outperform randomly-sampled additional demonstrations when the proportion of additional demonstrations sampled from the full task distribution is larger than the number of original (restrictive-distribution) demonstrations; when originals outnumber additional demos, no significant difference is found between corrective and random additional demos
claims.direction: corrective/recovery demos favored over random additional demos, conditional on relative dataset sizes
claims.conditions: real five-fingered robot hand, pick-and-place task, imitation learning; low-cost vision sensor (LeapMotion) used to collect demonstrations cheaply

why_deep_read: Directly answers whether to spend limited demo budget (our ~50-100 demos) on corrective/recovery demonstrations vs random additional demonstrations, with an explicit conditional rule -- central to Q13 for our data-collection plan.

title: Foldsformer: Learning Sequential Multi-Step Cloth Manipulation With Space-Time Attention

claims.claim: A space-time attention mechanism capturing instruction information from a single general demonstration significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on sequential multi-step cloth manipulation in simulation
claims.direction: space-time attention over demonstration history favored
claims.conditions: simulation, sequential multi-step manipulation

claims.claim: The learned policy transfers from simulation to the real world without additional training or domain randomization, and generalizes to unseen cloth shapes (T-shirts, shorts) despite training only on rectangular cloths
claims.direction: favors representation/architecture that generalizes across shape variation without domain randomization
claims.conditions: sim-to-real transfer, deformable object manipulation

title: Guided Data Augmentation for Offline Reinforcement Learning and Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Human-guided data augmentation (GuDA), which restricts augmentations to human-validated progress-making trajectory segments, outperforms both a random augmentation strategy and a model-based augmentation strategy, and enables learning from a small initial dataset of potentially suboptimal experience
claims.direction: guided/constrained augmentation favored over random or model-based augmentation
claims.conditions: physical robot soccer task plus simulated navigation/driving/soccer tasks; offline RL and behavior cloning

title: PolarNet: 3D Point Clouds for Language-Guided Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A 3D point-cloud-based policy (PolarNet) using point cloud encoders and multimodal transformers outperforms state-of-the-art 2D and 3D approaches in both single-task and multi-task learning on the RLBench benchmark, and is described as more data-efficient than 2D-image-based approaches, which struggle to combine multi-view cameras and infer precise 3D positions/relationships
claims.direction: 3D point-cloud representation favored over 2D image representation, especially for data efficiency and multi-view fusion
claims.conditions: simulation (RLBench benchmark) plus promising results on a real robot; language-guided manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly compares 2D-image vs 3D-point-cloud policy representations with a data-efficiency claim (relevant to our low-demo-count setting) and includes real-robot results -- central to the Q04 RGB-vs-depth/point-cloud decision.

title: One ACT Play: Single Demonstration Behavior Cloning with Action Chunking Transformers

claims.claim: A behavior cloning agent can be trained from a single human demonstration by using linear transforms to augment it into a set of trajectories spanning a wide range of initial conditions, successfully completing three block manipulation tasks
claims.direction: single demonstration + geometric augmentation viable substitute for many demonstrations
claims.conditions: block manipulation tasks, action chunking transformer (ACT) policy

claims.claim: Incorporating the standard deviation of action-chunk predictions into the temporal ensembling method (used by action-chunking agents at inference) makes the policy more robust to unforeseen environment changes, yielding significant performance improvements over standard temporal ensembling
claims.direction: uncertainty-weighted temporal ensembling favored over standard temporal ensembling at chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: action chunking transformer (ACT)-based policy, block manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly targets our two most acute pain points: 50-100 demo budget (single-demo augmentation) and jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries (improved temporal ensembling using prediction std-dev) -- would give concrete implementation details for ACT deployment on our setup.

title: Multistage Cable Routing Through Hierarchical Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Individually-trained primitives for each stage of a multistage task are impractical (success probability compounds toward negligible over stages), so a hierarchical imitation learning system trains a high-level sequencing policy on top of low-level vision-based motor policies to recover from failure and choose which controller to trigger
claims.direction: hierarchical imitation learning (sequencing + motor control policies trained separately, closing loop on vision) favored over single flat imitation policy for long-horizon multistage tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, deformable-object (cable routing) multistage manipulation, vision-based policies from demonstrations

claims.claim: The hierarchical system generalizes to very challenging clip-placement variations not seen in a simple flat policy
claims.direction: hierarchical structure favored for generalization to novel object/placement configurations
claims.conditions: real robot cable routing

why_deep_read: Real-robot demonstration that flat single-stage imitation is fragile for extended manipulation and that hierarchical sequencing + recovery substantially improves generalization -- relevant to whether we need chunking/hierarchy plus recovery behavior for a second (harder) task.

title: One-Shot Imitation Learning With Graph Neural Networks for Pick-and-Place Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: A GNN-based policy trained on synthetic demonstrations generalizes to novel numbers, positions, height distributions, and configurations of objects/goals, requiring only a single image of the desired goal configuration at inference (one-shot)
claims.direction: graph-structured state representation + synthetic demos favored for generalization with minimal per-task demonstration
claims.conditions: pick-and-place task, synthetic demonstrations (simulation implied), imitation learning

title: Waypoint-Based Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Automatic Waypoint Extraction (AWE), a preprocessing step that decomposes demonstrations into a minimal set of waypoints (linear-motion segment endpoints), increases the success rate of state-of-the-art BC algorithms by up to 25% in simulation and by 4-28% on real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, while reducing the decision-making horizon by up to a factor of 10
claims.direction: waypoint/reduced-horizon action representation favored over dense per-timestep BC targets to combat compounding errors
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation tasks + simulation, combined with existing BC algorithms, no additional human waypoint labeling required

why_deep_read: Quantified, real-world (bimanual) success-rate gains from restructuring the action/horizon representation via automatic waypoint extraction -- directly actionable for our chunking-horizon (Q06) and action-space (Q02) decisions and for combating compounding BC errors.

title: Visual Spatial Attention and Proprioceptive Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Robust Peg-in-Hole Task Under Variable Conditions

claims.claim: A vision+proprioceptive model with a spatial attention point network, trained offline with a sample-efficient sim-to-real framework, achieves higher success rate and shorter completion time than baselines when tested across 12 unknown holes, 16 initial positions, and 3 lighting conditions including two with misleading shadows
claims.direction: spatial-attention visual representation + proprioception favored over baselines for robustness to lighting/pose variation
claims.conditions: real industrial robot, peg-in-hole (anchor-bolt insertion) task, offline-trained then sim-to-real transferred

why_deep_read: Real-robot, controlled evaluation across lighting conditions (including misleading shadows) and pose variation directly mirrors our observed lighting-robustness failure mode (Q14) and the visual-attention design detail could transfer.

title: Affordances from Human Videos as a Versatile Representation for Robotics

claims.claim: A visual affordance model trained on internet videos of human behavior (rather than robot demonstrations) can be integrated with offline imitation learning, exploration, goal-conditioned learning, and RL action parameterization, demonstrated across 4 real-world environments, 10+ tasks, and 2 robot platforms
claims.direction: human-video-derived affordance representation favored as auxiliary/alternative supervision to robot-specific demonstration data
claims.conditions: real-world, multiple robot platforms and tasks

title: Domain Adaption as Auxiliary Task for Sim-to-Real Transfer in Vision-based Neuro-Robotic Control

claims.claim: An end-to-end visuomotor architecture that jointly (via shared latent encoding) reconstructs canonical simulation images from randomized inputs (domain adaptation) and predicts joint angles via differentiable forward kinematics, significantly increases accuracy over separate domain-adaptation + IK-solver architectures
claims.direction: joint domain-adaptation-as-auxiliary-task + inverse kinematics favored over decoupled modules

title: Ag2Manip: Learning Novel Manipulation Skills with Agent-Agnostic Visual and Action Representations

claims.claim: An agent-agnostic visual representation derived from human manipulation videos (embodiment details obscured), combined with an agent-agnostic action representation, gives a 325% performance increase over baselines (e.g. VIP, R3M) without relying on domain-specific demonstrations in simulated benchmarks; ablations confirm both the visual and action representation each contribute to this gain

why_deep_read: Ablation-backed comparison of visual/action representation choices with large real-world success-rate gains (50%->77.5%) directly informs whether to use an embodiment-agnostic pretrained encoder/action abstraction for our low-cost arm with limited demos (Q03/Q02).

title: VisuoSpatial Foresight for Multi-Step, Multi-Task Fabric Manipulation

title: Generalization Through Hand-Eye Coordination: An Action Space for Learning Spatially-Invariant Visuomotor Control

title: You Only Demonstrate Once: Category-Level Manipulation from Single Visual Demonstration

claims.claim: A category-level object representation learned in simulation lets a robot parse a task trajectory from a single demonstration video and generalize it to novel object instances and scene configurations, without per-instance demonstrations

title: Human-oriented Representation Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding human-oriented multi-task perceptual fine-tuning (Task Fusion Decoder) on top of pretrained visual encoders (R3M, MVP, EgoVLP) consistently improved the resulting representation's usefulness for downstream manipulation policy learning, compared to using those self-supervised encoders' representations directly

title: Domain Randomization via Entropy Maximization

claims.claim: Automatically shaping (increasing) the entropy/diversity of the domain-randomization sampling distribution during training, gated on maintaining high policy success probability, yields more adaptive and generalizable policies than representative fixed/hand-tuned domain-randomization baselines, and enables zero-shot sim2real transfer with unknown real-world dynamics
claims.direction: favors adaptive/automatic domain randomization scheduling over fixed-distribution domain randomization

title: Energy-based Models are Zero-Shot Planners for Compositional Scene Rearrangement

claims.direction: favors compositional/energy-based language grounding over direct reactive language-conditioned policies for complex multi-predicate instructions
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation robot rearrangement tasks, zero-shot execution on instructions with compositions not seen at training time

title: Policy Adaptation via Language Optimization: Decomposing Tasks for Few-Shot Imitation

claims.claim: Combining a handful of demonstrations with VLM-proposed language task decompositions (PALO) enables few-shot nonparametric adaptation to unseen long-horizon manipulation tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art pre-trained generalist policies and methods given the same demonstrations, without needing a larger fine-tuning dataset
claims.direction: favors language-decomposition-guided few-shot adaptation over standard fine-tuning of generalist policies on the same small demo set

title: Towards Synergistic, Generalized, and Efficient Dual-System for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A small diffusion-transformer specialist policy (merely 20M trainable parameters), conditioned on a large VLA generalist's high-level task understanding, achieves a 26.7% improvement in a real-world setting and 12% gain on the CALVIN benchmark compared to OpenVLA alone
claims.direction: favors a small specialist action-decoder conditioned on a large generalist's discretized output over using the large generalist policy alone

claims.claim: The dual-system (RoboDual) maintains strong performance using only 5% of the demonstration data
claims.direction: favors specialist+generalist conditioning for data efficiency over training a specialist from scratch on full data

claims.claim: RoboDual enables a 3.8 times higher control frequency in real-world deployment compared to the generalist VLA alone
claims.direction: favors the lightweight specialist head for higher control/inference frequency over running the large generalist model directly for action output
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, control frequency measured directly

why_deep_read: Directly quantifies how a small (20M-param) specialist action head conditioned on a large VLA can cut latency (3.8x control frequency), work with only 5% of demo data, and still outperform the base VLA -- this maps almost exactly onto our model-size/latency/data-quantity constraints and could inform whether to keep our SmolVLA as a slow planner with a small fast action head.

title: Cage: Causal Attention Enables Data-Efficient Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: With as few as 50 demonstrations from a single training environment, CAGE achieves robust generalization across diverse visual changes in objects, backgrounds, and viewpoints, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art RGB/RGB-D-based approaches
claims.direction: favors DINOv2-pretrained-vision + causal-attention-compressed + diffusion action head architecture for data-efficient generalization over other RGB/RGB-D SOTA approaches

claims.claim: CAGE uses the pretrained vision foundation model DINOv2 combined with LoRA fine-tuning for environment understanding as part of its architecture

claims.conditions: real-world manipulation policy

why_deep_read: This paper's setup (50 demos, single training env, generalization to background/object/viewpoint shift with a DINOv2+diffusion-head policy) is very close to our exact problem (SmolVLA breaking under lighting/object/camera shift with ~50-100 demos); the ablations on causal attention, LoRA fine-tuning, and diffusion head vs baselines would directly inform Q01/Q03/Q14 decisions.

title: Leveraging Pretrained Latent Representations for Few-Shot Imitation Learning on a Dexterous Robotic Hand

claims.claim: Using latent representations obtained from large-scale task-agnostic human-hand-motion datasets inside a transformer-based behavior cloning method yields enhanced performance compared to conventional behavior cloning, particularly in resilience to errors and noise in perception and proprioception
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained motion latent representations over conventional (non-pretrained) behavior cloning
claims.conditions: real-world 23-DoF dexterous robotic hand, few-shot imitation learning trained solely from human demonstrations (no teleoperation)

title: Should We Learn Contact-Rich Manipulation Policies From Sampling-Based Planners?

claims.claim: Popular sampling-based motion planners (e.g. RRT), while efficient for motion planning, produce demonstrations with unfavorably high entropy for behavior cloning; modifying the data-generation pipeline to prioritize demonstration consistency (while retaining solution coverage) is needed for effective policy learning
claims.direction: favors prioritizing low-entropy/consistent demonstrations over raw planner-sampled diverse demonstrations for behavior cloning data generation
claims.conditions: contact-rich dexterous manipulation tasks, diffusion-based goal-conditioned behavior cloning, zero-shot transfer to real hardware

title: A Dual Process VLA: Efficient Robotic Manipulation Leveraging VLM

claims.claim: A hierarchical dual-process design (large VLM 'System 2' running at low frequency for reasoning, small 'System 1' model for real-time motor control/sensory processing) achieves faster inference and higher task success rates than baseline VLA models on the RoboCasa dataset
claims.direction: favors splitting a large slow VLM reasoning module from a small fast real-time control module over running one monolithic VLA model for both reasoning and control

Full text would show achieved control frequency, model sizes, and whether the fast module is small enough for an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Multi-Task Hierarchical Imitation Learning for Home Automation

claims.claim: Hierarchical multi-task IL reusing demonstrations across related tasks reduces new-demo requirements: e.g. clearing table learned from 11.2 demos avg; setting table needs 19 new demos alone vs only 11.6 when reusing clearing-table demos; 4-level pyramid needs 5 demos alone vs 2.7 new demos reusing 3-level demos.

title: Learning Language-Conditioned Robot Behavior from Offline Data and Crowd-Sourced Annotation

claims.claim: Language-conditioned reward/policy learned from offline data + crowd-sourced language labels outperforms both goal-image specification and language-conditioned imitation baselines by more than 25% on manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: language conditioning (via learned classifier reward) favored over goal-image conditioning
claims.conditions: real Franka Emika Panda robot, offline multi-task RL, visuomotor tasks like 'open the right drawer'

title: A Novel Simulation-Reality Closed-Loop Learning Framework for Autonomous Robot Skill Learning

claims.claim: A pixel-level generative domain adaptation (Position-CycleGAN) translating real images to simulated images (and back) enables direct sim-to-real policy migration for vision-based manipulation, improving data efficiency and policy stability over training on real data alone.

title: Back to the Manifold: Recovering from Out-of-Distribution States

claims.claim: Adding a learned recovery policy (using a density estimate of training data and an equivariant latent mapping) lets the agent complete manipulation tasks after external perturbations, whereas plain behavioral cloning fails due to distributional shift.
claims.direction: recovery-policy augmentation favored over pure BC for robustness to state perturbations
claims.conditions: real robotic manipulation platform, image-based BC baseline compared against BC+recovery policy

title: VIOLA: Imitation Learning for Vision-Based Manipulation with Object Proposal Priors

claims.claim: Object-centric representations from a pretrained vision model's object proposals, reasoned over with a transformer policy, outperform state-of-the-art imitation learning methods by 45.8% in success rate.
claims.direction: object-centric/pretrained-proposal visual representation favored over generic end-to-end visual features
claims.conditions: real robot deployment, long-horizon tasks (table arrangement, coffee making), simulation + real quantitative eval

claims.claim: Object-based structural priors improve robustness against object variations and environmental perturbations compared to baseline imitation learning.

claims.conditions: real robot, long-horizon manipulation

title: SEIL: Simulation-augmented Equivariant Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Combining simulated transitions augmentation with an equivariant (O(2) symmetry) policy model learns non-trivial manipulation tasks within ten demonstrations, outperforming baselines by a significant margin.

title: Visual dexterity: In-hand reorientation of novel and complex object shapes

title: RoboCLIP: One Demonstration is Enough to Learn Robot Policies

title: Training Dense Object Nets: A Novel Approach

title: Multi-View Masked World Models for Visual Robotic Manipulation

title: Diffusion-EDFs: Bi-Equivariant Denoising Generative Modeling on SE(3) for Visual Robotic Manipulation

title: Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning

claims.conditions: 3 real robot tasks + 10 RLBench tasks with limited demos, ablation studies included

why_deep_read: Reports detailed ablations on 10 RLBench tasks with limited demonstrations; would clarify how much of the gain requires 3D voxel/depth input and foundation-model distillation versus simpler RGB-only encoders, relevant to our Q03/Q04 depth-camera decision.

title: Instruct2Act: Mapping Multi-modality Instructions to Robotic Actions with Large Language Model

claims.claim: An LLM-generated program pipeline (using SAM for segmentation and CLIP for classification) mapping language/multi-modal instructions to robot action code outperformed many state-of-the-art learning-based policies in several tabletop manipulation tasks in a zero-shot manner.

title: DABI: Evaluation of Data Augmentation Methods Using Downsampling in Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning with Images

title: Keypoints into the Future: Self-Supervised Correspondence in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

title: Implicit Behavioral Cloning

title: Imitation Learning via Simultaneous Optimization of Policies and Auxiliary Trajectories

title: Coarse-to-Fine Imitation Learning: Robot Manipulation from a Single Demonstration

title: Sample-Efficient Learning of Deformable Linear Object Manipulation in the Real World Through Self-Supervision

claims.claim: A self-supervised canonical-image forward model (CaVFM) achieves effective real-world rope goal-reaching using only 1,000 samples of real-world data, with no simulated or human demonstration data, outperforming prior methods in this extreme low-data regime and not losing performance when larger datasets become available.

title: Bayesian Imitation Learning for End-to-End Mobile Manipulation

title: Affordance Learning from Play for Sample-Efficient Policy Learning

title: Implicit Offline Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning

title: Q-Attention: Enabling Efficient Learning for Vision-Based Robotic Manipulation

title: Memory-Consistent Neural Networks for Imitation Learning

title: Learning Generalizable Manipulation Policies with Object-Centric 3D Representations

title: Language-Conditioned Semantic Search-Based Policy for Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: An online language-conditioned semantic-search-based policy that retrieves actions directly from the most similar demonstration trajectories surpasses baseline policies on the CALVIN benchmark and exhibits strong zero-shot adaptation with few task examples.

title: Decomposing the Generalization Gap in Imitation Learning for Visual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing the robot's environment into enumerable factors of variation (e.g. lighting conditions, camera placement) across a 19-task, 11-factor benchmark reveals that generalization difficulty differs greatly by factor; the authors determine a difficulty ordering of factors that is consistent across simulation and a real robot language-conditioned manipulation task.

title: ManipLLM: Embodied Multimodal Large Language Model for Object-Centric Robotic Manipulation

title: Thinking While Moving: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Concurrent Control

title: Grasping Unknown Objects by Coupling Deep Reinforcement Learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, and Visual Servoing

claims.claim: Using CycleGAN to translate real camera images back to the simulated domain (reverse real-to-sim) for a DRL grasping agent achieves 83% real-world grasp success on both previously seen and unseen semi-compliant objects with no real-world fine-tuning, outperforming both a DRL+CycleGAN-only baseline and a visual-servoing-only baseline

title: Learning from Guided Play: A Scheduled Hierarchical Approach for Improving Exploration in Adversarial Imitation Learning

title: Eliciting Compatible Demonstrations for Multi-Human Imitation Learning

claims.direction: favors curating/filtering demonstration data for consistency over accepting all raw collected demos

title: Equivariant Descriptor Fields: SE(3)-Equivariant Energy-Based Models for End-to-End Visual Robotic Manipulation Learning

claims.claim: SE(3)-equivariant energy-based models trained end-to-end from point clouds are highly sample efficient, requiring only 5-10 demonstrations to learn from scratch without prior knowledge

title: R3M: A Universal Visual Representation for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A frozen visual representation (R3M) pre-trained on human video (Ego4D) via time-contrastive learning + video-language alignment + sparsity penalty improves task success by over 20% compared to training vision from scratch, and by over 10% compared to state-of-the-art visual representations like CLIP and MoCo, across 12 simulated manipulation tasks

title: Goal-Conditioned Dual-Action Imitation Learning for Dexterous Dual-Arm Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard deep imitation learning that maps current sensory input to a single reactive action suffers from compounding errors caused by recurrent (step-wise) computation of actions in long-horizon dexterous manipulation
claims.direction: identifies pure step-wise/reactive action prediction as a source of compounding error, motivating a hybrid representation

claims.direction: favors adaptive/mixed chunk-length (trajectory chunking most of the time, short-horizon reactive prediction near contact) over a single fixed prediction horizon
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, long-horizon dexterous manipulation with deformable objects

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our Q06 chunking/execution-horizon question with a concrete real-robot mechanism (adaptive switching between trajectory-chunk and reactive step prediction) that could inform how we handle jerky motion at chunk boundaries.

title: DexMV: Imitation Learning for Dexterous Manipulation from Human Videos

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Pushing and Grasping Objects from Ungraspable Poses

claims.conditions: real robot, phone-based teleop, multi-step tasks, sparse reward RL+imitation

title: Goal-Conditioned End-to-End Visuomotor Control for Versatile Skill Primitives

claims.claim: An end-to-end goal-conditioned controller (predicting action sequences directly from image+goal) reports significant improvements in task success over representative MPC and one-shot imitation learning baselines
claims.direction: end-to-end learned conditioning favored over MPC/one-shot IL baselines
claims.conditions: simulated/real manipulation, pushing/pick-place primitives

claims.claim: Model generalizes to unseen tasks with visual noise, cluttered scenes, and unseen object geometries
claims.direction: favors goal-image conditioning for robustness
claims.conditions: not quantified in abstract

title: Human-in-the-Loop Imitation Learning using Remote Teleoperation

claims.claim: Policies trained on intervention-collected data (human takes over at failure bottlenecks) outperform policies trained on an equivalent number of samples from non-interventional demonstrators, and outperform multiple SOTA baselines
claims.direction: recovery/intervention demos favored over equal-count plain demos
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF robot, precision bottleneck tasks (threading, coffee-making)

why_deep_read: Directly tests recovery/intervention demonstrations vs equal-count plain demos on a real 6-DoF arm at precision bottlenecks -- full text ablations (data collection algorithm, sample-matched comparisons) would directly inform our Q13 data-collection strategy for a small demo budget.

title: RRL: Resnet as representation for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Fusing features from a pre-trained ResNet into the RL pipeline delivers performance comparable to learning directly from ground-truth state, and enables contact-rich dexterous behaviors where SOTA methods stall
claims.direction: favors pretrained visual features over learning vision from scratch/state-free
claims.conditions: simulated dexterous manipulation benchmark

title: Transporter Networks: Rearranging the Visual World for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Transporter Networks are 'orders of magnitude more sample efficient' than benchmarked end-to-end alternatives (including ones using ground-truth object poses) across 10 simulated manipulation tasks, and validated on real hardware
claims.direction: spatial-displacement action representation favored for sample efficiency over generic end-to-end regression
claims.conditions: sim (10 tasks) + real-world validation, stacking/kitting/rope/6DoF pick-place

claims.claim: Method can represent complex multi-modal policy distributions and generalizes to multi-step sequential tasks
claims.direction: favors spatial-action-map representation for multimodality
claims.conditions: sim+real

title: Transformer-based deep imitation learning for dual-arm robot manipulation

claims.claim: A Transformer/self-attention imitation-learning architecture attends to important sensory elements, reducing distraction from extra state dimensions and improving manipulation performance vs. a non-attention baseline architecture
claims.direction: self-attention architecture favored over baseline without attention
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, real-world tasks

title: Efficient Self-Supervised Data Collection for Offline Robot Learning

claims.claim: Actively collecting diverse data (goal-conditioned RL focusing on novel observations) leads to significant improvements in downstream learning tasks compared to less-diverse data collection policies
claims.direction: data diversity favored over count/random collection alone
claims.conditions: simulated robot manipulation tasks with visual inputs

title: Towards More Generalizable One-shot Visual Imitation Learning

claims.claim: MOSAIC (self-attention + temporal contrastive learning) outperforms prior SOTA one-shot imitation methods in learning efficiency, final performance, and generalization to novel tasks via fine-tuning, in a harder multi-task setting (7 tasks, 61 variations)
claims.direction: self-attention+contrastive auxiliary objective favored over prior one-shot IL architectures
claims.conditions: vision-based sim robot manipulation, multi-task

title: Gaze-Based Dual Resolution Deep Imitation Learning for High-Precision Dexterous Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Using high-resolution image cropped around (teleoperator) gaze point for fine positioning plus low-resolution peripheral image for reaching solves a high-precision needle-threading task and improves computational efficiency vs. presumably uniform full-resolution processing
claims.direction: dual-resolution/foveated camera-input strategy favored for precision manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot, needle threading, teleop-recorded gaze

title: Learning Dexterous Grasping with Object-Centric Visual Affordances

claims.claim: Object-centric visual affordance priors generalize better to novel objects, train 3x faster than baselines, and are more robust to noisy sensor readings and actuation, compared to learning from human demonstration trajectories directly
claims.direction: visual affordance prior favored over raw demonstration-trajectory imitation for generalization/robustness
claims.conditions: sim, 30-DoF 5-fingered hand, 40 objects across 2 datasets

title: CLIPort: What and Where Pathways for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining a pretrained CLIP (semantic 'what') stream with a spatial Transporter ('where') stream gives both broad semantic generalization and spatial precision for manipulation
claims.direction: pretrained vision-language encoder + spatial action representation favored over pure end-to-end learned representations
claims.conditions: sim+real tabletop tasks

claims.claim: Language-conditioned imitation agent solves tabletop tasks from packing unseen objects to folding cloths using natural language, generalizing to unseen semantic concepts
claims.direction: favors language conditioning via pretrained CLIP text/image embeddings
claims.conditions: sim (many tasks) + real-world (9 tasks)

claims.claim: Approach is data efficient in few-shot settings
claims.direction: pretrained multimodal encoder reduces demo requirements
claims.conditions: few-shot regime, sim+real

claims.claim: One multi-task policy trained across 10 simulated and 9 real-world tasks performs better than or comparable to separate single-task policies
claims.direction: single shared small(ish) multi-task model favored over per-task models
claims.conditions: sim+real multi-task tabletop

why_deep_read: Widely-cited foundational result combining pretrained vision-language (CLIP) semantics with spatial action maps; directly informs our Q03 (pretrained encoder choice), Q08 (language conditioning method), and Q13 (few-shot data efficiency) decisions -- full ablations (CLIP vs. from-scratch, language module choices, demo-count sweeps) would be very actionable.

title: Learning Fabric Manipulation in the Real World with Human Videos

claims.claim: Using only a handful of human (non-robot) video demonstrations, a pick-and-place policy can be learned and deployed on a real robot with no robot teleop data collection at all, reliably reaching folded states from crumpled configurations
claims.direction: favors small numbers of human-video demos as sufficient with the right pipeline
claims.conditions: real robot, fabric smoothing/folding, handful of demos

title: Learning Robust Real-World Dexterous Grasping Policies via Implicit Shape Augmentation

claims.claim: A correspondence-aware implicit generative model deforms object meshes and a small number of human demonstrated grasps to synthesize a much larger diverse training dataset, achieving 79% success grasping unseen objects in the real world
claims.direction: favors generative/synthetic augmentation of a small demo set over collecting more real demos
claims.conditions: real-world, four-fingered Allegro hand, novel semantic object classes

title: A System for Imitation Learning of Contact-Rich Bimanual Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Force/torque information available in teleoperated demonstrations is crucial for phase estimation and task success; including it substantially improves manipulation robustness, yielding a 90% success rate on a multipoint insertion task versus lower without it
claims.direction: favors adding force/torque observation channel over vision/proprioception alone
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, contact-rich insertion task

title: Motion Policy Networks

claims.claim: An end-to-end model generating collision-free motion from a single depth-camera point cloud is 46% better than prior neural motion planners and more robust than local control policies, and transfers to a real robot despite being trained only in simulation with noisy partial point clouds
claims.direction: favors depth/point-cloud input for motion generation
claims.conditions: trained on 3M+ planning problems in 500k+ sim environments, real-robot transfer with noisy point clouds

title: Vision-Based Manipulators Need to Also See from Their Hands

claims.claim: A hand-centric (eye-in-hand/wrist) camera perspective consistently improves training efficiency and out-of-distribution generalization compared to a third-person view, across many algorithms, settings, and sim/real robots -- but only when hand-centric observability is sufficient; otherwise third-person is necessary but then harms OOD generalization unless regularized via a variational information bottleneck
claims.direction: favors wrist/eye-in-hand camera for generalization and sample efficiency, with caveats on observability and third-person regularization
claims.conditions: 6 manipulation tasks adapted from Meta-World, sim and real robot, varying hand-centric observability

why_deep_read: Systematic controlled study directly on our Q11 camera-configuration decision (wrist vs scene camera) across many algorithms/settings and both sim and real robots; full text ablations and the information-bottleneck fix would directly inform whether/how to weight our wrist vs scene camera.

title: LISA: Learning Interpretable Skill Abstractions from Language

claims.claim: Learning discrete, language-correlated skill codes (VQ-based hierarchical imitation) outperforms a strong non-hierarchical Decision Transformer baseline in the low-data regime and composes skills to solve unseen long-range language instructions
claims.direction: favors discrete/VQ skill tokens with hierarchical language conditioning over direct full-instruction conditioning
claims.conditions: navigation and robotic manipulation sim environments, low-data regime

title: Transporters with Visual Foresight for Solving Unseen Rearrangement Tasks

claims.claim: Given only tens of expert demonstrations, adding a visual-foresight multi-modal action proposal module improves average success rate on unseen tasks from 55.4% to 78.5% in simulation and from 30% to 63.3% in real robot experiments, over a state-of-the-art imitation learning baseline (Goal-Conditioned Transporter Network)
claims.direction: favors visual-foresight-augmented action proposal architecture for few-demo generalization to unseen tasks
claims.conditions: real robot + sim, tens of expert demonstrations, rearrangement/pick-place tasks

why_deep_read: Quantified real-robot improvement (30%->63.3% success) from an architectural change under a tens-of-demonstrations budget, closely matching our low-data regime; full text would clarify which architectural component (foresight vs multi-modal action proposal) drives the gain.

title: What Matters in Language Conditioned Robotic Imitation Learning Over Unstructured Data

claims.claim: An extensive ablation study identifies specific techniques that improve language-conditioned imitation learning performance: hierarchical decomposition of control learning, a multimodal transformer encoder, discrete latent plans, and a self-supervised contrastive loss aligning video and language representations; combined, these significantly outperform SOTA on the CALVIN long-horizon language-manipulation benchmark
claims.direction: favors hierarchical/discrete-latent-plan + contrastive video-language alignment over naive single-stage language conditioning
claims.conditions: sim, CALVIN benchmark, offline free-form unstructured play data

why_deep_read: This is essentially a direct systematic ablation study answering our Q08 (best architecture/technique for language conditioning) on a standard long-horizon benchmark; the full paper's component-by-component ablation table would be highly actionable for our planned language-conditioned second-task extension.

title: TAIL: Task-specific Adapters for Imitation Learning with Large Pretrained Models

claims.claim: Among parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (Bottleneck Adapters, P-Tuning, LoRA) for adapting large pretrained imitation-learning models to new tasks with limited demonstration data, LoRA achieves the best post-adaptation performance using only 1% of the trainable parameters of full fine-tuning, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: favors LoRA-style parameter-efficient adaptation over full fine-tuning when demos are limited
claims.conditions: large-scale language-conditioned manipulation tasks, limited demonstration data, continual-learning setting

title: Identifying Expert Behavior in Offline Training Datasets Improves Behavioral Cloning of Robotic Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Vanilla behavioral cloning trained on expert-only data outperformed even the most advanced offline RL algorithms in the Real Robot Challenge III benchmark
claims.direction: favors simple BC over offline RL when data is expert-quality
claims.conditions: real robot challenge (dexterous manipulation), expert dataset

claims.claim: BC performance deteriorates when trained on mixed (expert+non-expert) data even though a large fraction is expert; identifying and isolating expert trajectories via a classifier restores strong performance
claims.direction: data quality/curation (isolating expert demos) favored over using all available mixed-quality data
claims.conditions: real robot challenge, mixed dataset with unlabeled expert/non-expert mixture

claims.claim: Augmenting the training dataset via geometric symmetry transformations further boosted BC performance, contributing to winning the competition
claims.direction: favors geometric/symmetry-based data augmentation
claims.conditions: real robot challenge arena with geometric symmetry

why_deep_read: Real-robot-challenge result directly comparing BC vs. offline RL and showing that data quality/curation (isolating expert trajectories) and simple geometric augmentation matter more than algorithm choice -- very actionable for our small, possibly imperfect teleop dataset.

title: Visual Imitation Made Easy

claims.claim: Behavior cloning policies trained on demonstrations were improved using 'a variety of data augmentations'; the paper provides 'an extensive analysis of its effects' on real-robot pushing and stacking tasks.
claims.direction: augmentation improves BC performance
claims.conditions: real robot, 1000 demos per task, standard behavior cloning, pushing (87% success) and stacking (62% success) tasks

claims.claim: 1000 diverse demonstrations per task collected via a low-cost reacher-grabber interface enabled real-robot generalization to unseen objects.
claims.direction: more diverse demos support generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, 1000 demos/task, novel objects at test time

title: Grasping with Chopsticks: Combating Covariate Shift in Model-free Imitation Learning for Fine Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding an invariant operator to increase data support at critical grasping steps, plus synthetic corrective labels (bounded noise + parametric/non-parametric methods), increased success rate from 37.3% to 80% (human expert baseline 82.6%) on a real chopstick-equipped robot performing fine manipulation.
claims.direction: synthetic corrective-label augmentation mitigates covariate shift and closes gap to human performance
claims.conditions: real robot, fine manipulation (chopsticks grasping), model-free BC, no interactive expert or model needed

title: Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning for Robot Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Incorporating unstructured natural language descriptions alongside demonstrations produces language-conditioned visuomotor policies compared against 'a variety of alternative methods' for a 7-DoF arm.
claims.direction: language conditioning aids fine-grained control and reduces situational ambiguity vs. non-language-conditioned baselines
claims.conditions: simulation, 7-DoF robot arm

title: Seeing All the Angles: Learning Multiview Manipulation Policies for Contact-Rich Tasks from Demonstrations

claims.claim: Training on demonstrations from a variety of viewpoints yields a multiview policy; 'learning from multiview data results in little, if any, penalty to performance for a fixed-view task compared to learning with an equivalent amount of fixed-view data.' Multiview policies implicitly learn spatially correlated features.
claims.direction: favors training with varied/multiple camera viewpoints over fixed single-view data; multiview data collection has essentially no cost to fixed-view performance
claims.conditions: real mobile-manipulation platform + simulation, imitation learning, multi-stage contact-rich tasks

why_deep_read: Directly informs the camera/viewpoint-robustness decision (Q11) for our fixed scene camera + wrist camera setup; full-text ablations on viewpoint count/placement and real-robot results would clarify whether viewpoint diversity during data collection is worth the overhead and how far viewpoint-shift robustness transfers to our exact 2-camera setup.

title: Adaptive t-Momentum-based Optimization for Unknown Ratio of Outliers in Amateur Data in Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Behavioral cloning with a robust t-momentum-based Adam optimizer showed empirical robustness to imperfect/noisy human demonstrations ('amateur data') and could take advantage of additional data while reducing the adverse effect of non-optimal behaviors, evaluated on two manipulation tasks with different robots.
claims.direction: favors robust optimization to tolerate noisy/imperfect demos over standard optimizers when demo quality is mixed
claims.conditions: real robots (two different robots), two manipulation tasks, demonstration data with unknown outlier ratio

title: Vote for Grasp Poses from Noisy Point Sets by Learning From Human

claims.claim: GVN (Grasp-Vote-Net), a 6-DoF grasp prediction model operating on point clouds, 'can achieve more robust performance than state-of-the-art works in dealing with noisy input' (e.g. reflective/cluttered scenes); grasp labels generated via human demonstration plus an automatic evaluation network (20K point clouds collected in 1 hour).
claims.direction: point-cloud-based grasp prediction is more robust to noisy/incomplete depth input than compared SOTA methods
claims.conditions: real-world data collection, point cloud input, grasp-pose prediction only (not full manipulation policy)

title: Learning needle insertion from sample task executions

claims.claim: A deep learning-from-demonstration model predicting the desired robot state at t+1 using an n-step history window (video of past N timesteps) 'is outperforming the existing methods' on a needle-insertion dataset.
claims.direction: using an observation-history window (memory) improves prediction over baselines without such history
claims.conditions: real surgical-robot dataset, 60 demonstration trials, two-arm needle insertion, not yet deployed on real robot control loop

title: Learning Continuous Grasping Function With a Dexterous Hand From Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A Conditional Variational Autoencoder (Continuous Grasping Function, CGF) trained via generative modeling on retargeted human demonstration data 'achieves significant improvement on success rate when transferred to grasping with the real Allegro Hand' compared to previous planning algorithms, while allowing sampling of diverse continuous grasping plans.
claims.direction: CVAE-based generative action model outperforms prior planning-based baselines for dexterous grasp generation and supports multimodal outputs
claims.conditions: real Allegro (dexterous) hand, large-scale human demonstrations retargeted via motion retargeting

title: Masked Imitation Learning: Discovering Environment-Invariant Modalities in Multimodal Demonstrations

claims.claim: Masked Imitation Learning (MIL) learns a binary mask over multimodal observation channels to filter out modalities causing 'state over-specification' (extraneous data that changes distribution across environments and hurts generalization); MIL 'outperforms baseline algorithms in simulated domains and effectively recovers the environment-invariant modalities on a multimodal dataset collected on a real robot.'
claims.direction: selectively masking/dropping uninformative or environment-variant observation modalities improves out-of-distribution generalization vs. naive use of all available modalities
claims.conditions: real robot multimodal dataset plus simulated domains; targets causal-confusion/copycat-style overfitting to spurious modalities

why_deep_read: Directly targets our observed failure mode (breaking under new lighting / moved camera) by identifying which observation channels are environment-invariant vs. spurious; full ablation/mask analysis would clarify whether to drop or reweight scene-camera RGB vs. depth vs. wrist-camera channels for robustness.

title: Residual Learning From Demonstration: Adapting DMPs for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: 'Applying residual learning directly in task space and operating on the full pose of the robot can significantly improve the overall performance of DMPs' compared to other ways of adapting DMPs (e.g. joint-space residual corrections).
claims.direction: task-space / end-effector full-pose residual action correction outperforms alternative (e.g. joint-space) DMP-adaptation formulations
claims.conditions: simulated + physical robot, contact-rich peg/gear/plug insertion tasks, DMP + RL residual framework

claims.claim: rLfD 'enables transfer to different geometries and frictions through few-shot task adaptation.'
claims.direction: residual correction on top of demonstration-learned primitives supports data-efficient few-shot generalization to novel object variants
claims.conditions: physical robot, peg/gear/plug insertion, few-shot adaptation

title: CALVIN: A Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: On the CALVIN long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation benchmark, 'a baseline model based on multi-context imitation learning performs poorly on CALVIN, suggesting that there is significant room for developing innovative agents' relating language to world models.
claims.direction: qualitative: current multi-context imitation-learning + language-conditioning baselines are insufficient for long-horizon, zero-shot language instruction following
