claims.conditions: simulated benchmark, zero-shot evaluation to novel language instructions and novel environments, flexible sensor-suite specification

title: An Embodied Generalist Agent in 3D World

claims.claim: The paper argues most current models 'rely on 2D images yet exhibit a limited capacity for 3D input,' motivating LEO, an embodied generalist agent trained with 3D vision-language(-action) alignment and instruction tuning, evaluated across 3D captioning, QA, embodied reasoning, navigation, and manipulation.
claims.direction: favors incorporating 3D input/grounding over 2D-only image input for embodied general-purpose agents
claims.conditions: large-scale multi-task/multi-domain training with an LLM-assisted 3D data pipeline; a large generalist foundation model, not a small single-task low-data policy

claims.claim: 'Ablative studies and scaling analyses further provide valuable insights for developing future embodied generalist agents' (no specific numbers given in the abstract).
claims.direction: unspecified in abstract
claims.conditions: large-scale generalist model

title: Behavior Retrieval: Few-Shot Imitation Learning by Querying Unlabeled Datasets

claims.claim: Using a small amount of downstream expert/task-specific demonstrations to selectively query relevant behaviors from a larger offline unlabeled dataset, then jointly training on expert+queried data, 'outperforms more complex goal-conditioned methods by 20% across simulated and real robotic manipulation tasks from images,' filtering out sub-optimal/task-irrelevant transitions compared to naively mixing all offline data with task data.
claims.direction: favors selective retrieval/filtering of relevant prior data over naive mixing of all offline data, or over using only the small task-specific demo set alone
claims.conditions: real + simulated robot manipulation from images; small amount of task-specific demonstrations combined with a larger unlabeled offline dataset

why_deep_read: Directly addresses how to get more out of ~50-100 demos by supplementing with unlabeled prior/offline data; full text would give exact demo counts, success-rate deltas, and the retrieval mechanism's details applicable to our low-data regime.

title: What Do We Learn from a Large-Scale Study of Pre-Trained Visual Representations in Sim and Real Environments?

claims.claim: A large empirical study of five pretrained visual representations (PVRs) across five manipulation/navigation tasks, three robots, and two policy-learning paradigms found that 'the performance trends of PVRs in the simulation are generally indicative of their trends in the real world' and PVRs enabled a 'first-of-its-kind result with indoor ImageNav (zero-shot transfer to a held-out scene in the real world).'
claims.direction: supports using pretrained visual encoders and suggests sim experiments with PVRs are a reasonably reliable proxy for real-world PVR performance/ranking
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation across 3 robots, 2 policy-learning paradigms, 5 manipulation/navigation tasks, 5 PVRs compared

claims.claim: 'The benefits from variations in PVRs, primarily data-augmentation and fine-tuning, also transfer to the real-world performance.'
claims.direction: data-augmentation and fine-tuning of pretrained visual encoders improve real-world policy performance, mirroring their benefit in simulation
claims.conditions: same multi-robot, multi-task real-world evaluation as above

why_deep_read: This is precisely the controlled, cross-robot ablation needed to choose a vision encoder (Q03) and decide whether/how to fine-tune and augment it (Q05); the full paper's per-PVR ranking and real-vs-sim correlation numbers would directly guide our encoder choice for the RealSense scene camera and wrist camera.

title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation Policies from Experience and Imitation

claims.claim: Nearest-neighbors interpolation over local time-varying controllers achieved higher performance than a deep-learning interpolation method for generalizing to new initial conditions, though the neural net had the advantage of working blind (tactile+proprioceptive only, no vision)
claims.direction: favors simpler nonparametric method over deep net for generalization in this low-data regime
claims.conditions: real five-finger dexterous hand, non-prehensile manipulation, trajectory-optimization-based local controllers, small training data

claims.claim: Local trajectory-based controllers for complex non-prehensile manipulation tasks can be constructed from surprisingly small amounts of training data
claims.direction: favors small-data sufficiency for local controllers
claims.conditions: real robot, kinesthetic/teleop-initialized trajectory optimization, limited range of initial conditions

title: O2A: One-Shot Observational Learning with Action Vectors

claims.claim: O2A (action-vector reward from single third-person demo + RL) outperforms baseline approaches under different domain shifts, including changes in viewpoint of observation, object properties, scene background, and manipulator morphology between demonstration and learning domains
claims.direction: favors action-representation approach for robustness to viewpoint/object/background shift
claims.conditions: real robot and simulation, one-shot (single) third-person demonstration, RL reward from learned action vectors

title: On-Policy Dataset Synthesis for Learning Robot Grasping Policies Using Fully Convolutional Deep Networks

claims.claim: A synthetic training-data sampling distribution combining policy-sampled grasps with guiding samples from a robust full-state-knowledge supervisor improves rate/reliability of the learned policy vs naive synthetic sampling; a fully convolutional architecture evaluates 5000x more grasp candidates in 0.625s than a prior iterative-sampling policy, achieving 296 mean picks/hour vs 250 MPPH for the iterative baseline
claims.direction: favors guided/curated synthetic data distribution and fully-convolutional dense evaluation over naive domain-randomized sampling and iterative grasp evaluation
claims.conditions: real robot bin-picking/grasping (4-DOF), point-cloud input, synthetic training data with domain randomization

title: SECANT: Self-Expert Cloning for Zero-Shot Generalization of Visual Policies

claims.claim: Two-stage self-expert cloning (RL expert trained with weak augmentation, then a student distilled via supervised learning with strong image augmentation) decouples robust representation learning from policy optimization and significantly improves zero-shot generalization; average reward improvement over prior SOTA is reported per domain including +337.8% in the robotic-manipulation domain
claims.direction: favors strong image augmentation combined with expert-to-student distillation for visual robustness
claims.conditions: simulated RL benchmarks across 4 domains (incl. robotic manipulation, DeepMind Control, driving, indoor navigation); zero-shot generalization to unseen visual environments with large distributional shift; not stated as real-robot or low-data imitation setting

claims.claim: Policies trained with this augmentation+distillation approach generalize zero-shot to visual environments with large distributional shift, substantially outperforming baselines
claims.direction: favors augmentation-based robust representation learning for robustness to visual shift
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Full text ablations would show which specific augmentations (photometric vs crop/shift vs background) drove the large manipulation-domain gain, and whether the two-stage distillation idea is applicable to our low-data real-robot imitation-learning setting rather than only simulated RL with plentiful data.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Robotic Grasping in Clutter and Occlusion

claims.claim: A multi-view change-observation approach (multiple cameras) is proposed to address camera occlusion during grasping; achieved average grasp success rates of 83.6% (cluttered objects), 86.3% (well-ordered objects), and 97.8% (occlusion scenario) in simulation
claims.direction: favors multiple camera viewpoints over a single view to handle occlusion
claims.conditions: simulation only, DRL-based push+grasp policy, cluttered/occluded object scenarios

title: Fast-Learning Grasping and Pre-Grasping via Clutter Quantization and Q-map Masking

claims.claim: Framework (FLG) is pre-trained in simulation and transferred to the real world with minimal fine-tuning, achieving similar or higher grasp success rate than SOTA baselines with a lesser amount of real-world training
claims.direction: favors sim-pretraining plus minimal real-world fine-tuning to reduce real-data/training-time requirements
claims.conditions: real robot, cluttered grasping scenario, DRL (fully convolutional Q-map) policy

claims.claim: 94% grasp success rate reported with demonstrated ability to generalize to novel objects not seen in training
claims.direction: favors the approach for novel-object generalization
claims.conditions: real-world grasping in clutter

title: Learning High Speed Precision Table Tennis on a Physical Robot

claims.claim: Iterative imitation learning (self-supervised goal reaching from undirected demonstration data) scales to a real, dynamic, high-speed precision task without reward design, value-function learning, or sim-to-real transfer, and the resulting policy performs on par or better than amateur humans
claims.direction: favors iterative/self-improving imitation learning over RL-with-reward-design for real-world dynamic control
claims.conditions: real robot, high-speed precision table tennis, continuous on-robot learning

claims.claim: A modest amount of unstructured/undirected bootstrap demonstration data provided up-front drastically speeds convergence of the general-purpose goal-reaching policy; approach is sample-efficient enough to train on a physical robot in just a few hours
claims.direction: favors modest demo counts for bootstrapping when combined with iterative self-improvement
claims.conditions: real robot, few hours of training

title: Learning Deformable Object Manipulation From Expert Demonstrations

claims.claim: DMfD, which uses expert demonstrations in three different ways to balance online exploration vs expert guidance, exceeds baseline performance by up to 12.9% on state-based tasks and up to 33.44% on image-based tasks, with comparable or better robustness to randomness
claims.direction: favors hybrid demonstration-guided exploration over baseline LfD/RL methods, with larger gains for image-based observations
claims.conditions: simulated deformable-object tasks (1D rope, 2D cloth, SoftGym suite), state and image observations

claims.claim: Deploying the sim-trained policy on a real robot incurs only ~6% loss in normalized performance relative to simulation
claims.direction: favors sim-trained demonstration-guided policies transferring with small real-world performance drop
claims.conditions: real robot deployment, cloth-folding task

title: Diverse Imitation Learning via Self-Organizing Generative Models

claims.claim: Existing latent-variable imitation-learning methods fail to correctly imitate individual modes of a multimodal expert; the proposed encoder-free Self-Organizing Generative (SOG) model for behavior cloning, combined with GAIL, significantly outperforms the state of the art at distinguishing and imitating different behavior modes across MuJoCo locomotion and manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors SOM-inspired generative multimodal action models over standard latent-variable approaches for capturing multimodality of human/expert demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation (MuJoCo), multimodal expert demonstrations, locomotion and manipulation tasks

title: Latent Plans for Task-Agnostic Offline Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A hierarchical approach combining a low-level imitation-learned latent-skill policy with a high-level offline-RL skill-chaining policy achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement over SOTA baselines at reaching temporally-extended goals from high-dimensional camera observations, producing previously-unseen skill combinations
claims.direction: favors hierarchical latent-skill (imitation) + offline-RL composition over pure imitation learning or pure offline RL alone
claims.conditions: simulated and real robot control tasks, long-horizon multi-subtask goals, camera observations

claims.claim: A single multi-task visuomotor policy trained with this method handles 25 distinct real-world manipulation tasks, outperforming both imitation learning and offline RL baselines
claims.direction: favors this hierarchical goal-chaining formulation for multi-task policies
claims.conditions: real robot, 25 distinct manipulation tasks under one shared policy

title: Practical Imitation Learning in the Real World via Task Consistency Loss

claims.claim: A self-supervised Task Consistency Loss built on GAN-based domain adaptation aligns simulated and real data at both feature and action-prediction levels, mitigating the sim-to-real reality gap for an end-to-end RGB+depth imitation-learning policy
claims.direction: favors explicit sim/real alignment loss over naively combining sim and real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator, door-opening/room-entry task, RGB+depth input

claims.claim: Combining simulated demonstrations with only ~16.2 hours of teleoperated real-world demonstrations achieves 72% success across sixteen seen and unseen door scenes, generalizing to doors not in the training data
claims.direction: favors supplementing limited real teleop demos with simulated demonstrations to reduce real-data burden
claims.conditions: real+sim demonstrations, mobile manipulation, generalization to unseen scenes

title: Masked Visual Pre-training for Motor Control

claims.claim: Self-supervised visual pre-training via masked modeling of real-world natural images, with the encoder then frozen (no task-specific fine-tuning) and only a control network trained via RL on top, consistently outperforms supervised encoders by up to 80% absolute success rate on a benchmark of motor-control/manipulation tasks, sometimes matching oracle state-based performance; in-the-wild images (e.g. YouTube, Egocentric video) yield better visual representations for manipulation than ImageNet images
claims.direction: favors frozen, self-supervised masked (MAE-style) pretrained visual encoders trained on diverse in-the-wild data over supervised ImageNet-pretrained or fine-tuned encoders
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark suite of varied hand-designed motor-control tasks/scenes/robots, frozen encoder, RL controller on top, no labels/state-estimation/expert demos used for the encoder

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to Q03 (pretrained/frozen vision encoder choice) with a large quantified benefit (up to 80% absolute success rate). Full text would give per-task breakdowns and clarify whether the frozen-encoder recipe and the in-the-wild-vs-ImageNet finding hold for a low-data real-robot imitation setup like ours (fixed scene + wrist camera, lighting/background shift).

title: The Power of the Senses: Generalizable Manipulation from Vision and Touch through Masked Multimodal Learning

claims.claim: Masked Multimodal Learning (M3L) jointly learns a policy and visual-tactile representations via masked autoencoding; jointly-learned multimodal representations improve sample efficiency and unlock generalization beyond either modality alone, and the benefit transfers to vision-only policies at test time
claims.direction: favors masked-reconstruction auxiliary objective (multimodal) for improving sample efficiency/generalization, with gains persisting when only vision is available at deployment
claims.conditions: simulation, three tasks (robotic insertion, door opening, dexterous in-hand manipulation) with visual+tactile observations, RL-trained policy

title: Sim2Real Viewpoint Invariant Visual Servoing by Recurrent Control

claims.claim: Recurrent controller trained sim2real can servo to previously unseen objects from novel viewpoints on a real Kuka IIWA robot, correcting mistakes online using memory of past movements rather than requiring a calibration phase.
claims.direction: favors recurrent/history-conditioned policies over single-step feedforward control for viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: real robot (Kuka IIWA), trained on simulated data + synthetic demonstrations + RL, transferred via adapting only visual layers

claims.claim: Memory of past actions/movements is used to disambiguate viewpoint-dependent control that is impossible to resolve in a single feedforward step.
claims.direction: favors observation/action history over memoryless policies for ambiguous viewpoint conditions
claims.conditions: real robot arm, sim-to-real transfer

title: Asymmetric Actor Critic for Image-Based Robot Learning

claims.claim: An actor-critic where the critic is trained on full simulator state while the actor (policy) is trained on images improves performance over standard image-based training on a range of simulated tasks.
claims.direction: favors privileged-information critic training to speed up learning of vision-based policies
claims.conditions: simulation, multiple manipulation tasks (picking, pushing, moving a block)

claims.claim: Combining asymmetric actor-critic training with domain randomization enabled sim-to-real transfer for several manipulation tasks with no real-world training data.
claims.direction: favors domain randomization augmentation for zero-shot sim2real transfer
claims.conditions: real robot validation, zero real demos, simulated training only

title: Mid-Level Visual Representations Improve Generalization and Sample Efficiency for Learning Visuomotor Policies

claims.claim: Using generic pretrained mid-level perceptual features (e.g. depth/edge estimators) as policy input gives significant advantages over training end-to-end from raw pixels/scratch: better generalization to novel test environments and significantly more sample-efficient training; gains require careful selection of which mid-level features to use (refined into a max-coverage feature set).
claims.direction: favors pretrained/mid-level visual representations over training vision encoder from scratch
claims.conditions: simulated navigation tasks (not manipulation), RL policy, train/test split across different buildings

title: Combining learned skills and reinforcement learning for robotic manipulations

claims.claim: Basic manipulation skills can be trained efficiently from few synthetic demonstrated trajectories, then composed by an RL policy (no demonstrations of the full composite task, no intermediate rewards) to achieve high success rates on a real robot for composite tasks like making a simple breakfast.
claims.direction: favors small numbers of (synthetic) demonstrations per skill plus RL composition over large real demo sets for long multi-step tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, synthetic training data only, composite/multi-step manipulation

claims.claim: Efficient skill training relies on exploring recent CNN architectures and data augmentation applied to few synthetic demonstrated trajectories.
claims.direction: favors data augmentation to make small synthetic demo sets sufficient
claims.conditions: synthetic demos, real robot deployment

title: Improving Task-Parameterised Movement Learning Generalisation with Frame-Weighted Trajectory Generation

claims.claim: A frame-weighted (variance-aware) Task-Parameterised GMM trained on demonstrations from novice users reduces grasping performance errors by ~40% and enables extrapolation to unseen grasp targets under real-world conditions, compared to standard TP-GMR extrapolation.
claims.direction: favors weighting demonstration relevance by variance to reduce reliance on high-quality/expert demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world grasping task, novice-user demonstrations

claims.claim: A modified Gaussian Mixture Regression action-generation method offers far-reaching, low-error extrapolation beyond the distribution of demonstrated trajectories, unlike existing learning methods tested.
claims.direction: favors GMM-based trajectory generation with task-parameter weighting for extrapolation robustness
claims.conditions: simulated reaching task + real-world manipulation task

title: FlowControl: Optical Flow Based Visual Servoing

claims.claim: One-shot imitation (a single demonstration video) is sufficient to program a manipulation task using optical-flow-based visual servoing, without requiring many demonstrations or 3D object models.
claims.direction: favors classical/optical-flow tracking methods over learned policies when only one demonstration is available
claims.conditions: RGB-D observation, foreground mask specifying object of interest, range of manipulation problems including precise motions

claims.claim: FlowControl inherits robustness to visual appearance changes from decades of optical flow research, shown across a range of problems requiring generalization.
claims.direction: favors optical-flow-based tracking for robustness to visual appearance variation
claims.conditions: real-time visual servoing, RGB-D input

title: Learning Arbitrary-Goal Fabric Folding with One Hour of Real Robot Experience

claims.claim: Fabric folding skills were learned from only one hour of self-supervised real-robot experience (no human demonstrations, no simulation), using a sparse reward defined only by a goal image, achieving state-of-the-art results versus prior approaches that required demonstrations or simulation.
claims.direction: favors small amounts of real-world self-supervised trial-and-error data over demonstration-heavy or simulation-based approaches for data efficiency
claims.conditions: real robot, deformable object (towel folding), goal-conditioned pick-place policy, fully convolutional network, sparse reward only

title: Learning to Manipulate Deformable Objects without Demonstrations

claims.claim: An iterative pick-place action space that explicitly encodes the conditional relationship between picking and placing (learning a placing policy conditioned on random pick points, then selecting the pick with Maximal Value under Placing) achieves an order of magnitude faster learning than independent (jointly-learned) pick/place action spaces on deformable object manipulation tasks with visual RGB observations.
claims.direction: favors structured/conditional action-space decomposition over independently parameterized action spaces
claims.conditions: simulation, model-free visual RL, deformable object (cloth/rope) tasks

claims.claim: Using domain randomization, policies trained in simulation transferred to a real PR2 robot for cloth and rope coverage tasks, with significant improvements over standard RL techniques on average coverage.
claims.direction: favors domain randomization for sim2real transfer
claims.conditions: real PR2 robot, deformable object coverage tasks

title: Acceleration of Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning for Visual Grasping by State Representation Learning Based on a Preprocessed Input Image

claims.claim: Typical representation-learning procedures are unsuitable for extracting information useful for grasping from complex raw visual input; a proposed preprocessed input image is key to capturing a compact representation that allows RL to learn grasping skills from highly varied visual inputs, transferring to a real robot with a 68% real-world grasp success rate.
claims.direction: favors task-specific image preprocessing/state representation learning over raw-image representation learning for vision-based RL grasping
claims.conditions: simulated training with varying preprocessing levels, real-world robot transfer, diverse objects

title: Contrastively Learning Visual Attention as Affordance Cues from Demonstrations for Robotic Grasping

claims.claim: An end-to-end imitation learning model that learns affordance cues as visual attention via a contrastive (Siamese encoder + coupled triplet loss) auxiliary objective achieves the highest grasping success rate in a simulated robot environment compared to alternatives that explicitly predict grasp configurations.
claims.direction: favors adding a contrastive attention/affordance auxiliary objective over explicit affordance/configuration prediction
claims.conditions: simulated robot grasping, learning from demonstrations

title: Learning to Manipulate Tools by Aligning Simulation to Video Demonstration

claims.claim: A tool-manipulation policy can be learned by replacing an expert (teleoperated) demonstration with a single YouTube video, using simulation-to-video alignment plus RL, with effectiveness shown transferring the trained policy for a spade tool to a real Franka Emika Panda robot.
claims.direction: favors using widely-available uncalibrated video demonstrations instead of expert/teleoperated demonstrations as the imitation signal
claims.conditions: real robot (Franka Panda) validation for one tool (spade); simulation results for others (scythe, hammer)

title: Imitation Learning with Inconsistent Demonstrations through Uncertainty-based Data Manipulation

claims.claim: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation can detect conflicts in a demonstration dataset arising from scenarios with equivalent/multimodal action choices, and directly altering the dataset based on this uncertainty lets a standard policy network fit the (de-conflicted) data appropriately; validated with real robot scenarios learning from inconsistent demonstrations, consistently achieving task objectives.
claims.direction: favors resolving/removing multimodal action conflicts in the demonstration data over using an explicitly multimodal action head to fit inconsistent demonstrations directly
claims.conditions: real robot, demonstrations with equivalent action choices (e.g., obstacle avoidance, multiple joint configurations)

title: Generalizing Object-Centric Task-Axes Controllers using Keypoints

claims.claim: Modular task policies composed of object-centric task-axes controllers, with controller parameters inferred from visual input via multi-view dense correspondence (keypoints) rather than monolithic neural network policies, generalize to large variance in object size, shape and geometry across 3 manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors keypoint/correspondence-based modular controllers over monolithic end-to-end policies for generalization to novel object shapes
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation tasks (3 tasks), no geometric object models required

title: Learning Variable Impedance Control via Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Force-Related Tasks

claims.claim: An inverse-RL approach recovering both variable-impedance policy and reward function from expert demonstrations shows that a learned reward/policy defined in the (impedance) gain action space has better transferability across task settings than one defined in the force action space, compared against behavior cloning and force-based IRL baselines.
claims.direction: favors an impedance/gain-based action representation over a force-based action representation for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot (FANUC LR Mate 200iD/7L), two contact-rich tasks (Peg-in-Hole, Cup-on-Plate), also tested in simulation

title: An imitation learning approach for the control of a low-cost low-accuracy robotic arm for unstructured environments

claims.claim: An image-based imitation learning controller for a low-cost, low-accuracy, non-repeatable-kinematics robot arm was trained on state/action pairs generated by a Belief Space Planning algorithm (not human demonstrations), requiring only limited training, and demonstrated efficient, robust, good real-world performance on a reaching task.
claims.direction: favors training imitation policies on planner-generated data (rather than human demonstrations) for low-cost/inaccurate arms, requiring limited training data
claims.conditions: real low-cost low-accuracy robotic arm, unstructured/dynamic environment, simple reaching task

claims.claim: The resulting lightweight manipulation system was robust despite the platform's inherent inaccuracy and non-repeatable kinematics, validated in real-world tests.
claims.direction: favors imitation-learning controllers as a way to make cheap, inaccurate hardware usable/robust
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost arm

why_deep_read: Directly matches our low-cost, imprecise-actuation robot setting; full text would show how much (planner-generated) training data was needed and what robustness was actually measured, informing Q13/Q14 for our SO-101 setup.

title: Efficient Planning in a Compact Latent Action Space

claims.claim: A state-conditional VQ-VAE that learns discrete/low-dimensional latent action codes (Trajectory Autoencoding Planner) surpasses existing model-based methods by a large margin and beats strong model-free actor-critic baselines on high-dimensional continuous-control Adroit robotic hand manipulation tasks, with decision latency indifferent to raw action dimensionality.
claims.direction: favors discrete/VQ latent action representations over raw continuous action planning or actor-critic baselines for high-dimensional manipulation
claims.conditions: offline RL setting, simulated Adroit dexterous hand manipulation tasks

title: Learning and Retrieval from Prior Data for Skill-based Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A skill-based imitation learning framework that extracts temporally-extended sensorimotor skills from prior (other-task) data, using representation-learning objectives for predictable skill representations plus a retrieval-based data-augmentation mechanism for policy training, significantly outperforms existing imitation learning and offline RL approaches on simulated and real-world manipulation domains for learning novel tasks data-efficiently.
claims.direction: favors reusing prior multi-task demonstration data (via skill extraction + retrieval augmentation) over learning each new task from scratch with only its own demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation domains, novel target tasks with prior data from other tasks available

title: Visuomotor Control in Multi-Object Scenes Using Object-Aware Representations

claims.claim: Self-supervised object-aware representations (learned by observing free interaction, queried for policy learning and object localization) outperform state-of-the-art object-agnostic self-supervised representation techniques as well as policies trained on raw RGB images.
claims.direction: favors object-aware self-supervised visual representations over raw-pixel input or object-agnostic representation learning
claims.conditions: multi-object scenes, real/sim robotic manipulation, implicit behavioral cloning (IBC) policy

claims.claim: In a low-data regime (1000 trajectories), the object-aware representation gives a 20% increase in policy performance compared to baselines.
claims.direction: favors better visual representations as a lever for data efficiency in low-data regimes
claims.conditions: 1000-trajectory training set, implicit behavioral cloning

why_deep_read: Gives a quantified (20%) effect of representation choice specifically in a low-data regime, directly bearing on Q03/Q13 trade-offs for our ~50-100 demo setting; full ablation tables would clarify which representation properties matter most.

title: Primitive shape recognition from real-life scenes using the PointNet deep neural network

claims.claim: PointNet trained only on artificial/synthetic geometric primitive shapes generalizes to recognize primitive shapes in real point-cloud scans of everyday objects with reasonable but limited accuracy (~78%); a shallow multi-layer-perceptron using extracted features reached ~83%.
claims.direction: reports point-cloud-based shape recognition transfers from synthetic to real with a measurable accuracy gap
claims.conditions: real 3D scans (Yale-CMU-Berkeley object set), synthetic-only training

claims.claim: Training the network with error-corrupted (augmented) synthetic scenes raised real-world recognition accuracy from ~78% to ~86% and improved training consistency.
claims.direction: favors adding noise/corruption augmentation to synthetic training data to improve sim-to-real generalization
claims.conditions: synthetic-to-real point cloud shape recognition

title: Divide & Conquer Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A method dividing a complex task into smaller goal-conditioned skills (chained together) can imitate complex robotic tasks from a single expert demonstration's states, in an extreme low-data regime where most imitation learning algorithms fail.
claims.direction: favors hierarchical/skill-decomposition approaches for learning from very few (as few as one) demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulated complex robotic manipulation task and a non-holonomic navigation task

claims.claim: The task is divided into smaller skills learned as a goal-conditioned policy that solves each skill and chains skills to solve the entire task, with very high sample efficiency.
claims.direction: favors temporal/skill decomposition (short-horizon goal-conditioned chaining) over monolithic long-horizon policies
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation and navigation tasks

title: Real2Sim or Sim2Real: Robotics Visual Insertion using Deep Reinforcement Learning and Real2Sim Policy Adaptation

claims.claim: A pure visual RL insertion policy can be adapted to reality using a proposed Real2Sim strategy that needs minimum infrastructure, avoiding the heavy image rendering, domain randomization training, or extensive tuning that most existing sim2real strategies require.
claims.direction: favors adapting the simulator/observations to match reality (Real2Sim) as an alternative to domain-randomization-heavy augmentation for sim2real transfer
claims.conditions: visual RL insertion task; comparative discussion vs domain randomization/rendering-heavy approaches

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Representation Learning for Visual Imitation

claims.claim: Decoupling visual representation learning (trained offline with standard supervised/self-supervised methods) from behavior learning improves visual imitation performance compared to standard end-to-end visual imitation frameworks that jointly learn representation and action-association, on both offline demonstration datasets and a real-robot door-opening task.
claims.direction: favors training the vision encoder separately (offline, self-supervised) rather than jointly end-to-end with the policy
claims.conditions: real robot door-opening task plus offline demonstration datasets

claims.claim: After decoupled representation learning, a simple non-parametric Locally Weighted Regression (rather than a large parametric action-prediction model) is sufficient to predict actions and outperforms prior visual imitation work.
claims.direction: favors simple non-parametric regression action heads over large parametric models when representations are already good
claims.conditions: real robot door opening, offline datasets

why_deep_read: Directly tests decoupling vision-representation learning from action learning and shows a simple non-parametric action head suffices with a real robot; full ablations would materially inform our Q01 (action head) and Q03 (encoder training) choices for a small-data, low-compute setup.

title: MixTBN: A Fully Test-Time Adaptation Method for Visual Reinforcement Learning on Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Optimizing/mixing statistics of Batch-Normalization layers at test time (without any additional parameters or reward signal) significantly improves generalization of a visual RL policy to unseen environments, achieving state-of-the-art performance on two robotic manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors lightweight test-time adaptation (BN statistic mixing) as an alternative/complement to data augmentation and domain randomization for robustness to environment shift
claims.conditions: simulated visual RL, two robotic manipulation tasks, unseen test environments

title: CRISP: Curriculum inducing Primitive Informed Subgoal Prediction for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Adaptively re-labeling a handful of expert demonstrations to generate reachable subgoals (primitive-informed parsing) plus an IRL regularizer stabilizes hierarchical RL training and improves success rates by more than 40% over strong hierarchical and flat baselines across six sparse-reward robotic navigation/manipulation benchmarks, transferring to real-world tasks.
claims.direction: favors using a small number of expert demonstrations to guide/stabilize subgoal generation in hierarchical policies rather than large demonstration sets
claims.conditions: six sparse-reward simulated navigation/manipulation benchmarks plus real-world transfer

title: Efficient Sim-to-real Transfer of Contact-Rich Manipulation Skills with Online Admittance Residual Learning

claims.claim: A hybrid framework learns robot motion and compliance/admittance control parameters offline in simulation (with domain randomization), then learns only the residual of the compliance parameters online in the real world using force sensor measurements, showing comparative improvements over existing methods on assembly, pivoting, and screwing tasks.
claims.direction: favors decomposing the action space into offline-learned nominal motion/compliance plus a lightweight online residual correction, rather than learning the full contact-rich policy online or purely offline
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-rich assembly/pivoting/screwing tasks, sim-to-real with domain randomization

title: Learning One-Shot Imitation From Humans Without Humans

claims.claim: Training one-shot imitation policies using only simulated (domain-randomized) demonstrations achieves similar real-robot performance to a system trained on real-world human demonstration data, on pushing/placing tasks
claims.direction: favors synthetic/simulated demo data as substitute for costly real human demonstrations
claims.conditions: real Kuka/robot eval, sim-to-real domain randomization, meta-learning one-shot imitation, pushing and placing tasks

title: Training Human Teacher to Improve Robot Learning from Demonstration: A Pilot Study on Kinesthetic Teaching

claims.claim: Kinesthetic teaching produced demonstrations 39% and 13% more similar to a minimum-jerk trajectory than observational and discovery-learning training respectively; observational training gave smoother velocity profiles (32.7% improvement vs 29.5% discovery and 21.9% kinesthetic)
claims.direction: demonstration collection method (kinesthetic vs observational vs discovery) materially affects trajectory quality/smoothness of demos used for LfD
claims.conditions: real 7-DoF Barrett WAM robot, pilot study with 9 novice human demonstrators, kinesthetic record-and-playback teaching

title: Image features for vision-based robot manipulation based on deep reinforcement learning

claims.claim: Comparing three observation types for DRL grasping (TCP position, raw fixed-camera images, and hand-crafted image features [Sobel, Laplacian, HOG, LBP]), image features gave higher success rate and faster learning than raw images or TCP position
claims.direction: favors engineered/compact visual feature representations over raw pixel input for sample-efficient manipulation learning
claims.conditions: simulation only, robotic grasping task, DRL (not imitation learning), fixed viewpoint camera

title: Generalization in Dexterous Manipulation via Geometry-Aware Multi-Task Learning

claims.claim: Multi-task RL policies using object point-cloud representations generalize better and even outperform single-object specialist policies on held-out real-world objects
claims.direction: favors point-cloud/geometry-aware representation over generic single-object policies for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation on over 100 geometrically-diverse objects, dexterous in-hand manipulation, RL-trained (not imitation learning)

title: From Play to Policy: Conditional Behavior Generation from Uncurated Robot Data

claims.claim: Conditional Behavior Transformers (C-BeT), which combine a multi-modal generative action head with future-conditioned goal specification, improve upon prior state-of-the-art learning from noisy multi-modal 'play' data by an average of 45.7% on simulated benchmark tasks
claims.direction: favors multi-modal generative action-head architectures (behavior-transformer-style) over standard regression when demonstration data is noisy/diverse/multi-modal
claims.conditions: simulated benchmark tasks + a real-world robot demo; uncurated non-expert 'play' data with no task labels or reward

claims.claim: Useful task-centric manipulation behaviors can be learned on a real-world robot purely from uncurated play data without task labels or reward information
claims.direction: supports that diverse/noisy uncurated demonstration data (not just clean curated task demos) can still yield usable policies via goal conditioning
claims.conditions: real-world robot, no task labels/rewards, goal/future-state conditioning

why_deep_read: Full text would give per-task quantitative comparisons and architecture/ablation details on handling multi-modal human demonstration data (relevant to our action-head choice, Q01) and on goal-conditioning strategies (Q08) under small, non-curated demo sets.

title: Perceiver-Actor: A Multi-Task Transformer for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Encoding language goals and RGB-D observations as 3D voxels via a Perceiver Transformer and outputting discretized 'next-best-voxel' actions provides a strong structural prior and significantly outperforms unstructured image-to-action agents and 3D ConvNet baselines for 6-DoF manipulation
claims.direction: favors voxelized 3D/point-cloud-like observation-action representation over 2D image-to-action formulations
claims.conditions: 18 simulated RLBench tasks (249 variations) + 7 real-world tasks (18 variations), trained from just a few demonstrations per task

claims.claim: A single language-conditioned multi-task Transformer policy can be trained across many distinct manipulation tasks simultaneously
claims.direction: supports language-token conditioning for multi-task generalization
claims.conditions: multi-task, few demos per task, real + simulated

why_deep_read: Directly tests the 3D/voxel vs. 2D-RGB action representation choice (Q04) with quantitative real-robot results using only a few demonstrations per task, closely matching our low-data setting; would clarify whether 3D voxelization is worth the extra depth-processing complexity for our RealSense setup.

title: Kinematic-aware Prompting for Generalizable Articulated Object Manipulation with LLMs

claims.claim: A kinematic-aware LLM prompting framework outperforms traditional methods on 8 seen articulated-object categories and generalizes zero-shot to 8 unseen categories using only 17 demonstrations total; validated with real-world experiments on 7 object categories
claims.direction: favors leveraging LLM semantic/kinematic reasoning to reduce required demonstrations for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world robot validation, only 17 demonstrations, articulated object manipulation (waypoint generation, not a learned continuous policy)

title: Vision-Language Foundation Models as Effective Robot Imitators

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained open-source vision-language model (OpenFlamingo) with a lightly-added explicit policy head, using only imitation-learning fine-tuning on language-conditioned manipulation data, exceeds prior state-of-the-art by a large margin; ablations reveal that different pretrained VLM backbones behave differently on manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors reusing large pretrained vision-language backbones (over training vision encoders from scratch) for language-conditioned manipulation policies
claims.conditions: benchmark language-conditioned manipulation dataset, imitation-learning-only fine-tuning, designed to allow open-loop control and deployment on low-performance platforms

claims.claim: Explicitly modeling sequential history information with a dedicated policy head (rather than relying on the VLM's own context) is part of the proposed decomposition
claims.direction: supports separating an explicit temporal/history module from the frozen/fine-tuned vision-language backbone
claims.conditions: same benchmark setting

why_deep_read: Directly informs our vision-encoder/backbone choice (Q03) and history-modeling design (Q07) for a SmolVLA-style policy; reports comparative behavior across different pretrained VLMs and an architecture aimed at low-performance-platform deployment, which matches our laptop-GPU latency constraint.

title: Revisiting Energy Based Models as Policies: Ranking Noise Contrastive Estimation and Interpolating Energy Models

claims.claim: A properly trained energy-based model policy (ranking noise-contrastive estimation + learnable negative samplers + non-adversarial joint training) competes with and even outperforms diffusion-model policies and other state-of-the-art approaches on multi-modal benchmarks (obstacle-avoidance path planning and contact-rich block pushing); the popular Implicit Behavior Cloning (IBC) training objective is shown to be biased even at the population level, explaining its poor empirical performance in prior work
claims.direction: challenges the common view that EBMs are impractical for continuous control; positions corrected EBM training as a viable alternative action-head to diffusion models for multi-modal action distributions
claims.conditions: multi-modal manipulation-style benchmarks (path planning, contact-rich block pushing); comparison is against diffusion models and IBC

why_deep_read: Directly addresses the Q01 action-head decision (EBM vs diffusion vs IBC for multimodal human demonstrations) with both theoretical and empirical comparison; relevant to choosing a compute-cheaper alternative to diffusion policies on our 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Dexterity from Touch: Self-Supervised Pre-Training of Tactile Representations with Robotic Play

claims.claim: Combining self-supervised pretrained tactile representations with vision outperforms purely vision-based or torque-based policies by an average of 1.7x across five challenging dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a non-visual sensing modality (tactile) alongside vision for fine-grained/contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real multi-fingered robot hand, 2.5 hours of self-supervised play data for pretraining, few demonstrations for downstream policy

title: From Virtual Demonstration to Real-World Manipulation Using LSTM and MDN

claims.claim: LSTM+MDN (mixture density network, multimodal) architecture outperformed feedforward networks and mean-squared-error-based training signals for generating manipulation trajectories from virtual demonstrations.
claims.direction: favors GMM/MDN multimodal output over plain MSE regression, and recurrent over feedforward
claims.conditions: real robot (Rethink Baxter), virtual-reality demonstrations transferred to physical robot, pick/manipulation task

claims.claim: An LSTM (recurrent, uses observation history) controller outperformed feedforward alternatives for trajectory generation.
claims.direction: favors observation history/recurrence over memoryless feedforward
claims.conditions: real robot, virtual demos, imperfect demos included to teach error correction

title: Hierarchical Foresight: Self-Supervised Learning of Long-Horizon Tasks via Visual Subgoal Generation

claims.claim: Hierarchical visual foresight (subgoal image generation + video-prediction planning) achieves nearly 200% performance improvement over planning without subgoals and over model-free RL, on 3 of 4 simulated vision-based manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors auxiliary visual subgoal/future-prediction models for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation (+ some real cluttered-scene experiments), vision-based manipulation, no action-chunking/imitation-learning framing

title: Bridge Data: Boosting Generalization of Robotic Skills with Cross-Domain Datasets

claims.claim: Jointly training with a large multi-task multi-domain dataset (7,200 demos, 71 tasks, 10 environments) plus 50 demonstrations of a never-before-seen task in a new domain gave on average a 2x improvement in success rate compared to using target-domain data alone.
claims.direction: favors diverse cross-domain/cross-task data augmentation of a small target dataset over collecting only in-domain demos
claims.conditions: real robot, low target data regime (50 demos of new task), end-to-end skill learning

claims.claim: Data from only a few tasks in a new domain can bridge the domain gap and let a robot perform prior tasks seen only in other domains.
claims.direction: favors data diversity for cross-domain generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, multi-domain dataset

why_deep_read: Directly quantifies how much diverse/cross-domain data helps a small (~50-demo) target task, which is exactly our data regime; full paper's ablations on data mixing ratios and which prior tasks/domains transfer best would materially inform our data-collection strategy (Q13/Q14).

title: Residual Reinforcement Learning from Demonstrations

claims.claim: Residual RL initialized from a demonstration-learned policy generalizes to unseen environment conditions more flexibly than either behavioral cloning alone or RL fine-tuning alone.
claims.direction: favors residual-RL-on-top-of-BC over pure BC for robustness/generalization
claims.conditions: simulation, 6-DoF UR5 arm and 28-DoF dexterous hand, sparse reward, visual+proprioceptive input

claims.claim: Pure behavioral cloning is outperformed in generalization by residual RL built on a BC base policy.
claims.direction: BC alone insufficient for generalization; residual correction helps
claims.conditions: simulation, sparse-reward manipulation tasks

title: Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning with ConvNets and Vision Transformers under Data Augmentation

claims.claim: Extensive data augmentation in image-based RL typically decreases sample efficiency or causes divergence due to high-variance Q-targets; a proposed stabilization technique restores stability and achieves generalization competitive with SOTA on unseen visuals.
claims.direction: augmentation helps generalization only if training instability is separately addressed
claims.conditions: simulation (DeepMind Control Suite + robotic manipulation tasks), off-policy RL, ConvNet and ViT backbones

claims.claim: The stabilization method scales to Vision-Transformer-based architectures as well as ConvNets, with augmentation being 'especially important' for ViT-based RL.
claims.direction: ViT backbones can work but need augmentation/stabilization more than ConvNets in this RL setting
claims.conditions: simulation, off-policy image-based RL

title: CACTI: A Framework for Scalable Multi-Task Multi-Scene Visual Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Using state-of-the-art generative models for data augmentation (as one stage of the CACTI pipeline) is part of what enables a single policy to be robust to varying layouts of distractors.
claims.direction: favors generative-model-based augmentation for background/scene diversity
claims.conditions: real robot kitchen manipulation, multi-task

claims.claim: Using pre-trained out-of-domain visual representations improves training efficiency of the imitation policy.
claims.direction: favors pretrained (out-of-domain) visual encoders over training from scratch
claims.conditions: real + simulated kitchen manipulation

claims.claim: A single policy trained with the CACTI framework performs 10 manipulation tasks on a real robot; in simulation, a single policy handles 18 semantic tasks across 100 layout variations each.
claims.direction: favors scaling data collection + augmentation + multi-task training over per-task narrow datasets
claims.conditions: real robot (kitchen objects) and simulation

claims.claim: The trained policy is robust to varying layouts of distractors in the real world.
claims.direction: supports data augmentation/scaling for distractor robustness
claims.conditions: real robot, kitchen manipulation, multi-task

why_deep_read: CACTI's four-stage pipeline (data collection, generative-model augmentation, pretrained visual representations, imitation training) directly parallels several of our open questions (Q03, Q05, Q13, Q14) simultaneously; the full paper's ablations on which stage contributes how much robustness/efficiency would help decide our augmentation and encoder choices.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Relational Inductive Bias in Vision-based Deep Reinforcement Learning of Robot Control

claims.claim: Training the image-encoding network separately (asymmetrically) from the control policy via supervised learning let a learned visual-scene representation replace explicit target coordinates without compromising policy quality or sample efficiency, and improved sample efficiency for a 6-DoF arm in a visually realistic 3D environment.
claims.direction: favors decoupled/pretrained vision encoder (trained separately from policy) over end-to-end joint training from scratch
claims.conditions: simulation only, 2-DoF planar and 6-DoF arm, RL not imitation learning

title: An Adaptive Imitation Learning Framework for Robotic Complex Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks

claims.claim: Introducing dynamic movement primitives into a hybrid trajectory+force imitation/RL framework reduces the number of human demonstrations needed to generalize across a class of topologically-similar insertion tasks, learning new task instances from a single demonstrated trajectory profile.
claims.direction: favors structured motion-primitive priors to reduce demo count for similar-task generalization
claims.conditions: simulation and real hardware, contact-rich insertion tasks

title: Play it by Ear: Learning Skills amidst Occlusion through Audio-Visual Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Online human interventions added during finetuning improved the success rate of offline imitation learning by about 20% on simulated partially-observed manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors adding online corrective/intervention demos on top of an initial offline demo set
claims.conditions: simulation, modest number of teleoperated demos + online interventions

claims.claim: On a real Franka Emika Panda robot, a policy using audio+vision achieved 70% success extracting keys from a bag (occluded task), 50 percentage points higher than a vision-only policy trained the same way.
claims.direction: additional modality (audio) helps under occlusion, but this used a non-camera sensor not in our setup
claims.conditions: real robot, modest teleoperated demo count + online interventions

title: Trade-Off Between Robustness and Rewards Adversarial Training for Deep Reinforcement Learning Under Large Perturbations

claims.claim: A vision-based grasping policy (7-DoF manipulator) trained in simulation with adversarial (TBRR) training transferred sim-to-real with 70% success rate under sensor impairment and physical perturbations without any retraining, outperforming baseline DRL training on standard benchmarks and a door-manipulation task.
claims.direction: favors adversarial/perturbation-robust training for camera/sensor and physical-disturbance robustness
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, vision-based grasping, 7DoF arm, RL (not imitation learning)

title: Self-Improving Robots: End-to-End Autonomous Visuomotor Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Starting from a small set of expert demonstrations, autonomous self-improvement (learning to do and undo the task, inferring reward from demos) improved success rate by 30-70% over behavior cloning trained on just the expert demonstrations, on real-robot manipulation tasks; also 30% better final performance than SOTA vision-based methods on a simulated non-episodic benchmark.
claims.direction: favors augmenting a small demo set with autonomous practice/self-improvement over pure behavior cloning on the demos alone
claims.conditions: real robot manipulation (larger environments than prior autonomous RL work) + simulated EARL benchmark; small initial expert demo set

title: Distilling and Retrieving Generalizable Knowledge for Robot Manipulation via Language Corrections

claims.claim: DROC (LLM-based system distilling/retrieving knowledge from online language corrections) outperforms baselines that directly generate robot code via LLMs, needing only half the corrections in the first round of a new task/object setting and little-to-no correction after two iterations.
claims.direction: favors retaining and retrieving a knowledge base of past language corrections over one-shot code generation
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation with online human language feedback (high-level and low-level corrections)

title: Mastering Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts through Pretraining and Multi-task Fine-tuning

claims.claim: A two-stage pipeline of inverse-dynamics pretraining followed by multi-task fine-tuning, with a multimodal (vision+text) prompt encoder, achieves a new SOTA on VIMA-BENCH with a 10% improvement in success rate over prior methods.
claims.direction: favors inverse-dynamics auxiliary pretraining before multi-task policy fine-tuning
claims.conditions: simulation (VIMA-BENCH), multi-task expert trajectories, multimodal (interleaved vision+text) prompts

claims.claim: Augmenting a pretrained LM with a residual connection to visual input for prompt encoding, modeling dependencies among action dimensions, improved multimodal instruction-following and produced strong in-context learning ability.
claims.direction: favors residual vision-conditioned language encoders for multimodal task conditioning
claims.conditions: simulation (VIMA-BENCH)

title: Using Single Demonstrations to Define Autonomous Manipulation Contact Tasks in Unstructured Environments via Object Affordances

claims.claim: A system using a single manipulation demonstration (captured via AR headset, encoded as an affordance-primitive representation) achieved a 96% manipulation success rate on a real mobile manipulator performing an industrial wheel-valve task, generalizing across 10 object manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: supports that a highly structured task representation can achieve high success from extremely few (a single) demonstrations, though not a general neural-network vision policy like ours
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator, single demo per task, affordance-primitive (non-neural, non-end-to-end) representation

title: Polybot: Training One Policy Across Robots While Embracing Variability

claims.claim: Using wrist cameras (rather than varying external viewpoints) to align observation spaces across different robot embodiments was a key design decision enabling a single policy to transfer across platforms.
claims.direction: favors wrist camera as the primary/aligned viewpoint for cross-platform (and by extension cross-setup) generalization
claims.conditions: real robots: WidowX 250S, Franka Emika Panda, Sawyer; 60 hours of data, 6 tasks

claims.claim: Aligning observation/action spaces (via wrist camera + unified codebase) and policy internal representations (via contrastive learning) across embodiments produced significant improvements in success rate and sample efficiency when using new task data collected on a different robot than the deployment robot.
claims.direction: favors cross-embodiment data reuse with representation alignment over training solely on same-robot data
claims.conditions: real robots, 60 hours across 3 robot platforms and 6 tasks

claims.claim: Aligning policy internal representations across embodiments via contrastive learning bridges remaining domain shift after observation/action space alignment.
claims.direction: favors contrastive representation alignment for cross-domain/cross-embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: real robots, multi-platform dataset

why_deep_read: Polybot's central finding -- that wrist-camera alignment (over external viewpoint) is what makes cross-embodiment/cross-setup policy reuse work -- speaks directly to our Q11 camera-design decision and to how much a camera/viewpoint shift (like ours) can be tolerated; the ablations on which alignment components (wrist camera vs contrastive loss) matter most would be directly actionable.

title: Hand-Object Interaction Pretraining from Videos

claims.claim: A task-agnostic base policy learned via generative modeling on retargeted in-the-wild hand-object interaction video trajectories serves as a manipulation prior that can be finetuned for downstream tasks.
claims.direction: favors video-based auxiliary pretraining of a manipulation prior before task-specific finetuning
claims.conditions: in-the-wild human videos retargeted to robot actions, then finetuned with RL or BC

claims.claim: Finetuning the video-pretrained base policy (with RL or BC) enables sample-efficient adaptation to downstream tasks compared to prior approaches.
claims.direction: favors leveraging large-scale passive video data to reduce needed robot demonstration data
claims.conditions: finetuning on downstream robot tasks, comparison is qualitative (no specific numbers given in abstract)

claims.claim: The video-pretrained prior improves robustness and generalizability compared to prior approaches.
claims.direction: favors video-pretrained manipulation priors for generalization
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: SE3-Pose-Nets: Structured Deep Dynamics Models for Visuomotor Planning and Control

claims.claim: A structured deep dynamics model trained on point-cloud/depth pairs enables closed-loop visuomotor control that 'outperforms the baseline methods on multiple control runs' and runs in real time.
claims.direction: favors depth/point-cloud structured representation over raw baseline networks
claims.conditions: real Baxter robot + simulation, depth data, model-based control via learned pose-space dynamics

claims.claim: Learning a pose-embedding + dynamics (auxiliary structured prediction of scene segmentation and motion) improves visuomotor control accuracy vs unstructured baselines.
claims.direction: favors auxiliary dynamics/pose prediction objective
claims.conditions: real Baxter robot, depth input, point-wise data association supervision

title: Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model for Robotic Policy Imitation

claims.claim: A Bayesian GMM policy representation quantifies per-state action uncertainty and can be fused with additional policies to handle states outside the demonstration distribution, validated on 3 manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors GMM-based probabilistic action head over deterministic regression for handling distribution shift from demos
claims.conditions: real Franka Panda robot, 3 manipulation tasks, continuous control, small demo sets (typical for GMM/DMP-style imitation)

title: Learning robust manipulation tasks involving contact using trajectory parameterized probabilistic principal component analysis

claims.claim: A small set of demonstrations (motion+wrench signals from passive observation) is compactly re-parameterized via traPPCA and sufficient to transfer contact-rich tasks to a robot.
claims.direction: favors small demo counts with structured trajectory encoding over large demo sets
claims.conditions: real robot setup, contact-rich manipulation, small number of demos

claims.claim: The learned representation increases robustness against imprecise sensors, tool adaptation, and changes in execution speed.
claims.direction: favors trajectory-parameterized probabilistic encoding for robustness to sensing/execution-speed variation
claims.conditions: real robot, contact/force-based manipulation tasks

title: Teaching robots to perform quasi-repetitive construction tasks through human demonstration

claims.claim: Trained with 3000 virtual + 85 real demonstration videos, LfD+RL achieved 78% success rate installing ceiling tiles, and success rate 'tends to continually rise with an increase in the number of real demonstration videos.'
claims.direction: favors more (real) demonstrations improving success rate; also shows synthetic/virtual demos can supplement real ones
claims.conditions: real KUKA mobile industrial arm + Gazebo sim, quasi-repetitive construction task, 60 test scenes

title: Concept2Robot: Learning manipulation concepts from instructions and human demonstrations

claims.claim: A single multi-task policy conditioned on natural language instruction + initial image, trained via imitation distillation from single-task RL policies, learns a large percentage of 78 different manipulation tasks and generalizes over environment variations and novel-but-similar instructions.
claims.direction: favors language-conditioned multi-task policy learned via imitation of per-task experts (staged RL-then-IL)
claims.conditions: simulation only, 78 manipulation tasks, no real robot reported

title: Learning Periodic Tasks from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Rhythmic dynamic movement primitives (rDMPs) optimized via Bayesian optimization from a single human video demonstration can capture periodic manipulation behaviors (wiping, winding, stirring) involving deformable/granular objects.
claims.direction: favors DMP-style parametric action representation for periodic/repetitive sub-tasks over generic per-step regression
claims.conditions: real hardware experiments, single human video demo per task, few robot trials, deformable/granular objects

claims.claim: A task-agnostic visual keypoint model is learned unsupervised from only 10 minutes of random unpaired robot/human interaction video, then a policy is fit from a single demonstration.
claims.direction: favors minimal demo counts (single demo) combined with self-supervised visual pretraining
claims.conditions: real robot + human video, no markers/manual annotation

title: Hierarchical Few-Shot Imitation with Skill Transition Models

claims.claim: FIST extracts skills from offline data and generalizes to unseen tasks given only a few downstream demonstrations, substantially outperforming prior baselines on 7-DoF robotic arm manipulation of previously unseen kitchen objects.
claims.direction: favors few-shot fine-tuning on top of offline-pretrained skill/inverse-dynamics models over training per-task from scratch
claims.conditions: navigation maze + 7-DoF arm kitchen manipulation, few downstream demos, offline pretraining

title: Efficient and Interpretable Robot Manipulation with Graph Neural Networks

claims.claim: A single GNN policy trained with imitation learning on only 20 expert demonstrations solves blockstacking, rearrangement, and dishwasher-loading tasks.
claims.direction: favors structured graph-based policy representations enabling very low demo counts (20 demos)
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world; long-horizon manipulation; 20 expert demos

claims.claim: Once the GNN policy learns the spatial structure of a task, it generalizes to a larger number of objects, new goal configurations, and transfers from simulation to the real world without additional demonstrations.
claims.direction: favors structured/relational (graph) action representation for generalization to novel object counts/configs and sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: simulation-trained, tested real-world; blockstacking/rearrangement/dishwasher tasks

claims.claim: Framing manipulation as classification over a graph of task-relevant entities (objects, goals) enables an imitation-learned policy to solve complex long-horizon tasks without detailed task descriptions.
claims.direction: favors graph-structured policy architecture over unstructured (flat) action regression for compositional/long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: 20 expert demos, simulation + real robot

why_deep_read: Directly relevant low-data regime (20 demos) claiming strong generalization to novel object counts and sim-to-real transfer; full ablations/tables would clarify how much of this generalization depends on graph/object-centric structure vs demo count, and whether it applies to unstructured pixel-level policies like ours (SO-101, no per-object segmentation).

title: Unsupervised Learning of Visual 3D Keypoints for Control

claims.claim: Learning 3D geometric structure (latent 3D keypoints) directly from images end-to-end, optimized with a multi-view consistency loss plus task objective, 'outperforms prior state-of-art methods across a variety of reinforcement learning benchmarks,' compared to prior 2D structured/unstructured representations.
claims.direction: favors learned 3D structured visual representations over 2D keypoints/unstructured representations
claims.conditions: simulation, multi-view images, RL control benchmarks (not demonstrated on real low-cost robot)

title: State-Only Imitation Learning for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: An inverse dynamics model trained jointly with the policy can predict actions from state-only demonstrations (no expert actions needed), performing on par with state-action imitation approaches and considerably outperforming RL alone.
claims.direction: favors inverse-dynamics-model-based action inference, enabling imitation from demonstrations lacking action labels (e.g., videos)
claims.conditions: dexterous manipulation, simulation; demonstrations with different dynamics/morphologies/objects than the learner

title: Chain of Thought Imitation with Procedure Cloning

claims.claim: Imitating the intermediate computations of an expert's decision procedure (not just input-observation-to-output-action mapping) via supervised sequence prediction ('procedure cloning') enables significantly better generalization than standard behavior cloning.
claims.direction: favors sequence/procedure-style imitation over flat single-step BC for generalization
claims.conditions: navigation, simulated robotic manipulation, and game-playing environments (sim only)

claims.claim: Procedure cloning shows 'significant generalization to unseen environment configurations, including those for which running the expert's procedure directly is infeasible.'
claims.direction: favors procedure-style imitation for robustness to novel configurations
claims.conditions: simulation experiments only

title: Bayesian Disturbance Injection: Robust Imitation Learning of Flexible Policies for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard imitation learning algorithms assume a single optimal action per state, contradicting human demonstrations which contain multiple optimal actions; BDI uses Bayesian inference to learn flexible non-parametric multi-action policies that better capture this multimodality, improving task performance on real-robot tasks.
claims.direction: favors flexible/non-parametric multimodal policy representations over single-mode (e.g., plain MSE regression) policies for imitating human demos
claims.conditions: real UR5e 6-DOF arm; table-sweep, shaft-reach, shaft-insertion tasks

claims.claim: Injecting risk-sensitive disturbances during training induces human-like recovery actions and improves 'demonstration feasibility' (robustness to deviation from the demonstrated trajectory).
claims.direction: favors disturbance injection to elicit recovery behavior over clean-demo-only training
claims.conditions: real robot, risk-sensitive simulations + real-robot experiments

why_deep_read: Directly addresses multimodality of human demonstrations (Q01) and recovery-from-deviation behavior (Q13) with real 6-DOF arm experiments across 3 manipulation tasks — full ablations would clarify how much of the improvement is from the multi-action policy vs. the disturbance-injection training scheme, both directly actionable for our jerky/OOD-recovery failure modes.

title: Hybrid control for combining model-based and model-free reinforcement learning

claims.claim: Systematically combining a learned predictive (world) model with an experience-based policy ('hybrid learning') improves performance and sample efficiency of learning motor skills; the approach was extended to imitation learning and tested on a real-world pick-and-place task.
claims.direction: favors combining a learned dynamics/world model with the policy over policy-only learning
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place task plus simulated robot control benchmarks

title: Towards Confidence-guided Shape Completion for Robotic Applications

claims.claim: An implicit 3D representation with per-point confidence, sampled at arbitrary resolution, is compared against a state-of-the-art (voxel-grid) shape-completion approach and deployed in a real robotic grasping pipeline from partial/occluded depth data.
claims.direction: favors implicit, confidence-aware 3D shape representations over fixed-resolution voxel grids for grasping-relevant 3D perception
claims.conditions: real robot grasping pipeline, partial/occluded depth sensing

title: SPOC: Imitating Shortest Paths in Simulation Enables Effective Navigation and Manipulation in the Real World

claims.claim: An end-to-end transformer policy using only RGB sensors (no depth map or GPS) can proficiently navigate, explore, and manipulate objects in both simulation and the real world.
claims.direction: favors RGB-only perception being sufficient, against needing depth/GPS
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation transfer, imitation of shortest-path planner demonstrations

claims.claim: 'Extensive image augmentation' paired with powerful visual encoders is cited as a key enabler (alongside data scale) of successful real-world transfer from simulation-only training.
claims.direction: favors heavy image augmentation for sim-to-real / real-world robustness
claims.conditions: transformer-based end-to-end policy, simulation-trained, real-world tested

claims.claim: Training on millions of frames of shortest-path-expert trajectories across ~200,000 procedurally generated houses (40,000 unique 3D assets) enabled effective real-world transfer, suggesting scale and diversity of demonstration-like data drive generalization.
claims.direction: favors large-scale, diverse (if lower-quality/algorithmic) demonstration data over small human demo sets
claims.conditions: simulation-generated expert trajectories, not human teleop demos; real-world evaluated

why_deep_read: Directly tests RGB-only (no-depth) real-world manipulation/navigation transfer with heavy augmentation and massive simulated data scale — full text ablations on augmentation type and data scale vs. real-world success rate would inform our RGB-only, low-data setup and how much augmentation can substitute for scale.

title: Offline Imitation Learning with Variational Counterfactual Reasoning

claims.claim: Generating counterfactual synthetic demonstrations via an identifiable variational autoencoder for expert-data augmentation ('OILCA') significantly outperforms baselines given scarce expert data.
claims.direction: favors generative/counterfactual synthetic-demo augmentation when expert data is scarce
claims.conditions: simulation only (DeepMind Control Suite, CausalWorld benchmarks), suboptimal/offline demonstration data without rewards

claims.claim: Counterfactual data augmentation improves out-of-distribution generalization, tested on the CausalWorld benchmark designed for OOD generalization evaluation.
claims.direction: favors counterfactual augmentation for OOD robustness over training on raw scarce demos alone
claims.conditions: simulation, CausalWorld OOD benchmark

title: Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation from Passive Human Videos

claims.claim: A model trained purely on diverse internet human videos to predict plausible human hand trajectories can be deployed zero-shot (with embodiment transformation) to solve coarse real-world manipulation tasks (opening/closing drawers, pushing, tool use) without any in-domain robot demonstrations.
claims.direction: favors leveraging out-of-domain human video data over collecting in-domain robot teleop demos, at least for coarse tasks
claims.conditions: real-world robot deployment, zero in-domain demonstrations, coarse manipulation tasks only

title: Learning Multi-Step Manipulation Tasks from A Single Human Demonstration

claims.claim: With a single human demonstration (RGBD video, no robot teleop) recorded in a mockup kitchen, mapped to robot primitives via Grounded-SAM key-pose detection, the system achieved 50-100% success per step and up to 40% whole-task success on real dishwashing with different objects in a real home kitchen.
claims.direction: favors single-demonstration, primitive/keypose-based imitation over many-demo end-to-end policies for multi-step tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, single human demo, multi-step long-horizon task (dishwashing), tested with novel objects/environment (home kitchen vs mockup)

why_deep_read: Reports quantitative real-robot success rates (50-100% per-step, 40% whole-task) from a single demo generalizing to a new kitchen/new objects — directly relevant to our extremely low-data (single-to-few-demo) regime and object generalization question; full text would clarify failure modes and how far this scales beyond 1 demo.

title: GenAug: Retargeting behaviors to unseen situations via Generative Augmentation

claims.claim: Using pre-trained image-text generative models (trained on non-robotics web data) as a 'semantic' data-augmentation tool for tabletop manipulation significantly improves policy generalization, requiring only marginal amounts of real-world data.
claims.direction: favors generative/semantic augmentation over standard photometric/geometric augmentation when data is scarce
claims.conditions: real-world tabletop manipulation, marginal real data plus generative augmentation

claims.claim: GenAug shows a 40% improvement in generalization to novel scenes and objects on real object manipulation problems.
claims.direction: favors generative augmentation for robustness to novel scenes/objects
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, tabletop manipulation, novel objects and scenes not in training data

why_deep_read: Directly reports a quantitative 40% generalization improvement to novel scenes/objects from generative augmentation with only marginal real data — squarely matches our failure modes (new-looking pumpkin, new background/lighting) and our need to avoid large new data collection; full text/ablations would clarify which augmentation types (background swap vs object appearance) matter most.

title: MimicPlay: Long-Horizon Imitation Learning by Watching Human Play

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework that learns latent plans from cheap, unlabeled human play video to guide low-level visuomotor control trained on only a small number of teleoperated demonstrations reduces the demonstration requirement for long-horizon tasks.
claims.direction: favors combining abundant cheap human play data with a small teleop demo set over collecting a large teleop-only dataset
claims.conditions: real-world, 14 long-horizon manipulation tasks, small number of teleoperated demos plus human play video

claims.claim: A hierarchical latent-plan-then-visuomotor-control policy architecture outperforms state-of-the-art (flat) imitation learning methods in task success rate, generalization, and robustness to disturbances.
claims.direction: favors hierarchical/plan-conditioned policy architecture over flat single-level IL baselines
claims.conditions: real-world, 14 long-horizon manipulation tasks
