claims.claim: MimicPlay improves robustness to disturbances compared to SOTA IL baselines.
claims.direction: favors hierarchical human-play-guided IL for disturbance robustness
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, 14 tasks

why_deep_read: Highly cited (367), real-world, systematic evaluation across 14 long-horizon tasks with quantitative comparison to SOTA IL on success rate/generalization/disturbance robustness, and directly tackles the small-teleop-demo-budget problem via cheap human play data — a candidate architecture pattern for our low-demo, robustness-limited setup; full tables would show how few teleop demos suffice and what disturbances were tested.

title: Robotic Offline RL from Internet Videos via Value-Function Pre-Training

claims.claim: Pre-training a value function via temporal-difference learning on large-scale human video datasets (e.g. Ego4D), then combining with offline RL on robot data, produces manipulation policies on a real WidowX robot that 'greatly improve over prior methods' in performance, robustness, and generalization.
claims.direction: favors auxiliary value-function pretraining from action-free human video as an auxiliary objective over training only on in-domain robot data
claims.conditions: real WidowX robot, several manipulation tasks, large-scale internet human video pretraining

title: LoHoRavens: A Long-Horizon Language-Conditioned Benchmark for Robotic Tabletop Manipulation

claims.claim: Comparing two ways of bridging observation feedback into LLM-based closed-loop planning for language-conditioned tabletop manipulation (caption generation vs. a learnable interface), both baselines 'struggle to solve some tasks,' indicating long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation remains challenging for current models.
claims.direction: neutral/cautionary: neither explicit (caption) nor implicit (learnable interface) language-observation bridging solves long-horizon tasks reliably
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, tabletop manipulation, long-horizon language-conditioned tasks

title: LIV: Language-Image Representations and Rewards for Robotic Control

claims.claim: A vision-language representation jointly pre-trained with a value/reward objective on action-free human video with text annotations (e.g. EpicKitchen), then optionally fine-tuned on target-domain data, 'consistently outperform[s] the best prior input state representations for imitation learning' across several simulated and real-world robot environments.
claims.direction: favors control-centric vision-language pretraining (LIV) over other pretrained visual/vision-language encoders as the IL backbone
claims.conditions: real-world + simulated robot environments, language- or image-goal specified tasks, optional domain-specific fine-tuning

claims.claim: The same LIV representation supports both language and image goal specification via a unified embedding, used for imitation learning and reward specification.
claims.direction: favors unified language/image goal embedding for conditioning policies
claims.conditions: real-world + simulated robots

claims.claim: Joint vision-language representation and (value-function) reward learning as an auxiliary/pretraining objective improves downstream imitation learning and reward-based policy synthesis versus representation-only or reward-only pretraining.
claims.direction: favors combined representation+reward auxiliary pretraining objective
claims.conditions: large human video pretraining, real+sim robot fine-tuning/evaluation

why_deep_read: Directly claims a pretrained vision-language representation beats prior state representations for imitation learning on real robots — this is central to our Q03 encoder choice (vs. DINOv2/SigLIP/CLIP/R3M/VC-1); full ablation tables would show magnitude of improvement and whether it holds for small low-cost-arm datasets like ours.

title: An offline learning of behavior correction policy for vision-based robotic manipulation

claims.claim: A two-stage agent (tentative action stage + image-crop-based correction stage) enables effective offline learning with a small dataset for vision-based manipulation, and 'task performance is significantly improved by the correction stage' when combined with conventional offline RL and imitation learning algorithms.
claims.direction: favors a coarse-then-refine two-stage action architecture over single-stage policies when data is limited
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation benchmark, small dataset, combined with offline RL and IL baselines

title: DART: Noise Injection for Robust Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Injecting optimized noise into supervisor demonstrations during collection (to elicit recovery behavior) outperformed plain Behavior Cloning by 62% average performance increase on a real grasping-in-clutter task with a Toyota HSR robot.
claims.direction: favors noise-injected/recovery demonstrations over plain BC demos
claims.conditions: real robot (Toyota HSR), grasping in clutter; also sim MuJoCo tasks; compared to DAgger and BC

claims.claim: DART is an off-policy method that avoids DAgger's need for online supervisor queries while still producing policies robust to compounding drift/errors, at much lower computational cost (up to 3x faster than DAgger on high-dim tasks) with only 5% supervisor reward decrease during data collection vs. DAgger's 80% decrease.
claims.direction: favors deliberately noised demonstrations for robustness to drift over vanilla demos or online DAgger
claims.conditions: sim (MuJoCo Walker/Humanoid/Hopper/HalfCheetah) and real robot grasping

title: Imitation and Mirror Systems in Robots through Deep Modality Blending Networks

claims.claim: A conditional-neural-process-based model that blends vision and proprioception into a common latent space and generates a complete multi-modal trajectory in one shot (rather than autoregressively) outperformed recent multimodal variational-autoencoder baselines on long-horizon, high-dimensional trajectory prediction, and can predict a missing modality (camera or joint angles) from the other.
claims.direction: favors joint multimodal latent-space auxiliary prediction/reconstruction over per-step autoregressive or single-modality models
claims.conditions: real arm-gripper robot + RGB camera, small simulation-style tabletop experiments

claims.claim: Mirror/imitation behavior required both proprioceptive and visual experience jointly; visual experience alone was insufficient to reproduce learned imitation behavior.
claims.direction: favors multimodal (proprioception+vision) observation history over vision-only
claims.conditions: real arm-gripper robot, one-shot trajectory generation avoiding compounding prediction error

title: Bottom-Up Skill Discovery From Unsegmented Demonstrations for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Skills discovered from multi-task demonstrations boosted average task success by 8% compared to skills discovered from individual-task demonstrations only, and the entire model could be trained on a small set of human demonstrations collected within 30 minutes with no further annotation.
claims.direction: favors diverse multi-task demonstration data over single-task data of equal collection effort
claims.conditions: real robot, unsegmented human demonstrations (~30 minutes collection), multi-stage manipulation tasks; also simulation

title: Language Conditioned Imitation Learning Over Unstructured Data

claims.claim: Incorporating free-form natural language conditioning end-to-end with unlabeled/unstructured demonstration data (no per-demo task or language labels) dramatically improved language-conditioned performance versus requiring labeled task/goal-image conditioning, while reducing the cost of language annotation to less than 1% of total data.
claims.direction: favors language conditioning trained on mostly-unlabeled play data plus a small fraction of language-labeled data, over fully-labeled task-id/goal-image conditioning
claims.conditions: single neural network doing perception+language understanding+multitask control; visuomotor policy in a 3D simulated manipulation environment, tested with live typed human instructions

claims.claim: A single language-conditioned policy trained mostly on unstructured, unlabeled play-style demonstration data generalized to a wide variety of manipulation skills specified only by natural-language description, including robustness to out-of-distribution synonym instructions without new demonstrations when combined with pretrained language models.
claims.direction: favors large amounts of unstructured/unlabeled demo data augmented with a small labeled subset over fully task-labeled datasets
claims.conditions: 3D simulated tabletop manipulation, multi-task

title: BC-Z: Zero-Shot Task Generalization with Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Scaling real-robot data collection to more than 100 distinct manipulation tasks, combined with an interactive imitation-learning system that learns from both demonstrations and human interventions, enabled the policy to perform 24 completely unseen manipulation tasks with average 44% success rate without any demonstrations of those specific tasks.
claims.direction: favors broad task-diversity scaling of demonstration+intervention data over per-task demonstration collection, for generalization to novel tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, vision-based manipulation, >100 training tasks, evaluated zero-shot on 24 unseen tasks

claims.claim: Conditioning the policy on pretrained embeddings of either natural language or videos of humans performing the task allowed task specification without robot demonstrations for the target task.
claims.direction: favors language/video embedding conditioning for task specification and zero-shot generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, large multi-task dataset

why_deep_read: Full paper's ablations on how much data/how many tasks and how much intervention data are needed for generalization, plus architecture details, would materially inform data-collection strategy (Q13) and language conditioning (Q08) tradeoffs for a small low-cost-robot dataset.

title: Modularity through Attention: Efficient Training and Transfer of Language-Conditioned Policies for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical-modularity architecture with supervised attention across sub-modules for language-conditioned manipulation outperformed current state-of-the-art language-conditioned policy methods and enabled sample-efficient transfer of the learned policy across 4 different robots.
claims.direction: favors modular attention-based language conditioning over monolithic end-to-end language-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: simulated and real world robot manipulation experiments

title: DeXtreme: Transfer of Agile In-hand Manipulation from Simulation to Reality

claims.claim: Policies trained in simulation with broad domain randomization across a wide range of conditions produced vision-based policies that significantly outperformed the best prior vision-based policies in the literature on an in-hand reorientation task, and were competitive with policies given privileged state via motion capture.
claims.direction: favors extensive domain-randomized simulation training for real-world vision robustness
claims.conditions: real Allegro Hand + camera, sim-to-real transfer, affordable/commonly-available robot hands and cameras

title: Look Closer: Bridging Egocentric and Third-Person Views With Transformers for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing a static third-person camera and a wrist-mounted egocentric camera with a cross-view attention Transformer raised real-robot hammer-manipulation success to 75%, versus 38% for a multi-view baseline (without the attention fusion) and 13% for a single (third-person only) view baseline.
claims.direction: favors wrist/egocentric camera + scene camera fused via cross-view attention over single-view or naive multi-view fusion
claims.conditions: real robot, RL policy, uncalibrated cameras, no privileged state information, precision manipulation tasks with high task variability

why_deep_read: Directly matches our two-camera (fixed scene + wrist) setup; the full paper's architecture and ablations for cross-view attention fusion could directly inform how to combine our two camera streams for viewpoint robustness (Q11), including why naive multi-view concatenation underperforms.

title: Behavior Transformers: Cloning k modes with one stone

claims.claim: Behavior Transformer (BeT), combining a transformer backbone with action discretization (k-means binning) and a multi-task offset-prediction action correction (inspired by object detection), significantly improves over prior state-of-the-art behavioral cloning and offline RL methods at capturing multiple modes present in unlabeled, reward-free human demonstration data across manipulation and driving datasets.
claims.direction: favors discretized/binned multimodal action-head with continuous offset correction over single-mode (unimodal Gaussian/MSE) behavioral cloning for multimodal human demonstration data
claims.conditions: variety of robotic manipulation and self-driving offline demonstration datasets (no reward labels); ablation study performed on each component

why_deep_read: This is a foundational comparative study on handling multimodality in human demonstrations for the action head (Q01). Its ablation of discretization+offset-correction components vs. plain regression would directly inform whether to move away from L1/MSE regression for our task given SmolVLA's current failures, and is a strong prior for CVAE/diffusion/VQ alternatives comparison.

title: Multimodal and Force-Matched Imitation Learning With a See-Through Visuotactile Sensor

claims.claim: On real-robot door-opening tasks, adding tactile-force matching (recreating recorded contact forces during kinesthetic teaching) raised policy success rates by 62.5%, learned visuotactile mode-switching (coupling vision/tactile sensor modes with motion policy) raised success by 30.3%, and simply adding visuotactile data as a policy input raised success by 42.5%, versus baselines without these components.
claims.direction: favors adding tactile/force modalities and mode-switching auxiliary structure over vision-only imitation learning for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, four door-opening tasks, kinesthetic teaching demonstrations, ablation across observation/algorithm configurations

title: Learning Multiple Robot Manipulation Tasks with Imperfect Demonstrations

claims.claim: A weighting strategy that down-weights unreliable/erroneous demonstrations when combining RL with imperfect expert demonstrations achieved over 85% average success rate across multiple manipulation tasks, superior to a state-of-the-art baseline, and was shown to be more robust than the baseline specifically when demonstrations contain errors.
claims.direction: favors quality-weighted use of imperfect demonstration data over treating all demonstrations equally
claims.conditions: simulation, dexterous/humanoid hand manipulation tasks, demonstrations generated with deep-learning methods (containing errors)

title: RLIF: Interactive Imitation Learning as Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Using human intervention signals themselves as RL rewards (rather than assuming near-optimal interventions as in DAgger) strongly outperformed DAgger-like interactive imitation learning approaches, especially when the intervening human expert was suboptimal, on both high-dimensional continuous control simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic vision-based manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors treating human corrections/interventions as reward signal (RL) over assuming near-optimal DAgger-style correction data
claims.conditions: real-world vision-based robotic manipulation tasks plus sim continuous control benchmarks; suboptimal human experts

title: Learning Fine Pinch-Grasp Skills using Tactile Sensing from A Few Real-world Demonstrations

claims.claim: A data-efficient imitation-learning framework using rich tactile sensing achieved robust fine bimanual pinch-grasping learned from only a few real-world demonstrations, generalizing to ten unseen novel objects and remaining robust to external pushes and object drops, using few-shot demonstration data.
claims.direction: favors incorporating rich contact/tactile sensing to reduce required real-world demonstration count
claims.conditions: real robot, few-shot (small number) real-world demonstrations, bimanual pinch grasping

claims.claim: A comparison against the same framework without encoded tactile features showed that incorporating rich contact information (via a convolutional autoencoder for tactile features) was clearly more effective for contact-aware sensorimotor skill learning.
claims.direction: favors auxiliary tactile-encoding/multimodal fusion over vision-only observation encoding
claims.conditions: real robot bimanual pinch-grasp task, ablation with/without tactile encoding

title: SPRINT: Scalable Policy Pre-Training via Language Instruction Relabeling

claims.claim: Automatically expanding pre-training tasks via LLM-based language instruction relabeling plus offline-RL cross-trajectory skill chaining substantially reduced human annotation effort versus manually labeling instructions, and led to substantially faster learning of new long-horizon tasks than prior language-conditioned pre-training approaches.
claims.direction: favors automatically-relabeled/LLM-generated language instructions over manually annotated instructions for pre-training language-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: household simulator and a real robot kitchen manipulation task

title: Scaling Robot Learning with Semantically Imagined Experience

claims.claim: Using text-to-image diffusion models to inpaint unseen objects, backgrounds, and distractors into existing real robot manipulation datasets (pure text-guided augmentation, no extra robot data collection) enabled manipulation policies to solve completely unseen tasks with new objects.
claims.direction: favors generative/diffusion-based data augmentation (object/background/distractor inpainting) over collecting more real demonstrations for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation experiments, augmenting existing robot datasets with no additional robot data

claims.claim: Policies trained on diffusion-augmented data behaved more robustly with respect to novel distractors, and the augmentation also improved robustness/generalization of higher-level tasks like success detection.
claims.direction: favors generative augmentation for robustness to novel distractors/objects
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, no additional robot demonstrations required

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our observed failure modes (new lighting/pumpkin/camera position) via cheap generative augmentation without collecting more real demos; full text's specifics on inpainting recipe, how much data was augmented, and quantitative success-rate deltas would be very actionable for our low-data setup.

title: RT-H: Action Hierarchies Using Language

claims.claim: Introducing an intermediate 'language motion' layer (fine-grained phrases like 'move arm forward') between high-level task language and low-level actions let the policy share structure across semantically diverse tasks and outperformed methods that learn only from teleoperated interventions, since the policy could also learn directly from human language corrections during execution.
claims.direction: favors hierarchical language conditioning (high-level task -> language-described motion primitives -> action) over flat single-level language-to-action conditioning, especially as tasks become more semantically diverse
claims.conditions: real robot, multi-task manipulation datasets, language interventions used as correction signal

title: Video Prediction Policy: A Generalist Robot Policy with Predictive Visual Representations

claims.claim: Learning an implicit inverse-dynamics model conditioned on visual representations predicted by a video diffusion model (fine-tuned on robot + internet human manipulation data) achieved an 18.6% relative improvement on the CALVIN ABC-D generalization benchmark over the prior state of the art, and a 31.6% increase in success rate on complex real-world dexterous manipulation tasks.
claims.direction: favors vision encoders/representations trained with future-prediction (video diffusion, dynamics-aware) auxiliary objectives over static single-image reconstruction or two-image contrastive pretraining
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation tasks plus CALVIN ABC-D sim benchmark; representation fine-tuned on robot data + internet human video

why_deep_read: Gives a concrete, large quantitative gain from a future-prediction/world-model auxiliary objective for the vision encoder (Q09) and choice of pretraining signal (Q03); worth checking model size and inference cost in the full text since our setup is compute- and latency-constrained (laptop GPU, ~2s current latency).

title: ILBiT: Imitation Learning for Robot Using Position and Torque Information based on Bilateral Control with Transformer

claims.claim: Replacing an LSTM-based action-prediction backbone with a Transformer for bilateral-control imitation learning (using position and torque information) improved handling of diverse datasets and detailed force adjustments versus the LSTM baseline.
claims.direction: favors Transformer-based sequence action head over LSTM for imitation learning with proprioceptive (position/torque) data
claims.conditions: real robot arm, bilateral control teleoperation demonstrations

claims.claim: The Transformer-based bilateral control policy operated at a high control frequency of 100 Hz, improving adaptability and response to varying environments and object hardness.
claims.direction: favors high-frequency, low-latency control loop for responsive manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot arm, real-world experiments across objects of varying hardness

title: TelePreview: A User-Friendly Teleoperation System with Virtual Arm Assistance for Enhanced Effectiveness

claims.claim: A low-cost (<$1000) teleoperation system that previews the robot's intended action as a virtual overlay before execution outperformed other teleoperation systems across five tasks and made it easier/safer for new users to give demonstrations.
claims.direction: favors improved teleoperation interfaces (virtual preview) for higher-quality demonstration collection over standard direct teleoperation
claims.conditions: real robot teleoperation, low-cost hardware, five manipulation tasks, comparison across teleoperation platforms

title: AutoRT: Embodied Foundation Models for Large Scale Orchestration of Robotic Agents

claims.claim: Using VLMs/LLMs to autonomously propose diverse, novel instructions for a fleet of robots (rather than only human-scripted tasks) produced significantly more diverse 'in-the-wild' data (77k real robot episodes across 20+ robots) than typical curated data collection.
claims.direction: favors foundation-model-guided autonomous task/instruction proposal for increasing demonstration diversity over manually scripted task collection
claims.conditions: real robots (20+, multiple buildings), teleoperation and autonomous policy data collection combined

title: Active Vision Might Be All You Need: Exploring Active Vision in Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Learning an active-vision policy that dynamically repositions an additional camera (in addition to the manipulation policy) to seek better viewpoints via human-guided demonstrations showed significant improvements over fixed cameras in imitation-learning tasks with limited visibility (occlusion, restricted field of view), in both real-world and simulation experiments.
claims.direction: favors dynamically-repositionable/active camera viewpoints over statically fixed cameras for imitation learning, especially under occlusion
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated bimanual manipulation (AV-ALOHA / ALOHA2-based system), extra 7-DoF camera-only arm

title: Click to Grasp: Zero-Shot Precise Manipulation via Visual Diffusion Descriptors

claims.claim: Dense semantic part correspondences extracted from web-trained text-to-image diffusion model features (no task-specific training) enabled zero-shot precise part-grasping generalizable across visually different instances of the same object category, without any manual grasping demonstrations.
claims.direction: favors large pretrained generative-model visual features (diffusion descriptors) over task-specific trained vision encoders for cross-instance/object generalization
claims.conditions: real-world tabletop manipulation, zero-shot (no grasp demonstrations), tested across visually diverse object instances

title: Data-Efficient Learning for Sim-to-Real Robotic Grasping using Deep Point Cloud Prediction Networks

claims.claim: Learning a domain-invariant 3D point cloud representation of objects and using it to train a grasping policy outperforms a 2.5D shape baseline by 10%
claims.direction: 3D point cloud representation favored over 2.5D/RGB shape representation
claims.conditions: sim-to-real table-top instance grasping; ~76K sim episodes for representation learning + ~530 real episodes; RGBD camera

claims.claim: Real-world data collection for the representation learning step needs only ~530 short episodes (snapshots), cheaper/faster than prior approaches
claims.direction: favors small real-data + sim pretraining over large real datasets
claims.conditions: real+sim grasping, RGBD snapshots

title: Intermittent Visual Servoing: Efficiently Learning Policies Robust to Instrument Changes for High-precision Surgical Manipulation

claims.claim: A learned visual-servo policy trained on only 180 human demonstrations (~2s each), combined with a coarse open-loop policy for non-precision segments, raised peg-transfer success rates from 72.9%->99.2%, 31.3%->99.2%, and 47.2%->100.0% across three surgical instruments with differing cable properties
claims.direction: favors small demo counts (~180) with closed-loop visual feedback restricted to high-precision segments, rather than full-trajectory open-loop control from encoders
claims.conditions: real da Vinci Research Kit, cable-driven surgical robot, backlash/hysteresis/variable tensioning present

claims.claim: Switching to a learned closed-loop visual servo policy only during high-precision segments (intermittent visual servoing) improves robustness to instrument/hardware changes vs relying on open-loop/encoder control throughout
claims.direction: favors intermittent closed-loop correction over continuous open-loop execution
claims.conditions: real robot, cable-driven arm with backlash/hysteresis analogous to low-cost servo drivetrains

title: Generalization in Reinforcement Learning by Soft Data Augmentation

claims.claim: SODA decouples data augmentation from policy optimization (soft constraint maximizing mutual information between augmented/non-augmented latents, RL update uses non-augmented data only) and 'significantly advances sample efficiency, generalization, and stability' vs state-of-the-art vision-based RL baselines that train directly on augmented data
claims.direction: favors decoupling photometric/crop augmentation from the policy loss (representation-only augmentation) over training the policy directly on augmented observations
claims.conditions: DeepMind Control suite tasks plus one robotic manipulation task, vision-based RL

title: Learning Visual Robotic Control Efficiently with Contrastive Pre-training and Data Augmentation

claims.claim: Given only 10 human demonstrations, a single real robot arm learned sparse-reward pixel-based manipulation policies (reaching, picking, moving, pulling a large object, flipping a switch, opening a drawer) in about 30 minutes of mean real-world training time
claims.direction: supports very small demo counts (~10) being sufficient when combined with the right pretraining/augmentation pipeline
claims.conditions: real single robot arm, pixel input, sparse reward, RL fine-tuned with demos

claims.claim: Contrastive pre-training of the visual representation is one of the components (with data augmentation, demonstrations, RL) whose combination enables data-efficient real-robot learning; the authors state each component alone (contrastive pretraining, augmentation, demonstrations, RL) is insufficient, but their combination is
claims.direction: favors contrastive-pretrained visual encoder combined with augmentation and demos, rather than any single technique alone
claims.conditions: real robot, pixels, low-data regime

why_deep_read: Ablation of which combination of contrastive pretraining + augmentation + demos + RL actually drives the gain would directly inform our vision-encoder and augmentation choices under an 8GB-GPU, ~50-100 demo budget.

title: Causal Reasoning in Simulation for Structure and Transfer Learning of Robot Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Restricting domain randomization to causally-relevant state variables (identified via simulated interventions) before sim-to-real transfer yields policies that are 'more robust to domain shifts, more sample efficient to learn, and scale to more complex settings' plus improved zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for block stacking, versus unrestricted/standard domain randomization
claims.direction: favors causally-informed/targeted domain randomization over naive full-state domain randomization
claims.conditions: sim pretraining + real-world fine-tuning, block stacking and crate opening manipulation tasks

title: Watch and Match: Supercharging Imitation with Regularized Optimal Transport

claims.claim: Adaptively combining optimal-transport trajectory-matching rewards with behavior cloning (ROT) achieves an average 7.8x faster imitation to reach 90% of expert performance vs prior SOTA across 20 visual control tasks (DMC, OpenAI Robotics Suite, Meta-World); on real-world robotic manipulation, with just ONE demonstration and one hour of online training, ROT reaches 90.1% average success across 14 tasks
claims.direction: favors augmenting behavior cloning with a trajectory-matching (optimal transport) reward/online fine-tuning over pure BC, especially in extremely low-demo regimes (as few as 1 demo)
claims.conditions: real-world robot manipulation, 1 demonstration + 1 hour online training, 14 tasks; also 20 sim visual-control benchmark tasks

why_deep_read: Directly targets our lowest-data regime (as few as 1 demo) with real-robot numbers; the full paper's task list/robot setup and failure modes would clarify whether BC+trajectory-matching fine-tuning is a viable alternative action-learning approach for our ~50-100 demo, single-arm pick-and-place setup.

title: Learning Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation from Human Grasp Affordance

claims.claim: An imitation objective combined with a geometric (3D) object-representation learning objective, trained on large-scale demonstrations generated from a human grasp affordance model over diverse 3D objects in a category, outperforms baselines by a large margin on manipulating novel objects; ablation confirms the importance of 3D object representation learning for generalization
claims.direction: favors auxiliary 3D/geometric object representation learning to improve generalization to novel object instances
claims.conditions: simulation, multi-finger dexterous hand, category-level generalization, large-scale generated demonstrations

title: Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robots Pick-and-Place Applications: A Case Study

claims.claim: Comparing pre-trained CNN backbones (ResNext, DenseNet, MobileNet, MNASNet) for feature extraction in a Q-learning pick-and-place policy trained in sim and deployed on a real cobot, MobileNet achieved the best result: 89.9% grasping success rate on a never-seen object using color+depth images
claims.direction: favors lightweight pretrained ImageNet CNN backbones (MobileNet specifically outperformed larger/other backbones) for real-robot grasping generalization to novel objects
claims.conditions: real collaborative robot (cobot), RGB-D input, sim-to-real transfer, novel/unseen object at test time

title: DayDreamer: World Models for Physical Robot Learning

claims.claim: Learning a world model (Dreamer) directly from real-world interaction and planning in imagination lets a quadruped learn to stand/walk in 1 hour without resets/simulators, and lets two different robot arms learn to pick and place multiple objects directly from camera images and sparse rewards, approaching human performance, all with the same hyperparameters across robots
claims.direction: favors world-model/model-based auxiliary learning (predicting outcomes of actions) over model-free RL for real-world sample efficiency
claims.conditions: real robots (quadruped, 2 arms, wheeled robot), camera image input, sparse rewards, online learning with no simulator, single set of hyperparameters across tasks

claims.claim: After physical perturbation, the world-model-based agent adapts within 10 minutes of further real-world interaction
claims.direction: supports online model-based adaptation for robustness/recovery
claims.conditions: real quadruped robot, physical perturbation test

why_deep_read: This is one of the few papers with real-robot, camera-based, data-efficient results directly testing whether a learned world model (auxiliary predictive objective) helps manipulation policies; full text ablations (architecture size, exact demo/interaction counts, failure cases) would clarify if a similar auxiliary objective is worth adding to a small imitation policy.

title: Action-Quantized Offline Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Skill Learning

claims.claim: Using a VQ-VAE to learn state-conditioned discrete action quantization (avoiding exponential blowup of naive discretization) lets several SOTA offline RL methods (IQL, CQL, BRAC) improve in performance, and on challenging long-horizon Robomimic manipulation tasks the discretized offline RL algorithms improve upon their continuous-action counterparts by 2-3x
claims.direction: favors discrete/VQ action tokenization over continuous action regression for long-horizon manipulation in the offline setting
claims.conditions: offline RL, Robomimic benchmark long-horizon manipulation tasks, learned-from-demonstration datasets

why_deep_read: Directly bears on Q01 (discrete/VQ action tokens vs continuous regression); the magnitude (2-3x) is a strong quantitative signal, and the full paper's task details/action-chunk length would clarify if this transfers to a small real low-cost-arm imitation setting rather than only offline-RL/Robomimic.

title: Learning to Act from Actionless Videos through Dense Correspondences

claims.claim: A video-based policy trained only on RGB videos (no action labels), using images as a task-agnostic state+action representation and dense correspondences between frames to infer closed-form actions, can reliably execute diverse table-top manipulation and navigation tasks across robots/environments from few video demonstrations, and can be trained with 4 GPUs within a single day
claims.direction: supports that action labels/teleop demonstrations may not be strictly necessary; a handful of video demos plus a learned frame-correspondence/action-inference model can substitute
claims.conditions: table-top manipulation and navigation tasks, few video demonstrations, no action annotations, small compute budget (4 GPUs, 1 day)

title: Robust Visual Sim-to-Real Transfer for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Systematic visual domain randomization (texture, lighting, object color, camera parameters), with DR parameters selected via an offline cube-localization proxy task, trains visuomotor policies in sim that achieve 93% average success when directly deployed on a real robot across a diverse set of challenging manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors comprehensive multi-factor visual domain randomization (texture+lighting+color+camera) for sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: sim-trained, zero real fine-tuning, real robot deployment, diverse manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Simulator-trained policies using this DR approach outperform policies learned using real but limited data, when evaluated on robustness to visual variations in real scenes
claims.direction: favors sim+domain-randomization training over training on a small amount of real data, for robustness to visual/lighting variation
claims.conditions: real robot evaluation, limited real-data baseline comparison

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our observed failure mode (breaks under new lighting/camera shift): a controlled study isolating which DR factors (texture/lighting/color/camera) matter, with a real robot showing DR-trained beats limited-real-data policies on visual robustness, is highly actionable for our augmentation strategy.

title: Seq2Seq Imitation Learning for Tactile Feedback-based Manipulation

claims.claim: A Seq2Seq imitation learning model (first estimates partially-observable contact/environment state from an interaction sequence, then maps to a control sequence) learns a simulated door-open task and a real snap-on insertion task from only 50 expert demonstrations, while state-of-the-art RL and IL baselines fail entirely on these tasks
claims.direction: favors sequence-to-sequence/history-conditioned imitation architectures over single-step RL/IL baselines when demos are scarce (~50) and the task is contact-rich/partially observable
claims.conditions: real robot (snap-on insertion) + simulated door-open task, 50 demonstrations, tactile feedback, partial observability

why_deep_read: Uses exactly our target demo count (~50) on a real contact-rich insertion task and reports baseline RL/IL methods failing outright; the architecture details (how history/contact-state is encoded) could directly inform our Q07 observation-history design.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Task and Motion Planning for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A TAMP-gated teleoperation system (HITL-TAMP) that automates non-contact-rich portions of a task and hands control to a human only for contact-rich segments let users collect more than 3x the number of demonstrations vs conventional teleoperation in the same time budget; policies with 75%+ success were trained from just 10 minutes of non-expert teleoperation data; 2.1K demos were collected across 12 contact-rich long-horizon tasks, often producing near-perfect agents
claims.direction: favors TAMP-assisted/structured teleoperation (automating easy sub-motions, human only for precision segments) over full manual teleoperation for demonstration collection efficiency
claims.conditions: real/simulated contact-rich long-horizon manipulation tasks, non-expert teleoperators, imitation learning on collected data

why_deep_read: Directly bears on our Q13 data-collection bottleneck (50-100 demos per task): a >3x demo-collection speedup and 75%+ success from only 10 minutes of non-expert teleop data could materially change our data-collection protocol if it transfers to a single low-cost arm.

title: Giving Robots a Hand: Learning Generalizable Manipulation with Eye-in-Hand Human Video Demonstrations

claims.claim: Augmenting narrow robot teleoperation datasets with broad, unlabeled eye-in-hand (wrist-camera) human video demonstrations -- with no explicit domain adaptation, only exploiting partial observability of eye-in-hand cameras plus a simple fixed image-masking scheme -- improves success rates of eye-in-hand manipulation policies by 58% absolute on average across 8 real-world tasks (3-DoF and 6-DoF arm control)
claims.direction: favors wrist/eye-in-hand camera policies augmented with cheap unlabeled human video over robot-teleop-only training data
claims.conditions: real robot, 8 tasks, 3-DoF and 6-DoF arm control, wrist camera, no explicit domain adaptation

claims.claim: The human-video-augmented eye-in-hand policies generalize to new environment configurations and to new tasks unseen in the robot demonstration data
claims.direction: favors this augmentation approach for cross-environment/cross-task generalization
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, unseen environments/tasks

why_deep_read: A 58% absolute success-rate gain from cheap human video plus wrist-camera partial observability is a large, directly-quantified effect very relevant to our wrist-camera setup and small-data budget; the mechanism (masking scheme instead of domain adaptation) is simple enough to consider adopting, so the full method details matter.

title: Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning With Base Skill Priors Under Unstructured Data

claims.claim: Combining base skill priors with imitation learning under unstructured data improves the average completed task length (number of tasks continuously completed) by more than 2.5x vs the baseline method HULC in simulation, and in a real-world zero-shot evaluation across ten tasks achieves an average 30% improvement over the current state-of-the-art approach
claims.direction: favors decomposing language-conditioned policies into reusable base-skill priors plus imitation learning (rather than a monolithic language-conditioned policy) for generalizing to unfamiliar environments
claims.conditions: simulated benchmark + real-world zero-shot evaluation across 10 tasks, unstructured/unlabeled play-style data

why_deep_read: Q08 (language conditioning) is one of our 14 decisions and this reports a real-world zero-shot generalization number (30%) against current SOTA; understanding the base-skill-prior architecture could inform whether to add a second (language-conditioned) task with a similarly modular design.

title: Visual Imitation Learning for robotic fresh mushroom harvesting

claims.claim: An end-to-end imitation-learning pipeline mapping pixels directly to reach/grasp/twist/pull motions can be trained on a standard laptop GPU in under one hour, with inference of an action taking less than 1.5ms on a laptop CPU
claims.direction: supports that small, lean models are sufficient/feasible for this class of manipulation task on consumer hardware
claims.conditions: simulated mushroom-harvesting task, laptop GPU training, laptop CPU inference

claims.claim: The method is evaluated on different kinds of visual input, namely grayscale images and depth maps, and tests robustness to randomization of camera extrinsic/intrinsic parameters and object size
claims.direction: qualitative only -- abstract does not state which visual input (grayscale vs depth) performed better
claims.conditions: simulated environment, camera and size randomization

title: Robotic Skill Acquisition via Instruction Augmentation with Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: DIAL uses semi-supervised language labels to propagate CLIP's semantic knowledge onto a large unlabeled demonstration dataset (only 3.5% of 80,000 demonstrations had crowd-sourced language annotations); across 1,300+ real-world evaluations, DIAL-trained imitation policies acquired new capabilities and generalized to 60 novel instructions unseen in the original labeled data
claims.direction: favors auto-propagating/augmenting language labels via a pretrained VLM rather than requiring fully human-labeled language-conditioned datasets
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation, large-scale dataset (80,000 demos), only 3.5% originally labeled, 1,300 real evaluations

title: Learning Robust Bed Making using Deep Imitation Learning with DART

claims.claim: Policies learned from 50 human demonstrations using DART (an LfD algorithm with noise injection) achieve 96% sheet coverage, over 200% better than a corner-detector baseline
claims.direction: favors DART-style noise-injected demo collection over baseline heuristic, supports small demo counts (~50) being viable
claims.conditions: real Toyota HSR robot, 1/2 scale bed, distractors, 50 demos, deep NN policy with pretrained YOLO features

title: Learning to Augment Synthetic Images for Sim2Real Policy Transfer

claims.claim: An optimized search over augmentation strategies (random transformation sequences) applied to synthetic depth images, using object localization as a proxy task, significantly improves real-robot accuracy on 3 manipulation tasks compared to naive sim2real transfer without optimized augmentation
claims.direction: favors task-optimized augmentation search over generic/no augmentation for depth-based sim2real policies
claims.conditions: real robot evaluation, 3 manipulation tasks, depth images, policy learned entirely in simulation with no real images

claims.claim: Depth images (rather than RGB) used as the sim2real transfer modality, augmented via searched transformations, enable policy-independent zero-real-image training
claims.direction: favors depth over RGB for reducing sim2real domain gap
claims.conditions: simulated training, real robot manipulation evaluation

title: Making Sense of Vision and Touch: Self-Supervised Learning of Multimodal Representations for Contact-Rich Tasks

claims.claim: Self-supervised learning of a compact multimodal (vision+haptic) representation improves sample efficiency of downstream RL policy learning on a peg insertion task, generalizing across geometry/configuration/clearance and robust to external perturbations
claims.direction: favors auxiliary self-supervised representation learning (multimodal) over training policy directly on raw high-dim inputs
claims.conditions: real robot peg insertion, simulation and real experiments, deep RL policy

title: Learning Deep Visuomotor Policies for Dexterous Hand Manipulation

claims.claim: Imitation-learned visuomotor policies for a 5-fingered dexterous hand can be trained efficiently with a few hundred expert demonstration trajectories
claims.direction: supports moderate (few hundred) demo counts being sufficient for complex manipulation
claims.conditions: simulated 5-fingered dexterous hand, imitation learning, visual+proprioceptive observation

claims.claim: Adding touch sensing information enables faster learning and better asymptotic performance specifically for tasks with high degree of occlusion
claims.direction: favors adding tactile modality as auxiliary input for occlusion-heavy tasks
claims.conditions: simulated dexterous hand manipulation tasks

title: Learning to Play by Imitating Humans

claims.claim: A goal-conditioned policy trained on human play data augmented with autonomously self-generated cloned play data substantially outperforms a policy trained only on the original (smaller) human play dataset, across 18 difficult manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors increasing data diversity/quantity via self-generated augmentation of demonstration data over using only the original small human dataset
claims.conditions: simulated robotic tabletop environment, behavioral cloning policy trained on relatively small quantity of human play, goal-conditioned multi-task policy

title: Visual Adversarial Imitation Learning using Variational Models

claims.claim: A variational model-based adversarial imitation learning approach (V-MAIL) that uses model-based representation learning as an auxiliary signal learns successful visuomotor policies more sample-efficiently, with better training stability and higher asymptotic performance than prior (model-free) adversarial imitation learning work
claims.direction: favors adding a learned world/representation model as auxiliary objective over model-free adversarial IL
claims.conditions: simulated vision-based locomotion and manipulation tasks; no real-robot results reported in abstract

title: Tidy-Up Tasks Using Trajectory-based Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A trajectory-based imitation learning method that restricts the RL workspace using only ONE human demonstration achieves 97% success rate on a laptop-folding task in simulation and is shown to enable safe, fast learning with only one demonstration video for a real drawer-arrangement task
claims.direction: favors combining a single demo with constrained-exploration RL over needing many demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation (laptop folding, 97%) and real robot (drawer arrangement), single demonstration

title: Learning Cloth Folding Tasks with Refined Flow Based Spatio-Temporal Graphs

claims.claim: Encoding demonstrations with a high-level abstraction (optical-flow-based spatiotemporal graph with visual correspondence descriptors) rather than low-level pixel encoding lets policy learning focus on key points/relations, allowing quick generalization across different environments
claims.direction: favors structured/high-level visual representations over raw pixel encoding for generalization
claims.conditions: real robotic platform, custom end-effector, cloth folding task (deformable object)

title: Bayesian Disturbance Injection: Robust Imitation Learning of Flexible Policies

claims.direction: favors variational/multi-modal policy representations over direct regression-style imitation for multimodal human demonstrations

why_deep_read: Directly targets multimodality of human demos (Q01) and disturbance-injection augmentation (Q05) with real low-cost-style arm validation; full text would give quantitative comparison numbers the abstract lacks and clarify how disturbance injection was designed, which is directly actionable for our teleop demo pipeline.

title: Bimanual Regrasping for Suture Needles using Reinforcement Learning for Rapid Motion Planning

title: LASER: Learning a Latent Action Space for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

title: Imitation from Observation using RL and Graph-based Representation of Demonstrations

title: Using human gaze in few-shot imitation learning for robot manipulation

title: Efficient Representations of Object Geometry for Reinforcement Learning of Interactive Grasping Policies

title: Universal Visual Decomposer: Long-Horizon Manipulation Made Easy

claims.claim: Automatically discovering subgoals by detecting phase shifts in a pre-trained visual representation's embedding space (zero additional training cost) and using them to condition goal-based policies yields significantly improved compositional generalization at test time on unseen long-horizon task sequences, substantially outperforming baselines in both imitation and RL settings

title: H-InDex: Visual Reinforcement Learning with Hand-Informed Representations for Dexterous Manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our Q03 decision (pretrained vs. scratch, frozen vs fine-tuned encoder) with a quantified claim that near-frozen pretrained representations beat generic visual foundation models on manipulation; full text would clarify which foundation models were beaten (DINOv2/CLIP/etc.) and whether findings transfer from RL-dexterous-hand setting to our low-data imitation setting on a simple arm.

title: Active Perception and Representation for Robotic Manipulation

title: Learning Semantic Keypoint Representations for Door Opening Manipulation

claims.direction: favors synthetic data augmentation to reduce required real-world data
claims.conditions: real robot hardware, door-opening task (not pick-place), small real dataset + large synthetic augmented dataset

title: Learning Rope Manipulation Policies Using Dense Object Descriptors Trained on Synthetic Depth Data

claims.direction: favors sim-only synthetic-data training with depth for transferable visual representations
claims.conditions: real robot (ABB YuMi), deformable 1D object (rope), 50 real trials, no real images needed for representation training

title: Deep Imitation Learning for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical modular architecture decomposing manipulation into movement primitives parameterized by a recurrent graph neural network generalizes better and achieves higher success rates than prior (non-hierarchical) imitation learning baselines, especially for objects in novel locations
claims.direction: favors hierarchical/modular primitive-based action representation over flat imitation learning policies
claims.conditions: simulated bimanual manipulation tasks; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: Making Sense of Vision and Touch: Learning Multimodal Representations for Contact-Rich Tasks

claims.claim: Learning a compact multimodal representation via self-supervised auxiliary objectives (combining vision and touch) improves sample efficiency of downstream policy learning on a real robot peg-insertion task, generalizing over varying geometries, configurations, clearances, while robust to external perturbations

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Industrial Insertion Tasks

claims.claim: Meta-RL policies pretrained on a family of simulated insertion tasks can adapt to real-world insertion using less than 20 trials of real-world experience
claims.direction: favors leveraging simulation + meta-learning to minimize needed real-world data

title: Variable Compliance Control for Robotic Peg-in-Hole Assembly: A Deep-Reinforcement-Learning Approach

claims.direction: favors domain randomization for sim2real transfer on position-controlled robots

title: LanCon-Learn: Learning with Language to Enable Generalization in Multi-Task Manipulation

title: PLATO: Predicting Latent Affordances Through Object-Centric Play

claims.direction: favors diverse/unstructured play-style demonstration data over narrow scripted demos for multi-task policy learning
claims.conditions: real world + 2D/3D simulation, play-collected demonstrations (no specific demo counts or success numbers given in abstract)

title: Output Feedback Tube MPC-Guided Data Augmentation for Robust, Efficient Sensorimotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Combining imitation learning with an output-feedback robust tube MPC to co-generate demonstrations, plus an MPC-guided data augmentation strategy, lets a neural sensorimotor (visuomotor) policy be learned from a single demonstration and be robust to sensing/process uncertainty
claims.direction: favors model-based-controller-guided data augmentation over collecting more raw demonstrations

claims.claim: The augmentation approach yields a two-orders-of-magnitude improvement in demonstration efficiency compared to existing IL methods (single demo vs. many)
claims.direction: favors augmentation over collecting more demonstrations to reduce data requirements

title: Real World Offline Reinforcement Learning with Realistic Data Source

title: Continuous control actions learning and adaptation for robotic manipulation through reinforcement learning

title: Immersive Demonstrations are the Key to Imitation Learning

title: A Unified Deep Imitation Learning and Control Framework for Robot-Assisted Sonography

title: Error-Aware Imitation Learning from Teleoperation Data for Mobile Manipulation

title: MoCoDA: Model-based Counterfactual Data Augmentation

title: On Bringing Robots Home

title: PartManip: Learning Cross-Category Generalizable Part Manipulation Policy from Point Cloud Observations

title: Stabilize to Act: Learning to Coordinate for Bimanual Manipulation

title: Why Does Action Chunking Improve Behavioral Cloning Performance in Robotic Control?

claims.direction: favors a hierarchical VLM-planner + flow-matching-DiT-executor architecture over end-to-end VLA baselines, especially for long-horizon and small-object/cluttered-scene tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments; claims are qualitative ('significantly outperforms'), no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Reinforcement Learning for Flow-Matching Policies with Density Transport

claims.claim: RLDT, an online RL fine-tuning method for flow-matching policies (using Stein Variational Gradient Descent to construct a transport field, then aligning the pretrained flow-matching policy to it via expected-target estimation to avoid unstable backprop-through-time), outperforms competitive baselines in reward quality and convergence speed across diverse continuous-control tasks including vision-based long-horizon robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors RL fine-tuning of pretrained flow-matching action policies (vs other RL fine-tuning approaches for flow/diffusion policies) for improving reward and convergence
claims.conditions: state- and vision-based long-horizon manipulation, dense and sparse reward settings; qualitative comparative claim, no specific numbers in abstract

title: Generalizable VLA Finetuning via Representation Anchoring and Language-Action Alignment

claims.claim: Standard behavior-cloning finetuning of a pretrained VLM/VLA progressively overwrites pretrained visual/semantic representations that support generalization; adding a Vision-Language Anchoring loss (distilling layer-wise representations from a frozen copy of the pretrained VLM during BC finetuning) prevents this drift
claims.direction: favors anchoring/distilling frozen pretrained representations during fine-tuning rather than plain BC finetuning (which erodes pretrained vision-language generalization) -- relevant to how much to fine-tune vs freeze a pretrained vision encoder
claims.conditions: physical xArm7 robot, two widely used VLA architectures

claims.claim: Co-training on web image-text data (a common remedy for representation drift) does NOT fix language-action misalignment because language and action losses are applied to separate observations; converting action targets into discrete motion-direction labels and jointly training language+action prediction on the same observation (Language-Action Alignment) improves real-robot success from 28% to 54% and from 37% to 60% across two VLA architectures on a physical xArm7 robot
claims.direction: favors jointly supervising language and action prediction on the same observation (rather than separately, or via generic web co-training) for language-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: real robot (xArm7), two VLA architectures; also shows consistent sim improvements on OOD perturbations, perceptual robustness, and long-horizon control (LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN)

why_deep_read: Large, quantified real-robot success-rate jumps (28%->54%, 37%->60%) directly address how to fine-tune a pretrained VLA without destroying its vision-language generalization -- central to our Q03 (fine-tune vs freeze vision encoder) and relevant to why our SmolVLA fine-tune may be losing robustness to lighting/object changes.

title: Pre-training Visual Dexterity in Simulation

claims.claim: Pre-training a causal transformer on 75 hours of simulation-collected (VR teleoperation of virtual objects) dexterous manipulation data, then fine-tuning on only 1-2 hours of physical demonstrations on a 56-DoF bimanual setup, outperforms training behavior-cloning policies from scratch on real data alone
claims.direction: favors simulation teleoperation pre-training (even with an off-hardware VR interface) followed by small real-data fine-tuning, over training from scratch on real demos only
claims.conditions: 56-DoF bimanual dexterous hand setup, real-world fine-tuning tasks

claims.claim: Ablation studies measure the benefits of history conditioning and short action chunks specifically for reactive control
claims.direction: suggests shorter action chunks (vs long chunks) benefit reactive/dexterous control, and observation history conditioning helps
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous bimanual manipulation; specific quantitative deltas not given in abstract

title: SafeLoop: Risk-Aware Rollback for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: A non-invasive external wrapper (risk predictor + lightweight rollback controller) added to a frozen VLA model, without changing its parameters, reduces hazard cases (collisions, object drops) by roughly 70% while preserving task success and the base-policy control rate
claims.direction: favors adding an external closed-loop hazard-prediction/rollback-recovery layer on top of an existing VLA policy rather than modifying the base policy itself
claims.conditions: 24 LIBERO sim tasks (16 seeds each) and three real-robot tasks (25 rollouts each)

title: Diff-Dagger: Uncertainty Estimation With Diffusion Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Diff-DAgger, a robot-gated interactive imitation learning algorithm using diffusion-policy training-objective-based uncertainty (rather than ensemble disagreement) to decide when to query expert help, improves task failure prediction by 39.0%, task completion rate by 20.6%, and reduces wall-clock data-collection time by a factor of 7.8x compared to prior robot-gated DAgger (e.g. Ensemble-DAgger)
claims.direction: favors diffusion-policy-native uncertainty estimation over ensemble-disagreement methods for deciding when to collect additional (corrective) demonstrations in an interactive imitation-learning loop
claims.conditions: real robot tasks (stacking, pushing, plugging)

title: CronusVLA: Towards Efficient and Robust Manipulation via Multi-Frame Vision-Language-Action Modeling

claims.claim: Extending a single-frame VLA to a multi-frame paradigm (two-stage: single-frame pretraining, then multi-frame post-training that aggregates historical features via feature chunking rather than feeding raw multi-frame images into the VLM backbone) achieves a 70.9% success rate on SimplerEnv and a 26.8% improvement over OpenVLA on LIBERO, while avoiding the computational overhead of directly feeding multiple raw frames
claims.direction: favors adding observation history via feature-level chunking/aggregation (not raw multi-frame input) over single-frame VLA policies
claims.conditions: three embodiments, simulated and real-world environments

claims.claim: On a new benchmark (SimplerEnv-OR) with 24 types of observational disturbances and 120 severity levels, the multi-frame history-aware model achieves the highest robustness score compared to baselines, demonstrating superior observational robustness under temporal and spatial disturbances
claims.direction: supports that incorporating observation history improves robustness to observational/environmental disturbances (relevant to our lighting/camera-shift robustness problem)
claims.conditions: new benchmark SimplerEnv-OR; sim and real-world testing across 3 embodiments

why_deep_read: Directly tests Q07 (observation history/memory) with a controlled two-stage design and reports both accuracy gains and a dedicated robustness benchmark against observational disturbances (lighting/camera-type shifts) -- precisely the failure modes we are trying to fix, while explicitly avoiding the naive multi-frame latency overhead relevant to our Q10 concerns.

title: KineDex: Learning Tactile-Informed Visuomotor Policies via Kinesthetic Teaching for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Hand-over-hand kinesthetic teaching (vs standard teleoperation) collects demonstration data over twice as fast across two tasks while maintaining near-100% collection success rate (vs under 50% for teleoperation); the resulting tactile-augmented visuomotor policy with force control achieves 74.4% average success (a 57.7% improvement over the variant without force control)
claims.direction: favors kinesthetic (direct physical) teaching over teleoperation for faster, higher-quality demonstration collection in contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real dexterous hand, contact-rich fine-grained manipulation tasks (e.g., squeezing toothpaste); different data-collection paradigm than leader/follower teleop

title: GSWorld: Closed-Loop Photo-Realistic Simulation Suite for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A photo-realistic simulator combining 3D Gaussian Splatting with a physics engine (GSDF asset format infusing Gaussian-on-Mesh with robot URDF) enables zero-shot sim2real pixel-to-action policy learning, automated DAgger data collection for deployment adaptation, and simulation data collection via virtual teleoperation
claims.direction: supports photo-realistic synthetic/simulated data generation (Gaussian splatting based) as a viable augmentation/data source for real-robot policies
claims.conditions: 3 robot embodiments (single-arm and bimanual), 40+ objects; capability demonstration rather than a controlled ablation with numbers in the abstract

title: METIS: Multi-Source Egocentric Training for Integrated Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Pretraining a VLA on a unified multi-source dataset of human and robotic egocentric data (EgoAtlas), using a compact discretized 'motion-aware dynamics' representation for supervision, achieves the highest average success rate among compared methods on six real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and shows superior generalization/robustness to out-of-distribution scenarios
claims.direction: favors pretraining on combined human+robot egocentric data with a compact discretized motion representation over robot-only or non-discretized supervision
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, six tasks; claims qualitative ('highest', 'superior'), no specific numbers in abstract

title: Learning Physics from Pretrained Video Models: A Multimodal Continuous and Sequential World Interaction Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: PhysGen treats a pretrained autoregressive video generation model as a proxy physics simulator, using a shared video-action token representation, and consistently outperforms baselines, surpassing OpenVLA and WorldVLA by 13.8% and 8.8% respectively on Libero and ManiSkill; in real-world scenarios it matches large-scale action-pretrained models like pi0 without needing action-specific pretraining
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained video-generation models as an auxiliary/world-model objective (transferring implicit physics knowledge) over training action-pretrained models from scratch, especially when action-labeled data is scarce
claims.conditions: sim (Libero, ManiSkill) and real-world; notably improves on physically complex tasks such as grasping transparent objects (a challenging generalization case)

title: GigaBrain-0.5M*: a VLA That Learns From World Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a VLA (pretrained on 10,000+ hours of robotic manipulation data) with world-model-based reinforcement learning (RAMP: RL via world-model-conditioned policy) yields roughly 30% performance gains over an RECAP baseline on challenging real-world long-horizon tasks (laundry folding, box packing, espresso preparation), with reliable long-horizon execution without failure in deployment videos
claims.direction: favors adding world-model-conditioned RL fine-tuning on top of a large pretrained VLA over the RECAP baseline approach for long-horizon task reliability
claims.conditions: large-scale foundation model (pretrained on 10k+ hours), real-world deployment; far larger scale than our target laptop-GPU setup

title: AtomicVLA: Unlocking the Potential of Atomic Skill Learning in Robots

claims.claim: Replacing a monolithic action decoder with a planning-and-execution framework that jointly generates task-level plans, atomic skill abstractions, and fine-grained actions (via a Skill-Guided Mixture-of-Experts action architecture with flexible routing for continual learning) outperforms pi_0 by 2.4% on LIBERO and 10% on LIBERO-LONG, and outperforms pi_0/pi_0.5 by 0.22/0.25 in average task length on CALVIN; real-world long-horizon and continual-learning tasks show 18.3% and 21% gains over baselines
claims.direction: favors decomposing action generation into atomic-skill mixture-of-experts (vs a single monolithic decoder trained on aggregated data) for long-horizon and continually-learned tasks
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, LIBERO-LONG, CALVIN) and real-world long-horizon/continual-learning tasks; MoE architecture likely larger-parameter than our laptop-scale budget

title: Fetch My Beer: Synthetic-to-Real Hierarchical Policy for Smooth Pick-and-Place

claims.claim: A hierarchical policy -- a high-level module producing SE(3) control targets plus a latent diffusion controller that plans in a compact latent space and then decodes dense action chunks -- enables the high control frequency needed for smooth, dynamically-stable motion, outperforming state-of-the-art manipulation policies in transport smoothness and dynamic stability for a task requiring suppression of sloshing/spillage
claims.direction: favors latent-space planning + dense action-chunk decoding (for high control frequency) over standard chunk-level diffusion policies when motion smoothness/dynamic stability matters, as opposed to only optimizing task completion
claims.conditions: synthetic-to-real pipeline (physically validated data generation via fluid simulation + VLM pose filtering); real-robot smoothness/stability comparison claimed qualitatively, no specific numbers in abstract

title: OxyGen: Unified KV Cache Management for VLA Inference under Multi-Task Parallelism

claims.claim: Treating the KV cache as a shared resource across tasks/time (cross-task KV sharing to eliminate redundant prefill of shared observations, cross-frame continuous batching to decouple language decoding from fixed-rate action generation) achieves up to 3.7x speedup over isolated execution, delivering 200+ tokens/s language throughput and 70 Hz action frequency simultaneously without degrading action quality, on RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Thor
claims.direction: favors unified/shared KV-cache inference-system design over naive isolated multi-task execution for reducing VLA inference latency and increasing action frequency on resource-constrained hardware
claims.conditions: implemented for pi_0.5 (a Mixture-of-Transformers VLA); evaluated on RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Thor (edge/on-device hardware), and validated on a real humanoid robot

title: Assistron: Bayesian Shared Autonomy with Off-the-shelf Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Using an off-the-shelf VLA without any fine-tuning (invoking it only for macro-reaching trajectories, with human intervention solicited at detected contact-rich failure points) protects the VLA's broad behavioral priors from catastrophic forgetting, avoiding the need for VLA fine-tuning altogether
claims.direction: favors keeping a pretrained VLA completely frozen (shared-autonomy wrapper instead of fine-tuning) to preserve generalization, at least for the macro-motion portion of tasks
claims.conditions: real-world multi-task scene-recovery benchmark of daily manipulation skills; qualitative improvement claims, no specific numbers given

title: Calibrated Predictive Safety for Heterogeneous Robots: An Action-Conditioned JEPA Framework with Model-Based Safety Shields

claims.claim: An action-conditioned JEPA world model that rolls candidate action chunks forward in a frozen-encoder latent space to predict task progress and physical risk, combined with a deterministic per-embodiment safety shield, improved success over a shield-only baseline and reduced collision false negatives at matched recall in 600-episode sim configurations
claims.direction: favors adding a JEPA-based predictive risk/progress model on top of action-chunk proposals (used for ranking/filtering candidates), rather than relying on a safety shield alone
claims.conditions: simulation only (LIBERO-Long); real-robot experiments explicitly left as future work

title: From Temporal-Evolving to Spatial-Fixing: A Keypoints-Based Learning Paradigm for Visual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard temporal-sequential behavior cloning accumulates prediction errors, pushing visual observations out of the training distribution; a hierarchical approach that predicts a fixed set of spatial waypoints directly from the initial observation (single-shot, rather than sequential primitive-by-primitive prediction) achieves comparable results with RL and outperforms existing offline BC approaches
claims.direction: favors single-shot, spatially-fixed waypoint prediction from the initial observation over sequential temporal-evolving action prediction, to eliminate compounding errors
claims.conditions: visual robotic manipulation; comparison against RL and offline BC baselines; environment (sim/real) not specified in abstract

title: On the Surprising Effectiveness of Spectral Clipping in Learning Stable Linear and Latent-Linear Dynamical Systems

claims.claim: A post-hoc 'spectral clipping' procedure (clipping eigenvalues of a learned linear/latent-linear dynamical system to enforce stability) can match or outperform strong baselines while being orders-of-magnitude faster, and can learn stable robot policies even when the training data includes unsuccessful or truncated demonstrations
claims.direction: supports that including unsuccessful/truncated demonstrations in training data need not hurt policy stability if combined with a stability-enforcing post-processing step
claims.conditions: benchmark datasets and dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robotic hands; latent-linear dynamics models, not directly diffusion/transformer policies

title: Geometry-aware RL for Manipulation of Varying Shapes and Deformable Objects

claims.claim: A heterogeneous-graph policy using SE(3)-equivariant message passing (HEPi) outperforms Transformer-based and non-heterogeneous equivariant policies in average returns, sample efficiency, and generalization to unseen objects
claims.direction: favors SE(3)-equivariant graph-based policy architectures over standard Transformer policies for tasks with varying object geometry
claims.conditions: RL benchmark (rigid insertion of diverse objects, rope/cloth manipulation with multiple end-effectors); RL training, not imitation learning; claims qualitative in abstract

title: Task-Guided and Object-Centric Conditioning for Effective and Adaptive Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Learning vision encoders from scratch tends to prioritize policy optimization over rich semantic feature extraction (suboptimal representations), while generic pre-trained large vision models fail to capture fine-grained task-specific information; TOC-DP, which integrates SlotAttention for object-centric representation learning with task-specific segmentation priors as inductive bias, achieves a 30% improvement in success rate over baseline methods on Meta-World and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors object-centric (SlotAttention-based, segmentation-prior-guided) visual representations over both from-scratch encoders and generic frozen pretrained vision encoders for manipulation
claims.conditions: Meta-World benchmark and real-world tasks; diffusion policy backbone

title: Grasping Unknown Objects With Only One Demonstration

claims.claim: A curriculum-learning RL method that uses only one human demonstration (recorded via wearable teleoperation as a reference trajectory, then refined via multimodal RL with point-cloud features in simulation, with curriculum progressing from similar to unknown objects) reduces dependence on large grasping datasets, improves learning efficiency, and achieves a higher success rate for grasping novel objects compared to the baseline method
claims.direction: favors combining a single demonstration with simulation-based RL curriculum learning over requiring many demonstrations for generalization to unknown objects
claims.conditions: anthropomorphic hand-arm system, sim-trained then deployed on real robots; claims comparative but no specific numbers given

title: Human-Guided Online Reward Adaptation for Real-Robot Arm Manipulation

claims.claim: Continuously recalibrating a pretrained VLM-based reward model online using lightweight updates from sparse human feedback (ARHI), rather than treating it as fixed, reduces human effort by 28.0% and achieves a 47.6% reduction in performance drop under challenging deployment shifts, across six real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: supports that online adaptation of a semantic reward/guidance signal (rather than a frozen one) substantially reduces performance degradation under deployment-time distribution shift
claims.conditions: real-world RL-based manipulation, six tasks; RL framework rather than pure imitation learning

title: Uncertainty-Gated Dual-path Probabilistic Depth Fusion for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Deterministic RGB-depth fusion (simple concatenation) ignores the reliability of noisy geometric cues; an uncertainty-gated fusion framework (predicting depth probabilities, lifting 2D visual features into 3D, and confidence-gating unreliable geometric cues) surpasses baseline fusion methods in manipulation effectiveness and success rate under challenging visual conditions
claims.direction: favors uncertainty/confidence-aware RGB-D fusion over naive concatenation-based fusion when depth is noisy
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmark; challenging visual conditions specifically tested

title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies

claims.claim: Conditioning action generation on compact latent visual subgoals (predicted by a latent-action-conditioned Latent World Model operating in a pretrained vision foundation model's latent space) rather than reconstructed future video, achieves SOTA or competitive success rates: 98.6% on LIBERO, 91.22% on RoboTwin, plus real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors latent-space (not pixel-space) world-model-conditioned action generation as an auxiliary/dynamics-aware objective
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboTwin) and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: LaWAM runs in 187 ms per action-chunk prediction, achieving up to 24x lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space World-Action-Models, while retaining the accuracy benefits of dynamics-aware conditioning
claims.direction: favors latent-space world-model conditioning specifically because it avoids the heavy inference latency of pixel-space video generation, making world-model-style auxiliary objectives practical for low-latency real-time control
claims.conditions: same sim/real evaluation; latency measured per action-chunk prediction

why_deep_read: Directly addresses two of our hardest problems simultaneously: whether to add a world-model/future-prediction auxiliary objective (Q09) and how to keep inference latency low enough for real-time control (Q10, our ~2s latency issue) -- with concrete millisecond-level numbers and large latency-reduction factor versus pixel-space alternatives.

title: FIT: Future-Aware Imitation Transformer for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A transformer policy that at every timestep predicts actions, latent representations of future states (to anticipate action outcomes), and a task embedding (for long-horizon awareness) outperforms all baselines, particularly on novel tasks where existing methods fail to generalize
claims.direction: favors adding future-state-prediction and task-embedding auxiliary heads alongside action prediction for long-horizon, generalizable imitation learning
claims.conditions: simulated LIBERO, Franka kitchen, and real-world xArm6 environments; claims qualitative ('outperforms all baselines'), no specific numbers given

title: Improving Imitation Learning Efficiency for Manipulation through Geometric Prior Pretraining

claims.claim: Pretraining an ACT policy on a purely synthetic, texture-free geometric dataset (scenes containing only a plane, an object, and a cube representing a hand -- generated automatically, morphology-agnostic) then fine-tuning on a small number of task demonstrations achieves higher success rates in early training stages than training from scratch, across three simulated robots (5 tasks each) and three real-world robot tasks
