claims.direction: favors cheap, morphology-agnostic geometric pretraining (requiring no real images or robot-specific data) as a useful prior before task-specific fine-tuning with limited demonstrations, over training an ACT policy from scratch
claims.conditions: ACT policy backbone; 3 simulated robots x 5 tasks + 3 real-world robot tasks; small number of task demonstrations in the fine-tuning stage

why_deep_read: Uses ACT (a common policy class for low-cost arms like ours) and specifically targets the low-demonstration regime with a nearly-free, robot-agnostic synthetic pretraining recipe -- directly actionable for our ~50-100-demo, small-model, single-GPU setup, and touches Q03/Q05/Q13 simultaneously.

title: TANDEM: Task and Motion Planning with As-Needed Demonstrations for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Fine-tuning

claims.claim: Combining task-and-motion planning (TAMP) with selective human teleoperation only for stages beyond the planner's capability collects 2.9x as many demonstrations as full-task teleoperation at the same human intervention time; fine-tuning a pretrained pi_0.5-DROID model on just 20 TANDEM demonstrations per task increases average task success from 0% to 60% across five long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors hybrid autonomous-planning-plus-selective-human-demonstration data collection over full-task human teleoperation for maximizing fine-tuning data efficiency
claims.conditions: real-robot, long-horizon manipulation tasks beyond a fixed TAMP domain's capability; fine-tuning a large pretrained VLA (pi_0.5-DROID)

title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: OpenVLA's visual encoder fuses pretrained features from DINOv2 and SigLIP (combined with a Llama 2 language backbone), trained on 970k real-world robot demonstrations
claims.direction: documents a specific, widely-adopted vision-encoder design choice (DINOv2+SigLIP fusion) for a VLA -- directly relevant precedent for choosing among DINOv2/SigLIP/CLIP/other pretrained encoders
claims.conditions: 7B-parameter model, large-scale real-world multi-embodiment training data

claims.claim: OpenVLA (7B parameters) outperforms the much larger closed model RT-2-X (55B parameters) by 16.5% absolute task success rate across 29 tasks and multiple robot embodiments, using 7x fewer parameters
claims.direction: shows a smaller, openly-trained VLA can outperform a much larger closed VLA, i.e. parameter count alone does not determine performance; data/architecture choices matter more
claims.conditions: real-world multi-embodiment evaluation, 29 tasks

claims.claim: OpenVLA (autoregressive token-based VLA) outperforms Diffusion Policy (an expressive from-scratch imitation learning method) by 20.4% in the reported comparison
claims.direction: favors a pretrained autoregressive VLA fine-tuned on the target task over training a from-scratch diffusion policy, at least in the settings evaluated
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, comparison against from-scratch Diffusion Policy baseline

claims.claim: OpenVLA can be effectively fine-tuned for new tasks/settings using modern low-rank adaptation (LoRA) methods on consumer GPUs, and served efficiently via quantization, without a hit to downstream success rate
claims.direction: supports parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) and quantized inference as practical for adapting large pretrained VLAs on limited (consumer-GPU) compute
claims.conditions: consumer GPU fine-tuning and quantized serving explicitly demonstrated

why_deep_read: Foundational, widely-cited VLA paper with concrete numbers directly relevant to several of our core decisions (Q03 vision-encoder fusion precedent, Q12 model size vs performance, Q01 autoregressive-VLA vs diffusion-policy comparison, Q13 LoRA/quantization for consumer-GPU fine-tuning) -- essential context for our design choices even though our target model must be far smaller than 7B.

title: VLA-OS: Structuring and Dissecting Planning Representations and Paradigms in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: In a unified VLA architecture series with controlled experiments isolating planning paradigm/representation from network architecture and training data (across rigid/deformable objects, 2D/3D visual modalities, sim/real environments, grippers/dexterous hands), visually-grounded planning representations are generally better than language planning representations for downstream task performance
claims.direction: favors visual/spatial goal representations over pure natural-language planning representations for conditioning VLA policies
claims.conditions: controlled multi-axis study: rigid and deformable objects, 2D and 3D visual modalities, simulation and real-world, grippers and dexterous hands

claims.claim: The Hierarchical-VLA paradigm (high-level planning + low-level action generation) generally achieves superior or comparable performance to other paradigms on task performance, pretraining, generalization, scalability, and continual learning, at the cost of slower training and inference speed
claims.direction: favors hierarchical planning-then-action paradigms over end-to-end paradigms on most performance axes, but flags a latency/speed cost tradeoff relevant to our real-time constraint
claims.conditions: same controlled multi-axis study as above

why_deep_read: This is a rare controlled ablation isolating planning representation and paradigm (language vs visual grounding; end-to-end vs hierarchical; 2D vs 3D; gripper vs dexterous) from confounds like architecture/data scale -- directly informative for our Q08 and Q04 decisions, though the noted inference-speed cost of hierarchical VLA is a concern given our latency problem (Q10).

title: Annotation-Free One-Shot Imitation Learning for Multi-Step Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: A method requiring only a single demonstration (no additional model training or manual annotation) achieves an average success rate of 82.5% on multi-step manipulation tasks and 90% on single-step tasks, matching or exceeding baseline performance
claims.direction: supports that one-shot imitation learning (without extra training/annotation) can handle multi-step long-horizon tasks, not just single-step tasks
claims.conditions: comparison also includes performance/computational efficiency of alternative pre-trained feature extractors within the same framework (relevant to Q03), though specific extractor rankings are not given in the abstract

title: Diagnosing Compositional Generalization in Sequential Robot Tasks

claims.claim: Exhaustive enumeration of all instruction/task combinations is unnecessary for compositional generalization: a structured training subset as small as one quarter of the full task space can recover strong out-of-distribution performance if it covers action-relevant dependencies; sparse training coverage often fails due to 'instruction steering' rather than missing low-level skills, and fine-tuning with just one additional demonstration per task improves OOD success from 0.4% to 54.7%
claims.direction: favors prioritizing dependency/relational coverage in the instruction and task space over exhaustive data volume, and shows that a small number of well-chosen additional demonstrations can produce dramatic OOD generalization gains
claims.conditions: sequential/compositional robot manipulation tasks; specific robot/sim-real setting not detailed in abstract, but framed as a general diagnostic study of instruction-space coverage

why_deep_read: A 0.4%-to-54.7% OOD-success jump from adding just one demonstration per task is an extremely striking, directly actionable number for our ~50-100-demo data collection strategy (Q13) -- worth reading in full to understand exactly what kind of additional demo/coverage produced this gain, and whether it generalizes beyond compositional-instruction settings to our simpler single/dual-object task.

title: Foresight Residual RL for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation with Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: In chained multi-skill manipulation, optimizing each subtask in isolation with sparse success rewards yields little/no gain once skills are chained, because terminal-state quality (handoff quality between subtasks) is uncontrolled; augmenting the reward with a learned 'foresight value' (probability of downstream success given the current subtask's terminal state) achieves 85.6% full-task success vs 54.5% for standard subtask residual RL and vs VLA baselines, on a 3-phase assembly task, while leaving per-subtask success unchanged
claims.direction: shows that improving long-horizon/chained task performance requires explicitly shaping which terminal states are produced at each sub-task/chunk boundary, not just per-subtask success -- relevant to smoothing transitions between action chunks
claims.conditions: 3-phase wrench nut-tightening assembly task in Isaac Gym (sim only); residual RL over a frozen VLA base policy

title: DATAFARM: Distribution-Aligned Task and Motion Planning for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Raw TAMP-generated (synthetic/scripted) trajectories provide surprisingly little benefit for fine-tuning a pretrained VLA despite successfully solving the target tasks, because of a behavioral distribution mismatch (joint configurations, motion style, temporal profile) with the VLA's pretraining data; aligning synthetic trajectory generation with the pretraining distribution (DATAFARM) achieves 56.7% average success vs only 8.3% for raw TAMP trajectories, approaching human teleoperation's 61.7%
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that any successful synthetic/scripted demonstration is useful augmentation data -- shows synthetic demos must be distribution-aligned with the base model's pretraining data (motion style/joint configs/timing) to be useful for fine-tuning, otherwise they can be nearly worthless
claims.conditions: three tabletop manipulation tasks solvable by TAMP, plus a cloth-folding task beyond TAMP's native capability; fine-tuning a pretrained VLA

title: BEE: Intervention-Adaptive Real-World Reinforcement Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Modeling human corrections not as actions-to-imitate but as evidence of a per-action-dimension constraint (tight where corrections are consistent, relaxed where they vary), for online RL fine-tuning of a frozen VLA on precision-critical phases, achieves 91.2% average success across three real-world tasks plus one sim task, vs 57.5% for RLT and 42.1% for DSRL, with the lowest human intervention rate on all real-world tasks at a matched online-data budget
claims.direction: favors treating human corrections as direction-specific constraints (rather than uniform supervision) for closed-loop RL fine-tuning of frozen VLA policies at precision-critical execution phases
claims.conditions: three real-world manipulation tasks, one LIBERO-Pro sim task; matched online-data budget across compared methods

title: Programmatically Grounded, Compositionally Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Conventional pretraining-finetuning of VL representations entangles domain-specific action learning with domain-general visual understanding, leading to less data-efficient training and poor generalization to unseen objects/tasks; a modular framework (ProgramPort) that parses language into an executable program of vision- and action-grounded functional modules disentangles action and perception, improving zero-shot and compositional generalization
claims.direction: favors structured/modular language-to-program grounding over end-to-end language-conditioned policies for data efficiency and generalization to unseen objects/tasks
claims.conditions: trained end-to-end with imitation learning objectives; claims qualitative in abstract, no specific numbers given

title: World Models for General Surgical Grasping

claims.claim: Encoding both depth and mask images into a single compact 3-channel image (64x64x3, dynamically zoomed into mask regions) minimizes information loss and enables a world-model RL policy to generalize to unseen objects and grippers with an average success rate of 69% on real robots
claims.direction: supports compact fused depth+segmentation-mask representations (rather than raw depth or RGB alone) for generalizing grasping across unseen objects
claims.conditions: real robot, surgical grasping domain (different task domain from tabletop pick-and-place, but the representation technique is domain-general)

claims.claim: The learned visuomotor policy demonstrates robustness across 6 tested disturbance conditions: background variation, target disturbance, camera pose variation, kinematic control error, image noise, and re-grasping after drops
claims.direction: supports that a world-model-based approach with a compact depth+mask representation can maintain robustness under camera-pose variation and image noise, similar to conditions we care about
claims.conditions: real robot, surgical domain

title: Morphological symmetries in robotics

claims.claim: Morphological symmetries (intrinsic kinematic/mass-distribution symmetries of a robot) can enhance sample efficiency and generalization of machine-learning models either through data augmentation using the symmetry group, or by building equivariant/invariant constraints directly into the model architecture
claims.direction: supports symmetry-based data augmentation or equivariant architectures as a way to improve sample efficiency/generalization, as a general physics-informed prior
claims.conditions: demonstrated on bipedal and quadrupedal robots (locomotion), synthetic and real-world experiments; not manipulation-specific, but the augmentation/equivariance principle is domain-general

title: From LLMs to Actions: Latent Codes as Bridges in Hierarchical Robot Control

claims.claim: Using a learnable latent code (rather than natural language) as the interface between an LLM planner and a low-level policy avoids destroying the pretrained word-token embedding space during end-to-end finetuning and avoids the expressiveness limits of language for tasks not easily described in words; LCB outperforms baselines that use pure language as the interface layer (including those using GPT-4V) on tasks requiring reasoning and multi-step behaviors
claims.direction: favors a learned latent-code interface over pure natural-language conditioning/interface for hierarchical control on complex, multi-step, reasoning-heavy tasks
claims.conditions: Language Table and Calvin benchmarks (sim, language-conditioned manipulation)

title: GeoManip: Geometric Constraints as General Interfaces for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing task instructions as geometric constraints between object parts (interpreted via symbolic language and large foundation models, training-free) rather than as an end-to-end language-to-action mapping achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior out-of-distribution generalization while avoiding costly VLA-style model training
claims.direction: favors a training-free geometric-constraint interface (derived from language via foundation models) over trained VLA-style language conditioning, particularly for OOD generalization
claims.conditions: evaluated in both simulation and real-world scenarios; qualitative SOTA/superior claims, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: 3D CAVLA: Leveraging Depth and 3D Context to Generalize Vision Language Action Models for Unseen Tasks

claims.claim: Adding depth-aware perception and task-oriented region-of-interest detection (alongside chain-of-thought reasoning) to VLA finetuning achieves 98.1% average success across diverse in-domain LIBERO task suites, and on unseen tasks delivers an absolute improvement of 8.8% in success rate over a baseline without 3D scene awareness, plus over 3x faster training convergence
claims.direction: favors incorporating depth/3D spatial awareness into VLA finetuning over RGB-only finetuning, specifically for generalization to unseen tasks and faster convergence
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation (in-domain and unseen task suites); validated on real-world tabletop experiments (25% gain in success rate on unseen real-world tasks), confirming sim-to-real transfer

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q04 (RGB vs RGB+depth) with a controlled comparison showing depth/3D context specifically improves generalization to unseen tasks (+8.8% sim, +25% real) and speeds convergence -- exactly the kind of ablation needed given we have a RealSense depth camera available but are currently likely RGB-only.

title: WARPED: Wrist-Aligned Rendering for Robot Policy Learning from Egocentric Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Synthesizing photo-realistic wrist-view observations (via Gaussian Splatting, from monocular egocentric human RGB video with hand-object tracking and retargeting to a robotic end-effector) achieves success rates comparable to policies trained on teleoperated demonstration data on five tabletop manipulation tasks
claims.direction: supports that wrist-camera observations synthesized from cheap monocular human video can substitute for teleoperated wrist-camera demonstrations without a success-rate penalty
claims.conditions: real robot, five tabletop manipulation tasks; requires only monocular RGB (no depth sensor or multiview rig) for the human-video source

claims.claim: This approach requires 5-8x less data collection time than standard teleoperation while matching its success rate
claims.direction: favors human-video-based wrist-observation synthesis over teleoperation for demonstration collection efficiency
claims.conditions: same real-robot tabletop tasks

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our wrist-camera setup (Q11) and demo-collection cost (Q13, ~50-100 teleop demos per task): a 5-8x data-collection speedup with comparable success rate, if it holds up in the full paper, could substantially cut our teleoperation burden for the wrist-view portion of data collection.

title: Robo-Harness K1: Harnessing Robot-Use Agents via Perception Augmentation

claims.claim: Exposing calibrated depth, persistent visual anchors, spatial measurements, and grasp hypotheses as callable tools to a VLM agent (rather than training a depth encoder into the policy) lets a VLM reach 77.8% accuracy on matched LIBERO-PRO tasks vs 61.1% for an RGB-only harness with a comparably capable VLM, and generalizes zero-shot (no fine-tuning) to three RoboSuite arms and dual-arm RoboTwin tasks (32.0% Easy, 28.0% Hard) with resilience to visual/environmental perturbations
claims.direction: favors exposing 3D/depth information as an external tool interface to a frozen VLM rather than training a dedicated depth encoder into the policy, for generalization across robots without target fine-tuning
claims.conditions: LIBERO-PRO, RoboSuite, RoboTwin sim benchmarks; no real-robot results reported in abstract

claims.claim: A small student model (Qwen3.5-9B) distilled from only 107 teacher episodes (using tool-call traces) reaches 44.2% accuracy on new initial states vs 30.2% for OpenVLA, and 13.9% on held-out task conditions vs 0.0% for OpenVLA
claims.direction: supports that a small distilled model trained on very few (107) demonstrations/traces can generalize better to novel conditions than a larger end-to-end VLA (OpenVLA) trained differently
claims.conditions: same sim benchmarks; small model, very low training-episode count relevant to our low-data setting

title: RefGuard: Identity-Aware Language-Guided Robot Manipulation via Joint Target-Anchor-Frame Grounding

claims.claim: In cluttered scenes with repeated/ambiguous objects, committing early to any one of (target, anchor, reference-frame) before execution causes silent 'identity switch' errors; maintaining a joint posterior over all three and delaying commitment (RefGuard) records zero identity switches and 90.0% correct execution on ambiguity-stress trials on a real UF850 arm, vs 33-46% identity-switch rates for fine-tuned VLA and LLM-based baselines, while retaining 93.3% success on unambiguous scenes
claims.direction: favors joint, delayed-commitment grounding of target/anchor/reference-frame over standard VLA/LLM language grounding when multiple similar or ambiguous objects/distractors are present
claims.conditions: real robot (UF850 arm); also raises correct execution from 56.6% to 80.5% on a 3200-episode procedural suite compared to an ablation that commits to anchor/frame before target

title: Object-Centric Conditioning for Visuomotor Flow Matching

claims.claim: Action-to-Action (A2A) flow matching (which initializes generation from historical action priors instead of noise, for inference efficiency) suffers reduced robustness under spatial out-of-distribution shifts and visual distractors because of stale historical motion patterns and entangled global visual representations; decoupling scene observations into semantic ('what') and lightweight spatial ('where') object-centric cues (SlotFlow) improves robustness under visual distractors and severe spatial perturbations while preserving A2A's low-step inference efficiency
claims.direction: favors object-centric (semantic+spatial decoupled) conditioning over entangled global visual representations for robustness to distractors and spatial shifts, while keeping fast flow-matching inference
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments; controlled initialization and perception ablations isolate object-centric grounding as the main source of the robustness gains, complementing (not replacing) historical action priors

title: SP-VLA: A Joint Model Scheduling and Token Pruning Approach for VLA Model Acceleration

claims.claim: Jointly addressing temporal redundancy (via action-aware scheduling that assigns 'deliberative' actions to the full VLA and 'intuitive' actions to a lightweight generator) and spatial redundancy (via spatio-semantic token pruning) achieves 1.5x lossless acceleration on LIBERO and 2.4x on SimplerEnv, with up to 6% average performance gain, and improves inference frequency/latency by 2.2x (SimplerEnv) and 1.4x (LIBERO)
claims.direction: favors combining adaptive model-scheduling (full model only for hard decision points) with visual-token pruning over uniform full-model execution at every step, for reducing VLA inference latency without sacrificing (and sometimes improving) accuracy
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks LIBERO and SimplerEnv; model-agnostic acceleration framework, not tied to a specific VLA architecture

title: Ego-centric Predictive Model Conditioned on Hand Trajectories

claims.claim: A two-stage model that first predicts future hand trajectories from multi-modal input (vision, language, action history) and then uses causal cross-attention to condition an image-based latent diffusion model on the inferred action to generate future video frames outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both action prediction and future video synthesis
claims.direction: favors jointly/sequentially predicting action and its visual consequence (hand-trajectory-conditioned video prediction) as an auxiliary objective, over separately trained action-only VLA or unconditioned video prediction models
claims.conditions: Ego4D, BridgeData, RLBench; qualitative outperformance claim, no specific numbers in abstract

title: AnyPos: Automated Task-Agnostic Actions for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Learning embodiment dynamics from large-scale, automatically-collected task-agnostic action data (independent image-action pairs covering the workspace, rather than task-specific sequential demonstrations), then coupling this with high-level policy models, achieves a 51% improvement in test accuracy over a standard baseline and raises success rates by 30-40% over strong baselines on manipulation tasks such as microwave operation, toasting, folding, watering, and scrubbing
claims.direction: favors supplementing/replacing task-specific demonstration collection with automated task-agnostic embodiment-dynamics data for improving generalization across tasks and platforms
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation tasks; large-scale automated exploration data plus inverse dynamics learning

title: DM1: MeanFlow with Dispersive Regularization for 1-Step Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Existing one-step flow-based policies (MeanFlow) suffer 'representation collapse' -- an inability to distinguish similar visual representations, causing failures in precise manipulation; adding dispersive regularization across multiple intermediate embedding layers (DM1) prevents this collapse while retaining one-step efficiency, improving success rates by 10-20 percentage points on RoboMimic benchmarks (e.g. Lift task: 99% vs 85% baseline)
claims.direction: favors one-step flow matching with dispersive regularization over standard one-step flow policies (which suffer representation collapse) or multi-step diffusion policies
claims.conditions: RoboMimic sim benchmarks; real-robot deployment on a Franka Panda validates sim-to-real transfer

claims.claim: DM1 achieves 20-40x faster inference than baseline diffusion policies (0.07s vs 2-3.5s) while matching or exceeding the task success rate of multi-step diffusion policies
claims.direction: favors one-step flow-matching action generation (with dispersive regularization) over multi-step diffusion for drastically reducing inference latency without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: same RoboMimic sim benchmarks and real Franka Panda deployment; baseline diffusion policy latency (2-3.5s) closely matches our own reported ~2s inference latency problem

why_deep_read: The reported baseline latency (2-3.5s) almost exactly matches our own stated ~2s inference-latency problem, and DM1 claims a 20-40x speedup with equal-or-better success on real Franka hardware -- this is one of the most directly actionable latency-fix candidates in the batch for Q01/Q10, worth reading in full for implementation details and whether the one-step MeanFlow + dispersive regularization recipe is portable to a smaller policy on our 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Dexplore: Scalable Neural Control for Dexterous Manipulation from Reference-Scoped Exploration

claims.claim: Treating imperfect/inaccurate MoCap demonstrations as 'soft guidance' (adaptive spatial scopes for RL exploration) rather than ground truth to imitate, in a unified single-loop retargeting+tracking optimization, preserves demonstration intent while improving robustness to noise and scaling to large, imperfect demonstration corpora
claims.direction: supports using noisy/imperfect demonstrations as soft guidance/reward shaping rather than requiring precise ground-truth imitation targets
claims.conditions: large-scale hand-object MoCap data, dexterous hand manipulation; distilled into a vision-based skill-conditioned controller for real-world deployment

title: Semantic-Geometric Task Representations for Bimanual Manipulation From Human Demonstrations to Robot Action Planning

claims.claim: A semantic-geometric graph-based task representation (jointly encoding object identities, inter-object relations, and per-object motion histories, decoupled from action labels via an encoder/decoder split) enables encoder reuse across embodiments through decoder-only finetuning on a small robot dataset, achieving full task success on two real-robot bimanual tasks and outperforming graph ablations, Transformer, decoder-only, and finetuned VLM baselines
claims.direction: favors structured, task-agnostic semantic-geometric scene representations (reusable across embodiments via lightweight finetuning) over simpler sequence-based or end-to-end VLM baselines, especially as task variability grows
claims.conditions: eleven bimanual tasks across two datasets; real-robot deployment on two tasks using learned Probabilistic Movement Primitives

title: Beyond Pixels: Learning Invariant Rewards for Real-World Robotics From a Few Demonstrations

claims.claim: A hybrid symbolic-numerical procedure distills 'behavioral invariants' (task-level properties constant across visual instantiations) from as few as five demonstrations, producing a reward function that achieves stronger process alignment and policy-rollout ranking than baselines that fit visual pixel features directly
claims.direction: favors extracting structural/symbolic invariants from very few demonstrations over fitting vision-based reward models to pixel distributions, for both data efficiency and generalization
claims.conditions: eight Meta-World tasks and three Franka manipulation tasks; three real-world out-of-distribution experiments

claims.claim: The learned invariant reward generalizes zero-shot to position, viewpoint, and object variations in real-world out-of-distribution experiments, allowing one learned reward to be reused across diverse task variants
claims.direction: supports that structural/symbolic (non-pixel) representations of task success generalize better to camera-viewpoint, position, and object changes than pixel-feature-based ones -- directly relevant to our lighting/object/camera-shift robustness problem, albeit for reward modeling rather than the action policy itself
claims.conditions: real-world OOD experiments varying position, viewpoint, and object identity

title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing predicted world states into per-object 'slots' (one robot slot + N object slots, each with a persistent address vector and time-varying content vector) so that a flow-matching action head can address a specific object, rather than representing the predicted world as a holistic image/video/global latent, matches strong VLA/WAM baselines on LIBERO (97.8%) and SimplerEnv (79.3%), and reaches SOTA on the most relevant LIBERO-Plus geometric perturbation axes
claims.direction: favors object-addressable (slot-based) world-action model representations over holistic world representations, especially for robustness under scene perturbations where instructions refer to specific objects
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, SimplerEnv, LIBERO-Plus); a causal slot-intervention test shows addressable representations bind object identity far more reliably (swap-binding cosine 0.87) than holistic baselines (at most 0.09)

title: FRMD: fast robot motion diffusion via trajectory-level consistency distillation

claims.claim: Predicting movement-primitive coefficients in a low-dimensional trajectory-parameter space and collapsing multi-step diffusion sampling into a single inference step via trajectory-level consistency distillation (FRMD) reduces policy latency from hundreds to tens of milliseconds, achieving 7x faster inference than vanilla diffusion policy and 10x faster than the SOTA MPD method, while matching multi-step diffusion policies' task success
claims.direction: favors trajectory-parameter-space, single-step consistency-distilled diffusion over standard multi-step pixel/joint-space diffusion policies for reducing inference latency without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: standard robotic manipulation task benchmarks; positioned as a plug-in replacement for the diffusion action-generation module in existing VLA systems, not requiring changes to vision/language encoders

title: Universal Pose Pretraining for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: VLA models built on VQA-optimized VLM backbones excel at semantic identification but overlook subtle 3D state variations needed for distinct action patterns; decoupling training into a pre-training phase that extracts universal 3D spatial priors (via discrete pose tokens in a unified camera-centric space, from diverse 3D datasets) followed by embodiment-specific post-training alignment (Pose-VLA) achieves 79.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 (SOTA) and 96.0% on LIBERO (competitive)
claims.direction: favors a decoupled pose/3D-spatial pretraining phase (separate from action/embodiment-specific training) over training spatial understanding jointly/implicitly with action prediction from VQA-style VLM backbones
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO) plus real-world experiments

claims.claim: Real-world experiments show robust generalization across diverse objects using only 100 demonstrations per task
claims.direction: supports that this pose-pretraining approach is compatible with small (~100) per-task demonstration counts while still generalizing across objects
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, 100 demos/task -- closely matching our own ~50-100 demo budget

title: Teleopit: A Full-Embodiment Humanoid Teleoperation System

claims.claim: ACT and GR00T N1.7 policies trained on 96 successful demonstrations collected with this teleoperation system achieve task success rates of 90.0% and 95.0% respectively when deployed on a real humanoid robot
claims.direction: provides a real-world data point that ~96 demonstrations can be sufficient for high success rates (90-95%) with ACT or a VLA foundation model, though on a humanoid platform rather than a simple arm
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot, coordinated locomotion/manipulation/viewpoint-control tasks; demo count (96) closely matches our own ~50-100 demo budget, though task/embodiment differ substantially

title: AcrossWAM1.0: A Modular Latent World-Action Stack for Compact Robot Policies

claims.claim: In a modularized latent world-action-model stack (policy adapter + latent world decoder + flow-matching action expert), replacing a Qwen3-VL-2B multimodal backbone with a much smaller Qwen3.5-0.8B backbone yields 97.45% success vs 98.00% for the 2B model on 2,000 paired LIBERO episodes (a 0.55-percentage-point difference, not statistically significant by exact McNemar test, p=0.266), while the resulting compact checkpoint has 42.4% fewer parameters (1,472.6M vs the original 2B policy)
claims.direction: supports that a much smaller multimodal backbone (0.8B vs 2B parameters) can retain almost all task performance within a world-action-model architecture, i.e. backbone size can be substantially reduced with statistically negligible performance loss for this architecture/benchmark
claims.conditions: sim only (2,000 paired LIBERO episodes); cross-family transfer (to a MiniCPM-V adapter) explicitly left as an open evaluation, not yet validated

why_deep_read: Directly targets our Q12 model-size decision with a controlled, statistically-tested backbone-swap ablation (2B vs 0.8B) inside a world-action-model architecture -- exactly the kind of evidence needed to decide how small our backbone can go on an 8GB laptop GPU while retaining auxiliary world-model benefits (Q09).

title: V2-STRep: VLM-Grounded Structured Task Representations for Reusable Robot Skills Acquired from Generated Videos

claims.claim: Converting AI-generated demonstration videos (from an initial scene image + task instruction) into reusable robot skills via VLM-grounded structured task representations (motion phases, geometric references/constraints lifted to 3D via RGB-D) shows improved execution success over baselines and reliable cross-scene transfer, without needing to record or generate a new video for each new scene/instruction
claims.direction: favors extracting reusable structured (geometric/constraint-based) representations from single generated videos over per-scene video generation or direct imitation from raw generated motion
claims.conditions: six real-world manipulation tasks; qualitative improvement claims, no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: A Framework for Improving Information Content of Human Demonstrations for Enabling Robots to Acquire Complex Tool Manipulation Skills

claims.claim: A multimodal demonstration-collection framework (speech, gesture, motion, video, 3D depth) that actively queries the human expert to improve information content per demonstration is proposed as a way to reduce the large number of demonstrations otherwise needed to learn a policy, for a complex granular-media transport task on a real robot
claims.direction: favors improving the information richness of each demonstration (via active querying and multimodal capture) over simply collecting more demonstrations of the same quality
claims.conditions: real robot, complex tool manipulation (granular media transport); qualitative effectiveness claim, no comparative numbers given

title: Sim-Grasp: Learning 6-DOF Grasp Policies for Cluttered Environments Using a Synthetic Benchmark

claims.claim: A grasp policy trained entirely on a large synthetic dataset (1,550 objects, 500 scenarios, 7.9M annotated labels) achieves 97.14% success for single objects and 87.43%/83.33% for mixed clutter (Levels 1-2 / Levels 3-4), with language models enabling text/box-prompted target identification for object-agnostic and target picking
claims.direction: supports that purely synthetic training data (no real demonstrations) can achieve high grasp success rates, including in cluttered scenes, when paired with a large-scale synthetic benchmark
claims.conditions: 6-DOF two-finger grasping, point-cloud input; synthetic benchmark, real-world transfer not detailed as a separate number in the abstract

title: ManualVLA: A Unified VLA Model for Chain-of-Thought Manual Generation and Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Mixture-of-Transformers VLA that first generates intermediate multimodal 'manuals' (images, position prompts, text instructions) via a planning expert, then feeds them through a Manual Chain-of-Thought process to an action expert (each manual step giving explicit control conditions plus implicit latent guidance), achieves a 32% higher average success rate than the previous hierarchical SOTA baseline on real-world LEGO assembly and object rearrangement
claims.direction: favors generating explicit intermediate visual+textual 'manual' representations as auxiliary guidance for the action expert, over direct sensory-to-action mapping or purely textual planning
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon tasks (LEGO assembly, object rearrangement); manual training data generated via a 3D-Gaussian-Splatting digital-twin toolkit to reduce data collection burden

title: Temporal-Spatial Representation Fusion for Dexterous Manipulation Learning with Unpaired Visual-Action Data

claims.claim: Learning temporal (LSTM-based trajectory reconstruction) and spatial (VAE-based action reconstruction) priors from action-only data (without paired visual observations, e.g. Internet videos or privacy-friendly action logs) and incorporating them as RL reward shaping achieves more than 30% increase in success rate compared with existing visual-pretraining methods, on three dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors leveraging unpaired action-only data (when paired visual-action data is unavailable/costly) as an auxiliary prior source over relying solely on visual pretraining
claims.conditions: dexterous robot manipulation, RL framework; not a direct imitation-learning comparison

title: ST-HONet: Spatio-Temporal Hierarchical Network for long-horizon bimanual visuomotor imitation

claims.claim: Most transformer-based action-chunking approaches use deterministic/unimodal action representations, limiting capture of multimodal expert behavior; formulating policy learning as conditional generation of extended action segments via a Transformer-based conditional VAE (with adaptive data augmentation, progressive latent regularization, multi-stage optimization) achieves consistently higher task success than baseline models on RoboTwin 2.0, with only minimal additional computational overhead
claims.direction: favors explicit multimodal latent modeling (CVAE) of extended action chunks over deterministic/unimodal chunk prediction, for long-horizon bimanual imitation
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmark, long-horizon bimanual manipulation under domain randomization; qualitative comparative claims, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: RoTri-Diff: A Spatial Robot-Object Triadic Interaction-Guided Diffusion Model for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Explicitly encoding the relative 6D pose triadic relationship between two arms and the manipulated object (RoTri) within a hierarchical diffusion policy outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 10.2% on 11 RLBench2 tasks and achieves stable performance on 4 real-world bimanual tasks
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling robot-object(s) geometric relationships within the diffusion action head over robot-centric or object-centric representations that ignore this relationship
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation (two arms + object), sim (RLBench2) and real-world; less directly applicable to our single-arm setup

title: Hand-in-the-Loop: Improving VLA Policies for Dexterous Manipulation via Seamless Hand-Arm Intervention

claims.claim: Directly taking over control via teleoperation during human intervention causes abrupt robot configuration changes ('gesture jumps') due to command mismatch between human input and policy execution; seamlessly blending human corrective intent with autonomous policy execution (HandITL) reduces intervention jitter by 99.8%, reduces grasp failures by 87.5%, and reduces mean completion time by 19.1%, compared to direct teleoperation takeover
claims.direction: favors blended/seamless human-policy control handoff over abrupt direct-teleoperation takeover, to avoid jitter/discontinuities at intervention points -- conceptually related to smoothing discontinuities at any human-robot or chunk-execution handoff
claims.conditions: real robot, bimanual dexterous manipulation requiring tool use and long-horizon coordination

claims.claim: Using HandITL-collected correction data to refine policies yields policies that outperform those trained with standard teleoperation data by 19% on average across three long-horizon dexterous tasks
claims.direction: favors collecting corrective intervention data via a seamless blending mechanism over standard teleoperation-only data collection, for downstream policy fine-tuning quality
claims.conditions: same real robot dexterous manipulation setting

title: A Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Action Tokenizer for In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics

claims.claim: A two-level hierarchical vector-quantization action tokenizer (fine-grained subclusters mapped to coarser clusters), extended to jointly recover input actions and their timestamps (HiST-AT), outperforms a non-hierarchical VQ tokenizer counterpart and establishes new SOTA performance in in-context imitation learning across multiple simulation and real robotic manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors hierarchical (two-level) discrete/VQ action tokenization over flat/non-hierarchical discrete tokenization for action representation
claims.conditions: multiple sim and real robot manipulation benchmarks; qualitative SOTA claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Twin-DP3: View-Invariant 3D Diffusion Policy With Digital Twin

claims.claim: Single-view point-cloud-based 3D diffusion policies (a simpler, more efficient alternative to multi-view point-cloud fusion) suffer performance degradation under significant viewpoint changes; augmenting the single-view point cloud in real time using a digital twin (6-DoF object pose tracking + a robot model generating robot-component point clouds), without requiring extra multi-view data collection, achieves notable improvements in policy robustness under novel viewpoints
claims.direction: favors single-view 3D point-cloud policies augmented with digital-twin-generated point clouds over either plain single-view (fragile to viewpoint shift) or costly multi-view point-cloud fusion, for viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: comprehensive experiments in both simulation and real-world environments; addresses camera-viewpoint shift specifically

why_deep_read: Directly targets our exact stated failure mode (policy breaks when the camera is slightly moved) using our exact available sensing modality (depth/point cloud from the RealSense) via a lightweight digital-twin augmentation that avoids needing additional multi-view cameras -- worth reading in full for the augmentation recipe and how much viewpoint-robustness improvement it buys in the real-world experiments.

title: Pipette: An Embodied Simulation Platform, Benchmark, and Data-Efficient Augmentation Framework for Wet-Lab Robotics

claims.claim: A simulation-based data augmentation pipeline that replays human demonstrations in simulation and applies lighting, camera, speed, and action perturbations (filtering generated episodes by automatic task-success checks) improves SmolVLA's average success rate from 40.4% to 71.8%, and pi0's from 37.3% to 44.1%, on a 12-task wet-lab embodied benchmark
claims.direction: strongly favors simulation-replay-based augmentation across lighting/camera/speed/action perturbations for improving a SmolVLA (our own base model) or pi0 policy's success rate, over training on raw limited demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: 12-task wet-lab robotics benchmark (different task domain from our pumpkin pick-and-place, but same base model SmolVLA and same general lighting/camera perturbation augmentation approach); only 30 demonstrations per task used

claims.claim: With only 30 demonstrations per task, ACT achieves a 60.3% average success rate on this benchmark
claims.direction: provides a real-world data point on ACT's performance at a demo count (30) below our own ~50-100 demo target
claims.conditions: same 12-task wet-lab benchmark; different task domain but same low-data regime as ours

why_deep_read: This is the closest match in the entire batch to our exact setup: it directly benchmarks SmolVLA (our current base model) and shows that simulation-replayed demonstrations with lighting/camera/speed/action perturbation augmentation nearly doubles its success rate (40.4% to 71.8%). This is highly actionable evidence for our Q05 augmentation decision and directly addresses our stated lighting/camera-shift failure modes -- worth reading in full for the exact augmentation recipe and whether the wet-lab task domain findings transfer to pick-and-place.

title: Generalize and Guide: Decomposing Rewards for Few-Shot Inverse Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A method that decomposes rewards into a generalizable discriminator (transferring shared structure from related-task demonstrations) and a proximity-based corrective-guidance function achieves an average success rate of 81.2% on navigation/manipulation tasks with substantial variations (object configurations, table layouts, initial poses), outperforming the strongest per-task baseline by 24.7 percentage points, using only a limited number of target-task demonstrations plus related-task demonstrations and online experience
claims.direction: favors combining a small number of target-task demonstrations with a larger set of related-task demonstrations (few-shot IRL with multi-task demos) over learning from target-task demonstrations alone, when task variation is substantial
claims.conditions: navigation and manipulation tasks under significant variations; inverse RL framework, not standard imitation learning

title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control

claims.claim: Representing robot actions as pixel motion ('action flow') as a shared visual world-model interface (rather than embodiment-specific action vectors) achieves 90.4% lower robot-motion error and 60.2% lower object-motion error than an action-conditioned baseline, while supporting zero-shot composition and data-efficient adaptation across embodiments, tasks, and environments
claims.direction: favors a shared pixel-motion action representation for world modeling over embodiment-specific action-conditioned world models, for cross-embodiment/task generalization and data efficiency
claims.conditions: RoboLab benchmark (Pearson r=0.96 between replayed and reference success rates); an inverse mode also predicts robot motion compatible with human-demonstrated object flow without task-specific expert robot demonstrations

title: MemBodied: Recurrent Associative Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Instead of retaining growing raw past observations in context (costly in latency and context size) for history-dependent manipulation tasks, a fixed-size episodic memory (an associative state recording cross-call interactions, plus a compact 'episode anchor' of the initial scene) lets the policy condition on memory components rather than raw history, achieving 7.81x the mean success rate of a stateless policy and 2.98x that of vanilla recurrent memory on five memory-requiring RMBench tasks, outperforming the strongest memory-augmented baseline by 1.3x with 10x fewer added parameters; on fully-observable LIBERO-Long it reaches 90.6%, a 5.4% improvement over the stateless pi0 policy
claims.direction: strongly favors a fixed-size, parameter-efficient episodic memory mechanism over both stateless policies and naive growing-context/recurrent-memory approaches for observation history -- directly addressing memory/copycat/causal-confusion concerns without inflating inference cost
claims.conditions: five RMBench memory-dependent tasks and LIBERO-Long; comparison against stateless pi0 and vanilla recurrent memory baselines

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our Q07 (observation history/memory) with a highly quantified, parameter-efficient solution (10x fewer added parameters than the next-best memory baseline) that explicitly avoids the latency cost of growing context -- relevant both to memory design and to our Q10 latency constraint, making it one of the most actionable papers in the batch for our small-model, single-GPU setup.

title: What Went Wrong? Closing the Sim-to-Real Gap via Differentiable Causal Discovery

claims.claim: Automatically discovering the causal relationship between simulator environment parameters and the sim-to-real gap (via a differentiable mapping governed by a learned causal graph), rather than manually selecting tunable parameters, achieves significant improvements in trajectory alignment and task success rate over strong domain-randomization/parameter-tuning baselines in several manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors automated, causally-guided simulator parameter alignment over manual/case-by-case domain randomization parameter tuning for closing the sim-to-real gap
claims.conditions: sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer experiments on manipulation tasks

title: Yell At Your Robot: Improving On-the-Fly from Language Corrections

claims.claim: Hierarchical policies where a high-level policy indexes into rich, expressive low-level language-conditioned skills can be supervised purely with human language corrections (including fine-grained corrections like 'move a bit to the left'), and incorporating such corrections into an iterative training scheme leads to significant performance improvement on long-horizon, dexterous manipulation tasks on real hardware, without any additional teleoperation
claims.direction: favors using natural-language corrections (rather than teleoperation demonstrations) as the supervision signal for iteratively improving a hierarchical language-conditioned policy's long-horizon performance
claims.conditions: real robot hardware, long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks; hierarchical high-level/low-level language-conditioned policy architecture

title: Learning to Prune Branches in Modern Tree-Fruit Orchards

claims.claim: A closed-loop visuomotor controller using only optical-flow images from a wrist-mounted camera (no full 3D reconstruction) can guide a cutter to a specified cut point in a cluttered environment, achieving zero-shot sim-to-real transfer with ~30% success rate (about half of an oracle planner's performance)
claims.direction: suggests a lightweight optical-flow-from-wrist-camera representation can partially substitute for full 3D reconstruction in a cluttered closed-loop control task, though with a substantial performance gap versus an oracle
claims.conditions: real-world orchard pruning task (different domain from tabletop pick-and-place); wrist-mounted camera only, trained in a custom orchard simulator

title: Combining Data Distribution and Adaptive Inference for Robotic Grasping in Vision-Language-Action

claims.claim: A compositional data collection strategy that decomposes the task state space into orientation and spatial factors (rather than randomly sampling demonstrations) efficiently expands state-space coverage with a limited number of demonstrations, achieving a 98% grasp success rate with only 81 demonstrations; embedding-space analysis shows performance saturates once relevant state-space dimensions are sufficiently covered
claims.direction: favors deliberately structuring/decomposing demonstration collection to cover orientation and spatial factors over unstructured demonstration collection, for maximizing success rate per demonstration
claims.conditions: real-robot grasping experiments; demo count (81) closely matches our own ~50-100 per-task budget

claims.claim: An adaptive inference mechanism that dynamically adjusts the execution horizon during critical task phases improves success rate from 90% to 97% on a moderately-covered dataset, though it cannot fully compensate for insufficient data-distribution design
claims.direction: favors dynamically adjusting the action-chunk execution horizon at critical phases (rather than a fixed horizon throughout) as a complementary lever to data coverage, but not a substitute for it
claims.conditions: same real-robot grasping setup

why_deep_read: Directly matches our demo-count budget (81 demos, close to our 50-100 target) with a concrete, real-robot-validated recipe for both data collection structure (Q13) and adaptive execution-horizon inference (Q06) -- exactly the two levers most actionable for our low-data, chunk-boundary-smoothness problems.

title: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A training-free online safeguard for generative action-chunked imitation policies (Rewind-IL) combines a zero-shot failure detector based on self-consistency across overlapping action chunks (Temporal Inter-chunk Discrepancy Estimate, calibrated via split conformal prediction) with a state-respawning mechanism that returns the robot to a semantically-verified safe checkpoint (identified offline by a VLM) upon detected failure, improving reliability on real-world and simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks, including transfer to flow-matching action-chunked policies
claims.direction: favors adding a training-free, chunk-consistency-based failure detector plus checkpoint-based rewind/respawn mechanism on top of existing action-chunked policies (diffusion or flow-matching), rather than relying on the base policy to recover from off-manifold drift on its own
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks; works with both diffusion-based and flow-matching action-chunked policies without modifying them

title: ElasticFlow: One-Step Physics-Consistent Policy with Elastic Time Horizons for Language-Guided Manipulation

claims.claim: Reconstructing Mean Field Theory to directly model the average velocity field enables a direct single-step mapping from noise to action (1-NFE inference, ~71Hz), addressing the high latency of iterative diffusion denoising without sacrificing physical consistency
claims.direction: favors one-step physics-consistent flow policies over iterative diffusion denoising for drastically reducing inference latency while maintaining physical plausibility
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN, and RoboTwin benchmarks (sim)

claims.claim: An 'Elastic Time Horizons' mechanism explicitly encodes control granularity to overcome spectral bias, achieving efficient alignment between semantic (language) instructions and physical execution horizons, and the resulting policy outperforms OpenVLA and pi0 on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors adaptively matching the action-chunk execution horizon to the granularity implied by the language instruction, rather than using a fixed horizon regardless of task semantics
claims.conditions: same sim benchmarks; compared against OpenVLA and pi0

title: Efficient Hybrid SE(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Flow Policy via Spherical Harmonics for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: E3Flow unifies efficient rectified flow with stable, multi-modal SE(3)-equivariant learning (via spherical-harmonic representations and a Feature Enhancement Module fusing point clouds and images), achieving a 3.12% improvement in average success rate over the state-of-the-art Spherical Diffusion Policy while delivering a 7x inference speedup
claims.direction: favors combining equivariant flow-matching with hybrid point-cloud+image fusion over pure equivariant diffusion policies, for both accuracy and inference speed
claims.conditions: 8 manipulation tasks from MimicGen (sim) plus 4 real-world experiments

title: BORA: Bridging Offline Reinforcement Learning and Online Residual Adaptation for Real-World Dexterous VLA Models

claims.claim: An offline-to-online RL post-training framework that freezes the VLA base and adds a lightweight, human-in-the-loop chunk-wise residual adaptation mechanism (guided by a critic taking both VLM cognition tokens and action chunks as input) significantly outperforms pure imitation learning and traditional decoupled RL baselines, achieving a 33% absolute increase in average success rate under standard settings and up to 43% improvement in unseen-object generalization
claims.direction: favors adding a frozen-base + chunk-wise residual RL correction layer (rather than retraining the whole policy or using decoupled RL) for correcting real-world execution errors in dexterous VLA policies
claims.conditions: five complex real-world dexterous manipulation tasks

title: DeMaVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Generalizable Deformable Manipulation

claims.claim: Constructing the flow-matching action expert by pruning every other transformer layer (while preserving layer-wise alignment with the VLM backbone) reduces training and inference cost while achieving competitive performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and strong real-world folding results
claims.direction: favors layer-pruned, alignment-preserving action experts over full-depth action experts for reducing compute cost without a corresponding drop in performance
claims.conditions: pretrained on ~5,000 hours of real-world dual-arm demonstrations; deformable-object (clothing) folding tasks

claims.claim: Post-training on mixed folding data that aggregates self-collected demonstrations with corrective trajectories from real-robot failures, collected via a human-in-the-loop DAgger pipeline, improves generalization across folding tasks
claims.direction: favors DAgger-style corrective-trajectory aggregation on top of self-collected demonstrations, over static demonstration sets alone
claims.conditions: real-world household folding benchmark

title: Mixture of Frames Policy: Multi-Frame Action Denoising for Bimanual Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Modern diffusion policies typically commit to a single predefined action coordinate frame (e.g. end-effector or base-aligned), forcing one denoiser to model unnecessarily complex distributions in that frame; performing synchronized action denoising across multiple coordinate frames simultaneously and fusing their noise predictions (Mixture of Frames) improves over both oracle single-frame selection and standard Mixture-of-Experts baselines, since the best action frame is task-dependent
claims.direction: favors representing/denoising actions across multiple coordinate frames simultaneously (rather than committing to one fixed frame, whether joint, end-effector, or base-aligned) since no single frame is best for all task phases
claims.conditions: nine simulated bimanual manipulation tasks; two real-world bimanual mobile manipulation tasks, outperforming all constituent single-frame baselines

title: ContactGuard: Pre-Contact Execution Monitoring with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models

claims.claim: In wrist-camera setups, close gripper-object views help observe contact but a poor approach may already push/miss/slip/disturb the object before conventional failure detectors react; ContactGuard predicts a planned action chunk's short-horizon consequence in latent visual space (from a world model trained on unlabelled trajectories to predict compact multi-view visual embeddings, avoiding pixel-level video prediction) and aborts execution if the predicted future indicates likely failure, predicting failure more accurately than direct and corrupted-action ablations on real-world contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight, pre-contact latent-world-model-based abort monitor specifically tuned to wrist-camera pre-contact cues, layered on top of an existing chunked policy without modifying it, over relying on the base policy or post-hoc detectors alone
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks; deploys as a pre-contact abort signal on a live robot without retraining the underlying policy

title: Topology-Informed Visual Prompting For Vision Language Action Policies

claims.claim: Using simulation-based planning with privileged geometry information to augment a nominal VLA fine-tuning dataset with topology-signature-labeled trajectories (Gauss-Linking-Integral representation), plus a VLM fine-tuned to predict topological signatures and end-effector waypoints as visual prompts at deployment, exceeds the strongest baseline by 40% in task success on a real-world hardware box-pickup task
claims.direction: favors augmenting demonstration data with simulation-derived topological/geometric signature labels and rendering vision-based prompts at deployment, over fine-tuning on nominal demonstrations alone or generic VLM-prompting
claims.conditions: three simulated bimanual tasks plus one real-world box-pickup task; addresses tasks with complex obstacle geometries under partial observability

title: Generating Velocity-Adaptive Manipulation Through Learning from Human Movement Speed Variations

claims.claim: Conditioning a policy explicitly on target motion velocity (rather than assuming temporally-aligned, uniformly-paced demonstrations) avoids the averaged/unreliable actions that standard behavior cloning produces when trained on naturally speed-varying human demonstrations, and generalizes across a wide range of target velocities, outperforming standard imitation learning baselines
claims.direction: favors explicit velocity-conditioning in the action space over standard (implicitly fixed-speed) behavior cloning, particularly when demonstrations have varied/uncontrolled motion speed (e.g. in-the-wild teleoperation)
claims.conditions: object manipulation including grasp-and-place, in both simulated and real-world environments; qualitative outperformance claim, no specific numbers given

title: HAND Me the Data: Fast Robot Adaptation via Hand Path Retrieval

claims.claim: Instead of collecting task-specific teleoperation demonstrations, extracting human-hand motion from a single easy-to-provide hand demonstration and retrieving matching robot sub-trajectories from task-agnostic robot play data (via visual-similarity filtering then behavior-similarity retrieval), then fine-tuning on the retrieved data, enables real-time task learning in under four minutes and outperforms retrieval baselines by over 2x in average task success rate on real robots
claims.direction: favors retrieving relevant behaviors from existing task-agnostic play data (guided by a cheap hand demonstration) over collecting new task-specific teleoperation demonstrations, for fast adaptation to new tasks
claims.conditions: real robots; no calibrated cameras or detailed hand pose estimation required

title: DiffusionRL: Efficient Training of Diffusion Policies for Robotic Grasping Using RL-Adapted Large-Scale Datasets

claims.claim: Training a lightweight diffusion policy on a large pre-built grasping dataset (DexGraspNet) enhanced/refined using RL, plus a pose-sampling validation algorithm, achieves an 80% success rate on three DexGraspNet objects for a five-fingered hand, eliminating the need for manual demonstration collection
claims.direction: favors RL-enhanced large synthetic datasets as training data for diffusion policies over manually-collected demonstrations
claims.conditions: dexterous five-fingered hand grasping; synthetic dataset origin (DexGraspNet)

title: Dual-Actor Fine-Tuning of VLA Models: A Talk-and-Tweak Human-in-the-Loop Approach

claims.claim: A human-in-the-loop dual-actor RL fine-tuning framework (a primary actor for robust multi-task performance plus a refinement actor for latent-space adaptation) achieves 100% success across three real-world multi-task experiments within 101 minutes of online fine-tuning, and sustains a 50% success rate over 12 consecutive operations for long-horizon tasks; scales to multi-robot training with up to 2x efficiency improvement using dual robots
claims.direction: favors a dual-actor (primary + refinement) online RL fine-tuning approach with lightweight human corrections over single-actor fine-tuning, for fast real-world adaptation
claims.conditions: real-world multi-task manipulation experiments; scalable to multiple robots

claims.claim: A lightweight 'talk-and-tweak' scheme converts human physical corrections into semantically grounded language commands, generating a new dataset for policy learning alongside standard physical interventions
claims.direction: favors converting human corrections into language-labeled supervision (in addition to physical intervention data) to enrich the fine-tuning signal
claims.conditions: same real-world multi-task setting

title: TypeTele: Releasing Dexterity in Teleoperation by Dexterous Manipulation Types

claims.claim: Introducing a library of dexterous manipulation 'types' (beyond human-motion-mimicking hand retargeting) into a teleoperation system, with an MLLM-assisted type-retrieval module to select the suitable type per task, significantly improves imitation-learning task success rates on real-world teleoperation-collected data compared to standard hand-retargeting teleoperation
claims.direction: favors type-guided teleoperation (leveraging a dexterous hand's structural advantages beyond pure human-motion mimicry) over standard hand-retargeting teleoperation, for higher-quality demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous hand teleoperation and imitation learning; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: AgiBot World Colosseo: A Large-Scale Manipulation Platform for Scalable and Intelligent Embodied Systems

claims.claim: AgiBot World, a large-scale platform with over 1 million trajectories across 217 tasks (an order-of-magnitude scale increase over prior datasets, collected via a standardized human-in-the-loop-verified pipeline), enables policies pre-trained on it to achieve an average 30% performance improvement over those trained on Open X-Embodiment, both in in-domain and out-of-distribution scenarios
claims.direction: favors pretraining on larger-scale, standardized, verified multi-task/multi-scenario data over prior smaller/less-standardized datasets, with performance scaling predictably with data volume
claims.conditions: large-scale foundation-model pretraining; results reported both in-domain and OOD

claims.claim: Genie Operator-1 (GO-1), a generalist policy using latent action representations to maximize data utilization, achieves over 60% success rate on complex real-world dexterous/long-horizon tasks, outperforming the prior RDT approach by 32%
claims.direction: favors latent action representations (vs. the compared RDT approach) for generalist policies trained on large heterogeneous datasets
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous and long-horizon tasks; large-scale foundation-model context, less directly transferable to our tiny-data single-task setting

title: FlowDPG: Deterministic Policy Gradient on Flow Matching Policies for Real-World Manipulation

claims.claim: FlowDPG, a DDPG-style method that distills the critic gradient into the velocity field of a flow-matching policy (bypassing backpropagation-through-time along the multi-step ODE), attains a 92% end-to-end success rate on a long-horizon, multi-stage, dual-arm AirPods assembly task, substantially outperforming recent RL methods based on value-conditioning, auxiliary-module adaptation, and adjoint-based critic-gradient approaches
claims.direction: favors this BPTT-free critic-gradient distillation approach for RL fine-tuning of flow-matching policies over other RL adaptation methods for flow/diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon multi-stage dual-arm assembly task

title: From Seeing to Simulating: Generative High-Fidelity Simulation with Digital Cousins for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation

claims.claim: A generative real-to-sim mapping from real-world panoramas to high-fidelity simulation scenes, further diversified via semantic/geometric editing into 'digital cousin' scenes, shows a strong sim-to-real correlation, and extensively scaling up this generated data leads to significantly better generalization to unseen scene and object variations
claims.direction: favors generative real-to-sim scene augmentation (creating many diverse synthetic 'cousin' scenes from a single real scan) over collecting additional real-world data, for improving generalization to novel scenes/objects
claims.conditions: interactive manipulation tasks combined with high-quality physics engines and realistic assets; also supports long-horizon navigation via multi-room stitching

title: VISTA: Enhancing Visual Conditioning via Track-Following Preference Optimization in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Extending large pretrained VLMs to the action space can induce vision-action misalignment where action predictions exhibit weak dependence on the current visual state; empirically, successful rollouts consistently exhibit stronger visual dependence than failed ones. A training framework that first aligns action prediction with visual input via preference optimization on a track-following surrogate task, then transfers this alignment to the instruction-following task via latent-space distillation during SFT, improves both visual conditioning and task performance for discrete OpenVLA, with consistent gains also on continuous OpenVLA-OFT -- without architectural changes or additional data collection
claims.direction: favors explicitly strengthening vision-action dependence via a track-following preference-optimization + distillation recipe over standard SFT alone, when a VLA's failures correlate with weak visual grounding of its action predictions
claims.conditions: OpenVLA (discrete) and OpenVLA-OFT (continuous) architectures; no additional data collection or architecture changes required

why_deep_read: This directly diagnoses a plausible root cause of our observed failures (breaking under new lighting/objects/camera shifts could reflect weak vision-action dependence) and offers a fix that requires no new data or architecture changes -- worth reading in full to see if the track-following preference-optimization recipe is applicable to a small SmolVLA-scale policy.

title: BEACON: Cross-Domain Co-Training of Generative Robot Policies via Best-Effort Adaptation

claims.claim: Casting cross-domain co-training (abundant source demonstrations, limited target demonstrations) as a discrepancy-aware importance-reweighting problem -- jointly learning a diffusion-based visuomotor policy and per-sample source weights that minimize a target-generalization-informed objective -- improves robustness and data efficiency over target-only training, fixed-ratio co-training, and feature-alignment baselines across sim-to-sim, sim-to-real, and multi-source manipulation settings
claims.direction: favors discrepancy-aware, per-sample-reweighted co-training of source and limited target demonstrations over naive fixed-ratio mixing or feature-alignment approaches, when target demonstrations are scarce
claims.conditions: sim-to-sim, sim-to-real, and multi-source manipulation settings; diffusion-based visuomotor policy backbone; qualitative comparative claims, no specific numbers given

title: DynaWM: A Base-VLA-Guided World Foundation Model for Moving-Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Rather than fine-tuning world-model modules end-to-end into a base VLA (which can degrade a well-pretrained model), DynaWM keeps the base VLA frozen/separate and layers a world-foundation model on top (Mamba-3 action encoder + V-JEPA 2.1 vision encoder + proprioceptive encoder, jointly conditioning a flow-matching DiT) to regenerate motion-aware action trajectories for moving-object manipulation; for fine-tuned base-VLA checkpoints, DynaWM improves success by 7.19, 45.31, 1.88, and 10.94 percentage points over SmolVLA, X-VLA, pi0, and pi0.5 respectively (for coarse-tuned checkpoints: +35.13, +44.06, +35.69, +26.13 pp)
claims.direction: favors adding a separate, base-VLA-guided world model on top of a frozen/lightly-tuned base VLA (rather than jointly fine-tuning world-model components into the base model) specifically to handle moving/dynamic objects
claims.conditions: DynaGrasp-32 benchmark (six categories of moving-object manipulation: velocity variation, trajectory variation, multi-object) and DynaGrasp-1600 dataset (32 scenarios, 1,600 demonstrations, ~1.53M images); explicitly tested with SmolVLA as one of the base-VLA checkpoints (our own base model)

claims.claim: Ablation experiments show visual encoding enhances success by 27.50%, while removing action conditioning reduces success by 45.44%
claims.direction: quantifies that both the vision encoder and the action-conditioning mechanism are each substantial, largely non-redundant contributors to robustness for moving-object manipulation
claims.conditions: same DynaGrasp benchmark ablations

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly benchmarks against SmolVLA -- our exact current base model -- and reports a specific percentage-point improvement (+7.19pp fine-tuned, +35.13pp coarse-tuned) from adding a world-model layer, which is unusually directly actionable evidence for our Q09 decision given our own model choice.

title: JoyAI-RA 0.5: Scaling Robot Manipulation Learning via Dual Action Alignment

claims.claim: On a real-world AgiBot benchmark, a generalist Vision-Language-World-Action framework that aligns action-free human egocentric video (via implicit latent-action inference) and explicit human/robot trajectory alignment shows task score improving consistently as the volume of human egocentric pretraining data increases, with no sign of plateauing at the largest scale tested
claims.direction: favors treating abundant, weakly-labeled human egocentric video as a primary (not merely auxiliary) scalable data source for manipulation learning, since naive pooling of heterogeneous data causes negative transfer without such alignment mechanisms
claims.conditions: real-world AgiBot benchmark; large-scale foundation-model context, less directly applicable to our tiny single-task dataset

title: Rethinking 3D Noise: Learning 3D-Aware Video Priors via Optimization-Free Morphological Perturbations

claims.claim: An optimization-free 3D augmentation technique (perturbing 3D Gaussian Splatting primitives' scale, rotation, and pruning, analogous to 2D pixel augmentation but preserving spatial/view consistency) reduces mean depth error by 12.5% over SOTA image-to-image 3D artifact refiners and boosts downstream robotics policy success rates by up to 8.0% across 3 of 4 manipulation tasks, when scaled to a 14B-parameter video model via ControlNet
claims.direction: favors 3D-consistent morphological perturbation augmentation (rather than per-scene 3DGS re-optimization) for improving both 3D scene-representation quality and downstream manipulation policy success
claims.conditions: large-scale (14B-parameter) video diffusion model; downstream evaluation on manipulation tasks

title: PSR: Predictive Sensorimotor Representation Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Pretraining a multimodal Transformer to learn a hierarchy of predictive representations (by jointly forecasting future interaction dynamics from multimodal sensorimotor signals) and injecting this hierarchy into the action stream of a VLA policy (PSR-VLA) achieves 91.7% overall success on six real-world contact-rich tasks, improving over pi0.5 and two force-augmented pi0.5 variants (ForceVLA, ForceVLA2) by 30.0, 22.5, and 19.2 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors augmenting the action stream with a pretrained hierarchy of predictive (future-forecasting) sensorimotor representations over simply adding raw force feedback as an additional input modality
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation, six tasks; relies on force/tactile sensing not present in our own sensor set, but the auxiliary predictive-representation principle (Q09) is domain-general

title: Improving Robot Skills by Integrating Task and Motion Planning with Learning from Demonstration

claims.claim: A sampling-based task-and-motion planner can autonomously generate a demonstration dataset (using a small library of scripted primitive skills) which an offline policy-learning algorithm then uses to extract and replace skills, without further environment interaction; this method is robust to suboptimal demonstrations and suitable for long-horizon tasks, with collision-free data collection
claims.direction: favors autonomously planner-generated demonstrations (self-generated by the robot) over exclusively human-collected demonstrations, particularly for reducing the embodiment gap and enabling safe, persistent real-world data collection
claims.conditions: simulation, three mobile manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: LLaDA-VLA: Vision Language Diffusion Action Models

claims.claim: Adapting pretrained masked-diffusion vision-language models (d-VLMs, a paradigm distinct from autoregressive VLMs) to robotic manipulation via localized special-token action classification (instead of full-vocabulary classification) and hierarchical action-structured decoding (respecting within- and across-action dependencies) significantly outperforms state-of-the-art VLAs on both simulation and real-world robots
claims.direction: favors masked-diffusion VLM backbones (with specialized action-token classification and hierarchical decoding) as an alternative to autoregressive-VLM-based or standard diffusion-policy VLAs
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world robots; qualitative outperformance claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: SSL-HWE: Semi-Supervised Learning-Based Hierarchical Waypoint Extraction for Imitation Learning in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Human demonstrations contain imperfections that complicate the action data distribution and cause compounding errors; a semi-supervised approach that identifies a small set of labeled 'key intervals' capturing critical actions, then applies hierarchical waypoint-extraction optimization to simplify/adjust the full demonstration dataset's actions, significantly enhances downstream imitation learning and outperforms a compared data-processing method by 30% to 50% in success rate in real-world experiments
