claims.direction: favors preprocessing/cleaning raw human demonstrations into simplified waypoint-based action representations (via semi-supervised key-interval segmentation) over training directly on raw, imperfect demonstration trajectories
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation experiments, combined with a state-of-the-art imitation learning method

title: Dense-Jump Flow Matching with Non-Uniform Time Scheduling for Robotic Policies: Mitigating Multi-Step Inference Degradation

claims.claim: Counter-intuitively, increasing the number of Euler integration steps during flow-matching inference universally degrades policy performance, because (i) uniformly-spaced extra steps oversample the late-time region, constraining actions toward training trajectories and reducing generalization, and (ii) the learned velocity field becomes non-Lipschitz as integration time approaches 1, causing instability; a non-uniform (U-shaped) time schedule during training plus a 'dense-jump' single-step-beyond-a-jump-point schedule at inference yields up to 23.7% performance gains over SOTA baselines across diverse robotic tasks
claims.direction: directly contradicts the common assumption that more denoising/integration steps improve flow-matching or diffusion policy quality -- shows that naively adding inference steps can hurt performance, and that non-uniform time scheduling plus early single-step jumps is better than uniform multi-step integration
claims.conditions: diverse robotic manipulation tasks; flow-matching policy backbone

title: Self-Augmented Robot Trajectory: Efficient Imitation Learning via Safe Self-augmentation with Demonstrator-annotated Precision

claims.claim: From a single human demonstration with demonstrator-annotated precision boundaries (spheres around key waypoints), a robot can safely self-augment by generating diverse, collision-free trajectories within these boundaries and reconnecting to the original demonstration, achieving substantially higher success rates than policies trained solely on human-collected demonstrations, while requiring only one human teaching session and one environment reset
claims.direction: favors a single annotated demonstration plus safe autonomous trajectory self-augmentation over collecting many human demonstrations or unconstrained autonomous exploration, for clearance-limited/precision tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation tasks (e.g. peg-in-hole-style clearance-limited tasks)

title: FutureVLA: Joint Visuomotor Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Naive joint visuomotor prediction methods become 'visually dominated': explicit future-prediction methods divert capacity to task-irrelevant visual details, while implicit sparse-frame-pair methods disrupt temporal continuity, entangling static scene context with dynamic action intent; FutureVLA instead structurally decouples visual-state preservation from temporal action modeling (via a Joint Visuomotor Gating mechanism), letting the motor stream focus on continuous physical dynamics while explicitly querying visual tokens for environmental constraints, and consistently improves VLA frameworks
claims.direction: favors explicitly decoupling visual-state representation from action/dynamics modeling within a joint visuomotor auxiliary-prediction objective, rather than entangling them, to avoid the 'visually dominated' failure mode of naive future-prediction auxiliary losses
claims.conditions: pretraining on heterogeneous manipulation datasets; a post-training latent-alignment strategy lets downstream VLA models use these priors without modifying their inference architecture (no added inference cost)

title: Pixel2Catch: Multi-Agent Sim-to-Real Transfer for Agile Manipulation With a Single RGB Camera

claims.claim: Recognizing object motion using pixel-level visual cues from consecutive RGB frames (rather than explicitly estimating 3D object position) is sufficient to reason about a thrown object's motion for a timely catching policy, successfully transferred from simulation to the real world
claims.direction: supports that pixel-level RGB motion cues can substitute for explicit 3D position estimation in at least some dynamic manipulation tasks, avoiding the need for a depth pipeline
claims.conditions: real-world sim-to-real transfer; dynamic catching task (not static pick-and-place), high-DoF arm+multi-fingered-hand system with heterogeneous multi-agent RL

title: RoboPocket: Improve Robot Policies Instantly with Your Phone

claims.claim: A portable system enabling robot-free policy iteration using a consumer smartphone -- visualizing the frozen policy's predicted trajectory via AR 'Visual Foresight' so operators can proactively target the policy's weak regions without needing physical robot access, combined with an asynchronous online-finetuning pipeline -- doubles data efficiency compared to offline scaling strategies and boosts sample efficiency by up to 2x in distributed settings with only a small number of interactive corrections per person
claims.direction: favors phone-based, policy-aware (AR-visualized) targeted data collection over blind open-loop handheld data collection or physical-robot-only DAgger, for maximizing data efficiency in scaling imitation learning
claims.conditions: consumer smartphone hardware; asynchronous online fine-tuning closes the loop in minutes

title: AnchorRefine: Synergy-Manipulation Based on Trajectory Anchor and Residual Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Generating actions within a single unified space forces macro-level transport and micro-level refinement to be optimized under the same objective, letting large motions dominate learning and suppress small but failure-critical corrective signals; factorizing VLA action modeling into a coarse trajectory-anchor planner plus a residual refinement module (with a decision-aware gripper-refinement mechanism) consistently improves both regression-based and diffusion-based VLA backbones, yielding gains of up to 7.8% in simulation success rate and 18% in real-world success rate
claims.direction: favors hierarchically factorizing action prediction into coarse trajectory anchors plus local residual refinement (rather than a single unified action-prediction space) for precision-critical manipulation, and shows this benefit generalizes across both regression and diffusion action-head types
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN (sim) and real-robot tasks; applicable as an addition to either regression-based or diffusion-based VLA backbones

title: Learning robust and generalizable bimanual skills: a spatiotemporal causal hierarchical diffusion framework with attention anti-interference

claims.claim: Existing diffusion-based bimanual policies struggle to simultaneously capture long-horizon temporal dependencies and fine spatial precision while remaining sensitive to spurious correlations and domain shifts; a framework that factorizes denoising into temporal/spatial branches, learns causal visual representations that minimize mutual information with confounding environmental factors (producing invariant features), models observation uncertainty with confidence-aware denoising, and adds attention anti-interference regularization against distractions, consistently outperforms existing diffusion-based and imitation-learning baselines under both clean and domain-randomized settings with minimal computational overhead
claims.direction: favors explicitly minimizing mutual information with confounding/environmental factors (causal representation learning) plus distraction-penalizing attention regularization over standard diffusion policies, specifically to address causal confusion and domain-shift robustness
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmark, bimanual manipulation; qualitative comparative claim ('consistently outperforms'), no specific numbers given in abstract

title: ArmnetBench v0.1: Parallel Real-World Evaluation of Manipulation Policies on a Low-Cost Arm Farm

claims.claim: A real-world benchmark run on a fleet of low-cost SO-101 robot cells compares 7 manipulation policies across 12 tasks (single-arm and bimanual configurations), with each policy trained or fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; the released dataset contains 2,518 policy rollouts plus 600 reference demonstrations, all human-scored with a three-way label (successful, suboptimal, failure)
claims.direction: provides a direct, shared-budget real-world leaderboard comparing multiple policy architectures under our exact hardware platform (SO-101) and our exact demonstration-count regime (50/task), rather than any single directional claim
claims.conditions: low-cost SO-101 arm farm; 50 demonstrations per task, matching our own target budget exactly

claims.claim: Quality-labeled trajectories (successful/suboptimal/failure) from real policy rollouts are released to support downstream learning including reward models, predictive world models, and policies trained on mixed-quality data
claims.direction: suggests mixed-quality (including suboptimal/failure) rollout data, not just clean demonstrations, can be leveraged for downstream policy or world-model training on this exact platform
claims.conditions: same SO-101 arm-farm benchmark

why_deep_read: This benchmark runs on our exact robot (SO-101) with our exact per-task demonstration budget (50 demos), comparing 7 policies across 12 tasks with human-scored quality labels -- it is very likely the single most directly transferable data point in the entire batch for choosing among action-head/policy architectures on our specific hardware, and should be read in full for the leaderboard results and per-policy breakdown.

title: Think Only When Needed: Prompt-Authority Control for Selective Slow-Path Intervention in Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: In a matched audit, appending raw retrieved text to a frozen VLA's executed prompt catastrophically collapses mean success from 92.47% to 3.00%, and this holds for both semantically meaningful and length-matched meaningless appends -- identifying 'prompt-form collapse', where changing the instruction's form (not adding useful semantics) dominates execution; a prompt-authority interface (TOWN-VLA) that only authorizes a canonical compact instruction under a fixed compatibility rule (otherwise restoring the original prompt exactly) raises success from 69.5% to 73.1% on a large LIBERO-Plus evaluation (10,030 episodes/method) and from 52.7% to 78.7% on a physical PiPER arm with a frozen pi0.5 checkpoint (p=3.16e-6, 150 trials/method)
claims.direction: strongly cautions against naively modifying/augmenting the language prompt fed to a frozen language-conditioned policy (e.g. via retrieval augmentation) -- even semantically-neutral changes to instruction form can destroy performance -- and shows that gating any prompt modification through a strict compatibility/authority check preserves and can improve real-robot success
claims.conditions: large-scale sim evaluation (LIBERO-Plus, 10,030 episodes/method) plus real-robot validation on a physical PiPER arm with a frozen pi0.5 checkpoint

title: Manipulation as in Simulation: Enabling Accurate Geometry Perception in Robots

claims.claim: Consumer depth cameras are limited in accuracy and susceptible to noise, which normally makes depth-based manipulation policies hard to transfer sim-to-real; Camera Depth Models (CDMs), a plugin trained on simulation-generated paired noisy/clean depth data that models a real depth camera's specific noise pattern, denoise raw RGB+depth input to near-simulation-level accurate metric depth, and a policy trained purely on clean simulated depth (no real-world fine-tuning, no synthetic noise added) generalizes seamlessly to real robots on two challenging long-horizon tasks involving articulated, reflective, and slender objects with little to no performance degradation
claims.direction: favors denoising/correcting raw depth-camera signal toward simulation-level accuracy (via a learned camera-specific noise model) over training directly on noisy raw depth or relying on RGB alone, enabling policies trained purely in simulation with clean depth to transfer to real hardware
claims.conditions: real robots, long-horizon tasks with articulated/reflective/slender objects (some of the hardest cases for depth sensing); directly relevant since our setup includes a RealSense RGB+depth camera

title: Interface Matters: Comparing First and Third-Person Perspective Interfaces for Bi-Manual Robot Behavioural Cloning

claims.claim: Comparing first-person and third-person perspective teleoperation interfaces for a dexterous bimanual shoe-lacing task revealed significant differences in demonstration execution time and consistency, with the first-person interface changing demonstration quality in ways that subsequently affect behavior-cloning learning performance
claims.direction: supports that teleoperation interface/viewpoint design choice materially affects demonstration quality (execution time, consistency) and thus downstream imitation-learning performance, independent of the amount of data collected
claims.conditions: real robot, dexterous bimanual deformable-object task (shoe-lacing); different task from our simple pick-and-place, but the interface-quality principle is general

title: Analyzing Key Objectives in Human-to-Robot Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Through real-world comparative ablation experiments on a comprehensive retargeting-objective formulation, the significance of individual factors (e.g. finger/joint alignment terms) in human-to-robot kinematic retargeting for teleoperation is evaluated, providing evidence on which retargeting objectives matter most for real-world teleoperated manipulation quality
claims.direction: informs which retargeting-objective components are most important for producing usable, physically-consistent demonstrations from human teleoperation, relevant to teleop data-collection quality
claims.conditions: real-world teleoperated dexterous manipulation tasks and kinematic posture retargeting; dexterous multi-fingered hand context, not directly our simple gripper leader/follower setup

title: PiL-World: A Chunk-Wise World Model for VLA Policy-in-the-Loop Evaluation

claims.claim: A chunk-wise world model that alternates between VLA inference and world-model prediction (conditioning video generation on action-derived visual control and latent task-execution history, and learning from both successful and failed execution trajectories) enables closed-loop VLA evaluation without real robot execution at every step, reducing the error between real-world-measured and world-model-estimated VLA success rates from 63.2% to 12.0%
claims.direction: favors chunk-wise, closed-loop-consistent world models (that also learn from failure trajectories) over open-loop world models for accurately estimating a VLA policy's real-world success rate without physical execution
claims.conditions: three real dual-arm manipulation tasks; primarily an evaluation/offline-testing tool rather than a training-time auxiliary objective

title: DeltaWAM: Delta World Action Models for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Existing world-action models predict dense future frames during training, repeatedly re-modeling largely unchanged content and coupling action-conditioned dynamics to nuisance appearance variations, and are bottlenecked at inference by processing each complete observation through a heavy video expert; jointly predicting sparse visual 'deltas' plus actions (with a Streaming Delta Memory that updates cached anchor context using compact observed deltas instead of reprocessing full frames) improves average success on RoboTwin over Fast-WAM from 81.3% to 85.4% in the clean setting and from 75.8% to 83.9% under visual randomization
claims.direction: favors sparse delta-based (rather than dense full-frame) visual prediction in world-action models, both for accuracy (especially under visual randomization/distribution shift) and for efficiency
claims.conditions: RoboTwin sim benchmark, clean and visually-randomized settings; also validated with real-world evaluations showing highest overall success and normalized progress among evaluated policies

claims.claim: The three DeltaWAM architecture variants reduce training FLOPs by 17.78-23.77%, while Streaming Delta Memory reduces one-step inference latency and FLOPs by 36.57% and 31.55% respectively, compared to dense-frame world-action-model baselines
claims.direction: favors delta/sparse-update world-model designs for substantially reducing both training and inference compute cost versus dense-frame prediction
claims.conditions: same RoboTwin benchmark and real-world evaluation

title: Guided Action Flow: Q-Guided Inference for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Guided Action Flow (QGF) keeps a pretrained SmolVLA policy completely frozen and steers its reverse-time action-flow sampling at inference time using gradients from a task-specific action-chunk critic (a visual Transformer critic/value model trained via offline Implicit Q-Learning on only 100 real-robot rollouts, conditioning on robot state, frozen dual-camera SmolVLA visual tokens, and the policy's normalized 50-step action chunk); on a real-robot water-bottle placement task, QGF (with beta=2) increases success from 19/40 (47.5%) to 34/40 (85.0%) episodes and reduces timeouts from 13 to 3, without any policy fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors inference-time, critic-guided steering of a frozen flow-matching VLA's action sampling (learned from a small number of real rollouts) over either frozen unguided rollout or full policy fine-tuning, for improving task success without disturbing the base model's behavior
claims.conditions: real robot, water-bottle placement task; base policy is SmolVLA (our own current base model), critic trained on only 100 real-robot rollouts

claims.claim: With a yellow tape measure added as a visual distractor, QGF completes 6/12 episodes successfully, compared with 0/11 for the frozen (unguided) SmolVLA policy
claims.direction: shows that critic-guided inference-time steering substantially improves robustness to visual distractors compared to the frozen base policy alone
claims.conditions: same real-robot setup with an added visual distractor object

why_deep_read: This paper directly uses SmolVLA -- our exact current base model -- and demonstrates both a large success-rate improvement (47.5% to 85.0%) and, critically, a distractor-robustness improvement (0/11 to 6/12) using only 100 real-robot rollouts and no fine-tuning of the frozen base policy. This is about as close a match to our own setup and failure modes (distractor/appearance robustness) as exists in the batch, and is highly actionable at our compute budget since it requires no VLA retraining.

title: Track4Action: Distilling World-Centric 3D Tracker into Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Distilling realized 3D scene-transition supervision (geometry, motion, visibility, camera change over the demonstration clip) from a frozen world-centric 3D tracker into a current-observation VLA policy -- via learnable track queries that align a pooled tracker feature with current VLA hidden states, with the tracker feature only used as a training-time alignment target (neither clip nor tracker used at deployment) -- reaches 82.3% on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus (+7.6 points over an alignment-free variant, +3.0 over LaMP), 80.44%/81.48% on clean/randomized RoboTwin 2.0, and 67.5% average success across four physical bimanual tasks (+25.0 points over the alignment-free variant)
claims.direction: favors using 3D-tracker-derived transition supervision as a training-time-only auxiliary alignment signal (no extra deployment-time compute or hardware) over training without this 3D-aware supervision, for both simulation and real-world generalization
claims.conditions: zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0 (clean and randomized splits), and four physical bimanual tasks; supervision-only technique adds zero inference-time cost or hardware

title: RAIL: Reachability-Aided Imitation Learning for Safe Policy Execution

claims.claim: Enforcing hard safety constraints (via a reachability-based safety filter) on imitation learning policies reveals that some of the highest-performing IL policies are only high-performing because they frequently violate safety constraints, and lose significant performance once hard constraints are enforced; conversely, hard constraints on lower-performing policies can occasionally increase their ability to perform tasks safely, and the method can operate in real time on real hardware
claims.direction: cautions that apparent task-success gains in IL policies may partly stem from constraint-violating (unsafe) behavior, and that adding a hard-constraint safety filter at execution time can change the effective ranking of policies rather than being a free/neutral addition
claims.conditions: state-of-the-art IL policies evaluated on mobile robot and manipulation tasks; real-time hardware evaluation confirmed

title: DemoHLM: From One Demonstration to Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

claims.claim: Starting from just a single simulation demonstration, a data-generation and imitation-learning pipeline synthesizes diverse synthetic training data, and experiments show a positive correlation between the amount of generated synthetic data and policy performance, with real-world experiments on a Unitree G1 robot confirming sim-to-real transfer and robustness to spatial variations
claims.direction: supports that a single demonstration plus scalable synthetic data generation can substitute for large-scale real-world data collection, with performance scaling with synthetic data volume
claims.conditions: humanoid loco-manipulation (different embodiment/task from our fixed-base arm pick-and-place), real-world validation on Unitree G1 with RGB-D camera

title: ReGen: Generative Robot Simulation via Inverse Design

claims.claim: Given a robot's observed behavior (motion trajectory or objective) and a textual description, ReGen uses LLMs to infer plausible causal scenarios/environments and synthesize a structured, executable simulation program, generating more diverse and complex simulated environments than existing simulations with high success rates, including controllable counterfactual scenario generation for corner cases
claims.direction: favors LLM-driven inverse-design generation of diverse simulated scenarios (including corner cases) for simulation/data augmentation, over manually authored simulation environments
claims.conditions: demonstrated in autonomous driving and robot manipulation tasks; qualitative comparative claims, no specific numbers given

title: Acting While Understanding: Asynchronous Semantic-Action Decoupling for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Separating semantic understanding from action generation along the internal semantic-action interface of an existing VLA (a low-frequency understanding module asynchronously updates reusable semantic conditions, while a high-frequency action module continuously outputs control actions without repeatedly invoking the full model), combined with historical action conditioning and time-misalignment training to handle stale semantics, achieves up to 35.6 Hz server-side action-module inference throughput and provides a low-intrusion path to high-frequency closed-loop control without running full VLA inference at control rate
claims.direction: favors decoupling slow semantic understanding from fast action generation inside an existing VLA (with explicit training for stale-semantics robustness) over running full-model inference at every control step, for both latency reduction and smoother async closed-loop control
claims.conditions: LIBERO with pi0.5 and UniVLA (sim), plus real-robot deployment using UniVLA; requires no redesign of the vision-language backbone or external planner

why_deep_read: This paper directly targets our exact stated failure (jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries under async inference, ~2s latency) with a specific architectural fix -- semantic/action decoupling plus explicit training for stale-semantics robustness -- validated on both sim and real robot; worth reading in full for the historical-action-conditioning and time-misalignment-training recipe, which could be retrofitted onto a small VLA like ours.

title: E-TTS: A New Embodied Test-Time Scaling Framework for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A modular, plug-and-play test-time scaling framework that performs reasoning-action joint sampling and scoring with vision-language verifiers, using a history buffer for historical context and closed-loop iterative refinement (rather than open-loop test-time scaling), consistently improves performance across 4 benchmarks, 6 environments, 3 embodiments, and 4 base VLA models without additional expert data collection or retraining, achieving up to a 33.14% increase in simulation and 26.62% in real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors closed-loop, history-aware test-time reasoning-and-action scaling (with iterative feedback-driven refinement) over open-loop test-time scaling or relying solely on current observations, as a training-free way to improve an existing VLA's performance
claims.conditions: broad evaluation across 4 benchmarks, 6 environments, 3 embodiments, 4 base VLA models; requires no additional training data or retraining of the base model

title: Attention-Enhanced Multimodal Robotic Arm Lift Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Comparing four lightweight attention mechanisms (channel, spatial, hybrid, multi-branch) embedded in the visual network of a multimodal (proprioception+vision) RL policy for a UR5 lift task, Global Attention Mechanism (GAM) and Split-Attention Networks (ResNest) performed best, while Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) stably outperformed a plain CNN baseline at lower computational cost
claims.direction: provides a comparative ranking of lightweight visual attention mechanisms for improving grasping stability/training efficiency, useful when choosing how to augment a vision encoder's feature representation cheaply
claims.conditions: Isaac Sim/IsaacLab simulation, UR5 arm with Robotiq 85 gripper, RL (not imitation learning) framework

title: VLA-Corrector: Lightweight Detect-and-Correct Inference for Adaptive Action Horizon

claims.claim: Standard action-chunk execution under a fixed horizon follows a 'predict-then-blindly-execute' open-loop paradigm where small local perturbations can rapidly amplify within the open-loop blind spot; a lightweight Latent-space Vision Monitor that continuously compares predicted vs actual visual feature evolution can detect persistent deviation and trigger truncation of the remaining stale chunk plus corrective replanning (Online Gradient Guidance), inducing an event-triggered adaptive action horizon that preserves long-horizon efficiency when reliable and shortens the horizon reactively when execution drifts -- all without modifying or retraining the backbone VLA policy
claims.direction: favors event-triggered adaptive action-chunk horizons (via lightweight external monitoring and correction) over static fixed-horizon chunking, to interrupt compounding errors in contact-rich long-horizon tasks while retaining most of chunking's efficiency benefit
claims.conditions: integrates into different VLA models without backbone retraining; framed generically for action-chunked VLA policies in contact-rich manipulation

title: RiEMann: Near Real-Time SE(3)-Equivariant Robot Manipulation without Point Cloud Segmentation

claims.claim: RiEMann, an SE(3)-equivariant imitation learning framework operating directly on scene point clouds (predicting target object poses without any object segmentation), learns a manipulation task from scratch with only 5 to 10 demonstrations
claims.direction: favors building SE(3) equivariance directly into a point-cloud-based policy architecture as a way to drastically cut required demonstration count (5-10, well below typical requirements)
claims.conditions: 6-DOF robot manipulation, 5 categories of tasks with 25 variants, simulation and real-world

claims.claim: RiEMann generalizes to unseen SE(3) transformations and object instances, resists visual interference of distracting objects, and follows near real-time pose changes of the target object; it outperforms baselines in task success rate and reduces SE(3) geodesic pose error by 68.6%, at 5.4 FPS inference
claims.direction: supports that equivariant, segmentation-free point-cloud policies are robust to distractors and to viewpoint/pose changes, addressing generalization concerns beyond training conditions
claims.conditions: same real+sim experiments; inference speed (5.4 FPS) reported explicitly

title: Variable-speed teaching-playback as real-world data augmentation for imitation learning

claims.claim: Applying teaching-playback of existing human demonstrations at variable speeds (rather than simulation-based augmentation or simple downsampling) increases both the quantity and quality of captured environmental reactions, and improves success rate and accuracy for pick-and-place and wiping tasks trained from only two human demonstrations at fixed speed
claims.direction: favors real-world variable-speed replay of existing demonstrations as a data augmentation technique (preserving real-world dynamics/force information) over simulation-based augmentation, particularly for force-control-relevant tasks
claims.conditions: bilateral (position-force) control-based imitation learning; real-world experiments; only 2 base human demonstrations per task

title: Sim-to-Real Dynamic Object Manipulation on Conveyor Systems via Optimization Path Shaping

claims.claim: An appearance-noise-annealing strategy that shapes the policy optimization path to prioritize geometry information over appearance (Geometry-Enhanced Model) allows a policy trained purely on simulated demonstrations to generalize across environment backgrounds, robot embodiments, motion dynamics, and object geometries; deployed on a real canteen tableware-collection task without any test-scene data, it achieves over 97% success across more than 10,000 operations
claims.direction: favors prioritizing geometric over appearance information during sim-trained policy optimization (via annealed appearance noise) for closing the sim-to-real appearance gap, over training with the raw simulated appearance
claims.conditions: real-world deployment (canteen), no real target-scene data used; dynamic object manipulation on a conveyor system

title: Advances on Affordable Hardware Platforms for Human Demonstration Acquisition in Agricultural Applications

claims.claim: Extending a low-cost hand-held UMI-style gripper interface with automatic extraction of individual samples from continuous demonstrations (using task-event segmentation) and improved trajectory reliability (via EKF fusion of onboard inertial measurements with external visual marker localization) reduces idle time and cognitive load during demonstration collection and outperforms the default UMI pipeline on a fruit-harvesting task
claims.direction: favors automatic event-based demonstration segmentation plus sensor-fused trajectory estimation over the default handheld-gripper data-collection pipeline, for improving both collection efficiency and downstream trajectory sample quality
claims.conditions: low-cost handheld gripper interface (UMI), agricultural fruit-harvesting task; real-world evaluation

title: Real-is-Sim: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap with a Dynamic Digital Twin

claims.claim: A dynamic digital twin (Embodied Gaussian simulator synchronized with the real world at 60Hz) that mediates between a behavior-cloning policy and the real robot -- so policies always act on the simulated robot state, continuously corrected with real-world measurements -- allows real-world training data to be augmented with virtual rollouts, and shows virtual evaluations are consistent with real-world results on a long-horizon manipulation task (PushT)
claims.direction: favors a continuously-synchronized digital-twin mediation layer (rather than a one-shot sim-to-real transfer or pure real-world training) for augmenting real data with virtual rollouts and for safely pre-validating policies
claims.conditions: long-horizon manipulation task (PushT); compares policies trained on different state representations (object poses vs rendered images from static and robot-mounted/wrist cameras)

title: XR-1: Towards Versatile Vision-Language-Action Models via Learning Unified Vision-Motion Representations

claims.claim: Encoding visual dynamics and robotic motion jointly into a discrete latent representation (Unified Vision-Motion Codes, learned via a dual-branch VQ-VAE) as an intermediate representation between observations and actions, then using a three-stage training paradigm (self-supervised UVMC learning, UVMC-guided cross-embodiment pretraining, task-specific post-training), consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines including pi0.5, pi0, RDT, UniVLA, and GR00T-N1.5 across more than 14,000 real-world rollouts spanning 6 different robot embodiments and 120+ manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors a unified discrete vision-motion latent code (bridging heterogeneous embodiments/data sources) as an intermediate representation over directly encoding visual dynamics or actions separately, for cross-embodiment generalist policy learning
claims.conditions: large-scale real-world evaluation (14,000+ rollouts, 6 embodiments, 120+ tasks)

claims.claim: XR-1 demonstrates strong generalization to novel objects, background variations, distractors, and illumination changes
claims.direction: supports that this unified vision-motion latent representation improves robustness specifically to the kinds of shifts we care about (lighting, background, distractors, novel objects)
claims.conditions: same large-scale real-world evaluation

why_deep_read: This paper reports one of the largest real-world evaluations in the batch (14,000+ rollouts, 6 embodiments) and explicitly tests generalization to novel objects, background variation, distractors, and illumination changes -- exactly our stated failure modes -- against many strong baselines (pi0, pi0.5, RDT, UniVLA, GR00T); worth reading in full for the specific illumination/object/distractor breakdown numbers.

title: Hyper-DP3: Frequency-Aware Right-Sizing of 3D Diffusion Policies for Visuomotor Control

claims.claim: Robot action trajectories are highly smooth, with most energy concentrated in a few low-frequency DCT modes; the authors show the optimal denoiser's error is bounded by the low-frequency subspace dimension and residual high-frequency energy, implying denoising error saturates after very few reverse steps and that action denoising needs a much simpler model than image generation. Motivated by this, Hyper-DP3 (HDP3), a 'pocket-scale' 3D diffusion policy with a lightweight Diffusion Mixer decoder supporting two-step DDIM inference, achieves SOTA performance across RoboTwin2.0, Adroit, MetaWorld, and real-world tasks using fewer than 1% of the parameters of prior 3D diffusion-based policies
claims.direction: favors radically smaller, frequency-theory-motivated diffusion action decoders (two-step inference, <1% of prior parameter counts) over standard heavier image-generation-style diffusion decoders, since action trajectories are inherently low-frequency/smooth and do not require large denoising capacity
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2.0, Adroit, MetaWorld (sim) and real-world tasks; substantially lower inference latency than prior 3D diffusion policies

why_deep_read: This directly addresses our combined Q12 (small model for 8GB GPU) and Q10 (low latency) needs with both a theoretical argument (frequency-domain analysis of action trajectories) and an extreme empirical result (<1% of prior parameter count, two-step inference, still SOTA on real-world tasks) -- one of the most directly actionable papers in the batch for our compute-constrained diffusion/3D-policy design choice.

title: Language-Driven Multi-Task Manipulation With Action-Mask-Enhanced Multimodal Learning

claims.claim: An explicit action-mask policy that jointly predicts actions and their validity enables real-time sub-task termination detection and robust switching across multiple sub-tasks without additional inference overhead, within an ACT-based low-level policy enhanced by temperature-scaled spatial attention and bidirectional cross-attention for language-vision fusion
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit, jointly-predicted action-validity/termination signal to an ACT-style chunked policy (at no extra inference cost) for detecting sub-task boundaries and switching smoothly, over relying on a fixed chunk/task schedule
claims.conditions: weighing and multi-object manipulation tasks; hierarchical VLM+LLM high-level planner plus ACT-based low-level policy; deployed on a distinct dual-arm platform in a new scenario to validate transferability

title: The N2D Haptic Glove: A Multi-Finger Glove for 2D Directional Force Feedback for Contact Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A directional (planar, 2-axis) fingertip force-feedback haptic glove significantly reduces contact-force error, improves trial-to-trial consistency, and enhances overall user experience during teleoperated contact-rich manipulation, compared to visual-only and single-axis haptic feedback baselines
claims.direction: favors richer (directional/planar) haptic feedback during teleoperation over visual-only or single-axis force feedback, for producing higher-quality (more consistent, lower-error) demonstrations in contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: user study with haptic teleoperation of a robotic arm/hand; requires specialized haptic-glove hardware we do not have

title: Fast Enough to Act: Spatio-Temporal Visual Token Merging for Low-Latency Robotic VLMs and VLAs

claims.claim: ST-Merge, a plug-and-play, training-free framework that fuses redundant visual tokens during the visual encoding phase (using explicit 3D spatiotemporal coordinates and a post-merge positional correction to preserve spatial awareness), achieves an 8.3x inference speedup on the pi0.5 VLA policy at 1024x1024 resolution while matching the baseline success rate at that resolution (with only a small accuracy drop at lower resolutions), and a 2x speedup with ~1% precision loss on Qwen2.5-VL for video QA
claims.direction: favors training-free visual token merging (exploiting spatiotemporal redundancy across frames) as a way to cut VLA inference latency substantially without retraining or modifying the underlying policy weights
claims.conditions: pi0.5 VLA policy and Qwen2.5-VL VLM; training-free, plug-and-play, no fine-tuning required

title: PhysBrain 1.0 Technical Report

claims.claim: Converting large-scale human egocentric video into structured physical-commonsense question-answer supervision (extracting scene elements, spatial dynamics, action execution, depth-aware relations) to pretrain a VLM, then transferring these physical priors to VLA policies via a capability-preserving, language-sensitive adaptation, achieves SOTA results across multimodal QA and embodied control benchmarks (ERQA, PhysBench, SimplerEnv-WidowX, LIBERO, RoboCasa), with especially strong out-of-domain performance on SimplerEnv
claims.direction: favors pretraining on human-egocentric-video-derived physical commonsense (as an auxiliary knowledge source distinct from robot action data) transferred via a capability-preserving adaptation, over training a VLA purely on robot trajectory data
claims.conditions: multiple multimodal QA and embodied control benchmarks (sim); qualitative SOTA claims, no specific numeric deltas given in abstract

title: Probabilistic Recurrent Intention Switching Model

claims.claim: A lightweight recurrent inverse-RL model (PRISM) that maps observation history to a per-step intention distribution (rather than assuming a single stationary reward or memoryless Markov-chain intention transitions) achieves the highest held-out log-likelihood while recovering nameable, temporally coherent intentions from unlabeled demonstrations on BridgeData V2 -- the first large-scale robotic application of multi-intention IRL
claims.direction: provides empirical evidence that human robotic manipulation demonstrations (BridgeData V2) contain discrete, temporally-structured multi-intention/goal-switching behavior rather than a single consistent policy, supporting the case for action-head designs (e.g. CVAE, discrete/multimodal heads) that can capture multimodality in human demonstrations rather than assuming unimodal behavior
claims.conditions: non-Markovian gridworld, mouse labyrinth, and BridgeData V2 real robotic manipulation demonstrations; IRL framework, not a direct action-head comparison

title: EgoWAM: World Action Models Beyond Pixels with In-the-Wild Egocentric Human Data

claims.claim: In a controlled human-robot co-training framework that fixes the policy backbone, action head, and data mixture while varying only the world-model prediction target, Pixel-based future prediction transfers weakly from egocentric human data, whereas DINO-feature and 3D-motion-flow targets yield substantial gains: DINO improves out-of-distribution object and scene generalization by up to 4x, and 3D flow improves in-domain performance by 20-30%, across three real-world bimanual tasks
claims.direction: favors abstracted/invariant world-prediction targets (DINO features or 3D motion flow) over raw pixel prediction as the auxiliary world-model objective for human-to-robot co-training, with DINO specifically best for OOD generalization and 3D flow best for in-domain performance
claims.conditions: controlled ablation (architecture and data mixture held fixed, only world-prediction target varied); real-world bimanual manipulation tasks; egocentric in-the-wild human co-training data

claims.claim: World-Action-Model co-training scales more effectively with in-the-wild egocentric human data than standard behavior cloning
claims.direction: favors WAM-style co-training (with an appropriately abstracted world-prediction target) over plain behavior cloning when leveraging human video as a scalable data source
claims.conditions: same real-world bimanual tasks

why_deep_read: This is a rare controlled ablation that isolates the world-prediction TARGET (pixel vs. DINO vs. 3D flow) while holding everything else fixed -- exactly the kind of clean evidence needed to decide what auxiliary/world-model representation to use for Q09, with a clear quantified split between what helps OOD generalization (DINO, our key concern) vs. in-domain performance (3D flow).

title: Expert-Play Contouring Control: Faster-than-Demonstration Planning from Slow Expert and Fast Play

claims.claim: Combining slow expert demonstrations (used to train a latent trajectory generator reparameterized into a time-independent progress contour) with separate fast, non-expert 'play' data (used to train a world model of fast-action outcomes) enables faster-than-demonstration execution; EPCC achieves 2.0x the throughput of an imitation-learning baseline on average across three visuomotor tasks, including 2.2x on a task with interaction-sensitive object dynamics
claims.direction: favors combining a small set of slow expert demonstrations (for task intent) with cheaper fast non-expert play data (for dynamics coverage at higher speed) over training purely on expert-demonstration timing, when faster execution is desired
claims.conditions: three visuomotor manipulation tasks; gains concentrate specifically where faster execution changes robot-object dynamics

title: DexArt: Benchmarking Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation with Articulated Objects

claims.claim: Using Reinforcement Learning with 3D point-cloud representation learning provides new insights into how 3D representation learning affects decision-making and generalization to unseen articulated objects in dexterous manipulation, compared to standard 2D approaches
claims.direction: supports 3D point-cloud representations as beneficial for generalization to novel articulated object instances, in an RL (not imitation-learning) setting
claims.conditions: dexterous multi-finger hand, simulated benchmark (DexArt); RL framework, high-DoF hand and object articulation

title: DexMimicGen: Automated Data Generation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation via Imitation Learning

claims.claim: An automated data-generation system synthesizes 21,000 demonstration trajectories from just 60 human source demonstrations for bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks (a ~350x amplification), and studies the effect of several data-generation and policy-learning decisions on agent performance; a real-to-sim-to-real pipeline successfully deploys the resulting policies on a real-world humanoid can-sorting task
claims.direction: favors automated simulation-based amplification of a small human demonstration seed set (rather than collecting proportionally more real demonstrations) for scaling bimanual dexterous manipulation data
claims.conditions: bimanual dexterous manipulation simulation environments; real-world validation via real-to-sim-to-real pipeline on a humanoid platform

title: DART: Dexterous Augmented Reality Teleoperation Platform for Large-Scale Robot Data Collection in Simulation

claims.claim: A cloud-based, AR-simulation teleoperation platform (avoiding physical robot hardware, setup, and reset fatigue) enables higher data-collection throughput and lower physical fatigue than real-world teleoperation, according to a user study
claims.direction: favors cloud/AR-simulation-based teleoperation over real-world teleoperation for crowdsourced, scalable data collection
claims.conditions: user study comparing DART to real-world teleoperation; policies trained on DART-collected data validated to transfer to reality

claims.claim: Policies trained using DART-collected datasets are robust to unseen visual disturbances after transferring to the real robot
claims.direction: supports that simulation/AR-collected demonstrations can produce policies robust to visual disturbances not seen during (simulated) data collection
claims.conditions: real-world transfer evaluation after training entirely on DART-collected (simulated) data

title: Viewpoint-Agnostic Manipulation Policies with Strategic Vantage Selection

claims.claim: Vision-based manipulation policies trained from a single viewpoint degrade when the camera view changes at deployment, and naively aggregating demonstrations from many random viewpoints destabilizes learning (excessive visual diversity acts as noise); Vantage instead formulates camera placement as an information-gain optimization problem and fine-tunes any pre-trained policy on a small, strategically-selected set of camera poses, increasing task success rate under viewpoint shift by 25% for diffusion policies (with only a handful of fine-tuning steps) compared to fixed, grid, or random viewpoint data-selection strategies
claims.direction: favors strategically selecting a small number of information-maximizing camera viewpoints for lightweight fine-tuning over either a single fixed camera or brute-force random/grid multi-view data collection, for viewpoint-robust deployment
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, multiple policy families; requires only a handful of additional fine-tuning steps on an already-trained policy, not full retraining

why_deep_read: This is one of the most directly actionable papers for our exact stated failure mode (policy breaks when the camera is slightly moved): it offers a lightweight fine-tuning recipe (not full retraining) that specifically targets viewpoint robustness with a quantified 25% gain, and explicitly warns that naive random multi-view data collection can backfire -- an important nuance for how we might try to fix camera-shift robustness.

title: Using Non-Expert Data to Robustify Imitation Learning via Offline Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Standard offline RL is largely ineffective at leveraging non-expert data (play data, suboptimal demonstrations, partial completions) under the sparse-data-coverage conditions typical of real-world manipulation, but simple algorithmic modifications allow imitation learning augmented by offline RL to broaden the policy distribution's support, significantly increasing the range of initial conditions where learned policies succeed, and to leverage all collected data including partial/suboptimal demonstrations
claims.direction: favors incorporating non-expert/suboptimal/partial demonstration data via a modified offline-RL augmentation (rather than discarding it or relying on imitation learning alone) for improving recovery behavior and generalization to broader initial conditions
claims.conditions: manipulation tasks; specific algorithmic modifications required, standard offline RL alone is not sufficient

title: RoboBERT: An End-to-end Multimodal Robotic Manipulation Model

claims.claim: A two-stage training paradigm -- first freezing most of the vision encoder and training with a single standard instruction phrasing to stabilize policy learning via a CNN-based diffusion policy, then unfreezing all modules and injecting diverse natural-language variants to align varied instructions without destabilizing performance -- achieves new SOTA mean episode lengths (4.52 on CALVIN ABCD-D, 3.79 on ABC-D) using only language-labeled expert demonstrations and a comparatively lightweight architecture, with real-robot trials confirming higher success rates than comparable methods trained on identical data
claims.direction: favors a staged freeze-then-unfreeze vision-encoder training schedule (stabilize policy learning first with a frozen encoder and simple instructions, then unfreeze for language diversity) over training everything jointly from the start, for both language generalization and overall performance with a lightweight architecture
claims.conditions: CALVIN ABCD-D/ABC-D sim benchmarks plus real-robot trials on a 6-DOF manipulator; systematic data augmentation for visual-perturbation robustness also used

title: Bridging Scale Discrepancies in Robotic Control via Language-Based Action Representations

claims.claim: A semantically-grounded linguistic (directional, scale-invariant) action representation -- rather than conventional discretized numeric action tokens sensitive to platform-specific numerical scale -- mitigates distribution shift across robotic platforms/tasks with differing action-command scales and narrows the feature distance between action tokens and standard vocabulary tokens, significantly improving generalization and transferability in multi-task robotic manipulation experiments
claims.direction: favors direction-based, scale-invariant linguistic action representations over raw numeric/discretized action tokens for cross-platform/cross-task pretraining transfer
claims.conditions: multi-task experiments on two benchmarks; qualitative improvement claim ('significantly improves'), no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Grounding Sim-to-Real Generalization in Robotic Manipulation: An Empirical Study with Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: An empirical study of over 10,000 real-world trials examines the primary determinants of Sim-to-Real generalization for generalist VLA policies across four dimensions -- multi-level domain randomization, photorealistic rendering, physics-realistic modeling, and reinforcement-learning updates -- using a standardized evaluation protocol that explicitly accounts for variations in background, lighting, distractors, object types, and spatial features
claims.direction: provides a principled, large-scale empirical grounding (rather than isolated algorithmic proposals) for which sim-to-real techniques actually matter for VLA generalization under exactly the kinds of shift we care about (background, lighting, distractors, object types)
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation protocol released publicly; over 10,000 real-world trials; explicitly designed to be a standardized benchmark for future comparison

why_deep_read: This is a large-scale (10k+ real-world trial), controlled empirical study specifically designed to determine which sim-to-real techniques (domain randomization, photorealistic rendering, physics modeling, RL updates) actually matter for VLA generalization to background/lighting/distractor/object shifts -- precisely our Q05/Q14 concerns -- and is worth reading in full for the ranked findings rather than relying on the abstract's summary alone.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Dexterous Grasping Based on Object Shape Completion Using Transformer

claims.claim: Completing an object's full 3D point-cloud shape from partial depth-camera observations (via a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, trained on mixed synthetic and real datasets) before grasp planning, combined with an improved PPO fine-tuned via fuzzy artificial-bee-colony optimization, achieves 96% real-time grasping accuracy on unseen but similar objects using a Kinect depth camera, outperforming five state-of-the-art grasping baselines
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D shape completion from depth input (rather than acting on raw partial point clouds or RGB alone) as a preprocessing step for grasp planning, for improved accuracy on unseen objects
claims.conditions: real hardware experiments, Kinect depth camera; RL-based (not imitation learning) grasping pipeline

title: Referring-Aware Visuomotor Policy Learning for Closed-Loop Manipulation

claims.claim: A closed-loop framework with coupled global and local diffusion heads -- the global head generates temporally sparse action anchors and locates where a sparse human/planner-provided referring point falls within them, while the local head adaptively interpolates adjacent anchors around that position -- enables real-time trajectory replanning at every execution step in response to dynamic scene changes or out-of-distribution execution errors, achieving higher success rates than baselines on challenging simulated and real-world tasks, while being trained only via targeted perturbations to expert demonstrations (no additional annotated data)
claims.direction: favors a hierarchical global-anchor plus local-interpolation diffusion action head (steerable by sparse referring points) over a single monolithic action-chunk diffusion head, for robustness to OOD execution errors and dynamic re-routing without extra data collection
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks; trained only with perturbation-augmented expert demonstrations, no extra annotation

title: Bayesian Optimization for Sample-Efficient Policy Improvement in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: BOpt-GMM first learns a skill model as a dynamical system (Gaussian Mixture Model) from only a few human demonstrations, then improves it with Bayesian optimization using a small number of autonomous skill executions in a sparse-reward setting, demonstrating sample efficiency on multiple complex manipulation skills in both simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors combining a few-shot imitation-learned skill model with a small amount of autonomous (Bayesian-optimization-guided) self-practice over collecting many additional human demonstrations, for sample-efficient skill refinement
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation experiments; code and pretrained models publicly released

title: HoMeR: Learning In-the-Wild Mobile Manipulation via Hybrid Imitation and Whole-Body Control

claims.claim: Within a reduced end-effector action space (managed by a fast kinematics-based whole-body controller), HoMeR learns to switch between absolute pose predictions for long-range movement and relative pose predictions for fine-grained manipulation, offloading low-level coordination to the controller so learning focuses on task-level decisions; across 3 simulated and 3 real household tasks, HoMeR achieves an overall success rate of 79.17% using just 20 demonstrations per task, outperforming the next-best baseline (without hybrid actions or whole-body control) by 29.17 percentage points on average
claims.direction: favors an explicit hybrid absolute/relative action-mode switch (absolute for coarse/long-range motion, relative/delta for fine-grained precision) over committing to a single fixed action-space convention throughout a task
claims.conditions: real household mobile manipulation tasks (holonomic base + 7-DoF arm), only 20 demonstrations per task; also compatible with VLMs for improved generalization to novel object appearances/layouts/clutter

why_deep_read: This gives a clean, real-world-validated answer to our Q02 action-space decision (hybrid absolute-for-coarse / relative-for-fine switching, rather than one fixed convention) with an unusually low demonstration count (20/task, near our own budget) and a large (29pp) improvement margin -- one of very few papers in the batch offering controlled evidence specifically on the absolute-vs-delta action space question.

title: Flow with the Force Field: Learning 3D Compliant Flow Matching Policies from Force and Demonstration-Guided Simulation Data

claims.claim: Generating force-informed training data in simulation from just a single human demonstration (rather than collecting many real demonstrations), then coupling it with a compliant policy, improves the performance of a visuomotor policy learned from this synthetic data on real-robot contact-rich tasks (non-prehensile block flipping, bimanual object moving), with reliable contact maintenance and adaptation to novel conditions
claims.direction: favors single-demonstration-guided simulation data generation (with force-aware compliance) over large-scale real-world data collection for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot validation; relies on force sensing/compliance modeling not present in our own sensor set, but the single-demo-to-simulation-scaling principle (Q05) is domain-general

title: NoiseGate: Learning Per-Latent Timestep Schedules as Information Gating in World Action Models

claims.claim: In joint video-action World Action Models, collapsing the per-latent-frame denoising timestep onto a single shared scalar imposes an unjustified assumption that every predicted future latent is equally reliable for action generation; treating the per-latent noise schedule as a learnable information-gating policy (via independent per-latent timestep sampling, a lightweight Gating Policy Network, and task-reward optimization) delivers consistent gains on diverse RoboTwin random-scene manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors learned, per-latent-frame-adaptive denoising schedules (rather than a single shared schedule) when using joint video-action world-action models as an auxiliary training signal
claims.conditions: RoboTwin sim benchmark, Mixture-of-Transformers joint video-action backbone; qualitative 'consistent gains' claim, no specific numbers given

title: PEAfowl: Perception-Enhanced Multi-View Vision-Language-Action for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing multi-view features via view-agnostic token concatenation (the common approach) yields limited cross-view spatial representations; predicting per-token depth distributions, performing differentiable 3D lifting, and aggregating local cross-view neighbors instead forms geometrically-grounded, cross-view-aligned representations, improving the strongest baseline by 23.0 percentage points in success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 under domain-randomized settings, with real-robot experiments confirming gains
claims.direction: favors geometry-grounded, depth-lifted cross-view feature aggregation over naive view-agnostic multi-view token concatenation, for robustness under occlusions/viewpoint changes/scene variation
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 domain-randomized benchmark plus real-robot bimanual experiments

claims.claim: Depth-distribution lifting naturally supports training-only depth distillation, where a pretrained depth teacher supervises the depth-distribution head to inject refined geometric priors from noisy/incomplete commodity RGB-D sensing, without adding any inference-time overhead
claims.direction: favors distilling depth-teacher supervision into a depth-prediction head at training time only (versus relying directly on noisy raw depth sensor input at inference) to get 3D-aware benefits without runtime cost
claims.conditions: same setup; commodity RGB-D sensing assumed noisy/incomplete, similar to our RealSense setup

claims.claim: Replacing global language conditioning with a Perceiver-style text-aware readout over frozen CLIP visual features (enabling iterative evidence accumulation) yields finer instruction grounding than injecting language as coarse global conditioning
claims.direction: favors iterative, text-aware readout mechanisms over frozen visual features for language grounding, over standard global-conditioning language injection
claims.conditions: same bimanual VLA setup

title: STEP: Warm-Started Visuomotor Policies with Spatiotemporal Consistency Prediction

claims.claim: A lightweight spatiotemporal consistency prediction mechanism constructs high-quality 'warm-start' actions (distributionally close to the target action and temporally consistent) to reduce the number of diffusion denoising steps needed, combined with a velocity-aware perturbation injection to prevent execution stall; with only 2 diffusion steps, STEP achieves 21.6% and 27.5% higher success rate than BRIDGER and DDIM respectively on RoboMimic and real-world tasks, advancing the Pareto frontier of inference latency vs. success rate
claims.direction: favors warm-starting diffusion action generation from a learned, temporally-consistent initial guess (rather than starting from pure noise or naively reducing sampling steps) to cut denoising steps without sacrificing (and here improving) success rate
claims.conditions: nine simulated benchmarks (RoboMimic etc.) plus two real-world tasks; theoretical analysis shows the prediction induces a locally contractive mapping ensuring convergence

title: ConsisVLA-4D: Advancing Spatiotemporal Consistency in Efficient 3D-Perception and 4D-Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard VLAs mapping 2D observations to actions exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal perception (spatial representations often need extra sensors; visual reasoning is typically limited to future-frame prediction disconnected from the instruction-grounded scene); a unified framework enforcing cross-view object-semantic consistency, cross-object spatial-geometric consistency, and cross-scene spatiotemporal consistency achieves 21.6% and 41.5% performance improvements over OpenVLA on LIBERO and real-world platforms respectively, along with 2.3x and 2.4x inference speedups
claims.direction: favors explicitly enforcing multi-level spatiotemporal consistency (cross-view, cross-object, cross-scene) within an efficient shared framework over standard 2D-observation-to-action mapping, achieving both accuracy AND speed gains simultaneously over a plain VLA baseline (OpenVLA)
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark and real-world platforms; compared directly against OpenVLA

title: Learning Part-Aware Dense 3D Feature Field for Generalizable Articulated Object Manipulation

claims.claim: A dense 3D feature field trained with part-aware contrastive learning from 3D part proposals (Part-Aware 3D Feature Field, PA3FF) consistently outperforms a range of 2D and 3D representations -- including CLIP, DINOv2, and Grounded-SAM -- when used as the visual representation within an imitation learning framework (Part-Aware Diffusion Policy) for generalizable articulated-object manipulation, evaluated on several simulated and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors part-aware, geometry-grounded 3D feature fields over generic 2D pretrained encoders (CLIP, DINOv2) or generic 3D-lifted 2D features (Grounded-SAM) for manipulation tasks requiring functional-part understanding
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world articulated-object manipulation tasks; point-cloud input required

title: CoRe-WAM: Correspondence-Aligned Temporal Residuals for World Action Models

claims.claim: Naively comparing current and past visual features at the same image location mixes different scene content when objects or the camera move; CoRe-WAM instead uses correspondences from a frozen tracking model to transport historical visual features to their current locations before computing signed differences (validity-gated temporal residuals) in a shared pretrained feature space, so the policy can use recent changes alongside current-scene information in a way that is robust to camera/object motion
claims.direction: favors correspondence-aligned (motion-compensated) temporal-difference features over naive same-location frame differencing for incorporating observation history, specifically to remain valid under camera or object movement
claims.conditions: built on the Motus world-action-model backbone with pretrained weights kept fully frozen

claims.claim: With the pretrained backbone frozen, only 1.59 million additional parameters are optimized (a lightweight adapter converting correspondence-aligned differences into residuals), and with a 5,000-update adaptation budget, CoRe-WAM achieves 92.22% clean success across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks (+3.56pp over Motus) and 89.60% on randomized evaluation (+2.58pp); integrating the same temporal interface (TraceDelta) into a different backbone (StarVLA) improves clean success from 58.10% to 67.62%, showing the technique transfers across backbones
claims.direction: favors a tiny, frozen-backbone, parameter-efficient temporal-residual adapter (1.59M params) over full fine-tuning or backbone modification for adding history-awareness, and shows the technique is portable across different base VLA/WAM architectures
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 clean and randomized splits; two different backbones (Motus, StarVLA) tested

why_deep_read: This paper directly addresses observation history (Q07) in a way explicitly designed to remain valid under camera/object motion -- precisely our camera-shift robustness concern -- using an extremely parameter-efficient (1.59M params, frozen backbone) adapter, which is unusually well matched to our tight compute budget (Q12) and shown to transfer across two different backbone architectures.

title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

claims.claim: A VLA pretrained on static and wheeled dual-arm platforms transfers surprisingly well to a humanoid's full action space, and co-training with HuMI (a humanoid analog of the Universal Manipulation Interface) extends the policy to new objects and instructions without additional whole-body teleoperation on those targets
claims.direction: supports that cross-embodiment pretraining (from simpler static/wheeled platforms) can transfer to more complex embodiments, and that UMI-style co-training data can extend generalization without proportionally more teleoperation on new targets
claims.conditions: humanoid loco-manipulation (different embodiment from our fixed-base arm), systematic one-variable-at-a-time empirical study

title: GRALP: A Generative Representation Framework for Action Refinement and Latent Planning in Offline Robotic Control

claims.claim: Using diffusion exclusively as a deterministic action decoder for executing fixed latent skills (while planning and value estimation operate entirely in latent space under conservative constraints, avoiding trajectory-level diffusion sampling at inference) achieves the highest average performance on Navigation, Sequential (Kitchen), and Adroit D4RL domains, and over 94% success on contact-rich RoboSuite manipulation (Lift, Pick-and-Place) with human demonstrations
claims.direction: favors architecturally separating diffusion (as a lightweight deterministic decoder) from planning/value estimation (done in latent space) rather than using diffusion for both generation and search/planning, for offline control combining expressivity with efficient inference
claims.conditions: unified D4RL benchmarks plus RoboSuite manipulation with human demonstrations; offline RL framework

title: Low-Fidelity Visuo-Tactile Pre-Training Improves Vision-Only Manipulation Performance

claims.claim: Pre-training an imitation-learning agent with a low-cost tactile sensor (BeadSight) and then disabling/removing the tactile sensor for downstream vision-only inference improved performance on a USB-cable-plugging task by up to 65% with vision-only inference at deployment; on a longer-horizon drawer pick-and-place task, tactile pre-training -- whether on a similar, dissimilar, or identical task -- consistently improved performance
claims.direction: favors using tactile sensing only as an auxiliary pre-training signal (dropped at deployment) to improve a vision-only policy, over either ignoring tactile information entirely or requiring tactile sensors at deployment
claims.conditions: real robot; even a low-fidelity, low-cost tactile sensor sufficed; auxiliary pretraining signal is not needed at inference time, making the approach compatible with vision-only deployment like ours

title: Data Scaling Laws in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: In a large-scale empirical study (40,000+ demonstrations collected, 15,000+ real-world robot rollouts executed under a rigorous evaluation protocol), a policy's generalization performance follows a roughly power-law relationship with the number of training environments and objects; critically, the diversity of environments and objects is far more important than the absolute number of demonstrations -- once demonstrations per environment/object reach a certain threshold, additional demonstrations have minimal effect
claims.direction: strongly favors prioritizing diversity of environments/objects over raw demonstration count once a per-environment/object threshold is reached -- directly informs how to allocate a limited demo budget (spread across more environment/object variations rather than piling up repeats of the same setup)
claims.conditions: large-scale real-world study across numerous environments and objects; based on these findings, four data collectors working one afternoon collected enough data for two tasks to reach ~90% success rates in novel environments with unseen objects, demonstrating a practical, efficient data-collection recipe

why_deep_read: This is a landmark, large-scale (40k+ demos, 15k+ real rollouts) rigorous empirical study establishing power-law generalization scaling and the primacy of diversity over raw count for imitation learning data collection -- exactly the central evidence needed for our Q13 decision on how to spend our ~50-100-demo-per-task budget (more environment/object variation vs. more repeats), with a concrete practical collection recipe.

title: ViTaMIn: Learning Contact-Rich Tasks Through Robot-Free Visuo-Tactile Manipulation Interface

claims.claim: An embodiment-free, hand-held gripper interface integrating visual and tactile sensing (avoiding the need for teleoperation hardware/setup) combined with pretrained tactile representations significantly outperforms baseline methods on seven contact-rich manipulation tasks, improving data efficiency and policy robustness
claims.direction: favors robot-free, hand-held data-collection interfaces (with integrated multimodal sensing) over standard teleoperation for contact-rich task data collection efficiency and robustness
claims.conditions: seven contact-rich manipulation tasks; requires specialized hand-held gripper hardware with tactile sensing

title: Visual Prompting for Robotic Manipulation with Annotation-Guided Pick-and-Place Using ACT

claims.claim: Using annotation-guided visual prompting (bounding boxes identifying pickable objects and placement locations as structured spatial guidance) combined with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to predict chunked action sequences from human demonstrations improves grasp accuracy and adaptability in cluttered retail pick-and-place scenes with dense object arrangements, occlusions, and variation in object color/shape/size/texture
claims.direction: favors visual (bounding-box) prompting as spatial guidance alongside an ACT-based chunked policy, over relying on step-by-step planning or language instructions alone, for cluttered/occluded pick-and-place scenes
claims.conditions: real convenience-store-style pick-and-place setting; ACT as the imitation-learning backbone (same policy family in common use for low-cost arms)

title: ViPRA: Video Prediction for Robot Actions

claims.claim: A pretraining-finetuning framework trains a video-language model on actionless human/teleoperated videos to predict future observations and motion-centric latent actions (trained with perceptual losses and optical-flow consistency), then uses a chunked flow-matching decoder to map these latent actions to robot-specific continuous action sequences using only 100 to 200 teleoperated demonstrations for the downstream control stage, avoiding expensive action annotation and supporting generalization across embodiments
claims.direction: favors pretraining latent 'what changes' representations on actionless video (avoiding costly per-frame action annotation) and only fine-tuning a lightweight chunked decoder with a modest number (100-200) of teleoperated demos for the target embodiment, over training action prediction end-to-end from scratch on annotated robot data alone
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks and SIMPLER sim benchmark; 100-200 demos is close to our own ~50-100 per-task budget

claims.claim: The chunked flow-matching decoder enables smooth, high-frequency continuous control up to 22 Hz via chunked action decoding, and the method outperforms strong baselines with a 16% gain on SIMPLER and a 13% improvement across real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: supports chunked flow-matching decoding of latent actions as compatible with high-frequency (22Hz), smooth control
claims.conditions: same real+sim evaluation

title: Long-VLA: Unleashing Long-Horizon Capability of Vision Language Action Model for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Existing VLA frameworks address short-horizon tasks poorly at long horizons due to challenges in skill chaining and subtask dependencies; a phase-aware input masking strategy that adaptively segments each subtask into 'moving' and 'interaction' phases (letting the model focus on phase-relevant sensory cues) is architecture-agnostic, integrates into existing VLA models without harming scalability/data efficiency, and significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods on both simulated and real-world long-horizon tasks (introducing the L-CALVIN benchmark)
claims.direction: favors explicitly segmenting each subtask into moving vs. interaction phases (with phase-aware input masking) over treating the whole subtask uniformly, to improve subtask compatibility and long-horizon skill chaining
claims.conditions: L-CALVIN benchmark (new) plus other simulated and real-world long-horizon tasks; module is architecture-agnostic and can be added to existing VLA models

title: Efficient Parallel PPO-Based Reinforcement Learning for Generalized Pick and Place with Dense Reward Shaping

claims.claim: A massively parallel (4096-environment) PPO training pipeline for an SO-101 robotic arm, using privileged state information (joint positions/velocities, object/target poses, previous action) rather than cameras, trains generalized single-object pick-and-place under randomized object/goal poses entirely in simulation on a single consumer GPU (RTX 5060 Ti, 16GB)
claims.direction: demonstrates that our exact robot platform (SO-101) can be trained at scale in simulation with privileged state and a single consumer GPU, though this is an RL/privileged-state approach rather than a vision-based imitation-learning policy comparable to our design decisions
claims.conditions: simulation only (Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab, PhysX 5); no camera/vision input used, so not directly comparable to our vision-based policy decisions, but notable for using the same robot (SO-101) and similar-class GPU

title: MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation

claims.claim: Challenging the prevailing view that simulation alone cannot achieve sim-to-real transfer without at least some real-world data or task-specific fine-tuning, the authors show that with sufficiently large-scale and diverse procedurally-generated simulated training data (1.8 million expert trajectories across procedurally-generated robots/tasks/environments), zero-shot transfer to the real world is effective for both static and mobile manipulation, with no real-world fine-tuning at all; on tabletop pick-and-place, their policy (MolmoBot) achieves 79.2% real-world success across 4 settings, outperforming pi0.5 at 39.2%
claims.direction: directly contradicts the common assumption that simulation-only training is insufficient for real-world transfer -- shows that procedural diversity and scale in simulation, without any real-world data or fine-tuning, can outperform a strong real-data-trained baseline (pi0.5) at zero-shot real-world deployment
claims.conditions: evaluated on Franka FR3 (tabletop) and Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 (mobile manipulator) platforms; zero real-world fine-tuning; large-scale procedural simulation data generation (MolmoBot-Engine/MolmoSpaces)

title: Robot-Factored World Models via Robot Rendering

claims.claim: Conditioning a video world model directly on action commands forces it to learn the robot's own action-realization process (motion + controller dynamics), while conditioning on logged future states leaks the interaction outcome being predicted; instead, rolling each action through the robot's own controller/kinematics into a deployment-available nominal trajectory, then rendering that trajectory through the robot's URDF (factoring geometry/kinematics/appearance out of the model into explicit rendered robot geometry, paired with end-effector+scene depth), outperforms vector-conditioned baselines and generalizes to unseen robot embodiments at inference
claims.direction: favors rendering the robot's nominal trajectory as explicit visual geometry (rather than conditioning on raw action vectors or leaking future states) as the interface between action and a world model, for cross-embodiment generalization
claims.conditions: action-conditioned video world model setting; also demonstrated generating robot manipulation videos from human demonstrations by retargeting/rendering hand motion as robot geometry (relevant to using human video as a Q13 data source)

title: Factored Diffusion Policies: Compositionally Generalized Robot Control with a Single Score Network
