claims.claim: Collecting expert demonstrations for every combination of task factors (object, obstacles, color, etc.) grows combinatorially; training a single shared diffusion network with per-factor null-token dropout, whose score decomposes additively across factors at inference (under approximate conditional independence), reduces the required training-task budget from a product of factor cardinalities to a sum, while a trajectory-tube certificate provides a bounded-error guarantee; on state-based multi-gate racing the factored policy matches an oracle (90% of held-out gates) while a multi-network composition baseline collapses to 3%, and on vision-based single-gate traversal it transfers zero-shot to an unseen venue with +11.7pp success and 2.4x lower crash rate
claims.direction: favors training one shared diffusion policy with per-factor conditioning dropout (compositional score decomposition) over either collecting demonstrations for every factor combination or training separate per-factor networks, to make data collection scale additively rather than combinatorially with task-factor diversity
claims.conditions: drone racing domain (not manipulation), sim and real; the compositional-generalization principle reinforces evidence elsewhere in this batch (e.g. Data Scaling Laws, Diagnosing Compositional Generalization) that factor/diversity coverage matters more than raw demo volume

title: GraspIT: A Dataset Bridging the Sim-to-Real gap and back for Validated Grasping SE(3) Pose Generation

claims.claim: A dataset of ~316k annotated RGB-D frame sets (1035 sim + 100 real scenes) with physically-validated grasp quality scores (via a four-stage physical slip-test in Isaac Sim, going beyond simple force-closure, and back-projected onto real-world scenes via a Real-Sim loop) provides graded hard negatives (grasps passing force-closure but failing the slip-test) and enables streaming of high-resolution simulated demonstrations for behavior cloning
claims.direction: supports using physically-validated (not just force-closure) simulated grasp annotations, including hard negatives, and a real-sim label back-projection loop, as a higher-quality synthetic data source for grasp-related imitation learning
claims.conditions: synthetic (Isaac Sim, Franka Panda) plus real-world scene annotation; dataset/tool release rather than a policy comparison

title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring

claims.claim: Rather than perturbing continuous actions through iterative denoising (expressive but hard to interpret and prone to implausible actions), the Large Discrete Policy selects actions from a large vocabulary of physically plausible discrete candidates and improves expressivity via stochastic iterative scoring (progressively re-scoring/pruning candidates with score-space stochasticity rather than perturbing the actions themselves), consistently outperforming strong discrete and continuous baselines in autonomous driving and exceeding or matching continuous generative policies in robotic manipulation
claims.direction: favors a discrete, large-vocabulary action representation with iterative candidate re-scoring over continuous diffusion/flow-based action generation, as an interpretable alternative that is at least competitive with continuous generative policies for manipulation
claims.conditions: evaluated across end-to-end planning, closed-loop driving, robotic manipulation, and VLA settings; manipulation-specific claim is 'exceeds or matches' (weaker than the driving-domain claim of consistently outperforming)

title: Think Like a World Model, Act Like a VLA: Distilling World-Model Representations into Compact Robot Policies

claims.claim: Standard VLA training has no objective accounting for how the world responds to actions, bounding robustness by data coverage alone; world models carry that missing grounding but are too slow (seconds per decision) to run in the control loop. Adding a single feature-alignment term to ordinary VLA training -- where a frozen world model is run over training frames ONCE and cached (no teacher loaded during training, and the projector is discarded after training) -- lets the student inherit the world model's grounding while leaving its slow generative machinery behind entirely
claims.direction: favors distilling a frozen world model's internal representations into a standard VLA via a one-time cached feature-alignment loss (rather than running a world model at inference, or training with no such auxiliary objective at all) to get world-model-grounded robustness at zero deployment cost
claims.conditions: the deployed policy is architecturally identical to the undistilled baseline -- no added parameters, no world model at inference

claims.claim: The deployed distilled policy runs in 32ms and 1.86GB of GPU memory on a consumer RTX 5090; a 0.8B-parameter student reaches 97.9% on LIBERO and improves from 48.2% to 50.5% on RoboCasa-GR1 humanoid manipulation, with the same objective carrying over to real hardware on both single-arm and bimanual platforms, and the gain surviving changes of student scale, backbone, alignment layer, and teacher
claims.direction: demonstrates that a small (0.8B) student model can gain measurable, robust performance improvements from world-model distillation without any increase in inference latency, memory footprint, or parameter count -- directly compatible with small-model, low-latency, limited-GPU deployment constraints
claims.conditions: real hardware validation (single-arm and bimanual); ablations across student scale, backbone architecture, alignment layer, and teacher model all preserve the gain, suggesting the technique is broadly robust rather than fragile

title: Learning Language-guided Robotic Manipulation via Efficient and Generalizable Feature Distillation

title: LaVA-Man: Learning Visual Action Representations for Robot Manipulation

title: GWM: Towards Scalable Gaussian World Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Training with a self-supervised future-state-prediction auxiliary objective (a Gaussian World Model predicting future 3D scene state under robot actions via latent diffusion transformer + 3D VAE) enhances visual representations for imitation learning and enables training policies that outperform the state-of-the-art by 'impressive margins'

title: AnchorVLA4D: an Anchor-Based Spatial-Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation

title: Aligning Flow Map Policies with Optimal Q-Guidance

claims.claim: Flow map policies, which learn to take arbitrary-size jumps (including one-step jumps) across the generative dynamics of flow-based policies, achieve state-of-the-art performance in offline-to-online RL, outperforming the previous one-step policy MVP by a relative 21.3% improvement in average success rate across 12 manipulation and locomotion tasks (OGBench, RoboMimic)

title: Continue or Replan? Bernoulli-Continuation Policy Learning for Adaptive Horizon Execution

claims.conditions: real robot (2 manipulation tasks) + RoboTwin 2.0 sim (50 tasks) + LIBERO/LIBERO-PRO transfer, base policies LingBot-VLA and pi_0.5

title: Humanoid World Models: Open World Foundation Models for Humanoid Robotics

title: DEFLECT: Temporal Counterfactual Preference Learning for Delay-Robust Asynchronous VLAs

title: UMI-3D: Extending Universal Manipulation Interface from Vision-Limited to 3D Spatial Perception

title: FocusVLA: Focused Visual Utilization for Vision-Language-Action Models

title: EgoBridge: Domain Adaptation for Generalizable Imitation from Egocentric Human Data

why_deep_read: A large (44 absolute pp) real-world improvement from co-training with cheap egocentric human video is directly relevant to our two core pain points -- limited teleop demos (50-100) and breaking under novel objects/scenes -- and could offer a low-cost way to expand effective training data beyond our own teleoperation without new hardware.

title: MGAD-FMDM: A Modular Robotic Multitask Imitation Learning Method

claims.claim: A modular imitation learning method that auto-generates primitive skill modules (adaptive discriminator) and uses a diffusion-model-based feedback mechanism (recognizing expert demonstration distribution, then evaluating imitated-trajectory fit) improves over state-of-the-art baselines on real robot tasks by 14.29-100.00% in success rate, 2.22-34.85% in Spearman rank correlation, 5.43-64.35% in earth mover's distance, and 21.74-30.10% in convergence speed
claims.direction: favors modular skill-discovery plus diffusion-based trajectory-distribution feedback over monolithic imitation learning baselines
claims.conditions: real robot tasks (practical robot tasks), multitask imitation learning

title: Global Prior Meets Local Consistency: Dual-Memory Augmented Vision-Language-Action Model for Efficient Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Replacing the isotropic Gaussian noise prior in generative VLA action heads with task-level priors retrieved from semantically similar trajectories (Global Prior Memory) shortens the generative path, reducing the number of function evaluations (denoising steps) needed and increasing inference speed by 2.9x, while the model achieves 98.6% average success on LIBERO, +13.5% over pi_0 on CALVIN, and 38% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 Hard
claims.direction: favors retrieval-based/non-Gaussian noise priors for generative action heads to cut inference steps/latency
claims.conditions: three simulation benchmarks (LIBERO, CALVIN, RoboTwin 2.0 Hard) plus real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Policies conditioned solely on the current observation lack awareness of task progress and are prone to temporally inconsistent, jerky trajectories; a Local Consistency Memory that dynamically models the executed action sequence to infer task progress and enforce a learned temporal-coherence/smoothness constraint substantially improves real-world performance, surpassing pi_0 by 42.9% on a Generalization suite and 52.4% on a Long-horizon suite
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit executed-action-history memory/consistency constraint over current-observation-only conditioning
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation on Generalization and Long-horizon task suites, baseline pi_0

why_deep_read: Directly targets two of our stated failure modes at once -- slow multi-step denoising latency and jerky/inconsistent motion from lacking observation history/temporal consistency -- with large, well-quantified real-world gains over the widely-used pi_0 baseline and a 2.9x speedup; highly actionable for our latency- and jerkiness-constrained SmolVLA replacement.

title: Dynamics-Aware Meta-Imitation for Generalization to Unseen Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A meta-imitation framework (DAMI) that builds a shared skill space via meta-learning, captures spatio-temporal dynamics from a single reference demonstration, and fuses multimodal observations, outperforms state-of-the-art baselines both on direct inference for seen tasks and on adaptation to unseen tasks via few-shot fine-tuning, in both simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors meta-learning-based dynamics-aware skill representations over standard in-domain imitation learning for generalization to unseen tasks
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, few-shot fine-tuning to unseen tasks

title: FetchMan: Learning Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Policies from Simulated Experiences

claims.claim: Cloning synthetic demonstrations (behavior cloning on simulated data) results in a low performance ceiling regardless of the amount of training data used; reinforcement learning (refining the cloned policy with Flow-GRPO on a single sparse reward) breaks through this ceiling and achieves performance that synthetic behavior cloning cannot match
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that scaling up (synthetic) demonstration quantity alone for behavior cloning is sufficient -- favors RL fine-tuning on top of BC to surpass a data-scaling plateau
claims.conditions: sim-to-real pipeline with 150,000+ simulated scenes, zero-shot real-world deployment on Unitree G1 humanoid, single-object reach-and-pick task (73.3% success)

title: LiMA: Bridging Long-term Imagination to Real-time Dexterous Manipulation via Asynchronous Diffusion

claims.claim: World-Action Models (WAMs) suffer high inference latency from iterative generation, causing temporal misalignment between planned intent and rapid physical contact changes; LiMA, an asynchronous dual-system framework that decouples slow long-horizon intent planning from a fast high-frequency motion-refinement system (aligned via a Latent Schrodinger Bridge Coupling), reduces inference latency by 45.8% compared with Cosmos-Policy while achieving an overall 70.8% success rate and 78.9% average subtask success across six bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks, maintaining performance in unseen scenarios
claims.direction: favors decoupling slow planning from fast reactive execution (dual-timescale asynchronous generation) over a single-timescale generative action model for reducing latency without sacrificing long-horizon competence
claims.conditions: six bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks spanning multiple horizons, unseen-scenario evaluation

why_deep_read: A dual-timescale (slow intent / fast reactive) asynchronous architecture that concretely cuts inference latency (45.8%) while preserving long-horizon success is a strong candidate design pattern for resolving our own 2s-latency and jerky async chunk-boundary problems; worth reading in full to see if the same slow/fast decoupling could apply to a much smaller SmolVLA-scale model.

title: Lift3D Policy: Lifting 2D Foundation Models for Robust 3D Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Progressively enhancing a 2D foundation model with implicit 3D representation (task-aware masked autoencoder reconstructing depth on task-relevant affordance patches) and then explicit 3D representation (mapping 3D points to the 2D model's positional embeddings so the 2D model directly encodes point clouds) outperforms prior state-of-the-art 3D manipulation policies across several simulation benchmarks and real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors lifting/adapting pretrained 2D foundation models into 3D representations over training 3D-specific encoders from scratch or using raw point-cloud encoders
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + real-world scenarios

title: Cortical Policy: A Dual-Stream View Transformer for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Jointly reasoning from a static-view stream (spatial understanding via pretrained 3D foundation model keypoints) and a dynamic-view stream (adaptive, gaze-estimation-based) outperforms single-stream/static-only view transformer baselines substantially on RLBench, COLOSSEUM, and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors combining static and dynamic (gaze-adaptive) view processing over static-only multi-view transformers
claims.conditions: RLBench, COLOSSEUM benchmark, real-world tasks, language-conditioned

title: DIAL: Decoupling Intent and Action via Latent World Modeling for End-to-End VLA

claims.claim: DIAL, which bridges a VLM-based 'System-2' latent world model (synthesizing latent visual foresight as an explicit intent bottleneck) with a lightweight 'System-1' policy that decodes this intent plus current observation into actions via latent inverse dynamics, establishes new state-of-the-art performance on the RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop benchmark using 10x fewer demonstrations than prior methods
claims.direction: favors a latent-world-model intent bottleneck (auxiliary future-prediction objective) decoupled from a lightweight action decoder to drastically cut required demonstration count
claims.conditions: RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop benchmark; two-stage training (decoupled warmup then joint fine-tuning)

claims.claim: By leveraging heterogeneous human demonstrations, DIAL learns physically grounded manipulation priors and shows robust zero-shot generalization to unseen objects and novel configurations in real-world deployment on a humanoid robot
claims.direction: favors world-model-based intent priors (trained partly on human data) for zero-shot object/configuration generalization
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid deployment, unseen objects and configurations

why_deep_read: A 10x reduction in required demonstrations to reach SOTA directly targets our core data-scarcity constraint (50-100 demos), and the explicit intent/world-model bottleneck plus reported zero-shot generalization to unseen objects speaks directly to Q09, Q13, and our object-generalization failures; worth checking whether the architecture is lightweight enough for an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Flow-Enabled Generalization to Human Demonstrations in Few-Shot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: SFCrP, combining a cross-embodiment Scene-Flow prediction model (learned from both robot and human videos, predicting arbitrary point trajectories) with a Flow-and-Cropped-point-cloud-conditioned Policy that adjusts precise actions based on observations, outperforms SOTA baselines across various real-world task settings while reducing the amount of required robot demonstrations by substituting some with human videos
claims.direction: favors flow-based (point-trajectory) conditioning bridging human video and robot demos over relying only on robot teleop demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world task settings, few-shot imitation learning

claims.claim: The method exhibits strong spatial and instance generalization to scenarios observed only in human videos (not in robot demonstrations)
claims.direction: favors flow-conditioned policies for generalizing beyond the robot's own demo distribution
claims.conditions: real-world, scenarios seen only in human video

title: SPACE: Enabling Learning from Cross-Robot Data Toward Generalist Policies

claims.claim: Using Cartesian end-effector state delta as a universal action representation (rather than directly predicting robot-specific low-level control commands), combined with a separate Action Adapter that converts the predicted Cartesian delta into robot-specific commands, substantially outperforms policies that directly predict control commands when learning from data collected across different embodiments or across different hardware units of the same embodiment; it also remains robust under deployment-time dynamics shifts including changes in control frequency, object weight, and controller gains
claims.direction: favors an end-effector Cartesian-delta action representation (decoupled from robot-specific low-level commands) over direct joint/control-command prediction, especially when data or hardware varies
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment and cross-hardware-unit experiments; robustness tests under control-frequency, payload, and gain changes

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q02 action-space question and specifically reports robustness to control-frequency changes -- directly relevant to our plan to move from 10fps to 30fps -- with a concrete, generalizable action representation (Cartesian delta + adapter) that could be a low-risk change for the SO-101.

title: ContactFlow: A video action conditioning that transfers across embodiments

claims.claim: An embodiment-agnostic action representation based on the trajectory of 3D contact points (discarding actor-specific appearance/kinematics) allows training a video world model on both human and robotic object-interaction videos, enabling transfer between human demonstrations and different robotic embodiments, validated on the DROID dataset and real-world tabletop manipulation
claims.direction: favors contact-point-trajectory conditioning as a shared signal to leverage human video data alongside robot demos
claims.conditions: DROID dataset + real-world tabletop tasks

claims.claim: A propose-imagine-verify-act pipeline, where a video world model's generated rollouts are assessed by a vision-language model before execution, predicts physically plausible manipulation outcomes
claims.direction: favors world-model rollout + VLM verification as an auxiliary planning/safety mechanism
claims.conditions: real-world tabletop manipulation

title: V-Link: Recovering Lost Visual Representations in Action DiT for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: VLA action experts typically have limited access to the 3D geometric and 2D semantic information present in VLM features, weakening perceptual grounding; V-Link recovers this by injecting complementary Spatial and Semantic Query representations from the VLM into the Action DiT via asymmetric pathways, improving average success rate over base model GR00T N1.6 by +1.9%, +31.2%, and +18.8% on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0 respectively, and by +20% and +24% on two real-world humanoid tasks (AGIBOT A3 Ultra)
claims.direction: favors explicitly re-injecting geometric+semantic VLM features into the action-generation module rather than relying on the action expert's implicit access to VLM features
claims.conditions: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0 simulation benchmarks plus two real-world humanoid tasks, baseline GR00T N1.6

title: WholeBodyWAM: Learning Whole-Body World Action Models with Scalable Motion Priors

claims.claim: Pretraining a language-conditioned 'Motion Expert' on a large heterogeneous motion corpus (4K+ hours from human videos, 3D motion datasets, and other humanoid platforms) without target-robot action supervision, then integrating it via Mixture-of-Transformers attention during robot post-training, substantially improves data efficiency under limited target-robot demonstrations and improves downstream task performance, with benefits scaling with motion-pretraining scale
claims.direction: favors large-scale cross-embodiment motion pretraining (even without action labels) to reduce required target-robot demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid manipulation, limited target-robot demonstrations

title: What Makes Pre-Trained Visual Representations Successful for Robust Manipulation?

claims.claim: Comparing 15 pretrained vision models (including manipulation-specific representations trained on human-video object-interaction datasets) under distribution shifts commonly seen in robotics (lighting changes, scene-texture changes, distractor objects), the paper finds visual representations designed specifically for manipulation/control do NOT necessarily generalize better under these shifts; instead, emergent segmentation ability among ViT models is a stronger predictor of out-of-distribution generalization than downstream ImageNet accuracy, in-domain accuracy, or shape-bias (cue-conflict) metrics
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that manipulation-specific pretraining (e.g. on human-interaction video) is inherently more robust; favors selecting encoders by emergent segmentation ability rather than by manipulation-specific pretraining or ImageNet accuracy
claims.conditions: ten tasks across two simulated manipulation environments, plus real-world validation on an ALOHA setup after offline training with 50 demonstrations, testing lighting/texture/distractor distribution shifts

claims.claim: On the real-world ALOHA setup, the segmentation-ability score of the chosen pretrained visual encoder predicts real-world task performance after training on only 50 demonstrations
claims.direction: favors using segmentation-ability as a practical, cheap proxy metric for choosing a vision encoder expected to generalize under lighting/scene changes
claims.conditions: real robot (ALOHA), 50 demonstrations, lighting/scene-texture/distractor-object distribution shifts

why_deep_read: This is a controlled, real-robot (ALOHA, 50 demos -- matching our own data scale) study of exactly our robustness failure modes (lighting, scene/background, distractor/novel objects) across 15 pretrained encoders, with a concrete, cheap, actionable selection metric (segmentation score); full text ablation tables would let us pick a vision encoder for our SO-101 setup with the strongest evidence base in this entire batch.

title: Using Implicit Behavior Cloning and Dynamic Movement Primitive to Facilitate Reinforcement Learning for Robot Motion Planning

claims.claim: Combining implicit behavior cloning (IBC, using human demonstration data) with dynamic movement primitives (DMP, as a heuristic motion-planning prior) to warm-start/guide an off-policy RL agent achieves faster training speed and higher scores than conventional RL agents without demonstrations, validated on a real-robot pick-and-place-derived assembly task
claims.direction: favors combining implicit behavior cloning with a DMP prior over pure RL from scratch for training speed and performance
claims.conditions: real-robot assembly task, human demonstration dataset from pick-and-place experiments

title: Video2Act: A Dual-System Video Diffusion Policy with Robotic Spatio-Motional Modeling

claims.claim: An asynchronous dual-system design -- a video diffusion model (VDM) as a slow 'System 2' extracting motion-aware spatial/motion representations, and a diffusion-transformer (DiT) action head as a fast 'System 1' -- maintains stable manipulation even with low-frequency updates from the slow VDM, mitigating the inference-latency cost of video diffusion models; Video2Act surpasses previous SOTA VLA methods by 7.7% in simulation and 21.7% in real-world tasks in average success rate
claims.direction: favors decoupling a slow, motion-aware video-diffusion perception/world-model system from a fast diffusion-transformer action head (asynchronous dual-system) over a single synchronous system, to hide latency while retaining rich dynamics modeling
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Directly targets our async-inference/latency problem with a slow-perception + fast-action dual-system architecture that explicitly tolerates low-frequency updates from the heavy component -- a promising pattern for our laptop-GPU deployment with ~2s inference latency -- backed by a large (21.7%) real-world success-rate gain over prior VLA methods.

title: InternVLA-A1: Unifying Understanding, Generation and Action for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A unified Mixture-of-Transformers architecture coordinating three experts (scene understanding, visual foresight generation, action execution) interacting via unified masked self-attention, pretrained on 692M+ frames of real robot data, synthetic simulation data, and human videos, consistently outperforms pi0.5: +4.4% on static manipulation tasks, +2.6% on RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, and +26.7% on dynamic manipulation tasks, evaluated on 12 real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors jointly unifying semantic understanding, visual-foresight (world-model) prediction, and action generation in one architecture over VLA-only or world-model-only approaches, especially for dynamic tasks
claims.conditions: 12 real-world robotic tasks + simulation benchmark, baseline pi0.5, mixed real/sim/human-video pretraining data

title: UltraDexGrasp: Learning Universal Dexterous Grasping for Bimanual Robots with Synthetic Data

claims.claim: A grasp policy trained exclusively on a large-scale synthetic dataset (20M frames, 1,000 objects) generated via a planning+optimization pipeline achieves robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, attaining 81.2% average success rate in real-world universal dexterous grasping of novel objects with varied shapes, sizes, and weights
claims.direction: favors large-scale, diverse synthetic-only training data (with careful physically-plausible generation) as sufficient for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous bimanual grasping, zero real-world training data, novel objects

title: Tool-Action Comprehension: A Cross-Morphology Imitation Learning Framework for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: TAC learns bimanual manipulation skills directly from human demonstration videos (no teleoperation device or manual annotation) by building an embodiment-agnostic, morphologically-invariant observation-action representation (via 3D reconstruction, tool pose alignment, and hand-morphology decoupling via segmentation); it achieves 81.5% average success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline by an absolute 62.2 percentage points
claims.direction: favors extracting embodiment-agnostic representations from raw human video (no teleop hardware) over standard teleoperation-collected demonstrations or baseline imitation methods
claims.conditions: real-robot bimanual manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The human-video-based data collection pipeline lets novices collect demonstrations 14.9% faster than experts using conventional methods, improving data-collection scalability
claims.direction: favors human-video demonstration collection for scalability/speed over conventional expert teleoperation
claims.conditions: human demonstration video collection, comparison of novice vs expert collection speed

title: Where Should Action Generation Begin? A Learnable Source Prior for Generative Robot Policies

claims.claim: Replacing the standard observation-independent Gaussian noise source in generative (flow-matching or diffusion) robot policies with a lightweight, proprioception-conditioned learnable source prior (LeaP) -- while keeping the downstream generator and inference solver unchanged -- achieves 81.6% average success on 15 RoboTwin manipulation tasks, beating deterministic-source, no-prior, and diffusion-bridge baselines by 6.5 to 25.5 percentage points, and improves both flow-matching and diffusion-bridge generators consistently, with gains carrying over to real-world deployment
claims.direction: favors an observation-informed, state-adaptive stochastic source distribution over a fixed uninformed Gaussian noise source for generative action heads
claims.conditions: 15 RoboTwin simulation tasks plus real-world deployment

claims.claim: The learnable source prior uses fewer parameters and converges faster than baseline generative-policy source distributions
claims.direction: favors this technique as a low-cost (small, fast-converging) addition for compute-constrained generative policies
claims.conditions: same RoboTwin + real-world setting

title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity

claims.claim: Reproducing spatially distributed tactile feedback from the remote manipulator on the operator's fingertip during teleoperation reduces the deviation between teleoperated and natural human trajectories by 29-79%, and increasing tactile feedback resolution compresses the state-space distribution of teleoperated motions, which the authors associate with improved training outcomes for autonomous robot policies
claims.direction: favors adding spatially distributed tactile feedback to the teleoperation interface to produce higher-quality (more natural, less variable) demonstrations for policy training
claims.conditions: teleoperation tasks with a bilateral force-feedback telemanipulator and tactile fingertip display

title: ReWeight: Leveraging Human Data for VLA Post-Training via Demonstration Retrieval and Sample Weighting

claims.claim: Directly mixing egocentric human demonstrations with robot data during VLA post-training only modestly helps (pi_0.5 average success 39% robot-only vs 44% with naive human-robot mixing in simulation) because of cross-embodiment discrepancies; ReWeight, which retrieves human demonstrations behaviorally similar to target robot data (via optimal transport over a joint visuomotor+future-action representation) and weights samples by similarity, raises simulation success to 57%, and achieves 68.8% in physical real-world experiments, outperforming the robot-only and naive-mixing baselines by 28.8 and 13.8 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors similarity-based retrieval and weighting of human demonstration data over naive human-robot data mixing when post-training VLA models with egocentric human data
claims.conditions: pi_0.5 backbone, 8 simulation tasks + 4 real-world tasks, clean and randomized settings

title: SculptDiff: Learning Robotic Clay Sculpting from Humans with Goal Conditioned Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: A goal-conditioned diffusion-based imitation learning policy operating on point-cloud state observations successfully learns real-world manipulation policies for a challenging 3D deformable-object task (clay sculpting toward diverse target shapes), reported as the first such successful real-world method
claims.direction: favors goal-conditioned diffusion policies with point-cloud input for complex deformable-object manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world robot, point-cloud observations, diverse target shapes

title: GR-3 Technical Report

claims.claim: GR-3, a large-scale VLA trained with co-training on web-scale vision-language data, VR-collected human trajectory data, and robot trajectory imitation learning, can be efficiently fine-tuned with minimal human trajectory data for rapid, cost-effective adaptation to new settings
claims.direction: favors heavy multi-source pretraining (web VL data + human VR trajectories + robot data) to reduce the amount of task-specific demonstration data needed at deployment time
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, bi-manual mobile robot (ByteMini), baseline pi_0

claims.claim: GR-3 generalizes to novel objects, environments, and instructions involving abstract concepts, and shows robust performance on long-horizon and dexterous bimanual/mobile tasks, surpassing pi_0 on a wide variety of challenging tasks
claims.direction: favors this multi-source-pretrained large VLA for object/environment/instruction generalization
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across many task types

title: Sim-and-Real Co-Training: A Simple Recipe for Vision-Based Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A systematic study of co-training vision-based manipulation policies on a mixture of simulation and real-world data (across a robot arm and a humanoid, diverse tasks) shows this strategy improves real-world task performance by an average of 38%, even with notable differences between the simulation and real-world data distributions, and the paper derives a general, simple recipe for how to combine sim and real data effectively
claims.direction: favors co-training on mixed simulation+real data over training on real data alone, and provides general practical guidance (not just a single narrow technique) on how to do so effectively
claims.conditions: two robot embodiments (arm and humanoid), multiple simulation and real-world datasets, diverse manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Unlike single narrow synthetic-data-generation tricks, this is presented as a systematic, general-purpose empirical recipe (derived from comprehensive experiments) for combining simulation with limited real data -- directly actionable for stretching our 50-100 real teleop demos with simulation data, and the practical 'recipe' framing is exactly the kind of transferable guidance we need rather than a one-off architecture.

title: FUNCTO: Function-Centric One-Shot Imitation Learning for Tool Manipulation

claims.claim: Establishing function-centric correspondences via 3D functional keypoints allows generalizing a tool-manipulation skill from a SINGLE human demonstration video to novel tools with the same function despite significant geometric variation, outperforming existing modular one-shot-imitation-learning methods and end-to-end behavior cloning in real-robot experiments
claims.direction: favors structured functional-keypoint correspondence for extreme (one-shot) demonstration efficiency over end-to-end behavior cloning, which needs more data to generalize across tool geometries
claims.conditions: real-robot tool manipulation, single demonstration, generalization to novel tool geometries with same function

title: Bridge Sim to Real Robot Manipulation: A Tri Level Hybrid Framework Combining Vision Language Models & RL with Deterministic Control

claims.claim: Explicitly extracting physical object properties (rigidity, friction, mass) via a VLM from RGB images and conditioning a residual RL policy plus impedance control on these properties yields an 82.1% improvement in task success, 2.9x faster convergence, and 87.8% success rate on novel objects with property-based generalization, versus not using explicit physical-property extraction
claims.direction: favors explicitly extracting and conditioning on physical object properties (via VLM) for sim-to-real generalization over standard domain randomization/system identification
claims.conditions: physics-based simulation only (no real-robot validation reported in abstract)

title: Concurrent Prehensile and Nonprehensile Manipulation: A Practical Approach to Multi-Stage Dexterous Tasks

claims.claim: DexMulti decomposes demonstrations into object-centric skills with well-defined temporal boundaries and executes them via a retrieve-align-execute paradigm (retrieving demonstrated skills based on current object geometry and aligning via an uncertainty-aware centroid/yaw estimator), achieving 66% average success on training objects using only 3-4 demonstrations per object across over 1,000 real-world trials, outperforming diffusion-policy baselines by 2-3x while requiring far fewer demonstrations, and generalizing to held-out objects and +/-25cm spatial variation
claims.direction: favors a retrieval/skill-decomposition approach over monolithic end-to-end diffusion policies when demonstrations are extremely scarce (3-4 per object)
claims.conditions: real-world multi-stage concurrent (prehensile+nonprehensile) manipulation, two dexterous hands (Allegro, LEAP), 1,000+ trials

title: ActiveGlasses: Learning Manipulation with Active Vision from Ego-centric Human Demonstration

claims.claim: Using a stereo camera on smart glasses as the sole perception device for both ego-centric human demonstration collection and (mounted on a 6-DoF perception arm) robot deployment, with an object-centric point-cloud policy jointly predicting manipulation and head/camera movement, achieves zero-shot transfer with active vision, consistently outperforming strong baselines under the same hardware and generalizing across two robot platforms, including on tasks involving occlusion
claims.direction: favors active, jointly-controlled camera viewpoint (learned head movement) plus a shared human/robot perception device over fixed-camera or handheld-device data collection
claims.conditions: real-world tasks with occlusion and precise interaction, two robot platforms

title: Smooth Operator: A Real-Time Sampling-Based Algorithm for Kinematic Hand Retargeting

claims.claim: Gradient-based teleoperation retargeting algorithms often converge to different local minima causing jitter that degrades demonstration data quality; a gradient-free Sampling-Based Retargeter (SBR) designed for low-jitter real-time retargeting achieved the highest overall task success rate (54.1%) and the lowest cognitive workload (NASA-TLX 36.4/100) versus gradient-based baselines in an 18-participant real-world user study across 3 manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors gradient-free, sampling-based retargeting over gradient-based retargeting to reduce jitter and improve demonstration data/teleoperation quality
claims.conditions: real-world user study, 18 participants, 3 complex manipulation tasks

title: ACE-Ego-0: Unifying Egocentric Human and Robotic Data for VLA Pretraining

claims.claim: A scalable egocentric video-to-action pipeline converts raw human videos into robot-format pseudo-action trajectories (via a unified camera-space action representation and morphology conditioning); combined with a reliability-aware training objective (human auxiliary loss concentrating supervision on reliable pseudo-action signals) to handle noisy human-video pseudo-labels, joint pretraining on 1.48K hours of pseudo-labeled human video plus 4.53K hours of robot/sim data achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop and RoboTwin 2.0, with strong transfer to real-world bimanual manipulation
claims.direction: favors reliability-weighted joint training on pseudo-labeled human video plus robot data over robot-only training
claims.conditions: large-scale mixed human-video and robot/sim pretraining, real-world bimanual transfer

title: A comparative study of imitation learning methods for robotic manipulation with data augmentation analysis based on LeRobot

claims.claim: A controlled comparison of Diffusion Policy, ACT, and VQ-BeT (using the open-source LeRobot framework, Push-T benchmark, 200K gradient steps, single RTX 3090) finds Diffusion Policy achieves the highest success rate (34%), VQ-BeT next (22%), while ACT achieves 0% success under default hyperparameters -- its success rate regresses from 2% (100K steps) to 0% (200K steps), indicating training instability rather than a fundamental architectural limitation; the Diffusion Policy vs VQ-BeT gap is statistically significant (p<0.05)
claims.direction: favors Diffusion Policy over ACT and VQ-BeT for this benchmark/framework, and flags ACT as prone to training instability (not just weaker capacity) under default LeRobot hyperparameters
claims.conditions: LeRobot framework, Push-T manipulation benchmark, single RTX 3090, 200K gradient steps, default hyperparameters

claims.claim: Enabling visual data augmentation on Diffusion Policy raises the average cumulative reward by 33.2% with no additional demonstrations, although the binary success rate is unchanged; the authors propose a practical algorithm-selection framework (MAAF) along three axes: task multimodality, inference-latency tolerance, and demonstration-data availability
claims.direction: favors adding visual data augmentation to diffusion policies (improves reward/near-miss quality even without changing binary success) and favors matching action-head choice to task multimodality/latency/data-availability constraints
claims.conditions: LeRobot Diffusion Policy, Push-T benchmark, ablation on visual augmentation only

why_deep_read: This uses the exact LeRobot framework we are likely building on and directly compares Diffusion Policy vs ACT vs VQ-BeT with statistical testing on modest hardware (single RTX 3090) -- extremely close to our own setup and directly answers our Q01 action-head question; the finding that ACT is prone to training instability (not just capacity) under default hyperparameters is a warning directly relevant to our current SmolVLA/ACT-style fine-tune, and the MAAF selection framework (multimodality/latency/data-availability) maps almost one-to-one onto our own design constraints.

title: OPEN TEACH: A Versatile Teleoperation System for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A low-cost ($500 Meta Quest 3) VR teleoperation system enabling real-time robot control at up to 90Hz with natural hand gestures showed significant improvement in teleoperation capability over the AnyTeleop framework in a user study, and the collected data was shown compatible with policy learning on 10 dexterous and contact-rich manipulation tasks across 38 tasks and multiple robot platforms
claims.direction: favors low-cost, high-frequency, immersive VR teleoperation interfaces over existing (e.g. AnyTeleop) teleoperation systems for demonstration collection quality/usability
claims.conditions: real-world user study, multiple robot platforms (Franka, xArm, Jaco, Allegro), 38 tasks

title: Predictive Inverse Dynamics Models are Scalable Learners for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Predicting actions via an inverse dynamics model conditioned on the robot's forecasted future visual states (closing the loop between a 'vision' world-model branch and an 'action' behavior-cloning branch, implemented as a Transformer named Seer, pretrained on large-scale robotic data like DROID) significantly outperforms previous methods: +13% on LIBERO-LONG, +21% on CALVIN ABC-D (new SOTA, average rollout length 4.28), and +43% in real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors combining a future-visual-state predictor with an inverse-dynamics action model (vision-action closed loop) over pure behavior cloning or pure representation-pretraining approaches
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (DROID) with little fine-tuning data, evaluated on LIBERO-LONG, CALVIN ABC-D, and real-world tasks

claims.claim: Seer exhibits superior generalization for novel objects, lighting conditions, and environments under high-intensity disturbances in real-world scenarios, compared to prior methods
claims.direction: favors the vision-forecasting + inverse-dynamics architecture for robustness to lighting/object/environment shifts
claims.conditions: real-world scenarios with novel objects, novel lighting, and environmental disturbances

why_deep_read: This paper reports large, well-quantified real-world gains (43%) and explicitly claims superior generalization to novel objects AND lighting conditions -- precisely our two biggest stated SmolVLA failure modes -- via a future-visual-prediction + inverse-dynamics design; worth reading in full to see if the architecture (and its little-fine-tuning-data requirement) is light enough to adapt to our 8GB-GPU, 50-100-demo setting.

title: BOSS: Benchmark for Observation Space Shift in Long-Horizon Task

claims.claim: When chaining individually-trained visuomotor skills for long-horizon tasks, the sequential execution of preceding skills shifts the observation space ("Observation Space Shift", OSS), disrupting subsequent skill policies; on the simplest of three introduced OSS challenges, average performance dropped 67%, 35%, 34%, and 54% (for three different Behavioral Cloning methods and OpenVLA respectively) when comparing skill performance with vs. without OSS
claims.direction: identifies observation-space shift from skill chaining as a major, largely unaddressed cause of long-horizon failure across both small BC policies and large VLA models (OpenVLA)
claims.conditions: BOSS benchmark, three BC methods plus OpenVLA

claims.claim: None of three tested mitigation strategies -- using frozen robotics-specific vision encoders, switching to 3D point-cloud input, or applying data augmentation to expand visual diversity -- was sufficient to resolve Observation Space Shift
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that better/frozen pretrained encoders, 3D point-cloud input, or visual data augmentation alone can fix distribution shift arising from skill-chaining/observation drift
claims.conditions: same BOSS benchmark and skill-chaining setting

why_deep_read: This is a rare, controlled negative result: it shows that our most likely go-to fixes for robustness (better/frozen vision encoders, 3D/point-cloud input, data augmentation) do NOT solve a major real failure mode (observation shift when skills/subtasks are chained) even for large VLA models like OpenVLA -- directly relevant to managing expectations about our own planned robustness fixes, and worth reading in full to see what, if anything, did help.

title: MOVE: A Simple Motion-Based Data Collection Paradigm for Spatial Generalization in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Individual demonstration trajectories are typically collected from a single, static spatial configuration (fixed object/target positions, fixed camera viewpoint), which restricts spatial-generalization data diversity; injecting motion into movable objects during each demonstration (MOVE) implicitly generates a dense, diverse set of spatial configurations within a single trajectory, achieving 39.1% average success on tasks requiring strong spatial generalization vs. 22.2% for the static-collection paradigm (76.1% relative improvement), and 2-5x data-efficiency gains on certain tasks
claims.direction: favors injecting object motion during demonstration collection (rather than static single-configuration demos) as a simple, low-cost way to increase effective spatial diversity per demonstration
claims.conditions: both simulation and real-world experiments, tasks requiring spatial generalization

why_deep_read: This is a simple, immediately actionable change to our own demonstration-collection procedure (move the pumpkin/tray slightly during recording rather than keeping them static) with large, well-quantified gains (76% relative improvement, 2-5x data efficiency) directly targeting our data-scarcity and spatial/camera-shift generalization problems -- very low-risk to test given our small demo budget.

title: When a Robot is More Capable than a Human: Learning from Constrained Demonstrators

claims.claim: Because constrained teleoperation interfaces (e.g. joystick control limited to a 2D plane) force suboptimal demonstrations, inferring a state-only reward (task progress signal) from demonstrations and allowing the agent to explore shorter, more efficient trajectories beyond direct imitation outperforms standard imitation learning in sample efficiency and task completion time; on a real WidowX arm the method completes the task in 12 seconds, 10x faster than behavioral cloning
claims.direction: favors going beyond direct behavior cloning (via inferred reward + exploration) over pure imitation when demonstrations are known to be suboptimal/constrained
claims.conditions: real WidowX robotic arm, constrained (e.g. joystick) teleoperation demonstrations

title: DepthCache: Depth-Guided Training-Free Visual Token Merging for Vision-Language-Action Model Inference

claims.claim: VLA inference latency is bottlenecked by the large number of visual tokens processed by the LLM backbone; DepthCache, a training-free framework that uses depth as a structural prior to apply spatially differentiated token-merge ratios (preserving the near-field workspace, compressing distant background) and exploits temporal redundancy across frames, achieves up to 1.28x inference speedup with less than 1% average success-rate degradation across three VLA models (pi_0.5, OpenVLA, GR00T) on LIBERO, versus 4-24% degradation for uniform pruning/merging baselines at comparable compression; real-world experiments show faster task throughput and more responsive closed-loop control
claims.direction: favors depth-guided, training-free visual token compression over uniform token pruning/merging for reducing VLA inference latency without retraining
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark across three VLA architectures, plus real-world physical manipulator experiments; requires depth input and no model modification

why_deep_read: A training-free (no retraining, no architecture change) technique that directly cuts VLA inference latency with minimal accuracy loss and works across three different VLA backbones is an unusually low-risk, high-value candidate to try on our laptop-GPU SmolVLA deployment to address our ~2s latency problem, and we already have a RealSense depth stream available to supply the depth prior it needs.

title: Training Vision-Language-Action Models with Dense Embodied Chain-of-Thought Supervision

claims.claim: ZR-0 uses a dual-stream architecture where a pretrained VLM ('System 2') generates structured Embodied Chain-of-Thought (ECoT) reasoning only during training, coupled via cross-attention to a Diffusion-Transformer action expert ('System 1') that produces continuous action chunks via flow matching; an attention mask restricts the action expert to prompt features only, so ECoT generation can be entirely skipped at inference time with no performance loss
claims.direction: favors training-time-only chain-of-thought supervision (dropped at inference) to gain reasoning benefits without paying an inference-time latency cost
claims.conditions: pretrained on ~60M frames/1000 hours (ProcCorpus-60M) with dense ECoT annotations; evaluated on LIBERO (single-arm), RoboTwin 2.0 (bimanual), RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop (humanoid), plus real-world xArm experiments

title: More Structure, Not More Capacity: Object-Centric Representations for Visuomotor Imitation Learning

claims.claim: With the trainable policy, goal token, rendering, and calibration held fixed and only the visual encoder changed, a frozen object-centric slot representation (SPOT: DINO ViT-B/16 + Slot Attention, no encoder fine-tuning) reaches 55.0+/-2.9% success on ManiSkill3 PickCube-v1 with held-out seeds, 22.4 percentage points above a dense DINO global-feature baseline (32.6+/-1.5%); a dense patch grid with 16x more tokens performs no better than the single global feature, showing that more visual tokens/capacity alone do not help
claims.direction: favors structuring visual features into object-centric slots over simply using more visual tokens/capacity from the same pretrained encoder (DINO)
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 PickCube-v1 (and harder StackCube-v1), frozen encoder, held-out-seed evaluation, simulation

claims.claim: Adding an explicit 2D spatial goal token and native-resolution rendering raises success to 68.7+/-4.2%, close to a privileged 3D-oracle upper bound (71.7+/-4.1%); a failure-mode taxonomy shows spatial grounding reduces near-miss (spatial-precision) failures but leaves no-grasp (object-tracking/occlusion) failures unchanged, pointing to occlusion as the main remaining bottleneck
claims.direction: favors adding explicit spatial goal conditioning for reducing spatial-precision errors specifically, while noting it does not fix occlusion-driven grasp failures
claims.conditions: same ManiSkill3 setting

title: Identifying Habit, Physics, and Nuisance in Robot World Models

claims.claim: Multimodality in teleoperated demonstrations (even under near-deterministic dynamics) mixes three distinct factors -- operator habit in action selection, shared physics, and observation nuisance; a structural causal model that freezes a shared physics readout and updates only a thin interface (rather than an entangled next-observation predictor that absorbs all three factors) improves low-shot transfer relative to training from scratch on StackCube, DROID, and RH20T, and extends from proprioception to pixel observations
claims.direction: favors explicitly disentangling operator habit / physics / observation nuisance (rather than a single entangled dynamics/world model) when using world-model-style representations for low-shot policy adaptation
claims.conditions: StackCube, DROID, RH20T benchmarks; low-shot transfer setting

title: Peg-in-hole assembly skill imitation learning method based on ProMPs under task geometric representation

claims.claim: Mapping sparse/imperfect human demonstration trajectories into a geometric feature space, aligning them via Dynamic Time Warping, and extracting Probabilistic Movement Primitives to generate many synthetic task trajectories for training a Behavior Cloning network achieves higher success rates than traditional imitation learning methods on a peg-in-hole assembly task, with reasonable generalization, validated in simulation (PyBullet+Gym) and on a real robot
claims.direction: favors augmenting sparse/imperfect human demonstrations via geometric/ProMP-based trajectory generation before behavior cloning, over training BC directly on raw sparse demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation (PyBullet+Gym) plus real-robot verification, peg-in-hole assembly task

title: ForceMimic: Force-Centric Imitation Learning with Force-Motion Capture System for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A force-aware, robot-free demonstration collection system (ForceCapture) lets an operator peel a zucchini in 5 minutes vs over 13 minutes (and frequent failure) with force-feedback teleoperation; training a hybrid force-position imitation learning model (HybridIL) on this force-centric data increases task success rates by 54.5% relatively compared to state-of-the-art pure-vision-based imitation learning on the contact-rich vegetable-peeling task
claims.direction: favors capturing and imitating force/contact information (not just vision/trajectory) for contact-rich tasks over pure-vision-based imitation learning, and favors force-aware demonstration capture over teleoperation for data collection speed
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation (vegetable peeling), requires specialized force-capture hardware not present in our sensor set

title: EvoVLA: Self-Evolving Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: VLA models suffer 'stage hallucination' in long-horizon tasks, where they exploit coarse evaluation signals to shortcut multi-step tasks and report high progress without truly completing them; EvoVLA, using a Stage-Aligned Reward with contrastive hard negatives, pose-based object-centric curiosity, and a long-horizon memory mechanism, improves average task success by 10.2 percentage points over the strongest baseline (OpenVLA-OFT), reaching 69.2%, with 1.5x better sample efficiency and reduces stage hallucination from 38.5% to 14.8%
claims.direction: favors explicit stage-progress-aware auxiliary rewards and long-horizon memory over standard coarse success signals for multi-stage manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: Discoverse-L long-horizon benchmark (3 multi-stage tasks) plus real-world deployment on 4 tasks (54.6% success, +11pts over OpenVLA-OFT)

title: Crossing the Human-Robot Embodiment Gap with Sim-to-Real RL using One Human Demonstration

claims.claim: Using only ONE RGB-D video of a human demonstrating a task (no wearables, teleoperation, or large-scale data collection), Human2Sim2Robot extracts an object pose trajectory (for an embodiment-agnostic reward) and pre-manipulation hand pose (to guide RL exploration in simulation) to train dexterous manipulation policies; in this single-human-demo regime it outperforms object-aware replay by over 55% and imitation learning by over 68% on grasping, non-prehensile manipulation, and multi-step tasks
claims.direction: favors extracting object-centric reward/reward-shaping signals from a single human video plus simulated RL over standard imitation learning when demonstration data is extremely scarce (a single demo)
claims.conditions: single human RGB-D demonstration, real-to-sim-to-real transfer, requires simulation environment and object pose estimation

title: Strategy Optimization and Imitation Learning for Bimanual Robots Based on Hierarchical Encoder-Decoder (HED)

claims.claim: A Hierarchical Encoder-Decoder model whose decoder generates trajectories using action chunking and temporal ensemble mechanisms (to reduce compounding errors) achieved 85-92% success in simulated complex fine-manipulation tasks, significantly outperforming traditional methods, and is proposed as enabling low-cost robots to perform high-precision manipulation
claims.direction: favors action chunking combined with temporal ensembling and multi-level (low/mid/high) feature encoding over traditional (non-chunked or non-hierarchical) imitation learning for precision tasks on low-cost robots
claims.conditions: simulated tests only, targeted at low-cost robot platforms

title: Robot-Gated Interactive Imitation Learning with Adaptive Intervention Mechanism

claims.claim: An Adaptive Intervention Mechanism (AIM) that learns a proxy Q-function to request human demonstrations only when the agent's actions diverge from the expert (rather than fixed/uncertainty-based schedules) reduces expert monitoring effort and achieves a 40% improvement in human take-over cost and learning efficiency compared to the uncertainty-based Thrifty-DAgger baseline, while collecting higher-quality expert demonstrations focused on safety-critical states
claims.direction: favors agent-initiated, alignment-based intervention requests over fixed or uncertainty-based schedules for reducing the human effort needed to collect high-quality corrective demonstrations
claims.conditions: expert-in-the-loop experiments, continuous and discrete control tasks

title: Self-Adaptive VLA for Robust Robot Deployment

claims.claim: VLA models are brittle to test-time hardware shifts such as actuation bias and joint encoder offsets caused by wear or imperfect calibration; a post-training recipe (Self-Adaptive VLA) that trains on shift-conditioned expert demonstrations and uses a lightweight context encoder (compressing visual observation, proprioception, and actions from the shifted environment into a latent token that modulates the policy via AdaLN) recovers over 80% of the base policy's performance under injected hardware shifts across four precision-critical bimanual/dexterous manipulation tasks, and generalizes better to new workstations than the base policy
claims.direction: favors an explicit hardware-shift-conditioned context/self-adaptation mechanism (using the policy's own rollouts as context) over a memoryless base VLA policy for robustness to actuation bias, encoder offset, and recalibration-related deployment shifts
claims.conditions: four precision-critical bimanual and dexterous manipulation tasks, injected hardware shifts (actuation bias, joint encoder offsets), new-workstation deployment

why_deep_read: This directly targets a failure mode extremely close to our own hardware reality -- SO-101's Feetech servo backlash, jitter, and calibration drift causing actuation/encoder-offset-like shifts -- with a lightweight, lightweight-context-token adaptation method recovering over 80% of lost performance; worth reading in full to see if the shift-conditioned fine-tuning recipe could be applied cheaply to our own low-cost, imprecise actuators.

title: RADAR: Closed-Loop Robotic Data Generation via Semantic Planning and Autonomous Causal Environment Reset

claims.claim: Anchored by only 2-5 3D human demonstrations as geometric priors, a fully autonomous closed-loop pipeline (VLM task generation + GNN in-context-imitation-learning policy + VLM success evaluation + FSM-driven autonomous environment reset) achieves up to 90% success on complex long-horizon tasks in simulation where traditional baselines drop to near-zero, and in real-world deployments executes diverse contact-rich skills (e.g. deformable object manipulation) via few-shot adaptation without domain-specific fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors autonomous, self-resetting closed-loop data generation/practice from only a handful (2-5) of human demonstrations over both traditional larger-scale human data collection and standard few-shot fine-tuning baselines
claims.conditions: simulation (long-horizon tasks) plus real-world deployment, only 2-5 human demonstrations as priors

title: iMaC: Translating Actions into Motion and Contact Images for Embodied World Models

claims.claim: Representing actions as raw visual (image-based) action tokens instead of low-dimensional structured action vectors (joint angles, end-effector poses) outperforms vector-based action control baselines in prediction accuracy, task success rate, and cross-scene generalization, while eliminating the need for manually defined action spaces
claims.direction: favors an image-based action representation over conventional joint-angle/end-effector vector action spaces for world-model-based control
claims.conditions: public embodied manipulation benchmarks plus real-world robotic scenarios

title: PRTS: A Primitive Reasoning and Tasking System via Contrastive Representations

claims.claim: Reformulating VLA pretraining as Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning (contrastive learning of a state-action/goal embedding space approximating log-discounted goal occupancy) instead of pure supervised behavior cloning, pretrained on 167B tokens of manipulation and embodied-reasoning data, reaches state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv, and a real-world suite of 14 complex tasks, with particularly large gains on long-horizon, contact-rich, and zero-shot novel-instruction settings
claims.direction: favors goal-reachability-aware (contrastive RL-style) pretraining over vanilla supervised behavior cloning pretraining for VLA foundation models, especially for long-horizon and novel-instruction generalization
claims.conditions: massive-scale pretraining (167B tokens), evaluated on multiple LIBERO variants, SimplerEnv, and 14 real-world tasks

title: Does Imitation Learning Preserve Temporal Robustness in Dexterous Manipulation? An Expert-Learner Comparison Across Task Execution Speeds

claims.claim: Comparing a scripted expert and an ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers) policy trained from the expert's demonstrations on a contact-rich task (ParcelStow), both achieve 100% success at nominal demonstrated speed, but performance diverges sharply as execution speed increases: at maximum demonstrated speed, expert success is 84% vs ACT's 53%; two ACT policies (different initializations) degrade 34 and 48 percentage points from nominal to max speed, vs only 16 points for the expert; equal nominal task success therefore does NOT imply the learner preserves the expert's robustness across execution speeds
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that matching expert success at nominal/demonstrated speed implies comparable robustness under faster execution; ACT-chunked policies are shown to be substantially less temporally robust than the demonstrator, with most extra failures being insertion/contact misalignments
claims.conditions: real robot task (ParcelStow, contact-rich parcel acquire-reorient-insert), ACT policy vs scripted expert, varying execution speed within the demonstrated range

why_deep_read: A rare, directly quantified controlled study of an ACT (action-chunking) policy's robustness to execution-speed changes -- exactly the architecture family relevant to our SO-101 setup and directly pertinent if we increase control frequency from 10fps to 30fps (effectively changing execution dynamics); the finding that ACT's success degrades far more than the expert's even at matched nominal performance is an important caution before we commit to an ACT-style action-chunked policy.

title: HIL-UMI: Bringing Human-in-the-Loop Post-Training of Vision-Language-Action Models to Universal Manipulation Interface

claims.claim: A robot-free human-in-the-loop post-training framework (HIL-UMI) that queries the current policy on the same observation stream as a handheld demonstration (without executing its predictions), uses an Energy Score to detect out-of-distribution discrepancy and trigger targeted data collection, and refines a progress-based advantage estimator for advantage-conditioned behavioral cloning, achieves consistent improvement over standard supervised fine-tuning on four real-world long-horizon/precise manipulation tasks, and outperforms HG-DAgger with lower per-frame collection time
claims.direction: favors targeted, policy-guided (OOD-triggered) demonstration collection combined with advantage-conditioned behavioral cloning over standard supervised fine-tuning or DAgger-style collection
claims.conditions: real-world tasks, handheld UMI-style demonstration collection (robot-free), four long-horizon/precise manipulation tasks

title: Benchmarking Smoothness and Reducing High-Frequency Oscillations in Continuous Control Policies

claims.claim: A systematic comparison of loss-regularization methods and architectural methods (plus proposed hybrids) for mitigating high-frequency action oscillations in continuous-control RL policies, benchmarked on Gymnasium environments, a complex manipulation task, and three real-world-deployed locomotion tasks, finds that a hybrid method combining both approaches performs best, improving control smoothness by 26.8% over baseline with only 2.8% worst-case performance degradation
claims.direction: favors combining loss-regularization and architectural smoothness techniques (a hybrid approach) over either alone for reducing jerky/high-frequency actions, with only minor performance cost
claims.conditions: manipulation task plus real-world hardware deployment on locomotion tasks (RL-trained policies, not diffusion/BC-specific)

title: Learning Semantic Atomic Skills for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: AtomSkill learns a semantically-aligned Atomic Skill Space (via semantic contrastive skill alignment partitioning demonstrations into variable-length atomic skills) and supports long-horizon execution via keypose imagination (predicting a skill's terminal keypose plus immediate actions, enabling progress-aware skill transitions and smooth chaining via an atomic skill diffusion sampler); this consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imitation learning and skill-based baselines in simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors semantically-aligned, variable-length atomic skill decomposition with keypose-based progress-aware chaining over both monolithic end-to-end imitation learning and prior skill-based decompositions
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world multi-task manipulation, addresses suboptimal/multimodal demonstrations and cross-task interference

title: Robotic VLA Benefits from Joint Learning with Motion Image Diffusion

claims.claim: Extending a VLA with a second 'motion head' (a Diffusion Transformer predicting optical-flow-based future motion images), trained jointly with the standard action head so the shared VLM backbone couples control with motion/dynamics knowledge, improves the success rate of pi-series VLAs to 97.5% on LIBERO and 58.0% on RoboTwin, and yields a 23% improvement in real-world performance
claims.direction: favors adding an auxiliary future-motion-prediction head (jointly trained, dropped at inference) over training the action head alone
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, RoboTwin) and real-world experiments, pi-series VLA backbone

claims.claim: Because the motion head is only used during training and not at inference, this joint-learning strategy improves performance without modifying the inference pathway or adding test-time latency to the standard VLA
claims.direction: favors auxiliary objectives that are training-only (no inference cost) over ones that add inference-time computation
claims.conditions: same setting; explicitly preserves standard VLA inference latency

title: Veo-Act: Enhancing VLA Policies with Frontier Video Models

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework using a frontier video generation model (Veo-3.1) as a high-level motion planner, handed off to a VLA policy as low-level reactive executor (via a multi-head inverse dynamics model converting generated frame pairs into actions and an interaction gate triggering handoff), improves instruction following and overall task success over a baseline VLA in novel and semantically complex manipulation settings, in both simulation and on a real robot
claims.direction: favors decoupling a high-level video-model planner from a low-level reactive VLA executor over a single VLA policy alone, for semantically complex/out-of-distribution scenarios
claims.conditions: simulation + real robot, novel/semantically complex manipulation settings

title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference

claims.claim: Embodied workloads show substantial cross-execution similarity, extending to internal model states (not just observations/actions); rMuscle exploits this via a dual-phase cache (a Context Cache reusing visual-token outputs, and an Action Cache reusing neuron activation patterns), with low overhead (online cache recomputation, sliding-window retrieval, mask sharing across denoising steps), achieving 1.29-1.42x inference speedup on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical manipulation tasks while maintaining original success rates on real-world robots
claims.direction: favors training-free, cross-execution caching of visual tokens and internal activations to reduce VLA inference latency without any accuracy loss, especially for repetitive/structured tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world physical manipulation tasks; tested on both a desktop GPU (RTX 4090) and an embedded platform (Jetson Thor)

title: Dexterous Robot Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Contact-Anchored Retargeting and Residual Policy Learning

claims.claim: A three-stage pipeline (physics refinement with a simulated MANO hand, contact-anchored retargeting that transfers only the contact structure independent of hand morphology, and a single shared residual RL policy that repairs kinematic recordings into physically consistent trajectories) converts human motion-capture recordings into dexterous robot policies with NO real-robot training data, reconstructing 25,454 single-hand trajectories (success rate 7.3%->59.3%) and 25 dual-hand tasks (16.0%->62.4%), transferring across four morphologically distinct robot hands (+62.4pp), and executing four contact-rich bimanual tasks on physical hardware with zero real-robot training data
claims.direction: favors extracting only the embodiment-invariant contact structure (not raw kinematics) from human demonstrations, repaired via one shared residual RL policy, over embodiment-specific retargeting or real-robot data collection
claims.conditions: zero real-robot training data; validated on physical hardware for four contact-rich bimanual tasks; requires human motion-capture recordings and a physics simulator

title: HoloBrain-0 Technical Report

claims.claim: An efficient 0.2B-parameter variant of the HoloBrain-0 VLA architecture (which explicitly incorporates robot embodiment priors -- multi-view camera parameters and kinematic/URDF descriptions -- to enhance 3D spatial reasoning) rivals significantly larger baseline VLA models on simulation benchmarks (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, GenieSim) and real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks, while enabling low-latency on-device deployment
claims.direction: favors explicitly encoding embodiment priors (camera geometry, kinematics) as a way to let a small (~0.2B parameter) model match much larger VLA baselines, rather than relying on scale alone
claims.conditions: pre-train-then-post-train paradigm; evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, GenieSim, and real-world long-horizon tasks; multiple embodiments supported

why_deep_read: This directly targets our Q12 model-size question with a concrete claim that a small (~0.2B parameter) model can rival much larger baselines when explicitly given embodiment priors (camera parameters, kinematics) -- exactly the kind of small, low-latency, on-device-deployable model we need for our 8GB laptop GPU; worth reading in full to see which specific embodiment-prior design choices let the small model compete.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Quantifying epistemic uncertainty in flow-matching VLA policies via velocity-field disagreement (VFD) across a small ensemble yields better-calibrated, failure-predictive uncertainty estimates; using VFD for uncertainty-guided active multitask fine-tuning (SAVE) requires at least 22% fewer expert demonstrations than baselines to adapt VLAs to new tasks, evaluated on the LIBERO benchmark
claims.direction: favors uncertainty-guided active selection of which new demonstrations to collect over passively collecting/using a fixed demonstration set, for flow-matching-based VLA policies
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, flow-matching VLA policies, active multitask fine-tuning setting

title: How to Better Train VLAs: Lessons Learned From the REAL-I Challenge at ICRA 2026

claims.claim: Comparing competing teams' approaches to learning robot policies from a fixed demonstration budget on a shared real-robot platform, the challenge organizers found that adapting to the deployment environment while retaining prior capabilities, treating demonstration quality at an appropriate temporal scale, and suppressing errors in inactive robot components were important success factors, and that offline action-prediction metrics have limited ability to forecast closed-loop success
claims.direction: favors evaluating and tuning fixed-demonstration-budget robot learning pipelines using closed-loop deployment testing rather than offline action-prediction metrics alone, and highlights deployment-adaptation and demonstration-quality curation as key levers
claims.conditions: real-robot competition (dual-arm humanoid platform), multiple competing teams' pretrained-VLA plus task-specific-IL approaches

title: Minimum Cost Averaging for Multivariate Time Series Using Constrained Dynamic Time Warping: A Case Study in Robotics

claims.claim: A Constrained-Dynamic-Time-Warping-based averaging algorithm (MCA-CDTW) that time-aligns a set of demonstration trajectories to a reference curve produces smooth mean trajectories (and extractable variability) even when there are large deviations between individual demonstrations, tested on both kinaesthetic-teaching and teleoperated-robot-arm demonstration datasets, with lower computational complexity than other averaging techniques from the literature
claims.direction: favors DTW-based trajectory alignment/averaging as a preprocessing step to obtain smoother reference trajectories from noisy/variable human demonstrations before training a policy
claims.conditions: kinaesthetic teaching dataset and a teleoperated robotic arm dataset (real demonstrations), not evaluated with a downstream learned policy in the abstract

title: GR-2: A Generative Video-Language-Action Model with Web-Scale Knowledge for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Pre-training on 38 million internet video clips (50B+ tokens) to capture world dynamics, then fine-tuning jointly for video generation and action prediction on robot trajectories, gives GR-2 an average success rate of 97.7% across more than 100 tasks and exceptional generalization to previously unseen backgrounds, environments, objects, and tasks
claims.direction: favors large-scale internet-video pretraining for world dynamics combined with joint video-generation + action-prediction fine-tuning, for both multi-task performance and generalization
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (38M video clips) plus robot-trajectory fine-tuning; over 100 tasks evaluated

claims.claim: GR-2 scales effectively with model size, with performance continuing to improve as the model grows
claims.direction: favors larger models for this pretraining paradigm (contrasts with our own compute-constrained small-model requirement)
claims.conditions: same large-scale pretraining setting

title: ViSaRL: Visual Reinforcement Learning Guided by Human Saliency

claims.claim: Incorporating human-saliency guidance into visual representation learning (for both CNN and Transformer-based encoders) significantly improves success rate, sample efficiency, and generalization of an RL agent across the DeepMind Control benchmark, simulated robot manipulation, and real-robot tasks, nearly doubling the success rate on real-robot tasks compared to a baseline that does not use saliency
claims.direction: favors guiding visual representation learning with (human) saliency toward task-relevant regions over standard full-image visual representation learning
claims.conditions: DeepMind Control benchmark, simulated manipulation, and real-robot manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Visual representations learned with saliency guidance are robust to various sources of visual perturbation, including perceptual noise and scene variations
claims.direction: favors saliency-guided representations for robustness to visual/scene perturbations
claims.conditions: same real-robot and simulated tasks, tested under perceptual noise and scene variation

title: Flow as the Cross-Domain Manipulation Interface
