claims.claim: Im2Flow2Act uses object flow (trained on human demonstration videos to generate flow from an initial scene image and task description) as a domain-bridging manipulation interface for a flow-conditioned policy trained entirely on SIMULATED robot play data; this policy deploys in the real world with minimal sim-to-real gap and requires NO real-world robot training data, demonstrated across rigid, articulated, and deformable object manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors object-flow as an intermediate, embodiment-agnostic representation bridging human video and simulated robot data over training directly on real robot teleoperation data
claims.conditions: real-world deployment (rigid, articulated, deformable objects), zero real-world robot training data, human videos + simulated robot play data only

title: Learning a thousand tasks in a day

claims.claim: Across 3450 real-world rollouts systematically comparing design choices, decomposing manipulation trajectories into sequential alignment and interaction phases plus retrieval-based generalization (rather than today's dominant single-phase monolithic behavioral-cloning policy) achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in data efficiency in the few-demonstrations-per-task regime (<10 demonstrations per task), with retrieval consistently outperforming behavioral cloning for both the alignment and interaction phases
claims.direction: contradicts the standard practice of training a single monolithic end-to-end behavior-cloning policy per task; favors decomposed alignment/interaction phases combined with retrieval-based (rather than purely learned/BC) generalization, especially when demonstrations are extremely scarce
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, <10 demonstrations per task regime, 3450+2200 real-world rollouts total

claims.claim: The resulting method (Multi-Task Trajectory Transfer, MT3) learns everyday manipulation tasks from as little as a single demonstration each, while generalizing to previously unseen object instances, enabling a robot to be taught 1000 distinct everyday tasks in under 24 hours of human demonstrator time
claims.direction: favors decomposition+retrieval methods for extreme (single-demonstration) data efficiency and rapid multi-task teaching over standard per-task BC data collection
claims.conditions: real-world, single demonstration per task, 1000 distinct tasks

why_deep_read: This is an unusually large, rigorous, real-world study (5650+ rollouts, published in Science Robotics) specifically targeting the <10-demonstrations-per-task regime that matches our own data budget, and it directly challenges the standard monolithic behavior-cloning paradigm with an order-of-magnitude data-efficiency gain from decomposition+retrieval -- this could fundamentally change our approach to the pick-and-place task (e.g., separate 'align to pumpkin' and 'place in tray' phases with retrieval) rather than training one monolithic SmolVLA policy end-to-end.

title: RhinoVLA Technical Report

claims.claim: VLM visual and context tokens are identified as a major source of VLA deployment latency (GEMM-dominated projection compute grows linearly with input token count); RhinoVLA, using a token-efficient Qwen3-VL backbone plus a continuous Action Expert and hardware-aware compilation/mixed-precision/parallel visual encoding, achieves performance comparable to pi0.5 at a similar parameter scale while reaching 11.69Hz end-to-end inference on an edge SoC (Huixi R1), meeting a 10Hz real-time closed-loop control target
claims.direction: favors reducing visual/context token count plus hardware-software co-design over larger token budgets, to hit real-time control frequencies on edge/low-power hardware
claims.conditions: edge SoC deployment (Huixi R1), comparable-parameter-scale comparison against pi0.5

title: Trajectory-Level Continuous Action Representation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: CAT encodes action trajectories within a fixed real-time interval as a set of continuous latent tokens (rather than entangling action representation with control frequency or fixed temporal parameterization), using frequency-aware positional encoding to establish a shared temporal coordinate system across different control frequencies; CAT-based policies consistently outperform both VQ-based and continuous visuomotor baselines under matched training settings across various model backbones and control frequencies, on LIBERO, MimicGen, and real-world long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors a control-frequency-agnostic, trajectory-level continuous action representation over representations tied to a fixed sampling rate or fixed temporal parameterization, especially when control frequency may vary
claims.conditions: LIBERO, MimicGen, and real-world long-horizon manipulation; tested across multiple model backbones and control frequencies

title: CLAP: Contrastive Latent Action Pretraining for Learning Vision-Language-Action Models from Human Videos

claims.claim: Prior Latent Action Models using human video suffer 'visual entanglement' (encoding appearance noise rather than manipulation skill); CLAP first learns an executable action-token vocabulary from robot trajectories (Act-VAE), then aligns human visual transitions to this vocabulary via contrastive learning, mapping unlabeled human videos into a physically-grounded latent action space rather than reconstructing appearance, enabling effective skill transfer from human videos to robotic execution while preserving instruction following and object generalization
claims.direction: favors contrastive alignment of human video to a robot-derived action-token vocabulary over reconstruction-based latent action models, to avoid encoding visual/appearance noise as if it were action information
claims.conditions: pretraining combines robot demonstrations with pseudo-labeled human videos

claims.claim: A post-training strategy combining a Rectified Flow action head (CLAP-RF) for low-latency continuous action-chunk prediction with Knowledge Matching regularization preserves pretrained semantic knowledge during target-domain fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors rectified-flow action heads for low-latency chunk prediction during deployment/fine-tuning
claims.conditions: target-domain adaptation setting

title: AIREC-Basic: Consistent Demonstration Data Collection for Imitation Learning with Redundant Robot Arms

claims.claim: Redundant (8-DoF) teleoperated arms can reduce demonstration consistency; a Soft Homing Control (SHC) strategy that mitigates redundancy while preserving intuitive operator control significantly reduces joint trajectory variance and improves task success rates for ACT, Diffusion Policy, and HSARNN across three household tasks, particularly with strong trajectory constraints and frequent contacts
claims.direction: favors actively controlling/reducing kinematic redundancy during teleoperated demonstration collection (rather than leaving it unconstrained) to improve downstream IL policy performance across multiple action-head types
claims.conditions: leader-follower teleoperation, dual-arm mobile manipulator, three household tasks, compared across ACT/Diffusion Policy/HSARNN

title: VOLT: Vision and Language Trajectory Segmentation for Faster-than-Demonstration Policies

claims.claim: Uniformly downsampling recorded demonstrations to train policies that execute faster than the human demonstration pace can be problematic because some task segments (unconstrained motion) can be safely sped up while others (object interactions, fine manipulation) require the original slower, precise motion; VOLT, a vision-and-language trajectory segmentation method, identifies which segments require careful precision and selectively downsamples the rest, producing reformatted trajectories usable with standard imitation learning (e.g. diffusion policies) that execute tasks faster while maintaining strong performance, outperforming baseline segmentation approaches
claims.direction: favors segment-aware (rather than uniform) downsampling of demonstrations, informed by vision-language reasoning about which phases tolerate speed-up, over naive uniform downsampling for training faster-than-demonstration policies
claims.conditions: used with standard imitation learning approaches such as diffusion policies

title: What's the Move? Hybrid Imitation Learning via Salient Points

claims.claim: SPHINX, a hybrid imitation learning policy combining multimodal observations (point clouds + wrist images) with a hybrid action space (low-frequency sparse waypoints for long-range free-space motion, high-frequency dense end-effector movements for precise contact phases, switching based on inferred 3D 'salient points'), achieves 86.7% success across 4 real-world and 2 simulated tasks, outperforming the next-best SOTA imitation learning baseline by 41.1% relatively across 440 real-world trials
claims.direction: favors a hybrid action space (sparse waypoints + dense EE control, switched via salient-point proximity) and hybrid point-cloud+wrist-image observation fusion over a single fixed action representation or single-camera-modality policy
claims.conditions: 440 real-world trials across 4 real + 2 sim tasks, point-cloud plus wrist-camera-image observations

claims.claim: SPHINX additionally generalizes to novel viewpoints, visual distractors, spatial arrangements, and execution speeds, with a 1.7x speedup over the most competitive baseline
claims.direction: favors the salient-point-anchored hybrid approach for robustness to viewpoint shift, distractor objects, spatial rearrangement, and execution-speed variation
claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation, explicit tests of viewpoint/distractor/speed generalization

why_deep_read: This paper hits nearly every one of our core questions at once -- hybrid sparse/dense action space (Q01/Q02), point-cloud + wrist-camera fusion matching our exact fixed+wrist camera setup (Q04/Q11), and explicit tested robustness to viewpoint shift, distractors, and speed changes (Q14) -- backed by a large (440-trial) real-world evaluation with a strong quantified margin (+41.1% relative) over the best prior method; this is one of the most comprehensively applicable papers in the batch and worth a full read before finalizing our action-space and camera-fusion design.

title: 3D Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Incorporating a compact 3D visual representation (extracted from sparse point clouds via an efficient point encoder) into a diffusion policy (DP3) handles most of 72 simulation tasks with just 10 demonstrations, surpassing baselines by a 24.2% relative improvement, and on 4 real robot tasks achieves 85% success given only 40 demonstrations of each task, with excellent generalization across space, viewpoint, appearance, and instance
claims.direction: favors compact 3D point-cloud representations over 2D-only visual representations for imitation-learning diffusion policies, especially for data efficiency and generalization
claims.conditions: 72 simulation tasks (10 demos each) plus 4 real robot tasks (40 demos each)

claims.claim: In real robot experiments, DP3 rarely violates safety requirements, in contrast to baseline methods (including 2D-based policies) which frequently do, necessitating human intervention
claims.direction: favors 3D point-cloud-based diffusion policies over baseline (2D) methods for safer, more reliable real-world deployment
claims.conditions: real robot tasks, comparison against baseline (non-3D) imitation learning methods

why_deep_read: A highly-cited, foundational result directly on our Q04 question (3D/point-cloud vs RGB) at a data scale (10-40 demonstrations) very close to our own 50-100 demo budget, with strong generalization claims across space/viewpoint/appearance/instance that mirror our stated lighting/object/camera-shift failures; since we have a RealSense with depth available, this is highly actionable and worth reading in full before deciding whether to add point-cloud input.

title: 3D-VLA: A 3D Vision-Language-Action Generative World Model

claims.claim: Building a VLA on top of a 3D-based large language model, with interaction tokens engaging the embodied environment and embodied diffusion models predicting future goal images and point clouds (aligned into the LLM), significantly improves reasoning, multimodal generation, and planning capabilities in embodied environments compared to 2D-input-only VLA models
claims.direction: favors integrating explicit 3D perception and a generative world model (predicting future 3D states) into the VLA backbone over 2D-only, direct perception-to-action VLA models
claims.conditions: held-in dataset evaluation, large-scale curated 3D embodied instruction dataset

title: Versatile and Generalizable Manipulation via Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning with Grounded Object Detection

claims.claim: Using a pre-trained object detection model to identify a target object from a text prompt and generate a mask for goal conditioning (object-agnostic cues) in Goal-Conditioned RL maintains a ~90% success rate in grasping both in-distribution and out-of-distribution objects, while also achieving faster convergence to higher returns, in a simulated reach-and-grasp task
claims.direction: favors mask-based (object-agnostic, detector-grounded) goal conditioning over object-specific goal representations for generalizing to novel/out-of-distribution objects
claims.conditions: simulated reach-and-grasp task, text-prompted object identification

title: GSR: Learning Structured Reasoning for Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: Explicitly modeling world-state evolution as transitions over semantically grounded scene graphs (rather than implicitly embedding task reasoning in high-dimensional latent representations) enables step-wise reasoning about action preconditions, consequences, and goal satisfaction, and significantly improves zero-shot generalization and long-horizon task completion over prompting-based baselines across RLBench, LIBERO, a GSR-benchmark, and real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit, structured (scene-graph) world-state representations as an inductive bias over purely latent/implicit world-state reasoning for long-horizon generalization
claims.conditions: RLBench, LIBERO, GSR-benchmark, and real-world tasks; requires a large supervised dataset (Manip-Cognition-1.6M) for training the reasoning module

title: Rotation-Aware Point-Cloud Embeddings for Vision-Based In-Hand Reorientation

claims.claim: Generic visual point-cloud pretraining is insufficient for current-vs-goal point-cloud comparison tasks because it discards task-relevant state and preserves only shape features; a rotation-aware point-cloud embedding, explicitly calibrated so Euclidean latent distance matches SO(3) geodesic error between object orientations, allows a model-free RL policy to match privileged-state and distillation-based baselines without needing explicit pose, relative pose, dense flow, or teacher-action supervision
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that generic (task-agnostic) point-cloud pretraining is sufficient; favors task-specific representation learning (here, rotation-calibrated embeddings) explicitly designed around the downstream control signal needed
claims.conditions: in-hand reorientation experiments (dexterous hand), simulation

title: MemoryVAM: Integrating Memory into Video Action Model for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Video-world-model policies conditioned on only a short observation window render long-horizon manipulation non-Markovian when the correct action depends on earlier, no-longer-visible events (causal confusion); MemoryVAM adds an episodic memory mechanism (a Perceiver-based Recap Compressor mapping per-frame CLIP embeddings into compact memory tokens, plus a Cue Gate estimating task completion, injected into both the video backbone and action decoder, trained with video prediction + delta-reconstruction + episode-boundary supervision, needing no per-frame progress labels) that improves average success on LIBERO-Mem from 5% to 42.5%, and achieves 78.3%/80.0%/75.0% success on real-robot counting, spatial-recall, and sequential-tracking tasks respectively
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit episodic-memory mechanism (compact learned memory tokens injected into both perception and action modules) over short-window/memoryless conditioning for tasks requiring long-horizon history (counting, recall, tracking)
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Mem benchmark plus real-robot tasks explicitly requiring memory of past events (counting, spatial recall, sequential tracking); applies to both UNet and DiT video-model backbones

why_deep_read: An 8x jump in success (5% to 42.5%) on a memory-specific benchmark, plus strong real-robot validation, is one of the largest and most specific quantified results for Q07 (observation history/memory) in the whole batch; directly relevant if our single-current-frame SmolVLA fine-tune is suffering from causal confusion or forgetting during the pick-and-place-in-tray sequence, and the mechanism is described as requiring no per-frame progress labels, which fits our limited-annotation setting.

title: HumDex: Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation Made Easy

claims.claim: A two-stage imitation learning framework that first pre-trains on diverse human motion data (collected via a portable IMU-based teleoperation system) to learn generalizable priors, then fine-tunes on robot data to bridge the embodiment gap, significantly improves generalization to new configurations, objects, and backgrounds with minimal additional data acquisition cost
claims.direction: favors pretraining on cheaply-collected human motion data followed by robot-data fine-tuning over training only on robot-specific demonstrations, for generalization at low data-collection cost
claims.conditions: humanoid whole-body dexterous manipulation, portable teleoperation system

title: RoboPaint: From Human Demonstration to Any Robot and Any View

claims.claim: A real-sim-real pipeline that captures multimodal human demonstrations (RGB-D, glove joint angles, tactile), tactile-aware-retargets them to robot dex-hand states, and renders the retargeted trajectories in photorealistic Isaac Sim (rather than direct robot teleoperation) produces training data on which retargeted dex-hand trajectories achieve 84% success across 10 diverse real-world object manipulation tasks, and VLA policies (pi0.5) trained EXCLUSIVELY on this generated data achieve 80% average success on three representative real-world tasks (pick-and-place, pushing, pouring)
claims.direction: favors a real-sim-real, tactile-aware demonstration-generation pipeline over direct robot teleoperation for scaling training data, with reported minimal performance loss
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, VLA (pi0.5) trained only on generated (non-teleoperated) data

title: COBALT: Crowdsourcing Robot Learning via Cloud-Based Teleoperation with Smartphones

claims.claim: A scalable, load-balanced cloud teleoperation platform enabling phone-based teleoperation (no specialized hardware) sustains dozens of concurrent users at 20Hz with sub-100ms latency; a user study found phone-based teleoperation performs comparably to or better than specialized hardware, and a structured user-training curriculum significantly improves data-collection quality, enabling a crowdsourced pilot dataset of 7500+ demonstrations (50+ hours) across nine countries in five days
claims.direction: favors low-cost, widely-accessible smartphone-based teleoperation (with structured operator training and real-time quality filtering) over specialized teleoperation hardware for scaling demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated teleoperation, cloud-based infrastructure, user study

title: ActionCache: Training-Free Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Models with Action Caching and Refinement

claims.claim: The iterative denoising process in flow-matching-based VLA action heads is a major inference-latency bottleneck; ActionCache, a plug-and-play external cache storing intermediate actions with compact multimodal keys (retrievable across episodes or even different tasks) to warm-start generation from the vicinity of the target action, maintains high task success rates while achieving action-head inference acceleration of up to 10.44x for pi_0.5 and 40.17x for GR00T-N1.6, in both simulation and real-world environments
claims.direction: favors training-free action-caching/warm-starting of the denoising process over running full iterative denoising from scratch each timestep, for large latency reductions with minimal accuracy loss
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world environments, evaluated on pi_0.5 and GR00T-N1.6 flow-matching VLAs

title: What Matters, When? Diagnosing and Improving Conditional Visual Grounding in Visuomotor Imitation Policies

claims.claim: Visuomotor imitation policies (studied using Action Chunking with Transformers, ACT) that perform well in-distribution fail when visually similar distractor objects or receptacles are introduced; distractor sensitivity is specific to both the type of visual similarity (color vs. shape) and the manipulation stage (picking vs. placement), showing that visual distractors can cause incorrect object/destination selection even when the underlying manipulation skill remains intact
claims.direction: identifies that failures under distractor objects are a distinct 'conditional visual grounding' problem (not a general skill failure), varying by similarity type and task phase -- directly matching a 'different-looking object confuses the policy' failure pattern
claims.conditions: ACT policy, simulation and real UR3e robot, controlled color/shape-similarity distractors; also observed in a pretrained VLA on a state-conditioned instrument-handling task

claims.claim: Three complementary interventions -- distractor augmentation, phase-dependent attention regularization, and appearance-based visual prompting -- substantially improve robustness/target-selection accuracy while preserving the spatial information required for control, in both simulation and on the physical UR3e
claims.direction: favors combining distractor-focused data augmentation with attention regularization and visual prompting (rather than only more data or a better encoder alone) to fix distractor-induced failures
claims.conditions: same ACT-based real/sim setting

why_deep_read: This is a rare, precisely-targeted diagnosis of exactly our stated failure mode -- the policy breaking when a 'different-looking pumpkin' or distractor object appears -- using ACT (a strong candidate action-head family for our setup), with real robot (UR3e) validation of three concrete, complementary fixes; reading the full methodology could let us directly apply the same interventions to our SO-101 pumpkin-pick-and-place task.

title: PRISE: LLM-Style Sequence Compression for Learning Temporal Action Abstractions in Control

claims.claim: Applying byte-pair-encoding-style sequence compression (borrowed from LLM tokenization) to continuous-action-quantized sequences (PRISE) discovers variable-time-span high-level skills from a multitask set of robotic manipulation demonstrations that significantly boost the performance of both multitask imitation learning and few-shot imitation learning on unseen tasks
claims.direction: favors learning temporal action abstractions via sequence-compression/tokenization methods over fixed-length action chunking for multitask and few-shot imitation learning
claims.conditions: multitask robotic manipulation demonstrations, few-shot transfer to unseen tasks

title: Enhancing Robustness in Language-Driven Robotics: A Modular Approach to Failure Reduction

claims.claim: A modular architecture around a smaller, locally-executable LLM (adding an 'expected outcomes' module to prevent subgoal mischaracterization and a feedback mechanism for real-time error recovery, formalized within a goal-conditioned POMDP) achieves significantly improved success rates for pick-and-place and manipulation tasks, surpassing baselines that use larger language models, while running efficiently and locally on physical robots
claims.direction: favors a smaller LLM plus targeted architectural fixes (expected-outcomes module, feedback/error-recovery) over simply using a larger LLM for robust language-driven task execution
claims.conditions: simulation and physical robot experiments, pick-and-place and manipulation tasks

title: Novel Demonstration Generation with Gaussian Splatting Enables Robust One-Shot Manipulation

claims.claim: RoboSplat generates diverse, visually realistic demonstrations by directly editing a 3D-Gaussian-Splatting reconstruction of the real scene (rather than 2D RGB-space augmentation or inaccurate physics-simulation Real2Sim2Real), augmenting across six generalization axes (object type, scene appearance, robot embodiment, object pose, lighting conditions, camera viewpoint, and novel object content) using five techniques (3D Gaussian replacement, equivariant transforms, visual attribute editing, novel view synthesis, 3D content generation)
claims.direction: favors directly manipulating a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene reconstruction for demonstration augmentation over both 2D RGB-space augmentation and physics-simulator-based Real2Sim2Real pipelines
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across six generalization types

claims.claim: While policies trained on hundreds of real-world demonstrations plus additional 2D data augmentation achieve an average success rate of 57.2% under diverse disturbances, RoboSplat attains 87.8% using only ONE real demonstration (one-shot) across the same six generalization types
claims.direction: favors 3DGS-based one-shot augmentation as dramatically more data-efficient than collecting hundreds of demonstrations plus standard 2D augmentation
claims.conditions: real-world, one-shot (single demonstration) setting vs. hundreds-of-demonstrations baseline

why_deep_read: An 87.8% one-shot success rate vs. 57.2% from hundreds of demos plus 2D augmentation is one of the largest, most directly relevant quantified results in the batch for our Q05 augmentation decision, and it explicitly includes lighting-condition and camera-viewpoint generalization -- exactly our stated SmolVLA failure modes; worth reading in full to assess whether a 3DGS reconstruction of our own pumpkin/tray scene is feasible on our hardware to generate similar low-shot augmented data.

title: H-RDT: Human Manipulation Enhanced Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: H-RDT, a 2B-parameter diffusion transformer using flow matching, pretrains on large-scale egocentric human manipulation videos with paired 3D hand-pose annotations, then cross-embodiment-fine-tunes on robot-specific data via modular action encoders/decoders; this outperforms training from scratch and existing SOTA methods (pi0, RDT), with improvements of 13.9% (simulation) and 40.5% (real-world) over training from scratch, across single-task, multitask, few-shot, and robustness evaluations
claims.direction: favors large-scale human-manipulation-video pretraining plus modular cross-embodiment fine-tuning over training a robot policy from scratch or using existing cross-embodiment robot-only pretraining
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world, single-task/multitask/few-shot/robustness evaluations, bimanual manipulation

title: RoboClaw: An Agentic Framework for Scalable Long-Horizon Robotic Tasks

claims.claim: Entangled Action Pairs (coupling forward manipulation behaviors with inverse recovery actions to form self-resetting loops) enable continuous on-policy data acquisition and iterative policy refinement with minimal human intervention; in real-world manipulation experiments this achieves a 25% improvement in success rate over baseline methods on long-horizon tasks and reduces human time investment by 53.7%
claims.direction: favors self-resetting (forward+inverse recovery action pair) autonomous data collection loops over conventional manually-reset data collection pipelines
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, long-horizon, VLM-driven unified controller

title: PhysMani: Physics-principled 3D World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Coupling a physics-principled 3D Gaussian world model (learning a divergence-free Gaussian velocity field via online optimization for physically-grounded future dynamics prediction) with a future-aware action policy (integrating predicted 3D scene dynamics via learnable token-based cross-attention) achieves a superior success rate over strong baselines on a new 16-task dynamic-manipulation benchmark, in both simulation and real-world robot experiments
claims.direction: favors physics-grounded 3D world models (not just image-based world models) for manipulating fast, dynamically moving targets
claims.conditions: PhysMani-Bench (16 tasks), simulation + real-world

title: Complexity-Aware Policy via Heterogeneous Experts for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Robotic manipulation tasks have imbalanced complexity at inter-task, intra-task, and noise-timestep levels; a Complexity-Aware Policy (CAP) that combines Rectified Flow with a Transformer backbone and a Mixture-of-Heterogeneous-Experts structure, dynamically adjusting model capacity based on assessed task complexity (e.g. object counts, precision needs), achieves faster convergence, more efficient computational resource usage, and state-of-the-art performance on CALVIN, LIBERO, and SimplerEnv, consistently outperforming baselines across six real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors dynamically allocating more/less model capacity per-task/per-timestep (mixture-of-experts) based on assessed complexity, rather than a fixed uniform model capacity/budget for all tasks and timesteps
claims.conditions: CALVIN, LIBERO, SimplerEnv benchmarks plus six real-world experiments

title: Learning to See While Learning to Act: Diffusion Models for Active Perception in Robot Imitation

claims.claim: See2Act conditions action prediction on a sequence of actively-inferred viewpoints at test time (coupling action denoising with viewpoint refinement), trained using camera poses anchored to keyframe actions from offline demonstrations (implicitly learning where to look while learning how to act); it recovers informative viewpoints under severe occlusion in Ravens and improves RLBench performance by up to 34% over prior methods, and after collecting only 50 real-world demonstrations in a digital twin, achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on pick-and-place tasks using depth observations, handling significant occlusions
claims.direction: favors jointly learning active viewpoint/camera-pose selection together with action prediction (rather than a fixed camera viewpoint) for robustness under occlusion
claims.conditions: Ravens and RLBench simulation, plus zero-shot sim-to-real transfer from only 50 demonstrations using depth observations

title: SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Aligning intermediate visual features of a VLA (pi_0) with dense object-level 3D representations extracted by a frozen 3D teacher (SAM3D) during TRAINING ONLY lets the policy internalize target-object 3D information while preserving the original RGB-language-to-action inference pipeline -- requiring no depth, point clouds, masks, SAM3D, or additional 3D modules at test time -- achieving 99.1% on LIBERO and an average rollout length of 4.11 on CALVIN, with real-world gains especially in long-horizon multi-subtask scenarios
claims.direction: favors injecting 3D object-centric supervision only during training (zero added test-time cost/sensing) over requiring explicit 3D input (depth/point cloud) at inference for object-centric grounding under occlusion, pose variation, and scale changes
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN simulation benchmarks, plus real-world long-horizon multi-subtask experiments; base policy pi_0

title: WARPD: World model Assisted Reactive Policy Diffusion

claims.claim: Diffusion Policy suffers a trade-off between performance and action horizon (fewer diffusion queries mean larger trajectory chunks that accumulate tracking errors); WARPD instead generates closed-loop policies (neural-network weights) directly by learning behavioral distributions in parameter space rather than trajectory space, outperforming Diffusion Policy in long-horizon and perturbed environments while matching its multitask performance
claims.direction: favors generating closed-loop policy weights (parameter-space diffusion) over generating open-loop action trajectories (trajectory-space diffusion) for long-horizon robustness to perturbation
claims.conditions: long-horizon and perturbed manipulation/locomotion environments, multitask comparison against Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: WARPD achieves multitask performance on par with Diffusion Policy while requiring only about 1/45th of the inference-time FLOPs per step
claims.direction: favors this closed-loop parameter-space approach for drastically reduced inference computation/latency versus standard trajectory-diffusion policies
claims.conditions: same comparison setting

title: Human2Robot: Learning Robot Actions from Paired Human-Robot Videos

claims.claim: Treating fine-grained human-robot alignment as a conditional video generation problem -- using a Video Prediction Model trained on a new precisely-synchronized third-person human-robot video dataset (H&R, 2,600 episodes via VR teleoperation) to generate robot video from human input, which then guides a decoupled action decoder -- captures frame-level dynamics that coarsely-aligned video-pair methods miss
claims.direction: favors frame-level (not just task/global-level) human-robot video alignment via conditional video generation for distilling manipulation knowledge from human demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, requires a precisely time-synchronized human-robot video dataset

claims.claim: This approach achieves high performance on seen tasks and exhibits significant one-shot generalization to novel positions, objects, instances, and even new task categories
claims.direction: favors frame-level human-video-conditioned action generation for extreme (one-shot) generalization to novel objects/positions/tasks
claims.conditions: real-world one-shot generalization tests

title: Sequentially Teaching Sequential Tasks (ST)2: Teaching Robots Long-Horizon Manipulation Skills

claims.claim: In a real user study with 16 participants teaching a long-horizon restocking task, a sequential (step-by-step, keypoint-segmented) demonstration-teaching paradigm showed superior task performance for most users (10 of 16) compared with the traditional monolithic (whole-trajectory-at-once) teaching paradigm (5 of 16, with one tie), though some teachers subjectively preferred the monolithic approach for its simplicity
claims.direction: favors segmenting long-horizon demonstrations into sequential, keypoint-structured teaching episodes over monolithic single-pass demonstrations, for most users/tasks, though not universally preferred
claims.conditions: real user study (16 participants), realistic retail restocking task

title: Genie Centurion: Accelerating Scalable Real-World Robot Training with Human Rewind-and-Refine Guidance

claims.claim: GCENT, a data-collection paradigm where an imperfect deployed policy is corrected via a rewind mechanism (reverting to a prior state on failure) plus teleoperator corrective demonstrations, with a Task Sentinel module autonomously predicting task success/soliciting intervention (enabling one-human-to-many-robots supervision), achieves up to 40% higher task success rates than state-of-the-art data collection methods and reaches comparable performance using less than half the data on long-horizon and precise tasks
claims.direction: favors interactive rewind-and-refine, policy-in-the-loop data collection (with autonomous intervention-soliciting) over standard one-shot human teleoperation data collection for both quality and data efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, one-human-to-many-robots supervision scheme, long-horizon and precise tasks

title: WeaveLA: Event Driven Cross-Subtask Latent Memory Weaving for Repetitive Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Short-window VLA policies lack an explicit channel for routing information across sub-task boundaries, making them brittle exactly where a stage depends on what was just completed (e.g. repetitive sub-tasks); WeaveLA compresses each completed segment into latent tokens (via query-driven attention pooling triggered at sub-goal completion events) and routes them directly into the action-generation path of the next sub-task, on top of a frozen pi_0.5 backbone; on the hardest repetition slice (SwingXtimes, N=3) success rises from 0% to 47.8%, while single-execution episodes are unchanged, with gains confined specifically to tasks whose causal structure requires cross-subtask information
claims.direction: favors an event-triggered (sub-goal-completion-based), action-side cross-subtask memory channel over either no memory or memory that writes every frame/retrieves from demonstration-time stages, for repetitive/counting-style long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: RoboMME benchmark, pi_0.5 backbone, stratified per-episode paired analysis

title: Influence of Gripper Design on Human Demonstration Quality for Robot Learning

claims.claim: In an 8-participant user study comparing UMI-style handheld gripper tools (distributed-load grippers, concentrated-load grippers, and bare hands) for demonstrating a bandage-opening task, concentrated-load grippers improved performance (success rate, time, damage, perceived workload) relative to distributed-load grippers but remained substantially slower and less effective than using bare hands
claims.direction: favors ergonomic/mechanical refinement of handheld demonstration-collection tools (load distribution design) to reduce operator burden and improve demonstration quality, while noting even the best handheld tool still lags behind bare-hand demonstration
claims.conditions: real user study (8 participants), handheld UMI-style gripper tool, healthcare/medical packaging task

title: FineVLA: Fine-Grained Instruction Alignment for Steerable Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Training VLA policies with a controlled mixture of fine-grained (execution-detail: active arm, approach direction, contact region) and raw goal-level language instructions, rather than goal-level language alone, does not sacrifice goal-level success (fine-grained-only improves over raw-only by +1.4 to +8.1 success-rate points) and the two instruction granularities are complementary, following an inverted-U trend peaking around a 1:2 to 1:1 fine-grained:raw ratio; the best mixed setting reaches 86.8%/82.5% success in RoboTwin simulation and 62.7/100 in real-world dual-arm manipulation, versus 49.9 for raw-only in the real world
claims.direction: favors augmenting goal-level language instructions with fine-grained execution-detail language (specifying how, not just what) over goal-level-only conditioning
claims.conditions: RoboTwin simulation and real-world dual-arm manipulation, held-out benchmark with human-verified fine-grained annotations

claims.claim: The largest real-world gains from fine-grained supervision appear specifically on steerable-control factors where goal-level instructions give no guidance: pose (+23 points), color (+18), and approach direction (+18)
claims.direction: favors fine-grained language specifically for steering execution-level choices (pose, approach direction) not expressible in goal-level instructions alone
claims.conditions: same real-world dual-arm evaluation

title: Scaling Bimanual Household Manipulation from 1,500 hours of Demonstrations to On-Policy Corrections

claims.claim: Training XR-2, a VLA model, on a large released corpus (1,500 hours of bimanual household demonstrations) and systematically varying both the amount of expert demonstration data and the amount of post-training DAgger correction data (from real-time human interventions), task success rate improves steadily and shows a clear, consistent scaling trend over the probed data ranges for both axes
claims.direction: favors continued scaling of both raw expert demonstration volume and on-policy DAgger-style correction data as both contributing positively (no saturation observed in the tested range) to bimanual manipulation performance
claims.conditions: large-scale (1,500-hour) demonstration corpus, systematic data-scaling ablation across both demonstration volume and correction-data volume

title: Demonstration Synthesis from a Single Scan via Gaussian Splatting for Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: GaussianFactory reconstructs a scene as an editable 3D Gaussian Splatting replica from a SINGLE video scan (no physics engine in the generation loop except a once-pretrained contact model for grasp formation), plans grasps/trajectories kinematically on the reconstruction, and renders photorealistic demonstrations matching the target environment; a standard diffusion policy trained solely on these synthesized demonstrations achieves 95.1% success in a simulated stand-in setup and 84.2% success on a real UR10e robot
claims.direction: favors single-scan, physics-light 3D-Gaussian-Splatting-based demonstration synthesis (rather than full physics simulation or manual demonstration collection) for training visuomotor policies
claims.conditions: end-to-end scan-to-deployment workflow, real UR10e robot; policy trained exclusively on synthesized data

title: SkillMimicGen: Automated Demonstration Generation for Efficient Skill Learning and Deployment

claims.claim: SkillMimicGen segments a small set of human demonstrations into manipulation skills, adapts them to new contexts, and stitches them together via free-space transit/transfer motion to automatically generate large demonstration datasets; from just 60 human demonstrations it generates over 24,000 demonstrations across 18 task variants in simulation, and agents trained on this data are on average 24% more successful than a state-of-the-art data-generation framework, including in scenes with large variation and clutter; it also shows zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a long-horizon real-world assembly task after training on 3 real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors automated skill-based demonstration generation (segment, adapt, stitch) from a small human-demo seed set over both manual large-scale data collection and prior automated data-generation baselines
claims.conditions: 60 human seed demonstrations -> 24K generated demonstrations, 18 simulated task variants, plus 3 real-world tasks and one long-horizon real-world assembly task

claims.claim: A Hybrid Skill Policy (HSP) framework learns skill initiation, control, and termination components separately from SkillGen-generated data, enabling skills to be sequenced via motion planning at test time
claims.direction: favors decomposing policies into separately-learned initiation/control/termination skill components (sequenced at test time) over a single monolithic end-to-end policy for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: same SkillGen-generated dataset setting

why_deep_read: Starting from only 60 human demonstrations -- almost exactly our own data budget (50-100) -- and automatically amplifying them into 24,000+ demonstrations with a 24% success-rate improvement over prior automated generation, plus real-world zero-shot transfer, makes this one of the most directly transferable data-augmentation references for our exact data-scarcity situation; worth reading in full to see whether the skill-segmentation-and-stitching approach is implementable for our two-stage pumpkin pick-and-place-in-tray task.

title: Multimodal fusion with vision-language-action models for robotic manipulation: A systematic review

claims.claim: A meta-analytic benchmarking protocol across 102 VLA models, 26 datasets, and 12 simulation platforms finds that diffusion-based action decoders demonstrate superior cross-domain transfer and robustness compared to autoregressive action heads, and that hierarchical/late-fusion multimodal architectures achieve the highest manipulation success and generalization compared to early/simple fusion strategies
claims.direction: favors diffusion-based action decoders over autoregressive decoders, and hierarchical/late multimodal fusion over early/simple fusion, based on a cross-paper meta-analysis rather than a single controlled experiment
claims.conditions: meta-analysis/systematic review across 102 models, 26 datasets, 12 simulators (not a single controlled study)

title: LiteFlow: A Low-Cost Vision-Based Measurement and Control Framework for Bimanual Household Manipulation

claims.claim: On a real low-cost bimanual robot platform, LiteFlow fuses multi-view RGB images and robot states, models future action chunks via conditional flow matching, and applies a model-agnostic Zero-interpolation Bezier Optimizer (ZIBO) to smooth trajectories while preserving key poses; this improves task success rate and execution stability over representative imitation-learning baselines, and ZIBO significantly reduces joint acceleration fluctuations
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight, model-agnostic post-hoc trajectory smoothing step (ZIBO) on top of chunked flow-matching action generation, over using the raw predicted action chunks directly, to reduce jitter on low-cost hardware
claims.conditions: real low-cost bimanual household manipulation platform

title: Foundational World Models Accurately Detect Bimanual Manipulator Failures

claims.claim: Training a probabilistic, history-informed world model within the compressed latent space of a pretrained vision foundation model (NVIDIA Cosmos Tokenizer), and using its uncertainty estimates as conformal-prediction non-conformity scores, enables a runtime failure monitor that considerably outperforms statistical anomaly/OOD-detection baselines while requiring about 1/20th of the trainable parameters of the next-best learning-based approach, yet still outperforming it by 3.8% in failure-detection rate
claims.direction: favors building failure/anomaly detectors on top of a compact latent world model in a pretrained foundation-model's representation space, over both classical statistical detectors and larger dedicated learned detectors
claims.conditions: simulated Push-T environment and a new Bimanual Cable Manipulation dataset with annotated failures

title: Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Applying activation injection, sparse autoencoders, and linear probes to six VLA models (80M-7B params, including SmolVLA, pi_0.5, GR00T, X-VLA) across 394,000+ rollouts on four benchmarks shows the VISUAL pathway dominates action generation across ALL architectures: injecting baseline activations into null-prompt episodes recovers near-identical behavior, and cross-task activation injection steers the robot toward the SOURCE task's positions in 99.8% of X-VLA episodes, revealing 'spatially bound motor programs tied to scene coordinates' rather than abstract task representations
claims.direction: favors treating VLA action generation as fundamentally visually/spatially driven (motor programs bound to scene coordinates), with language playing a comparatively minor causal role in the action pathway itself, across all tested architectures
claims.conditions: six VLA models spanning 80M-7B params (including SmolVLA), four benchmarks, mechanistic interpretability methods (not a behavioral ablation)

claims.claim: Language sensitivity depends on TASK STRUCTURE, not model design or size: when the visual scene uniquely specifies the task, language instructions are effectively ignored by the policy, but when multiple goals share the same visual scene, language becomes essential (e.g. X-VLA on libero_goal: 94%->10% success under wrong prompts, vs. libero_object: 60-100% regardless of prompt correctness); in all three multi-pathway architectures tested (pi_0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T), expert (action) pathways encode motor programs while VLM pathways encode goal semantics, occupying separable activation subspaces
claims.direction: favors expecting language conditioning to matter only when the visual scene is genuinely ambiguous between multiple valid goals/objects -- otherwise language instructions may be largely ignored by the action pathway regardless of how they are encoded
claims.conditions: same six-model, four-benchmark mechanistic study, explicitly includes SmolVLA

why_deep_read: This is a mechanistic-interpretability study that directly includes SmolVLA (our current base model) and reveals that language conditioning may be effectively ignored by the action pathway unless the visual scene is genuinely ambiguous between multiple objects/goals; this has direct, immediate implications for whether adding a second object with language conditioning (per our stated future plan) will actually work with SmolVLA's architecture, and is worth reading in full before investing in a language-conditioning approach.

title: Beyond World-Frame Action Heads: Motion-Centric Action Frames for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: MCF-Proto, a lightweight action head that predicts a per-step SO(3) rotation to define a motion-centric local action frame and composes actions from learned prototypes in that local frame (mapped back to world frame for training, using only standard demonstrations with no auxiliary supervision), induces a stable emergent geometric structure aligned with demonstrated end-effector motion, yields more compact action representations, and improves robustness especially under geometric perturbations, compared to standard fixed-world-frame action heads
claims.direction: favors predicting actions in a learned, motion-centric local frame (rather than a fixed world coordinate frame) for improved compactness and robustness to geometric perturbation
claims.conditions: standard demonstration data, no auxiliary supervision required

title: Look Before You Leap: Distilling Tree Search into Action Evaluation for Frozen VLA Models

claims.claim: A diagnostic pass@k study shows a frozen VLA's overall success rate rises from 33% at pass@1 to 92% at pass@32, indicating that competent behaviors already exist in its output distribution and the main bottleneck is ACTION EVALUATION/SELECTION, not action generation; SVA distills Monte-Carlo-tree-search-explored trajectories (with empirical returns) into a lightweight Q-value model that re-ranks candidate actions from a frozen VLA at deployment (no simulator needed), enabling a 9B-parameter VLA to outperform a 27B-parameter VLA by 7 points while using 27% LOWER inference latency
claims.direction: favors scaling test-time action evaluation (via a small, distilled value model re-ranking multiple sampled candidates) over scaling base VLA model size, as a more cost-effective way to improve both performance and generalization
claims.conditions: embodied manipulation benchmarks with MCTS-based training-time exploration in simulation, deployment requires no simulator access

why_deep_read: A direct, well-quantified answer to whether we should pursue a bigger model versus smarter test-time computation: a 9B model with lightweight action-evaluation outperforms a 27B model at lower latency, and the underlying pass@k diagnostic (33%->92%) suggests our SmolVLA fine-tune might already contain good actions that a cheap evaluator could surface -- directly relevant to our Q12 model-size decision and Q10 latency constraint on an 8GB GPU.

title: GeniWorld: A Generalizable Interactive World Model for Robotic Manipulation via Visual Actions

claims.claim: GeniWorld builds on pretrained video generative models and uses URDF-based rendering to convert numerical actions into visual (spatially grounded) action representations, explicitly decoupling embodiment kinematics from environmental dynamics; even when trained solely on limited fixed-scene data, it achieves robust zero-shot generalization to highly randomized, unseen environments, and can serve as a scalable policy evaluator and generator of diverse synthetic manipulation trajectories that improve downstream policy performance and robustness in complex environments, even with limited real-world demonstrations
claims.direction: favors decoupling embodiment kinematics from scene dynamics via visual (rendered) action representations in a world model, to mitigate scene overfitting and support zero-shot generalization from limited, fixed-scene training data
claims.conditions: trained on limited fixed-scene data, evaluated on highly randomized/unseen environments; supports closed-loop control via autoregressive video prediction

title: MINERVA: How Small Can a Manipulation Policy Be and Still Solve LIBERO?

claims.claim: A deliberately compact 0.54M-parameter visuomotor policy achieves 95.1% average success over 2,000 LIBERO rollouts, only 2.4 points below the reported LeRobot pi_0.5 result despite using 7,700x fewer parameters; performance saturates near 1M parameters and collapses below 0.25M; the 0.54M policy replans every control step in 5-9ms per chunk on a LAPTOP CPU (no GPU), 113x faster than SmolVLA and 1,400x faster than pi_0.5
claims.direction: favors much smaller policies than commonly used (down to ~0.5-1M parameters) for LIBERO-scale manipulation tasks, with large latency benefits, against the assumption that large VLA backbones are needed
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (four standard suites plus LIBERO-90), laptop CPU inference, no GPU required

claims.claim: Across broad architectural, training, and inference sweeps of this compact policy family, flow matching provides no detectable advantage over direct L1 (MSE-style) regression across three seeds, while L1 regression is up to 3.8x faster on GPU; only action-chunk length and vision capacity consistently exceeded a training-seed noise band as design factors that mattered
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that flow-matching/diffusion action heads are necessary for good performance at this task scale -- favors simple L1 regression for comparable success with much lower compute, at least on LIBERO-scale tasks
claims.conditions: same compact-policy family and LIBERO benchmark, controlled ablation across architecture/training/inference choices

claims.claim: A task-ID permutation probe shows standard LIBERO instruction conditioning primarily selects among memorized tasks (changing only the task-ID mapping reduces success to near chance); moreover, while the same compact-policy recipe achieves 94.6% success on LIBERO-90, LIBERO-Plus (visual/dynamics) perturbations reduce performance to 46-56%, with NEAR-ZERO robustness to photometric (lighting-style) shifts specifically
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that high in-distribution LIBERO success implies real task/instruction understanding or visual robustness -- reveals that even strong benchmark performance can mask near-total fragility to photometric/lighting perturbations
claims.conditions: LIBERO-90 and LIBERO-Plus perturbation benchmark, same compact-policy family

why_deep_read: This paper is almost a direct blueprint for our exact situation: a laptop-CPU-deployable, sub-1M-parameter policy nearly matching pi_0.5's LIBERO performance, a controlled finding that flow matching gives no advantage over simple L1 regression at this scale (directly answering Q01/Q12 for compute-constrained setups), and -- critically -- a demonstrated near-zero robustness to photometric/lighting shifts despite high nominal success, which may explain exactly why our current SmolVLA fine-tune breaks under new lighting; essential full reading before finalizing model size and action-head choice.

title: NFPO: Stabilized Policy Optimization of Normalizing Flow for Robotic Policy Learning

claims.claim: Replacing the de facto diagonal-covariance multivariate Gaussian policy parameterization in DRL with a Normalizing Flow (which can model multi-modal distributions with closed-form log-probability and low compute/memory overhead) causes training instability if done naively; NFPO addresses this instability with a targeted technique and obtains robust, strong performance on widely-used robotic learning tasks, successfully transferring to real-world robots
claims.direction: favors normalizing-flow-based multi-modal policy parameterization over standard diagonal-Gaussian policies for RL-trained robotic control, once training instability is addressed
claims.conditions: multiple simulation environments plus real-world robot transfer, online RL setting (not offline imitation learning)

title: Enhancing Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning With Symbolic Planning for Long-Horizon Tasks

claims.claim: Learning independent policies for actions defined by high-level symbolic-planning operators (rather than a single policy for an entire long-horizon task) achieves about 95% success in policy chaining for comprehensive plan execution, 84% success when planning/executing an entirely new task (door-opening) not seen during training, and 85% when using a new operator, remaining robust (~90% success) in dynamic environments and outperforming all baselines
claims.direction: favors decomposing long-horizon tasks into independently-learned, symbolic-operator-defined sub-policies (reusable and recombinable) over a single monolithic policy trained on the full long-horizon task
claims.conditions: long-horizon manipulation tasks (stacking, inserting, door-opening), generalization to new tasks/operators tested

title: SimToolReal: An Object-Centric Policy for Zero-Shot Dexterous Tool Manipulation

claims.claim: Procedurally generating a large variety of tool-like object primitives in simulation and training a single RL policy with the universal goal of manipulating each to random goal poses (rather than modeling a specific object/task with hand-tuned rewards) enables zero-shot dexterous tool manipulation that outperforms prior retargeting and fixed-grasp methods by 37%, while matching specialist policies trained on specific target objects/tasks
claims.direction: favors procedural, task-agnostic simulation training over per-object/per-task engineered simulation and reward tuning, for generalizable zero-shot sim-to-real tool manipulation
claims.conditions: sim-to-real RL, zero-shot evaluation over 120 real-world rollouts spanning 24 tasks, 12 object instances, 6 tool categories

title: Robot-DIFT: Correspondence-Sensitive Diffusion Features for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Contact-rich manipulation failures often occur 'in the final millimeters' because standard semantic visual encoders are trained for semantic invariance, which suppresses the correspondence cues (discriminative responses to pose offsets, boundaries, pre-contact alignment) needed for precise closed-loop control; Robot-DIFT, a deterministic backbone distilled from diffusion-model features (which have strong dense-correspondence priors) via Manifold Distillation into a clean, single-pass student, outperforms vision-language, self-supervised, geometry-oriented, and diffusion-based baseline encoders on contact-sensitive tasks across RoboCasa, LIBERO-10, and real robots
claims.direction: contradicts the common practice of using semantically-invariant pretrained encoders (e.g. DINOv2/CLIP-style) for precision/contact-sensitive manipulation -- favors correspondence-sensitive (diffusion-feature-derived) visual representations instead for fine-grained, contact-rich control
claims.conditions: RoboCasa, LIBERO-10 simulation benchmarks, plus real robots; controlled backbone/readout swap ablations included

title: Learning Multi-Modal Trajectory Policies for Data-Efficient Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Processing heterogeneous modalities (vision, language, trajectory) within a shared parameter space in standard transformer-based policies causes modality interference and inefficient representation learning, especially with scarce demonstrations; MATE, a Mixture-of-Experts trajectory-prediction framework with fine-grained sub-token feature decoupling and a cross-modal cosine router (with temperature-controlled routing and stochastic noise injection to prevent expert collapse), consistently outperforms prior work under data scarcity, achieving a 4.75% improvement in average success rate over a trajectory-guided counterpart on LIBERO
claims.direction: favors a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with modality-aware, stable routing over a shared-parameter-space transformer for multimodal (vision+language+trajectory) policies, particularly when demonstrations are scarce
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark under data scarcity, plus a real-world robotic ping-pong trajectory-prediction experiment

title: A Single Diffusion-Policy Controller for Multi-Task Block Pushing with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer

claims.claim: Training a diffusion policy from scratch via reinforcement learning (using a reweighted evidence-lower-bound policy loss that can seamlessly plug into RL, plus reverse curriculum generation and objective-centric representations to address exploration without demonstrations) supports learning multi-task block-pushing policies for multiple shapes under sparse reward
claims.direction: favors RL-trained (rather than only BC-trained) diffusion policies as feasible for multi-task manipulation without demonstrations
claims.conditions: sparse-reward simulation training

claims.claim: The RL-trained diffusion policy transfers zero-shot to real-world block-pushing under varying goal positions, block shapes, block weights, and surface friction
claims.direction: favors this RL-diffusion training pipeline for zero-shot robustness to several types of environmental/object variation
claims.conditions: real-world block-pushing, varied environmental conditions

title: TimewarpVAE: Simultaneous Time-Warping and Representation Learning of Trajectories

claims.claim: TimewarpVAE, a fully differentiable manifold-learning algorithm incorporating Dynamic Time Warping, simultaneously factors out timing variation from spatial-path variation in human demonstration trajectories, achieving lower spatial reconstruction test error than baseline approaches on handwriting and fork-manipulation datasets, and can generate novel, semantically meaningful (including high-speed) robotic-arm trajectories from its learned low-dimensional representation
claims.direction: favors explicitly factoring timing variation from spatial variation when learning trajectory representations from noisy/variable-speed human demonstrations, over representations that entangle the two
claims.conditions: handwriting and fork-manipulation human demonstration datasets, robotic arm trajectory generation

title: FoAM: Foresight-Augmented Multi-Task Imitation Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: FoAM, a multi-task imitation learning policy that uses multi-modal goal conditions as input and adds a 'foresight augmentation' (reasoning about the visual consequences of its own actions) in addition to standard action reconstruction, significantly enhances multi-task imitation learning performance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines by up to 41% in success rate across over 100 tasks in simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit foresight/future-visual-consequence auxiliary objective to standard action-reconstruction imitation learning, especially for multi-task policies
claims.conditions: over 100 tasks across more than 10 scenarios, simulation and real-world

claims.claim: FoAM's foresight-augmented, multi-modal-goal-conditioned representations help the policy generalize to unseen tasks using only a few expert demonstrations while maintaining action reliability (avoiding abnormal action sequences)
claims.direction: favors foresight-augmented multi-task training for few-shot generalization to new tasks
claims.conditions: few-expert-demonstration generalization setting, same evaluation suite

title: NanoVLA: Routing Decoupled Vision-Language Understanding for Nano-sized Generalist Robotic Policies

claims.claim: NanoVLA achieves up to 52x faster inference on edge devices (e.g. Jetson Orin Nano) compared to previous state-of-the-art VLA models, using 98% fewer parameters, while maintaining or surpassing their task accuracy and generalization, via three techniques: (1) vision-language decoupling that moves fusion of vision and language inputs to a late stage (enabling caching and reducing per-step overhead), (2) long-short action chunking for smooth multi-step planning without sacrificing real-time responsiveness, and (3) dynamic routing that adaptively assigns lightweight or heavy backbones based on task complexity
claims.direction: favors a family of specific architectural techniques (late vision-language fusion for caching, mixed-length action chunking, complexity-based dynamic routing) to achieve large VLA parameter/latency reductions on resource-constrained edge hardware without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: several benchmarks plus real-world deployments on resource-constrained edge devices (e.g. Jetson Orin Nano)

claims.claim: Ablations confirm the vision-language decoupling strategy preserves cross-task transferability, and the dynamic-routing module improves the cost-performance trade-off for real-time inference
claims.direction: favors these specific decoupling/routing mechanisms as not sacrificing transfer/generalization despite large latency gains
claims.conditions: same edge-device benchmarks

title: GenManip: LLM-driven Simulation for Generalizable Instruction-Following Manipulation

claims.claim: Evaluating modular manipulation systems (integrating foundation models for perception, reasoning, planning) versus end-to-end policies (trained via scalable data collection) on a new generalization benchmark (GenManip-Bench, 200 human-corrected scenarios), the study finds that while data scaling benefits end-to-end methods, modular systems enhanced with foundation models generalize more effectively across diverse scenarios
claims.direction: favors modular, foundation-model-integrated manipulation systems over pure end-to-end policies specifically for cross-scenario generalization, though end-to-end methods benefit more directly from added data
claims.conditions: GenManip-Bench, LLM-driven task-oriented scene-graph-synthesized tasks using 10K annotated 3D object assets

title: Towards Generalizable Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation: A Benchmark and LLM-Guided 3D Policy

claims.claim: On a new generalization benchmark (GemBench, spanning four generalization levels: novel placements, rigid/articulated objects, and long-horizon tasks), 3D-LOTUS, which leverages rich 3D information for language-conditioned action prediction, excels in both efficiency and performance on SEEN tasks but struggles to generalize to NOVEL tasks
claims.direction: suggests 3D information alone (without additional task/object-planning support) improves seen-task performance/efficiency but is insufficient on its own for generalizing to genuinely novel tasks
claims.conditions: GemBench simulation benchmark, seven action primitives, four generalization levels

claims.claim: 3D-LOTUS++, which integrates 3D-LOTUS's motion-planning capability with LLM-based task planning and VLM-based object grounding, achieves state-of-the-art performance specifically on GemBench's novel-task generalization level, setting a new standard for generalization in robotic manipulation
claims.direction: favors combining a 3D motion-planning policy with separate LLM task-planning and VLM object-grounding modules over a single end-to-end 3D policy for generalizing to novel tasks/instructions
claims.conditions: same GemBench benchmark, novel-task generalization level

title: Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds

claims.claim: A single self-supervised point-transformer encoder (Utonia) trained jointly across diverse point-cloud domains (remote sensing, outdoor LiDAR, indoor RGB-D, CAD models, and point clouds lifted from RGB-only video) learns a consistent representation space that transfers across domains; conditioning vision-language-action policies on Utonia features improves robotic manipulation performance, and integrating Utonia into vision-language models yields gains on spatial reasoning
claims.direction: favors a single, domain-diverse, jointly-trained 3D point-cloud encoder over domain-specific or RGB-only encoders for both manipulation policy conditioning and spatial reasoning
claims.conditions: cross-domain joint pretraining (remote sensing, LiDAR, RGB-D, CAD, video-lifted point clouds); downstream VLA manipulation and VLM spatial reasoning evaluation, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: Scaling Short-Term Memory of Visuomotor Policies for Long-Horizon Tasks

claims.claim: PRISM, a transformer-based visuomotor policy architecture using gated attention (filtering retrieved history to suppress irrelevant/spurious information) and a hierarchical architecture (compressing local information into compact tokens before integrating temporally-extended dependencies), scales short-term memory in visuomotor policies for up to two minutes and consistently outperforms prior memory architectures (recurrent nets, transformers, and their variants) by an absolute 5-12% on a new 8-task short-term-memory benchmark (ReMemBench)
claims.direction: favors gated-attention plus hierarchical memory compression over recurrent architectures or plain transformer history-conditioning for scaling short-term memory in visuomotor control
claims.conditions: ReMemBench (8 household manipulation tasks, 4 memory categories), no large-scale pretraining used

claims.claim: On RoboCasa and LIBERO, PRISM achieves 11-15% absolute improvement over both its own no-memory variant and over fine-tuned, large-scale-pretrained VLA baselines (GR00T-N1-3B, OpenVLA), despite PRISM not leveraging any large-scale pretraining itself
claims.direction: favors a small, well-designed memory-augmented architecture over larger pretrained VLA models specifically for memory-dependent long-horizon tasks, without requiring large-scale pretraining
claims.conditions: RoboCasa and LIBERO benchmarks, comparison against GR00T-N1-3B and OpenVLA

title: Interactive World Simulator for Robot Policy Training and Evaluation

claims.claim: Using consistency models for both image decoding and latent-space dynamics prediction (rather than standard diffusion), an interactive world model built from a moderate-sized robot interaction dataset produces interaction-consistent pixel-level predictions and supports stable long-horizon interaction for over 10 minutes at 15 FPS on a single RTX 4090; policies trained on data generated entirely within this world model perform COMPARABLY to policies trained on the same amount of real-world data, with strong correlation between simulated and real-world policy performance across diverse tasks (rigid, deformable, piles)
claims.direction: favors fast, consistency-model-based interactive world models as a viable substitute for real-world demonstration data collection and for policy evaluation, given a moderate real-data seed set
claims.conditions: single RTX 4090 GPU, moderate-sized seed interaction dataset, diverse real-world task evaluation for validation

title: Learning to Explore Informative Trajectories and Samples for Embodied Perception

claims.claim: Building a 3D semantic distribution map from multi-view observations and training an exploration policy (self-supervised via semantic-distribution-disagreement and semantic-distribution-uncertainty rewards) to seek out high-uncertainty/high-disagreement viewpoints, then selecting hard training samples based on that uncertainty, yields a perception model that outperforms baselines trained with other exploration policies, with robustness confirmed in real-robot experiments
claims.direction: favors active, uncertainty-driven multi-view exploration and hard-sample selection over passive/random data collection for efficiently gathering informative training samples for perception fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments, embodied perception fine-tuning

title: Bridging the Semantic-Action Gap in Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLA Inference

claims.claim: Directly applying VLM-oriented visual token pruning (based on context-prefill semantic salience) to VLA inference causes severe manipulation performance degradation because VLA inference has distinct attention patterns between the vision-language prefill stage and the action-decode stage, so semantic-salience-only pruning removes action-critical visual tokens; VLA-Pruner instead estimates token importance from both semantic prefilling AND temporally-smoothed action relevance, achieving up to 1.99x speedup with comparable manipulation quality across multiple VLA architectures, outperforming state-of-the-art pruning approaches
claims.direction: favors action-relevance-aware (not purely semantic-salience-based) visual token pruning for VLA inference acceleration
claims.conditions: multiple VLA architectures, plug-and-play method

title: VQ-VLA: Improving Vision-Language-Action Models via Scaling Vector-Quantized Action Tokenizers

claims.claim: Training a vector-quantized action tokenizer on the largest-scale action trajectory dataset to date (100x more data than prior approaches, including large amounts of SYNTHETIC trajectory data) finds the domain gap between synthetic and real action trajectories is marginal, allowing effective use of vast synthetic data without compromising real-world performance; as synthetic data volume increases, downstream task performance improves significantly, achieving up to 30% higher success rate on two real-world long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors scaling up synthetic action-trajectory data for training discrete action tokenizers, given the marginal synthetic-to-real domain gap observed
claims.conditions: simulated environments plus real robotic platforms, long-horizon tasks

claims.claim: The resulting vector-quantized action tokenizer, once trained, adapts zero-shot to a wide range of downstream tasks (short-horizon reactive to long-horizon planning), accelerating inference while producing smoother, more coherent action outputs than prior action tokenization approaches
claims.direction: favors VQ-based discrete action tokenization (trained at scale) for both inference speed and action smoothness/coherence
claims.conditions: zero-shot transfer across task horizons, real robotic platforms

title: Dream2Flow: Bridging Video Generation and Open-World Manipulation with 3D Object Flow

claims.claim: Reconstructing 3D object motion from videos generated by a pretrained video model, and formulating manipulation as tracking this reconstructed object trajectory, separates state changes from the actuators realizing them, enabling zero-shot guidance from pretrained video generation models to manipulate diverse object categories (rigid, articulated, deformable, granular) without any task-specific demonstrations
claims.direction: favors 3D object flow as an embodiment-agnostic intermediate representation for converting pretrained video-generation priors into executable manipulation, without needing new demonstrations per task
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments across diverse object categories, zero task-specific demonstrations

title: Point Policy: Unifying Observations and Actions with Key Points for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Point Policy learns robot manipulation policies EXCLUSIVELY from offline human demonstration videos, with NO teleoperation data at all, by translating human hand poses into robot poses and capturing object states via semantically meaningful key points, yielding a morphology-agnostic representation; across 8 real-world tasks it shows a 75 percentage-point absolute improvement over prior (teleoperation-based or other video-based) works evaluated in identical training settings
claims.direction: favors learning entirely from human video (no teleoperation) via key-point-based morphology-agnostic representation over methods requiring teleoperation data collection
claims.conditions: 8 real-world tasks, identical evaluation settings as training

claims.claim: Point Policy exhibits a 74 percentage-point gain across tasks for novel object instances and is robust to significant background clutter
claims.direction: favors this key-point/human-video approach for generalization to novel objects and background clutter
claims.conditions: same real-world task suite, novel object instances and cluttered backgrounds

title: Beyond Point-Attached Semantics: Stable Object-Centric Semantic Fields for Robust Manipulation

claims.claim: Features directly attached to observed 3D points vary with viewpoint and sensor noise, giving a policy inconsistent representations of the same object part; building a continuous object-centric semantic field (reading features from independently-resampled 3D locations using the full object cloud as context, trained with part classification, cross-instance alignment, and perturbation consistency) instead of using point-wise features improves average success rates to 69.3% (RoboTwin simulation) and 67.5% (real-world bimanual tasks), an improvement of 7.0 and 32.5 percentage points respectively over a point-wise baseline (Utonia Point-wise)
claims.direction: favors continuous, perturbation-consistent object-centric semantic fields over raw point-attached visual features for part-aware manipulation representations, especially for real-world robustness
claims.conditions: 4 RoboTwin simulation tasks and 4 real-world bimanual tasks, tested on held-out (novel) objects, DP3-based policy

title: Illumination-Aware Fine-Tuning of a Vision-Language-Action Model for Autonomous Lunar Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard fine-tuning of a pretrained VLA does not address extreme illumination-driven visual domain shift; an illumination-aware fine-tuning strategy combining LoRA-based lightweight adaptation with three complementary augmentations -- low-angle shadow synthesis, brightness/contrast perturbation, and color-temperature shift -- improves success rate over both zero-shot deployment and standard fine-tuning under adverse illumination conditions, while maintaining strong performance under normal lighting
claims.direction: favors combining LoRA-based lightweight adaptation with targeted illumination-specific augmentations (shadow synthesis, brightness/contrast, color temperature) over standard fine-tuning alone, specifically to address lighting-driven domain shift
claims.conditions: evaluated on a custom robot (LunarBot) across three controlled illumination conditions

title: Contrastive Conceptor Activation Steering (COAST): Unlocking Vision-Language-Action Models through Hidden States

claims.claim: COAST uses 'conceptors' (linear operators that soft-project data into a target distribution's principal components) built from just a few success/failure rollout examples to identify success-critical latent subspaces for a task, then steers VLA hidden-state activations toward these subspaces at inference time (no fine-tuning); across three architecturally distinct policies (flow-matching VLA, autoregressive VLA, Diffusion Policy) this improves absolute mean task success rate by over 20% in simulation and over 40% on real robots
