claims.direction: favors lightweight, training-free inference-time latent steering (using a few example rollouts) over standard fine-tuning or retraining to unlock existing task-relevant knowledge already present in VLA latent representations, and shows the technique generalizes across very different action-head architectures
claims.conditions: three distinct neural policy architectures, both simulation and real-robot evaluation

claims.claim: Activation subspace geometry reveals that failure modes share substantial structure across tasks, while success representations remain largely task-specific; this lets previously-fitted conceptors improve performance on new tasks (without refitting) when tasks share similar failure modes
claims.direction: suggests failure-mode representations (not success representations) are the more transferable/reusable structure across tasks for this kind of intervention
claims.conditions: same three-architecture evaluation, cross-task conceptor reuse tested

title: UniviewVLA: A Unified Multiview Vision-Language-Action Model with World Modeling

claims.claim: Rather than deploying additional physical cameras or relying on costly explicit 3D reconstruction to handle occlusion, UniviewVLA infers multiview scene evolution (revealing occluded cues and future scene evolution) from only STANDARD two-camera (agent-view + wrist-view) observations using a world model; on customized occlusion-focused tasks this improves success rate from 40.0% to 73.3% and improves average real-robot success by 33.4 points, while still achieving 95.8% on standard occlusion-free LIBERO and 4.60 on CALVIN ABCD-to-D without sacrificing standard-benchmark performance
claims.direction: favors inferring additional (multiview/occlusion-revealing) visual information from a world model conditioned on the same two standard cameras, over adding extra physical cameras or explicit 3D reconstruction, for occlusion robustness
claims.conditions: standard two-camera setup (agent-view + wrist-view, matching common fixed+wrist camera configurations), LIBERO, CALVIN, and custom occlusion-focused real-robot tasks

claims.claim: A Motion-Informative Token Compression mechanism compresses each generated future view from 625 to 16 tokens, reducing per-view world-model latency from 6-7 seconds to 0.2-0.3 seconds, and a training-free Action-Entropy View Selection dynamically picks the most action-informative view at each inference stage
claims.direction: favors aggressive token compression plus dynamic view selection to make multiview world-model-based occlusion handling practical at low latency
claims.conditions: same evaluation setting

title: MoMo: Dial Motion Mode in Robot Manipulation with Spatiotemporal Action Tokenization

claims.claim: A two-stage imitation-learning framework (spatiotemporal action tokenizer plus a behavior-cloning transformer conditioned on task and a continuous 'motion mode' variable) learns execution-style variation (steady, dynamic, intermediate -- differing in joint speed, acceleration, end-effector approach pitch) as a reusable behavioral factor shared across six real-robot manipulation tasks; on tasks demonstrated in only one motion mode, the framework transfers an unseen requested mode while largely preserving task success
claims.direction: favors explicitly conditioning the policy on a continuous, reusable 'motion mode' variable (decoupled from the task itself) to control HOW a skill is executed, enabling compositional generalization to unseen task-mode combinations from single-mode demonstrations
claims.conditions: six real-robot manipulation tasks, human-rated behavior distinguishability

title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning

claims.claim: Diagnostic evaluation (WorldEcho, using visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment over a broad action distribution, not just expert actions) shows current action-conditioned world models reasonably execute expert actions but struggle with diverse off-expert action trajectories, either ignoring commanded actions or producing visually invalid rollouts; WorldSync, which broadens training distribution over action consequences, grounds intermediate representations in action-induced dynamics, and aligns predicted changes under interventions with ground-truth futures, improves action-following and serves as a more reliable simulator for iterative policy improvement on RoboTwin and real-robot tasks
claims.direction: cautions that world models trained/evaluated only on expert-like actions may not faithfully simulate the off-distribution actions a policy-in-training will actually take, and favors explicitly training/evaluating world models on broader (off-expert) action distributions before relying on them for policy improvement
claims.conditions: RoboTwin benchmarks and real-robot tasks

title: LUMOS: Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning with World Models

claims.claim: LUMOS learns skills by practicing them over many long-horizon rollouts in the latent space of a learned world model (on-policy), which mitigates the policy-induced distribution shift that most offline imitation learning methods suffer from, and transfers these skills zero-shot to a real robot; on the difficult long-horizon CALVIN benchmark LUMOS outperforms prior comparable learning-based methods on chained multi-task evaluations
claims.direction: favors on-policy practice within a learned world model's latent space (rather than purely offline imitation learning) to reduce distribution-shift-related failures in long-horizon, multi-task settings
claims.conditions: CALVIN long-horizon benchmark, zero-shot transfer to a real robot

claims.claim: LUMOS learns from unstructured play data with fewer than 1% hindsight language annotations, yet remains steerable with language commands at test time, achieved via combining latent planning with image- and language-based hindsight goal relabeling
claims.direction: favors combining minimal (sub-1%) language annotation with hindsight relabeling for language-conditioned imitation learning, over labeling all training data with language
claims.conditions: unstructured play data, real-world robot deployment

title: Learning Video Generation for Robotic Manipulation with Collaborative Trajectory Control

claims.claim: RoboMaster models inter-object dynamics for trajectory-controlled video generation by decomposing the manipulation interaction into pre-interaction, interaction, and post-interaction sub-stages (each modeled by the currently dominant object -- robotic arm or manipulated object), combined with appearance/shape-aware latent representations for subject consistency, establishing new state-of-the-art performance in trajectory-controlled video generation for robotic manipulation on the Bridge dataset plus RLBench and SIMPLER benchmarks
claims.direction: favors phase-decomposed, dominant-object-based modeling of multi-object interactions over prior single/decomposed-object video-generation approaches, for generating higher-fidelity synthetic manipulation video/training data involving multi-object interaction
claims.conditions: video-generation-quality benchmarks (Bridge, RLBench, SIMPLER); no downstream policy success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: RoboMamba: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Reasoning and Manipulation

claims.claim: RoboMamba (Mamba-based VLA) achieves inference speeds 3x faster than existing VLA models
claims.direction: favors efficient SSM backbone over standard transformer VLA for low latency
claims.conditions: real+sim robot experiments, VLA model with linear-complexity SSM

claims.claim: Once sufficient reasoning capability is learned, manipulation/pose-prediction skills can be acquired with minimal fine-tuning parameters (0.1% of model) and time
claims.direction: favors small added action head / parameter-efficient fine-tuning over full fine-tuning of large VLA
claims.conditions: VLA model, SE(3) pose prediction head, sim+real

title: Shortcut Learning in Generalist Robot Policies: The Role of Dataset Diversity and Fragmentation

claims.claim: Limited diversity within individual sub-datasets and distributional disparities across sub-datasets (fragmentation) cause shortcut learning (reliance on task-irrelevant features), limiting generalization
claims.direction: favors diverse, non-fragmented data collection over larger but fragmented aggregations
claims.conditions: large-scale generalist datasets (OXE), sim+real, pi0 model

claims.claim: Carefully selected robotic data augmentation strategies can reduce shortcut learning in existing offline datasets and improve generalization of generalist policies (e.g., pi0) when new large-scale data collection is impractical
claims.direction: favors targeted augmentation as substitute for more data
claims.conditions: pi0 generalist policy, sim and real-world evaluation

title: One Demonstration Is Enough for Real-World Robotic Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A single demonstration plus automated intervention/recovery mechanisms (AutoSERL) matches HIL-SERL and outperforms behavior cloning, SERL with 20 demonstrations, and a one-shot imitation baseline (MILES), reaching 100% success on insertion tasks
claims.direction: favors combining minimal demos with online RL/intervention over pure behavior cloning with more demos
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-intensive tasks (insertion, hanging, hinge), two robot platforms, online RL not pure BC

title: PIDiff: Integrating a High-Performance Transformer Into Diffusion Models for Robust and Efficient Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A linear-complexity Transformer used as noise predictor inside a diffusion policy (PIDiff) retains multimodal distribution modeling while improving prediction accuracy and robustness over baseline imitation learning methods
claims.direction: favors diffusion policy with efficient transformer noise-predictor over standard diffusion/transformer baselines
claims.conditions: multiple sim manipulation benchmarks + real-world scenarios

claims.claim: PIDiff achieves faster inference speeds and reduced GPU memory usage compared to baseline methods
claims.direction: favors architecture optimized for efficiency (linear transformer) for low-latency, low-memory deployment
claims.conditions: real-world robot deployment, no exact numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: A PointNet-based encoder is used to efficiently extract visual features, improving environment understanding and learning efficiency
claims.direction: favors point-cloud/PointNet encoder over image-only encoders
claims.conditions: sim + real, multiple benchmark platforms

why_deep_read: Abstract claims faster inference and reduced GPU memory vs baselines with real-world validation, directly relevant to our latency/GPU-memory constraint; full paper would give exact numbers and whether gains transfer to low-cost arms.

title: Action Images: End-to-End Policy Learning via Multiview Video Generation

claims.claim: Formulating actions as pixel-grounded multiview 'action images' generated by a video backbone allows the video model itself to act as a zero-shot policy without a separate action head, achieving the strongest zero-shot success rates among compared world-action models on RLBench and real-world evaluations
claims.direction: favors pixel-grounded video-generation action representation over low-dimensional action tokens/separate action heads
claims.conditions: RLBench sim + real-world, multiview cameras, world-action-model architecture (likely large/compute-heavy)

title: TS-Mask VLA: 2D Temporal-Spatial Masking for Vision-Language-Action Model with Effective Bridging

claims.claim: TS-Mask VLA achieves 95.7% average success rate on LIBERO with only 0.5B parameters, outperforming significantly larger VLA models
claims.direction: favors small model size (0.5B) over larger VLA backbones given right architecture
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark

claims.claim: A Discrete Diffusion Action Expert with a Bridge Attention conditioning mechanism gives more accurate and stable action generation than plain autoregressive next-token action prediction
claims.direction: favors discrete-diffusion action generation over standard autoregressive token-based action generation
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks LIBERO/CALVIN

claims.claim: A temporal-spatial 2D masking strategy over discrete action tokens strengthens cross-time dependency modeling, improving long-horizon performance (best average sequence length 4.19 on CALVIN)
claims.direction: favors explicit temporal-spatial structure in action-chunk modeling over unstructured token sequences
claims.conditions: CALVIN long-horizon sim benchmark

why_deep_read: Small (0.5B) model beating larger VLAs on LIBERO is directly relevant to Q12 for our 8GB GPU constraint; full paper's ablations on masking/action-expert design would clarify what's transferable to a low-cost single/dual-camera setup.

title: Sample-Efficient Robot Skill Learning for Construction Tasks: Benchmarking Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning and Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: A VLA model shows strong generalization and few-shot capability, achieving 60% and 100% success in a pick-up phase across two scenarios, while a DQN-based RL baseline can be made robust but requires additional noise/tuning effort
claims.direction: favors VLA/imitation-style approach over RL (DQN) for practical deployment with minimal data
claims.conditions: real construction robot teleoperation-collected demos, multistage panel installation task

title: Shared Execution-Clock Drifting Policy for Dynamic Precision Manipulation

claims.claim: A one-step action-generation policy (SECD) that jointly predicts a progress-indexed action curve and a shared monotone execution clock keeps a fixed-rate control interface while requiring only one network evaluation, achieving 77.00% task-averaged success across 300 real-robot trials on 4 tasks (e.g., 91% success intercepting an object on a 16 m/min conveyor, 54% folding a crumpled shirt within 90s), outperforming other evaluated one-step baselines on every task
claims.direction: favors explicit modeling of execution rhythm/timing jointly with one-step (distilled) action generation over standard fixed-rate chunk execution, to reduce latency and improve timing under real-time constraints
claims.conditions: real robot, 4 tasks, NVIDIA Thor inference, one-step generative policy

claims.claim: Making execution rhythm (a shared monotone clock mapping control times to a progress-indexed action curve) an explicit, learned part of action-chunk generation improves task success versus baselines that leave temporal allocation implicit in action chunks
claims.direction: favors explicit temporal/execution-clock modeling within action chunking over standard fixed action-chunk execution
claims.conditions: real robot, time-critical manipulation, ablations also run in state-based RoboMimic (Transport, Square)

why_deep_read: Directly targets jerky motion / timing at chunk boundaries under real-time constraints (our SmolVLA failure mode) with real-robot success-rate numbers; full text ablations on the clock mechanism and baseline comparisons would inform how to fix chunk-boundary jerkiness and latency in our setup.

title: Language Conditioned Multi-Finger Dexterous Manipulation Enabled by Physical Compliance and Switching of Controllers

claims.claim: A switching-controller architecture that combines a large VLA (for high-level language-conditioned reasoning) with small, lightweight subtask-level dexterous policies requires minimal demonstration data to fine-tune, and additional skills/compliant hands can be added without retraining the large VLA
claims.direction: favors hybrid large-VLA + small task-specific policy over a single monolithic large policy
claims.conditions: custom compliant 13-DoF anthropomorphic hand, real robot, language-conditioned dexterous tasks

claims.claim: Event-driven switching between a fine-tuned VLA (predicting event/subtask-completion signals) and lightweight subtask policies enables language-conditioned multi-step dexterous manipulation
claims.direction: supports combining language conditioning at a high (VLA) level with non-language-conditioned low-level control policies
claims.conditions: real robot, qualitative validation across language-conditioned tasks, no comparative success-rate numbers given

title: HACMan++: Spatially-Grounded Motion Primitives for Manipulation

claims.claim: A discrete-continuous action space (primitive type + spatial grounding location + continuous motion parameters) lets an RL policy chain motion primitives and generalize across object shape and pose variations, significantly outperforming existing (implicitly end-to-end continuous action) methods on complex long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors structured discrete-continuous/primitive action spaces over flat continuous end-to-end action regression for generalization
claims.conditions: RL-trained, sim-to-real zero-shot transfer, real-world manipulation with unseen objects

claims.claim: Grounding action primitives on a spatial location in the environment improves generalization to unseen object shapes and poses versus end-to-end learned policies
claims.direction: favors spatially-grounded/structured action representations for object/pose generalization
claims.conditions: zero-shot sim-to-real, real-world unseen objects, no exact success numbers given in abstract

title: RLDG: Robotic Generalist Policy Distillation via Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Generalist policies fine-tuned on RL-generated training data consistently outperform those fine-tuned on human demonstrations, achieving up to 40% higher success rates and better generalization to new tasks; gains attributed to optimized action distributions and improved state coverage versus human demos
claims.direction: contradicts common practice of using only human teleop demos for fine-tuning; favors RL-generated (or RL-filtered/augmented) demonstration data for quality over raw human demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world precise manipulation tasks (connector insertion, assembly), generalist foundation policy fine-tuning

why_deep_read: Directly contradicts the assumption that more human teleop demos = better data; understanding WHY RL-generated data beats human demos (state coverage, action distribution) could inform how we curate/augment our 50-100 human teleop demos or add corrective/recovery data.

title: VRobotix: A Scalable and Cost-Effective Virtual-Reality-Based Robotic Manipulation Dataset Generation Framework

claims.claim: Imitation learning policies trained on just 50 VR-teleoperated demonstration trials achieve a 100% task success rate on pushing, grasping, and stacking tasks (data collection success rate averaging 92.0%)
claims.direction: supports that ~50 demonstrations can be sufficient for simple manipulation tasks (matches our target demo budget)
claims.conditions: physics-accurate simulation (not necessarily real hardware), VR-teleoperated human-in-the-loop data collection, simple pick/push/stack tasks

title: How to Instruct Your Robot: Dense Language Annotations Power Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Re-labeling demonstrations with dense, multi-aspect VLM-generated language annotations (physical motion, scene composition, arm pose, reasoning), selected per-task by a learned instructor at deployment, raises policy success by 5 points over a task-only (sparse language) baseline on RoboCasa, coming within 3 points of a per-task oracle annotation
claims.direction: favors dense/rich language conditioning over sparse task-name-only language conditioning, without collecting new demonstrations
claims.conditions: large-scale corpus (1M+ robot clips, 50K egocentric videos), applied to both a VLA policy and a video-based world-action model, simulation (RoboCasa) benchmark

title: CRAFT: Video Diffusion for Bimanual Robot Data Generation

claims.claim: A video-diffusion-based augmentation pipeline conditioned on edge-based structural cues from simulated trajectories generates physically-plausible, action-consistent demonstration videos with varied object poses, camera viewpoints, lighting, and backgrounds, starting from only a few real-world demonstrations, and improves success rates over existing augmentation strategies and straightforward data scaling
claims.direction: favors generative (video-diffusion) synthetic augmentation over simple data scaling or classical augmentation for expanding visual diversity from few real demos
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, bimanual manipulation tasks, cross-embodiment/multi-view synthesis, real+sim evaluation

claims.claim: Starting from only a handful of real demonstrations, CRAFT can generate a large, visually diverse synthetic dataset that improves generalization for dual-arm manipulation without replaying demos on the real robot
claims.direction: favors synthetic data generation to multiply a small real demo set rather than collecting more real demos
claims.conditions: bimanual tasks, sim+real

why_deep_read: Directly targets our stated failure modes (new lighting, moved camera, different-looking object) via generative augmentation from a handful of real demos; full text would clarify whether single-arm/low-cost setups can use the same pipeline and what success-rate deltas look like numerically.

title: Imagining the Sense of Touch: Touch-Informed Manipulation via Imagined Tactile Representations

claims.claim: An auxiliary model (TacImag) trained on paired visuotactile demonstrations to predict tactile observations from vision+proprioception, then used to guide the manipulation policy at test time using only vision (no tactile hardware at deployment), improves real-world contact-sensitive task performance by 44.4% on average (imagined force fields) and texture-sensitive task performance by 23.3% (imagined tactile images)
claims.direction: favors adding a tactile-prediction auxiliary objective/representation during training (even without tactile sensors at deployment) over vision-only policies with no such auxiliary signal
claims.conditions: 6 sim + 4 real-world manipulation tasks, requires paired visuotactile demonstrations for training (not available in our current setup)

why_deep_read: Strong quantified real-world numbers (44.4%, 23.3%) for an auxiliary-objective approach relevant to Q09; would clarify whether the visuotactile pretraining data requirement could be substituted or skipped for our tactile-sensor-free SO-101 setup.

title: FOCAL-VLA: Subtask-Guided Geometry Distillation and Implicit World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Combining subtask-guided geometry distillation (from a 3D foundation model, VGGT) with implicit world modeling (predicting future interaction dynamics via Track4World features) as auxiliary training signals improves action generation over baselines, without running the extra geometry/world models at inference time
claims.direction: favors auxiliary 3D-geometry and future-dynamics prediction objectives during training (with no added inference cost) over VLA models trained on 2D observations alone
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + real-world manipulation tasks, no exact success numbers in abstract

claims.claim: Distilling geometric knowledge from a pretrained 3D vision foundation model (VGGT) into 2D-observation VLA policies improves spatial understanding for precise, long-horizon manipulation
claims.direction: favors distilling 3D-aware pretrained representations into the vision encoder rather than using plain 2D pretrained encoders alone
claims.conditions: sim + real, VLA architecture

title: SAGE: Bridging Semantic and Actionable Parts for GEneralizable Articulated-Object Manipulation under Language Instructions

claims.claim: Joint proposal and knowledge fusion between a large vision-language model (general intuitions) and a small domain-specific model (expert facts for part perception) is key to handling diverse articulated-object manipulation under language instructions
claims.direction: favors hybrid large-VLM + small domain-specific model over a single monolithic model
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot experiments, qualitative effectiveness claims only, no comparative success-rate numbers in abstract

claims.claim: Grounding natural-language instructions to actionable object parts (rather than whole-object semantics) enables generalizable manipulation across diverse articulated objects
claims.direction: supports part-level language grounding over whole-object/coarse language conditioning
claims.conditions: sim + real, qualitative

title: Intelligent robotic object grasping system using computer vision and deep reinforcement learning techniques

claims.claim: Using depth image information (via SAC) to determine optimal gripping areas combined with YOLOv3 detection improved grasping success rate to 87.3% and accuracy by 27% and execution efficiency by 35% versus traditional (non-depth-based) gripping approaches
claims.direction: favors depth-based grasp-point selection over RGB-only/traditional gripping heuristics
claims.conditions: COCO-pretrained YOLO + transfer learning, RL (SAC) grasp policy, 10-fold cross-validation for robustness; task is generic object grasping, not full manipulation policy

title: MM-ACT: Learn from Multimodal Parallel Generation to Act

claims.claim: A one-step parallel decoding strategy for action generation (vs. autoregressive/iterative decoding) combined with shared multimodal token space achieves 96.3% success on LIBERO, 72.0% on real Franka tasks, and 52.38% on RoboTwin2.0 bimanual tasks
claims.direction: favors one-step parallel action decoding for efficiency while retaining/improving accuracy, over slower autoregressive or multi-step diffusion decoding
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim, real Franka robot, RoboTwin2.0 bimanual sim benchmark

claims.claim: Context-Shared Multimodal Learning, which jointly supervises text, image, and action generation from shared context (auxiliary text/image generation objectives), improves action generation, yielding an additional 9.25% success-rate gain from cross-modal learning on RoboTwin2.0
claims.direction: favors adding auxiliary text/image generation objectives jointly trained with action generation, over training the action head alone
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2.0 bimanual sim benchmark, ablation quantifying the cross-modal-learning contribution

why_deep_read: Quantified ablation (+9.25%) isolates the benefit of joint multimodal auxiliary objectives on action generation (Q09), and one-step parallel decoding (Q01) is directly relevant to our latency problem; full text would clarify compute cost and whether the gains hold for small models on limited GPU memory.

title: Extremum Flow Matching for Offline Goal Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A Flow-Matching-based method (using deterministic transport to estimate distribution extrema) supports goal-conditioned imitation/RL policies that were validated on a real humanoid (Talos) performing pick-and-place and articulated-object manipulation from high-dimensional image observations
claims.direction: supports flow matching as a viable action-generation approach for real-robot manipulation from images, compared across different architectural configurations (critic/planner/actor/world-model combinations)
claims.conditions: real humanoid hardware (Talos), image observations, offline goal-conditioned setting; no exact success numbers given in abstract

title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Repurposing a pretrained geometric foundation model (GFM) as a shared substrate for perception, temporal prediction, and action decoding (splitting it at an intermediate layer for encoder vs. future-predictor/decoder) preserves rich geometric priors while adding language-conditioned temporal world modeling with minimal architectural modification
claims.direction: favors reusing a single pretrained 3D/geometric foundation model backbone for both vision encoding and action decoding over separate 2D vision encoder + action head
claims.conditions: broad suite of simulation and real-robot manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Inserting a causal future predictor at an intermediate layer of the geometric backbone to forecast future latent tokens (conditioned on language, proprioception, action history) improves accuracy and robustness versus current foundation-model-scale baselines that operate on 2D image frames without explicit future/geometry prediction
claims.direction: favors auxiliary future-latent prediction grounded in 3D geometry over 2D-only VLA/WAM baselines
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot benchmarks

claims.claim: GAM is reported to be faster and lighter than current foundation-model-scale baselines while being more accurate and robust
claims.direction: favors a single unified, lighter backbone over larger foundation-model-scale VLA/WAM baselines
claims.conditions: sim + real, no exact parameter counts or latency numbers given in abstract

why_deep_read: Claims simultaneous gains in accuracy, robustness, speed, and size versus foundation-model-scale baselines by unifying geometric encoding, future prediction, and action decoding; directly relevant to Q03/Q09/Q12 trade-offs we face on an 8GB laptop GPU, and the full paper would give the actual parameter counts/latency needed to judge feasibility.

title: Athena-Brain Technical Report: An Efficient Robot Brain for General Intelligence and Embodied Interaction

claims.claim: An 8B on-device LLM (Athena-Brain-8B), post-trained with a multi-stage pipeline (SFT, RL, embodied expert training, model merge), consistently outperforms models of similar scale and surpasses several substantially larger frontier models on in-domain embodied benchmarks (zero-shot), while generating much shorter responses than a comparable general-purpose 8B model
claims.direction: favors compact, specifically post-trained models over larger general-purpose frontier models for embodied high-level reasoning
claims.conditions: on-device 8B LLM used as high-level 'brain' (not the low-level action policy itself), evaluated zero-shot on embodied benchmarks; qualitative claim, no exact numbers in abstract

title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Across Diffusion Policy, pi0.5, and FastWAM, visuo-tactile policy variants achieve higher task success in all six policy-suite comparisons and higher deformation-aware success rate (DSR) in five of six under distribution shift, whereas in-distribution benefits from adding touch are mixed
claims.direction: favors adding tactile modality specifically for robustness under distribution shift, not necessarily for in-distribution performance; contradicts assumption that adding a sensing modality automatically improves fusion/performance in-distribution
claims.conditions: 4,000 expert demonstrations, 50+ deformable/rigid assets, real visuo-tactile dataset, evaluated with standard policies (Diffusion Policy, pi0.5, FastWAM)

claims.claim: In 0.7-24% of successful in-distribution rollouts across all 12 tested configurations, policies violate a deformation tolerance (excessive compression/slip) despite counting as a task success under standard success metrics, showing task-success alone hides poor physical interaction quality
claims.direction: suggests standard success-rate metrics can overstate policy quality; auxiliary physical-interaction-aware supervision/metrics may be needed beyond binary task success
claims.conditions: deformable-object manipulation, FEM-based ground-truth evaluation, evaluator-only signal (not used by the policy)

why_deep_read: Directly tests standard policies (Diffusion Policy, pi0.5) under distribution shift with and without added tactile modality, giving controlled evidence relevant to our robustness (Q14) and auxiliary-modality (Q09) questions, though our setup lacks tactile sensors so the specific fusion mechanism needs checking in the full text.

title: VLBiMan++: Expanding the Generalization Boundary of Vision-Language Anchored One-Shot Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Starting from a single human demonstration, task-aware decomposition plus vision-language grounded geometric adaptation can transfer skills to novel task/object/scene/embodiment configurations without retraining
claims.direction: favors one-shot demonstration plus geometric/language-grounded adaptation over collecting many demonstrations or retraining per new configuration
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation, qualitative claims of 'strong task success' across generalization axes, no exact success-rate numbers given

claims.claim: The extended framework maintains task success under object generalization (unseen categories, articulated/deformable objects), scene generalization (clutter, occlusion, dynamic interference), embodiment generalization (heterogeneous dual-arm platforms), and long-horizon deployment with repeated external perturbations
claims.direction: supports vision-language-grounded geometric adaptation as a generalization strategy across multiple robustness axes
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual experiments, qualitative

title: RoboGSim: A Real2Sim2Real Robotic Gaussian Splatting Simulator

claims.claim: A policy trained on RoboGSim-synthesized data (novel views, objects, trajectories, scenes generated via 3D Gaussian Splatting) achieves zero-shot performance on the real robot comparable to a policy trained on real robot data
claims.direction: favors photorealistic Gaussian-Splatting-based synthetic augmentation/generation as a substitute for additional real-robot data collection
claims.conditions: real2sim2real transfer, comparison of RoboGSim-data-trained vs real-data-trained models on both simulator and real robot

claims.claim: In experiments with novel camera perspectives and novel scenes, the model trained on RoboGSim synthetic data performed even better on the real robot than the model trained on real robot data
claims.direction: favors synthetic multi-viewpoint data generation for improving robustness to novel camera viewpoints/scenes over training on real data alone
claims.conditions: real robot evaluation under viewpoint/scene shift

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our 'camera slightly moved' and appearance-shift failure modes: claims synthetic-data-trained policy can outperform real-data-trained policy under novel viewpoint/scene; full text needed to see if this holds for single-arm low-cost setups and what augmentation of camera viewpoint specifically contributed.

title: Video Generators are Robot Policies

claims.claim: Video Policy, a modular framework combining video generation and action generation trained end-to-end, achieves superior performance compared to traditional behavior cloning by using video generation as a proxy for policy learning
claims.direction: favors video-generation-based policy learning over standard behavior-cloning action heads
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation, qualitative comparison to BC, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Learning to generate videos of robot behavior allows policy extraction with minimal demonstration data, significantly improving sample efficiency, and action-free video data provides critical benefits for generalizing to novel tasks
claims.direction: favors leveraging action-free video data plus minimal demonstrations over relying solely on larger labeled action datasets
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, minimal demo regime

claims.claim: The method shows strong generalization to unseen objects, backgrounds, and tasks in both simulation and the real world, with task success closely tied to the quality of the generated video
claims.direction: favors video-generation-based policies for robustness to novel objects/backgrounds over standard BC policies
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, qualitative claims of strong generalization

why_deep_read: Directly challenges our current BC-style (SmolVLA) approach with claimed superior generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds using minimal demos; since object/background/lighting generalization is our core failure mode, the full paper's quantitative comparisons to BC would be valuable, though the video-generation approach may be too compute-heavy for our 8GB GPU.

title: Toward Human-Robot Teaming: Learning Handover Behaviors from 3D Scenes

claims.claim: Sparse-view Gaussian Splatting reconstruction of scenes can generate robot demonstrations (image-action pairs) entirely from RGB images without real-robot data collection or training, serving as an effective representation for training a handover policy
claims.direction: favors Gaussian-Splatting-based synthetic demonstration generation over real-robot teleoperated data collection
claims.conditions: human-to-robot handover task, real-world + reconstructed-scene experiments, qualitative claim of effectiveness

claims.claim: Camera pose changes in a reconstructed 3D scene, captured via a gripper-mounted camera, can be directly translated into gripper pose changes for policy training
claims.direction: supports using a wrist/gripper-mounted camera viewpoint as the basis for both demonstration synthesis and control, given its direct link between visual viewpoint and action
claims.conditions: gripper-mounted camera, Gaussian Splatting reconstructed scenes plus real-world validation

title: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success

claims.claim: An Optimized Fine-Tuning (OFT) recipe using a simple L1 regression-based learning objective (rather than diffusion) for the action head, combined with parallel decoding and action chunking, boosts OpenVLA's average success rate on LIBERO from 76.5% to 97.1%
claims.direction: favors simple L1/MSE regression action objective over diffusion-based objectives for fine-tuning a pretrained VLA, when combined with parallel decoding and chunking
claims.conditions: OpenVLA base model, LIBERO sim benchmark (4 task suites)

claims.claim: The OFT recipe increases action generation throughput by 26x via parallel decoding of action chunks, versus the default autoregressive decoding
claims.direction: favors parallel (non-autoregressive) decoding of action chunks for much higher throughput / lower latency
claims.conditions: OpenVLA on LIBERO; also validated as enabling dexterous, high-frequency control on a real bimanual ALOHA robot

claims.claim: OpenVLA-OFT (large pretrained VLA fine-tuned with OFT recipe) outperforms other VLAs (pi0, RDT-1B) fine-tuned with their default recipes, and outperforms strong imitation learning policies trained from scratch (Diffusion Policy and ACT) by up to 15% absolute average success rate on a real bimanual ALOHA robot
claims.direction: favors fine-tuning a large pretrained VLA with an optimized recipe over training smaller specialist policies (Diffusion Policy, ACT) from scratch, on high-frequency dexterous real-robot tasks

claims.claim: A continuous action representation (vs. discretized tokens) is one of the key components of the effective fine-tuning recipe, alongside action chunking and parallel decoding
claims.direction: favors continuous action representation over discrete action tokens for VLA fine-tuning
claims.conditions: OpenVLA on LIBERO + real ALOHA

why_deep_read: This is a controlled ablation study of action-decoding scheme, action representation, and learning objective for VLA fine-tuning with large, quantified gains (76.5%->97.1% success, 26x throughput, up to 15% absolute over Diffusion Policy/ACT) directly on real bimanual hardware -- centrally relevant to our Q01/Q02/Q06/Q10/Q12 decisions and our jerky-motion/latency failure mode; the full paper's per-component ablation would let us adopt only the parts that fit our compute budget.

title: AXIS: A Growable Community-Driven Data Engine for Scalable Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Continual pretraining on the AXIS dataset (207 tasks, 50K+ community-collected, quality-filtered and augmented trajectories) improves the overall success rate of pi0.5 by 5.8%, and outperforms a model pretrained on RoboCasa365 by 37.3%, with performance scaling consistently as data volume increases

claims.conditions: VLA policy (pi0.5) pretraining, systematic held-out evaluation protocol, browser-based teleoperation data collection

claims.claim: The largest performance gains from AXIS pretraining are observed under layout, sensor-noise, and camera-perturbation test conditions
claims.direction: supports that data diversity/scale/augmentation targeted at layout, sensor-noise, and camera perturbations specifically improves robustness to those perturbations

why_deep_read: Quantifies how much data scale/diversity/augmentation improves a generalist VLA's robustness specifically to camera perturbations and sensor noise -- our exact failure modes (moved camera, lighting) -- and contrasts it with a same-purpose but less diverse dataset; the ablation on data volume vs. robustness gain would help decide how much augmentation/diversity we need for our own ~50-100 demo dataset.

title: PALM: Progress-Aware Policy Learning via Affordance Reasoning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Distilling affordance representations (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, motion dynamics) as task-relevant anchors, plus predicting continuous within-subtask progress as an auxiliary signal, stabilizes long-horizon execution and reduces critical errors (repeated actions, missed steps, premature termination) versus VLA baselines without such reasoning mechanisms
claims.direction: favors adding affordance-distillation and progress-prediction auxiliary objectives to a VLA over a plain VLA policy for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO-LONG, CALVIN ABC->D) and real-world long-horizon generalization settings

claims.claim: PALM achieves a 91.8% success rate on LIBERO-LONG, a 12.5% improvement in average completed sequence length on CALVIN ABC->D, and a 2x improvement over real-world baselines across three long-horizon generalization settings
claims.direction: quantifies generalization gains from progress/affordance-aware policy learning under long-horizon, out-of-distribution-like real-world settings
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon manipulation, comparison against unspecified baselines

why_deep_read: Provides quantified real-world generalization gains (2x over baselines) directly attributable to specific auxiliary objectives (affordance + progress prediction), relevant to Q09; full text ablations would clarify how much of the gain each auxiliary component contributes and whether it is feasible on a small model.

title: HapCompass: A Rotational Haptic Device for Contact-Rich Robotic Teleoperation

claims.claim: A preliminary imitation-learning evaluation suggests that directional haptic feedback during teleoperation (vs. vision-only or non-directional feedback) enhances the quality of collected demonstration data and, in turn, the performance of the trained policy
claims.direction: favors improving teleoperation feedback modality to raise demonstration quality, as an alternative/complement to collecting more demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world teleoperation with a wearable haptic device, preliminary evaluation, no quantitative policy success numbers given

title: Lighting-Robust Behavioral Cloning via Bayesian Visual Encoding for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Modeling a posterior distribution over convolutional visual-encoder weights (Bayesian deep learning) with a KL-regularized evidence lower bound, rather than a deterministic encoder, improves robustness to illumination-induced distribution shift while maintaining sample efficiency with only a single Monte Carlo sample at inference
claims.direction: favors Bayesian/probabilistic visual encoding over deterministic CNN encoders for lighting robustness
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments across seven illumination regimes

claims.claim: In real-world experiments across seven illumination regimes, including distribution-shifted conditions, the Bayesian-encoder BC method consistently outperforms standard BC baselines and remains stable under severe lighting changes; in simulation it also achieves higher success rates and shorter rollout lengths than deterministic baselines
claims.direction: directly supports Bayesian visual encoding as a fix for lighting-induced policy degradation in behavior cloning
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, 7 illumination regimes, deterministic-baseline comparison

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled real-world study (7 illumination regimes) of exactly our #1 stated failure mode -- policy breaking under new lighting -- with a concrete fix (Bayesian visual encoder) and quantified outperformance over deterministic BC baselines; the full text's architecture/training details are worth extracting to potentially apply directly to our SmolVLA fine-tune.

title: CoLA-Flow Policy: Temporally Coherent Imitation Learning via Continuous Latent Action Flow Matching for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Performing flow matching in a continuous latent action space (encoding action sequences into temporally coherent latent trajectories) rather than in the raw action space decouples global motion structure from low-level control noise, improving trajectory smoothness by up to 93.7% and task success by up to 25 percentage points over raw action-space flow baselines
claims.direction: favors latent-space flow matching over raw-action-space flow matching for smoother, more successful long-horizon execution
claims.conditions: sim + real robot experiments, trajectory-level imitation learning

claims.claim: CoLA-Flow Policy achieves near-single-step inference while remaining significantly faster than diffusion-based policies, addressing the latency/expressiveness trade-off between diffusion and flow matching
claims.direction: favors latent flow matching for low-latency, real-time inference over diffusion-based action generation
claims.conditions: sim + real robot, long-horizon manipulation

claims.claim: Geometry-aware point cloud conditioning integrated with execution-time multimodal (visual) modulation enhances real-world robustness
claims.direction: supports combining point-cloud geometric conditioning with visual cues over vision-only conditioning
claims.conditions: real robot, no exact ablation numbers given for point-cloud contribution alone

why_deep_read: Directly targets our jerky-motion-at-chunk-boundaries and inference-latency failure modes with quantified real-robot smoothness (+93.7%) and success (+25pp) gains from latent-space (vs raw-action-space) flow matching; full text needed for architecture details to judge feasibility on our 8GB GPU.

title: Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency

claims.claim: A training-free, test-time correction framework (RTCF) that retrieves aligned successful-trajectory experience and transfers a low-frequency residual onto a frozen VLA's action chunk raises aggregate LIBERO success from 86.4% to 88.4% (and LIBERO-Long from 61.6% to 68.6%) with no parameter updates, no repeated VLA inference, and only ~11ms added latency per action chunk, running on CPU
claims.direction: favors lightweight, training-free, CPU-side test-time correction of action chunks over retraining or added GPU inference cost to fix accumulated execution error
claims.conditions: frozen VLA policy, 4 LIBERO suites, 2000 episodes/condition, sim benchmark

claims.claim: Separating 'which experience to retrieve' from 'which part of the action to transfer' (correcting only low-frequency motion channels while leaving higher-frequency components and gripper decisions to the frozen policy) avoids overwriting the reactive structure of action chunks that naive replay/time-domain fusion would disrupt
claims.direction: favors frequency-selective correction of action chunks over naive full-chunk replay or time-domain fusion for reducing execution error across chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: frozen VLA action-chunk policies, sim benchmark

title: MAAP: Multi-Agent Active Perception for Collaborative Manipulation

claims.claim: Widening the perception regime from a single fixed camera to one active wrist-mounted camera view raises average success from 56.5% to 62.5% across four simulated tasks, and using all available wrist views raises it to 70.0%; adding a role-aware controller (MAAP+RAIL) reaches 79.2%
claims.direction: favors active/moving wrist camera viewpoints over a single fixed scene camera for perception quality
claims.conditions: multi-arm simulated manipulation tasks (up to 3 arms), each arm carrying its own wrist camera

claims.claim: On a real dual-arm platform, MAAP+RAIL succeeds in 14 of 20 placement trials versus 0 of 20 for a fixed-view ACT baseline
claims.direction: strongly favors moving/wrist camera perception over fixed single-camera perception for real-robot success
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, placement task, ACT baseline with fixed camera fails completely

title: PoCo: Policy Composition from and for Heterogeneous Robot Learning

claims.claim: Composing diffusion-model-represented policies trained on heterogeneous data (different modalities such as color/depth/tactile/proprioceptive, and different domains such as simulation, real robot, and human video) outperforms baselines trained from a single data source, and outperforms simple baselines that naively pool very heterogeneous data together
claims.direction: favors compositional combination of separately-trained diffusion policies over either single-source training or naive data pooling across heterogeneous domains/modalities
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot tool-use tasks, qualitative 'robust and dexterous performance' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Diffusion models are used as the representation for composing different data distributions, and can be further composed at inference time with analytic cost functions to adapt policy behavior
claims.direction: supports diffusion-based action/behavior representations as amenable to test-time composition/adaptation
claims.conditions: sim + real, multi-task and multi-domain composition

title: FMimic: Foundation Models are Fine-grained Action Learners from Human Videos

claims.claim: Learning fine-grained manipulation skills directly from a limited number of human demonstration videos (as few as 1, strongly improving with 5), using keypoint/waypoint-based hierarchical constraint representations instead of predefined motion primitives, outperforms baselines by over 39% (RLBench) and 29% (real-world), and by more than 34% on high-precision tasks and 47% on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors extracting fine-grained, keypoint-based skill representations from very few human videos over relying on predefined motion primitives or larger demonstration sets
claims.conditions: RLBench sim benchmark + real-world manipulation, human video demonstrations (not robot teleop), 1-5 videos

title: High-Fidelity Simulated Data Generation for Real-World Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation Learning With Gaussian Splatting

claims.claim: RoboSimGS reconstructs real-world scenes with a hybrid representation (3D Gaussian Splatting for photorealistic appearance + mesh primitives for interactive-object physics), using an MLLM to automatically infer physical properties and kinematic structure of objects from visual data, enabling policies trained entirely on this synthetic data to achieve successful zero-shot Sim2Real transfer across diverse real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors automated photorealistic+physical simulation (Gaussian-Splatting-based Real2Sim2Real) synthetic data generation over real-robot data collection for training deployable policies
claims.conditions: zero-shot sim-to-real, diverse real-world manipulation tasks, qualitative claim ('successful zero-shot transfer'), no exact success numbers given

claims.claim: Data generated by RoboSimGS significantly enhances the performance and generalization capabilities of SOTA methods beyond what real data alone achieves
claims.direction: supports synthetic Real2Sim2Real data as a generalization booster on top of/instead of additional real data collection
claims.conditions: comparison against SOTA methods, qualitative claim

title: VLA-Thinker: Boosting Vision-Language-Action Models through Thinking-with-Image Reasoning

claims.claim: Treating perception as a dynamically invocable reasoning action ('thinking-with-image') rather than static visual context, trained via an SFT cold-start plus GRPO-based RL alignment, significantly improves manipulation performance, achieving 97.5% success on LIBERO and strong gains on long-horizon RoboTwin 2.0 tasks
claims.direction: favors an auxiliary active-perception/reasoning objective (revisiting the image during reasoning) over standard static text-based chain-of-thought VLA reasoning
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0), no real-robot results given in abstract

title: TapSampling: Inference-Time Sampling with a Task-Progress-Understanding Verifier for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A plug-and-play, policy-agnostic inference-time sampling framework (drawing multiple latent action candidates via an Action-VAE and selecting among them with a task-progress verifier) substantially improves multiple generalist policies without any further policy fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors improving performance via inference-time sampling/verification strategies rather than scaling training data or model size
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, applied on top of existing generalist policies, no exact success numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Representing policy-generated actions in a low-dimensional latent space (Action-VAE) allows multiple candidate action samples to be efficiently drawn and decoded to approximate the true (multimodal) action distribution at inference time
claims.direction: supports latent action-space sampling as a way to capture multimodality beyond a single deterministic/single-sample rollout
claims.conditions: generalist policies, sim + real-world

title: Performant robotic manipulation with real-world reinforcement learning

claims.claim: RL-100 unifies imitation and RL under a single clipped-PPO-style surrogate objective applied within a diffusion visuomotor policy's denoising process, and uses lightweight consistency distillation to compress the multistep diffusion policy into a one-step controller for high-frequency control
claims.direction: favors diffusion policies refined with RL (not pure BC) and then distilled to one-step for deployment, over either pure BC diffusion or non-distilled multistep diffusion
claims.conditions: real-world, 8 diverse manipulation tasks, task/embodiment/representation-agnostic, supports single-action and action-chunking control

claims.claim: Consistency-distilling a multistep diffusion policy into a one-step controller meets high-frequency control latency requirements while achieving 100% success in evaluated trials (1000/1000 episodes, including 250/250 consecutive on one task) under a predefined real-world evaluation protocol, matching or surpassing expert teleoperators in completion time
claims.direction: strongly favors one-step-distilled diffusion policies for combining high task success with low-latency, high-frequency real-time control
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, 8 tasks including pushing, bowling, pouring, cloth folding, unscrewing, juicing, box folding

claims.claim: Without retraining, a single RL-100 policy attains ~90% zero-shot success under environmental and dynamics shifts, adapts to substantial task variations in a few-shot regime (86.7%), remains robust to human perturbations (~96%), and operated a juicing robot continuously for ~7 hours without failure when deployed zero-shot in a public shopping mall
claims.direction: provides strong real-world quantified evidence that RL-refined, distilled diffusion policies can generalize/remain robust under environmental shift and physical perturbation far beyond typical pure-BC robustness
claims.conditions: real-world public deployment, zero-shot and few-shot conditions, multiple task types

why_deep_read: Landmark real-world result (published in Science Robotics) directly bearing on our latency problem (one-step consistency-distilled diffusion for high-frequency control) and robustness under environmental/dynamics shift; full text needed for the exact distillation recipe and how much real-world RL interaction (vs. pure demos) was required, since our setup is teleop-demo-only.

title: Fine-Tuning VLAs with Self-Demonstrated Generative Control for Multi-Task Manipulation

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained VLA (e.g. pi0.5) directly on in-domain expert data from a new robot embodiment improves performance on the target task but causes a loss of the model's original instruction-following ability and behavioral priors (catastrophic narrowing), even when the hardware mismatch from pretraining is only minor
claims.direction: identifies a specific failure mode of naive fine-tuning on a small new-embodiment demo set, motivating augmentation strategies that preserve generalist priors
claims.conditions: pretrained generalist VLA, new robot embodiment, standard fine-tuning on expert data

claims.claim: Augmenting fine-tuning data with self-supervised online interaction rollouts generated by the zero-shot VLA itself (rather than relying purely on new in-domain expert demonstrations) yields policies that retain prior-task/instruction-following behavior while learning the new skill with improved sample efficiency
claims.direction: favors mixing self-generated rollout data with a small expert demo set over fine-tuning on the expert demos alone
claims.conditions: real ALOHA robot + RoboTwin simulation benchmark, multi-task evaluation

title: LIMT: Language-Informed Multi-Task Visual World Models

claims.claim: Model-based multi-task RL using learned visual world models shows a clear advantage over the more common model-free multi-task RL paradigm, which is otherwise very sample-inefficient even for single-task agents
claims.direction: favors model-based (world-model) approaches over model-free RL for sample efficiency in multi-task settings

claims.conditions: multi-task RL simulation, qualitative

title: VLMimic: Vision Language Models are Visual Imitation Learner for Fine-grained Actions

claims.claim: Using only 5 human demonstration videos, grounding object-centric movements and learning fine-grained skills via hierarchical constraint representations (rather than predefined motion primitives) yields improvements of over 27% (RLBench) and 21% (real-world), and over 37% on long-horizon tasks versus baselines
claims.direction: favors extracting fine-grained skill representations from very few (5) human videos over predefined motion primitives or larger training sets
claims.conditions: RLBench sim + real-world manipulation, human video demonstrations (not robot teleop)

title: Fidelity-Aware Data Composition for Robust Robot Generalization

claims.claim: Naively mixing real and synthetic/generative-augmentation data can corrupt the learning signal by prioritizing visual diversity over information fidelity; a principled, fidelity-aware composition framework (CIFT) that identifies a 'Decoherence Point' where training stability degrades, combined with a Multi-View Video Augmentation generative engine, improves out-of-distribution success rates by over 54% when applied to pi0 and Diffusion Policy
claims.direction: favors carefully-tuned, fidelity-aware mixing ratios of real+synthetic data over simply maximizing visual diversity/quantity of augmented data
claims.conditions: policy architectures pi0 and Diffusion Policy, OOD evaluation, quantified 54%+ improvement

claims.claim: Generalist policies trained on large, visually homogeneous datasets are susceptible to shortcut learning that impairs OOD generalization, which fidelity-aware data composition specifically addresses
claims.direction: supports diagnosing/fixing shortcut learning via data composition tuning rather than just adding more diverse data
claims.conditions: generalist policy architectures, OOD generalization testing

why_deep_read: Gives a concrete, quantified (+54% OOD) recipe for HOW to mix real and synthetic/augmented data without corrupting the learning signal -- directly actionable for our small (50-100 demo) dataset if we add synthetic/augmented data to fix lighting/camera/object generalization; the 'Decoherence Point' diagnostic could be a practical tool.

title: Generalist Robot Manipulation beyond Action Labeled Data

claims.claim: Self-supervised pretraining on action-unlabeled human and robot videos (via a 3D dynamics predictor at the hand/gripper location, later tuned into an action predictor using a smaller labeled dataset) improves downstream generalist robot policies and enables learning new tasks without any action labels for those new tasks
claims.direction: favors leveraging cheap action-free video data plus a small labeled set over relying solely on larger action-labeled demonstration datasets
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated settings, qualitative improvement claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Extracting dense, dynamic 3D point clouds at the hand/gripper location is used as the self-supervised prediction target for learning manipulation-relevant dynamics from unlabeled video
claims.direction: supports 3D point-cloud-based dynamics representations as a self-supervision signal, complementary to RGB
claims.conditions: real + sim, self-supervised pretraining stage

title: A Hybrid Framework Using Diffusion Policy and Residual RL for Force-Sensitive Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining a diffusion policy (imitation learning, generating smooth expert-like motion-force trajectories) with a residual RL module (online adaptation of force commands to unmodeled contact dynamics) achieves an 88% average success rate across 12 unseen scenarios on a real 7-DOF arm, outperforming SOTA baselines
claims.direction: favors hybrid diffusion-IL + residual-RL over pure diffusion IL or pure RL for contact-rich tasks requiring both smooth motion and online force adaptation
claims.conditions: real 7-DOF robotic arm, basin-cleaning force-sensitive tasks, 12 unseen scenarios

claims.claim: Multimodal perception combining RGB point clouds, force feedback, and proprioceptive data supports robust force-sensitive manipulation in unstructured environments
claims.direction: supports adding point-cloud/force modalities beyond RGB for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, force-sensitive manipulation

title: EchoVLA: Robotic Vision-Language-Action Model with Synergistic Declarative Memory for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding a synergistic declarative memory (a scene memory of spatial-semantic maps plus an episodic memory of task-level experiences, fused via coarse- and fine-grained attention to guide diffusion policies) improves success rate over the strong pi0.5 baseline by +0.20 (to 0.52) on manipulation/navigation tasks and +0.11 (to 0.31) on mobile manipulation tasks in simulation

claims.conditions: simulated mobile manipulation benchmark (MoMani), plus real-robot validation; comparison against pi0.5 baseline

title: ProbeFlow: Training-Free Adaptive Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A training-free adaptive inference framework that evaluates geometric trajectory complexity (cosine similarity between initial and lookahead velocity vectors) to dynamically prune redundant ODE-solver steps in a flow-matching action head accelerates action decoding by 14.8x (average integration steps reduced from 50 to 2.6) and cuts end-to-end system latency by 2.8x on MetaWorld, without compromising success rate; real-world deployments confirm mitigated latency while preserving execution stability
claims.direction: favors training-free, adaptive-step flow-matching inference (fewer ODE solver evaluations when trajectories are geometrically simple) over fixed many-step integration schedules, to cut action-head latency specifically (as opposed to only optimizing the VLM backbone)
claims.conditions: MetaWorld sim benchmark + real-world physical deployment, flow-matching VLA action heads

claims.claim: On the long-horizon LIBERO benchmark, the same adaptive scheduler automatically allocates denser integration schedules at semantic bottlenecks, showing that flow-matching action-head latency (not just VLM backbone latency) is a solvable, task-dependent bottleneck
claims.direction: supports flow matching as a viable action head if its solver-step latency is adaptively managed, rather than a fixed per-step cost
claims.conditions: LIBERO long-horizon sim benchmark

title: LA4VLA: Learning to Act without Seeing via Language-Action Pretraining

claims.claim: Because dense visual-action supervision can dominate the sparser language-action signal during standard VLA pretraining, policies may rely on visual shortcuts rather than learning how language conditions actions, making them sensitive to visual variations; pretraining policies on language-action pairs derived from decomposed demonstration trajectories WITHOUT visual observations (LA-only pretraining) yields reusable, scene-agnostic manipulation-skill priors
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit language-action (vision-free) pretraining stage to reduce reliance on scene-specific visual cues, rather than relying purely on joint vision+language+action training
claims.conditions: LA-33K dataset (33K language-action episodes) derived from existing demonstrations with no new robot data collection, lightweight 1B-parameter VLA (LA4VLA-1B)

claims.claim: Mixed language-action + vision-language-action (LA-VLA) pretraining improves the average success rate of a 1B-parameter VLA over a no-pretraining baseline by up to 17.8 percentage points in simulation and 45.0 percentage points in real-world tasks, consistently outperforming matched VLA-only pretraining
claims.direction: strongly supports combining vision-free language-action pretraining with standard VLA pretraining to reduce visual-shortcut sensitivity and improve real-world robustness/success
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks, 1B-parameter VLA model

why_deep_read: Diagnoses precisely the mechanism behind our stated failure mode (policy breaking under new lighting/appearance because it learned visual shortcuts instead of language/action-conditioned priors), and proposes a data-cheap fix (decompose existing demos into language-action pairs, no new robot data) with large real-world gains (+45pp); worth extracting the exact LA-pair construction recipe to see if it transfers to our small demo set.

title: DAISS: Phase-Aware Imitation Learning for Dual-Arm Robotic Ultrasound-Guided Interventions

claims.claim: A lightweight, phase-aware imitation policy with a dynamic mask loss can learn personalized expert strategies for asymmetric bimanual ultrasound-guided tasks from limited demonstrations
claims.direction: supports phase-aware architectural design (rather than more data) as a way to remain data-efficient on complex asymmetric bimanual tasks
claims.conditions: real teleoperated dual-arm surgical platform, qualitative claim of learning from 'limited demonstrations', no exact numbers given

title: Emergence of Human to Robot Transfer in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A simple co-training recipe combining human video data with robot demonstration data shows human-to-robot skill transfer only 'emerges' (i.e., produces a benefit) once the VLA is pretrained on a sufficiently large and diverse scale of robot scenes/tasks/embodiments; below that scale threshold, human video co-training does not clearly help

claims.claim: With sufficiently diverse robot pre-training, the co-training method nearly doubles performance on generalization settings that were seen only in the human demonstration data (not the robot data)
claims.direction: supports human video data as a generalization booster, but only above a data-scale/diversity threshold
claims.conditions: large-scale VLA pretraining regime

title: CoStream: Composing Simple Behaviors for Generalizable Complex Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing manipulation capability into composable core behaviors (a foundation-model-based semantic behavior, a predictive behavior forecasting trajectories via keypoint tracking in imagined/generated videos, and a reactive behavior providing high-frequency tactile/force corrections), combined on a shared SE(3) interface, achieves robust recovery from manual perturbations across 8 real-world tasks including precision assembly
claims.direction: favors decomposing a monolithic policy into composable semantic/predictive/reactive behavior streams over a single end-to-end policy, especially for precision, contact-rich, out-of-distribution tasks

title: RayViT: Ray-Conditioned Visual Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Injecting camera geometry (as a Plucker ray map, patchified into ray features) into a pretrained ViT backbone via gated cross-attention -- replacing the class token with a ray-conditioned one and adding ray features as dense positional embeddings, plus an auxiliary cosine-similarity loss -- is a lightweight way to make a pretrained vision encoder geometry-aware without training from scratch
claims.direction: favors augmenting pretrained ViT encoders with explicit camera-geometry conditioning over using RGB-only pretrained encoders for policies exposed to camera perturbations
claims.conditions: sim (RoboCasa multi-task benchmark) and real-robot multi-task experiments

claims.claim: RayViT improves robustness by approximately 13 percentage points under camera perturbations on the multi-task RoboCasa benchmark, and by 1.78 average completed stages in real-world multi-task success rate compared to baselines
claims.direction: directly supports geometry-aware (ray-conditioned) visual encoding as a fix for camera-viewpoint/pose sensitivity
claims.conditions: sim (RoboCasa) + real-robot multi-task, explicit camera-perturbation evaluation

claims.claim: RGB-only visual imitation learning policies lack explicit geometric cues, making them brittle to camera perturbations; adding explicit camera geometry conditioning is shown to directly mitigate this brittleness
claims.direction: identifies camera-perturbation brittleness as a core limitation of RGB-only IL policies (matching our reported camera-shift failure) and offers a concrete architectural fix
claims.conditions: sim + real, multi-task

why_deep_read: This is a near-exact match to our reported 'breaks when camera is slightly moved' failure mode, with a lightweight (drop-in on pretrained ViT backbones) architectural fix and quantified sim (+13pp) and real-world (+1.78 stages) gains; full text needed for the Plucker-ray conditioning implementation details to judge feasibility with our single fixed RealSense + wrist camera setup.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Decoupling slow, expressive action-chunk generation (from a large pretrained VLA) from fast, reactive action edits (via a lightweight edit policy conditioned on the latest observation) and RL-fine-tuning this combination (Real-Time EXPO-FT) improves average policy performance from 42% to 97% on four dynamic real-world tasks (object passing, ball balancing, table-soccer kicking, dynamic object picking), using only 10 minutes of online robot data and no human intervention
claims.direction: favors a two-speed architecture (slow VLA action-chunk proposer + fast lightweight reactive edit policy, RL-tuned) over single-speed asynchronous execution of a large VLA's action chunks, to handle inference latency and stale observations in dynamic real-time tasks
claims.conditions: real-world dynamic manipulation tasks, RL fine-tuning on top of a pretrained VLA (EXPO-FT), only 10 minutes of online data required

title: Dynamic Behavior Cloning With Temporal Feature Prediction: Enhancing Robotic Arm Manipulation in Moving Object Tasks

claims.claim: Standard behavior cloning, which relies primarily on the current-frame observation/state to predict actions, falls short in dynamic (moving-object) contexts due to its static nature; leveraging historical frames to capture dynamic features addresses this limitation
claims.direction: favors incorporating observation history over single-frame/memoryless BC policies for tasks with moving objects or dynamic scenes
claims.conditions: custom benchmark of 8 task scenarios (6 foundational, 2 advanced), comparison to traditional BC

claims.claim: Adding an auxiliary future-scene-image prediction objective (MSE loss between predicted and ground-truth future frame), integrated with behavior cloning via a temporal-feature-prediction module, significantly improves the success rate of BC in dynamic scenarios compared to traditional behavior cloning
claims.direction: favors an auxiliary future-frame-prediction objective jointly trained with the action-prediction objective, over standard BC with no auxiliary visual-prediction loss
claims.conditions: custom 8-task benchmark, comparison against traditional BC; qualitative 'significantly improves', no exact numbers given

title: TwinAligner: Visual-Dynamic Alignment Empowers Physics-aware Real2Sim2Real for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Real2Sim2Real system (TwinAligner) that aligns both visual appearance (via SDF reconstruction + editable 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering) and physical dynamics (identifying rigid-body physics from robot-object interaction) enables policies trained in simulation to achieve strong zero-shot generalization to the real world, with high consistency between real-world and simulated policy performance
claims.direction: favors jointly aligning visual AND dynamic gaps (not just visual) in Real2Sim2Real pipelines for reliable sim-trained policy transfer
claims.conditions: sim-to-real transfer, qualitative claim of 'strong zero-shot generalization' and 'high consistency', no exact numbers given

title: BitVLA: 1-bit Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics Manipulation

claims.claim: A fully native 1-bit VLA model (BitVLA, ternary {-1,0,1} weights, built on BitNet b1.58 2B4T) matches the performance of the full-precision OpenVLA-OFT baseline across simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks while reducing model memory by 11.0x
claims.direction: strongly favors extreme weight quantization (1-bit/ternary) for VLA policies over full-precision models when performance parity can be maintained, for memory-constrained deployment
claims.conditions: real-world tasks + simulation benchmarks, comparison against full-precision OpenVLA-OFT

claims.claim: BitVLA reduces end-to-end latency by 4.4x compared to the full-precision baseline while matching task performance
claims.direction: supports extreme quantization as a direct lever for reducing inference latency without sacrificing success rate
claims.conditions: real-world + sim, same comparison as above

claims.claim: A 'Quantize-then-Distill' post-training quantization-aware training strategy compresses a full-precision vision encoder to 1.58-bit weights while a full-precision teacher guides representation alignment during training, further reducing the vision backbone's memory footprint without the accuracy loss typical of naive post-hoc quantization
claims.direction: favors quantization-aware distillation (teacher-guided) over naive post-hoc compression for the vision encoder specifically
claims.conditions: vision encoder within a VLA pipeline, real-world + sim tasks

why_deep_read: Directly targets our exact hardware constraint (8GB laptop GPU, ~2s inference latency) with quantified, matched-performance results (11x memory reduction, 4.4x latency reduction); the full paper's quantization/distillation recipe is very likely reusable for shrinking our SmolVLA fine-tune to fit comfortably and run faster on our hardware.

title: Clutter-Robust Vision-Language-Action Models through Object-Centric and Geometry Grounding

claims.claim: Monolithic VLA pipelines that map raw RGB directly to actions erode language-conditioned grounding; explicitly disentangling perception from action reasoning via a VLM-based object-centric grounding stage (selecting task-relevant object regions across camera views) plus a geometric grounding stage (emphasizing 3D structure over appearance) substantially improves robustness over strong VLA baselines
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit object-centric + geometry-aware perception module in front of the action policy over feeding raw RGB directly into a monolithic VLA
claims.conditions: real-world UR10e tabletop setup, policy fine-tuned exclusively on single-object demonstrations collected WITHOUT clutter or non-target objects

claims.claim: In real-world tests, standard VLA policies over-grasp when the target is absent, are distracted by clutter, and overfit to background appearance; OBEYED-VLA substantially improves robustness across four regimes -- distractor objects, absent-target rejection, background appearance changes, and cluttered manipulation of unseen objects -- and ablations confirm both semantic and geometric grounding are critical to these gains
claims.direction: directly supports object-centric + geometric grounding as a fix for background-appearance overfitting, distractor sensitivity, and false-positive grasping, using a policy trained only on clean single-object demos
claims.conditions: real-world UR10e, trained on single-object clutter-free demos, tested under clutter/distractors/background-shift/unseen objects

why_deep_read: This paper's stated real-world failure modes (over-grasping when target absent, distraction by clutter, background-appearance overfitting) and training setup (fine-tuned only on single-object, clutter-free demos) are almost a direct description of our own setup and observed SmolVLA failures (breaks with new lighting/different pumpkin/moved camera); the ablations on which grounding component matters most would be highly actionable for us.

title: Emerging Extrinsic Dexterity in Cluttered Scenes via Dynamics-aware Policy Learning

claims.claim: Conditioning RL on a learned representation of contact-induced object dynamics (via explicit world modeling), rather than hand-crafted contact heuristics or reward shaping, lets extrinsic dexterity emerge, outperforming prehensile manipulation, human teleoperation, and prior representation-based policies by over 25% success rate on unseen simulated cluttered scenes; real-world success reaches ~50% across 10 cluttered scenes with a practical grocery deployment
claims.direction: favors an explicit learned world-model/dynamics-representation auxiliary objective over hand-crafted heuristics for policies operating in cluttered, contact-rich scenes
claims.conditions: RL-trained, sim + real-world (grocery deployment), cluttered scenes with varying densities

title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
