claims.claim: Feeding transformer-based policies dense pre-trained ViT patch tokens directly (via a block-causal attention mask that preserves temporal causality while attending over many patch tokens per observation), instead of compressing each observation into a single global token or training a visual backbone from scratch, achieves a 40% relative improvement over policies using state-of-the-art global-pooled representations
claims.direction: favors dense per-patch pretrained visual features over global-pooled single-token representations or from-scratch visual backbones
claims.conditions: 4 simulated + 3 real-world environment suites

claims.claim: Patch Policy surpasses fine-tuned OpenVLA-OFT by 18% (relative success) while using roughly 0.7% of the parameters, avoiding the full cost of a billion-parameter VLM backbone
claims.direction: strongly favors a small, lightweight architecture built around dense pretrained patch features over a billion-parameter VLA backbone, when the goal is efficient high-frequency control
claims.conditions: comparison against fine-tuned OpenVLA-OFT, sim + real-world

claims.claim: Patch Policy is described as lightweight and fast, suitable for high-frequency, reactive control without sacrificing training efficiency or inference speed
claims.direction: supports architectures that avoid full VLM backbones specifically to preserve low-latency, high-frequency control
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, comparison to heavier VLA-based dense-patch policies

why_deep_read: Claims beating fine-tuned OpenVLA-OFT while using only ~0.7% of its parameters is exceptionally relevant to our 8GB-GPU / low-latency constraints; the full paper's exact architecture (block-causal attention over patch tokens) could plausibly be adopted directly in place of our SmolVLA fine-tune to fix both the vision-representation and latency problems simultaneously.

title: LILAC: Language-Conditioned Object-Centric Optical Flow for Open-Loop Trajectory Generation

claims.claim: Generating object-centric 2D optical flow from an RGB image and language instruction, then converting the flow into a 6-DoF manipulator trajectory (rather than directly regressing actions), outperformed existing approaches in generated flow quality and demonstrated superior real-world task success with free-form instructions
claims.direction: favors an intermediate optical-flow action representation over direct action regression for language-conditioned manipulation
claims.conditions: physical robot experiments with free-form instructions, multiple benchmarks; qualitative 'superior' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: The flow-based approach enables training on human and web videos of object manipulation and requires only minimal embodiment-specific (robot) data
claims.direction: favors leveraging human/web video plus minimal robot-specific data over collecting large robot teleop datasets
claims.conditions: flow-based VLA, minimal embodiment-specific fine-tuning data

title: Gaze2Act: Gaze-Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Policies for Interactive Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Augmenting language conditioning with human gaze (mapped from first-person to robot perspective, producing an object mask and gaze point) as an additional intent signal, integrated via perception-level prompting and action-level conditioning, achieves state-of-the-art intent accuracy and task success versus baselines across 16 real-robot tasks, particularly for object disambiguation among similar candidates
claims.direction: favors supplementing language conditioning with an additional, more precise intent signal (here, gaze) when language alone is ambiguous about which object/location is intended
claims.conditions: real-robot humanoid (Unitree G1), 16 tasks across 7 categories; qualitative 'state-of-the-art' claim relative to unspecified baselines

title: MemoryWAM: Efficient World Action Modeling with Persistent Memory

claims.claim: A hybrid memory design combining recent frames, event-boundary anchor frames, and compact 'gist' tokens summarizing long-range history (retrieved via a tailored attention mechanism) resolves the trade-off between bounded-window world-action models (which struggle in non-Markovian settings) and full-history models (whose cost grows with sequence length), outperforming strong VLA and world-action-model baselines on long-horizon, memory-dependent manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors structured hybrid short+long-term memory over both a fixed bounded observation window and naive full-history retention for tasks requiring memory
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, long-horizon memory-dependent manipulation

claims.claim: The hybrid memory design achieves this performance while maintaining reduced inference latency and GPU memory usage relative to full-history alternatives
claims.direction: supports memory-efficient architectures that keep long-horizon context without the latency/memory cost of retaining full history
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, no exact latency/memory numbers given in abstract

title: Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for Token Compression in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Compressing VLA tokens (via stale-KV reuse or token pruning) guided by an 'Action-JND' criterion -- how much a token can change before causing an unacceptable deviation in the policy's downstream action, rather than generic redundancy/attention/saliency cues -- consistently improves compression reliability on LIBERO with OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT, especially under aggressive compression ratios
claims.direction: favors action-outcome-aware (not just visual-redundancy-aware) criteria for deciding which tokens to compress/prune/reuse, when the goal is reducing VLA inference latency without harming action quality
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark, OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT backbones, plug-and-play with existing compression paradigms

title: CogACT: A Foundational Vision-Language-Action Model for Synergizing Cognition and Action in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a specialized diffusion-action-transformer action module conditioned on (rather than directly repurposing) VLM output for simple action quantization gives strong performance enhancement and favorable scaling behavior; the resulting model (7B) exceeds OpenVLA's (similar 7B size) average success rate by over 35% in simulation and 55% in real robot experiments, and outperforms the much larger RT-2-X (55B) by 18% absolute success rate in simulation
claims.direction: strongly favors a dedicated diffusion-transformer action module (componentized architecture) over naive action-token quantization directly on VLM outputs, and shows this design choice matters more than raw model scale
claims.conditions: 5 robot embodiments, sim + real-world, comparison against OpenVLA (7B) and RT-2-X (55B)

claims.claim: A componentized 7B VLA with a specialized diffusion action module outperforms a much larger (55B) VLA, showing that action-module design can substitute for scale
claims.direction: supports investing in action-head/module architecture over simply scaling total model size
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment sim + real evaluation

title: Compliant Residual DAgger: Improving Real-World Contact-Rich Manipulation with Human Corrections

claims.claim: Collecting small amounts of targeted human correction/recovery data (via a compliant intervention interface allowing gentle delta-action corrections without interrupting ongoing policy execution) and updating the policy with a compliant residual formulation improves base policy success rates by 64% on four challenging contact-rich tasks (book flipping, belt assembly, cable routing, gear insertion), outperforming both retraining-from-scratch and standard fine-tuning approaches with the same or more data
claims.direction: strongly favors targeted human correction/recovery demonstrations (DAgger-style) plus a residual policy update over collecting more full demonstrations or naive fine-tuning/retraining
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation, minimal correction data, comparison against retrain-from-scratch and fine-tuning baselines

claims.claim: Learning a residual (delta) action policy that incorporates force feedback and force control on top of a base policy, updated from human corrections, is more effective for precise contact-rich tasks than updating the whole (absolute-action) policy directly
claims.direction: favors residual/delta action-space formulations (with force feedback) over directly retraining an absolute-action base policy
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Directly answers a core question in our Q13 (recovery demos vs. more raw demos) with a strong quantified real-world number (+64% success from minimal correction data, beating retrain-from-scratch and fine-tuning); highly actionable for our 50-100 demo budget since a small set of targeted corrections could be far more valuable than collecting more full demonstrations, and the compliant-intervention interface detail is worth extracting for our own teleop setup.

title: VideoWeaver: Multimodal Multi-View Video-to-Video Transfer for Embodied Agents

claims.claim: A multi-view video-to-video translation framework, grounding all camera views in a shared 4D latent space from a spatial foundation model, allows pretrained robot policy demonstrations to be resimulated into new environments/appearances without additional data collection, achieving physically and stylistically consistent multi-view translations even under wide baselines and dynamic camera motion
claims.direction: favors multi-view-consistent generative video re-rendering as a way to transfer/augment existing demonstrations to new visual conditions rather than collecting new demonstrations in each new environment
claims.conditions: embodied AI multi-camera setups including egocentric and heterogeneous-camera setups, comparison to single-view V2V baselines, qualitative claim of 'superior or similar' benchmark performance

claims.claim: Naively applying single-view video-translation models independently to each of several synchronized cameras produces inconsistent appearance across views; a multi-view-consistent approach is needed to preserve cross-camera coherence for multi-camera policy learning
claims.direction: identifies cross-view consistency as a specific requirement/failure mode for multi-camera (e.g., scene + wrist camera) setups when applying visual augmentation/domain randomization
claims.conditions: multi-camera embodied AI setups

title: WorldContact: A Contact-Centric World Model for Scalable Robot Learning

claims.claim: A contact-centric world model built from a limited set of high-quality trajectories can generate additional training data efficiently (10x speedup over the source numerical simulator on a single H100 GPU); fine-tuning a VLA policy on source-simulation data alone gives 65% single-attempt real-robot success in a bag-lifting task, versus 95% when fine-tuned on the dataset expanded with WorldContact-generated data
claims.direction: strongly favors expanding a small set of real/simulated trajectories with a learned world model's generated data over training on the limited source data alone, for real-robot policy fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real robot deployment, deformable-object (shopping-bag) manipulation, VLA policy fine-tuning, 16 tasks

claims.claim: A world model that predicts object dynamics with larger time steps than the source simulator can efficiently generate large amounts of additional, useful training data from a limited set of high-quality demonstrations
claims.direction: favors learned-world-model-based data generation/augmentation over relying on the (slow) source simulator or collecting more real demonstrations directly
claims.conditions: deformable-object manipulation, real robot deployment

title: REPO: Reactive Policies with Observation Augmentation

claims.claim: In dynamic environments where object positions or external forces change unpredictably, multi-step open-loop action-chunk execution (used by current SOTA IL methods for temporal consistency) hinders reactivity and adaptation; predicting single-step actions instead, conditioned on a sequence of past image observations, consistently improves performance on a diverse set of real and simulated robotic tasks with unpredictable perturbations
claims.direction: contradicts the common practice of long open-loop action chunking for temporal consistency; favors single-step, closed-loop reactive prediction (with observation history) for dynamic/perturbed environments
claims.conditions: real + simulated robotic tasks with unpredictable perturbations, transformer-based action policy (variants RePO-BCT and RePO-DP)

claims.claim: Using a sequence of past image observations (rather than a single current frame or long open-loop chunks) provides temporal consistency for single-step reactive action prediction
claims.direction: favors moderate observation history for single-step reactive control, as an alternative to relying on action chunking for temporal consistency
claims.conditions: real + sim, transformer-based policies

claims.claim: Injecting adversarial noise into low-dimensional spatial image embeddings during training mitigates covariate shift from longer observation horizons, improving robustness to out-of-distribution states while preserving semantic content
claims.direction: favors adversarial-noise regularization of visual embeddings as a robustness technique for policies using observation history
claims.conditions: real + simulated robotic tasks, qualitative 'consistently improves' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Mitigating Covariate Shift in Offline Imitation Learning via Trajectory Synthesis

claims.claim: Synthetic Imitation Learning (SynIL) augments a small set of demonstrations with synthetic recovery trajectories (generated via generative dynamics models, or for high-dimensional visual manipulation, a training-free pipeline combining pretrained video generation, segmentation, point tracking, and monocular depth estimation) rather than only filtering/reweighting existing logged data, treating imperfect/failed trials as useful signal for off-manifold recovery states
claims.direction: favors synthesizing recovery trajectories from imperfect/failed data (or purely generatively) over collecting more successful demonstrations, to supply recovery supervision that plain behavior cloning lacks
claims.conditions: 15 D4RL low-dimensional benchmark tasks (first/second place on 8 of 15) plus real-world UR5 high-dimensional manipulation experiments

claims.claim: Real-world UR5 experiments show SynIL improves average success rate by 17.5% over behavior cloning, indicating synthetic recovery data can improve closed-loop robustness without any online environment interaction
claims.direction: supports synthetic recovery-trajectory augmentation as a practical, interaction-free way to close the covariate-shift gap that plain BC suffers from
claims.conditions: real-world UR5 robot, comparison directly against a behavior-cloning baseline

title: MirrorDuo: Reflection-Consistent Visuomotor Learning from Mirrored Demonstration Pairs

claims.claim: Generating a mirrored counterpart (image, proprioception, and 6-DoF end-effector action all reflected) for each original demonstration effectively doubles the training data for free ('collect one, get one for free'), applicable as an augmentation on top of standard behavior cloning or diffusion policy, or as a structural prior for reflection-equivariant policy networks
claims.direction: favors reflection-based mirroring as a near-zero-cost data augmentation/structural prior for single-camera visuomotor behavior cloning
claims.conditions: image-based BC/diffusion policy, 6-DoF end-effector action space, workspace with left-right symmetry

claims.claim: When demonstrations are confined to one side of the workspace, MirrorDuo enables efficient skill transfer to the mirrored (untrained) side with as few as zero or five demonstrations in the target arrangement
claims.direction: favors exploiting reflection symmetry to extend a small demo set's spatial coverage rather than collecting new demonstrations across the whole workspace
claims.conditions: workspace with left-right symmetry, same data budget comparison against non-mirrored training

title: LeapBot-WA: World-Anchor Action Models via Predictive Latent Alignments

claims.claim: Forcing world-action models to reconstruct pixel-level video details dissipates representational capacity and makes policies vulnerable to visual distractors; instead extracting abstract physical dynamics directly in a latent (JEPA-style) foundation space via 'Predictive Semantic Alignment' avoids this, achieving state-of-the-art performance among predictive models on LIBERO and matching top-tier generative WAMs on RoboTwin 2.0 without large-scale trajectory pre-training
claims.direction: favors latent/semantic future-prediction (JEPA-style) auxiliary objectives over pixel-level video-generation-based world models for both efficiency and distractor robustness
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0) + real-world transfer, no large-scale trajectory pretraining required

claims.claim: An asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers design uses a heavy 'Anchor Diffusion Transformer' only during training to guide the action-generation transformer, and prunes this heavy dynamics branch at inference, enabling zero-overhead execution
claims.direction: favors training-time-only auxiliary world-model branches that are discarded at inference, to get world-model benefits without added inference latency
claims.conditions: sim + real-world deployment

claims.claim: LeapBot-WA demonstrates superior zero-shot robustness to unseen environments and successful real-world transfer
claims.direction: supports latent-space (non-pixel) world modeling as a route to better generalization to unseen environments
claims.conditions: real-world transfer, qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Changes in End Effector Trajectory Jitter Amplitude under the Interaction of Lerobot Diffusion Policy Denoising Steps and SLAM Loopback Frequency

claims.claim: In a controlled experiment with a LeRobot Diffusion Policy, increasing the number of denoising steps reduced normalized end-effector trajectory jitter to about 47% of baseline under low-frequency disturbance conditions, but only to about 83% of baseline under high-frequency disturbance conditions -- a statistically significant interaction effect (two-way ANOVA) showing that denoising-step benefits for smoothness depend strongly on the disturbance/correction frequency the system experiences
claims.direction: shows that adding more diffusion denoising steps to reduce jitter has diminishing (and much weaker) returns when the system is subject to higher-frequency perturbations/corrections, i.e., smoothing strength must be co-tuned with disturbance frequency rather than maximized in isolation
claims.conditions: LeRobot Diffusion Policy, mobile manipulation system with SLAM loop-closure corrections as the disturbance source, controlled 2-way ANOVA design

claims.claim: Frequency-domain analysis shows that dense (high-frequency) loop-closure-like disturbances can induce delayed compensation and low-frequency energy accumulation when excessive denoising/smoothing is applied to an action-chunk-based policy, limiting the benefit of additional denoising steps
claims.direction: cautions against simply maximizing denoising steps/smoothing for chunk-based action generation when the system also experiences frequent external corrections, since this can itself introduce lag/energy accumulation
claims.conditions: LeRobot Diffusion Policy, mobile manipulation, controlled experimental framework

title: GeomVLA: Unifying Scene, Motion, and Action in 3D

claims.claim: Lifting pretrained VLM features into spatially grounded 3D scene tokens (using depth and camera calibration), while retaining VLM-pretrained semantic representations, and unifying perception, latent scene-motion prediction, and action generation in a shared robot-centric 3D coordinate frame achieves state-of-the-art performance on CALVIN, competitive performance on LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0, and outperforms strong baselines in real-world manipulation without robot-action pretraining
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D-grounded scene tokens (depth+calibration lifted into 3D) fused with 2D VLM semantics, over purely 2D image-token VLA representations
claims.conditions: sim (CALVIN, LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0) + real-world manipulation, no robot-action pretraining needed

claims.claim: Rather than executing a predicted future-scene trajectory as an open-loop plan, extracting intermediate motion tokens from a 3D Scene Trajectory Denoiser and using them to condition a 3D flow-based action denoiser (via geometry-aware attention) improves action generation
claims.direction: favors conditioning a flow-matching action head on intermediate learned motion tokens rather than directly executing predicted trajectories open-loop
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation

claims.claim: Ablations show that future-motion reasoning alone is insufficient for the observed gains; the primary benefit comes from maintaining geometric consistency among scene representation, motion prediction, and robot actions throughout the pipeline
claims.direction: identifies geometric consistency (not just adding a future-prediction auxiliary task) as the key ingredient for auxiliary world-modeling objectives to help action generation
claims.conditions: ablation study across sim benchmarks

title: PolyTask: Learning Unified Policies through Behavior Distillation

claims.claim: A 'learn then distill' approach -- training task-specific policies from a few demonstrations per task, then distilling them into a single unified policy via Behavior Distillation -- outperforms prior state-of-the-art approaches in multi-task and lifelong learning settings by significant margins
claims.direction: favors training many small task-specific policies from few demos each, then distilling into one unified model, over directly training one large multi-task policy on all data jointly
claims.conditions: 3 simulated environment suites + 1 real-robot suite, multi-task and lifelong learning settings, qualitative 'significant margins' claim

claims.claim: A single distilled policy can consolidate behaviors learned by many task-specific policies while conditioning on task variables, without needing interactive access to all tasks simultaneously
claims.direction: supports policy distillation as a route to a single compact deployable model rather than maintaining many separate task-specific models or one very large multi-task model
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot, lifelong learning setting

title: Dexterous Functional Grasping

claims.claim: Using eigengrasps (a small number of human-data-derived basis directions) to reduce the search space of an RL action policy leads to more stable and physically realistic motion than a full-dimensional action space, beating baselines in simulation, outperforming hardcoded grasping in the real world, and matching or outperforming a trained human teleoperator
claims.direction: favors a reduced-dimensionality, human-data-informed action space (eigengrasps) over a full-DoF raw action space for dexterous grasping
claims.conditions: multi-fingered dexterous hand, sim-trained low-level policy + affordance matching, real-world evaluation; not a parallel-jaw gripper setup

title: GRAPE: Generalizing Robot Policy via Preference Alignment

claims.claim: Aligning a VLA on trajectory-level preferences, implicitly modeling reward from both successful AND failure trials (rather than behavior cloning exclusively from successful rollouts), with preference modeling automatically guided by spatiotemporal keypoint constraints from a large VLM, increases success rates on in-domain and unseen manipulation tasks by 51.79% and 58.20% respectively over the base VLA
claims.direction: strongly favors adding a preference-alignment training objective that uses failure trials as negative signal, over behavior cloning exclusively on successful demonstrations
claims.conditions: state-of-the-art VLA models, real-world + simulated environments, diverse task set

claims.claim: GRAPE can be aligned with different auxiliary objectives (safety, efficiency) at test/training time, reducing collision rates by 37.44% and rollout step-length by 11.15% respectively, without retraining the base task-completion capability
claims.direction: supports flexible post-hoc preference alignment for shaping specific robustness/efficiency properties beyond raw task success
claims.conditions: same VLA models, real + sim

title: UniVLA: Learning to Act Anywhere with Task-centric Latent Actions

claims.claim: Deriving task-centric latent action representations from videos (rather than direct low-level action regression), with a latent action model built within a pretrained DINO feature space and incorporating language instructions to filter out task-irrelevant dynamics, enables learning from internet-scale video across many embodiments and viewpoints, and decoding efficiently to any specific robot at deployment
claims.direction: favors video-derived latent action representations (decoded per-embodiment at deployment) over embodiment-specific direct action regression, to exploit heterogeneous video data
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment, sim + real-robot deployments, multiple manipulation and navigation benchmarks

claims.claim: UniVLA achieves state-of-the-art results while using less than 1/20 of the pretraining compute and 1/10 of the downstream (task-specific) data compared to OpenVLA, with continuous performance improvements as heterogeneous data (including human videos) is added to training
claims.direction: strongly favors this latent-action pretraining approach for compute- and data-efficiency, directly relevant to low-compute, low-data deployments
claims.conditions: comparison against OpenVLA, cross-embodiment benchmarks + real-robot

claims.claim: Grounding the latent action model in a pretrained DINO (self-supervised ViT) feature space, rather than training vision representations from scratch or using other pretraining schemes, is central to filtering task-irrelevant dynamics and enabling transfer
claims.direction: supports DINO-pretrained features as the vision-representation substrate for latent action learning
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment latent action model

why_deep_read: A highly-cited (442) result directly hitting our two biggest constraints simultaneously -- less than 1/20th the pretraining compute and 1/10th the downstream data of OpenVLA while achieving SOTA -- using a DINO-feature latent-action approach; the full paper's latent-action decoding recipe is worth extracting to see if it can be adapted to our 8GB-GPU, ~50-100 demo, dual-camera SO-101 setup.

title: Chain-of-Modality: Learning Manipulation Programs from Multimodal Human Videos with Vision-Language-Models

claims.claim: A prompting strategy (Chain-of-Modality) that progressively integrates information from video, muscle-activity (armband), and audio signals lets a VLM refine a task plan and generate detailed control parameters (e.g., force) from a single multimodal human demonstration, delivering a threefold improvement in accuracy for extracting task plans/control parameters versus baselines, with strong generalization to new task setups and objects
claims.direction: favors conditioning on richer multimodal (not just visual+language) demonstration signals when force/control parameters must be inferred, over vision-language-only conditioning
claims.conditions: human video demonstrations plus wearable sensors (armband EMG, microphone), real-world robot experiments

claims.claim: Learning from a single multimodal human video prompt (rather than multiple robot teleop demonstrations) can extract a task plan and control parameters sufficient for real-world execution
claims.direction: supports single-demonstration, multimodal human-video-based task specification as a data-efficient alternative to collecting many robot teleop demos, when a force/control parameter must be inferred
claims.conditions: single multimodal human video prompt, real-world robot experiments, requires extra sensors (armband, microphone) not available in a plain vision-only setup

title: CCDP: Composition of Conditional Diffusion Policies with Guided Sampling

claims.claim: An enhanced diffusion-policy sampling strategy that refines the sampling distribution to avoid previously-unsuccessful actions (rather than naively re-sampling until success) can infer recovery actions using ONLY data from successful demonstrations -- no additional exploratory/failure data or high-level controller needed -- by decomposing the diffusion model into smaller sub-problems that adapt to variable failure counts
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that explicit failure/recovery demonstrations are required to learn recovery behavior; favors smarter sampling-time composition of a diffusion policy trained only on successes
claims.conditions: door opening (unknown direction), object manipulation, and button-searching tasks; comparison against traditional (re-sampling) diffusion-policy baselines

claims.claim: Recovery behavior can be obtained without collecting additional exploratory or failure-recovery demonstrations, by exploiting only the successful-demonstration data already collected
claims.direction: suggests that better inference-time composition/sampling of an existing demo set can substitute for collecting explicit recovery demonstrations
claims.conditions: same task set as above, qualitative 'outperforms traditional baselines' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Towards a Generalizable Bimanual Foundation Policy via Flow-based Video Prediction

claims.claim: Using optical flow as an intermediate representation (a two-stage text-to-flow then flow-to-video pipeline built on a pretrained text-to-video model, followed by a lightweight diffusion policy for action generation) mitigates the ambiguity of directly predicting video from language in a single stage
claims.direction: favors optical-flow-mediated action/video generation over single-stage text-to-video-to-action pipelines
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, real dual-arm robot + simulation

claims.claim: This approach significantly reduces the robot-data requirement by avoiding direct use of low-level action data when fine-tuning large pretrained text-to-video models
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained video models via an intermediate flow representation to cut down on needed labeled action data
claims.conditions: bimanual real robot + sim, qualitative claim of 'significantly reduces' requirement, no exact numbers given

title: GigaWorld-Policy: An Efficient Action-Centered World-Action Model

claims.claim: An action-centered world-action model that predicts future action sequences conditioned on the current observation and only optionally generates future video (a causal design prevents future-video tokens from influencing action tokens, so video generation can be skipped at inference) runs 9x faster than the leading world-action-model baseline (Motus)
claims.direction: strongly favors decoupling action prediction from (optional) video generation at inference, so heavy video-generation compute is not required for action decoding, to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world robotic platforms, comparison against Motus (leading WAM baseline)

claims.claim: Supervising the policy by BOTH action prediction and video generation during training (jointly, but with the causal separation described above) improves task success rate by 7% over the baseline WAM and improves performance by 95% over pi-0.5 on RoboTwin 2.0
claims.direction: favors joint action+video training supervision (even if video generation is skipped at inference) over training the action head alone, and over a standard VLA (pi-0.5) baseline
claims.conditions: real-world robotic platforms + RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmark

claims.claim: Using video generation as an auxiliary training signal (physically-plausible visual-dynamics constraints) while keeping it optional at inference decouples the auxiliary-objective benefit from its inference-time cost
claims.direction: supports auxiliary future-video-prediction objectives that are pruned/skipped at deployment, to gain training-time benefit without inference-time cost
claims.conditions: real-world deployment + RoboTwin2.0

title: Direct Action-Head Injection of A Grounded 3D Point Unlocks Spatial and Task Generalization

claims.claim: Representing a grounding signal (target location) in 3D, computing its relative displacement to the gripper, and injecting the resulting spatial embedding directly into the action head via adaptive layer normalization (a lightweight, backbone-agnostic 2-layer MLP module requiring no changes to the VLA backbone or pretraining) is far more effective than representing the same grounding signal via language or 2D visual prompting
claims.direction: strongly favors direct 3D-point injection into the action head over language-based or 2D-pixel-based spatial grounding for improving spatial/task generalization
claims.conditions: LIBERO-PRO sim benchmark, tested on GR00T-N1.6 and pi_0.5 backbones (backbone-agnostic)

claims.claim: On LIBERO-PRO, this module improves GR00T-N1.6's average success rate from 31.2 to 77.5 (+46.3 points) under task (language instruction) perturbation, and from 28.1 to 60.2 (+32.1 points) under position (object location) perturbation; comparable gains are seen for pi_0.5
claims.direction: provides a large, controlled, quantified fix for both task-generalization and spatial/position-generalization brittleness in VLAs, via a minimal architectural addition
claims.conditions: LIBERO-PRO benchmark, two different VLA backbones, controlled perturbation evaluation

why_deep_read: A lightweight (2-layer MLP, no backbone changes), backbone-agnostic module giving huge, controlled quantified gains (+46pp task generalization, +32pp position generalization) is exactly the kind of low-compute-cost fix that fits our resource constraints and directly addresses our 'camera slightly moved' / novel-object-position robustness failure mode; worth extracting the exact 3D-point construction and adaptive-layer-norm injection recipe.

title: GenVid2Robot: From Video Generation to Robot Manipulation via Rigid-Geometric Consistency

claims.claim: Generated videos provide useful visual motion priors but are not directly physically executable; verifying generated video motion against real first-frame RGB-D anchors under a sparse relative SE(3) model (rather than direct trajectory replay) and applying a bounded depth-compensation module improves the reliability of generated-video-guided real-robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors geometrically-verified/grounded generated-video motion (checked against real depth/grasp constraints) over direct replay of generated video trajectories, when using video generation as a source of training or execution guidance
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments, qualitative 'improves reliability' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Beyond Dense Futures: World Models as Structured Planners for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Dense future-frame prediction introduces visual redundancy and accumulates errors causing long-horizon plan drift, while purely semantic/latent sparse representations lack explicit kinematic grounding; predicting sparse, physically-meaningful 'structured frames' (derived from intrinsic kinematic cues like gripper transitions and kinematic turning points) as the auxiliary world-model target, then mapping this structured foresight to low-level actions, achieves 75.0% success on SimplerEnv-WidowX and 94.8% on LIBERO with robust real-world generalization
claims.direction: favors sparse, kinematically-grounded structured-frame prediction as the auxiliary future-prediction target over both dense pixel-level video prediction and purely semantic/latent sparse goals
claims.conditions: sim (SimplerEnv-WidowX, LIBERO) + real-world deployment, basic pick-and-place and complex long-horizon tasks

title: JEPA Policy: Diffusion-Free Imitation Learning via Paired Action and Future Representation Prediction

claims.claim: A diffusion-free framework that uses the action chunk and its observed future representation as paired training targets, with action and future-representation tokens interacting in a shared Transformer refined through two forward passes, improves mean success over an action-only (MIP) baseline and outperforms Diffusion Policy under the evaluated configurations
claims.direction: favors a diffusion-free, JEPA-style paired action/future-representation prediction objective over both plain action-only regression and diffusion-based action generation
claims.conditions: 9 simulated tasks + a 5-task, 630-episode real-robot study, same pooled ranking across sim and real

claims.claim: The shared-topology future-prediction mechanism adds only 0.29 ms to the base (MIP) model's latency, avoiding the iterative generative sampling cost of diffusion policies while still improving success
claims.direction: strongly favors this low-overhead paired-prediction approach over diffusion policies specifically for low-latency visuomotor imitation
claims.conditions: real-robot + sim, direct latency comparison to the MIP baseline

claims.claim: Dual-branch and gradient-routing control experiments attribute the performance gain to the shared action/future-representation Transformer topology itself (not merely to having an auxiliary prediction head), and audits find no complete representation collapse under action supervision, with future-prediction error serving as a task-conditioned failure-ranking signal
claims.direction: supports tightly coupling (shared-topology, two-pass) future-representation prediction with action generation, rather than treating future prediction as a separate auxiliary head bolted onto the action policy
claims.conditions: ablation/audit experiments across 9 sim tasks

why_deep_read: Directly targets our stated ~2s inference latency problem with a diffusion-free alternative that adds only 0.29ms overhead while beating Diffusion Policy in evaluated settings, validated on a real robot across 630 episodes; the paired action/future-representation training recipe could plausibly replace a diffusion action head in our SmolVLA fine-tune to cut latency drastically while keeping or improving success rate.

title: KITE: Keypoint-Conditioned Policies for Semantic Manipulation

claims.claim: Grounding a language instruction in a visual scene via 2D image keypoints (rather than pre-trained VLM features or end-to-end visuomotor control) provides a highly accurate object-centric bias for downstream skill execution, achieving 75%, 70%, and 71% overall success rates on three real-world instruction-following tasks (long-horizon 6-DoF tabletop manipulation, semantic grasping, high-precision coffee-making)
claims.direction: favors keypoint-based grounding as an intermediate action representation over both VLM-feature-conditioned policies and end-to-end visuomotor control
claims.conditions: real-world robot, RGB-D observation, 3 distinct real environments

claims.claim: KITE outperforms frameworks using pre-trained VLMs for grounding or end-to-end visuomotor control while being trained from fewer or comparable amounts of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors keypoint-conditioned skills for better performance at equal or lower data budgets than end-to-end or VLM-based alternatives
claims.conditions: real-world, 3 environments, comparison against VLM-based and end-to-end baselines

title: Vid2Robot: End-to-end Video-conditioned Policy Learning with Cross-Attention Transformers

claims.claim: An end-to-end video-conditioned policy (using cross-attention transformer layers between human-demonstration-video features and current robot state, with auxiliary contrastive losses aligning prompt-video and robot-video representations) enables a robot to infer and perform a task from a human video, achieving over 20% improvement over BC-Z on real-world robots when using human prompt videos
claims.direction: favors conditioning policies on video demonstrations (via cross-attention + contrastive alignment) as an alternative/complement to language conditioning, when instructions are more naturally given by demonstration
claims.conditions: real-world robots, large dataset of prompt-video/robot-trajectory pairs, comparison against BC-Z

claims.claim: Video-conditioned policies trained this way exhibit cross-object motion transfer: a motion observed on one object in the prompt video can be transferred to a different object in the robot's own environment
claims.direction: supports video-conditioning as a way to generalize demonstrated motions to new objects without new demonstrations for each object
claims.conditions: real-world robots, cross-object transfer evaluation

title: Evaluating the Effect of State and Action Selection on In-Hand Manipulation Performance for Transferability

claims.claim: State and action space selection significantly affects overall policy performance and its robustness to both sim-to-real transfer and transfer across different hand/embodiment geometries; domain randomization/adaptation alone only partially bridge these gaps
claims.direction: identifies state/action-space choice (not just domain randomization) as a first-order lever for cross-embodiment and sim-to-real transferability
claims.conditions: two exemplar in-hand manipulation tasks, RL-trained policies, sim-to-real and cross-hand-geometry transfer evaluation

claims.claim: A reduced state space that avoids hand/embodiment-specific information is preferable for both sim-to-real and cross-embodiment transfer, even though it provides strictly less information than a full state space
claims.direction: counterintuitively favors a smaller, embodiment-agnostic observation/state space over a richer, embodiment-specific one, when transferability is the goal
claims.conditions: same two manipulation tasks, RL-trained, transfer evaluation across hand geometries and sim-to-real

title: PRISM: Pointcloud Reintegrated Inference via Segmentation and Cross-Attention for Manipulation

claims.claim: An end-to-end framework that directly learns from raw point cloud observations (segmenting the point cloud into object clusters and encoding local geometric detail, then cross-attending with robot joint states) surpasses both 2D (fixed camera view) and 3D (keyframe-based point cloud) baseline policies in accuracy and efficiency in cluttered, object-dense, contact-intensive scenarios
claims.direction: favors raw point-cloud-based perception with object segmentation over fixed-camera 2D views or keyframe-limited 3D methods, for cluttered/contact-intensive tasks
claims.conditions: simulated environments, no pre-trained models or external datasets used

claims.claim: PRISM was trained with 100 demonstrations per task and outperformed baseline policies under this data budget
claims.direction: provides a direct data point on point-cloud-based policy performance in a demo-count range (100 demos/task) close to our target 50-100 demo budget
claims.conditions: simulated environments, 100 demos/task

claims.claim: A diffusion module translates the fused (point-cloud + robot-state) representation into smooth robot actions
claims.direction: supports using a diffusion action head on top of point-cloud+state fused features for smooth action generation
claims.conditions: simulated environments

title: Dita: Scaling Diffusion Transformer for Generalist Vision-Language-Action Policy

claims.claim: Using in-context conditioning -- enabling fine-grained alignment between denoised actions and raw visual tokens from historical observations, within a unified multimodal diffusion Transformer -- rather than conditioning denoising on fused embeddings via shallow networks, explicitly models action deltas and environmental nuances and achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance across extensive benchmarks
claims.direction: favors deep in-context conditioning of a diffusion action Transformer on raw visual tokens over shallow-network fusion of pooled embeddings
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment datasets, diverse camera perspectives, sim benchmarks

claims.claim: Dita achieves robust real-world adaptation to environmental variances and complex long-horizon tasks through only 10-shot finetuning
claims.direction: supports that a well-designed diffusion-transformer VLA architecture can adapt to a new real-world setting with as few as 10 demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world robot, third-person camera only, 10-shot fine-tuning

claims.claim: Robust real-world adaptation and long-horizon task execution is demonstrated using only third-person (scene) camera inputs, without a wrist camera
claims.direction: suggests a well-designed diffusion-transformer VLA can achieve robust performance from a scene camera alone, though this does not establish that adding a wrist camera would not help further
claims.conditions: real-world robot, 10-shot finetuning, third-person camera only

claims.claim: The architecture explicitly models action deltas (rather than absolute actions) as part of its in-context diffusion conditioning design
claims.direction: favors delta/relative action representations within the diffusion-transformer conditioning scheme
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment, diverse action spaces

title: VLA-Precision: Asymmetric Co-Bootstrapping for Efficient Real-World Online RL of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: An asymmetric co-bootstrapping RL post-training scheme with invariant-state decoupling and on-demand streaming (ACoB-Stream) delivers up to 10.9x improvements in throughput and computational efficiency for online RL fine-tuning of large VLAs, achieving 98.3% mean success rate at 1.2x-1.8x the speed of VLA/RL baselines on high-precision tasks
claims.direction: favors architectural decoupling of state/experience streaming from policy computation to reduce large-VLA overhead during online RL post-training, for both higher throughput and higher final success
claims.conditions: real-world, 9 high-precision chemistry tasks, 4 robot embodiments, online RL post-training of pretrained VLAs (not pure imitation learning)

title: TAMEn: Tactile-Aware Manipulation Engine for Closed-Loop Data Collection in Contact-Rich Tasks

claims.claim: Unifying large-scale tactile pretraining, task-specific bimanual demonstrations, and human-in-the-loop recovery data (collected via a cross-morphology handheld interface with online feasibility checking) into a pyramid-structured data regime increases task success rates from 34% to 75% across diverse bimanual manipulation tasks
claims.direction: strongly favors deliberately collecting human-in-the-loop recovery/correction data (in addition to standard demonstrations) as part of the data collection pipeline, over demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich bimanual manipulation, cross-morphology handheld data-collection hardware (precision motion-capture mode + portable VR mode)

claims.claim: Incorporating large-scale tactile pretraining alongside task-specific visual demonstrations, within a visuo-tactile learning framework, contributes to the large success-rate improvement (34% to 75%)
claims.direction: supports tactile pretraining as a valuable auxiliary/pretraining signal even when the deployed policy is primarily visual
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual tasks, requires a tactile-sensorized handheld data-collection tool

title: Muninn: Your Trajectory Diffusion Model But Faster

claims.claim: A training-free caching wrapper (Muninn) tracks a calibrated per-step 'uncertainty budget' during diffusion sampling and, at each denoising step, chooses between reusing a cached denoiser output (when predicted deviation is small) or recomputing it (when it is not), delivering up to 4.6x wall-clock speedups across several trajectory-diffusion planners and diffusion policies, without retraining the model or sacrificing task performance/safety metrics
claims.direction: strongly favors training-free, uncertainty-aware caching of diffusion denoiser evaluations over either full recomputation every step or sampler/network modifications that require retraining, as a way to make diffusion-based action/trajectory generation fast enough for real-time control
claims.conditions: D4RL offline RL planning, configuration-space motion planning, and visuomotor diffusion policies; validated in real-time closed-loop navigation and manipulation hardware deployments

claims.claim: Muninn certifies, at a user-chosen deviation tolerance and risk level, that cached (accelerated) rollouts remain within a specified distance of their full-compute counterparts, providing a principled way to trade off action-chunk/trajectory quality against inference speed
claims.direction: supports explicit, certifiable speed/quality trade-off control for diffusion-based action-chunk generation, rather than an uncontrolled quality loss from naive acceleration
claims.conditions: same benchmarks and hardware deployments as above

why_deep_read: Directly and practically addresses our ~2s inference-latency problem: a training-free wrapper (no retraining our SmolVLA/diffusion policy needed) that gives up to 4.6x speedup on diffusion-based policies while preserving task performance, validated on real hardware; worth extracting exact implementation details since it could be a drop-in fix rather than requiring a new architecture.

title: Feeling the Unexpected: ResTacVLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation via Residual Tactile Representation

claims.claim: Reformulating tactile input as a 'Residual Tactile Representation' (the discrepancy between visual priors and actual physical sensation, discretized via a VQ bottleneck into Latent Contact Primitives), rather than treating raw tactile data as a direct input, resolves the bandwidth mismatch/modality collapse where high-bandwidth vision overshadows sparse tactile cues in VLA models, consistently outperforming baselines on contact-rich tasks and remaining robust to unexpected disturbances
claims.direction: favors residual (surprise-gated) tactile representations over raw tactile fusion for combining vision and touch in a VLA, to avoid visual modality dominance
claims.conditions: diverse contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensors, qualitative 'consistently outperforms' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Potential-Field Action Representation for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: In a controlled comparison using the same RL algorithm, an action representation based on artificial-potential-field parameters (PA-RL, generating a state-dependent guidance direction executed via Cartesian impedance control) reaches 100% success on peg-in-hole insertion within the allotted training time, versus 92.6% for the best of three alternative action spaces tested (Cartesian velocity, Cartesian pose, variable impedance)
claims.direction: favors a potential-field-parameterized action space over direct Cartesian velocity/pose or variable-impedance commands for contact-rich tasks, in a controlled same-algorithm comparison
claims.conditions: simulation, peg-in-hole insertion task, same RL algorithm across all compared action spaces

claims.claim: The potential-field action representation reduces joint-torque variation by 55.4% and Cartesian acceleration variation by 70.8% relative to the best baseline action space, without any explicit motion-quality penalty in the reward, and the simulation-trained policy completes 9/9 real-robot insertions zero-shot without fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors this action representation specifically for producing smoother (lower-jerk) motion as an emergent property, and shows it transfers zero-shot from sim to a real robot
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, peg-in-hole, zero-shot deployment (no real-world fine-tuning)

why_deep_read: A rare controlled, same-algorithm ablation across multiple action-space choices (Q02) with a clean real-robot zero-shot transfer result, and it directly quantifies smoothness gains (55-71% reduction in torque/acceleration variation) relevant to our jerky-motion problem; worth extracting the potential-field parameterization to see if an analogous representation could reduce action-chunk-boundary jerk in our position-controlled SO-101 setup.

title: MURM: Utilization of Multi-Views for Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A single-view baseline fails to solve complex manipulation tasks (placing objects at goal positions, picking up randomly positioned objects), whereas a framework using multiple camera views (each encoded via a per-view VQVAE) succeeds
claims.direction: favors multi-camera-view observations over a single camera view for goal-conditioned manipulation policies
claims.conditions: simulation (PyBullet), offline RL (IQL) with goal images, scripted-expert-collected demos with added noise

claims.claim: Learning a structured latent representation per camera view via a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQVAE), rather than using high-dimensional raw images directly, makes offline RL training more feasible
claims.direction: supports VQVAE-based discrete latent visual representations as a practical intermediate encoding for RL from images
claims.conditions: simulation, offline RL, multi-view

title: Open-World Object Manipulation using Pre-trained Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Conditioning a robot policy on object-identifying information extracted from a pre-trained vision-language model (given the language command and current image), rather than relying only on first-hand robot interaction data, allows the policy (MOO) to generalize zero-shot to a wide range of novel object categories and environments on a real mobile manipulator
claims.direction: favors extracting object-identifying conditioning signals from pre-trained VLMs over training only on first-hand robot interaction data with seen objects
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator, zero-shot to novel object categories, also extends to non-language input modalities (e.g., finger pointing)

claims.claim: MOO generalizes zero-shot to object categories the robot has never interacted with before, directly addressing novel-object generalization
claims.direction: supports VLM-based object grounding as a mechanism for generalizing to novel objects not seen in the robot's own training data, similar to our 'different-looking pumpkin' failure mode
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator, qualitative 'wide range' claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: VITaL Pretraining: Visuo-Tactile Pretraining for Tactile and Non-Tactile Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Incorporating visuo-tactile pretraining improves imitation learning performance not only for policies that use tactile information at inference, but ALSO for non-tactile agents (policies that do NOT use tactile information at inference); for example, pretraining with tactile information improved a non-tactile agent's accuracy on USB plugging from 20% to 85%, reaching parity with (and in some cases surpassing) visuo-tactile agents
claims.direction: strongly favors adding a tactile-informed pretraining stage even when the deployed policy will be vision-only at inference, as an auxiliary-objective strategy
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks (e.g. USB plugging), requires paired visuo-tactile data during a pretraining phase (not needed at deployment)

title: Video-Language Critic: Transferable Reward Functions for Language-Conditioned Robotics

claims.claim: A reward model trained via contrastive learning and a temporal ranking objective on readily-available cross-embodiment data (Open X-Embodiment), separating 'what to accomplish' (language-grounded, transferable) from 'how to accomplish it' (embodiment-specific), enables 2x more sample-efficient policy training on Meta-World tasks than a sparse reward alone, despite a significant domain gap
claims.direction: favors cross-embodiment, video-language-grounded reward models (trained once, reused across embodiments) over embodiment-specific reward engineering or sparse rewards for language-conditioned policy training
claims.conditions: trained on Open X-Embodiment cross-embodiment data, evaluated on Meta-World tasks; this concerns RL reward shaping rather than direct imitation-learning conditioning

title: LAGEA: Language Guided Embodied Agents for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Converting episodic, schema-constrained VLM reflections in natural language into temporally-grounded, step-wise shaping rewards (with an adaptive failure-aware coefficient) improves average RL success over SOTA methods by 9.0% on random goals, 5.3% on fixed goals, and 17% on fetch tasks, while converging faster
claims.direction: favors using structured, temporally-grounded language feedback as a training signal (reward shaping) over standard sparse-reward RL or unstructured language feedback
claims.conditions: Meta-World MT10 and Robotic Fetch benchmarks, RL training (not pure imitation learning)

title: DexWild: Dexterous Human Interactions for In-the-Wild Robot Policies

claims.claim: Co-training on both a large volume of cheaply-collected human hand demonstrations (via a low-cost mobile hand-tracking device, DexWild-System) and a smaller set of robot demonstrations improves performance over training on either dataset alone
claims.direction: favors mixing cheap, large-scale human-hand data with a smaller robot-specific demo set over relying on robot demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, multiple environments/objects/embodiments

claims.claim: DexWild achieves a 68.5% success rate in unseen environments -- nearly four times higher than policies trained with robot data only -- and offers 5.8x better cross-embodiment generalization
claims.direction: strongly supports human-hand-data co-training as a route to substantially better generalization to unseen environments and embodiments than robot-only training
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation in unseen environments, cross-embodiment testing

title: BridgeVLA: Input-Output Alignment for Efficient 3D Manipulation Learning with Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Projecting 3D inputs to multiple 2D images (aligning input with the pretrained VLM backbone's native modality) and using 2D heatmaps for action prediction (unifying input and output spaces in a consistent 2D image space), with a scalable pre-training stage teaching the VLM backbone to predict 2D heatmaps before downstream policy learning, improves RLBench average success from 81.4% to 88.2% and COLOSSEUM (generalization benchmark) from 56.7% to 64.0% versus prior baselines, plus +32% average on real-robot experiments
claims.direction: favors projecting 3D signals into the VLM's native 2D image space (rather than adding separate 3D encoders/tokens) and matching input/output representations, for efficient and effective 3D-aware VLA learning
claims.conditions: 3 simulation benchmarks (RLBench, COLOSSEUM, GemBench) + real-robot experiments

claims.claim: BridgeVLA achieves a 96.8% success rate on 10+ tasks using only 3 demonstration trajectories per task, after the proposed heatmap pre-training stage
claims.direction: provides an extreme, precisely-quantified data-efficiency result: with the right pretraining, only 3 demos/task can suffice for high success
claims.conditions: comparison setting with 3 trajectories/task, specific benchmark tasks, requires the proposed pre-training stage (not from-scratch fine-tuning)

claims.claim: BridgeVLA generalizes robustly in multiple out-of-distribution settings, including visual disturbances and unseen instructions
claims.direction: supports the 2D-heatmap-unified 3D representation as contributing to robustness against visual disturbances, relevant to lighting/appearance shift concerns
claims.conditions: real-robot OOD evaluation, qualitative claim alongside the quantified benchmark numbers above

why_deep_read: The claim of 96.8% success from only 3 demonstrations per task, plus quantified generalization gains under visual disturbance (COLOSSEUM +7.3pp, real-robot +32%), is an extraordinary and precisely-quantified data-efficiency result directly relevant to our ~50-100 demo budget; worth extracting the exact heatmap-prediction pretraining recipe to see whether it is adoptable without a large 3D-capable VLM backbone on our 8GB GPU.

title: R2RGEN: Real-to-Real 3D Data Generation for Spatially Generalized Manipulation

claims.claim: A simulator- and rendering-free framework directly augments point-cloud observation-action pairs from a small set of source demonstrations (pre-processing under different camera setups into a shared 3D space, augmenting object/robot positions via group-wise backtracking, and aligning distribution with real-world 3D sensors via camera-aware post-processing) to generate additional real-world-like training data, substantially enhancing data efficiency for spatial generalization
claims.direction: favors direct point-cloud-space data augmentation (real-to-real, no simulator/rendering) over either collecting many real demonstrations across all spatial configurations or simulator-based augmentation with a sim-to-real gap
claims.conditions: point-cloud-based visuomotor policies, multiple camera setups, no fixed-base/predefined-viewpoint constraint

claims.claim: Spatial generalization (robustness to different spatial distributions of objects, environment, and agent) is identified as the most fundamental generalization capability, and this augmentation approach is shown to substantially improve it without the sim-to-real gap of simulator-based methods
claims.direction: supports point-cloud-space real-to-real augmentation specifically as a fix for spatial (object/camera/agent-position) generalization
claims.conditions: extensive experiments, qualitative 'substantially enhances' claim, no exact numbers given

title: YOTO++: Learning Long-Horizon Closed-Loop Bimanual Manipulation From One-Shot Human Video Demonstrations

claims.claim: A scalable demonstration-proliferation strategy synthetically augments a single one-shot human-video demonstration into diverse training samples, enabling a customized bimanual diffusion policy to generalize to novel skills and objects, and to transfer across an unseen dual-arm robot platform without additional retraining
claims.direction: favors synthetic proliferation of a single demonstration (rather than collecting many demonstrations) as a route to broad generalization and cross-embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon bimanual tasks, one-shot human video source, qualitative 'impressive performance' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Distilling extracted 3D hand motions into compact keyframe-based trajectories to train a diffusion policy, plus a visual alignment mechanism for closed-loop replanning at the initial manipulation stage, enables timely adaptation to perturbations during execution
claims.direction: supports keyframe/trajectory-distilled diffusion policies combined with closed-loop visual re-alignment over open-loop trajectory replay
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual tasks, qualitative claim

title: Lagrangian Perturbation Diffusion Steering: Latent Reinforcement Learning for Generative Policies

claims.claim: Rather than fine-tuning a large generative (diffusion/flow-matching) policy's action decoder with RL -- which is frequently unstable and sample-inefficient -- learning a compact noise-space perturbation in front of a FROZEN decoder, optimized with a Lagrangian trust-region objective, improves downstream value/success/return (up to 25% return improvement over prior baselines) while constraining deviation from the latent prior and maintaining higher action-space entropy than unconstrained noise-space steering
claims.direction: favors lightweight noise-space perturbation of a frozen large generative policy over directly fine-tuning/updating the large action decoder, for post-hoc RL improvement
claims.conditions: RoboMimic manipulation, OpenAI Gym locomotion, Adroit dexterous manipulation benchmarks, plus flow-matching backbones, a large VLA, and physical Franka deployment

claims.claim: This method is validated as not limited to compact diffusion policies or simulated benchmarks, extending to a large VLA and physical robot deployment, without needing to update the large decoder's weights
claims.direction: supports lightweight, decoder-frozen adaptation methods as a way to improve large generative policies without the compute cost of updating the full model, relevant to compute-constrained deployment
claims.conditions: physical Franka robot, large VLA backbone tested

title: PRISM: Polynomial Representations for Interaction-Structured Motor Control

claims.claim: Replacing linear proprioceptive conditioning in Diffusion Policy with a factorized polynomial layer (that makes higher-order interactions among physical observation variables, e.g. products encoding power/inertial effects/contact/slip/compliance, explicit and learnable) improves performance over standard MLP-based conditioning across humanoid locomotion and contact-rich manipulation
claims.direction: favors explicit polynomial (interaction-aware) proprioceptive conditioning over standard linear/MLP conditioning of proprioceptive state in a diffusion policy
claims.conditions: humanoid locomotion + contact-rich manipulation, RL and imitation learning settings

claims.claim: PRISM improves over both standard MLP policies and LARGER MLPs with matched parameter capacity, showing that interaction structure (not just added capacity) is what drives the improvement, and yields sensorless compliant behavior without force/tactile/contact sensors
claims.direction: supports that structured (interaction-aware) small architectures can outperform simply scaling up a generic MLP, relevant to small-model design under compute constraints
claims.conditions: comparison against larger matched-capacity MLPs, no tactile/force sensing used

title: Triplet2Track: A Hierarchical System with Object-Centric Representations for Reliable Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: A closed-loop long-horizon imitation learning system that represents high-level subgoals as instance-grounded triplets (extracted from human videos, reducing reliance on robot-collected data) and translates them into continuous track priors for execution, achieves a 74.8% average success rate on diverse real-world long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors deriving subgoal structure from human videos (rather than only robot-collected demonstrations) plus online monitoring/replanning, over open-loop hierarchical pipelines trained purely on robot data
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks, human-video-derived subgoal representations

claims.claim: The system supports object-level and compositional generalization by monitoring task progress from observations and replanning online, rather than executing a fixed open-loop plan
claims.direction: supports online replanning grounded in observations as a mechanism for compositional/object generalization in long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon tasks

title: Rethinking Visual Embodiment Dependence in Visuomotor Policies

claims.claim: Through cue-conflict interventions across representative policies, visible robot configuration (the robot's own appearance/pose in the visual observation) can become a shortcut to predicting task progress/actions, rather than the policy relying on genuinely task-relevant cues -- a previously under-recognized failure mode ('visual embodiment dependence', VED) distinct from background/lighting/object shortcut learning
claims.direction: identifies robot-self-appearance as an additional, specific shortcut-learning risk factor for visuomotor policies, beyond the commonly-discussed background/lighting/object shortcuts
claims.conditions: cue-conflict intervention experiments across multiple representative visuomotor policies

claims.claim: Rather than eliminating embodiment information from the visual input, replacing the original embodiment representation in 3D point clouds with a canonical end-effector representation (CER, preserving control-relevant geometry while abstracting away embodiment-specific morphology) substantially improves human-to-robot policy transfer without any robot demonstrations; simply removing embodiment information (without preserving control-relevant geometry) is insufficient, and CER itself can become a new configuration-based shortcut unless combined with configuration-decorrelation augmentation
claims.direction: favors structuring (canonicalizing) embodiment-relevant visual information rather than either including raw embodiment appearance or removing it entirely, and shows that any single fix (e.g. just removing embodiment cues) can itself introduce a new shortcut
claims.conditions: human-to-robot transfer without robot demonstrations, 3D point-cloud representation, additional configuration-decorrelation augmentation needed to fully mitigate shortcuts

why_deep_read: Identifies a subtle, specific shortcut-learning mechanism (policies keying off their own visible arm/gripper configuration) that is a plausible additional contributor to our camera-shift and appearance-shift failures beyond the usual background/lighting explanations, and proposes and validates a concrete fix (canonical end-effector representation in point clouds, plus decorrelation augmentation); worth reading in full to see if a lightweight version of this canonicalization could be applied to our RGB(+depth) setup without full 3D reconstruction.

title: Cherry-Picking with Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: By integrating an imprecise simulator, suboptimal demonstrations, and external state estimation, a real-world RL system (CherryBot) shows continual improvement through only 30 minutes of real-world interaction, achieving near-100% success on a demanding dynamic fine-manipulation task (chopstick grasping of swinging small objects) and robustness to external disturbances
claims.direction: favors combining imprecise simulation with suboptimal demonstrations and a short real-world interaction budget over relying on either large-scale precise demonstrations or simulation alone
claims.conditions: real-world robot, dynamic fine manipulation task, RL (not pure imitation learning), 30 minutes of real interaction

title: Learning Visuotactile Skills With Two Multifingered Hands

claims.claim: Using a low-cost hands-arms teleoperation system (HATO) for bimanual multifingered data collection, the authors empirically investigate the effects of dataset size, sensing modality, and visual input preprocessing on policy learning for long-horizon, high-precision tasks that are difficult without multifingered dexterity and touch feedback
claims.direction: provides a direct empirical study of how dataset size, sensing modality, and visual preprocessing choices each affect policy learning performance on a real low-cost teleoperated system
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual multifingered manipulation, low-cost teleoperation hardware, ablation across dataset size/modality/preprocessing

claims.claim: Incorporating visuotactile (touch) sensing alongside vision enables completing long-horizon, high-precision tasks that are difficult to achieve with vision alone
claims.direction: supports adding tactile sensing as a modality that materially expands the class of achievable tasks, complementing vision-only observation
claims.conditions: real-world, requires touch-sensorized (repurposed prosthetic) hands

title: Zero-Shot Transfer of a Tactile-based Continuous Force Control Policy from Simulation to Robot

claims.claim: A model-free RL force-control policy trained entirely in a simulation with realistic simulated normal forces transfers zero-shot to a real robot without fine-tuning, performing similarly to or better than a hand-crafted baseline; ablations show the proposed inductive bias and domain randomization are what enable this sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: supports domain randomization plus an appropriate inductive bias (not just realistic simulation alone) as necessary ingredients for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: simulation training, zero-shot real-robot deployment, tactile-based force control task, ablation study

title: UniTacHand: Unified Spatio-Tactile Representation for Human to Robotic Hand Skill Transfer

claims.claim: Aligning human (glove-collected) and robot tactile data into a unified latent space via contrastive learning, trained on only 10 minutes of paired data, enables zero-shot tactile-based policy transfer from humans to a real robot generalizing to unseen objects; co-training on mixed human+robot data (via this alignment) yields better performance and data efficiency than using robot data alone
claims.direction: favors cheap human (glove) data co-trained with a small amount of paired alignment data over collecting more robot-only tactile demonstrations
claims.conditions: real robot, requires tactile gloves and tactile-sensorized robotic hands, only 10 minutes of paired alignment data needed

title: Improving the performance of AI-powered Affordable Robotics for Assistive Tasks

claims.claim: A novel Phased Action Chunking Transformer (PACT) that captures temporal dependencies and segments motion dynamics, combined with a Temporal Ensemble (TE) method that refines trajectories, achieves over 90% task accuracy on a low-cost 6-servo assistive robot arm (up to 40% higher than baselines) across three real-world tasks (feeding, cleaning spills, fetching medicine), evaluated with ten hours of real-world testing
claims.direction: favors phase-aware action chunking combined with temporal ensembling over standard action chunking without phase segmentation or ensembling, for accuracy and smoothness on a low-cost servo-driven arm
claims.conditions: real-world low-cost robotic arm (six servo motors, dual cameras, 3D-printed grippers), leader-arm teleoperation data collection (50,000 video frames across 3 tasks), evaluated across 5 model sizes and 4 architectures

claims.claim: PACT enabled a 5x model size reduction while maintaining 75% accuracy, evaluated across five different model sizes and four architectures
claims.direction: provides a direct, quantified data point on the accuracy/model-size trade-off for action-chunking transformer policies on a low-cost servo-driven arm, closely matching our own hardware class
claims.conditions: same low-cost 6-servo arm setup, systematic comparison across 5 model sizes

claims.claim: Saliency analysis showed the policy relies on key visual cues and phase-token gradients peak at critical trajectory moments, indicating effective temporal reasoning underlying the smoothness/accuracy gains from the phase-aware chunking plus temporal ensembling design
claims.direction: supports phase-aware chunking + temporal ensembling as a mechanism for smoother, more reliable execution (relevant to jerkiness at chunk boundaries) validated with interpretability analysis
claims.conditions: real-world, same low-cost arm

why_deep_read: This paper's hardware (six-servo low-cost arm, dual cameras, 3D-printed grippers, leader-arm teleoperation) and problem framing (action chunking + temporal ensembling for smoothness, model-size vs. accuracy trade-off) are nearly identical to our own SO-101 setup and stated failure modes (jerky motion at chunk boundaries, need for a small model); this is one of the most directly transferable papers in the batch and merits full extraction of the PACT+TE architecture and the 5-model-size accuracy/size trade-off data.

title: TARS: Tactile Affordance in Robot Synesthesia for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Merging visual affordance (external cameras) with tactile feedback (local optical tactile sensors) via a unified point-cloud representation ('robotic synesthesia') handles both contact and non-contact manipulation phases better than visual-only affordance prediction
claims.direction: favors fusing tactile and visual affordance signals in a shared point-cloud representation over vision-only affordance prediction, particularly for contact-transition handling
claims.conditions: simulated tactile perception, 4 manipulation tasks, ablation of different modules; requires optical tactile sensors

title: Few-Shot Neural Differentiable Simulator: Real-to-Sim Rigid-Contact Modeling

claims.claim: Calibrating an analytical simulator with only a small amount of real-world data (few-shot), then using a mesh-based GNN with surrogate gradients for full differentiability, allows learning-based simulators to outperform differentiable baselines in replicating real-world trajectories and increases the efficiency of downstream policy learning
claims.direction: favors few-shot real-to-sim calibration (analytical + GNN hybrid) over either purely analytical simulators or large-data learned simulators, for generating training data with better contact fidelity
claims.conditions: multi-object interaction scenarios, simulation-based policy learning, qualitative 'improves' claims, no exact numbers given

title: Affordance Transfer Across Object Instances via Semantically Anchored Functional Map

claims.claim: Starting from a single visual demonstration, identifying semantically corresponding functional regions between objects (via semantic anchors and functional-map propagation over a coarse reconstructed mesh) enables demonstrated interaction regions to be transferred across geometrically diverse objects sharing similar functionality, with modest computational cost
claims.direction: favors single-demonstration affordance transfer via semantic-geometric correspondence over collecting separate demonstrations for each object variant
claims.conditions: synthetic object categories + real-world robotic manipulation tasks, qualitative 'accurate transfer' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: The method enables generalization of a demonstrated interaction to objects that vary significantly in geometry but share functional similarity (e.g., different-shaped instances of the same object category)
claims.direction: supports semantic-functional correspondence as a mechanism for object-shape/appearance generalization, relevant to a 'different-looking' target object
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation, qualitative claim

title: An Empirical Study of Action and Observation Spaces for Imitation Learning in Contact-Rich Pushing

claims.claim: In a systematic comparison of action/observation-space compositions (end-effector states, object states, interaction forces) for a diffusion-based visuomotor policy on a contact-rich pushing task, position-based action representations give stable behavior but can lead to slow task execution under impedance control, whereas force-aware representations better capture interaction dynamics but suffer from high variability due to frictional contacts and sampling limitations
