claims.direction: identifies a concrete stability-vs-speed-vs-variability trade-off between position-based and force-aware action/observation representations for contact-rich imitation learning, rather than favoring one universally
claims.conditions: MuJoCo simulation, push-box task, impedance-controlled teacher policy demonstrations, diffusion-based visuomotor policy

title: See What Matters: Differentiable Grid Sample Pruning for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Reframing visual token compression as geometry-aware, continuous token resampling (a Differentiable Grid Sampler that adaptively predicts a minimal set of salient coordinates and extracts features via differentiable interpolation), rather than discrete token pruning, preserves essential spatial/contact-point information even at extreme compression rates
claims.direction: favors continuous, geometry-aware resampling of visual tokens over discrete pruning methods, which discard critical geometric details (e.g. contact points) under aggressive compression
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark + real robotic platform

claims.claim: Using fewer than 10% of the original visual tokens, this method achieves a 76% reduction in FLOPs with no degradation in success rate, the lowest feasible visual token count reported to date at that time
claims.direction: strongly supports aggressive, geometry-aware visual token compression as a way to cut VLA inference cost (FLOPs) without sacrificing task success, directly relevant to real-time deployment on constrained hardware
claims.conditions: LIBERO + real robot, plug-and-play module added to existing VLA vision encoders

title: A Pragmatic VLA Foundation Model

claims.claim: LingBot-VLA, trained on ~20,000 hours of real-world data from 9 dual-arm robot configurations, achieves clear superiority over competitors on a systematic assessment across 4 robotic platforms (100 tasks each, 130 post-training episodes per task)
claims.direction: supports large-scale, multi-embodiment pretraining data as a route to strong generalist post-training performance, though at a data scale far beyond our budget
claims.conditions: 4 robotic platforms, large-scale multi-embodiment pretraining plus per-task post-training episodes

claims.claim: An efficient training codebase delivers 261 samples/second throughput on an 8-GPU setup, a 1.5-2.8x speedup over existing VLA-oriented codebases (depending on the underlying VLM base model)
claims.direction: supports engineering/codebase-level optimizations as a lever for VLA training efficiency, distinct from architectural choices
claims.conditions: 8-GPU training setup, comparison against existing VLA codebases; concerns training throughput, not inference latency

title: GAINS: Leveraging Inconsistent Human Intervention Signals in Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Modeling the return variability induced by sparse task rewards AND inconsistent/delayed human intervention timing (via distributional RL with quantile Q-networks and a pessimistic exploration strategy), rather than treating human corrections as perfectly reliable, achieves a 22% higher task success rate than RLIF and improves recovery success by up to 43% in failure scenarios
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling the imperfection/inconsistency of human intervention signals (not just the actions given) over standard intervention-based learning that assumes reliable correction timing
claims.conditions: 4 simulated manipulation tasks + 2 real-world scenarios, intervention-based RL (not pure offline imitation learning)

title: HABILIS Brain 0: Geometry-Change Supervision for Vision-Language-Action and Residual Flow Recovery

claims.claim: Learning to predict multiview future-current 'geometry-change' tokens from current observations (using offline frame pairs at a nominal 0.5-second horizon, with future observations used only to construct training targets, never executed at inference) as an embodiment-agnostic pretraining objective, then aligning a continuous ActionExpert with robot actions, achieves 95.20% success on LIBERO
claims.direction: favors an embodiment-agnostic geometry-change prediction auxiliary objective (pretrainable across robot and egocentric video) over standard next-frame or embodiment-specific auxiliary objectives
claims.conditions: multi-stage training pipeline, LIBERO sim benchmark, offline-constructed training targets only (not used at inference)

claims.claim: Freezing the geometry-change VLA and adding a Geometry-Conditioned Residual Flow (GCRF) module -- a binary intervention router plus a single bounded residual velocity policy learned from closed-loop feedback -- further raises LIBERO success from 95.20% to 99.55%
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight, bounded residual flow-correction policy on top of a frozen base VLA (rather than retraining/fine-tuning the whole model) for closed-loop refinement
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark, frozen base model, additional residual-flow training stage

title: Keypoint Action Tokens Enable In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics

claims.claim: An off-the-shelf, text-only-pretrained Transformer (GPT-4 Turbo, no additional training) can perform few-shot in-context visual imitation learning by tokenizing visual keypoint observations and action trajectories into text-like token sequences (Keypoint Action Tokens), translating tokenized keypoint observations directly into action trajectories
claims.direction: favors a keypoint-tokenization action representation that lets a frozen, off-the-shelf language model perform imitation learning in-context, as an alternative to training any new policy network
claims.conditions: real-world everyday manipulation tasks, no policy training required, in-context (few-shot) demonstration

claims.claim: This in-context approach performs on par with or better than state-of-the-art diffusion policies specifically in the low-data regime on a suite of real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors in-context, training-free imitation learning over training a diffusion policy from scratch, specifically when demonstration data is scarce
claims.conditions: real-world tasks, low-data regime comparison against diffusion policies

title: CroSTAta: Cross-State Transition Attention Transformer for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A State Transition Attention (STA) mechanism that modulates standard attention weights based on learned state-evolution patterns (e.g. failure-and-recovery patterns in demonstration history), combined with temporal masking during training (randomly removing visual information from recent timesteps to encourage temporal reasoning), consistently outperforms standard attention and other temporal modeling methods (TCN, LSTM), achieving more than 2x improvement over cross-attention on precision-critical tasks
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling state-transition/temporal structure (not just attending over a raw history window) for observation-history conditioning, especially to handle execution variations and failure/recovery patterns not explicitly covered in training
claims.conditions: simulation evaluation, comparison against standard attention, TCN, and LSTM baselines

title: Iterative Compositional Data Generation for Robot Control

claims.claim: A semantic compositional diffusion transformer that factorizes transitions into robot-, object-, obstacle-, and objective-specific components (learning their interactions via attention), trained on a limited subset of tasks, can zero-shot generate high-quality synthetic transitions for unseen task combinations; an iterative self-improvement loop (validating synthetic data via offline RL and incorporating it into subsequent training) substantially improves zero-shot performance over monolithic and hard-coded compositional baselines
claims.direction: favors compositionally-factorized generative data augmentation (rather than monolithic generative models or hard-coded composition rules) for generalizing to unseen combinations of objects/obstacles/objectives from limited real training tasks
claims.conditions: multi-object, multi-robot, multi-environment settings, offline RL used to validate synthetic data quality

title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-world Deployment

claims.claim: Grafting a flow-matching continuous-action expert onto a discrete-token VLM backbone via per-layer KV-cache conditioning (rather than using a purely discrete-token or purely continuous-diffusion action head) lets MolmoAct2 outperform strong baselines including pi-0.5 across 7 simulation and real-world benchmarks
claims.direction: favors a hybrid discrete-VLM-plus-continuous-flow-matching-expert architecture over either a purely discrete-action or purely continuous-diffusion VLA design
claims.conditions: 7 sim + real-world benchmarks, open-weight model, comparison against pi-0.5 and other strong baselines

claims.claim: MolmoThink, an adaptive-depth reasoning variant, re-predicts depth/geometric tokens only for scene regions that change between timesteps (rather than recomputing full-scene geometric grounding every step), retaining geometric grounding accuracy at a fraction of the latency of prior reasoning-augmented policies
claims.direction: favors change-region-only recomputation of auxiliary geometric/reasoning tokens over full recomputation every timestep, to cut inference latency while keeping reasoning benefits
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, reasoning-augmented VLA setting

claims.claim: The released training data explicitly includes quality-filtered SO100/101 subsets (the same low-cost arm family used in our project) alongside a 720-hour open bimanual dataset (MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM) and Franka (DROID) data, plus an open-weight action tokenizer (OpenFAST) trained across five embodiments
claims.direction: provides an openly available, quality-filtered SO-100/101-specific dataset and pretrained tokenizer that could plausibly be used directly for pretraining or co-training a policy for our exact robot family
claims.conditions: open-source release, low-to-medium-cost platform data explicitly included

why_deep_read: This is one of the only papers in the batch whose released training data and benchmarks explicitly include our exact robot family (SO100/101), alongside an open action tokenizer and a latency-reducing adaptive-depth reasoning mechanism; the full paper and released artifacts (weights, OpenFAST tokenizer, SO-101 data subset) could be directly usable for our project rather than just informing a design decision.

title: Dynamic Neural Koopman Distillation for Real-Time Robot Control Using Diffusion Models

claims.claim: A Factorized Dynamic Koopman layer, modeling the multistep diffusion denoising process as a factorized latent transition with state-dependent modal gains, distills multistep diffusion inference into a single forward pass while retaining the teacher model's multimodal expressivity, significantly outperforming existing one-step distillation approaches on D4RL MuJoCo locomotion benchmarks
claims.direction: favors Koopman-operator-based distillation of diffusion policies to a single forward pass over other one-step distillation methods, to preserve multimodality while cutting inference cost
claims.conditions: D4RL MuJoCo locomotion benchmarks + physical Kinova manipulator hardware experiment

claims.claim: On a physical Kinova manipulator, the distilled single-forward-pass policy reduces inference latency to the millisecond regime (versus the multistep teacher diffusion policy) while enabling smooth and fast closed-loop execution with maintained task success and comparable accuracy
claims.direction: strongly supports single-step Koopman-distilled diffusion policies as a way to make diffusion-based control real-time-capable and smooth on real hardware
claims.conditions: real Kinova manipulator, direct comparison to multistep teacher diffusion policy

title: SegDiff: Segmented Trajectory Diffusion for Consistent and Adaptive Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing demonstrations into motion segments between keyposes and predicting the continuous trajectory from the current state to the next keypose (rather than either short-horizon continuous chunks alone, which suffer compounding error, or keypose-only prediction, which needs an external planner) enables long-horizon prediction with real-time refinement, showing significant performance gains over both existing paradigms across simulated and real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors a hybrid continuous-segment-to-next-keypose action representation over either pure short-horizon continuous action chunking or pure discrete keypose prediction
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation scenarios

claims.claim: A Dynamic Temporal Ensembling mechanism (leveraging diffusion models and DDIM inversion) allows the policy to efficiently respond to dynamic environments and mitigate discontinuities caused by inconsistent multi-modal sampling across action chunks
claims.direction: favors dynamic (adaptive) temporal ensembling over static/fixed temporal ensembling for reducing discontinuities at action-chunk transitions in a diffusion policy
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation, qualitative 'significant performance gains' claim, no exact numbers given

title: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Because tactile signals are directly grounded in physical contact, they can exhibit a smaller simulation-to-real gap than purely visual observations; leveraging public real tactile datasets plus a constructed simulation environment to scale visuo-tactile-action data, then pretraining and finetuning a world model on this data, generates physically meaningful rollouts that improve downstream tactile-policy performance through scalable data augmentation
claims.direction: favors tactile-grounded data augmentation/world-model rollouts (exploiting tactile's smaller sim-to-real gap) over purely visual data augmentation for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensors/datasets, qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: An action-conditioned visuo-tactile world model can serve both to synthesize rollouts for policy improvement and to evaluate policies by predicting action-conditioned visuo-tactile outcomes under controlled action sequences
claims.direction: supports a visuo-tactile world model as a dual-purpose auxiliary tool (data augmentation + policy evaluation), not just an auxiliary training loss
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation, requires tactile sensing

title: PPGuide: Steering Diffusion Policies with Performance Predictive Guidance

claims.claim: A lightweight, self-supervised classifier-based framework (PPGuide) that uses attention-based multiple instance learning to automatically label which observation-action chunks from a pretrained diffusion policy's own rollouts are relevant to success/failure, then trains a performance predictor providing a real-time gradient at inference time, consistently improves performance across diverse tasks from Robomimic and MimicGen, without needing expert-augmented datasets or a full predictive world model
claims.direction: favors lightweight, self-labeled inference-time guidance for a frozen diffusion policy over either augmenting the training dataset with more expert demonstrations or learning a full (computationally expensive) predictive world model
claims.conditions: Robomimic + MimicGen benchmarks, self-supervised labeling requires no additional human annotation

claims.claim: Because PPGuide is lightweight and classifier-based (not a full world model), it can steer a pre-trained diffusion policy away from failure modes at inference time with modest added compute
claims.direction: supports lightweight inference-time correction mechanisms as a low-compute-cost way to reduce compounding errors in diffusion action sequences
claims.conditions: same benchmarks, qualitative 'consistent improvements' claim, no exact numbers given

title: StageWAM: Joint-Embedding Stage Prediction for World-Action Models in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Distinguishing a short-term physical future (local scene evolution for action execution) from a stage-level semantic future (how a task should progress to its next stage), and predicting the latter via a goal-conditioned JEPA module (Stage-JEPA, using a frozen V-JEPA2 encoder) on top of a Motus-based World Action Model, achieves 90.25% overall success across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks in clean and randomized environments
claims.direction: favors adding a separate stage-level semantic future-prediction auxiliary objective (distinct from short-term next-chunk video/action prediction) to a world-action model
claims.conditions: 50 RoboTwin2.0 sim tasks, clean and randomized environment variants

claims.claim: StageWAM reduces the mean number of execution steps in successful rollouts by 5.97% relative to the strongest baseline, by conditioning on inferred task-stage progress rather than only local scene dynamics
claims.direction: supports stage-aware conditioning as a way to improve execution efficiency/horizon planning beyond what pure short-horizon chunk prediction provides
claims.conditions: same 50-task RoboTwin2.0 benchmark

title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Existing force-aware VLA models exhibit limited capability in precise force tracking and rapid successive adjustments specifically because of action-chunk execution strategies and the latency between perception and real-time control; a Control-aware Compliance VLA (CC-VLA) using a multimodal mixture-of-experts to encode force sequences and vision-language features, plus a VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller, significantly improves success rates in force-perception tasks and force-control precision under partial-OOD pose-shift settings
claims.direction: identifies action-chunk execution latency as a root cause of force-control failures in force-aware VLA models, and favors an adaptive compliance controller layer plus MoE force encoding as a fix
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, force/torque perception, partial-OOD pose-shift settings, qualitative 'significantly improves' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: A VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller (rather than a fixed action interface) facilitates precise position tracking during contact-free motion and optimal force-position tracking for contact-rich phases within the same policy
claims.direction: favors an adaptive, compliance-based action/control interface that switches behavior between contact-free and contact-rich phases, over a single fixed action-space formulation
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich tasks, adversarial shared teleoperation used for demonstration collection

title: VLPSA: Vision-Language-Poisson-Safe Actions for Full-Body Safety of Learned Policies

claims.claim: A safety-filtering layer (synthesizing Poisson Safety Functions online from perception data into a Control Barrier Function, enforced via a CBF-QP filter over the full robot body and grasped object) added on top of a VLA policy without retraining increases collision avoidance from 23.1% for the base pi0.5 policy to 91.2%, while also surpassing the base policy's task success rate
claims.direction: favors adding an external, non-learned safety filter on top of a VLA policy (rather than retraining the policy itself) to fix collision-avoidance robustness in cluttered/dynamic out-of-distribution environments
claims.conditions: SafeLIBERO benchmark + real Franka FR3 deployment in cluttered dynamic scenes with human interference

title: Dynamic Non-Prehensile Object Transport via Model-Predictive Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Pretraining an ensemble of value functions from demonstration data and using them online within an uncertainty-aware MPC scheme (rather than pure behavior cloning) enables robust real-world deployment of a dynamic manipulation policy learned from only 50-100 demonstrations, matching our own target demo-count range
claims.direction: supports that 50-100 demonstrations can be sufficient for a real dynamic manipulation task when combined with a value-function-plus-MPC approach rather than pure BC
claims.conditions: real Franka Panda robot, dynamic non-prehensile object transport ('robot waiter') task, sparsely labeled task-space demonstrations

claims.claim: The learned value functions generalize to novel objects not seen during training and can improve upon suboptimal demonstrations, rather than simply replicating demonstrated behavior
claims.direction: supports value-function-based approaches (vs. direct behavior cloning) for generalizing beyond the exact objects/behaviors demonstrated
claims.conditions: real-world Franka Panda, novel object evaluation

title: EO-1: An Open Unified Embodied Foundation Model for General Robot Control

claims.claim: Training a unified architecture through synergies between auto-regressive decoding and flow-matching denoising on a large interleaved vision-text-action dataset (EO-Data1.5M, 1.5M+ samples) enables seamless robot action generation together with multimodal embodied reasoning, validated on long-horizon dexterous manipulation across multiple embodiments
claims.direction: favors a hybrid autoregressive-plus-flow-matching action generation architecture, jointly trained on interleaved multimodal (not action-only) data, over an action-only or single-decoding-paradigm VLA
claims.conditions: large-scale multimodal pretraining, multiple embodiments, qualitative 'effectiveness demonstrated' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Interleaved vision-text-action pretraining (processing image, text, video, and action indiscriminately within one architecture) improves open-world understanding and generalization compared to standard co-training on separate robot and visual-text data
claims.direction: supports interleaving reasoning and action tokens during pretraining/conditioning rather than treating language conditioning as a separate, upstream module
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining, qualitative claim

title: VGGT-DP: Generalizable Robot Control via Vision Foundation Models

claims.claim: Using a pretrained 3D geometric foundation model (VGGT, Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer) as the visual encoder, combined with a proprioception-guided visual learning strategy that aligns perception with internal robot states, significantly outperforms strong baselines (Diffusion Policy and DP3) on challenging MetaWorld tasks, particularly precision-critical and long-horizon ones
claims.direction: favors pretrained 3D geometric foundation-model encoders combined with proprioception-alignment over standard 2D visual encoders or unaligned 3D encoders for spatial grounding and closed-loop control
claims.conditions: MetaWorld sim benchmark, comparison against DP and DP3

claims.claim: A frame-wise token reuse (FTR) mechanism reuses cached visual-encoder aggregator tokens from overlapping observation frames and computes features only for the newest frame, substantially reducing redundant visual encoding and inference latency; random token pruning is additionally used to improve robustness and reduce overfitting
claims.direction: favors caching/reusing visual tokens across overlapping frames (rather than fully re-encoding every observation) as a latency-reduction technique for vision-heavy policies
claims.conditions: MetaWorld sim benchmark, no exact latency numbers given in abstract

title: Enhancing Reusability of Learned Skills for Robot Manipulation via Gaze Information and Motion Bottlenecks

claims.claim: Leveraging gaze information and motion bottlenecks (rather than only raw visuomotor imitation) achieves high success rates compared with state-of-the-art imitation learning methods particularly when object positions and end-effector poses differ from those in the provided demonstrations
claims.direction: favors gaze-plus-motion-bottleneck-based skill representations for generalizing learned skills to novel object/end-effector configurations, over standard imitation learning that memorizes exact demonstrated configurations
claims.conditions: real teleoperation-derived demonstrations with gaze annotations, comparison against SOTA IL methods, qualitative 'high success rates' claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: Gaze information, treated as a crucial conditioning feature for object manipulation alongside motion bottlenecks, is entirely data-driven once a demonstration dataset with gaze data is provided, requiring no additional manual engineering
claims.direction: supports gaze as an additional, cheaply-obtainable conditioning signal for improving skill reusability, complementary to language conditioning
claims.conditions: requires eye-tracking during demonstration collection, not part of our current setup

title: Uncertainty-Aware Robotic World Model Makes Offline Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Work on Real Robots

claims.claim: Extending autoregressive world models with epistemic uncertainty estimation (RWM-U), enabling temporally consistent multi-step rollouts with uncertainty propagated over long horizons, and combining this with uncertainty-penalized on-policy optimization (MOPO-PPO), lets offline model-based RL policies consistently outperform model-free and uncertainty-unaware model-based baselines on real quadruped and humanoid robots, entirely from offline datasets
claims.direction: favors explicit uncertainty modeling in world models over uncertainty-unaware world models, specifically to make offline model-based RL viable on noisy, biased, real-robot datasets
claims.conditions: real quadruped and humanoid robots, offline datasets only, plus simulation manipulation/locomotion tasks

title: On-Device Robotic Planning: Eliminating Inference Redundancy for Efficient Decision-Making

claims.claim: Robotic reasoning workloads contain substantial temporal redundancy, where consecutive observations frequently produce identical actions/subgoals; a framework (REIS) combining lightweight scene gating, KV-steered affordance routing, and deliberative reasoning exploits this to significantly suppress reasoning overhead while maintaining competitive task performance on ALFRED and real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors detecting and skipping redundant re-reasoning across consecutive near-identical observations, over re-running full reasoning/planning at every control step, to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: ALFRED benchmark + real-world robotic tasks, reasoning-based (LLM/VLM) robotic policies

title: Forecast-aware Gaussian Splatting for Predictive 3D Representation in Language-Guided Pick-and-Place Manipulation

claims.claim: Explicitly forecasting the task-completed 3D state (rather than only reasoning over the current scene) via Forecast-aware Gaussian Splatting, and using this forecast for candidate-action evaluation, achieves real-world pick-and-place success rates of 21/25, 23/25, and 16/25 on three tasks, outperforming the ReKep baseline's 15/25, 19/25, and 10/25 on the same tasks
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling and evaluating candidate actions against a forecasted task-completed 3D state, over relational-keypoint/current-scene-only reasoning baselines like ReKep
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place tasks (Cutter-to-Box, Apple-to-Bowl, Sponge-to-Tray), 25 trials/task, same robot platform and sensing setup for both methods

claims.claim: A Gaussian-Splatting-based 3D representation supports both accurate spatial/semantic goal evaluation and interpretable bridging between language understanding and manipulation planning; a diagnostic human-assisted candidate-selection setting further raises success (23/25, 24/25, 19/25), indicating the 3D representation/candidate generation is effective while automatic ranking remains the weaker link
claims.direction: supports 3D Gaussian-Splatting representations as effective for candidate generation, while flagging automatic final-state ranking (not the 3D representation itself) as the main remaining bottleneck
claims.conditions: same real-world pick-and-place tasks, human-assisted vs fully automatic comparison

title: Learning High-Frequency Continuous Action Chunks in Latent Space

claims.claim: Action chunking improves temporal consistency at moderate action frequencies but becomes insufficient at higher frequencies (e.g. 60 Hz), where policies often fail to generate actions that are both temporally smooth and spatially consistent; shifting high-frequency action learning from the raw action space to a latent space via a variational autoencoder significantly improves both temporal and spatial consistency of high-frequency control
claims.direction: favors learning action chunks in a learned latent (VAE) space rather than directly in the raw action space, specifically to fix smoothness/consistency problems that emerge at high control frequencies
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich robotic tasks, high control frequency (up to 60 Hz)

claims.claim: A 'Reuse-then-Refine' chunk-level refine strategy improves continuity between adjacent action chunks specifically under asynchronous inference, enabling robots to execute complex contact-rich tasks continuously with fewer pauses and less jerky motion; experiments on three real-world contact-rich tasks show consistently smooth task completion
claims.direction: directly targets and fixes jerky motion / discontinuity at action-chunk boundaries under asynchronous inference, matching exactly the smoothness failure mode described for our own SmolVLA deployment
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich tasks, asynchronous inference execution, high-frequency (60Hz) control

why_deep_read: This paper's stated problem -- action chunking producing jerky, spatially/temporally inconsistent motion at higher control frequencies, especially under asynchronous inference -- is essentially a verbatim match to our own reported failure mode (jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries with async inference); the latent-space (VAE) action-chunk formulation and the 'Reuse-then-Refine' chunk-continuity strategy are concrete, likely-adoptable fixes worth extracting in full detail, especially since we could also raise our data rate toward 30fps as the abstract's high-frequency regime discusses.

title: World Action Models Enable Continual Imitation Learning with Recurrent Generative Replays

claims.claim: A world-action model's generative (future-observation-prediction) capability can be recursively queried to synthesize pseudo-replay trajectories conditioned only on prior task instructions and current-task observations, enabling a policy to rehearse previously learned tasks without storing original human demonstrations, reducing catastrophic forgetting by up to 50% relative to sequential fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors using a world-action model's generative capability for pseudo-replay of prior tasks over storing and replaying original demonstrations, when adapting a policy to new tasks sequentially
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation, continual/sequential multi-task adaptation setting (not directly our single/dual-task setup)

claims.claim: Long-horizon visual degradation and action-observation inconsistency in the generated pseudo-replay are identified as the primary bottlenecks limiting how well this generative-replay approach approaches privileged (real-data) replay performance
claims.direction: identifies specific failure modes (visual degradation, action-observation drift) that limit purely generative data substitutes for real demonstration data in continual learning settings
claims.conditions: same continual imitation learning setting

title: RoboBRIDGE: A Modular Framework for Bridging Policies to Robust Real-World Robotic Agents

claims.claim: Wrapping a pretrained VLA with a modular orchestration layer (Monitor for rapid failure detection + hierarchical recovery, Planner for replanning when the environment diverges, Perceptor for asynchronous scene-understanding updates, Controller with domain-invariant primitive-skill LoRA adapters) consistently outperforms both standalone policies and prior augmented-VLA deployments across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world case studies on multiple robot platforms/VLA backbones
claims.direction: favors structured orchestration (failure monitoring, replanning, domain-invariant primitive fine-tuning) around an off-the-shelf pretrained VLA over relying on the VLA alone or scaling the action predictor further, for robustness to observation/task/embodiment shifts
claims.conditions: multiple sim benchmarks + real-world, multiple robot platforms and VLA backbones

claims.claim: The Perceptor updates scene understanding asynchronously (in parallel with plan execution) specifically to avoid execution stalls while the Planner replans, addressing latency introduced by re-planning
claims.direction: supports asynchronous perception/planning updates (rather than blocking execution while replanning) as a way to avoid execution stalls/latency spikes
claims.conditions: same modular framework, multiple platforms

title: Decoupling Vision, Language, and Action for Efficient Multi-Task Robot Policies

claims.claim: In a standardized comparison holding demonstrations, training-step budget, tasks, evaluation protocol, and measurement platform fixed against 7 VLA baselines (including GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5), a Decoupled Embodiment Model (DEM) -- a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision encoder + frozen NeoBERT language encoder + MeanFlow action head generating a full action chunk in one forward pass -- needs only 6.1ms per policy forward pass and a maximum throughput of 162.7 policy calls/second, drawing ~2.07J of GPU energy per call: 8-17x the throughput and 6-15x less energy than VLM-backbone (billion-parameter) VLA policies on the same workstation
claims.direction: strongly favors a decoupled (separate small vision + frozen language encoder + compact one-shot action head) architecture over running a billion-parameter VLM backbone at every inference step, when latency and energy matter
claims.conditions: 18 RoboCasa sim tasks (held-out instruction paraphrases, randomized scenes) + 3 real-robot tasks, standardized comparison against 7 VLA baselines, same training budget and evaluation protocol for all

claims.claim: DEM reaches 55.6% mean success on RoboCasa (vs 56.9% for GR00T N1.7 and 54.6% for pi0.5) and 66.0% on real-robot tasks (vs 68.0% for GR00T N1.7) -- i.e., success within ~1-2 percentage points of billion-parameter VLM-backbone baselines despite being far smaller and decoupled -- placing it on the observed success-latency-energy frontier as a strong efficient baseline
claims.direction: shows that a small, decoupled architecture can match large VLM-backbone VLAs in success rate almost exactly while being drastically cheaper, directly supporting favoring small/efficient architectures under compute constraints when performance parity can be achieved
claims.conditions: same standardized comparison as above, within-trained-task regime (not testing OOD generalization specifically)

claims.claim: A fine-tuned DINOv3 vision encoder (rather than a full VLM vision-language backbone) is sufficient as the vision component when paired with a frozen language encoder and a capable compact action head
claims.direction: favors a dedicated fine-tuned self-supervised ViT (DINOv3) vision encoder over relying on a large pretrained VLM's vision pathway
claims.conditions: same standardized comparison

claims.claim: A frozen NeoBERT language encoder (not a large VLM's language pathway, and not further fine-tuned) is sufficient for language conditioning, evaluated specifically on held-out instruction paraphrases
claims.direction: favors a small, frozen, dedicated language encoder over a large VLM's language understanding module for language-conditioned action prediction, even under paraphrase generalization testing
claims.conditions: same standardized comparison, held-out instruction paraphrase evaluation

claims.claim: A MeanFlow action head that generates a full action chunk in a single forward pass (rather than iterative diffusion/flow denoising steps) is a key contributor to DEM's low latency while maintaining competitive success
claims.direction: favors one-forward-pass (MeanFlow-style) action generation over multi-step iterative denoising action heads, when both success and latency are counted
claims.conditions: same standardized comparison

why_deep_read: This is a rigorously controlled, apples-to-apples comparison (same demos/budget/tasks/platform) of a small decoupled architecture against 7 VLA baselines including GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5, showing near-parity success (within ~1-2pp) at 8-17x the throughput and 6-15x less energy -- an almost perfect match to our exact problem (RTX 5060 8GB laptop, ~2s inference latency, wanting a small robust policy); the specific component choices (DINOv3, frozen NeoBERT, MeanFlow one-pass action head) are a concrete, directly adoptable recipe worth extracting in full.

title: iVideoGPT: Interactive VideoGPTs are Scalable World Models

claims.claim: A scalable autoregressive transformer that integrates visual observations, actions, and rewards into a single token sequence (using a novel compressive tokenization technique for high-dimensional visual observations), pre-trained on millions of human and robotic manipulation trajectories, achieves competitive performance on action-conditioned video prediction, visual planning, and model-based RL compared with state-of-the-art methods
claims.direction: supports large-scale interactive video-world-model pretraining (jointly over vision, action, reward tokens) as a general-purpose foundation adaptable to multiple downstream robot-learning tasks
claims.conditions: pretraining on millions of human+robot trajectories, competitive (not necessarily state-of-the-art) performance, qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

claims.claim: A compressive tokenization technique efficiently discretizes high-dimensional visual observations for scalable interactive world modeling
claims.direction: supports compressive/discrete visual tokenization schemes as a practical way to make large-scale video+action world models tractable
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining setting

title: VITAL: Interactive Few-Shot Imitation Learning via Visual Human-in-the-Loop Corrections

claims.claim: Starting from a handful of real demonstrations, large-scale training data can be generated via simulation-based augmentation, and combining this with human-in-the-loop corrections (both in simulation and real-world integration) enhances the generalizability and robustness of the learned policies, including generalizing to new tasks not directly demonstrated
claims.direction: favors combining simulation-based augmentation of a small real demo set with human-in-the-loop correction over collecting a large real-only demonstration set
claims.conditions: real + simulated environments, tasks of varying complexity (bottle collecting, stacking, hammering, and generalization to a new drink-tray task), qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: EL3DD: Extended Latent 3D Diffusion for Language Conditioned Multitask Manipulation

claims.claim: Extending a latent 3D diffusion visuomotor policy (merging visual and textual inputs) with improved embeddings and image-generation-diffusion-adapted techniques improves performance on the CALVIN benchmark and increases long-horizon success rate when multiple tasks are executed in sequence
claims.direction: supports 3D latent diffusion policies with improved multimodal embeddings for language-conditioned multitask manipulation over simpler diffusion or non-3D baselines
claims.conditions: CALVIN sim benchmark, qualitative 'enhanced performance' claim, no exact numbers given

title: What Matters in Learning from Large-Scale Datasets for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A controlled, large-scale dataset-composition study (procedurally emulating common sources of diversity such as sensor placements and object types/arrangements) finds that camera poses and spatial arrangements are crucial dimensions for BOTH diversity in data collection and alignment in retrieval, more so than other tested diversity dimensions
claims.direction: favors prioritizing camera-pose and spatial-arrangement diversity specifically when deciding what data to collect for a fixed demo budget, over other forms of diversity
claims.conditions: controlled simulation study with procedurally generated datasets, insights validated to carry over to real-world settings

claims.claim: Camera pose is identified as one of the most critical dimensions of dataset diversity for downstream policy learning, both for collection and for retrieval-based data selection
claims.direction: directly supports varying camera pose/viewpoint deliberately when collecting a limited demonstration set, as a high-leverage diversity axis
claims.conditions: same controlled study, real-world validation on DROID

claims.claim: In real-world settings, retrieval strategies (selecting relevant demonstrations from existing large datasets like DROID based on the identified critical diversity dimensions) allow policies to consistently outperform existing training strategies by up to 70%
claims.direction: strongly supports that intelligently selecting/aligning training data along the right diversity axes (rather than simply using more data) drives large downstream generalization gains
claims.conditions: real-world robot learning, retrieval from the DROID dataset, comparison against existing training strategies

why_deep_read: A systematic, controlled dataset-composition study that pinpoints camera pose and spatial arrangement as the highest-leverage diversity axes for both collection and retrieval, with a real-world +70% result on DROID; directly informs how we should structure our own ~50-100 demo collection (e.g., deliberately varying camera pose/object placement) to maximize robustness for the same data budget, which is one of our most actionable open questions (Q13).

title: LeVR: A Modular VR Teleoperation Framework for Imitation Learning in Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A public dataset of 100 expert demonstrations, collected via a modular VR teleoperation framework natively integrated with the LeRobot imitation learning framework, was sufficient to successfully fine-tune state-of-the-art visuomotor policies end-to-end from data collection to real-world deployment
claims.direction: provides a concrete existence proof that ~100 demonstrations collected via a LeRobot-integrated teleoperation pipeline can support successful fine-tuning of visuomotor policies
claims.conditions: Franka FER arm + RobotEra XHand platform, LeRobot framework, 100 demonstrations, no comparative success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: Real-time Iteration Scheme for Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Adapting the Real-Time Iteration (RTI) scheme from optimal control -- reusing the previous timestep's denoising solution as an initial guess for the next diffusion inference step, plus a scaling-based method for handling discrete actions like grasping -- significantly reduces runtime computational cost for diffusion-policy inference without requiring distillation or policy redesign, achieving a substantial reduction in inference time with comparable overall performance to full-step-denoising Diffusion Policy
claims.direction: favors training-free, warm-start-based acceleration of diffusion policy inference (reusing prior-step solutions) over distillation or architecture changes, for reducing latency on already-pretrained diffusion policies
claims.conditions: extensive simulation experiments, comparison against full-step-denoising Diffusion Policy, applicable to large pretrained diffusion-based models without retraining

title: Reverse to Advance: Teleoperation-Cost Effective Hard Policy Learning from Reversed Easy Tasks

claims.claim: Many manipulation tasks exhibit directional asymmetry (the forward hard task is difficult, but reversing/relaxing the environment is comparatively easy); using reversed easy-task trajectories (collected via a closed-loop pipeline that alternates hard-task and easy-task policies to autonomously reset the environment) as a scalable supervision signal, refined via kinematic priors and a critic-guided advantage filter, improves hard-task success rates with higher data efficiency and more stable training than reversal-based and RL baselines, without requiring extensive hard-task teleoperation
claims.direction: favors exploiting task reversibility (collecting cheap 'easy-direction' demonstrations and temporally inverting them) as a substitute for costly direct teleoperation of the hard task itself
claims.conditions: 2 simulated benchmarks + real-robot experiments, tasks with directional asymmetry (hard-to-do but easy-to-undo), qualitative 'improves' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Real-Time Robot Execution with Masked Action Chunking

claims.claim: Under asynchronous inference (predicting the next action chunk while the current one executes), prior work attributed execution failures to inter-chunk discontinuity and developed test-time chunk-boundary smoothing algorithms; this paper identifies a second, previously overlooked factor -- intra-chunk inconsistency, where the robot's executed action chunk partially misaligns with its current perception mid-chunk -- as also critical to real-time execution failure
claims.direction: identifies intra-chunk inconsistency (not just inter-chunk boundary discontinuity) as an additional, distinct root cause of asynchronous-inference execution failure in action-chunking policies, directly matching our own reported 'jerky motion at chunk boundaries with async inference' symptom
claims.conditions: asynchronous inference execution setting, action-chunking policies, both simulation and real-world

claims.claim: REMAC learns corrective adjustments on a pretrained policy through masked action chunking (making the policy resilient to mismatches between intended and actually-executed actions) plus a prefix-preserved sampling procedure reinforcing inter-chunk continuity, delivering more reliable policies without incurring additional latency, with faster task execution, robustness across varying delays, and consistently higher completion rates
claims.direction: favors training a lightweight corrective adjustment (masked action chunking) on top of an existing pretrained action-chunking policy over redesigning the base policy or adding latency-costly runtime correction, to fix asynchronous-inference execution failures
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, applied on top of pretrained action-chunking policies, no additional inference latency incurred

why_deep_read: Names and directly targets the exact failure mode we reported (jerky/failed execution at action-chunk boundaries under asynchronous inference), going beyond prior inter-chunk-discontinuity fixes to also address intra-chunk inconsistency, with a no-added-latency corrective-adjustment method; the full paper's masked-action-chunking training recipe and prefix-preserved sampling procedure are worth extracting as a likely-adoptable fix for our SmolVLA deployment.

title: MG-Grasp: Metric-Scale Geometric 6-DoF Grasping Framework with Sparse RGB Observations

claims.claim: Leveraging a two-view 3D foundation model (with camera intrinsics/extrinsics) to reconstruct metric-scale, multi-view-consistent dense point clouds from sparse RGB images (no depth sensor) achieves state-of-the-art 6-DoF grasp performance among RGB-based grasping methods on GraspNet-1Billion and real-world tests
claims.direction: shows that accurate metric-scale 3D geometry for grasping can be recovered from RGB alone (via a pretrained 3D foundation model) without a physical depth sensor, though this does not directly compare against using an available depth sensor's readings
claims.conditions: GraspNet-1Billion benchmark + real-world, RGB-only input, comparison against other RGB-based (not RGB-D) 6-DoF grasping methods

title: PointACT: Vision-Language-Action Models with Multi-Scale Point-Action Interaction

claims.claim: Integrating hierarchical 3D point-cloud representations directly into the action-decoding process of a dual-system VLA (via a multi-scale point-action interaction mechanism with efficient bottleneck window self-attention letting action tokens densely attend to both local geometric detail and global scene structure) increases success rates by 10% on the challenging RLBench-10Tasks suite over state-of-the-art pretrained VLAs; ablations show tightly coupling hierarchical 3D geometry with pretrained 2D semantic representations is critical for robust, spatially grounded control
claims.direction: favors deeply integrating 3D point-cloud geometry into the action-decoding pathway (not just as an auxiliary input) over 2D-only VLA baselines or simple point-cloud input augmentation
claims.conditions: LIBERO + RLBench sim benchmarks, comparison against monolithic and dual-system VLA baselines including point-cloud-augmented variants

claims.claim: Even larger gains from adding 3D point-action interaction are observed when the vision-language backbone is FROZEN and the action expert is trained from scratch, compared to fine-tuning a large pretrained backbone
claims.direction: supports that a frozen large backbone plus a small, geometry-aware, from-scratch-trained action expert can be more effective than fine-tuning the whole large model, relevant to compute-constrained setups
claims.conditions: same sim benchmarks, ablation comparing frozen-backbone vs fine-tuned-backbone configurations

title: Auditing Instruction–Trajectory Mismatches in Multimodal Robot Demonstrations

claims.claim: A training-free auditing framework (Multimodal Probabilistic Fusion, treating each modality as an expert and fusing via predictive-entropy-weighted product of experts) detects and corrects Instruction-Trajectory Mismatches -- demonstrations that are behaviorally correct but paired with the wrong language instruction -- achieving the strongest overall detection/correction accuracy on LIBERO and noisy real-robot data, and improving most downstream policy learning in settings where language is needed to disambiguate the task
claims.direction: favors auditing and correcting/filtering mislabeled demonstrations (a subtle data-quality issue distinct from failed rollouts) before training, over training on a raw demonstration set that may contain silently mislabeled trajectories
claims.conditions: LIBERO with injected instruction mismatches + noisy real-robot data, training-free method, trade-off noted between filtering vs. relabeling demonstrations

claims.claim: Instruction-Trajectory Mismatches specifically corrupt the language-behavior mapping learned by a policy, and this harm is most pronounced in settings where language is actually needed to disambiguate between similar tasks
claims.direction: highlights that language-conditioning quality is highly sensitive to demonstration-instruction labeling accuracy, particularly for multi-task/language-disambiguation settings
claims.conditions: same experimental settings

title: RoboMP2: A Robotic Multimodal Perception-Planning Framework with Multimodal Large Language Models

claims.claim: A Goal-Conditioned Multimodal Perceptor built on tailored MLLMs (with semantic reasoning and localization abilities) that captures multimodal environment state, combined with a Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Planner using coarse-to-fine retrieval of the k most-relevant policies as in-context demonstrations, improves performance by around 10% over baselines on the VIMA benchmark and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit multimodal environment-state perception plus retrieval-augmented in-context policy selection over end-to-end MLLM policies or human-selected-prompt approaches that overlook multimodal environment information
claims.conditions: VIMA sim benchmark + real-world tasks, comparison against end-to-end MLLM and prompt-based baselines

title: Goal-Directed Visual Diffusion Policy for Efficient Data Collection in Robot Learning

claims.claim: Generating synthetic demonstration data from multiple single-shot camera observations of a goal location, integrated with traditional motion planning within a diffusion policy framework, significantly reduces the need for task demonstrations while maintaining comparable accuracy, validated in both simulation and lab experiments
claims.direction: favors combining classical motion planning with diffusion-policy-based synthetic demonstration generation over collecting full task demonstrations for every new goal/scene
claims.conditions: sim + real lab experiments, qualitative 'significantly reduces' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Vision in Action: Learning Active Perception from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: An active perception system with a 6-DoF robotic neck (enabling flexible, human-like head/camera movements), learning task-relevant active perceptual strategies (searching, tracking, focusing) directly from human demonstrations via a VR teleoperation interface, significantly outperforms baseline (fixed-camera) systems on complex, multi-stage bimanual manipulation tasks involving visual occlusions
claims.direction: favors an actively-moving camera viewpoint (learned from human demonstration) over a fixed camera setup, particularly for tasks involving occlusion
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation with visual occlusions, requires an additional actuated camera/neck mechanism not present in a simple fixed-camera setup, qualitative 'significantly outperforming' claim

title: Fast-in-Slow: A Dual-System VLA Model Unifying Fast Manipulation within Slow Reasoning

claims.claim: Rather than maintaining a VLM-based System 2 (high-level reasoning) and a separate System 1 (real-time action) as two fully separate models, embedding System 1 within System 2 by partially sharing parameters lets System 1 fully leverage System 2's rich pretrained knowledge while still supporting high-frequency execution, using heterogeneous modality inputs and asynchronous operating frequencies for the two systems, coordinated via a dual-aware co-training strategy
claims.direction: favors a parameter-sharing dual-system architecture (fast execution module embedded within a slow-reasoning VLM) over maintaining fully separate System-1/System-2 models
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: FiS-VLA outperforms previous state-of-the-art dual-system methods by 8% in simulation and 11% in real-world tasks in average success rate, while achieving high-frequency execution suitable for real-time control
claims.direction: quantifies that parameter-sharing dual-system design improves both success rate and execution frequency versus prior (separate-model) dual-system approaches
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, comparison against prior dual-system (System1/System2) VLA methods

claims.claim: Partial parameter sharing between the fast execution module and the slow VLM reasoning module is more parameter-efficient than maintaining two fully separate models
claims.direction: supports parameter sharing as an efficiency mechanism for combining fast reactive control with slow semantic reasoning in a single model
claims.conditions: same dual-system comparison

title: DRACO: Depth-Assisted Robot ACtOr with Language-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching Policy

claims.claim: Feeding the real-world 3D position of each pixel (with respect to the camera coordinate frame, derived from depth) into a modified PointNet encoder, alongside multi-view RGB-D images, proprioceptive states, and language instructions, enhances both performance and data efficiency compared to not integrating depth modality, on the CALVIN benchmark
claims.direction: favors explicitly incorporating depth/3D pixel-position information into the visual encoder over RGB-only observation, for both task performance and data efficiency
claims.conditions: CALVIN sim benchmark, multi-view RGB-D input, Transformer-based Flow Matching backbone

claims.claim: The depth-integrated flow-matching policy maintains low memory requirements of only 2.8 GB of GPU VRAM during inference
claims.direction: demonstrates that adding depth/3D information does not necessarily require large GPU memory, directly relevant to memory-constrained deployment
claims.conditions: CALVIN sim benchmark, inference-time memory measurement

claims.claim: A Transformer-based Flow Matching backbone, trained end-to-end via imitation behavioral cloning to predict an action trajectory, is used as the policy architecture for this depth-and-language-conditioned setting
claims.direction: supports flow matching as a viable action-generation backbone when combined with depth-augmented, language-conditioned multimodal inputs
claims.conditions: CALVIN sim benchmark

why_deep_read: Directly answers our open Q04 question (should we use the depth channel from our RealSense camera?) with a concrete 'yes, improves both performance and data efficiency' finding, and reports an inference memory footprint (2.8GB) comfortably within our 8GB GPU budget; worth extracting the depth-to-PointNet integration recipe as a likely low-risk addition to our current RGB-only SmolVLA pipeline.

title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Generalizable and Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

claims.claim: A world-model-conditioned framework that learns compact action-conditioned latent dynamics from proprioception, depth, tactile sensing, and actions (supervised by multimodal reconstruction and reward prediction), used as recurrent task context for an asymmetric actor-critic policy (rather than for latent imagination/policy optimization), shows via ablation that predictive world modeling, clean-depth supervision, and tactile contact cues all shape the learned state and improve robustness to pose shifts, force disturbances, and object variation
claims.direction: favors using a multimodal world model purely as a context/state-representation provider (not for planning/imagination) for a downstream RL policy, with ablations isolating the contribution of each modality/auxiliary head
claims.conditions: dexterous in-hand manipulation, tactile+depth+proprioception sensing, sim + real-robot transfer

claims.claim: The World Synesthesia Model is explicitly trained to reconstruct clean depth targets from noisy depth inputs, providing a denoised geometric state that improves real-robot deployment; a world model pretrained on 9 objects serves as a reusable prior improving downstream policy learning across 49 objects
claims.direction: supports depth-denoising as an explicit auxiliary training objective (not just using raw noisy depth) and shows this pretrained representation transfers across a much larger set of objects
claims.conditions: real-robot dexterous manipulation, pretraining on 9 objects, downstream on 49 objects

title: Res-HIL: Human-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning for Sample-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: With only 20 initial demonstrations, learning a residual (corrective) policy on top of a frozen imitation policy via human-in-the-loop residual RL (using each intervention as both direct residual supervision and reward shaping of preceding autonomous behavior, with zero-initialized residual policy) outperforms state-of-the-art full-policy HIL RL and residual fine-tuning without human guidance on every task after ten minutes of online training, and outperforms imitation policies trained with five times more demonstrations
claims.direction: favors human-guided residual RL on top of a frozen base IL policy, using few demonstrations plus brief online correction, over collecting 5x more demonstrations for pure imitation learning
claims.conditions: 5 contact-rich manipulation tasks (high-precision and long-horizon), 20 initial demos, 10 minutes of online training

claims.claim: An ablation shows direct residual supervision (learning corrective residual actions on top of the frozen base policy) is critical to performance, while intervention-aware reward shaping substantially improves training efficiency
claims.direction: supports a residual (delta-on-top-of-frozen-policy) action formulation, isolating direct residual supervision as the more critical of two complementary learning signals from human interventions
claims.conditions: same 5-task evaluation, ablation study

title: BiKC+: Bimanual Hierarchical Imitation With Keypose-Conditioned Coordination-Aware Consistency Policies

claims.claim: Formulating the low-level trajectory generator as a consistency model (generating action sequences in a single inference step, conditioned on historical observations and predicted keyposes) rather than a full multi-step diffusion process significantly outperforms baseline methods in success rate and operational efficiency for bimanual manipulation
claims.direction: favors a consistency-model action head (single-step generation) over multi-step diffusion for combining fast inference with multimodal action distribution modeling
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world bimanual manipulation, multi-stage tasks

claims.claim: A high-level keypose predictor generates sub-goals that indicate stage boundaries, and the low-level trajectory generator conditions on these predicted keyposes to structure long-horizon, multi-stage bimanual tasks, improving per-stage reliability and mitigating cascading failures across stages
claims.direction: favors hierarchical (keypose-conditioned) structuring of long-horizon action generation over flat, unstructured chunk prediction for multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: same evaluation, bimanual multi-stage manipulation

title: Deep Sensorimotor Control by Imitating Predictive Models of Human Motion

claims.claim: Training a model to predict future human end-effector keypoint trajectories from current scene+task, then using it as a reward model (combined with a simple sparse task-specific reward) to train sensorimotor policies via massively parallel RL in simulation, circumvents the need for per-scene digital-twin reconstruction (real2sim) and per-task manual reward design when learning from large-scale human video data
claims.direction: favors a unified human-motion-prediction reward model (trained once across diverse human video) over per-task manual reward engineering or per-scene real2sim reconstruction for leveraging human video data at scale
claims.conditions: extended-abstract-level description, simulation-based RL training, qualitative claims, no exact numbers given

title: AssemLM: A Spatial Reasoning Multimodal Large Language Model for Robotic Assembly

claims.claim: Integrating assembly manuals, point clouds, and textual instructions via a specialized point cloud encoder (extracting fine-grained geometric/rotational features) achieves state-of-the-art 6D pose reasoning performance for fine-grained, multi-step assembly, versus VLM approaches relying on coarse 2D perception which struggle with complex 3D geometry
claims.direction: favors explicit point-cloud-based 3D encoding over 2D-only VLM perception for tasks requiring precise geometric/rotational reasoning
claims.conditions: large-scale benchmark (AssemBench, 900K+ samples) + real-robot evaluation, assembly-specific domain

title: Learning Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation from Joint Sensors with Proprioceptive Transformer

claims.claim: A Transformer architecture operating solely on joint position/velocity history (distilled from a privileged teacher policy trained with object-state information), without any vision or tactile input, extracts implicit object-state information from temporal patterns in proprioception, achieving 3.1x higher rotation speed and 23.4% lower object-position RMSE than an MLP baseline on the same proprioception-only input
claims.direction: favors a Transformer (over an MLP) for extracting exteroceptive-like information purely from proprioceptive time-series, when vision/tactile sensing is unavailable or unreliable
claims.conditions: real tendon-driven dexterous hand (ORCA hand), joint-sensing only, teacher-student distillation setup

title: Optimal Transport Q-Learning for Flow Policy Steering and Acceleration

claims.claim: Fine-tuning suboptimal flow-matching policies using the robot's own experience via advantage-weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching (OTQL), with an interaction budget of only 50-60 episodes and without computationally expensive distillation, increases average success from 36% to 86% for single-task policies and from 38% to 76% for a pre-trained VLA
claims.direction: strongly favors RL post-training of flow-matching policies via optimal-transport-guided fine-tuning over relying on imitation learning alone or expensive distillation-based acceleration
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world robot tasks, comparison of pre/post OTQL fine-tuning on both single-task flow policies and a pretrained VLA

claims.claim: The same OTQL fine-tuning reduces the number of inference steps per action generation by 70%, simultaneously improving success rate and cutting inference cost
claims.direction: supports that RL post-training of flow policies can jointly improve both success rate and inference speed, rather than trading one off against the other
claims.conditions: same experimental setup as above

title: VANE: Reliable Test-Time Training for Vision-Language-Action Models via Future Visual Representation Prediction

claims.claim: A test-time training framework that conditions prompt adaptation on the current vision-language context and learns from the FUTURE visual consequences of executed actions (isolating candidate updates from the live policy, evaluating them on subsequent observations, and committing only when supported by future evidence) improves average success by 3.2 percentage points over a corresponding TTT baseline on SimplerEnv WidowX, though gains are task- and embodiment-dependent on Google Robot
claims.direction: favors evidence-gated, future-outcome-verified test-time adaptation over naive online TTT that commits updates before observing their consequences, though the benefit is modest and not universal
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv WidowX + Google Robot sim benchmarks, direct comparison to a TTT baseline

title: Any2Policy: Learning Visuomotor Policy with Any-Modality

claims.claim: A versatile modality network that adapts to diverse input combinations (text-image, audio-image, text-point cloud, or single modalities) and connects to policy networks for control shows promising capability for embodied agents to handle tasks specified via various modality combinations, validated on Franka Kitchen, Maniskill2, and a real-world 30-task dataset
claims.direction: supports training a general any-modality conditioning network (rather than a language-only conditioning module) for broader task-specification flexibility
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real-world, qualitative 'promising capability' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Training Fast Robot Policies with Slow Foundation Models

claims.claim: Visually-Grounded Reward Synthesis (VGRS) uses large foundation models (an LLM to synthesize executable reward code, and a frozen VLM to analyze failed trajectories and diagnose failure modes for reward rewriting) ONLY DURING TRAINING to train a lightweight hierarchical policy; deployment requires only the learned lightweight policy, achieving success rates above 55% on challenging long-horizon sim and real-world navigation/manipulation tasks with no foundation-model inference cost at deployment
claims.direction: favors using expensive foundation models exclusively during training (for reward synthesis and failure diagnosis) while deploying only a small, fast policy, over running the foundation model at every inference step during deployment
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world navigation and manipulation tasks, comparison implied against Language-to-Reward (L2R) methods lacking physical grounding

claims.claim: The deployed policy is a lightweight hierarchical policy, trained via foundation-model-synthesized rewards but requiring no foundation model at deployment time
claims.direction: supports training small, cheap-to-deploy policies using expensive teacher signals (rewards, diagnostics) rather than deploying the large model itself
claims.conditions: same tasks as above

title: GUIDES: Guidance Using Instructor-Distilled Embeddings for Pre-trained Robot Policy Enhancement

claims.claim: A lightweight framework (GUIDES) augments an already-trained, validated pre-trained policy with semantic guidance from foundation models WITHOUT architectural redesign: a fine-tuned VLM ('Instructor') generates contextual instructions encoded into guidance embeddings that are injected into the policy's latent space, requiring only brief, targeted fine-tuning for the legacy model to adapt to this new semantic input
claims.direction: favors non-invasively injecting semantic guidance embeddings into an existing pretrained policy's latent space over replacing/redesigning the policy architecture to add semantic awareness
claims.conditions: RoboCasa simulation across diverse existing policy architectures, plus real-world UR5 deployment

claims.claim: An LLM-based 'Reflector' monitors the Instructor's confidence and, when confidence is low, triggers a reasoning loop (analyzing execution history, retrieving relevant examples, augmenting VLM context) to refine subsequent actions, and real-world UR5 deployment shows enhanced motion precision for critical sub-tasks such as grasping
claims.direction: supports an inference-time, confidence-gated reasoning fallback as a way to improve robustness of an existing policy without retraining it for every new failure mode
claims.conditions: real-world UR5 robot, critical sub-tasks (e.g. grasping), qualitative 'consistent and substantial improvements' claim, no exact numbers given

title: RoboTransfer: Controllable Geometry-Consistent Video Diffusion for Manipulation Policy Transfer

claims.claim: A diffusion-based video generation framework that leverages cross-view feature interactions and globally consistent 3D geometry to synthesize robotic training data (with fine-grained control over background editing and object replacement) produces videos with superior geometric consistency and visual fidelity compared to prior video-generation-based augmentation, while maintaining multi-view consistency
claims.direction: favors geometry-consistent, multi-view-aware generative video augmentation (with explicit background/object editing control) over less geometrically-grounded generative augmentation methods
claims.conditions: comparison against other video-generation augmentation baselines, simulation-derived training data used for sim-to-real

claims.claim: Policies trained on this synthetic (background-edited, object-replaced) data exhibit enhanced generalization to novel, unseen scenarios compared to policies trained without this augmentation
claims.direction: supports geometry-consistent background/object-editing augmentation as a way to improve generalization to novel scenes/objects, directly relevant to lighting/background/object-appearance shift robustness
claims.conditions: qualitative 'enhanced generalization' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Filtering Learning Histories Enhances In-Context Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Reweighting and filtering imitated learning histories based on their improvement/stability characteristics (Learning History Filtering, LHF), rather than imitating a source RL algorithm's complete (possibly suboptimal) learning histories unfiltered, enhances in-context RL performance, with the benefit becoming more pronounced when the source data is noisy
claims.direction: favors filtering/reweighting training data by quality signals (rather than using all available demonstration/learning-history data unfiltered) especially as data noise increases
claims.conditions: in-context RL benchmarks including continuous robotic manipulation tasks, combined with 3 SOTA in-context-RL backbones, this concerns in-context RL data preprocessing rather than standard offline imitation learning

title: Segment, Compare, and Learn: Creating Movement Libraries of Complex Task for Learning from Demonstration

claims.claim: An algorithm using unsupervised heuristic segmentation, Gaussian Mixture Model clustering, and Gaussian Optimal Transport (comparing segment groups via the energy cost of transforming one Gaussian Process into another) automatically generates reusable motion-primitive libraries from demonstrations, without prior task knowledge, validated on real-robot manipulation and shown to compare favorably with state-of-the-art algorithms
claims.direction: favors automatic, unsupervised motion-primitive discovery and grouping (via GP-based optimal transport comparison) over manually engineering separate motion primitives per task
claims.conditions: real robot manipulation tasks, comparison against SOTA algorithms, qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Towards Exploratory and Focused Manipulation with Bimanual Active Perception

claims.claim: A Bimanual Active Perception strategy, using one arm to provide active vision (moving to reduce occlusion) and the other to provide force sensing while manipulating, is verified effective in an imitation-learning manner on a new benchmark (EFM-10) of tasks specifically requiring exploration or focus to gather task-relevant visual information
claims.direction: supports dedicating one arm/camera to active viewpoint control (rather than a purely fixed camera) specifically for tasks where visual occlusion prevents task completion
claims.conditions: new benchmark (bimanual setup required), qualitative 'successfully verify effectiveness' claim, not directly applicable to a single-arm setup

title: Tacmap: Bridging the Tactile Sim-to-Real Gap via Geometry-Consistent Penetration Depth Map

claims.claim: Unifying simulated and real tactile sensing through a shared 'deform map' representation (3D intersection-volume depth maps in simulation, learned mapping from raw tactile images to ground-truth depth maps in the real world) minimizes tactile sim-to-real domain shift while maintaining physical consistency, enabling a policy trained exclusively in simulation to achieve zero-shot transfer to a physical robot on an in-hand rotation task
claims.direction: favors a shared geometric (depth-map) representation to bridge sim-to-real domain gap for a sensing modality (tactile), over training directly on raw, modality-specific simulated signals
claims.conditions: requires vision-based tactile sensors, in-hand rotation task, zero-shot sim-to-real transfer

title: WM-DAgger: Enabling Efficient Data Aggregation for Imitation Learning with World Models

claims.claim: For an eye-in-hand (wrist-camera) robotic arm with only few-shot demonstrations, a World-Model-based data aggregation framework (WM-DAgger) synthesizes out-of-distribution recovery data WITHOUT requiring human involvement, using a Corrective Action Synthesis Module (generating task-oriented recovery actions to avoid misleading supervision) and a Consistency-Guided Filtering Module (discarding physically implausible synthesized trajectories by anchoring to real expert-demonstration frames), achieving a 93.3% success rate in soft bag pushing with only five demonstrations
claims.direction: strongly favors synthesizing recovery/OOD data via a world model (with explicit hallucination-mitigation mechanisms) over collecting more human demonstrations or relying on continuous human-in-the-loop DAgger, specifically for few-shot, wrist-camera setups
claims.conditions: eye-in-hand robotic arm, few-shot (as low as 5) demonstrations, multiple real-world robotic tasks

why_deep_read: Matches our setup unusually closely: an eye-in-hand (wrist camera) arm with a small number of demonstrations, needing recovery/robustness data without extra teleoperation effort; the 93.3% success from just 5 demos via world-model-synthesized recovery data (with explicit anti-hallucination filtering) is directly actionable for augmenting our 50-100 demo dataset with synthesized corrective data rather than collecting more teleop demos.

title: From Abstraction to Instantiation: Learning Behavioral Representation for Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: A causal Mamba-based Visuomotor Behavior Encoder that aggregates long-horizon trajectory information into a single temporally-coherent behavior representation, paired with a Phase-conditioned Behavior Decoder that dynamically aligns task-level priors with real-time execution progress, addresses short-horizon temporal fragmentation and static execution-alignment problems in prior action-centric latent-variable VLA approaches
claims.direction: favors long-horizon, temporally-coherent behavior representations (via a causal state-space/Mamba encoder) over short-horizon action-centric latent variables for robust manipulation under distribution shift
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, CALVIN sim benchmarks plus real-world sim-to-real transfer

claims.claim: In real-world sim-to-real transfer, BehaviorVLA matches the performance of OpenVLA-OFT while using only 50% of the demonstration data, demonstrating superior data efficiency
claims.direction: supports temporally-coherent behavioral representation learning as a way to roughly halve the demonstration count needed to match a strong existing baseline's performance
claims.conditions: real-world sim-to-real transfer, direct comparison against OpenVLA-OFT at matched performance

claims.claim: BehaviorVLA achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 58%, 98%, and 4.36 (average length) on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and CALVIN respectively, indicating robust generalization across varying environments (a proxy for distribution-shift robustness, the central motivation of the paper)
claims.direction: supports temporally-coherent behavior representations as a route to better distribution-shift robustness than prior VLA behavior-representation approaches
claims.conditions: 3 sim benchmarks, SOTA comparison

title: ST-HADP: Spatio-Temporal hierarchical attention diffusion policy for long-horizon generalizable bimanual visuomotor imitation

claims.claim: A Temporal Abstraction Module models action sequences across multiple timescales via hierarchical latent variables (facilitating coarse-to-fine action generation aligned with long-horizon task progression), combined with a Spatial Attention Module learning arm-specific focus over task-relevant 3D regions, consistently outperforms baseline diffusion policies that use flat temporal horizons and globally pooled visual features, with only modest additional computational overhead
claims.direction: favors explicit hierarchical (multi-timescale) temporal structuring plus spatially-focused attention over flat action-chunk horizons and globally-pooled visual features, for long-horizon bimanual coordination
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 platform, 6 dual-arm robot configurations, diverse morphologies and tasks

claims.claim: Using only 50 automatically generated expert demonstrations, ST-HADP consistently outperforms baseline policies under this limited-demonstration setting
