claims.direction: provides a direct data point that spatial+temporal hierarchical structuring can improve performance specifically under a limited (50-demo) demonstration budget matching our own target range
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0, 50 automatically generated demonstrations, dual-arm setting

claims.claim: The framework explicitly extends 3D diffusion policies (rather than 2D image-based diffusion policies) with spatial and temporal structuring
claims.direction: supports building hierarchical structuring on top of a 3D (point-cloud/geometry-aware) diffusion policy base rather than a 2D-image-only base
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0, 3D diffusion policy base

title: M2RL: A Multimodal Multi-Interface Dataset for Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Evaluation of SOTA imitation learning algorithms on the M2RL dataset showed clear performance improvements when training on data from diverse teleoperation interfaces and utilizing inputs from multiple camera streams (wrist + two exo-views)
claims.direction: favors multi-view/multi-camera inputs and multi-interface demo data over single-view/single-interface
claims.conditions: human teleop demos, non-expert users, 3 camera perspectives (wrist + 2 exo), 4 task categories, 3 teleoperation interfaces

claims.claim: Multimodal, multi-interface demonstration data improves robustness of learned policies compared to single-modality/single-interface data
claims.direction: favors diversity of demonstration collection interfaces/modalities over raw count alone
claims.conditions: dataset paper, non-expert demonstrators

title: ContextVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Amortized Multi-Frame Context

claims.claim: Prior behavior-cloning work showed inconsistent performance gains from multi-frame observations, but VLA models (built on VLMs) more effectively utilize multi-frame context; ContextVLA compresses past observations into a single context token and consistently improves over single-frame VLAs, achieving benefits of full multi-frame training with reduced training/inference time
claims.direction: favors compressed observation-history conditioning over both pure single-frame and naive full multi-frame VLA training
claims.conditions: VLA policy models; real/sim setting not specified in abstract

title: PlayWorld: Learning Robot World Models from Autonomous Play

claims.claim: A video world model trained fully from autonomous robot self-play (no human demos) generates physically consistent predictions for contact-rich interactions not captured by world models trained on human-collected data, and enables fine-grained failure prediction and policy evaluation with up to 40% improvement over human-data world models; using the world model for RL improved real-world policy success rate by 65%
claims.direction: favors self-play-collected data and world-model auxiliary training/evaluation over human-demo-only world models
claims.conditions: real-world robot deployment, autonomous self-play data collection, diverse manipulation tasks

title: Robotic Manipulation is Vision-to-Geometry Mapping (f(v) -> G): Vision-Geometry Backbones over Language and Video Models

claims.claim: Replacing conventional vision-language or video-predictive backbones with a pretrained 3D world model backbone (Vision-Geometry-Action, VGA) outperforms leading VLA, 3D-VLA and WAM baselines including pi_0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, GeoVLA, and Motus across simulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors 3D/geometry-pretrained vision backbones over 2D vision-language or video-pretrained backbones for action generation
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks, comparison against multiple strong VLA baselines

claims.claim: Jointly training action and 3D property prediction (via Progressive Volumetric Modulation) preserves geometric representations and improves manipulation performance versus backbones without explicit 3D/geometric conditioning
claims.direction: favors 3D/geometric representation learning auxiliary objective over pure RGB/2D semantic representations
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world deployment

claims.claim: In real-world deployments, VGA surpasses pi_0.5 under unseen viewpoints and accurately follows language instructions for target grasping
claims.direction: favors 3D-grounded representations for robustness to camera viewpoint shift
claims.conditions: real-world robot deployment, unseen viewpoint generalization test, language-conditioned grasping

why_deep_read: Abstract claims a controlled real-world comparison against pi_0.5/OpenVLA-OFT under viewpoint shift, directly relevant to our camera-shift robustness failure and vision-encoder choice (Q03/Q04); full text ablations on the 3D backbone vs 2D backbone would clarify how much of the gain is architecture vs data scale.

title: Real-Time Mask-Conditioned Surgical Grasping via Action Chunking Transformers

claims.claim: An Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) policy trained on synchronized RGB images, SAM+XMem-generated masks, robot states, and actions was evaluated on a Needle Pick task in simulation and real world
claims.direction: uses ACT-style chunking as base policy with added mask conditioning
claims.conditions: real + sim (SurRoL), teleoperated demonstrations, surgical grasping

claims.claim: Using RGB images and segmentation masks as dual visual streams helps the policy separate appearance from task-relevant spatial cues, consistently improving task success and robustness to occlusion versus RGB-only input
claims.direction: favors mask/segmentation-conditioned input for robustness to occlusion/appearance changes over RGB-only
claims.conditions: real + sim surgical grasping, minimal user input for mask generation

title: You've Got a Golden Ticket: Improving Generative Robot Policies With A Single Noise Vector

claims.claim: Replacing random Gaussian initial noise with a single well-chosen constant 'golden ticket' noise vector (found via Monte-Carlo search, no retraining) improved a frozen pretrained diffusion/flow-matching policy's success rate in 46 of 51 simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, by up to 55% absolute in some simulated tasks and 28% within 60 search episodes in real-world tasks; a single noise vector also improved average multi-task VLA performance across 7 tasks by 14%
claims.direction: shows diffusion/flow-matching action heads have exploitable sensitivity to initial noise choice; a cheap inference-time search can substantially boost their performance without retraining
claims.conditions: frozen pretrained diffusion/flow-matching policies and VLAs, sim + real-world benchmarks

title: Selective Perception for Robot: Task-Aware Attention in Multimodal VLA

claims.claim: A lightweight adaptive routing module analyzes the text prompt and wrist-camera observations to predict task-relevance of multiple camera views in real time, attenuating computation for low-utility views and passing only essential visual features to the policy network
claims.direction: favors dynamic, task-aware weighting/selection of multi-camera inputs over static uniform fusion of all views
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation, multi-view VLA, wrist camera used as relevance signal

claims.claim: Real-world experiments show the dynamic information fusion approach achieves significant improvements in both inference efficiency and control performance compared to existing VLA models, with computation cost scaling with task relevance rather than being fixed
claims.direction: favors conditional/selective computation for reducing inference latency in real-time VLA control
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation, resource-constrained real-time control

why_deep_read: Abstract directly targets our two active problems (2s inference latency and multi-camera fusion for a fixed scene+wrist camera setup) with real-world efficiency numbers; full text would give the actual latency/success trade-off numbers needed to judge if this generalizes to an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Depth-augmented diffusion policy with pseudo-depth for robust robotic manipulation

claims.claim: On a real-world distance-sensitive manipulation task (closing a toilet-seat lid), a depth-augmented diffusion policy achieved 95% success with sensor depth and 90% with pseudo-depth (from a pretrained monocular estimator), versus 50% for an RGB-only diffusion-policy baseline and 75% for 3D Diffusion Policy
claims.direction: strongly favors adding depth (real or estimated) over RGB-only for tasks requiring precise distance-aware motion
claims.conditions: real robot (Somatic Jinx), single real-world task, additional LIBERO sim benchmark with modest consistent gains

claims.claim: Method is built on Diffusion Policy as the action head, comparing against a 3D Diffusion Policy baseline
claims.direction: diffusion policy as base action head, augmented rather than replaced
claims.conditions: real robot + LIBERO sim

claims.claim: Pseudo-depth generated by the pretrained Depth Anything V2 monocular estimator can substitute for real hardware depth sensing with only a small performance drop (90% vs 95% success), removing dependence on an RGB-D camera
claims.direction: favors using a pretrained monocular depth estimator when hardware depth is unavailable or noisy
claims.conditions: real robot, comparison of sensor depth vs pretrained pseudo-depth vs RGB-only

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q04 depth-vs-RGB question with concrete real-robot success-rate numbers (50/75/90/95%) using a RealSense-like depth-capable setup close to ours; full text would show whether pseudo-depth-from-RGB could let us skip depth hardware entirely, and give the fusion mechanism (stochastic feature addition + modality dropout) we could reuse.

title: FARM: Reading Failure Signals from the Internal Predictive States of a Frozen Robotic World Model

claims.claim: A small (33,985-parameter) supervised readout trained on the frozen internal predictive states of a pretrained VLA-JEPA world model detects step-wise failure with 85.68/88.59 pooled AUROC/AUPRC across seven tasks, and transfers with fixed or lightly-adapted readouts across real-robot platforms including PIPER X, SO-101, and Franka, adding only 0.2256 ms latency
claims.direction: supports reusing frozen world-model predictive states as auxiliary features (for failure monitoring) rather than training dedicated monitoring components from scratch
claims.conditions: real robot, includes SO-101 arm explicitly, frozen pretrained world model, negligible added latency

title: ARMADA: Augmented Reality for Robot Manipulation and Robot-Free Data Acquisition

claims.claim: A user study with 15 participants across 3 tasks under 3 feedback conditions found that providing live virtual-robot feedback during barehanded (robot-free) demonstration collection dramatically improved the quality of collected data, verified by replaying trajectories on physical robot hardware
claims.direction: favors real-time embodiment feedback during demo collection for improving demonstration quality even without a physical robot present
claims.conditions: human demonstrations via AR (Apple Vision Pro), no physical robot during collection, 3 manipulation tasks, 15 participants

title: Imitation Learning with Limited Actions via Diffusion Planners and Deep Koopman Controllers

claims.claim: A plan-then-control framework using a Deep Koopman Operator to learn latent action representations from observation-only (action-unlabeled) trajectories, decoded via a linear action decoder, significantly enhances action-data efficiency and achieves high task success with limited action-labeled data
claims.direction: favors leveraging observation-only demonstrations plus minimal action-labeled data over requiring full action labels on all demos
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation tasks + real robot experiment, multi-modal expert demonstrations

claims.claim: Diffusion-based planners combined with a Koopman-based inverse dynamics controller were used to imitate multi-modal human behaviors
claims.direction: diffusion planner used as generative action/plan representation to capture multimodality
claims.conditions: sim + real robot

title: Vidar: Embodied Video Diffusion Model for Generalist Manipulation

claims.claim: With only 20 minutes of human demonstrations on an unseen robot (1% of typical data), Vidar (an embodied video diffusion prior + masked inverse dynamics adapter) outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and generalizes to unseen tasks, backgrounds, and camera layouts
claims.direction: favors large-scale video-diffusion pretraining + minimal on-robot demo alignment over collecting large per-embodiment demonstration sets
claims.conditions: real-world robots, embodied pretraining on 750K multi-view trajectories from 3 real robot platforms, then 20 min demos on a new unseen robot

claims.claim: End-to-end pixel-to-action pipelines may degenerate under background and viewpoint shifts, whereas Vidar's video-diffusion prior with a masked inverse dynamics model generalizes to unseen tasks, backgrounds, and camera layouts
claims.direction: favors internet/video-pretrained generalizable priors for robustness to background/camera-layout shift over raw end-to-end pixel-to-action policies
claims.conditions: real-world robots, unseen embodiment, background and camera layout generalization tests

claims.claim: The masked inverse dynamics model (MIDM) learns action-relevant pixel masks without dense labels, grounding the video-diffusion prior into the target embodiment's action space while suppressing distractors
claims.direction: favors an internet-scale pretrained video diffusion vision backbone adapted via a lightweight learned mask/adapter over training a vision encoder per-embodiment from scratch
claims.conditions: real-world robots, cross-embodiment adaptation

why_deep_read: Directly targets our two hardest problems at once -- very low demo count (20 min on a new robot) and robustness to background/camera-layout shift -- with real multi-platform robot results; full text would clarify the compute/model-size cost of the video-diffusion prior, which matters given our 8GB laptop GPU constraint.

title: Imagine2Act: Leveraging Object-Action Motion Consistency from Imagined Goals for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A 3D imitation-learning policy that conditions on imagined goal point clouds and enforces object-action motion consistency (soft pose supervision aligning predicted end-effector motion with predicted object transformation) outperforms previous state-of-the-art policies in both simulation and the real world on relational object rearrangement tasks
claims.direction: favors coupling action prediction with explicit object-transformation/geometric consistency objectives over generating goal images alone or predicting actions from raw demonstrations
claims.conditions: real world + simulation, precision object rearrangement tasks

title: ObjectVLA: End-to-End Open-World Object Manipulation Without Demonstration

claims.claim: ObjectVLA, evaluated on a real robotic platform, generalizes learned pick/hand-over skills to 100 novel objects not seen during training with a 64% success rate in selecting the correct object, without requiring explicit human demonstrations for each new object
claims.direction: favors injecting object generalization via vision-language pair data (not per-object demos) for handling novel-looking objects at test time
claims.conditions: real robot, VLA model, 100 novel objects, language-conditioned object selection/manipulation

claims.claim: Object generalization is achieved by leveraging vision-language pair data to establish an implicit link between the object referred to in language and the desired action, including a lightweight fine-tuning method using only a few smartphone-captured images per new object
claims.direction: favors language/vision-language grounding as the mechanism for novel-object generalization, with cheap smartphone-image fine-tuning as an accessible adaptation route
claims.conditions: real robot, VLA, low-cost per-object adaptation (smartphone photos, no teleop demos needed)

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our 'different-looking pumpkin' novel-object generalization failure with a real-robot, quantified (64% on 100 objects) result and a cheap smartphone-photo adaptation recipe that could be practically reused for our second-object task.

title: Action-Effect Memory Pretraining for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: AEM pretrains a compact temporal representation (Mamba-encoded single-vector history bottleneck) from interleaved vision-action history via masked modeling, and ablations show history-aware pretraining surpasses both single-frame pretraining and direct frame stacking on manipulation performance, including on non-Markovian tasks
claims.direction: favors learned compact history representations over both single-frame observations and naive frame-stacking for handling partial observability
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, evaluated with both Diffusion Policy and Flow Policy action heads, clean/cluttered/random scenes

claims.claim: The single-vector temporal bottleneck design keeps inference efficient, reducing inference latency and computational cost compared to alternative history-encoding baselines
claims.direction: favors compact bottlenecked history representations for lower inference latency
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, real-time control setting

claims.claim: AEM was evaluated as a pretraining/representation add-on to both Diffusion Policy and Flow Policy action heads and consistently improved both
claims.direction: history-aware pretraining is action-head-agnostic, benefiting diffusion and flow-matching heads alike
claims.conditions: sim + real, two action-head types tested

why_deep_read: Abstract reports a direct ablation of history representation vs. single-frame vs. frame-stacking with both latency and success-rate effects on diffusion/flow policies -- this is precisely our Q07/Q10 tradeoff (observation memory vs. jerky/slow inference); full tables would give concrete numbers for our chunk-boundary smoothness and latency budget.

title: ICLR: In-Context Imitation Learning with Visual Reasoning

claims.claim: In-context imitation learning enables adaptation to new tasks from a small number of demonstrations without additional training; augmenting demonstration prompts with visual reasoning traces (anticipated future trajectories in image space) gave consistent improvements in success rate and generalization to unseen tasks/object configurations versus other in-context IL methods
claims.direction: favors adding explicit visual-reasoning/intent traces to in-context demonstration conditioning over state-action-only conditioning, for few-shot adaptation
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation, small number of demonstrations, no additional training/fine-tuning

claims.claim: A unified autoregressive transformer jointly generates reasoning traces and low-level actions
claims.direction: single autoregressive-token action head jointly modeling reasoning and actions
claims.conditions: sim + real

title: KAI: A Kinematic-Aware Interface for Data-Efficient Articulated Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Embedding interpretable kinematic/geometric priors as a structured intermediate representation (KAI) achieves an average 82.9% success rate across six simulation tasks, matching or surpassing baseline performance while using only half the demonstration data
claims.direction: favors structured kinematic/geometric intermediate representations as inductive bias for improving sample efficiency over raw end-to-end policies trained on more demos
claims.conditions: 6 simulation tasks, half the demo count vs baseline

claims.claim: KAI exhibits robust generalization to unseen backgrounds and visual distractors, transferring from a single clean training environment to cluttered real-world scenes, and with co-training on human interaction videos achieves over 70% average success rate under diverse visual distractions
claims.direction: favors action-agnostic structured representations plus human-video co-training for robustness to background/distractor shift
claims.conditions: trained in a single clean sim/real environment, tested on cluttered real-world scenes with distractors

why_deep_read: Reports a direct half-the-data ablation (82.9% success with 50% of demos) plus clean-to-cluttered background/distractor generalization -- both core to our low-demo-count and lighting/background robustness questions; full text would show whether the kinematic-prior approach is applicable to a simple rigid-object pick-place task like ours or only articulated objects.

title: SID: Sliding into Distribution for Robust Few-Demonstration Manipulation

claims.claim: Across six real-world tasks, SID achieves approximately 90% success under out-of-distribution (OOD) initializations using only two demonstrations
claims.direction: favors structured object-centric motion-field correction over pure end-to-end visuomotor policies for making few-demonstration policies robust
claims.conditions: real-world, only 2 demonstrations, 6 tasks

claims.claim: An object-centric motion field learned from canonicalized demonstrations iteratively slides the system toward the demonstrated manifold under substantial pose and viewpoint shifts, with under a 10% success drop under distractors and external disturbances
claims.direction: favors explicit distribution-shift-correction mechanisms (rather than relying on policy generalization alone) for robustness to pose/viewpoint shift and distractors
claims.conditions: real-world, 6 tasks, OOD initial poses/viewpoints, distractors and disturbances tested

claims.claim: Kinematically consistent point-cloud reprojection augmentation preserves action-observation consistency for the egocentric conditioned-flow-matching execution policy
claims.direction: favors geometry-consistent point-cloud reprojection as an augmentation strategy over generic image augmentation
claims.conditions: real-world, flow-matching policy, point-cloud observations

why_deep_read: Abstract gives concrete real-robot numbers (~90% success with only 2 demos, <10% drop under distractors) that speak directly to both our few-demo (50-100) and robustness-to-shift (camera moved, distractors) priorities; full text ablation of the motion-field-recovery mechanism vs a plain policy would clarify how much of the gain is the recovery mechanism vs the flow-matching head.

title: CoRE-VLA: Towards Scalable and Robust Vision-Language-Action Modeling via Conditional Routing of Experts

claims.claim: CoRE-VLA gates modality-specialized experts by sensor availability (focusing on depth as the representative auxiliary modality), enabling graceful degradation under missing sensors without retraining; experiments on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, and real-world dual-arm manipulation show it outperforms a dense-action-generator ablation and a strong pretrained VLA baseline, and it exploits auxiliary depth when available while remaining robust when depth is unavailable at deployment
claims.direction: favors a sparse, sensor-gated expert architecture that can optionally exploit depth over a policy that hard-requires a fixed sensor set
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboCasa) + real-world dual-arm manipulation, comparison vs dense-action-generator and pretrained VLA baseline

claims.claim: Existing VLA policies couple action generation to a fixed sensor set, making them brittle when sensors are missing; task-intent-based routing to task-relevant experts improved specialization across diverse tasks and long-horizon subgoals
claims.direction: favors conditional/sparse computation over shared dense fusion of all camera/sensor inputs for robustness to sensor variability
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, multi-task and long-horizon benchmarks

title: Fast and Accurate: An Adaptive VLA Inference Framework through Environment-aware Model Selection

claims.claim: Environment-aware Model Selection (EMS) uses a fully decoupled dual-system architecture (large deliberative planner + lightweight reactive controller) with an RL-based switching policy that dynamically chooses which system to invoke; on LIBERO, EMS matches the large-scale baseline's success rate while increasing effective action frequency to 93.4 Hz, and in real-world dual-arm manipulation it accelerates task completion while maintaining robust performance
claims.direction: favors a decoupled fast/slow dual-system with adaptive switching over a single monolithic VLA or a tightly-coupled dual-process architecture, for reducing inference latency while preserving success rate
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO) + real-world dual-arm manipulation

title: Towards Effective Utilization of Mixed-Quality Demonstrations in Robotic Manipulation via Segment-Level Selection and Optimization

title: Memory-Efficient Policy Libraries with Low-Rank Adaptation in Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: LoRA fine-tuning of a baseline PPO policy for multi-task robotics reduced memory usage by a factor of 20-160 compared to full fine-tuning (90-95% storage saving for a library of 10-50 specialized policies), with no significant difference in success rate between full fine-tuning and LoRA fine-tuning on the selected tasks

title: Ordered Action Tokens for Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Ordered Action Tokenization (OAT) discretizes action chunks into an ordered token sequence (via transformer with registers + finite scalar quantization) satisfying high compression, total decodability, and ordering, so that early tokens carry coarse control and later tokens refine detail; across three policy backbones and 60+ tasks (five sim benchmarks + real-world settings), OAT consistently delivers strong policy performance versus existing discrete/analytical/learned-latent action tokenizers

title: TLA: Tactile-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation

title: AhaRobot: A Low-Cost Open-Source Bimanual Mobile Manipulator for Embodied AI

title: Learning Dual-Arm Coordination for Grasping Large Flat Objects

claims.direction: supports zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and generalization to novel/unseen objects when using a pretrained grasp-pose-detection feature backbone

title: From Watch to Imagine: Steering Long-horizon Manipulation via Human Demonstration and Future Envisionment

title: Rethinking the Practicality of Vision-language-action Model: A Comprehensive Benchmark and An Improved Baseline

claims.claim: LLaVA-VLA, a lightweight VLA integrating a compact VLM backbone, was designed specifically for practical deployment on consumer-grade GPUs, avoiding the excessive parameter scales and prohibitive pre-training requirements of existing VLAs, while a two-stage post-training + fine-tuning paradigm eliminates reliance on costly large-scale pre-training

title: VLA Grounder: Language-Conditioning Space Optimization for Black-Box VLA Models

claims.claim: Optimizing the phrasing of the language instruction fed to a frozen VLA policy (via RL over a 'language-conditioning space' initialized from failure-derived priors) improves success on instruction-sensitive, symbolic, and multi-object manipulation tasks without updating any action-policy weights
claims.direction: shows frozen VLA behavior is highly sensitive to instruction phrasing, and that phrasing/prompt optimization is a viable lever distinct from action-weight fine-tuning
claims.conditions: RL4VLA and VL-Think benchmarks (real/sim not specified in abstract), frozen downstream VLA

title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies

claims.claim: An auxiliary loss (Latent Semantic Scaffolding, LSS) applied only during human-demonstration pretraining aligns VLA action-token representations to text embeddings of physical-reasoning rationales via a small projection head that is dropped at inference; aligning each action token to its own manipulation-phase rationale (Dense LSS) rather than one pooled episode-level embedding (Pooled LSS) gives markedly better transfer to held-out tasks, with Dense LSS attaining both best in-distribution success and best transfer, while pooled alignment over-specializes
claims.direction: favors phase-local (dense) auxiliary reasoning-alignment objectives over episode-level pooled objectives, and over paying reasoning cost at inference time
claims.conditions: VLA models, human-demonstration pretraining, held-out task transfer evaluation (real/sim not specified)

claims.claim: The reasoning-alignment auxiliary head is dropped before deployment, leaving the unmodified base policy with zero added inference cost
claims.direction: favors training-time-only auxiliary objectives (no inference-time reasoning tokens or rollouts) to get causal-reasoning benefits without any added latency
claims.conditions: VLA models, deployment/inference-time cost consideration

why_deep_read: This is exactly the kind of auxiliary objective we need given our hard 2s-latency constraint: it claims the benefits of reasoning/world-model-style objectives with zero added inference cost, and gives a specific mechanism (dense per-phase alignment) that would be useful to replicate; full text ablation of dense vs pooled would clarify how much of the gain depends on having phase labels.

title: WHALE: Towards Generalizable and Scalable World Models for Embodied Decision-making

claims.claim: Behavior-conditioning and retracing-rollout techniques improve world-model generalization to OOD regions and enable uncertainty estimation without model ensembles, universal across neural architectures for world model learning
claims.direction: favors these two generalization/uncertainty techniques as auxiliary components for world models used in embodied decision-making
claims.conditions: simulation tasks (value estimation accuracy, video generation fidelity) plus real-world manipulation evaluation

claims.direction: favors large-scale cross-embodiment world-model pretraining to reduce the number of task-specific demonstrations needed
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, minimal task-specific demonstrations, 414M parameter model pretrained on Open X-Embodiment

claims.direction: reports a concrete parameter count for a world model shown to generalize well, though this is larger than what would fit comfortably alongside a policy on an 8GB GPU

title: RoboMatrix: A Skill-centric Hierarchical Framework for Scalable Robot Task Planning and Execution in Open-World

claims.claim: RoboMatrix, a skill-centric hierarchical framework that extracts general meta-skills for composition rather than requiring end-to-end task-specific data, achieves a 50% higher success rate than task-centric baselines when applied to unseen objects, scenes, and tasks
claims.direction: favors skill-centric/hierarchical composition over task-centric end-to-end data collection for generalizing to unseen objects/scenes/tasks
claims.conditions: open-world robot tasks, comparison vs task-centric baselines

title: ManiDP: Manipulability-Aware Diffusion Policy for Posture-Dependent Bimanual Manipulation

title: Cosmos-H-Surgical: Learning Surgical Robot Policies from Videos via World Modeling

claims.direction: favors augmenting/replacing real action-labeled demonstrations with world-model-generated synthetic paired video-action data when unlabeled video is abundant but action-labeled data is scarce

claims.claim: A generative world model (Cosmos-H-Surgical) trained on curated action-description data can generate diverse, generalizable, realistic task videos used to produce synthetic action-labeled data via inverse dynamics
claims.direction: favors world models as a data-generation/auxiliary tool for producing action-labeled training data cheaply
claims.conditions: real surgical robot, surgical domain

title: Hierarchical Equivariant Policy via Frame Transfer

claims.claim: A hierarchical policy that uses the high-level agent's output as a coordinate frame for the low-level agent (frame transfer interface) and integrates domain symmetries/equivariance at both levels achieves state-of-the-art performance with significant improvements in both simulation and real-world settings, addressing the need for extensive demonstrations in hierarchical methods that ignore domain symmetry
claims.direction: favors building domain-symmetry/equivariance into the hierarchical policy interface to reduce the demonstration count needed for robust performance
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation, hierarchical high/low-level policy

title: MemER: Scaling Up Memory for Robot Control via Experience Retrieval

claims.claim: Naively conditioning on long observation histories is computationally expensive and brittle under covariate shift, while indiscriminate history subsampling loses relevant information; a hierarchical policy where a high-level VLA (finetuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct) selects and tracks relevant past keyframes, then issues text instructions to a low-level VLA (finetuned pi_0.5), outperforms prior methods on three real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring minutes of memory

title: Latent MeanFlow Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning

title: Bimanual Tactile-Augmented Teleoperation for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation: A Pilot Evaluation

title: Atomic Motion Coordinate for Language-Steerable and Force-Responsive Manipulation

claims.direction: favors explicit geometry-grounded language-to-motion coordinate injection over standard (implicit) language conditioning for making VLA behavior reliably steerable by instruction
claims.conditions: 7,520 offline horizon interventions, real-robot validation, single and dual-arm settings

title: BAKU: An Efficient Transformer for Multi-Task Policy Learning

title: GIFT: Generalizing Intent for Flexible Test-Time Rewards

claims.claim: GIFT grounds reward generalization in LLM-inferred human intent (contrasting preferred vs non-preferred behaviors) rather than surface visual/semantic similarity, and at deployment maps novel test states to behaviorally-equivalent training states; across four simulated tabletop manipulation tasks with over 50 unseen objects, GIFT consistently outperforms visual and semantic similarity baselines in test-time win rate and state-alignment F1, and reliably transfers to a real 7-DoF Franka Panda robot

claims.conditions: simulated tabletop manipulation with 50+ unseen objects, real-world 7-DoF Franka Panda validation

title: LiLo-VLA: Compositional Long-Horizon Manipulation via Linked Object-Centric Policies

claims.claim: LiLo-VLA decouples transport (a Reaching Module for global motion) from interaction (an object-centric VLA Interaction Module processing only isolated objects of interest); on a 21-task simulation benchmark (LIBERO-Long++ and Ultra-Long) it achieves a 69% average success rate, outperforming Pi0.5 by 41% and OpenVLA-OFT by 67%
claims.direction: favors a modular, object-centric decomposition (separating navigation/reaching from object interaction) over monolithic end-to-end VLA architectures like pi0.5/OpenVLA-OFT for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation (21-task benchmark), comparison vs pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT baselines

claims.claim: Object-centric processing of isolated objects ensures robustness against irrelevant visual features and invariance to spatial configurations; real-world evaluations across 8 long-horizon tasks demonstrate an average success rate of 85%, and modularity enables failure recovery via dynamic replanning and skill reuse, mitigating cascading errors seen in end-to-end approaches
claims.direction: favors object-centric visual processing plus modular failure recovery for robustness to irrelevant background features and cascading-error avoidance
claims.conditions: real-world, 8 long-horizon tasks, zero-shot generalization to novel task compositions not trained on

why_deep_read: Reports a direct, large-margin comparison against pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT (models in the same family as our SmolVLA baseline) with both sim and real-world numbers; the object-centric modularity claim (robustness to irrelevant visual features/background) speaks directly to our lighting/background/camera-shift failures, so the mechanism is worth reading in detail.

title: LangForce: Bayesian Decomposition of Vision Language Action Models via Latent Action Queries

claims.claim: In goal-driven demonstration datasets, language instructions become highly predictable from visual observations alone, causing conditional mutual information between instructions and actions to vanish ('Information Collapse'); this makes VLA models degenerate into vision-only policies that ignore language and fail out-of-distribution. LangForce, which estimates a vision-only prior and a language-conditioned posterior via learnable Latent Action Queries and maximizes pointwise mutual information between actions and instructions, significantly improves generalization without new data, including an 11.3% improvement on the challenging OOD SimplerEnv benchmark
claims.direction: identifies a specific failure mode (language conditioning becoming a vision shortcut / being ignored) common in standard VLA training, and shows a Bayesian-decomposition training objective (not new data) fixes it and improves OOD generalization
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv and RoboCasa benchmarks (sim), no new demonstration data required, applied on top of existing VLA training pipelines

why_deep_read: Directly diagnoses why naive language conditioning can fail to actually influence the policy (a plausible contributor to our own generalization failures if we add language for a second object) and proposes a training-only fix requiring no extra data; worth reading to see if it's applicable to a small VLA like ours on a single-camera-pair setup.

title: Learning Diverse Skills for Behavior Models with Mixture of Experts

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained Di-BM on novel tasks exhibits superior data efficiency and reuse of expert-learned knowledge compared to baselines
claims.direction: favors MoE-based pretraining for better data-efficient transfer to new tasks
claims.conditions: real-world, novel-task fine-tuning

title: AffordTrajDP: Dynamic Affordance-Guided Visuomotor Policy Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.direction: favors dynamic, object-pose-propagated affordance guidance (using RGB-D/geometric object pose) over static affordance/fixed contact-point approaches
claims.conditions: simulation (ManiSkill3) + real-world (Galaxea A1 and UR7e arms), 6 real tasks including insertion and pick-place

claims.claim: Real-world experiments across 6 tasks validate robustness under object placement variations and appearance changes, with both seen and unseen object instances evaluated; ablations confirm the contribution of each proposed component

claims.conditions: real-world, object placement variation and appearance-change tests, seen/unseen object instances, component-wise ablation

why_deep_read: Directly reports real-robot robustness to object placement variation and appearance changes (matching our lighting/pumpkin-appearance shift concerns) with component-wise ablations; worth reading to see which specific component (affordance propagation vs RGB-D input vs other) drives the robustness gain.

title: Visual Sim-to-Real Learning for Robotic Insertion under Geometric Variations: Application to Rebar Installation

claims.claim: A privileged state-based RL teacher trained over procedurally generated object geometries is distilled into a multi-view student mapping raw RGB and proprioception to actions under extensive domain randomization; visual sim-to-real transfer depends on appearance randomization and a DAgger mixture strategy -- removing either one sharply lowers success
claims.direction: favors combining domain randomization (appearance) with DAgger-style online distillation for successful zero-shot visual sim-to-real transfer; ablation shows both components are necessary
claims.conditions: sim-trained teacher + student, zero-shot real-world transfer, real factory production parts, controlled ablation of randomization and DAgger components

claims.claim: A student policy pretrained across a diverse set of nominal object designs adapts to a new design with 4-6x fewer distillation samples than one trained from scratch, and outperforms a single-design specialist even on that specialist's own design
claims.direction: favors pretraining across diverse task/object variants to reduce the demonstration/sample count needed for a new but related task
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, geometric design variation, distillation sample-efficiency comparison

claims.claim: The distilled student transfers zero-shot to the real world, seating rebars from a real factory production run in 91.3% of real-robot rollouts, with geometry diversity in training improving zero-shot success on unseen designs for both teacher and student
claims.direction: favors training over diverse geometric variations (not a single nominal design) for robust zero-shot generalization to novel/unseen object geometry variants
claims.conditions: real robot, real factory parts, contact-rich 1.4mm-clearance insertion task, zero-shot sim-to-real

why_deep_read: This is a controlled, real-robot ablation (91.3% success) directly isolating the contributions of appearance domain randomization vs. DAgger-style distillation for sim-to-real robustness -- exactly the kind of evidence needed to decide our Q05 augmentation strategy; also gives a concrete sample-efficiency multiplier (4-6x) for pretraining across design variation relevant to our second-object extension.

title: Hierarchical Hybrid Learning for Long-Horizon Contact-Rich Robotic Assembly

claims.claim: A high-level policy for selecting and parameterizing low-level primitive skills was learned via imitation learning from only a handful of demonstrations, without requiring teleoperation, while low-level skills combine RL and model-based policies; ARCH outperforms baseline methods in terms of success rate and data efficiency
claims.direction: favors a hierarchical modular decomposition (few demos for high-level skill selection, separate primitive skill library) over end-to-end imitation learning requiring large demonstration sets, for data efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation + real robotic manipulation platform, long-horizon contact-rich assembly

claims.claim: ARCH generalizes well to unseen objects
claims.direction: favors the hierarchical primitive-skill approach for generalization to novel objects over end-to-end IL/RL baselines
claims.conditions: simulation + real robot, unseen object generalization test

title: STRAP: Robot Sub-Trajectory Retrieval for Augmented Policy Learning

claims.claim: Retrieval at the sub-trajectory (rather than full-trajectory) granularity, using pretrained vision foundation models and dynamic time warping to retrieve relevant sub-sequences from large offline training corpora, enables significantly improved data utilization, generalization, and robustness versus full-trajectory retrieval or standard multi-task learning; STRAP outperforms both prior retrieval algorithms and multi-task learning methods in simulated and real experiments, and can learn robust control policies with just a handful of real-world demonstrations by leveraging cross-task shared sub-trajectory content
claims.direction: favors sub-trajectory-level retrieval/augmentation from large prior datasets over full-trajectory retrieval or generic multi-task training, especially for boosting policies trained on only a handful of real demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, scales to large offline datasets, handful of real-world target-task demonstrations

why_deep_read: Directly targets our low-demo-count regime (a handful of real demos) via sub-trajectory retrieval augmentation from larger prior data, which could directly extend our ~50-100 demo dataset; full text would clarify what scale/source of prior data is needed for the retrieval to help, and whether it needs cross-task overlap we don't have.

title: VLA-RAIL: A Real-Time Asynchronous Inference Linker for VLA Models and Robots

claims.claim: Existing async-inference VLA deployment methods suffer from jitter, stalling, or pauses in action execution at chunk boundaries, limiting speed and success rate; VLA-RAIL performs model inference and robot motion control asynchronously, using a Trajectory Smoother (polynomial fitting to filter noise/jitter within one action chunk) and a Chunk Fuser (aligning the currently executing trajectory with the newly arrived chunk to ensure position/velocity/acceleration continuity), significantly reducing motion jitter, enhancing execution speed, and improving task success rates on both dynamic simulation tasks and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: directly favors explicit trajectory-smoothing and chunk-fusion mechanisms for async inference over naive chunk-queue replacement, to eliminate jerky motion at chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: simulation (dynamic tasks) + real-world manipulation, asynchronous VLA inference/control setting

claims.claim: The action-chunk fusing mechanism ensures continuity (position, velocity, acceleration) between two successive action chunks during asynchronous execution
claims.direction: favors explicit inter-chunk continuity enforcement as part of the chunking/execution-horizon design, rather than treating chunks as independent
claims.conditions: real-world + sim, async VLA inference

why_deep_read: This paper's stated problem -- 'jitter, stalling, or pauses in robotic action execution' at chunk boundaries under async inference -- is a near-exact restatement of our own reported failure mode (jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries with async inference); the Trajectory Smoother + Chunk Fuser mechanism looks directly applicable and the full method details/ablations should be read closely.

title: CRISP—Compliant ROS2 Controllers for Learning-Based Manipulation Policies and Teleoperation

claims.claim: Learning-based controllers such as diffusion policies and foundation models output low-frequency and discontinuous target states; CRISP provides lightweight compliant Cartesian and joint-space controllers (ROS2) that smoothly track such high-level commands, converting them into joint torques for compliant, contact-rich execution, validated on multiple manipulator platforms
claims.direction: favors adding a compliant low-level Cartesian/joint controller layer between a learned high-level policy and the robot, to smooth out low-frequency/discontinuous policy outputs rather than sending them directly as position targets
claims.conditions: multiple real robot platforms (Franka FR3, UR5, Duatic), integration layer for diffusion policies/foundation models, no comparative success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: The controllers support both Cartesian and joint-space effort/torque-based control, contrasting with position-control-only interfaces
claims.direction: supports torque/effort-based low-level control interfaces (vs. position-only) as the target for learned policy outputs
claims.conditions: real robots with joint effort interface (our Feetech position-control servos would not directly support this)

title: Multi-Length Skills with Priors for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Using a select set of skill lengths (rather than single-length skills or every possible length/options) -- long skills for repetitive/monotonous action sequences and short skills for unique/complex sequences -- via a hierarchical latent variable model with learned length and skill priors, significantly accelerates downstream task learning on complex robotic manipulation tasks versus competitive benchmarks
claims.direction: favors variable/adaptive temporal horizon selection (multi-length skills) over fixed single-length skill/action-chunk horizons
claims.conditions: complex robotic manipulation tasks (real/sim not specified), RL with learned skill priors

title: ManipArena: Comprehensive Real-world Evaluation of Reasoning-Oriented Generalist Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A standardized real-robot evaluation framework (20 tasks, 10,812 expert trajectories, ~188 robot hours) with stratified in-domain, visual-shift, and semantic-OOD trials found that real-robot conclusions about VLA/world-action-model policies depend not only on architecture but also on model provenance, fine-tuning regime, data sampling, and annotation granularity
claims.direction: cautions that architecture comparisons alone (without controlling fine-tuning/data/annotation factors) may not predict real-robot robustness to visual shift or semantic OOD conditions
claims.conditions: real-robot, tabletop + mobile manipulation, 7 tabletop VLA/world-action-model configurations compared, matched physical conditions

title: Scene2Demo: Self-Evolving Embodied Data Generation via Object-Action Graph

claims.claim: Scene2Demo generates simulated scenes, task configurations, and offline robot-learning datasets from a single real-world RGB image and a user query, using an object-action graph with feedback-agent self-evolution to refine failed executions; behavior cloning policies trained on this generated data achieve 96.0% and 92.0% success on two representative tasks, validating that automatically generated synthetic demonstration data can support downstream policy learning
claims.direction: favors generating synthetic training demonstrations automatically from a single real image plus simulation, as a viable substitute/supplement for collecting real teleop demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation-generated data, behavior cloning evaluation, comparison against RoboGen and GenSim2 data-generation baselines

title: One Step Is Enough: Dispersive MeanFlow Policy Optimization

claims.claim: Dispersive MeanFlow Policy Optimization (DMPO) combines MeanFlow (mathematically-derived single-step inference without knowledge distillation), dispersive regularization to prevent representation collapse, and RL fine-tuning to surpass expert demonstrations, achieving competitive or superior performance to multi-step diffusion/flow-matching baselines on RoboMimic manipulation and OpenAI Gym locomotion benchmarks
claims.direction: favors single-step MeanFlow generative action heads over multi-step diffusion/flow-matching policies, without needing separate distillation
claims.conditions: RoboMimic manipulation + locomotion benchmarks (sim), physical deployment on Franka-Emika-Panda

claims.claim: With a lightweight model architecture and the three algorithmic components working together, DMPO exceeds real-time control requirements (>120Hz) with a 5-20x inference speedup over multi-step baselines, reaching hundreds of Hz on high-performance GPUs, validated via physical deployment on a Franka-Emika-Panda robot
claims.direction: strongly favors one-step generative policies for drastically reducing inference latency versus multi-step diffusion/flow-matching, directly addressing real-time control needs
claims.conditions: real robot (Franka-Emika-Panda), high-performance GPU (not stated whether tested on constrained/laptop-class GPU)

why_deep_read: A 5-20x inference speedup with real-robot validation directly targets our ~2s inference latency bottleneck if we use a diffusion/flow-matching action head; full text would clarify whether the speedup holds on lower-end GPUs like our 8GB laptop card, not just 'high-performance GPUs'.

title: Decompose and Reorganize: Planning with Primitives and Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations

claims.claim: DR-LfD decomposes human demonstrations into atomic, contact-relationship-defined skills that are reproduced as visuomotor policies or object-centric primitives within a TAMP-gated system; this transforms the demonstration-data requirement from scaling exponentially with possible skill sequences to scaling only with the number of distinct skill types, each requiring limited data
claims.direction: favors decomposing long-horizon tasks into a library of atomic visuomotor skills (reused/reorganized via TAMP) over end-to-end imitation learning that requires demonstrations of every task/skill-sequence combination
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, comprehensive benchmarking across diverse scenarios

claims.claim: DR-LfD demonstrates strong performance on tasks involving multiple steps, unseen setups, and physical constraints
claims.direction: favors the TAMP-gated atomic-skill decomposition for generalizing to unseen task setups/constraints versus pure end-to-end visuomotor imitation learning (which the abstract states is limited in spatial generalization)
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, unseen setup generalization test

why_deep_read: The claim that demonstration burden shifts from exponential (over skill sequences) to linear (over skill types) is a strong, checkable claim relevant to whether we should decompose our pick-and-place-in-tray task (and future 2nd-object task) into reusable atomic skills rather than training one end-to-end policy per task.

title: Multi-Stage Manipulation with Demonstration-Augmented Reward, Policy, and World Model Learning

claims.claim: DEMO3 exploits the multi-stage structure of long-horizon tasks (multi-stage dense reward learning, bi-phasic training, world model learning within a demonstration-augmented RL framework) to improve data-efficiency by an average of 40% (70% on particularly difficult tasks) compared to state-of-the-art approaches, validated across 16 sparse-reward tasks in four domains using as few as five demonstrations, including challenging humanoid visual control tasks
claims.direction: favors decomposing long-horizon tasks into multi-stage dense rewards plus world-model learning, demonstration-augmented, over standard sparse-reward RL or plain behavior cloning, to reach strong performance with very few (as few as 5) demonstrations
claims.conditions: 16 sparse-reward tasks across 4 domains, visual inputs, as few as 5 demonstrations, includes humanoid visual control

claims.claim: World model learning is incorporated as one of three components (alongside multi-stage reward learning and bi-phasic training) contributing to the data-efficiency gains
claims.direction: supports world-model learning as a beneficial auxiliary component for sample-efficient policy learning from very few demonstrations
claims.conditions: sim, sparse-reward multi-stage manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: A concrete 'as few as five demonstrations' result with 40-70% data-efficiency gains is squarely in our target data regime (50-100 demos, could be even less); full text would clarify how much of the gain depends on having a simulator/RL environment (which we may not have for real-world-only teleop) versus being applicable to pure imitation learning.

title: LACY: A Vision-Language Model-based Language-Action Cycle for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: LACY jointly trains a single VLM on language-to-action (L2A), action-to-language (A2L, explaining observed actions), and language-consistency-verification (L2C) tasks, enabling a self-improving cycle that autonomously generates and filters new training data (targeting low-confidence cases) without additional human labels; on pick-and-place tasks in simulation and the real world, LACY improves task success rates by 56.46% on average and yields more robust language-action grounding
claims.direction: favors bidirectional language-action training (not just one-way language-to-action) plus self-supervised data augmentation/filtering over standard one-way L2A language-conditioned policy training
claims.conditions: pick-and-place tasks, simulation + real world, no additional human labels required for the self-improvement cycle

why_deep_read: A 56% average success-rate improvement from adding bidirectional language-action training plus self-supervised data filtering (no extra human labels) is a large, concrete claim directly relevant to our planned language-conditioned second-object task; worth checking whether the technique needs large-scale VLM backbones incompatible with our compute budget.

title: TIC-VLA: A Think-in-Control Vision-Language-Action Model for Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments

claims.claim: TIC-VLA explicitly models delayed semantic/language reasoning relative to real-time action by conditioning action generation on delayed vision-language semantic states plus explicit latency metadata, and trains with a latency-consistent pipeline that injects reasoning-inference delays during both imitation learning and online RL to match asynchronous deployment; it consistently outperforms prior VLA models while maintaining robust real-time control under multi-second reasoning latency
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling and training for inference latency (rather than assuming synchronous reasoning/control) when a policy must run under multi-second reasoning delays
claims.conditions: simulation (DynaNav) + real robot, navigation domain (not tabletop manipulation), multi-second latency conditions

why_deep_read: Although this is a navigation paper, the core problem (VLA action generation under multi-second reasoning latency) is exactly our ~2s inference latency issue; the latency-consistent training approach (training with injected delays to match deployment) could be directly transferable to our async-inference manipulation setup and deserves a closer read.

title: GazeVLA: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A VLA model pretrained on large-scale egocentric human video (to capture human intention via gaze, which precedes physical action) and then finetuned on only a small set of robot and human data consistently outperforms strong baselines and generalizes better, evaluated under few-shot and robustness benchmarks in simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors pretraining on human (not robot) egocentric data plus gaze-based intention modeling to reduce the amount of robot demonstration data needed
claims.conditions: large-scale egocentric human pretraining, small robot+human finetuning set, sim + real-world, few-shot and robustness evaluation

claims.claim: The model uses a Chain-of-Thought-style auxiliary objective, sequentially predicting gaze-based intention before executing the action, as an auxiliary/intermediate prediction target
claims.direction: favors predicting an intermediate human-intention/gaze representation as an auxiliary objective before action generation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, long-horizon and fine-grained tasks

title: Inductive Generalization for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard robustness evaluation (testing on unstructured domain shifts like lighting, clutter, diverse objects) only measures interpolation on known distributions; a new 'inductive generalization' protocol testing progressively harder, structurally out-of-distribution task variants finds that SoTA Vision-Language-Action models, and policies that appear robust to prior domain shifts (distractors etc.), fail inductive generalization tests
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common practice of treating robustness to lighting/clutter/distractor shifts as evidence of true generalization; shows this is a distinct, unsolved axis orthogonal to data/model scaling
claims.conditions: formal evaluation protocol applicable to any manipulation policy; baselines include SoTA VLA models (real/sim not specified)

why_deep_read: This directly contradicts an assumption implicit in our own robustness testing plan (that surviving lighting/object/camera-shift tests means the policy generalizes); worth reading to understand the inductive-generalization protocol and whether our evaluation should be redesigned around it.

title: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval for Data-Efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval (HSR) decomposes a target task into candidate skill sequences, evaluates plans by semantic plausibility and prior-dataset skill reliability, then retrieves demonstrations via hybrid subtask-level language retrieval plus behavior-feature reranking, followed by a two-stage pretrain/finetune pipeline; on LIBERO and several real-world manipulation tasks, HSR improves average success rate by 10.3% and 21.3% respectively over the strongest baseline
claims.direction: favors subtask/skill-level retrieval (over visual-similarity, state-action, or task-level language retrieval) for data-efficient adaptation of pretrained VLAs to new tasks with limited task-specific demonstrations
claims.conditions: LIBERO (sim) + real-world robot manipulation tasks, pretrained VLA adaptation with limited target-task demos

title: TEMPO: Learning Temporal Context for Dynamic Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: VLA models operating on a single observation suffer from two failures that persist regardless of model scale or inference latency: motion ambiguity (single observation cannot anticipate moving-object dynamics) and state aliasing (visually similar observations at different task points requiring different actions); TEMPO augments a pretrained VLA with a motion summary from a frozen video foundation model (resolves motion ambiguity) and a compact proprioceptive history (resolves state aliasing), requiring no backbone modification and minimal added compute
claims.direction: favors adding lightweight temporal-context signals (motion summary + proprioceptive history) to an existing pretrained VLA over increasing model capacity, for handling dynamic manipulation
claims.conditions: real/sim not specified, four dynamic manipulation tasks, works as an add-on to any pretrained VLA backbone with minimal compute overhead

claims.claim: Across four dynamic manipulation tasks, TEMPO improves Bottle Handover success from 44% to 74% and is the only method tested that solves state aliasing; ablations confirm each temporal signal independently addresses its corresponding failure mode
claims.direction: quantifies a large (44% to 74%) success-rate gain from adding temporal context, with ablations isolating which signal fixes which failure
claims.conditions: four dynamic manipulation tasks, component-wise ablation, released benchmark (TEMPO-Bench, 50k+ annotated frames)

why_deep_read: TEMPO is a lightweight, backbone-agnostic, minimal-compute add-on (motion summary + proprioceptive history) with a concrete before/after number (44% to 74%) and clean per-signal ablations -- directly actionable for our Q07 observation-history decision without the latency cost of larger context windows, which matters given our 2s inference budget.

title: Learning Cross-hand Policies for High-DOF Reaching and Grasping

claims.claim: A two-stage method (gripper-agnostic policy predicting displacements of pre-defined key points on the gripper, plus a gripper-specific adaptation model translating these into joint adjustments) significantly outperforms baseline methods and transfers across different dexterous grippers
claims.direction: favors a gripper-agnostic keypoint-displacement action representation with a separate gripper-specific joint-adaptation layer, over directly predicting joint-space actions tied to one specific gripper morphology
claims.conditions: evaluated across several dexterous grippers and diverse objects (real/sim not specified)

title: DIRIGENt: End-To-End Robotic Imitation of Human Demonstrations Based on a Diffusion Model

claims.claim: An end-to-end diffusion model directly generates robot joint values from RGB images of human demonstrations (no explicit human-robot pose mapping), and this combination (novel paired human-robot dataset, diffusion input limiting redundant joint configurations, end-to-end perception-to-action architecture) outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches for generating joint values from RGB images
claims.direction: favors an end-to-end diffusion-based action head that directly maps RGB images to joint values over approaches requiring explicit human-robot kinematic mapping
claims.conditions: humanoid robot imitation of human demonstrations, RGB image input, joint-value action output

title: SimpleVLA-RL: Scaling VLA Training via Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: SimpleVLA-RL, an RL framework applied to OpenVLA-OFT, achieves SoTA performance on LIBERO and outperforms pi0 on RoboTwin 1.0/2.0, reducing dependence on large-scale human-operated demonstration data and enabling robust generalization to distribution shift, while remarkably surpassing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) in real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors RL fine-tuning of a pretrained VLA (beyond SFT alone) to reduce dependence on large-scale demonstration data and improve generalization to distribution shift
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboTwin) + real-world tasks, applied to OpenVLA-OFT, comparison vs pi0 and vs plain SFT

claims.claim: A novel phenomenon termed 'pushcut' was observed during RL training, where the policy discovers previously unseen action patterns beyond those present in prior training data
claims.direction: suggests RL fine-tuning (vs. pure imitation/SFT) can discover novel useful behaviors not present in the demonstration data
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLA

title: Hybrid Training for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Embodied chain-of-thought (generating thoughts before actions) improves VLA performance but increases inference time because generated outputs grow longer; Hybrid Training (HyT) enables a VLA to learn from thoughts and gain the associated performance benefits while allowing CoT generation to be left out at inference, and by learning to conditionally predict diverse outputs supports flexible inference-time behavior (predict actions directly, generate thoughts, or follow instructions)
claims.direction: favors training-time-only reasoning supervision (learn from CoT but skip it at inference) over always generating chain-of-thought at inference, to get reasoning benefits without paying the latency cost
claims.conditions: simulated benchmarks + real-world experiments, VLA models

claims.claim: Delaying an agent's actions in real-world execution because of long chain-of-thought generation strongly affects usability for tasks requiring long action sequences
claims.direction: identifies inference-time CoT length as a direct usability/latency cost, motivating training-time-only reasoning objectives
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation, long action sequences

title: VLA-AST: Toward Spatially-Precise and Physically-Smooth Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: VLA-AST introduces a Trajectory Smoothing Module (TSM) to ensure temporal consistency across predicted action segments, addressing physical discontinuities arising from discrete action chunking, and significantly outperforms a number of baseline models particularly in spatially intensive tasks
claims.direction: favors an explicit trajectory-smoothing module across action-chunk boundaries over untreated discrete action chunking
claims.conditions: VLA-based framework, comparison vs baseline VLA models (real/sim not specified)

claims.claim: The Spatial Attention Booster (SAB) enhances geometric awareness by adaptively reweighting visual tokens through task-conditioned spatial attention, addressing limited spatial reasoning in existing VLA models
claims.direction: favors task-conditioned spatial reweighting of visual tokens over uniform visual token treatment for precise spatial manipulation
claims.conditions: VLA-based framework

title: Self-Supervised Anchoring of Fingertip Sensing to Proprioception and Proactive Actions for Robot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Naively adding complementary fingertip sensor signals (tactile + proximity) to a policy does not consistently improve performance and can even underperform a vision-only policy, because sparse, phase-dependent sensor signals are difficult to exploit from limited demonstrations
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that adding more sensing modalities always helps; shows naive multimodal fusion can hurt performance relative to vision-only, especially with limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, limited demonstrations, additional tactile/proximity sensors (not depth, but a cautionary finding relevant to any extra-modality fusion decision)

claims.claim: A proprioception-anchored pretraining method (PROPRA) that independently aligns each extra sensor's history with proprioceptive and action segments recovers the benefit of the extra modality, improving success rate over both vision-only and naive image-anchored pretraining baselines
claims.direction: favors an explicit auxiliary alignment/pretraining objective (linking extra sensor history to proprioception/action) rather than naive concatenation, when incorporating sparse extra sensing signals
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, limited demonstrations

title: WARP: Whole-Body Retargeting for Learning from Offline Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: WARP explicitly models embodiment differences using a closed-form geometric solver to extract precise, unique whole-body actions from offline human pose demonstrations, achieving the first zero-shot whole-body mobile manipulation directly from offline human demonstrations, eliminating the need for human-in-the-loop teleoperation to collect action data
claims.direction: favors retargeting from offline human demonstration data (avoiding teleoperation entirely) when embodiment gaps can be explicitly modeled with a geometric solver
claims.conditions: whole-body mobile manipulation (humanoid, different embodiment from our simple 6-DoF arm), offline human pose data, open-loop real-world replay evaluation

title: CoRAL: Contact-Rich Adaptive LLM-based Control for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: CoRAL uses LLMs not as direct action policies but as cost-function designers for a sampling-based motion planner (MPPI), combined with online system identification and a retrieval-based memory of successful strategies; this modular reasoning-planner architecture outperforms state-of-the-art VLA and foundation-model-based planner baselines by boosting success rates over 50% on average in unseen contact-rich scenarios
claims.direction: favors decoupling high-level LLM/VLM reasoning (as cost/objective design) from low-level reactive sampling-based control, over an end-to-end learned VLA policy, for contact-rich generalization to unseen tasks
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world hardware, novel contact-rich tasks, comparison vs VLA and foundation-model planner baselines

title: What to Ignore, What to React: Visually Robust RL Fine-Tuning of VLA Models

claims.claim: PAIR-VLA adds two auxiliary objectives over paired visual variants during PPO RL fine-tuning: an invariance term reducing action-distribution discrepancy for task-preserving visual pairs (e.g., different distractors) and a sensitivity objective encouraging separable action distributions for task-altering pairs (e.g., target object pose change); evaluated on ManiSkill3 across OpenVLA and pi0.5 under distractors, texture changes, target-pose variation, viewpoint shifts, and lighting changes, it consistently improves over standard PPO with average gains of 16.62% on pi0.5 and 9.10% on OpenVLA
claims.direction: favors explicitly training for invariance to task-irrelevant visual changes (distractors, texture, lighting) and sensitivity to task-relevant changes (object pose) via paired-variant auxiliary objectives, over standard reward-only RL fine-tuning, for robustness to exactly the visual shifts (lighting, viewpoint, distractors) we care about
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 simulation, OpenVLA and pi0.5 architectures (same family as SmolVLA/pi0), diverse OOD visual shift categories tested

claims.claim: Ablations show invariance guidance learned from distractor and texture variants transfers to target-pose and lighting shifts, while adding sensitivity guidance on target-pose variants further improves robustness to nuisance shifts, indicating broader transferability of behavior-level RL guidance across different visual-shift categories not explicitly trained on
claims.direction: favors paired-variant augmentation with behavior-level (invariance/sensitivity) supervision over simple photometric/geometric data augmentation alone, since the learned invariance transfers to shift categories not directly trained on
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 simulation, cross-shift-category transfer ablation

why_deep_read: This is a controlled ablation directly on pi0.5/OpenVLA (our policy family) across the exact shift categories that break our current SmolVLA fine-tune (lighting, viewpoint/camera shift, distractors, object pose); the cross-category transfer finding (distractor/texture training generalizing to lighting/pose shifts) is a specific, checkable, high-value result for our Q14/Q05 decisions.

title: PLUME: Probabilistic Latent Unified World Modeling and Parameter Estimation for Multi-Finger Manipulation

claims.claim: A world model that jointly learns to evolve a belief over physical parameter values (shape, pose, friction) and system dynamics conditioned on those parameters enables efficient online parameter inference at deployment (rather than re-training/fine-tuning), achieving zero-shot transfer of a simulation-trained policy on a hardware screwdriver-turning task and outperforming SOTA offline RL and world-model-augmented behavior cloning baselines
claims.direction: favors a world model with explicit online parameter-belief inference over standard domain randomization or offline RL/BC baselines for handling unknown physical parameters at deployment
claims.conditions: sim (4 tasks) + real hardware screwdriver-turning task, multi-finger dexterous hand (different embodiment from our gripper)

title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model

claims.claim: RynnBrain 1.1 spans 2B, 9B, and 122B-A10B parameter scales; the largest (122B-A10B) model outperforms all evaluated proprietary and open-source models on spatial/embodied cognition benchmarks
claims.direction: reports that larger models achieve the strongest results on embodied cognition/spatial benchmarks, though these scales are far beyond what fits on an 8GB laptop GPU
claims.conditions: embodied foundation model family, benchmark evaluation (VSI-Bench, MMSI, RefSpatial-Bench), multiple real robots (Unitree G1, Astribot-S1, Tianji-Wuji)

claims.claim: Joint multi-task and multi-embodiment training improves process scores and success rates over per-task training, and RynnBrain-initialized policies outperform Qwen-based and representative generalist VLAs in real-robot experiments
claims.direction: favors multi-task/multi-embodiment pretraining over per-task training for improving downstream success rate, when adapting a foundation model to a specific robot
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments across 3 different robot embodiments

title: FoldNet++: a Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for Robotic T-Shirt Folding and Unfolding

claims.claim: Visuomotor policies trained solely on a large-scale synthetic dataset (rule-based demonstration generation over simulated deformable garments with diverse appearances) achieve over 90% end-to-end task success when directly deployed to unseen real-world environments and previously unseen garment instances from arbitrary initial configurations
claims.direction: favors large-scale synthetic-only demonstration generation (with appearance/environment diversity) as sufficient for high real-world zero-shot success, at least for this deformable-object task
claims.conditions: synthetic training only (no real demos), zero-shot real-world deployment, deformable garment folding task (different object type from our rigid pumpkin)

title: RACER: Rich Language-Guided Failure Recovery Policies for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A scalable data generation pipeline automatically augments expert demonstrations with failure-recovery trajectories and fine-grained language annotations; RACER (a VLM supervisor providing detailed online language guidance plus a language-conditioned visuomotor actor) outperforms the state-of-the-art Robotic View Transformer (RVT) on RLBench across standard long-horizon tasks, dynamic goal-change tasks, and zero-shot unseen tasks, in both simulated and real-world environments
claims.direction: favors augmenting demonstrations with synthesized failure-recovery trajectories plus rich (not just short-label) language guidance over standard language-conditioned imitation learning without recovery data
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench) + real world, comparison vs RVT baseline, includes zero-shot unseen task evaluation

claims.claim: RACER achieves superior performance on dynamic goal-change tasks and zero-shot unseen tasks
claims.direction: favors rich language-guided recovery mechanisms for robustness to goal changes and generalization to unseen tasks
claims.conditions: sim + real world, zero-shot generalization test

title: Robo-Dopamine: General Process Reward Modeling for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: After a General Reward Model is adapted to a new task in a one-shot manner from a single expert trajectory, the resulting dense, step-aware, multi-view process reward enables Dopamine-RL to improve a policy from near-zero to 95% success with only 150 online rollouts (approximately 1 hour of real robot interaction), while retaining strong cross-task generalization
claims.direction: favors dense, step-aware, multi-view process reward modeling (adaptable from a single demonstration) plus RL fine-tuning over sparse-reward RL or pure imitation learning, for reaching high success with minimal real-robot interaction
claims.conditions: real robot, one-shot reward-model adaptation from a single expert trajectory, ~1 hour real interaction, diverse simulated and real-world tasks

title: Learning Bimanual Manipulation via Action Chunking and Inter-Arm Coordination with Transformers

claims.claim: An action-chunking imitation-learning architecture with differentiated left/right-arm branches plus an intermediate Inter-Arm Coordinated transformer Encoder (IACE) for synchronization and temporal alignment demonstrated a high success rate compared to alternative architectures on bimanual coordination tasks
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit cross-branch temporal-alignment encoder within an action-chunking transformer architecture when actions from separate branches must stay synchronized (relevant if chunking multiple action streams, e.g., arm plus gripper)
claims.conditions: bimanual robot tasks (different embodiment from our single-arm setup)

title: ImagineBench: Evaluating Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Model Rollouts

claims.claim: Simply applying existing offline RL algorithms to a mix of real and LLM-generated ('imaginary') rollouts leads to suboptimal performance on unseen hard tasks (35.44% success) compared to training on real rollouts alone for hard tasks (64.37% success), indicating current algorithms cannot yet effectively leverage LLM-imagined synthetic experience
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the assumption that adding LLM-generated synthetic rollouts straightforwardly helps; naive use of such synthetic data can underperform training on real data alone, absent algorithmic advances to exploit it
claims.conditions: offline RL benchmark spanning locomotion, robotic manipulation, and navigation domains, language-conditioned tasks

title: HAMLET: Switch your Vision-Language-Action Model into a History-Aware Policy
