claims.claim: Most VLAs rely solely on the current observation, ignoring preceding context; HAMLET introduces compact 'moment tokens' (initialized with time-contrastive learning) per timestep plus a lightweight memory module integrating them across past timesteps into memory features used for action prediction. On top of GR00T N1.5, HAMLET achieves 76.4% average success on history-dependent real-world tasks, a 47.2-percentage-point improvement over the (non-history-aware) baseline, and also pushes RoboCasa Kitchen (100-demo setup) from 64.1% to 66.4% and LIBERO from 95.6% to 97.7%
claims.direction: strongly favors adding a lightweight retrofit memory module (moment tokens + memory integration) to an existing pretrained VLA over relying on current-observation-only VLAs, especially for history-dependent tasks
claims.conditions: real-world history-dependent tasks (built on GR00T N1.5), plus RoboCasa Kitchen (100-demo setup, matching our demo-count regime) and LIBERO sim benchmarks

why_deep_read: The 47.2-percentage-point real-world success-rate gain from a lightweight, retrofittable memory module is one of the largest and most concrete Q07 (observation history) results in the batch, and it is validated at a 100-demo scale close to our own; it is directly relevant to our copycat/causal-confusion and long-horizon concerns and looks feasible to retrofit onto a small VLA.

title: Understanding Asynchronous Inference Methods for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A systematic, controlled comparison of four concurrently-proposed methods for mitigating observation staleness under asynchronous VLA inference -- inference-time inpainting (IT-RTC), training-time delay simulation (TT-RTC), future-state-aware conditioning (VLASH), and lightweight residual correction (A2C2) -- on Kinetix (MLPMixer policies) and LIBERO (with SmolVLA), sweeping inference delays up to d=20 control steps, finds: A2C2's per-step residual correction is most effective on Kinetix (holds above 90% solve rate up to d=8) and also leads on LIBERO from d=4 onward; IT-RTC is competitive at low delays but degrades sharply under long action chunks (H=30) and high delays; TT-RTC is the most robust training-based method (stable across delay ranges, generalizes beyond its training delay distribution, zero inference overhead); VLASH shows a low-delay vs. high-delay trade-off governed by its fine-tuning delay range
claims.direction: provides a controlled ranking of async-inference mitigation strategies for exactly our chunk-boundary/staleness problem, favoring A2C2-style lightweight residual correction for best solve rate at higher delays, and TT-RTC when zero added inference overhead and robustness across untested delay ranges is prioritized
claims.conditions: benchmarked directly on SmolVLA (our base model family) on LIBERO, plus Kinetix with MLPMixer policies, controlled sweep of inference delay 0-20 steps

claims.claim: IT-RTC's performance degrades sharply under long action chunks (H=30) combined with high delays, while other methods are comparatively more robust to chunk length interacting with delay
claims.direction: shows that the interaction between action-chunk horizon length and inference delay materially affects which async-mitigation method is best, informing the choice of chunk/execution horizon jointly with the mitigation strategy
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, SmolVLA, varying chunk horizon H and delay d

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled benchmark of exactly our reported failure mode (jerky motion / staleness from async inference) using SmolVLA (our own base model) on LIBERO, comparing four named mitigation methods with concrete solve-rate-vs-delay curves -- almost certainly the single most actionable paper in this batch for our Q10 decision, and the full tables/code would let us pick a specific method (A2C2 or TT-RTC) to implement directly.

title: Human-as-Humanoid: Enabling Zero-Shot Humanoid Learning from Ego-Exo Human Videos with Human-Aligned Embodiments

claims.claim: Converting synchronized ego-exo human videos into controller-aligned action-chunk supervision (via staged IK retargeting and FK-aware training) yields a 4.8-7.2x raw demonstration-throughput gain over humanoid teleoperation, and policies post-trained only with the converted human labels generalize to real-robot deployment without any target-task robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors converting human video demonstrations into robot action supervision (when embodiment can be carefully aligned) over collecting equivalent volumes of robot teleoperation data
claims.conditions: high-DoF (60-DoF) humanoid upper body, human-aligned embodiment (PrimeU), real-robot deployment validation (different embodiment from our simple 6-DoF arm)

title: Failure Detection With Zero-Shot Error Correction in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A two-stage Failure Detection and Error Correction (FDEC) framework -- a lightweight visual dynamics model for fast predictive monitoring, escalating to a VLM only when a threshold switch triggers high-precision verification and correction -- improves detection speed by 2.1x over pure VLM-based detectors and raises task success by 26.7% on RLBench and physical platforms, for a Diffusion Policy base
claims.direction: favors a cheap always-on monitor with selective escalation to an expensive VLM (rather than running the expensive VLM at every step) for combining responsiveness with generalization in failure detection/correction, applicable to reducing average inference cost
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench) + physical robot platforms, Diffusion Policy base policy

title: SkiP: When to Skip and When to Refine for Efficient Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Most control steps in a manipulation trajectory traverse free space and carry little task-relevant information, while a small fraction of key steps around contacts/grasps/alignment need dense prediction; SkiP uses an action-relabeling mechanism (replacing the BC target in a skip segment with the action at the entrance of the next key segment) plus task-agnostic Motion Spectrum Keying to automatically partition demonstrations into key/skip segments, without a learned skip planner or hierarchical structure
claims.direction: favors adaptively varying prediction/execution granularity within a single unified policy (dense in contact-rich phases, coarse in free-space phases) over uniform per-step prediction at every control step
claims.conditions: 72 simulated manipulation tasks + 3 real-robot tasks, tested across various policy backbones, no manual annotation needed

claims.claim: SkiP reduces the number of executed steps by 15-40% while matching or improving success rates across various policy backbones
claims.direction: favors adaptive step-skipping for reducing execution/inference overhead without sacrificing (and sometimes improving) success rate
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot, multiple policy backbones

why_deep_read: A 15-40% reduction in executed control steps with matched-or-better success, requiring no learned planner or hierarchy and working 'across various policy backbones,' is directly actionable for reducing our per-episode inference calls and could complement chunking/async fixes; worth checking backbone list for compatibility with a small model like ours.

title: InternVLA-A1.5: Unifying Understanding, Latent Foresight, and Action for Compositional Generalization

claims.claim: Future prediction is recast as latent-querying: a small set of learnable foresight tokens condense task-relevant future into a compact latent code supervised by a frozen pretrained video generation model, so the policy inherits world-model dynamics priors without learning pixel-level generation; the video branch is discarded at inference, keeping real-time control, and the model (pretrained on 1.2M robot episodes + 3M multimodal samples) achieves the best overall results on all six simulation benchmarks tested
claims.direction: favors compact latent-foresight auxiliary supervision (distilled from a frozen video generator, dropped at inference) over either learning full pixel-level future prediction or forgoing dynamics priors entirely, for combining world-model benefits with real-time inference
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (1.2M robot episodes), six simulation benchmarks, real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Keeping the VLM backbone training on VQA/subtask prediction (rather than eroding its semantics with pure action fine-tuning) delivers the strongest compositional generalization on held-out instruction bindings in the real world
claims.direction: favors preserving general VLM semantic/language understanding (via continued VQA/subtask training) alongside action-generation training, for better compositional generalization to novel instruction combinations
claims.conditions: real-world, held-out instruction-binding compositional generalization test

title: JEPA-WAM: Learning Vision-Language-Action Policies with Joint-Embedding World Modeling

claims.claim: JEPA-WAM couples latent transition prediction (in a pretrained V-JEPA space) with continuous action generation through a shared predictor, predicting a spatially structured joint current-future target while preserving dense patch-level correspondence; on LIBERO-Plus it achieves 79.2% (best result without large-scale robot-policy pretraining), and instantiated on pretrained pi0.5 it reaches 86.3% (best overall)
claims.direction: favors coupling world-model-style latent transition prediction directly into the same predictor used for action generation (rather than a separate/decoupled world model) for improving manipulation success, and shows the technique composes well with an existing pi0.5-family policy
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus simulation benchmark, tested both standalone and as an add-on to pretrained pi0.5

claims.claim: Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 and real-world bimanual manipulation demonstrate strong generalization under visual and spatial shifts
claims.direction: favors the joint-embedding world-modeling approach for robustness to visual/spatial distribution shift
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0) + real-world bimanual manipulation

title: Learning Video-Conditioned Policies for Unseen Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Video-conditioned Policy learning (ViP) maps unlabelled robot trajectories plus corresponding robot videos, together with human demonstration videos recorded in natural diverse human environments (not robot environments), to robot manipulation skills, using pre-trained human-action-recognition video embeddings to bridge human and robot videos; this enables zero-shot robot control from human video demonstrations of previously unseen tasks, without paired human-instruction/robot-trajectory data during training, and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on challenging multi-task manipulation environments
claims.direction: favors conditioning policies on video (rather than only teleop demonstrations) to leverage abundant natural human videos and reduce the paired robot-demonstration data needed for new/unseen tasks
claims.conditions: multi-task robot manipulation environments, zero-shot unseen-task setup, no paired human-robot training data required

title: Match Policy: A Simple Pipeline from Point Cloud Registration to Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Instead of predicting actions directly, Match Policy registers pick-and-place targets to stored demonstrations, transferring action inference into a point-cloud registration task; this enables high-precision manipulation policies with no training at all (a training-free pipeline), achieving state-of-the-art performance across various tasks on the RLBench benchmark compared with several strong learned baselines, and validated on a real robot across six tasks
claims.direction: favors a training-free, geometric point-cloud-registration action-generation approach over learned regression/generative action heads, for high-precision key-frame pick-and-place tasks with strong geometric structure/symmetry
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench) + real robot (6 tasks), key-frame task setting, requires point cloud/depth observations

claims.claim: By leveraging geometric interaction and task symmetries, Match Policy achieves extremely high sample efficiency and generalizability to unseen configurations, needing only stored demonstrations as registration references rather than a trained model
claims.direction: favors geometry-based few-shot/no-training approaches over data-hungry learned policies when tasks have strong pose/symmetry structure
claims.conditions: sim + real robot, unseen configuration generalization test

claims.claim: The approach relies on point cloud registration, requiring depth/point-cloud observations rather than RGB alone
claims.direction: favors point-cloud/depth-based representations over RGB-only when using a registration-based action-generation approach
claims.conditions: sim + real robot, point cloud input required

title: Robust Instant Policy: Leveraging Student's t-Regression Model for Robust In-context Imitation Learning of Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Robust Instant Policy (RIP) generates several candidate trajectories from an LLM-based in-context imitation policy conditioned on a few demonstrations, then aggregates them using a Student's t-distribution to ignore hallucinated outlier trajectories; in both simulated and real-world environments this significantly outperforms state-of-the-art imitation learning methods, with at least a 26% improvement in task success rate, particularly in low-data scenarios for everyday tasks
claims.direction: favors robust statistical aggregation (Student's t) over multiple in-context-generated candidate trajectories, over both single-shot in-context policies and standard trained IL methods, specifically in low-data regimes
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, low-data scenarios, in-context imitation learning (no explicit network training on large-scale demos), everyday manipulation tasks

claims.claim: In-context IL using off-the-shelf LLMs as 'instant policies' can generate poor/hallucinated trajectories deviating from given demonstrations, which RIP's robust aggregation specifically mitigates
claims.direction: identifies hallucination as a specific failure mode of LLM/in-context-based action generation, distinct from failures of trained regression/generative action heads
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, in-context imitation learning

title: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Fruit Harvesting

claims.claim: A custom Mujoco simulation environment (FruitGym) for autonomous strawberry harvesting used extensive domain randomization (lighting, object placement, sensor noise) to train a policy (via Dormant Ratio Minimization for sample efficiency) that transferred directly to the real world with promising performance, on occluded and clustered fruit
claims.direction: favors extensive domain randomization (lighting, placement, sensor noise) in simulation for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on fruit-picking manipulation, a domain closely analogous to our pumpkin pick-and-place task
claims.conditions: sim-trained (Franka Panda), zero-shot real-world lab transfer, occluded/clustered fruit picking, RL not imitation learning

title: VTLA: Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Model with Preference Learning for Insertion Manipulation

claims.claim: VTLA, using Direct Preference Optimization to bridge classification-based next-token-prediction loss with continuous robotic tasks, outperforms traditional imitation learning methods (e.g., diffusion policies) and existing multimodal baselines (TLA/VLA) on a fingertip insertion task, achieving over 90% success on unseen peg shapes, with real-world peg-in-hole experiments demonstrating strong Sim2Real transfer
claims.direction: favors DPO-based training of a multimodal (vision-tactile-language) action model over standard diffusion-policy imitation learning for contact-rich tasks with strong generalization to unseen object geometry (though relies on tactile sensing outside our current sensor set)
claims.conditions: simulation (low-cost multi-modal dataset) + real-world Sim2Real peg-in-hole, tactile sensor required, unseen peg shape generalization test

title: Mitty: Diffusion-based Human-to-Robot Video Generation

claims.claim: Mitty, a Diffusion Transformer built on a pretrained video diffusion model, translates human demonstration videos into robot-execution videos end-to-end (no action labels or intermediate keypoint/trajectory abstractions), using an automatic synthesis pipeline to produce human-robot paired data from large egocentric datasets to mitigate paired-data scarcity; it achieves state-of-the-art results and strong generalization to unseen environments on Human2Robot and EPIC-Kitchens
claims.direction: favors end-to-end video-diffusion translation of human demonstrations (avoiding intermediate keypoint/trajectory representations that introduce information loss) plus automatic paired-data synthesis, over keypoint/trajectory-based human-to-robot demonstration transfer
claims.conditions: Human2Robot and EPIC-Kitchens benchmarks, automatic human-robot pair synthesis from egocentric video, unseen-environment generalization test

title: DiffusionAnything: End-to-End In-context Diffusion Learning for Unified Navigation and Pre-Grasp Motion

claims.claim: A unified image-space diffusion policy operates purely from RGB input (no depth sensor or vision-language model needed) using multi-scale FiLM conditioning on task mode, depth scale, and spatial attention to enable both meter-scale navigation and centimeter-scale manipulation in a single model
claims.direction: favors an RGB-only diffusion policy with learned/predicted depth scale conditioning over requiring an explicit depth sensor or a large VLM backbone
claims.conditions: RGB input only, self-supervised training, both navigation and pre-grasp manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Trajectory-aligned depth prediction (predicted from RGB, not sensed) focuses metric 3D reasoning along generated waypoints, replacing the need for an RGB-D sensor
claims.direction: favors predicted/estimated depth over hardware depth sensing for 3D-aware action generation
claims.conditions: RGB-only input, self-supervised attention (AnyTraverse) providing goal-directed inference without VLMs or depth sensors

claims.claim: The model operates with only 2.0 GB memory and 10 Hz inference speed, remaining suitable for onboard deployment, in contrast to VLA models that 'demand massive computational resources, extensive training data, and fail zero-shot in novel scenes'
claims.direction: favors a small, purpose-built diffusion policy (2.0 GB memory, 10 Hz) over large VLA models for resource-constrained onboard deployment
claims.conditions: onboard/edge deployment, comparison framing vs typical VLA compute/data requirements

claims.claim: The model achieves robust zero-shot generalization to novel scenes using only 5 minutes of self-supervised data per task
claims.direction: favors self-supervised data collection (5 minutes per task) over large-scale labeled demonstration collection for achieving zero-shot generalization
claims.conditions: self-supervised data collection, zero-shot novel-scene generalization test

why_deep_read: This paper's stated resource profile (2.0 GB memory, 10 Hz, RGB-only, only 5 minutes of self-supervised data per task) is unusually close to our exact constraints (8GB laptop GPU, 640x480 RGB+depth cameras, ~50-100 demos); worth reading in full to see if the multi-scale FiLM/depth-prediction approach could apply to our pick-and-place-in-tray task instead of navigation.

title: 3DVLA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Models via 3D Spatial and Instance Understanding

claims.claim: 3DVLA is a plug-and-play framework that injects 3D reasoning into pretrained VLAs without requiring extra manual instance-level annotations or discarding existing VLM priors, via pervasive 3D feature encoding with explicit multi-view consistency constraints, an instance-estimation module, and a masked self-supervised 3D encoding branch for occlusion robustness
claims.direction: favors retrofitting 3D spatial/instance understanding onto an existing pretrained VLA (plug-and-play, no extra labels) over training/using a VLA without 3D-aware enhancements
claims.conditions: integrated with multiple VLA baselines, evaluated on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 (sim), no extra manual annotations required

claims.claim: Results show consistent and significant gains in manipulation performance when adding 3D spatial/multi-view/occlusion-robust encoding to VLA baselines, validating plug-and-play compatibility
claims.direction: favors adding explicit 3D/multi-view consistency signals over relying on 2D-only VLA visual encoding, particularly for handling occlusion
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0), multiple VLA baselines

title: Shortcut Trajectory Planning for Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Shortcut Trajectory Planning (STP) trains a conditional shortcut trajectory model in a single stage (avoiding the two-stage teacher-student distillation that consistency-based planners require), supporting adjustable one-step and few-step inference via step-size conditioning, and achieves strong performance across D4RL locomotion, navigation, manipulation, and dexterous control benchmarks
claims.direction: favors single-stage shortcut-model training over two-stage consistency-distillation for building fast, few-step generative trajectory/action models
claims.conditions: D4RL benchmarks (sim), offline model-based RL, includes manipulation and dexterous control tasks

claims.claim: STP supports adjustable one-step and few-step inference through step-size conditioning, simplifying the training pipeline for fast generative planning
claims.direction: favors adjustable-step generative models for trading off inference speed vs. quality at deployment time, without separate distillation
claims.conditions: D4RL benchmarks (sim)

title: Lights, Camera, Malfunction: When Illumination Robustness Leaves VLA Models Blind to Color

claims.claim: Naive data augmentation used as a defense against illumination/lighting attacks incorrectly conditions VLA models to discard color as noise, collapsing visual perception into a purely shape-biased processor; a diagnostic grayscale evaluation shows the naively-defended model maintains high success on grayscale inputs while its success rate on benign, color-dependent real-world tasks drops to at most 47.5%, well below the undefended baseline
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common practice of adding generic lighting/photometric data augmentation as a robustness fix; shows it can silently destroy color-dependent task performance by inducing shape-bias, and that a naive fix can be worse than no fix for benign performance
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF robotic platform, color-dependent manipulation tasks, comparison of naive vs. undefended vs. proposed augmentation

claims.claim: A physical spotlight attack (FLARE) drops baseline VLA task success rates to zero via targeted illumination alone (no access to model internals needed); ChromaGuard, a chroma-preserving adversarial training method, achieves 97.5% and 92.5% success in benign and attacked color-dependent tasks respectively, substantially outperforming the naive shape-biased defense
claims.direction: favors chroma-preserving (color-aware) robustness training specifically over generic/naive lighting augmentation, for maintaining both benign performance and robustness to lighting-based failures
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF robotic platform, physical spotlight illumination attack and benign lighting variation, color-dependent manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: This is a direct, real-robot, controlled study of exactly our 'breaks under new lighting' failure mode, and it uncovers a specific, non-obvious pitfall (naive lighting/photometric augmentation causing color-shortcut collapse) that could apply directly to how we augment our own training data; the ChromaGuard fix and its concrete before/after numbers (47.5% vs 97.5%/92.5%) are highly actionable for our Q05/Q14 decisions.

title: HiL-ResRL: A Model-Agnostic Finetuning Adapter via Human-in-the-loop Residual Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A model-agnostic residual policy (compatible with any VLA, treating VLA-generated actions as a unified interface to be corrected) trained with human-in-the-loop guidance for safe exploration achieves over 95% average success rate on real robots within only 1.5 hours of real-world online RL training, directly addressing compounding-error and distributional-shift limitations of pure behavior cloning
claims.direction: favors a lightweight, model-agnostic residual RL fine-tuning layer on top of an existing behavior-cloned VLA (rather than retraining or using architecture-specific RL fine-tuning) for fast, practical real-world performance improvement
claims.conditions: real-world robotic settings, any VLA base policy (model-agnostic), only 1.5 hours of online RL training, human-in-the-loop safety guidance

title: S2-VLA: State-Space Guided Vision-Language-Action Models for Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: S2-VLA introduces a State-Space Guided Adaptive Attention (SSGAA) mechanism that maintains a belief state tracking task progression and generates dynamic gating weights to adaptively fuse visual, task-intent, and temporal-action representations across task phases; despite its compact 2B parameter size, S2-VLA consistently outperforms larger 7B-scale VLA models and achieves state-of-the-art results on long-horizon manipulation benchmarks (LIBERO, SimplerEnv)
claims.direction: directly favors a smaller model (2B) with adaptive, phase-aware feature fusion over simply scaling up to a larger model (7B) for long-horizon manipulation performance
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, SimplerEnv), comparison vs 7B-scale VLA baselines

why_deep_read: This is a direct, concrete counterexample to 'bigger is better' for VLA model size (2B beats 7B) via an architectural mechanism (adaptive state-space-guided fusion) rather than scale, which is exactly the kind of evidence we need for our Q12 small-model decision on an 8GB GPU; worth reading to see if the SSGAA mechanism is applicable at even smaller scale.

title: NOD-TAMP: Generalizable Long-Horizon Planning with Neural Object Descriptors

claims.claim: NOD-TAMP extracts short manipulation trajectories from a handful of human demonstrations, adapts them using generalizable object-centric Neural Object Descriptor features, and composes them via TAMP to solve long-horizon, contact-rich tasks, solving existing manipulation benchmarks with only a handful of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors combining object-centric neural descriptors with TAMP-based skill composition over end-to-end learning, to solve tasks with only a handful of demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + real-world deployment (tool-use, high-precision insertion), handful of human demonstrations

claims.claim: NOD-TAMP significantly outperforms prior NOD-based approaches on new tabletop manipulation tasks requiring diverse generalization
claims.direction: favors the NOD+TAMP composition approach for generalizing to new tabletop tasks/objects over prior object-descriptor-only approaches
claims.conditions: new tabletop manipulation tasks, real-world deployment

title: Recasting Generic Pretrained Vision Transformers As Object-Centric Scene Encoders For Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: SOFT(*), a training-free wrapper around pretrained vision transformers (PVT) that individuates and locates object-like entities from PVT attentions (rather than using only final-layer activations) to produce an object-centric embedding, causes policies trained on SOFT(PVT) to far outstrip standard PVT representations for manipulation tasks in both simulated and real settings, approaching the state-of-the-art of robotics-specific pretrained representations, across multiple choices of generic pretrained ViT backbone
claims.direction: favors extracting object-centric representations from generic pretrained vision transformers (via an attention-based wrapper, no further training) over both raw generic PVT features and the cost of training/using robotics-specific pretrained encoders
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation tasks, multiple generic pretrained ViT backbones tested, no additional training required for the wrapper itself

why_deep_read: A training-free method to substantially improve any generic pretrained ViT (e.g., DINOv2, CLIP) for manipulation, without needing costly robotics-specific pretraining data, is directly actionable for our Q03 vision-encoder decision given our limited compute/data; worth reading to see the exact wrapper mechanism and whether it adds meaningful inference latency.

title: ISS Policy : Scalable Diffusion Policy with Implicit Scene Supervision

claims.claim: ISS Policy augments action diffusion with a supervised robot motion predictor and a future point-cloud forecasting objective (using predicted motion plus gripper intent), providing dynamics-aware geometric auxiliary supervision using only expert demonstrations (no additional annotations or auxiliary modules at inference time); it achieves state-of-the-art performance on single-arm MetaWorld and dexterous Adroit tasks, with real-world dual-arm experiments confirming effectiveness
claims.direction: favors adding a future-point-cloud/geometric-consequence auxiliary prediction objective (derived only from existing demonstrations, zero extra inference cost) to a diffusion policy over action imitation alone
claims.conditions: sim (MetaWorld single-arm, Adroit dexterous) + real-world dual-arm, DiT-backbone diffusion policy, point-cloud observations, no extra annotations needed

claims.claim: The auxiliary objective operates on point-cloud observations, explicitly modeling how actions affect the surrounding 3D scene geometry
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-based scene representations (over RGB-only) when adding geometric auxiliary supervision to a diffusion policy
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, point-cloud input required

title: SlotVLA: Towards Modeling of Object-Relation Representations in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: SlotVLA uses a slot-attention-based visual tokenizer and relation-centric decoder to produce object-relation-centric embeddings instead of dense embeddings that entangle object and background cues; on the LIBERO+ benchmark, object-centric slot and object-relation slot representations drastically reduce the number of required visual tokens while providing competitive generalization
claims.direction: favors compact object/object-relation-centric visual tokenization over dense whole-image embeddings for efficiency, with competitive (not necessarily superior) generalization
claims.conditions: LIBERO+ benchmark (sim), fine-grained object-centric annotations required for training

title: TempoFit: Plug-and-Play Layer-Wise Temporal KV Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: TempoFit is a training-free temporal retrofit for frozen VLAs: it stores layer-wise FIFO prefix K/V attention states at selected intermediate layers (which already form a model-native, content-addressable runtime state) and reuses them across timesteps via parameter-free K-to-K retrieval with a fixed recency bias (Frame-Gap Temporal Bias), injecting retrieved context via pre-attention residual loading with norm-preserving rescaling -- introducing history without new visual tokens or any trainable modules, unlike frame-stacking (which scales tokens/latency) or learned temporal interfaces (which require retraining)
claims.direction: favors training-free, KV-cache-based history injection over both frame-stacking and learned temporal-interface retraining, for adding memory to an already-pretrained, frozen VLA
claims.conditions: frozen pretrained VLA backbones (no retraining), real-robot + LIBERO-LONG + CALVIN long-horizon tasks

claims.claim: On LIBERO-LONG, TempoFit improves strong pretrained backbones by up to +4.0% average success rate while maintaining near-real-time latency, transferring consistently to CALVIN and real-robot long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors this retrofit approach specifically because it preserves near-real-time latency while adding history, unlike frame-stacking which increases latency via more visual tokens
claims.conditions: LIBERO-LONG, CALVIN, real-robot long-horizon tasks, latency-preserving claim

why_deep_read: This is a training-free, drop-in fix for observation history (Q07) that explicitly preserves near-real-time latency (Q10) on a frozen pretrained VLA -- exactly the two constraints we face (need memory but cannot afford retraining or added latency); worth reading in detail to check if it is compatible with a small model like SmolVLA.

title: Instant-Fold: In-Context Imitation Learning for Deformable Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Given a single human demonstration, Instant-Fold infers and executes diverse manipulation modes (variations in spatial execution and ordering) without gradient updates, using deformation-aware visual representations from temporal contrastive pretraining plus a flow-matching transformer policy conditioned on the demonstration; trained entirely in simulation, it generalizes across diverse folding modes and transfers zero-shot to the real world without additional data collection or finetuning
claims.direction: favors in-context (no-gradient-update) conditioning on a single demonstration plus a flow-matching policy over standard per-task fine-tuning, for one-shot generalization across task variants
claims.conditions: deformable object (cloth folding) manipulation, sim-trained, zero-shot real-world transfer, single demonstration at inference

title: Kuramoto Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: KORL learns an object-centric world model (via a Kuramoto Slot Attention for Video module combined with a graph-neural-network dynamics predictor over structured object-centric latents, rather than a single global latent vector) and outperforms object-centric model-free and model-based baselines on visually diverse object-oriented manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors structured, object-centric world-model latents (with explicit object-interaction inductive bias) over single global latent vectors for sample-efficient model-based RL in object-oriented tasks
claims.conditions: visually diverse object-oriented robotic manipulation tasks (real/sim not specified), model-based RL

title: VEGA: Visual Encoder Grounding Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: VEGA directly aligns a VLA's visual encoder output (before any linguistic entanglement) with spatially-aware features from DINOv2-FiT3D (a DINOv2 model fine-tuned with multi-view-consistent 3D Gaussian Splatting supervision), via a lightweight projector trained with a cosine similarity loss alongside the standard action-prediction objective; the projector is discarded at inference, adding no extra computational overhead, and VEGA consistently outperforms existing implicit spatial-grounding baselines on simulation and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors aligning the visual encoder itself (not later LLM-level tokens) with a 3D-supervised DINOv2 variant, as a zero-inference-cost way to improve spatial awareness in VLAs, over prior implicit spatial-grounding methods that rely on empirical layer search at the language-entangled token level
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark + real-world manipulation tasks, DINOv2-based visual encoder

claims.claim: The spatially-aware target features come from a 3D Gaussian-Splatting-supervised DINOv2 variant (DINOv2-FiT3D), injecting 3D/multi-view geometric grounding into what is otherwise a 2D visual encoder, without requiring depth input at inference
claims.direction: favors distilling 3D-aware supervision into a 2D visual encoder (via training-time-only alignment) as an alternative to using depth/point-cloud inputs directly at inference
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, no depth sensor needed at inference

why_deep_read: Q03 in our decision list explicitly names DINOv2 as a pretraining option, and this paper offers a concrete, zero-inference-cost way to make a DINOv2-based visual encoder more spatially aware without needing a depth sensor at inference -- directly actionable for our vision-encoder choice given we only have RGB+depth from one fixed camera and a wrist camera.

title: RoboHarness: Memory-Driven Orchestration of Heterogeneous Robot Policies for Long-Horizon Planning

claims.claim: RoboHarness encapsulates independently developed robot control systems (VLAs, RL policies, TAMP systems) as reusable agentic skills, using multi-modal execution memory and online evidence to characterize policy capability boundaries and a Memory Bridge that retrieves execution trajectories to guide handoffs into a policy's in-distribution state region without joint retraining; across three public benchmarks, 500 customized tasks, and 135 real-robot experiments it yields substantial improvements in zero-shot long-horizon planning and out-of-distribution robustness
claims.direction: favors capability-aware orchestration/routing among multiple heterogeneous pretrained policies (rather than a single monolithic policy) for improving OOD robustness on long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: 3 public benchmarks + 500 customized tasks + 135 real-robot experiments, heterogeneous policy types (VLA, RL, TAMP)

title: CompCPZ: Preserving Multi-Modal Intent in Language-Guided Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard language-conditioned policies collapse disjunctive instructions (e.g., 'place the cup near the red plate or the blue plate') into a single connected representation and may reach a geometrically-averaged point satisfying neither option ('silent semantic failure'); CompCPZ, an algebraic layer recursively composing per-primitive constrained polynomial zonotope enclosures along the language parse tree, outperforms convex-set baselines, multi-peak decoders, and a zero-shot VLA on a closed-loop ManiSkill3 benchmark (1,900/1,918 paired wins), and transfers without retuning to real-robot trials
claims.direction: identifies and fixes a specific failure mode of standard language-conditioned policies (averaging across disjunctive instruction options rather than committing to one valid mode) via an explicit multi-modal feasibility-set representation
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 tabletop manipulation (sim) + real-robot planar trials (quadruped platform), disjunctive/multi-modal language instructions

title: Breaking the Vision-Action Shortcut: Latent Interface Training for Generalizable Robotics Foundation Models

claims.claim: Robot foundation models can exploit task-irrelevant visual cues that correlate with demonstrated actions within the training distribution ('vision-action shortcuts'), which undermines generalization when those correlations change under distribution shift (e.g., unseen camera configurations, lighting variations, distractors) -- a plausible root cause of exactly this kind of failure mode
claims.direction: identifies vision-action shortcut learning as a specific, previously under-addressed mechanism behind poor generalization to lighting/camera/distractor shifts in VLA-style policies
claims.conditions: four VLA/world-action architectures tested (Pi0.5, MolmoAct2, FAST-WAM, ImageWAM), sim (LIBERO-Plus/LIBERO) + real-world

claims.claim: Latent Interface Training (LIT) is a framework-agnostic two-stage strategy: Stage 1 trains the action expert to generate action chunks conditioned on language, robot state, and each demonstrated chunk's terminal SE(3) end-effector pose, WITHOUT images, learning goal-directed action generation independent of visual cues; Stage 2 introduces a latent interface (the policy's only visual conditioning pathway) supervised to reconstruct that terminal pose, retaining goal-relevant spatial information while constraining what visual information can influence actions. Across four VLA/WAM architectures (including Pi0.5, our policy family), LIT improves overall LIBERO-Plus success by 3.87-10.70 percentage points while preserving/improving average LIBERO success, and real-world evaluations show 13.30-16.70 percentage-point gains aggregated across three tasks under unseen camera configurations, lighting variations, and distractors
claims.direction: favors explicitly constraining the visual-to-action pathway (via a pose-supervised bottleneck interface) over allowing an action expert unrestricted access to raw visual features, to prevent shortcut learning and improve real-world robustness to exactly camera/lighting/distractor shifts
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation with unseen camera configurations, lighting variations, and distractors -- directly matching our failure modes; tested on Pi0.5 (same lineage as our SmolVLA)

why_deep_read: This paper directly names and diagnoses the likely mechanism behind our reported failures (breaks under new lighting, different pumpkin, moved camera) as vision-action shortcut learning, and demonstrates a concrete real-world fix (13-17 percentage-point gains under exactly those shift types) on Pi0.5, the closest published relative to our SmolVLA baseline; this is a top-priority full-text read.

title: Distillation for Efficient Multitask Manipulation Policies via Conditional Flow Matching

claims.claim: Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) trained with expert demonstrations outperforms existing methods on single-task robot manipulation benchmarks; naively training one CFM policy on a concatenated multi-task dataset either requires increased model capacity or degrades performance
claims.direction: confirms CFM as a strong single-task action head, but flags that naive multi-task training on a fixed-size model hurts performance without additional technique
claims.conditions: RLBench, single-task vs naive multi-task comparison

claims.claim: Distilling learned velocity fields from single-task CFM experts into a shared multi-task policy (combined with the original CFM objective) improves multi-task policy performance over naive multi-task training while maintaining a FIXED model size
claims.direction: favors expert distillation into a shared model over either training separate per-task models or naively concatenating multi-task data, when model size must stay fixed/small
claims.conditions: RLBench (sim), fixed model size constraint, multi-task setting

title: InterACT: Inter-dependency Aware Action Chunking with Hierarchical Attention Transformers for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: InterACT uses a Hierarchical Attention Encoder (segment-wise and cross-segment attention over multi-modal inputs) and a Multi-arm Decoder with synchronization blocks sharing intermediate output between arms; ablation studies show CLS tokens, cross-segment encoders, and synchronization blocks each significantly contribute to task performance, and the full method outperforms existing action-chunking baselines on simulated and real-world bimanual tasks
claims.direction: favors adding explicit hierarchical/cross-segment attention and inter-dependency synchronization components to an action-chunking transformer (validated via ablation) over a plain single-stream action-chunking transformer, when action streams must stay coordinated
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world bimanual manipulation (different embodiment from our single-arm setup), component-wise ablation

title: Elastic Motion Policy: An Adaptive Dynamical System for Robust and Efficient One-Shot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Elastic Motion Policy (EMP) is trained from a SINGLE demonstration and follows a dynamical-systems paradigm (first-order differential equations with formal convergence guarantees) rather than a data-hungry deep policy; it uses Laplacian editing in full end-effector space (R3 x SO(3)) and online convex learning of Lyapunov functions to adapt online to new contexts without collecting new demonstrations
claims.direction: favors a dynamical-systems/geometric one-shot imitation approach (with formal convergence guarantees) over standard behavior cloning that requires large demonstration sets and lacks convergence guarantees, especially for adapting to scene changes without new data
claims.conditions: real robot experiments, single demonstration, dynamic environments with obstacles

claims.claim: EMP robustly and efficiently adapts to scene changes, obstacle avoidance, and multi-step tasks online, and allows/recovers from physical interactions with humans, without needing new demonstrations or retraining -- addressing an inherent generalization limitation of standard behavior cloning that persists regardless of how much training data is collected
claims.direction: favors online geometric adaptation mechanisms over collecting more demonstration data as the solution to out-of-distribution scene changes and physical perturbations
claims.conditions: real robot, dynamic environments, obstacle avoidance and multi-step task tests

claims.claim: The method explicitly argues that behavior cloning's out-of-distribution performance is sub-par 'regardless of how much training data is available' and lacks formal convergence guarantees, motivating a non-BC (dynamical-systems) action-generation approach instead
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common practice of 'just collect more demonstrations' to fix BC generalization failures, arguing for a fundamentally different (geometric/dynamical-systems) action-generation paradigm instead
claims.conditions: real robot, one-shot learning, dynamic human-centric environments

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly argues that scaling demonstration count cannot fix BC's OOD generalization problem -- a claim directly relevant to whether we should keep collecting more pumpkin demos or consider a fundamentally different action representation; the one-shot, formally-grounded dynamical-systems alternative is worth understanding in detail as a candidate departure from our current BC-style approach.

title: EdgeVLA: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Eliminating the autoregressive requirement for end-effector position prediction leads to a 7x speedup in VLA inference, enabling real-time performance on edge/resource-constrained mobile manipulation systems while maintaining representational power comparable to OpenVLA
claims.direction: favors non-autoregressive end-effector position prediction over autoregressive token-by-token action decoding, specifically to cut inference latency for edge deployment
claims.conditions: edge/resource-constrained devices, comparison vs OpenVLA training characteristics

claims.claim: Leveraging Small Language Models (SLMs) as the VLA backbone demonstrates training performance comparable to larger models with significantly reduced computational demands and memory footprint
claims.direction: favors small language model backbones over large ones for VLA policies deployed on resource-constrained hardware, without necessarily sacrificing training performance
claims.conditions: edge devices, comparison vs larger VLM-backboned VLAs (e.g., OpenVLA)

claims.claim: EdgeVLA modifies the action-generation interface itself (removing autoregression for end-effector position) as the primary lever for efficiency, rather than only compressing/quantizing an existing architecture
claims.direction: favors redesigning the action-decoding mechanism (non-autoregressive) as a first-class design choice for efficient VLAs, not just applying compression post-hoc
claims.conditions: edge/resource-constrained deployment

why_deep_read: EdgeVLA is explicitly designed for exactly our deployment scenario (resource-constrained VLA inference for mobile manipulation) with a concrete 7x speedup number and a small-language-model backbone strategy; this is one of the most directly transferable papers in the batch for solving our ~2s inference latency problem on an 8GB laptop GPU, and the specific architectural change (non-autoregressive end-effector prediction) is worth understanding fully before deciding our own action-head design.

title: U-DiT Policy: U-shaped Diffusion Transformers for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: U-DiT Policy, a U-shaped Diffusion Transformer preserving U-Net's multi-scale feature fusion while adding Transformer global context modeling, achieves a 10% average performance gain over baseline diffusion-policy methods in simulation and surpasses Transformer-based diffusion policies using AdaLN blocks by 6% under comparable parameter budgets; on real-world tasks it achieves a 22.5% average improvement over standard U-Net-based Diffusion Policy (DP-U)
claims.direction: favors a U-shaped diffusion-transformer hybrid architecture over both pure U-Net diffusion policies and standard AdaLN-based transformer diffusion policies, at comparable parameter counts
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world robotic manipulation, comparable parameter budgets across compared architectures

claims.claim: Robustness and generalization experiments under distractor and lighting variations further highlight the advantages of U-DiT over baseline diffusion policy architectures
claims.direction: favors the U-DiT architecture for robustness to distractor and lighting shift specifically, relative to standard diffusion-policy baselines
claims.conditions: real-world, distractor and lighting variation robustness tests

title: RLRC: Reinforcement Learning-Based Recovery for Compressed Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: RLRC, a three-stage pipeline (structured pruning, SFT+RL performance recovery with critic warm-up and BC loss regularization, then quantization), achieves up to an 8x memory reduction for VLA models while maintaining the original task success rate, consistently outperforming existing compression baselines across multiple VLA backbones
claims.direction: favors structured pruning plus RL-based recovery (with BC regularization) over standard compression/quantization alone, for shrinking VLA model memory footprint without losing success rate
claims.conditions: multiple VLA backbones tested, empirical study of model compression for VLAs

claims.claim: The same RLRC pipeline achieves a 2.3x inference speedup while maintaining task success rate
claims.direction: favors this compression+recovery pipeline as a way to reduce inference latency (2.3x) alongside memory footprint, without success-rate loss
claims.conditions: multiple VLA backbones

title: AutoTrialGen: Automated Data Generation From Few Human Demonstrations via Trajectory Annotation and Simulation Trials

claims.claim: AutoTrialGen uses a VLM to decompose a few unprocessed human demonstrations into a library of reusable object-centric skill primitives, then intelligently composes these primitives in simulation (with a weighted manipulability selection mechanism) to generate large, diverse datasets of successful simulated demonstrations via trial-and-error; policies trained on this sim-augmented data show improved performance and enhanced data efficiency across six diverse real-world manipulation tasks compared to a baseline
claims.direction: favors automatically expanding a small set of human demonstrations into a much larger simulated dataset (via primitive decomposition and recomposition) over collecting more real human demonstrations directly
claims.conditions: few human demonstrations as seed, simulation-based expansion, six real-world manipulation tasks for evaluation

title: CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: CIDER freezes the accumulated historical policy as a teacher before learning each new task, interleaving task learning with distillation-based retention and gradient routing to separate new-task gradients from retention gradients; with a single shared actor across six real-world household/industrial tasks, this maintains high success on previously learned tasks while acquiring each new task in 10-20 minutes, whereas every baseline forgets at least one previous task
claims.direction: favors explicit teacher-distillation-based retention (with gradient routing) over naive sequential fine-tuning, when a single shared policy must learn a new task without forgetting a previous one -- directly relevant if we extend from one task to a second object/task
claims.conditions: real-world, human-in-the-loop RL, six-task sequence, single shared actor, 10-20 minutes per new task

title: Robotic Scene Cloning: Advancing Zero-Shot Robotic Scene Adaptation in Manipulation via Visual Prompt Editing

claims.claim: Robotic Scene Cloning (RSC) edits existing robot operation trajectories' visuals using a visual prompting mechanism and a tuned condition injection module, transferring textures and performing moderate shape adaptations to generate scene-consistent samples for scene-specific adaptation, without requiring extensive on-site data collection
claims.direction: favors editing/augmenting existing demonstration visuals (texture and moderate shape adaptation via visual prompts) over collecting new on-site demonstrations for adapting a pretrained policy to a new deployment scene
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world environments, scene-specific adaptation without new data collection

claims.claim: RSC significantly enhances policy generalization in target environments across various object types
claims.direction: favors this visual-editing-based adaptation approach for improving generalization to new deployment scenes/objects
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, various object types tested

title: Pallet-ACT: A Unified Data-Training-Inference Framework for Industrial Robotic Palletizing

claims.claim: PalletACT applies Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to divide sequential palletizing tasks into consistent motion segments, significantly reducing error accumulation over time, learning directly from multi-angle camera feeds and internal robot states without explicit object tracking or pose estimation; on a real six-axis industrial robot it achieves a 94% success rate, outperforming inverse-kinematics planning and RL baselines
claims.direction: favors ACT-style action chunking directly from multi-camera RGB + robot state (no explicit pose estimation) over classical IK planning or RL baselines for a real industrial pick-and-place-style task
claims.conditions: real six-axis industrial robot, VR teleoperation data collection, multi-angle camera feeds

claims.claim: The system delivers real-time efficiency and maintains strong robustness even when subjected to practical environmental disruptions
claims.direction: favors ACT-based chunked visuomotor policies for robustness to environmental disruptions in a real industrial deployment
claims.conditions: real six-axis industrial robot, practical environmental disruption tests

title: Feat2Go: Visual Feature-Grounded Value Estimation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Feat2Go derives a continuous progress target from a pretrained visual world model (patch-level similarity to subgoal states, trend-based clustering into semantic stages), trains an embodied value model to predict this structural progress, and uses it to reshape terminal rewards for RL fine-tuning of VLA policies, without manual reward engineering, compatible with PPO/GRPO pipelines
claims.direction: favors deriving dense reward/value signals from a pretrained world model's feature similarity (rather than manual reward engineering or sparse terminal reward) for RL fine-tuning of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 + RoboTwin 2.0 (sim), single-arm and bimanual settings, applied to existing VLA policies (OpenVLA-OFT)

claims.claim: On ManiSkill3, Feat2Go improves OpenVLA-OFT's average out-of-distribution success from 17.5% to 82.9% while retaining 96.9% of in-distribution performance; on RoboTwin 2.0 it achieves 88.8% average success in domain-randomized task settings, outperforming prior RL methods
claims.direction: shows RL fine-tuning with world-model-derived dense value estimation can produce a very large (17.5% to 82.9%) improvement in out-of-distribution generalization for an existing VLA, without sacrificing in-distribution performance
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 + RoboTwin 2.0 (sim), OOD evaluation, domain-randomized settings

title: Proxy Policy Steering

claims.claim: Proxy Policy Steering (PPS) trains two lightweight proxy policies (a reference proxy modeling the frozen base's behavior on target-task observations, and a task proxy capturing how behavior changes under task supervision); their calibrated velocity-space difference steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step, requiring only forward velocity predictions from the base (no access to base parameters needed). On 8 real-world and 4 simulation manipulation tasks, PPS lifts the state-of-the-art pi0.5 base policy by 53% absolute success rate on average, with zero-to-one gains on tasks the base never solves, while preserving the base's broad capabilities (including failure-recovery behaviors not exercised by the demonstrations)
claims.direction: favors lightweight inference-time steering (via a calibrated proxy-policy velocity residual, base never modified) over LoRA fine-tuning, from-scratch specialists, or residual policies, for specializing a large generalist policy to a new task from limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: 8 real-world + 4 simulation manipulation tasks, base policy is pi0.5 (same lineage as our SmolVLA), outperforms LoRA fine-tuning and residual-policy baselines

claims.claim: PPS outperforms LoRA fine-tuning, from-scratch specialists, residual policies, and prior inference-time steering methods for specializing a frozen flow-matching-based generalist policy
claims.direction: favors this specific inference-time steering formulation over other common specialization methods (LoRA, residual policy, from-scratch) for flow-matching/diffusion-style generalist policies
claims.conditions: 8 real-world + 4 simulation tasks, pi0.5 base policy

why_deep_read: A 53-percentage-point absolute success-rate gain from a lightweight, parameter-access-free adaptation method on pi0.5 (our closest published policy relative) is an exceptionally large and directly transferable result for adapting a generalist base policy to our specific pick-and-place-in-tray task with our limited demonstrations, without the risk of catastrophic forgetting that fine-tuning can cause; this is a top-priority full-text read.

title: FoldQuantVLA: Native Low-Bit Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models via Consistent Folding

claims.claim: FoldQuantVLA, a post-training quantization framework requiring no policy retraining, executes VLA projections (language backbone and iterative action expert) with 4-bit weights/activations (W4A4) on Ada GPUs and Jetson AGX Orin; retaining language attention-output and feed-forward down-projections at 8 bits (W8A8) improves held-out action fidelity across four checkpoints (three GR00T checkpoints and pi0.5)
claims.direction: favors mixed-precision post-training quantization (W4A4 with selective W8A8 retention) over uniform low-bit quantization, for shrinking VLA model footprint without retraining
claims.conditions: LIBERO, SimplerEnv, two robot platforms, tested on GR00T and pi0.5 checkpoints, Jetson AGX Orin and desktop Ada GPUs (no retraining required)

claims.claim: W4A4 achieves 1.20-1.33x inference speedups over floating-point TensorRT on Jetson Orin and 1.25-1.52x on desktop; across four real-robot tasks the mixed W8A8/W4A4 configuration raises GR00T N1.7 observed success from 80.0% (uniform W4A4) to 92.5% over 80 trials per configuration, with only 1ms additional latency on Orin
claims.direction: favors mixed-precision quantization over uniform ultra-low-bit quantization for balancing inference speedup against real-robot task success, with minimal added latency
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks (4), Jetson AGX Orin edge hardware, 80 trials per configuration

title: DynaMo: In-Domain Dynamics Pretraining for Visuo-Motor Control

claims.claim: Current imitation learning's poor data efficiency stems largely from visual representations being either pretrained on out-of-domain data or trained purely via the behavior-cloning objective; DynaMo instead jointly learns a latent inverse-dynamics model and forward-dynamics model over a sequence of in-domain image embeddings (predicting the next frame in latent space) using only the expert demonstrations themselves, no augmentations, contrastive sampling, ground-truth actions, or out-of-domain/internet/cross-embodiment data
claims.direction: favors in-domain, self-supervised dynamics pretraining (using only the target task's own demonstrations) over both out-of-domain-pretrained encoders (DINOv2/CLIP/R3M/VC-1 style) and pure behavior-cloning-trained visual features, for improving data efficiency
claims.conditions: 6 simulated and real environments, self-supervised (no ground-truth actions needed for the representation-learning stage)

claims.claim: Representations learned with DynaMo significantly improve downstream imitation learning performance over prior self-supervised objectives and out-of-domain pretrained representations, with gains holding across multiple policy classes (Behavior Transformer, Diffusion Policy, MLP, nearest neighbors)
claims.direction: shows the in-domain dynamics-pretraining benefit is action-head-agnostic, transferring across very different policy architectures
claims.conditions: 6 sim/real environments, 4 different policy classes tested, component-wise ablations reported

title: AC-DiT: Adaptive Coordination Diffusion Transformer for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: AC-DiT uses a perception-aware multimodal conditioning strategy that dynamically adjusts fusion weights between 2D visual images and 3D point clouds depending on the current perceptual needs of the manipulation stage (relying more on 2D when semantic information is crucial, more on 3D point clouds when precise spatial understanding is required), validated on simulated and real-world mobile manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors dynamically/adaptively weighting RGB vs point-cloud (3D) inputs by task stage over using a single fixed observation modality (all-2D or all-3D) throughout a manipulation episode
claims.conditions: sim + real-world mobile manipulation, includes a mobility-to-body conditioning mechanism for base-manipulator coordination (different embodiment from our fixed-base arm)

title: HRT1: One-Shot Human-to-Robot Trajectory Transfer for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: A four-module pipeline (AR-headset human demo collection, video understanding to extract 3D hand trajectories, human-to-robot end-effector trajectory transfer, and trajectory optimization in robot configuration space) enables a robot to watch a single human demonstration video once and then repeat the manipulation task in different environments, even when objects are placed differently than in the demonstration
claims.direction: favors one-shot human-video-to-robot-trajectory transfer (via explicit 3D trajectory extraction and optimization, not learned end-to-end) over collecting multiple robot teleoperation demonstrations, for generalizing to new object placements after a single demo
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulator, single human demonstration video, generalization to new object placements/environments

title: SuFIA-BC: Generating High Quality Demonstration Data for Visuomotor Policy Learning in Surgical Subtasks

claims.claim: Investigating visual observation spaces including multi-view cameras and 3D visual representations extracted from a single endoscopic camera view, the authors found that current state-of-the-art behavior cloning techniques struggle to solve contact-rich and complex surgical tasks REGARDLESS of their underlying perception or control architecture
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the assumption that swapping in a better perception pipeline or control architecture alone is sufficient to solve contact-rich, complex tasks; highlights that perception/control customization AND larger curated synthetic datasets are both needed
claims.conditions: photorealistic surgical simulator, synthetic demonstration data, multiple behavior-cloning architectures tested, contact-rich surgical subtasks

claims.claim: Curating larger-scale synthetic datasets tailored to the specific demands of the task domain is highlighted as necessary alongside architecture customization
claims.direction: favors investing in larger, domain-tailored synthetic dataset curation, not just architecture choice, for hard contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: photorealistic surgical simulation, synthetic data generation

title: RealDexUMI: A Wearable Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Robot Learning

claims.claim: A wearable interface with a shared dexterous end-effector module (integrating hand, in-hand vision, and fingertip tactile sensing) yields 'zero-gap' end-effector data with matched in-hand observations between collection and deployment; across eight real-robot tasks (fine-grained, contact-rich, long-horizon, bimanual), policies trained on this data achieve an average 88.75% success rate, generalize to unseen initial poses, and transfer across three embodiments
claims.direction: favors minimizing the observation/data gap between demonstration collection and deployment (via shared physical sensing hardware) over retargeting-based or robot-teleoperation-based data collection, for cross-embodiment generalization
claims.conditions: real-world, 8 tasks, dexterous multi-fingered hand (different embodiment from our simple gripper), 3-embodiment transfer test

title: Information Filtering via Variational Regularization for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Oversized denoising decoders in 3D diffusion-based visuomotor policies introduce redundancy/noise in intermediate features (confirmed by finding that randomly masking backbone features or skipping intermediate DiT layers at inference, without retraining, can improve performance); Variational Regularization (VR), a plug-and-play context-conditioned Gaussian + KL-divergence information bottleneck, consistently improves task success rates over baseline for both DP3-UNet and DP3-DiT across RoboTwin2.0, Adroit, and MetaWorld, achieving new SOTA, with real-world experiments confirming practical benefit
claims.direction: favors adding an information-bottleneck regularizer to diffusion-policy denoising decoders (rather than simply increasing decoder capacity) to remove task-irrelevant noise and improve performance
claims.conditions: 3D diffusion policies (point-cloud input), sim (RoboTwin2.0, Adroit, MetaWorld) + real-world

title: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: VLA-FAIL combines two lightweight, minimal-overhead failure detectors -- last-layer Mahalanobis distance (LLMD, measuring token-wise deviation in last-layer features from training data) and action chunk consistency (ACC, exploiting receding-horizon overlap to detect inconsistency between consecutive action chunks) -- without requiring failure rollout data or expensive action sampling; the two detectors capture complementary failure modes and, combined, frequently outperform significantly more expensive baseline detection methods
claims.direction: favors lightweight, architecture-agnostic failure detectors (feature-distance and chunk-consistency based) over computationally expensive action-sampling-based failure detection
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, finetuned VLA models, no failure data required for training the detectors

claims.claim: Action chunk consistency (ACC) exploits the temporal overlap induced by receding-horizon control to detect failures when consecutive predicted action chunks become inconsistent with each other
claims.direction: suggests action-chunk-to-chunk consistency as a useful signal both for failure detection and, implicitly, for diagnosing chunk-boundary-related execution problems
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, receding-horizon/action-chunked VLA control

title: A Systematic Study of Data Modalities and Strategies for Co-training Large Behavior Models for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: In a large-scale empirical study (4,000 hours of robot+human data, 50M vision-language samples, 89 policies evaluated over 58,000 simulation rollouts and 2,835 real-world rollouts), co-training with standard vision-language data and cross-embodiment robot data substantially improved generalization to distribution shifts, unseen tasks, and language following; combining effective modalities produced cumulative gains enabling rapid adaptation to unseen long-horizon dexterous tasks via fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors co-training with vision-language and cross-embodiment robot data over training on target-robot data alone, for improving distribution-shift robustness, unseen-task generalization, and language-following
claims.conditions: large-scale study, single- and multi-phase co-training strategies, 89 policies, sim + real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Among five co-training data modalities tested (vision-language data, dense language annotations, cross-embodiment robot data, human videos, discrete robot action tokens), discrete robot action tokens as a co-training modality yielded NO significant benefit
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the idea that co-training with discrete/tokenized action representations (as opposed to continuous actions) meaningfully helps generalist policy performance, in this large controlled study
claims.conditions: large-scale study, controlled comparison of 5 co-training modalities

claims.claim: Explicitly conditioning action generation on chain-of-thought traces learned from co-training data did NOT improve performance in their simulation benchmark
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that adding chain-of-thought/reasoning-trace conditioning improves manipulation policy performance, at least in this large-scale controlled setting
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, large-scale co-training study

claims.claim: Training exclusively on robot data degrades the visiolinguistic understanding of the VLM backbone, while co-training with effective modalities (vision-language, cross-embodiment) restores these capabilities
claims.direction: favors always co-training with vision-language/cross-embodiment data rather than fine-tuning purely on robot demonstration data, to avoid degrading the backbone's general visual-language understanding
claims.conditions: large-scale study, VLA policies built on VLM backbones

why_deep_read: This is one of the largest, most rigorously controlled studies in the batch (89 policies, ~61,000 combined rollouts) and it directly contradicts two popular design trends relevant to our decisions -- that discrete action tokens help (Q01) and that chain-of-thought/reasoning conditioning helps (Q09) -- while giving clear positive guidance on co-training modalities (Q08) and backbone degradation (Q13); given its scale and direct bearing on multiple decisions, the full paper's per-modality tables are worth reading before finalizing our action-head and language-conditioning choices.

title: SG-WAM: Self-Guided World Modeling in Geometry-Aware Policy Space

claims.claim: SG-WAM learns geometry-aware, action-conditioned dynamics directly in the policy-derived representation space (using learnable dynamics tokens, a Self-Guided World Predictor supervised by an EMA copy of the same policy backbone, plus geometric supervision on image-token representations), jointly optimized end-to-end with flow-matching action generation; built on a 0.9B model WITHOUT large-scale embodied pretraining, it achieves 98.5% average success on LIBERO and 73% on LIBERO-Plus, outperforming strong baselines in-distribution and out-of-distribution
claims.direction: favors jointly-optimized, policy-space (rather than pixel-space or disjoint-latent-space) geometric world modeling for improving both in-distribution and OOD manipulation success, without requiring large-scale embodied pretraining
claims.conditions: 0.9B parameter model, no large-scale embodied pretraining, LIBERO + LIBERO-Plus (sim), real-world in-distribution and OOD evaluation

claims.claim: Strong results (98.5% LIBERO, 73% LIBERO-Plus) are achieved with a relatively compact 0.9B model, without large-scale embodied pretraining
claims.direction: supports that a sub-1B-parameter model can achieve strong manipulation performance when equipped with the right auxiliary geometric/world-model objective, without requiring massive pretraining
claims.conditions: 0.9B model, sim (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus) + real-world

title: Towards Diverse Behaviors: A Benchmark for Imitation Learning with Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: D3IL introduces simulation environments and datasets with diverse, multi-object, closed-loop-feedback-requiring human demonstrations, plus tractable metrics for quantifying a model's ability to capture and reproduce multi-modal human behavior, and conducts a thorough evaluation of state-of-the-art imitation learning methods on this task suite as a benchmark for multi-modal behavior learning
claims.direction: provides a benchmark and quantitative metrics for comparing action-head choices (e.g., regression vs. generative methods) specifically on their ability to capture multimodal human demonstration behavior, rather than declaring a single winner in the abstract
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, multi-object multi-sub-task environments requiring closed-loop feedback

title: GPA-RAM: Grasp-Pretraining Augmented Robotic Attention Mamba for Spatial Task Learning

claims.claim: Grasp-Pretraining Augmentation (GPA), which incorporates grasp priors from task demonstrations into imitation policies with no additional grasp-pose data or annotation needed, raises RVT2's average RLBench success from 79.3% to 84.2%, and when added to ACT raises success on ALOHA cube transfer and bimanual insertion from 86%/16% to 98%/38% respectively
claims.direction: favors incorporating grasp priors (extracted from existing demonstrations, no extra annotation) into imitation policies over standard imitation learning without explicit grasp-pose priors, especially for tasks where inaccurate initial grasps cause cascading errors
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench) + real (ALOHA), added on top of both RVT2 and ACT baselines

claims.claim: Robotic Attention Mamba (RAM), combining attention-based spatial feature extraction with state-space modeling for efficient long-range dependency capture, offsets GPA's added computational cost and enables the combined GPA-RAM framework to operate at approximately 71 frames per second while supporting both discrete keyframe prediction and continuous action generation
claims.direction: favors combining attention with state-space (Mamba) modeling for real-time-capable long-range dependency modeling, over pure-attention architectures that would otherwise be too slow once grasp-prior augmentation is added
claims.conditions: evaluated on 4 platforms including physical UR5 and ARX R5, 71 fps real-time deployment

claims.claim: GPA-RAM achieves 87.5% average success on RLBench (outperforming RVT2 by 8.2pp and ARP+ by 2.6pp) and 98%/56% success on ALOHA cube transfer/bimanual insertion (12pp/40pp over ACT), while running in real time on physical hardware
claims.direction: demonstrates that a specifically-designed efficient architecture (attention + state-space) can outperform larger/heavier baselines while remaining deployable in real time on physical robots
claims.conditions: real robot (physical UR5, ARX R5) + sim (RLBench, ALOHA)

title: DemoGen: Synthetic Demonstration Generation for Data-Efficient Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Using only ONE human-collected demonstration per task, DemoGen generates spatially-augmented synthetic demonstrations by adapting the demonstrated action trajectory to novel object configurations (via 3D point-cloud editing/rearrangement of scene subjects), significantly enhancing policy performance across a diverse range of real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors synthetic, geometry-based demonstration augmentation from a single real demo (spatial generalization via 3D editing) over collecting many real demonstrations across different object configurations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, single human demonstration per task, point-cloud-based scene editing, tested on deformable objects, dexterous hands, and bimanual platforms too

claims.claim: DemoGen can be extended to enable additional out-of-distribution capabilities including disturbance resistance and obstacle avoidance, beyond the originally demonstrated behavior
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-based synthetic augmentation as a route to acquiring robustness capabilities (disturbance resistance, obstacle avoidance) not present in the original demonstration, without collecting new real demos for those capabilities
claims.conditions: real-world, extension beyond spatial generalization to disturbance/obstacle robustness

title: Task Specification and Generalization in Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A transformer-based demonstration-encoding task-specification mechanism allows multi-task RL agents to accomplish new tasks from only a few demonstrations, surpassing methods based on imitation learning and meta-learning
claims.direction: favors transformer-encoded few-shot demonstration conditioning over standard imitation learning or meta-learning approaches for new-task generalization with few demonstrations
claims.conditions: thesis work, multi-task RL setting, few demonstrations per new task

claims.claim: A method linking environment-state-based task specification with natural-language task specification (by composing environment visualization functions with vision-language models) enables goal generation from textual descriptions and automatic creation of semantically diverse goals, without requiring any textual training data for the agents themselves
claims.direction: favors composing pretrained vision-language models with environment-state visualization (rather than collecting paired text-training data) to achieve language-conditioned goal generation
claims.conditions: thesis work, avoids need for text-annotated training data

title: GE-Sim 2.0: A Roadmap Towards Comprehensive Closed-loop Video World Simulators for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: GE-Sim 2.0 is a closed-loop, action-conditioned video world simulator retrained on thousands of hours of real-world robot data, adding a state expert (decoding proprioceptive state from video latents for next-chunk prediction by downstream VLA policies) and a world judge (scoring rollouts against task instructions for machine-verifiable rewards); policies trained against its rollouts and rewards translate into measurable real-world gains
claims.direction: favors using a closed-loop video world model as both a training-signal source (verifiable rewards) and evaluation surrogate for downstream VLA policies, over manual inspection or real-robot-only evaluation
claims.conditions: large-scale real-world robot data (teleoperation, contact-rich interaction, on-robot deployment), downstream real-world gains reported
