claims.claim: GE-Sim 2.0 tops the public WorldArena leaderboard at only 2B parameters (with acceleration delivering a 25-frame rollout in 2.3 seconds on a single H100), outperforming both dedicated robotic world models and closed-source general video generators
claims.direction: shows a relatively compact (2B parameter) world model can outperform larger dedicated/closed-source alternatives, though inference still requires a high-end GPU (H100), unlike our 8GB laptop GPU
claims.conditions: single H100 GPU for inference, not directly applicable to our laptop-GPU constraint

title: WAM-TTT: Steering World-Action Models by Watching Human Play at Test Time

claims.claim: WAM-TTT absorbs raw, unlabeled human videos into a lightweight adaptive memory inside a frozen world-action model through self-supervised video prediction (rather than treating the videos as trajectories to imitate), using a meta-training stage that aligns human demonstrations with robot behaviors via paired human-robot data; at test time only unlabeled human videos are needed to steer the frozen model toward new task variants or preferences, requiring no additional robot demonstrations, task-specific fine-tuning, or robot actions
claims.direction: favors test-time steering of a frozen world-action model via human-video-derived memory (no fine-tuning, no new robot demos) over collecting additional robot demonstrations or fine-tuning for new task variants
claims.conditions: frozen pretrained WAM, unlabeled human videos only at test time, diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings

claims.claim: WAM-TTT consistently outperforms in-context human-video conditioning baselines across diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings
claims.direction: favors this memory-based test-time-training approach over simpler in-context human-video conditioning for steering foundation models
claims.conditions: diverse manipulation tasks, generalization settings

title: SkillPlug: Unsupervised Skill Mining for Few-Shot Adaptation in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: SkillPlug is a plug-in module that augments an existing visuomotor policy with a skill-conditioning module, mining a shared, transferable skill library from raw multi-task demonstrations via self-supervised objectives (compact, reusable, non-redundant behavior primitives); after mining, specializing to unseen tasks requires fine-tuning only a lightweight router and action head (not full end-to-end retraining), and mined skills consistently improve both multi-task performance and few-shot adaptation on two simulation benchmarks and a real robot
claims.direction: favors mining a reusable skill library (via self-supervision on existing multi-task demos) plus lightweight router/head fine-tuning over full end-to-end retraining, for efficient few-shot adaptation to new tasks
claims.conditions: 2 simulation benchmarks + 1 real robot, plug-in to existing visuomotor policies

title: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning

claims.claim: Under a fixed budget of action-labeled demonstrations, action-free video pretraining (learning surgical visual dynamics from abundant unlabeled endoscopic video, then fine-tuning on the fixed action-labeled budget) improves average closed-loop success rate from 63.5% to 77.8% across four simulated surgical manipulation tasks, including a 20-percentage-point gain on PegTransfer, with the largest improvements on contact-rich and bimanual tasks
claims.direction: favors action-free video pretraining of a world-action model (exploiting abundant unlabeled video) as a way to improve closed-loop control performance under a FIXED, limited action-labeled demonstration budget, rather than collecting more action-labeled demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulated surgical manipulation tasks, fixed action-labeled demonstration budget, receding-horizon closed-loop control at deployment

claims.claim: The world-action model acts as a closed-loop, receding-horizon controller (executing a short prefix of each predicted action chunk and replanning from the resulting observation) built on a generative model jointly predicting future observations and action chunks
claims.direction: supports receding-horizon/short-prefix execution of predicted action chunks as the deployment strategy for a world-action model under limited action-labeled data
claims.conditions: simulated surgical tasks

title: GIFT: Goal-Injected Fine-Tuning for Efficient Manipulation Policy Adaptation

claims.claim: GIFT introduces generated goal-image features into a pretrained VLA's observations via a zero-initialized convolution that progressively grows its parameters from zero (preventing harmful noise from disrupting the pretrained policy), gradually incorporating goal information during fine-tuning; a refined image-editing method generates semantically/visually consistent goal images from initial observations and task instructions. With only a SINGLE EPOCH of fine-tuning, GIFT outperforms the base model by 6.0% and 13.4% on two SIMPLER settings and by 4.7% on LIBERO
claims.direction: favors adding generated-goal-image conditioning as a lightweight, low-training-cost (single-epoch) fine-tuning addition to multiple pretrained VLA models, over foundation models that never incorporate goal-image conditioning due to its usual high training cost
claims.conditions: multiple representative pretrained VLA models, SIMPLER and LIBERO sim benchmarks, single-epoch fine-tuning

title: RoCoDA: Counterfactual Data Augmentation for Data-Efficient Robot Learning from Demonstrations

claims.claim: RoCoDA unifies causal invariance (modifying task-irrelevant subsets of the environment state without affecting policy output) and SE(3) equivariance (applying rigid-body transformations to object poses plus adjusting corresponding actions) within a single data-augmentation framework; across five robotic manipulation tasks it improves policy performance, generalization, and sample efficiency compared to state-of-the-art data augmentation methods, with policies exhibiting robust generalization to unseen object poses, textures, and the presence of distractors
claims.direction: favors principled causal-invariance + SE(3)-equivariance-based data augmentation over standard/generic data augmentation methods, for improving generalization specifically to unseen object poses, textures, and distractors
claims.conditions: five robotic manipulation tasks (real/sim not specified in abstract), comparison vs SOTA data augmentation baselines, emergent re-grasping behavior observed

title: Dexterity from Smart Lenses: Multi-Fingered Robot Manipulation with In-the-Wild Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Using lightweight, portable AR glasses (Aria Gen 2, with RGB camera, on-board 3D head/hand pose, and stereo depth estimation) to collect in-the-wild human demonstration data anywhere without a robot, the AINA framework learns 3D point-based multi-fingered manipulation policies deployable directly without ANY robot data (no online corrections, RL, or simulation needed)
claims.direction: favors collecting demonstrations via wearable AR glasses from human activity in arbitrary natural environments (avoiding both robot teleoperation and simulation entirely) for policy learning
claims.conditions: 9 everyday manipulation tasks, multi-fingered hand (different embodiment), no robot data used

claims.claim: Policies learned from this in-the-wild human data are robust to background changes when deployed
claims.direction: favors human-video-derived, 3D point-based policies for robustness to background variation at deployment
claims.conditions: 9 everyday manipulation tasks, background-change robustness

title: Adaptive Capacity Allocation for Vision Language Action Fine-tuning

claims.claim: Spectral analysis shows VLA fine-tuning requires much higher and task-varying intrinsic rank than LLM fine-tuning (LLMs suffice with r in {4,8}; VLAs may need r~128 or near-full rank), a mismatch that worsens in multi-task settings; LoRA-SP (Select-Prune), a rank-adaptive method using an SVD-style parameterization with a router selecting an energy-thresholded active set of singular directions, matches or exceeds full fine-tuning with far fewer trainable parameters and improves multi-task success by up to 31.6% over standard fixed-rank LoRA, while being robust to rank choice
claims.direction: favors rank-ADAPTIVE parameter-efficient fine-tuning (selecting capacity per input/layer via an energy criterion) over fixed-rank LoRA for VLA fine-tuning, since VLAs need substantially higher and more variable capacity than LLMs
claims.conditions: four real-robot manipulation tasks on an UNSEEN AgileX PiPER arm, tested on TWO VLA backbones: pi0 AND SmolVLA (our exact base model)

why_deep_read: This paper directly benchmarks parameter-efficient fine-tuning on SmolVLA (our exact base model) on a real robot arm, with a concrete finding (standard fixed-rank LoRA is suboptimal; rank-adaptive LoRA-SP gives up to 31.6% higher multi-task success) that is immediately actionable for how we should fine-tune our own SmolVLA policy -- essential full-text reading before we pick a fine-tuning rank/strategy.

title: Learning Object-Centric Spatial Reasoning for Sequential Manipulation in Cluttered Environments

claims.claim: Unveiler explicitly decouples high-level spatial reasoning (a lightweight transformer-based Spatial Relationship Encoder sequentially identifying the most critical obstacle) from low-level action execution (a rotation-invariant Action Decoder); this decoupled architecture significantly outperforms both classic end-to-end policies and modern large-model-based baselines in retrieving targets from dense clutter, achieving up to 97.6% success in partially occluded and 90.0% in fully occluded scenarios
claims.direction: favors a decoupled, specialized (spatial-reasoning + action) architecture over monolithic end-to-end large-model policies for cluttered/occluded manipulation
claims.conditions: simulation training, zero-shot transfer to real scenes and validation on a physical robot requiring only geometric workspace calibration (no learned components retrained)

claims.claim: The decoupled architecture is more computationally efficient in terms of parameter count and inference time than end-to-end and large-model-based baselines
claims.direction: favors smaller, task-decomposed specialized models over large monolithic ones for both efficiency and accuracy in this setting
claims.conditions: sim + real, comparison vs large-model baselines

title: LUCID: Learning Embodiment-Agnostic Intent Models from Unstructured Human Videos for Scalable Dexterous Robot Skill Acquisition

claims.claim: LUCID learns a short-horizon intent model (predicting what should happen next in the scene) from unstructured, internet-scale human videos, then converts intent into robot actions via an embodiment-specific sensorimotor policy trained in massively-parallel simulation; the shared intent interface applies across embodiments, from a dexterous hand to a parallel-jaw gripper (matching our end-effector type). Evaluated on stirring, wiping, and binning supervised only by internet video (zero-shot transfer to novel scenes/objects), and push-T/cable-routing supervised by just 1 hour each of self-collected smartphone video
claims.direction: favors decoupling task-intent learning (from abundant internet human video) from embodiment-specific action policy learning (from simulation), over collecting large robot-specific demonstration sets, for a parallel-jaw-gripper-compatible pipeline
claims.conditions: 5 real-world manipulation tasks, parallel-jaw gripper embodiment tested, zero-shot to novel scenes/objects for internet-video-only tasks

claims.claim: Tasks supervised only by internet video achieve zero-shot transfer to novel scenes and object instances at deployment
claims.direction: favors internet-video-derived intent models for zero-shot generalization to novel scenes/objects, without robot-specific data collection for those generalization axes
claims.conditions: real-world, zero-shot novel scene/object test

title: HyperSim: A Holistic Sim-To-Real Framework For Robust Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: HyperSim combines three pillars -- high-fidelity environment synthesis, adversarial trajectory generation, and sim-and-real co-training -- to bridge the sim-to-real domain gap; in a large-scale empirical study of 400 real-world task executions across two representative manipulation models, the complete pipeline achieves sim-to-real success rates of 80% (ACT) and 95% (pi0)
claims.direction: favors combining high-fidelity synthesis + adversarial trajectory generation + sim/real co-training (rather than any single technique alone) for maximizing sim-to-real transfer success, with concrete numbers on ACT and pi0 (relevant policy families)
claims.conditions: 400 real-world task executions, two manipulation models (ACT, pi0), three fine-grained evaluation metrics

claims.claim: Policies trained on HyperSim's adversarial trajectories exhibit significantly enhanced robustness against dynamic uncertainties, achieving a 35% higher completion rate under physical perturbations
claims.direction: favors adversarial trajectory generation specifically (as opposed to only high-fidelity synthesis or co-training) for robustness to physical/dynamic perturbations at deployment
claims.conditions: real-world, physical perturbation robustness test

title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents

claims.claim: End-to-end VLA models are trained on in-distribution task trajectories and often fail under deployment perturbations such as semantic retargeting, goal re-binding, spatial-layout shifts, and unstable local contacts -- closely matching our own reported failure modes (lighting/object/camera changes, jerky contact). Harness VLA composes a frozen VLA (used only for local contact-rich phases) with a small fixed library of analytic primitives via a memory-augmented planner that learns the operating range of these primitives from execution traces and failure models, WITHOUT any finetuning of the VLA. It improves over the strongest baselines by 38.6 and 25.4 percentage points on LIBERO-Pro and RoboCasa365 respectively, and reaches 58.4% on RoboTwin C2R
claims.direction: favors composing a frozen, unmodified VLA (reserved for its local contact-rich strength) with an analytic-primitive planner that absorbs semantic re-grounding and spatial-layout adaptation, over relying on the end-to-end VLA alone or retraining/fine-tuning it, for robustness to deployment-time perturbations
claims.conditions: perturbed tabletop, household kitchen, and clean-to-randomized bimanual manipulation benchmarks (LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin C2R), frozen VLA (no finetuning)

claims.claim: The framework explicitly separates semantic re-grounding and goal re-binding (planner-level reasoning) from local contact-rich execution (frozen VLA), rather than expecting a single VLA to handle both robustly
claims.direction: favors hybrid planner+frozen-VLA composition over expecting a single end-to-end language-conditioned VLA to handle both high-level semantic re-grounding and low-level contact-rich control robustly
claims.conditions: perturbed tabletop/household/bimanual benchmarks

why_deep_read: The paper's stated failure modes for standalone VLAs (semantic retargeting, goal re-binding, spatial-layout shifts, unstable local contacts) map almost one-to-one onto our own reported failures (new lighting, different pumpkin, moved camera, jerky contact); and its fix requires NO fine-tuning of the base VLA, which is attractive given our limited compute -- this is a top-priority read for our Q14 robustness strategy.

title: GIF: Agentic Generation of Interactive and Functional Object Compositions for Robot Learning

claims.claim: GIF, an agentic framework combining 2D/3D generative models (CoGen for instance-disentangled mesh generation, GPRM for physically-guided relative pose refinement, VLM verification), generates fine-grained functional object compositions for simulation, improving asset quality and relation matching while reducing collision rate below 1%; data synthesized this way reveals diversity scaling benefits in both simulation and real-world policy deployment
claims.direction: favors fine-grained, physically-verified generative scene/object composition (over coarse scene-layout generation) for producing training data with better diversity scaling for downstream policy learning
claims.conditions: benchmark across 8 contact-geometry classes, sim + real-world deployment of policies trained on synthesized data

title: Digital-Twin-Assisted Skill Learning for 3C Assembly Tasks

claims.claim: A multimodal digital-twin environment (visual, tactile-force, proprioception) collects VR demonstration data, parses it into a skill knowledge base of primitive policy sequences, then trains primitives via curriculum learning + residual RL + domain randomization before transferring to the real world for complex, long-horizon, high-precision 3C assembly
claims.direction: favors combining VR-collected multimodal demos with curriculum/residual-RL/domain-randomization training in a digital twin for transferring complex high-precision skills to real hardware, over direct real-world skill learning
claims.conditions: digital-twin sim-to-real, 3C electronics assembly (different task domain from our pick-and-place)

claims.claim: Multimodal skill parsing of demonstration data into a reusable primitive skill knowledge base supports acquisition of long-horizon, high-precision skills that could not be effectively accomplished through manual programming or conventional skill-learning methods
claims.direction: favors decomposing demonstrations into a reusable primitive library over direct end-to-end learning for long-horizon, high-precision tasks
claims.conditions: digital-twin sim-to-real, 3C assembly

title: Whole-Body Teleoperation for Mobile Manipulation at Zero Added Cost

claims.claim: MoMa-Teleop infers end-effector motions from existing standard interfaces (joysticks, hand guidance) while delegating base motions to a pretrained RL agent, letting the operator focus solely on task-relevant end-effector motion without additional hardware; this significantly reduces task completion time and produces demonstration data covering diverse whole-body motions without embodiment mismatch, enabling skills that transfer to unseen settings (new obstacles, changed object positions) from as little as FIVE demonstrations
claims.direction: favors offloading non-task-relevant motion (base movement) to an automated controller during teleoperation, letting the operator focus purely on end-effector actions, to collect higher-quality, more efficient demonstrations that generalize from very few (5) examples
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulators, standard teleop interfaces (joystick/hand guidance), various robots/tasks, only 5 demonstrations for unseen-setting transfer

claims.claim: Skills learned from this teleoperation approach transfer to unseen settings such as new obstacles or changed object positions
claims.direction: favors task-focused (end-effector-only) teleoperation data collection for generalization to novel object positions/obstacles
claims.conditions: real mobile manipulators, unseen-setting generalization test

title: MEMBOT: Memory-Based Robot in Intermittent POMDP

claims.claim: MEMBOT decouples belief inference from policy learning via a two-phase process: offline multi-task pretraining of a task-agnostic latent belief encoder (a state-space model + LSTM integrating temporal observation/action sequences) using reconstruction losses, then behavior-cloning fine-tuning of task-specific policies; on 10 manipulation benchmark tasks (MetaWorld, Robomimic) under varying observation dropout rates, MEMBOT consistently outperforms both memoryless and naively recurrent baselines, maintaining up to 80% of peak performance under 50% observation availability
claims.direction: favors explicit, separately-pretrained belief/memory modeling (over both memoryless policies and naive recurrent architectures trained end-to-end) for robustness to intermittent/dropped observations
claims.conditions: 10 manipulation tasks (MetaWorld, Robomimic, sim), varying observation dropout rates 0-50%

title: ZeroMimic: Distilling Robotic Manipulation Skills from Web Videos

claims.claim: ZeroMimic distills immediately deployable, image-goal-conditioned skill policies for common manipulation categories (opening, closing, pouring, pick&place, cutting, stirring) from EpicKitchens human videos, exploiting semantic/geometric visual understanding of human video plus grasp-affordance detectors and imitation policy classes, WITHOUT any robot-specific demonstrations or exploration
claims.direction: favors distilling policies purely from large pre-recorded human video datasets (zero robot demonstrations, zero robot-specific exploration) over standard imitation learning requiring same-robot/same-room/same-object demonstrations
claims.conditions: trained on EpicKitchens (web human video), evaluated out-of-the-box in varied real-world and simulated kitchen settings, two different robot embodiments

claims.claim: ZeroMimic demonstrates impressive abilities handling varied tasks across diverse unseen task setups and two different robot embodiments without further training
claims.direction: favors this human-video-distillation approach for generalizing across unseen task setups and multiple robot embodiments without robot-specific fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real-world + sim kitchen settings, two robot embodiments, zero robot-specific training

title: Learning to Grasp Anything by Playing with Random Toys

claims.claim: Training grasping policies only on randomly-assembled 'toy' objects composed from four simple shape primitives (spheres, cuboids, cylinders, rings) enables robust zero-shot generalization to real-world novel objects, achieving 67% real-world grasping success on the YCB dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches that rely on substantially more in-domain data
claims.direction: favors training on simple, diverse synthetic shape-primitive objects (rather than collecting demonstrations on the actual target object categories) for achieving generalization to novel real-world objects
claims.conditions: real-world (physical robots) + simulation, YCB object dataset evaluation, comparison vs SOTA methods using more in-domain data

claims.claim: The key mechanism enabling generalization is an object-centric visual representation induced by a proposed detection pooling mechanism, rather than the diversity of training objects alone
claims.direction: favors an explicit object-centric visual representation/pooling mechanism as the critical ingredient for cross-object generalization, over simply scaling up training object diversity
claims.conditions: real + sim, ablation over training toy number/diversity and demonstrations per toy

claims.claim: Zero-shot generalization performance was studied as a function of the number and diversity of training toys and the number of demonstrations per toy
claims.direction: provides a scaling study relating training-object diversity/demo-count to generalization performance, relevant for deciding how to allocate a limited demonstration budget across object variety vs. per-object repetition
claims.conditions: real + sim, systematic scaling ablation

title: Beyond Success: Refining Elegant Robot Manipulation from Mixed-Quality Data via Just-in-Time Intervention

claims.claim: Variable execution quality in learned VLA policies is attributed to the mixed-quality nature of human demonstrations (implicit task constraints only partially satisfied); a decoupled refinement framework (an Elegance Critic trained via offline Calibrated Q-Learning, intervening only at decision-critical moments via Just-in-Time Intervention) substantially improves execution quality WITHOUT modifying or retraining the base VLA policy, even on unseen tasks
claims.direction: favors a decoupled, selectively-intervening quality-refinement critic (trained separately, applied only when needed) over retraining the base policy to address mixed-quality demonstration effects
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Elegant benchmark + real-world manipulation tasks, does not require retraining base VLA policy

title: Evo-Depth: A Lightweight Depth-Enhanced Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Rather than using explicit 3D inputs (depth maps/point clouds, which increase system complexity, require extra sensors, and are vulnerable to sensing noise) or implicit 3D-aware modeling via large geometry foundation models (high training/deployment cost), Evo-Depth uses a lightweight Implicit Depth Encoding Module to extract compact depth features directly from multi-view RGB images, with no additional sensing hardware required
claims.direction: favors lightweight, learned implicit depth estimation from RGB over both explicit depth-sensor input and heavyweight geometry-foundation-model-based implicit 3D reasoning, for spatially-grounded manipulation without added hardware or major compute cost
claims.conditions: multi-view RGB input, no extra depth sensor, four simulation benchmarks + real-world experiments

claims.claim: With only 0.9B parameters, Evo-Depth achieves superior performance across four simulation benchmarks, and in real-world experiments attains the highest average success rate while ALSO exhibiting the smallest model size, lowest GPU memory usage, and highest inference frequency among all compared methods
claims.direction: strongly favors a small (0.9B), depth-aware architecture over larger VLA baselines, showing accuracy, model size, memory, and inference speed can all be improved simultaneously with the right lightweight depth-conditioning design
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, comparison against multiple VLA baselines on model size/GPU memory/inference frequency/success rate simultaneously

claims.claim: A Spatial Enhancement Module incorporates the implicit depth features into vision-language representations via depth-aware modulation, with a Progressive Alignment Training strategy aligning depth-enhanced representations with downstream action learning
claims.direction: favors depth-aware modulation of vision-language features (with staged/progressive training alignment) over directly concatenating raw depth or ignoring depth in the visual encoder
claims.conditions: multi-view RGB, no extra depth sensor, progressive training strategy

why_deep_read: This paper's design goals (spatial/depth awareness without extra sensing hardware, smallest model size, lowest GPU memory, highest inference frequency, best real-world success rate, all simultaneously) match our constraints almost point-for-point (8GB laptop GPU, RGB+depth cameras available but latency-critical, small model needed); this is a top-priority read for jointly settling our Q03/Q04/Q12/Q10 decisions.

title: MKT-GMM: A Motion Knowledge Transferring Framework for Robot Trajectory Adaptation to Variable Via-Points

claims.claim: A Gaussian Mixture Model encoding of source-task demonstrations (each Gaussian representing a local motion primitive) can be adapted to a target task specified only by new task constraints, via affine transformation of GMM parameters plus constraint-error minimization, generating feasible trajectories for previously unseen task configurations WITHOUT additional demonstrations or model retraining
claims.direction: favors classical statistical motion-primitive representations (GMM/GMR) with explicit transfer mechanisms over deep-learned policies, specifically for adapting to new spatial constraints/via-points without collecting new demonstrations
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation platform, handwriting motion learning + pick-and-place under varying task configurations, kinesthetic teaching for source demonstrations

claims.claim: A pseudo via-point mechanism automatically generates intermediate constraints when explicit via-points are unavailable, improving robustness of trajectory transfer
claims.direction: supports adding automatically-inferred intermediate waypoint constraints as an alternative/complement to purely learned end-to-end action generation
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation platform, pick-and-place and handwriting tasks

title: From Human Demonstrations to Robotic Actions: Real2Sim Verification of a Diffusion Policy for Autonomous Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Reproducing the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) handheld-demonstration-to-diffusion-policy pipeline and transferring a policy trained on handheld human demonstrations onto a simulated Franka Emika embodiment (with explicit coordinate/action-frame transformations), the authors report pick-and-place rollout statistics across randomized object configurations and identify the VISUAL DOMAIN GAP between rendered and real observations as the dominant remaining barrier to transfer, despite subcentimeter trajectory-tracking accuracy
claims.direction: identifies visual (rendering) domain gap, rather than kinematic/control transfer, as the primary remaining bottleneck when moving a handheld-demonstration-trained diffusion policy from real-world collection to simulated/real deployment
claims.conditions: Franka Emika arm, ViT-B/16 vision backbone, handheld (UMI-style) demonstration collection, ISAAC Sim reconstruction

claims.claim: A ViT-B/16 Vision Transformer serves as the policy's vision backbone in this diffusion-policy reproduction
claims.direction: reports the specific vision backbone choice (ViT-B/16) used successfully in a UMI-style handheld-demonstration diffusion policy pipeline
claims.conditions: real + simulated Franka Emika arm

title: PCK-RL: A Unified Framework for Vision-Language Model and Reinforcement Learning-Based Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: PCK-RL bridges semantic reasoning and low-level control via semantic subplan decomposition, object keypoint localization (with PCA-normalized VLM inputs/outputs as intermediate representations), and a hybrid RRT*-RL method that refines zero-shot reference trajectories with closed-loop RL feedback for long-horizon tasks; validated in simulated and real-world robotic environments across diverse objects
claims.direction: favors a hybrid keypoint-based, PCA-normalized intermediate representation combined with RL-refined planning over purely end-to-end learned action generation for long-horizon, diverse-object manipulation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, long-horizon tasks, diverse objects

title: IndustrialVLA-Bench: A Traceable Multi-Axis Evaluation of Open Robot Policy Models

claims.claim: Across six released VLA/WAM systems evaluated under a unified protocol, clean (in-distribution) LIBERO capability scores differ by only 1.58 points between systems, whereas non-language robustness (LIBERO-Plus) and instruction-paraphrase sensitivity (LIBERO-Para) summaries span 14.62 and 31.08 points respectively; restricting to only protocol-faithful systems preserves this pattern (1.36, 14.62, 23.10 points)
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common practice of using clean/in-distribution benchmark success as the primary basis for comparing policies; shows that clean-task performance barely differentiates models while robustness and language-sensitivity differ enormously, meaning clean benchmark leaderboards are a poor proxy for real-world robustness
claims.conditions: six released VLA and WAM systems, unified evaluation protocol (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Para), 3 seeds per evaluation, also reports inference latency/peak memory/runtime mode per system

claims.claim: Instruction-paraphrase sensitivity (LIBERO-Para) showed the largest spread (31.08 points) among all axes tested, larger than either clean capability or non-language visual robustness
claims.direction: highlights language/instruction-paraphrase robustness as the axis with the greatest inter-model variance, suggesting it deserves more attention in VLA evaluation and design than it typically receives
claims.conditions: six VLA/WAM systems, LIBERO-Para benchmark

claims.claim: The benchmark reports observed inference latency, peak memory, and runtime mode for every evaluated system alongside task scores
claims.direction: supports reporting latency/memory/runtime-mode alongside success rate as a standard practice for comparing VLA/WAM systems, rather than success rate alone
claims.conditions: six VLA/WAM systems, unified fixed checkpoint and inference configuration

title: Subconscious Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Subconscious Robotic Imitation Learning (SRIL) combines cognitive offloading with historical action chunking to reduce delays caused by model inference, further enhanced by subconscious downsampling and a pattern-augmented learning policy using quantized sampling to address intent-rich information; execution speeds of SRIL were 100% to 200% faster than SOTA policies for comprehensive dual-arm tasks, with consistently higher success rates
claims.direction: favors combining historical action-chunk reuse with downsampling/quantized-sampling techniques to cut model-inference-induced delay, over standard multi-model trajectory prediction at every step
claims.conditions: dual-arm manipulation tasks (real/sim not specified), comparison vs SOTA imitation-learning policies

claims.claim: Historical action chunking (reusing/carrying forward prior action-chunk information) is a core mechanism for reducing per-step inference delay while maintaining task execution accuracy
claims.direction: favors reusing historical action-chunk context to reduce the frequency/cost of full re-inference, rather than always predicting a fresh chunk from scratch
claims.conditions: dual-arm manipulation tasks

title: OmniSAT: Compact Action Token, Faster Auto Regression

claims.claim: OmniSAT (Omni Swift Action Tokenizer) normalizes value ranges/temporal horizons with B-Spline encoding, then applies multi-stage residual quantization separately to position, rotation, and gripper subspaces, producing coarse-to-fine discrete tokens; after pretraining on the large-scale Droid dataset, this shortens training sequence length by 6.8x and lowers target entropy compared to prior entropy-guided/token-frequency compression techniques, while enabling faster autoregressive training convergence and preserving reconstruction quality
claims.direction: favors structured, subspace-specific (position/rotation/gripper) residual-quantization action tokenization over generic entropy-guided or token-frequency-based compression, for autoregressive VLA action generation with compact, high-fidelity discrete tokens
claims.conditions: pretrained on Droid (large-scale robot dataset), real-robot and simulation experiments

claims.claim: A cross-embodiment learning strategy built on the unified action-pattern space jointly leverages robot and human demonstrations, enabling scalable auxiliary supervision from heterogeneous egocentric videos
claims.direction: favors a shared discrete action-token space as a mechanism for jointly training on robot and human video data to expand effective training data without requiring action labels for the human video portion
claims.conditions: real-robot + simulation, cross-embodiment (robot + human video) training

title: ActiveVLA: Injecting Active Perception into Vision-Language-Action Models for Precise 3D Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Most existing VLA approaches rely on static, wrist-mounted cameras providing only an end-effector-centric viewpoint and cannot adaptively select optimal viewpoints/resolutions during execution, limiting long-horizon and fine-grained performance; ActiveVLA instead identifies critical 3D regions from multi-view 2D projections and uses an active view-selection strategy to choose optimal viewpoints that maximize relevance/diversity while minimizing occlusion, plus a 3D zoom-in for resolution in key areas, outperforming SOTA baselines on three simulation benchmarks and transferring seamlessly to real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors active, task-adaptive viewpoint/resolution selection (choosing among available camera views/regions dynamically) over relying on a single fixed camera viewpoint (e.g., wrist-only) for precise, fine-grained, long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: 3 simulation benchmarks + real-world transfer, requires multiple available camera viewpoints (not single fixed wrist camera)

claims.claim: Critical region localization is performed by projecting 3D inputs onto multi-view 2D projections to support dynamic spatial awareness
claims.direction: favors leveraging 3D spatial structure (via multi-view projection) as the basis for identifying task-relevant regions, rather than working from a single 2D view
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, 3D input required

title: H2RBench: A Real-to-Sim Benchmark for Evaluating Human-to-Robot Transfer

claims.claim: Systematically characterizing how multiple human-to-robot (H2R) transfer methods scale with the amount of human demonstration data reveals that methods differ substantially in their ability to leverage additional human data; simulation performance is broadly predictive of real-world robot performance (Pearson r=0.89, Spearman rho=0.85, Mean Maximum Rank Violation 0.06) across method-task configurations
claims.direction: supports using simulation-based evaluation as a reliable, scalable proxy for real-world performance when comparing different human-video-to-robot transfer strategies, and highlights that H2R methods vary widely in how well they scale with more human data
claims.conditions: standardized Real2Sim protocol, 4 manipulation tasks, multiple H2R transfer methods compared

title: BFA++: Hierarchical Best-Feature-Aware Token Prune for Multi-View Vision Language Action Model

claims.claim: BFA++ introduces a hierarchical dynamic token-pruning framework with two importance predictors: an intra-view predictor that highlights task-relevant regions within each image (suppressing spatial noise) and an inter-view predictor that identifies critical camera views across manipulation phases (reducing cross-view redundancy); on the RoboTwin benchmark and real-world robotic tasks, BFA++ improves success rate by about 10% on BOTH pi0 and RDT models while achieving speedups of 1.8x and 1.5x respectively
claims.direction: favors context-sensitive, task-aware, hierarchical (intra-view + inter-view) token pruning over generic VLM token-pruning techniques applied naively to multi-view VLA inputs, since naive pruning degrades performance by ignoring cross-view relationships and task phase
claims.conditions: RoboTwin benchmark (sim) + real-world robotic tasks, applied to pi0 (same lineage as SmolVLA) and RDT, multi-view camera input

claims.claim: The inter-view importance predictor identifies which camera views are critical at different manipulation phases, reducing cross-view redundancy while preserving essential visual cues from multiple cameras
claims.direction: favors dynamically weighting/pruning across multiple camera views by manipulation phase (rather than processing all views uniformly at full resolution) when using more than one camera (e.g., our fixed scene camera + wrist camera)
claims.conditions: RoboTwin + real-world, multi-view (2+ camera) VLA setup

why_deep_read: This directly targets both our multi-camera setup (fixed scene camera + wrist camera, Q11) and our inference-latency problem (Q10) simultaneously, with concrete ~10% success-rate gains AND 1.5-1.8x speedups measured on pi0 (our policy family); the hierarchical intra/inter-view pruning mechanism is concrete and implementable, making this a high-priority full-text read.

title: GEM-4D: Geometry-Enhanced Video World Models for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: GEM-4D injects dense 4D correspondence supervision (distilled from a pretrained geometry foundation model) into a video generative backbone during training, enabling the model to jointly capture appearance and geometric structure while RETAINING A SINGLE-STREAM ARCHITECTURE WITH NO ADDITIONAL INFERENCE COST; an inverse dynamics module converts correspondence-consistent video rollouts into executable robot trajectories, improving real-world manipulation success from 61% to 81%
claims.direction: favors injecting geometric (4D correspondence) auxiliary supervision into a video/world-model backbone at training time only (zero added inference cost) over either ignoring geometric consistency or paying extra inference cost for explicit geometric reasoning
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation, single-stream architecture (no added inference-time cost), video world model + inverse dynamics for action extraction

claims.claim: The 4D correspondence supervision is distilled from a pretrained geometry foundation model, injecting explicit geometric/point-tracking structure into an otherwise RGB-video-based world model
claims.direction: favors distilling geometric/3D correspondence knowledge into an RGB-video-based model (training-time only) rather than requiring depth/point-cloud sensing at inference
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, no depth sensor needed at inference

title: Spotlighting Task-Relevant Features: Object-Centric Representations for Better Generalization in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Both dominant visual representation types from pretrained encoders -- global pooled features and dense patch-wise features -- mix task-relevant and irrelevant information, leading to poor generalization under distribution shifts (lighting, textures, distractors); Slot-Based Object-Centric Representations (SBOCR), which group dense features into a finite set of object-like entities, reduce this noise while retaining task-relevant information
claims.direction: favors an intermediate, structured slot-based object-centric visual representation over both global pooled features and raw dense patch features, for reducing task-irrelevant noise passed to the policy
claims.conditions: suite of simulated and real-world manipulation tasks (simple to complex), benchmarked against global and dense representations from pretrained encoders

claims.claim: Benchmarked across diverse visual conditions including changes in lighting, texture, and the presence of distractors, SBOCR-based policies outperform both dense- and global-representation-based policies in generalization, even WITHOUT task-specific pretraining
claims.direction: favors slot-based object-centric representations specifically for robustness to lighting, texture, and distractor shifts -- directly matching our reported failure modes -- without requiring extra task-specific pretraining
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, controlled comparison across lighting/texture/distractor shift conditions, no task-specific pretraining needed for the slot representation

why_deep_read: This is a controlled, direct comparison of visual-representation types (global vs. dense vs. slot-based) specifically under lighting, texture, and distractor shifts -- exactly our Q03 vision-encoder decision and exactly our reported robustness failures -- with a clear winner (SBOCR) that requires no extra task-specific pretraining; a top-priority read for deciding how to process our two camera feeds.

title: DockAnywhere: Data-Efficient Visuomotor Policy Learning for Mobile Manipulation via Novel Demonstration Generation

claims.claim: DockAnywhere lifts a single demonstration to diverse feasible docking (base/camera) configurations by decoupling docking-dependent base motions from contact-rich manipulation skills that remain invariant across viewpoints, then synthesizes visual observations via 3D point-cloud editing to keep observation-action consistency across viewpoints; this substantially improves policy success and generalizes to novel viewpoints from unseen docking points
claims.direction: favors decoupling viewpoint-dependent from viewpoint-invariant components of a task and synthetically generating viewpoint-varied training data from a single demonstration, over collecting many demonstrations across many camera/base positions, for robustness to viewpoint/camera shift
claims.conditions: ManiSkill (sim) + real-world mobile manipulation platforms, single demonstration lifted to many docking/viewpoint configurations

claims.claim: Visual observations are synthesized in 3D space via point-cloud representation and point-level spatial editing to preserve observation-action consistency across synthesized viewpoints
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-based synthetic viewpoint augmentation over simple 2D image augmentation for maintaining action validity under camera-viewpoint changes
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, point-cloud observations required

title: GuidedVLA: Specifying Task-Relevant Factors via Plug-and-Play Action Attention Specialization

claims.claim: Existing VLAs rely on end-to-end supervision to implicitly learn task-relevant features, causing them to often overfit to spurious correlations such as visual shortcuts or environmental noise, limiting generalization; GuidedVLA treats the action decoder as an assembly of functional components, supervising individual attention heads with manually-defined auxiliary signals (object grounding, spatial geometry, temporal skill logic) to explicitly capture distinct task-relevant factors
claims.direction: favors explicit, factor-specific supervision of action-decoder attention heads over purely implicit end-to-end supervision, to prevent overfitting to visual shortcuts/environmental noise
claims.conditions: simulation + real-robot experiments, in-domain and out-of-domain settings, three specialized attention heads instantiated

claims.claim: GuidedVLA improves success rates in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings compared to strong VLA baselines, and the quality of the specialized factors correlates positively with task performance
claims.direction: favors explicitly-guided, decoupled feature learning for improving both in-domain and OOD generalization over implicit end-to-end feature learning
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot, in-domain and OOD evaluation

title: Teaching Tiny VLA Models Where to Look and How to Move

claims.claim: XS-VLA is built on a SmolVLM2-0.25B backbone (a tiny VLA in the same size class as our SmolVLA); on LIBERO it improves average success from 82.8% to 90.3% over SmolVLA-0.25B and improves LIBERO-Long from 63.0% to 89.0%; in real-world experiments across single-arm placement, precision bimanual stacking, and long-horizon sequential coordination, XS-VLA improves average task success from 21.7% to 65.0%
claims.direction: directly favors adding explicit spatial-grounding distillation plus structured latent action generation to a tiny (0.25B) SmolVLA-family backbone over the plain SmolVLA baseline, showing tiny models can be made dramatically more capable (real-world success nearly tripled) without increasing deployment-time model cost
claims.conditions: real-world tasks + LIBERO/LIBERO-Long sim, SmolVLM2-0.25B / SmolVLA-0.25B backbone (our exact model family), no increase in deployment-time model cost

claims.claim: Coarse-Grained Spatial Distillation uses a larger teacher model (Qwen3-VL-4B) to produce coarse image-plane location labels for task-relevant objects, quantized into a spatial vocabulary and distilled into the tiny backbone WITHOUT any human annotations
claims.direction: favors distilling spatial grounding from a larger teacher VLM (no human labels needed) into a tiny deployed model, over training the tiny model's spatial understanding from scratch on raw demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: teacher-student distillation, no human annotation required, tiny backbone deployment

claims.claim: Latent Flow Matching combines a CVAE-style latent variable with flow-based policy learning to organize multimodal demonstrations during training and produce stable action chunks at deployment
claims.direction: favors combining a CVAE-style latent (for capturing demonstration multimodality) with flow matching (for stable chunked action generation) over either a plain CVAE or plain flow-matching action head alone
claims.conditions: tiny VLA backbone, real-world + LIBERO

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly benchmarks against SmolVLA-0.25B by name -- almost certainly the exact model underlying our current fine-tune -- and reports a real-world success-rate improvement from 21.7% to 65.0%; this is very likely the single most directly applicable paper in the entire batch and must be read in full before finalizing our action-head/vision-grounding design.

title: SkillMemo: Expert-guided Skill Memory Framework for Compositional Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: SkillMemo uses a Mixture-of-Experts-based expert-guided trajectory segmentation module to implicitly partition long-horizon demonstrations into latent atomic skills (via learned gating coefficients), stores compact skill representations in a dynamic episodic memory bank, and retrieves/fuses relevant skill primitives with the current gating distribution at inference to refine action predictions; this consistently enhances both Diffusion Policy and VLA backbones, achieving SOTA and outperforming pi0.5
claims.direction: favors an episodic skill-memory retrieval mechanism (implicitly learned skill segmentation, no manual annotation) layered on top of existing DP/VLA backbones over relying on the backbone alone, for compositional generalization to OOD scenarios
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark + real-world manipulation tasks, applied on top of both DP and VLA (including pi0.5) backbones

claims.claim: The framework addresses insufficient compositional generalization in OOD scenarios caused by scarcity of large-scale embodied trajectory datasets, by making reusable skill structures explicit via the memory bank
claims.direction: favors explicit reusable-skill memory as a way to improve data efficiency/compositional generalization when large-scale trajectory data is scarce
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, data-scarce OOD compositional generalization

title: KnowDemo: Knowledge-Guided Robot Demonstration Generation from Human Videos

claims.claim: KnowDemo uses a VLM-based knowledge extraction/reasoning module to distinguish task requirements from demonstration-specific choices in human videos, then resolves this structured knowledge against target-scene geometry to guide candidate generation and screening (before motion planning and simulation), producing diverse robot demonstrations with alternative contact strategies and valid subtask orders (more behavioral diversity than motion-reference-only adaptation methods)
claims.direction: favors knowledge-guided (task-requirement-aware) demonstration generation from human videos over motion-reference-only adaptation, for producing more behaviorally diverse synthetic demonstrations
claims.conditions: human videos as source, target workspace scene geometry, simulation-based demonstration generation and validation

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained pi0.5 model on the resulting simulation-generated data achieves sim-to-real transfer across three tasks
claims.direction: supports fine-tuning an existing pretrained generalist policy (pi0.5) on simulation-generated demonstrations (derived from human video knowledge extraction) as a viable route to real-world task competence
claims.conditions: pi0.5 base model, simulation-generated training data, real-world transfer across 3 tasks

title: EgoMimic: Scaling Imitation Learning via Egocentric Video

claims.claim: EgoMimic co-trains a single imitation learning architecture on egocentric human video (captured via Project Aria glasses with 3D hand tracking) and robot data, treating both as equally valid embodied demonstration data (rather than only extracting high-level intent from human video); this achieves significant improvement on diverse long-horizon single-arm and bimanual manipulation tasks over SOTA imitation learning and enables generalization to entirely new scenes
claims.direction: favors co-training on human and robot demonstration data as equal embodied data sources (via a low-cost bimanual manipulator minimizing kinematic gap, plus cross-domain alignment) over robot-only training or human-video-as-high-level-intent-only approaches
claims.conditions: real robot, long-horizon single-arm and bimanual tasks, egocentric human video + robot demonstrations

claims.claim: EgoMimic shows a favorable scaling trend where adding 1 hour of additional human hand data is significantly MORE valuable than 1 hour of additional robot demonstration data
claims.direction: favors prioritizing collection of additional human egocentric video data over additional robot teleoperation data when scaling a demonstration dataset, given the same time budget
claims.conditions: real robot, scaling trend analysis, cross-embodiment data

title: Pick-and-place Manipulation Across Grippers Without Retraining: A Learning-optimization Diffusion Policy Approach

claims.claim: A diffusion-based policy learns manipulation primitives from demonstrations on a single base gripper, and at inference a diffusion-based optimization strategy (constrained denoising) dynamically enforces kinematic/safety constraints so generated trajectories adapt to unseen gripper parameters (tool-center-point offset, jaw width) without any retraining or new data collection; validated on a Franka Panda across six gripper configurations, achieving 93.3% average task success versus 23.3-26.7% for standard diffusion policy baselines
claims.direction: strongly favors a hybrid learning+constrained-optimization approach (learn primitives once, adapt via inference-time constrained denoising) over standard diffusion policy for achieving zero-shot cross-gripper generalization, since naively-trained diffusion policies fail almost completely (23-27%) on unseen grippers
claims.conditions: real robot (Franka Panda), 6 gripper configurations tested (3D-printed fingertips, flexible silicone, Robotiq 2F-85), tool-center-point variation 16-23.5cm, jaw width 7.5-11.5cm

claims.claim: The method combines a learned diffusion policy for manipulation primitives with a constrained optimization/denoising procedure at inference, rather than a purely learned or purely optimization-based approach
claims.direction: favors a hybrid learning-optimization diffusion action head over either pure learned diffusion or pure model-based optimization alone
claims.conditions: real robot, 6 gripper configurations

title: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach to Robotic Manipulation with VLM-Generated Iterative Keypoint Rewards

claims.claim: IKER uses a VLM to generate and iteratively refine a keypoint-based Python reward function from RGB-D observations and free-form language, reconstructs the real scene in simulation, trains an RL policy against this reward, and deploys it back to the real world (real-to-sim-to-real); this enables multi-step task execution with spontaneous error recovery and on-the-fly strategy adjustment across diverse prehensile and non-prehensile tasks
claims.direction: favors VLM-generated, keypoint-based dynamic reward specification (real-to-sim-to-real loop) over static hand-crafted rewards or pure imitation learning, for flexible multi-step task specification with error recovery
claims.conditions: real-to-sim-to-real, RGB-D + language instructions, diverse prehensile/non-prehensile tasks

title: MSG: Multi-Stream Generative Policies for Sample-Efficient Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Multi-Stream Generative Policy (MSG), a model-agnostic, inference-only framework that trains multiple object-centric generative (e.g., Flow Matching) policies and composes them at inference, learns high-quality policies from AS FEW AS FIVE DEMONSTRATIONS, a 95% reduction in demonstrations versus baselines, and improves policy performance by 89% compared to single-stream object-centric approaches
claims.direction: favors training multiple object-centric generative policy streams and composing them at inference time (rather than a single generative stream, even an object-centric one) for drastically improving sample efficiency of flow-matching/generative policies
claims.conditions: simulation + real robot, as few as 5 demonstrations, model-agnostic (applicable to various generative policies)

claims.claim: MSG enables zero-shot object instance transfer
claims.direction: favors the multi-stream object-centric composition approach for generalizing to novel object instances without additional training
claims.conditions: sim + real robot, zero-shot object-instance generalization test

claims.claim: The method addresses Flow Matching's known sample-inefficiency (a generative action head class) via inference-time policy composition rather than architectural changes to the generative model itself
claims.direction: shows sample-inefficiency of flow-matching action heads can be addressed by an inference-time composition wrapper rather than only by collecting more data or changing the base generative architecture
claims.conditions: sim + real robot

title: HiMaCon: Discovering Hierarchical Manipulation Concepts from Unlabeled Multi-Modal Data

claims.claim: A self-supervised framework combines a cross-modal correlation network (identifying persistent patterns across sensory modalities without human annotation) with a multi-horizon predictor (organizing representations hierarchically across temporal scales) to learn 'manipulation concepts'; concept-enhanced policies show significant performance improvements across simulated benchmarks and real-world deployments, and the learned concepts resemble human-interpretable manipulation primitives despite no semantic supervision
claims.direction: favors self-supervised, cross-modal, multi-horizon representation learning (no human annotation) as an auxiliary/pretraining objective for improving manipulation policy performance and interpretability
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, self-supervised (no human annotation), multi-modal sensory input

claims.claim: The multi-horizon predictor organizes representations hierarchically across temporal scales, enabling policies to maintain awareness of both immediate actions and longer-term goals
claims.direction: favors explicit multi-timescale temporal representation (rather than single-timescale observation processing) for balancing short-term reactivity with long-term goal awareness
claims.conditions: sim + real-world

title: In-Context Policy Adaptation via Cross-Domain Skill Diffusion

claims.claim: A cross-domain skill diffusion scheme jointly learns domain-agnostic prototype skills and a domain-grounded skill adapter through cross-domain consistent diffusion processes, enabling rapid adaptation of skill-based RL policies to diverse target domains under NO model updates and only limited target-domain data, achieving superior policy adaptation under limited target-domain data across differences in environment dynamics, agent embodiment, and task horizon
claims.direction: favors domain-agnostic prototype-skill diffusion with a lightweight domain-grounded adapter (no model updates at adaptation time) over full model fine-tuning, when only limited target-domain data is available
claims.conditions: Metaworld robotic manipulation + CARLA autonomous driving, limited target-domain data, no model updates at adaptation

claims.claim: A dynamic domain prompting scheme guides the diffusion-based skill adapter toward better alignment with the target domain, improving in-context adaptation performance
claims.direction: supports dynamic prompting as a mechanism for improving diffusion-based skill transfer across domains
claims.conditions: Metaworld + CARLA, cross-domain configurations

title: Preference-Calibrated Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: PACT identifies suboptimal segments within otherwise-successful human demonstrations/interventions (using a progress model), builds preference pairs from human vs. resampled-policy actions at intervention states to define a counterfactual advantage that recalibrates credit assignment for those suboptimal segments (rather than uniformly propagating terminal reward), and directly aligns policy with human corrective actions; across five real-robot manipulation tasks this improves average success rate by 24.5% and achieves 1.3x faster convergence versus standard human-in-the-loop RL
claims.direction: favors segment-level credit recalibration based on human-intervention preference signals (rather than uniform credit assignment across a trajectory) for human-in-the-loop RL fine-tuning, when demonstrations/interventions may include suboptimal segments
claims.conditions: 5 real-robot manipulation tasks, human-in-the-loop RL with online interventions

title: PriorVLA: Prior-Preserving Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: PriorVLA keeps a frozen 'Prior Expert' as a read-only source of pretrained scene/motor priors and trains a separate 'Adaptation Expert' for downstream specialization, guided by Expert Queries; this updates only 25% of the parameters that full fine-tuning would update, and WITH ONLY 10 DEMONSTRATIONS PER TASK, PriorVLA reaches 48% in-distribution and 32% out-of-distribution success, surpassing pi0.5 by 24 and 22 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors preserving pretrained priors via a frozen expert + lightweight adaptation expert (rather than full fine-tuning, which risks overwriting broad priors with narrow training-distribution patterns) especially when only a handful of demonstrations per task are available
claims.conditions: real-world (8 tasks, 2 embodiments) + RoboTwin 2.0 + LIBERO, only 10 demonstrations per task, compared against pi0.5 and other SOTA VLA baselines

claims.claim: Full fine-tuning of a pretrained VLA can shift broad priors toward narrow training-distribution patterns; PriorVLA achieves its largest gains specifically under out-of-distribution and few-shot settings, improving over pi0.5 by 11 points on RoboTwin 2.0-Hard, and reaching 99.1% average success on LIBERO, with 81% ID / 57% OOD success on real-world tasks using standard (non-few-shot) data amounts
claims.direction: favors prior-preserving adaptation specifically because standard full fine-tuning degrades OOD generalization; the gap between PriorVLA and pi0.5/full fine-tuning widens precisely in the OOD regime we care about
claims.conditions: real-world (8 tasks, 2 embodiments), RoboTwin 2.0-Hard, LIBERO, standard and few-shot (10-demo) data regimes

claims.claim: PriorVLA updates only 25% of the parameters that full fine-tuning would update, while achieving stronger overall performance
claims.direction: favors a smaller, targeted set of trainable parameters (via the frozen-prior + adaptation-expert split) over updating the full model during fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real-world + sim, parameter-update-count comparison vs full fine-tuning

why_deep_read: This paper reports results in almost exactly our target regime -- only 10 demonstrations per task, evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution success, built as an adaptation strategy for pi0.5 (our policy family) -- with large, concrete percentage-point gains over standard fine-tuning; given our own ~50-100 demo budget and generalization failures, this is a top-priority read for how we should fine-tune our own pretrained VLA.

title: Contact-Anchored Policies: Contact Conditioning Creates Strong Robot Utility Models

claims.claim: Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP) replace language conditioning with points of physical contact in space, arguing that language is often too abstract to guide the concrete physical understanding required for robust manipulation
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common practice of using language as the primary task-conditioning signal; proposes physical contact points as a more concrete, generalizable conditioning signal for robust manipulation
claims.conditions: three fundamental manipulation skills, novel environments and embodiments tested out of the box

claims.claim: CAP is structured as a library of modular utility models (not a monolithic generalist policy) with a real-to-sim iteration cycle (using a lightweight simulation benchmark, EgoGym, to rapidly identify failure modes and refine models/datasets before real-world deployment); CAP generalizes to novel environments and embodiments using only 23 HOURS of demonstration data
claims.direction: favors a modular utility-model library plus a real-to-sim refinement loop over a monolithic generalist policy trained on large-scale data, for achieving strong generalization with a relatively small (23-hour) demonstration budget
claims.conditions: 3 fundamental manipulation skills, 23 hours of demonstration data, real-to-sim iteration via EgoGym

claims.claim: By conditioning on contact and iterating via simulation, CAP outperforms large, state-of-the-art VLAs in zero-shot evaluations by 56%
claims.direction: favors contact-anchored conditioning plus modular utility models over large monolithic VLAs for zero-shot generalization to novel environments/embodiments
claims.conditions: zero-shot evaluation, novel environments and embodiments, comparison vs large SOTA VLAs

title: The Gate, Not the Cache: Gate Provenance Bounds the Closed-Loop Reliability of Training-Free VLA Token Skipping

claims.claim: In training-free VLA token-skipping acceleration (reuse or deletion of visual tokens based on a gate), when the gate signal is harvested from the model's own previous accelerated (already-skipped) forward pass, damage compounds across control steps and closed-loop performance silently collapses -- at a 0.9 skip ratio on LIBERO-Object, reuse collapses to 0.68 and deletion to 0.31 (vs. 1.00 dense), and this collapse is INVISIBLE to standard action-level failure detectors
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the assumption that training-free token-skipping/pruning acceleration is safe as long as an action-level detector would catch failures; shows the failure mode is specifically about gate provenance (a 'dirty' self-harvested gate) and is invisible to typical monitoring
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Object, skip ratio 0.9, tested across 2 VLA policies, 4 LIBERO suites, 4 SIMPLER tasks

claims.claim: Actuation-slack refresh -- running one additional dense (non-skipped) forward pass while the robot executes its current action chunk, off the critical path, to hand the next control step a clean gate and fresh KV cache -- recovers performance to 0.98 (near-dense) while keeping most of the speed benefit, dropping serving latency 18-22% below dense inference, verified in simulation and on a physical robot
claims.direction: favors an unconditional 'actuation-slack refresh' (a dense pass computed during the current chunk's execution window, off the critical path) as a low-cost fix that makes token-skipping acceleration reliable in closed loop, rather than trusting the accelerated gate signal directly
claims.conditions: 2 VLA policies, 4 LIBERO suites, 4 SIMPLER tasks, physical robot validation, 18-22% latency reduction vs dense

why_deep_read: If we ever apply token-skipping/pruning to speed up our VLA inference (a natural response to our ~2s latency problem), this paper shows a specific, silent failure mode that would be invisible to normal monitoring, plus a concrete, cheap fix (actuation-slack refresh, exploiting the execution window of the current action chunk) that also fits naturally with async/chunked execution; essential reading before implementing any acceleration technique for our latency problem.

title: SIRModel: Learning Spatial Intermediate Representation to Parameter-Efficiently Fine-Tune a Vision Language Model for Manipulation

claims.claim: An automatic geometric enhancement pipeline converts raw robot demonstration videos into near/mid/late-stage 3D Gaussian interaction-region supervision (via foreground extraction, metric depth estimation, camera aggregation, end-effector localization, 3D lifting, temporal grouping) WITHOUT manual 3D interaction annotation; a shared vision-language backbone predicts structured subtasks and these Gaussian interaction regions as an explicit planning interface, while a conditional diffusion executor generates action chunks conditioned on them, improving trajectory-tracking success from 55.7% to 70.8% over a same-backbone direct VLA baseline
claims.direction: favors an explicit, automatically-derived 3D geometric intermediate representation (Gaussian interaction regions) as a planning interface between vision-language reasoning and action generation, over acquiring geometry implicitly from visual tokens or via costly manual 3D annotation
claims.conditions: mixed real-robot dataset (LHManip, RH20T), same-backbone comparison vs direct VLA baseline, no manual 3D annotation required

claims.claim: With 80% of the backbone parameters frozen, the framework achieves 85.3% average task success on closed-loop LIBERO simulation evaluation
claims.direction: favors parameter-efficient adaptation (80% of backbone frozen) combined with the explicit geometric intermediate representation, rather than full fine-tuning of the VLM backbone
claims.conditions: LIBERO closed-loop simulation, 80% backbone parameters frozen

title: ReShoot: Generative Visual Domain Randomization of Recorded Robot Demonstrations for Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: ReShoot re-renders previously recorded demonstrations under altered visual appearance (a VLM captions the scene and edits a targeted attribute such as background, object color, or material; an edge-conditioned video generator re-renders both camera views to match), while COPYING the original action sequence and proprioceptive trajectory VERBATIM (no relabeling needed); on LIBERO, a policy trained on an equal mixture of recorded and re-rendered demonstrations matches recorded-only training (96.5% vs 96.9%) while improving robustness to scene perturbations on LIBERO-Plus (85.5% vs 82.3%)
claims.direction: favors shifting the burden of visual-diversity data augmentation from re-collecting real demonstrations in each new visual context to generatively re-rendering existing recorded demonstrations (with actions/proprioception unchanged), over either collecting new demos per appearance or standard image-level augmentation
claims.conditions: LIBERO + LIBERO-Plus (sim), equal mixture of recorded + re-rendered demos

claims.claim: Imitation-learned policies are frequently overfit to visual conditions in training demonstrations, causing substantial performance degradation under object color or background variation; across two physical robotic platforms, deploying ReShoot with only 43 and 100 pre-collected demonstrations increased success rate on RECOLORED objects from 0.0% to 42.9% and 47.5% respectively, while maintaining performance under the original recorded appearance
claims.direction: directly demonstrates that without appearance augmentation, real-robot policies get ZERO success on recolored/different-looking objects (matching our exact 'different-looking pumpkin' failure mode), and that ReShoot recovers to ~43-48% success at demo counts (43, 100) very close to our own ~50-100 demo budget
claims.conditions: real robot, two physical platforms, 43 and 100 pre-collected demonstrations, recolored-object generalization test

why_deep_read: The reported 0.0% success on recolored objects without augmentation is a near-exact match to our own 'different-looking pumpkin' failure, and the fix (re-rendering existing recorded demos with a VLM+video generator, no action relabeling) requires no new physical data collection, tested at demo counts (43-100) matching our own budget; this is one of the most directly actionable Q05/Q14 results in the batch and merits a full-text read.

title: Variable Time Step Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Applications

claims.claim: Variable Time Step RL (VTS-RL), instantiated as Multi-Objective Soft Elastic Actor-Critic (MOSEAC), uses adaptive control frequencies (executing actions only when necessary, extending the action space to include action duration) rather than a fixed-frequency control loop; validated in simulation and on real robots, it shows faster convergence, better training results, and reduced energy consumption relative to fixed- or other variable-frequency approaches
claims.direction: favors adaptive, learned control/action frequency (varying execution horizon per decision) over a fixed control-loop frequency, for reducing computational demand and improving training efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation + real robots, RL (not imitation learning) setting

title: Text-Aware Diffusion for Policy Learning

claims.claim: TADPoLe uses a pretrained, frozen text-conditioned diffusion model to compute dense zero-shot reward signals for text-aligned policy learning, exploiting priors encoded in large-scale pretrained generative models; it learns novel goal-achievement/behavior policies specified by natural language with no ground-truth rewards or expert demonstrations, and performs competitively on Meta-World manipulation tasks without in-domain demonstrations
claims.direction: favors using a frozen, pretrained large generative model as a zero-shot dense reward source for language-specified behaviors over hand-designed reward functions or requiring expert demonstrations
claims.conditions: Humanoid/Dog locomotion (primary) + Meta-World manipulation (secondary), zero-shot, no in-domain demonstrations for Meta-World

claims.claim: The reward is directly conditioned on natural language descriptions of the desired behavior via the frozen text-conditioned diffusion model
claims.direction: supports natural-language-conditioned reward computation (rather than task-specific reward engineering) as a mechanism for specifying novel goals
claims.conditions: language-specified goals, frozen pretrained diffusion model

title: RT-Cache: Training-Free Retrieval for Real-Time Manipulation

claims.claim: RT-Cache is a training-free retrieval-as-control pipeline that caches diverse image-action trajectories in a unified vector memory and, at test time, embeds the current frame to retrieve and replay multi-step snippets, REPLACING per-step model calls entirely (rather than accelerating them); a hierarchical search keeps lookups sub-second at million-item scale, shifting cost from compute to storage and enabling real-time control on MODEST GPUs
claims.direction: favors replacing per-step neural-network inference with retrieval-and-replay of cached trajectory snippets (a fundamentally different latency-reduction paradigm from model acceleration/compression) for real-time control on modest/resource-constrained GPUs
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks + large open logs, modest GPU hardware, training-free (no fine-tuning)

claims.claim: Across real-robot tasks, RT-Cache achieves approximately 2x higher success and ~30% faster completion than strong retrieval baselines, and a single-episode anchoring study shows immediate adaptation to a more complex, contact-rich task without any fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors an append-only experience memory (adaptable from a single new episode, no fine-tuning) over standard retrieval baselines or fine-tuning-based adaptation, for rapid few-shot deployment to new tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks, single-episode adaptation test, no fine-tuning required

why_deep_read: The explicit framing 'real-time control on modest GPUs' via training-free retrieval (rather than accelerating a neural network) is a fundamentally different latency-reduction strategy directly relevant to our 8GB-GPU, ~2s-inference-latency problem, and the single-episode adaptation claim also speaks to our low-demo-count setting; worth reading in full to assess whether a retrieval-based control loop could complement or replace parts of our VLA inference pipeline.

title: Action Tokenizer Matters in In-Context Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Existing action tokenizers preserve action trajectories but fail to keep temporal smoothness; a Lipschitz-constrained VQ-VAE (LipVQ-VAE) improves in-context imitation learning performance by more than 5.3% in high-fidelity simulators
claims.direction: favors VQ/discrete tokenization with smoothness constraint over naive tokenizers
claims.conditions: sim (high-fidelity simulators) + real-world experiments confirming smoother trajectories

title: Learning Human-Intention Priors from Large-Scale Human Demonstrations for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Hierarchical VLA (MoT-HRA) pretrained on 2.2M human-video episodes (HA-2.2M) with a separate intention expert improves motion plausibility and robust control under distribution shift on real-world robot tasks
claims.direction: favors using large-scale human demo priors to supplement small robot datasets
claims.conditions: real-world robot tasks, qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: VAG: Dual-Stream Video-Action Generation for Embodied Data Synthesis

claims.claim: A dual-stream flow-matching model jointly generating video and action produces synthetic pretraining data that 'improves downstream policy generalization' across simulated and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors generative/synthetic-demo augmentation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, qualitative claim (no specific numbers)

title: SeedPolicy: Horizon Scaling via Self-Evolving Diffusion Policy for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Naively increasing stacked observation horizon degrades Diffusion Policy; adding a gated-attention temporal module (SEGA) resolves this, giving 36.8% relative improvement in clean settings and 169% relative improvement in randomized/challenging settings over vanilla Diffusion Policy on RoboTwin 2.0 (50 tasks)
claims.direction: favors compact recurrent latent memory over naive longer observation stacking for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: sim benchmark (RoboTwin 2.0), CNN and Transformer backbones, averaged results

claims.claim: SeedPolicy achieves stronger performance than RDT (a 1.2B-parameter VLA) in the clean setting while using one to two orders of magnitude fewer parameters
claims.direction: favors small specialized models over large VLA models for comparable/better performance
claims.conditions: sim benchmark (RoboTwin 2.0)

why_deep_read: Directly compares small diffusion-policy model sizes against a 1.2B-parameter VLA (RDT) and reports horizon/memory ablations that would materially inform model-size and chunking/horizon choices for our 8GB-GPU laptop setup; full ablation tables and ratio of parameters would clarify what fraction of RDT-scale performance is retained at our scale.

title: Data-Efficient and Contact-Rich Manipulation Through Diffusion Augmentation and Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Diffusion-based augmentation synthesizing geometrically consistent images and action labels reduces demonstration requirements for contact-rich manipulation in clutter
claims.direction: favors generative/diffusion augmentation to cut demo counts
claims.conditions: qualitative talk-abstract claim, no specific numbers; introduces ManipBench for evaluating VLM low-level manipulation ability

title: Toward Reliable Imitation Learning With Limited Expert Demonstrations via Search-Based Inverse Dynamic Learning

claims.claim: SIDIL augments limited expert demonstrations via nearest-neighbor trajectory perturbation/stitching with an inverse-dynamics model, outperforming baseline algorithms with higher success rates and enlarging the recoverable region around expert demonstrations (covariate-shift robustness)
