claims.direction: favors trajectory-stitching data augmentation over vanilla behavior cloning under limited demos
claims.conditions: various robotic manipulation tasks (sim/real unspecified), qualitative 'higher success rates', no exact numbers given

title: GHOST: Hierarchical Sub-Goal Policies for Generalizing Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Factorizing control into a high-level 3D-subgoal policy plus a low-level goal-conditioned controller 'consistently improves performance and robustness compared to a flat Diffusion Policy' across a suite of manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors hierarchical sub-goal factorization over flat diffusion policy
claims.conditions: multi-view RGB-D observations, mixed human-video + robot data; sim/real unspecified in abstract

claims.claim: Because sub-goals are embodiment-agnostic, the high-level policy can be trained on human video and adapted to novel objects/task variations using a small number of human demonstrations
claims.direction: favors leveraging human video plus few robot demos over pure robot teleop data
claims.conditions: qualitative claim

title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: An optimized block-parallel implementation accelerates model-side action decoding by up to 29.2x relative to the base implementation under the reported profiling setup
claims.direction: favors block-parallel decoding architectures to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: real Franka Research 3 robot, masked-diffusion backbone pretrained on ~1.33M trajectories from 48 Open X-Embodiment datasets

claims.claim: Joint action + next-observation (world-model style) denoising with goal guidance improves shifted-instruction success over action-only decoding on real robot manipulation (78.4% average success across four conditions on Franka Research 3)
claims.direction: favors auxiliary future-prediction/world-model objectives over action-only prediction
claims.conditions: real robot (Franka Research 3), large pretrained VLA (likely far above our compute budget)

title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation

claims.claim: Demonstrations shaped by a deterministic 25Hz tactile reflex controller at collection time (rather than manual gripper control) let an ACT policy recover the teacher's grasping profile and achieve 95% stable grasps on a nominal plastic-cup task, substantially outperforming visually-screened manual demonstrations
claims.direction: favors controller-assisted/teacher-shaped demo collection over pure manual teleop demos for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, ACT (small transformer model), single task (plastic cup, some generalization tested on paper-cup variant)

claims.claim: Under randomized external disturbance, a reflex-shaped-data π0.5 policy still fails in 45% of policy-only trials, while a deployment-time reflex arbiter (controller in the loop) retains all grasps -- i.e. tactile-free learned policies alone do not fully generalize disturbance rejection, controller-dependent feedback still needed
claims.direction: shows limits of pure imitation-learned policies (even large π0.5) for robustness to physical disturbance without runtime feedback control
claims.conditions: real robot, compares ACT and π0.5 policies, contact force-sensitive grasping

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our low-cost teleop setup: reports concrete real-robot success/failure percentages for ACT vs π0.5 under disturbance, and shows how demonstration collection method (controller-shaped vs manual) changes learned grasping robustness -- full text would give the ablation details needed to decide on data-collection strategy and disturbance robustness limits for our pumpkin-grasping task.

title: Language-Conditioned Robotic Manipulation with Fast and Slow Thinking

claims.claim: A dual-system (fast/slow-thinking) architecture that routes instructions to either a direct policy or a VLM-reasoning system 'adeptly manages intricate tasks that demand intent recognition and reasoning' in both simulation and real-world tests
claims.direction: favors instruction-adaptive dual-pathway language conditioning over single fixed policy for language-conditioned tasks
claims.conditions: real-world trajectories dataset built by the authors, plus simulation; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: P3-PO: Prescriptive Point Priors for Visuo-Spatial Generalization of Robot Policies

claims.claim: Using human-annotated semantic keypoints propagated through the dataset (instead of raw pixel/visual input) as the policy's state representation gives an overall 43% absolute improvement over prior methods in identical training-evaluation settings, plus 58% and 80% gains for new object instances and more cluttered environments respectively
claims.direction: favors structured point/keypoint state representations over raw visual features for out-of-distribution generalization (novel objects, clutter)
claims.conditions: real-world, four real-world tasks, single human-prescribed demonstration frame propagated via off-the-shelf vision models

why_deep_read: Real-robot, quantified generalization gains specifically for novel objects and cluttered scenes (directly matching our failure modes: different-looking pumpkin, lighting/background change); full text would show how much annotation effort is required and whether keypoint propagation is robust under our camera setup.

title: Closed-Loop Visuomotor Control with Generative Expectation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: CLOVER, a closed-loop framework using a text-conditioned video diffusion model to generate visual plans plus a feedback-driven controller that replans as needed, improves 8% over previous open-loop counterparts on the CALVIN benchmark
claims.direction: favors closed-loop feedback/replanning (video-diffusion generated goals + error quantification) over open-loop chunk execution
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark (sim) plus real-world robotic tasks; long-horizon tasks

title: SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning

claims.claim: Constrained safe-RL alignment (ISA) reduces cumulative cost of safety violations by 83.58% compared to state-of-the-art while improving task success rate by 3.85%, and shows robust generalization of learned safety behaviors to various out-of-distribution perturbations
claims.direction: favors constrained/safety-aware RL fine-tuning for OOD robustness over unconstrained VLA policies
claims.conditions: long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks, benchmark environment introduced by authors

title: Embodiment Transfer Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Synthetic Continued Pretraining (SCP) using synthetically generated data to warm up a VLA for a new embodiment bypasses the need for real human demonstrations and reduces data-collection costs; the resulting ET-VLA outperforms OpenVLA on six real-world tasks by 53.2%
claims.direction: favors synthetic pretraining data to reduce reliance on real teleop demonstrations when adapting to a new embodiment
claims.conditions: real robots, bimanual embodiments (three different ones), plus simulation benchmarks

title: Cross-Modal Instructions for Robot Motion Generation

claims.claim: Using rough cross-modal annotations (sketches/text) in lieu of physical teleoperation/kinaesthetic demonstrations, combined with a VLM and a fine-grained pointing model, produces executable robot behaviors that generalize beyond the limited instruction examples, evaluated on benchmark simulation tasks and real hardware without additional fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors cheaper cross-modal instruction data collection as an alternative/supplement to costly physical demonstration collection
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real hardware, qualitative claim

title: Uni-Skill: Building Self-Evolving Skill Repository for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Retrieving semantic supervision and spatial-trajectory references from a large-scale auto-annotated skill repository (SkillFolder) enables few-shot skill inference without deployment-time demonstrations, and Uni-Skill verifies state-of-the-art performance over existing VLM-based skill-centric approaches in simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors retrieval-augmented few-shot skill acquisition over per-task demonstration collection
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, qualitative comparative claim, no specific numbers given

title: Causally Debiased Latent Action Model for Embodied Action Conditioned World Models

claims.claim: CD-LAM's causally-debiased fine-tuning objectives (embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, latent-space calibration) substantially improve latent-action controllability and require only 6k fine-tuning steps and more than 12x fewer robot-action adaptation updates than baseline latent action models
claims.direction: favors causally-debiased auxiliary latent-action/world-model objectives over plain reconstruction-only auxiliary objectives, for data efficiency
claims.conditions: 2B and 14B action-conditioned world-model backbones (large scale, likely beyond our compute budget)

title: Task Editing for Generalizable 3D Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Task-Edit decomposes a task into scene/skill/object components and recombines them to generate diverse synthetic trajectories, significantly improving generalization of 3D visuomotor policies for long-horizon tasks including disturbance resistance, obstacle avoidance, and unseen cluttered scenes, validated via real-world experiments across robot embodiments
claims.direction: favors task-centric (compositional) demonstration generation over object-centric pose/scale augmentation alone, for 3D visuomotor policies
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, multiple robot embodiments, qualitative claim (no specific numbers given)

title: TriRelVLA: Triadic Relational Structure for Generalizable Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: Replacing implicit visual representations with an explicit object-hand-task triadic relational structure (relation-aware graph transformer, compressed into an LLM action-prediction bottleneck) reduces reliance on appearance statistics and shows 'clear gains in cross-scene, cross-object, and cross-task generalization' on a new real-world robotic dataset
claims.direction: favors explicit relational/structured intermediate representations over implicit end-to-end visual features for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world dataset introduced by authors, qualitative claim, no specific numbers

title: GloVLA: Let Geometry Move and Local VLA Interact for Robust Object-Centric Manipulation in Unstructured Environments

claims.claim: On a newly introduced LIBERO-Challenge benchmark (clutter, distractors, illumination changes, visual shifts, obstruction), a full end-to-end VLA (GR00T N1.6, full-trajectory execution) degrades to 20.9% average success, while GloVLA (geometric transport controller + short-horizon local VLA) retains 88.5% average success
claims.direction: favors separating long-range geometric transport from short-horizon contact-rich VLA interaction over a single end-to-end VLA policy, especially under illumination/visual-shift/clutter perturbations
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus/LIBERO-Challenge) and real physical UR10e robot

claims.claim: On a physical UR10e robot, overall task success improves from 35.6% (full end-to-end VLA) to 90.0% (GloVLA) while mean inference time is more than halved
claims.direction: favors hybrid geometric+local-VLA architecture for both higher success and lower inference latency
claims.conditions: real robot (UR10e), model-agnostic wrapper requiring no additional demonstrations or action-space changes

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our robustness failures (illumination, camera/visual shift, clutter) and our latency concern, with strong real-robot quantitative numbers (35.6%->90.0% success, inference time halved); worth reading in full to see if the geometric-transport/local-interaction split is adaptable to our single-arm low-cost setup.

title: Beyond Appearance Shifts: Task-Semantic Action Calibration for VLA Models

claims.claim: On OpenPI-pi0.5/LIBERO-Object Milk-Swap benchmark, BAS-VLA maintains 98.0% success on clean conditions and 97.5% on semantics-preserving appearance shifts (style, illumination, clutter, paraphrasing), while correctly suppressing stale behavior (reducing clean-criterion success to 0.0%) under deliberate target-object swaps; on validated style-preserving shifts it improves success from 42% to 70% without degrading clean performance
claims.direction: favors explicit task-semantic action calibration (distinguishing appearance-only nuisance shifts from true task-semantic changes) over frozen base VLA policies that either drift unnecessarily or fail to adapt when the target object changes
claims.conditions: benchmark built on OpenPI π0.5 policy and LIBERO-Object variants (sim); frozen base VLA + calibration module

why_deep_read: Directly matches our reported failure mode (breaks under new lighting / different-looking object): quantifies success under illumination/style shift (42%->70%) vs. object-identity changes, on a π0.5-based policy; full text would clarify whether the calibration module is lightweight enough to add to a small model.

title: Robot Utility Models: General Policies for Zero-Shot Deployment in New Environments

claims.claim: Training data (quantity, diversity and quality) matters more than training algorithm or policy class for zero-shot generalization to new environments; the paper offers explicit guidance on data scaling and states diverse yet high-quality demonstrations are necessary, achieving on average 90% success rate in unseen, novel environments with unseen objects
claims.direction: favors prioritizing data diversity/quality over model/algorithm choice for robustness and zero-shot generalization
claims.conditions: real robot -- Hello Robot Stretch (a cheap commodity robot), five utility-model tasks (cabinet doors, drawers, napkins, paper bags, reorienting fallen objects), multi-modal imitation learning with an external mLLM verifier for retrying

why_deep_read: This is a low-cost commodity robot (like our SO-101) achieving 90% zero-shot success in new environments; its stated lesson that 'training data matters more than training algorithm or policy class' directly bears on how we should prioritize demo collection vs architecture search, and the deep_read would give the data-scaling recipe and diversity requirements.

title: Multi-Task Interactive Robot Fleet Learning with Visual World Models

claims.claim: Sirius-Fleet uses a visual world model to predict outcomes of future actions and anomaly predictors (that adapt automatically as autonomy improves) to decide when to request human intervention, demonstrating effectiveness in improving multi-task policy performance and monitoring accuracy on RoboCasa (sim) and Mutex (real-world) benchmarks
claims.direction: favors adding a visual world-model auxiliary/monitoring module for failure detection alongside the base policy
claims.conditions: sim (RoboCasa) and real-world (Mutex) large-scale multi-task benchmarks, qualitative claim (no exact numbers)

title: SpeedAug: Policy Acceleration via Tempo-Enriched Policy and RL Fine-Tuning

claims.claim: SpeedAug learns task-optimal execution tempo via RL fine-tuning on top of a tempo-enriched imitation-learned prior; applied to a real-world manipulation task it improves task throughput by 1.8x using only 16 minutes of online interaction without compromising success rate
claims.direction: favors learned execution-speed optimization (RL fine-tuning of tempo) over fixed/heuristic execution speed from demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation task plus additional robotic manipulation benchmarks

title: Multi-Group Equivariant Augmentation for Reinforcement Learning in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Non-isometric multi-group equivariant data augmentation (applying independent group transformations across spatial and temporal dimensions, combined with a voxel-based translation-equivariant visual representation) improves sampling efficiency for offline RL manipulation, validated in extensive simulation and real-robot experiments across two manipulation domains
claims.direction: favors non-isometric symmetry-based augmentation over standard isometric symmetry augmentation for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments (two manipulation domains) plus simulation, qualitative effectiveness claim

title: ExpertGen: Scalable Sim-to-Real Expert Policy Learning from Imperfect Behavior Priors

claims.claim: Initializing a diffusion-policy behavior prior from imperfect (LLM-synthesized or human) demonstrations, then using RL to steer the frozen prior via noise optimization, produces high-quality expert policies with no reward engineering, achieving 90.5% success on industrial assembly and 85% on long-horizon manipulation tasks, later distilled to real hardware via DAgger
claims.direction: favors combining imperfect/cheap demonstrations with RL refinement over requiring large volumes of high-quality teleop demonstrations
claims.conditions: sim-to-real; state-based experts distilled into visuomotor policies via DAgger and deployed on real robotic hardware

title: LaST0: Latent Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought for Robotic Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Explicit linguistic reasoning/future-observation-prediction before acting incurs non-negligible inference latency; LaST0 instead uses a token-efficient latent spatio-temporal Chain-of-Thought plus a dual-system Mixture-of-Transformers (low-frequency reasoning expert + high-frequency acting expert trained with heterogeneous operation frequencies) to enable efficient reasoning-before-acting, improving mean success rates by 13%, 14%, and 14% over prior SOTA VLA methods on tabletop, mobile, and dexterous-hand manipulation respectively, across 10 real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors latent (non-verbal) spatio-temporal reasoning plus asynchronous dual-frequency execution over explicit linguistic CoT or single-frequency action generation, for both accuracy and latency
claims.conditions: real-world, 10 tasks across tabletop/mobile/dexterous-hand manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly targets our core pain point (latency + jerky motion from single-frequency inference): a dual-frequency latent-CoT architecture with quantified real-world gains could directly inform how to restructure our SmolVLA-style policy to reduce inference latency while retaining reasoning benefits.

title: Beyond Task Success: Behavioral and Representational Diagnostics for WAM and VLA

claims.claim: Across 7 policies (direct VLAs and joint/sequential/auxiliary World-Action-Models) evaluated on LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0, success rate alone hides key differences: WAMs often improve object-level behavior and target selectivity, but their gains depend on architecture and incur higher inference cost; sequential WAMs show the clearest predictive structure while auxiliary and joint WAMs respectively compress or entangle future information
claims.direction: qualifies (partially contradicts blanket claims that) future-prediction/world-model auxiliary objectives always help -- benefit is architecture-dependent and comes with an inference-cost penalty
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 (sim benchmarks), 7 policies spanning direct VLA and three WAM variants (joint, sequential, auxiliary)

why_deep_read: Directly informs the cost/benefit tradeoff of adding a world-model/future-prediction auxiliary objective (Q09) under our tight latency budget (Q10, ~2s inference on laptop already too slow) -- distinguishes which WAM architecture types are worth the extra inference cost, which is exactly the decision we need evidence on rather than a blanket 'world models help'.

title: Zeva-Ego: Egocentric Mid-Training with In-Context Causal Learning for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Scaling egocentric human video mid-training data to 10K hours improves RoboTwin success from 63.8% to 75.3%, matching the performance of 2K hours of real robot demonstrations (74.7%) -- an empirical human-video-to-robot-demo data ratio of roughly 4-5:1; additionally, in-context causal learning (parameter-free adaptation from action-effect feedback) improves success from 58% to 89% within four attempts without any parameter updates
claims.direction: favors supplementing scarce robot teleop demonstrations with large-scale egocentric human video mid-training, and favors in-context/parameter-free adaptation at deployment over further fine-tuning
claims.conditions: RoboTwin (sim benchmark); egocentric video mid-training + VLA; exact demo-equivalence ratio given

why_deep_read: Gives a concrete, quantified human-video-to-robot-demo equivalence ratio (~4-5:1) plus a parameter-free deployment-time adaptation method that could raise success rate from 58% to 89% in 4 attempts -- both are highly actionable for our low-demo-count (50-100 demos) setting, worth reading in full for the mid-training recipe and adaptation mechanism details.

title: One-Policy-Fits-All: Geometry-Aware Action Latents for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

claims.claim: Cross-embodiment co-training with a shared geometry-aware latent action space improves success rates by more than 50% compared to single-source (single-embodiment) training across 11 different end-effectors; with only 8 demonstrations from a new embodiment, the co-trained model achieves performance comparable to a single-embodiment model trained with 72 demonstrations
claims.direction: favors cross-embodiment pretraining/co-training with a shared latent action representation over training from scratch on a single embodiment's demos, to sharply cut the number of demos needed for a new robot
claims.conditions: 11 different end-effectors (various grippers and dexterous hands), extensive experiments (sim/real mix implied but not explicit in abstract)

why_deep_read: Gives a concrete demo-count equivalence (8 demos with cross-embodiment pretraining ~ 72 demos from scratch) which is directly actionable for our ~50-100 demo budget -- worth checking whether a similar pretrained shared action space (e.g. from Open X-Embodiment style data) could let us cut required demos for the SO-101.

title: Flowing With Purpose: Latent Action Guided Flow Matching Policies For Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard flow-matching policies use a globally fixed isotropic Gaussian source distribution despite fragmented/heteroscedastic action-space structure; replacing it with an adaptive library of learned prior distributions grounded in a latent action model (LAFM), which selects a specialized base distribution per observation, increases task success rates by 23.4% in real-world robotic deployments and by 10.4% on the LIBERO-90 benchmark over standard flow matching
claims.direction: favors structured/adaptive source-distribution flow matching over vanilla isotropic-Gaussian flow matching for multimodal human demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world robotic deployments plus LIBERO-90 (sim)

claims.claim: LAFM achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing massively pre-trained vision-language-action models while using significantly smaller architectures
claims.direction: favors small, specialized architectures with better-structured action heads over large pretrained VLAs
claims.conditions: comparison against massively pretrained VLA baselines; real-world + LIBERO-90

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our Q01 action-head choice (flow matching, handling multimodal human demos) and Q12 (small model beating large VLA) with real-world quantitative gains (23.4%) -- worth reading in full to see if the latent-action-guided source distribution is implementable in a small model on our compute budget.

title: DC-WAM: Dynamic-Centric Visual Supervision and Reasoning for World-Action Models

claims.claim: Redirecting a world-action model's video-prediction supervision from appearance-dominated (photorealistic) reconstruction toward interaction-induced visual dynamics (temporal-difference flow matching + trajectory-guided weighting + token-wise dynamic-relevance attention bias) 'consistently improves policy performance, especially under out-of-distribution perturbations in lighting, object appearance, and background texture', in both simulation and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors dynamic/interaction-centric auxiliary visual supervision over standard photorealistic future-frame prediction, specifically for robustness to lighting/appearance/background shift
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: SAVLA: Symmetry-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: An end-to-end symmetry-aware VLA (frozen pretrained VLM backbone + equivariant flow-matching action head + learned canonicalizer that transforms oblique-view images into a canonical frame) improves mean success rate under rotation on LIBERO-Goal from 41.5% (GR00T N1.5 baseline) to 90.4%, and improves average success across all four LIBERO suites by 5.1 points over the baseline
claims.direction: favors building explicit viewpoint/rotation equivariance into the action head and a canonicalizer over relying on a frozen VLM's implicit spatial competence for camera-pose/viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO), frozen pretrained vision-language backbone, compared against GR00T N1.5 baseline

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our observed failure under 'a slightly moved camera' (Q11/viewpoint robustness): reports a large, specific improvement (41.5% -> 90.4%) from adding equivariant/canonicalization structure with a frozen backbone, which is compute-cheap and could be directly relevant to our low-compute setup.

title: Insert-One: One-Shot Robust Visual-Force Servoing for Novel Object Insertion with 6-DoF Tracking

claims.claim: A hybrid 6-DoF visual-tracking + impedance-control framework performs high-precision insertion of novel objects from randomly presented orientations using just a single demonstration image, requiring no pre-training, and is validated across various high-precision real-world assembly tasks
claims.direction: favors classical hybrid visual-servo/impedance control with one-shot demonstration over learned policies requiring many demonstrations, for precision contact-rich insertion
claims.conditions: real-world, one demonstration image, resilient to camera calibration errors and in-hand pose disturbances

title: Phys2Real: Fusing VLM Priors with Interactive Online Adaptation for Uncertainty-Aware Sim-to-Real Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining VLM-inferred physical-parameter priors with online interaction-based parameter estimation (real-to-sim-to-real RL) substantially outperforms a domain-randomization baseline: 100% vs 79% success for a bottom-weighted T-block, 57% vs 23% for a top-weighted T-block, and 15% faster average task completion for hammer pushing
claims.direction: favors VLM-prior-guided + online physical-parameter adaptation over plain domain randomization for sim-to-real transfer under varying object physical properties
claims.conditions: real-world planar pushing tasks with varying center-of-mass objects; RL-based, not imitation learning

title: RationalVLA: A Rational Vision-Language-Action Model with Dual System

claims.claim: A dual-system VLA (high-level VLM + low-level manipulation policy linked via learnable latent embeddings) that reasons over instructions and rejects infeasible/defective commands outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the RAMA benchmark by a 14.5% higher success rate and 0.94 average task length, while maintaining competitive performance on standard manipulation tasks; real-world trials confirm effectiveness
claims.direction: favors dual-system language conditioning with explicit instruction-feasibility reasoning over single-stream language-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: new RAMA benchmark (14,000+ samples with defective instructions) plus real-world trials

title: X-Diffusion: Training Diffusion Policies on Cross-Embodiment Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: X-Diffusion (based on Ambient Diffusion, which treats human actions as noisy counterparts of robot actions and only incorporates them at high-noise timesteps) improves average success rates by 16% over naive co-training and manual data filtering across five real-world manipulation tasks, allowing effective use of easy-to-collect human video without sacrificing robot feasibility
claims.direction: favors selectively incorporating human-video demonstrations at high-noise diffusion timesteps over naive co-training or manual filtering, for boosting diffusion-policy performance with scarce robot data
claims.conditions: real-world, five manipulation tasks, diffusion policy trained with mixed human-video + robot demonstration data

why_deep_read: Gives a specific, quantified real-world benefit (+16%) of a principled method for mixing human video with our (50-100) robot demos in diffusion-policy training, directly relevant to whether/how we should supplement our teleop data with human video for the pumpkin task.

title: BlockVLA: Accelerating Autoregressive VLA via Block Diffusion Finetuning

claims.claim: Adapting a pretrained autoregressive VLA into a block-diffusion policy (parallel denoising within blocks, autoregressive across blocks, with prefix KV-cache reuse) achieves 3.3x inference acceleration over standard discrete diffusion baselines and faster training convergence, especially in complex long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors block-diffusion decoding over both pure autoregressive and standard full discrete-diffusion decoding, to cut inference latency while retaining long-horizon performance
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks only (LIBERO and SimplerEnv), not validated on real hardware in the abstract

title: HeteroGenManip: Generalizable Manipulation For Heterogeneous Object Interactions

claims.claim: A two-stage framework that decouples initial grasp (via structural-prior-guided contact alignment) from interaction execution (via category-routed diffusion policies) achieves an average 31% performance improvement in simulation on broad object-type settings and a 36.7% gain across four real-world tasks with different interaction types, versus end-to-end baselines
claims.direction: favors decoupling grasp localization from interaction-trajectory generation (two-stage) over end-to-end single-model manipulation policies for generalization across heterogeneous object categories
claims.conditions: sim + real-world (four real-world tasks)

title: FingerViP: Learning Real-World Dexterous Manipulation with Fingertip Visual Perception

claims.claim: Adding miniature fingertip cameras (multi-view, close-range) to a multi-fingered hand, combined with a diffusion whole-body policy conditioned on third-view + multi-view fingertip vision, achieves a 56.6% relative improvement in average success rate over a baseline using only an external third-view camera and a wrist-mounted camera, including tasks with occlusion (retrieving objects behind a curtain)
claims.direction: favors adding close-range/occlusion-resistant camera viewpoints beyond scene+wrist cameras when occlusion is a failure mode
claims.conditions: real-world, multi-fingered dexterous hand (not a simple 2-finger gripper), diffusion policy

title: Bridging the Embodiment Gap: Disentangled Cross-Embodiment Video Editing

claims.claim: A generative framework that disentangles task and embodiment representations (dual contrastive objective) and injects them into a frozen video diffusion model can synthesize a coherent robot execution video from a single human demonstration without paired cross-embodiment data, generating 'temporally consistent and morphologically accurate' synthetic robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors disentangled generative video editing for synthesizing robot-specific training demonstrations from human video over directly co-training on unedited human video
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no quantitative success-rate numbers given; generative/synthetic data method, real deployment not stated in abstract

title: $\pi_0$-EqM: Equilibrium Matching for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Control

claims.claim: Standard flow-matching action decoders in VLAs are deployed with fixed sampling horizons, limiting state-dependent compute and temporal reuse across control cycles; replacing the flow-matching expert in pi_0 with an Equilibrium Matching (EqM) decoder, under a matched 300-step compute budget, improves RoboTwin average success from 40.4% to 50.2% across 19 tasks and is competitive on LIBERO (87.0% on LIBERO-10)
claims.direction: favors equilibrium-matching decoders (which allow variable/state-dependent inference depth and temporal reuse) over fixed-horizon flow-matching decoders for closed-loop control
claims.conditions: RoboTwin (19 tasks) and LIBERO benchmarks (sim), built on the pi_0 VLA stack, matched compute budget

claims.claim: Two threshold scans reveal a task-dependent, non-monotonic relation between residual error and task success (the 'stationarity-executability gap'), suggesting inference depth/compute allocation during closed-loop control is itself a policy-design choice, not just a fixed hyperparameter
claims.direction: favors treating inference-time compute/horizon as a tunable, task-dependent part of the control loop rather than a fixed chunking/horizon setting
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin, LIBERO), pi_0 backbone

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries under async inference (Q10) and horizon/chunking design (Q06): the equilibrium-matching decoder framing (state-dependent compute reuse across control cycles) could directly address our latency/smoothness problem, and is built on the same pi_0-style backbone family we may be adapting from.

title: GeoProp: Grounding Robot State in Vision for Generalist Manipulation

claims.claim: A lightweight, plug-and-play adapter (GeoProp) that geometrically grounds proprioception in vision (projecting robot state onto the image plane, sampling localized visual features, injecting spatial priors via FiLM, and sampling look-ahead features at a predicted short-horizon coordinate) improves Diffusion Policy by 8.7% on 63 simulation tasks and pi_0 by 4.0% on a RoboTwin subset, and yields a 10.6% average real-world gain across both policy families, while adding only 2-3% to parameter count
claims.direction: favors explicit geometric/visual grounding of proprioception (rather than treating it as an isolated vector fused naively) for observation-history/state fusion, with minimal extra compute
claims.conditions: 67 tasks total across sim (63 tasks) and real world; tested on two different policy families (Diffusion Policy and pi_0)

why_deep_read: Near-zero-cost (2-3% extra parameters) architectural change with consistent real-world gains across two different policy families (Diffusion Policy and pi_0) -- directly actionable for our compute-constrained laptop setup to better fuse proprioception with our two camera views.

title: GWM-VLA: Geometry-Aware Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Learning

claims.claim: A geometry-aware latent world model that jointly aggregates multi-view observations (VGGT-based) and predicts next-step patch tokens of a target view (using the wrist view to emphasize end-effector/gripper-object interaction), with shared latent-action representations conditioning both the world model and a flow-matching action head, 'demonstrates effectiveness and robustness' in both simulation and real-world environments, addressing degradation of VLAs under visual/environmental shifts
claims.direction: favors geometry-aware, multi-view-consistent latent world modeling (as opposed to per-view-independent dynamics prediction) as an auxiliary objective for robustness under visual shift
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: vla.simd: Efficient CPU Inference for Language-Conditioned Manipulation

claims.claim: vla.simd, a CPU inference engine (shared SIMD micro-kernels, reusable computation), achieves ~1.4x median speedup over compiled PyTorch references across six policies and four CPUs while preserving fp32 numerical fidelity; the authors' own ACT-based policy IMPACT (cached text representations, language-modulated visual features) supplies at least 30 actions/s on a Raspberry Pi 5 (33.5 actions/s fp32, 81.2 actions/s int8 after thermal soak), and achieves 76.4% mean success across four LIBERO suites without robot pretraining (GPU eval)
claims.direction: favors compact ACT-style policies with cached/precomputed language features plus CPU-optimized inference kernels over GPU-only large VLA inference, for real-time low-compute deployment
claims.conditions: IMPACT policy tested directly on an SO-101 arm, and SmolVLA tested on a UR10e with Robotiq gripper -- CPU deployment demonstrated on two robot embodiments including our exact robot

why_deep_read: This paper tests directly on an SO-101 arm (our exact robot) and specifically targets the latency problem we reported (2s inference on a laptop); its IMPACT policy design (cached text, language-modulated visual features, ACT-based) and CPU/int8 inference numbers are maximally applicable and should be read in full for implementation details.

title: Rational Inverse Reasoning

claims.claim: Casting few-shot imitation as inference over latent 'explanation programs' (VLM-proposed, planner-grounded task-and-motion-planning specifications) rather than direct behavior reproduction lets a real Franka FR3 recover transferable task structure from as little as one demonstration, outperforming VLM-planning baselines lacking explicit rationality/planning-grounded inference by 34 and 28 percentage points in one-shot and three-shot settings respectively, when generalizing to substantially new layouts and object sets
claims.direction: favors inferring latent task intent/structure (rather than reproducing low-level motion) for generalization from very few demonstrations to new layouts/objects
claims.conditions: real Franka FR3 robot plus a 2D reasoning benchmark; one- and three-shot demonstration settings; relies on a VLM + hierarchical TAMP planner rather than a learned low-level visuomotor policy

title: MoTVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Unified Fast-Slow Reasoning

claims.claim: A mixture-of-transformers VLA where a domain-expert transformer generates fast, domain-specific reasoning (e.g. robot motion decomposition) conditioning the action expert, avoids the significant inference latency of full explicit reasoning while still improving language steerability, confirmed across NLP benchmarks, robotic simulation, and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors a fast-slow mixture-of-transformers split (domain-specific fast reasoning conditioning the action head) over either no-reasoning policies (limited steerability) or full explicit-reasoning policies (high latency)
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative superiority claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: SARM: Stage-Aware Reward Modeling for Long Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A stage-aware video-based reward model (predicting task stage + fine-grained progress from language subtask annotations) used to filter and reweight demonstrations (Reward-Aligned Behavior Cloning) dramatically improves downstream policy success on T-shirt folding: 83% success from the flattened state and 67% from the crumpled state, versus 8% and 0% with vanilla behavior cloning on the same (inconsistent-quality) demonstration data
claims.direction: favors reward-based demonstration filtering/reweighting over naive behavior cloning when demonstration quality is inconsistent, especially for long-horizon contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world rollouts and human validation; long-horizon deformable-object task (T-shirt folding)

title: Enhancement of Position Accuracy via DPB-Embedded ACT Model for Fine-Grained Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding a Dynamic Position Bias (DPB) module to ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers) to enhance cross-scale feature capture and multimodal alignment yields 'significant performance improvements' over the original ACT model and other baselines on Cube Transfer and Bimanual Insertion tasks
claims.direction: favors augmenting ACT's action-chunking transformer with a dynamic position-bias module for improved spatial perception and multimodal fusion
claims.conditions: Aloha simulation platform only; qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: DreamPlan: Efficient Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Planners via Video World Models

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a VLM planner entirely within an action-conditioned video world model's 'imagination' (trained on sub-optimal zero-shot-VLM-collected exploratory data) via RL, rather than costly real-world rollouts, 'significantly improves manipulation success rates' including for deformable-object manipulation, without large-scale real-world data collection
claims.direction: favors using a learned video world model as a surrogate training environment (auxiliary/world-model objective) over direct costly real-world RL fine-tuning
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no exact numbers given; focuses on high-level VLM planner rather than low-level visuomotor policy

title: BridgeACT: Bridging Human Demonstrations to Robot Actions via Unified Tool-Target Affordances

claims.claim: BridgeACT learns manipulation directly from human videos with NO robot demonstration data, by modeling an embodiment-agnostic affordance representation (where to grasp + task-conditioned 3D motion affordance) mapped to robot actions via a grasping module and lightweight closed-loop motion controller; real-world experiments show it outperforms prior baselines and generalizes to unseen objects, scenes, and viewpoints
claims.direction: favors affordance-based transfer from human video (zero robot demonstrations) over methods requiring robot demonstration data for downstream adaptation
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: Seeing Farther and Smarter: Value-Guided Multi-Path Reflection for VLM Policy Optimization

claims.claim: Decoupling state evaluation (advantage estimation via a scalable critic + beam search over multiple future paths) from action generation, plus a lightweight confidence-based early-exit trigger that invokes reflection only when necessary, improves success rate by 24.6% over SOTA baselines on diverse multi-stage manipulation tasks while reducing inference time by 56.5%
claims.direction: favors decoupled critic-guided reflection with selective (confidence-gated) invocation over always-on single-greedy-trajectory reflective planning, for both accuracy and latency
claims.conditions: unseen multi-stage robotic manipulation tasks; sim/real not specified in abstract; VLM-based high-level planner rather than low-level visuomotor policy

title: Robot Self-Improvement via Human-Video Dynamics Models

claims.claim: Embodiment-agnostic action/dynamics/value representations learned from human videos enable a training-free Dynamics-Guided Action Correction (DGAC) method that treats each robot failure as a query for proposing and ranking corrective actions, improving success rates from 40% to 81% across seven real-world manipulation tasks spanning a mobile manipulator and a static manipulator arm, across multiple policy backbones
claims.direction: favors using human-video-derived dynamics/value priors for training-free failure correction/recovery over leaving base policies to fail without correction, i.e. treating failures as supervision rather than discarding them
claims.conditions: real-world, seven manipulation tasks, cross-embodiment (mobile + static arm), multiple policy backbones, training-free at deployment

why_deep_read: Very large real-world improvement (40% -> 81% success) from a training-free correction method usable with our existing policy backbone, directly relevant to recovering from the kinds of failures we observe (lighting/object/camera shift) without needing to collect new demonstrations -- worth reading in full for implementation feasibility on our SO-101 setup.

title: $\pi\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies

claims.claim: Action-chunking flow policies normally run open-loop because replanning is too slow (large backbone + many denoising steps), leaving committed actions stale; piR2 splits conditioning into a fast channel (proprioception, updated every tick) and an asynchronously-updated slow channel (vision-language features), plus a latency-adaptive flow schedule (in-flight actions as inpainting conditioning, one denoising step per call) that lets one trained model adapt to varying hardware latency -- applied to GR00T-N1.7 on a real xArm6+XHand platform, it replans ~4x faster (~25Hz on an A5000 GPU, fresh observation every 40ms) and improves success rate by up to 23% in simulation and 30% in the real world over the strongest baseline
claims.direction: favors splitting fast (proprioceptive) and slow (vision-language) conditioning channels with a latency-adaptive, single-step-per-call flow schedule over standard fixed-horizon open-loop action-chunk execution, to fix staleness/jerkiness from committed stale actions
claims.conditions: real xArm6+XHand platform and simulation; built on GR00T-N1.7 pretrained backbone; minimal architecture modification, finetuned from a pretrained policy

why_deep_read: This paper's stated problem (open-loop action chunks going stale under perception-to-action latency, causing jerkiness) is almost exactly our reported failure (jerky motion at chunk boundaries with async inference, ~2s latency); its fast/slow conditioning split and latency-adaptive one-step flow schedule are a concrete, quantified (4x faster replanning, +23-30% success) candidate fix worth reading in full for adaptation to our laptop GPU.

title: Vision Language Models are In-Context Value Learners

claims.claim: Generative Value Learning (GVL) poses value estimation as a temporal-ordering problem over shuffled video frames (rather than direct progress prediction), enabling a VLM to zero-shot/few-shot predict effective task-progress values for more than 300 distinct real-world tasks across diverse robot platforms without any robot- or task-specific training; this supports downstream applications including dataset filtering, success detection, and advantage-weighted regression for policy learning, and permits in-context learning from heterogeneous embodiments including human videos
claims.direction: favors reframing VLM value/progress estimation as temporal ordering (vs. naive per-frame scoring) to get better zero-shot value functions usable for data curation and policy training, without extra model training
claims.conditions: 300+ real-world tasks across diverse robot platforms, zero training/finetuning; general capability paper rather than a controlled ablation with numeric task-success deltas

title: SViP: Sequencing Bimanual Visuomotor Policies with Object-Centric Motion Primitives

claims.claim: Using only 20 real-world demonstrations, partitioned via a semantic scene-graph monitor into bimanual/unimanual segments to train a switching-condition generator for parameterized scripted primitives, SViP enables visuomotor policies to generalize across out-of-distribution initial conditions without needing object pose estimators, and outperforms state-of-the-art generative imitation-learning methods in real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors decomposing visuomotor policies into TAMP-integrated scripted primitives (guided by a small number of demonstrations) over end-to-end generative IL policies for OOD robustness with very few demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation, only 20 demonstrations, previously unseen tasks handled via automatic primitive discovery

title: Learning Task-Sufficient World Models by Synergizing Agentic Exploration and Structured Modeling

claims.claim: Distilling compact, task-sufficient (rather than generic high-dimensional) latent representations via a closed-loop synergy between active agentic exploration and structured world-model learning improves sample efficiency and generalization -- including across skills, object-skill compositions, and previously unseen tasks -- on standard continuous-control and robotic-manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors compact task-sufficient latent world-model representations over generic high-dimensional visual embeddings for auxiliary world-model objectives
claims.conditions: standard continuous-control and robotic-manipulation benchmarks (sim), qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: Compliance for Free: Learning Identifiable Impedance via Bilateral Teleoperation

claims.claim: Four-channel bilateral teleoperation (leader arm as a separate measurement of intended equilibrium) makes per-axis stiffness/compliance identifiable by regression using only joint-torque sensing already on the manipulator, yielding per-timestep compliance labels at zero extra annotation cost; fine-tuning a VLA to emit stiffness alongside pose was the only policy (of five compared) whose contact force changed appropriately when the instruction asked for a firm vs normal wipe (6.4N normal vs 9.1N firm RMS, Cohen's d=0.89, p=0.023) on a real Franka Research 3 wiping task
claims.direction: favors extracting free compliance/force supervision from bilateral leader-follower teleoperation data (rather than requiring dedicated force/tactile hardware) to enable force-aware action prediction
claims.conditions: real Franka Research 3, contact-rich wiping task, bilateral (leader-follower) teleoperation setup -- directly analogous to our leader/follower teleop hardware

why_deep_read: Our data collection already uses leader/follower bilateral teleoperation on Feetech servos -- this paper shows how to extract compliance/force labels 'for free' from that exact teleop structure (via joint-torque sensing) to improve contact-rich manipulation, which is directly and cheaply applicable to our pumpkin pick-place setup without new hardware.

title: Improving Generalization Ability of Robotic Imitation Learning by Resolving Causal Confusion in Observations

claims.claim: Explicitly learning the causal relationship between observation components and expert actions (via a causal structural function learned by intervention on the imitation-learning policy, without requiring disentangled feature representations) and embedding this into Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) 'considerably mitigates' the generalization problem caused by causal confusion under domain shift
claims.direction: favors explicit causal-structure learning over standard observation-history conditioning to avoid causal confusion (e.g. copycat problem) in ACT-style policies
claims.conditions: simulation only (ALOHA bimanual arms in Mujoco); qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: ESPADA: Execution Speedup via Semantics Aware Demonstration Data Downsampling for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Segmenting demonstrations with a VLM-LLM pipeline plus 3D gripper-object relations (from a single annotated episode, propagated via Dynamic Time Warping) enables aggressive downsampling of non-critical demonstration segments while preserving precision-critical phases, achieving approximately a 2x speed-up in execution while maintaining success rates, with no extra data, architecture changes, or retraining required, tested with both ACT and Diffusion Policy baselines in simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors semantics-aware (task-phase-dependent) temporal downsampling of demonstrations over uniform/heuristic speed-up methods, to remove the slow conservative tempo of human teleop demonstrations without hurting task success
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, tested directly on ACT and Diffusion Policy (both plausible candidates for our action head)

why_deep_read: Directly actionable and low-cost: requires no retraining or architecture change, tested on ACT and Diffusion Policy specifically (our candidate action heads), and addresses execution speed/tempo which is closely related to our jerky-motion/latency concerns -- worth reading in full for how segment labels are produced and how well the 2x speedup holds for a low-cost single-arm setup.

title: PartInstruct: Part-level Instruction Following for Fine-grained Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Evaluating several state-of-the-art robot manipulation approaches (end-to-end vision-language policy learning and bi-level planning models) on a new part-level instruction-following benchmark (513 objects, 1302 fine-grained tasks) reveals that current models 'struggle to robustly ground part concepts and predict actions in 3D space, and face challenges when manipulating object parts in long-horizon tasks'
claims.direction: highlights a limitation of current language-conditioned policies (both end-to-end and bi-level planning) at fine-grained part-level grounding, suggesting simple task-level language conditioning may be insufficient for fine-grained instructions
claims.conditions: simulated 3D benchmark (10,000+ expert demonstrations synthesized in simulator); evaluates existing SOTA methods rather than proposing a new architecture

title: RoboCade: Gamifying Robot Data Collection

claims.claim: Co-training robot policies with data collected via a gamified remote teleoperation platform (visual feedback, sound effects, progress bars, leaderboards) improves success rate on non-gamified target tasks by +16-56%, and a user study shows novice users find the gamified platform significantly more enjoyable (+24%) than a standard non-gamified teleoperation platform
claims.direction: favors gamified remote teleoperation interfaces to scale up demonstration collection (more engaging, and co-training with the extra data improves downstream task success) over standard non-gamified teleoperation
claims.conditions: three manipulation tasks (spatial arrangement, scanning, insertion); real demonstration data collected through the platform; crowd/novice-user data collection rather than single expert operator

title: Q-Transformer: Scalable Offline Reinforcement Learning via Autoregressive Q-Functions

claims.claim: Discretizing each action dimension and representing per-dimension Q-values as separate tokens (enabling high-capacity sequence modeling for Q-learning) lets Q-Transformer outperform prior offline RL algorithms and imitation learning techniques on a large, diverse real-world robotic manipulation task suite
claims.direction: favors autoregressive discrete-token Q-function modeling (offline RL) over standard imitation learning techniques on large diverse real-world task suites when autonomously collected data is also available
claims.conditions: real-world, large diverse manipulation task suite, combines human demonstrations with autonomously collected data; offline RL rather than pure behavior cloning

title: Temporally Masked Diffusion: An Effective Behavioral Cloning Method in Robot Action Sequence Generation

claims.claim: TM-Diff (a diffusion policy augmented with a self-supervised temporal-masking reconstruction auxiliary task, via a time-series diffusion Transformer) particularly benefits small-sample demonstration datasets, achieving a 6.2% improvement in success rate on the square task and a 10.1% improvement in target coverage ratio on the Push-T task, using only 50 demonstration samples, compared to standard diffusion-based policies and observation-to-action methods
claims.direction: favors adding a temporal-masking self-supervised auxiliary reconstruction objective to diffusion policies over standard diffusion/observation-to-action baselines, specifically in low-demonstration-count regimes
claims.conditions: six complex manipulation tasks, specifically tested at 50 demonstrations (directly matching our ~50-100 demo budget); sim/real not explicitly stated but framed for IIoT/home-service/healthcare deployment

why_deep_read: Explicitly evaluated at 50 demonstrations -- the low end of our planned demo count -- with a lightweight self-supervised auxiliary objective (temporal masking) added to diffusion policy; worth reading in full to see if this transfers to our exact data regime and action-chunking setup.

title: GDLAM: Group-Disentangled Latent Action Model for Highly Disentangled Embodied Pretraining

claims.claim: Factorizing a latent action model's code into causally-distinct groups (via independent variational bottlenecks, spatially gated routing, and information-geometric disentanglement objectives) rather than a single entangled latent vector improves label-free disentanglement metrics by wide margins, and pretraining with GDLAM 'substantially improves task success rates over previous methods across multiple simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic manipulation tasks' for both world models and VLA policies
claims.direction: favors disentangled/factorized latent-action pretraining representations over monolithic entangled latent action codes for downstream VLA policy performance
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real-world robotic manipulation tasks; qualitative 'substantially improves' claim without exact numbers

title: MOP: A Multimodal Object-Aware Policy for Robotic Manipulation via Geometry-Guided Fusion and Trajectory Prediction

claims.claim: A geometry-guided fusion module that adaptively integrates 2D semantic features with 3D geometry (rather than relying on 3D geometry alone, which struggles with small objects due to geometric sparsity), plus a lightweight auxiliary Object Position Prediction module trained with labels from a cost-effective vision-based tracker (replacing expensive motion-capture hardware), significantly outperforms baselines across 56 simulated tasks (3 benchmarks) with higher success rates, lower variance, and efficient inference, further validated on 4 real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors fusing 2D semantic features with 3D geometry (rather than 3D-only) for small-object/high-precision manipulation, plus cheap auxiliary position-prediction supervision from vision trackers instead of motion capture
claims.conditions: 56 simulated tasks across 3 benchmarks, 4 real-world tasks

title: ARM: Advantage Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: A cost-effective tri-state (Progressive/Regressive/Stagnant) demonstration labeling strategy, used to train an Advantage Reward Model that enables adaptive action-reward reweighting (filtering suboptimal samples, including fragmented DAgger-style data) in an offline RL pipeline, achieves a 99.4% success rate on a challenging long-horizon towel-folding task, with improved stability and data efficiency over current VLA baselines and near-zero human intervention during policy training
claims.direction: favors relative (tri-state) advantage labeling over dense absolute progress rewards for filtering/reweighting imperfect demonstrations, especially for tasks with non-monotonic behaviors like backtracking/recovery
claims.conditions: long-horizon deformable-object task (towel folding); comparison against 'current VLA baselines'; real-world/sim not explicit but framed as practical deployment

title: Adapt3R: Adaptive 3D Scene Representation for Domain Transfer in Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Standard 3D scene representations from calibrated RGBD cameras show only modest improvement under unseen embodiments and camera viewpoints; Adapt3R instead uses a pretrained 2D backbone for semantic information and 3D purely to localize that information relative to the end-effector, and when trained end-to-end with a variety of imitation-learning algorithms across 93 simulated and 6 real tasks, it maintains those algorithms' learning capacity while enabling zero-shot transfer to novel embodiments and camera poses
claims.direction: favors using 3D geometry only as a localization medium for 2D semantic features (rather than learning 3D representations directly) to achieve viewpoint/camera-pose robustness, over standard RGBD 3D scene encoders
claims.conditions: 93 simulated tasks + 6 real tasks; tested across multiple different IL algorithms as a general-purpose observation encoder; explicitly tests unseen embodiments and camera viewpoints

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported failure mode of 'a slightly moved camera': shows standard 3D/RGBD encoders give only modest robustness while a 2D-semantic + 3D-localization design gives zero-shot transfer to novel camera poses across a large multi-task evaluation -- worth reading in full for how to build this encoder for our RealSense + wrist camera setup.

title: Inference-Time Enhancement of Generative Robot Policies via Predictive World Modeling

claims.claim: Generative predictive control (GPC) augments a frozen, already-trained diffusion policy at deployment time with an action-conditioned predictive world model that ranks/refines action proposals via model-based look-ahead (no retraining or fine-tuning); across diverse manipulation tasks (state- and vision-based, sim and real hardware), GPC 'consistently outperforms standard behavior cloning and compares favorably to other inference-time adaptation baselines'
claims.direction: favors adding inference-time predictive-world-model look-ahead planning on top of a frozen diffusion policy over retraining/fine-tuning, for behavior improvement without added training cost
claims.conditions: sim and real hardware, multiple manipulation tasks; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given; adds inference-time compute (relevant tradeoff against our latency constraints)

title: RoBridge: A Hierarchical Architecture Bridging Cognition and Execution for General Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: RoBridge (a hierarchical architecture: VLM-based high-level cognitive planner + invariant operable representation as a symbolic bridge + RL-based guided embodied agent) achieves a 75% success rate on new tasks and an 83% average success rate in sim-to-real generalization using only five real-world data samples per task
claims.direction: favors a hierarchical cognition/execution split (VLM planner + symbolic bridge + RL executor) over end-to-end policies to drastically cut the number of real-world demonstrations needed per task for sim-to-real generalization
claims.conditions: sim-to-real generalization, five real-world demonstrations per task, new/unseen tasks

why_deep_read: Reports sim-to-real generalization with only 5 real demonstrations per task (an order of magnitude below our 50-100 demo budget) -- worth reading in full to see whether the hierarchical cognition/symbolic-bridge/execution architecture could be adapted to cut our own data-collection burden.

title: Environment-Aware Adaptive Pruning with Interleaved Inference Orchestration for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: EcoVLA, a training-free, plug-and-play adaptive channel-pruning framework (exploiting temporal consistency of the physical environment plus FLOPs-bubble-aware interleaved scheduling), achieves up to 1.60x inference speedup with only a 0.4% drop in success rate, and 2.18x speedup with only 0.5% degradation when combined with token pruning, validated on real-world robots across diverse VLA models and benchmarks
claims.direction: favors training-free adaptive pruning (channel + token, environment-aware) over static pruning or retraining-based compression for cutting VLA inference latency with minimal accuracy loss
claims.conditions: real-world robots, multiple VLA models and benchmarks, orthogonal/combinable with other VLA acceleration methods

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our ~2s inference latency problem with a training-free, plug-and-play method (no retraining needed) giving a quantified 1.6-2.18x speedup at <0.5% success-rate cost, validated on real robots -- highly actionable and worth reading in full for applicability to our laptop GPU deployment.

title: ViVa: A Video-Generative Value Model for Robot Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: ViVa repurposes a pretrained video generator to jointly predict future proprioception and a scalar value (grounding value estimation in anticipated embodiment dynamics rather than static VLM snapshots), achieving state-of-the-art metric-based value-estimation results across three tasks and, when integrated into RECAP, an average success rate of 80%
claims.direction: favors video-generative (spatiotemporal, embodiment-grounded) value/future-prediction models over standard VLM-based value functions for long-horizon task-progress estimation and policy improvement
claims.conditions: three tasks, integrated into a policy-improvement pipeline (RECAP); sim/real unspecified in abstract

title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization

claims.claim: Zero-WAM, a causal video-action model trained with an in-context future-chunk-prediction objective (which suppresses shortcuts from seen tasks) on 74.2K automatically-generated human-robot in-context-learning pairs (HumanGen), executes unseen manipulation tasks by following a human video as in-context guidance, achieving 47.0% average success on seven unseen RoboTwin 2.0 tasks -- a 29.5 percentage-point absolute improvement over the strongest video-action baseline -- and generalizes in real-world evaluations to unseen multi-object, long-horizon, and fine-grained-insertion task configurations
claims.direction: favors specifying novel tasks via an in-context human-video prompt (rather than fine-tuning or language instruction alone) plus an objective that suppresses seen-task shortcuts, for zero-shot cross-task generalization
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0, 7 unseen tasks) and real-world; requires an automatic human-video-to-robot-trajectory pairing pipeline

title: ForceDelta-VLA: Distilling Force-Conditioned ActionCorrections for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Distilling an explicit force-correction target (from paired predictions of a frozen teacher's force-conditioned vs. force-agnostic modes) into a lightweight policy that adjusts reference actions using recent force history without regenerating full action chunks achieves an 82.2% mean success rate across nine single-arm and bimanual contact-rich tasks, versus 54.4% for the original ForceVLA baseline, while reducing mean peak contact force over successful trials by approximately 26%
claims.direction: favors decomposing force-aware action prediction into a reusable reference action plus a distilled correction term (rather than a single combined force-conditioned prediction) for contact-rich manipulation
claims.conditions: nine single-arm and bimanual contact-rich tasks across two platforms; requires force/contact sensing not present in our vision-only setup

title: From Passive Video to Editable Experience: Physically Grounded Experience Synthesis for Embodied Intelligence

claims.claim: Pegasus translates human demonstration videos into robot-learnable data via a graph-based intermediate representation (Task Graph -> Affordance/Constraint Graphs -> Robot Planning Graph) plus a closed-loop physics verifier (kinematic feasibility, collision, joint limits) that filters invalid generations, demonstrating 'reliable cross-embodiment translation' across egocentric benchmarks (GTEA Gaze+, EPIC-KITCHENS-100) and diverse robot embodiments
claims.direction: favors structured graph-based knowledge transfer (with physics-based filtering) over raw video-conditioned generation for turning internet human videos into usable robot training data
claims.conditions: egocentric manipulation benchmarks and diverse robot embodiments; qualitative claim (Task Correctness/Executability/State Consistency/Learnability metrics), no single headline success-rate number given

title: Human2Any: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Constraint-Aware Compositional Planning

claims.claim: Human2Any learns reusable object-centric interaction priors from human videos (representing manipulation as object-object interaction motion, abstracting away embodiment-specific details) and composes them with robot-side feasibility reasoning/motion planning, validated in real-world experiments on both a Franka tabletop setup and an RBY-1 humanoid mobile robot, 'demonstrating robust interaction-centric manipulation without real-world robot training data'
claims.direction: favors object-centric interaction-motion priors from human video (composed with classical feasibility/motion planning) over requiring robot demonstrations in the target task context
claims.conditions: real-world, two different robot embodiments (Franka arm, RBY-1 humanoid); qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: Vision-based manipulation from single human video with open-world object graphs

claims.claim: ORION extracts an object-centric manipulation plan from a single RGB or RGB-D human video (captured on daily mobile devices) and derives a policy conditioned on that plan, achieving an average 74.4% success rate across varied short- and long-horizon tasks and demonstration types, while generalizing to deployment environments with varying visual backgrounds, camera angles, spatial layouts, and novel object instances
claims.direction: favors extracting an explicit object-centric plan from a single video demonstration (rather than many teleop demonstrations) to achieve robustness to background, camera-angle, and novel-object variation
claims.conditions: real-world, single human-video demonstrations (RGB or RGB-D), both short- and long-horizon tasks

why_deep_read: Directly matches our stated failure modes (breaks under new lighting/background, different-looking object, moved camera) and reports a quantified 74.4% success generalizing across exactly those variation types, using only a single video demonstration -- worth reading in full to assess if the object-centric plan-extraction approach is adaptable to our SO-101 setup with far fewer demos than we currently plan to collect.

title: Beyond Monotonic Progress: Retry-Supervised Value Learning for Robot Imitation

claims.claim: ReTVL learns a mistake-sensitive value function from mixed-quality demonstrations by combining global progress calibration with local pairwise preference learning induced by sparsely-annotated retry keypoints, then reweights demonstration chunks for behavior cloning; on real-robot manipulation tasks this produces more fine-grained value estimates than progress-based baselines and improves imitation learning from imperfect demonstrations
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling and leveraging corrective/retry segments in demonstrations (rather than treating them as noise) for reweighting behavior-cloning data
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation tasks; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation

claims.claim: RA-VLA integrates behavior-aligned context retrieval with a grounded execution pipeline for training-free in-context imitation learning, addressing the 'adaptation bottleneck' of prior retrieval-based ICIL methods, and achieves superior success rates and computational efficiency versus baselines on LIBERO and a real-world UR5e environment
claims.direction: favors behavior-aligned retrieval (over superficial retrieval mechanisms) for training-free test-time task adaptation, preserving inference efficiency
claims.conditions: LIBERO (sim) + real-world UR5e; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: GraphPoint: Semantic Entity Graphs and Point Trajectories for Compositional Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: GraphPoint connects semantic entity graphs (organizing gripper/objects by semantic roles, conditioned on action types/modifiers) to geometric control via predicted future gripper point trajectories, validated on the new CoMani benchmark which specifically controls for visual shortcuts (matched initial scenes, single semantic factor changes) to test whether policies generalize compositionally by language rather than by memorized visual-action mappings
claims.direction: favors explicit semantic-graph + point-trajectory conditioning over implicit visual-action mapping for compositional instruction-dependent generalization (reusing familiar entities/actions across new combinations)
claims.conditions: new CoMani benchmark (sim), qualitative effectiveness validation via ablations, no absolute success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: MOMA-Force: Visual-Force Imitation for Real-World Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining representation learning (perception) with imitation learning (motion generation) and admittance whole-body control (system robustness) lets a mobile manipulator learn multiple contact-rich tasks with higher success rates and smaller/less variable contact forces in a real household setting, compared to baseline methods without force imitation or without the admittance control component
claims.direction: favors hybrid imitation-learning + classical admittance/force control (rather than pure end-to-end learned actions) for contact-rich task robustness and controllability
claims.conditions: real household setting, mobile manipulator, multiple contact-rich tasks; qualitative comparative claim ('outperforms', 'smaller'), no exact percentages given

title: Watch and Act: Learning Robotic Manipulation From Visual Demonstration

claims.claim: A 'watch-and-act' pipeline that translates a demonstration video into a command sentence (captioning module) and then executes it via an instance-segmentation + affordance-prediction manipulation module validates each module's superiority over existing methods separately, and demonstrates the full system on a real robotic arm across diverse scenarios, without requiring paired observation-action demonstration data
claims.direction: favors learning from unlabeled visual demonstration (video-to-caption-to-affordance) over standard observation-action-pair imitation learning, reducing the need for action-labeled demonstrations
claims.conditions: real robotic arm, diverse scenarios; qualitative comparative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: DINOBot: Robot Manipulation via Retrieval and Alignment with Vision Foundation Models

claims.claim: Leveraging both image-level and pixel-level features from a Vision Transformer trained with DINO (retrieving the most visually-similar demonstrated object, then aligning the end-effector to a novel object using pixel-level correspondences) enables 'unprecedented learning efficiency and generalisation' in real-world everyday manipulation tasks, without any task-specific training of the vision backbone
claims.direction: favors using frozen DINO-pretrained ViT features (both image- and pixel-level) for retrieval-and-alignment style imitation learning over training a vision encoder from scratch or using non-self-supervised pretrained encoders
claims.conditions: real-world, everyday tasks, frozen pretrained DINO features (no fine-tuning of the vision backbone), few demonstrations implied by retrieval-based approach

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our Q03 vision-encoder choice (DINOv2 is explicitly one of the pretraining options we're considering) with a real-world, training-free retrieval-and-alignment method claiming strong data efficiency and generalization -- worth reading in full for whether this frozen-DINO retrieval approach could substitute for or complement full policy fine-tuning on our 50-100 demos.

title: KWE-ASG: Key Waypoint Extraction and Action Sequence Generation-based Imitation Learning for Dual-arm-hand Manipulation

claims.claim: Predicting key waypoints and shortening the decision horizon during training (rather than dense per-step action prediction) mitigates error accumulation in long-horizon dual-arm-hand manipulation, achieving 84% success on cup pouring and 76% on cable winding on a real dual-arm robot, significantly outperforming other imitation learning methods; a tactile ablation additionally shows tactile feedback significantly improves task success rates
claims.direction: favors key-waypoint-based action generation (shortened effective decision horizon) over dense step-wise action chunking for reducing compounding error in long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: real dual-arm-hand robot, two long-horizon contact-rich tasks; includes tactile sensing not present in our vision-only setup

title: MAPLE: Encoding Dexterous Robotic Manipulation Priors Learned From Egocentric Videos

claims.claim: Learning features to predict object contact points and hand poses at contact time from large-scale egocentric human video, then using these features to train downstream manipulation policies, demonstrates effectiveness across 4 existing simulation benchmarks plus 4 newly designed challenging tasks, with benefits further confirmed in real-world experiments on a 17-DoF dexterous hand
claims.direction: favors pretraining manipulation-relevant contact-point/hand-pose features from egocentric human video before downstream policy training, over training vision features purely on robot demonstration data
claims.conditions: sim (8 benchmark tasks total) + real-world (17-DoF dexterous hand); qualitative effectiveness claim

title: SwitchVLA: Execution-Aware Task Switching for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Modeling task switching as behavior modulation conditioned on execution state (demonstrations segmented into temporally-grounded contact phases, policy infers task progress and adjusts behavior) via a multi-behavior conditional policy enables smooth, reactive task switching without external planners or additional switch-specific data, outperforming prior VLA baselines in both task success rate and interaction naturalness in simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors execution-state-conditioned behavior modulation over static single-intent policies for handling mid-execution instruction changes
claims.conditions: sim + real-world robotic manipulation; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: RoboCurate: Harnessing Diversity with Action-Verified Neural Trajectory for Robot Learning

claims.claim: Filtering synthetic (video-generative) robot data by replaying predicted actions in a simulator and measuring motion consistency between the simulator rollout and the generated video (rather than relying on VLM-based video-quality judgment alone), combined with image-to-image and video-to-video augmentation for observation/appearance diversity, yields substantial relative success-rate improvements over using real data only: +70.1% on GR-1 Tabletop (300 demos), +16.1% on DexMimicGen pretraining, and +179.9% on real-world ALLEX humanoid dexterous manipulation
claims.direction: favors simulation-replay-verified synthetic data filtering (over unfiltered generative synthetic data or VLM-only quality checks) for augmenting scarce real demonstrations
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (GR-1 Tabletop 300 demos, DexMimicGen) plus a challenging real-world humanoid dexterous manipulation setting

title: See like a Robot: Robot-Centric Pointmaps for VLA Models
