claims.claim: Transforming depth-lifted pointmaps into a robot-centric frame (end-effector origin, robot-base-aligned axes) and adding their features to RGB tokens (without increasing token count) improves average success over RGB-only pi_0.5 by 6.4 percentage points on 24 sim RoboCasa tasks and by 32.5 percentage points on four real-world tasks, exceeding the strongest evaluated 3D-augmented baseline (PointVLA) by 3.5 and 23.7 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors robot-centric (end-effector-origin, base-aligned) pointmap/depth representations over camera-frame 3D representations or RGB-only input, especially for real-world performance
claims.conditions: 24 RoboCasa sim tasks + 4 real-world tasks; built on pi_0.5; ablations show benefit grows as training camera viewpoints diversify

claims.claim: Ablations show end-effector-centered coordinates are most effective when combined with robot-base-aligned axes, and that the benefit of robot-centric pointmaps over camera-frame representations grows as training viewpoints diversify
claims.direction: favors robot-centric (viewpoint-invariant) 3D coordinate representations over camera-frame-dependent ones specifically for robustness across varied camera placements
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Joint-Guided Spatial and Semantic Sensitive Diffusion Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing depth and semantic maps with RGB and proprioceptive inputs (rather than relying on generic CV-pretrained visual encoders alone), via a Joint-Guided Dynamic Attention module that keeps computational overhead controlled, yields 'consistent performance gains over state-of-the-art methods' across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit depth+semantic map fusion (structured spatial-semantic features) over generic pretrained visual encoders alone for diffusion-policy manipulation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: World Pilot: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models with World-Action Priors

claims.claim: Augmenting a VLA with priors from a World-Action Model via two pathways -- Latent Steering (conditioning perception on a scene-evolution latent) and Action Steering (an anticipated trajectory as motion prior) -- attains a state-of-the-art 84.7% total success rate on the LIBERO-Plus zero-shot OOD benchmark and the highest success rate on every real-robot setting across four manipulation tasks, with the largest margins specifically under shifts in viewpoint, geometry, deformable state, and pose; the scene-evolution prior remains effective even from a video-pretrained world model that has not been action-post-trained
claims.direction: favors steering a VLA's perception and action generation with world-model-derived scene-evolution and motion priors (rather than relying on static image-text semantic grounding alone) for robustness specifically to viewpoint/geometry/pose shifts
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus (sim, zero-shot OOD) + four real-robot manipulation tasks; works even with a video-only pretrained world model (no action post-training needed)

title: Evolving Cache Schedules for Fast Diffusion Policy Inference

claims.claim: EVO, a training-free acceleration framework that globally schedules cache refreshes across the block-timestep lattice via evolutionary search (with redundancy-aware initialization and target-conditioned early stopping), preserves near-full closed-loop rollout performance on manipulation benchmarks while achieving up to 8.05x action-generation speedup and reducing FLOPs from 15.77G to as low as 1.96G, and can be directly plugged into pretrained diffusion policies without retraining
claims.direction: favors non-uniform, search-optimized cache-reuse schedules over uniform training-free caching (or full denoising) for accelerating diffusion-policy inference with minimal performance loss
claims.conditions: manipulation benchmarks (sim presumably), applied to pretrained diffusion policies, no retraining required

why_deep_read: Training-free, retraining-free, and directly plugs into diffusion policy (one of our candidate action heads) with an 8x inference speedup -- this is one of the most directly actionable fixes for our stated 2s-inference-latency problem and deserves a full read for implementation on our laptop GPU.

title: HarvestPoint-ACT: Explicit Target Selection and Harvest-Point Conditioning for Robotic Fruit Harvesting under Occlusion

claims.claim: Making target-object selection and the exact gripper-closing point explicit (via an instance-segmentation+keypoint front end feeding an 8-dimensional harvest-point state into an Action Chunking Transformer, with re-detection/re-ranking after each attempt) rather than leaving these implicit in end-to-end ACT achieves an 88% success rate on a canopy mock-up, dropping to 75% under heavy occlusion
claims.direction: favors explicit keypoint/target-selection conditioning fed into ACT over purely implicit pixel-to-action learning, especially for picking a specific object under partial occlusion
claims.conditions: real hardware (canopy mock-up), ACT-based policy, fruit-picking task closely analogous to our pumpkin pick-and-place task

title: WLA$^3$: World Latent Action Modeling for Semantics, Dynamics, and Kinematics

claims.claim: A World Latent Action Model that learns compact local latent actions and richer transition features from synchronized multi-camera views and embodiment-state changes (reused for physical-dynamics modeling, VLM supervision via a Semantic Latent Aggregate, and joint latent-action + robot-control prediction) achieves 81.9% average success across six real-robot tasks versus 66.2% for a pi_0.5 baseline, with performance improving as generalist mid-training data scales and human videos supporting human-to-robot transfer
claims.direction: favors a unified world-latent-action representation (jointly supervised by semantics, dynamics, and kinematics, trained partly on human video) over a standard VLA baseline (pi_0.5) for real-robot task success
claims.conditions: real-robot, six tasks, compared directly against pi_0.5 baseline; benefits from human video transition supervision

title: ReMoBot: Retrieval-Based Few-Shot Imitation Learning for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: ReMoBot, a fully training-free, trajectory-conditioned retrieval framework (combining state-level similarity, history-aware trajectory alignment, and action-sequence consistency using vision foundation models), with only 20 demonstrations per task outperforms baselines trained directly on real-world data, achieving 70% success on Table Uncover and 80% on Gap Cover on a real Boston Dynamics Spot robot, and generalizes across varying robot positions, object sizes, and material properties
claims.direction: favors training-free retrieval-based few-shot imitation (using vision-foundation-model similarity/alignment) over parametric policies trained on more real-world data, for data-efficient generalization
claims.conditions: real-world (Boston Dynamics Spot) and simulation, only 20 demonstrations per task, egocentric mobile manipulation

title: SEBVS: Synthetic Event-based Visual Servoing for Robot Navigation and Manipulation

claims.claim: Transformer-based event-based robotic policies (ERPs), trained via behavior cloning on synthetic event streams generated from RGB feeds, 'consistently deliver competitive advantages' over RGB-based counterparts under challenging conditions such as motion blur, occlusion, and illumination changes, evaluated on object-following and object-detection-and-grasping tasks
claims.direction: favors event-camera-based (or synthetic-event-augmented) perception over standard RGB for robustness to illumination changes and motion blur
claims.conditions: synthetic event streams generated via v2e from RGB in Gazebo simulation; requires event-camera-like sensing not present in our RealSense RGB-D setup

title: DiTEA: Mixture-of-Experts for Vision-Language-Action Model in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing a Mixture-of-Experts module into the action head of a diffusion-based VLA (Action MoE) with a language-instruction-driven Task-Instruction Gate that routes to task-specialized experts mitigates 'skill forgetting' after multi-task fine-tuning and improves instruction-following ability, with 'excellent improvement in multi-task' performance versus baseline and other VLAs in simulation and real-world evaluation
claims.direction: favors task-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts action heads over a single shared action head for multi-task diffusion VLA fine-tuning, to reduce cross-task weight conflicts (skill forgetting)
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: A Data-Driven Learning-from-Demonstration Framework for Robotic Grasping

claims.claim: Encoding human-demonstrated grasping strategies as Dynamic Movement Primitives (parameters predicted by a neural network) plus a separate grasp-pose-estimation network, with synthetic datasets generated via data augmentation of recorded trajectories, reduces required demonstration effort while achieving a high real-world success rate on four objects with varying shapes/sizes, and allows incorporating new objects with minimal additional effort
claims.direction: favors DMP-parameterization plus trajectory-augmentation-generated synthetic data over collecting many raw demonstrations per new object, for low-effort grasp generalization
claims.conditions: real system, four objects with varying shapes/sizes; qualitative 'high success rate' claim, no exact percentage given

title: Canonical Policy: Learning Canonical 3-D Representation for SE(3)-Equivariant Policy

claims.claim: Canonical Policy grounds 3D point-cloud observations (seen and novel) in a learned canonical representation with theoretically-grounded 3D equivariance, and achieves an average improvement of 18.0% in simulation and 39.7% in real-world experiments over state-of-the-art imitation-learning policies, evaluated across 12 simulated and 4 real-world tasks with variations in object color, shape, camera viewpoint, and robot platform (16 configurations total)
claims.direction: favors canonicalized, SE(3)-equivariant 3D point-cloud representations over standard (non-canonicalized) 3D or RGB representations for generalizing to novel object appearance and camera viewpoint simultaneously
claims.conditions: 12 sim tasks + 4 real-world tasks across 16 configurations; explicitly varies object color/shape and camera viewpoint, directly matching our reported failure modes

title: Restoring the Right Stream: Training-Free OOD Robustness for Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: On LIBERO-Plus, VLA policies that solve clean tasks at high rates can fall below 30% success when the camera viewpoint or robot initial pose is perturbed; standard training-free image-stream remedies (augmenting/purifying/selecting visual observations) improve mean success by only about 3 points and leave robot-initial-state failures largely unresolved, because that perturbation shifts the proprioceptive token rather than the visual one; a proposed Gated Per-Stream Manifold Restoration wrapper (stream-specific off-manifold detection and restoration for vision vs. proprioception) improves total success by +5.3 points (vs +3.2 for image-only), raises the most fragile factor from 20% to 38%, and in an independent confirmation improves robot-initial-state success from 26.3% to 32.2% (+5.8 points, 95% CI [3.2,8.5], p<0.001)
claims.direction: favors diagnosing and separately restoring each input modality/stream (vision vs. proprioception vs. language) rather than only intervening on the visual stream, when addressing OOD robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-pose shifts in frozen VLA policies
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus benchmark (sim), training-free wrapper for a frozen policy, large controlled paired evaluations (280 + 1120 + 600 episodes) with statistical significance testing

title: X-DiffVLA: X-Embodied Diffusion Action Heads for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A diffusion-based VLA with a unified cross-embodied action head (Embodiment Forcing classifier-free guidance + Morphological Tree Diffusion to strengthen behavioral correlations across different end-effectors) achieves state-of-the-art performance with improvements of 15.3% (RoboCasa) and 12.5% (Isaac Gym) over baselines, spanning embodiments from grippers to dexterous hands, with real-world evaluations further validating robustness
claims.direction: favors a single diffusion action head with embodiment-conditioning mechanisms over embodiment-specific fine-tuned heads, for cross-embodiment transfer without per-robot fine-tuning
claims.conditions: sim (RoboCasa, Isaac Gym) plus real-world validation; cross-embodiment setting with shared robotic bases and heterogeneous end-effectors

title: NativeMEM: Native Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Repurposing a pretrained VLA's own vision encoder to compress each historical frame (per camera view) into a single memory token, appended to the input sequence so the pretrained VLA attends over long-term history with negligible latency overhead (no external planner or freshly-initialized memory module needed), boosts success rates from 32.4% to 84.0% in simulation and up to 98.7% on real robots, while maintaining low inference latency and GPU memory usage, and achieves competitive results using only 20% of the training data versus prior methods
claims.direction: favors native, in-sequence memory-token compression (reusing the existing vision encoder) over external memory modules for retaining long-horizon visual history, with large gains in both task success and data efficiency at negligible added latency
claims.conditions: sim + real robots; large magnitude gains (32.4%->84.0% sim, up to 98.7% real); explicitly reports low latency overhead and reduced training-data requirement (20% of data)

title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation

claims.claim: Formulating VLA deployment as an adaptive execution-horizon decision problem -- estimating step-wise action reliability via divergence between two flow-matching-generated trajectories under small noise perturbations, and truncating execution with a dual-threshold rule to trigger timely replanning (Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision) -- improves real-hardware task success from 55% to 60% for needle manipulation and from 55% to 80% for tissue manipulation over fixed-length open-loop VLA baselines, with largest gains in final manipulation stages
claims.direction: favors adaptive, reliability-estimated execution horizons (truncating/replanning open-loop action chunks when trajectory divergence is high) over fixed-length open-loop action-chunk execution for reducing accumulated errors under changing scene conditions
claims.conditions: real dual-arm da Vinci-like surgical robot benchmark, 600 teleoperated demonstrations, 20 trials per task setting; flow-matching-based VLA

title: 3DWay: Generalizing Robot Manipulation via 3D Consistent Waypoints

claims.claim: Predicting 3D-consistent waypoints by reformulating 3D waypoint prediction as generating multi-view-consistent 2D waypoints followed by geometric triangulation (rather than predicting trajectories directly in 2D image space or using 2D+depth, both of which leave ambiguity) 'substantially improves 3D spatial grounding and vision-language reasoning' for guiding VLA models or direct execution
claims.direction: favors multi-view-triangulated 3D waypoint prediction over single-view 2D (or 2D+depth) trajectory representations as an intermediate representation bridging VLMs and manipulation policies
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given; requires multi-view camera input

title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models

claims.claim: A high-capacity model (RT-X) trained on a standardized cross-embodiment dataset assembled from 22 different robots (527 skills, 160,266 tasks across 21 institutions) exhibits positive transfer, improving the capabilities of multiple individual robots by leveraging experience from other robot platforms
claims.direction: favors large-scale cross-embodiment pretraining (co-training across many robots' data) over training separate models per robot/environment, since it produces positive transfer to individual robots
claims.conditions: 22 real robots, large standardized dataset; foundational large-scale result, not a controlled ablation specific to low-cost/low-data settings

title: Learning Autonomous Viewpoint Adjustment from Human Demonstrations for Telemanipulation

claims.claim: A data-driven viewpoint-prediction model (trained via contrastive learning on human-demonstrated camera trajectories) autonomously adjusts a dynamic camera during telemanipulation; a user study shows it outperforms several camera control methods in control experience, reduces perceived task load compared to manual camera control, and significantly reduces task completion time for users who adopt its recommendations
claims.direction: favors learned autonomous viewpoint/camera-position adjustment (from human demonstration) over fixed or manually-controlled camera viewpoints during teleoperation-based data collection or deployment
claims.conditions: real-world robotic telemanipulation system integration, user study; about camera control during teleoperation rather than policy learning robustness per se

title: View-Invariant Policy Learning via Zero-Shot Novel View Synthesis

claims.claim: View Synthesis Augmentation (VISTA) uses zero-shot single-image novel-view-synthesis models (3D-aware scene-level priors) to augment single-viewpoint demonstration data with synthetic alternate-camera-viewpoint images; policies trained with this augmentation outperform baselines in robustness to out-of-distribution camera viewpoints in both simulated and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors synthetic novel-view-synthesis-based data augmentation over training only on the original single-viewpoint demonstration images, specifically to achieve viewpoint-invariant policies
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation tasks; zero-shot view synthesis models (no task-specific retraining of the synthesis model needed); directly targets camera-viewpoint OOD robustness

title: InternData-A1: Pioneering High-Fidelity Synthetic Data for Pre-training Generalist Policy

claims.claim: A VLA (pi_0 architecture) pre-trained entirely on a large-scale synthetic dataset (InternData-A1: 630k+ trajectories, 7,433 hours, 4 embodiments, 18 skills, 70 tasks, 227 scenes, generated via a fully-decoupled compositional simulation pipeline) matches the official real-data-pretrained pi_0 across 49 simulation tasks, 5 real-world tasks, and 4 long-horizon dexterous tasks, and exhibits zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on several challenging tasks
claims.direction: favors large-scale, diverse synthetic simulation data as a viable substitute for large-scale real-robot pretraining data (first evidence at this scale), rather than assuming real demonstration data is required for strong pretraining
claims.conditions: same architecture as pi_0; compared directly against the official real-data pi_0 model; sim benchmarks plus 5 real-world tasks and 4 real long-horizon dexterous tasks

title: Play2Perfect: What Matters in Dexterous Play Pretraining for Precise Assembly?

claims.claim: Task-agnostic RL pretraining through 'play' on diverse objects/goals (acquiring reusable manipulation priors like grasping, in-hand reorientation, pose reaching) before fine-tuning on a precise target task is 33x more sample-efficient than RL training from scratch (even with dense multi-stage rewards), achieving zero-shot sim-to-real transfer with 60% success on tight insertions (0.5mm clearance) and over 50% success on long-horizon multi-part assembly/screwing
claims.direction: favors task-agnostic play-based pretraining (acquiring general manipulation priors before specializing) over direct RL training from scratch on the target task, for sample efficiency in contact-rich precision tasks
claims.conditions: multi-fingered dexterous hand (not a simple gripper), RL-based (not imitation learning from teleop), sim pretraining with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer

title: Teaching the Teacher: Live Foundation Model and Augmented Reality Feedback for Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer

claims.claim: A learning-from-demonstration system that gives end-users live foundation-model-based textual feedback (helping decompose tasks) plus augmented-reality visual feedback (showing how well demonstrations perform/generalize) during kinesthetic demonstration collection improves the quality and generalizability of the resulting robot policies compared to AR-only, FM-only, or no feedback, in a human-subjects study across two manipulation domains
claims.direction: favors giving non-expert demonstrators real-time FM+AR guidance during data collection (rather than unguided demonstration collection) to improve demonstration quality and downstream policy generalization
claims.conditions: human-subjects study, kinesthetic teaching, two robotic manipulation domains; qualitative 'positive results' claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: Learning Hybrid-Control Policies for High-Precision In-Contact Manipulation Under Uncertainty

claims.claim: MATCH (Mode-Aware Training for Contact Handling), which learns to dynamically select between force and position control per control dimension rather than predicting end-effector pose changes alone, substantially outperforms pose-only policies on fragile peg-in-hole tasks under extreme localization uncertainty (up to 10% higher success, 5x fewer peg breaks) with equal data efficiency; in high-noise settings on a real Franka FR3, MATCH succeeds twice as often as pose policies (68% vs 33%) and applies ~30% less force than variable-impedance policies, across 1600+ sim-to-real experiments
claims.direction: favors hybrid position/force action spaces with learned per-dimension mode selection over pure pose-based action prediction for high-precision contact-rich manipulation under uncertainty
claims.conditions: real Franka FR3, fragile peg-in-hole insertion tasks, requires force/torque sensing (not confirmed present on our Feetech-servo SO-101 setup)

title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

claims.claim: Reformulating the conventional VLA V-to-L-to-A pathway (project vision into an LLM, then decode to actions) as a direct V+L-to-A mapping -- independently encoding vision and language, exchanging information via lightweight bidirectional vision-language interaction, and predicting continuous action chunks with a compact decoder -- achieves 97.7% average success on LIBERO with only 0.2B parameters, 31.2ms inference latency, and 0.9GB inference VRAM on a consumer RTX 4090, matching or outperforming substantially larger LLM-centric VLA policies
claims.direction: favors bypassing the large-LLM-as-central-interface design entirely (direct lightweight vision-language fusion into a compact action decoder) over standard LLM-centric VLA architectures, for both small model size and low latency without sacrificing (and even improving) success rate
claims.conditions: LIBERO (sim benchmark); consumer-grade GPU (RTX 4090), comparable in class to (though more powerful than) our RTX 5060 8GB laptop GPU

why_deep_read: Reports a 0.2B-parameter model achieving 97.7% success on LIBERO with 31ms latency and <1GB VRAM on a consumer GPU -- this is close to a direct blueprint for a small, fast action-head/vision-fusion architecture matching our exact constraints (RTX 5060 8GB, ~2s current latency, need for real-time smooth control); worth reading in full for the architecture details to potentially replace our SmolVLA fine-tune.

title: StreamPI: Streaming Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: StreamPI adds temporal reasoning to a single-frame VLA (pi0.5) with no additional parameters, using instruction-anchored temporal modeling (bidirectional attention within each observation-instruction pair, causal attention across pairs) and a random-interval streaming training strategy (varying the inter-frame interval, e.g. every 3 frames) that both enables faster/smoother action execution and improves robustness to frame-timing perturbations, supporting asynchronous real-robot deployment; StreamPI outperforms pi0.5 across diverse real-robot and LIBERO tasks including memory-dependent and precise-perception scenarios
claims.direction: favors explicit streaming/asynchronous-aware temporal training (with randomized inter-frame intervals) over single-frame synchronous training, to directly improve robustness to the timing mismatches that occur under real asynchronous deployment
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks + LIBERO (sim); built on pi0.5 backbone; zero additional parameters versus the single-frame baseline

why_deep_read: Directly targets the exact problem we reported (jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries under async inference): a zero-extra-parameter streaming training strategy specifically designed for robustness to frame-timing/asynchronous deployment mismatches, built on the pi0.5 family -- worth reading in full for whether the random-interval streaming training recipe can be applied to our SmolVLA fine-tune.

title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A transformer-based multimodal framework fusing RGB-D vision with robot proprioception (no dedicated tactile hardware) can infer binary contact states as a usable pseudo-tactile signal; a single contact-prediction model trained on multiple objects supports downstream RL for in-hand object reorientation and generalizes to novel objects, validated in both simulation and on a real-world robot
claims.direction: favors inferring contact from vision+proprioception (scalable, no extra hardware) as an alternative to dedicated tactile sensors for tasks needing contact-state information
claims.conditions: sim + real-world robot; validated for in-hand reorientation with a dexterous hand rather than a parallel gripper

title: $\pi_0$: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control

claims.claim: A flow-matching action-generation architecture built on top of a pre-trained vision-language model (inheriting internet-scale semantic knowledge), trained on a large diverse dataset spanning single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile-manipulator platforms, can perform zero-shot tasks after pretraining, follow language instructions, and acquire new skills via fine-tuning across a wide variety of dexterous tasks (e.g. laundry folding, table cleaning, box assembly)
claims.direction: favors flow-matching action generation on top of a pretrained VLM backbone, and large-scale cross-embodiment pretraining, as a general recipe for generalist robot policies (foundational reference architecture for the flow-matching action-head option)
claims.conditions: multiple real dexterous robot platforms; large-scale multi-embodiment pretraining dataset; largely a systems/capabilities paper rather than a controlled ablation, no specific numeric success-rate deltas given in the abstract

title: Look, Zoom, Understand: The Robotic Eyeball for Embodied Perception

claims.claim: EyeVLA, a unified autoregressive VLA that jointly reasons about perception, language, and physical pan-tilt-zoom camera control (via a hierarchical action encoding for continuous camera adjustments), is trained with only 500 real-world samples (pseudo-labeling, IoU-controlled refinement, and GRPO reinforcement learning) and achieves a 96% average task-completion rate across 50 diverse real-world scenes for acquiring the most informative camera view for a given instruction
claims.direction: favors an active, language-guided camera-control policy (deciding where/how to look, not just where to act) over passive fixed-camera perception, achievable with very little real-world training data
claims.conditions: real-world, requires a motorized pan-tilt-zoom camera (not our fixed scene camera + wrist camera setup, though conceptually relevant to active viewpoint selection)

title: GrOMP: Grasped Object Manifold Projection for Multimodal Imitation Learning of Manipulation

claims.claim: GrOMP mitigates compounding trajectory errors in imitation learning by constraining a non-rigidly grasped object to a lower-dimensional manifold learned from the same expert dataset used to train the base IL policy (with an n-arm-bandit interactive adjustment component), with a theoretical basis for improving upon the standard IL compounding-error bound, demonstrated on four precise assembly tasks using tactile feedback while remaining modality-agnostic
claims.direction: favors adding a post-hoc manifold-projection correction layer (learned from the same demonstration data, no extra demos needed) over relying on the base IL policy alone to control compounding error in precision tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, four precise assembly tasks with tactile feedback, but stated to be modality-agnostic (could apply to vision-only setups)

title: Novel Vision-Based One-Shot Adaptation of Learned Skills

claims.claim: VASO adapts a learned manipulation skill to a new environment using a single demonstration, combining visual keypoint representations, Fast-Marching-Square-inspired trajectory modeling, a VAE for grasp-pose selection, and an Elastic-Map-inspired deformation technique, achieving 'robust one-shot generalization without iterative re-planning' in both simulated and real-world dynamic, cluttered scenarios
claims.direction: favors keypoint-based one-shot skill adaptation (single new demonstration, deformation-based generalization) over retraining or iterative re-planning when facing new waypoints/constraints
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, cluttered/dynamic environments; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: HMC: Learning Heterogeneous Meta-Control for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation

claims.claim: A mixture-of-experts-style policy (HMC-Policy) that unifies position, impedance, and hybrid force-position control modalities, learned from a combination of large-scale position-only data and fine-grained force-aware demonstrations, achieves over 50% relative improvement versus baselines on a real humanoid robot for challenging contact-rich tasks like compliant table wiping and drawer opening
claims.direction: favors blending multiple control modalities (position/impedance/force) within one policy architecture over a pure positional-controller action space for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot; requires torque/impedance control capability beyond simple position control (may not directly transfer to Feetech position-servo hardware)

title: MimicIK: Real-Time Generative Inverse Kinematics from Teleoperation with FK Consistency

claims.claim: MimicIK learns smooth, robust joint-space motion priors directly from noisy human teleoperation data via conditional flow matching plus a differentiable forward-kinematics (FK) consistency loss, predicting continuous delta-joint commands; on a real-world 6-DOF robot dataset (8,848 teleoperation demonstrations) it achieves a mean position error of 4.65mm, a 10mm success rate of 92.01%, and a trajectory spike rate of only 7.99%, remaining stable near kinematic singularities where deterministic MLP baselines catastrophically diverge
claims.direction: favors learning delta-joint IK priors from teleoperation data with FK-consistency regularization (over classical numerical IK solvers or naive learned MLP/diffusion IK) for smoothness and stability under real teleop-collected data noise
claims.conditions: real-world 6-DOF robot, 8,848 teleoperation demonstrations -- directly analogous to our leader/follower teleop data collection setup

claims.claim: Compared with a UNet diffusion baseline, MimicIK improves both spatial accuracy and motion smoothness while reducing inference latency from 21.66ms to 6.74ms, enabling robust 20Hz real-time control on deployment hardware
claims.direction: favors a lightweight flow-matching-based IK model (two-step iterative refinement) over a heavier UNet-diffusion IK model for low-latency, smooth real-time control
claims.conditions: same real-world 6-DOF teleoperation dataset; deployment hardware inference benchmark

why_deep_read: This targets the low-level joint/delta-action smoothness problem directly on a real 6-DOF teleoperated robot dataset closely analogous to our SO-101 leader/follower setup, with concrete latency (6.74ms) and smoothness (7.99% spike rate) numbers -- worth reading in full for whether this IK-smoothing layer could reduce our jerky motion at chunk boundaries independent of the higher-level policy choice.

title: Diversity You Can Actually Measure: A Fast, Model-Free Diversity Metric for Robotics Datasets

claims.claim: FAKTUAL, a model-free data-curation algorithm based on signature-transform entropy over a demonstration dataset's Gram matrix (requiring no access to the policy or rollouts), selects a subset of demonstrations maximizing entropy for a given budget; across image- and state-based RoboMimic and MetaWorld benchmarks plus four real-world manipulation tasks, diversity-aware curation with FAKTUAL 'consistently improves downstream success rates over random selection' while being substantially more computationally efficient than recent robot data curation methods
claims.direction: favors explicitly measuring and maximizing demonstration-set diversity (entropy-based curation) over collecting/using a larger but less diverse or randomly-selected demonstration set, when demonstration budget is limited
claims.conditions: sim (RoboMimic, MetaWorld) plus four real-world manipulation tasks; model-free, negligible overhead relative to policy training

why_deep_read: Directly answers the 'diversity vs. count' sub-question in our Q13 with a practical, model-free, low-overhead demonstration curation tool validated on real-world tasks -- worth reading in full to see if it can help us decide which of our ~50-100 pumpkin-task demonstrations are most valuable, or guide which additional demos to collect.

title: Learning to Grasp Clothing Structural Regions for Garment Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: A neural network perception system trained with only a 10-minute video of a human manipulating shirts generalizes to other shirts regardless of texture and to other collared garment types, and the resulting grasping strategy achieves 92%, 80%, and 50% success rates for one folded, one crumpled, and three crumpled garments respectively, considerably outperforming baselines that ignore structural/part-level information
claims.direction: favors training a structural/part-aware perception module from a very small amount of demonstration video over generic end-to-end grasping baselines, for deformable-object manipulation generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, open-loop control policy built on the perception+grasping strategy; only 10 minutes of demonstration video used to train perception

title: DiffTOP: Differentiable Trajectory Optimization for Deep Reinforcement and Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Using differentiable trajectory optimization (with learned cost and dynamics functions, trained end-to-end by differentiating the policy-gradient loss through the optimization process) as the policy/action representation outperforms prior state-of-the-art feed-forward policy classes, Energy-Based Models, and Diffusion Policy across 35 imitation-learning manipulation tasks with high-dimensional image and point-cloud inputs (and 15 model-based RL tasks)
claims.direction: favors differentiable trajectory optimization as an action-generation head over standard feed-forward, EBM, or diffusion-based action heads for imitation learning with high-dimensional visual observations
claims.conditions: broad benchmark suite (35 IL tasks + 15 RL tasks), image and point-cloud observation modalities, sim (task suites, real-world not specified in abstract)

title: EmbodiedMAE: A Unified 3D Multi-Modal Representation for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A multi-modal masked autoencoder (EmbodiedMAE) that jointly learns RGB, depth, and point-cloud representations via stochastic masking and cross-modal fusion, trained on an enhanced DROID-3D dataset, 'consistently outperforms state-of-the-art vision foundation models in both training efficiency and final performance' across 70 simulation tasks and 20 real-world manipulation tasks on two robot platforms, exhibiting strong scaling behavior with model size
claims.direction: favors a unified multi-modal (RGB+depth+point-cloud) pretrained representation over single-modality pretrained vision foundation models (e.g., RGB-only DINOv2/CLIP-style encoders) for tabletop manipulation where spatial perception is critical
claims.conditions: 70 sim tasks + 20 real-world tasks across two robot platforms; requires depth/point-cloud input alongside RGB (available given our RealSense depth capability)

title: ConRFT: A Reinforced Fine-tuning Method for VLA Models via Consistency Policy

claims.claim: ConRFT, a reinforced fine-tuning approach combining offline (behavior cloning + Q-learning on a small demonstration set) and online (consistency-policy-based, human-intervention-guided) fine-tuning with a unified consistency-based training objective, addresses the failure of supervised fine-tuning under 'limited, inconsistent demonstrations, especially in contact-rich environments'; across eight diverse real-world manipulation tasks it achieves 96.3% average success within 45-90 minutes of online fine-tuning, a 144% improvement in success rate and 1.9x shorter episode length over prior supervised (behavior-cloning-only) fine-tuning methods
claims.direction: favors reinforcement-learning-based (offline+online, human-intervention-assisted) fine-tuning of a VLA over pure supervised fine-tuning when demonstrations are limited and inconsistent, especially for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world, eight diverse manipulation tasks, small initial demonstration sets, 45-90 minutes of online fine-tuning with human safety interventions

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our exact stated problem -- 'limited, inconsistent demonstrations, especially in contact-rich environments' -- with an extremely large reported real-world improvement (144% success-rate gain, 96.3% average success across 8 tasks) from a moderate (45-90 min) online RL fine-tuning stage on top of a small demo set; worth reading in full for feasibility of adding an online consistency-policy RL fine-tuning stage to our SmolVLA pipeline.

title: Joint Flow Trajectory Optimization For Feasible Robot Motion Generation from Video Demonstrations

claims.claim: Rather than directly imitating human hand motions from video, JFTO treats human video demonstrations as object-centric guides and extends flow matching to SE(3) for probabilistic (density-aware, mode-avoiding) modeling of object trajectories, jointly optimizing grasp-pose feasibility, trajectory likelihood, and collision-free execution within robot kinematics, validated in both simulation and real-world experiments across diverse manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors object-centric (rather than hand-motion-imitating) video-based learning-from-demonstration, using SE(3) flow matching to capture multimodal demonstrated trajectories, for feasible cross-embodiment robot motion generation from video
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative validation claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: DEPT-BT: Learning Parameterized and Revisable Behavior Trees From a Single Demonstration

claims.claim: DEPT-BT transforms a single demonstration into a parameterized, executable behavior tree using anchor-based parameterized skill operators (decoupling skills from the specific demonstration objects) and a verify-revise closed-loop mechanism for symbolic conditions; across four manipulation tasks it achieves an overall success rate of ~90%, 95% success when transferring skills to novel objects (versus 0% for the baseline), and reduces failure-recovery time by 64% compared to full re-demonstration
claims.direction: favors object-decoupled, parameterized single-demonstration behavior-tree representations over instance-bound learned policies, for generalizing to novel objects and enabling fast failure recovery without new demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world (implied), four manipulation tasks; structured/symbolic representation rather than an end-to-end neural policy

title: Embodied Multimodal Grounding for Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation via Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting

claims.claim: A system integrating active multi-view Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting, reachability-aware base positioning, and a diffusion-based VLA (with 3D semantic cues injected only into late action-expert blocks to preserve pretrained action priors) achieves, in 50-trial real-robot evaluations, 60% long-horizon success (vs. 40% PointVLA, 28% DexVLA), 74% success in heavy clutter (vs. 52%/46% for single-view/PointVLA variants), 75% success under a 75cm camera height shift, and eliminates photo-induced false grasps
claims.direction: favors an explicit, refreshable 3D semantic scene representation (Gaussian Splatting) injected late into a diffusion VLA's action-expert blocks over standard 2D/implicit 3D representations, for robustness to clutter, occlusion, viewpoint/height shift, and false-positive grasps from photos
claims.conditions: real-robot, 50-trial evaluations, mobile manipulation setting (more complex than our fixed-base setup), compared directly against PointVLA and DexVLA baselines

title: Prompt-Responsive Object Retrieval with Memory-Augmented Student-Teacher Learning

claims.claim: Combining a promptable foundation model (SAM2) as a perception backbone to infer the object of interest from user prompts, with a memory-augmented student-teacher framework that uses the temporal sequence of imperfect detections for implicit state estimation, successfully learns prompt-responsive dexterous manipulation policies for picking objects from cluttered scenes
claims.direction: favors combining promptable foundation-model perception with memory-augmented state estimation (to handle imperfect/noisy detections over time) over relying on a single-frame detection for prompt-conditioned manipulation in clutter
claims.conditions: demonstrated on picking from cluttered scenes; qualitative success claim, no exact numbers given

title: On the Generalization Capabilities, Design Choices and Limitations of Keypoint Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Keypoint Imitation Learning (KIL), using visual-foundation-model one-shot keypoint extraction as an intermediate representation, achieves a 75% overall success rate across five tasks over 2000+ real-world rollouts, significantly outperforming an RGB-only baseline (47%) and performing on par with S2-diffusion (73%), confirming KIL as a data-efficient approach, though it does not outperform all alternative representations and inherits the limitations of its underlying foundation models
claims.direction: favors keypoint-based intermediate visual representations over raw RGB input for data-efficient generalization to unseen objects/scenes, though not necessarily superior to other structured representations like S2-diffusion
claims.conditions: real-world, five tasks, over 2000 rollouts; also extends to multi-object-instance tasks and analyzes foundation-model limitations

title: InfiNoVA: Infinite Novel View Augmentation for Viewpoint Invariant Robot Policies

claims.claim: InfiNoVA reconstructs each manipulation trajectory as a time-varying 3D Gaussian representation and renders novel observations from sampled camera poses (preserving state-action correspondence), producing a dense distribution of geometrically-consistent training views from synchronized multi-camera demonstrations; across four real-world manipulation tasks, policies trained with InfiNoVA achieve 5.4x higher average success under unseen randomized viewpoints than both VISTA-based generative augmentation and the unaugmented policy, and 1.7x higher success than training directly on all five physical camera views
claims.direction: favors dense, explicit 3D-Gaussian-based geometric view augmentation over both generative (diffusion-style) novel-view augmentation and simply collecting more physical camera viewpoints, for achieving camera-viewpoint-robust policies without changing the policy architecture
claims.conditions: real-world, four manipulation tasks, synchronized multi-camera demonstrations required to build the 3D Gaussian representation

why_deep_read: Reports an exceptionally large (5.4x) improvement in robustness to unseen camera viewpoints -- directly and quantitatively addressing our 'a slightly moved camera' failure mode -- and claims this augmentation beats even collecting more physical camera views; worth reading in full to assess whether the multi-camera 3D-Gaussian reconstruction step is feasible with our single fixed camera + wrist camera setup (may require adding temporary extra viewpoints during data collection only).

title: Towards a Data Flywheel for Embodied Intelligence in Logistics

claims.claim: WM-DAgger, a World-Model-based data aggregation framework, synthesizes out-of-distribution recovery data for robust imitation learning, as part of a data-centric 'flywheel' that converts daily logistics operations into reusable data assets and feeds deployment feedback back into policy improvement
claims.direction: favors using learned world models to synthesize OOD recovery demonstrations (rather than only collecting more in-distribution demonstrations) to improve imitation-learning robustness
claims.conditions: industrial logistics deployment context; early-stage/positional description, no controlled quantitative comparison given

title: NPU Offloading of a Frozen Visual Encoder for Robot Policy Training

claims.claim: Offloading a frozen visual encoder's forward pass (INT8, on a low-power NPU) while training the action-expert head in FP32 on the GPU reduces training energy per sample by 17.1% (offloading ResNet18 + 1 layer) to 27.9% (offloading ResNet18 + 4 layers), at the cost of 15.2-37.7% longer training time and a 0.44-1.89 percentage-point drop in policy success rate (93.33% GPU-only vs. 91.44-92.89% with NPU offloading), evaluated over 4,500 simulator rollouts
claims.direction: favors NPU-offloading of a frozen visual encoder during training as a viable energy/compute tradeoff (small success-rate cost) when GPU memory or energy is constrained, over always running the frozen encoder on GPU
claims.conditions: sim (300 seeds x 15 policies = 4,500 rollouts); requires an available NPU accelerator (e.g., Mobilint Aries2) alongside the training GPU (RTX 5060 Ti in the paper, close to our RTX 5060 laptop GPU)

title: LIBERO-VPro: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Visual Robustness of Robotic Foundation Models

claims.claim: Evaluating three VLAs and three World-Action Models across ~196,000 simulated episodes plus 200 real-world rollouts on a Franka Research 3, across four robustness dimensions (Visual Evidence Degradation, Camera Staleness, Visual Source Consistency, Task-Relevant Scene Variation; 12 challenge categories, 96 settings), finds models often remain successful despite severe object-level occlusion, yet degrade sharply when local interaction cues are disrupted or familiar spatial priors are violated; they are also highly sensitive to stale or missing observations and struggle when changed task preconditions require behavioral adaptation, with VLAs and WAMs showing distinct, architecture-dependent robustness profiles
claims.direction: shows that visual robustness is multi-dimensional and not well predicted by nominal (clean-condition) benchmark performance -- occlusion robustness does not imply robustness to camera staleness or local-cue disruption, contradicting the assumption that a single robustness number generalizes across perturbation types
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO-VPro, ~196,000 episodes) plus 200 real-world rollouts on Franka Research 3; evaluates 3 VLAs and 3 WAMs

title: Proleptic Temporal Ensemble for Improving the Speed of Robot Tasks Generated by Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A 'proleptic' temporal ensemble method that executes future actions ahead of the demonstrator's original pace (using existing demonstration data and pre-trained policies, requiring no additional computation and easy to implement) achieves up to a 3x increase in task execution speed while maintaining a high success rate, validated in real-world robotic block color-sorting experiments, compared to the standard Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) temporal ensembling approach
claims.direction: favors a proleptic (forward-shifted) temporal ensembling scheme over standard ACT-style temporal ensembling when the demonstrator's execution speed (not the robot's capability) is the bottleneck, for imitation-learning policies limited by conservative human demonstration pace
claims.conditions: real-world robot experiments (block color sorting); directly compared against ACT, one of our candidate action-chunking architectures; requires no additional training/computation

why_deep_read: Directly targets our Q06 sub-question on temporal ensembling with a real-world, ACT-comparison result (3x speedup, high success maintained) requiring no retraining -- a strong, low-risk candidate technique for reducing the 'jerky/slow' feel of our demonstrations-paced policy, worth reading in full for implementation details.

title: Extended residual learning with one-shot imitation learning for robotic assembly in semi-structured environment

claims.claim: OEC-IRRL combines an object-embodiment-centric task representation, a single-demonstration imitation-learned base policy (via-point movement primitives for generalization), and residual reinforcement learning for uncertainty-aware refinement; requiring only a single demonstration and less than 1.2 hours of environment interaction, it improves assembly success rates by 46% and reduces assembly time by 25% versus baseline residual-RL approaches that rely on hand-designed base policies or extensive demonstrations
claims.direction: favors combining a single-demonstration structured base policy with residual RL refinement over either hand-designed base policies or purely demonstration-heavy imitation learning, for semi-structured assembly tasks
claims.conditions: real-world (implied), single demonstration, less than 1.2h of online interaction

title: CLASP: General-Purpose Clothes Manipulation with Semantic Keypoints

claims.claim: Using sparse semantic keypoints (e.g. 'left sleeve', 'right shoulder') as an intermediate representation connecting VLM-based high-level task planning with keypoint-conditioned low-level manipulation skills, CLASP 'outperforms state-of-the-art baseline methods on multiple tasks across diverse clothes types' in simulation, with further real-world confirmation on a Franka dual-arm system across four distinct tasks
claims.direction: favors semantic (named, language-groundable) keypoints as the intermediate representation bridging language-conditioned planning and low-level skill execution, over generic geometric or learned latent representations, for cross-task/cross-object-type generalization
claims.conditions: sim + real-world (Franka dual-arm), deformable object (clothes) domain; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: ReWiND: Language-Guided Rewards Teach Robot Policies without New Demonstrations

claims.claim: ReWiND learns a data-efficient, language-conditioned reward function from a small demonstration dataset, pretrains a language-conditioned policy offline with these rewards, and then fine-tunes on unseen task variations using minimal online interaction (no new per-task demonstrations); it outperforms baselines by up to 2.4x in reward generalization/policy alignment, is 2x more sample-efficient in simulation adaptation, and improves real-world pretrained bimanual policies by 5x
claims.direction: favors learning a language-conditioned reward model from an initial small demo set (then fine-tuning with RL against that reward for new task variants) over collecting new demonstrations for every task variation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world bimanual policies; language-conditioned reward and policy

title: Towards Extrinsic Dexterity Grasping in Unrestricted Environments

claims.claim: ExDiff uses a Vision-Language Model to perceive environment state and generate high-level instructions, followed by a Goal-Conditioned Action Diffusion model (conditioned on high-level instructions and cumulative rewards) to predict low-level action sequences for grasping large/flat 'ungraspable' objects via extrinsic dexterity (e.g. using walls/table edges); simulation and real-world deployment show it generalizes to previously unseen target objects and scenes
claims.direction: favors VLM-perceived high-level instructions conditioning a goal-conditioned diffusion action model over task-specific hand-crafted policies for extrinsic-dexterity grasping generalization
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: BT-TL-DMPs: A Novel Robot TAMP Framework Combining Behavior Tree, Temporal Logic and Dynamical Movement Primitives

claims.claim: An STL-constrained DMP optimization method that adapts learned Dynamical Movement Primitives to satisfy formally-specified spatiotemporal task constraints (while preserving the essential dynamics learned from demonstrations), combined with Behavior-Tree-based high-level decision structure derived from Signal Temporal Logic specifications, 'effectively bridges the symbolic-motion gap' for generalizing learned skills to novel long-horizon scenarios, validated in simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors DMP-based motion primitives constrained by formal temporal-logic specifications (rather than pure end-to-end learned chunking) for generalizing learned motions to new long-horizon task/constraint combinations
claims.conditions: sim + real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: CoPL: Counterfactual Offline Policy Learning via Large Language Models

claims.claim: CoPL uses an LLM to generate full counterfactual trajectories (states, actions, and their temporal evolution) from real trajectory seeds by rewriting the original goal into a semantically-valid but behaviorally-distinct counterfactual goal, then repairs/filters and merges these with real offline data; this improves generalization on unseen tasks under semantic and linguistic shifts, including a 55.8% relative improvement (17.2% to 26.8% success rate) on the CLEVR-Robot CF-Easy setting
claims.direction: favors LLM-generated full counterfactual trajectory augmentation (not just relabeling instructions/actions) over standard offline-data relabeling for improving generalization to behaviorally-distinct unseen goals
claims.conditions: sim (CLEVR-Robot benchmark), offline RL setting rather than direct imitation learning

title: FODMP: Fast One-Step Diffusion of Movement Primitives Generation for Time-Dependent Robot Actions

claims.claim: Standard action-chunking diffusion policies (e.g. ManiCM) predict short reactive motion segments but cannot capture time-dependent motion primitives (e.g. spring-damper-like acceleration/deceleration profiles); Movement Primitive Diffusion (MPD) parameterizes full trajectories via Probabilistic DMPs but has prohibitively high multi-step diffusion inference latency; FODMP distills diffusion into the ProDMP parameter space with a single-step decoder, retaining temporal structure while running up to 10x faster than MPD and 7x faster than action-chunking diffusion policies, matching or exceeding their success rates on MetaWorld and ManiSkill
claims.direction: favors single-step-distilled movement-primitive parameterization over both short-horizon action-chunking diffusion and full multi-step trajectory-diffusion, to get both temporal structure (dynamic acceleration/deceleration) and low inference latency simultaneously
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (MetaWorld, ManiSkill); demonstrates value via a fast-ball-catching task requiring real-time high-speed reaction that action-chunking diffusion and MPD are both too slow for

title: Build on Priors: Vision-Language-Guided Neuro-Symbolic Imitation Learning for Data-Efficient Real-World Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A neuro-symbolic framework autonomously constructs symbolic planning domains and data-efficient control policies from as few as one to thirty unannotated skill demonstrations (segmenting demonstrations, using a VLM to classify skills and build a state-transition graph, then synthesizing a PDDL domain via Answer Set Programming), learning policies at the control-reference level (smoother/less noisy target) rather than raw actuator signals, and enables real-world data augmentation by projecting a single demonstration onto other objects in the scene; validated on a real industrial forklift and cross-platform on a Kinova Gen3 arm
claims.direction: favors autonomously-constructed symbolic/skill abstractions from very few (1-30) unannotated demonstrations, plus control-reference-level (not raw-actuator) policy learning and single-demo object-projection augmentation, over large-demonstration end-to-end policy learning
claims.conditions: real industrial forklift (statistically rigorous trials) and a Kinova Gen3 arm across two standard benchmarks; cross-platform generality demonstrated

title: Beyond Imitation: Reinforcement Learning-Based Sim-Real Co-Training for VLA Models

claims.claim: An RL-based sim-real co-training framework (SFT warm-start on mixed real+sim demos, then RL fine-tuning in simulation with an auxiliary supervised loss on real data to prevent catastrophic forgetting) yields consistent improvements over both real-only fine-tuning and SFT-based sim-real co-training on four real-world tabletop manipulation tasks, with two VLA architectures (OpenVLA, pi0.5): +24% real-world success for OpenVLA and +20% for pi0.5, plus stronger generalization to unseen task variations and improved real-world data efficiency
claims.direction: favors RL-based (rather than purely supervised) sim-real co-training, with an anchoring loss on real data, for extracting more value from simulation without sacrificing real-world performance
claims.conditions: real-world, four tabletop manipulation tasks, tested on both OpenVLA and pi0.5 architectures

title: SafeFlowMPC: Predictive and Safe Trajectory Planning for Robot Manipulators with Learning-based Policies

claims.claim: SafeFlowMPC combines a learned flow-matching policy with online model-predictive-control optimization (a suboptimal MPC formulation designed for real-time execution) to guarantee safety at all times while retaining the flexibility/generalization of learned policies; it achieves strong performance in three real-world experiments on a KUKA 7-DoF manipulator, including two grasping experiments and a dynamic human-robot object handover
claims.direction: favors combining a learned flow-matching action generator with an online safety-guaranteeing MPC layer over either pure learned policies (no safety guarantee) or pure optimization-based control (insufficient flexibility/generalization)
claims.conditions: real-world, KUKA 7-DoF manipulator, includes a dynamic human-robot handover task; qualitative 'strong performance' claim, no exact numbers given

title: Robometer: Scaling General-Purpose Robotic Reward Models via Trajectory Comparisons

claims.claim: ROBOMETER combines frame-level progress supervision with trajectory-level pairwise-preference supervision (trained on RBM-1M, over one million multi-embodiment trajectories including abundant suboptimal/failed trajectories) to learn a generalizable reward model that 'improves downstream robot learning performance' and supports imitation-learning data filtering/retrieval and automated failure detection, validated across benchmarks and real-world evaluations at multiple institutions
claims.direction: favors combining frame-level and trajectory-comparison reward supervision (learning from both successful and failed trajectories at scale) over frame-progress-only reward models for downstream data filtering and RL/IL improvement
claims.conditions: large multi-embodiment dataset (1M trajectories, 21 embodiments); real-world evaluations at 3 institutions; qualitative claim, no single headline success-rate delta given

title: Efficient Sim-to-Real Transfer of World-Action Models from Synthetic Priors

claims.claim: A world-action model (built on Cosmos Policy, a video-diffusion model adapted for visuomotor control) trained purely on ~800 synthetic demonstrations per task (with extensive domain randomization, no real demonstrations at all) achieves a 35% average success rate when deployed zero-shot on a real Franka robot across object-lifting, drawer-opening, and pick-and-place tasks -- reported as the first successful sim-to-real transfer of a world-action model for robotic manipulation
claims.direction: favors training world-action models purely on synthetic/simulated data with domain randomization (zero real demonstrations) as a viable, if still modest-performing, path to real-robot deployment
claims.conditions: real Franka robot, zero-shot deployment, no real demonstrations, ~800 synthetic demos/task; modest absolute success rate (35%)

title: Probabilistic Reachable-Action Verification of Visuomotor Policies via Set-Based Training

claims.claim: By freezing the visual encoder and confining set propagation to a low-dimensional interface (calibrated from held-out camera-pose perturbations), then training with zonotope-based set propagation and rollout-level conformal calibration, set-based training reduces the probabilistic reachable-action radius (a formal measure of how much actions can deviate under camera-pose perturbation) while preserving closed-loop task capability, outperforming behavior-only, observational-consistency, and pointwise-adversarial training controls
claims.direction: favors explicit set-based/reachability-aware training targeting camera-pose perturbation robustness over standard behavior cloning or adversarial-training-style robustness methods, when a formal robustness guarantee (not just empirical success rate) is desired
claims.conditions: controlled manipulation experiments (sim/real unspecified in abstract); frozen visual encoder assumed

title: DriftingVLA: Native One-Step Vision-Language-Action Generation via Per-Dimension Temporal Drifting

claims.claim: DriftingVLA generates a complete action chunk with a single action-expert forward pass (a distribution-drifting objective learning a direct noise-to-action-chunk mapping, rather than a flow field requiring iterative integration), achieving 98.32% success on LIBERO, 81.09% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 77.67% across six real-world single- and dual-arm tasks, outperforming evaluated multi-step flow-matching and one-step VLA baselines while delivering a 3.36x speedup in action-chunk generation
claims.direction: favors native one-step (distribution-drifting) action-chunk generation over multi-step flow-matching decoding for VLA action heads, to cut inference latency without sacrificing (and in this case improving) task success
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0) + real-world (six single/dual-arm tasks); Per-Dimension Temporal Drifting models each action dimension's full temporal trajectory separately during training while still generating the full action chunk jointly at inference

title: GRAPPA: Generalizing and Adapting Robot Policies via Online Agentic Guidance

claims.claim: An agentic framework of role-specialized conversational agents (advisor, grounding, monitoring, robotic) iteratively grounds a base robot policy on relevant objects in the environment and uses visuomotor cues to shift the policy's action distribution toward more desirable states online, guiding manipulation policies to 'significantly higher success rates' in both simulation and real-world experiments, without additional human demonstrations or extensive exploration, and remaining agnostic to robot hardware
claims.direction: favors online, foundation-model-driven agentic guidance/self-improvement of a base policy (no new demonstrations needed) over collecting additional task-specific demonstrations for adapting to new environments
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given; hardware-agnostic framework

title: Semantically controllable augmentations for generalizable robot learning

claims.claim: A generative augmentation framework using pre-trained image-text generative models (web-scale priors) for semantically controllable data augmentation rapidly multiplies robot datasets with rich variations at no extra human-collection cost; policies trained on these augmented datasets are shown to be deployable both in simulation and unseen real-world environments (kitchens, table-tops)
claims.direction: favors generative (image-text-model-based) semantic augmentation of existing robot demonstrations over collecting additional real-world demonstrations, for boosting real-world generalization
claims.conditions: real-world deployment (kitchens, tabletops) and simulation; qualitative effectiveness claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: $\pi_{0.5}$: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization

claims.claim: pi0.5 uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks and data sources (multiple robots, high-level semantic prediction, web data, hybrid multi-modal examples combining images, language, object detections, semantic subtask prediction, and low-level actions) to enable, for the first time, an end-to-end learning-enabled robotic system performing long-horizon dexterous manipulation (e.g. cleaning a kitchen or bedroom) in entirely new homes; the authors state this kind of heterogeneous knowledge transfer 'is essential for effective generalization'
claims.direction: favors heterogeneous multi-source co-training (mixing robot data, web data, and semantic subtask supervision) over training on a single robot's demonstration data alone, for open-world generalization to entirely new environments
claims.conditions: large-scale multi-robot real-world deployment; foundational systems paper, no specific numeric ablation deltas in the abstract

title: 3D Flow Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Generating Flow in 3D Space

claims.claim: 3D Flow Diffusion Policy predicts temporal trajectories of sampled 3D query points (scene-level 3D flow) as a structured intermediate representation and conditions action generation on these interaction-aware flows within a unified diffusion architecture, achieving state-of-the-art performance across 50 MetaWorld tasks (especially medium/hard settings) and consistently outperforming prior baselines on eight real-robot contact-rich and non-prehensile tasks
claims.direction: favors scene-level 3D flow (localized point-trajectory motion cues) as an intermediate representation over direct observation-to-action mapping or global/object-centric feature compression, for contact-rich and non-prehensile manipulation
claims.conditions: sim (MetaWorld, 50 tasks) + real-world (8 tasks); contact-rich and non-prehensile scenarios specifically highlighted

title: RESample: A Robust Data Augmentation Framework via Exploratory Sampling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: RESample trains a conservative coverage function to identify real-distribution failure modes missing from standard successful demonstrations, then actively samples exploration+recovery-action trajectories to extend training-data coverage for failure recovery; on LIBERO and real-world manipulation tasks this consistently improves policy success rates, achieving up to a 12% absolute gain with no more than 20% additional samples
claims.direction: favors coverage-guided active sampling of failure-recovery trajectories (targeted at the actual deployment failure distribution) over simply adding more successful demonstrations, to improve robustness to execution deviations
claims.conditions: LIBERO (sim) + real-world manipulation tasks; targeted, budget-efficient augmentation (only up to 20% extra samples)

title: SANTS: A State-Adaptive Scheduler for World Action Models

claims.claim: For pixel-space World Action Models, the fully-denoised video is not always the best action-conditioning point; SANTS, a lightweight scheduler that jointly predicts a cumulative stopping hazard and relative noise-progression ratio (post-trained with a path-level reward on final action quality), reaches 94.4% overall success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 73.1% average success across seven real-robot tasks while reducing latency by 81.7% and 79.0% respectively relative to full video denoising
claims.direction: favors state-adaptive, early-stopped video-denoising depth (rather than always denoising to completion) for conditioning action generation in World Action Models, to preserve control benefits while removing most of the redundant inference cost
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0) + seven real-robot tasks; pixel-space WAM-style video-to-action diffusion policies

title: ReCoVLA: VLM-Guided Reward Compilation for Failure Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: ReCoVLA keeps a pretrained VLA frozen and uses an external VLM purely as a semantic reward selector (inferring failure mode/recovery stage to compile a structured reward, not to generate actions/rewards directly) for training a residual recovery policy in simulation, then deploys it zero-shot to real robots; in simulation this improves average success from 36.7% (fine-tuned pi0.5 baseline) to 66.7%, and achieves 61.7% average success in physical zero-shot sim-to-real experiments across short-horizon, long-horizon, and contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors a frozen-base-VLA-plus-residual-recovery-policy architecture (with VLM-compiled semantic rewards for recovery-policy training) over fine-tuning the base VLA directly, for handling off-nominal/failure states
claims.conditions: sim training + zero-shot sim-to-real deployment; directly compares against a fine-tuned pi0.5 baseline

title: From Flow to One Step: Real-Time Multi-Modal Trajectory Policies via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation-based Distribution Distillation

claims.claim: Distilling a Conditional Flow Matching expert into a fast single-step student via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation with a bi-directional Chamfer distance (a set-level objective promoting both mode coverage and fidelity) preserves the teacher's multi-modal action distribution in a single forward pass, avoiding the distributional collapse ('averaged trajectories') seen in prior single-step acceleration methods, and supports real-time receding-horizon re-planning with improved robustness under dynamic disturbances
claims.direction: favors distribution-preserving (set-level, mode-covering) single-step distillation over naive single-step distillation methods that collapse multimodal flow-matching action distributions into an averaged trajectory
claims.conditions: multi-view RGB, depth, point clouds, and proprioception jointly encoded; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: EgoSpeedUp: Transferring Human Manipulation Tempo to Robot Policies

claims.claim: EgoSpeedUp aligns corresponding manipulation phases between slow robot demonstrations and human demonstrations of the same task, estimates each phase's task-appropriate relative execution tempo from multiple human demonstrations, and retimes the robot demonstrations accordingly before standard behavior cloning; across two real-world manipulation tasks this improves task success rate by an average of 25 percentage points while reducing successful execution time by 36.5%
claims.direction: favors using human demonstration video as a source of phase-wise tempo/timing supervision (rather than robot-side heuristics or fixed tempo factors) to retime training demonstrations, improving both speed and success rate of the resulting behavior-cloned policy
claims.conditions: real-world, two manipulation tasks; requires paired human + robot demonstrations of the same task for tempo alignment

title: From Demonstrations to Rewards: Test-Time Prompt Optimization for VLM Reward Models

claims.claim: Demo2Reward optimizes a VLM reward model's language instruction at test time using only 3-10 demonstration trajectories (no additional model training) to reduce false-positive reward predictions while preserving true positives, consistently outperforming existing zero-/few-shot VLM reward models across simulated robotic tasks and policy backbones, with effective transfer to a real-world robotic learning scenario
claims.direction: favors test-time prompt optimization of a VLM reward model using a handful of demonstrations over zero-shot VLM reward prompting, to reduce false-positive rewards that would otherwise degrade downstream policy learning
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; 3-10 demonstration trajectories used for reward-prompt optimization, no policy retraining required

title: VINE: Taming Generative Control Policies for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: VINE reconstructs a new interpolation state at every denoising step (rather than following a single flow trajectory) to create a stable differentiable path for value-gradient propagation through flow-matching policies; despite backpropagating through all ten denoising steps end-to-end, VINE achieves stable policy improvement and 'consistently outperforms state-of-the-art RL methods' on the OGBench offline RL benchmark and a real-world robotic manipulation task
claims.direction: favors a reconstructed-interpolation sampling strategy over the vanilla flow-matching sampling strategy (designed for behavior cloning) when applying end-to-end value-gradient RL fine-tuning to flow-matching action heads
claims.conditions: OGBench (sim) + real-world manipulation task; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Dex-X: Learning Visual-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation From Human Videos with Simulated Interaction

claims.claim: DEX-X reconstructs monocular human hand-object interaction videos in simulation to recover physically-grounded tactile/contact supervision unavailable in the original video, trains a visual-tactile teacher policy (65.9% average success across six task categories in simulation), and distills it into a deployable point-cloud+tactile policy achieving 93% success on real-world cube picking and 53% on table cleaning with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and generalization to unseen object geometries
claims.direction: favors using simulation as a 'tactile completion engine' to recover missing contact supervision from human video (rather than requiring real robot-side tactile data collection) for training deployable visual-tactile policies
claims.conditions: real-world, dexterous hand-arm platform with tactile sensing (not our vision-only parallel-gripper setup); zero-shot sim-to-real transfer

title: VT-Bridge: Bridging Pretrained Foundation VLAs to VTLAs via Lightweight Residual Adaptation

claims.claim: VT-Bridge adds a lightweight, identical residual-adapter architecture (0.98M parameters) across different pretrained VLA backbones to refine actions with tactile information at robot execution frequency, requiring only up to 50 vision-tactile demonstrations per task; tested on three representative VLA backbones (pi_0, pi_0.5, and SmolVLA) across four contact-rich manipulation tasks, it raises average task completion rate from 11.7% (task-level VLA fine-tuning alone) to 62.9%
claims.direction: favors adding a small residual tactile-conditioned adapter on top of a frozen/lightly-fine-tuned pretrained VLA (rather than training a full vision-tactile-language-action model from scratch) for contact-rich manipulation, requiring only a small number of extra demonstrations
claims.conditions: tested directly on SmolVLA (our current base model) as well as pi_0 and pi_0.5; up to 50 vision-tactile demonstrations per task; requires tactile sensing hardware not currently on our SO-101 gripper

why_deep_read: Tests directly on SmolVLA -- our current base model -- and reports a very large improvement (11.7% to 62.9% task completion) from adding a tiny (0.98M parameter) residual tactile adapter trained on as few as 50 demonstrations per task; worth reading in full to assess whether adding low-cost tactile/force sensing to our SO-101 gripper and this adapter method could substantially improve our contact-rich pick-and-place performance without retraining the whole policy.

title: Modeling Dynamic Hand-Object Interactions with Applications to Human-Robot Handovers

claims.claim: Generating synthetic human-robot handover interactions to increase training diversity by 100x, a user study found no difference between policies trained on synthetic vs. real motions
claims.direction: favors synthetic interaction data (at large multiplicative scale) as an equally valid substitute for real motion-capture data for this interaction-modeling task, based on a user study showing no detectable difference
claims.conditions: human-robot handover domain, dissertation-level research combining physical simulation, RL, and sim-to-real student-teacher transfer; user-study evidence rather than task-success-rate benchmark

title: SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: SAFE learns from a generalist VLA's own internal features (which the authors find already encode sufficient high-level knowledge about task success/failure, generic across tasks) to predict a scalar failure-likelihood signal; trained on both successful and failed rollouts and evaluated on unseen tasks with OpenVLA, pi_0, and pi_0-FAST in simulated and real-world environments, SAFE achieves state-of-the-art failure-detection performance and the best accuracy/detection-time trade-off (via conformal prediction) compared to diverse baselines
claims.direction: favors probing a VLA's own internal feature space for a generic, cross-task failure signal over task-specific failure detectors, enabling timely stop/backtrack/ask-for-help behavior on unseen tasks
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, evaluated across OpenVLA, pi_0, and pi_0-FAST backbones; multitask/unseen-task generalization emphasized

title: FACTR: Force-Attending Curriculum Training for Contact-Rich Policy Learning

claims.claim: A low-cost bilateral teleoperation setup that relays external follower-arm forces back to the teacher/leader arm during data collection, combined with FACTR -- a curriculum that corrupts visual input with decreasing intensity throughout training to prevent a transformer policy from over-fitting to vision and force it to properly attend to the force modality -- significantly improves generalization to unseen objects by 43% compared to baseline approaches without the curriculum
claims.direction: favors incorporating readily-available arm force/torque feedback (via low-cost bilateral teleoperation) plus a visual-corruption curriculum that forces attention to force modality, over vision-only policies, specifically to improve generalization to novel objects
