claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost bilateral teleoperation setup (leader/follower, closely analogous to our SO-101 teleop hardware); contact-rich tasks like box pickup and dough rolling

why_deep_read: Uses a low-cost bilateral leader-follower teleoperation setup directly analogous to ours, and reports a concrete 43% generalization improvement to unseen objects (our exact stated failure mode: 'a different-looking pumpkin') from adding force feedback plus a visual-corruption curriculum; worth reading in full to assess whether our Feetech servos can supply usable force/torque signal and whether this curriculum technique is applicable to our vision-based SmolVLA fine-tune even without dedicated force sensors.

title: Fabrica: Dual-Arm Assembly of General Multi-Part Objects via Integrated Planning and Learning

claims.claim: A lightweight reinforcement learning framework that trains generalist contact-rich-assembly policies across object geometries, assembly directions, and grasp poses (guided by equivariance and residual actions obtained from a global plan, rather than human demonstrations) transfers zero-shot to the real world and achieves 80% successful steps, without domain knowledge or human demonstrations
claims.direction: favors planner-guided residual RL with equivariance (no human demonstrations required) over demonstration-based imitation learning for generalizing contact-rich manipulation across object geometries
claims.conditions: real-world, dual-arm assembly benchmark suite; zero human demonstrations used

title: NovaPlan: Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Manipulation via Closed-Loop Video Language Planning

claims.claim: NovaPlan performs zero-shot long-horizon manipulation (no prior demonstrations or task-specific training) by having a closed-loop VLM planner decompose tasks into sub-goals and monitor execution for autonomous re-planning after single-step failures, extracting task-relevant object keypoints and human hand poses from generated videos as kinematic priors (with a switching mechanism choosing the more reliable one under occlusion/depth inaccuracy) to compute low-level robot actions, validated on the Functional Manipulation Benchmark and other long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors zero-demonstration, VLM-planned closed-loop execution with video-derived keypoint/hand-pose kinematic priors over demonstration-trained policies, when no task-specific demonstrations are available
claims.conditions: real-world (implied) plus FMB; qualitative claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: Towards Robot Skill Learning and Adaptation With Gaussian Processes

claims.claim: A Gaussian-Process-based skill model with sparse via-points (preserving the demonstrated trajectory's first/second derivatives) combined with three adaptation methods (optimization agent, behavior-cloning agent, and RL agent) outperforms every benchmark in success rate across three tasks (drawer opening, cube-pushing, bar manipulation) in both simulation and hardware, while preserving the kinematic profile under large deviations from a single demonstrated skill
claims.direction: favors compact, expressive GP-based skill representations (adapted via optimization/BC/RL) over standard neural-network skill models for robust adaptation to large configuration deviations from a single demonstration
claims.conditions: sim + real hardware, three tasks, single demonstrated skill per task

title: VLM4VLA: Revisiting Vision-Language-Models in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Using a minimal adaptation pipeline (few new learnable parameters) to systematically compare how different pretrained VLMs translate into downstream VLA performance across three benchmarks, the authors find: (1) VLM initialization gives a consistent benefit over training from scratch, but (2) a VLM's general capability is a poor predictor of downstream manipulation performance, (3) fine-tuning a VLM on auxiliary embodied tasks (embodied QA, visual pointing, depth estimation) does not guarantee better downstream control, and (4) modality-level ablations identify the visual module (not the language component) of the VLM as the primary performance bottleneck -- injecting control-relevant supervision into the vision encoder yields consistent gains even when the encoder stays frozen during downstream fine-tuning
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that a more capable/general-purpose pretrained VLM backbone automatically yields a better VLA policy; instead favors focusing pretraining/adaptation effort specifically on the visual encoder's control-relevant supervision rather than on overall VLM capability or language-side improvements
claims.conditions: three benchmarks, systematic ablation across multiple VLM choices and seven auxiliary embodied fine-tuning tasks; minimal-parameter adaptation pipeline for fair comparison

why_deep_read: This directly and rigorously informs our Q03 vision-encoder decision with a counter-intuitive, well-controlled finding (visual encoder quality -- not overall VLM competence or language capability -- is the bottleneck, and general VLM capability doesn't predict downstream success); worth reading in full since it could change how we prioritize pretraining/fine-tuning effort for our SmolVLA vision backbone versus chasing a 'smarter' VLM.

title: SEVO: Semantic-Enhanced Virtual Observation for Robust VLA Manipulation via Active Illumination and Data-Centric Collection

claims.claim: Using the original ACT and SmolVLA policies on low-cost hardware, the full SEVO pipeline (body-fixed cameras covering the full workspace, active red-spectrum illumination normalizing object appearance, and real-time YOLO segmentation overlay providing a background-invariant semantic cue, plus a diversified data-collection protocol systematically varying lighting/backgrounds/distractors during teleoperation) achieves 95% grasp success with ACT and 83% with SmolVLA in the training environment, transferring to novel environments at 85% and 75% respectively; WITHOUT SEVO, the same policies achieve only 75%/70% in the training environment and collapse to 30-35% in novel environments
claims.direction: favors data-centric observation design (fixed multi-camera coverage, active illumination normalization, semantic segmentation overlay) plus diversified data collection over model/architecture changes for cross-environment robustness -- the paper explicitly concludes this, not model scaling, is what lets low-cost robots generalize
claims.conditions: real-world, two mobile platforms, target objects include transparent water bottles (visually blending with surroundings, closely analogous to our lighting-sensitive pumpkin problem); directly evaluates ACT and SmolVLA, our exact candidate architectures

why_deep_read: This is possibly the single most directly applicable paper in the batch: it evaluates ACT and SmolVLA (our current candidate/base architectures) on low-cost hardware, explicitly reproduces the 'near-zero transfer to new environments' failure we are experiencing, and shows a purely data-centric/observation fix (no architecture change) recovers most of the performance (e.g. SmolVLA 30-35% -> 75% in novel environments). Must read in full for the exact recipe (camera placement, illumination, segmentation overlay, data diversification protocol).

title: HELP: Human-Efficient Large-Scale Robot Post-Training with Rollout Segmentation

claims.claim: Specializing human roles (a Teleoperator providing high-value interventions/recovery demos, a Floor Operator monitoring/resetting a robot fleet) combined with an automatic rollout-segmentation critic (separating trajectories into progress-making, idle, failure-inducing, and recovery segments to retain only useful segments) achieves 80-95% success rates and improves task throughput by 1.7x-4.2x over the base model across four real-world manipulation tasks; under matched human-in-the-loop recovery budgets, the segmentation critic further amplifies throughput gains by 1.2x-3.43x and success-rate gains by 1.5x-3.0x over HITL-only updates
claims.direction: favors role-specialized human supervision plus automatic segmentation/filtering of mixed-quality rollout data (retaining only useful segments) over undifferentiated human-in-the-loop data collection, for maximizing policy improvement per unit of human effort
claims.conditions: real-world, four manipulation tasks, large-scale (twelve concurrent robots) post-training setting

title: Deliberate Practice: Learning Robot Skills under a Budget

claims.claim: Deliberate Practice (DP) computes a provably budget-optimal allocation of limited practice time across skills (via a bilinear program estimating both time-to-master and cumulative task-plan reward), allowing robots to optimally use a limited practice budget to acquire useful policies for long-horizon tasks, validated in simulated and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors formally optimizing which skills/demonstrations to practice/collect under a fixed budget (rather than uniform or ad hoc allocation) to maximize downstream long-horizon task performance
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, long-horizon manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Towards Generalizable Zero-Shot Manipulation via Translating Human Interaction Plans

claims.claim: A factorized approach that learns a 'human plan predictor' (future hand/object configurations) from large-scale human videos, combined with a separate 'translation' module (requiring only a small amount of in-domain robot data) that converts human plans into a plan-conditioned robot policy, achieves over 16 manipulation skills generalizing to 40 objects across 100 real-world tabletop and in-the-wild tasks, in a zero-shot manner with no deployment-time training
claims.direction: favors factorizing 'what to do' (learned from abundant human video) from 'how to translate to the robot' (learned from a small amount of in-domain data) over end-to-end robot-only imitation learning, for zero-shot generalization to novel objects
claims.conditions: real-world, 40 objects, 100 tasks; only a small amount of in-domain robot data needed for the translation module

title: Curriculum is more influential than haptic feedback when learning object manipulation

claims.claim: Using model-free RL with a simulated three-finger robotic hand to compare curriculum (combinations of lift/rotation tasks) versus haptic information (no-tactile vs. 3D-force) for learning dexterous lift-and-rotate manipulation, the choice of curriculum biases learning progression far more than the presence of haptic information; unexpectedly, learning is achieved even in the complete absence of haptic/tactile information
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that haptic/tactile feedback is necessary for learning dexterous manipulation -- curriculum design (task sequencing) matters more than adding a tactile/force sensing modality for this task
claims.conditions: simulation only, three-finger robotic hand, RL rather than imitation learning; lift-and-rotate-against-gravity task with intermittent contact

title: Self-Correcting Robot Manipulation via Gaussian-Splatted Foresight

claims.claim: Representing the current scene with 3D Gaussian Splatting and training a prediction network to forecast the future Gaussian-splat scene conditioned on planned actions, then detecting failure when the predicted future significantly deviates from real post-action observation (triggering a rollback to the previous action), integrated with the PerACT framework, outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 12.0% success rate on average across ten RLBench tasks (166 variations)
claims.direction: favors 3D-Gaussian-Splatting-based foresight prediction for failure detection and single-step rollback correction over methods without explicit future-scene prediction, for language-conditioned manipulation robustness
claims.conditions: sim only (RLBench, 10 tasks, 166 variations); built on the PerACT policy framework

title: MoMaGen: Generating Demonstrations under Soft and Hard Constraints for Multi-Step Bimanual Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Formulating automated demonstration generation as a constrained optimization problem (satisfying hard reachability constraints while balancing soft visibility constraints for an active camera) enables generation of much more diverse datasets than previous methods from a single source demonstration; policies trained on MoMaGen-generated data can then be fine-tuned with a small amount of real-world data (40 demos) for successful real-robot deployment
claims.direction: favors constrained-optimization-based automated demonstration generation (accounting for base reachability and camera visibility) over naive scene-randomization augmentation, especially for mobile/active-camera settings, to reduce needed real-world fine-tuning demos to a small number (40)
claims.conditions: four multi-step bimanual mobile manipulation tasks; real-world fine-tuning used only 40 demos (close to our own planned demo count)

title: Hierarchical Impedance, Force, and Manipulability Control for Robot Learning of Skills

claims.claim: A learning-from-demonstration framework that jointly captures motion trajectories, force profiles, and posture-dependent manipulability ellipsoids, reproduced via a hierarchical torque controller (impedance control + manipulability control) plus an optimization-based force controller with online stiffness adaptation, achieves comparable-or-better performance than state-of-the-art in simulated tasks and is further verified in two real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors jointly learning and reproducing multiple manipulation features (motion + force + manipulability), not motion trajectories alone, as the action representation for LfD-based skill transfer
claims.conditions: sim + 2 real-world scenarios; requires torque control and force sensing beyond simple position control

title: DualVLA: Building a Generalizable Embodied Agent via Partial Decoupling of Reasoning and Action

claims.claim: Naively incorporating mixed annotated robot data with multimodal reasoning data to restore broader reasoning capability in a specialist VLA causes 'action degeneration' -- degraded action performance compared to the pre-fine-tuning specialist model; DualVLA addresses this via dual-layer data pruning (removing redundant embodied reasoning that would adversely influence action learning) and dual-teacher adaptive distillation (different supervision per data domain), achieving 61.0 average success in SimplerEnv and 65.4 average score across eight multimodal benchmarks
claims.direction: warns that adding reasoning/language capability to a specialist manipulation policy can hurt action performance unless carefully decoupled (pruning + distillation), contradicting the assumption that adding more (reasoning) data/capability is purely beneficial for a VLA's action performance
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv + eight multimodal benchmarks; identifies and names the 'action degeneration' phenomenon as a general risk when combining reasoning and action training

title: HARP-VLA: Human-Robot Aligned Representation Learning for Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: HARP uses limited paired human-robot demonstrations as cross-embodiment bridges plus abundant unpaired human/robot videos as scalable dynamics supervision, training a robot-adapted visual encoder and latent action model with a source-relative pair-discriminative alignment loss (adapting robot representations toward human semantics while preserving pair-level discrimination); this improves human-robot representation alignment and downstream policy performance, achieving 4.481 average rollout length on CALVIN ABC-to-D and a 7.1% real-world success-rate gain over the strongest baseline
claims.direction: favors explicitly aligning robot and human visual/latent-action representations (via limited paired data + abundant unpaired video) over training latent action models on visual features alone, when co-training VLA policies with human video
claims.conditions: CALVIN (sim) + real-world manipulation; requires a limited set of paired human-robot demonstrations plus larger unpaired human and robot video corpora

title: AT-VLA: Adaptive Tactile Injection for Enhanced Feedback Reaction in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: AT-VLA's Adaptive Tactile Injection mechanism dynamically determines when/where to inject tactile signals (only when they significantly contribute to action generation, minimizing disruption of pretrained VLA representations), combined with a Tactile Reaction Dual-Stream mechanism that decouples a slow visual-language stream (low-frequency perceptual reasoning) from a fast tactile control stream (high-frequency physical interaction understanding), achieving real-time closed-loop responses within 0.04s, validated on real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors decoupled dual-frequency processing (slow semantic stream + fast reactive stream triggered adaptively) over uniformly injecting a new modality into a pretrained VLA at a single frequency, both to preserve pretrained capability and to achieve fast (0.04s) reactive control
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation; requires tactile sensing hardware not present on our vision-only SO-101 setup

title: Safe Policies Post-Training: Constraining Streaming Flow Models for Adapting Learned Robot Trajectory Distributions

claims.claim: CASF augments streaming flow policies with differentiable constraint-distance metrics (pulled back into control space) that reshape the learned velocity field online during rollout -- attenuating/redirecting motion near constraint boundaries (joint limits, collisions, workspace bounds) while leaving it unchanged elsewhere -- producing constraint-satisfying trajectories that remain smooth and dynamically consistent, outperforming standard post-hoc projection baselines in simulated and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors online constraint-aware reshaping of a streaming flow policy's velocity field over post-hoc action projection, for enforcing safety/task constraints without sacrificing the smooth, reactive, multi-modal properties of flow-based policies
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation tasks; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Self-Improving VLA Policies: Selected Diffusion Noise for Spurious-Robust Action Smoothing

claims.claim: Selected Diffusion Noise (SDN), a training-free test-time method, dynamically samples diffusion-noise vectors that are maximally separated from a reference set (to mitigate reliance on spurious visual cues) while selecting candidates yielding more coherent action trajectories; evaluated on two simulation benchmarks (Google Robot, Widow-X) and two real-world robotic datasets across multiple VLA policies (pi_0, Groot-N1.5, Groot-N1.6), SDN consistently improves success rates by +8% in simulation and +10% in real-world settings while reducing action jitter, without modifying model parameters
claims.direction: favors a training-free, test-time diffusion-noise-selection mechanism (exploiting the noise space as a controllable degree of freedom) over standard fixed/random noise sampling in diffusion-based VLA action generation, to simultaneously reduce action jitter and improve robustness to spurious visual correlations
claims.conditions: sim (Google Robot, Widow-X) + real-world robotic datasets; multiple VLA policies (pi_0, Groot-N1.5, Groot-N1.6); no retraining or parameter changes required

title: ORPA: Online Residual Policy Adaptation for Robot Manipulation Control with Human Feedback

claims.claim: ORPA augments a pretrained ACT policy with a lightweight, feedback-conditioned module that predicts residual joint-space adjustments at runtime (without modifying the underlying policy parameters or requiring dataset aggregation/retraining), evaluated on precision-sensitive manipulation tasks on the ALOHA platform, demonstrating improved success rate and recovery from small perturbations compared to baseline ACT and rule-based inverse-kinematics corrections
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight runtime residual-correction module on top of a frozen ACT policy over full dataset-aggregation retraining, for correcting small execution errors/perturbations
claims.conditions: real-world (ALOHA platform), directly built on ACT (one of our candidate architectures); requires online human feedback signal

title: X-Imitator: Spatial-Aware Imitation Learning via Bidirectional Action-Pose Interaction

claims.claim: X-Imitator models spatial (pose) perception and action execution as a tightly coupled bidirectional loop (conditioning current pose predictions on past actions and vice versa, mimicking a human internal forward model) as a modular add-on integrable into various visuomotor policies; across 24 simulated and 3 real-world tasks it significantly outperforms both vanilla policies and prior methods using explicit (unidirectional) pose guidance
claims.direction: favors bidirectional coupling between pose/spatial-perception prediction and action generation over either decoupled or strictly unidirectional pose-guidance approaches for visuomotor policy learning
claims.conditions: 24 sim + 3 real-world tasks; modular, designed to integrate into existing visuomotor policy architectures

title: BiCoord: A Bimanual Manipulation Benchmark towards Long-Horizon Spatial-Temporal Coordination

claims.claim: Evaluating representative manipulation policies (Diffusion Policy, RDT, Pi0, OpenVLA-OFT) on a new benchmark of long-horizon, tightly-coordinated bimanual tasks (continuous inter-arm dependency, dynamic role exchange across multiple sub-goals) shows that all of them 'struggle with long-duration and highly coupled tasks,' revealing fundamental challenges in achieving long-horizon, tightly-coordinated manipulation even for current strong policy architectures
claims.direction: reveals a shared limitation across several leading policy architectures (including Pi0 and Diffusion Policy, relevant candidates for us) in long-horizon temporal/spatial coordination, suggesting current chunking/horizon designs may not by themselves solve tightly-coupled long-horizon coordination
claims.conditions: new sim benchmark (BiCoord); bimanual tasks specifically, though the coordination-difficulty finding may generalize to long single-arm sequences too

title: Learning Structural Latent Points for Efficient Visual Representations in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A hybrid 3D representation ('structural latent points') that inserts a point-wise latent VAE into a point-cloud autoencoder's latent space (jointly regularizing point-wise features and coordinates toward a Gaussian prior, combined with a lightweight 3DGS-based rendering pipeline) shows consistent gains in task success, sample efficiency, and robustness to viewpoint and scene variations over strong baselines, validated on RLBench, ManiSkill2, and a real-robot platform, with ablations confirming each component's contribution
claims.direction: favors a hybrid implicit/explicit 3D pretraining representation (combining expressiveness of implicit fields with structural priors of explicit point clouds) over either purely implicit neural fields or purely explicit geometric primitives, for viewpoint/scene-variation robustness and sample efficiency
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench, ManiSkill2) + real-robot platform

title: HumanEgo: Zero-Shot Robot Learning from Minutes of Human Egocentric Videos

claims.claim: HumanEgo lifts each human egocentric demonstration to an entity-level hand-object-interaction representation and trains a flow-matching policy with dense auxiliary objectives (robot-data-free, hardware-agnostic); with only 30 minutes of human video per task it achieves 92.5% average success across four real-world tasks (75% with just 15 minutes), outperforming matched-time robot teleoperation by 41%, and robustly transfers zero-shot across novel robots, cameras, and environments
claims.direction: favors learning directly from a small amount (minutes, not hours) of human egocentric video -- with no robot demonstrations at all -- over matched-time robot teleoperation data collection, for both success rate and zero-shot generalization to novel cameras/environments
claims.conditions: real-world, four tasks; zero robot demonstrations used; explicitly tests zero-shot transfer across novel robots, cameras, and environments (directly relevant to our camera-shift concern)

why_deep_read: Reports that just 15-30 minutes of human egocentric video (zero robot teleop demonstrations) outperforms matched-time robot teleoperation by 41% and generalizes zero-shot to novel cameras/environments -- if this holds up, it could be dramatically more time-efficient than our planned 50-100 teleop demos per task; worth reading in full to assess feasibility of collecting a human egocentric video for the pumpkin task instead of/in addition to teleop demos.

title: RynnWorld-4D: 4D Embodied World Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: RynnWorld-4D co-produces future RGB frames, depth maps, and optical flow (RGB-DF, a physically-grounded 4D representation) from a single RGB-D image and language instruction in one unified diffusion process (tri-branch architecture, cross-modal attention, frame-wise 3D RoPE), trained on a curated 254.4-million-frame dataset of egocentric human and robot manipulation videos; an inverse-dynamics head (RynnWorld-4D-Policy) consumes its internal 4D representations in a single forward pass, bypassing expensive multi-step denoising, achieving state-of-the-art performance on real-world dexterous bimanual manipulation tasks requiring spatial precision and temporal coordination
claims.direction: favors a unified RGB+depth+optical-flow ('4D') generative world-model representation, combined with single-forward-pass inverse-dynamics action extraction (avoiding iterative denoising), over 2D-pixel-only video world models or standard multi-step-denoising action decoding
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining dataset (254.4M frames); real-world dexterous bimanual manipulation tasks

title: Skills in Weights, Memory in Code: Hybrid Learning for Memory-Dependent Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: HyMeS learns low-level motor skills via gradient-based imitation learning while a separate coding agent learns high-level memory-management strategies via heuristic learning from rollout feedback (steering a Markovian VLA for non-Markovian, memory-dependent tasks), closing the loop via multimodal stage-completion verification; on RoboMemArena it improves mean cumulative success from 52.5% to 66.2% and mean task success from 41.3% to 60.1% over a pi0.5 baseline, outperforming PrediMem by 4.5/14.5 points, while requiring demonstrations only for reusable motor skills rather than every history-dependent task configuration
claims.direction: favors separating memory-management/history-reasoning (handled symbolically/heuristically by a coding agent) from low-level motor-skill learning (handled by gradient-based IL) over end-to-end memory-augmented VLA training, for both performance and demonstration efficiency on memory-dependent tasks
claims.conditions: RoboMemArena benchmark; directly compared against a pi0.5 baseline and PrediMem

title: Latent Policy Steering: An Efficient and Flexible Framework for Cross-Embodiment Transfer

claims.claim: Latent Policy Steering (LPS) pretrains an embodiment-agnostic image-based World Model with optical flow across diverse embodiments, fine-tunes it on the target embodiment with robot actions, then steers a frozen base policy toward better actions by searching the World Model's latent space for plans close to the fine-tuning data (policy-agnostic, no retraining of the base policy needed); with only 50 demonstrations on an unseen target embodiment, LPS improves the average performance of Diffusion Policy relatively by 16% (Robomimic) and 62% (real-world), and of Pi0.5 by 8% and 14% respectively
claims.direction: favors steering a frozen base policy at inference time via an embodiment-agnostic world-model latent search (rather than retraining/fine-tuning the policy itself) for cross-embodiment transfer, when only a small number of target-embodiment demonstrations (e.g. 50) are available
claims.conditions: Robomimic (sim) + real-world; tested with both Diffusion Policy and Pi0.5 as base policies; exactly 50 demonstrations on the unseen target embodiment, matching our planned demo count

why_deep_read: Directly tests with 50 demonstrations (matching our planned per-task demo count) on an unseen embodiment, improving both Diffusion Policy and Pi0.5 substantially without retraining either -- a policy-agnostic, inference-time steering method that could be layered on top of whatever action head we choose; worth reading in full for feasibility of building/reusing an embodiment-agnostic world model for our SO-101 setup.

title: CCIL: Continuity-based Data Augmentation for Corrective Imitation Learning

claims.claim: CCIL generates corrective labels by constructing a locally-Lipschitz-continuous dynamics model from expert demonstrations alone (no interactive expert labeling, no additional offline datasets, no domain-specific invariances required), producing corrective action labels in the neighborhood of demonstrated states/actions but beyond the actual dataset; training on this augmented data enhances an agent's ability to recover from perturbations and compounding errors, validated across diverse robotics domains including tabletop manipulation, drone flying, legged locomotion, and high-dimensional-sensor navigation
claims.direction: favors continuity-based corrective-label generation from the demonstration set alone (minimal extra assumptions) over interactive expert (DAgger-style) labeling or additional offline datasets, for reducing compounding-error sensitivity in behavior cloning
claims.conditions: simulation, multiple robotics domains including tabletop manipulation; requires only access to expert demonstration data, no interactive expert or extra hardware

title: DexH2R: Task-Oriented Dexterous Manipulation From Human to Robots

claims.claim: Enhancing retargeted human-hand motions with a residual policy trained via reinforcement learning (incorporating object/environment information) lets robots autonomously correct retargeting errors without real-time human correction, outperforming baseline approaches by approximately 40% in task success rates on both seen and unseen objects across multiple robot hand embodiments
claims.direction: favors a residual RL correction layer on top of retargeted human demonstrations over pure retargeting or human-in-the-loop correction, for scalable dexterous data collection generalizing to unseen objects
claims.conditions: multiple dexterous robot hand embodiments; unseen-object generalization explicitly tested

title: Robotic Offline RL from Internet Videos via Value-Function Learning

claims.claim: V-PTR learns value functions via temporal-difference learning on large-scale human video datasets (e.g. Ego4D, which lack action/reward annotations), producing representations more conducive to downstream robotic offline RL than other video-learning approaches; combined with offline RL on diverse robot data, it produces policies that perform better, act more robustly, and generalize more broadly on a real WidowX robot and in simulation than prior methods
claims.direction: favors value-function (TD-learning) pretraining on action-free human video as the bridge to downstream robot offline RL, over other representation-learning approaches for leveraging observation-only video data
claims.conditions: real WidowX robot + simulation; offline RL rather than direct imitation learning

title: Learning human-to-robot handovers through 3D scene reconstruction

claims.claim: H2RH-SGS learns robot handover policies solely from sparse-view Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of RGB images (no real-robot training or data collection), translating simulated camera-pose changes in the reconstructed scene directly into gripper pose changes to generate image-action demonstration pairs; a policy trained on 16 household objects this way is directly deployed and validated in the real environment
claims.direction: favors Gaussian-Splatting-based scene reconstruction to synthesize image-action training pairs (avoiding real-robot demonstration collection entirely) over standard real-world teleoperation data collection, for the handover sub-task
claims.conditions: real-world deployment validated after training entirely on reconstructed-scene demonstrations; 16 household objects

title: AVR: Active Vision-Driven Precise Robot Manipulation with Viewpoint and Focal Length Optimization

claims.claim: AVR unifies head-tracked viewpoint control (HMD-to-2-DoF gimbal) with motorized optical zoom to keep manipulation targets centered at an appropriate scale during both data collection and deployment; in simulation, emulating active vision as a data-augmentation plugin (ROI-conditioned viewpoint change, aspect-ratio-preserving zoom crops, super-resolution) yields 5-17% task-success gains, and on a real-world platform AVR improves success on most tasks with over 25% gains versus a static-view baseline, with further studies confirming robustness under occlusion, clutter, and lighting disturbances and generalization to unseen environments/objects
claims.direction: favors active, motorized viewpoint and zoom control (both for data collection and deployment) over static fixed cameras, for precision manipulation and robustness to occlusion/clutter/lighting/novel environments
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin-based augmentation) + real-world bimanual teleoperation platform; requires motorized camera/zoom hardware beyond our currently fixed scene + wrist cameras

title: Speech-to-Trajectory: Learning Human-Like Verbal Guidance for Robot Motion

claims.claim: The Directive Language Model directly maps verbal commands to executable motion trajectories via behavior cloning on simulated demonstrations (bypassing predefined phrase matching), using GPT-based semantic augmentation to generate diverse paraphrases labeled with the same trajectory, plus diffusion-policy-based trajectory generation for adaptive refinement; this improves command generalization and reduces dependence on structured phrasing compared to LLM-based methods, while remaining embodiment-agnostic since it learns from trajectory data
claims.direction: favors direct language-to-trajectory behavior cloning with paraphrase augmentation over LLM-prompt-based command interpretation, for robust generalization to varied natural-language phrasing
claims.conditions: simulated demonstrations; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: Accurate and affordable cobot calibration without external measurement devices

claims.claim: A low-cost, 3D-printable two-socket spherical-joint calibration tool plus an optimization routine that updates the nominal kinematic model reduces mean absolute end-effector error from approximately 10mm to 0.2mm on Franka robots (also validated on KUKA and Kinova); a peg-in-hole task with 0.4mm tolerance and a repeated drawing/LfD task both fail without calibration and consistently succeed with the calibrated model
claims.direction: favors performing a low-cost kinematic calibration pass on the robot arm before precision manipulation/LfD deployment over relying on the manufacturer's nominal (uncalibrated) kinematic model, especially for tight-tolerance tasks
claims.conditions: real robots (Franka, KUKA, Kinova); demonstrates calibration is a prerequisite (not just a nice-to-have) for certain precision tasks to succeed at all

title: Translation as a Bridging Action: Transferring Manipulation Skills from Humans to Robots

claims.claim: Learning rotation-inclusive 6DoF action signals from noisy human hand-pose estimates is sub-optimal for human-to-robot transfer (because human finger contact patterns differ fundamentally from parallel-gripper contact); instead, using relative wrist translation within the initial head-camera frame as a bridging action representation (shared between humans and robots, with a pi_0-like VLA using interleaved action tokens and attention masking to handle missing action components) transfers human manipulation knowledge to a bi-manual parallel-gripper robot far more effectively than noisy 6DoF human actions, and scales with the amount of human data used
claims.direction: favors a reduced, translation-only bridging action space (discarding noisy rotation estimates) over full noisy 6DoF human action imitation, when transferring manipulation skills from human demonstrations to a parallel-gripper robot
claims.conditions: bi-manual robot with parallel grippers; built on a pi_0-like VLA architecture; novel bimanual manipulation task suite

title: Beyond Human Demonstrations: Diffusion-Based Reinforcement Learning to Generate Data for VLA Training

claims.claim: A modified diffusion-policy RL optimization algorithm generates smoother, more consistent (lower-variance) trajectories than either human demonstrations or standard Gaussian RL policies on the LIBERO benchmark (130 long-horizon tasks); training a VLA model EXCLUSIVELY on this diffusion-RL-generated data achieves an average success rate of 81.9%, outperforming a model trained on human demonstration data by +5.3 percentage points and one trained on Gaussian-RL-generated data by +12.6 points
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the assumption that human demonstrations are the highest-quality data source for VLA training -- shows that autonomously RL-generated (diffusion-policy) trajectories can produce a better-performing VLA than training on the equivalent human demonstrations, at least on this sim benchmark
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (sim), 130 long-horizon manipulation tasks; VLA trained exclusively on synthetic RL-generated trajectories vs. exclusively on human demos vs. exclusively on Gaussian-RL data

title: MoWAM: Explicit Future Motion Prediction for Efficient World Action Models

claims.claim: MoWAM replaces explicit future-video generation in World Action Models with a compact structured future-motion prediction (learned jointly with actions during training via a Mixture-of-Transformer architecture), allowing video generation to be removed entirely at inference while retaining an explicit future representation; on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and real-world tasks, this achieves strong in-distribution performance, improved out-of-distribution robustness, and higher average real-world success than representative WAM baselines, with further gains from inference-time candidate scaling
claims.direction: favors predicting a compact structured motion abstraction of the future (rather than full future video frames) as the WAM conditioning signal, to remove the major inference-time cost of video generation while retaining OOD-robustness benefits
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus) + real-world manipulation tasks

title: Beyond Binary Success: A Diagnostic Meta-Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Manipulation

claims.claim: Disentangling manipulation competency into understanding/perception/controlled-behavior axes via a diagnostic meta-evaluation framework (MetaFine) exposes severe dimension-specific failures in current VLA models invisible to binary success metrics; targeted causal intervention identifies the visual encoder's ability to preserve local spatial structure as a key bottleneck for fine-grained precision, and improving it directly unlocks previously inaccessible manipulation capabilities without modifying downstream policies
claims.direction: corroborates (independently of VLM4VLA) that the visual encoder's spatial-structure fidelity, not downstream policy architecture, is the key bottleneck for fine-grained manipulation precision
claims.conditions: diagnostic benchmark built from heterogeneous external benchmarks; causal intervention methodology rather than a simple ablation, hybrid real-sim validation

title: Object-Centric Instruction Augmentation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a Multi-modal LLM to weave object-position cues into natural-language instructions (Object-Centric Instruction Augmentation), plus a feature-reuse mechanism integrating vision-language features from the pretrained MLLM into the policy network, lets imitation policies trained with these enhanced instructions outperform those relying solely on traditional (position-agnostic) language instructions across simulated and real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors augmenting language instructions with explicit spatial/positional cues (derived via MLLM) over using semantically-rich but position-agnostic instructions alone, for language-conditioned manipulation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world; qualitative comparative claim, no exact numbers given

title: DITTO: Demonstration Imitation by Trajectory Transformation

claims.claim: DITTO performs one-shot imitation from a single RGB-D human demonstration video by offline-extracting an object-centric demonstration trajectory (segmentation + relative-motion estimation), then online re-detecting objects and warping the demonstration trajectory to the current scene for execution (leveraging off-the-shelf segmentation, relative-pose-estimation, and grasp-prediction models); the method is validated across ten diverse tasks including pick-and-place and articulated-object manipulation, with extensive real-robot evaluation
claims.direction: favors trajectory-warping-based one-shot imitation from a single demonstration (re-detect + warp + execute) over training a parametric policy on many demonstrations, for quickly teaching new pick-and-place-style skills
claims.conditions: real robot, ten diverse tasks; relies on several off-the-shelf perception models (segmentation, pose estimation, grasp prediction)

title: MoE-DP: An MoE-Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Robust Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Skill Decomposition and Failure Recovery

claims.claim: Inserting a Mixture-of-Experts layer between the visual encoder and the diffusion model (decomposing policy knowledge into specialized experts dynamically activated per task phase) significantly improves recovery from disturbances versus standard diffusion-policy baselines, yielding a 36% average relative improvement in success rate under disturbed conditions across 6 long-horizon simulation tasks, further validated with significant real-world gains; the learned expert decomposition is interpretable (experts correspond to semantic primitives like approaching/grasping) and supports subtask rearrangement at inference time without retraining
claims.direction: favors inserting a Mixture-of-Experts layer between the vision encoder and diffusion action head (for interpretable, phase-specialized sub-policies) over a monolithic diffusion policy, specifically for robustness/recovery under disturbances in long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: 6 long-horizon sim tasks + real-world validation; diffusion policy backbone

title: DATRN: Adaptive Trajectory Learning from Demonstrations for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A dynamic adaptive trajectory radial network (using radial basis function neural networks) for real-time trajectory generation achieves higher training-time reduction, higher trajectory-fitting accuracy, and better long-horizon stabilization than dynamic movement primitives (DMPs) across four representative tasks (pick & place, stacking, lateral pushing, surface wiping)
claims.direction: favors an RBFN-based adaptive trajectory representation over DMPs (which require careful hyperparameter tuning and struggle with complex non-linear/long-horizon motion) as the low-level trajectory-generation representation
claims.conditions: not explicitly stated whether sim or real; four representative manipulation tasks; comparison specifically against DMP baseline

title: Integration of Gaussian Mixture Models and Extended Kalman Filter for Trajectory Generation in Robotic Manipulators

claims.claim: Encoding motion patterns from a limited number of demonstrations with Gaussian Mixture Models/Gaussian Mixture Regression, then refining GMR's velocity predictions with an Extended Kalman Filter to reduce noise, significantly enhances trajectory precision and smoothness and corrects the endpoint-deviation problem that plain GMR exhibits, in simulated experiments
claims.direction: favors augmenting GMM/GMR trajectory encoding with Kalman-filter-based velocity refinement over plain GMR alone, to fix endpoint deviations from a small number of demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation only; from a limited number of demonstrations

title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies

claims.claim: Kuafu automatically synthesizes 'SUN Programs' (typed executables where geometric/contact relations compile once into aligned MPC costs, satisfaction predicates, RL rewards, transition guards) from language and scene semantics via VLMs, screens feasibility via MPC, and trains stage-conditioned policies without demonstrations or manual dense rewards; across nine tasks it achieves 82.03% macro-success (vs. 35.67% sparse-reward and 24.75% Stage-BC baselines), generates 10.57x the successful trajectory time per hour of human teleoperation at scale, and with 500 trajectories/task trains DP3 policies to 46.0% simulation success (vs 22.4% for alternatives) and 34.7% on physical Franka and Kinova robots
claims.direction: favors simulation-screened, semantically-unified program synthesis (unifying MPC, RL rewards, and BC targets from language/scene semantics) over demonstration-based or sparse-reward RL training, to generate far more usable trajectory-hours per hour of costly human teleoperation
claims.conditions: nine tasks, sim + physical Franka and Kinova robots; DP3 (a diffusion-policy variant) used as the downstream policy

title: Bounding Boxes as Goals: Language-Conditioned Grasping via Neuro-Symbolic Planning

claims.claim: GRASP translates natural-language queries into neuro-symbolic goal states via a pretrained VLM, grounded in the physical world through a bounding-box detection pipeline (rather than fixed color lists or hard-coded coordinates), enabling robots to interpret abstract spatial concepts (e.g. 'top shelf') and execute open-vocabulary tabletop manipulation without task-specific training, achieving 73.3% overall success across 90 real-robot trials at three difficulty levels
claims.direction: favors VLM-grounded bounding-box goal specification (open-vocabulary, no fine-tuning) over fixed color-list or hard-coded-coordinate grounding, for zero-training language-conditioned grasping
claims.conditions: real-robot, 90 trials, three difficulty levels; no task-specific fine-tuning required

title: 3PoinTr: From Human Videos to Robot Policies with 3D Point-Track Plans

claims.claim: 3PoinTr predicts a global 3D point-track plan from human videos (dense 3D point tracks spanning the full task, compressed into a small set of fixed plan tokens via Perceiver-IO), which the policy combines with the current observation at each query to predict robot actions; this transfers exceptionally well even when human demonstration motions are infeasible for robots, achieving 25.0 percentage points higher success than the strongest behavior-cloning/video-pretraining baselines on real-world tasks and 29.6 points higher in simulation
claims.direction: favors a compact, fixed, non-embodiment-specific 3D point-track global plan (predicted once from human video) over direct imitation of human motion or per-step video-pretraining features, for transferring human video demonstrations to robot policies
claims.conditions: controlled sim + real-world evaluations; ablations show benefit of predicting tracks once as a global plan, Perceiver-IO compression, and residual cross-attention; retains supervision for occluded points unlike a 3D-flow baseline

title: Learning Forward & Reverse Skills from a Single Unfinished Demonstration for Constrained Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: A unified one-shot framework learns both forward and reverse execution of constrained, contact-rich manipulation skills from a single, possibly unfinished demonstration, by decomposing it into non-contact phases (encoded as DMPs) and contact phases (encoded as screw motion primitives via a geometry-driven twist-direction segmentation algorithm), executed under admittance-guided pose correction; this improves success rates and robustness over segmentation and one-shot trajectory-learning baselines on peg insertion, battery insertion, lock opening, and screw driving tasks
claims.direction: favors decomposing a single (even incomplete) demonstration into non-contact DMP + contact screw-primitive segments (enabling execution beyond the demonstrated trajectory length and reverse execution with no extra data) over requiring multiple complete demonstrations for constrained manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world, four contact-rich constrained-manipulation tasks; single demonstration, which may be unfinished/incomplete

title: Reuse Before You Retrieve: Diagnosing Headroom and Complementarity for Test-Time Augmentation of Embodied Multimodal Policies

claims.claim: An episode-level retry selector (choosing among a frozen VLA's own stochastic rollouts, without external demonstrations) consistently recovers substantial latent capability across all tested VLA backbones on LIBERO, with gains of up to 21.0 success-rate points that closely track a measurable 'recoverable headroom' factor; it transfers to a different robot/simulator and remains effective under degraded observations, while a separate 'retrieval complementarity' factor determines when introducing external action priors (rather than resampling) is instead the more useful intervention
claims.direction: favors first diagnosing whether better behavior already exists within a frozen policy's own stochastic rollouts (and exploiting it via retry/resampling) before resorting to external retrieval-augmentation, since the two interventions help under different, separately measurable conditions
claims.conditions: LIBERO, multiple frozen VLA backbones (including OpenVLA); explicitly tested under degraded observations and transferred to a different robot/simulator

title: Visual Robotic Manipulation with Depth-Aware Pretraining

claims.claim: RGB-only backbone pretrained with depth-aware contrastive learning (using depth as auxiliary signal, not needed at inference) improves manipulation policy performance vs standard 2D-only pretraining
claims.direction: depth-aware self-supervised pretraining > plain 2D pretraining, while keeping RGB-only inference
claims.conditions: sim and real robot, various manipulation tasks

claims.claim: 3D scene understanding learned during pretraining transfers benefit to RGB-only manipulation policy without needing depth/point-cloud at inference
claims.direction: depth as auxiliary pretraining signal, RGB-only at deployment
claims.conditions: real+sim robots, unseen objects and visual environments

title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset

claims.claim: Training with a large, diverse in-the-wild dataset (76k trajectories, 350 hours, 564 scenes, 86 tasks, 52 buildings) yields policies with higher performance than less diverse data
claims.direction: diversity of demonstration data favors generalization
claims.conditions: real robots, multiple embodiments/buildings, large-scale (76k trajectories)

claims.claim: Policies trained on DROID show greater robustness and improved generalization ability compared to baselines
claims.direction: more diverse real-world data improves robustness/generalization
claims.conditions: real-world, cross-scene/cross-building evaluation

claims.claim: Each episode uses three synchronized RGB camera streams plus depth and calibration
claims.direction: multi-view camera setup used for data collection
claims.conditions: real robot, in-the-wild settings

title: Visuotactile Diffusion Policy: Automated Failure Recovery in Assistive Tasks with Tactile Manipulation Using Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A diffusion-policy imitation learning framework augmented with tactile sensing enables automated failure recovery in fine-grained grasping
claims.direction: diffusion policy + tactile modality favored for recovery over vision-only imitation learning
claims.conditions: real-world assistive robotic grasping tasks

claims.claim: Adding tactile modality is proposed as a way to counter covariate shift and the copycat problem (expert-copying without task completion) common in imitation learning
claims.direction: tactile sensing helps mitigate copycat/causal-confusion issues
claims.conditions: real robot, assistive grasping/manipulation

title: RoboTwin: Dual-Arm Robot Benchmark with Generative Digital Twins

claims.claim: Policies pre-trained on generative-digital-twin (synthetic) data and fine-tuned with limited real-world samples improve success rates by over 70% for single-arm tasks and over 40% for dual-arm tasks compared to training solely on real-world data
claims.direction: synthetic/generated demonstration data + small real fine-tuning set outperforms real-only training
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm robot (COBOT Magic), limited real demos, simulated+real benchmark

claims.claim: Combining generated synthetic demonstrations with limited real samples substantially reduces need for large real demo counts
claims.direction: synthetic data supplementation favored when real demos are scarce
claims.conditions: real + sim, dual-arm manipulation tasks

title: Balancing Signal and Variance: Adaptive Offline RL Post-Training for VLA Flow Models

claims.claim: Offline RL post-training (ARFM) applied to flow-matching VLA action heads improves generalization, robustness, few-shot learning, and continual learning versus pure imitation-learning post-training
claims.direction: flow-matching action head + RL post-training favored over flow-matching + pure IL fine-tuning
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world robot experiments, VLA flow models

title: PointVLA: Injecting the 3D World into Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Injecting point-cloud features into a frozen pretrained 2D VLA action expert (via lightweight modular block, added only to identified low-utility blocks) outperforms 2D-only imitation learning baselines (OpenVLA, Diffusion Policy, DexVLA) on simulated and real tasks
claims.direction: point cloud/3D injection > pure RGB 2D imitation learning
claims.conditions: real + sim robots, pretrained VLA backbone, no retraining of base model

claims.claim: PointVLA performs few-shot multi-tasking, successfully executing four different tasks using only 20 demonstrations each
claims.direction: 3D-augmented VLA enables strong performance with as few as 20 demos per task
claims.conditions: real robot, 20 demos/task, multi-task

claims.claim: Point-cloud integration lets the robot adapt to objects at varying table heights unseen during training, unlike conventional 2D imitation learning methods
claims.direction: 3D input favored for viewpoint/height robustness over 2D-only
claims.conditions: real robot, novel table heights

why_deep_read: Directly tests whether adding 3D/point-cloud input to a small pretrained action expert improves few-shot (20-demo) performance and height/viewpoint robustness -- close analogue to our RGB+depth, low-demo setup; ablation details on the skip-block injection strategy would inform Q04 design.

title: ActionX: pre-training action experts with reinforcement learning for vision-language action models

claims.claim: Pretraining the action-expert head with reinforcement learning (on top of a frozen pretrained VLM backbone), then fine-tuning end-to-end with a small amount of expert data, achieves +16% success rate compared to state-of-the-art VLA models trained with large-scale demonstrations
claims.direction: RL-pretrained action expert + small IL fine-tune > standard large-scale IL-only VLA training
claims.conditions: LIBERO and Meta-World benchmarks plus real-world robot manipulation, less than 100 expert demonstrations for real-robot training

claims.claim: Real robot tasks required fewer than 100 expert demonstrations for the whole training phase while still outperforming SOTA VLAs trained on large-scale demo datasets
claims.direction: small demo counts (<100) sufficient when action expert is RL-pretrained
claims.conditions: real robot manipulation, <100 demos total

why_deep_read: Reports a controlled comparison at <100 real demos (matching our data budget) with a quantified success-rate gain; full text ablations on the RL-pretraining recipe and demo count sensitivity would directly inform Q01/Q13 for our setup.

title: DriftWorld: Fast World Modeling through Drifting

claims.claim: An action-conditioned world model trained to 'drift' (single forward pass) rather than iteratively denoise achieves state-of-the-art decision-making performance with far less inference time than diffusion-based world model baselines, and can serve as an offline simulator for ranking policies with rollout scores correlating up to 0.99 with ground truth
claims.direction: single-pass drift world model favored over multistep diffusion world models for rollout speed/accuracy trade-off
claims.conditions: vision-based manipulation benchmarks: Bridge-V2, RT-1, Language Table, Push-T, Robomimic

claims.claim: DriftWorld generates future-frame rollouts at 30+ fps, 17x faster on average than diffusion-based world model baselines
claims.direction: drift-based (single-step) generative model >> multistep diffusion for inference speed
claims.conditions: standard vision-based manipulation benchmarks

title: IM-ENGINE: Image Editing for Embodied Data Generation

claims.claim: Using image editing as an intermediate representation (on rendered scenes with known geometry/depth/segmentation), grounded and refined in physics, generates scalable, physically-valid synthetic supervision (grasps and goal states) for robot learning
claims.direction: generative image-editing + simulator-grounding favored as a synthetic-data-generation approach over pure simulation or pure human demonstration
claims.conditions: simulated scenes with known geometry, dexterous grasp synthesis and goal-state generation tasks

title: Vision-Based Grasping for Industrial Robots Guided by Deep Q-Networks

claims.claim: A DQN-based vision-to-grasp system achieved over 90% grasp success on physical hardware and generalized to new objects, partial occlusions, and lighting changes in robustness tests; failure analysis identified spatial alignment and reflection as the main failure modes
claims.direction: vision-guided RL grasping shown robust to lighting changes, but reflections/spatial alignment remain primary failure sources
claims.conditions: real UR5e robot with RGB-D camera, industrial pick task, mixed/cluttered environments, 200k training steps in sim then real-world transfer

title: Steering Generative Reinforcement Learning into Stable Robotic Controller

claims.claim: Stochasticity inherent to diffusion/flow-based generative policies is described as unsuitable for stable, precise control in high-dimensional robotic systems, since small action variations can accumulate into inconsistent motion and reduced robustness; the paper proposes steering a trained generative policy into a deterministic controller via a learned latent actor to fix this
claims.direction: deterministic latent-steered control favored over raw stochastic diffusion/flow sampling for stable deployment
claims.conditions: sim only: six Isaac Lab benchmarks + Unitree G1 locomotion task (not manipulation)

claims.claim: Separating exploration (stochastic generative sampling) from deployment (deterministic latent steering) produces more stable inference-time behavior and more reliable command responses
claims.direction: deterministic control at inference time favored for smoothness over stochastic generative sampling
claims.conditions: sim only, Isaac Lab + humanoid locomotion

title: FM-VLA: Force-based Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models in Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Encoding force histories into compact 'force memory tokens' (via a VAE pretrained on force time-series reconstruction) and conditioning the action expert on them enables VLAs to resolve non-Markovian, temporally-ambiguous contact-rich tasks (e.g., counting repeated contacts) that vision-only memory approaches struggle with
claims.direction: force-based memory favored over vision-based (sampled past image frame) memory for contact-rich, visually-ambiguous temporal tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks: finding a hidden block, pressing a button, wiping a dish a specific number of times

claims.claim: A VAE pretrained with force time-series reconstruction (auxiliary objective) is used to build compact force representations for conditioning the action expert
claims.direction: reconstruction-based auxiliary pretraining of a force encoder aids downstream memory-dependent manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-rich tasks

title: Policy Compression for Intelligent Continuous Control on Low-Power Edge Devices

claims.claim: An improved policy-distillation method for continuous-action DRL policies compressed models up to 750% (size reduction) while maintaining or exceeding teacher performance by up to 41% on continuous control tasks
claims.direction: much smaller distilled student policy can match/exceed a larger teacher policy
claims.conditions: low-power edge device deployment, two continuous control benchmark tasks (not manipulation-specific)

title: Ctrl-World: A Controllable Generative World Model for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A controllable multi-view world model with pose-conditioned memory retrieval and frame-level action conditioning can rank generalist policy performance accurately without real-world rollouts
claims.direction: world model as auxiliary evaluation/training tool favored to reduce costly real rollouts
claims.conditions: trained on DROID (95k trajectories, 564 scenes), evaluated on generalist VLA policies

claims.claim: Synthesizing successful trajectories in the world model's imagination space and using them for supervised fine-tuning improves policy success by 44.7%
claims.direction: imagined/synthetic successful rollouts used as augmented training data improve real policy success
claims.conditions: generalist robot policies, DROID-scale pretraining

claims.claim: World-model-based imagination can substitute for costly additional real-world corrective demonstration collection
claims.direction: synthetic imagined data reduces need for more real demos
claims.conditions: generalist policies, multi-view, novel scenarios/camera placements

title: Cross-Modality Alignment Perception and Multi-Head Self-Attention Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action of Humanoid Robot

claims.claim: A memory-gated filtering attention mechanism significantly alleviated robot-arm jitter during multi-step imitation-learning-based manipulation compared to standard multi-head self-attention
claims.direction: gated/filtered attention over raw self-attention reduces jitter/motion trajectory errors
claims.conditions: humanoid robot arm, complex multi-step operations

claims.claim: The proposed attention mechanism reduced video memory occupation by 72% and improved training speed from 1.35s to 0.129s per batch versus standard multi-head self-attention, while maintaining higher action accuracy
claims.direction: lighter/gated attention module favored over full multi-head self-attention for compute-constrained training
claims.conditions: humanoid robot VLA training

claims.claim: A few-shot data-collection strategy focused on key steps, combined with cross-modal alignment perception during training, improved task success rate
claims.direction: targeted few-shot demonstration collection (key steps) favored over larger undifferentiated demo sets
claims.conditions: humanoid robot manipulation, few-shot demos

title: Hybrid Consistency Policy: Decoupling Multi-Modal Diversity and Real-Time Efficiency in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A hybrid consistency policy (short stochastic diffusion prefix + one-step consistency jump, trained via time-varying consistency distillation) approaches the mode coverage and accuracy of an 80-step DDPM diffusion teacher while requiring far fewer sampling steps (25 SDE steps + 1 jump)
claims.direction: consistency-distilled hybrid sampling retains diffusion policy's multimodality while cutting inference steps drastically
claims.conditions: both simulation and real robot manipulation

claims.claim: The proposed switch-time mechanism decouples multimodal action diversity from inference speed, significantly reducing latency versus a full multistep DDPM policy without sacrificing much accuracy
claims.direction: fewer denoising/consistency steps favored for latency reduction without abandoning diffusion-style multimodality
claims.conditions: real robot deployment, real-time control

why_deep_read: Directly targets our ~2s inference latency and jerky/chunk-boundary motion problem by showing a diffusion-style action head can be made near-real-time without losing multimodal coverage; full paper's real-robot latency numbers and failure modes would materially inform Q01/Q10 choice of action head.

title: Robust Instant Policy: Student's-t-Based Trajectory Aggregation for Reliable In-Context Imitation Learning in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Aggregating multiple LLM-sampled trajectories via a Student's-t mixture model (to capture multimodality and suppress hallucinated outliers) outperforms state-of-the-art imitation learning methods, especially where multiple valid strategies exist in human demonstrations
claims.direction: robust statistical trajectory aggregation favored over single-trajectory or naive-averaging in-context imitation policies for multimodal demonstrations
claims.conditions: 15 everyday manipulation tasks, sim and real-world, in-context (no retraining) few-shot setting

claims.claim: The proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art IL methods particularly in low-data regimes
claims.direction: robust trajectory aggregation favored when demonstration count is small
claims.conditions: few-demonstration in-context imitation learning, sim+real

title: EquiForm: Noise-Robust SE(3)-Equivariant Policy Learning from 3D Point Clouds

claims.claim: EquiForm, a noise-robust SE(3)-equivariant point-cloud policy with a geometric denoising module and contrastive equivariant alignment, achieves an average improvement of 17.2% in simulation and 28.1% in real-world experiments over state-of-the-art point-cloud imitation learning methods
claims.direction: noise-robust equivariant point-cloud policy > standard point-cloud imitation learning baselines
claims.conditions: 16 simulated tasks, 4 real-world manipulation tasks, diverse objects/layouts

claims.claim: Point-cloud-based policies are highly sensitive to sensor noise, pose perturbations and occlusion artifacts unless explicitly corrected; EquiForm's denoising restores robustness under noisy/incomplete observations
claims.direction: explicit noise-correction needed for point-cloud policies to generalize; plain equivariant architectures alone are insufficient
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation with sensor noise/occlusion

title: M2-VLA: Boosting Vision-Language Models for Generalizable Manipulation via Layer Mixture and Meta-Skills

claims.claim: A Mixture-of-Layers strategy that selectively extracts task-critical information from a generalized (not end-to-end fine-tuned) VLM's dense semantic features preserves VLM generalization better than full end-to-end fine-tuning, which is shown to compromise generalization and cause catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: selective layer extraction from a largely frozen/generalized VLM favored over full end-to-end fine-tuning
claims.conditions: sim and real-world manipulation, ablation studies included

claims.claim: A Meta Skill Module with strong inductive biases facilitates efficient trajectory learning under constrained model capacity
claims.direction: inductive-bias modules help small/constrained-capacity models learn trajectories efficiently
claims.conditions: sim+real manipulation, ablation confirms component contributions

title: Surface Constraint Policy for Learning Surface-Constrained and Dynamically Feasible Robot Skills

claims.claim: Augmenting a diffusion-based imitation-learning policy with explicit surface-geometry-constraint encoding (Gaussian kernel from demonstrations) and mapping intentions to dynamic movement primitives yields superior task success rates and contact stability versus existing diffusion-based techniques lacking explicit geometric constraint modeling
claims.direction: structured/constrained diffusion policy > plain diffusion policy for tasks with geometric/contact constraints
claims.conditions: multiple real surface manipulation tasks, comparison to existing techniques

title: Mag-VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Magnetically Actuated Microrobot Manipulation

claims.claim: Ablation studies show an ACT-based (Action Chunking Transformer) decoder substantially outperforms alternative generative action heads for temporally coherent multi-step control
claims.direction: ACT decoder favored over other generative action heads in ablation
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot arms, teleoperated microrobot manipulation dataset, three task configurations

claims.claim: A VLA built on a frozen VLM backbone (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) fine-tuned with LoRA, combined with a phase-conditioned ACT decoder, achieves 90% approach success and 50-80% transport success as task difficulty increases
claims.direction: LoRA-adapted frozen VLM + phase-conditioned action decoder is a viable low-cost adaptation strategy
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, language-conditioned tasks

title: Action chunking transformer-based imitation learning with dynamic programming optimization for low-cost robotic assembly tasks

claims.claim: Integrating dynamic programming into the ACT inference chain for local trajectory correction (while maintaining control-loop frequency) increased assembly success rate from 62% to 82% on a low-cost manipulator
claims.direction: ACT + DP-based local trajectory correction outperforms plain ACT chunking
claims.conditions: real low-cost SO100 robot with Feetech actuators, 160 teleoperated demos, 3-stage precision assembly task, 100 evaluation trials

claims.claim: The DP-based correction significantly improved trajectory efficiency while maintaining comparable task completion times, addressing reliability issues from limited mechanical repeatability
claims.direction: runtime trajectory correction favored to counter low-cost servo backlash/repeatability issues without added latency cost
claims.conditions: real SO100 (Feetech actuators) low-cost arm

claims.claim: 160 teleoperated demonstrations were sufficient to train an ACT-based policy for a 3-stage precision assembly task on a low-cost arm
claims.direction: on the order of 160 demos used for a multi-stage low-cost-arm task
claims.conditions: real SO100 robot, offline training from teleoperated demos

why_deep_read: This uses the SAME low-cost robot family (SO100, Feetech actuators) and ACT baseline as our setup, with a concrete before/after success-rate comparison (62%->82%) from adding runtime trajectory correction -- directly actionable for our Q06/Q10 chunking-and-jitter problem; full text would give the DP correction algorithm details and failure analysis.

title: Grounded Action Model: 3D Grounding as a Foundation for Robotics

claims.claim: Grounded Action Models (GAM), conditioned on language/points/boxes transformed into an object-centric representation mixing target-focused visual features and metric 3D object geometry with robot state history, achieve 55.3% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 across 50 tasks vs 52.0% for Spatial Forcing, and 61% on LIBERO-PRO vs 53% for pi_0.5 across 16 perturbation settings
claims.direction: explicit 3D/metric object grounding outperforms baseline VLA/world-action-model approaches lacking metric grounding
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-PRO) and real robots (bimanual YAM, Franka)

claims.claim: Under scene randomization, GAM achieves 47.6% success vs 30.4% for Abot-M0; on a real bimanual YAM robot under visual shift, GAM retains 17/20 successes vs 4/20 for pi_0.5
claims.direction: explicit 3D grounding markedly more robust to visual/scene shift than baseline VLA/world-action models
claims.conditions: real robot (bimanual YAM), visual shift test, scene randomization in sim, action policy trained only on clean-scene demonstrations

claims.claim: Composing GAM with a high-level planner (Molmo2) enables long-horizon, memory-dependent manipulation, achieving 64.7% in-distribution and 49.8% out-of-distribution step completion
claims.direction: object-centric 3D grounding as a low-level controller enables better long-horizon/memory-dependent task completion when paired with a planner
claims.conditions: real Franka robot, long-horizon memory-dependent tasks

why_deep_read: Gives quantified real-robot robustness-under-visual-shift comparisons (17/20 vs 4/20) directly analogous to our camera-shift/lighting failure mode, plus a controlled ablation of 3D/metric grounding vs standard VLA/world-action baselines across sim and real; full text failure analysis would directly inform Q04/Q14 design choices.

title: RoVi-Aug: Robot and Viewpoint Augmentation for Cross-Embodiment Robot Learning

claims.claim: Using image-to-image generative models to augment robot demonstration data by synthesizing demonstrations with different robots and camera viewpoints (RoVi-Aug) allows zero-shot deployment on an unseen robot with significantly different camera angles, and co-training on original+augmented data improves success rates by up to 30%
claims.direction: generative robot/viewpoint data augmentation favored over training on original camera-angle-limited data alone
claims.conditions: real physical robot experiments, cross-embodiment, multi-robot/multi-task co-training

claims.claim: Robot datasets often have imbalanced camera-angle distributions causing policies to overfit to specific viewpoints; RoVi-Aug-augmented training removes need to assume known test-time camera angles (unlike test-time-adaptation baselines such as Mirage)
claims.direction: training-time viewpoint augmentation favored over test-time camera-angle adaptation
claims.conditions: real robot, unseen camera viewpoints

claims.claim: RoVi-Aug requires no extra test-time processing and allows further policy fine-tuning, unlike prior test-time adaptation approaches, while still generalizing to unseen robots/viewpoints
claims.direction: augmentation-based generalization favored over test-time-only adaptation for robustness to camera/embodiment shift
claims.conditions: real robot cross-embodiment deployment

why_deep_read: Directly targets our 'slightly moved camera' failure mode via a concrete, quantified (up to 30% success-rate gain) viewpoint-augmentation recipe; full text would give the augmentation pipeline details and how much viewpoint shift it tolerates, materially informing Q05/Q11/Q14.

title: MoManipVLA: Transferring Vision-language-action Models for General Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: By adapting a pre-trained VLA model via a bi-level trajectory optimization (rather than end-to-end retraining), the approach achieves a 4.2% higher success rate than state-of-the-art mobile manipulation methods while requiring only about 50 training-cost demonstrations for real-world deployment
claims.direction: leveraging a strongly pretrained VLA plus lightweight adaptation needs far fewer real demos than training a mobile-manipulation policy from scratch
claims.conditions: OVMM benchmark and real-world mobile manipulation, ~50 real-world demos

title: TabletopGen: Tabletop Scene Generation and Interactive Simulation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A training-free, automated tabletop scene generation pipeline (from text/single image) producing physically plausible, interactable simulated scenes achieves state-of-the-art visual fidelity, layout accuracy and physical plausibility for synthesizing manipulation data, with trajectories validated on a real arm via zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: generated synthetic tabletop scenes favored as a scalable data source, validated to transfer to real robot execution
claims.conditions: real robotic arm, zero-shot sim-to-real trajectory transfer

title: LatBot: Distilling Universal Latent Actions for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: With only 10 real-world trajectories per task collected on a Franka robot, the approach successfully completes all five challenging real tasks, demonstrating strong few-shot transferability
claims.direction: universal latent-action pretraining enables policy success from as few as 10 real demos per task
claims.conditions: real Franka robot, 10 demos/task, 5 tasks

claims.claim: Decomposing latent actions into learnable motion and scene tokens (distinguishing robot movement from environmental change) and jointly optimizing future-frame reconstruction with action-sequence prediction improves generalization over reconstruction-only latent action objectives
claims.direction: joint reconstruction+action-prediction latent-action pretraining favored over reconstruction-only objectives
claims.conditions: simulated (SIMPLER, LIBERO) and real-world settings, distilled into latest VLA models

title: ReconVLA: Reconstructive Vision-Language-Action Model as Effective Robot Perceiver

claims.claim: Empirical analysis finds current VLAs struggle to allocate visual attention to target manipulated objects (attention stays dispersed rather than focused)
claims.direction: identifies a failure mode of standard VLA visual encoders/attention, motivating explicit grounding mechanisms
claims.conditions: analysis of existing VLA models, simulation and real-world

claims.claim: Adding an auxiliary reconstruction objective (a diffusion transformer reconstructing the gaze/target region conditioned on the model's visual output) as implicit grounding improves fine-grained visual representation learning and manipulation precision/generalization versus models without this auxiliary objective
