claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (100k+ trajectories, 2M samples) plus sim and real-world manipulation experiments

title: DTP: A Simple yet Effective Distracting Token Pruning Framework for Vision-Language Action Models

claims.claim: VLA models by default over-attend to task-irrelevant image regions ('distracting tokens'); dynamically pruning these tokens (plug-and-play, no architecture change) consistently improves task success rate across different VLA models on the SIMPLER benchmark, and there is a negative correlation between success rate and attention on task-irrelevant regions across all tested models
claims.direction: pruning/correcting visual attention to task-relevant regions improves manipulation success over unpruned baseline VLAs
claims.conditions: SIMPLER benchmark (sim), multiple transformer-based VLA models

title: RoboFlow4D: A Lightweight Flow World Model Toward Real-Time Flow-Guided Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A lightweight end-to-end flow world model that directly predicts multi-frame 3D flow from vision+language (instead of a modular multi-submodel pipeline) improves manipulation success rate versus modular flow-planner pipelines with high computational overhead
claims.direction: unified lightweight flow-world-model favored over stacked modular pipelines for both accuracy and efficiency
claims.conditions: sim and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: Slow-fast collaboration between flow prediction and action control enables real-time, resource-efficient manipulation
claims.direction: decoupled slow (flow) / fast (control) loop favored for real-time performance
claims.conditions: real and simulated manipulation

title: Learning Variable Impedance Skills for Contact-rich Tasks with Passivity Guarantees

claims.claim: An arc-length parameterized Gaussian Mixture Model that decouples temporal factors from spatial encoding learns coordinated position-orientation-force dynamics from human demonstrations, enabling stable, consistent, human-like contact-rich manipulation (apple peeling)
claims.direction: GMM-based skill representation (with temporal decoupling) favored for contact-rich, force-varying demonstration data over standard time-indexed representations
claims.conditions: real robot, apple-peeling demonstrations with varying execution speed

title: OASIS: From Simulation Data Collection to Real-World Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

claims.claim: Simulation-collected demonstrations (teleoperated in sim with reconstructed real-world object assets, then augmented with diverse domain randomization) trained a policy that achieves higher success rates on most real-world tasks than a policy trained on real-robot teleoperation data of equal/comparable scale
claims.direction: domain-randomized simulation data > real-robot teleoperation data for zero-shot real-world deployment

claims.claim: The success-rate advantage of sim-trained policies is attributed largely to broad lighting and environmental variations covered by simulation rendering, which real-robot teleoperation data fails to capture
claims.direction: lighting/environment diversity in (simulated) training data is the key driver of real-world robustness, more so than using real data alone
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot, zero-shot deployment across varied real lighting/environments

title: GigaWorld-1: A Roadmap to Build World Models for Robot Policy Evaluation

claims.claim: Across a systematic study of 7 video world models, 4 action representation schemes, and 324,000+ simulated rollouts matched to real robot executions, evaluator/world-model quality for robot policy assessment is dominated by long-horizon, action-faithful rollout consistency rather than short-term visual realism
claims.direction: long-horizon action-consistency is a more important world-model design target than short-horizon visual fidelity
claims.conditions: large-scale benchmark (WMBench) built from real-robot teleoperation data and matched rollouts, multiple model families

claims.claim: Architectural choices including memory design strongly determine a world model's alignment with real-world robot behavior
claims.direction: explicit memory-design choices materially affect long-horizon behavioral fidelity
claims.conditions: systematic multi-model benchmark study

claims.claim: Action representation/encoding scheme is one of the architectural choices strongly determining world-model alignment with real robot behavior
claims.direction: action encoding choice matters for downstream fidelity, though the study does not name a single best encoding in the abstract
claims.conditions: 4 action representation schemes compared across 7 video world models

title: CoRDE: Concept-Prior Routed Diffusion Experts for Structural Generalization in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A structure-guided variational Mixture-of-Experts diffusion policy (concept-prior routed, LoRA-based parameter-efficient experts on a frozen shared backbone) systematically reduces routing collapse and achieves superior action quality vs monolithic diffusion architectures and naive data-driven MoE, in multi-task/long-horizon settings with gradient conflicts between semantic sub-stages
claims.direction: concept-guided, parameter-efficient MoE diffusion policy favored over monolithic diffusion or naive MoE for multi-task/long-horizon behavioral diversity
claims.conditions: multi-task, long-horizon robot manipulation (sim/real not specified in abstract)

claims.claim: Semantic sub-stage routing derived from a frozen concept encoder improves incremental learning efficiency across multiple tasks
claims.direction: concept/semantic-conditioned expert routing favored over undifferentiated multi-task training
claims.conditions: multi-task manipulation

title: DLAM: Distributional Latent Actions with Temporal Constraints

claims.claim: Modeling latent action transitions as diagonal Gaussians with normalized composition/reversal constraints over triplets (rather than deterministic transition points) yields more temporally consistent latent dynamics and stronger reconstruction on held-out videos than existing latent-action baselines; ablations show normalized mean constraints account for most of the reconstruction gain
claims.direction: distributional (Gaussian) latent-action modeling with temporal consistency constraints favored over deterministic latent-action baselines
claims.conditions: action-free video pretraining, controlled ablations

claims.claim: Freezing the latent-action encoder and training a flow-matching policy on top improves downstream policy performance on MetaWorld MT50, LIBERO, and real-world manipulation under a controlled transfer protocol, leveraging abundant action-free video to compensate for scarce action-labeled robot data
claims.direction: pretraining on action-free video to build latent-action priors reduces reliance on scarce labeled robot demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation plus MetaWorld MT50 and LIBERO, controlled pi_0 transfer protocol

title: GaussianDream++: Efficient 3D Gaussian World Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Inserting training-only 'World State/Prediction Tokens' decoded (during training only) into Current/Future 3D Gaussian representations gives effective 3D supervision to a VLA backbone without requiring depth/point-cloud input or extra compute at inference (only ~20 world tokens retained, no online Gaussian decoding or rollout at deployment)

claims.claim: Method achieves 98.6% on LIBERO and 87.8% on LIBERO-Plus, and real-robot experiments improve average success from 29.2% (reproduced pi_0.5 baseline) to 52.5%
claims.direction: training-time future/current 3D-Gaussian prediction auxiliary objective substantially outperforms a strong VLA baseline (pi_0.5) without this objective
claims.conditions: real robot, reproduced pi_0.5 baseline for comparison

claims.claim: Method shows clear performance gains specifically under Camera and Layout shifts on LIBERO-Plus versus baseline
claims.direction: training-time 3D auxiliary supervision improves robustness to camera-viewpoint and scene-layout shift
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus perturbation benchmark

why_deep_read: Reports a large, concrete real-robot success-rate jump (29.2%->52.5%) over a named strong baseline (pi_0.5) plus explicit camera/layout-shift robustness gains, while keeping inference cost unchanged (no 3D input needed at deployment) -- directly actionable for our compute-constrained, camera-shift-prone setup (Q04/Q09/Q14); worth reading the ablation on how much of the gain survives without full Gaussian supervision.

title: Grasping Deformable Objects via Reinforcement Learning with Cross-Modal Attention to Visuo-Tactile Inputs

claims.claim: A cross-modal attention module fusing visual and tactile inputs, trained self-supervised via the RL loss, outperforms early- and late-fusion multi-modal baselines
claims.direction: cross-modal attention fusion favored over early/late fusion for combining vision and tactile sensing
claims.conditions: soft/deformable object grasping, simulation-based RL training

claims.claim: The cross-modal attention approach generalizes better to unseen robot motions and objects than baseline fusion methods across different environments
claims.direction: cross-modal attention fusion favored for generalization to unseen objects/motions
claims.conditions: deformable object grasping, multiple test environments

title: UniJEPA: Enhancing Robot Policy via Unified Continuous and Discrete Representation Learning

claims.claim: Pretraining a unified continuous+discrete visual representation model on over 1M internet-scale instructional manipulation videos, then fine-tuning on robot embodiment data, outperforms baseline representation/VLA methods by 9% (simulation) and 12% (real-world out-of-distribution tasks)

claims.claim: Dynamically modeling high-dimensional visual features (JEPA-style future representation prediction) as pretraining before learning action mappings improves downstream policy performance
claims.direction: predictive/future-representation auxiliary pretraining favored over direct action-only fine-tuning
claims.conditions: internet-video pretraining + robot fine-tuning

claims.claim: Gains are specifically reported on real-world out-of-distribution tasks (12% improvement), indicating better generalization under distribution shift
claims.direction: unified representation pretraining improves OOD/real-world generalization
claims.conditions: real-world OOD manipulation tasks

title: Spatial-Aware VLA Pretraining through Visual-Physical Alignment from Human Videos

claims.claim: Explicitly aligning 2D visual space with 3D physical space during VLA pretraining (using 3D annotations extracted from large-scale human demonstration videos), rather than relying on 2D-only visual-language pretraining, achieves significantly improved grounding between 2D vision and 3D action
claims.direction: 3D-aligned pretraining favored over standard 2D-only VLM pretraining for action grounding
claims.conditions: large-scale human video pretraining, downstream robot task adaptation

claims.claim: A dual-encoder architecture (VIPA-VLA) that augments semantic visual features with a dedicated 3D visual encoder results in more robust and generalizable robotic policies than 2D-only baselines
claims.direction: added 3D visual encoder branch favored over RGB-only encoder
claims.conditions: downstream robot manipulation tasks

title: FORGE-Tree: Diffusion-Forcing Tree Search for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Coupling a stage-aligned Diffusion Forcing head (frozen VLA encoder) with test-time Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion, partially denoising only a target trajectory segment while freezing others, improves LIBERO success rate by 13.4 to 17.2 percentage points over native VLA baselines (OpenVLA and Octo-Base), with gains persisting under comparable compute budgets
claims.direction: stage-aligned, tree-searched partial-denoising diffusion action generation outperforms standard fixed-hyperparameter full-trajectory diffusion/VLA baselines, especially long-horizon
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (sim), OpenVLA and Octo-Base baselines

claims.claim: Standard diffusion VLA policies that denoise the entire trajectory with fixed hyperparameters cause small geometric errors to compound across long-horizon subtask stages (drift/exposure bias); allocating extra test-time compute to tight-clearance segments via tree search mitigates this
claims.direction: adaptive, stage-aware test-time refinement of action chunks favored over uniform fixed-horizon denoising for long-horizon accuracy
claims.conditions: long-horizon LIBERO task variants

title: Decoupling Semantics and Geometric Grounding: Spatial Visual Prompts for Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Decoupling semantic reasoning from spatial control -- by parsing language instructions into zero-shot geometric masks (Spatial Visual Prompts) via a VLM and injecting them into a continuous action generator via lightweight feature fusion -- improves average success rate on highly ambiguous language-conditioned tasks from 24.0% to 39.5% versus monolithic end-to-end VLA baselines, reaching 67.8% on standard benchmarks
claims.direction: decoupled spatial-prompt language conditioning favored over monolithic end-to-end language-conditioned VLA for target disambiguation
claims.conditions: trained on 50 to 100 demonstrations, sim benchmarks plus real-world robot validation

claims.claim: Explicit spatial grounding provides stable optimization under low-data regimes (50-100 demos), significantly outperforming state-of-the-art VLAs and pure visuomotor baselines at this data scale
claims.direction: explicit geometric grounding injected via prompts favored over monolithic VLA when only 50-100 demos are available
claims.conditions: 50-100 demonstrations, real-world robotic experiments

why_deep_read: Uses almost exactly our demonstration budget (50-100 demos) and quantifies a large success-rate jump (24.0%->39.5%) for language-conditioned disambiguation via a decoupled spatial-prompt architecture -- directly relevant to our planned language-conditioned second-object task (Q08) and low-data regime (Q13); worth reading the fusion-mechanism details and failure cases.

title: DexVerse: A Modular Benchmark for Multi-Task, Multi-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Benchmarking representative methods (Diffusion Policy, DP3, OpenVLA, pi_0.5) across 19 tasks under configurable visual variations (textures, background, lighting, camera viewpoints) reveals substantial challenges in visuomotor robustness for all tested methods
claims.direction: none of the tested representative policy families (2D diffusion, 3D point-cloud diffusion, VLA) is robust to combined lighting/background/viewpoint variation
claims.conditions: large-scale modular sim benchmark, 3 robot arms, 6 dexterous hands, 3,180 VR-teleoperated demonstrations with RGB/depth/point-cloud/proprioception

claims.claim: DP3 (point-cloud-based diffusion policy) is benchmarked directly against 2D Diffusion Policy and VLA baselines (OpenVLA, pi_0.5) under the same controlled visual-variation conditions
claims.direction: provides a controlled comparison point for point-cloud vs RGB-only policies under visual shift (specific winner not stated in abstract)
claims.conditions: same benchmark, 19 tasks

claims.claim: The benchmark explicitly varies camera viewpoint as one of its controllable visual conditions to test cross-viewpoint generalization
claims.direction: establishes camera-viewpoint robustness as a first-class, separately measurable axis
claims.conditions: modular benchmark with configurable camera viewpoints

why_deep_read: This is a controlled, multi-baseline (Diffusion Policy vs DP3 vs OpenVLA vs pi_0.5) benchmark specifically varying lighting/background/camera-viewpoint -- exactly our Q03/Q04/Q11/Q14 robustness questions; the full results table would show which action-head/vision-input combination degrades least under our exact failure modes (lighting, camera shift).

title: XPACE: Joint World and Action Modeling from Heterogeneous Experience

claims.claim: A shared video backbone jointly trained as world-action model (predicting actions+future video) and world simulator (predicting visual consequences of actions), using action-unlabeled video plus action-labeled demonstrations with a coarse-to-fine curriculum, improves robustness and enables transfer of human-observed skills to tasks absent from robot demonstrations; self-generated recovery trajectories from the simulator further improve real-world task completion
claims.direction: joint world+action modeling with self-generated recovery data favored over action-only imitation learning
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot (XPENG IRON), heterogeneous human+robot demonstration data

title: Robotic Strawberry Harvesting with Robust Vision and Deep Reinforcement Learning based Sim-to-Real Control

claims.claim: A sim-trained (Isaac Lab) PPO policy producing smooth joint-position commands generated stable and dynamically smoother motion than an inverse-kinematics-based MoveIt planner baseline in controlled in-house tests
claims.direction: learned RL policy favored over classical IK-based planning baseline for motion smoothness
claims.conditions: real UR10e robot, greenhouse harvesting task, sim-to-real transfer

title: Turning Video Models into Generalist Robot Policies

claims.claim: Decoupling an embodiment-agnostic action-free video world model from a separately-trained, embodiment-specific inverse dynamics model (IDM) based on the robot's Jacobian is a data-efficient and scalable alternative to jointly finetuning a video model with action-labeled data; the same video planner can be reused across multiple embodiments by swapping only the IDM
claims.direction: decoupled video-planner + embodiment-specific IDM favored over jointly-finetuned video+action foundation models for data efficiency and embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world benchmarks, zero-shot Panda arm manipulation and 16-DoF Allegro-hand tasks

claims.claim: Video prediction pretraining (action-free) serves as the core world-modeling signal, with the IDM trained independently using readily available self-play data
claims.direction: video-prediction pretraining plus separate IDM favored over end-to-end action-video co-training
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment sim+real evaluation

title: G0.5: One Autoregressive Stream for Robot Reasoning and Action

claims.claim: A single autoregressive transformer emitting both reasoning and action tokens under one objective (with a cross-embodiment action tokenizer and visual-memory module) surpasses the standard 'VLM + separately-trained flow-matching action expert' recipe: real-world fine-tuning success 76.7% vs 53.3% for pi_0.5 and 24.4% for GR00T-N1.7; LIBERO 98.9%; RoboTwin 2.0 93.3%; SimplerEnv-Bridge 87.3%
claims.direction: unified autoregressive reasoning+action stream favored over decoupled VLM-context-encoder + separate flow-matching action-expert architecture
claims.conditions: real R1lite/R1pro robots, plus multiple sim benchmarks, foundation-model-scale pretraining on large robot+VQA data

claims.claim: Because reasoning and action share one set of weights, natural-language prompts directly steer action granularity, task horizon, and out-of-distribution scene handling without further training
claims.direction: shared reasoning/action weights favored for flexible language-conditioned control over separate planner+action-expert designs
claims.conditions: real robots, out-of-distribution scenes

claims.claim: DROID post-training followed by zero-shot transfer to an unseen environment and objects reaches 82.5% success
claims.direction: large-scale post-training enables zero-shot generalization to new environments/objects
claims.conditions: DROID-scale post-training, zero-shot real-world evaluation

title: ContextFlow: In-Context Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A conditional flow-matching model conditioned on demonstrations/observations (with perceiver-style multimodal context compressors) outperforms an autoregressive in-context imitation baseline (ICRT) by 35 percentage points average success rate on unseen LIBERO task configurations, and matches a task-specific fine-tuned flow-matching VLA (pi_0) without any fine-tuning on unseen tasks
claims.direction: flow-matching-based in-context imitation favored over autoregressive/discretized-action in-context imitation, and can match fine-tuned performance without fine-tuning
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark, unseen task configurations; real single-arm and bimanual robots for generalization tests

claims.claim: On real robots, the method generalizes to unseen configurations without task-specific fine-tuning, achieving 40% success on a new pen-uncapping configuration
claims.direction: in-context conditioning on demonstrations (rather than fine-tuning) is sufficient for some novel real-world configurations
claims.conditions: real robot, novel/unseen task configuration

title: Transferring the Intelligence of VLMs to Robotic Control

claims.claim: An agentic VLM controlling a robot in closed loop via a compact discrete command interface (translation/rotation/gripper), with no task-specific robot training, outperforms several strong policies trained on benchmark-specific robot data in a zero-shot setting; one in-context demonstration further raises RoboTwin 2.0 C2R success from 53.2% (zero-shot) to 73.6% (one-shot), exceeding a pi_0.5 baseline (46.0%)
claims.direction: VLM-driven closed-loop discrete-command control (with optional single-shot in-context demo) favored over trained task-specific policies in some benchmarks
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 C2R and RoboDojo sim benchmarks; also transfers to real Franka robot (block-in-basket, block stacking)

claims.claim: A single in-context demonstration substantially improves success rate over zero-shot VLM control, without any robot-specific training
claims.direction: one-shot in-context demonstration favored over zero-shot-only or full task-specific training when demo budget is minimal
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real Franka robot

title: STEER: Flexible Robotic Manipulation via Dense Language Grounding

claims.claim: Training language-grounded policies on dense natural-language annotations of modular manipulation skills allows learned skills to be recombined to synthesize novel behaviors for new situations or tasks without additional data collection or training
claims.direction: dense, modular language-grounded skill decomposition favored over monolithic task-specific language-conditioned policies for compositional generalization
claims.conditions: real robot experiments (skill composition demonstrated qualitatively)

title: Meta-Controller: Few-Shot Imitation of Unseen Embodiments and Tasks in Continuous Control

claims.claim: A few-shot behavior-cloning framework using as few as five reward-free demonstrations, with a joint-level input-output representation and structure-motion state encoder, shows superior few-shot generalization to unseen embodiments and tasks compared to modular policy-learning and other few-shot imitation-learning approaches
claims.direction: joint-level unified representation + matching-based policy favored over modular policy learning or standard few-shot IL for 5-demo generalization
claims.conditions: DeepMind Control suite (simulation), continuous control tasks, unseen embodiments/tasks

title: Teaching Metric Distance to Discrete Autoregressive Language Models

claims.claim: Replacing one-hot targets with a distance-aware, reward-weighted target distribution (DIST2Loss) for discrete autoregressive action-token prediction accelerates robotic manipulation learning by improving action learning, in addition to improving visual grounding and vector-quantized image generation
claims.direction: distance-aware supervision for discrete/tokenized action prediction favored over standard one-hot cross-entropy supervision
claims.conditions: discrete/VQ action-token models, multiple domains including robotic manipulation

title: VILP: Imitation Learning With Latent Video Planning

claims.claim: A latent video diffusion model generating temporally-consistent, multi-view predictive robot videos, used for imitation-learning-based policy, outperforms existing video-generation robot policies on training cost, inference speed, temporal consistency, and downstream policy performance, and possesses robust capability to represent multi-modal action distributions
claims.direction: latent (rather than pixel-space) video-planning diffusion policy favored over prior video-generation-based robot policies
claims.conditions: multi-view (2 views), low-resolution (96x160) generated video, comparison to existing video-gen robot policy baselines

claims.claim: The video generation model runs at 5 Hz for two views x six frames at 96x160 resolution, described as highly time-efficient relative to baselines
claims.direction: latent video planning favored over pixel-space/heavier video generation for inference speed
claims.conditions: low-resolution multi-view video generation

claims.claim: VILP can rely less on extensive high-quality task-specific robot action data while still maintaining robust policy performance compared to other imitation learning methods
claims.direction: latent video planning reduces dependence on large task-specific demonstration datasets
claims.conditions: comparison against other imitation learning methods

title: TARAD: Task-Aware Robot Affordance-Centric Diffusion Policy Learned From LLM-Generated Demonstrations

claims.claim: An affordance-centric 3D diffusion policy, with affordances incorporated into the observation space via LLM/VLM-derived high-level planning, combines the precise control of imitation learning with the generalization of foundation models
claims.direction: affordance-conditioned diffusion policy favored over plain diffusion/imitation-learning policies lacking affordance/foundation-model grounding
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation and real-world UR5e experiments

claims.claim: A heuristic motion planner plus LLM/VLM planning enables fully automatic, zero-shot generation of a labeled training dataset (with language labels and affordances), without relying on expert demonstrations or predefined motion primitives
claims.direction: LLM/VLM-generated synthetic demonstrations favored as a substitute for costly expert teleoperation data collection
claims.conditions: RLBench sim + real UR5e, zero-shot dataset generation

title: Constraint-Preserving Data Generation for Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Constraint-Preserving Data Generation (CP-Gen) uses a SINGLE expert trajectory to generate demonstrations with novel object geometries/poses, by formulating robot skills as keypoint-trajectory constraints relative to task-relevant objects; policies trained on CP-Gen-generated data achieve an average 77% success rate across 16 sim tasks and 4 real-world tasks, versus 50% for the best baseline
claims.direction: geometry-aware, constraint-preserving synthetic demonstration generation from one real trajectory outperforms prior pose-variation data-generation baselines
claims.conditions: single real expert trajectory as seed, 16 simulation + 4 real-world tasks including multi-stage, non-prehensile, and tight-tolerance manipulation; zero-shot real-world transfer

claims.claim: Policies transfer zero-shot to the real world and generalize across object geometry/pose variation despite being generated from just one expert demonstration
claims.direction: one real demonstration, expanded via constraint-preserving generation, can substitute for many additional real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot transfer, single seed trajectory per task

why_deep_read: Directly tests the extreme low-data regime relevant to our project (expanding from a single real demo to a full generalizing policy) with a concrete, large success-rate gap (77% vs 50%) over the best baseline across both sim and real tasks; the mechanism (keypoint-trajectory constraints) could let us multiply our ~50-100 pumpkin demos into many more object-pose variations without extra teleoperation.

title: World In Your Hands: A Large-Scale and Open-source Ecosystem for Learning Human-centric Manipulation in the Wild

claims.claim: Integrating WIYH's large-scale (1,000+ hours) human-centric manipulation data (collected in-the-wild with millimeter-scale motion accuracy via a wearable kit) improves robotic manipulation success rates from 8% to 60% in cluttered scenes
claims.direction: supplementing robot training data with large-scale human-centric demonstration data strongly favored over robot-only demonstration data, especially in cluttered scenes
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment policy learning, cluttered real-world scenes

claims.claim: The large success-rate jump (8% to 60%) is specifically reported for cluttered-scene manipulation, indicating human data helps generalization/robustness to clutter
claims.direction: human-centric demonstration data aids robustness to cluttered/distractor-rich scenes
claims.conditions: cluttered real-world scenes

title: PointACT: Automatic Robot Manipulation with Cross-Modal Action Chunking Transformer on Image-Point Cloud

claims.claim: Fusing RGB images with 3D point clouds (point clouds re-rendered into virtual perspectives) into an Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) gives an absolute accuracy improvement of 17.2% over single-modality (RGB-only or point-cloud-only) ACT baselines
claims.direction: cross-modal RGB+point-cloud fusion favored over single-modality (RGB-only) ACT for precise manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world robot manipulation tasks (cup grasping, drawer opening, shape sorting)

claims.claim: PointACT achieves a 70% average success rate with just 50 demonstrations per task, outperforming state-of-the-art performance on three real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: cross-modal (RGB+point cloud) ACT achieves strong performance at only 50 demos/task
claims.conditions: real-world robot, 50 demonstrations per task, 3 tasks

why_deep_read: Uses the same ACT baseline family as common low-cost-arm setups and exactly our demo budget (50/task) with a quantified accuracy gain (17.2%) from adding point-cloud input -- directly answers whether depth/point-cloud fusion is worth the added complexity at our data scale (Q04/Q13); worth reading the point-cloud re-rendering method and per-task breakdown.

title: TwinRL: Digital Twin-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Real-World Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A digital-twin-guided RL post-training framework (SFT warm-up, twin RL warm-up expanding the SFT-induced exploration space, then real-world RL) achieves near-100% success in-distribution and out-of-distribution, delivering over 30% faster convergence than prior real-world RL methods
claims.direction: digital-twin-guided exploration expansion favored over standard real-world-only RL fine-tuning of VLA models
claims.conditions: real-world robot, four tasks, high-fidelity twin reconstructed from smartphone-captured scenes

claims.claim: The approach requires only 20 minutes of on-robot interaction to reach near-100% success after SFT, versus more real-world RL interaction time for prior methods
claims.direction: twin-guided RL warm-up sharply reduces required real-robot interaction time versus real-world-only RL
claims.conditions: real-world robot, minimal (20 min) additional on-robot interaction beyond SFT

title: Structural Action Transformer for 3D Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Reframing each action chunk as a variable-length, unordered sequence of joint-wise trajectories (rather than a temporal sequence) generated via continuous-time flow matching from 3D point clouds consistently outperforms all baselines in sample efficiency and cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: structural (joint-wise, order-invariant) action-chunk representation with flow matching favored over standard temporal-sequence action-chunk representations, especially for heterogeneous/high-DoF embodiments
claims.conditions: pre-training on large-scale heterogeneous datasets, fine-tuning on sim and real-world dexterous manipulation

claims.claim: Learning to generate trajectories directly from 3D point clouds (rather than 2D observations) is necessary to capture 3D spatial relations for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation
claims.direction: point-cloud input favored over 2D-only observations for structural/cross-embodiment policies
claims.conditions: sim and real-world dexterous (multi-fingered) manipulation

title: Agile-VLA: Few-Shot Industrial Pose Rectification via Implicit Affordance Anchoring

claims.claim: Decoupling perception (10 Hz) from control (50 Hz) via an asynchronous dual-stream architecture, combined with an Implicit Affordance Anchoring mechanism that maps geometric visual cues directly into structured parametric action primitives (bypassing high-latency semantic inference in the control loop), mitigates the frequency mismatch between high-latency semantic inference and high-frequency control needed for dynamic manipulation on edge devices
claims.direction: asynchronous perception/control decoupling plus lightweight geometric-anchor action primitives favored over synchronous high-latency semantic-inference control loops on edge hardware
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF manipulator, NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano edge device

claims.claim: The system achieves robust rectification of complex, irregular workpieces using only 5-shot demonstrations
claims.direction: implicit affordance anchoring enables strong performance from as few as 5 demonstrations
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF manipulator, industrial pose-reorientation task, 5-shot demos

why_deep_read: Directly targets our exact pain point -- high-latency semantic inference vs. high-frequency control mismatch on an edge GPU -- with an async dual-stream design (10Hz perception/50Hz control) plus only 5-shot demonstrations; full text would give the affordance-anchoring mechanism details and latency numbers directly transferable to our chunk-boundary jerkiness and 2s-latency problem (Q10/Q13).

title: TSD: A Physics-Inspired Trajectory Saliency Detector for Efficient Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A training-free saliency detector using spatial entropy (fine-grained manipulation) and centripetal acceleration (agile maneuvering) identifies which parts of a demonstration trajectory are most critical to task success versus prevalent-but-less-relevant transitional motions; models trained on TSD-condensed datasets achieve comparable or superior performance using 25% less data on average, in both simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: saliency-based dataset compression/expansion (prioritizing precise/agile segments) favored over uniform use of full, undifferentiated demonstration trajectories
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world imitation learning experiments

title: WetRobo: A Reproducible Robot Kit for Coding Agents in Biological Laboratories

claims.claim: A VLA policy fine-tuned on demonstrations from one laboratory succeeded in that lab but failed to transfer to a second laboratory (different environment), whereas an LLM coding agent (not a learned visuomotor policy) succeeded in both labs on the same real-world task (removing a bottle cap)
claims.direction: a fine-tuned VLA's success does not generalize across environment/lab changes, in contrast to a non-learned coding-agent approach
claims.conditions: real robot arm, two different real laboratories (Lab X, Lab Y), simple manipulation tasks

title: IN-RIL: Interleaved Reinforcement and Imitation Learning for Policy Fine-Tuning

claims.claim: Periodically interleaving IL updates after multiple RL updates during fine-tuning (with gradient-separation into orthogonal subspaces to avoid destructive interference) stabilizes learning and improves sample efficiency versus standard sequential IL-pretrain-then-RL-finetune, e.g. improving Robomimic Transport success rate from 12% to 88% (6.3x)
claims.direction: interleaved IL+RL fine-tuning favored over pure sequential IL-then-RL for policy fine-tuning stability/efficiency
claims.conditions: 14 manipulation and locomotion tasks across FurnitureBench, OpenAI Gym, and Robomimic (simulation only)

claims.claim: Interleaving expert-demonstration-guided IL updates during RL fine-tuning significantly improves sample efficiency and mitigates performance collapse in both long- and short-horizon tasks with sparse or dense rewards
claims.direction: periodic reuse of demonstration data during RL fine-tuning favored over demo-free RL fine-tuning for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks, plug-in compatible with various RL algorithms

title: ActiveUMI: Robotic Manipulation with Active Perception from Robot-Free Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Capturing an operator's deliberate head movements (active, egocentric perception) during portable VR teleoperation data collection, and training policies on this active-perception data, links visual attention to manipulation and contributes to strong task performance
claims.direction: active/egocentric camera-attention data collection favored over passive fixed-viewpoint demonstration collection
claims.conditions: portable VR teleoperation kit, six challenging bimanual real-robot tasks

claims.claim: Policies trained exclusively on ActiveUMI data achieve 70% average success on in-distribution tasks and retain 56% success when tested on novel objects and in new environments
claims.direction: active-perception-based demonstration collection yields policies that generalize substantially (though with some drop) to novel objects/environments
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, novel objects and new environments

claims.claim: A portable, robot-free human demonstration collection system (no physical robot needed for data collection) is proposed as a scalable pathway to generate large amounts of demonstration data
claims.direction: robot-free portable data collection favored for scalability over teleoperation requiring the physical robot
claims.conditions: human demonstrations mapped to robot end-effector kinematics

title: Observer Actor: Active Vision Imitation Learning with Sparse View Gaussian Splatting

claims.claim: Dynamically moving an 'observer' camera/arm to an optimal viewpoint (found by virtually exploring a 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction built from three images) before the 'actor' arm executes its policy, keeps observations closer to the occlusion-free training distribution and significantly outperforms static-camera setups
claims.direction: active/optimized camera viewpoint selection favored over static fixed-camera observation for policy execution
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot with wrist-mounted cameras, tested with trajectory-transfer and behavior-cloning imitation learning methods

claims.claim: Trajectory transfer improves by 145% without occlusion and 233% with occlusion, and behavior cloning improves by 75% and 143% respectively, when using the active-vision observer setup versus static cameras
claims.direction: active viewpoint selection dramatically improves robustness specifically under occlusion versus static camera setups
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, occlusion and non-occlusion conditions

title: SpatialVLA: Exploring Spatial Representations for Visual-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Pre-learned spatial action grids can be re-discretized to capture robot-specific spatial action movements when transferring to new real-world robot setups, showing strong in-distribution generalization and out-of-distribution adaptation
claims.direction: spatial-grid-based discretized action representation (re-discretizable per new robot embodiment) favored for cross-setup adaptation
claims.conditions: real-world setups, generalist robot policy learning (abstract text truncated in source)

claims.claim: Spatial-aware visual-language representations are described as crucial for generalist robot policy learning performance
claims.direction: spatial-aware representation learning favored over standard (non-spatial-aware) VLM representations
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation evaluations (abstract truncated)

title: Towards Efficient Robot Learning: Diffusion-Style Skill Learning and Transfer on Platform with Multi-Modal Perception and Force Feedback

claims.claim: An efficient 3D point cloud encoder is introduced to enhance diffusion-style manipulation policy performance on a multi-modal, force-feedback bimanual platform
claims.direction: added 3D point-cloud encoding favored for diffusion policies over vision-only encoding in contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real bimanual Franka leader-follower platform, contact-rich multimodal tasks

claims.claim: An inpainting-based method is proposed specifically to improve action continuity in diffusion-style policies (addressing discontinuities likely at chunk boundaries), alongside a stochastic interpolation framework to reduce distribution discrepancies
claims.direction: inpainting-based action-continuity correction favored over naive chunked diffusion sampling for smoother execution
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, contact-rich multimodal tasks (e.g., cooking/serving scenario)

claims.claim: LLMs are incorporated for natural language interaction, task instruction parsing, and semantic execution alongside the diffusion policy
claims.direction: LLM-based language parsing layered on top of a diffusion visuomotor policy for multi-step task execution
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, natural-language task instructions

title: Integrated design of compliance control and intelligent interaction for bionic manipulator based on deep learning

claims.claim: A 3D visual attention-based imitation learning module (combined with adaptive impedance control and a multimodal Transformer for intent parsing) achieves a 17.3% improvement in success rate for complex manipulation tasks compared to traditional methods, plus 96.7% intent recognition accuracy and a 65.2% reduction in contact-force tracking error
claims.direction: 3D visual-attention-based imitation learning module favored over traditional (non-attention) imitation learning approaches
claims.conditions: real custom 7-DoF biomimetic robotic arm, unstructured/variable-stiffness environments

title: ACE: Agentic Control for Embodied Manipulation via Zero-shot Workflow Reasoning

claims.claim: Combining agentic workflow reasoning with a mask-mediated vision-action interface (grounding language sub-goals into a tracked target/destination mask passed to a task-agnostic pick-and-place primitive) achieves 50% success in zero-shot equation formation and 70% in constraint-based object retrieval, where standard end-to-end baselines struggle to complete these logically demanding tasks at all
claims.direction: decoupled agentic workflow reasoning + mask-mediated grounding favored over end-to-end language-conditioned policies for logically complex, long-horizon language tasks
claims.conditions: zero-shot tabletop pick-and-place, novel semantic constraints and randomized scenes, closed-loop verification/replanning

title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a similarity-based recall-ranking-re-ranking pipeline to mine only ~1.49M task-relevant samples (<5% of a ~32M egocentric human video pool) for VLA post-training improves overall success rate from 47.7% to 61.1%, compared to a baseline trained on an equal amount of randomly sampled human data
claims.direction: curated, task-relevant data selection favored over indiscriminate/random data mixing of the same size, i.e. data relevance/diversity matters more than raw quantity
claims.conditions: VLA post-training with human egocentric video data, morphology-agnostic action space, no architecture changes

title: MENTOR: Mixture-of-Experts Network with Task-Oriented Perturbation for Visual Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Replacing a standard MLP backbone with a mixture-of-experts (MoE) backbone, plus a task-oriented perturbation mechanism, outperforms state-of-the-art methods across three simulation benchmarks and achieves 83% average success on three real-world robotic manipulation tasks, versus 32% for the strongest existing model-free visual RL algorithm
claims.direction: MoE backbone + task-oriented perturbation favored over standard MLP backbones for visual RL sample efficiency and real-world manipulation performance
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation tasks (visual RL, not imitation learning)

claims.claim: The architecture/optimization changes are specifically framed as improving sample efficiency, a critical bottleneck for practical real-world visual RL
claims.direction: architectural sample-efficiency improvements favored to reduce real-world data/interaction requirements
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation

title: A Self-Correcting Vision-Language-Action Model for Fast and Slow System Manipulation

claims.claim: Integrating a fast system (parameter-efficient fine-tuned pose predictor) with a slow system (chain-of-thought-based failure reflection and corrective action generation) within a single VLA policy improves manipulation accuracy over a prior SOTA VLA baseline, with an efficient correction process demonstrated in both simulation and real-world tasks
claims.direction: dual fast/slow-system VLA architecture (with explicit failure reflection) favored over a single fast-system-only VLA for robustness to novel/complex tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation, seen and unseen tasks

claims.claim: The self-correction mechanism improves manipulation accuracy on both seen and unseen tasks compared to the previous SOTA VLA
claims.direction: explicit failure-reflection/correction mechanism favored for generalization to unseen tasks
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation, unseen tasks

title: Smooth Filtering Neural Network for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A neural network architecture (Smonet) with explicit low-pass filtering ability (serial filtering layers with inertia cells and an adaptive cell) learns a low-frequency representation in hidden layers, alleviating policy non-smoothness under observation noise/disturbances without compromising control performance, versus standard MLP and GRU architectures
claims.direction: architecture-level low-pass filtering favored over standard MLP/GRU policy networks for producing smooth control signals
claims.conditions: simulated robot control tasks and a real-world mobile robot obstacle-avoidance experiment (RL policies, not action-chunking imitation learning)

claims.claim: Smonet achieves up to a 72.7% reduction in the action fluctuation ratio compared to traditional (MLP/GRU) network structures across diverse simulated and one real-world control task
claims.direction: filtering-based architecture strongly favored over standard architectures for reducing action fluctuation/jerkiness
claims.conditions: real-world mobile robot obstacle avoidance plus simulated control tasks, various observation noise levels

why_deep_read: Directly targets our jerky-motion problem with a concrete, large quantified smoothness gain (72.7% less action fluctuation) via an architectural (frequency-domain filtering) fix rather than an inference-scheduling fix; worth checking whether this filtering approach is compatible with action-chunked imitation-learning policies (vs. the RL setting tested here) for Q06/Q10.

title: PvP: Data-Efficient Humanoid Robot Learning with Proprioceptive-Privileged Contrastive Representations

claims.claim: A contrastive representation-learning framework exploiting complementarity between proprioceptive and privileged states, without hand-crafted data augmentation, improves sample efficiency and final performance versus baseline state-representation-learning methods
claims.direction: proprioceptive-privileged contrastive representation learning favored over baseline SRL methods for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: humanoid whole-body-control tasks (velocity tracking, motion imitation), not manipulation; real humanoid robot (LimX Oli)

title: SAGE: State-Aware Guided End-to-End Policy for Multi-Stage Sequential Tasks via Hidden Markov Decision Process

claims.claim: Modeling multi-stage manipulation tasks as a Hidden Markov Decision Process, with a state-transition network inferring latent task stages and a state-aware action policy conditioning on both observation and inferred hidden state, resolves state ambiguity (visually similar observations requiring different actions) that plain end-to-end policies cannot disambiguate; SAGE achieves 100% task success in real-world multi-stage tasks with state ambiguity, markedly surpassing baselines
claims.direction: explicit hidden-state/latent-stage modeling favored over standard observation-only end-to-end policies for resolving visual state ambiguity in multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: real-world multi-stage sequential manipulation tasks with state ambiguity

claims.claim: A semi-automatic labeling pipeline (active learning + soft label interpolation) maintains this near-100% performance while requiring manual stage labeling on only about 13% of states
claims.direction: minimal manual state-labeling (13%) suffices when combined with active learning/soft interpolation, reducing annotation burden for hidden-state supervision
claims.conditions: real-world multi-stage tasks

why_deep_read: Directly addresses causal confusion / state ambiguity (explicitly named in our Q07), with a 100% real-world success rate against baselines that presumably fail on ambiguous, visually-similar states -- this is exactly the class of problem underlying jerky/incorrect behavior when a single fixed-camera view can't disambiguate task stage; worth reading how much labeling/complexity this adds for our pick-and-place-in-tray task.

title: UniSkill: Imitating Human Videos via Cross-Embodiment Skill Representations

claims.claim: Embodiment-agnostic skill representations learned from large-scale, unlabeled cross-embodiment video data (no shared scenes/tasks required between human and robot data) can guide robot policies trained only on robot data, successfully transferring to unseen human video prompts
claims.direction: unlabeled cross-embodiment video pretraining favored over requiring paired human-robot demonstration data for skill transfer
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world environments, unseen human video prompts as conditioning

claims.claim: Skill representations extracted from video (rather than from paired action-labeled data) can effectively condition/guide a robot policy's action selection
claims.direction: video-derived skill/latent conditioning favored as an alternative to action-labeled skill representations
claims.conditions: sim + real-world

title: Learning-based Cooperative Robotic Paper Wrapping: A Unified Control Policy with Residual Force Control

claims.claim: A Sub-task Aware Robotic Transformer (START) that introduces explicit sub-task IDs for temporal grounding across a full long-horizon manipulation sequence outperforms vanilla Action Chunking with Transformer (ACT), which is typically only applied to short tasks, achieving a 97% success rate on real-world long-horizon deformable-object wrapping
claims.direction: sub-task-ID-conditioned unified chunking policy favored over vanilla ACT for long-horizon, multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: real-world robot, long-horizon gift-wrapping task combining LLM high-level planning with hybrid IL+RL low-level policy

claims.claim: A unified transformer-based policy that learns sub-goals (rather than merely replicating motion sequences) reduces the need for specialized per-stage models while bridging high-level intent with fine-grained force control
claims.direction: single unified sub-goal-aware policy favored over multiple specialized per-stage models
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon deformable object manipulation

title: Action with Visual Primitives

claims.claim: Decoupling a VLM (which infers the next-stage target and emits visual-primitive tokens) from a flow-matching action expert that is conditioned on those tokens (supervised via end-effector kinematics), rather than mapping language+vision to actions in a single forward pass, improves real-robot pick-and-place success rate by 37.04% over pi_0.5 and outperforms other recent methods
claims.direction: visual-primitive-centric interface (decoupling cognition/perception from motor control) favored over single-forward-pass VLA architectures
claims.conditions: real-robot general pick-and-place tasks

claims.claim: Entangling instruction comprehension, spatial scene understanding, and motor control in a single learning objective forces the action expert to implicitly relearn cognitive/perceptual capabilities already present in the pretrained VLM, limiting learning efficiency and generalization
claims.direction: preserving/reusing pretrained VLM capabilities via an explicit visual-primitive interface favored over forcing the action expert to relearn them
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation, pretrained VLM backbone

claims.claim: AVP shows consistent gains in data efficiency, spatial-compositional generalization, and object-level transfer compared to baselines
claims.direction: visual-primitive-conditioned architecture favored for data efficiency over baseline VLA architectures
claims.conditions: real-robot pick-and-place, generalization/transfer evaluation

title: Act2Goal: From World Model To General Goal-conditioned Policy

claims.claim: A goal-conditioned visual world model that generates a plausible sequence of intermediate visual states (rather than single-step action prediction) captures long-horizon task structure and, when coupled to motor control via cross-attention, achieves strong performance across long-horizon manipulation tasks
claims.direction: goal-conditioned world-model-based multi-step planning favored over single-step action-prediction policies for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world environments, initialized from large-scale imitation learning

claims.claim: Multi-Scale Temporal Hashing decomposes the imagined trajectory into dense proximal frames for fine-grained closed-loop control and sparse distal frames for global task consistency, enabling coherent long-horizon behavior while remaining reactive to local disturbances
claims.direction: multi-scale (dense near-term + sparse far-term) temporal representation favored over a single fixed prediction horizon for long-horizon control
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated long-horizon manipulation

claims.claim: Reward-free online autonomous improvement via hindsight goal relabeling and LoRA-based finetuning improves real-world success rates from 30% to 90% on challenging out-of-distribution tasks within minutes of autonomous interaction
claims.direction: brief autonomous online fine-tuning (no external supervision/reward) dramatically improves OOD task success beyond offline-only imitation learning
claims.conditions: real-world robot, out-of-distribution tasks, minutes of online autonomous interaction

title: TRACT: Temporally Routed Action Chunks with Chronological Phase Authority for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: When a predicted action-chunk horizon crosses a procedural/phase boundary, assigning the current phase label to the entire chunk creates a structural temporal mismatch; factorizing phase-structured action chunking into an accepted current phase plus a single CURRENT-to-NEXT boundary inside the future horizon (with chronological phase authority) eliminates this mismatch, reducing observed phase ambiguity from 8/10 to 0/10 trials and stalls from 4/10 to 0/10
claims.direction: explicit within-chunk phase-boundary routing favored over flat, single-phase-labeled action chunking for tasks crossing procedural boundaries
claims.conditions: six real-robot task variants, ten trials each, contact-rich (wiping) manipulation

claims.claim: Full TRACT (routed phase representation + causal response-deficit integrator for contact execution) achieves 10/10 full-sequence success and 99.00% median wipe completion, versus 6/10 success and 77.08% median completion for a flat (non-routed) package, and versus 3/10 success and 8.03% median completion under a different comparison setting
claims.direction: phase-boundary-aware action-chunk routing plus contact-response compensation favored over flat chunking for reliable, non-stalling contact-rich execution
claims.conditions: real-robot contact-rich manipulation, six variants x ten trials

why_deep_read: This is the most direct match to our observed 'jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries' failure: it explicitly diagnoses the chunk/procedural-boundary mismatch and reports concrete real-robot before/after numbers (phase ambiguity 8/10->0/10, stalls 4/10->0/10, success 6/10->10/10). Reading the routing/boundary mechanism in full would let us directly adapt it to our own chunked action head for Q06/Q10.

title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Injecting perturbation and bridging segments into demonstrations (a 'Retry' mechanism decoupling robot pose from environment state) lets a policy autonomously handle common execution deviations, rather than relying solely on trajectory-monotonic, failure-free demonstrations
claims.direction: augmenting demonstrations with perturbation/recovery segments favored over training only on clean, failure-free demonstrations
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation tasks, VLA models

claims.claim: A 'Reset' pipeline that uses an MLLM to automatically identify out-of-distribution failure states from execution videos, and trains a small library of object-centric reset skills, significantly improves task success and robustness on challenging manipulation tasks versus baseline VLAs without recovery mechanisms
claims.direction: explicit failure-detection-and-reset skill library favored over VLAs lacking any recovery mechanism for OOD/state-breaking failures
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation, online MLLM monitor arbitrating execution vs reset

title: Energy-Regularized Imitation Learning for Force- and Work-Aware Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding a differentiable, learned mechanical-work predictor as a regularizer when fine-tuning a pretrained manipulation policy (RVT-2 on RLBench, 12 tasks) reduces average mechanical work from 208.8J to 204.4J (2.1% reduction) while task success rate slightly increases from 86.2% to 86.9%
claims.direction: energy/work-aware auxiliary regularization favored over standard fine-tuning without it, for suppressing physically inefficient motion without hurting (and slightly helping) success rate
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation, 12 manipulation tasks, RVT-2 policy

title: Learning Grasping for Robot with Parallel Gripper from Human Demonstration via Contact Analysis

claims.claim: Among three proposed schemes for mapping high-DoF human hand poses to a low-DoF parallel-jaw gripper action, the optimal mapping scheme achieves an overall success rate of 87% in real-world robotic grasping, outperforming the other mapping schemes
claims.direction: a specific human-to-gripper action-mapping scheme is empirically superior to alternative mapping schemes for parallel grippers
claims.conditions: real-world robot with parallel jaw gripper, human demonstration via contact analysis

title: BiKC: Keypose-Conditioned Consistency Policy for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A consistency-model-based trajectory generator (trained from scratch without distillation), conditioned on high-level predicted keyposes, surpasses baseline imitation-learning methods (implied diffusion-policy-style baselines) in both success rate and operational efficiency
claims.direction: keypose-conditioned consistency-model action head favored over standard (e.g., diffusion) action heads for multi-stage bimanual tasks
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world bimanual manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical structure with a high-level keypose predictor marking sub-stage completion, combined with a low-level trajectory generator conditioned on those keyposes, addresses step-wise and stage-wise challenges of multi-stage bimanual tasks better than flat, non-hierarchical chunking
claims.direction: hierarchical keypose-based sub-stage decomposition favored over flat action chunking for multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world bimanual manipulation

claims.claim: The consistency-model trajectory generator provides fast inference speed compared to standard diffusion-based action generation
claims.direction: consistency-model action generation favored over standard multi-step diffusion sampling for low-latency inference
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated bimanual manipulation

title: Learning Diverse Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Skills from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A teacher-student framework (state-based teacher distilled into a vision-based student policy) trained across 141 auto-constructed tasks from human demonstrations achieves a 74.59% task fulfillment rate on trained tasks and 51.07% on unseen tasks
claims.direction: teacher-student distillation from diverse auto-constructed human-demonstration-derived tasks favored for generalization to unseen bimanual dexterous tasks
claims.conditions: TACO dataset benchmark, 141 tasks across six categories, simulated bimanual dexterous hands

title: Context Representation via Action-Free Transformer encoder-decoder for Meta Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Inferring task/context representations solely from sequences of states and rewards (removing dependence on actions) decouples task inference from policy optimization and achieves faster adaptation, improved generalization, and more effective exploration versus context-adaptive meta-RL baselines that rely on complete action information
claims.direction: action-free context/history representation favored over action-conditioned context inference for task adaptation and generalization
claims.conditions: MetaWorld ML-10 robotic manipulation benchmark (simulation)

title: One-shot learning for rapid generation of structured robotic manipulation tasks from 3D video demonstrations

claims.claim: A single 3D video recording of a human demonstration (with hand/gaze tracking and one-shot object segmentation) is sufficient to decompose and generate a structured, executable robotic manipulation task, transferable across different robot types and manipulation scenarios
claims.direction: one-shot (single demonstration) task generation favored over collecting many demonstrations per task for structured manipulation task acquisition
claims.conditions: collaborative robot, single 3D video demonstration, heterogeneous manipulation tasks

title: FieldGen: From Teleoperated Pre-Manipulation Trajectories to Field-Guided Data Generation

claims.claim: Decomposing manipulation into a pre-manipulation phase (where an attraction field automatically generates diverse trajectories converging to successful configurations from human-captured key contact/pose information) and a fine manipulation phase (requiring expert precision, captured directly from demonstration) yields policies with higher success rates and improved stability than teleoperation-only baselines, while significantly reducing human effort
claims.direction: field-guided automatic generation of pre-manipulation trajectory diversity (combined with precise human-demonstrated fine manipulation) favored over pure teleoperation-based data collection
claims.conditions: real-world data collection, long-term data collection scenario

claims.claim: Reward-annotated augmentation of generated data (FieldGen-Reward) further enhances policy learning while reducing the human labor needed for scaling real-world demonstration data
claims.direction: automatically generated, reward-annotated trajectory diversity favored over purely human-collected demonstrations for scaling data quantity/diversity
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation data collection

title: ATK: Automatic Task-driven Keypoint Selection for Robust Policy Learning

claims.claim: Automatically selecting a minimal, task-driven set of 2D keypoints (rather than using raw RGB pixels directly, or full 6D pose state estimation) as the state representation for a distilled policy provides a flexible representation for both sim-to-real transfer and real-world imitation learning
claims.direction: minimal task-driven keypoint representation favored over both raw-pixel-only policies and full 6D-pose-based policies for representation robustness and scalability
claims.conditions: sim-to-real transfer and real-world imitation learning, expert data distilled from simulation or human demonstration

claims.claim: Policies operating on the automatically-selected minimal keypoint set significantly improve robustness to visual disturbances and environmental variations, including transparent objects, fine-grained tasks, and deformable object manipulation, compared to raw sensor-based policies
claims.direction: task-driven keypoint-based state representation favored over raw-pixel policies for robustness under visual/environmental variation
claims.conditions: real-world robotic tasks with wide scene variation and perceptual challenges

why_deep_read: Directly targets our robustness failure modes (new lighting, different-looking object, moved camera) via an explicit, minimal, automatically-selected keypoint representation rather than raw pixels -- if the keypoint-selection method generalizes to a pumpkin-in-tray task, it could be a concrete architectural fix for Q03/Q14; worth reading how keypoints are selected/tracked and the magnitude of robustness gains versus raw-pixel baselines.

title: OneVLA: A Unified Framework for Embodied Tasks

claims.claim: A single unified action head capable of generating both navigation and manipulation actions (rather than task-specific action-head variants), combined with a multi-stage progressive training strategy with Chain-of-Thought fine-tuning, significantly outperforms both specialized single-task and existing cross-task models
claims.direction: unified cross-task action head with staged CoT training favored over task-specific action-head architectures
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world environments, navigation and manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Chain-of-Thought fine-tuning and curated multi-stage training facilitate positive transfer and mutual reinforcement between navigation and manipulation task domains
claims.direction: CoT-based multi-task training favored over training each task domain in isolation
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, navigation and manipulation

title: OCRA: Object-Centric Learning with 3D and Tactile Priors for Human-to-Robot Action Transfer

claims.claim: Reconstructing object-centric 3D point clouds from multi-view RGB human-demonstration videos (using the VGGT 3D foundation model plus detection/segmentation) and fusing them with tactile priors through a multimodal module (ResFiLM) into a Diffusion Policy significantly outperforms existing baselines and ablations on both vision-only and visuo-tactile manipulation tasks
claims.direction: object-centric 3D reconstruction (filtering out background) plus tactile priors favored over standard vision-only or non-object-centric representations for learning from human demonstration video
claims.conditions: human demonstration videos, vision-only and visuo-tactile manipulation tasks, ablation studies included

claims.claim: Incorporating tactile priors (from a large-scale >1M-image tactile dataset) as an auxiliary modality fused via ResFiLM improves performance on properties not easily perceived by vision alone
claims.direction: auxiliary tactile-prior fusion favored over vision-only modeling for properties vision alone misses
claims.conditions: visuo-tactile manipulation tasks

title: SmoothVLA: Aligning Vision-Language-Action Models with Physical Constraints via Intrinsic Smoothness Optimization

claims.claim: A physics-informed hybrid reward (binary sparse task reward + continuous dense term derived from trajectory jerk), computed intrinsically from policy rollouts without extrinsic environment feedback, and optimized via GRPO, makes trajectory smoothness an explicit optimization prior; SmoothVLA outperforms standard RL fine-tuning by 13.8% in smoothness on the LIBERO benchmark
claims.direction: intrinsic jerk-based smoothness reward during RL fine-tuning favored over standard RL fine-tuning (which induces erratic, jittery trajectories) for producing physically feasible, smooth control
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (simulation), RL fine-tuning of a VLA model

claims.claim: RL fine-tuning improves exploration/generalization over Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), which is constrained by demonstration quality, but standard RL induces erratic jittery trajectories unless explicitly regularized for smoothness; SmoothVLA significantly surpasses SFT in generalization across diverse tasks while maintaining smoothness
claims.direction: smoothness-regularized RL fine-tuning favored over both plain SFT (limited generalization) and un-regularized RL (jittery) for post-training a VLA action head
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, simulation

title: Spatially Generalizable Mobile Manipulation via Adaptive Experience Selection and Dynamic Imagination

claims.claim: An Adaptive Experience Selection mechanism that focuses learning on critical experience fragments within long trajectories (rather than treating all experience uniformly) improves skill-chain learning and mitigates skill forgetting in long-horizon mobile manipulation
claims.direction: selective attention to critical trajectory fragments favored over uniform experience replay for long-horizon skill retention
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated long-horizon mobile manipulation

claims.claim: A Recurrent State-Space Model used for model-based dynamic imagination (predicting coupled mobile-base and manipulator dynamics) improves generalization to new spatial layouts versus policies without such model-based imagination
claims.direction: model-based imagination auxiliary component favored over pure model-free policy learning for spatial generalization
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated mobile manipulation, comparative studies across configurations

title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Augmenting a feed-forward VLA policy with a closed-loop Feasibility Operator (checks dynamic consistency of candidate actions), an Action Explanation Operator, and an LLM-based Reflection Module (diagnoses state discrepancies for corrective guidance) improves stage-wise stability and overall task success by an average of 5.4% over representative VLA baselines on multi-stage, contact-rich real-world manipulation
claims.direction: execution-time physical-feasibility checking plus self-reflective correction favored over standard feed-forward VLA execution for reliability
claims.conditions: real-world multi-stage, contact-rich manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Ablations show both feasibility checking and reflection-based correction independently contribute to improved execution robustness
claims.direction: each auxiliary reliability component (feasibility check, reflection) contributes incrementally, supporting their combined use
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, ablation study

title: Safe Vision Language Action Models via Barrier Enhanced Flow Matching

claims.claim: Modifying the flow-matching denoising process itself (rather than applying an external safety filter to final output) with a smooth Log-Sum-Exponential aggregate Control Barrier Function achieves formal safety guarantees with minimal added computational overhead and without degrading success rate, and without needing safety-specific datasets or retraining
claims.direction: safety constraints embedded directly in the flow-matching generative process favored over post-hoc output filtering for flow-matching action heads
claims.conditions: two real robotic manipulation platforms and a 2D navigation benchmark

claims.claim: The barrier is enforced over entire action chunks (not just single timesteps), maintaining safety guarantees across the whole predicted horizon
claims.direction: chunk-level (not just per-step) safety enforcement favored for action-chunked flow-matching policies
claims.conditions: real robotic manipulation platforms

title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning

claims.claim: A small subset of replay-buffer experiences ('Memory Anchors'), located in regions where representations of new-task observations collapse onto those of old-task observations despite requiring conflicting actions (e.g., a familiar object manipulated in a new way), are disproportionately responsible for anchoring past performance against catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: targeted rehearsal of representation-collapse/high-conflict experiences favored over uniformly-random replay-buffer sampling
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark suites (simulation) and a real robot performing two continual task sequences

claims.claim: Excluding only 10% of Memory Anchors before random buffer sampling leads to a more than 4.5x increase in catastrophic forgetting on LIBERO; conversely, enriching the replay buffer with Memory Anchors decreases high-conflict task forgetting by 63% and enables successful continual (multi-task) learning of two task sequences on a real robot
claims.direction: prioritizing high-conflict/ambiguous-representation experiences in the replay buffer strongly favored over standard random-sampling replay for continual multi-task learning
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation benchmark and real-robot continual learning of two task sequences

title: Distilling Morphology-Conditioned Hypernetworks for Efficient Universal Morphology Control

claims.claim: A morphology-conditioned hypernetwork that generates robot-wise MLP policies, combined with policy distillation from a universal transformer teacher, matches the transformer teacher's performance on both training and unseen test robots while reducing model size by 6-14x and computational cost by 67-160x at inference time
claims.direction: distilled hypernetwork-generated small MLP policies favored over large transformer policies for inference efficiency without performance loss
claims.conditions: UNIMAL benchmark (simulation), hundreds of diverse robot morphologies

title: ReinFlow: Fine-tuning Flow Matching Policy with Online Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Injecting learnable noise into a flow-matching policy's deterministic path (converting it to a discrete-time Markov process) enables online RL fine-tuning of flow-matching policies at very few or even one denoising step; Rectified Flow policies obtained an average net growth of 135.36% episode reward after fine-tuning in legged locomotion, and Shortcut Model policies achieved an average net success-rate increase of 40.34% in state and visual manipulation tasks after fine-tuning at 1-4 denoising steps
claims.direction: RL-fine-tuned few-step flow-matching policies favored over un-fine-tuned flow policies, and are competitive with diffusion policies fine-tuned via more expensive methods
claims.conditions: long-horizon planning with visual input and sparse reward, representative locomotion and manipulation benchmark tasks

claims.claim: ReinFlow fine-tuning at very few (or one) denoising steps saves 82.63% of wall time versus a state-of-the-art diffusion RL fine-tuning method (DPPO) in locomotion, and achieves comparable performance to fine-tuned DDIM policies in manipulation while saving 23.20% computation time
claims.direction: few-step flow-matching policies (fine-tuned online) favored over many-step diffusion policies for inference/training compute cost
claims.conditions: locomotion and manipulation benchmarks

title: Multi-Modal Manipulation via Multi-Modal Policy Consensus

claims.claim: Factorizing the policy into per-modality diffusion models (e.g., one for vision, one for touch) combined via a router network that learns adaptive consensus weights significantly outperforms standard feature-concatenation fusion baselines on tasks requiring multimodal reasoning, and allows incremental addition of new modalities without retraining
claims.direction: factorized per-modality diffusion experts with learned consensus routing favored over monolithic feature-concatenation fusion for multi-modal (vision+touch) policies -- CONTRADICTS the common practice of simple feature concatenation
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation and real-world tasks: occluded object picking, in-hand spoon reorientation, puzzle insertion

claims.claim: The consensus-routed multimodal policy demonstrates robustness to physical perturbations and sensor corruption, with perturbation-based importance analysis revealing adaptive shifts in reliance between modalities under corruption
claims.direction: adaptive multimodal consensus routing favored over fixed-fusion architectures for robustness to sensor corruption/perturbation
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks under physical perturbation and sensor corruption

title: SemanticVLA: Semantic-Aligned Sparsification and Enhancement for Efficient Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining SigLIP (instruction-driven pruning of global action cues/local semantic anchors) and DINOv2 (spatial-aggregation pruning of geometry-rich features into task-adaptive tokens) via a hierarchical fuser, rather than using a single vision-language encoder alone, sets a new SOTA in both performance and efficiency for VLA manipulation
claims.direction: dual-encoder (SigLIP+DINOv2) semantic+geometric sparsification and fusion favored over single-encoder or unpruned dense-token VLA vision processing
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO) and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: SemanticVLA reduces inference latency by 2.7x compared to OpenVLA while surpassing it by 21.1% in success rate on the LIBERO benchmark
claims.direction: semantic-guided token sparsification favored over dense unpruned visual token processing for simultaneously improving accuracy and cutting inference latency
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, real-world tasks

claims.claim: The sparsification approach also reduces training cost by 3.0x relative to OpenVLA
claims.direction: pruned/sparsified visual-token VLA favored over dense-token VLA for training efficiency
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, real-world tasks

why_deep_read: Reports a concrete, large joint gain (+21.1% success, 2.7x lower inference latency, 3.0x lower training cost) from a specific, nameable vision-encoder recipe (SigLIP+DINOv2 pruning and fusion) -- directly actionable for our 8GB-laptop, ~2s-inference-latency, small-model setup (Q03/Q10/Q12); worth reading the pruning/fusion mechanism details to see if it is implementable at our scale.

title: Learning from Demonstrations via Deformable Residual Multi-Attention Domain-Adaptive Meta-Learning
