claims.claim: A Residual Multi-Attention Domain-Adaptive Meta-Learning framework (DRMA-DAML) significantly enhances performance without increasing neural network depth, avoiding overfitting and vanishing-gradient problems typical of deeper architectures, unlike traditional meta-learning methods that rely on deepening/widening networks for only marginal gains
claims.direction: attention-based architectural enhancement at fixed depth favored over deepening/widening networks for meta-learning adaptation performance
claims.conditions: simulated environments and real-world object manipulation

claims.claim: DRMA-DAML improves adaptation accuracy by 11.18% on benchmark tasks and achieves a 97.64% success rate in real-world object manipulation, enabling rapid adaptation to previously unencountered/novel environments from limited (one-shot/few-shot) data
claims.direction: domain-adaptive meta-learning favored over standard fine-tuning for rapid few-shot adaptation to novel environments
claims.conditions: real-world object manipulation, few-shot/one-shot adaptation setting

title: Reshaping Action Error Distributions for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Replacing/augmenting standard MSE-based continuous-action regression with a trajectory-level Minimum Error Entropy (MEE) objective (plus two weighted variants) yields consistent improvements in success rate and robustness across standard, few-shot, and noisy settings on multiple representative VLA architectures, with negligible additional training cost and no impact on inference efficiency
claims.direction: MEE-augmented action-error-distribution reshaping favored over plain MSE regression loss for continuous-action VLA training
claims.conditions: LIBERO and SimplerEnv simulation benchmarks plus real-world robotic manipulation, standard/few-shot/noisy data regimes

claims.claim: Gains from MEE-based supervision persist under imbalanced/few-shot data regimes within a characterized operating range
claims.direction: distributional (MEE) loss reshaping favored over MSE particularly in few-shot data regimes
claims.conditions: few-shot setting, multiple VLA architectures

title: Learning From Videos Through Graph-to-Graphs Generative Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Pretraining on video data via Graph-to-Graphs generative modeling (predicting future object/action graphs) lets the downstream control policy attain superior performance using merely 20% action-labeled data relative to comparable approaches, outperforming the state-of-the-art by over 19% in simulation and 23% in real-world experiments, and over 35% in cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: graph-based video pretraining favored over relying primarily on action-labeled robot demonstration data for reducing labeled-data requirements
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, cross-embodiment transfer, long-horizon tasks

claims.claim: Predicting future graph representations (object and visual-action vertices capturing state/spatial relationships) conditioned on the current frame's graph serves as an effective auxiliary/pretraining objective that guides the control policy
claims.direction: graph-structured future-prediction auxiliary objective favored over direct pixel-level future-frame prediction for encoding spatial relationships
claims.conditions: video pretraining, robot fine-tuning

title: SKIP: Sparse Keyframe Interpolation Paradigm for Efficient Embodied World Models

claims.claim: Synthetic video rollouts generated by SKIP (sparse keyframe generation + learned gap predictor and action-conditioned interpolator) are effective policy-training data: even when they fully replace real demonstrations, pi_0.5 success drops only 1.3 percentage points in LIBERO simulation and 6.7 points on the real robot, whereas fully dense frame-by-frame video generation collapses performance by 48 to 58 points
claims.direction: sparse, event-preserving keyframe-based synthetic video generation can nearly substitute for real demonstrations, while naive dense frame-by-frame synthetic generation cannot
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation and real-robot manipulation, pi_0.5 policy trained on synthetic-only data

claims.claim: Identifying task-relevant keyframes (approach, contact, grasp, release) via robot-aware multimodal features and synthesizing only these with a sparse video diffusion model generates dense rollouts 4.16x faster than a dense baseline while improving visual fidelity (89.0% lower aggregate FVD)
claims.direction: event-preserving sparse keyframe world modeling favored over dense frame-by-frame world modeling for both speed and fidelity
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, embodied world model rollout generation

why_deep_read: Reports an unusually strong, real-robot-validated result that synthetic (keyframe-generated) video can almost fully replace real demonstrations (only 6.7pp real-robot drop) -- if this generalizes, it directly changes how many real teleop demos we need to collect for the pumpkin task (Q05/Q13); worth reading how the keyframe/interpolation method works and whether it requires large pretraining data itself.

title: RoHIL: Robust Human-in-the-Loop Robotic Reinforcement Learning Against Illumination Variations

claims.claim: Human-in-the-loop RL policies that achieve near-perfect success on their training workstation collapse when the robot is moved a few meters to a workstation with different lamp positions/window light, and naive fine-tuning on the new lighting triggers catastrophic forgetting of the original workstation
claims.direction: identifies illumination/workstation shift as a policy-breaking failure mode distinct from and not fixed by naive fine-tuning -- directly matches a 'breaks under new lighting' failure pattern
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation, cross-workstation illumination shift (new lamp positions, window light)

claims.claim: An offline framework that re-synthesizes source-workstation training images under multiple virtual HDRI lighting environments (keeping actions/rewards real), combined with illumination-retention replay and an anchored policy regularizer, substantially improves performance under shifted lighting across four real-robot manipulation tasks while preserving original-workstation performance, without any extra real-robot interaction or data re-collection
claims.direction: offline image-relighting augmentation (synthetic lighting variation from existing trajectories) favored over re-collecting demonstrations or naive fine-tuning for illumination-shift robustness
claims.conditions: four real-robot manipulation tasks, significant cross-workstation illumination variation, no extra real-robot interaction required

why_deep_read: This is a near-exact match to our #1 stated failure ('breaks under new lighting') and its proposed fix (offline HDRI-based relighting of existing trajectories, no new data collection) is directly actionable for our fixed-camera pumpkin setup; worth reading the relighting/anti-forgetting mechanism details and the magnitude of the shifted-light recovery for Q05/Q14.

title: Temporal Self-Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Mining temporally-efficient successful trajectories generated during RL training and converting them into reusable, efficiency-weighted self-imitation supervision consistently improves learning efficiency, task-completion efficiency, and robustness versus standard reward-shaping-only reinforcement learning
claims.direction: temporal-efficiency-based self-imitation supervision favored over reward-shaping-only RL for long-horizon manipulation policy learning
claims.conditions: 15 distinct long-horizon manipulation tasks (simulation)

title: τ: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision

claims.claim: Learning an action-conditioned spatiotemporal tactile representation via future-visual-supervision (JEPA-style, latent-space, training-only with no deployment overhead) and fusing it with vision-language features outperforms existing tactile-augmented VLA baselines that use only instantaneous contact states or 6D wrench sequences
claims.direction: training-only, future-prediction-based tactile representation learning favored over instantaneous-contact or wrench-sequence tactile modeling for contact-rich VLA manipulation
claims.conditions: four representative contact-rich manipulation tasks, real robot (TacAura dataset with synchronized vision/proprioception/tactile)

claims.claim: The touch-augmented model generalizes to unseen objects and scenes, delivering improved manipulation performance and robustness versus existing models
claims.direction: tactile-augmented representation favored for generalization to unseen objects/scenes
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-rich manipulation, unseen objects/scenes

title: 3D-ViTac: Learning Fine-Grained Manipulation with Visuo-Tactile Sensing

claims.claim: Fusing dense low-cost tactile sensor data with visual data into a unified 3D representation space (preserving 3D structure/spatial relationships), then coupling with diffusion policies, lets low-cost robots perform precise manipulation and significantly outperform vision-only policies, particularly in safe interactions with fragile items and long-horizon in-hand manipulation
claims.direction: unified 3D visuo-tactile representation favored over vision-only representation for fine-grained/fragile/long-horizon manipulation on low-cost hardware
claims.conditions: real low-cost robot hardware, dexterous bimanual manipulation, diffusion-policy imitation learning

claims.claim: Low-cost, flexible tactile sensors with dense sensing units effectively complement visual information for contact-rich fine-grained tasks
claims.direction: low-cost tactile sensing as a complementary auxiliary modality favored over vision-only sensing
claims.conditions: real low-cost robot hardware

title: WildLMa: Long Horizon Loco-Manipulation in the Wild

claims.claim: High-quality training data enables a higher grasping success rate than existing RL baselines using only tens of demonstrations
claims.direction: a small number (tens) of high-quality demonstrations favored over RL-from-scratch baselines for grasping skill acquisition
claims.conditions: real quadruped-with-manipulator robot, in-the-wild environments

claims.claim: CLIP-based language-conditioned imitation learning empirically generalizes to objects unseen in training demonstrations
claims.direction: CLIP-grounded language conditioning favored for generalization to novel objects over non-language-grounded imitation learning
claims.conditions: real robot, in-the-wild long-horizon tasks

title: Constrained Bootstrapped Learning for Few-Shot Robot Skill Adaptation

claims.claim: Seeding learning with a compact, structured skill model (hybrid LfD+RL) and bootstrapping a fast refinement policy trained in simulation across varied initial conditions, then quickly adapting to new real-world conditions, achieves an average success rate of 90% across three tasks of varying difficulty, versus 56.6% for the state-of-the-art
claims.direction: structured skill-model-seeded bootstrapped adaptation favored over standard state-of-the-art few-shot adaptation baselines
claims.conditions: simulation and real hardware, multiple environments, varying task complexity

claims.claim: The bootstrapped refinement process adapts the learned skill model to new initial conditions in only a few learning iterations, correcting for sim-to-real discrepancies
claims.direction: few-iteration online adaptation favored over extensive re-training or re-collection of demonstrations for new initial conditions
claims.conditions: real hardware deployment

title: EquiContact: A Hierarchical SE(3) Vision-to-Force Equivariant Policy for Spatially Generalizable Contact-rich Tasks

claims.claim: Producing actions defined in the end-effector frame (rather than a fixed world/joint frame), combined with SE(3)-equivariant design from perception through force control, is a key component enabling spatial generalization from a small number of demonstrations
claims.direction: end-effector-frame, equivariant action representation favored over world/joint-frame action representation for spatial generalization
claims.conditions: real-world peg-in-hole, screwing, and surface-wiping tasks, trained from a small number of demonstrations

claims.claim: The low-level policy (G-CompACT) operates using only localized observations -- geometrically consistent error vectors, force-torque readings, and wrist-mounted RGB images -- without needing a scene/external camera view
claims.direction: wrist-camera-only, localized observation policy favored over policies requiring a fixed external scene camera, for spatial generalization to unseen configurations
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The hierarchical equivariant framework achieves near-perfect success rate and robust generalization to unseen spatial configurations when trained from only a small number of demonstrations
claims.direction: compliance + localized policy + induced equivariance jointly favored over standard (non-equivariant) policies for small-demo-count spatial generalization
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich tasks, small number of demonstrations

title: Reducing Sim-to-Real Domain Gaps of Visual Sensors for Learning Environment-Constrained Visuomotor Policy

claims.claim: A correlation-attentive, task-related GAN (LCTGAN) with mask-level Q-value-mapping consistency reduces texture leakage/elimination seen in prior pixel-level sim-to-real adaptation methods that optimize visual realism over task-specific learning, and enables zero-shot sim-to-real policy transfer
claims.direction: task-aware (not purely photorealism-focused) domain-adaptation GAN favored over standard pixel-level image-translation domain adaptation for sim-to-real visual policy transfer
claims.conditions: real robot deployment, cluttered scenes, zero-shot transfer

claims.claim: A Q-learning-based visuomotor policy integrated with the domain-transfer network generalizes zero-shot to real, cluttered scenarios where objects may lack directly graspable configurations
claims.direction: combined domain-adaptation + constraint-aware policy favored for robustness to cluttered/non-trivial real scenes
claims.conditions: real robot, cluttered scenes with environmental constraints

title: Bidirectional Decoding Collaborating with Hierarchical Imitation for Long-Horizon Task Learning

claims.claim: A Bidirectional Decoding mechanism that dynamically reassesses action sequences against strong and weak policy predictions (using backward temporal coherence and forward robustness contrast) resolves the rigidity of traditional action chunking, outperforming existing approaches in task success rate and cumulative reward on long-horizon tasks; ablations confirm its critical role
claims.direction: bidirectional, dynamically-reassessed action decoding favored over rigid, fixed-direction action chunking for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: Franka Kitchen simulation environment, hierarchical RL + IL framework

claims.claim: The hierarchical IL+HRL framework efficiently handles dynamic, diverse long-horizon tasks even with limited demonstration data
claims.direction: hierarchical decomposition (subtasks via IL, refinement via HRL) favored over flat single-policy IL when demonstration data is limited
claims.conditions: Franka Kitchen simulation, limited demonstration data

title: SKIL: Semantic Keypoint Imitation Learning for Generalizable Data-efficient Manipulation

claims.claim: Automatically obtaining semantic keypoints via vision foundation models, and forming a semantic-keypoint descriptor as the state representation (rather than raw RGB pixels), doubles the performance of baseline imitation-learning methods on real-world tasks such as picking a cup or mouse
claims.direction: semantic-keypoint-based state representation favored over raw-pixel-based representation for sample-efficient, generalizable imitation learning
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks (garment manipulation, table rearrangement, pick tasks)

claims.claim: For a long-horizon task (hanging a towel on a rack) where previous methods fail completely, SKIL achieves a mean success rate of 70% with as few as 30 demonstrations
claims.direction: semantic-keypoint representation favored for enabling long-horizon task success from very few (30) demonstrations, where prior methods achieve near-zero success
claims.conditions: real-world long-horizon manipulation, 30 demonstrations

claims.claim: SKIL demonstrates exceptional robustness to variations in objects, environmental changes, and distractors, and even human videos bring considerable improvement to learning performance due to the semantic-keypoint abstraction supporting cross-embodiment learning
claims.direction: semantic-keypoint abstraction favored over raw-pixel representations for robustness to object/environment/distractor variation, and for leveraging cross-embodiment (human video) data
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation under object variation, environmental changes, distractors; cross-embodiment human video data

why_deep_read: This is an unusually strong, concrete match to our setup: doubles baseline success, achieves 70% success on a long-horizon task with just 30 demonstrations where prior methods fail completely, and explicitly reports robustness to object/environment/distractor variation (i.e., our exact 'new lighting / different pumpkin / moved camera' failure modes). Worth reading how semantic keypoints are extracted/tracked and whether the approach needs per-task keypoint definitions, directly informing Q03/Q13/Q14.

title: Improving Robustness to Out-of-Distribution States in Imitation Learning via Deep Koopman-Boosted Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: A dual-branch diffusion policy (D3P) that decouples a visual-only branch (tracks task progression) from a fused visual+proprioceptive branch (precise manipulation), plus a deep Koopman operator module for structured temporal dynamics, outperforms the state-of-the-art diffusion policy by an average of 14.6% in 6 simulated RLBench tasks and 15.0% on 3 real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: dual-branch (decoupled visual vs. fused visual-proprioceptive) diffusion policy with Koopman temporal modeling favored over single-branch diffusion policies
claims.conditions: 6 simulated RLBench tasks and 3 real-world robot manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Standard diffusion-based action chunking policies can overfit to proprioceptive cues at the expense of visually-derived task features, causing failures; decoupling visual and proprioceptive roles into separate branches lets the policy dynamically fall back to the visual branch to recover toward previously observed states and retry the task when it fails an intermediate goal
claims.direction: explicit vision/proprioception decoupling favored over fused single-stream conditioning to avoid proprioceptive overfitting (a form of causal confusion) and to enable failure recovery
claims.conditions: real and simulated manipulation with intermediate sub-goals (e.g., grasping a drawer handle)

claims.claim: Using the generative model's test-time loss as a confidence signal to guide aggregation of temporally-overlapping predicted action chunks enhances the reliability of policy execution
claims.direction: confidence-weighted aggregation of overlapping action chunks favored over naive/uniform chunk aggregation
claims.conditions: real and simulated manipulation with action-chunked diffusion policies

title: Worlds in One Demo: A Synthetic Data Engine for Learning Open-World Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Reconstructing background Gaussian splats and robot-object interaction trajectories from one real demonstration, then rearranging contact-rich interaction segments into extensive new spatial configurations via whole-body motion planning, and synthesizing photo-realistic observations by compositing rendered robot/object meshes with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds, generates policies with long-horizon robustness and broad spatial/cross-environment generalization from just one real demonstration
claims.direction: synthetic trajectory generation from a single real demo (via Gaussian-splat scene reconstruction and re-composition) favored over collecting many additional real teleoperation demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated mobile manipulation, one source real demonstration

claims.claim: Corrective State Expansion increases robot and object state diversity at different stages of the task specifically to improve long-horizon robustness from minimal source data
claims.direction: deliberate state-diversity expansion from a single demo favored over relying on naturally-occurring demonstration diversity
claims.conditions: long-horizon mobile manipulation, one source demonstration

claims.claim: Trajectories synthesized on diverse generated 3D worlds (from everyday photos) unlock cross-environment generalization, and the approach naturally supports cross-embodiment data generation, validated by zero-shot deployment on a mobile manipulator with a distinct morphology
claims.direction: synthetic multi-environment/multi-embodiment data generation favored for cross-environment and cross-embodiment generalization over embodiment/environment-specific real data collection
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot deployment on a different mobile manipulator morphology

title: ΔVLA: Prior-Guided Vision-Language-Action Models via World Knowledge Variation

claims.claim: Modeling world-knowledge variation relative to an explicit current-world-knowledge prior (rather than regressing absolute future world states) for action generation achieves state-of-the-art performance while improving efficiency versus prior predictive-paradigm VLAs that forecast absolute future outcomes
claims.direction: variation-relative (differential) world-knowledge modeling favored over absolute future-state prediction as an auxiliary/predictive objective for action generation
claims.conditions: simulated benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks

claims.claim: Encoding world-knowledge variation into a compact discrete latent space via a VQ-VAE objective (rather than predicting full-modality future states) reduces redundancy while preserving action-relevant information
claims.direction: discrete VQ-based latent variation encoding favored over full-modality (e.g., pixel-space) future-state regression for conditioning the action generation process
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation

title: ViTaR: Visuo-Tactile Residual Adaptation for Foundation VLA Manipulation

claims.claim: Reframing tactile feedback as a bounded residual-correction execution modulator on top of a frozen VLA (rather than modifying VLA internals or requiring risky online RL near failure), via Effect-Guided Modeling plus Residual Action Modulation, achieves 61.3% average success on the UniVTAC benchmark (seven contact-rich tasks) -- a 30.6 percentage-point improvement over the frozen VLA base -- and surpasses purpose-built tactile baselines, with physical-robot experiments confirming transfer to real sensor noise/dynamics
claims.direction: bounded residual tactile correction atop a frozen pretrained VLA favored over modifying VLA internals or online-RL-based tactile integration, for preserving pretrained capabilities while adding contact-awareness
claims.conditions: UniVTAC benchmark (7 contact-rich tasks) plus physical-robot validation

title: Robust In-Hand Reorientation With Hierarchical RL-Based Motion Primitives and Model-Based Regrasping

claims.claim: A hierarchical RL approach using only a single RGB camera (no depth camera or tactile sensors, unlike typical prior in-hand manipulation work requiring expensive dexterous hands/depth/tactile) achieves continuous cube reorientation for nearly 20 minutes on a low-cost LEAP Hand, and won a robotic manipulation competition
claims.direction: single-RGB-camera, low-cost sensing suite shown sufficient for a complex dexterous task, versus prior work relying on depth cameras and tactile sensors
claims.conditions: real low-cost hardware (LEAP Hand, single RGB camera), in-hand cube reorientation

title: LaST-R1: Reinforcing Robotic Manipulation via Adaptive Physical Latent Reasoning

claims.claim: Jointly optimizing latent Chain-of-Thought reasoning and action generation within a single RL loop (Latent-to-Action Policy Optimization), with an adaptive mechanism that dynamically modulates reasoning horizon based on environment state, achieves near-perfect 99.9% average success on LIBERO with only a one-shot supervised warm-up, improving convergence speed and performance over prior SOTA
claims.direction: RL-optimized latent reasoning-before-acting favored over static imitation-learning-only latent-reasoning VLAs for adaptability/generalization
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, one-shot supervised warm-up before RL

claims.claim: In real-world deployments, LaST-R1 yields up to a 22.5% average improvement over the SOTA supervised fine-tuning approach across four complex tasks (single-arm and dual-arm), starting from minimal (one-shot) supervised warm-up
claims.direction: minimal supervised warm-up plus RL-based latent-reasoning post-training favored over standard supervised fine-tuning when demonstration data is very limited
claims.conditions: real-world single-arm and dual-arm manipulation, one-shot warm-up

title: Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A large fixed action-chunk size reduces model responsiveness to new information, while a small fixed chunk size increases mode-jumping (jerky behavior from discontinuities between chunks); the dominant current practice of an empirically fixed chunk length at inference time is identified as a key limitation on VLA scalability and performance across diverse tasks
claims.direction: identifies fixed-size action chunking itself (regardless of the chosen size) as suboptimal, motivating chunk-size adaptivity
claims.conditions: analysis of current VLA models' action-chunking practice

claims.claim: Adaptive Action Chunking (AAC), which uses action-prediction entropy as a cue to adaptively determine chunk size at inference time on a per-prediction basis, substantially improves performance over state-of-the-art fixed-chunk-size alternatives across a wide range of simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks
claims.direction: entropy-based adaptive chunk sizing at inference time favored over any single fixed chunk size for balancing reactivity and motion consistency/smoothness
claims.conditions: wide range of simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: This paper frames our exact stated problem (jerky motion from action-chunk discontinuities vs. responsiveness trade-off, current VLAs using an arbitrary fixed chunk length) almost verbatim, and proposes a concrete, lightweight inference-time fix (entropy-based adaptive chunk sizing) validated on both sim and real tasks -- directly actionable for Q06/Q10 without retraining our action head; worth reading the entropy-cue mechanism and real-robot smoothness/latency numbers.

title: Sample-Efficient Diffusion-based Reinforcement Learning with Critic Guidance

claims.claim: Critic-Guided diffusion Policy Optimization (CGPO), which steers diffusion-policy action generation toward high-value regions via training-free critic guidance during denoising (rather than pure sampling-based or pure gradient-based diffusion RL), balances exploration and exploitation better, achieving state-of-the-art performance among diffusion-based RL methods and the first successful real-world RL diffusion-policy result on a Franka robot arm grasping task
claims.direction: critic-guided denoising-time steering favored over both pure sampling-based and pure gradient-based diffusion policy optimization for real-world RL
claims.conditions: 5 MuJoCo locomotion tasks (sim) plus real-world Franka robot arm grasping

title: Learning More from Less: Reinforcement Learning from Hindsight

claims.claim: Learning from Hindsight (LfH) relabels failed rollouts against the tasks they actually achieved (using a VLM to propose a hindsight instruction and score satisfaction), letting the policy learn from otherwise-wasted failed-but-coherent rollouts; on out-of-distribution LIBERO-PRO tasks, where standard RL improves only slowly, LfH achieves a 5x improvement in sample efficiency and outperforms a dense progress-reward baseline
claims.direction: hindsight relabeling of failed rollouts favored over standard sparse-reward RL post-training for sample-efficient VLA fine-tuning, especially under sparse rewards
claims.conditions: out-of-distribution LIBERO-PRO tasks, RL post-training of VLA models, gains hold across VLA backbones and on a physical Franka robot

claims.claim: Because VLAs generalize across language, relabeling failed rollouts in natural language (rather than only via reward relabeling) lets the policy learn more from the same collected trajectories
claims.direction: language-based hindsight relabeling favored over reward-only relabeling for RL post-training of language-conditioned action models
claims.conditions: physical Franka robot plus multiple VLA backbones

title: Attention from Action, for Action: Emergent Visual Bottlenecks for Policy Learning

claims.claim: Seeker learns a task- and state-conditioned attention readout on top of frozen DINOv3 features, supervised solely by action prediction (no external spatial labels like gaze/object-class/affordance annotations), producing progression-aware regions-of-interest that avoid the fixed-timing/fixed-scale misalignment of label-free action-derived crop baselines (e.g., crops centered on projected end-effector position)
claims.direction: action-supervised, learned, progression-aware visual attention/ROI favored over both no-crop raw-image policies and fixed-heuristic action-derived crop baselines
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation, frozen DINOv3 backbone

claims.claim: On real robots, Seeker raises average in-domain success from the best baseline's 48.3% to 76.7%, and success under lighting/background shifts from 20.0% to 60.0%
claims.direction: learned action-conditioned visual attention strongly favored over no-crop/augmentation/fixed-crop baselines specifically for robustness to lighting and background shift
claims.conditions: real robot manipulation, lighting and background distribution shift

why_deep_read: This reports a very large, concrete real-robot improvement (20.0%->60.0% success) specifically under lighting/background shift -- exactly our stated failure mode -- using a frozen pretrained vision encoder (DINOv3) plus an action-supervised attention/crop mechanism that adds no extra labeling burden; directly actionable for Q03/Q14 and worth reading the attention-readout mechanism in detail.

title: FetchBench: A Simulation Benchmark for Robot Fetching

claims.claim: Across multiple baselines spanning traditional sense-plan-act pipelines to end-to-end behavior-cloning models, the best method achieves a maximum success rate of only 20% on a benchmark combining grasping and motion-planning challenges, revealing substantial headroom and specific bottlenecks in both pipeline types
claims.direction: neither classical sense-plan-act pipelines nor current end-to-end behavior models are yet reliable for combined grasping+planning fetch tasks; identifies concrete bottlenecks for improvement
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, diverse procedural scenes combining grasping and motion planning

title: PRIME: Scaffolding Manipulation Tasks With Behavior Primitives for Data-Efficient Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Decomposing task demonstrations into behavior-primitive sequences, then learning a high-level control policy to sequence primitives via imitation learning (rather than predicting raw low-level action chunks directly), significantly improves performance in multi-stage manipulation tasks versus state-of-the-art baselines, achieving 10-34% higher success rates in simulation and 20-48% higher on physical hardware
claims.direction: primitive-based hierarchical task scaffolding favored over flat, low-level action-chunk imitation learning for multi-stage/long-horizon tasks

claims.claim: Primitive-based scaffolding improves data efficiency of imitation learning by reducing compounding errors that accumulate over long task horizons in low-level action prediction
claims.direction: primitive-based task decomposition favored over flat imitation learning for reducing sample complexity in long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and physical hardware

title: Should We Ever Prefer Decision Transformer for Offline Reinforcement Learning?

claims.claim: On robotic manipulation (Robomimic) and locomotion (D4RL) benchmarks, a simple MLP-based Filtered Behavior Cloning (which merely filters out low-performing trajectories then does ordinary behavior cloning) achieves competitive or superior performance compared to the Decision Transformer, contradicting a prior claim that Decision Transformer is superior in sparse-reward/low-quality-data settings
claims.direction: simple filtered-data MLP behavior cloning favored over Decision Transformer (sequence-modeling transformer) for sparse-reward offline manipulation -- CONTRADICTS the trend toward transformer-based sequence-modeling action heads
claims.conditions: Robomimic manipulation tasks and D4RL locomotion benchmarks (simulation), sparse-reward settings

claims.claim: Filtered Behavior Cloning requires less training data and is computationally more efficient than Decision Transformer while matching or exceeding its performance
claims.direction: simpler, smaller MLP-based model favored over larger transformer sequence model for both performance and efficiency in this setting
claims.conditions: Robomimic and D4RL benchmarks

title: LaDi-WM: A Latent Diffusion-based World Model for Predictive Manipulation

claims.claim: Predicting the evolution of a latent space aligned with pretrained Visual Foundation Models (DINO-based geometric features + CLIP-based semantic features) via diffusion modeling, rather than directly predicting pixel-level future images, is easier to learn and more generalizable, and a diffusion policy that iteratively refines actions using these forecasted latent states enhances policy performance by 27.9% on LIBERO-LONG and 20% on a real-world scenario
claims.direction: latent-space (VFM-aligned) world-model prediction favored over pixel-space future-frame prediction as an auxiliary/planning signal for action generation
claims.conditions: synthetic (LIBERO-LONG) and real-world manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Leveraging a latent space already aligned with pretrained DINO (geometric) and CLIP (semantic) features provides an effective substrate for world-model prediction, rather than training a representation from scratch
claims.direction: reuse of pretrained DINO/CLIP-aligned latent representations favored over learning representations from scratch for world-model-based policy improvement
claims.conditions: real-world and synthetic benchmarks, generalizability demonstrated in real-world experiments

title: Object-Focus Actor for Data-efficient Robot Generalization Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical pipeline (object perception/pose estimation, then pre-manipulation pose arrival, then a focused policy exploiting consistent end trajectories) achieves robust performance with only 10 demonstrations, highlighting strong data efficiency versus standard VLA approaches that rely on large-scale data for generalization
claims.direction: object-centric, pose-arrival-decoupled hierarchical policy favored over standard end-to-end VLA training for data efficiency at very low (10) demo counts
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across seven manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Object-Focus Actor significantly outperforms baseline methods in both positional and background generalization tests, remaining focused and efficient even in varied backgrounds and positional layouts
claims.direction: object-centric hierarchical decomposition favored over standard imitation learning for robustness to background and object-position variation
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, varied backgrounds and object placements

title: From Demonstrations to Safe Deployment: Path-Consistent Safety Filtering for Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Path-consistent safety filtering (braking along the trajectory computed from generated diffusion-policy actions, keeping execution consistent with the training distribution) preserves task success rates and provides formal safety guarantees, whereas external safety filters that alter actions in ways unseen during training cause unpredictable behavior and performance degradation
claims.direction: training-distribution-consistent (path-consistent) safety filtering favored over generic external safety filters for diffusion-policy deployment
claims.conditions: simulation and three real-world human-robot interaction tasks

claims.claim: PACS outperforms reactive safety approaches such as control barrier functions by up to 68% in terms of task success, while providing set-based reachability safety guarantees in dynamic environments
claims.direction: trajectory/chunk-level path-consistent filtering favored over per-step reactive safety filters (e.g., CBFs) for action-chunked diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real-world human-robot interaction tasks, dynamic environments

title: Generalizable Multistage Assembly via One-Shot Category-Level Demonstration

claims.claim: A generalized multistage manipulation network learns a multistage screw-nut assembly task from a SINGLE demonstration and generalizes to new object instances with varying shapes/sizes via category-level pose estimation and manipulation-pose generalization
claims.direction: one-shot, category-level demonstration generalization favored over collecting many demonstrations per object instance for multistage assembly
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, category-level generalization to novel shapes/sizes

claims.claim: Real-time action correction using force feedback adjusts the trajectory to adapt to unexpected collisions during execution, addressing performance degradation from novel scenarios that most existing one/few-shot IL methods do not handle
claims.direction: force-feedback-based real-time trajectory correction favored over open-loop replay of a single demonstration for handling novel-scenario disturbances
claims.conditions: real-world execution with potential object collisions

title: How to Learn from What a Human Would Avoid? Intervention-Aware World Models with Real-World RL for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding a per-state intervention-probability prediction head to a latent world model (predicting the likelihood of a human safety takeover at future states) as an auxiliary risk-shaping signal achieves a 96.7% success rate on complex real-world grasping tasks while reducing operator intervention burden by up to 84% (step-weighted), versus treating human interventions only as reactive corrections
claims.direction: predictive intervention-probability auxiliary head favored over reactive-only human-intervention handling for real-world human-in-the-loop RL
claims.conditions: real 16-DoF LEAP Hand, convex/irregular grasping, prismatic manipulation, long-horizon multi-stage tasks

title: Learning New Tasks via Reusable Skills: Skill-Compositional Experts for Embodied Continual Learning

claims.claim: Feature drift accumulated under closed-loop control progressively propagates through sequential decision-making, causing more severe catastrophic forgetting in embodied continual learning than in conventional (non-closed-loop) continual learning settings
claims.direction: identifies closed-loop feature drift as a distinct, more severe forgetting mechanism requiring explicit handling beyond standard continual-learning techniques
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Explicitly organizing learned skills via Compositional Skill Grounding plus Dual Execution-and-Transition Experts (rather than learning skills without structuring them for coherent multi-task execution) consistently improves retention and overall task performance across sequentially learned manipulation tasks
claims.direction: structured, composable skill-expert architecture favored over unstructured skill learning for multi-task/continual manipulation retention
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks, ablation studies included

title: AC2-VLA: Action-Context-Aware Adaptive Computation in Vision-Language-Action Models for Efficient Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning computation on current visual observations, language instructions, and previous action states (rather than re-running the full VLA backbone every timestep) enables adaptive cognition reuse, token pruning, and selective component execution, achieving up to a 1.79x inference speedup while reducing FLOPs to 29.4% of the dense baseline, with comparable task success
claims.direction: action-context-conditioned adaptive computation favored over dense, uniform per-timestep VLA inference for reducing closed-loop latency/compute without sacrificing success rate
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation benchmarks, action-guided self-distillation from a dense VLA policy

claims.direction: distilled, structurally-sparsified VLA favored over the original dense VLA for efficient deployment while retaining task performance
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation benchmarks, cross-task/setting transfer

title: ForesightSafety-VLA: A Unified Diagnostic Safety Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Across representative VLA baselines evaluated on 66 safety-augmented scenarios (RoboTwin, 5 embodiments) under controlled variation in scene structure, language command, and visual observation, scene-structure and visual-observation variation induce substantially stronger safety/performance degradation than ordinary language variation, and even the strongest policy incurs non-trivial safety cost and unsafe nominal success

claims.conditions: RoboTwin simulation, 66 safety-augmented scenarios across 5 embodiments

title: BWM: A Low-Cost High-Fidelity World Simulator for Robot Learning

claims.claim: An action-conditioned world model combining initial-environment guidance, dynamic visual history, and temporally-aligned robot-action conditioning for stateful autoregressive future-observation prediction serves effectively both as a policy evaluator (closed-loop assessment, risk anticipation, policy ranking) and as a data engine, ranking first overall in the WorldArena Challenge
claims.direction: low-cost, action-conditioned autoregressive world model favored over costlier physics-simulator asset construction or uncontrolled video generators for both evaluation and data augmentation
claims.conditions: WorldArena benchmark and physical robots

claims.claim: The world model augments imitation-learning data with action-aligned synthetic rollouts constructed via trajectory replay, overlapping clip sampling, and initial-observation enhancement
claims.direction: action-aligned synthetic rollout generation favored as a low-cost supplement to real demonstration data
claims.conditions: physical robots and WorldArena benchmark

title: FlashVLA: Streaming Action Decoding for Fast and Asynchronous VLA Inference

claims.claim: Maintaining a streaming action buffer holding multiple chunks at different noise levels and decoding them via chunk-wise causal attention (producing one executable action chunk per inference step) implicitly preserves action continuity across chunk boundaries, enabling smooth asynchronous execution without requiring extra future-state conditioning
claims.direction: chunk-wise causal streaming decoding favored over conventional independent per-chunk flow-matching decoding for eliminating boundary discontinuities in asynchronous execution
claims.conditions: flow-matching-based VLA models, simulated and real-world experiments

claims.claim: FlashVLA achieves greater than or equal to 30 Hz control frequency on a single GPU with smooth asynchronous inference in real-world deployment, substantially improving inference speed while maintaining strong task performance versus existing efficient-inference and asynchronous-execution methods that fail to jointly achieve both low latency and temporally consistent asynchronous execution
claims.direction: unified streaming/asynchronous decoding framework favored over separately optimizing either inference speed or asynchronous consistency, for real-time single-GPU deployment
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, single GPU, flow-matching VLA

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly targets the exact combination of problems we face -- high inference latency AND unstable/jerky asynchronous execution in a flow-matching-style VLA on limited hardware -- and reports a concrete, unified fix (streaming chunk-wise decoding) reaching >=30Hz on a single GPU with smooth async execution; this is one of the most directly transferable results for our laptop-RTX-5060 deployment (Q06/Q10), worth reading the streaming-buffer/causal-attention mechanism in detail.

title: ARNOLD: A Benchmark for Language-Grounded Task Learning With Continuous States in Realistic 3D Scenes

claims.claim: Current language-conditioned policy-learning models, evaluated on 8 language-conditioned tasks requiring understanding of continuous (not just binary) object goal states, continue to experience significant challenges in generalizing to novel goal states
claims.direction: identifies a specific weakness of current language-conditioned policies: continuous goal-state understanding/generalization, not just discrete/binary goal specification
claims.conditions: realistic 3D simulated scenes, template-generated language instructions, expert demonstrations

claims.claim: State-of-the-art language-conditioned manipulation models show significant performance degradation under scene generalization and object generalization (not just goal-state generalization), highlighting a broad generalization gap in current models
claims.direction: reveals that scene and object generalization remain major unresolved weaknesses for language-conditioned manipulation policies, motivating research into causes/fixes
claims.conditions: realistic 3D simulated benchmark, novel scenes and novel objects

title: DexHub and DART: Towards Internet Scale Robot Data Collection

claims.claim: A cloud-based simulation plus augmented-reality crowdsourced teleoperation platform (DART) enables higher data collection throughput and lower physical fatigue compared to real-world teleoperation
claims.direction: cloud/AR-based crowdsourced teleoperation favored over conventional real-world teleoperation for scaling demonstration data collection
claims.conditions: user studies comparing DART to real-world teleoperation

claims.claim: Policies trained using DART-collected (simulation-plus-AR) datasets successfully transfer to reality and are robust to unseen visual disturbances
claims.direction: cloud-simulation-collected demonstration data favored for producing policies robust to unseen visual disturbances, comparable to real-world-collected data
claims.conditions: sim-to-real policy transfer, unseen visual disturbances

title: ControlTac: Scaling Tactile Data with Physically Controlled Tactile Image Generation

claims.claim: A two-stage controllable tactile image generation framework, conditioned on a single reference tactile image plus contact force and contact pose (physical priors), generates realistic synthetic tactile data across different sensors that consistently improves downstream task performance (object insertion, imitation learning, object weighting) versus prior simulation-based or free-form tactile generation approaches
claims.direction: physically-grounded controllable generative data augmentation favored over simulation-based or free-form synthetic data generation for scaling training data
claims.conditions: real-world downstream tasks, multiple tactile sensor instances

title: Residual Rotation Correction Using Tactile Equivariance

claims.claim: An SO(2)-equivariant network predicting a yaw residual from a single tactile frame, composed with a pretrained visuomotor policy's output, achieves robust generalization to unseen object orientations within the gripper using very few training samples, on a real robot, where baseline approaches fail even when given more training data
claims.direction: equivariance-structured residual correction favored over standard (non-equivariant) policies for sample-efficient generalization to unseen object orientations -- baselines fail even with MORE data, i.e. more data does not substitute for the right inductive bias
claims.conditions: real robot, parallel gripper, visuotactile policy, unseen object orientations

claims.claim: A lightweight residual correction mechanism (predicting only a rotational offset from tactile input) applied on top of a frozen pretrained visuomotor policy's action output is sufficient to correct orientation errors, rather than retraining the full action-generation policy
claims.direction: residual/corrective action-space augmentation favored over full policy retraining for handling specific systematic error modes (orientation)
claims.conditions: real robot, parallel-gripper manipulation

title: Evaluating Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning on MetaWorld ML10 Benchmark: Fast Adaptation in Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: MAML-TRPO achieves only 21.0% success on training tasks and 13.2% on held-out test tasks after one-shot adaptation on MetaWorld ML10, with a generalization gap emerging during meta-training (test performance plateaus while training performance keeps improving) and high variance (0% to 80%) across different manipulation skills
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS an optimistic view of gradient-based meta-learning for few-shot manipulation adaptation -- absolute success rates remain low and highly inconsistent across skills, despite one-shot adaptation gains being 'clear' in a relative sense
claims.conditions: MetaWorld ML10 benchmark (simulation), one-shot gradient adaptation

title: SafeBimanual: Diffusion-based Trajectory Optimization for Safe Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: A test-time trajectory optimization framework applied to any pre-trained diffusion-based bimanual policy (imposing safety cost functions via guided sampling during the denoising process, scheduled by a VLM based on keypoints/pairwise relations) improves success rate by 13.7% and reduces unsafe interactions by 18.8% over state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods on 8 simulated RoboTwin tasks, and improves real-world success rate by 32.5% on 4 real-world tasks
claims.direction: test-time, VLM-scheduled safety-constrained guided sampling favored over standard (unconstrained) diffusion-policy denoising, without needing to retrain the base policy
claims.conditions: 8 simulated RoboTwin bimanual tasks and 4 real-world bimanual tasks

claims.claim: Safety cost functions are imposed on the entire denoising process of action generation (not just final output), guiding trajectory-level (not just per-step) optimization for dual-arm coordination
claims.direction: trajectory/chunk-level guided denoising favored over per-step post-hoc correction for enforcing physical constraints in action-chunked diffusion policies
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world bimanual manipulation

title: MagiClaw: A Dual-Use, Vision-Based Soft Gripper for Bridging the Human Demonstration to Robotic Deployment Gap

claims.claim: Using an interchangeable handheld/robotic end-effector with embedded vision-based force sensing and fused multi-modal (RGB, LiDAR-depth, 6D pose) data streaming ensures hardware consistency between human demonstration collection and robotic policy deployment, lowering the barrier to collecting high-fidelity, contact-rich datasets
claims.direction: hardware-consistent handheld/robot-interchangeable end-effector favored over mismatched demonstration/deployment hardware for reducing the demonstration-to-deployment domain gap
claims.conditions: real hardware, contact-rich data collection and teleoperation

title: StreamVLA: Breaking the Reason-Act Cycle via Completion-State Gating

claims.claim: A 'Lock-and-Gated' mechanism that only triggers slow multimodal reasoning (textual instruction + imagined visual completion state) when a sub-task transition is detected, rather than at every timestep, produces a time-invariant goal anchor that locks to condition the action head during steady execution, making the policy robust to execution-speed variations
claims.direction: transition-triggered (gated) high-level reasoning, with a time-invariant completion-state goal anchor, favored over per-timestep re-reasoning for stable long-horizon action generation
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark and real-world manipulation with interference scenarios

claims.claim: By locking high-level intent and bypassing expensive autoregressive decoding for 72% of timesteps, StreamVLA achieves a 98.5% success rate on LIBERO and a 48% reduction in inference latency compared to full-reasoning baselines, with robust recovery in real-world interference scenarios
claims.direction: selectively-gated reasoning (skipping full reasoning most timesteps) favored over always-on full reasoning for reducing inference latency without sacrificing (and here improving) success rate
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (98.5% success) and real-world manipulation with interference

title: Update-Free On-Policy Steering via Verifiers

claims.claim: Training verifier functions from a base policy's own rollout data, then using them to steer (not retrain) a black-box diffusion policy toward higher-success-likelihood actions at execution time, improves success rate by an average of 49% over the base policy across 5 real tasks, without changing the base policy's parameters
claims.direction: lightweight, update-free verifier-based steering favored over retraining/fine-tuning a brittle base behavior-cloning/diffusion policy for improving precision
claims.conditions: real-world tasks (5 tasks) plus simulation, diffusion-policy base

title: F2F-AP: Flow-to-Future Asynchronous Policy for Real-time Dynamic Manipulation

claims.claim: Predicting object flow to synthesize future observations, and aligning predicted-observation visual features with ground-truth future states via a flow-based contrastive learning objective, gives an asynchronous policy the capacity for proactive planning that explicitly compensates for inference latency, significantly enhancing responsiveness and success rates in dynamic manipulation tasks involving actively moving objects
claims.direction: latency-compensating, future-anticipating asynchronous policy favored over standard asynchronous inference (which lags behind a moving real-time environment) for dynamic manipulation
claims.conditions: dynamic manipulation tasks involving actively moving objects (asynchronous inference setting)

title: Task aware Dynamic Movement Primitives for failure detection and recovery in contact rich manipulation

claims.claim: A single demonstration encoded as a Dynamic Movement Primitive, combined with real-time stage classification using goal-relative position features, generalizes to unseen goal positions without requiring retraining, matching DMPs' inherent generalization capability
claims.direction: single-demonstration DMP with goal-relative-feature stage classification favored over collecting per-goal-position demonstrations
claims.conditions: real peg-in-hole assembly setup, single demonstration

claims.claim: Online anomaly detection via a Mahalanobis distance metric over force features, triggering a spiral-search recovery policy upon detected contact-induced failure, achieves 95% stage-classification accuracy and reliable recovery under lateral misalignments up to 3mm
claims.direction: force-feature-based online anomaly detection plus an active recovery policy favored over open-loop DMP replay for contact-rich task reliability
claims.conditions: real peg-in-hole assembly, single demonstration, lateral misalignments up to 3mm

title: N0-TWAM: Scaling Tactile-Native World-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A tactile-native world-action model pre-trained at large scale (six embodiments, 450 tasks) that jointly predicts future vision and future contact (using a unified force-based tactile representation, NeoForce) improves capability on contact-rich tasks and benefits from data scaling for precise tactile and action prediction
claims.direction: joint vision+touch future prediction, pretrained at large scale, favored over vision-only world-action models for contact-rich manipulation
claims.conditions: real and simulated benchmarks, six embodiments, 450 tasks

claims.claim: An asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers architecture (a full-width expert for video prediction paired with slim experts for downstream action and tactile prediction) is used to achieve real-time efficiency for a tactile world-action model
claims.direction: asymmetric expert-sizing (large shared perception expert, small task-specific experts) favored over uniformly-sized experts for real-time efficiency
claims.conditions: large-scale tactile-vision-action world model

title: TONAV: Task-Oriented Navigation and Action-Velocity Chunk Learning for Articulated Object Quadrupedal Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: A position-velocity-coupled teleoperation framework that explicitly captures motion dynamics improves master-follower consistency and yields smoother, more temporally-consistent demonstrations than position-only teleoperation capture
claims.direction: jointly capturing/modeling position AND velocity (rather than position alone) favored for demonstration quality and downstream action smoothness
claims.conditions: real-world teleoperation, articulated-object quadrupedal mobile manipulation

claims.claim: Action-velocity chunk learning, which jointly models joint positions and their temporal transitions under velocity supervision, enables smooth and stable sustained-contact manipulation and mitigates tracking lag/motion jitter/contact instability seen in prior methods, achieving higher success rates in real-world experiments
claims.direction: velocity-supervised joint position-chunk learning favored over position-only chunk prediction for reducing jitter/instability in sustained-contact tasks
claims.conditions: real-world diverse articulated-object manipulation tasks

title: Raise One and Infer Three: Toward Reasoning- and Memory-Augmented Diffusion Policy Generalization

claims.claim: Encoding skill-level reasoning-graph representations directly into the diffusion model's initial noise space (Chain-of-Skill Noise Watermark) enables temporally coherent multi-step reasoning throughout the diffusion process under distribution shift, improving on approaches relying solely on instantaneous observations/geometric-perceptual representations
claims.direction: reasoning-structured noise initialization favored over standard unstructured diffusion-policy initialization for OOD robustness
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world environments

claims.claim: A Self-evolving Policy Knowledge Bank that discretizes spatio-temporally refined trajectories into reusable skill primitives via VQ-VAE provides an explicit, adaptive memory mechanism to guide and refine action generation, addressing the lack of accumulated/reusable policy knowledge in standard diffusion policies
claims.direction: explicit discretized-memory-bank mechanism favored over policies with no persistent memory of previously learned trajectories
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: The combined reasoning+memory approach demonstrates superiority and robustness specifically under out-of-distribution visual shifts and with limited demonstrations, versus approaches relying only on improved geometric/perceptual representations
claims.direction: reasoning+memory augmentation favored over representation-only improvements for OOD and low-data robustness
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world environments, limited demonstrations

title: Cloud-Based Hierarchical Imitation Learning for Scalable Transfer of Construction Skills from Human Workers to Assisting Robots

claims.claim: A Hierarchical Imitation Learning model decomposes human manipulation skills into sequential and reactive sub-skills (two layers), represented by deep generative models, to enable adaptive robot control rather than flat, monolithic skill representation
claims.direction: hierarchical sequential+reactive sub-skill decomposition favored over flat, non-hierarchical imitation learning for adaptive construction-task control
claims.conditions: cloud robotics virtual demonstration framework

claims.claim: An immersive cloud-based virtual demonstration framework with reusable, federated demonstrations reduces the need for workers to repeatedly physically demonstrate full-scale tasks
claims.direction: reusable, digitalized virtual demonstrations favored over repeated physical full-scale demonstrations for scaling skill transfer
claims.conditions: construction robotics, virtual demonstration collection

title: CyberDemo: Augmenting Simulated Human Demonstration for Real-World Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Simulated human demonstrations combined with extensive data augmentation in the simulated environment OUTPERFORM traditional in-domain real-world demonstrations when the resulting policy is transferred to the real world, across various tasks and diverse physical/visual conditions
claims.direction: heavily-augmented simulated demonstrations favored over real-world in-domain demonstrations for real-world transfer -- CONTRADICTS the default assumption that real demonstrations are preferable to simulated ones
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, transfer from simulation

claims.claim: CyberDemo exhibits generalizability to previously unseen objects, e.g. successfully rotating novel tetra-valve and penta-valve objects despite human demonstrations only involving tri-valves
claims.direction: simulation-augmented training favored over real-demo-only training for generalization to novel object variants (different shape/complexity) not seen in demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, unseen object categories at test time

why_deep_read: A well-established (44-citation) result directly contradicting the assumption that more real demonstrations are always better: heavily-augmented simulated demos beat real in-domain demos for real-world transfer, including generalizing to unseen object variants -- squarely relevant to our 'different-looking pumpkin' generalization failure and our limited real-demo budget (Q05/Q14); worth reading exactly which augmentations were used and whether they'd transfer to a simple parallel-gripper pick-and-place setup.

title: ICRT: In-Context Imitation Learning via Next-Token Prediction

claims.claim: A causal transformer performing autoregressive next-token prediction jointly over images, proprioceptive states, and actions (in-context, training-free at test time) can adapt to new environment configurations differing from both the prompt and training data
claims.direction: autoregressive in-context sensorimotor sequence modeling favored over standard fine-tuning-based action generation for flexible test-time adaptation without retraining
claims.conditions: real Franka Emika robot, novel environment configurations

claims.claim: In a multi-task setup, ICRT significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art robot foundation models on generalization to unseen tasks, using only in-context demonstration examples rather than additional training
claims.direction: in-context (prompt-based) task specification favored over foundation-model fine-tuning for generalizing to unseen tasks given demonstration examples
claims.conditions: real robot, multi-task, unseen-task generalization

title: OG-VLA: Orthographic Image Generation for 3D-Aware Vision-Language Action Model

claims.claim: Unprojecting input RGBD observations from diverse views into a point cloud, then rendering canonical orthographic views (ensuring input-view invariance and input/output space consistency) before processing with a vision backbone/LLM/diffusion model, combines the precise-manipulation strength of 3D-aware policies with the generalization strength of VLAs, achieving state-of-the-art generalization to unseen environments with over 40% relative improvement on the Arnold and Colosseum benchmarks while maintaining robust performance in seen settings
claims.direction: canonical-orthographic-view 3D representation favored over both raw multi-view RGBD (sensitive to camera/robot pose) and standard 2D VLA representations (poor generalization to unseen scenes) for combining precision and generalization
claims.conditions: Arnold and Colosseum simulation benchmarks; real-world validation

claims.claim: Standard VLAs are sensitive to camera and robot pose variations, whereas OG-VLA's canonical orthographic projection is designed to be invariant to input viewpoint
claims.direction: viewpoint-invariant canonical projection favored over raw camera-frame processing for robustness to camera/robot pose variation
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation, varying camera/robot poses

claims.claim: OG-VLA shows real-world adaptation to new tasks/settings using only 3 to 5 demonstrations, along with strong generalization
claims.direction: 3D-aware canonical representation favored for enabling adaptation from very few (3-5) real-world demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world robot, 3-5 demonstrations

why_deep_read: Directly targets our exact 'slightly moved camera' failure via a concrete, quantified fix (canonical orthographic/view-invariant 3D representation, +40% relative generalization gain) and separately reports real-world adaptation from just 3-5 demonstrations -- a near-ideal match for both Q04/Q11 (camera robustness) and Q13 (extremely low demo count); worth reading the unprojection/canonical-rendering pipeline to assess feasibility on our RealSense + wrist-camera RGB-D setup.

title: Right-Side-Out: Learning Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Garment Reversal

claims.claim: A fully automated, GPU-parallel Material Point Method simulator with domain randomization over geometry, material parameters, and viewpoints produces training data (depth, masks, keypoint labels) without any human demonstrations, and a policy trained entirely in this simulation deploys zero-shot on real hardware with up to 81.3% success on a highly dynamic, severely occluded task
claims.direction: fully-automated, domain-randomized simulation data generation (with no human demonstrations at all) favored over teleoperated demonstration collection for a highly dynamic, hard-to-demonstrate task
claims.conditions: real hardware, single depth camera, zero-shot sim-to-real, dynamic and severely occluded manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing the task into keypoint-parameterized bimanual primitives sharply reduces the action space while preserving robustness, enabling the task to be solved without any human demonstrations
claims.direction: keypoint-parameterized primitive action space favored over raw low-level action learning when no human demonstrations are available
claims.conditions: real hardware, zero human demonstrations

title: NVSPolicy: Adaptive Novel-View Synthesis for Generalizable Language-Conditioned Policy Learning

claims.claim: Dynamically selecting an informative viewpoint and synthesizing an adaptive novel-view image (via a cycle-consistent VAE that disentangles semantic from remaining visual features) to enrich visual context achieves an average success rate of 90.4% across all CALVIN tasks, greatly outperforming recent methods; ablations confirm the significance of the adaptive novel-view-synthesis paradigm
claims.direction: adaptive, learned novel-view synthesis favored over relying on a single fixed observed viewpoint for generalizable policy learning
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark (simulation) plus real-world robotic platform evaluation

claims.claim: The semantic feature disentangled from synthesized novel views informs high-level meta-skill selection in a hierarchical policy, while the remaining feature guides low-level action estimation, for language-conditioned policy learning
claims.direction: disentangled semantic/geometric features feeding a hierarchical (meta-skill + low-level action) policy favored over a monolithic language-conditioned policy
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark, real-world robotic platform

title: Intelligent Robotic Manipulation for IV Bag Quality Control: A Contamination-Aware Learning System

claims.claim: Using a leader-follower architecture with dual SO-ARM101 low-cost robot arms, the system learns visual-motor mappings from just 50 expert demonstrations, achieving 96% and 98% success rates for loading and unloading operations respectively
claims.direction: 50 demonstrations on a low-cost SO-ARM101 leader-follower arm are sufficient for high (96-98%) success rates on a real pick/place-style manipulation task
claims.conditions: real dual SO-ARM101 low-cost robot arms, leader-follower teleoperation, 50 expert demonstrations

claims.claim: The contamination-aware approach demonstrates 94% success detecting contaminated IV bags and 90% adaptation to new scenarios, with zero safety incidents during testing, validated with 95% confidence intervals
claims.direction: learned visual-motor mapping with integrated quality-feedback favored for robust adaptation to new (contamination) scenarios on a low-cost arm
claims.conditions: real dual SO-ARM101 arms, contamination detection scenarios

claims.claim: Eye-in-hand (wrist-mounted) RGB vision is used as the primary sensing modality for the low-cost dual-arm system, coordinated through an open-source ROS2 architecture
claims.direction: eye-in-hand wrist camera sensing favored/sufficient for this low-cost arm manipulation task
claims.conditions: real dual SO-ARM101 low-cost arms

why_deep_read: This uses the SAME robot family as our setup (SO-ARM101, the successor/sibling of SO-101) with eye-in-hand vision, leader-follower teleoperation, and exactly our target demo count (50), reporting concrete high success rates (96-98%) plus adaptation/robustness numbers -- about as close a real-world analog to our exact hardware and data budget as exists in this batch; worth reading the visual-motor mapping architecture and demo-collection details directly for our SO-101 setup (Q11/Q13/Q14).

title: Unified Learning of Temporal Task Structure and Action Timing for Bimanual Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A 3-D Gaussian-Mixture-Model-based subsymbolic representation of action timing, combined with a symbolic (Allen-relation) task-structure inference method, produces temporal task constraints that are more accurate than prior heuristic approaches, and generated plans are temporally closer to human demonstrations than the single most characteristic demonstration
claims.direction: learned joint symbolic+subsymbolic temporal-structure representation favored over heuristic task-structure inference or naively replaying the most characteristic demonstration for bimanual timing/coordination
claims.conditions: human demonstrations, simulation and real-robot orchestrated task execution

title: Action-Controlled Scale-Wise Flow Matching for Embodied World Models

claims.claim: Treating action-conditioned prediction as a scale-decoupled controlled dynamical system (scale-wise flow matching over a continuous latent pyramid, with a multi-scale temporal planner) improves visual prediction quality, action alignment, counterfactual accuracy, no-op residual suppression, and long-horizon rollout consistency over strong discrete and continuous world-model baselines
claims.direction: scale-decoupled, action-controlled flow-matching world-model design favored over conventional action-conditioned video generation for long-horizon rollout stability and action-faithfulness
claims.conditions: action-conditioned robotic manipulation, visual planning, model-based RL, and action-free driving video prediction

claims.claim: An Action-Controlled Velocity Field separates action-free passive drift from action-induced residual dynamics, making the action an explicit, bounded control input to the predicted dynamics rather than a passive conditioning token
claims.direction: explicit, bounded action-as-control-input formulation favored over treating action as a passive conditioning signal, for world-model action alignment and counterfactual accuracy
claims.conditions: action-conditioned robotic manipulation and visual planning benchmarks

title: EasyMimic: A Low-Cost Framework for Robot Imitation Learning from Human Videos

claims.claim: Extracting 3D hand trajectories from standard-RGB-camera human videos, mapping them to a low-cost robot's gripper control space via an action-alignment module, and applying a simple hand visual-augmentation strategy to bridge the human-to-robot domain gap, enables policies to be learned largely from human video rather than robot teleoperation data
claims.direction: human-video-derived demonstrations (with hand visual augmentation) favored over collecting large-scale real low-cost-robot teleoperation data
claims.conditions: low-cost LeRobot platform, standard RGB cameras, human video demonstrations

claims.claim: A co-training method that fine-tunes on both processed human video data and only a small amount of real robot data achieves high performance across various manipulation tasks and enables rapid adaptation to new tasks, significantly reducing reliance on expensive robot data collection
claims.direction: co-training on abundant human video + a small amount of real robot data favored over collecting large real-robot-only demonstration datasets, for low-cost home robots
claims.conditions: low-cost LeRobot platform, small amount of supplementary real robot data

why_deep_read: This targets almost exactly our situation: a low-cost LeRobot-family platform with a limited demo budget, proposing to substitute cheap human RGB video (with a simple hand-augmentation trick) for most of the real teleoperation data. Worth reading the action-alignment and hand-augmentation details to see if we can apply this directly to cut our own teleop burden for the pumpkin task (Q05/Q13).

title: Towards Human-like Physical Intelligence: Lifelong Vision-Language-Action Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A cache-efficient stochastic replay strategy preserves balanced retention signals for previously learned manipulation behaviors without requiring full-trajectory storage
claims.direction: cache-efficient partial-trajectory replay favored over full-trajectory replay buffers for memory-efficient continual learning
claims.conditions: real xArm robot, lifelong/continual manipulation learning

claims.claim: A dual-timescale LoRA gating module that decomposes VLA adaptation into a short-term (plasticity) and long-term (stability) adapter, integrated via a task-aware gate, outperforms existing baselines in efficient skill expansion and robust retention across sequentially learned tasks
claims.direction: dual-timescale, gated LoRA adaptation favored over single-timescale continual fine-tuning for balancing new-task learning with retention of prior skills
claims.conditions: real xArm robot, sequential/lifelong task learning

title: RoboMP-DINOv2: Prompts, Not Filters for Robust Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Extracting dense DINOv2 features from the FULL observation and injecting learned region-specific embeddings at mask-indicated locations (treating masks as spatial prompts rather than hard visibility filters that discard context), then jointly contextualizing prompted and unprompted tokens for action prediction, outperforms a DINOv2-based Diffusion Policy that uses masks as hard filters
claims.direction: mask-as-prompt (soft, context-preserving) DINOv2 conditioning favored over mask-as-filter (context-discarding) approaches for action prediction
claims.conditions: seven simulated manipulation settings

claims.claim: RoboMP-DINOv2 achieves 60.7% success under spatial shifts and 59.7% under scene clutter, versus 50.7% and 41.0% respectively for a DINOv2-based Diffusion Policy baseline; with added masked-region color randomization (RoboMP-DINOv2-MCR), it achieves 72.5% success under unseen object colors versus 35.1% for the strongest color-randomized baseline
claims.direction: mask-prompted DINOv2 (plus masked-region color randomization) strongly favored over standard DINOv2-based diffusion policy and standard color-randomization baselines specifically for robustness to spatial shift, clutter, and unseen object appearance/color
claims.conditions: seven simulated manipulation settings, spatial shift, scene clutter, and unseen object color conditions

why_deep_read: Reports large, concrete robustness gains (72.5% vs 35.1% under unseen object color; 59.7% vs 41.0% under clutter) using DINOv2 -- one of the vision encoders explicitly named in our Q03 -- via a simple mask-as-prompt plus color-randomization recipe; this maps almost directly onto our 'different-looking pumpkin' and cluttered-tray robustness concerns and is worth reading for the exact prompting/randomization mechanism (Q03/Q14).

title: Pushing the Limits of Cross-Embodiment Learning for Manipulation and Navigation

claims.claim: Co-training a single goal-conditioned policy with navigation data (from robotic arms, quadcopters, quadrupeds, and mobile bases framed as a shared goal-reaching task) enhances robustness and performance in goal-conditioned manipulation specifically when using a wrist-mounted camera
claims.direction: cross-embodiment/cross-domain (navigation+manipulation) co-training favored over manipulation-only training data for improving wrist-camera-based manipulation robustness
claims.conditions: heterogeneous embodiments (arms, quadcopters, quadrupeds, mobile bases), wrist-mounted camera manipulation

claims.claim: A policy trained only from navigation-only and static-manipulation-only data can control a novel embodiment (a mobile manipulator) in a zero-shot manner when deployed, without embodiment-specific training data
claims.direction: diverse cross-embodiment training data favored over embodiment-specific data collection for zero-shot transfer to a novel embodiment
claims.conditions: zero-shot deployment on a mobile manipulator not seen during training

title: Learning In-Hand Translation Using Tactile Skin with Shear and Normal Force Sensing

claims.claim: A 3-axis (shear+normal) tactile-sensing RL policy consistently outperforms baselines using only shear forces, only normal forces, or only proprioception, for dexterous in-hand translation via sliding contact
claims.direction: combined shear+normal tactile sensing favored over any single tactile modality or proprioception alone as an auxiliary input
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous in-hand manipulation, sim-to-real tactile sensor model

title: VideoVLA: Video Generators Can Be Generalizable Robot Manipulators
