claims.direction: favors supplementing scarce teleoperated robot demonstrations with larger-scale egocentric human video data via a unified state-action embodiment mapping
claims.conditions: humanoid robot, egocentric human dataset (PH2D), co-trained with smaller robot dataset

title: 4D Visual Pre-Training for Robot Learning

claims.claim: Framing visual pre-training as a next-point-cloud-prediction (4D) problem modeled as a diffusion model and pre-trained on larger public datasets (FVP) boosts the average success rate of 3D Diffusion Policy (DP3) by 28% across twelve real-world manipulation tasks, achieving SOTA among imitation learning methods, and its efficacy transfers across different point-cloud encoders and datasets
claims.direction: favors 3D/4D (point-cloud-based) visual pre-training objectives over 2D-image-based pre-training for policies that use point-cloud/3D input
claims.conditions: real-world, twelve manipulation tasks, 3D Diffusion Policy backbone, also applied to a larger VLA (RDT-1B)

claims.claim: Using a next-point-cloud-prediction (future-prediction) auxiliary/pretraining objective, rather than only observation-to-action mapping, is the source of the reported performance gains, and also enhances a larger VLA model (RDT-1B) on various robot tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a future-frame/future-point-cloud prediction auxiliary pretraining objective
claims.conditions: real-world, transfers to a large VLA (RDT-1B) as well as smaller 3D diffusion policies

title: A latency-aware framework for visuomotor policy learning on industrial robots

claims.claim: A latency-aware execution strategy that timestamps policy-predicted action-chunk sequences and schedules only temporally feasible actions (rather than blocking or naively executing asynchronously) preserves smooth motion, compliant contact, and demonstration-consistent task progression across inference latencies of 100-500ms; latency-aware execution kept task duration and motion smoothness within 13% and 9% of the demonstration reference, avoiding latency-dependent slowdown (blocking) and large contact-force overshoots (naive async)
claims.direction: favors explicit timestamp-based scheduling of action chunks over both blocking execution and naive asynchronous execution, without modifying the policy architecture or training
claims.conditions: real industrial robot, contact-rich assembly task, inference latencies 100-500ms systematically varied, works with any pre-trained policy architecture

why_deep_read: Directly matches our ~2s-latency/jerky-chunk-boundary problem with a policy-architecture-agnostic scheduling fix tested across a controlled range of latencies with quantified smoothness/duration numbers — likely one of the most directly actionable papers in the batch for Q10

title: OpenSPM: An Environment-Transferable Robotic Key Spatial Pose Memory and Closed-Loop High-Frequency Flow-Matching Action Generation Model

claims.claim: A lightweight conditional flow-matching action model combined with retrieved object-centric spatial pose memory and closed-loop proprioceptive/residual correction achieves 85.6% success on ten LIBERO-GOAL tasks at an equivalent control frequency of 1033.3 Hz while requiring minimal inference compute; ablations show structured spatial memory and closed-loop residual correction are crucial for suppressing trajectory error accumulation
claims.direction: favors lightweight flow-matching action generation plus explicit spatial memory and closed-loop residual correction over heavier end-to-end architectures, for high-frequency, low-compute deployment
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO-GOAL), lightweight model, high control frequency, low compute requirement

title: FreqPolicy: Frequency Autoregressive Visuomotor Policy with Continuous Tokens

claims.claim: Representing actions in the frequency domain (low-frequency components for global movement, high-frequency for fine local detail) with progressive hierarchical modeling and continuous latent tokens outperforms existing action-representation methods in both accuracy and efficiency across diverse 2D and 3D robotic manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors a frequency-domain autoregressive action representation with continuous tokens as an alternative to standard per-timestep regression, diffusion, or discrete-token action heads
claims.conditions: 2D and 3D manipulation benchmarks (mix of sim/real not fully specified in abstract)

title: GenFlowRL: Shaping Rewards with Generative Object-Centric Flow in Visual Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Deriving shaped rewards from generated object-centric flow (trained from diverse cross-embodiment datasets) enables learning generalizable, robust policies using low-dimensional, object-centric features rather than raw pixels, consistently achieving superior performance across 10 manipulation tasks in simulation and real-world cross-embodiment evaluations
claims.direction: favors low-dimensional object-centric (flow-based) visual features over raw high-dimensional pixel input for policy robustness/generalization
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated, cross-embodiment, 10 manipulation tasks

title: ManiVID-3D: Generalizable View-Invariant Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation via Disentangled 3D Representations

claims.claim: A policy trained from a fixed front-facing camera may fail when the camera is shifted; a lightweight module (ViewNet) that aligns point-cloud observations from arbitrary viewpoints into a unified coordinate system without extrinsic calibration achieves a 40.6% higher success rate than SOTA methods under viewpoint variations while using 80% fewer parameters, across 10 simulated and 5 real-world tasks, with strong sim-to-real performance under severe perspective changes
claims.direction: favors explicit view-invariant 3D (point-cloud) representation learning over pixel-based policies for robustness to camera viewpoint/position shift
claims.conditions: real-world (5 tasks) and simulated (10 tasks), no extrinsic camera calibration required, smaller parameter count than baselines

why_deep_read: Directly targets our 'camera slightly moved' robustness failure with a quantified real-world result (40.6% higher success under viewpoint shift) using 80% fewer parameters — highly relevant to Q04/Q11/Q12 jointly; full text would clarify data/compute requirements and whether RGB-only (no depth) variants exist

title: E0: Enhancing Generalization and Fine-Grained Control in VLA Models via Tweedie Discrete Diffusion

claims.claim: Formulating action generation as iterative denoising over quantized (discrete) action tokens via a Tweedie discrete-diffusion process, motivated by the inherent multi-peaked (multimodal) nature of action distributions and token-based reasoning of VLM/VLA backbones, achieves SOTA performance across 14 diverse environments (LIBERO, VLABench, ManiSkill, and a real-world Franka arm), outperforming strong baselines by 10.7% on average
claims.direction: favors discrete/quantized-token diffusion action heads (explicitly modeling multimodal action distributions) over standard continuous diffusion or single-mode regression heads
claims.conditions: real-world Franka arm plus multiple sim benchmarks, VLA backbone

claims.claim: A spherical viewpoint perturbation augmentation enhances robustness to camera shifts without requiring additional real data collection
claims.direction: favors synthetic camera-viewpoint perturbation augmentation (no new demos needed) for robustness to camera shift
claims.conditions: applied on top of existing demonstrations, tested across the same 14 environments

why_deep_read: Addresses two of our exact failure modes at once — action multimodality (Q01) via discrete diffusion and camera-shift robustness (Q05) via cheap viewpoint-perturbation augmentation requiring no new demos — with real Franka-arm results; full text would give the augmentation recipe we could directly try

title: RelAfford6D: Relational 6D Affordance Graphs for Constraint-Driven Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A training-free framework using a Relational 6D Affordance Graph (deducing semantic topology and precise SE(3) poses via vision foundation models, then tracking kinematic-constraint manifolds with closed-loop replanning) achieves superior zero-shot success rates, cross-category generalization, and execution robustness compared to existing data-driven baselines, in both simulation and real-world environments
claims.direction: contrasts with common practice: a training-free, geometry/constraint-based approach outperforms data-driven learned policies on generalization/robustness for articulated-object manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation, articulated objects, zero-shot (no task-specific training data)

title: Constraint-Manifold-Guided Diffusion and Mode-Aware Compliance for Bimanual Assembly

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework combining a constraint-guided diffusion policy (for long-horizon planning, trained on real dual-arm hardware data, bypassing simulated-contact fidelity gaps) with a mode-aware residual policy (using sparse kinesthetic corrections for fine contact adaptation) achieves 88-92% success rates, consistently outperforming classical, learning-based, and ablated baselines on real dual-arm bimanual assembly tasks
claims.direction: favors combining a diffusion-based planning action head with a separate residual/corrective policy for contact-rich fine adjustment, trained directly on real robot data rather than simulation
claims.conditions: real dual-UR5 hardware, three bimanual assembly tasks, trained directly on real data (no sim)

title: SIR: Structured Image Representations for Explainable Robot Learning

claims.claim: Using scene graphs (with an end-to-end learned sparsification module producing a task-relevant sub-graph) as an intermediate visual representation for the action-generation model outperforms image-based baseline policies on RoboCasa (19.5% vs 14.81% success rate) and makes the model's attention explainable, revealing dataset biases such as spurious correlations and positional biases
claims.direction: favors structured, sparsified graph-based visual representations over standard learned image embeddings, for both accuracy and interpretability/distraction-sensitivity diagnosis
claims.conditions: RoboCasa simulation benchmark

title: Uncovering and Mitigating Positional Blind Spots in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Even with instruction and every other scene factor held fixed, merely relocating a task-irrelevant distractor can sharply raise failure probability within localized, spatially coherent regions of the workspace ('Positional Blind Spots'), which the authors find pervasive and spatially concentrated (failure rates up to 0.58) across five SOTA VLA policies on two benchmarks
claims.direction: confirms that policy robustness is not spatially uniform even under otherwise identical conditions -- distractor position alone can localize failure
claims.conditions: five SOTA VLA policies, two benchmarks (not stated as real-world in abstract)

claims.claim: Targeted LoRA fine-tuning on demonstrations collected specifically from the identified Positional-Blind-Spot regions reduces overall failure rate by 40.00%-85.19% while largely preserving performance elsewhere
claims.direction: favors targeted collection of additional demonstrations in diagnosed failure regions over generic additional data collection
claims.conditions: LoRA fine-tuning on small targeted demo sets per identified region

title: SmoothRL: Online Reinforcement Learning During Asynchronous Execution

claims.claim: SmoothRL explicitly models the asynchronous inference process during training by partitioning each generated action chunk into committed, execution, and discarded regions, propagating value-function gradients only through the execution region, aligning policy optimization with the actual trajectory distribution induced by asynchronous chunked execution; evaluated on real-world tasks requiring both high precision and highly dynamic asynchronous execution
claims.direction: favors training/fine-tuning policies with explicit awareness of the asynchronous execution/chunk-partition structure rather than training as if execution were synchronous
claims.conditions: real-world robotic tasks, online RL fine-tuning of a pretrained chunked policy under asynchronous inference

title: Grasp It Like a Pro 2.0: A Data-Driven Approach Exploiting Basic Shape Decomposition and Human Data for Grasping Unknown Objects

claims.claim: A grasp-planning algorithm that decomposes objects into basic shapes and uses a small number of human demonstrations to generalize to unknown objects' geometry achieves a 94.0% success rate over 150 grasps across 30 objects with a soft underactuated hand, and 85.0% over 80 grasps across 16 objects with a rigid gripper
claims.direction: favors leveraging a small number of human demonstrations plus geometric shape-decomposition priors, rather than large demonstration datasets, for grasp generalization to novel/unknown objects
claims.conditions: real robot, multiple grippers, many object categories, small number of human demonstrations used as prior

title: Latent Action Pretraining from Videos

claims.claim: LAPA pretrains a VLA using unsupervised discrete latent actions (learned via VQ-VAE between video frames) from action-label-free internet-scale human/robot videos, then finetunes on only small-scale robot manipulation data to map latent to robot actions; this significantly outperforms existing techniques that train from large-scale videos, and even outperforms a SOTA VLA trained with real robot action labels on tasks requiring language conditioning, generalization to unseen objects, and semantic generalization to unseen instructions
claims.direction: favors unsupervised latent-action (VQ-based) pretraining from action-label-free video over requiring large-scale teleoperated action-labeled data
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, small-scale robot fine-tuning data after large video pretraining

claims.claim: Latent actions are learned as discrete tokens via a VQ-VAE-based objective between image frames, before being mapped to continuous robot actions during finetuning
claims.direction: favors discrete/VQ latent-token action representations as an intermediate learning target
claims.conditions: pretraining stage uses discrete latent tokens; final robot action mapping learned via small-scale finetuning

title: CDP: Towards Robust Autoregressive Visuomotor Policy Learning via Causal Diffusion

claims.claim: Causal Diffusion Policy (CDP) conditions action prediction on historical action sequences (rather than only instantaneous state/scene observations), achieving significantly higher accuracy than existing methods across diverse simulated and real-world 2D and 3D manipulation tasks, and maintains remarkable precision even under degraded input observation quality by reasoning through temporal continuity
claims.direction: favors conditioning diffusion-based action prediction on observation/action history over single-frame instantaneous observations, especially for robustness to degraded/noisy observations
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated, 2D and 3D manipulation tasks, transformer-based diffusion model

claims.claim: A caching mechanism storing attention key-value pairs from previous timesteps substantially reduces redundant computation during autoregressive inference, mitigating the computational cost of history-conditioned diffusion
claims.direction: favors KV-caching to reduce inference latency/cost of history-conditioned autoregressive diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation, autoregressive diffusion inference

title: SOLD: Slot Object-Centric Latent Dynamics Models for Relational Manipulation Learning from Pixels

claims.claim: An unsupervised object-centric (slot-attention) latent dynamics world model learned from pixels outperforms DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 (state-of-the-art model-based RL algorithms) across benchmark robotic environments requiring relational reasoning and manipulation
claims.direction: favors structured, object-centric world-model representations over holistic/monolithic latent dynamics models for relational manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: benchmark robotic simulation environments (not stated as real-world), model-based RL

title: DreamArrangement: Learning Language-Conditioned Robotic Rearrangement of Objects via Denoising Diffusion and VLM Planner

claims.claim: A policy learned from a synthetic simulator-generated tabletop rearrangement dataset (with a transformer-based denoising diffusion model for arrangement generation and a VLM-derived policy from text/visual state) transfers to the real world without extra human intervention, given only a few-shot instruction examples
claims.direction: favors training primarily on synthetic/simulated data with diffusion-based generation and language-conditioned VLM planning, transferring zero-shot/few-shot to real-world execution
claims.conditions: synthetic 2D tabletop dataset for training, real-world robotic evaluation for transfer

title: Language-Guided Dual-Mode Policy for Dual-Arm Manipulation

claims.claim: A language-guided routing layer that predicts motion mode (synchronous vs asynchronous coordination) from semantic/temporal information, combined with FiLM-based injection of language into the visual backbone for task-aware feature modulation, outperforms existing baselines (including RDT) by 14.5 percentage points on the RoboTwin 2 dual-arm benchmark and remains robust under unseen temporal-coordination instruction variants at inference
claims.direction: favors FiLM-style language conditioning combined with explicit mode-routing (rather than a single shared policy) for language-conditioned multi-task control
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2 simulation benchmark, dual-arm tasks

title: Primary-Fine Decoupling for Action Generation in Robotic Imitation

claims.claim: A two-stage action-generation framework (PF-DAG) that first compresses action chunks into a small set of discrete coarse modes (avoiding 'mode bouncing') and then generates high-fidelity continuous actions via a mode-conditioned MeanFlow policy achieves a theoretically proven strictly lower MSE bound than single-stage generative policies, and empirically outperforms SOTA baselines across 56 tasks (Adroit, DexArt, MetaWorld) plus real-world tactile dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors an explicit two-stage discrete-mode-then-continuous-refinement action head over pure discrete-token or pure single-stage continuous (e.g., single diffusion/flow) action heads, for resolving action multimodality
claims.conditions: mostly simulation benchmarks (56 tasks) plus generalization check on real-world tactile dexterous manipulation

title: Training-Free Interaction-Aligned Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: A training-free method (IAprune) that jointly decides per-frame visual-token budget and within-budget token selection using semantic-motion spatial agreement matches unpruned-policy accuracy on LIBERO with a 1.54x speedup, and achieves 1.48x acceleration on a real-robot platform, across four embodied manipulation policies and three simulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors training-free visual-token pruning (rather than architecture/retraining changes) as a way to cut inference latency without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: real robot plus 3 sim benchmarks, 4 existing embodied manipulation policies, no retraining required

title: AnyWorld: Factorized Egocentric World Models for Cross-Embodiment Generalization

claims.claim: Factorizing a human interaction video into action, camera, and embodiment components allows a world model to recompose a single human video into many robot-native synthetic rollouts (varying embodiment, viewpoint, scene) without paired human-robot demonstrations, and using this generated data improves manipulation performance on the RoboCasa GR1 tabletop benchmark and a real IRON humanoid robot
claims.direction: favors generative recomposition of existing human video data (varying camera/viewpoint/embodiment) over collecting new paired demonstrations, to expand training data diversity
claims.conditions: sim benchmark (RoboCasa GR1) plus real-world IRON humanoid robot

title: BayesFP: Posterior Estimation for Flow-Based Policies via Feynman-Kac Sampling

claims.claim: Formulating constrained trajectory generation for pretrained diffusion/flow-matching policies as Bayesian posterior sampling (learned demonstration distribution as prior, inference-time cost as likelihood) via a Feynman-Kac corrector allows retraining-free, inference-time steering of flow/diffusion policies (validated on Diffusion Policy, GR00T-N1.6, pi_0.5) toward feasible/optimal trajectories, improving over the base pi_0.5 on zero-shot tasks
claims.direction: favors retraining-free, inference-time posterior-sampling correction of diffusion/flow-matching action heads to satisfy new constraints/objectives
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, applied on top of existing pretrained diffusion/flow policies without retraining

title: MoDem-V2: Visuo-Motor World Models for Real-World Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A model-based RL system (MoDem-V2) is, to the authors' knowledge, the first successful demonstration-augmented visual world-model RL system trained directly in the uninstrumented real world, identifying exploration centering, agency handover, and actor-critic ensembles as key ingredients for safely leveraging demonstrations during model learning on four contact-rich visuo-motor manipulation problems
claims.direction: favors combining a learned world model with demonstration-bootstrapping and specific safety-oriented exploration mechanisms for real-world (not just sim) contact-rich manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world (and simulation), contact-rich dexterous manipulation, demo-bootstrapped model-based RL

title: Synergistic Pushing and Grasping for Enhanced Robotic Manipulation Using Deep Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A model that jointly predicts pushing and grasping actions (via two fully convolutional Q-networks) from heightmap images achieves 87% grasp success in cluttered environments versus 60% for a grasp-only policy, with completion rates up to 100% and grasp success up to 95.8%, generalizing to unseen objects and configurations
claims.direction: favors combining a non-prehensile action (pushing) with grasping to improve robustness/generalization to novel objects/clutter, versus grasp-only policies
claims.conditions: simulation, cluttered bin/tabletop scenes, novel objects and configurations tested

title: Learning Generalizable 3D Manipulation With 10 Demonstrations

claims.claim: A framework learns 3D manipulation policies from only 10 demonstrations while achieving robust generalization to unseen spatial configurations, via a Semantic-Guided Perception module (extracting task-aware 3D representations from RGB-D using semantic priors) and a Spatial-Generalized Decision module (a diffusion-based policy preserving spatial equivariance)
claims.direction: favors semantic-prior-guided 3D (RGB-D) representations plus spatially-equivariant diffusion policies over generic end-to-end policies, for extreme few-demo generalization
claims.conditions: both simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic systems, only 10 demonstrations

claims.claim: A spatially equivariant training strategy adapts 2D data augmentation principles to 3D by maintaining gripper-object spatial relationships during trajectory augmentation, contributing to significant success-rate improvement over SOTA, particularly under significant object pose variation
claims.direction: favors spatially-equivariant (relationship-preserving) trajectory augmentation over generic random augmentation, for object-pose generalization
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated, tested specifically under object pose variation

title: Bridging Simulation and Reality: Cross-Domain Transfer with Semantic 2D Gaussian Splatting

claims.claim: Extracting object-centric, domain-invariant spatial features via Semantic 2D Gaussian Splatting (multi-view 2D semantic fields projected into a unified 3D space, with background filtered out) as policy input, rather than raw pixels, significantly improves sim-to-real transferability and maintains high, stable task performance in real-world deployment, when used with a Diffusion Policy trained in the ManiSkill simulator
claims.direction: favors domain-invariant, background-filtered, object-centric 3D-projected visual features over raw pixel input to close the sim-to-real domain gap
claims.conditions: trained in ManiSkill simulation, evaluated with real-world deployment, Diffusion Policy backbone

title: CometVLA: Co-Training on an Embodied Data Pyramid towards Physical Understanding

claims.claim: Introducing Global Action Prior (GAP) tokens, a compact learnable bottleneck isolating task-agnostic motion regularities so the action head can consume physical-commonsense knowledge from a co-trained VLM without corrupting the pretrained VLM backbone, allows co-training across an embodied data pyramid (teleoperation, simulation, egocentric video, VQA); CometVLA consistently outperforms strong VLA baselines on real-world manipulation and RoboTwin simulation, and stronger VLM physical-understanding performance correlates with higher VLA success rates
claims.direction: favors explicitly co-training on physically-grounded auxiliary QA/video data (with a dedicated bottleneck token) alongside action data, over action-only training
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation plus RoboTwin simulation, multi-source co-training (teleop + sim + egocentric + VQA)

title: EmbodimentSemantic: A Spatial Scene-Graph Dataset and Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Embodied Manipulation Trajectories

claims.claim: Using real-world manipulation observations collected with the low-cost SO101 robot arm (paired third-person/scene and wrist camera views) plus a simulator-grounded LIBERO benchmark (60K+ frames, 120K+ scene graphs), the authors find that current VLMs often predict plausible spatial relations but struggle with exact depth-aware and viewpoint-dependent spatial structure
claims.direction: identifies depth-aware and viewpoint-dependent spatial grounding as a specific current weakness of VLM/VLA perception, tested with paired scene+wrist camera views
claims.conditions: real-world data collected on an SO101 arm (same platform as our setup) plus paired sim (LIBERO) benchmark with third-person and wrist views

title: ExToken: Structured Exploration for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Fine-tuning

claims.claim: Trajectory diversity is fundamentally more important to sample efficiency than the sheer quantity of collected rollouts in VLA-RL fine-tuning; conditioning policies on discrete behavioral-prior tokens derived from offline demonstrations to encourage diverse exploration substantially improves state-action coverage, convergence, and task performance under constrained interaction budgets, on both simulated and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors prioritizing behavioral/trajectory diversity over raw rollout/demo quantity, echoing similar findings on the demo-diversity-vs-quantity question
claims.conditions: VLA reinforcement fine-tuning, simulated and real-world manipulation, constrained interaction budgets

title: Squint: Fast Visual Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Robotics

claims.claim: Squint, a visual Soft Actor-Critic method using parallel simulation, a distributional critic, resolution 'squinting', layer normalization, a tuned update-to-data ratio, and an optimized implementation, trains visual RL policies in 15 minutes on a single RTX 3090 GPU (most tasks converging in under 6 minutes) and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer to a real SO-101 robot, evaluated on the new SO-101 Task Set (eight manipulation tasks in ManiSkill3 with heavy domain randomization)
claims.direction: demonstrates that fast, modest-compute (single consumer GPU, minutes not hours) visual RL training with heavy domain randomization can transfer sim-to-real on the exact SO-101 platform
claims.conditions: real SO-101 robot (our exact platform), single consumer GPU (RTX 3090), sim-to-real via heavy domain randomization, RL not imitation learning

why_deep_read: Directly uses our target SO-101 platform with a fast, single-consumer-GPU training recipe and demonstrated sim-to-real transfer — extremely relevant to our compute-constrained (8GB laptop) setup even though it is RL rather than imitation learning; worth checking if any lessons (domain randomization recipe, resolution/compute tricks) transfer to our BC/teleop-demo setting

title: TAM: Torque Adaptation Module for Robust Motion Transfer in Manipulation

claims.claim: A learned Torque Adaptation Module that adapts torque commands using only a proprioceptive-history encoder (not policy observations or action space) can be reused zero-shot across policies with different action spaces (joint targets, end-effector targets, or direct torques) to correct for sim-to-real dynamics/payload/robot-instance mismatch, improving zero-shot real-robot execution over system identification and RMA baselines on a real Franka Panda, without requiring the base policy to be trained with domain randomization
claims.direction: favors decoupling a robot/dynamics-specific torque-correction module (trained entirely in simulation) from the action-space choice of the base policy, so any action-space policy can be made more robust to actuator/dynamics discrepancies without retraining
claims.conditions: real Franka Panda robot, zero-shot evaluation, module trained via multi-robot simulation pretraining plus robot-specific fine-tuning (no real-robot data needed for the module itself)

title: Compositional Motion Generation From Demonstration With Object-Centric Neural Fields

claims.claim: A generative LfD framework combining object-centric neural-field scene representations with a temporal mixture-of-experts of object-conditioned movement primitives requires significantly less training data than other image-based baselines to complete long-horizon manipulation tasks in simulation, while real-world experiments show robustness to noise and category-level generalization via language-based segmentation
claims.direction: favors compositional, object-centric movement-primitive representations over generic image-based end-to-end policies for data efficiency and category-level generalization
claims.conditions: simulation (long-horizon tasks) plus real-world robustness/generalization tests

title: Learning modular language-conditioned robot policies through attention

claims.claim: A Hierarchical Modularity approach using Supervised Attention to bridge modular and end-to-end learning enables more efficient training of language-conditioned policies and their transfer across different robot types/dynamics, validated through simulated and real-world manipulation experiments
claims.direction: favors modular, attention-bridged language-conditioned architectures over monolithic end-to-end language-conditioned policies for cross-robot transfer efficiency
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world robot manipulation, multiple robot embodiments

title: Local Policies Enable Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: ManipGen's 'local policies' (invariant to absolute robot/object pose, skill ordering, and global scene configuration), combined with vision/language/motion-planning foundation models, achieve 97% zero-shot success on Robosuite sim benchmark tasks, and after sim-to-real transfer solve unseen long-horizon manipulation tasks with up to 8 stages under significant pose/object/scene variation, outperforming SayCan, OpenVLA, LLMTrajGen, and VoxPoser by 36%, 76%, 62%, and 60% respectively across 50 real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors locality/pose-invariance as an explicit architectural property for generalizing to novel scene configurations, over globally-conditioned end-to-end policies (including VLA baselines like OpenVLA)
claims.conditions: real-world, 50 manipulation tasks, sim-to-real transfer, long-horizon (up to 8 stages), significant scene/object/pose variation

title: RoboEngine: Plug-and-Play Robot Data Augmentation with Semantic Robot Segmentation and Background Generation

claims.claim: RoboEngine, a plug-and-play toolkit combining a generalizable robot-segmentation model and a fine-tuned background-generation model, requires no camera calibration or green-screen setup and generates physics/task-aware augmented scenes from ordinary demonstrations; using it, a policy trained from demonstrations collected in a single scene generalizes to six entirely new scenes with more than 200% performance improvement over a no-augmentation baseline
claims.direction: strongly favors plug-and-play generative background/scene augmentation (no green screen or calibration needed) over collecting new demonstrations for cross-scene generalization
claims.conditions: real-world imitation learning, demonstrations from a single scene, evaluated across six new scenes

why_deep_read: A large (>200%), directly quantified real-world generalization gain from an easy-to-use augmentation toolkit requiring no green screen/calibration — this closely matches our exact problem (policy breaks under new lighting/background with only demos from one scene) and our simple hardware setup; full text would clarify compute cost and compatibility with a small custom pipeline

title: SAGA: Open-World Mobile Manipulation via Structured Affordance Grounding

claims.claim: Grounding a unified affordance-based task representation into 3D affordance heatmaps via multimodal foundation models, highlighting task-relevant entities while abstracting away spurious appearance variation, enables a conditional policy trained on multi-task demonstrations to consistently outperform end-to-end and modular baselines by substantial margins across eleven real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors 3D affordance-heatmap task representations (abstracting appearance) over direct end-to-end visuomotor mapping for generalization across environments and task specifications
claims.conditions: real-world, quadrupedal mobile manipulator, eleven tasks, multiple task-specification forms (language, points, demonstrations)

title: RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction

claims.claim: A lightweight multimodal model trained on a large-scale failure-centric dataset (9,440 erroneous trajectories, 78,623 QA pairs) achieves 34.1% higher failure-analysis accuracy than GPT-4o, and when integrated as an external supervisor in a real-world VLA control pipeline yields a 29.1% relative improvement across four tasks while reducing latency relative to GPT-4o
claims.direction: favors a dedicated lightweight failure-analysis/correction model (trained on failure data) as an external supervisor over relying on large general-purpose VLMs, for both accuracy and latency
claims.conditions: real-world VLA control pipeline, four tasks, lightweight model enabling local deployment

title: SIMPACT: Simulation-Enabled Action Planning using Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Equipping a VLM with test-time physical reasoning via simulation-in-the-loop world modeling (constructed from a single RGB-D observation, no additional training) achieves state-of-the-art performance on five challenging real-world rigid-body and deformable manipulation tasks requiring fine-grained physical reasoning, outperforming existing general-purpose robotic manipulation models
claims.direction: favors test-time simulation-based physical reasoning (a world-model auxiliary) over purely learned/general-purpose policies for fine-grained physical/contact reasoning
claims.conditions: real-world, five tasks, single RGB-D observation, no additional training required

title: SEM: Enhancing Spatial Understanding for Robust Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A diffusion-based policy that augments visual representations with explicit 3D geometric context (a 'spatial enhancer') and adds a graph-based robot-state encoder capturing embodiment-aware joint dependencies significantly improves spatial understanding, leading to more robust and generalizable manipulation than existing 3D-point-cloud-only or 2D-image-only baselines across diverse tasks
claims.direction: favors combining 2D image features with explicit added 3D geometric context (rather than pure point-cloud or pure 2D encoders) plus embodiment-aware state encoding
claims.conditions: diffusion-policy framework, diverse manipulation tasks (sim/real not fully specified in abstract)

title: HapticVLA: Contact-Rich Manipulation via Vision-Language-Action Model without Inference-Time Tactile Sensing

claims.claim: Distilling a tactile-aware auxiliary signal (learned offline via safety-aware reward-weighted flow matching) into a compact token that a student VLA learns to predict from vision and state alone allows tactile-aware action generation at inference without any onboard tactile sensor, achieving 86.7% mean real-world success and consistently outperforming baseline VLAs, including ones given direct tactile feedback at inference
claims.direction: favors distilling auxiliary sensory-derived knowledge into the main policy at training time (removing the sensor at deployment) rather than requiring the extra sensor modality at inference
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation, offline distillation, no tactile hardware needed at deployment

title: Where to Touch, How to Contact: A Hierarchical RL-MPC Framework for Geometry-Aware Sim-to-Real Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing contact-rich manipulation hierarchically (high-level RL policy predicts an object-centric 'contact intention'; low-level contact-implicit MPC handles local contact dynamics) achieves high success rates with substantially reduced data (40x fewer RL decision steps and 2x fewer control steps than an end-to-end comparison) and robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: favors hierarchical decomposition (high-level geometric decision + low-level contact control) over end-to-end policies for data efficiency in contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: non-prehensile manipulation tasks (pushing, pivoting/flipping, repositioning), sim-to-real, zero-shot transfer

title: AGM: Achievement-Grounded Memory for Closed-Loop Agents with Frozen VLA Policies

claims.claim: A lightweight (2.43M-parameter) verification head that advances a subgoal-sequence memory only after physical evidence (proprioceptive cues plus coherent point tracking and cross-view language comparison) confirms progress, rather than assuming attempted actions are completed, surpasses the strongest memory-augmented baseline on the RoboMME Counting benchmark and yields decisive gains on a physical robot, while keeping the base VLA policy frozen
claims.direction: favors verified, evidence-gated progress memory over naive external memory that assumes attempted actions succeeded, for frozen open-loop-chunked VLA policies
claims.conditions: benchmark (RoboMME) plus physical robot, frozen VLA policy, lightweight added verification head

title: Improving Cross-embodiment Transfer in Latent Action Models with Action-Similarity Supervision

claims.claim: In a controlled cross-embodiment study on RoboTwin 2.0, predicting latent actions (rather than ground-truth robot actions) more than doubles cross-embodiment success; training latent-action similarity to match ground-truth end-effector-motion similarity (rather than an auxiliary loss predicting ground-truth actions) transfers better across two bimanual robots with disjoint task sets
claims.direction: favors learning a latent (not raw/ground-truth) action representation supervised via end-effector-motion similarity, over predicting raw joint-space actions, for cross-embodiment generalization
claims.conditions: sim benchmark (RoboTwin 2.0), controlled ablation, two bimanual robot embodiments with disjoint tasks

title: Grounding Language with Visual Affordances over Unstructured Data

claims.claim: A self-supervised visuo-lingual affordance model learns general-purpose language-conditioned robot skills from unstructured, offline, reset-free real-world data, requiring language annotation on as little as 1% of the total data, achieving SOTA on the CALVIN benchmark and learning over 25 distinct visuomotor manipulation tasks with a single real-world policy while requiring an order of magnitude less data than previous approaches
claims.direction: favors self-supervised affordance-based language grounding from mostly-unannotated, unstructured (reset-free) real-world data over fully-annotated, curated demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world, 25+ tasks with a single policy, CALVIN benchmark, 1% of data language-annotated

claims.claim: Paired with LLMs to decompose abstract natural-language instructions into subgoals via few-shot prompting, the affordance-grounded policy completes long-horizon, multi-tier tasks in the real world
claims.direction: favors combining a learned visual-language affordance model with LLM-based subgoal decomposition for long-horizon language-conditioned tasks
claims.conditions: real-world, long-horizon multi-tier task execution

why_deep_read: Strong, highly data-efficient real-world result (order-of-magnitude less data, only 1% language-annotated, 25+ tasks with one policy) directly relevant to our planned future step of adding a second object with language conditioning under a similarly small demo budget (Q08/Q13); full text would give the affordance-model architecture and annotation recipe

title: UMI on Legs: Making Manipulation Policies Mobile with Manipulation-Centric Whole-body Controllers

claims.claim: Scaling task-centric manipulation data collection in the real world using a cheap hand-held gripper (UMI, no robot needed) and combining it with a separately-trained simulated whole-body controller (interfaced via end-effector trajectories in the task frame) achieves over 70% success rate across prehensile, non-prehensile, and dynamic manipulation tasks, and enables zero-shot cross-embodiment deployment of a manipulation policy checkpoint originally trained for a fixed-base arm
claims.direction: favors decoupling cheap hand-held-gripper demonstration collection (no robot required) from a separately simulation-trained embodiment controller, interfaced via end-effector trajectories, for scalable and cross-embodiment-transferable data collection
claims.conditions: real-world, quadruped mobile manipulation, end-effector-trajectory interface between manipulation policy and whole-body controller

title: SurgiPose: Estimating Surgical Tool Kinematics from Monocular Video for Surgical Robot Learning

claims.claim: Imitation learning policies trained on kinematics estimated from monocular video (via differentiable-rendering pose estimation, no ground-truth kinematics needed) achieve comparable success rates to policies trained on ground-truth measured kinematics, on two real robotic surgical tasks
claims.direction: favors video-derived (estimated) action/kinematic labels as a viable substitute for costly ground-truth kinematic instrumentation when collecting demonstration data
claims.conditions: real robot (da Vinci Research Kit Si), two surgical manipulation tasks, comparison of estimated vs ground-truth kinematic labels

title: Mechanistic interpretability for steering vision-language-action models

claims.claim: Projecting feedforward transformer activations onto the token embedding basis identifies sparse semantic directions (e.g., speed, direction) causally linked to action selection in Pi0 and OpenVLA; a general-purpose activation-steering method built on these directions modulates policy behavior in real time, without fine-tuning, reward signals, or environment interaction, demonstrated zero-shot in simulation (LIBERO) and on a physical UR5 robot
claims.direction: favors direct inference-time activation steering (e.g., of speed/direction) as a training-free way to adjust policy behavior/motion characteristics
claims.conditions: real UR5 robot plus LIBERO sim, existing pretrained VLAs (Pi0, OpenVLA), no fine-tuning or retraining

title: Duet: Dual-Robot Understanding via Efficient Teaching

claims.claim: Pretraining an Action Chunking Transformer-based collaborative policy on human-human demonstrations (collected via a synchronized VR teleoperation and tracking pipeline), then finetuning on a minimal set of real-robot teleoperation trajectories, yields superior task performance versus baselines trained only on robot data, while reducing total human data-collection effort (5.4x acceleration from teleoperation)
claims.direction: favors pretraining on cheaper human-human demonstration data before finetuning on a small real-robot demonstration set, over collecting robot-only demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world, dual-robot collaborative mobile manipulation, ACT-based policy architecture

title: Keyframe-Guided Structured Rewards for Reinforcement Learning in Long-Horizon Laboratory Robotics

claims.claim: A framework that extracts kinematics-aware keyframes from demonstrations and constructs a geometric progress-based reward (via a diffusion-based stage-wise target predictor) to guide online RL fine-tuning on a VLA backbone achieves 82% average success across four real-world laboratory tasks after 40-60 minutes of fine-tuning, versus 42% (HG-DAgger) and 47% (Hil-ConRFT)
claims.direction: favors keyframe/progress-based structured auxiliary reward signals over standard sparse-reward or pure-DAgger approaches for long-horizon precision tasks
claims.conditions: real-world laboratory automation tasks, VLA backbone, online RL fine-tuning

title: Ada3Drift: Adaptive Training-Time Drifting for One-Step 3D Visuomotor Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Ada3Drift, a point-cloud-conditioned policy using a regression-to-drifting training curriculum (paired action regression, then progressively-introduced distribution-drifting regularization), generates action chunks in a single forward pass (1 NFE) and achieves the highest reported average success rates among evaluated baselines on Adroit, Meta-World, RoboTwin, and five real-world tasks, compared with 10 NFE required by diffusion baselines
claims.direction: favors one-step (drifting-model-based) generative action heads over multi-step diffusion for retaining action-distribution quality while cutting inference steps
claims.conditions: real-world (5 tasks) plus sim benchmarks (Adroit, Meta-World, RoboTwin), point-cloud input, controlled ablations at matched demonstration budgets

title: GeoLAM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Latent Actions from Unlabeled Human Videos

claims.claim: GeoLAM learns geometry-grounded continuous latent actions from action-free human videos (using a frozen geometric feature hierarchy for future-frame reconstruction plus motion supervision from a training-only 4D geometry teacher, without hand-pose/trajectory annotations), then uses these as transition targets for a world-action model trained on action-labeled robot demonstrations; the geometry teacher and future-video generation are not required at deployment, keeping inference efficient
claims.direction: favors geometry-grounded (not purely appearance-based) latent action pretraining from unlabeled human video, with auxiliary supervision discarded at deployment for efficiency
claims.conditions: video pretraining without action labels, then robot-demonstration finetuning; evaluated on a latent-action benchmark and robotic manipulation tasks

title: Grasping Unstructured Objects with Full Convolutional Network in Clutter

claims.claim: Combining depth information with a DQN-based fully-convolutional grasping framework significantly improves grasping performance on novel, previously-unseen objects in cluttered scenes compared to conventional grasping techniques, demonstrating adaptability and robustness
claims.direction: favors depth-informed RL-based grasping for generalization to novel objects in clutter, over conventional (non-learned or RGB-only) techniques
claims.conditions: real-world (implied), cluttered scenes, novel/unstructured objects

title: GR-MG: Leveraging Partially-Annotated Data via Multi-Modal Goal-Conditioned Policy

claims.claim: GR-MG conditions on both a text instruction and a goal image (generated via diffusion-based image editing at inference when only text is given), allowing it to leverage partially-annotated data (action-unlabeled human videos, text-unlabeled robot trajectories) rather than requiring fully text-and-action-annotated trajectories; in real-robot experiments across 58 different tasks it improves success rate from 68.7% to 78.1% (simple settings) and from 44.4% to 60.6% (generalization settings) versus baselines, and outperforms comparison methods in few-shot learning of novel skills
claims.direction: favors goal-image-plus-language conditioning that can exploit partially-annotated (mixed video/robot) data over requiring fully action-and-text-labeled demonstrations for every trajectory
claims.conditions: real-world, 58 tasks, simulation experiments also reported, few-shot novel-skill learning tested

title: Gen2Sim: Scaling up Robot Learning in Simulation with Generative Models

claims.claim: Automating generation of 3D assets (lifting 2D object-centric images to 3D via diffusion models), task descriptions, task decompositions, and reward functions using pretrained language/vision generative models allows Gen2Sim to learn policies for diverse long-horizon tasks where RL with non-temporally-decomposed rewards fails
claims.direction: favors using generative models to automatically scale up synthetic simulated training assets/tasks/rewards rather than hand-authoring simulation content
claims.conditions: simulation only, RL-based skill learning, human involvement removed from asset/task/reward creation

title: OMP: One-step Meanflow Policy with Directional Alignment

claims.claim: A one-step MeanFlow policy (OMP), with a lightweight directional-alignment mechanism to correct spectral bias/gradient starvation in low-velocity regimes and a Differential Derivation Equation to approximate the JVP operator (reducing memory complexity), outperforms SOTA diffusion and flow-based methods in success rate and trajectory accuracy on Adroit and Meta-World, particularly in high-precision tasks, while retaining single-step-generation inference efficiency
claims.direction: favors single-step flow-matching (MeanFlow-based) action heads over multi-step diffusion or standard flow-matching policies, for high-precision manipulation with lower inference cost
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks (Adroit, Meta-World); real-world not explicitly stated

title: MoLe-VLA: Dynamic Layer-skipping Vision Language Action Model via Mixture-of-Layers for Efficient Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: MoLe-VLA dynamically activates only parts of the LLM backbone's layers per robot state (via a Spatial-Temporal Aware Router treating each layer as an expert) and uses Cognitive self-Knowledge Distillation to compensate for lost capability, improving mean success rate by 9.7% across ten RLBench simulation tasks while accelerating inference by 36.8% over OpenVLA, with real-world experiments also reported
claims.direction: favors dynamic, state-conditioned layer-skipping (rather than static early-exit or the full dense backbone) to jointly reduce inference latency and improve task performance
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation plus real-world environments, compared directly against OpenVLA

title: A Flexible Field-Based Policy Learning Framework for Diverse Robotic Systems and Sensors

claims.claim: A cross-robot visuomotor framework combining diffusion-policy control with 3D semantic scene representations (D3Fields), supporting diverse robot-camera configurations (UR5+Kinect array, bimanual+Intel RealSense) through a low-latency control stack, achieves an 80% success rate on a grasp-and-lift block task after only 100 demonstration episodes, with robust skill transfer between platforms and sensing modalities
claims.direction: favors 3D semantic-field scene representations (sensor/platform-agnostic) combined with a diffusion policy, validated at a demonstration count (100) matching a typical small real-world budget
claims.conditions: real-world, multiple robot-camera configurations including Intel RealSense sensors, only 100 demonstrations

title: Beyond the Majority: Long-tail Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Conventional long-tail learning strategies (e.g., re-sampling) fail to improve policy performance on data-scarce tail tasks; the authors find that data scarcity on tail tasks directly impairs the policy's spatial reasoning capability, and introduce Approaching-Phase Augmentation (APA), which transfers knowledge from data-rich head tasks to data-scarce tail tasks without requiring any external/new demonstrations, validated in both simulation and real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors targeted knowledge-transfer augmentation from data-rich to data-scarce tasks over collecting more demonstrations or naive re-sampling, when adding new tasks/objects with few demos
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation, multi-task policies with head/tail task imbalance

title: Learning to Accelerate Vision-Language-Action Models through Adaptive Visual Token Caching

claims.claim: A learned, task-aware token-caching policy (a Cached Token Selector plus a Cache Ratio Predictor, trained end-to-end via differentiable relaxation) achieves a 1.76x wall-clock inference speedup while simultaneously improving average success rate by 1.9 percentage points on LIBERO (75.0% to 76.9%) and by 5.0 percentage points on real-world tasks, outperforming static/heuristic caching or pruning baselines
claims.direction: favors learned, dynamic, task-aware visual-token caching (over static/heuristic caching or pruning) for reducing VLA inference latency without sacrificing (and even improving) accuracy
claims.conditions: LIBERO and SIMPLER sim benchmarks plus real-robot evaluations

title: RoboEvolve: Co-Evolving Planner-Simulator for Robotic Manipulation with Limited Data

claims.claim: A co-evolutionary VLM-planner/VGM-simulator loop operating purely on unlabeled seed images elevates base planners by 30 absolute points and amplifies simulator success by 48% on average, surpasses fully supervised baselines using merely 500 unlabeled seeds (a 50x reduction in labeled data), and demonstrates robust continual learning without catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: favors a self-improving planner-simulator co-evolution loop over collecting more labeled/supervised demonstration data, for extreme data efficiency
claims.conditions: unlabeled seed images (500), autonomous progressive curriculum, evaluated for data efficiency and continual learning (sim/generation-based, not clearly real-robot in abstract)

title: From Imagined Futures to Executable Actions: Mixture of Latent Actions for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Rather than conditioning the policy directly on video-model-predicted future frames (which emphasize perceptual realism over control relevance), a mixture of pretrained inverse-dynamics models (capturing semantic, depth, and flow cues) infers a structured, physically-grounded mixture of latent actions from generated visual transitions, yielding consistent gains in task success, temporal consistency, and generalization on LIBERO, CALVIN, LIBERO-Plus, and real-world robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors an inverse-dynamics-based control-oriented interface between video/world-model imagination and the action policy, rather than directly decoding predicted frames or video into actions
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, CALVIN, LIBERO-Plus) plus real-world manipulation tasks

title: MaskWAM: Unifying Mask Prompting and Prediction for World-Action Models

claims.claim: An object-centric world-action model that jointly integrates segmentation masks as both explicit inputs and prediction targets (via a unified Mixture of Transformers) suppresses task-irrelevant visual noise and, combined with first-frame mask prompts as a spatial anchor, significantly outperforms baselines on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world tasks in both language-clear and language-ambiguous conditions
claims.direction: favors predicting object-centric masks (rather than unstructured RGB) as the world-model auxiliary target, and using mask-based visual prompts to reduce language/referential ambiguity in cluttered scenes
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, RoboTwin) plus real-world tasks

title: Teach and Grow: An Agent-Centered Architecture for General Robot Learning

claims.claim: A training-free architecture (TGL) that turns a few successful demonstrations into reusable, verified Skill Blocks (using a large multimodal LLM agent, no gradient updates/fine-tuning/RL) reaches 99.9% mean success on four LIBERO suites and 92.4% on seven LIBERO-Plus perturbation categories, with taught skills persisting and improving related-task execution under the same frozen model weights
claims.direction: favors training-free, large-agent-driven skill acquisition from a handful of demonstrations over gradient-based fine-tuning, though this relies on a large general-purpose multimodal LLM/agent rather than a small local model
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus), large frozen foundation model (GPT-scale) as the reasoning agent

title: DIA: Denoising Intermediate Advantage for Diffusion Policy Optimization

claims.claim: Assigning distinct, learned state-dependent credit to each denoising step of a diffusion action chunk (rather than uniform environment-level credit across all steps) during RL fine-tuning of a BC-pretrained diffusion policy consistently improves final performance over existing diffusion-policy fine-tuning methods across Robomimic, FurnitureBench, Franka Kitchen, and D3IL
claims.direction: favors step-wise (denoising-level) credit assignment over uniform credit when using RL to fine-tune a diffusion action head pretrained via behavior cloning
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks (Robomimic, FurnitureBench, Franka Kitchen, D3IL)

title: Beyond Teleoperation: Enhancing VLA Robustness via Explicit Kinematic Retargeting of Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A lightweight pipeline that kinematically retargets human interaction data (DexYCB) onto 6-DoF manipulator trajectories via constrained inverse kinematics (with an object-based grasping heuristic, no heavy visual synthesis) to fine-tune a pi0.5-based policy significantly outperforms standard teleoperation-only training (40.6% success), reaching 65.6% via co-training and a peak 78.1% via two-stage cross-embodiment co-training
claims.direction: favors supplementing/replacing costly teleoperated data with kinematically-retargeted human demonstration data, via co-training with a pretrained VLA
claims.conditions: real-world, 6-DoF manipulator, pi0.5 architecture, physical evaluations

claims.claim: Under extreme visual clutter, policies fine-tuned with explicitly retargeted human data exhibit immunity to semantic visual distractors, whereas the abstract also identifies a 'Terminal State Ambiguity' failure mode where generative policies fail to terminate tasks when exposed to scenarios resembling human-video priors
claims.direction: favors kinematic retargeting (which strips away human-video visual appearance) for robustness to visual distractors, but flags a task-termination failure mode as a side effect
claims.conditions: real-world, extreme visual clutter conditions tested

title: DexCap: Scalable and Portable Mocap Data Collection System for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A portable hand motion-capture system (DexCap, SLAM plus electromagnetic field tracking with 3D environment observations) combined with an inverse-kinematics and point-cloud-based imitation algorithm (DexIL), optionally with human-in-the-loop rollout correction, demonstrates superior performance across six challenging dexterous manipulation tasks and can learn effectively from in-the-wild mocap data (not requiring a physical robot present during collection)
claims.direction: favors portable human-mocap-based demonstration collection (with point-cloud-based imitation) over standard robot teleoperation for scalability
claims.conditions: real robot, six dexterous manipulation tasks, in-the-wild mocap data collection

title: Offline Imitation Learning Through Graph Search and Retrieval

claims.claim: GSR, which organizes suboptimal/unstructured interaction experience into a graph via pretrained representations, performs graph search to value different behaviors, then retrieves and behavior-clones the best action per state, achieves a 10-30% higher success rate and over 30% higher proficiency than baselines on real-world and simulated manipulation tasks with complex visual inputs and suboptimal demonstrations
claims.direction: favors graph-search/retrieval-based extraction of the best behavior from suboptimal/unstructured demonstrations over standard offline RL or naive behavior cloning on all data
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated manipulation, suboptimal/unstructured demonstrations, precise and dexterous skills

title: Touch begins where vision ends: Generalizable policies for contact-rich manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing fine-grained manipulation into a VLM-based scene-level reaching phase and a reusable, scene-agnostic local interaction policy (trained once in a canonical setting) that generalizes via a 'localize-then-execute' strategy achieves around 90% success on contact-rich tasks in unseen environments and is robust to distractors
claims.direction: favors factoring policies into a scene-agnostic local skill plus a separate high-level localization step, so that only localization (not the low-level skill) needs to generalize across scenes/backgrounds/distractors
claims.conditions: real-world, contact-rich tasks, unseen environments, egocentric vision plus tactile sensing for the local policy

title: Using Temperature Sampling to Effectively Train Robot Learning Policies on Imbalanced Datasets

claims.claim: A simple temperature-sampling strategy addressing physical-action imbalance across nominally distinct tasks (e.g., 'pick up an apple' vs 'pick up an orange' share very similar action sequences) substantially improves generalization on low-resource tasks without degrading high-resource task performance, validated both in pre-training small models and fine-tuning large foundation models, including real-world experiments on a Franka Panda across diverse tasks
claims.direction: favors resampling training data by underlying physical-action similarity/frequency (not just by task label) to prevent low-resource tasks from being starved during multi-task training
claims.conditions: real-world Franka Panda robot, diverse tasks, both small-model pretraining and large-model fine-tuning settings

title: Enabling Practical Dexterous Grasping: A Low-Cost VR Teleoperation System with Diffusion Policy and Factor Analysis

claims.claim: Systematic real-world experiments on a low-cost VR-teleoperated diffusion-policy system analyze the influence of key factors on policy performance, including the amount of demonstrations, action sequence (chunk) length, demonstration generalization level, and action space representation, providing actionable insights for reliable low-cost imitation learning systems
claims.direction: provides a controlled real-world study of exactly the factors in our Q02/Q06/Q13 decisions (demo count, chunk length, action space) rather than a single fixed recipe
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost platform (Kinova Gen2 + open-source LEAP Hand), VR teleoperation, diffusion policy, limited number of demonstrations

title: UAD: Unsupervised Affordance Distillation for Generalization in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: UAD distills affordance knowledge from foundation models (large vision models plus VLMs) into a lightweight task-conditioned decoder atop frozen features, without any manual annotation, and trained only on rendered simulation objects; using UAD's affordance as the policy's observation space, an imitation learning policy trained on as few as 10 demonstrations generalizes to unseen object instances, unseen object categories, and variations in task instruction
claims.direction: favors a distilled, foundation-model-derived affordance representation as the observation space (instead of raw pixels) to obtain strong generalization from an extremely small number of demonstrations
claims.conditions: trained only on rendered sim objects (no manual annotation), evaluated on in-the-wild robotic scenes and real human activities, only 10 demonstrations for the downstream imitation policy

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our low-data regime: only 10 demonstrations plus a foundation-model-distilled affordance observation space generalizes to unseen objects/categories/instructions — worth checking whether the affordance decoder is lightweight enough to run alongside a policy on an 8GB laptop GPU

title: EgoMI: Learning Active Vision and Whole-Body Manipulation from Egocentric Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Because humans actively coordinate head and hand movement with pre-action visual fixation search, causing dynamic task-driven viewpoint changes that static robot cameras cannot replicate, a memory-augmented policy that selectively incorporates historical observations to handle rapid, wide-spanning head-viewpoint changes consistently outperforms baseline methods without explicit head/viewpoint-motion modeling, on a bimanual robot with an actuated camera head
claims.direction: favors explicit modeling of viewpoint/camera history (memory of past observations) over single-frame observation when camera viewpoint moves during a task
claims.conditions: real-world, bimanual robot with actuated camera head, egocentric human demonstration data retargeted to the robot

title: ReMAP-DP: Reprojected Multi-view Aligned PointMaps for Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: A dual-stream diffusion policy that fuses standardized-perspective-reprojected views with pixel-aligned PointMaps (frozen semantic features plus explicit geometric descriptors via learnable modality embeddings) attains 59.3% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 (+6.6% over the DP3 3D-diffusion-policy baseline) and a 28% improvement over DP3 on ManiSkill3's geometrically challenging Stack Cube task, with real-world robustness and superior data efficiency from only a handful of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors fusing explicit reprojected geometric (pointmap) features with frozen 2D semantic features over pure point-cloud (DP3-style) 3D representations, for both accuracy and data efficiency
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0, ManiSkill3) plus real-world, only a handful of demonstrations for real-world tasks

title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a large pretrained video model (Cosmos-Predict2) in a single post-training stage, with actions generated as latent frames within the model's own video-latent diffusion process (no new architectural components), achieves SOTA on LIBERO (98.5%) and RoboCasa (67.1%) and the highest average score on real-world bimanual manipulation, outperforming diffusion policies trained from scratch, other video-model-based policies, and SOTA VLA models fine-tuned on the same robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors reusing a large pretrained video model's own generative/diffusion process directly for action generation (rather than bolting on a separate action head) over training diffusion policies from scratch
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation plus LIBERO/RoboCasa sim, requires post-training a large pretrained video foundation model (likely far beyond an 8GB laptop GPU budget)

title: TMRL: Diffusion Timestep-Modulated Pretraining Enables Exploration for Efficient Policy Finetuning

claims.claim: Injecting forward-diffusion noise into policy inputs during BC pretraining (Context-Smoothed Pretraining), then modulating the diffusion timestep during RL fine-tuning to control exploration (TMRL), improves RL fine-tuning sample efficiency and enables successful real-world fine-tuning on complex manipulation tasks in under one hour, working with arbitrary policy inputs (states, 3D point clouds, or image-based VLA policies)
claims.direction: favors diffusion-timestep-based exploration control to bridge narrow BC-pretrained action distributions and RL fine-tuning, over standard BC pretraining alone
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, applicable to multiple input modalities and policy types

title: In-Context VLA: Endowing Vision-Language-Action Models with Language via In-Context Post-Training and Agentic Tool Use

claims.claim: Free-form textual chain-of-thought reasoning degrades low-level VLA control both empirically and analytically: the generated reasoning is ungrounded, its latency breaks closed-loop timing, and reasoning/action tokens are optimized against conflicting objectives so the policy learns to narrate rather than to act
claims.direction: contradicts the common practice of adding explicit textual chain-of-thought reasoning to action policies -- CoT reasoning can hurt control quality and introduces latency that disrupts closed-loop timing
claims.conditions: VLA models, compared against CoT-based reasoning approaches

claims.claim: Instead of generating language, injecting perceptual evidence as structured context (in-context post-training, supervised only on actions) plus an agentic tool-use interface (querying open-vocabulary detectors, monocular depth, and a VLM for task-relevant information) achieves SOTA results in both performance and efficiency versus CoT-based approaches, across RoboCasa-GR1, SimplerEnv, and LIBERO plus 8 real-world robot manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors having the policy consume grounded language/perceptual context (not generate free-form reasoning text) for language conditioning
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks plus 8 real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: A clear contradiction of the increasingly common practice of adding chain-of-thought reasoning to action models, with both an analytical argument and real-world evidence (8 tasks) that CoT latency/ungrounded reasoning hurts control — directly relevant to our Q08/Q09/Q10 decisions about whether to add reasoning/latency-costly auxiliary computation

title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Guiding intermediate policy features to preserve control-relevant structure (geometry governing motion feasibility, affordance encoding instruction-relevant entities, goal-region grounding) via training-time constraints (geometry alignment, affordance prediction, goal-region reconstruction), instantiated across a VLA, a direct-action World-Action Model, and an inverse-dynamics WAM, improves zero-shot transfer to LIBERO-Plus by 4.6-12.6 points and on RoboCasa by 8.4-12.6 points over baselines, with especially large gains on articulated-object tasks and high-precision real-world manipulation under unseen visual/spatial perturbations
claims.direction: favors adding structured auxiliary feature-training objectives (geometry, affordance, goal-region) regardless of the underlying action-generation formulation, over relying on native action/visual-prediction objectives alone
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa) plus real-world manipulation under unseen visual/spatial perturbations, tested across three different action-model architectures

title: Imitation Learning of Robotic Arm with Hierarchical Training Based on Human Videos

claims.claim: Computing positional movements from frame-to-frame disparities in human demonstration videos, after image translation to bridge morphological differences and keypoint detection to extract a latent motion representation, enables a robotic arm policy to replicate operational skills learned purely from human videos
claims.direction: favors learning from human video (via image translation and keypoint-based latent motion) as a demonstration source for imitation learning
claims.conditions: not clearly stated whether real or simulated robot arm; qualitative validation only, no quantified success numbers given

title: Improving Generalization of Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A two-stage framework (target-localization stage for picking, region-determination stage for placing) with an instance-level semantic fusion module aligning image crops with text embeddings learns object-arrangement tasks from just a few demonstrations, fine-tunes with few demos to improve generalization, and demonstrates zero-shot ability in real-robot manipulation scenarios, without requiring large-scale VLM fine-tuning data
claims.direction: favors decomposing language-conditioned manipulation into localization + placement stages with instance-level vision-language fusion, over end-to-end VLM fine-tuning, for generalization from a small number of demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world robotic environments, few demonstrations, zero-shot real-robot generalization

title: VITA-VLA: Efficiently Teaching Vision-Language Models to Act via Action Expert Distillation

claims.claim: Distilling action knowledge from a pretrained small action model into a VLM (by aligning VLM hidden states to the small model's action space and reusing its pretrained action decoder, adding only an action token and state encoder) achieves 97.3% average success on LIBERO (+11.8%) and 93.5% on LIBERO-LONG (+24.5%) versus prior SOTA, and 82.0% real-world success (+17% over the teacher small action model) across five manipulation tasks, at substantially lower training cost than training a large VLA from scratch
claims.direction: favors reusing/distilling a pretrained small action model's decoder into a larger VLM rather than training large VLA action generation from scratch
claims.conditions: real-world (5 tasks) plus LIBERO/LIBERO-LONG sim, distillation-based two-stage training

title: MoCam-VR: An Occlusion-Resilient Low-Cost Dexterous Hand-arm Teleoperation System for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A low-cost teleoperation system using a dynamic multi-perspective camera setup (displayed in VR) to eliminate finger/hand occlusion and calibration requirements outperforms other low-cost vision-based teleoperation systems in dexterity and reliability, achieving performance comparable to high-end motion-capture solutions
claims.direction: favors dynamic multi-perspective camera-based teleoperation over fixed-camera low-cost systems for higher-quality demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world teleoperation, off-the-shelf/3D-printed low-cost hardware

title: StageACT: Stage-Conditioned Imitation for Robust Humanoid Door Opening

claims.claim: Standard behavior cloning is prone to mode collapse under partial observability (e.g., an unobservable latch state), yielding blended or out-of-sequence actions; augmenting low-level policies with task-stage inputs (StageACT) increases robustness to this ambiguity, achieving a 55% success rate on previously unseen doors on a real humanoid, more than doubling the best baseline, with shorter completion times
claims.direction: favors explicit stage/phase conditioning as a lightweight fix for behavior-cloning mode collapse/multimodality caused by hidden task state, over relying on the base action head alone
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid, office environment, previously unseen doors (generalization test)

why_deep_read: Directly addresses BC mode collapse from hidden/ambiguous task state via a simple, lightweight stage-conditioning mechanism with a large, quantified real-world generalization gain (more than doubling baseline) — worth checking if this technique is applicable to our simple pick-and-place task where sub-phases (approach/grasp/transport/place) could serve as the 'stage' signal

title: REVOLVE: An Automated Closed-Loop Framework for Evolving Robot Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention

claims.claim: An automated closed-loop framework integrating automated environment reset/correction and dual-loop continual policy/agent improvement, feeding real-world failure-correction data back into training, improves average policy success rate by 18.5% and agent judgment accuracy by 8.5% after five iterations across four real-world manipulation tasks, while reducing human effort in data collection and deployment testing by 94.4% and 95.1% respectively
claims.direction: favors automating failure correction/data collection and continual learning loops over static demonstration datasets, to reduce human labeling/supervision effort while improving performance
claims.conditions: real-world, four manipulation tasks, five improvement iterations

title: Instrumentation for Imitation Learning: Enhancing Training Datasets for Clothes Hanger Insertion

claims.claim: Diffusion policies trained with access to instrumented (sensor-in-object) state information outperform vision-only counterparts by 14-25 percentage points on a clothes-hanger-insertion task using 180 teleoperated demonstrations, and a black-box policy learns to prioritise instrumentation signals over vision without explicit guidance
claims.direction: favors adding privileged instrumented-state signals as an auxiliary training input over vision alone, when such instrumentation is available
claims.conditions: real-world, 180 teleoperated demonstrations, diffusion policies with vs without instrumentation data

claims.claim: Enhancing the teleoperation dataset with rollouts from an instrumented expert policy allows a vision-only student policy trained on this augmented data to match the instrumented expert's performance, surpassing the original vision-only policy trained only on human teleoperation demonstrations
claims.direction: favors augmenting a vision-only training dataset with rollouts from a privileged (instrumented) expert policy, rather than collecting more human teleoperation demonstrations, to improve a vision-only deployment policy
claims.conditions: real-world, distillation from an instrumented expert into a vision-only student

title: STARRY: Spatial-Temporal Action-Centric World Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: STARRY jointly denoises future spatial-temporal latents and actions through a unified diffusion process (rather than leaving predictive representation weakly coupled to action execution), using Geometry-Aware Selective Attention Modulation to convert predicted depth and end-effector geometry into token-aligned action-attention weights; on RoboTwin 2.0 it achieves 93.82%/93.30% average success (Clean/Randomized) across 50 bimanual tasks, and in real-world experiments improves average success from 42.5% to 70.8% compared with pi0.5
claims.direction: favors tightly coupling future spatial-temporal (geometry-aware) prediction with action generation in a single diffusion process, over treating future-state prediction as a separate/auxiliary head, for precise spatial-temporal coordination
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0, 50 bimanual tasks) plus real-world, compared directly against pi0.5
