title: JAMB: Joint Action-Motion Diffusion for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: JAMB jointly denoises bimanual actions and future 3D point tracks within a shared Transformer (rather than using future state only as fixed/auxiliary conditioning), grounded in a shared spatiotemporal coordinate system; across 16 RoboTwin 2.0 simulation tasks it achieves 83.4% average success, outperforming the strongest baseline by 23.9 percentage points, and on three real-world tasks outperforms action-only and auxiliary-geometry-prediction methods by 50.0 and 21.2 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors jointly denoising actions with future 3D geometric point tracks (mutual refinement) over both action-only policies and standard auxiliary future-prediction, for coordinated bimanual manipulation
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0, 16 tasks) plus 3 real-world tasks

claims.claim: JAMB shows stronger generalization to cluttered scenes and out-of-distribution backgrounds than the evaluated baselines
claims.direction: favors joint action-motion (future-geometry-aware) modeling for robustness to clutter/background shift
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated cluttered/OOD-background settings

why_deep_read: An extremely large real-world margin (+50pp over action-only) from jointly denoising actions with future point tracks, plus an explicit OOD-background/clutter generalization advantage — highly relevant to both our Q09 (auxiliary objective) and Q14 (background/clutter robustness) decisions

title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation

claims.claim: With only 50 demonstrations per task, co-training behavior-cloning policies with existing (unrelated) static ALOHA tabletop-manipulation datasets increases success rates by up to 90 percentage points, allowing a low-cost whole-body teleoperation system to autonomously complete complex mobile manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors co-training on existing unrelated robot demonstration datasets alongside a small (50-demo) task-specific dataset, rather than training on the small task dataset alone
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost teleoperation system, 50 demonstrations per new task, co-trained with a separate existing tabletop dataset

why_deep_read: Uses exactly our target demo count (50 per task) and reports a very large co-training benefit on a low-cost real system — directly actionable for our Q13 decision on how to get more out of a 50-100 demo budget by co-training with other available data (e.g., public LeRobot datasets)

title: Bridging Perception and Action: Spatially-Grounded Mid-Level Representations for Robot Generalization

claims.claim: Training specialist encoders via supervised learning on interpretable mid-level representations (object-centricity, pose-awareness, depth-awareness) and combining them via a mixture-of-experts diffusion-policy architecture achieves an average success rate 11% higher than a language-grounded baseline and 24% higher than a standard diffusion-policy baseline on real-world dexterous bimanual manipulation tasks; using these mid-level representations as auxiliary action-supervision signals within weighted imitation learning yields a further 10% improvement
claims.direction: favors combining multiple specialized mid-level visual representations (object-centric, pose, depth) via a mixture-of-experts policy, and using them as auxiliary action-alignment supervision, over a single global representation or standard diffusion policy alone
claims.conditions: real-world, dexterous bimanual manipulation tasks

title: RynnVLA-001: Using Human Demonstrations to Improve Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A two-stage pretraining approach first trains an Image-to-Video model on 12M ego-centric human manipulation videos to predict future frames (Ego-Centric Video Generative Pretraining), then extends this to jointly predict future keypoint trajectories (Human-Centric Trajectory-Aware Modeling), bridging visual frame prediction with action prediction; when finetuned on the same downstream robotics datasets, this achieves superior performance over SOTA baselines
claims.direction: favors large-scale future-frame/keypoint-trajectory video pretraining as an initialization for action policies, over training action prediction from scratch on robot data alone
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (12M ego-centric videos) then finetuning on downstream robot datasets

claims.claim: ActionVAE, a variational autoencoder that compresses sequences of actions into compact latent embeddings, reduces the complexity of the VLA output space to improve action representation
claims.direction: favors compact learned latent (VAE-compressed) action-sequence representations over predicting raw high-dimensional action sequences directly
claims.conditions: used as part of the RynnVLA-001 pretraining/finetuning pipeline

title: HACTS: a Human-As-Copilot Teleoperation System for Robot Learning

claims.claim: A low-cost, 3D-printed bilateral teleoperation system with real-time joint synchronization between robot arm and teleoperation hardware (enabling seamless human intervention and correction-data collection) significantly enhances imitation-learning recovery capabilities and data efficiency, and facilitates human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning
claims.direction: favors bilateral (force/position-synchronized) low-cost teleoperation hardware over unilateral teleoperation, for higher-quality/more data-efficient demonstration and correction-data collection
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost 3D-printed hardware, imitation learning and reinforcement learning tasks

title: Zeva: In-Context Causal Learning for Generalizable Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: Zeva encodes an executed action and its induced state change into a causal interaction signal stored in a dual-timescale causal memory, retrieving relevant signals as context for a frozen policy at deployment time (no gradient updates); it achieves the best performance among compared frontier VLAs and WAMs in simulation and real-world manipulation, with success rate continuing to improve as the robot accumulates interaction experience, generalizing across tasks
claims.direction: favors in-context causal-interaction memory (built from the robot's own deployment experience) over a frozen policy with no memory, or over gradient-based continual updates
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation, frozen base policy, memory accumulated online during deployment

title: PhysGraph: Physically-Grounded Graph-Transformer Policies for Bimanual Dexterous Hand-Tool-Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing the bimanual system as a kinematic graph with per-link tokenization and physically-grounded structural biases (kinematic distance, contact states, geometric proximity, anatomical properties) injected into attention significantly outperforms a single-configuration-vector baseline (ManipTrans) in precision and success rate while using only 51% of the baseline's parameters
claims.direction: favors structured, physically-grounded graph/token representations of robot state over a single flat configuration vector, achieving better performance with fewer parameters
claims.conditions: bimanual dexterous hand-tool-object manipulation, tested across three robotic hands (Shadow, Allegro, Inspire)

title: ATOM-Bench: A Real-World Benchmark for Atomic Skills and Compositional Generalization in Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Across 2,700 physical rollouts on five representative manipulation policies fine-tuned on 3,000 human demonstrations of atomic tasks, current policies acquire simple instruction-grounding skills but struggle with fine-grained motor atoms, counting, and logical filtering; strong atomic-skill performance does not reliably transfer to held-out compositional tasks
claims.direction: identifies that good performance on individually-trained atomic skills does not guarantee compositional generalization to new task structures combining those skills
claims.conditions: real-world, single-arm and dual-arm tracks, 30 atomic tasks / 24 held-out compositional tasks

title: Difference-Aware Retrieval Policies for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: DARP, a semi-parametric retrieval-based imitation learning approach that predicts actions from k-nearest-neighbor expert demonstrations plus relative distance vectors between neighbor and query states (rather than a direct global state-to-action mapping), achieves consistent improvements of 15-46% over standard behavior cloning across diverse domains including robotic manipulation and high-dimensional visual features, without requiring additional data collection, online expert feedback, or task-specific knowledge
claims.direction: favors a semi-parametric, retrieval/local-neighborhood-based policy over a pure parametric global behavior-cloning policy, to reduce out-of-distribution compounding-error failures
claims.conditions: diverse domains including continuous control and robotic manipulation, high-dimensional visual features, no extra data or supervision required beyond standard BC

title: Max-Q Selective Imitation for Human-in-the-Loop Online Robot Learning

claims.claim: On a real USB pick-and-insertion task with only 20 demonstrations, ACT QChunk-MCBC (an MC Q-chunk critic combined with max-Q selective imitation that switches between imitating human interventions and on-policy self-improvement) attains 99% success within 30 minutes of human-in-the-loop training, whereas HIL-SERL requires about 5 hours to converge; in simulation, ACT/Flow Q-chunk variants reach >=96% success within roughly half an hour, outperforming HIL-SERL, EXPO, and E2HiL on the success-time frontier
claims.direction: favors combining action-chunked policies with Monte-Carlo Q-chunk critics and selective (max-Q) imitation of human interventions over standard HIL-RL methods, for extremely fast convergence from very few demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world USB pick-and-insertion task, only 20 demonstrations, human-in-the-loop online training, action-chunking policy backbone (ACT)

why_deep_read: An extremely fast (30 minutes vs 5 hours), very-low-data (20 demos) real-world result built on an action-chunking policy backbone (ACT) similar to what we might use — highly relevant to our Q13 data-efficiency question and worth checking if the online HIL component is feasible in our teleop setup

title: A Minimalist Prompt for Zero-Shot Policy Learning

claims.claim: In a contextual RL setting, conditioning a decision transformer on explicit task parameters alone enables zero-shot generalization on par with or better than conditioning on full demonstration prompts, suggesting demonstrations are mainly useful insofar as they let the model recover the underlying task parameters; adding a learnable prompt further boosts zero-shot generalization across robotic control, manipulation, and navigation benchmarks
claims.direction: suggests that explicit, compact task-specification signals (task parameters or a learned prompt) can substitute for costly full demonstration-based task conditioning without losing generalization
claims.conditions: contextual RL benchmarks (robotic control, manipulation, navigation), meta-RL/multi-task setting, not necessarily real-world teleoperation demos

title: FoundationGrasp: Generalizable Task-Oriented Grasping With Foundation Models

claims.claim: Leveraging open-ended knowledge from foundation models (rather than closed-set prior knowledge) for task-oriented grasping demonstrates superior generalization to novel object instances, object classes, and tasks outside the training set, validated in real-robot grasping and manipulation experiments on a 7-DoF arm
claims.direction: favors foundation-model-derived open-ended semantic/geometric priors over closed-set learned priors for generalizing grasping to novel objects/tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot, 7-DoF arm, novel object instances/classes/tasks

title: From Foresight to Forethought: VLM-In-the-Loop Policy Steering via Latent Alignment

claims.claim: FOREWARN decouples predicting action outcomes (a latent world model imagining future latent states given diverse low-level action plans) from evaluation (aligning a VLM with these predicted latent states to reason in natural language and filter proposed plans), providing robust, generalizable runtime policy steering across diverse robotic manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors combining a learned latent world model (for outcome prediction) with a VLM (for language-based evaluation/filtering) as a runtime action-verifier, rather than using either alone
claims.conditions: diverse robotic manipulation tasks (sim/real not fully specified in abstract)

title: DynaRend: Learning 3D Dynamics via Masked Future Rendering for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: DynaRend jointly learns 3D-aware and dynamics-informed triplane features via masked reconstruction and future prediction using differentiable volumetric rendering, pretrained on multi-view RGB-D video, jointly capturing spatial geometry, future dynamics, and task semantics in a unified representation; transferred to downstream manipulation via action-value-map prediction, it substantially improves policy success rate, generalization to environmental perturbations, and real-world applicability on RLBench, Colosseum, and real-world robots
claims.direction: favors a unified 3D-aware pretraining objective combining masked reconstruction AND future-dynamics prediction (rather than either 2D masked-image modeling or 2D video prediction alone) for representations that transfer to manipulation
claims.conditions: pretrained on multi-view RGB-D video, evaluated on RLBench, Colosseum sim benchmarks and real-world robotic experiments, explicitly tested under environmental perturbations

title: How to Train Your Robots? The Impact of Demonstration Modality on Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Comparing kinesthetic teaching, VR-controller teleoperation, and spacemouse teleoperation across three table-top manipulation tasks with different motion constraints, kinesthetic teaching is rated most intuitive by users and provides the cleanest data for the best downstream imitation-learning performance, but is not preferred for large-scale data collection due to physical load; a data-collection scheme mixing a small number of kinesthetic demonstrations with teleoperation-collected data achieves the best overall learning performance while keeping collection effort low
claims.direction: favors mixing a small number of higher-quality (kinesthetic) demonstrations into a larger teleoperation-collected dataset over using either modality alone
claims.conditions: real-world, three table-top manipulation tasks, direct comparison of demonstration-collection modalities on downstream IL performance plus user-experience survey

title: Scaling Single Human Demonstrations for Imitation Learning using Generative Foundational Models

claims.claim: Real2Gen trains a manipulation policy from a single human demonstration by extracting task information into a simulation environment where a programmable expert agent replays the task arbitrarily many times, generating unlimited training data for a flow-matching policy; evaluated on three real-world tasks, it achieves an average 26.6% higher success rate than a recent baseline and better generalization due to data abundance/diversity, and the purely simulation-trained policy deploys zero-shot in the real world
claims.direction: favors extracting task structure from a single human demonstration and generating unlimited synthetic training data in simulation, over collecting many real robot/teleoperated demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation (3 tasks) of a policy trained purely on simulation-generated data derived from one human demonstration, zero-shot sim-to-real deployment

title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments

claims.claim: Using a task-relevant spherical-coordinate azimuthal-angle feature with Gaussian Mixture Model/Gaussian Mixture Regression for imitation learning generates bimanual dressing trajectories that adapt to different human arm postures, validated through various experiments
claims.direction: favors task-relevant coordinate reparameterization combined with GMM/GMR imitation learning for generalizing trajectories across varying object/body configurations
claims.conditions: bimanual robot-assisted dressing task, adaptation to different human arm postures

title: Learning Actionable Manipulation Recovery via Counterfactual Failure Synthesis

claims.claim: Dream2Fix synthesizes photorealistic, counterfactual failure rollouts directly from successful real-world demonstrations by perturbing actions within a generative world model (no simulator needed), producing a verified 120k-sample paired failure-correction dataset used to fine-tune a VLM to jointly predict failure types and precise recovery trajectories
claims.direction: favors synthesizing failure-recovery training data from existing successful demonstrations via a generative world model, rather than costly/unsafe real-world failure data collection or simulator-based perturbation (which introduces sim-to-real gap)
claims.conditions: real-world robotic experiments, dataset generated purely from successful real demonstrations plus generative perturbation

claims.claim: This approach achieves state-of-the-art correction accuracy, improving from 19.7% to 81.3% over prior baselines, and successfully enables zero-shot closed-loop failure recovery in physical deployments
claims.direction: favors training explicit failure-recovery capability (via synthesized counterfactual data) for robust real-world deployment, rather than relying on the base policy's implicit robustness
claims.conditions: real-world physical deployment, zero-shot

title: SaPaVe: Towards Active Perception and Manipulation in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics

claims.claim: Decoupling camera-control actions from manipulation actions (rather than a shared action space), with a bottom-up training strategy (semantic camera control trained first on a large dataset, then jointly optimized with manipulation using hybrid data) plus a 3D geometry-aware module for robustness under dynamic viewpoints, outperforms recent VLA models (GR00T N1, pi0) by up to 31.25% higher success rates in real-world tasks under viewpoint variation
claims.direction: favors active, semantically-driven camera control decoupled from the manipulation action space, plus explicit 3D geometric awareness, for viewpoint-invariant execution -- rather than fixed-camera policies or a single shared action space for camera+manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation, evaluated specifically on active/viewpoint-variable manipulation settings, compared directly against GR00T N1 and pi0

title: WorldToken: Time-First Sequence Modeling for Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Under same-checkpoint history truncation, reducing visible history to one or two policy timesteps lowers closed-loop success for all 50 RoboCasa policies tested; on RMBench Blocks Ranking, reducing visible history from 146 to 8 seconds drops evaluator success from 95% to 28%, while an exploratory extended rollout sustains behavior over 850 seconds
claims.direction: strongly favors providing substantial observation history/temporal context to the policy rather than only 1-2 recent timesteps, especially for tasks with longer effective memory requirements
claims.conditions: RoboCasa sim benchmark (23 tasks), factorial sweep over dataset sizes/model sizes/seeds, time-first world-token architecture with diffusion action head

claims.claim: A complete factorial sweep over five dataset sizes and five model sizes shows consistent gains from additional target-domain data but diminishing returns beyond a moderate model size (85.3M-parameter policy trained mostly from scratch)
claims.direction: favors moderate model size with more target-domain data over further scaling model size, for this imitation-learning setup
claims.conditions: RoboCasa sim, 2,900 generated demonstrations per task, frozen pretrained CLIP text encoder only

why_deep_read: A controlled factorial ablation showing a dramatic (95% to 28%) success-rate collapse when visible observation history is shortened is directly relevant to our Q07 decision, and the model-size/data-size sweep bears on Q12; worth checking exact history length needed and whether findings transfer from sim to a small real low-cost setup

title: UniDex-ViTac: Learning Unified Visuo-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation Policy from Human Video Data

claims.claim: From only 50 human demonstrations across ten objects, human-video-guided simulation with object-specific residual RL specialists generates 10,000 simulated trajectories to train a single ACT-based generalist policy; without any real-robot demonstrations or fine-tuning, it succeeds in 66.4% of physical trials (vs 54.5% for a point-cloud-only baseline) across seen and unseen objects
claims.direction: favors using a small number of human demonstrations to bootstrap large-scale simulated data generation (via per-object RL specialists), rather than collecting large-scale real robot demonstrations directly
claims.conditions: real-world physical trials (110), zero real-robot demonstrations or fine-tuning, ACT-based policy

title: Multi-Stage Reinforcement Learning for Non-Prehensile Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing observations and goals as point clouds with motion (State-Goal Fusion Representation) improves the policy's perception of scene layout and task goal, and the resulting multi-stage RL policy generalizes to unseen objects with shapes outside the training distribution, transferring to the real world zero-shot with 95% success on an occluded grasping task
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-with-motion representations over static geometric or image-based representations for generalization to novel object shapes
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot transfer, occluded grasping task, novel object shapes

title: X-Sim: Cross-Embodiment Learning via Real-to-Sim-to-Real

claims.claim: X-Sim reconstructs a photorealistic simulation from an RGBD human video, uses tracked object motion as a dense object-centric reward to train an RL policy in simulation (no robot teleoperation data required), then distills it into an image-conditioned diffusion policy using synthetic rollouts, plus online domain adaptation for real-world transfer; across 5 manipulation tasks in 2 environments it improves task progress by 30% over hand-tracking/sim-to-real baselines and matches behavior cloning with 10x less data collection time
claims.direction: favors object-motion-driven real-to-sim-to-real learning (no robot teleoperation needed) over standard teleoperated behavior cloning, for large reductions in data-collection time
claims.conditions: real-world, 5 tasks, 2 environments, no robot teleoperation data used for training

claims.claim: Distilling the simulation-trained policy using synthetic rollouts rendered with varied viewpoints and lighting, combined with online domain adaptation aligning real and simulated observations at deployment, enables generalization to new camera viewpoints and test-time visual changes
claims.direction: favors synthetic rollout rendering with randomized viewpoint/lighting plus online domain adaptation for robustness to camera and lighting changes
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, tested specifically for generalization to new camera viewpoints and test-time changes

why_deep_read: Directly addresses camera-viewpoint and lighting generalization (our core robustness failure) while requiring no robot teleoperation data and 10x less data-collection time than standard BC — highly relevant to Q13/Q05/Q11 jointly; worth checking the real-to-sim reconstruction requirements for feasibility with our fixed scene + wrist camera setup

title: Neural Dynamics Augmented Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Training a diffusion policy in a small local support region using only 1 to 30 few-shot demonstrations, then using offline-trained neural dynamics models (learned from off-policy data, no expert guidance needed) to rearrange objects outside this covered region into it, allows the combined method to robustly cover a significantly larger area of scene configurations than a diffusion policy trained purely from the same few demonstrations, across granular manipulation, contact-rich, and multi-object tasks in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors combining a small number of demonstrations (for a diffusion policy in a local region) with an offline dynamics model (to extend spatial coverage) over collecting more demonstrations to cover a larger configuration space
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated, 1-30 demonstrations, granular/contact-rich/multi-object tasks

title: CF-VLA: Efficient Coarse-to-Fine Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: CF-VLA restructures flow-based VLA action generation into a coarse initialization step (learning a conditional posterior over endpoint velocity to construct an action-aware starting point) followed by a single-step local refinement, rather than shortening the multi-step sampling trajectory from Gaussian noise; on CALVIN and LIBERO it reduces action sampling latency by 75.4% and achieves the best average real-robot success rate (83.0%), outperforming a 10-NFE pi0.5 baseline by 4.0 points and MIP by 19.5 points
claims.direction: favors restructuring the starting point of flow-based action generation (coarse-to-fine) over simply reducing sampling steps, to jointly improve inference speed and accuracy
claims.conditions: real-robot evaluation plus CALVIN/LIBERO sim, compared directly against pi0.5 and MIP baselines

title: HybridFlow: A 2-NFE Generative Policy for Real-Time Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: HybridFlow reuses a single unified MeanFlow-based model (no distillation) through a three-stage 2-NFE inference procedure (Global Jump, parameter-free ReNoise interpolation, Local Refine); across five real-robot settings all running on the same Jetson AGX Thor edge device, it improves normalized task performance over 16-step Diffusion Policy by 13-68 points with roughly eightfold lower action-generation latency, and is compatible as a drop-in action expert within a VLA framework
claims.direction: favors a 2-NFE hybrid coarse-then-refine generative action head over standard multi-step diffusion policies, for real-time inference on edge/embedded compute
claims.conditions: real-robot, edge compute hardware (Jetson AGX Thor), compared directly against 16-step Diffusion Policy, controlled RoboMimic ablations included

why_deep_read: Tested on real robots running on an edge GPU (Jetson AGX Thor) — a compute budget closer to our laptop constraint than most VLA papers — with an 8x latency reduction and large performance gains over standard diffusion policy; directly actionable for our Q01/Q10/Q12 latency and small-hardware questions

title: Task-Relevant and Irrelevant Region-Aware Augmentation for Generalizable Vision-Based Imitation Learning in Agricultural Manipulation

claims.claim: DRAIL explicitly separates visual observations into task-relevant regions (augmented in a domain-knowledge-driven manner to preserve essential visual characteristics, addressing object-appearance diversity) and task-irrelevant regions (aggressively randomized to suppress spurious background correlations, addressing background variation); evaluated on diffusion-policy visuomotor controllers for real robot vegetable harvesting and lettuce leaf-picking tasks, it shows consistent improvements in success rate under unseen visual conditions versus baseline augmentation, with attention analysis confirming reliance on task-essential features
claims.direction: favors region-differentiated augmentation (mild, structure-preserving on the object; aggressive randomization on background) over uniform augmentation strategies, for generalizing to novel object appearance and background combined
claims.conditions: real robot, agricultural manipulation (crop-appearance diversity plus background variation), diffusion-policy visuomotor controller, scarce demonstration data

why_deep_read: The problem framing (scarce demos, generalizing to novel object appearance AND background variation) is nearly identical to our pumpkin/lighting/background robustness problem, and the region-differentiated augmentation strategy with real-robot validation is directly actionable; full text would give the augmentation recipe and how much domain knowledge it needs about the object

title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation

claims.claim: DynaFLIP pretrains an image-only visual encoder using image-language-3D-flow triplets constructed from heterogeneous human and robot videos, with a simplex-volume-minimization objective (plus cosine regularization and a contrastive term) encouraging the three modalities to align in a shared hyperspherical space, pushing motion/dynamics understanding upstream into perception rather than leaving it to downstream policies; the resulting dynamics-aware visual backbone consistently outperforms baselines (including VLAs) across diverse downstream policies in simulation and real-world setups, with gains reaching +22.5% under out-of-distribution scenarios
claims.direction: favors dynamics-aware (motion/action-relevant) visual pretraining objectives over standard static-recognition or vision-language-alignment pretraining (e.g., CLIP/DINOv2-style), especially for OOD robustness
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated, diverse downstream policies including VLAs, explicitly tested under out-of-distribution scenarios

title: Behavior Cloning of MPC for 3-DOF Robotic Manipulators

claims.claim: Behavior cloning of an MPC policy (combining Inverse Kinematics with MPC as the teacher) for a 3-DOF manipulator achieves a 3x reduction in inference latency versus running MPC directly, with 84.98% success under relaxed tolerances, though a precision gap remains under strict tolerances
claims.direction: favors distilling a computationally expensive controller (MPC) into a fast behavior-cloned policy to cut inference latency, at some cost to precision under tight tolerances
claims.conditions: 3-DOF robotic manipulator, evaluated online and offline

claims.claim: Comparing classical regression algorithms and deep MLPs against RNN (temporal) architectures for cloning the MPC policy, static (non-temporal) architectures outperform temporal variants, confirming the sufficiency of instantaneous state observations for this task
claims.direction: contradicts the general expectation that adding observation history/temporal modeling improves imitation policies -- for this MPC-cloning task, single-timestep (Markovian) state was sufficient and temporal architectures did not help
claims.conditions: 3-DOF manipulator, MPC-cloning task (not necessarily generalizing to more complex/partially-observable manipulation tasks)

why_deep_read: Reports a result that cuts against the field's usual emphasis on history/temporal conditioning (Q07) for a controller-distillation task, and separately shows a concrete latency win (Q10) from BC-distilling an expensive controller — worth reading to see whether the 'static suffices' finding is task-specific (simple 3-DOF, fully observed) versus likely to hold for our teleop-demo-based, partially-observed pick-and-place

title: SUREFlow: State-space Uncertainty-aware REsidual Flow Matching for Robust Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: SUREFlow, built on a Mamba (state-space) backbone with only 179M parameters, attains on LIBERO-PRO performance comparable to large VLAs with 3-7B parameters, and on LIBERO achieves 92.5% average success rate, outperforming the Mamba-based MaIL baseline by 34.2%
claims.direction: favors a much smaller state-space-backbone model with explicit uncertainty modeling over large-parameter VLAs, showing small models can match large-VLA performance under the right architecture
claims.conditions: LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO sim benchmarks, 179M-parameter model compared against 3-7B-parameter VLAs

claims.claim: Jointly predicting action velocities and input-dependent residual uncertainty (rather than assuming homoscedastic residuals) enables selective refinement of unreliable action dimensions without environment feedback, improving robustness under noise, partial observability, and stochastic initial conditions during extended rollouts
claims.direction: favors explicit per-dimension uncertainty-aware residual correction within a flow-matching action head, over standard flow/diffusion policies that assume uniform residual noise
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO), extended/iterative rollouts

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our small-model-on-8GB-GPU constraint: a 179M-parameter model reportedly matches 3-7B-parameter VLA performance, which is a strong, quantified small-vs-large comparison (Q12); also relevant to robustness under noisy/jittery hardware (our Feetech backlash/jitter) via explicit uncertainty modeling (Q01)

title: Process-aware robotic food assembly: Closed-loop visual monitoring across heterogeneous ingredients

claims.claim: A process-aware VLA built on pi0, combining step-specific language instructions, a predefined sequential controller, and learned visual monitoring for automatic step transitions, completed 10 of 10 trials on a seven-step salad-packing task, whereas the unaugmented end-to-end pi0 baseline completed only 3 of 10 trials, with no sequence errors observed in the process-aware trials
claims.direction: strongly favors explicit step/phase-aware conditioning and monitoring layered on top of an end-to-end chunked VLA policy, over relying on the base policy alone for multi-step sequential tasks
claims.conditions: real-world seven-step food-assembly task, built on the pi0 VLA policy

title: Learning Beyond What Humans Can Demonstrate

claims.claim: GLIDE infers task-specific failure modes from a task description and teleoperation code, converting them into executable guardrails that filter teleoperation/policy commands and iteratively improve from trajectory feedback, raising data-collection success from 0-10% to 70-90% across three dynamically-demanding tasks, with mixed-data guarded policies then reaching 60-70% execution success
claims.direction: favors automatically-discovered, iteratively-refined guardrails over naive teleoperation or hand-coded domain-expert guardrails, for collecting usable demonstrations on tasks that are hard/infeasible for humans to demonstrate directly
claims.conditions: real-world, three tasks requiring dynamic stability/precise contact timing/dexterous coordination that are difficult for direct human teleoperation

title: MUTEX: Learning Unified Policies from Multimodal Task Specifications

claims.claim: MUTEX trains a transformer architecture with masked modeling and cross-modal matching objectives in a two-stage procedure to follow task specifications in any of six modalities (video demonstrations, goal images, text goal descriptions, text instructions, speech goal descriptions, speech instructions) or combinations thereof, and shows improved performance over methods trained specifically for any single modality, evaluated on 100 simulated and 50 real-world tasks with multiple task-specification instances per modality
claims.direction: favors joint cross-modal training across multiple task-specification modalities (even if only one, e.g. language, is used at deployment) over training a policy for a single modality alone
claims.conditions: real-world (50 tasks) and simulation (100 tasks), multiple modalities of task specification available during training

title: Leveraging Locality to Boost Sample Efficiency in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: SGRv2 incorporates an action-locality inductive bias (actions predominantly influenced by the target object and its local environment) into visual and action representations; it excels in RLBench keyframe-control tasks using merely 5 demonstrations, surpassing the RVT baseline in 23 of 26 tasks, and in real-world environments with only 8 demonstrations performs a variety of tasks at markedly higher success rate than baselines
claims.direction: favors an action-locality inductive bias (local, object-relative representations) over global scene representations for extreme sample efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world (8 demos) and simulated (RLBench 5 demos, ManiSkill2/MimicGen dense control) benchmarks

why_deep_read: Reports strong real-world performance from only 8 demonstrations (below even our low end of 50-100) using an action-locality inductive bias — directly relevant to our Q13 data-efficiency question and Q02 action-representation choice; worth checking if the locality bias requires point-cloud/keyframe control incompatible with our continuous chunked setup

title: A Vision-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Dexterous Robotic Grasping Using Gaussian Processes and Transformers

claims.claim: Adding Transformer-based multi-modal sensory fusion for force modulation achieves a 95.6% grasp success rate, surpassing LSTM (91.3%) and Gaussian Process (91.3%) models for grasp force/configuration prediction
claims.direction: favors Transformer-based multi-modal fusion over LSTM or GP-based approaches for grasp force modulation
claims.conditions: real-world (implied) diverse object dataset, two- and three-finger grasps; limitations noted for five-finger grasps

title: CEED-VLA: Consistency Vision-Language-Action Model with Early-Exit Decoding

claims.claim: Consistency distillation training (predicting multiple correct action tokens per iteration) combined with mixed-label supervision and an early-exit decoding strategy (relaxing convergence conditions) achieves more than 4x inference acceleration across different VLA baselines while maintaining high task success rates in both simulated and real-world robot tasks
claims.direction: favors consistency-distillation plus early-exit decoding over standard autoregressive or Jacobi decoding for accelerating VLA inference
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated robot tasks, multiple VLA baselines

title: DAM-VLA: A Dynamic Action Model-Based Vision-Language-Action Framework for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: DAM-VLA uses an action-routing mechanism to select specialized diffusion-based action models for arm movement vs gripper manipulation based on task-specific visual/linguistic cues, with a dual-scale weighting mechanism coordinating the two, achieving superior success rates over SOTA VLA methods in simulated (SIMPLER, FurnitureBench) and real-world settings, with robust generalization from standard pick-and-place to long-horizon/contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors routing between specialized (arm vs gripper) action sub-models rather than a single unified action head for tasks requiring both gross and precise motion
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated (SIMPLER, FurnitureBench)

title: HEX: Humanoid-Aligned Experts for Cross-Embodiment Whole-Body Manipulation

claims.claim: HEX uses lightweight history tokens to summarize past observations, avoiding repeated encoding of historical images during inference, to efficiently capture temporal visual context, combined with a residual-gated fusion mechanism and flow-matching action head; this achieves SOTA task success and generalization on real-world humanoid manipulation, particularly in fast-reaction and long-horizon scenarios
claims.direction: favors compact learned history-summary tokens (rather than re-encoding raw historical images) as an efficient way to provide observation history to the policy
claims.conditions: real-world full-sized bipedal humanoid, cross-embodiment multi-embodiment trajectory pretraining

title: Shallow-π: Knowledge Distillation for Flow-based VLAs

claims.claim: Shallow-pi, a knowledge distillation framework that aggressively reduces transformer depth of both the VLM backbone and flow-based action head (from 18 to 6 layers), achieves over 2x faster inference with less than 1% absolute drop in success rate on standard manipulation benchmarks, establishing SOTA among reduced VLA models
claims.direction: favors aggressive transformer-depth reduction via knowledge distillation (rather than token-level pruning alone) for compressing flow-based VLA models with minimal accuracy loss
claims.conditions: validated via industrial-scale real-world experiments on Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor edge devices across multiple robot platforms, including humanoid systems, in complex/dynamic manipulation scenarios

title: A Low-Cost VLA-RL Framework for Dexterous Multi-Category Fruit Harvesting in Orchards

claims.claim: Using SmolVLA as backbone with PPO online fine-tuning on top of an initial imitation-learning policy, the framework is evaluated across Vision, Semantic, and Execution generalization dimensions under new backgrounds, dynamic lighting, unseen fruit types, multi-object scenes, and variations in initial pose; in real-world trials the model achieves a task success rate over 80%, demonstrating improved adaptability/stability under these conditions with reduced hardware requirements and deployment cost
claims.direction: favors adding online RL (PPO) fine-tuning on top of a SmolVLA imitation-learning policy to improve robustness specifically to lighting, background, and novel-object-type shifts, rather than imitation learning alone
claims.conditions: real-world orchard fruit harvesting (pick-and-place), same SmolVLA backbone we currently use, explicitly tested under new backgrounds/dynamic lighting/unseen fruit types/multi-object scenes/pose variation, low-cost hardware

why_deep_read: Uses the exact same backbone (SmolVLA) we are fine-tuning, on an agriculture pick-and-place task, and directly tests robustness to lighting/background/novel-object shifts — our exact reported failure modes; full text would give the specific PPO fine-tuning recipe added on top of the imitation-learned SmolVLA policy

title: ForceFlow: Learning to Feel and Act via Contact-Driven Flow Matching

claims.claim: ForceFlow hierarchically decomposes manipulation into a vision-dominant approach stage (VLM-based pointing for target localization) and a touch-dominant interaction stage (force-driven contact execution), with an explicit Vision-to-Force handover decoupling spatial generalization from contact regulation; across six real-world contact-rich tasks it achieves a 37% success-rate improvement over the strong baseline ForceVLA at lower cost, with better zero-shot OOD generalization
claims.direction: favors explicitly decoupling coarse vision-based localization from fine contact-driven execution (rather than a single end-to-end policy) for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world, six contact-rich tasks, force/tactile sensing required for the interaction stage

title: Spatial Attention: Adapting Execution Horizons for Diffusion Policies via Observation Sensitivity

claims.claim: Defining 'Spatial Attention' as the expected squared norm of the gradient of the action log-likelihood with respect to the observation, the authors show that the execution horizon minimizing cumulative likelihood drop under disturbances decreases as Spatial Attention increases; by forecasting future Spatial Attention and dynamically assigning shorter execution horizons to high-sensitivity phases and longer horizons to low-sensitivity phases (rather than a fixed execution horizon), their method significantly improves success rates over fixed-horizon diffusion-policy baselines on standard and perturbed tasks, in both simulation and on a real robot, while maintaining the same average execution horizon
claims.direction: favors adaptively varying the action-chunk execution horizon based on observation sensitivity, rather than using a fixed execution horizon, especially under disturbances/perturbations
claims.conditions: real robot plus simulation, standard and perturbed tasks, diffusion-policy backbone

why_deep_read: Directly targets our Q06 execution-horizon decision with a principled, observation-sensitivity-driven adaptive scheme validated on a real robot under perturbations — highly relevant to reducing jerkiness/inconsistency at chunk boundaries (Q10) while improving robustness; worth checking implementation overhead for our latency-constrained setup

title: GLOVER: Generalizable Open-Vocabulary Affordance Reasoning for Task-Oriented Grasping

claims.claim: GLOVER fine-tunes LLMs to predict visual affordance of graspable object parts directly in RGB feature space (rather than time-consuming 3D radiance modeling), combined with a non-parametric grasp planner (Affordance-Aware Grasping Estimation) aligning gripper pose to a superquadric surface; across 30 real-world table-top scenes it achieves 86.0% part-identification and 76.3% grasping success, running approximately 29x faster in affordance reasoning and 40x faster in grasping-pose estimation than prior SOTA, and generalizes across embodiments including humanoid dexterous hands
claims.direction: favors RGB-feature-space (2D) affordance prediction over 3D radiance-field-based grasp planning, for both open-vocabulary language-driven grasping and large inference-speed gains
claims.conditions: real-world, 30 table-top scenes, cross-embodiment validation including humanoid hands

title: cVLA: Towards Efficient Camera-Space VLAs

claims.claim: Predicting robot end-effector trajectory waypoints in image-frame (camera-space) coordinates, rather than low-level joint/end-effector controls, allows a lightweight next-token-prediction VLA to be both cheaper to train and embodiment-agnostic, while still learning meaningful, executable robot trajectories with strong sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: favors predicting actions/waypoints in camera/image-frame coordinates rather than robot-frame low-level control commands, for training efficiency and embodiment-agnosticism
claims.conditions: trained on a simulated dataset, evaluated with a combination of simulated and real data on a real robotic system

title: PinchBot: Long-Horizon Deformable Manipulation with Guided Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: PinchBot combines a goal-conditioned diffusion policy with pre-trained 3D point-cloud embeddings, task-progress prediction, and collision-constrained action projection to successfully create a variety of simple pottery goals via long-horizon, highly multi-modal deformable manipulation using only pinch-based actions
claims.direction: favors augmenting a diffusion policy with pretrained point-cloud embeddings plus an explicit task-progress prediction signal and action-projection constraints for long-horizon, highly multimodal deformable-object tasks
claims.conditions: real-world (implied via project website/demonstration dataset), long-horizon deformable manipulation

title: VAT: Vision Action Transformer by Unlocking Full Representation of ViT

claims.claim: Most methods discard information by using only the final ViT layer's features for action generation; VAT instead processes specialized action tokens together with visual features across all ViT transformer layers, enabling deep progressive fusion of perception and action; this achieves a 98.15% average success rate across four LIBERO benchmarks, establishing a new SOTA by outperforming prior methods including OpenVLA-OFT
claims.direction: favors using the full multi-layer feature hierarchy of a vision transformer (fused with action tokens at every layer) over using only the final-layer visual features for action generation
claims.conditions: simulated LIBERO benchmarks (real-world not stated in abstract), ViT-based vision encoder

title: Image-Based Hand Pose Data Acquisition Framework for Robot Learning

claims.claim: An image-based hand-pose data-acquisition framework using deep-learning pose estimation on ordinary videos (rather than requiring specialized mocap hardware) captures detailed finger articulation and contact-rich interaction dynamics, showing superior performance over SOTA models for bridging human demonstrations to robotic skill acquisition
claims.direction: favors video-based (camera-only) hand-pose data acquisition over specialized motion-capture hardware for scalable demonstration collection focused on detailed finger/contact dynamics
claims.conditions: comparison against SOTA pose-estimation/data-acquisition models; real-world applicability claimed but no robot-policy success numbers given

title: InstructVLA: Vision-Language-Action Instruction Tuning from Understanding to Manipulation

claims.claim: A Vision-Language-Action Instruction Tuning paradigm using mixture-of-experts adaptation to jointly optimize embodied reasoning and action generation (rather than sacrificing one for the other or suffering catastrophic forgetting of pretrained VLM capabilities) achieves 33% improvement over SpatialVLA in-domain, outperforms a fine-tuned OpenVLA by 96% and a GPT-4o-aided action expert by 29% on an 80-task generalization benchmark requiring closed-loop control and high-level instruction understanding, and shows inference-time scaling where additional textual reasoning boosts manipulation performance in both simulated and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors jointly training embodied reasoning and action generation with mixture-of-experts adaptation (preserving VLM reasoning ability) over action-only fine-tuning that risks catastrophic forgetting
claims.conditions: simulated (SimplerEnv, SimplerEnv-Instruct) plus real-world settings; large VLM-backed VLA architecture

title: Generalizable Domain Adaptation for Sim-and-Real Policy Co-Training

claims.claim: A sim-and-real co-training framework that aligns the joint distribution of observations AND their corresponding actions across domains (via an Optimal-Transport-inspired loss, extended to Unbalanced OT to handle the imbalance between abundant simulation data and few real demonstrations) learns a domain-invariant, task-relevant feature space using only a few real-world demonstrations plus abundant simulation data, achieving up to a 30% improvement in real-world success rate and generalizing to scenarios seen only in simulation
claims.direction: favors aligning joint observation-action distributions (not just observations) across sim and real domains when co-training with abundant sim data and few real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, few real-world demonstrations plus abundant simulation data

title: OpenEAI-Platform: An Open-source Embodied Artificial Intelligence Hardware-Software Unified Platform

claims.claim: OpenEAI-VLA, built on Qwen3-VL-4B with a Diffusion Transformer action head and trained in two stages using only open-source robot and multimodal datasets, achieves success rates comparable to the large-scale pretrained pi0 baseline despite having only limited pretraining data, and the open-source low-cost OpenEAI-Arm outperforms two commercial 6+1-DoF arms under the same policy, across four real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors that a modestly-sized, openly-trained VLA with a diffusion-transformer action head can match a much more heavily-pretrained proprietary-style baseline (pi0) despite limited pretraining data, and that low-cost open-source arm hardware can match or exceed commercial arms under the same policy
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost open-source 6+1-DoF arm, limited pretraining data, four manipulation tasks, direct comparison against commercial arms and against pi0

why_deep_read: A low-cost, open-source robot-arm-plus-VLA platform (conceptually similar to our SO-101 setup) reporting performance comparable to pi0 despite limited pretraining data — directly relevant evidence that our low-cost hardware need not be a fundamental performance ceiling; worth checking hardware/compute requirements for feasibility on our 8GB laptop

title: Robots That Know What to Ask: Recovering Misaligned Rewards through Targeted Explanations

claims.claim: Detecting underspecified features in demonstrations (features that vary widely across demos rather than being consistently optimized) and actively soliciting targeted corrective demonstrations addressing exactly those gaps significantly improves reward recovery compared to random querying and passive data collection, validated in simulated tabletop manipulation and a user study with a real Franka robot
claims.direction: favors targeted, gap-driven active querying for additional demonstrations over random/passive additional data collection when demonstrations are imperfect/underspecified
claims.conditions: simulated tabletop manipulation plus real Franka user study, reward-learning-from-demonstration setting

title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding

claims.claim: AffordanceVLA introduces structured affordance forecasting (object-centric grounding via visual latent prediction, 2D affordance-map interaction localization, and 3D geometric reasoning) as a task-oriented intermediate representation bridging VLM semantics and embodied control, integrated into a Mixture-of-Transformer architecture with a three-stage progressive training curriculum and an automated affordance-label data-augmentation pipeline; extensive simulation and real-world experiments show strong performance across diverse manipulation scenarios
claims.direction: favors structured, staged affordance intermediate representations (2D localization plus 3D reasoning) over direct VLM-semantics-to-action mapping
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation, automated affordance-label augmentation to address label scarcity

title: ABot-M0: VLA Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation with Action Manifold Learning

claims.claim: Under the Action Manifold Hypothesis (effective robot actions lie on a low-dimensional, smooth manifold governed by physical laws and task constraints rather than the full high-dimensional action space), Action Manifold Learning uses a DiT backbone to directly predict clean, continuous action sequences via projection onto the feasible manifold instead of iterative denoising, improving decoding speed and policy stability versus standard diffusion action heads
claims.direction: favors direct manifold-projection action generation over iterative denoising-based diffusion for faster, more stable action decoding
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining on UniACT-dataset (6M+ trajectories, 9,500 hours, six public datasets, diverse robot morphologies)

claims.claim: Modular perception via a dual-stream mechanism integrating VLM semantics with geometric priors and multi-view inputs from plug-and-play 3D modules (e.g., VGGT, Qwen-Image-Edit) enhances spatial understanding without modifying the backbone, and components are shown to operate independently with additive benefits
claims.direction: favors adding plug-and-play 3D/geometric modules on top of a frozen VLM backbone (rather than retraining the backbone) to add spatial understanding
claims.conditions: large-scale multi-embodiment pretraining dataset

title: STORM: Slot-based Task-aware Object-centric Representation for robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: STORM augments a frozen visual foundation model with a small set of task-aware object-centric slots, trained via an efficient two-stage strategy (visual-semantic pretraining of slots using language embeddings, then joint adaptation with the manipulation policy) rather than fully fine-tuning the large backbone; this staged learning prevents degenerate slot formation and improves control performance and generalization to visual shifts (distractors, textures, lighting) compared to using frozen or fully fine-tuned foundation-model features directly, or existing object-centric representations
claims.direction: favors a lightweight, staged object-centric adaptation module on top of a frozen foundation-model backbone over either using frozen features directly or fully fine-tuning the backbone, for robustness to distractors/texture/lighting shifts
claims.conditions: object discovery benchmarks plus robotic manipulation tasks (sim/real not fully specified in abstract), frozen large visual foundation model backbone

why_deep_read: Directly targets generalization to distractors/texture/lighting shifts (our core robustness failure) via a lightweight, compute-cheap adaptation of a frozen backbone rather than full fine-tuning — well matched to our 8GB-GPU compute budget; worth checking exact compute/parameter overhead of the slot module

title: DiffusionVS: A Generative Framework for Robust Visual Servoing Based on Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Regression-based visual servoing frequently experiences trajectory jitter from noise-sensitive single-step mappings and error accumulation; a diffusion-policy-based approach that predicts action sequences (rather than single-step regression) maintains temporal consistency and improves robustness, and existing visual servoing networks consistently achieve improved performance when integrated with this diffusion-based module, achieving success rates near 100% in simulation and 93% in real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors sequence-predicting diffusion-based action generation over single-step regression mappings to reduce trajectory jitter and improve robustness, as a generally-applicable module
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation, visual servoing task (camera-based tag tracking, not full manipulation), online training paradigm expanding data diversity

title: Addressing the Orchestration Gap in Generalist Robots via Physical Agency

claims.claim: Rather than baking planning, success detection, recovery, and low-level control all into one learned policy via large-scale pretraining, decomposing these into a general language-conditioned policy/control agent plus a separate closed-loop high-level orchestrator (Pigey) that plans, decomposes goals, commands the frozen low-level policy, verifies outcomes, and recovers from failures -- without any additional data collection or post-training -- advances LIBERO-PRO state-of-the-art by over 4x (12.8% to 53.3%) and lifts a real-robot frozen policy from near-zero to over 90% success on reasoning-limited tasks
claims.direction: favors architecturally decomposing high-level reasoning/orchestration from a frozen low-level action policy (rather than training one monolithic pretrained policy to do everything) especially for reasoning-limited failure modes
claims.conditions: real-world plus LIBERO-PRO sim benchmark, works with existing frozen VLA policies, no additional data collection or post-training required

why_deep_read: An extremely large, directly comparable real-world improvement (near-zero to >90%) from adding a training-free orchestration layer around an existing frozen policy — highly relevant to our Q09/Q10 decisions about whether complex reasoning/recovery should be handled by a separate lightweight layer rather than trained end-to-end into our small policy, which could be more compute-friendly for our 8GB GPU

title: Optimization of vision-based deep reinforcement learning frameworks to improve robotic manipulation tasks by means of sophisticated greedy osprey optimizer

claims.claim: Combining Vision Transformers for perceptual encoding with a policy network optimized by a metaheuristic (Advanced Greedy Osprey Optimizer), validated on the Open X-Embodiment Dataset, is reported to be more successful, less prone to generalization breakpoints, and more computationally efficient than state-of-the-art baselines
claims.direction: favors ViT-based perceptual encoding combined with metaheuristic policy optimization over standard gradient-based RL baselines
claims.conditions: Open X-Embodiment Dataset, vision-based deep RL (not imitation learning), curriculum learning and skill decomposition used

title: One-Shot Imitation Learning with Invariance Matching for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Learning invariant regions of state space (rather than direct end-effector pose regression) enables learning a novel task from a single unannotated demonstration without fine-tuning, achieving avg 11.5% success rate improvement over SOTA on 22 novel tasks, plus one-shot sim-to-real transfer with a single real demo
claims.direction: invariance-based representation favored for extreme low-data (one-shot) generalization over direct pose regression
claims.conditions: RLBench sim (18 train tasks, 22 novel test tasks) + one real-robot one-shot sim-to-real demo

title: ReSeFlow: Rectifying SE(3)-Equivariant Policy Learning Flows

claims.claim: Rectifying SE(3)-equivariant diffusion policies into flow-matching form enables single-step inference with better performance (lower geodesic distance) than baseline SE(3)-diffusion using 100-step inference, up to 48.5% error reduction on a painting task and 21.9% on a rotating-triangle task
claims.direction: rectified flow matching favored over standard diffusion for equivalent/better accuracy with far fewer inference steps
claims.conditions: simulated benchmarks only, SE(3)-equivariant network architecture

claims.claim: Single-step rectified-flow inference drastically reduces inference cost vs 100-step diffusion baseline while maintaining/improving accuracy
claims.direction: flow matching favored over multi-step diffusion for latency
claims.conditions: simulation only

title: dVLA: Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model with Multimodal Chain-of-Thought

claims.claim: Prefix attention mask + KV caching acceleration strategies yield up to several-times inference speedup for a diffusion VLA at test time, enabling practical deployment
claims.direction: KV-caching/attention-mask acceleration favored for reducing diffusion-VLA inference latency
claims.conditions: real Franka robot + LIBERO sim benchmark, large foundation-model-scale VLA

claims.claim: Diffusion-based VLA with joint perception-language-action objective achieves 96.4% avg success on LIBERO, surpassing both discrete-token and continuous-regression action policies
claims.direction: diffusion action head favored over discrete-token and simple continuous regression
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO) + real Franka bin-picking, large-scale foundation VLA model

title: FlowVLA: Visual Chain of Thought-Based Motion Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Explicitly predicting optical flow (motion dynamics) as an intermediate step before next-frame prediction, rather than directly predicting future appearance, produces more physically plausible visual forecasts and achieves state-of-the-art policy performance with substantially improved sample efficiency
claims.direction: explicit motion/flow-based auxiliary prediction favored over direct next-frame appearance prediction as an auxiliary/world-model objective
claims.conditions: robotics manipulation benchmarks + real-robot evaluations, autoregressive transformer world model

title: Recurrent-Depth VLA: Implicit Test-Time Compute Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models via Latent Iterative Reasoning

claims.claim: A recurrent, weight-tied action head with adaptive-stopping latent iterative refinement achieves up to 80x inference speedup over prior reasoning-based VLA methods while allocating variable compute per task difficulty
claims.direction: recurrent/latent iterative refinement favored over explicit token-based chain-of-thought reasoning for latency-efficient adaptive compute
claims.conditions: challenging manipulation tasks (setting real/sim not specified in abstract)

claims.claim: Tasks that fail entirely (0% success) with single-iteration inference exceed 90% success with four iterations of the same recurrent action head, showing depth of iterative refinement is critical for complex manipulation
claims.direction: iterative/recurrent refinement of action output favored over single-pass action decoding for complex tasks
claims.conditions: manipulation tasks, constant memory footprint recurrent head

title: SADP: Subgoal-Aware Diffusion Policy for Long-Horizon Manipulation Learned from Foundation Model Generated Demonstrations

claims.claim: Adding a lightweight auxiliary head predicting a subgoal continuation score (language-conditioned subgoal progress) to a diffusion policy maintains competitive task performance while exposing temporally aligned progress-monitoring signals, without degrading task-level performance
claims.direction: auxiliary subgoal/progress-prediction head favored as a low-cost addition that does not hurt base diffusion policy performance
claims.conditions: RLBench sim + real-world UR5e robot, diffusion policy backbone

title: RFS: Reinforcement Learning with Residual Flow Steering for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Behavior-cloned flow-matching policies pretrained on demonstrations show limited generalization and benefit from RL fine-tuning via residual action + latent noise steering, enabling efficient adaptation while retaining pretrained policy's expressive structure
claims.direction: flow-matching action head is viable for pretraining but benefits from residual RL fine-tuning to fix generalization/local execution errors
claims.conditions: dexterous manipulation tasks, both simulation and real-world settings

title: WorldScape Policy 2.0: Empowering Steerable World Action Modeling with Reasoning-Augmented Memory

claims.claim: Organizing historical VLM outputs into global-history, local-active, and event-boundary long short-term memory (rather than only recent-frame short-term memory) improves progress-aware retrieval and long-horizon autonomous planning and fine-grained instruction following
claims.direction: structured long+short-term observation history/memory favored over short-context-only conditioning for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world platforms, large-scale world-action-model pretrained on ~5M event segments

title: NAC: Neural Action Codec for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: An audio-codec-inspired residual-vector-quantization action tokenizer (Neural Action Codec) achieves lower reconstruction error and higher success rates than binning, FAST, and prior VQ-based action tokenizers at comparable or better compression, across LIBERO-10, RoboMimic, and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: learned RVQ-based discrete action tokenization favored over naive binning and prior VQ/FAST tokenizers for autoregressive VLA action heads
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO-10, RoboMimic) + real-world manipulation tasks, autoregressive VLA policy

why_deep_read: Directly targets Q01 (discrete/VQ token action representation) with a controlled comparison against binning/FAST/VQ baselines across sim+real tasks; full text ablations on tokenizer design and compression/latency tradeoffs could inform whether discrete tokenization is worth the complexity for our small low-data setup.

title: SWIM: Vision-Language-Grounded Soft Whole-Body Interactive Manipulation

claims.claim: Executing generated action-command sequences via iterative virtual rollout with intrinsic mechanical compliance (rather than direct online policy deployment) improved hardware success rates from 75/40/25% (direct online deployment) to 100/80/75% (packing/reaching/grasping)
claims.direction: open-loop chunk execution with embodied/mechanical compliance favored over closed-loop online policy queries for this platform
claims.conditions: real tendon-driven soft/continuum robot hardware, diffusion action head VLA policy, limited demonstrations

claims.claim: A diffusion action head combined with a visual soft-proprioception auxiliary supervision signal outperforms an adapted OpenVLA-OFT baseline and controlled ablations in simulation (100%/96%/88% vs baseline)
claims.direction: diffusion action head + auxiliary proprioception supervision favored over adapted large VLA baseline
claims.conditions: simulation, planar tendon-driven soft robot, limited demonstrations

title: RaC: Robot Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks by Scaling Recovery and Correction

claims.claim: Fine-tuning an imitation-pretrained policy on human intervention data illustrating recovery-and-correction behavior (rewind to in-distribution state + corrective completion) outperforms standard imitation learning by over 2x on long-horizon tasks, while requiring roughly 10x less data collection time and fewer samples than the best known prior method
claims.direction: recovery/correction demonstrations strongly favored over pure expert demonstrations for long-horizon robustness and data efficiency
claims.conditions: 3 real-world bimanual tasks (shirt hanging, lid sealing, takeout box packing) + 1 simulated assembly task, human-in-the-loop intervention data collection

why_deep_read: Directly addresses Q13's 'recovery demos' question with a controlled comparison (2x over standard IL, 10x less data collection time) on real bimanual tasks; full text on how interventions are timed/labeled and how much recovery data is needed relative to base demos would directly inform our 50-100 demo budget and failure-recovery strategy.

title: AutoFocus-IL: VLM-based Saliency Maps for Data-Efficient Visual Imitation Learning without Extra Human Annotations

claims.claim: Regularizing behavior-cloning policies with VLM-generated temporal saliency maps (highlighting task-relevant objects, suppressing distractors) improves data efficiency and generalization, outperforming both standard BC and prior SOTA methods that use privileged human gaze supervision
claims.direction: automatic VLM-based saliency/attention regularization favored over standard BC and even over gaze-supervised baselines for robustness to distractors
claims.conditions: CARLA simulator + real-robot manipulation tasks, no extra human annotation required

title: Compose by Focus: Scene Graph-based Atomic Skills

claims.claim: A scene-graph representation focusing on task-relevant objects/relations (combined with GNN + diffusion imitation learning) mitigates visuomotor policy failures under distribution shifts induced by scene composition, achieving substantially higher success rates than SOTA baselines on long-horizon compositional tasks
claims.direction: structured scene-graph visual representation favored over raw end-to-end visual encoding for robustness to scene composition changes
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks, diffusion-based imitation learning with GNN + VLM planner

title: VLA-Bridge: A Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Framework for Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Modeling

claims.claim: A dynamic cross-modal low-rank adapter projecting visual/language tokens into a compact shared action-latent space achieves performance on par with full fine-tuning while reducing trainable parameters by two orders of magnitude and decreasing inference latency significantly
claims.direction: parameter-efficient adapter-based fine-tuning favored over full fine-tuning for resource-constrained/edge deployment without performance loss
claims.conditions: established embodied benchmarks (setting real/sim not specified in abstract), targeting edge/resource-constrained robotic hardware

title: ConLA: Contrastive Latent Action Learning from Human Videos for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A contrastive disentanglement mechanism isolating motion dynamics from visual content when learning latent actions from unlabeled human videos avoids shortcut learning of prior VQ-VAE latent-action methods; pretraining solely on human videos surpasses, for the first time, pretraining on real robot trajectories
claims.direction: human-video-only pretraining (with contrastive disentanglement) favored over real-robot-trajectory pretraining for representation quality
claims.conditions: diverse benchmarks (setting not fully specified in abstract, appears sim/mixed), unsupervised pretraining framework

title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs

claims.claim: A VLA that self-acquires new primitive skills via VLM-guided rollouts (without full-task human demonstrations for each new task) achieves 92% and 96% success on newly acquired twisting and pouring skills on hardware, versus 32% and 16% for a zero-shot VLM-planner baseline; composing acquired skills into a 14-primitive task reaches 80% success with no combined-task demonstrations
claims.direction: self-guided primitive acquisition (reusing known primitives + targeted new-primitive data collection) favored over requiring full human demonstrations per new task, and over zero-shot VLM-only control
claims.conditions: 6 simulated and real-world tasks, hardware evaluation included, no human demos of target skills

title: SnapFlow: One-Step Action Generation for Flow-Matching VLAs via Progressive Self-Distillation

claims.claim: Self-distilling a flow-matching VLA's multi-step (10-step ODE) denoising into a single forward pass reduces end-to-end latency from 274ms to 83ms on pi0.5 (3B) while matching/slightly exceeding the 10-step teacher's success rate (98.75% vs 97.75% avg on 4 LIBERO suites, 40 tasks); on SmolVLA (500M) it achieves 3.56x end-to-end acceleration with 8.3% MSE reduction, and denoising was measured to account for 80% of end-to-end inference time before distillation
claims.direction: one-step distilled flow-matching action generation favored over standard multi-step denoising for latency, with no success-rate cost
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark, tested on pi0/pi0.5/SmolVLA architectures spanning a 6x parameter range, single-GPU distillation (~12h)

claims.claim: Naively reducing ODE step count in flow-matching policies is unreliable and degrades success on most tasks because the velocity field is uncalibrated for single-step jumps; a self-distillation scheme with consistency targets from two-step Euler shortcuts fixes this
claims.direction: trained one-step distillation favored over naive step-reduction for flow-matching action heads
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim, flow-matching VLA architectures including SmolVLA (directly matches our baseline model)

why_deep_read: Directly measures latency and accuracy on SmolVLA, our current baseline model, addressing our exact ~2s inference latency and chunk-boundary jerkiness problem; full text ablations on distillation procedure and its effect on execution-horizon smoothness would be directly actionable for our setup.

title: Learning from Mixed-Quality Deployment Experience for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A predictive chunk-level critic that converts action-chunk Q-values into discrete quality conditions to guide a diffusion actor allows learning from naturally accumulated mixed-quality (successes, partial progress, failures) autonomous rollouts without human corrections, consistently improving over the pretrained policy and outperforming strong imitation learning and offline RL baselines
claims.direction: quality-conditioned learning from mixed-quality post-deployment data favored over treating all rollouts as equal supervision (naive imitation) or standard offline RL
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world robot manipulation tasks, diffusion actor with chunk-level critic, post-deployment setting (no extra human intervention)

title: AxisGuide: Grounding Robot Action Coordinate System in RGB Observations for Robust Visuomotor Manipulation

claims.claim: Even with identical scene layout, camera viewpoint, and illumination, visuomotor policies degrade substantially when objects are placed at unseen locations; this is attributed to insufficient grounding of the action coordinate system in image space rather than semantic scene understanding failures
claims.direction: identifies action-coordinate grounding (not scene semantics) as the bottleneck for position/location generalization failures
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation + real-world environments, standard large-scale behavior-cloned visuomotor policies

claims.claim: Rendering the robot's base-frame action axes (+x/+y/+z) onto RGB observations as additional cue channels (using camera parameters and end-effector pose) yields substantial performance gains and improved generalization for visuomotor policies, as a lightweight add-on requiring no architecture change
claims.direction: explicit visual action-coordinate grounding cues favored as a cheap way to improve action-space interpretability/generalization
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim + real-world, lightweight guidance method added to existing behavior-cloned policies

why_deep_read: Directly targets a failure mode we care about (policy breaking when object/camera position shifts slightly) with a cheap, architecture-agnostic fix (rendered coordinate-axis cues); full text would clarify exact success-rate deltas and whether this transfers to a small low-cost 6-DoF arm with fixed+wrist camera.

title: SurgVIL: Scaling Surgical Robot Imitation Learning with Open-source Surgical Videos

claims.claim: Augmenting kinematically-labeled phantom robot demonstrations with weakly-labeled (estimated kinematics) open-source video data substantially improves generalization to real-tissue and out-of-distribution settings, across ACT, pi0, and GR00T-H policy backbones
claims.direction: mixing weakly-labeled video data with accurately-labeled demonstrations favored over demonstrations alone for OOD generalization
claims.conditions: real da Vinci surgical robot, 2 tasks (needle pick-up, cholecystectomy cutting), different domain (surgical) but generalizable data-scaling insight

title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning

claims.claim: Representing long-horizon memory as compact segment-level plans (language + sparse visual context) rather than repeatedly conditioning the executor on full raw history achieves 83.3% success on RMBench and 78.0% on real-robot tasks while keeping executor inference latency approximately constant as task history grows
claims.direction: structured plan-as-memory (segment-level, fixed executor context) favored over growing-window/full-history conditioning for long-horizon non-Markovian tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks + RMBench simulation benchmark, requires KV-caching-compatible architecture

title: Imperfection for Precision: Upcycling Imperfect Data for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining low-precision, target-task data (used at high noise levels) with high-precision but task-mismatched data (used at low noise levels) along the flow-matching trajectory improves policy performance by up to 31.7 percentage points versus using low-precision data alone, and can replace an equal amount of task-specific high-quality data with only an average 4.2 percentage point performance drop
claims.direction: strategically mixing imperfect/mismatched data by noise-level in flow-matching training favored over requiring uniformly high-quality task-specific data
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments, sub-millimeter high-precision tasks and coarse-grained tasks, flow-matching VLA

why_deep_read: Gives a concrete, quantified strategy (noise-level-conditioned data mixing) for substituting costly high-quality demos with cheaper imperfect data on real-robot precision tasks; directly relevant to our constrained 50-100 demo budget and whether we can supplement with lower-quality/off-task data.

title: Offline-to-online Reinforcement Learning for Image-based Grasping with Scarce Demonstrations
