claims.claim: With only 50 real human teleop demonstrations for an image-based grasping task, standard behavior cloning fails the majority of the time (distribution shift), but an offline-to-online RL algorithm (replacing target network with a neural-tangent-kernel-inspired regularizer) reaches above 90% success rate after under two hours of additional real-world interaction
claims.direction: offline-to-online RL fine-tuning favored over pure behavior cloning when demonstration count is scarce (~50 demos)
claims.conditions: real-life image-based robotic vacuum grasping task, exactly 50 human demonstrations

why_deep_read: Uses the exact demo count regime we plan for (50 demos) on a real image-based grasping task and reports a concrete BC-failure/RL-fix comparison; full text on task difficulty, camera setup, and RL fine-tuning cost would clarify whether this is feasible on our laptop-GPU low-cost arm setup.

title: AffordDP: Generalizable Diffusion Policy with Transferable Affordance

claims.claim: Modeling affordances (3D contact points + post-contact trajectories) and using foundation-model-based point cloud registration to transfer them to novel object instances/categories, with affordance-guided diffusion sampling, consistently outperforms previous diffusion-policy baselines when generalizing to unseen object instances and categories, where prior methods fail
claims.direction: affordance-guided diffusion policy favored over standard diffusion policies (with only improved visual encoders) for generalization to novel objects
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world environments, requires 3D point clouds + foundation vision models for affordance transfer

claims.claim: 3D contact-point/affordance representations (derived via point cloud registration) provide the generalization signal that plain RGB-based visual feature improvements do not, for cross-category object generalization
claims.direction: 3D/point-cloud-based affordance representation favored over RGB-only visual feature improvement for novel-object generalization
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly targets our 'different-looking pumpkin' generalization failure with a real-world-tested affordance/point-cloud method; full text would clarify how much 3D data and foundation-model compute this requires versus our RGB-only, laptop-GPU budget, and whether a lighter-weight version of the idea is feasible.

title: AnchorDream: Repurposing Video Diffusion for Embodiment-Aware Robot Data Synthesis

claims.claim: Conditioning a pretrained video diffusion model on robot motion renderings (to anchor embodiment and prevent hallucination) allows scaling a handful of human teleoperation demonstrations into large, diverse, high-quality synthetic datasets, yielding relative gains of 36.4% in simulator benchmarks and nearly double performance in real-world studies for downstream policy learning
claims.direction: embodiment-anchored generative video synthesis favored over collecting more real demonstrations or using standard simulators for scaling training data
claims.conditions: starts from only a handful of real human teleoperation demonstrations, evaluated in both simulator benchmarks and real-world studies

why_deep_read: Directly proposes a low-demo-count data scaling strategy (generative augmentation from a handful of demos) with quantified real-world gains, which is highly relevant to our 50-100 demo budget; full text would clarify compute cost of the video diffusion model and whether it's feasible on a single laptop GPU.

title: Let Me Show You: Learning by Retrieving from Egocentric Video for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Retrieving task-relevant human egocentric video (with extracted affordance masks and hand-motion trajectories as extra policy inputs) improves manipulation performance and generalization to tasks beyond the training set, versus conventional robotic systems without such retrieval
claims.direction: external human-video retrieval augmentation favored over training on robot demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: multiple simulated and real-world settings; qualitative 'marked improvement', no specific numbers given

title: SERNF: Sample-Efficient Real-World Dexterous Policy Fine-Tuning via Action-Chunked Critics and Normalizing Flows

claims.claim: Diffusion-based action policies do not permit conservative likelihood-based fine-tuning updates because action probabilities are intractable, whereas conventional Gaussian policies collapse under multimodality especially with chunked execution; a normalizing-flow policy yields exact likelihoods for multimodal action chunks, enabling stable conservative fine-tuning where standard methods struggle
claims.direction: normalizing-flow action head favored over diffusion (for likelihood-based fine-tuning) and over Gaussian policies (for multimodality) in the real-world RL fine-tuning setting
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, 2 tasks (scissor cutting, in-hand cube rotation), limited real-world interaction budget

claims.claim: An action-chunked critic (evaluating entire action sequences rather than per-step) aligns value estimation with chunked policy execution and improves long-horizon credit assignment versus standard per-step critics
claims.direction: chunk-level critic favored over per-step critic when policy executes actions in chunks
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation hardware

title: Gentle Manipulation of Long-Horizon Tasks Without Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Distilling compliant long-horizon manipulation policies from VLM-generated (rather than human) expert demonstration datasets via diffusion-based imitation learning enables successful real-robot deployment; the paper evaluates multiple control modes and distillation strategies with quantitative validation across diverse simulated long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: diffusion policy distillation from VLM/RL-generated synthetic demonstrations favored as a substitute for human demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation training + real robot deployment, tactile-sensing-integrated gentle manipulation

title: SA-VLA: Spatially-Aware Flow-Matching for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: RL fine-tuning of flow-matching VLA policies commonly degrades robustness under spatial distribution shifts because sparse rewards and spatially agnostic exploration erode spatial inductive bias, favoring short-horizon visual cues; preserving spatial grounding (via fused spatial representations, dense geometric-progress rewards, and spatially-conditioned exploration) improves zero-shot spatial generalization on multi-object/cluttered benchmarks
claims.direction: spatially-aware RL adaptation favored over naive RL fine-tuning for maintaining spatial generalization
claims.conditions: challenging multi-object and cluttered manipulation benchmarks (setting not fully specified, appears simulation)

title: LAP: Language-Action Pre-training Enables Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Transfer

claims.claim: Representing low-level robot actions directly in natural language (rather than a learned tokenizer/discretization) to supervise a vision-language backbone (LAP-3B) achieves over 50% average zero-shot success on previously unseen single-arm manipulators, roughly 2x improvement over the strongest prior VLAs, and up to 52% vs 0% for a SOTA VLA baseline on a specific cross-embodiment transfer test
claims.direction: natural-language action representation favored over learned action tokenizers for cross-embodiment generalization
claims.conditions: multiple novel real single-arm manipulators and manipulation tasks, large VLA model (3B), zero-shot (no per-embodiment fine-tuning)

title: Analytic Concept-Centric Memory for Agentic Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: Organizing memory around structured analytic concepts (semantic parts, parametric templates, grounded poses, affordances, manipulation states, plus transition/skill memory) with coarse-to-fine retrieval improves task completion, retrieval accuracy, object re-identification, and cross-object skill generalization over unstructured and embedding-based memory baselines
claims.direction: structured concept-centric memory favored over unstructured/embedding-based history representations for long-horizon memory-dependent manipulation
claims.conditions: memory-dependent manipulation, articulated-object generalization, real-world memory evaluation + ablations

title: Hermite Curves as Trajectory Priors for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Parameterizing each action chunk as a piecewise cubic Hermite curve (endpoint positions+velocities) applied as an auxiliary training regularization (not a runtime constraint) improves a pi0.5 baseline's success rate from 95.9% to 98.7% on LIBERO, 85.7% to 90.9% on LIBERO-plus, and 63.4% to 90.0% averaged across four real-robot tasks, with no additional inference overhead; flattening chunks into per-timestep controls without such priors causes jagged motion and boundary discontinuities
claims.direction: explicit smoothness/continuity trajectory prior (as training-time inductive bias) strongly favored over unconstrained per-timestep chunk prediction for reducing jagged motion and boundary discontinuities
claims.conditions: LIBERO + LIBERO-plus simulation and 4 real-robot tasks, applied to pi0.5 flow-matching/diffusion-style VLA, zero added inference cost

why_deep_read: Directly targets our observed jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries with a concrete, zero-inference-cost training regularizer and large real-robot success-rate gains (63.4%->90.0%); full text on how the Hermite regularization is implemented and how sensitive the gains are to model/chunk size would let us adopt it directly for our SmolVLA-style chunked policy.

title: Recovering Aggressively Pruned Vision-Language-Action Models with Offline Hidden-State Distillation

claims.claim: Removing 63% of OpenVLA-OFT's language backbone drops LIBERO-Long success from 93.2% to 0.8%; offline hidden-state distillation (matching teacher/student hidden states directly via width pruning, no online RL) recovers the model to within 3.5 points of the teacher in about 8 GPU-hours, versus prior online RL recovery needing hundreds of GPU-hours; gains from distillation grow with pruning ratio (+2.1 to +22.1 points depending on model/ratio)
claims.direction: width pruning + offline hidden-state distillation favored over supervised-only recovery or online-RL recovery for producing small, high-performing VLA models
claims.conditions: OpenVLA-OFT and CogACT VLA backbones, LIBERO-Long sim benchmark

claims.claim: On a real 6-DoF manipulator, a distilled student model at 72% parameter reduction reaches 77.5% success (vs 59.5% for supervised-only recovery), runs 2.23x faster onboard than the teacher, and uses 62% less memory; at matched compression, width pruning yields higher success while depth pruning yields lower latency
claims.direction: width-pruned + hidden-state-distilled small VLA favored for real-robot onboard speed/memory with acceptable success, over larger teacher or supervised-recovery baselines
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF manipulator hardware, pruned+distilled VLA model

title: AdaManip: Adaptive Articulated Object Manipulation Environments and Policy Learning

claims.claim: An adaptive demonstration collection pipeline combined with 3D visual diffusion-based imitation learning enables learning manipulation policies for articulated objects whose internal state (e.g., lock status) cannot be inferred from a single visual observation, requiring trial-and-error adaptive demonstrations rather than one-shot visual inference; effectiveness validated in both simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: adaptive (trial-and-error-informed) demonstration collection + 3D diffusion IL favored over standard one-shot-inference demonstration collection for objects with hidden internal state
claims.conditions: 9 categories of articulated objects, simulation + real-world

title: SPIDER: Scalable Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting

claims.claim: Physics-based retargeting that augments kinematic-only human demonstrations with curriculum-style virtual contact guidance (rather than standard sampling) improves downstream policy success rates by 18% while being 10x faster than RL baselines, enabling generation of a 2.4M-frame dynamically-feasible dataset from human motion data across 9 embodiments and 6 datasets

claims.conditions: dexterous hand/humanoid embodiments (not arm+gripper), simulation-based physics refinement of human motion capture/video data

title: From Code to Action: Hierarchical Learning of Diffusion-VLM Policies

claims.claim: A hierarchical architecture with a memory mechanism maintaining subtask context across time (for non-Markovian tasks like object swapping), combined with a code-generating VLM decomposing tasks into subroutines grounded by a low-level diffusion policy, improves generalization compared to flat (non-hierarchical) policies
claims.direction: hierarchical policy with explicit subtask memory favored over flat end-to-end policies for non-Markovian, long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: imitation learning for robotic manipulation, setting (real/sim) not specified in abstract

title: Improving Policy Learning via Language-Guided State Representation in World Models

claims.claim: Using language-based task descriptions as priors to guide state-representation encoding within a world model (suppressing task-irrelevant information under limited representation capacity) significantly improves the efficiency and success rate of downstream policy learning versus representations without language guidance
claims.direction: language-guided state representation favored over language-agnostic state representation in world-model-based policy learning
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark (simulation), multi-task language-conditioned manipulation

title: UAOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A training-free, plug-and-play module that reinjects key visual observation information into FFN layers only at high-uncertainty (high action-entropy) decision points consistently improves diverse VLA models across simulation and real-world tasks with minimal overhead, without requiring extra observation modalities like depth maps or point clouds or additional auxiliary encoders
claims.direction: targeted, uncertainty-triggered observation reinjection favored over adding extra sensing modalities (depth/point clouds) or auxiliary encoder modules to improve VLA precision
claims.conditions: multiple VLA models, simulation and real-world tasks, training-free plug-in

title: Sim-to-Real Diffusion Policies for Robotic Alignment in Manufacturing

claims.claim: A semantic-consistent visual preprocessing pipeline (segmentation + recoloring to align real observations with simulation) combined with a diffusion-based visuomotor policy achieves high success rates and strong robustness across diverse geometries and perturbations, including improved robustness under lighting variations and occlusions
claims.direction: semantic-consistent sim-real visual alignment (segmentation/recoloring) favored over raw RGB matching for robustness to lighting variation and occlusion
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world push-based manipulation, contact-rich manufacturing/alignment tasks

title: ROEP: A Robotics-Oriented Evaluation Protocol for Deployment-Facing Vision-Language-Action Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Applying a deployment-oriented evaluation protocol (clean vs. medium visual perturbation conditions, repeated-run variability, timeout-failure analysis) to OpenVLA, X-VLA, and VLA-Adapter on LIBERO Goal/Object tasks finds VLA-Adapter maintains strong clean Goal-suite performance but shows a substantial clean-to-perturbation success drop on the Object suite, dominated by timeout terminations, while runtime-interface fidelity/checkpoint provenance materially affect measured X-VLA/OpenVLA Object results
claims.direction: highlights that different VLA architectures degrade very differently (and sometimes are measured unreliably) under visual perturbation, cautioning against relying on single-condition success-rate comparisons
claims.conditions: LIBERO Goal and Object simulation tasks only, no real robot

title: ActionDiT: A Causal Diffusion Transformer Policy for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A causal diffusion transformer that represents the entire action trajectory as a unified token sequence with AdaLN conditioning (rather than U-Net or encoder-decoder transformer diffusion architectures adapted from other domains) achieves higher success rates and more stable performance than existing imitation learning and diffusion-based policy baselines on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: causal transformer-based diffusion architecture (purpose-built for sequential control) favored over U-Net/encoder-decoder diffusion architectures for long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: benchmark datasets + real-world robotic tasks (tool-based pushing, pick-and-place, 6-DoF pouring, long-horizon stacking)

title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch

claims.claim: An action-centered world-action-model formulation that uses future-visual-dynamics supervision only during training (not at inference) and a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture separating visual-dynamics and action experts achieves 85ms inference latency on an RTX 4090, while preserving the training benefits of future-video supervision that competing approaches only get by generating videos at inference (incurring substantial overhead)
claims.direction: training-time-only world-model supervision with action-only inference favored over explicit video generation at inference time for real-time closed-loop deployment
claims.conditions: local RTX 4090 setup, world-action-model robot policy

title: Making two action heads agree: coordination mechanisms and a runtime collapse certificate for flow-matching policies

claims.claim: A dual-representation flow-matching policy that decodes each predicted motion into both joint and end-effector spaces provides a physically interpretable runtime residual signal for detecting policy failure/collapse, but on multimodal tasks benign multimodality (independently valid different modes chosen by each branch) adds 1.57 percentage points of false alarms on LIBERO-Plus, which remains the strongest evaluated failure-detection signal despite this

claims.conditions: two robot environments + one non-robotic testbed, LIBERO-Plus benchmark, flow-matching policy architecture

title: RetoVLA: Reusing Register Tokens for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Repurposing existing Vision Transformer register tokens (normally discarded, originally added to mitigate attention artifacts) as a dense global spatial-context signal fed into the action-planning module recovers 3D spatial reasoning lost during model compression, without increasing total parameter count, yielding a 17.1 percentage point improvement in average success rate over baseline on a real 7-DOF manipulator

title: See Once, Then Act: Vision-Language-Action Model with Task Learning from One-Shot Video Demonstrations

claims.claim: A generalist VLA (ViVLA) that jointly processes a single expert demonstration video plus the robot's own observations at test time, trained on a large synthesized expert-agent paired dataset (892,911 samples from human videos + curated public datasets), acquires novel manipulation skills from only one demonstration video, achieving over 30% improvement on unseen LIBERO tasks, 35%+ gains with cross-embodiment videos, and 38%+ improvement on unseen real-world tasks
claims.direction: test-time one-shot video imitation (enabled by large-scale paired pretraining) favored over requiring task-specific fine-tuning demonstrations for novel tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim + real-world experiments, requires large paired-data pretraining pipeline (not itself low-data)

title: Provable Ordering and Continuity in Vision-Language Pretraining for Generalizable Embodied Agents

claims.claim: Pretraining vision-language representations on human action videos using Action Temporal Coherence Learning (contrasting semantic frame differences plus a local Brownian-bridge smoothness constraint, instead of goal-reaching time-contrastive learning) significantly enhances downstream manipulation performance and robustness to different linguistic styles of instructions, versus standard goal-based time-contrastive pretraining
claims.direction: temporally-coherent/continuous vision-language pretraining objective favored over goal-reaching time-contrastive pretraining for downstream imitation learning robustness
claims.conditions: simulated and real robots, imitation learning downstream tasks

title: ARMimic: Learning Robotic Manipulation from Passive Human Demonstrations in Augmented Reality

claims.claim: Collecting demonstrations via a lightweight XR-headset-based passive human observation pipeline (egocentric hand tracking + AR robot overlay + depth sensing, treating human and virtual-robot trajectories as interchangeable) reduces demonstration collection time by 50% compared to teleoperation and improves task success by 11% over ACT (a SOTA baseline trained on teleoperated data)
claims.direction: passive XR-based human demonstration collection favored over teleoperation for both collection efficiency and downstream policy success, including on a challenging long-horizon bowl-stacking task
claims.conditions: 2 real manipulation tasks including long-horizon bowl stacking, comparison against ACT trained on teleoperated data

title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification

claims.claim: Exploiting the natural alternation between 'active' states (requiring precise action) and 'inactive' states (where actions matter less) in manipulation enables long-action-length speculative prediction during inactive states with selective verification during active states; on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill, this significantly reduces end-to-end latency while preserving task success rate
claims.direction: state-aware speculative decoding (exploiting active/inactive state alternation) favored over uniform per-step inference for reducing VLA latency without success-rate loss
claims.conditions: LIBERO and ManiSkill simulation benchmarks, OpenVLA/RDT backbones, requires a heterogeneous GPU + robotic-specific hardware module (custom accelerator)

title: VLA Knows Its Limits

claims.claim: Varying the execution horizon (number of actions executed per predicted chunk) in flow-based VLAs causes substantial performance deviations -- performance first improves then declines as horizon increases; attention analysis shows intra-chunk actions attend invariantly to vision-language tokens (limiting adaptability to environmental changes) while initial/terminal action tokens act as stable anchors organizing intermediate actions

claims.conditions: simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, flow-based VLA models

claims.claim: AutoHorizon, a test-time method using action self-attention weights as a proxy for the model's predictive limit, dynamically estimates the execution horizon per predicted chunk to adapt to changing perceptual conditions, with negligible computational overhead, generalizing across diverse tasks and flow-based models
claims.direction: dynamic/adaptive execution horizon (test-time, attention-based) favored over a fixed execution horizon for chunked action-chunking policies
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, flow-based VLA models, negligible added inference cost

why_deep_read: Directly targets our exact Q06 problem (jerky motion at chunk boundaries from async execution horizon choice) with an attention-based analysis of why fixed horizons fail and a practical negligible-overhead fix (AutoHorizon) validated on real robots; full text would give the actual horizon-vs-performance curve and implementation detail we could adapt for SmolVLA-style async inference.

title: Multi-View Unified Camera Fields: Geometry-Shaped Action-Facing Representations for RGB-Only Multi-Camera VLA Policies

claims.claim: A training-only framework that adds a coordinate-query depth objective and a cross-view correspondence objective during training (removed at deployment, so inference stays RGB-only with no extra FLOPs) recovers metric-depth-aware, cross-view-consistent representations for multi-camera VLA policies; under matched GR00T-N1.6 settings this reaches 98.9% on LIBERO, +22.4 points on LIBERO-Plus, and +23.3 points across six RoboTwin tasks versus naive multi-view token concatenation
claims.direction: training-time-only geometric/depth supervision (with RGB-only deployment) favored over either adding explicit depth sensors/inputs at inference or naively concatenating multi-camera view tokens without geometric grounding
claims.conditions: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin simulation benchmarks + real-world humanoid experiments, RGB-only multi-camera VLA deployment

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our two-camera (scene+wrist) RGB setup: shows how to get depth/cross-view geometric grounding benefits without adding inference-time compute or extra sensors, which matters a lot for our 8GB-GPU latency budget; full text would clarify the training procedure cost and whether it needs ground-truth depth (we do have a RealSense) or camera calibration only.

title: Beyond Data Scaling: Representation-Centric Continued Pre-training for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Under a fixed robot-data budget, representation-centric continued pre-training (preserving broad VLM prior, multi-head continuous action co-supervision, partially unified cross-embodiment action layout) consistently improves downstream VLA performance more than merely scaling task-specific data; on RoboCasa-GR1 (unseen humanoid embodiment) the approach using only 20% of downstream trajectories outperforms a full-data GR00T-N1.6 baseline, achieved with a modest 16-GPU training budget
claims.direction: representation-quality-focused continued pretraining favored over raw downstream-data scaling for sample efficiency and cross-embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa-GR1 simulation benchmarks + real-world, modest (16-GPU) compute budget relative to typical VLA training

title: CORN: Contact-based Object Representation for Nonprehensile Manipulation of General Unseen Objects

claims.claim: A contact-based object representation learned from point clouds via a lightweight patch-based transformer encoder (enabling massively parallel RL training across thousands of environments) facilitates more time- and data-efficient learning than training from scratch or other shape-representation baselines, and zero-shot transfers to novel real-world objects
claims.direction: point-cloud-based contact representation favored over learning shape representations from scratch or simpler baselines for generalizing to unseen object geometries
claims.conditions: RL-trained nonprehensile manipulation, real-world zero-shot transfer to novel objects

title: Behavior Generation with Latent Actions

claims.claim: VQ-BeT (hierarchical vector-quantization tokenization of continuous actions, replacing BeT's k-means discretization) improves over both Behavior Transformer (BeT) and Diffusion Policies across seven environments including simulated manipulation, autonomous driving, and robotics, better capturing multimodal behavior while using gradient-based (not k-means) discretization that scales to high-dimensional/long action sequences
claims.direction: learned hierarchical VQ action tokenization favored over both k-means-based discrete tokenization (BeT) and diffusion-based continuous action generation for multimodal behavior modeling
claims.conditions: 7 environments spanning simulated manipulation, autonomous driving, and robotics

claims.claim: VQ-BeT accelerates inference speed by 5x over Diffusion Policies while improving the ability to capture behavior modes
claims.direction: VQ-token action head favored over diffusion action head for inference latency, without sacrificing (and while improving) multimodal capture
claims.conditions: same 7-environment evaluation suite

why_deep_read: A foundational, widely-cited controlled comparison of discrete VQ action tokenization vs diffusion vs k-means-based (BeT) action heads with a direct 5x latency advantage over diffusion, central to our Q01 action-head decision and Q10 latency concern; full text ablations on tokenization granularity and multimodality capture would help decide between VQ-tokens and diffusion/flow-matching for our small-model, low-latency setup.

title: MLA: A Multisensory Language-Action Model for Multimodal Understanding and Forecasting in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: An encoder-free multimodal alignment scheme that repurposes the LLM itself to jointly interpret 2D images, 3D point clouds, and tactile tokens (aligned by positional correspondence), combined with a future multisensory generation post-training objective, outperforms the previous SOTA 2D VLA method by 12% and the previous SOTA 3D VLA method by 24% on complex, contact-rich real-world tasks, with improved generalization to unseen configurations
claims.direction: joint 2D+3D+tactile multisensory representation favored over either 2D-only or 3D-only VLA representations
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensing hardware not present in a pure RGB setup

title: Align-Then-stEer: Adapting the Vision-Language Action Models through Unified Latent Guidance

claims.claim: A data-efficient, plug-and-play adaptation framework (Align-Then-stEer/ATE) that aligns disparate action spaces via a KL-constrained VAE latent space and steers a diffusion/flow-based VLA's generation during fine-tuning improves average multi-task success rate by up to 9.8% in simulation and achieves a 32% success rate gain in a real-world cross-embodiment setting, compared to direct fine-tuning of representative VLAs
claims.direction: latent-space action alignment + guided fine-tuning favored over direct fine-tuning when adapting a pretrained VLA to a new embodiment/task with limited data
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment and cross-task manipulation, simulation + real-world, applies to diffusion- or flow-based VLA backbones

why_deep_read: Directly addresses data-efficient adaptation of a pretrained diffusion/flow VLA (like SmolVLA) to a new embodiment/task with large real-world gains (32%) using a lightweight, plug-and-play method; full text on the VAE alignment procedure and required amount of adaptation data would be directly actionable for fine-tuning our own low-cost-arm setup with only 50-100 demos.

title: KEMO: Event-Driven Keyframe Memory for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation with VLA Policies

claims.claim: A lightweight plug-in memory that selectively preserves keyframes tied to detected task-relevant state changes (via kinematics + visual event filtering), encoded as compact temporally-ordered tokens fused via cross-attention, improves aggregate Task Success Rate by 23.6% and Stage Completion Rate by 34.1% over a memory-free pi0.5 baseline on real-world long-horizon dual-arm tasks (830-2846 execution steps); ablations show event-driven keyframe selection outperforms both uniform sampling and recent-frame-only retention
claims.direction: event-driven sparse keyframe memory favored over both memory-free (Markovian) policies and naive dense/recent-frame history retention for long-horizon disambiguation
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm manipulation, long-horizon multi-subtask tasks (2-6 subtasks), pi0.5 backbone

title: CoVA-IL: Zero-Shot Imitation Learning via Contrastive Viewpoint Alignment on Object-Centric Representation

claims.claim: Learning viewpoint-invariant latent representations via contrastive alignment on the target object's point cloud (rather than raw RGB/global features) allows zero-shot policy deployment in novel environments without retraining; real-world experiments maintain average task success rates of 82.5% and 80% under substantial background and viewpoint changes respectively, and the method works from a small number of real demonstrations
claims.direction: object-centric, viewpoint-invariant point-cloud representation favored over standard (viewpoint-entangled) visual representations for robustness to camera/viewpoint and background shift
claims.conditions: real-world tabletop manipulation (pick-and-place, tool use), multi-scene evaluation, requires accurate depth sensing and reliable target-object extraction; degrades in cluttered/multi-object scenes

why_deep_read: Directly targets our 'slightly moved camera' and background-shift failure mode with quantified real-world success rates (82.5%/80%) and explicitly states it reduces demonstrations needed; full text would clarify how much depth/point-cloud quality is required (we have a RealSense) and whether it works for small-object clutter like a pumpkin+tray scene.

title: AnyCamVLA: Zero-Shot Camera Adaptation for Viewpoint Robust Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Virtually re-rendering test-time camera observations to match the training camera configuration (via a feed-forward novel-view-synthesis model, no fine-tuning or extra demonstrations required) consistently outperforms both data-augmentation-based fine-tuning and additional-3D-feature baselines for viewpoint robustness on LIBERO, and enhances real-world viewpoint robustness including varying extrinsics/intrinsics and freely moving handheld cameras
claims.direction: test-time novel-view-synthesis camera normalization favored over policy fine-tuning with augmented data or added 3D-aware architecture features for viewpoint/camera-shift robustness
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation + real-world robotic manipulation, zero-shot (no additional demonstration data, fine-tuning, or architecture change), plug-and-play on any RGB-based policy

why_deep_read: Directly and cheaply addresses our 'slightly moved camera' failure mode without requiring new demonstrations or retraining, which is highly attractive given our small data budget; full text would clarify the compute cost/latency of the novel-view-synthesis step on our 8GB laptop GPU and whether it works with a single fixed camera plus wrist camera.

title: Pelican-VLA 0.5: Attending Before Acting Benefits Generalization

claims.claim: A learnable Bottleneck Token inserted between perception and action modules, trained via joint vision-language understanding, future-frame generation, and action prediction, induces manipulation-centric attention (focusing on the relevant object/contact region) without any object annotations, segmentation masks, or attention supervision, persisting across unseen scenes and unseen robot embodiments and substantially stronger than other open-source VLA baselines
claims.direction: bottleneck-token auxiliary architecture (with future-frame prediction) favored over standard VLA architectures for inducing task-relevant visual attention and generalization, without added supervision
claims.conditions: unified VLA architecture, tested across unseen scenes and embodiments (setting not fully specified, comparison vs other open-source VLA baselines)

title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: An action-conditioned routing interface that dynamically mixes cached VLM layer representations and reuses earlier action-module representations (rather than using fixed per-action-layer VLM assignments) improves StarVLA-pi and pi0.5 by up to 7.2 points on LIBERO-Long, using only 0.31%-3.87% additional parameters
claims.direction: dynamic, action-conditioned layer routing/reuse favored over fixed-layer VLM-to-action interfaces, for a large accuracy gain at minimal parameter cost
claims.conditions: diverse simulation and real-world benchmarks, applied to existing pretrained VLA backbones

title: From Imitation to Refinement - Residual RL for Precise Assembly

claims.claim: Behavior cloning performance on precision tasks saturates with increasing data due to (a) distribution shift from offline data and (b) the lack of closed-loop corrective control caused by action chunking (predicting future action sets executed open-loop), which makes chunked BC policies behave more like trajectory planners than reliable closed-loop controllers
claims.direction: identifies action chunking + open-loop execution as a root cause of BC's precision/reliability ceiling, independent of data quantity
claims.conditions: precision assembly tasks, chunked behavior-cloning policies

claims.claim: Augmenting a frozen, chunked BC model with a fully closed-loop residual policy trained via RL (Resip) overcomes the BC reliability ceiling for precision tasks while retaining BC's ease of teaching and long-horizon capability, by adding closed-loop corrections over the BC trajectory planner's open-loop chunk execution
claims.direction: BC (as coarse trajectory planner) + closed-loop residual RL correction favored over BC alone (open-loop chunk execution) for precision manipulation
claims.conditions: real-robot precision assembly tasks

why_deep_read: Directly diagnoses a root cause of exactly the kind of chunk-boundary/precision problems we observe (jerky, unreliable execution from open-loop action chunking) and proposes a concrete, retrofit-friendly fix (frozen BC + closed-loop residual RL); full text would clarify how much RL interaction/real-robot time is needed and whether the residual policy could run within our latency budget.

title: SpatialVLA: Exploring Spatial Representations for Visual-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Injecting 3D information into VLA visual inputs via Ego3D Position Encoding, combined with Adaptive Action Grids (adaptive discretized action representations) for cross-robot action spaces, enables a VLA pre-trained on 1.1M real-world robot episodes to achieve superior zero-shot cross-robot/cross-task generalization and strong in-domain multi-task performance versus prior spatial-representation choices
claims.direction: explicit 3D position encoding + adaptive discretized action grids favored over standard 2D-only visual input and fixed/continuous action representations for cross-robot spatial generalization
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining (1.1M real-world episodes) across multiple robots/tasks, evaluated in simulation and real-world, zero-shot and fine-tuned settings

claims.claim: Re-discretizing the pre-learned Adaptive Action Grids to a new robot's specific spatial action movements provides an effective and data-efficient way to fine-tune the pre-trained model for new simulation/real-world setups, showing strong in-distribution generalization and out-of-distribution adaptation
claims.direction: adaptive/re-discretizable action-grid representation favored over fixed continuous or fixed discretization schemes when adapting a generalist policy to a new robot embodiment
claims.conditions: new simulation and real-world robot setups, fine-tuning from a large pretrained spatial-VLA checkpoint

title: ManiLong-Shot: Interaction-Aware One-Shot Imitation Learning for Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Structuring long-horizon manipulation as a sequence of interaction-aware primitives (each learned via invariant-region matching from demonstrations) instead of directly imitating continuous trajectories allows training on only 10 short-horizon tasks to generalize via one-shot imitation to 20 unseen long-horizon tasks, achieving a 22.8% relative improvement over SOTA in simulation, with real-robot validation on three long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: primitive/interaction-event decomposition + one-shot per-primitive imitation favored over direct trajectory imitation for extending one-shot imitation learning to long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation (10 train tasks, 20 unseen long-horizon test tasks across 3 difficulty levels) + real-robot validation

title: Object-Centric Representations Improve Policy Generalization in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Benchmarking object-centric, global, and dense visual encoders across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks (simple to complex) shows object-centric representations (which segment visual input into a finite set of entities) outperform dense and global representations in generalization settings, even without task-specific pretraining
claims.direction: object-centric visual representation favored over dense/global visual features for policy generalization
claims.conditions: suite of simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, controlled encoder benchmark

claims.claim: OCR-based policies generalize better than dense/global representations specifically under diverse visual condition changes including lighting, texture changes, and the presence of distractors
claims.direction: object-centric representation favored over dense/global features for robustness to lighting, texture, and distractor shifts
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite, explicit evaluation under lighting/texture/distractor variation

why_deep_read: A controlled, direct benchmark of vision-encoder representation types (Q03) precisely under our observed failure conditions (lighting, texture/appearance changes, distractors -> Q14); full text would give the actual success-rate deltas and which object-centric method (e.g., slot attention vs segmentation-based) was used, to decide if it's adoptable on our 8GB-GPU two-camera low-cost setup.

title: Sample-Efficient Learning of a Robotic Tube Insertion Policy

claims.claim: Adding force/torque inputs, pretrained image encoders, layer normalization, and actor-critic network warmup to a contrastive-pretraining+data-augmentation+demonstrations+RL framework (CoDER) achieves 98.1% average insertion success across several different medical tube types with a policy trained on only a single tube type, using just 800 episodes (~6 hours) with sparse rewards
claims.direction: pretrained image encoders + contrastive pretraining + light architectural tweaks favored for sample-efficient real-robot RL that generalizes across object instances from single-instance training
claims.conditions: real robot, fine manipulation (tube insertion), 800 training episodes, category-level generalization from single training instance

title: MotionForge: A Data Generation Pipeline and Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon Manipulation of Dynamic Objects with Domain Shifts

claims.claim: Systematic evaluation of representative general-purpose robot policies under both single-factor (e.g. background-only) and joint domain shifts (simultaneous object+background+lighting+speed shifts) reveals substantial performance limitations specifically under joint domain shifts, exposing a critical gap between current policy capabilities and robustness requirements for dynamic manipulation
claims.direction: highlights that current general-purpose policies handle single-factor domain shifts far better than joint/combined shifts (e.g., simultaneous lighting+background+object change), which is directly relevant to compounded real-world shift
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, 40 dynamic interaction tasks / 17 long-horizon tasks, tests representative general-purpose robot policies

title: SPARC: Reliable Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations at Scale

claims.claim: Policies trained on spatial annotations (bounding boxes, object trajectories, phase labels) generated with a reliability-calibrated pipeline (leveraging spatio-temporal structure of robot tasks rather than raw detector confidence) outperform baselines in cluttered, visually ambiguous real-world scenes, while the pipeline retains three times more high-precision samples than detection-only annotation baselines
claims.direction: reliability-calibrated automatic spatial annotation favored over uncalibrated detector-confidence-based annotation for training policies robust to clutter/visual ambiguity
claims.conditions: 1.7k human-annotated demonstrations for benchmark validation, diverse embodiments, real-world cluttered scene evaluation

title: Stability-Guided Exploration for Diverse Motion Generation

claims.claim: Combining RRT-style search with sampling-based MPC and a stability-guided sampling scheme (sampling from a manifold of stable states while growing a search tree via simulation) discovers diverse long-horizon manipulation strategies (pushing, grasping, pivoting, throwing, tool use) across different robot morphologies without task-specific guidance, addressing the narrowness of human-teleoperated demonstration data
claims.direction: simulation-based stability-guided synthetic demonstration generation favored over relying solely on narrow, task-specific human teleoperation demonstrations for data diversity
claims.conditions: black-box simulation, multiple robot morphologies, no real-robot validation mentioned

title: ParticleSplat: Self-supervised Object-centric Latent Particle Splatting

claims.claim: A self-supervised object-centric 3D latent representation (particles transformed into particle-aligned 3D Gaussians via multi-view novel-view-synthesis training) inherently learns object masks without supervision and improves downstream performance on robotic manipulation tasks, versus the underlying 2D-only Deep Latent Particles representation it extends
claims.direction: 3D object-centric latent representation (via feedforward Gaussian Splatting) favored over 2D-only object-centric latent representations for downstream manipulation performance
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world datasets, self-supervised representation learning, requires multi-view training data with camera poses

title: CycleManip: Enabling Cyclic Task Manipulation via Effective Historical Perception and Understanding

claims.claim: Standard imitation methods fail to complete cyclic/repetitive manipulation tasks within the expected terminal time due to ineffective utilization of observation history; a cost-aware history-sampling strategy plus multi-task learning (added without extra models, hierarchical structure, or significant compute overhead) achieves high success rates and is plug-and-play on existing imitation policies including VLA models, across bi-arm, dexterous-hand, and humanoid platforms
claims.direction: improved history-sampling/utilization strategy favored over standard fixed-window history conditioning for tasks requiring counting/progress-tracking (cyclic tasks), as a lightweight plug-in
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world settings, multiple robot platforms, plug-in compatible with existing imitation/VLA policies

title: FreqPolicy: Efficient Flow-based Visuomotor Policy via Frequency Consistency

claims.claim: Imposing frequency-domain consistency constraints (aligning frequency-domain action features across flow timesteps) on a flow-based visuomotor policy enables high-quality one-step action generation with real-world inference frequency of 93.5 Hz, and when integrated into a VLA model achieves inference acceleration without performance degradation on 40 LIBERO tasks
claims.direction: frequency-consistency-regularized one-step flow generation favored over standard multi-step flow/diffusion sampling for real-time inference speed without accuracy loss
claims.conditions: 53 tasks across 3 simulation benchmarks + real-world robotic scenarios, applied on top of flow-based VLA models

claims.claim: Standard acceleration techniques borrowed from image generation ignore that robotic action generation requires temporal continuity/coherence across an action trajectory (unlike independent image samples); explicitly enforcing frequency-domain temporal-structure consistency addresses this and outperforms existing one-step action generators
claims.direction: explicit temporal-coherence-aware one-step action generation favored over directly repurposed image-generation acceleration techniques for chunked/sequential action trajectories
claims.conditions: same 53-task, 3-benchmark simulation evaluation plus real-world tests

why_deep_read: Directly targets both our latency problem (one-step flow generation, 93.5Hz real-world inference) and our chunk-boundary jerkiness problem (explicit temporal-coherence constraint for action trajectories, unlike naive image-generation-derived speedups); full text would give exact architecture and whether it's compatible with a SmolVLA-scale flow-matching policy on an 8GB GPU.

title: Unified Embodied VLM Reasoning with Robotic Action via Autoregressive Discretized Pre-training

claims.claim: FACT, a flow-matching-based action tokenizer that converts continuous control into discrete sequences while preserving high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction, enables a unified reasoning+action model (GenieReasoner) to outperform both continuous-action and prior discrete-action baselines on real-world tasks
claims.direction: flow-matching-derived discrete action tokenization favored over both plain continuous action regression and prior (non-flow-based) discrete tokenization schemes
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, large embodied-reasoning-focused VLM backbone

title: VLATest: Testing and Evaluating Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A fuzzing framework generating diverse robotic manipulation test scenes was used to empirically evaluate seven representative VLA models, finding they lack the robustness necessary for practical deployment; the study specifically examines the impact of confounding (distractor) objects, lighting conditions, camera poses, unseen objects, and task instruction wording/mutations on VLA performance
claims.direction: empirically demonstrates that current VLA models are broadly fragile to exactly the factors we care about (lighting, camera pose, distractors, novel objects, instruction phrasing), arguing existing hand-crafted evaluation scenes overstate real robustness
claims.conditions: seven representative VLA models, fuzzing-generated test scenes (setting appears simulation-based benchmark testing)

why_deep_read: This is a systematic empirical robustness study across exactly our failure axes (lighting, camera pose, distractor/confounding objects, unseen objects, instruction wording) on multiple VLA models; full text would give per-factor sensitivity numbers that could directly prioritize which robustness intervention (Q05 augmentation, Q11 camera robustness, Q14 generalization) matters most for our setup.

title: ScoRe-Flow: Complete Distributional Control via Score-Based Reinforcement Learning for Flow Matching

claims.claim: Modulating the drift of a flow-matching policy via the score function (gradient of log-density, computed in closed form from the velocity field, no auxiliary networks needed) rather than relying only on learnable noise injection achieves 2.4x faster convergence than flow-based SOTA RL fine-tuning on D4RL locomotion and up to 5.4% higher success rates on Robomimic and Franka Kitchen manipulation tasks
claims.direction: score/drift-modulated RL fine-tuning favored over noise-injection-only SDE conversion for fine-tuning flow-matching imitation-pretrained policies with RL
claims.conditions: simulation only (D4RL locomotion, Robomimic, Franka Kitchen manipulation benchmarks)

title: CT-VAM: A Cerebello-Thalamic-Inspired Vision-Action Model for Efficient Visuomotor Control

claims.claim: A compact local execution policy with only 68M parameters (separating high-level semantic reasoning from fast local closed-loop control) achieves LIBERO success rates competitive with substantially larger VLA models while reducing inference latency
claims.direction: small (68M-parameter), task-conditioned local policy favored over large monolithic VLA models for matching accuracy at much lower latency
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation benchmark + real-world deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms

claims.claim: A stream-separated conditional attention decoder (TARS) that independently routes action, visual, and task streams (preventing dense sensory tokens from overwhelming compact task conditions), combined with flow-consistent inpainting for asynchronous chunk execution, supports high-frequency control and robust real-world deployment on resource-constrained hardware
claims.direction: stream-separated attention + flow-consistent inpainting for async chunk execution favored over standard joint attention/dense conditioning for low-latency, jerk-free real-world control on constrained hardware
claims.conditions: dual-view visual observations (matches scene+wrist camera setups) + proprioception, resource-constrained real robot hardware

why_deep_read: Very close match to our setup: dual-view (scene+wrist) camera input, small model size in a similar ballpark to what an 8GB laptop GPU could run, and an explicit mechanism (flow-consistent inpainting) for smoothing asynchronous chunk execution -- precisely our jerky-motion problem; full text would give exact parameter budget, latency numbers, and whether TARS/inpainting could be retrofitted onto a SmolVLA-style architecture.

title: ViserDex: Visual Sim-to-Real for Robust Dexterous In-hand Reorientation

claims.claim: Performing domain randomization directly in a 3D Gaussian Splatting representation (physically-consistent, pre-rendering augmentations applied to 3D Gaussians) produces a pose estimator that outperforms one trained with conventional rendering-based domain randomization in challenging visual/lighting environments, using only monocular RGB
claims.direction: 3DGS-space domain randomization favored over conventional rendering-based domain randomization for RGB-only sim-to-real visual robustness
claims.conditions: real multi-fingered hand with single RGB camera, dexterous in-hand reorientation of 5 objects under challenging lighting

claims.claim: Both perception and control models can be trained independently on consumer-grade hardware (no large compute clusters needed) using curriculum RL with teacher-student distillation
claims.direction: favors independently-trained, compute-light perception+control pipeline over large joint end-to-end training requiring compute clusters
claims.conditions: consumer-grade hardware training, real robot deployment

title: ABot-M0.5: Unified Mobility-and-Manipulation World Action Model

claims.claim: Existing world-action models are poorly aligned with fine-grained manipulation because they operate on coarse video chunks and train inverse dynamics under supervision mismatched with autoregressive inference; introducing intermediate latent actions (bridging video latents and embodiment-specific controls) to align temporal granularity, plus a dream-forcing training strategy for train-test consistency, achieves SOTA long-horizon task success and fine-grained control accuracy
claims.direction: granularity-aligned intermediate latent actions + train-test-consistent (dream-forcing) training favored over coarse video-chunk world-action modeling for fine-grained contact-rich control
claims.conditions: challenging mobile and fine-grained manipulation benchmarks (setting not fully specified in abstract)

title: Bimanual Manipulation Within an 8 GB Budget: Zero-Copy Sensing and Quantized ACT on an Entry-Level Jetson

claims.claim: Training ACT and Diffusion Policy on identical demonstrations at their respective reference budgets (100k steps for ACT, 200k for Diffusion Policy) on a real bimanual SO-101 system, ACT converges to a task-competent policy (19/20 trials) while Diffusion Policy fails to converge to a usable policy (0/10 trials) even at twice the step count, attributed to differing convergence cost rather than an accuracy ceiling
claims.direction: ACT (transformer + action chunking, L1/CVAE-style regression) favored over Diffusion Policy for faster/more reliable convergence on a real low-cost SO-101 arm under limited training budget
claims.conditions: real bimanual SO-101 robot, pick-and-place of a deformable beanbag, embedded Jetson Orin Nano (8GB) deployment, RTX 3070 for offline training

claims.claim: Converting ACT to TensorRT: FP16 reduces mean inference latency from 114.02ms to 17.93ms (6.4x) and INT8 to 12.65ms (9.0x), with task success preserved at all precisions (19/20, 18/20, 19/20); INT8 calibration quantizes the ResNet18 visual backbone but accepts zero of 145 transformer layers, explaining INT8's negligible additional size reduction (0.9%) over FP16 despite a further 28% latency gain
claims.direction: FP16/INT8 TensorRT quantization of a small transformer-based (ACT) policy strongly favored for real-time onboard latency on entry-level embedded hardware, with FP16 already capturing most of the benefit since transformer layers resist INT8 quantization
claims.conditions: real bimanual SO-101, NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (8GB) for inference

claims.claim: The need for quantization (and its feasibility) is conditional on the action-chunking configuration: full precision is feasible at n_action_steps=100, but not when per-step re-prediction with temporal ensembling is required, since the latter demands much lower per-step latency
claims.direction: identifies action-chunking/execution-horizon configuration as directly determining whether quantization is necessary for real-time performance
claims.conditions: real bimanual SO-101, embedded Jetson deployment

why_deep_read: This paper directly benchmarks our exact platform (SO-101), an 8GB compute budget, ACT vs Diffusion Policy convergence, and TensorRT quantization latency numbers for chunked action policies -- essentially a blueprint for our own system's Q01/Q06/Q10/Q12 decisions; full text would give exact implementation details (camera pipeline, chunking config, quantization recipe) directly transferable to our SO-101 setup.

title: Agile-WAM: An Agile Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Control

claims.claim: An agile tactile world-action model that encodes vision and tactile into a shared latent for flow-matching action generation, using multi-horizon multimodal prediction (supervising visual latents at a larger temporal offset while predicting tactile latents at the next frame, reflecting their different natural timescales), outperforms the strongest baseline in success rate (29.4% relative gain in real-world experiments) while achieving 11.9ms inference latency
claims.direction: timescale-aware multi-horizon multimodal prediction (different prediction horizons per modality) favored over uniform-horizon prediction for agile, low-latency contact-rich control
claims.conditions: 9 simulated + 5 real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensing

title: AirExo: Low-Cost Exoskeletons for Learning Whole-Arm Manipulation in the Wild

claims.claim: With only 3 minutes of teleoperated demonstrations, augmenting with diverse and extensive in-the-wild demonstrations (collected cheaply via a low-cost exoskeleton, not full teleoperation) yields a policy comparable to or better than one learned from over 20 minutes of teleoperated demonstrations alone, and produces more general/robust policies across task stages, including under disturbances
claims.direction: a small core of teleoperated demonstrations plus large-scale cheap in-the-wild demonstrations favored over relying solely on more extensive teleoperated demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world whole-arm manipulation tasks, low-cost exoskeleton data collection device

title: Disambiguate Gripper State in Grasp-Based Tasks: Pseudo-Tactile as Feedback Enables Pure Simulation Learning

claims.claim: Gripper state ambiguity (a major source of imitation-learning policy fragility in grasp-based tasks) is rooted in lack of tactile feedback; using a force-controlled gripper as a pseudo-tactile sensor to provide a noise-free binary gripper-state observation improves policy robustness without extra data collection or hardware, and enables policies trained purely in simulation to transfer to real grasp-based tasks
claims.direction: pseudo-tactile (force-controlled) binary gripper-state feedback favored over raw position-only gripper state observation for resolving gripper-state ambiguity, especially enabling sim-only training
claims.conditions: 3 real-world grasp-based tasks, no additional hardware/tactile sensor required beyond existing force-controlled gripper

title: CodeDiffuser: Attention-Enhanced Diffusion Policy via VLM-Generated Code for Instruction Ambiguity

claims.claim: Using a VLM to generate task-specific interpretable code that produces 3D attention maps (integrating spatial and semantic information) to condition a diffusion policy resolves language instruction ambiguity and multi-object referent ambiguity better than end-to-end language-conditioned policies, which the authors show adapt poorly to language and environmental variations
claims.direction: VLM-code-generated explicit attention grounding favored over end-to-end joint semantic+action language-conditioned policies for handling ambiguous instructions and multi-object scenes
claims.conditions: manipulation tasks involving language ambiguity, contact-rich manipulation, and multi-object interactions (setting not fully specified, appears to include real-world experiments)

title: Exploiting Policy Idling for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Learned manipulation policies commonly 'idle' (stop moving in a small region of states, often at critical precision points like pre-grasp) as a reflection of small-action training data; applying perturbations specifically at detected idling states (Pause-Induced Perturbations) improves test-time performance with no additional supervision or training, and using the resulting escaped episodes for further training gives better iterative policy improvement than prior data-filtering/control-frequency-modification approaches, yielding a 15-35% absolute success-rate improvement on a real-world insertion task
claims.direction: targeted perturbation at detected idling states (both at test time and for iterative data collection) favored over filtering training data or modifying control frequency to address policy idling from small-action-heavy demonstration data
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm/multi-finger insertion task requiring high precision, simulated dual-arm tasks

title: Bidirectional transition consistency between multi-domain observations for visual reinforcement learning generalization

claims.claim: A model that predicts both forward and backward environmental transitions across multiple visually-perturbed domains of the same observation (rather than enforcing simple visual consistency or relying only on forward model-based transitions) improves generalization by up to 124.1% on a 'Reach' manipulation task and 73.5% on a 'Peg in Box' task under visual perturbations, versus prior visual-RL generalization approaches
claims.direction: bidirectional multi-domain transition-consistency representation learning favored over single-direction/visual-consistency-only approaches for visual generalization under perturbation
claims.conditions: simulated visual RL benchmarks (DeepMind Control Suite, robotic manipulation benchmarks, CARLA driving)

title: Learning Wrist Policies for Anthropomorphic Soft Power Grasping in Handle and Door Manipulation

claims.claim: Incorporating wrist compliance via combined impedance-force control (rather than pure position control) compensates for uncertainty in object position/orientation, yielding only 1 failure in 30 trials with an underactuated hand under up to 8cm translation and 33 degree rotation errors, and 0 failures for a fully-actuated hand under up to 12cm/30 degrees error, significantly outperforming SOTA end-to-end RL approaches
claims.direction: impedance/force-compliant control at the wrist favored over pure position-controlled end-effector for robustness to pose uncertainty, outperforming end-to-end learned RL policies
claims.conditions: real service humanoid robot, door/handle grasping and opening tasks, sim-trained policy transferred without additional learning

title: ATG-MoE: Autoregressive trajectory generation with mixture-of-experts for assembly skill learning

claims.claim: An end-to-end autoregressive trajectory generation architecture with a mixture-of-experts module (unifying multi-skill learning within a single model, directly incorporating RGB-D visual information into trajectory generation rather than separating perception and control) achieves a 96.3% average grasp success rate and 91.8% average overall success rate across 8 assembly skills in simulation, with real-world verification
claims.direction: autoregressive MoE trajectory generation with integrated multi-modal (RGB-D+language+proprioception) fusion favored over separated perception/control pipelines or single-skill-per-model designs for multi-skill assembly
claims.conditions: simulation (8 assembly skills from a pressure-reducing valve task) + real-world verification

title: RoboCousin: Build Your Own Simulation Playground for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Automatically converting user-provided object images into simulation-ready assets with grasp-contact candidates and constructing 'digital cousins' (varying compatible objects, backgrounds, layouts, language instructions while preserving affordances) generates over one million expert trajectories across 50 tasks; the automatically generated interaction annotations are comparable to curated annotations, and tabletop 'cousins' improve transfer beyond training on a single reconstructed scene
claims.direction: automated digital-cousin synthetic data generation (object/scene variation preserving affordances) favored over training only on a single reconstructed real scene for sim-to-real transfer and data scale
claims.conditions: simulation (built on RoboTwin 2.0) + real-robot experiments, bimanual manipulation

title: Action-to-Action Flow Matching

claims.claim: Action-to-Action flow matching (A2A) initializes the denoising/flow process from an embedding of the previous proprioceptive action sequence (instead of random Gaussian noise), bypassing costly iterative denoising; this enables high-quality action generation in as few as a single inference step, with high training efficiency, fast inference, and improved generalization to unseen configurations and robustness to visual perturbations, compared to standard noise-initialized flow/diffusion policies
claims.direction: proprioception-informed flow initialization favored over random-noise initialization for flow-matching action heads, for both speed and robustness
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation policy experiments (setting not fully detailed in abstract, appears to include real and/or sim), also extended to video generation

claims.claim: By embedding historical proprioceptive sequences as the flow starting point, A2A effectively captures the robot's physical dynamics and temporal continuity, directly informing frame-to-frame/chunk-to-chunk consistency
claims.direction: proprioception-conditioned flow initialization favored over static/noise-based conditioning for preserving temporal continuity across action generation
claims.conditions: same experimental setting as above

why_deep_read: Proposes a simple, architecture-light fix (initialize flow-matching denoising from previous proprioceptive action instead of noise) that could directly address both our latency problem (single-step generation) and our chunk-boundary jerkiness problem (temporal continuity from proprioception-informed init); full text would clarify exact latency/success numbers and whether it's compatible with a SmolVLA-style small flow-matching action head.

title: SPaRL: Spatially-aware Reinforcement Learning with Language

claims.claim: Conditioning an LLM-based RL policy on a structured, dynamically-pruned 3D scene graph (objects + spatial relations, serialized into natural language) consistently improves performance over a vision-only LLM policy on language-conditioned rearrangement tasks, especially as task difficulty increases
claims.direction: explicit structured scene-graph spatial representation (fused with language) favored over vision-only representations for complex spatial reasoning and multi-object manipulation
claims.conditions: simulated language-conditioned rearrangement tasks in Habitat, frozen LLM backbone

title: Affordance-based robot manipulation with flow matching

claims.claim: Representing a robot visuomotor policy as a flow-matching process (flowing random waypoints to desired robot actions) yields more stable training and faster inference than diffusion policy; specifically, 1-step flow matching achieves accuracy comparable to 16-step DDIM diffusion while reducing inference time by roughly 85%
claims.direction: flow matching (especially 1-step) favored over multi-step DDIM diffusion policies for comparable accuracy at much lower inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world dataset with 10 manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Parameter-efficient prompt tuning (prepending learnable text prompts to a frozen vision model to predict affordances) achieves competitive or superior performance to other fine-tuning protocols across data scales, while using far fewer trainable parameters
claims.direction: prompt-tuning-based adaptation of a frozen large vision model favored over full fine-tuning for affordance prediction, especially at smaller data scales
claims.conditions: real-world dataset, 10 tasks, multi-task affordance learning

title: RE4: Transformation-aware Imitation of Object Interactions Using Manipulation Modes

claims.claim: An interpretable framework using model-free pose estimation, mode-aware demonstration retrieval, mode-aware transformation, and constrained replanning (instead of end-to-end diffusion/flow policies) shows particular robustness in sparse/low-data regions of the demonstration distribution, evaluated via an adversarial benchmark on image-based Push-T
claims.direction: interpretable, mode-aware retrieval-and-transform imitation favored over end-to-end diffusion/flow policies specifically in low-data/sparse-demonstration regimes, at some cost to raw performance elsewhere
claims.conditions: state-based and image-based Push-T and Robomimic benchmarks (simulation), explicit low-data-regime and adversarial sparse-data evaluation

title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback

claims.claim: Chunk-based VLA policies predict complete action chunks from observations collected before execution, leaving conditioning stale by the time later actions in the chunk execute; replacing the standard action expert with a streaming action expert that conditions on evolving observations during execution (with attention restricted to actions nearing execution) achieves 65% and 69% average success on simulated and real-world contact-rich tasks respectively, outperforming strong baselines
claims.direction: streaming, execution-time-conditioned action generation favored over standard fixed chunk-then-execute prediction for reducing observation staleness during chunk execution
claims.conditions: 6 simulated UniVTAC tasks + 3 real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensing for the specific instantiation but the staleness problem framing applies to chunked execution generally

title: RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: A Physically Interpretable Unified Action Space that unifies action representations across different robots while preserving the physical meaning of original actions facilitates learning transferrable physical knowledge and helps address training-data scarcity for a diffusion foundation model
claims.direction: physically-grounded unified/shared action-space representation favored over robot-specific raw action spaces for cross-embodiment data pooling
claims.conditions: large-scale multi-robot pretraining (1.2B-parameter diffusion transformer), fine-tuned on 6K+ episode multi-task bimanual dataset, real robot evaluation

claims.claim: After large-scale pretraining, the resulting model learns new manipulation skills with just 1-5 demonstrations and exhibits zero-shot generalization to unseen objects and scenes on real robots
claims.direction: large-scale cross-embodiment pretraining favored as a route to making downstream task-specific fine-tuning extremely demonstration-efficient (1-5 demos)
claims.conditions: real robot experiments, requires substantial upstream multi-robot pretraining compute/data not available in our own small-scale setting

title: HiRT: Enhancing Robotic Control with Hierarchical Robot Transformers

claims.claim: Running the large VLM backbone at a low update frequency (to capture temporally-invariant features) while a lightweight high-frequency vision-based policy acts on those slowly-updated features doubles the control frequency at comparable success rates on static tasks, and improves success rate on novel real-world dynamic manipulation tasks from 48% to 75% versus baseline VLA methods that run the full VLM at every control step
claims.direction: hierarchical decoupling of slow semantic (VLM) and fast reactive (vision-policy) inference favored over running a full large VLA backbone at every control step, for both latency and dynamic-task success
claims.conditions: real-world dynamic manipulation tasks + simulation, large VLM-backed VLA architecture split into hierarchical slow/fast components

title: Rethinking Latent Redundancy in Behavior Cloning: An Information Bottleneck Approach for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A systematic study across multiple methods, visual backbones, and experimental settings finds that learned latent representations in behavior cloning commonly contain redundant (task-irrelevant) information; applying an Information Bottleneck objective to compress this redundancy while preserving task-relevant features yields significant performance improvements on CortexBench and LIBERO benchmarks
claims.direction: explicit information-bottleneck-regularized (redundancy-minimizing) visual/latent representation favored over standard unregularized BC representations for both single-modality and multi-modality (visual+language) inputs
claims.conditions: CortexBench and LIBERO benchmarks, evaluated across multiple encoder backbones and BC method variants (setting appears primarily simulation/benchmark-based)

title: Real2Render2Real: Scaling Robot Data Without Dynamics Simulation or Robot Hardware

claims.claim: Rendering thousands of high-visual-fidelity, robot-agnostic demonstrations from a single smartphone object scan plus a single human demonstration video (via 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction and 6-DoF object motion tracking, no dynamics simulation or teleoperation) produces training data such that models trained on it match the performance of models trained on 150 human teleoperation demonstrations
claims.direction: generative rendering from a single human demo + object scan favored over collecting large numbers of real teleoperated demonstrations, for comparable downstream policy performance
claims.conditions: physical robot experiments, compatible with VLA and imitation-learning policies that consume proprioceptive state + image observations, rigid and articulated objects supported

why_deep_read: Directly quantifies a huge data-efficiency gain (1 human demo + object scan matching 150 teleoperated demos) that is precisely the kind of trade we'd want given our 50-100 demo budget; full text would clarify the smartphone-scan/rendering pipeline cost, whether it needs a GPU-heavy 3DGS step, and how well it transfers to our specific pumpkin-pick-and-place setup with two cameras.

title: Towards Efficient and Expressive Offline RL via Flow-Anchored Noise-conditioned Q-Learning

claims.claim: Using a single flow-policy iteration (instead of iterative sampling) plus a single Gaussian noise sample for distributional critics (instead of multi-sample quantile computation) achieves state-of-the-art offline RL performance on robotic manipulation and locomotion tasks while significantly reducing both training and inference runtimes versus standard expressive flow-policy + distributional-critic offline RL
claims.direction: single-sample flow policy + single-noise-sample critic favored over iterative multi-sample flow/distributional approaches for efficiency without performance loss
claims.conditions: simulated robotic manipulation and locomotion benchmarks (offline RL setting)

title: Robust and Adaptive Compliant Deep Reinforcement Learning With Vision-Force Integration for Embodied Multiple Peg-in-Hole Assembly

claims.claim: Synchronized data augmentation applied consistently across stacked visual frames with a temporal-consistency regularization (Data-regularized Q) enhances visual feature robustness specifically under target pose uncertainty in a contact-rich assembly task, improving reliable sim-to-real transfer and robustness under challenging perturbations
claims.direction: temporally-consistent synchronized frame augmentation favored over unregularized/independent per-frame augmentation for robustness to pose uncertainty in contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real electrical socket peg-in-hole assembly, vision+force integration, variable impedance control for compliance

title: FreMotion: A Frequency-Motion Synergy Framework for Imitation Learning in Robust Robotic Fine Manipulation

claims.claim: Explicitly disentangling and fusing high-frequency (precision) and low-frequency (motion smoothness) information via a dual-path Frequency-Aware Decoder, combined with a Temporal Dynamic Encoder using linear attention with dynamic gating to mitigate long-horizon error accumulation, resolves the trade-off between millimeter-level positioning precision and motion smoothness that causes jittery, actuator-wearing control in standard imitation-learned policies on bimanual fine manipulation tasks
claims.direction: explicit frequency-domain decomposition (low-frequency smoothness + high-frequency precision) favored over standard single-path imitation-learning decoders for reducing jittery control in long-horizon fine manipulation
claims.conditions: real bimanual robotic fine-manipulation tasks, standard robotic arms, task-specific expert demonstrations required

claims.claim: FreMotion, with orders of magnitude fewer parameters (~100M vs Billions for VLA baselines), outperforms state-of-the-art VLA methods in success rate while also achieving faster inference time
claims.direction: small (~100M parameter) task-specific architecture favored over billion-parameter VLA models for both accuracy and inference speed on fine manipulation
claims.conditions: real bimanual robotic tasks, standard (non-specialized) robotic arms, no expensive additional sensors required

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly targets our exact symptom description ('jittery controls that cause actuator wear and failure') with a small (~100M param) model achieving both millimeter precision and fast inference on real bimanual arms; full text would give the frequency-decomposition architecture details and whether it's adaptable to a single 6-DoF SO-101 arm with our two-camera setup and 50-100 demo budget.

title: A Few-Shot VLM-Driven Perception-to-Action Pipeline for Robotic Pick-and-Place
