claims.claim: A modular pipeline combining SAM2 (segmentation), CLIP (few-shot recognition), and GPT-4o (instruction grounding) with a fixed manipulation routine allows onboarding a new object category with roughly 10 reference images and no model retraining, achieving F1 scores of 96.3%/97.4% on two novel object classes and 94.1% action-grounding accuracy on autogenerated commands in cluttered real-world scenes
claims.direction: modular few-shot perception (no policy retraining needed for new objects) favored over end-to-end learned policies requiring per-object retraining, for rapid novel-object onboarding
claims.conditions: real Fanuc arm, 43 cluttered real-world scenes, top-down RGB only, fixed non-learned motion primitive for execution

title: Latent Diffusion Policy: Shaping Latent Spaces for Diffusion-Based Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Diffusion-based visuomotor policies operating directly in raw action space must have their velocity field simultaneously encode scene information and generate precise trajectories, increasing learning complexity; performing flow matching instead in a latent space shaped by an observation-conditioned CVAE encoder (absorbing scene understanding separately) produces a smoother velocity field and substantially outperforms DP3 on coordination-intensive bimanual tasks, transferring effectively to real-world deployment
claims.direction: two-stage latent-space flow matching (scene understanding factored out via CVAE) favored over single-stage raw-action-space diffusion/flow policies for coordination-intensive multi-arm tasks
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 simulation benchmark + real-world bimanual deployment

claims.claim: By pre-concentrating the conditional distribution of each observation into a shaped latent space, the flow model avoids implicitly resolving scene-dependent structure, simplifying learning from limited demonstrations
claims.direction: latent-space-shaped flow matching favored over raw-action-space flow/diffusion for data efficiency with limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: same RoboTwin 2.0 + real-world bimanual setting

title: Robo-Dopamine 2.0: History-Conditioned and OOD-Aware Process Reward Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Existing learned visual reward models relying on static before-after observations cause temporal ambiguity and weak discrimination between robustness-preserving variations and true task-invalid failures under out-of-distribution execution; a history-conditioned, OOD-aware process reward model (using rollout history rather than static endpoint comparison) improves visual order consistency and, when used for downstream RL refinement of a pretrained VLA, achieves 86.8% mean success on RoboTwin and 71/80 successful real-world insertions
claims.direction: history-conditioned reward modeling (using rollout history) favored over static before/after reward comparison for reliably distinguishing OOD-but-valid execution from true failure, improving downstream RL-refined VLA robustness
claims.conditions: RoboTwin simulation + real-world insertion tasks, used to fine-tune a pretrained VLA via RL

title: RouteRLT: Learning When and Which RL Specialist Should Control a Vision-Language-Action Policy

claims.claim: A routing framework with a phase selector, a switch-suppressing stabilizer, and an action-boundary manager (handling transitions between chunked policy outputs) learns to hand control from a generalist VLA to task-specific RL specialists during precision-critical phases; in simulation, learned routing improves over the base VLA and matches routing with privileged phase boundaries, and real-world evaluation validates automatic routing for a cable pickup + port-insertion task
claims.direction: learned routing between a generalist chunked VLA and specialized RL policies (with explicit handling of chunk-boundary transitions) favored over relying solely on a single generalist chunked policy for precision-critical task phases
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation (multi-object pick-and-place) + real-world cable pickup/port-insertion with multiple precision-critical stages

title: The Ingredients for Robotic Diffusion Transformers

claims.claim: Identifying and improving key architectural design decisions for combining high-capacity Transformer architectures with diffusion models (previously lacking a clear, well-understood design process) yields a DiT-Block Policy that significantly outperforms the state of the art on long-horizon (1500+ timestep) dexterous bimanual tasks on a real ALOHA robot, without per-setup hyperparameter tuning
claims.direction: a systematically-chosen diffusion transformer architecture (specific design ingredients identified via ablation) favored over ad-hoc combinations of Transformer + diffusion for long-horizon dexterous real-robot tasks
claims.conditions: real bimanual ALOHA robot, long-horizon (1500+ timestep) dexterous tasks

claims.claim: The improved diffusion transformer policies show better scaling performance when trained on 10 hours of highly multi-modal, language-annotated demonstration data versus less-optimized architectures
claims.direction: well-designed diffusion transformer architecture favored for making better use of additional multi-modal training data (better scaling), versus architectures without the identified design improvements
claims.conditions: real ALOHA robot, 10-hour multi-task, language-annotated demonstration dataset

title: Behavior-Actor: Behavioral Decomposition and Efficient-Training for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Training a single end-to-end actor from scratch on 11 real-world tasks decomposed into 40 behaviors, using only 276 demonstrations total (averaging just 7 demonstrations per behavior), achieves a 68% average success rate on seen commands and a 45% average success rate on unseen commands (double the baseline's performance), by having an LLM decompose language commands into executable behaviors (RAG-style) that a single trained actor executes
claims.direction: LLM-based behavior decomposition + single actor trained on very few (~7) demonstrations per behavior favored over training one large policy per full task/command combination, for both data efficiency and unseen-command generalization
claims.conditions: real-world robot, 11 tasks / 40 behaviors, ~7 demos per behavior on average, LLM-agnostic design (no LLM fine-tuning required)

title: Deformpam: Data-Efficient Learning for Long-Horizon Deformable Object Manipulation Via Preference-Based Action Alignment

claims.claim: Decomposing long-horizon tasks into action primitives, modeling action distributions with 3D point-cloud-conditioned diffusion models, and using an implicit reward model trained on human preference data to select among multiple candidate diffusion-generated actions at inference time improves both task completion quality and efficiency compared to baseline imitation learning methods, even with limited training data, on real-world long-horizon deformable-object tasks
claims.direction: preference-guided best-of-many action selection at inference (on top of a diffusion action model) favored over single-sample diffusion action generation for data-limited long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: 3 real-world long-horizon deformable-object manipulation tasks, 3D point cloud inputs

title: Grounding Bodily Awareness in Visual Representations for Efficient Policy Learning

claims.claim: A contrastive auxiliary loss (Inter-token Contrast, ICon) that enforces separation between agent-specific and environment-specific ViT token representations, added to end-to-end policy learning with no architecture change, improves policy performance across various manipulation tasks and facilitates policy transfer across different robots
claims.direction: agent/environment-token-separated (body-aware) visual representation favored over undifferentiated ViT token representations for policy performance and cross-robot transfer
claims.conditions: end-to-end policy learning, auxiliary contrastive loss added to existing ViT-based visual encoders

title: Adaptive Vision-Language-Action Models for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation in Unstructured Environments

claims.claim: AdaptVLA, combining a hierarchical attention mechanism (balancing local object features with global scene context), a contrastive language grounding module, and an adaptive action decoder that adjusts to environmental feedback, achieves 91.2% task success on seen tasks and 76.8% on novel task-object combinations across 47 manipulation tasks (household/industrial/lab), a 12.3% improvement over SOTA VLA baselines, with successful real-world zero-shot transfer to unseen objects with complex geometries
claims.direction: hierarchical local+global attention plus adaptive action decoding favored over standard VLA architectures for generalizing to novel task-object combinations
claims.conditions: 47-task benchmark spanning household/industrial/lab domains, real-world zero-shot experiments, 15Hz control frequency reported

title: Cross-Modal Visuo-Tactile Representation Learning with Action Chunking Transformers for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Aligning external RGB observations and tactile images in a shared embedding space via a CLIP-style contrastive objective, then feeding the resulting representation into an ACT policy, improves average task completion rate on contact-rich manipulation from 30% (vision-only ACT baseline) to 42% (raw tactile added) to 54% (with contrastive pretraining), showing that explicit visual-tactile alignment adds more value than naively adding tactile input
claims.direction: contrastively-aligned multi-modal (visual+tactile) representation favored over both vision-only and naively-fused vision+tactile representations for contact-rich ACT-based policies
claims.conditions: real contact-rich manipulation tasks, custom low-cost visuo-tactile gripper (LVTG), ACT policy backbone -- requires tactile hardware

title: TPRU: Advancing Temporal and Procedural Understanding in Large Multimodal Models

claims.claim: Training resource-efficient (smaller, deployable) multimodal models on a large-scale dataset specifically designed to cultivate temporal reasoning (temporal reordering, next-frame prediction, previous-frame review, with challenging negative samples) via RL fine-tuning dramatically improves temporal/procedural understanding accuracy (50.33% to 75.70% on a curated test set for a 7B model), outperforming much larger baselines including GPT-4o, with generalization to established benchmarks
claims.direction: explicit temporal-reasoning-focused pretraining/fine-tuning data favored over standard passive-observation training for small/deployable multimodal models needing temporal and procedural understanding
claims.conditions: large multimodal models (including small deployable variants), embodied scenarios including robotic manipulation and GUI navigation, RL fine-tuning methodology

title: FAR: Failure-Aware Retry for Test-Time Recovery and Continual Policy Improvement

claims.claim: Combining Failure-Contrastive Preference Adaptation (constructing preference-learning data from the robot's own past failures to steer away from unsuccessful behaviors) with lightweight action perturbations during retries, plus feeding successful recovery trajectories back into training, substantially improves success rates: average gains of 17.6% over standard diffusion policy in simulation and 11.7% in the real world, while improving data efficiency under both reset and timestep budgets during continual policy improvement
claims.direction: test-time failure-aware retry and continual learning from the policy's own failures favored over static diffusion-policy deployment without failure-informed adaptation
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, diffusion policy baseline, no human intervention required for recovery

title: Unified Visuomotor Targets: Supervising VLAs Beyond Physical Actions

claims.claim: Replacing the plain action-prediction training target with a Unified Visuomotor Target (UVT) -- a single latent prediction target that jointly encodes motor control and visual scene-transition information, requiring no architectural changes and no additional data -- improves training efficiency, final task performance, and policy robustness across two representative VLA systems, with particularly strong gains under limited training budgets and challenging environmental conditions
claims.direction: a unified action+future-visual-state latent training target favored over predicting physical actions alone, as a free (no architecture/data change) auxiliary-objective-style improvement, especially valuable when training budget/data is limited
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + real bimanual manipulation tasks, applied to 2 existing VLA architectures without modification

why_deep_read: Claims particularly strong gains under limited training budgets (matching our 50-100 demo, single-laptop-GPU constraint) via a drop-in training-target change with zero architecture or data cost; full text would clarify exactly how the unified latent target is constructed and whether it is compatible with a SmolVLA-scale flow-matching policy, since this could be an easy win for our setup.

title: EmbodiedSkills: A Unified Framework for Orchestrating, Training, and Deploying VLA Agents

claims.claim: A task-adapted low-level VLA policy instantiated within a skill-orchestration framework with prerequisite-checking and outcome-verification achieves 86.20% average success across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and 97.40% across LIBERO suites, but only 12.5% average success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks, highlighting that current VLA execution approaches struggle substantially more on tasks specifically requiring memory of past states versus standard reactive tasks
claims.direction: highlights a large performance gap between standard (largely memoryless) manipulation tasks and memory-dependent long-horizon tasks for current VLA-based execution approaches, even within a verification-augmented framework
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO simulation benchmarks + RMBench memory-dependent tasks, Qwen3-VL + OpenPI/pi0.5 backbones

title: SkipVLA: Skipping VLA Steps with Classical Planning for Fast Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A hybrid policy that uses a classical motion planner for free-space motion and only queries a pretrained VLA for contact-rich skills (grasping, placing) -- predicting target poses via the frozen VLA vision-language backbone with no additional demonstrations required -- achieves up to 2.5x faster task completion and significantly lower energy consumption than running the VLA for the entire task, while maintaining the same task success rate, across three VLA backbones on 13 LIBERO tasks and three real pick-and-place tasks on a physical 6-DoF arm
claims.direction: hybrid classical-planner + selectively-queried VLA favored over running a learned VLA policy continuously for the entire task, for latency and energy efficiency with no accuracy loss and no extra demonstrations needed
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation (3 VLA backbones, 13 tasks) + real 6-DoF YAM arm, 3 real pick-and-place tasks

title: Fine-Tuning Multimodal Transformer Models for Generating Actions in Virtual and Real Environments

claims.claim: Adapting a pre-trained bimodal (text-image) transformer, originally trained on general vision-language tasks (language modeling, VQA, captioning, etc.), to robotic manipulation by organizing text/image/action tokens in the input sequence adapts well to new tasks and shows better results with fine-tuning than training completely from scratch, in both simulation and on a real robot
claims.direction: fine-tuning a large pretrained general-purpose vision-language transformer favored over training a manipulation policy from scratch
claims.conditions: simulation + real robot object manipulation with language instructions, requires new dataset collection/annotation for sim-to-real transfer

title: Adapting by Analogy: OOD Generalization of Visuomotor Policies via Functional Correspondence

claims.claim: Task success under visually out-of-distribution conditions (novel objects, backgrounds, environment changes) does not always require new robot behaviors: in-distribution behaviors can be directly transferred to OOD observations that are functionally similar to training observations (e.g., a policy trained on pens applied to a visually-different pencil), by detecting OOD state, soliciting minimal expert feedback on which in-distribution behavior functionally corresponds, and substituting the ID observation at deployment time; this improves generalization of a vision-based diffusion policy to OOD objects/environments with low feedback, versus collecting and retraining on new corrective demonstrations for every OOD encounter
claims.direction: test-time functional-correspondence substitution (reusing in-distribution behavior for functionally similar OOD objects) favored over collecting new corrective demonstrations for each novel object/environment encountered
claims.conditions: real-world Franka Panda manipulation tasks, vision-based diffusion policy, requires occasional low-effort expert feedback rather than full demonstrations

title: Hybrid Imitation Learning: Teleoperation Augmentation Primitives that Policies Learn to Trigger

claims.claim: Teleoperation Augmentation Primitives (TAPs) -- axis locks, perching waypoints, pose anchors, and embodiment-specific routines that an operator triggers during demonstration (by speech, AR menu, or button) and which are recorded and can be learned/invoked by the policy itself -- improve downstream policy success on a wrist-camera-only peg insertion task from 0.372 to 0.531, on a mug-cleanup task with a learned 'remember this pose' anchor from 0.203 to 0.323 (simulation), and on a real-robot unscrewing task from 38% to 67% success where a plain policy cannot resolve the multi-turn motion from images alone
claims.direction: augmenting teleoperated demonstrations with recordable, policy-learnable primitives (for motions hard for a human operator to demonstrate directly, like exact orientations or multi-turn twists) favored over collecting only raw teleoperated trajectories, especially for wrist-camera-only setups
claims.conditions: simulation (wrist-camera-only peg insertion, mug cleanup) + real robot (3 tasks including multi-turn unscrewing), directly applicable to teleoperation-based data collection pipelines

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our wrist-camera teleop data-collection pipeline: shows that adding simple, recordable operator-triggered primitives (not architecture changes) meaningfully improves policy success on tasks that are hard to demonstrate via raw teleoperation, exactly the kind of low-cost intervention available to us; full text would give the exact primitive implementations and whether they need any robot/software support beyond what a leader-follower SO-101 teleop rig already has.

title: HAMSTER: Hierarchical Action Models For Open-World Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical VLA where a high-level VLM (fine-tuned to predict a coarse 2D end-effector path from an RGB image + task description, using off-domain data such as action-free videos/sketches) guides a low-level 3D-aware control policy transfers across significant domain gaps (embodiment, dynamics, visual appearance, task semantics) between off-domain fine-tuning data and real-robot deployment; real-robot experiments show an average 20 percentage-point (50% relative) improvement in success rate over OpenVLA across seven different generalization axes
claims.direction: hierarchical decomposition (coarse 2D path prediction by high-level VLM + precise low-level 3D control) favored over monolithic VLA fine-tuning for effectively leveraging cheap off-domain data and generalizing across domain gaps
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments across 7 generalization axes, off-domain data (action-free video/sketches) used for high-level VLM training

title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation

claims.claim: Equipping a data-efficient 3D VLA (which preserves pretrained-VLM input-output alignment by projecting point clouds into multi-view images and predicting intermediate heatmaps) with a unified spatio-temporal memory architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance on memory-dependent manipulation benchmarks without sacrificing the original model's data efficiency or generalization, and extends to bimanual settings and an additional real-world robot platform
claims.direction: adding explicit spatio-temporal memory to an already data-efficient 3D VLA favored over either sacrificing memory capability or sacrificing data efficiency/generalization to add memory
claims.conditions: memory-dependent manipulation benchmarks + bimanual settings + additional real-world robotic platform

title: VeriSpace: Spatially Grounded Action Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A 3D-aware test-time action verifier that jointly preserves visual semantics and explicit 3D geometry, and reasons over spatial relations/geometric validity/goal progress to select among multiple candidate VLA-proposed actions, consistently improves decision reliability over both the underlying VLA policy and prior (non-3D) verification methods, with substantial gains in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings
claims.direction: 3D-geometry-aware test-time action verification/selection favored over one-shot action prediction or non-3D verification for improving reliability, especially OOD
claims.conditions: public benchmarks + real-world robotic manipulation tasks, compatible as a plug-in with existing VLA policies

title: CheckVLA: Execution-Time Verification with Action-Conditioned World Model for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Open-loop action chunks commit to a sequence of actions without new visual input; when execution deviates from the expected observation trajectory partway through a chunk, the remaining committed actions continue to propagate the error, and neither commit-time confidence nor observation-only anomaly detection can catch this; verifying execution against a separately-trained, frozen action-conditioned world model (with conformally-calibrated intervention thresholds and latency-aware hard prefixing that only replaces still-deployable actions) achieves 36.1% average success vs 27.6% for periodic replanning (+8.5 points), and raises timely-intervention recall to 77.9% vs 48.6% (observation-only) and 37.9% (action-shuffled control) at a matched 5% false-alarm rate
claims.direction: action-conditioned (not observation-only) execution-time verification of chunked action sequences favored over periodic replanning or observation-only anomaly detection for catching and correcting mid-chunk deviations
claims.conditions: RoboCasa365 simulation benchmark, long-horizon mobile manipulation, open-loop action-chunk execution

title: R^3: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Mid-training a VLM on expert-generated free-form reasoning traces, then improving it with single-step rubric-based RL from offline action data (rather than using structured reasoning traces only as auxiliary supervision), produces natural-language test-time guidance for low-level manipulation policies that improves exploration and generalization to unseen tasks, significantly outperforming instruction-only imitation learning baselines
claims.direction: free-form language reasoning as a test-time-compute steering mechanism for low-level policies favored over instruction-only (non-reasoning) imitation learning conditioning
claims.conditions: Language Table + simulated bimanual grocery packing testbeds

title: From Gameplay to Policy: Towards Scalable Robot Data Collection via Gamified Robot-Free Interaction

claims.claim: Extracting embodiment-invariant affordance cues (contact points, sub-goal states) from a VR-based gamified data-collection platform, pre-training an affordance model on this game-collected data, then jointly fine-tuning with downstream policies using only a handful of real-robot demonstrations, improves average success rates by 10.0 points in simulation and 18.3 points on real robots in the few-shot setting versus not using the game-collected data
claims.direction: gamified, robot-free human interaction data (pretraining affordance model) combined with a handful of real-robot demonstrations favored over relying only on the handful of real-robot demonstrations, for few-shot policy learning
claims.conditions: few-shot real-robot fine-tuning setting, requires a VR gamified data-collection platform (Project Kitchen) as an additional data source

title: PLEX: Making the Most of the Available Data for Robotic Manipulation Pretraining

claims.claim: Combining a small amount of task-agnostic visuomotor trajectories (observations+actions) to induce a latent feature space with a much larger amount of task-conditioned, video-only (action-free) object manipulation demonstrations to teach planning in that space produces a generalizable sensorimotor multi-task policy, establishing SOTA performance on Robosuite and generalizing on Meta-World-v2, more effectively than architectures needing full action-labeled data for all tasks
claims.direction: combining scarce action-labeled trajectories with abundant action-free video demonstrations favored over relying solely on action-labeled demonstrations for multi-task policy pretraining
claims.conditions: Meta-World-v2 and Robosuite simulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Using relative positional encoding in PLEX's transformer architecture further increases data efficiency when learning from human-collected demonstrations
claims.direction: relative (vs absolute) positional encoding favored for transformer-based policies learning from human demonstrations, for data efficiency
claims.conditions: same simulation benchmarks

title: How Much Progress Did I Make? An Unexplored Human Feedback Signal for Teaching Robots

claims.claim: A dataset of 40 non-expert demonstrations for an ice-cream topping-adding task is observed to be multi-policy and sub-optimal, with sub-optimality arising not only from teleoperation errors but also from exploratory actions and deliberate attempts, and progress signals (percentage task completion) can identify unproductive-but-harmless behaviors within these demonstrations
claims.direction: highlights that non-expert-collected demonstration data is inherently multi-modal/sub-optimal for reasons beyond simple execution error (exploration, attempts), a caution for anyone relying on raw non-expert teleop demonstrations as clean supervision
claims.conditions: real-world non-expert demonstration collection (76 online + 40 public-space participants), teleoperation-based data collection

title: Tilde: Teleoperation for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation Learning with a DeltaHand

claims.claim: A low-cost, kinematically-twinned teleoperation interface enabling precise one-to-one joint control during demonstration collection, combined with diffusion-policy imitation learning, achieves fully autonomous closed-loop deployment with an average 90% success rate across seven dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: precise, kinematically-matched low-cost teleoperation hardware favored for producing high-quality demonstrations that enable high real-world success rates with diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous in-hand manipulation, low-cost soft dexterous hand (DeltaHand), diffusion policy

title: RISE: 3D Perception Makes Real-World Robot Imitation Simple and Effective

claims.claim: Image-based policies model object positions from fixed cameras and are sensitive to camera-view changes, while typical 3D-point-cloud policies predict keyframes rather than continuous actions (posing difficulty in dynamic, contact-rich scenarios); RISE compresses single-view point clouds into tokens via a sparse 3D encoder, featurizes them with a transformer, and decodes continuous actions via a diffusion head, surpassing representative 2D and 3D policies by a large margin in both accuracy and efficiency when trained with 50 demonstrations per real-world task
claims.direction: single-view point-cloud + continuous-action diffusion head favored over both 2D image-based policies (camera-view sensitive) and standard keyframe-based 3D point-cloud policies
claims.conditions: real-world imitation learning, exactly 50 demonstrations per task, single RGB-D camera view

claims.claim: RISE is demonstrated to be more general and robust to environmental change than previous 2D and 3D policy baselines
claims.direction: single-view point-cloud continuous-action policy favored over 2D image-based and keyframe-based 3D baselines for robustness to environmental change
claims.conditions: real-world imitation learning tasks, same 50-demo-per-task setting

why_deep_read: Nearly matches our exact constraints: 50 demonstrations per real-world task, single-view depth camera (we have a RealSense), continuous (not keyframe) action output, and explicitly targets camera-view-change robustness (one of our stated failure modes); full text would give exact success-rate deltas vs 2D baselines and the point-cloud encoder's compute cost to check feasibility on an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Scalable Vision-Language-Action Model Pretraining for Robotic Manipulation with Real-Life Human Activity Videos

claims.claim: Pretraining a dexterous-hand VLA model on a fully-automatically-labeled dataset of 1M episodes / 26M frames derived from unscripted, unannotated egocentric human hand videos gives strong zero-shot capability on unseen real-world observations; fine-tuning on only a small amount of real robot action data significantly improves task success rate and generalization to novel objects, with task performance scaling favorably with pretraining data volume
claims.direction: large-scale automated pretraining on unannotated human hand videos (treating the hand as the end-effector) favored over relying only on scarce robot-collected demonstrations, as a route to small-data fine-tuning with strong generalization
claims.conditions: real-world fine-tuning and testing, requires substantial upstream video-processing/pretraining pipeline not itself part of the small-data fine-tuning budget

title: UMIGen: A Unified Framework for Egocentric Point Cloud Generation and Cross-Embodiment Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A handheld data-collection device that requires no visual SLAM and directly records point-cloud observation-action pairs (Cloud-UMI), combined with a visibility-aware optimization that generates only points within the camera's field of view for egocentric 3D data augmentation, supports strong cross-embodiment generalization and accelerates data generation/collection across diverse manipulation tasks in both simulated and real-world settings
claims.direction: point-cloud-based (rather than RGB-only) low-cost handheld data collection, paired with visibility-aware 3D data augmentation, favored for cross-embodiment transfer and faster data collection/generation
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, requires depth/point-cloud-capable handheld capture hardware

title: GRITS: A Spillage-Aware Guided Diffusion Policy for Robot Food Scooping Tasks

claims.claim: A differentiable spillage predictor (trained on simulated food-spillage scenarios across varied physical properties) used as a guidance signal to steer diffusion-policy sampling toward safer trajectories, while preserving task success, achieves 82% task success and only 4% spillage rate on a real robotic food-scooping platform, reducing spillage by over 40% versus a diffusion policy baseline without this guidance
claims.direction: guided diffusion sampling (with a task-specific differentiable safety/quality predictor) favored over standard unguided diffusion-policy sampling for reducing task-specific failure modes
claims.conditions: real-world robotic food scooping, trained on 6 food categories, evaluated on 10 unseen categories with different shapes/quantities

title: EDAR: Learning Environment-Dependent Action Representations for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Grounding action tokens in both executable control structure and their expected environment-conditioned visual consequences (rather than encoding only the structure of the action stream itself, treating environment effects as implicit) improves downstream policy learning, especially in long-horizon manipulation, on simulated and real-robot benchmarks
claims.direction: environment-conditioned (effect-aware) action representation favored over action-structure-only representations, particularly for long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: simulated and real-robot manipulation benchmarks

title: RoboEdit: Turning Human Manipulation Videos into Scalable Robot Experience

claims.claim: An automatic human-to-robot video editing pipeline that reconstructs and retargets 3D hand-object interactions from RGB human videos across embodiments (producing a 174K-pair, 14M-frame dataset spanning 7 robot embodiments) achieves state-of-the-art video-editing quality and supports downstream real-world robot control policies when used as supervision
claims.direction: cross-embodiment human-to-robot video translation/editing favored over using unedited human videos directly, or relying only on robot-collected data, as scalable training supervision
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation downstream policy tasks, requires a substantial video-editing/retargeting pipeline

title: Embedding Morphology into Transformers for Cross-Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Injecting robot morphology into a transformer-based (VLA) policy via kinematic tokens (factorizing actions per-joint with per-joint temporal chunking), topology-aware attention bias (encoding kinematic structure as an inductive bias in self-attention), and joint-attribute conditioning consistently improves performance over a vanilla pi0.5 VLA baseline both within a single embodiment and across embodiments
claims.direction: morphology-aware (kinematic-structure-injected) transformer action architecture favored over embodiment-agnostic transformer policies that must infer kinematic structure purely from observations
claims.conditions: range of embodiments tested (setting not fully specified, appears to include real and/or sim), pi0.5 VLA baseline comparison

title: Motion-Focused Latent Action Enables Cross-Embodiment VLA Training from Human EgoVideos

claims.claim: Pre-training a VLM backbone exclusively on unlabeled human egocentric videos using a Hybrid Disentangled VQ-VAE (that decouples motion dynamics from environmental background via physical masks, building a cross-embodiment action codebook), with an intent-perception decoupling strategy at adaptation time (VLM predicts intent, a separate frozen visual encoder supplies state features), performs competitively with SOTA VLA models trained on massive annotated robot datasets, while requiring only 50 trajectories for downstream embodiment-specific adaptation
claims.direction: unlabeled human-egovideo pretraining with motion/background disentanglement favored over requiring massive annotated robot datasets, for making downstream adaptation extremely data-efficient (50 trajectories)
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world environments, requires substantial upstream video-pretraining infrastructure not part of the 50-trajectory downstream budget

title: URF: A Unified Robot Control-Policy Framework for Stable Contact Aware Manipulation

claims.claim: Predicting not only a compliant action (virtual target) but also the low-level controller behavior needed to execute it -- specifically a stiffness matrix and an impedance-admittance switch ratio, supervised via switch-ratio labels derived from measured contact forces rather than ground-truth environment stiffness -- achieves higher task success and fewer failure modes (force buildup, oscillation, tool breakage, safety stops) than admittance-only execution on real contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: jointly predicting compliant action + controller-mode/stiffness parameters favored over predicting action alone and leaving controller behavior fixed (e.g., admittance-only), for contact-rich manipulation
claims.conditions: real-robot box-flipping and line-pressing tasks

title: ScrewMimic: Bimanual Imitation from Human Videos with Screw Space Projection

claims.claim: Modeling the interaction between two hands as a screw motion and defining a new 'screw action' space for bimanual manipulation enables learning several complex bimanual behaviors from a single human video demonstration plus self-supervised fine-tuning, outperforming baselines that interpret demonstrations and fine-tune directly in the original (per-arm) motion space
claims.direction: a structured, kinematically-motivated action space (screw motion) favored over raw per-arm/joint action spaces for learning from very few (single) human video demonstrations
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, single human video demonstration, self-supervised policy fine-tuning through interaction

title: DemoGrasp: Universal Dexterous Grasping from a Single Demonstration

claims.claim: Starting from a single successful demonstration trajectory and editing it (wrist pose determines where to grasp, joint angles determine how to grasp), formulated as a single-step MDP optimized with RL across hundreds of objects in parallel simulation with a simple reward, achieves 95% success on DexGraspNet objects and 84.6% average success across diverse dexterous-hand embodiments on six unseen object datasets while trained on only 175 objects
claims.direction: single-demonstration trajectory-editing + RL-based generalization favored over training a closed-loop grasping policy from scratch with extensive reward/curriculum design, for object- and embodiment-generalizable grasping
claims.conditions: simulation training (175 objects), zero-shot to unseen object datasets

claims.claim: Through vision-based imitation learning distilled from the simulation-trained policy, the system grasps 110 unseen real-world objects including small, thin items, and generalizes to spatial, background, and lighting changes, supporting both RGB and depth inputs and extending to language-guided grasping in cluttered scenes
claims.direction: single-demo-edited, RL-optimized grasping policy (distilled to vision-based imitation) favored for robustness to spatial/background/lighting shift and novel real-world objects
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, 110 unseen objects, RGB and depth input support

title: PoCoDP3: Pose- and Contact-Aware Visual-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich 3D Manipulation

claims.claim: A reference-guided diffusion policy that leverages reference action offsets to reduce the number of denoising steps significantly accelerates inference while maintaining action quality, and combined with dual-branch tactile+3D point-cloud fusion, consistently outperforms representative 2D and 3D policies in both accuracy and inference efficiency on contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: reference-guided (offset-based) diffusion sampling favored over standard full-step diffusion sampling for inference speed without quality loss, when combined with multi-modal (point cloud + tactile) fusion
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, requires tactile sensing hardware

title: DISC: Decoupling Instruction from State-Conditioned Control via Policy Generation

claims.claim: Standard language-conditioned policies that process instructions and observations through shared parameters are prone to 'observation leakage' (learning scene-to-action shortcuts that bypass language grounding); DISC instead uses a hypernetwork to generate an entire task-specific visuomotor policy's parameters from the instruction alone (the generated policy never directly accesses language), structurally eliminating this leakage pathway, outperforming all entangled (shared-parameter) baselines on LIBERO-90 and Meta-World and even surpassing large-scale pretrained pi0 despite using no external pretraining data; on a real-world benchmark where all tasks share identical visual context, DISC substantially outperforms entangled alternatives, confirming language (not visual shortcuts) drives behavior
claims.direction: hypernetwork-generated, language-only-conditioned policy weights (structurally decoupling instruction from state) favored over standard shared-parameter language-conditioned architectures for genuine language grounding and avoiding scene-to-action shortcut learning
claims.conditions: LIBERO-90 + Meta-World simulation, plus a real-world benchmark with identical visual context across tasks (isolating language grounding), trained entirely from scratch on standard data budgets

title: World Tokens: Enhancing Embodied Policies with Training-Time World Modeling

claims.claim: A World Adapter transforms VLM features into a fixed set of world tokens that jointly condition a future-video denoiser (during training only) and serve as the action expert's sole visual-language context, letting gradients from future-video-denoising training shape the action-relevant representation; at deployment the world-model branch is removed entirely (no online video-model inference), and with only a 2B backbone and no embodied action pretraining, this is highly competitive on LIBERO, best-reported average on SIMPLER, and substantially improves real-world success over a matched action-only baseline, while generating each action chunk at standard VLA-level latency
claims.direction: training-time-only world-model auxiliary objective (removed at deployment) favored over either no world modeling or retaining an online video-world-model in the control loop, for improving action policy quality with zero added inference cost
claims.conditions: LIBERO + SIMPLER simulation benchmarks + real-world (R1 Pro) experiments, 2B-parameter backbone, no embodied action pretraining

title: Planning-Guided Diffusion Policy Learning for Generalizable Contact-Rich Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Using model-based motion planners to generate large-scale, high-quality synthetic demonstration trajectories in high-fidelity physics simulation (across randomized environments and diverse objects), then training a task-conditioned diffusion policy via behavior cloning on this synthetic data, enables a bimanual robot to manipulate diverse objects effectively in both simulation and the real world, addressing the difficulty of acquiring sufficient demonstration data for contact-rich bimanual tasks
claims.direction: planner-generated synthetic demonstrations favored over relying solely on collected human demonstrations for contact-rich bimanual tasks with limited natural data availability
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, simulation-generated demonstrations + real-world evaluation, specific feature extraction/task representation/augmentation choices needed to close sim-to-real gap

title: RoboAgent: Generalization and Efficiency in Robot Manipulation via Semantic Augmentations and Action Chunking

claims.claim: Using semantic data augmentations to rapidly multiply an existing dataset, combined with an action-chunking representation designed to extract performant policies from small yet diverse multi-modal datasets without overfitting, a single policy (RoboAgent) trained on merely 7500 demonstrations learns 12 unique skills and generalizes over 38 tasks across diverse kitchen scenes, outperforming prior methods by over 40% in unseen situations while being more sample efficient
claims.direction: semantic augmentation + action-chunking representation favored over naive scaling of raw demonstrations for multi-task generalization under a limited data budget
claims.conditions: real-world kitchen manipulation, 7500 total demonstrations across 12 skills/38 tasks

title: Rapidly Adapting Policies to the Real World via Simulation-Guided Fine-Tuning

claims.claim: Using a value function learned in simulation to guide real-world exploration during RL fine-tuning (Simulation-Guided Fine-Tuning, SGFT) substantially outperforms baseline fine-tuning methods across five real-world dexterous manipulation tasks where zero-shot sim-to-real transfer fails entirely, requiring up to an order of magnitude fewer real-world samples and succeeding at difficult tasks where prior approaches fail entirely
claims.direction: simulation-derived value-function-guided exploration favored over unstructured real-world exploration for sample-efficient real-world RL fine-tuning after failed zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: 5 real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, precise/force-sensitive manipulation where physics-engine misspecification breaks direct sim-to-real transfer

title: Latent Diffusion Planning for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Separating a diffusion-based planner (which can leverage action-free demonstrations) from a diffusion-based inverse-dynamics model (which can leverage suboptimal data), both operating over a learned compact latent space, lets Latent Diffusion Planning benefit from denser supervision from suboptimal and action-free data that standard imitation-learning architectures cannot use, outperforming SOTA IL approaches on simulated visual robotic manipulation tasks
claims.direction: modular planner+inverse-dynamics decomposition (able to use action-free and suboptimal data) favored over monolithic end-to-end imitation policies limited to expert action-labeled demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulated visual robotic manipulation tasks

title: SAPS: Shared Autonomy for Policy Steering by Blending Teleoperation with a Pretrained VLA

claims.claim: Blending real-time human teleoperation commands with a pretrained VLA's actions at the action level (via arbitration strategies such as dynamic cosine-similarity agreement between human and policy actions, requiring no policy retraining, auxiliary models, or architectural changes) improves task success rate over autonomous execution by up to 82% in both simulation (LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, CALVIN) and real-world robot hardware, while drastically reducing human intervention compared to pure teleoperation and achieving faster completion than either autonomous execution or pure teleoperation alone
claims.direction: action-level shared autonomy (blending brittle pretrained VLA actions with lightweight human correction) favored over either pure autonomous VLA execution or pure teleoperation for reliability under out-of-distribution perturbations, with zero retraining cost
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, CALVIN) + real-world robot hardware, model-agnostic (works with any pretrained VLA policy)

title: Long-Horizon Manipulation via Trace-Conditioned VLA Planning

claims.claim: Decoupling a task-management VLM (which predicts a progress-aware remaining plan combining a done+remaining subtask split and a compact 2D visual-trace keypoint trajectory) from the executor VLA, invoked in a receding-horizon manner, yields an implicit closed loop where failed steps persist in subsequent plan outputs and traces update accordingly, enabling automatic continuation/replanning without hand-crafted recovery logic; this shows strong gains in long-horizon success, robustness, and OOD generalization on simulation and a real Franka robot
claims.direction: progress-aware, trace-conditioned receding-horizon planning (implicit closed-loop replanning) favored over flat long-horizon VLA execution or hand-crafted recovery logic
claims.conditions: simulation + real Franka robot, long-horizon multi-step manipulation tasks

title: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models via Zero-Shot Geometric Evaluation

claims.claim: Ranking sampled rollouts of a world-action model by cross-view depth-reprojection consistency of their predicted futures (using a frozen geometry foundation model, training-free) improves fixed-budget Best-of-N task success in every tested setting (e.g., RoboCasa average 66.3% to 68.4% with one backbone, 80.8% to 82.5% with another); a lightweight gating mechanism that only triggers extra sampling when the initial rollout looks internally inconsistent recovers 74.8% of the always-on success gain while only sampling extra on 26.2% of decision points
claims.direction: training-free, geometry-consistency-based selective test-time scaling (gated Best-of-N) favored over always-on best-of-N sampling or no test-time scaling, for efficiently trading extra compute for success rate
claims.conditions: RoboCasa, LIBERO Long, RoboTwin 2.0 simulation benchmarks, multiple WAM backbones, requires a world-action model that predicts future observations alongside actions

title: Generalizable Robotic Insertion with World Models

claims.claim: A single world model trained on up to 90 insertion tasks with geometrically diverse parts, combining robot proprioception with raw visual observations from a wrist-mounted camera, achieves 56% zero-shot success on unseen objects with unknown geometry, compared to just 7% for a model-free baseline
claims.direction: model-based (world-model) approach using wrist-camera + proprioception favored over model-free baselines for zero-shot generalization to novel object geometries
claims.conditions: real-robot insertion tasks, wrist-mounted camera + proprioceptive input, up to 90 training tasks with diverse parts

claims.claim: Performance improves as more objects are included in the training dataset (demonstrating scalability), and fine-tuning the generalist world model on held-out objects is significantly more data-efficient than training from scratch, in some cases achieving better asymptotic performance
claims.direction: scaling training-object diversity + fine-tuning a pretrained generalist world model favored over training task-specific models from scratch for both generalization and data efficiency on held-out objects
claims.conditions: real-world insertion tasks, wrist-camera + proprioception input

why_deep_read: Uses exactly our sensor configuration (wrist-mounted camera + proprioception) and directly quantifies generalization to unseen object geometry (56% vs 7%), which mirrors our 'different-looking pumpkin' failure mode; full text would clarify the world-model architecture/training cost and whether the scalability trend (more objects -> better zero-shot) holds at our much smaller task/demo scale.

title: EquivAct: SIM(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Policies beyond Rigid Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Using SIM(3)-equivariant network structures for both the visual object representation and the policy architecture guarantees generalization across all possible object translations, 3D rotations, and scales by construction (unlike data-augmentation-based approaches, which do not guarantee such generalization); trained with only 20 human demonstrations of a tabletop task, the learned policy transfers zero-shot to a mobile manipulation task in a much larger setup with objects differing substantially in scale, position, and orientation from the demonstrations
claims.direction: built-in SIM(3) equivariance (architectural guarantee) favored over data-augmentation-only approaches for generalizing to novel object scale/position/orientation
claims.conditions: 20 human demonstrations, real-robot experiments across deformable and articulated object manipulation tasks, zero-shot transfer to substantially different scale/setup

title: Survey of π0, π0-FAST, and π0.5: Vision-Language-Action Models in the Physical AI Framework

claims.claim: pi0-FAST's Frequency-space Action Sequence Tokenization (FAST) scheme enables up to 5 times faster training than pi0's diffusion-based action policy while matching diffusion model performance; pi0.5 extends the architecture with co-training on diverse data sources and a hierarchical policy structure to achieve, for the first time in this model family, successful robotic manipulation in entirely new unseen environments
claims.direction: frequency-domain discrete action tokenization (FAST) favored over diffusion action heads for training speed at matched performance; hierarchical policy + diverse co-training favored for novel-environment generalization
claims.conditions: comparative survey of the pi0 model family (foundation VLA models), not original experiments

title: ArticuBot: Learning Universal Articulated Object Manipulation Policy via Large Scale Simulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical policy representation, where a high-level policy learns the end-effector sub-goal and a low-level policy learns how to move the end-effector conditioned on that predicted goal, achieves much better object-level generalization than a non-hierarchical version of the same system, when distilling 42.3k simulation-generated demonstrations into a point-cloud-based neural policy for zero-shot sim2real transfer
claims.direction: hierarchical (sub-goal-conditioned) policy decomposition favored over a flat/non-hierarchical policy for generalizing across large variations in object geometry, size, and articulation type
claims.conditions: real-robot zero-shot sim2real transfer, multiple real robot platforms (fixed Franka arms at two labs, mobile X-Arm), point-cloud input

claims.claim: A weighted displacement model for the high-level policy that grounds predictions into the existing 3D structure of the scene outperforms alternative (non-3D-grounded) high-level policy representations
claims.direction: 3D-scene-structure-grounded high-level action prediction favored over ungrounded alternative representations
claims.conditions: same real-robot zero-shot sim2real setting, point-cloud-based policy

title: Learning Real-World Action-Video Dynamics with Heterogeneous Masked Autoregression

claims.claim: Heterogeneous pre-training from observations and action sequences across different robotic embodiments, domains, and tasks, using masked autoregression over quantized/soft video tokens, achieves better visual fidelity and controllability than previous robotic video generation models while running 15 times faster in the real world, enabling the resulting model to serve as a video simulator for policy evaluation and synthetic data generation
claims.direction: heterogeneous cross-embodiment masked-autoregressive video-dynamics pretraining favored over embodiment-specific or single-domain robotic video world models, for both quality and speed
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment, cross-domain, cross-task pretraining; used post-hoc as a video simulator/data generator, not evaluated as a direct control policy

title: Ego2Robot: Scalable Robot Data Synthesis from Egocentric Human Data

claims.claim: Joint pretraining on Ego2Robot-synthesized data (converted from egocentric human manipulation videos via action retargeting and robot-arm visual synthesis, 18,561 hours across 15 robot morphologies) plus real robot data consistently improves out-of-distribution generalization across multiple disentangled perturbation types -- visual appearance, scene layout, embodiment morphology, and task semantics -- evaluated on an extended RoboTwin2.0 benchmark, with benefits validated on real-robot deployment
claims.direction: large-scale egocentric-human-video-derived synthetic robot data (joint pretraining with real robot data) favored over training on robot data alone, specifically for robustness to visual-appearance and scene-layout perturbations among others
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2.0-based simulation benchmark with disentangled perturbation axes + real-robot deployment validation, requires substantial upstream video-to-robot synthesis pipeline

title: Direction-Scale Decomposition in Action Representation: Rethinking What to Tokenize for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Conventional pose-increment (delta) action representations are sensitive to execution speed and dataset-specific normalization, obscuring shared geometric structure; decomposing translation/rotation increments into separate direction and scale components before tokenization (Direction-Scale Decomposition, DSD) improves average success rates with both uniform-binning and B-spline-based tokenizers on LIBERO, and outperforms plain binning by 10.3 percentage points on SimplerEnv under mixed-dataset training, with real-robot gains both with and without robotics pretraining
claims.direction: direction/scale-decomposed delta action representation favored over raw pose-increment tokenization, especially for training on large/diverse dataset mixtures
claims.conditions: LIBERO + SimplerEnv simulation, real-robot experiments, discrete-token VLA models (tested with binning and BEAST tokenizers)

title: DualCoT-VLA: Visual-Linguistic Chain of Thought via Parallel Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Standard step-by-step autoregressive Chain-of-Thought reasoning in VLA models causes high inference latency and compounding errors; replacing it with a parallel CoT mechanism (separate learnable query tokens for visual low-level spatial CoT and linguistic high-level planning CoT, processed via single-step forward reasoning instead of autoregressive decoding) achieves state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO and RoboCasa GR1 benchmarks as well as real-world platforms
claims.direction: parallel (single-step) dual-modality CoT reasoning favored over sequential autoregressive single-modality CoT for reducing inference latency while retaining both low-level spatial and high-level planning reasoning
claims.conditions: LIBERO + RoboCasa GR1 simulation benchmarks + real-world platforms

title: Emergent Dexterity via Diverse Resets and Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Systematically generating diverse simulator resets (exposing the RL algorithm to a wide range of robot-object interactions) rather than relying on reward/curriculum engineering or human demonstrations lets on-policy RL solve long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks using a single fixed reward and hyperparameters, scaling gracefully with compute and learning robust policies over much wider ranges of initial conditions than baselines; visuomotor policies distilled from this approach show robust retrying behavior and substantially higher success rates than baselines when transferred to the real world zero-shot
claims.direction: diverse programmatic simulator resets favored over reward/curriculum engineering or demonstration-based approaches for scaling RL to long-horizon dexterous tasks and improving real-world zero-shot transfer
claims.conditions: long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks, large-scale parallel simulation, zero-shot sim-to-real transfer

title: Bi-HIL: Bilateral Control-Based Multimodal Hierarchical Imitation Learning via Subtask-Level Progress Rate and Keyframe Memory for Long-Horizon Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Stabilizing hierarchical policy coordination by integrating keyframe memory with a subtask-level progress rate (modeling phase progression within the active subtask, conditioning both high- and low-level policies) achieves consistent improvements over flat policies and ablated variants on unimanual and bimanual real-robot long-horizon contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: keyframe memory + explicit subtask-progress conditioning favored over flat (non-hierarchical, non-progress-aware) imitation policies for long-horizon coordination under contact uncertainty
claims.conditions: real-robot unimanual and bimanual manipulation tasks, bilateral (force-aware) control

title: MAGMA-GEN: Validated Recovery Supervision from Ambiguous Failures via Counterfactual Re-Execution

claims.claim: Converting ambiguous failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision -- by having a privileged coach hypothesize an early decision-level error and propose a correction, retaining the candidate only if re-execution from the same state improves downstream progress -- produces supervised recovery examples from the agent's own failure distribution without per-step human demonstrations, improving task success and recovery capability over distillation and trajectory-repair baselines in both simulation and real-robot execution
claims.direction: self-generated, re-execution-validated recovery supervision favored over both standard supervised learning (which lacks recovery-state data) and trajectory-repair/distillation baselines for teaching recovery behavior without extra human demonstrations
claims.conditions: interactive long-horizon manipulation tasks, simulation and real-robot execution

title: Q-Learning With World Models

claims.claim: Using a world model to perform test-time search over imagined trajectories on top of Q-learning (selecting high-value actions during rollouts and evaluation), while training the policy and value function only on real transitions (avoiding compounding model bias from optimizing directly on imagined rollouts), significantly outperforms strong prior state-of-the-art methods on Robomimic and LIBERO in both sample efficiency and performance
claims.direction: world-model-guided test-time search grounded in real-transition-trained Q-learning favored over directly optimizing policy/value on imagined rollouts, for sample-efficient manipulation RL/fine-tuning
claims.conditions: Robomimic and LIBERO simulation benchmarks (offline-to-online RL / VLA fine-tuning setting)

title: Manipulate-Anything: Automating Real-World Robots using Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: A scalable automated demonstration-generation method using VLMs, requiring no privileged state information and no hand-designed skills, generates trajectories for all 7 real-world and 14 simulation test tasks (outperforming existing automated methods like VoxPoser); behavior cloning policies trained on these VLM-generated demonstrations are MORE robust than policies trained on human demonstrations, or on data generated by VoxPoser, Scaling-up, and Code-As-Policies
claims.direction: VLM-automated demonstration generation favored over human teleoperated demonstrations (and over prior automated-generation baselines) for training more robust behavior-cloning policies
claims.conditions: 7 real-world + 14 simulation manipulation tasks, no privileged state information required, static objects

title: EnerVerse: Envisioning Embodied Future Space for Robotics Manipulation

claims.claim: A policy head (EnerVerse-A) that reuses features from the first denoising step of a chunk-wise autoregressive video-diffusion world model and predicts action chunks directly (rather than requiring full video generation at inference) achieves state-of-the-art performance in both simulation and real-world tasks while running at about 280ms per 8-step action chunk on a single RTX 4090
claims.direction: reusing first-denoising-step features for direct action-chunk prediction (instead of full future-video generation at inference) favored for combining world-model-quality action generation with practical inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation manipulation tasks, multi-view video representation, single RTX 4090 GPU

title: CLAR: Learning 3D Representations for Robotic Manipulation by Fusing Masked Reconstruction with Multi-Level Contrastive Alignment

claims.claim: Masked Autoencoding (MAE) on 3D point clouds captures spatial-geometric features but lacks semantics, while contrastive learning distills semantics from 2D foundation models but is ill-suited to fine-grained manipulation details; unifying MAE with global cross-modal contrastive learning plus an adaptive local alignment mechanism (deformable attention forcing correspondence between local 3D geometry and 2D visual features) achieves state-of-the-art visuomotor policy learning performance in simulation and the real world, significantly outperforming existing 3D pretraining methods
claims.direction: combined global (contrastive semantic) + local (geometry-aligned) 3D representation pretraining favored over either pure MAE or pure global contrastive pretraining alone for manipulation policy learning
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world visuomotor policy learning, point-cloud-based pretraining

title: Knowledge-Driven Imitation Learning: Enabling Generalization Across Diverse Conditions

claims.claim: Using external structural semantic knowledge (a semantic keypoint graph as a category-level knowledge template, matched via a coarse-to-fine structural+semantic algorithm) to abstract object representations, the method surpasses image-based diffusion policies while using only one-quarter of the expert demonstrations, on three real-world robotic manipulation tasks
claims.direction: knowledge-template-based (keypoint-graph) object abstraction favored over image-based diffusion policies for demonstration-efficient imitation learning
claims.conditions: 3 real-world robotic manipulation tasks, category-level generalization

claims.claim: The knowledge-driven approach demonstrates robustness across novel objects, backgrounds, and lighting conditions not seen during training
claims.direction: semantic keypoint-graph object abstraction favored over standard image-based policies for robustness to novel objects, backgrounds, and lighting
claims.conditions: same 3 real-world tasks, explicit generalization testing across objects/backgrounds/lighting

title: ControlVLA: Few-shot Object-centric Adaptation for Pre-trained Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Bridging a pre-trained VLA model with object-centric representations via a ControlNet-style architecture (zero-initialized projection layers that gradually adapt the pretrained policy without overwriting prior knowledge) achieves a 76.7% success rate across 6 diverse real-world tasks (pouring cubes, folding clothes, etc.) while requiring only 10-20 demonstrations, versus traditional fine-tuning approaches needing more than 100 demonstrations for comparable success
claims.direction: ControlNet-style zero-initialized object-centric adapter fine-tuning favored over standard full/direct fine-tuning of a pretrained VLA for data-efficient adaptation in data-scarce real-world settings
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, 6 diverse tasks, 10-20 demonstrations per task

claims.claim: ControlVLA extends to long-horizon tasks and is robust to unseen objects and backgrounds
claims.direction: object-centric ControlNet-adapter fine-tuning favored over standard fine-tuning for robustness to novel objects/backgrounds even in a low-demonstration regime
claims.conditions: same real-world experimental setting

why_deep_read: Almost exactly our scenario: fine-tuning a pretrained VLA with very few real-world demonstrations (10-20, close to our 50-100 budget) while remaining robust to unseen objects/backgrounds, with a concrete large quantified gain over standard fine-tuning (76.7% success at 10-20 demos vs needing 100+ for comparable results); full text would give the exact adapter architecture and whether it is compatible with a SmolVLA-scale backbone for our SO-101 setup.

title: ProgressVLA: Progress-Guided Diffusion Policy for Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Pre-training a task-progress estimator on large-scale unsupervised video-text robotic datasets achieves a low prediction residual (0.07 on a [0,1] scale) and zero-shot generalizes to unseen real-world samples; wrapping this in a differentiable pipeline (an inverse dynamics world model maps predicted action tokens to future latent visual states, scored by the progress estimator, with maximal-progress regularization refining the action tokens) yields substantial improvements in success rate and generalization over strong baselines on CALVIN, LIBERO, and real-world robot deployment
claims.direction: differentiable progress-guided action refinement (using a pretrained, zero-shot-generalizing progress estimator) favored over VLA models lacking progress awareness (relying on hand-crafted task-termination heuristics), especially for long-horizon cascaded sub-goal tasks
claims.conditions: CALVIN + LIBERO simulation benchmarks + real-world robot deployment

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Whole-Body Motion Control for Humanoids With Position-Controlled Joints

claims.claim: Real-world position-controlled joints (e.g., NAO robot) have hidden, proprietary control loops and nonlinear dynamics that most simulators (assuming torque-controlled or idealized PD actuators) fail to capture; performing system identification on the physical robot to estimate an equivalent torque-space PID actuator model, combined with a learnable inverse-kinematics module, enables a simulation-trained RL policy to transfer directly to the real position-controlled robot with zero fine-tuning
claims.direction: explicit actuator system identification (equivalent torque-space PID model for position-controlled joints) favored over assuming idealized/torque-controlled actuator dynamics in simulation, for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real position-controlled hardware
claims.conditions: real position-controlled humanoid robot (NAO), whole-body motion control (not manipulation), zero-shot transfer with no real-robot fine-tuning

title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Selectively invoking world-model imagination only at interaction-relevant states (rather than at every step), with bounded multi-view rollouts scored by progress/completion signals used to refine actions from real interaction contexts, applied to both pi0 and pi0.5, yields consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full (always-on) imagination, and shows substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts
claims.direction: selectively-scheduled, bounded world-model imagination favored over always-on/unbounded imagination for efficient VLA post-training, on the same pi0/pi0.5 model family relevant to our SmolVLA-class setup
claims.conditions: pi0 and pi0.5 backbones, diverse manipulation tasks, real-world distribution-shift evaluation

title: ARP: Enhancing Quantized Skill Abstractions via Visual Alignment and Iterative Refinement for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Discrete quantized skill representations for long-horizon manipulation have weak visual-semantic grounding (since prior methods encode only action trajectories into latent skills) and incur precision errors from discrete tokenization; adding a contrastive visual-action alignment objective (grounding skill selection in visual embeddings) plus a lightweight Iterative Residual Head that performs two-step refinement to recover fine-grained control achieves SOTA performance on LIBERO and Meta-World, validated with real-robot gains on a humanoid platform
claims.direction: visually-grounded discrete skill tokens plus a residual refinement head favored over ungrounded discrete skill tokenization alone, for combining semantic skill selection with precise low-level execution
claims.conditions: LIBERO + Meta-World simulation, real-robot experiments on Kuavo 4 Pro humanoid, two manipulation tasks

title: PlayFusion: Skill Acquisition via Diffusion from Language-Annotated Play

claims.claim: Learning a multi-task conditional denoising diffusion model over unstructured, uncurated 'play' data (labeled with language in hindsight, rather than curated task-specific demonstrations) can gracefully handle the multimodality and noise of such data and generate diverse, interesting robot behaviors, demonstrated effectively across a wide variety of simulated and real-world environments
claims.direction: diffusion-based skill extraction from unstructured hindsight-labeled play data favored over requiring curated, goal-directed expert demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world environments, language-annotated play data

claims.claim: Introducing discrete bottlenecks into the conditional diffusion behavior-generation process encourages the robotic agent to acquire a reusable, interpretable vocabulary of skills
claims.direction: discrete bottleneck combined with continuous diffusion generation favored over pure continuous diffusion for producing a structured, reusable skill vocabulary
claims.conditions: same play-data learning setting

title: Human Demonstrations are Generalizable Knowledge for Robots

claims.claim: Treating human demonstration videos as a source of distillable, hierarchical, generalizable knowledge (observation knowledge -> action knowledge -> pattern/task-object knowledge), rather than as literal instruction sequences to replicate, allows an LLM-based planner to retrieve and apply relevant knowledge to new tasks/object instances, substantially enhancing task success rate versus treating demonstrations as direct instructions
claims.direction: knowledge-distillation-based use of human demonstrations favored over treating demonstration videos as literal action-sequence instructions, for generalizing to new tasks/objects
claims.conditions: real-world robot experiments across a range of tasks and scenes

title: ManiCM: Real-time 3D Diffusion Policy via Consistency Model for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Imposing a consistency constraint on a point-cloud-conditioned diffusion process (via consistency distillation that predicts the action sample directly rather than the noise) enables one-step-inference robot action generation, accelerating the state-of-the-art diffusion method by 10x in average inference speed across 31 robotic manipulation tasks (Adroit, Metaworld) while maintaining competitive average success rate
claims.direction: consistency-distilled one-step 3D diffusion policy favored over standard multi-step diffusion policies for point-cloud-conditioned action generation, for large latency reduction with minimal accuracy loss
claims.conditions: 31 simulated manipulation tasks (Adroit, Metaworld benchmarks), point-cloud observation input

title: Lambda: A Benchmark for Data-Efficiency in Long-Horizon Indoor Mobile Manipulation Robotics

claims.claim: On a realistically-sized benchmark of 571 human-collected long-horizon, language-conditioned, multi-room pick-and-place demonstrations, end-to-end learning methods yield lower success rates even when pretrained, while a modular neuro-symbolic approach combining foundation models with task-and-motion planning performs significantly better while requiring less data
claims.direction: modular neuro-symbolic (foundation model + TAMP) approach favored over end-to-end learned policies for data efficiency on long-horizon, data-scarce mobile manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: 571 human-collected demonstrations, long-horizon multi-room/multi-floor mobile manipulation, simulated and real-world settings

title: RynnWorld-Teleop: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Digital Teleoperation

claims.claim: Replacing physical teleoperation with 'digital teleoperation' -- an operator's hand-pose stream drives a generative world model to synthesize high-fidelity egocentric robot videos from a single reference image, with the pose stream serving as an embodiment-agnostic action label retargetable to any robot -- produces policies that achieve effective zero-shot Sim2Real transfer when trained exclusively on this synthetic data, and augmenting real-world datasets with this digitally-teleoperated data consistently improves success rates
claims.direction: generative-world-model-based 'digital teleoperation' (decoupled from physical robot hardware) favored over physical teleoperation alone, both as a standalone data source and as an augmentation to real demonstrations
claims.conditions: dexterous and diverse bimanual tasks, real-time generation (40+ FPS on a single H100 GPU) via streaming autoregressive distillation

title: Towards Predictive, Aligned, and Scalable Robot Learning

claims.claim: Standard reconstruction-based action tokenization objectives induce latent representations biased toward low-level signal fidelity, causing misalignment between reconstruction quality and downstream control performance; a multi-stage modality pre-alignment strategy that progressively aligns action representations with latent world dynamics, vision, and language (rather than direct reconstruction) induces a more structured latent space, and the resulting model (Lumo-2) consistently outperforms strong VLA and world-action-model baselines, especially on tasks requiring temporal reasoning, physical understanding, or high control complexity
claims.direction: progressive multi-stage cross-modal alignment (world dynamics -> vision -> language) of action representations favored over direct reconstruction-based action tokenization for downstream control quality
claims.conditions: challenging real-world tasks including long-horizon and dexterous manipulation

title: SoftMimicGen: A Data Generation System for Scalable Robot Learning in Deformable Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Extending automated synthetic data generation (in the style of prior rigid-body MimicGen approaches) to deformable object manipulation tasks (threading, whipping, folding, pick-and-place on stuffed animals, rope, tissue, towel) across four robot embodiments including a single-arm manipulator enables training high-performing policies from the generated data, addressing a gap since synthetic-data generation had previously been limited to easy-to-simulate rigid-body tasks
claims.direction: automated synthetic demonstration generation (previously rigid-body-only) extended to deformable-object tasks favored over relying on real-world collected demonstrations for these harder-to-simulate task types
claims.conditions: simulated deformable-object manipulation across single-arm, bimanual, humanoid, and surgical robot embodiments

title: Learning Robust Execution in Robotic Manipulation with Agentic Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: An agentic policy that reasons over recent execution history and selects among a small set of execution modes (rather than directly learning low-level corrective actions) to detect execution-quality degradation and trigger recovery to previously-visited nominal states achieves up to 13.7% improvement in success rate under standard settings and up to 39.2% improvement under disturbance settings on LIBERO, versus VLA baselines lacking explicit execution-stability assessment/recovery mechanisms
claims.direction: high-level agentic monitoring + recovery-mode selection (added on top of a base VLA) favored over VLA policies without explicit execution-stability mechanisms, especially under disturbance/perturbation
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation benchmark, standard and disturbance settings

title: Unified Condition-Action Modeling for Accurate One-Step Action Generation

claims.claim: Representing observation conditions, timestep conditions, interval conditions, and action tokens in a single unified sequence processed by a Unified Condition-Action Transformer (rather than treating conditions as auxiliary/static signals separate from evolving action trajectories) improves average success rate by 9.3 percentage points over the strongest baseline while achieving 45.6x and 33.4x speedups over DP3 and Simple DP3 respectively, and remaining 4.3x/2.3x faster than one-step FlowPolicy/MP1
