claims.direction: jointly-evolving, unified condition-action token modeling favored over treating conditions as static auxiliary signals, for simultaneously improving one-step action-generation accuracy and inference speed
claims.conditions: comparison against DP3, Simple DP3, FlowPolicy, MP1 baselines (setting/benchmark not fully specified in abstract)

title: 2AM: Grounding Agent-Side Memory as Guidance for Steerable Action Models in Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Keeping task memory entirely on the agent side (a multimodal Agent compiles interaction history into subtask language plus optional 2D grasp/place/move hints) while the Action Model itself remains a single RGB-based, episodically stateless executor (no depth, online geometry, or planner-based object motion) reaches 76.3% average completion on LIBERO-Mem, a 61.5-point improvement over the strongest reported baseline (14.8%), when the VLA is trained with structured hint labels under condition dropout, spatial noise, and temporal jitter to tolerate imperfect Agent outputs
claims.direction: agent-side (not policy-side) memory with a stateless, RGB-only action-executor favored over embedding memory/depth/geometry directly into the action policy, for long-horizon memory-dependent tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Mem benchmark, RGB-only action model (no depth or online geometry required for the executor)

title: Robot World Models Are Not Invariant to How the Actions Are Written

claims.claim: A latent dynamics/world model trained on one action parameterization (absolute joint targets vs deltas relative to current state) catastrophically fails when handed the identical commanded trajectory written in the other parameterization: retrieval performance degrades 2.6-13.4x across three robot datasets and two morphologies, goal-conditioned action selection success falls from 53% to 15%, and on PushT the two latent beliefs about the same future are nearly orthogonal (cosine similarity 0.067, worst case -0.377) -- even though the two encodings are mutually reconstructible with R^2=0.996, meaning no information is technically lost
claims.direction: absolute vs delta action parameterization are NOT interchangeable for a model conditioned on actions, even when mathematically mutually reconstructible; this is a caution against treating action-space choice as an arbitrary/free engineering decision that models will adapt to gracefully
claims.conditions: three robot datasets, two robot morphologies, evaluated via a proposed test distinguishing valid re-parameterization from lossy summary/sensor swap; a partial repair (averaging over the two encodings in the training objective) restores task performance on most but not all tested axes

why_deep_read: Directly and surprisingly informs our Q02 action-space decision (absolute vs delta): shows that switching representation is not a benign choice for anything conditioned on actions (e.g., a world-model auxiliary objective, Q09) even though the encodings carry the same information; full text would clarify whether this failure mode also applies to plain action-only (non-world-model) policies and what the 'averaging' partial fix requires, which is directly actionable for our Q02/Q09 design.

title: EquAct: An SE(3)-Equivariant Multi-Task Transformer for Open-Loop Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard transformers processing 3D observations and language instructions lack built-in geometric-consistency guarantees, resulting in unpredictable behavior under SE(3) transformations of the scene; a theoretically-guaranteed SE(3)-equivariant transformer (equivariant point-cloud U-net with spherical Fourier features + SE(3)-invariant FiLM layers for language conditioning) achieves state-of-the-art spatial generalization across 18 RLBench simulation tasks under both SE(3) and SE(2) perturbations, and on 4 physical tasks
claims.direction: architecturally-guaranteed SE(3)-equivariant policy/vision design favored over standard (non-equivariant) transformers for robustness to scene pose transformations, as an alternative to purely data-augmentation-based robustness
claims.conditions: 18 RLBench simulation tasks with SE(3)/SE(2) scene perturbations + 4 real physical tasks, 3D point-cloud input, language-conditioned multi-task policy

title: DynaMimicGen: A Data Generation Framework for Robot Learning of Dynamic Tasks

claims.claim: Starting from only a few human demonstrations (potentially as few as one), segmenting them into sub-tasks and using Dynamic Movement Primitives to generalize each skill to novel, continually-changing scenes (rather than assuming static environments or simple interpolation, as prior data-generation methods do) increases dataset-generation success rates by 3.6% to 232.7% over MimicGen (which itself requires ten demonstrations) across five manipulation tasks, and the resulting more-variable datasets let Diffusion Policy and Behavior Cloning agents consistently outperform MimicGen-trained policies
claims.direction: DMP-based dynamic-scene-aware synthetic data generation from very few (potentially single) demonstrations favored over prior static-environment synthetic-data-generation methods (which need more seed demonstrations) for both data quality and downstream policy performance
claims.conditions: 5 manipulation tasks (Stack, Square, HammerCleanup, MugCleanup, NutAssembly), both static and dynamic task settings, injects dynamic perturbations during generation

title: TGM-VLA: Task-Guided Mixup for Sampling-Efficient and Robust Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Redesigning keyframe sampling to reduce keyframe redundancy and imbalanced temporal distribution reduces memory consumption by 80% and accelerates training speed by 5x versus the prevalent RLBench sampling strategy, without sacrificing performance
claims.direction: redesigned, non-redundant keyframe sampling favored over standard dense/imbalanced keyframe sampling for training efficiency
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation benchmark, keyframe-based imitation learning

claims.claim: A task-guided mixup technique that dynamically fuses point clouds and action heatmaps according to task instructions greatly improves robustness to distractors and performance in multi-goal scenarios, achieving 90.5% success on RLBench and 68.8% on the COLOSSEUM benchmark under challenging interference conditions, state-of-the-art
claims.direction: task-conditioned mixup augmentation of point-cloud/action representations favored over standard training for robustness to distractor objects
claims.conditions: RLBench + COLOSSEUM simulation benchmarks, point-cloud-based multi-view policy, also notes that reprojecting point clouds onto multi-view images with a black background makes dark objects hard to distinguish, motivating a color-inversion projection fix

title: Beyond Attention Magnitude: Leveraging Inter-layer Rank Consistency for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: High-attention visual tokens in VLA models are task-dependent and using attention magnitude alone as a static token-pruning criterion can even degrade policy performance; a training-free dynamic framework (TIES) that adaptively balances attention magnitude with inter-layer token-ranking consistency improves average success rate by 6% while reducing visual token usage by 78% on the CogACT+SIMPLER benchmark, generalizing across diverse decoders and benchmarks
claims.direction: dynamic, rank-consistency-guided visual token selection favored over static attention-magnitude-based token pruning for simultaneously improving both latency (fewer tokens) and accuracy, with no additional training
claims.conditions: CogACT + SIMPLER benchmark (simulation), training-free method applicable to existing VLA decoders

title: PGDG: Physically Grounded Data Generation for Robust Bimanual Policy Learning from a Single Demonstration

claims.claim: Iterating between a physics-grounded sampler and a dataset curator to expand a single demonstration into a compact dataset of physically plausible, successful, and diverse recovery behaviors (relabeling risky states with corrective actions via short-horizon sampling-based control) consistently outperforms spatial-only augmentation across four bimanual manipulation tasks in both simulation and zero-shot real-world transfer; on RotateBox-Pitch, success improves from 38% to 93% in simulation and 35% to 82% in the real world, and the method also boosts foundation-model fine-tuning (GR00T) from 46% to 77% success
claims.direction: physically-grounded, single-demonstration-expanded recovery-behavior data generation favored over spatial-only data augmentation for both training-from-scratch policies and fine-tuning pretrained foundation models
claims.conditions: 4 bimanual manipulation tasks, simulation + zero-shot real-world transfer, also validated for GR00T foundation model fine-tuning

title: LAMP: Latent Motion Prior-Guided Real-World Learning for Dexterous Hand Manipulation

claims.claim: A latent motion prior module that maps recent hand-action histories to a compact, history-conditioned latent prior (decoded into executable high-dimensional targets) lets online residual RL make local corrections near demonstrated, contact-consistent motions rather than perturbing every joint independently; starting from small task-specific demonstration sets, this raises average IL success from 56.25% to 98.75% after online RL (100% on 3/4 real-robot tasks), versus raw, linear, and discrete hand-action interfaces
claims.direction: a shared, decodable latent motion-prior action interface favored over raw/linear/discrete high-dimensional action interfaces for making online RL fine-tuning of an imitation-pretrained policy sample-efficient and safe on real hardware
claims.conditions: 4 real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, small task-specific demonstration sets, imitation pretraining + online residual RL

title: RynnValue: Scaling Robotic Value Foundation Models with Temporal Distance

claims.claim: Replacing preference- or progress-based reward supervision anchors with temporal distance (directed cost-to-go to a language-specified goal, derivable directly from timestamps with no preference/progress annotation) lets a value foundation model scale to over 7,000 hours / 3M clips; it surpasses fully preference-supervised SOTA (Kendall's tau 0.675 vs 0.655) and more than doubles a progress-only counterpart (0.292), generalizing zero-shot to unseen tasks/embodiments/viewpoints, and raises real-world policy success from 52.5% to 72.5% online and 63.8% to 82.5% offline when converted to dense rewards
claims.direction: temporal-distance-based value/reward supervision (label-free, timestamp-derived) favored over preference- or progress-annotation-based reward models for scaling value learning and improving real-world RL-refined policy success
claims.conditions: large-scale heterogeneous robot corpora (7000+ hours), real-world online and offline RL policy refinement

title: Learning to Stack: Cube-Stacking Imitation Learning from Virtual Reality Demonstrations

claims.claim: A VR-based teleoperation pipeline (HTC Vive Pro 2 + Manus Quantum gloves) that separates demonstration collection from dataset construction (allowing recorded trajectories to be replayed and re-rendered for new observation/action spaces without repeating human teleoperation) collected 200 virtual demonstrations in 30 minutes, compared with 45 real-world demonstrations, and Isaac Mimic generated 100 additional synthetic samples from these
claims.direction: VR-based demonstration collection (decoupled from dataset construction, reusable across observation/action space changes) favored over direct real-world teleoperation for faster demonstration collection throughput
claims.conditions: 5-DoF arm in simulation, LeRobot-style dual-camera observations, behavior-cloning policy trained and evaluated in simulation only

title: Robot Generating Data for Learning Generalizable Visual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Training a separate data-generation policy operating on the state space to automatically self-generate meaningful actions and trajectories of ever-growing complexity ('robot self-teaching'), instead of relying on human-collected demonstrations, produces training data whose resulting visual policy can accomplish novel long-horizon testing goals with strong compositional generalization
claims.direction: self-generated (robot self-teaching) training trajectories favored over human-demonstrator-collected data for building visual policies with compositional generalization to novel long-horizon goals
claims.conditions: 2 simulated visual manipulation testbeds (multi-object stacking, Franka Kitchen)

title: VQ-ACE: Efficient Policy Search for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Action Chunking Embedding

claims.claim: Compressing human hand motion into a quantized latent space (Vector Quantized Action Chunking Embedding) significantly reduces action-space dimensionality while preserving key motion characteristics; combined with RL, this action-chunking embedding accelerates learning and improves exploration (faster convergence in cube stacking and in-hand reorientation tasks) versus learning directly in the raw high-dimensional action space
claims.direction: VQ-based action-chunk embedding favored over raw high-dimensional action-space exploration for both MPC-based (more human-like behavior, higher success) and RL-based (faster convergence) dexterous manipulation policy search
claims.conditions: dexterous biomimetic robotic hand, simulation tasks (Ball Rolling, Object Picking, cube stacking, in-hand cube reorientation)

title: RoboHorizon: An LLM-Assisted Multi-View World Model for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a pretrained LLM to generate dense reward structures for multi-stage sub-tasks from language instructions, combined with keyframe discovery integrated into a multi-view masked-autoencoder world-model architecture (to strengthen multi-stage perception), outperforms state-of-the-art visual model-based RL methods by 23.35% on short-horizon RLBench tasks and 29.23% on long-horizon RLBench + FurnitureBench tasks
claims.direction: LLM-generated dense sub-task rewards + multi-view keyframe-aware world model favored over standard sparse-reward visual model-based RL for long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: RLBench (4 short-horizon, 6 long-horizon tasks) + FurnitureBench (3 assembly tasks), simulation only

title: Posterior Behavioral Cloning: Pretraining BC Policies for Efficient RL Finetuning

claims.claim: Standard behavioral cloning (training a policy to directly match the exact actions played by the demonstrator) can fail to ensure coverage over the demonstrator's action distribution, a minimal condition necessary for effective downstream RL fine-tuning; instead training the policy to model the posterior distribution of demonstrator behavior given the dataset (Posterior Behavioral Cloning, PostBC) ensures this coverage while matching standard BC's pretrained performance, and is practically implementable with modern generative models using only standard supervised learning
claims.direction: posterior-distribution-modeling BC pretraining favored over standard exact-action-matching BC specifically as an initialization for subsequent RL fine-tuning, with no cost to pretrained-only performance
claims.conditions: realistic robotic control benchmarks + real-world robotic manipulation tasks, theoretical analysis plus empirical validation

claims.claim: Policies pretrained with PostBC lead to significantly improved RL fine-tuning performance compared to standard BC pretraining, on both benchmark and real-world tasks
claims.direction: PostBC pretraining favored over standard BC pretraining when the downstream plan involves RL fine-tuning after limited-demonstration BC pretraining
claims.conditions: same benchmark + real-world settings

title: Pose Estimation and Grasp Planning for Industrial Robot Manipulators in Unstructured Environments Based on Deep Learning

claims.claim: Fusing RGB-D and point-cloud data in a multimodal perception network to estimate 6D object pose, combined with a deep-RL-based grasp planner that adaptively optimizes grasping strategy based on environmental uncertainty, achieves superior pose accuracy, grasp success rate, and computational efficiency compared to traditional geometric and data-driven baseline methods under unpredictable lighting, occlusions, and background clutter
claims.direction: RGB-D + point cloud fused pose estimation with adaptive RL grasp planning favored over either purely geometric or purely RGB-only data-driven baselines for robustness to lighting/occlusion/clutter
claims.conditions: real industrial robotic platform (DOBOT CR5 + parallel gripper), various industrial unstructured-environment scenarios

title: LodeStar: Long-horizon Dexterity via Synthetic Data Augmentation from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Automatically decomposing task demonstrations into semantically meaningful skills using off-the-shelf foundation models, then generating diverse synthetic demonstration datasets from a few human demos via reinforcement learning (rather than collecting comprehensive real datasets directly), enables robust per-skill training; a Skill Routing Transformer policy chaining these learned skills significantly improves task performance and robustness versus previous baselines on three challenging real-world long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: foundation-model-guided skill decomposition + RL-generated synthetic per-skill demonstrations (from a few human demos) favored over direct large-scale real-demonstration collection for long-horizon dexterous tasks
claims.conditions: 3 real-world long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks

title: Impact of Visual Encoders on VLA Models in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A controlled comparative evaluation of visual encoders for VLA models (SigLIP, SigLIPv2, DINOv2, DINOv3, InternViT, plus fused SigLIP+DINOv2 and SigLIPv2+DINOv3 backbones) finds dual-encoder fusion outperforms standalone encoders; a SigLIPv2+DINOv3 fused backbone achieves the highest action-token accuracy measured (89.10%), while standalone DINOv2 achieves 88.18% (nearly matching the fused result) at half the parameter cost of a fused configuration
claims.direction: dual pretrained-encoder fusion (e.g., DINO-family + SigLIP-family) favored over any single standalone pretrained visual encoder for VLA action-prediction accuracy, but a standalone DINOv2 is a strong, much cheaper alternative nearly matching fusion performance
claims.conditions: OpenVLA-style two-part visual encoder architecture, action-token accuracy metric, setting (sim/real) not specified in abstract

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled head-to-head comparison of the exact vision-encoder pretraining choices in our Q03 (DINOv2, SigLIP/CLIP, and fused variants) with a concrete accuracy metric; full text would give the per-encoder accuracy table, compute/parameter cost breakdown, and whether DINOv2-alone (half the cost of fusion) is the right pragmatic choice for our 8GB-GPU, single-camera-pair setup.

title: Factor-Aware Mixture-of-Experts with Pretrained Encoder for Combinatorial Generalization

claims.claim: A three-stage training process -- (1) warm up a diffusion policy on standard-environment data with a frozen pretrained encoder, (2) train lightweight factor-specific adapters (inserted between the frozen encoder and the temporarily-frozen policy) on data customized per environmental variation (e.g., lighting, surface texture), (3) jointly fine-tune a central router that softly weights these adapters as a dense mixture-of-experts -- outperforms diffusion-policy baselines by 34% on Meta-World and achieves a 35% improvement in generalization under real-world variations on a real pick-and-place task using a compact model trained on newly collected data
claims.direction: factor-aware mixture-of-experts with lightweight per-variation adapters over a frozen pretrained encoder favored over a single diffusion policy trained/fine-tuned without factor-specific decomposition, for generalizing to lighting/texture environmental variation
claims.conditions: Meta-World simulation benchmark + real-world pick-and-place task, compact model architecture suitable for constrained deployment

why_deep_read: Directly targets our lighting/appearance-shift failure mode with a compact, real-world-validated architecture (34-35% quantified gains) rather than a large foundation model; full text would clarify how many factor-specific adapters/how much per-factor data is needed, and whether this compact MoE approach fits our 8GB GPU and 50-100 demo budget for handling lighting shift and a different-looking object.

title: ManiSkillFormer: Demonstration-Free Compositional Manipulation via Geometric Contracts and Agentic Skill Graph

claims.claim: Using LLM agents to generate explicit geometric contracts (specifying required geometry primitives and motion templates per reusable skill schema) that ground perception to 3D geometry and instantiate motion templates, without any task-specific demonstrations, achieves 88.97% success on demonstration-free pick-and-place (30 instances, 8 categories), 75.00% on functional manipulation (unscrewing, pouring, pressing, folding), and 50-80% completion on long-horizon tasks on a real dual-arm robot, outperforming evaluated baselines and ablations

title: Robot Learning on the Job: Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy and Learning During Deployment

claims.claim: Reweighting training samples with approximated human trust and optimizing with weighted behavioral cloning (Sirius framework) outperforms state-of-the-art baseline policy success rate by 8% in simulation and 27% on real hardware, with twice faster convergence and 85% memory size reduction
claims.direction: human-in-the-loop trust-weighted data collection/reweighting improves data quality over standard BC on same data
claims.conditions: real hardware + simulation, contact-rich manipulation tasks, human-robot shared autonomy during deployment

title: Hierarchical Vision-Language Planning for Multi-Step Humanoid Manipulation

title: A Study on Enhancing the Generalization Ability of Visuomotor Policies via Data Augmentation

claims.direction: supports robustness under lighting/camera/background shift via randomized augmentation
claims.conditions: low-cost manipulator, zero-shot sim-to-real

why_deep_read: Directly studies which scene randomization factors (camera pose, lighting, texture, table height) matter for a low-cost manipulator with sim-to-real transfer -- full text ablation tables would tell us which single factors matter most for our exact failure modes (lighting, moved camera, pumpkin appearance).

title: A Diffusion-Driven Local Planner for Robotic Manipulators in Constrained Environments

claims.claim: An enhanced Diffusion Policy using DiT blocks with AdaLN-Zero conditioning and U-ViT-style long skip connections achieves 94.5% success on the Push-T benchmark, significantly outperforming the baseline diffusion transformer architecture

title: Pix2Act: Image-Space Manipulation Policies with Equivariant Augmentation

claims.claim: Representing actions as continuous 2D image-space keypoint trajectories (recovered to end-effector poses via triangulation) reformulates 3D control as a simpler, more learnable 2D prediction problem and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse simulated and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Network architecture fuses multiple camera views while respecting per-view rotations
claims.direction: supports multi-view fusion designed for robustness
claims.conditions: multi-camera setup

claims.claim: Pix2Act 'remains robust under camera perturbations' compared to baselines

title: Pose-Agnostic Robotic Functional Grasping via Observation-Action Canonicalization

claims.claim: A canonicalized visuomotor RL policy (AnyMug) that transforms depth observations and predicted end-effector actions into a shared object-centric frame achieves over 93% success on unseen mugs in simulation and 80% success on 5 held-out physical mugs zero-shot on a real Franka Panda

title: PointZero: 3D Point Track Completion for Learning Transferable 3D Dynamics

title: Human2LocoMan: Learning Versatile Quadrupedal Manipulation with Human Pretraining

claims.claim: Cross-embodiment pretraining on human demonstration data (in addition to robot demos) improved average real-world manipulation success rate by 41.9% overall and 79.7% under out-of-distribution settings vs a robot-only baseline; human-data pretraining alone contributed 38.6% overall / 82.7% OOD improvement and enabled matching performance with only half the robot demonstration data

title: MemoryVLA++: Temporal Modeling via Memory and Imagination in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Adding a working-memory + episodic Perceptual-Cognitive Memory Bank (retrieving relevant historical context) to a VLA yields real-robot gains of +9% on general tasks and +26% on memory-dependent tasks versus a baseline without explicit memory
claims.direction: favors explicit observation-history/memory mechanisms over single-current-observation policies, especially for long-horizon/memory-dependent tasks

claims.claim: Adding a world-model 'imagination' module (denoising latent future-state prediction feeding a diffusion action expert) yields +28% real-robot gains on imagination-dependent tasks
claims.direction: favors auxiliary future-prediction/world-model objectives conditioning the action head, particularly for tasks requiring anticipation

claims.claim: Temporally-aware tokens (memory+imagination) condition a diffusion action expert to predict temporally consistent action sequences
claims.direction: supports diffusion-based chunked action prediction integrated with temporal context for consistency
claims.conditions: real and simulated manipulation benchmarks

why_deep_read: Real-robot ablation separates gains from memory (history) vs imagination (world-model) components with concrete per-category numbers (+9/+26/+28%), directly informative for our Q06/Q07/Q09 decisions about whether to add history or auxiliary future-prediction objectives to a small policy.

title: Hi-WM: Human-in-the-World-Model for Scalable Robot Post-Training

claims.claim: Post-training with corrective trajectories generated by human intervention inside a learned world model (rather than on the real robot) improved real-world manipulation success by 37.9 points on average over the base policy and by 19.0 points over a world-model closed-loop baseline, on three real-world tasks (rigid and deformable) across two policy backbones

claims.claim: A learned action-conditioned world model can serve as a reusable corrective substrate (not just for imagination/evaluation) for generating dense supervision around failure states
claims.direction: supports using world models as an auxiliary tool for generating additional training data around failure modes
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

title: SpatialVAM: Spatial-Aware Multi-View Video Diffusion as a Data-Efficient Robot Policy

claims.claim: With only ten demonstration trajectories and no additional pretraining, SpatialVAM handles long-horizon and contact-rich tasks and generalizes to out-of-distribution settings
claims.direction: favors a 3D-aware video-diffusion action model for extreme low-data regimes (10 demos)
claims.conditions: real-world robotic platform plus Meta-World and RoboCasa sim benchmarks

claims.claim: Simultaneously predicting spatial-aware multi-view heatmap videos and RGB videos (injecting 3D information into a video foundation model) outperforms other video action models, VLA models, and 3D-based policies by 22% on Meta-World, 15% on RoboCasa, and 16% on real-world robotic platforms

why_deep_read: Claims strong data efficiency (10 demos) and quantified gains from injecting 3D/spatial structure into a video-diffusion policy, tested on a real robot -- directly bears on our Q13 (very low demo counts) and Q04 (3D vs RGB) decisions; would want to see the real-robot task setup and whether it fits an 8GB-GPU laptop budget.

title: From Instrument-Mounted Demonstrations to In-Vivo Execution: Learning Bimanual Laparoscopic Appendectomy Without Robot-Collected Demonstrations

claims.claim: A diffusion policy trained on 849 in-vivo demonstrations (collected without the robot, via an instrument-mounted sensor logger) completed a full bimanual appendectomy in 3 of 4 live-animal trials after deployment
claims.direction: supports diffusion policy as viable action head for a real, safety-critical manipulation task learned from a modest real demonstration set

claims.claim: The diffusion policy uses a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision backbone, with the design selected via closed-loop rollouts in a physics simulator reconstructed from depth maps before real deployment

claims.conditions: sim-based design selection then real in-vivo deployment

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a VLA pretrained on egocentric human video with only a few robot manipulation demonstrations yields significant improvements over baselines on a bimanual manipulation benchmark, and ablations show human video data is important to this gain (no specific percentages given in abstract)
claims.direction: favors supplementing limited robot demos with large-scale human egocentric video pretraining
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark (Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark), few robot demonstrations for fine-tuning

title: VisualThink-VLA: Visual Intermediate Reasoning for Effective and Low-Latency Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Replacing textual chain-of-thought reasoning with a compact visual-evidence interface plus selective token routing reduces per-step latency from 8.377s (with text-based ECoT reasoning) to 0.367s on BridgeData V2, a 22.8x speedup, while achieving the highest success rate on most benchmarks in real-robot evaluation

title: Multi-Camera View Scaling for Data-Efficient Robot Imitation Learning

title: Simulation Distillation: Pretraining World Models in Simulation for Rapid Real-World Adaptation

claims.claim: SimDist pretrains a world model in simulation, then adapts only the latent dynamics model with real-world data; on contact-rich manipulation and quadruped locomotion tasks it substantially outperforms baselines using only 15-30 minutes of real-world interaction data, while prior adaptation methods struggle to make progress or degrade during online finetuning
claims.direction: favors simulation-pretrained world models plus minimal (15-30 min) real-world adaptation over methods that require larger real-world interaction budgets

title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment

title: Dynamic Execution Horizon Prediction for Chunk-based Robot Policies

why_deep_read: Directly matches our core constraints (small model, laptop-scale compute, need for speed and robustness to lighting/object-appearance/background/position shifts, limited pretraining). Full text ablations on backbone size, diffusion decoder design, and exact latency/success numbers vs OpenVLA would be very actionable for our Q01/Q03/Q10/Q12/Q14 decisions.

title: AIM: Intent-Aware Unified world action Modeling with Spatial Value Maps

claims.claim: Predicting an aligned spatial value map (an explicit control-oriented abstraction of future dynamics, derived from a pretrained video generation model) rather than decoding actions directly from future visual representations achieves 94.0% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, significantly outperforming prior unified world-action-model baselines, with larger gains on long-horizon and contact-sensitive tasks
claims.direction: favors an explicit spatial-intent/value-map auxiliary representation between world-model prediction and action decoding over decoding actions directly from raw future visual features
claims.conditions: simulated RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, trained on 30K simulated manipulation trajectories

title: Tune to Learn: How Controller Gains Shape Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Systematic experiments across multiple tasks and robot embodiments show behavior cloning benefits from compliant and overdamped position-controller gain regimes; reinforcement learning can succeed across all gain regimes given compatible hyperparameter tuning; and sim-to-real transfer is harmed by stiff and overdamped gain regimes -- optimal gain selection depends on the learning paradigm (BC vs RL vs sim-to-real), not on desired task stiffness
claims.direction: favors compliant/overdamped position-controller gains specifically for behavior-cloning policies, as opposed to selecting gains for task stiffness/compliance alone
claims.conditions: position-controlled manipulation, multiple tasks and robot embodiments, compares BC, RL-from-scratch, and sim-to-real transfer

why_deep_read: Directly addresses controller-gain selection for position-controlled behavior-cloning policies -- exactly our SO-101 setup (Feetech servos, position control, backlash/jitter) -- and claims BC specifically wants compliant/overdamped gains; full text would give concrete gain ranges/tasks tested and whether findings transfer to low-cost servo hardware.

title: Knowing When to Stop: Adaptive Action Chunking via Internal Cross-Attention Dynamics in VLAs

claims.claim: As prediction horizon extends, action-to-observation cross-attention in the action expert becomes increasingly dispersed (rising entropy toward a plateau), which correlates with higher action prediction error; a training-free truncation mechanism that detects sustained high-entropy plateaus to dynamically select the execution horizon improves average task success over both fixed-horizon and other adaptive-chunking baselines on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and three real-world manipulation tasks (tested on pi_0.5 and X-VLA)
claims.direction: favors dynamically truncating the execution horizon based on an internal attention-entropy signal over using a fixed execution horizon or other adaptive-chunking heuristics
claims.conditions: real-world (3 tasks) + sim (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO) evaluation on pi_0.5 and X-VLA backbones; training-free, negligible added inference overhead

claims.claim: The proposed adaptive truncation preserves efficient closed-loop control while improving success, using attention weights the policy already computes (negligible additional overhead)
claims.direction: favors low-overhead adaptive execution-horizon selection (vs fixed horizon) for maintaining real-time closed-loop performance
claims.conditions: real-world + sim, pi_0.5/X-VLA

why_deep_read: Training-free, near-zero-overhead method to fix exactly our reported jerky motion at fixed chunk boundaries by adaptively truncating the execution horizon using attention entropy already computed by the model -- highly actionable for a compute-constrained laptop setup; want details on how it interacts with async inference latency.

title: Waypoint-Based Reinforcement Learning for Robot Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Learning a small number of high-level waypoints (interpolated by existing controllers) instead of a low-level dense-action policy, framed as a sequence of multi-armed bandits, learns new manipulation tasks more quickly than state-of-the-art RL baselines in benchmark simulations and two real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors coarse waypoint-based action representations over dense per-timestep low-level action policies for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: benchmark simulations plus two real-world manipulation experiments, RL (not IL) setting

title: Being-H0: Vision-Language-Action Pretraining from Large-Scale Human Videos

claims.claim: Pretraining a VLA on large-scale human videos (via physical instruction tuning and a part-level motion tokenization achieving millimeter-level hand-trajectory reconstruction) yields gains in real-world robotic manipulation as physical instruction tuning is applied
claims.direction: favors large-scale human-video pretraining before robot-specific fine-tuning to reduce reliance on teleoperated demonstrations
claims.conditions: large-scale human video pretraining (motion capture, VR, RGB-only), post-training adaptation to real robot tasks; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers in abstract

claims.claim: Being-H0 scales well with both model size and data size
claims.direction: reports positive scaling trend for both parameter count and dataset size on human-video-pretrained VLAs
claims.conditions: human video pretraining plus robot fine-tuning

title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation

claims.claim: Deriving future 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints (joints, end-effector) purely from forward kinematics of proprioceptive states, and injecting them as auxiliary predictive spatio-temporal supervision via a plug-and-play lightweight track decoder (discarded at inference, with gradient isolation preserving the pretrained VLM backbone), consistently improves over strong VLA baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks, with substantial gains under out-of-distribution camera, background, and layout shifts
claims.direction: favors adding a near-zero-cost auxiliary future-keypoint-track prediction objective (derived only from proprioception, no external trackers/reconstruction, no inference-time overhead) to improve OOD robustness
claims.conditions: sim (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0) + real-world manipulation; auxiliary branch discarded at inference so no added latency

claims.claim: Substantial gains specifically under out-of-distribution perturbations including camera, background, and layout shifts
claims.direction: supports this auxiliary-supervision approach for camera-shift/background robustness specifically
claims.conditions: real-world + sim OOD perturbation tests

why_deep_read: This is a rare zero-inference-cost auxiliary objective (discarded at inference, derived only from proprioception/forward-kinematics, no extra sensors) that specifically targets camera/background/layout OOD robustness -- exactly our stated failure modes -- without adding to our tight latency budget; worth checking real numbers and demo counts.

title: A4A: Cross-Embodiment Transfer of Action-Oriented 4D Affordances from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Pretraining robot policies on action-oriented 4D affordances (language-conditioned future trajectories of interaction-relevant 3D points, derived from human-object interaction videos and RGB-D demonstrations) before manipulation fine-tuning consistently improves manipulation performance across diverse VLA policies in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors 4D-affordance-trajectory pretraining as an auxiliary/pretraining objective before task fine-tuning
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, cross-embodiment; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: The affordance representation is built from existing human-object interaction video data plus complementary RGB-D demonstrations, providing transferable interaction priors without needing embodiment-specific action labels
claims.direction: favors leveraging human video data to supplement limited robot action-labeled demonstrations
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment transfer from human videos

title: Policy-Induced Hand Priors in Humanoid Dual-Arm Manipulation: Diagnosing and Mitigating Initial-Pose Dependence

claims.claim: Across multiple policies and 17 initial configurations, expanding initial-pose coverage in the training dataset substantially improves robustness, and targeted augmentation around a specific low-performing initial configuration increases that configuration's success rate
claims.direction: favors deliberately covering/augmenting diverse initial poses in the demonstration set over uniform/incidental pose coverage
claims.conditions: humanoid dual-arm manipulation, multiple policies compared, simulation and/or real (not specified in abstract)

claims.claim: Wrist-camera observations influence hand/arm selection and task performance, and the same initial pose produces substantially different success rates across different policies
claims.direction: highlights wrist-camera view as a factor in action selection sensitivity, relevant to camera configuration robustness
claims.conditions: humanoid dual-arm, wrist camera present

title: EquiBot: SIM(3)-Equivariant Diffusion Policy for Generalizable and Data Efficient Learning

claims.claim: Combining SIM(3)-equivariant neural network architectures with diffusion models ensures learned policies are invariant to changes in scale, rotation, and translation while retaining diffusion's multi-modality and robustness benefits, reducing data requirements and improving generalization to novel scenarios versus a non-equivariant diffusion policy baseline across 6 simulation tasks
claims.direction: favors building explicit SIM(3) equivariance into the diffusion policy architecture over standard (non-equivariant) diffusion policies
claims.conditions: 6 simulation tasks; real-world validation on 10 variations of 6 mobile manipulation tasks

claims.claim: In the real world, the method generalizes easily to novel objects and scenes after learning from just 5 minutes of human demonstrations per task
claims.direction: favors equivariant architecture as a way to drastically cut required demonstration time/count while still generalizing
claims.conditions: real-world mobile manipulation, 5 minutes of demonstrations per task, 10 scene/object variations

claims.claim: The policy generalizes to novel objects and scenes not seen during the 5-minute demonstration collection
claims.direction: supports equivariance-based generalization to novel object/scene variation
claims.conditions: real-world mobile manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Extremely strong data-efficiency claim (5 minutes of real demos per task) with real-world generalization to novel objects/scenes, directly relevant to our ~50-100 demo budget and need for robustness to a different-looking pumpkin/moved camera; worth checking whether SIM(3) equivariance requires point-cloud/depth input we may or may not have reliably from the RealSense.

title: Learning From Imperfect Demonstrations With Self-Supervision for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Self-Supervised Data Filtering framework computes quality scores for segments of failed/imperfect trajectories (without reward labels) and uses high-quality segments to expand the training dataset; this improved success rates for all tested robotic manipulation tasks on ManiSkill2 (Sapien simulator) and real-world tasks with a Franka arm, when combined with downstream IL policy learning
claims.direction: favors reusing/filtering imperfect (failed) demonstration data to expand the effective training set, rather than discarding all non-expert data as standard IL does
claims.conditions: simulation (ManiSkill2/Sapien) + real-world Franka arm, works with any downstream policy learning method

title: Building Explicit World Model for Zero-Shot Open-World Object Manipulation

claims.claim: An explicit-world-model framework (open-set perception + digital-twin reconstruction + simulated strategy sampling/evaluation) performs multiple open-set manipulation tasks with zero-shot generalization on both task and object levels without any task-specific action demonstrations
claims.direction: favors building an explicit physically-grounded world model/digital twin plus simulated planning over collecting large-scale action demonstrations for generalization
claims.conditions: real-world deployment after simulated strategy search; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: A physically grounded digital-twin world model is used to explore and evaluate manipulation strategies before real-world deployment
claims.direction: supports using an explicit (not learned end-to-end) world model as the core mechanism rather than a black-box action-prediction network
claims.conditions: real-world deployment

title: FlowDAgger: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptation of Generative Robot Policies in Latent Space

claims.claim: FlowDAgger adapts frozen pretrained flow-matching/diffusion generative robot policies from a handful of human interventions (via action inversion: mapping each expert action to the noise that would have produced it under the frozen base policy, using reverse-time integration plus local refinement, to supervise a lightweight latent policy) and outperforms supervised fine-tuning and latent-space RL baselines while preserving pretrained skills on held-out tasks
claims.direction: favors sample- and compute-efficient latent-space DAgger-style correction from a small number of interventions over full supervised fine-tuning or online RL for closing out-of-distribution gaps
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world bimanual and single-arm manipulation; adapts both action-head VLAs and world-action models

claims.claim: The method is specifically designed to work with flow-matching and diffusion-based generative action policies, exploiting the invertibility of the denoising/flow process
claims.direction: supports flow-matching/diffusion action heads as being more amenable to this kind of cheap latent-space online correction than other action-head types
claims.conditions: pretrained flow/diffusion action-head policies

why_deep_read: Offers a concrete, low-cost way (few human interventions, no full retraining) to correct exactly the kind of brittleness we see in our SmolVLA fine-tune (new lighting, moved camera) while preserving prior skills; relevant to deciding on a flow-matching/diffusion action head partly because it becomes correctable this way after deployment.

title: VCA: Vision-Click-Action Framework for Precise Manipulation of Segmented Objects in Target Ambiguous Environments

claims.claim: Replacing verbose textual language commands with direct click-based visual target selection (using pretrained segmentation models on the robot's 2D camera view) reduces interpretation errors and cognitive load, and achieves effective instance-level manipulation of specified target objects in environments with multiple visually similar objects
claims.direction: favors click/visual-selection conditioning as an alternative to pure language conditioning when object identification is ambiguous
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation with visually similar/ambiguous objects; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: EgoVerse: An Egocentric Human Dataset for Robot Learning from Around the World

claims.claim: In a large-scale, multi-lab study of human-to-robot transfer (replicated across multiple labs, tasks, and robot embodiments under shared protocols, using a 1,362-hour/80k-episode egocentric human dataset), policy performance generally improves with increased human data, but effective scaling depends critically on alignment between the human data and the robot's learning objectives -- more human data alone is not sufficient
claims.direction: nuances/contradicts the assumption that simply adding more human demonstration/video data reliably improves robot policy performance; alignment between human data and target task/embodiment matters as much as volume
claims.conditions: multi-lab replicated study, multiple robot embodiments and tasks, large egocentric human dataset (1,965 tasks, 240 scenes, 2,087 demonstrators)

title: FLASH: Efficient Visuomotor Policy via Sparse Sampling

claims.claim: Replacing discrete action-chunk generation with a continuous Legendre-polynomial trajectory representation, fit to expert demonstrations under sparse temporal sampling, lets a single inference cover a significantly extended action horizon, and analytic polynomial differentiation directly supplies smooth velocity feed-forward signals to the torque controller without numerical approximation
claims.direction: favors continuous polynomial trajectory representations over discrete per-step action chunks for both extended horizon coverage and smoothness
claims.conditions: 5 simulated + 2 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Initiating flow matching from history polynomial coefficients (instead of Gaussian noise) shortens the transport distance enabling accurate single-step inference; FLASH achieves >=92% success across all tasks with 31.40ms per-episode inference time, up to 175x faster than diffusion policies and 18x faster than prior flow-matching policies, with 4x faster training convergence than ACT
claims.direction: favors history-anchored flow matching (vs noise-initialized diffusion/flow) for large latency reductions while maintaining/improving success rate
claims.conditions: 5 sim + 2 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Compared to discrete-action baselines (e.g., ACT-style chunking), FLASH reduces controller tracking error by 5x-7x
claims.direction: favors continuous trajectory/polynomial action representation over discrete-action-chunk action heads for tracking accuracy
claims.conditions: 5 sim + 2 real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Reports concrete, very large latency (31.4ms vs our ~2s), smoothness (5-7x tracking error reduction), and success-rate numbers from a real-robot-validated architecture that directly targets both of our stated failure modes (2s inference latency and jerky chunk-boundary motion) simultaneously; this is one of the most directly actionable papers in the batch for our Q06/Q10/Q01 decisions.

title: Simple-to-Complex Structured Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Learning

claims.claim: Organizing demonstration collection by (i) decomposing complex tasks into progressively learnable sub-skills, (ii) standardizing the interaction environment to reduce unnecessary variability, and (iii) ordering demonstrations by increasing task complexity yields consistent improvements in task success rate and training stability compared to directly collecting end-to-end complete task trajectories, on a real dual-arm robot across block grasping/sorting and towel folding tasks
claims.direction: favors structuring/curriculum-ordering demonstration collection (simple-to-complex, standardized environment) over unstructured end-to-end demo collection, for the same demonstration budget
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robotic platform, two manipulation tasks; qualitative comparative claim (consistent improvement), no specific percentage numbers given in abstract

title: Adaptive Contact-Rich Manipulation Through Few-Shot Imitation Learning With Force-Torque Feedback and Pre-Trained Object Representations

claims.claim: Integrating real-time force-torque feedback with pre-trained object representations in a few-shot imitation learning setup achieved 96% accuracy in applying a reference wiping force in real-world tests across 40 scenarios (10 sponges x 4 surface heights not seen during training), versus only 4% accuracy for a comparable method lacking the force-torque feedback loop
claims.direction: favors adding force-torque feedback (when available) to a few-shot IL policy for adapting to unseen physical/surface conditions, versus vision/pretrained-representation-only policies
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich wiping task, few-shot demonstrations, requires an FT sensor not present in our target setup

title: Dynamic Test-Time Compute Scaling in Control Policy: Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy

claims.claim: A difficulty classifier that dynamically selects the denoising step budget, solver variant, and ODE/SDE integration mode per control cycle (Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy) achieves a 2.6-4.4x reduction in total computation time while maintaining task success rates comparable to fixed maximum-computation baselines, across diverse manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors adaptively allocating diffusion/flow inference compute based on per-step task difficulty over using a fixed inference budget at every control step
claims.conditions: benchmark manipulation tasks (sim, per abstract); applies to diffusion- and flow-based policies generally

title: On the Fragility of State-Space Augmentation in Diffusion-Based Robot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Evaluating Gaussian noise injection and feature dropout applied to state inputs of state-only diffusion policies across four Meta-World manipulation tasks in a low-data regime, BOTH augmentation strategies consistently REDUCED task success compared to baselines trained on unmodified demonstrations
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that state-space perturbation augmentation improves generalization in low-data imitation learning -- here it consistently hurt performance, suggesting naive state perturbations disrupt task-relevant information rather than promoting generalization
claims.conditions: simulation only (Meta-World), state-only (non-visual) diffusion policies, low-data regime, four manipulation tasks

title: Finetuning Vision-Language-Action Models Requires Fewer Layers Than You Think

claims.claim: Pretrained VLA foundation policies (e.g., pi_0, GR00T-N1.5) exhibit severe layer-wise representational redundancy; a training-free structural compression pipeline (using Centered Kernel Alignment on a single forward pass to identify and remove redundant twin layers) permanently compresses model depth by up to 50% across both the VLM backbone and the action policy head, while matching or exceeding full-scale base model performance on LIBERO, RoboCasa, SimplerEnv, and 10 real-world tasks across 4 robot embodiments
claims.direction: favors aggressively compressing/pruning large pretrained VLA backbones (up to 50% fewer layers) over using the full-scale pretrained model, since much of the depth is redundant
claims.conditions: 3 sim benchmarks + 10 real-world tasks across 4 embodiments; training-free layer removal applied before downstream fine-tuning

claims.claim: The compressed architecture yields a 40-50% reduction in fine-tuning training time and up to 30% faster real-time inference versus the full-scale model
claims.direction: favors layer-pruned smaller VLA backbones for reduced inference latency
claims.conditions: same real-world + sim evaluation suite

why_deep_read: Directly actionable for our RTX 5060 8GB laptop constraint: a training-free method to cut a large pretrained VLA (like pi_0) down by up to 50% of its layers with matched performance and ~30% faster inference, which could let us use a larger pretrained backbone than would otherwise fit, or run a smaller version faster; want to check if compression was validated starting from small backbones too or only very large ones.

title: Action-Geometry Prediction with 3D Geometric Prior for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing geometry-aware latents from a pretrained 3D geometric foundation model (reconstructing 3D structure directly from RGB images, without requiring explicit point clouds), 2D semantic features, and proprioception into a unified state representation outperforms both 2D-based and explicit-point-cloud-based baselines in manipulation success, inter-arm coordination, and 3D spatial prediction accuracy, on RoboTwin benchmark and real-world robot executions
claims.direction: favors deriving 3D structure from RGB via a pretrained 3D geometric foundation model over both plain 2D RGB features and explicit point-cloud/depth-sensor input
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, RoboTwin sim benchmark + real-world robot

claims.claim: A diffusion model jointly predicts a future action chunk and a future 3D latent that decodes into a dense pointmap (auxiliary 3D-future-prediction objective alongside action prediction)
claims.direction: favors jointly predicting future 3D scene structure alongside actions as an auxiliary objective
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, RoboTwin + real-world

title: Failing Forward: Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Using a pretrained VLA to generate its own online failure rollouts (no handcrafted failure modes or human intervention needed) and jointly training paired success/failure diffusion action generators that share a backbone consistently improves task success rate and robustness over existing VLA baselines across in-domain and out-of-domain, short- and long-horizon manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors self-generated failure trajectories as adaptive negative training signal over success-only behavioral cloning
claims.conditions: in-domain and out-of-domain manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: KAM-WM: Kinematic Affordance Maps from Latent World Models for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Querying a frozen latent video world model once (no rollout, no fine-tuning) and interpreting its single-step latent velocity as a Kinematic Affordance Map -- compressed into tokens conditioning a diffusion policy alongside RGB and proprioception -- reaches 90.6% average success on LIBERO and 65.7%/22.4% success on RoboTwin2.0 Easy/Hard; controlled comparison against a zero-order segmentation-mask prior shows part of the gain comes from directional motion information beyond spatial localization alone
claims.direction: favors a cheap (single-query, no-rollout) world-model-derived directional affordance signal over a static spatial mask prior as auxiliary conditioning for a diffusion policy
claims.conditions: simulation only (LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0), works from few demonstrations per the framing of the paper (few-shot manipulation)

claims.claim: The approach is framed explicitly for learning manipulation from few demonstrations
claims.direction: supports using cheap world-model-derived priors to reduce demonstration requirements
claims.conditions: simulation only

title: ARGUS: Aligning Robot Scene Geometry Under Shifting Views with Large 3D Vision Models

claims.claim: An observation-preprocessing pipeline that uses large-scale 3D vision models to align image observations from arbitrary camera viewpoints into a canonical viewpoint before passing them to a downstream visuomotor policy consistently outperforms prior approaches across both limited-view and view-diverse training regimes (evaluated on datasets like DROID and BridgeV2-style viewpoint diversity)
claims.direction: favors explicit viewpoint canonicalization as an observation pre-processing step over letting the policy learn viewpoint-entangled scene geometry directly
claims.conditions: training datasets with varying viewpoint diversity, from fixed multi-view to highly varied camera placements

claims.claim: Leveraging large-scale pretrained 3D vision models to disentangle scene geometry from viewpoint reduces the learning burden on visuomotor policies, converging to high success rates 4-6x faster than previous methods when learning from view-diverse data
claims.direction: favors using pretrained 3D vision models for geometry-viewpoint disentanglement over training the policy to implicitly learn both together
claims.conditions: view-diverse robot manipulation datasets

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported failure mode of policy breaking under a slightly moved camera, via a general canonicalization pre-processing step that can wrap any downstream policy; the 4-6x faster convergence number and applicability to fixed/limited-view setups (like ours, one scene camera + one wrist camera) make this worth a closer look.

title: Learning with Language-Guided State Abstractions

claims.claim: Using a pretrained language model to translate a natural-language task description into a state-abstraction function (masking irrelevant visual features) before training an imitation policy on a small number of demonstrations yields abstractions similar to those designed by humans but in a fraction of the time, and improves generalization and robustness in the presence of spurious correlations and ambiguous specifications
claims.direction: favors using language to automatically derive task-relevant state abstractions/masks (rather than raw pixels or hand-designed features) for imitation learning, especially to guard against spurious correlations
claims.conditions: simulated robotic tasks plus mobile manipulation tasks with a real Spot robot; small number of demonstrations

claims.claim: Language-derived state abstractions improve robustness in the presence of spurious correlations
claims.direction: supports masking out irrelevant/spurious visual features (e.g., background) via language-guided abstraction for robustness
claims.conditions: simulated + real Spot robot tasks

title: PCHands: PCA-Based Hand Pose Synergy Representation on Manipulators with N-DoF

claims.claim: Encoding observation and action spaces of RL manipulation policies using a PCA-derived postural-synergy latent representation (unified across 2-finger grippers through 5-finger anthropomorphic hands) outperforms a baseline that learns the same tasks directly in joint space, in terms of learning efficiency and consistency, and performs robustly when demonstrations for RL-from-demonstration come from a different manipulator than the one being controlled
claims.direction: favors a compact PCA/synergy-based action-space representation over raw joint-space action representation for both learning efficiency and cross-embodiment demonstration reuse
claims.conditions: RL policies, tested with real-world experiments including a 2-finger gripper and a 4-finger anthropomorphic hand

title: ImMimic: Cross-Domain Imitation from Human Videos via Mapping and Interpolation

claims.claim: Co-training on retargeted human-hand-pose trajectories (mapped to robot joints via Dynamic Time Warping) plus a small amount of teleoperated robot demonstrations, interpolated via MixUp to create intermediate domains, improves task success rates and execution smoothness across four real-world manipulation tasks and four robotic embodiments versus using robot demonstrations alone
claims.direction: favors co-training with mapped/interpolated human video data alongside a small robot demo set over robot-only demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world, four tasks (Pick and Place, Push, Hammer, Flip), four embodiments (Robotiq, Fin Ray, Allegro, Ability); qualitative claim, no specific numbers in abstract

claims.claim: The interpolation-based co-training also improves execution smoothness
claims.direction: supports human-video co-training as a route to smoother motion, not just higher success
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

title: LoLA: Long Horizon Latent Action Learning for General Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Encoding long-term multi-view observation history and robot proprioception through a State-Aware Latent Re-representation module (grounding VL embeddings in physical scale via a learnable 'embodiment-anchored' latent space, rather than simply concatenating proprioception with VL embeddings) significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods including pi0, particularly on long-horizon manipulation tasks, on SIMPLER/LIBERO sim benchmarks and real-world Franka and Bi-Manual Aloha tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit multi-view + proprioceptive history encoding grounded in a learned embodiment-anchored latent space over simple concatenation of current proprioception with vision-language embeddings, especially for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: sim (SIMPLER, LIBERO) + real-world (Franka, Bi-Manual Aloha); qualitative 'significantly outperforms' claim vs pi0, no exact numbers given in abstract

title: Generalizable Hierarchical Skill Learning via Object-Centric Representation

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework (GSL) that decomposes demonstrations into transferable, object-canonicalized skill primitives using foundation models, trained with only 3 demonstrations per task, outperforms baselines trained with 30x more data (90 demos) by 15.5% on unseen tasks in simulation; in real-world experiments GSL also surpasses a baseline trained with 10x more data
claims.direction: favors decomposing demonstrations into object-centric, canonicalized skill primitives (bridging a high-level VLM planner and low-level visuomotor policy) over training an end-to-end policy directly on raw (non-canonicalized) demonstrations, for extreme data efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation (3 vs 90 demos/task) and real-world (vs 10x-more-data baseline)

claims.claim: The structured object-centric skill design improves generalization across unseen spatial arrangements, object appearances, and task compositions
claims.direction: supports object-centric canonicalization for robustness to spatial/appearance variation
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world

why_deep_read: One of the strongest data-efficiency numbers in the batch (3 demos beating a 90-demo baseline by 15.5%, also validated in the real world against a 10x-more-data baseline) -- directly relevant to whether object-centric skill canonicalization could let us get away with far fewer than 50-100 demos; would want to see the real-robot task complexity and whether it needs a VLM planner we could run on our laptop.

title: DINOv3-Diffusion Policy: Self-Supervised Large Visual Model for Visuomotor Diffusion Policy Learning

claims.claim: Comparing DINOv3 (self-supervised) against ResNet-18 (supervised ImageNet-pretrained) as the vision backbone for a FiLM-conditioned diffusion policy, under three regimes (train-from-scratch, frozen, finetuned) across four benchmark tasks (Push-T, Lift, Can, Square): finetuned DINOv3 matches or exceeds ResNet-18 on several tasks (up to 10% absolute success-rate increase on Can), frozen DINOv3 remains competitive (indicating strong transferable priors), and self-supervised DINOv3 features improve sample efficiency and robustness relative to ResNet-18
claims.direction: favors a large self-supervised pretrained vision backbone (DINOv3), fine-tuned or even frozen, over a supervised ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 backbone for diffusion-policy visuomotor learning
claims.conditions: four benchmark manipulation tasks (Push-T, Lift, Can, Square) -- appears to be simulation benchmarks; direct controlled comparison of encoder choice and frozen-vs-finetuned regime

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled ablation of exactly our Q03 vision-encoder decision (DINOv3 vs ResNet18-ImageNet, frozen vs finetuned) with concrete numbers (up to 10% absolute gain); worth reading in full for per-task breakdowns and whether frozen DINOv3 (cheaper on our 8GB GPU) is close enough to finetuned to skip fine-tuning the backbone.

title: PD-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Model Integrated with Action Chunking via Parallel Decoding

claims.claim: Reformulating autoregressive action-chunk decoding as a nonlinear system solved by parallel fixed-point iterations (training-free, no architecture changes) preserves model performance with mathematical guarantees while achieving 2.52x execution frequency on a 7-DoF manipulator compared to the base VLA model, validated in both simulation and real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors parallel decoding of action chunks over standard autoregressive decoding for reducing inference latency, without retraining or architecture changes
claims.conditions: 7-DoF manipulator, simulation + real-world; training-free, composable with other acceleration techniques

claims.claim: Action chunking linearly scales up action dimensions with increased chunk size, reducing inference efficiency; this method specifically targets that scaling cost
claims.direction: identifies chunk-size-driven inference cost as a problem that parallel decoding addresses
claims.conditions: VLA models integrated with action chunking

title: LAR-MoE: Latent-Aligned Routing for Mixture of Experts in Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: LAR-MoE, a two-stage Mixture-of-Experts framework with unsupervised latent-aligned expert routing (learned via student-teacher co-training, then regularized to follow the learned latent space rather than requiring supervised skill-phase labels), achieves a 95.2% average success rate on the LIBERO benchmark with 150M parameters
claims.direction: reports a specific small parameter count (150M) sufficient for strong (95.2%) benchmark performance when using a latent-routed MoE architecture
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark (sim); also validated on a real surgical bowel grasping/retraction task with zero-shot transfer to ex vivo porcine tissue

claims.claim: Latent-aligned MoE routing prevents expert collapse and avoids the need for hand-specified skill decomposition/phase annotations, addressing the problem that single models 'average over distinct behavioral modes present in demonstrations'
claims.direction: favors an MoE action-head architecture (with unsupervised latent routing) over a single monolithic action head, specifically to handle multimodal demonstration behavior
claims.conditions: LIBERO + real surgical hardware task

title: TeNet: Text-to-Network for Compact Policy Synthesis

claims.claim: A hypernetwork conditioned once on text embeddings (from a pretrained LLM) at policy-instantiation time generates fully executable, low-dimensional-state policies that are 'orders of magnitude smaller than sequence-based baselines' while achieving strong performance and supporting high-frequency control, on MuJoCo and Meta-World benchmarks
claims.direction: favors instantiating a compact task-specific network once from language (rather than continuously conditioning a large sequence model on language at every step) for resource-constrained, high-frequency control
claims.conditions: MuJoCo and Meta-World benchmarks, state-based (not image-based) control; simulation only

claims.claim: Language is used only once, at policy instantiation, rather than as continuous input at every control step
claims.direction: supports a one-shot language-to-policy-weights conditioning scheme over per-step language token conditioning, for lightweight execution
claims.conditions: simulation, state-based control

title: SSI-Policy: Learning Structured Scene Interfaces for Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Structured Scene Interface -- a unified RGB-only intermediate representation jointly encoding monocular depth features, language-grounded object layouts, and instruction-conditioned 2D motion trajectories, trainable from action-free video -- avoids the need for explicit depth sensing while remaining robot-agnostic
claims.direction: favors an RGB-only representation with monocular-depth features and 2D motion cues over requiring explicit point-cloud/depth-sensor input for spatial grounding
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark plus 13 real-world tasks spanning spatial reasoning, cross-embodiment transfer, and contact-rich manipulation

claims.claim: On LIBERO with only 10 demonstrations per task, SSI-Policy improves over the strongest prior method by nearly 15% and remains competitive with methods using 50 demonstrations per task plus large-scale external pretraining
claims.direction: favors this structured RGB-only scene interface for extreme few-demo (10-demo) data efficiency
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, 10 demos/task; also validated on 13 real-world tasks

claims.claim: Ablations show geometric (depth) and motion (trajectory) cues provide complementary benefits within the shared interface used for language-grounded object layouts
claims.direction: supports combining language-grounded layout with geometric and motion cues rather than language conditioning alone
claims.conditions: LIBERO + 13 real-world tasks

why_deep_read: Directly matches our sensor constraints (RGB-only, no reliance on point clouds/depth sensors) and low-data regime (10 demos/task, ~15% gain), with real-world validation across 13 tasks including cross-embodiment transfer; worth checking whether the monocular-depth-feature extraction is lightweight enough for our laptop GPU and how it compares to a plain RGB baseline at our demo scale.

title: Temporal Policy: History-Initialized Action Generation for Robotic Learning from Demonstration

claims.claim: Initializing a stochastic-interpolant generative flow at the robot's recent history (instead of an uninformative Gaussian prior) explicitly couples past states to future action sequences, reducing transport cost by nearly an order of magnitude compared to noise-initialized baselines and achieving 19.1ms inference latency on a single NVIDIA RTX 4080, while matching the success rates of state-of-the-art baselines, validated on visuomotor sim benchmarks and a physical Barrett WAM 2x7-DoF teleoperation platform
claims.direction: favors history-coupled (rather than noise-initialized) generative action policies for large latency reductions without sacrificing success rate
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real physical Barrett WAM platform

claims.claim: Data-dependent coupling to recent history produces straighter vector fields, bypassing the computational bottleneck of independent Gaussian priors and enabling high-frequency closed-loop control
claims.direction: supports history-conditioned action generation as a way to enable tighter closed-loop control frequency (relevant to reducing chunk-boundary/open-loop issues)
claims.conditions: real physical robot + sim

title: WIS: world-guided instruction semantic diffusion policy for predictive bimanual manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework combining a language-conditioned world model (forecasting future state trajectories from current state, actions, and language) with a diffusion policy, where world-model predictions guide action refinement via prediction-aware sampling, consistently outperforms strong baselines on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark with minimal computational overhead relative to baselines
claims.direction: favors guiding a diffusion action policy with an explicit language-conditioned future-state world model over a purely reactive diffusion policy, for bimanual coordination
claims.conditions: simulation only (RoboTwin 2.0, Aloha-AgileX bimanual robots); qualitative claim, no specific numbers in abstract

title: ALPHA-alpha and Bi-ACT Are All You Need: Importance of Position and Force Information/Control for Imitation Learning of Unimanual and Bimanual Robotic Manipulation with Low-Cost System

claims.claim: Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning via Action Chunking with Transformers (Bi-ACT), which uses both position AND force information/control (rather than position-only control), shows superior performance and adaptability on real low-cost hardware (ALPHA-alpha) across unimanual tasks with objects varying in hardness, shape, and weight, and achieves high success rates on bimanual tasks (Egg Handling, Open Cap) requiring delicate force modulation
claims.direction: favors incorporating bilateral force information/control alongside position control (not position-only control) for imitation learning action chunking, especially for delicate/varying-hardness objects
claims.conditions: real low-cost robotic hardware (ALPHA-alpha), unimanual and bimanual tasks; qualitative 'superior performance' claim, no specific percentage numbers given in abstract; requires force-sensing/bilateral control hardware not present in our current setup

title: Imitating What Works: Simulation-Filtered Modular Policy Learning from Human Videos

claims.claim: A modular policy (dedicated grasp generator + human-video-derived post-grasp motion, with grasp-trajectory pairs filtered/labeled for task-suitability in simulation) learns precise prehensile manipulation skills efficiently without any robot demonstration data, performing significantly more robustly than naively combining a grasp generator with human video motion
claims.direction: favors a modular design (separate grasp generation + video-derived motion, filtered via simulation) over a naive combination, when learning from human video with zero robot-collected demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world experiments; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Active Stereo-Camera Outperforms Multi-Sensor Setup in ACT Imitation Learning for Humanoid Manipulation

claims.claim: Benchmarking 14 sensor combinations (tactile, proprioceptive, active vision) for ACT imitation learning on a Unitree G1 humanoid across two manipulation tasks shows that additional sensor modalities often DEGRADE performance in data-limited regimes; a minimal active stereo-camera-only setup outperformed complex multi-sensor configurations, achieving 87.5% success in a spatial-generalization task and 94.4% in a structured manipulation task, while adding pressure/tactile sensors to this setup REDUCED success to 67.3% on the structured task due to low signal-to-noise ratio
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that adding more sensor modalities (tactile, extra cameras) improves imitation-learning performance -- here, a minimal camera-only setup beat richer multi-sensor setups specifically in the data-limited regime; strategic (minimal) sensor selection outperformed complex configurations while reducing computational overhead
claims.conditions: real Unitree G1 humanoid with three-finger hands, ACT imitation learning, data-limited regime, open-source Unified Ablation Framework with sensor masking on a shared master dataset

why_deep_read: A rare controlled 14-way sensor-combination ablation directly relevant to our camera/sensor-configuration decision (Q11) in a data-limited regime matching our own (~50-100 demos); the finding that extra modalities can HURT performance is an important, actionable contradiction of the intuition that more sensors are always better, and worth checking whether it generalizes to our two-camera (no tactile) RGB setup.

title: AWM-VLA: AlignedWorld Modeling for Efficient and Explainable Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Embedding aligned world modeling directly inside a diffusion-transformer policy via learnable future tokens whose intermediate activations are aligned with vision-language embeddings of future observations (rather than reconstructing future frames in pixel space, and rather than decoupling a separate world model from the policy) outperforms prior VLA and world-model baselines by up to 21% in success rate on RoboCasa and humanoid tabletop manipulation benchmarks, improves generalization to novel objects/instructions, and adds only a few learnable tokens (compatible with any diffusion or flow-matching policy)
claims.direction: favors a lightweight, latent (not pixel-space) future-alignment auxiliary objective embedded directly in the action policy, over both pixel-space future-frame reconstruction and decoupled world models, for cheap gains in success rate and generalization
claims.conditions: RoboCasa + humanoid tabletop manipulation benchmarks (appears simulation-based); adds negligible parameters/compute, compatible with existing diffusion/flow-matching action heads

claims.claim: An additional object-centric decoupled alignment objective (predicting future object-level semantics alongside the global future embedding) improves both interpretability and multi-instruction generalization, and produces object-centric rationales preferred by human raters in 83% of cases
claims.direction: supports adding object-level (not just global-scene) future-semantic alignment for better generalization and interpretability
claims.conditions: same benchmarks

title: Imagination Policy: Using Generative Point Cloud Models for Learning Manipulation Policies
