claims.claim: Instead of learning actions directly, Imagination Policy generates point clouds representing imagined goal states (leveraging pick-and-place symmetries) which are then translated to actions via rigid action estimation, achieving state-of-the-art performance across various high-precision pick-and-place tasks on the RLBench benchmark compared to several strong baselines, and validated on a real robot
claims.direction: favors a generative-point-cloud/key-frame goal-imagination action formulation over direct action regression for high-precision pick-and-place tasks
claims.conditions: RLBench sim benchmark, real-robot validation

claims.claim: The approach relies on point-cloud representations (rather than RGB) to exploit task symmetries for generation
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-based state/goal representation for tasks with exploitable geometric symmetry
claims.conditions: RLBench + real robot

claims.claim: Leveraging pick-and-place symmetries in the generative process achieves extremely high sample efficiency and generalizability to unseen configurations
claims.direction: favors symmetry-exploiting generative point-cloud policies for sample efficiency in low-data settings
claims.conditions: RLBench + real robot

title: Learning Diffusion Policies from Demonstrations For Compliant Contact-rich Manipulation

claims.claim: DIPCOM, a diffusion-based policy that predicts Cartesian end-effector poses AND adjusts arm stiffness/compliance jointly, enhances force control through multimodal distribution modeling for contact-rich compliant tasks (e.g., powder grinding), validated in real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors extending a diffusion action head to jointly output compliance/stiffness parameters alongside pose for contact-rich tasks, rather than pose-only diffusion output
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation (powder grinding); qualitative comparison to prior methods, no specific numbers given in abstract; requires compliant/impedance control capability

title: KOROL: Learning Visualizable Object Feature with Koopman Operator Rollout for Manipulation

claims.claim: A Koopman-operator-based dynamics model that auto-regressively advances learned, visually-interpretable object features (rather than requiring ground-truth object state at runtime) outperformed the image-to-action Diffusion Policy baseline by 1.16x and a model-based imitation-learning baseline (NDP) by 1.08x on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, without needing ground-truth object states
claims.direction: favors a Koopman-operator dynamics-model-based policy over a direct image-to-action Diffusion Policy, for maintaining task success while removing the need for ground-truth object state at runtime
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world robot manipulation tasks; modest but direct quantified improvement (8-16%) over a Diffusion Policy baseline

claims.claim: Training a feature extractor to embed scene information into object features that a Koopman operator can propagate forward in time serves as an auxiliary dynamics-learning objective enabling accurate propagation of robot trajectories
claims.direction: supports learning an explicit (linear-in-latent-space) forward dynamics model as an auxiliary/structuring objective for the policy
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation

title: Learning to Feel the Future: DreamTacVLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Finetuning a VLA with a tactile world model that predicts future high-resolution tactile signals (aligned spatially with wrist and third-person vision via a Hierarchical Spatial Alignment loss) outperforms state-of-the-art VLA baselines on contact-rich manipulation tasks, achieving up to 95% success
claims.direction: favors predicting future tactile states as an auxiliary objective for contact-rich tasks, over vision/language-only VLA baselines
claims.conditions: requires high-resolution tactile sensors not present in our target setup; hybrid digital-twin + real-world dataset

title: Salience-Invariant Consistent Policy Learning for Generalization in Visual Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A saliency-guided value-consistency module plus a policy-consistency module (KL-constrained across original and perturbed observations) for visual RL achieves average performance improvements of 14%, 39%, and 69% over state-of-the-art generalization methods on DMC video-hard, Robotic-manipulation-hard, and CARLA benchmarks respectively
claims.direction: favors explicitly enforcing representation and policy consistency between clean and visually-perturbed (distracting-background) observations for robustness to visual distractors
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks (DMC-GB, Robotic Manipulation, CARLA); reinforcement-learning setting, not imitation learning

title: Latent Policy Barrier: Learning Robust Visuomotor Policies by Staying In-Distribution

claims.claim: Decoupling precise expert imitation (a base diffusion policy trained only on expert data) from out-of-distribution recovery (a separate dynamics model trained on expert plus suboptimal policy-rollout data, used at inference to pull predicted latent states back toward the expert distribution, inspired by Control Barrier Functions) improves both policy robustness and data efficiency in both simulated and real-world experiments, without requiring additional human corrections, synthetic augmentation, or annotation
claims.direction: favors an inference-time latent in-distribution barrier over human-in-the-loop correction or synthetic data augmentation for mitigating covariate shift with limited expert demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world visuomotor manipulation; qualitative comparative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: The framework directly targets the compounding-error/covariate-shift failure mode common in behavior-cloned visuomotor policies
claims.direction: supports addressing distribution-shift robustness via an inference-time barrier rather than only via more diverse training data
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world

title: DexWorldModel: Causal Latent World Modeling towards Automated Learning of Embodied Tasks

claims.claim: Speculative Asynchronous Inference (SAI) masks partial diffusion denoising behind physical execution time, cutting blocking latency by about 50%, addressing the sequential-inference-latency bottleneck of generative world-action models
claims.direction: favors overlapping/hiding diffusion denoising computation behind ongoing physical action execution (asynchronous speculative inference) to cut real deployment latency roughly in half
claims.conditions: complex dual-arm simulation plus zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on physical robots

claims.claim: The Causal Latent World Model (CLWM) uses DINOv3 features as generative targets (rather than raw pixels) to disentangle interaction semantics from visual noise, achieving state-of-the-art performance and 'unprecedented zero-shot sim-to-real transfer,' outperforming baselines explicitly finetuned on real-world data
claims.direction: favors predicting pretrained self-supervised feature targets (DINOv3) rather than raw pixels as the world-model generative objective, for robust domain generalization
claims.conditions: dual-arm sim + zero-shot sim-to-real

claims.claim: DINOv3 features are used as generative targets specifically because they disentangle interaction semantics from visual noise
claims.direction: supports DINOv3 as a strong perceptual feature space for world-model-style auxiliary objectives
claims.conditions: dual-arm sim + real

claims.claim: A Dual-State Test-Time-Training (TTT) Memory guarantees strict O(1) memory footprint for long-horizon tasks, overcoming the O(T) memory scaling of naive world-action models
claims.direction: favors a bounded-memory (O(1)) history/memory mechanism over unbounded growing history buffers for long-horizon world-action modeling
claims.conditions: long-horizon dual-arm tasks

why_deep_read: Directly proposes a technique (masking diffusion denoising behind physical execution, ~50% latency cut) for exactly our jerky/latency problem with async inference, plus uses DINOv3 (one of our Q03 candidate encoders) and a memory mechanism with bounded cost (Q07); this cluster of matches to our specific failure modes and open questions makes it worth a closer read despite being sim-centric.

title: HarmoWAM: Harmonizing Generalizable and Precise Manipulation via Adaptive World Action Models

claims.claim: Systematic experiments reveal a trade-off between 'Imagine-then-Execute' world-action models (video prediction + inverse dynamics: generalizable but imprecise) and 'Joint Modeling' world-action models (jointly modeling actions and video: precise but constrained to the training distribution); a unified model with a Process-Adaptive Gating Mechanism that switches between a predictive expert and a reactive expert achieves both generalizable transit and precise manipulation, significantly outperforming prior state-of-the-art VLA models and world-action models by margins of 33% and 29% respectively
claims.direction: favors an adaptive combination of predictive (imagine-then-execute) and reactive (joint modeling) action-generation experts, gated by task stage, over committing to either paradigm alone
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation on six robotic tasks across three training-unseen test environments varying background, position, and object semantics

claims.claim: Achieves strong zero-shot generalization across environments varying in background, position, and object semantics
claims.direction: supports this adaptive world-action-model architecture for robustness to background/position/object-identity shifts, matching several of our stated failure modes
claims.conditions: real-world, 3 unseen test environments, 6 tasks

title: ReGIL: Retrieval-Guided Imitation Learning from a Single Demonstration

claims.claim: Treating a single demonstration as an external memory that is repeatedly queried during training (to guide exploration, generate a regularization buffer, and construct step-wise rewards via local temporal alignment) outperforms prior baselines in both success rate and training efficiency on LIBERO and Meta-World under the single-demonstration setting; in real-robot experiments, using only ONE demonstration and less than one hour of online training, ReGIL achieves over 75% success rate across three manipulation tasks with randomized initial robot pose and target position
claims.direction: favors retrieval/reward-guided online policy improvement from a single demonstration (treated as reusable memory) over standard behavior cloning on the same single demonstration
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments, single demonstration, <1 hour online training, 3 tasks with pose/position randomization; also LIBERO and Meta-World sim benchmarks

why_deep_read: An extremely low-data real-robot result (1 demonstration, <1hr online training, >75% success with pose/position randomization) that is highly relevant to whether we could get away with far fewer than 50-100 demos if paired with a short on-robot online refinement phase; want to check how much online interaction/reward computation this requires and whether it needs privileged simulation or reward access we might not have.

title: UniSteer: Unified Noise Steering for Efficient Human-Guided VLA Adaptation

claims.claim: Combining human corrective actions (inverted into noise-space targets via the frozen flow-matching decoder, providing supervised guidance) with noise-space reinforcement learning (updating only a lightweight actor predicting the noise, keeping the pretrained VLA fixed) adapts more efficiently than strong noise-space-RL-only and action-space human-in-the-loop-only baselines, improving success rate from 20% to 90% in 66 minutes on average across four real-world adaptation tasks
claims.direction: favors combining human corrective guidance with noise-space RL (over either technique alone) for rapid, low-interaction-budget real-world adaptation of a pretrained flow-matching VLA
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, four adaptation tasks, pretrained diffusion/flow-matching VLA kept frozen, only a lightweight noise-predicting actor updated

claims.claim: The method specifically exploits the flow-matching decoder's invertibility (mapping actions to noise) to translate human corrections into training signal
claims.direction: supports flow-matching action heads as particularly amenable to this kind of efficient post-deployment human-guided correction
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: One of the most concrete real-world adaptation results in the batch (20% to 90% success in 66 minutes) for fixing a pretrained flow-matching VLA's real-world failures using minimal human correction plus lightweight RL, directly relevant to how we might cheaply fix our SmolVLA's brittleness to lighting/camera/object changes after initial deployment without full retraining.

title: WorldBagel: Uncovering the Power of Unified Multimodal Models for Vision-Language-Action-World Modeling

claims.claim: Building a unified Vision-Language-Action-World model on top of a modern unified multimodal generation model (BAGEL) consistently outperforms task-specific alternatives and learns action representations that are more structured and semantically aligned with visual/linguistic context, across multi-task robotic manipulation and cross-domain experiments (LIBERO, Language Table, Franka)
claims.direction: favors building world-model + VLA capability on a single unified multimodal generative backbone over separate task-specific models
claims.conditions: LIBERO, Language Table sim benchmarks + real Franka; qualitative comparative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: VIDP: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation from Diverse Demonstrations

claims.claim: VIDP infers task compliance/stiffness directly from kinematic (force-agnostic) demonstration trajectory distributions -- using a Task-Parameterized Directionality-Aware Mixture Model to distinguish intentional compliance from mere geometric adaptation -- and jointly predicts pose actions and compliance WITHOUT force sensors, significantly outperforming fixed-impedance baselines in task success while reducing interaction forces (vs high-stiffness controllers) and tracking errors (vs low-stiffness baselines) in real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors inferring variable compliance/impedance from kinematic demonstration data alone (no force sensor needed) and extending the diffusion action head to output compliance alongside pose, over fixed-impedance position-only control
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation; no force sensor required, compatible with position-controlled hardware with an impedance/compliance-capable low-level controller

title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation

claims.claim: A sensorless residual-torque estimator (HSR-Force) infers contact strength and its temporal variation from proprioceptive/kinematic signals alone (no force/torque sensor retrofit needed), encodes it as tokens injected into the VLA action expert, and is validated in real-world whiteboard-wiping and door-opening tasks after fine-tuning on a 5,000+ episode dataset
claims.direction: favors sensorless force/contact estimation as an auxiliary conditioning signal injected into the action expert, avoiding the hardware cost of retrofitting force/torque sensors
claims.conditions: real-world wheeled-legged robot loco-manipulation; different platform from our tabletop arm setup

title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning

claims.claim: Across four task suites (130 tasks total) with high-quality human-teleoperated demonstrations, extensive experiments found that no single visual encoder architecture excels at all types of knowledge transfer (declarative vs procedural)
claims.direction: cautions against assuming any one vision-encoder architecture is universally best; encoder choice should be matched to the type of knowledge/transfer required
claims.conditions: lifelong robot manipulation benchmark, human-teleoperated demonstration data, multiple policy architectures compared

claims.claim: Naive supervised pretraining can hinder agents' performance in subsequent lifelong-learning-in-decision-making settings, and sequential finetuning outperforms existing purpose-built lifelong learning methods in forward transfer
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that more/naive pretraining is always beneficial -- here naive supervised pretraining actively hurt subsequent task performance in some settings, and simple sequential finetuning beat specialized lifelong-learning algorithms
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, 130 tasks across 4 suites, human-teleoperated demonstrations

title: Curriculum Is More Influential Than Haptic Information During Reinforcement Learning of Object Manipulation Against Gravity

claims.claim: Comparing curricula and two haptic-information modalities (no-tactile vs 3D-force sensing) for a fingertip lift-and-rotate task with a simulated three-fingered hand (no vision), the choice of curriculum greatly biased which manipulation features were learned, and successful learning was achieved even in the absence of tactile feedback -- curriculum design was more influential than the presence of haptic information
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the assumption that tactile/haptic feedback is necessary for dexterous manipulation learning; suggests curriculum/training-schedule design should be prioritized over adding sensing modalities
claims.conditions: simulated three-fingered hand, no visual input, in-hand ball lifting/rotation against gravity; RL not IL

title: Online Imitation Learning for Manipulation via Decaying Relative Correction through Teleoperation

claims.claim: A cable-driven teleoperation system providing 6-DoF spatial corrections to a policy's rollout, using a Decaying Relative Correction (DRC) method (a temporary spatial offset vector rather than a standing absolute correction), reduces the required expert intervention rate by 30% compared to a standard absolute corrective method, and integrating DRC within an online imitation learning framework rapidly increases success rate on raspberry harvesting and cloth wiping tasks
claims.direction: favors decaying/relative corrective feedback over standing/absolute corrective feedback for reducing expert intervention burden during online imitation learning correction
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks (raspberry harvesting, cloth wiping), cable-driven teleoperation hardware for corrections

title: Learning Diffusion Policies for Robotic Manipulation of Timber Joinery under Fabrication Uncertainty

claims.claim: A sensory-motor diffusion policy trained on teleoperated demonstrations for a tight-clearance industrial assembly task achieved 100% success under nominal conditions and 75% average success under randomized positional perturbations up to 10mm (far exceeding joint clearance)
claims.direction: favors diffusion policies for maintaining reasonable robustness to positional/geometric perturbation in high-precision contact-rich assembly
claims.conditions: industrial robotic workcell with force/torque sensing, construction-scale timber joinery task; two-phase evaluation (nominal vs perturbed)

title: CAAT: Contact-Aware Attention Scaling and Tactile Masking for Data-Efficient Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A lightweight contact-aware fusion module (attention scaling to emphasize vision pre-contact / tactile during contact, plus dynamic tactile masking against a non-contact reference), integrated into ACT without modifying action decoders, improves average success rate by 18.0pp over direct visuo-tactile token concatenation and 10.0pp over learnable gated fusion in simulation; on a real visuo-tactile UMI platform it achieves 60.0% average success across ACT, Diffusion Policy, and pi0, outperforming the strongest baseline by 21.1pp
claims.direction: favors explicit contact-aware priors (attention scaling + dynamic masking) over naive token concatenation or learned gating when fusing tactile and visual modalities
claims.conditions: real-world visuo-tactile UMI platform + simulation; requires tactile sensing not present in our target setup, but the fusion mechanism generalizes across ACT/Diffusion Policy/pi0 action heads

title: Action-Based Contrastive Unsupervised Representations for Reinforcement Learning Toward Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding action information as a constraint to a contrastive representation-learning loss (Action-CURL) outperforms the original CURL algorithm across simulated and real-world environments, reaching comparable performance to CURL in only 58.85% of the training time on the DMControl 500k benchmark
claims.direction: favors action-conditioned contrastive visual representation learning over standard (action-agnostic) contrastive representation learning for sample/time efficiency
claims.conditions: DMControl suite benchmark plus real-world environments; reinforcement-learning setting, not imitation learning

title: DetAug: Obstacle-Blind Trajectory Augmentation for Zero-shot Obstacle Avoidance

claims.claim: Applying an obstacle-blind augmentation scheme only to the transit (free-space) phases of a teleoperated dataset -- leaving object-interaction segments untouched -- and recording augmentation parameters as an explicit conditioning label, then at inference sampling multiple labels and executing the trajectory with lowest predicted collision cost, achieves a collision-free success rate more than 20 percentage points above the next-best method on the SafeLIBERO benchmark, and selecting over the label space outperforms guidance on the same policy by 26 percentage points
claims.direction: favors phase-selective (transit-only) trajectory augmentation with explicit conditioning labels sampled/selected at inference over both training-time augmentation requiring known obstacle geometry and inference-time-only steering
claims.conditions: SafeLIBERO benchmark; real-hardware validation also performed

claims.claim: On real hardware, inference-time steering methods collapse on tasks requiring large detours, while DetAug matches or exceeds an obstacle-conditioned baseline despite never seeing obstacles during training
claims.direction: supports this augmentation strategy for zero-shot generalization to novel obstacle configurations not present in training data
claims.conditions: real hardware

title: Leveraging Pretrained Latent Representations for Few-Shot Imitation Learning on an Anthropomorphic Robotic Hand

claims.claim: Leveraging latent representations pretrained on multiple large-scale task-agnostic human-hand-motion datasets (encoding motion subtrajectories) within a transformer-based behavior-cloning method, relying solely on human demonstrations (no teleoperation needed), yields enhanced performance versus conventional behavior cloning, particularly in resilience to perception/proprioception errors and noise, with policies successfully transferred to a real-world 23-DoF robotic hand
claims.direction: favors pretrained motion-subtrajectory latent representations (from human hand video/motion data, no teleoperation) over conventional behavior cloning trained only on robot-specific demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world 23-DoF anthropomorphic robotic hand; few-shot imitation learning; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Pretrained latent representations from large-scale task-agnostic human motion datasets improve resilience to perception and proprioception noise
claims.direction: supports leveraging large out-of-domain pretraining for the representation/encoder even for a very different embodiment (anthropomorphic hand)
claims.conditions: real-world robotic hand

title: The Better You Learn, The Smarter You Prune: Towards Efficient Vision-language-action Models via Differentiable Token Pruning

claims.claim: LightVLA, a differentiable, performance-driven visual-token pruning framework (dynamic queries + Gumbel softmax for token selection, no heuristic thresholds, no additional trainable parameters), reduces FLOPs by 59.1% and latency by 38.2% while IMPROVING task success rate by 2.6% on the LIBERO benchmark, outperforming other VLA models and existing token-pruning methods
claims.direction: favors adaptive, learned visual-token pruning (keeping only performance-relevant tokens) over using the full set of visual tokens, for simultaneously reducing compute/latency and improving performance
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark; training-free at inference (pruning learned during fine-tuning), compatible with existing VLA inference frameworks, no added parameters

why_deep_read: A concrete, drop-in efficiency method (no added parameters, no heuristics) that cuts both compute and latency substantially while IMPROVING success rate on a standard benchmark -- directly relevant to fitting a capable VLA on our 8GB laptop GPU within a tight latency budget; worth checking if gains hold for small backbones and two-camera (more tokens) setups like ours.

title: SOP: A Scalable Online Post-Training System for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A closed-loop system where a fleet of robots streams on-policy experience and human intervention signals to a centralized learner for online post-training (via interactive imitation learning HG-DAgger or RL RECAP) substantially improves pretrained VLA performance on real-world tasks (cloth folding, box assembly, grocery restocking) within HOURS of real-world interaction, with performance scaling near-linearly with fleet size
claims.direction: favors online, closed-loop post-training with human intervention signals over static offline fine-tuning, achieving strong gains within hours rather than requiring large offline demonstration sets
claims.conditions: real-world multi-robot fleet deployment; requires infrastructure for streaming experience to a centralized learner and redistributing updated policies, which may not be available in a single-robot low-cost setup

title: Foundation and Small Models Coordination for Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Coordinating pretrained vision foundation models (a segmentation model that identifies robot and target object, rendered with fixed role colors on a constant background -- 'semantic repainting' -- and a monocular depth foundation model providing normalized depth as an alternative/additional geometric cue) with a small flow-matching policy model demonstrates substantial improvements in task success under evaluated appearance shifts, on simulation benchmarks and two real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors preprocessing observations through frozen foundation models into an appearance-invariant, semantically/geometrically normalized representation (fed to a small policy) over training a small policy directly on raw RGB appearance, specifically to handle object/background appearance shift
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + 2 real-world robotic tasks, flow-matching policy architecture; perception foundation models held fixed during policy training (only adapted with in-distribution data where needed)

claims.claim: Pretrained segmentation and depth foundation models are held fixed while only the small policy model is trained on their outputs, decoupling representation learning from action learning
claims.direction: favors using frozen large foundation models purely as a fixed pre-processing/normalization stage, keeping the trained policy itself small
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

claims.claim: Replacing the target object's role color with normalized monocular depth (from a depth foundation model) provides additional useful geometric cues beyond semantic segmentation alone
claims.direction: supports incorporating monocular-depth-foundation-model cues (not necessarily a physical depth sensor) into the observation representation
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

claims.claim: A small policy model, when given appearance-normalized inputs from frozen foundation models, achieves substantial task-success improvements under appearance shift, rather than requiring a larger end-to-end policy to implicitly learn appearance invariance
claims.direction: favors keeping the trained policy small and offloading appearance-invariance to fixed pretrained foundation models rather than scaling up the policy itself
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: This directly targets our exact stated failure modes (breaks under new lighting, different-looking pumpkin) using a SMALL policy model (matching our size/compute constraint) combined with frozen segmentation+depth foundation models for appearance normalization -- arguably the single most directly applicable paper in the batch to our core robustness problem; want to check compute cost of the foundation models at inference on our 8GB GPU and real-task success numbers.

title: AnySlot: Goal-Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Policies for Zero-Shot Slot-Level Placement

claims.claim: Converting a language instruction into an explicit visual goal (rendering a spatial marker at the intended placement slot) and executing it with a goal-conditioned VLA policy -- decoupling high-level slot selection from low-level execution -- significantly outperforms flat end-to-end VLA baselines and modular grounding methods on a new slot-level placement benchmark (SlotBench) requiring centimeter-level precision
claims.direction: favors converting language conditioning into an intermediate explicit visual/spatial goal representation (rather than direct end-to-end language-to-action mapping) for tasks requiring high spatial precision
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark (SlotBench, 9 task categories); qualitative 'significantly outperforms' claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Reward guided behavior cloning from suboptimal demonstrations

claims.claim: Starting from only 10 teleoperated demonstrations, synthesizing a large mixed-quality dataset (1,800+ trajectories including failures via Isaac Lab Mimic), then reweighting the BC training loss by a per-frame quality score (from a deep ensemble classifier operating on a learned latent dynamics representation) achieves 59% success on a cube-stacking task vs 44% for standard BC on the same mixed data and 51% for BC trained 400 additional epochs on the same data
claims.direction: favors quality-reweighted BC on a small-seed-plus-synthesized mixed-quality dataset over standard BC or simply training longer on the same data
claims.conditions: simulation (Isaac Lab), Franka Emika Panda, cube stacking, only 10 original teleoperated demonstrations

title: The Curse of Precision: A Data Scaling Law for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: For closed-world high-precision manipulation tasks, the number of demonstrations N required to reach a fixed success rate grows super-exponentially as target precision P approaches a system-specific limit c, following log(N) proportional to 1/(P-c); this law is validated on canonical manipulation tasks
claims.direction: provides a quantitative scaling law showing that pushing precision requirements even slightly higher than a system's achievable limit requires disproportionately (super-exponentially) more demonstrations -- i.e., beyond some point, more demos give rapidly diminishing returns unless the system itself improves
claims.conditions: canonical manipulation tasks (precision/assembly-style, closed-world); appears to be controlled experiments, sim and/or real not specified precisely in abstract

claims.claim: The limit precision c is not a static physical property of the task but an emergent property of the whole agent system (sensors + expert policy); the authors demonstrate that adding a wrist camera, or using a more effective expert, measurably LOWERS c, thereby expanding the system's achievable precision
claims.direction: provides direct quantitative-framework support for adding a wrist camera specifically as a way to reduce the demonstration count needed for a given precision target
claims.conditions: same manipulation task experiments

why_deep_read: Offers a principled, validated scaling law connecting demo count to achievable task precision, and explicitly shows a wrist camera lowers the precision limit (directly validating our two-camera setup choice); this could let us reason quantitatively about whether our ~50-100 demo budget is sufficient for the precision the pumpkin-in-tray task requires, and what system upgrades would help most.

title: WAM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for World Action Models

claims.claim: A frozen teacher world-action-model labels a student's own generated (on-policy) histories with coherent video and action targets, repairing capability lost during distillation without needing sparse-reward RL; in preliminary RoboTwin 2.0 studies, a compressed one-video/one-action-step Flash-WAM improved from 0.0% to 58.3% success on one task and 16.7% to 33.3% on another after this on-policy distillation
claims.direction: favors on-policy distillation with teacher-labeled student-induced histories as a post-training repair method for compressed/accelerated world-action models
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 sim, two tasks; explicitly framed by the authors as a preliminary capability proof, not evidence of broad generalization

title: PECHC: Robust Tactile Grasping Stabilization in Vision-Denied Peripersonal Space

claims.claim: Using a single sparse, failure-triggered human expert correction on just ONE calibration object (Hybrid Correction Imitation Learning), plus physically-grounded behavioral constraint scheduling and tactile-history-based implicit system identification, PECHC achieves a 97.3% real-robot success rate across 149 additional held-out objects with no further intervention, a +42.8% improvement over a Vanilla-PPO-with-domain-randomization sim-to-real baseline
claims.direction: favors a single, targeted, failure-triggered correction (rather than per-object or continuous correction) combined with physical constraint priors, generalizing broadly across many held-out objects
claims.conditions: real-robot, vision-denied (last-centimeter/occluded) grasping, requires multi-finger tactile sensing not present in our target setup

title: Grounding Language Plans in Demonstrations Through Counterfactual Perturbations

claims.claim: Replaying a few human demonstrations with synthetic perturbations generates coverage of the demonstration state space, including both additional successful executions and counterfactual failures, and training on this augmented success/failure data (explanation-based learning) improves the interpretability and reactivity of imitation learning across 2D navigation and simulated and real robot manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors perturbation-based counterfactual data augmentation (generating labeled failures alongside successes from a few demos) over training on successful demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: 2D navigation + simulated and real robot manipulation; qualitative claim, no specific numbers in abstract

claims.claim: Learned mode-family classifiers (grounding low-level states/images without dense labeling) enable translating high-level LLM language plans into reactive low-level policies in an interpretable manner
claims.direction: supports grounding language plans via learned intermediate motion/mode abstractions rather than direct language-to-action mapping
claims.conditions: real + sim manipulation tasks

title: Phoenix: A Motion-Based Self-Reflection Framework for Fine-Grained Robotic Action Correction

claims.claim: Bridging high-level semantic failure reflection (from an MLLM) to low-level action correction via an intermediate coarse motion-instruction adjustment, which then conditions a multi-task motion-conditioned diffusion policy for fine-grained correction, shows superior generalization and robustness across manipulation tasks in RoboMimic simulation and real-world scenarios versus baselines
claims.direction: favors a motion-instruction intermediate representation bridging MLLM semantic self-reflection and low-level diffusion-based action correction, over direct end-to-end correction
claims.conditions: RoboMimic sim + real-world; qualitative claim, no specific numbers in abstract

claims.claim: A lifelong learning method built on this framework automatically improves the model's capability from interactions with dynamic environments
claims.direction: supports using failure-triggered self-reflection as a mechanism for continual post-deployment improvement rather than fixed offline training
claims.conditions: RoboMimic + real-world

title: Asynchronous Fast-Slow Vision-Language-Action Policies for Whole-Body Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A truly asynchronous Fast-Slow VLA architecture (a fast pathway for high-frequency action generation, a slow pathway for VLM reasoning, bridged by a latent representation buffer, jointly trained end-to-end) supports a 3B-parameter VLM while achieving 30Hz whole-body action-chunk generation, approximately 3x faster than prior VLA models of comparable size, with real-world experiments showing improved task success and significantly enhanced responsiveness versus synchronous Fast-Slow VLA baselines
claims.direction: favors truly asynchronous fast/slow execution (with a latent buffer, not just separate frequencies) over mandatory synchronous VLM+action execution, for both speed and responsiveness
claims.conditions: real-world whole-body manipulation (humanoid/whole-body platform, different from our tabletop arm), 3B-parameter VLM

title: EMMA: Generalizing Real-World Robot Manipulation via Generative Visual Transfer

claims.claim: DreamTransfer, a diffusion-Transformer-based generative video editor, allows visual editing of robot demonstration videos (changing foreground, background, AND lighting) via prompts while preserving 3D structure/geometric validity; training on a hybrid real+generated dataset (with AdaMix adaptively weighting harder samples by policy performance) achieves a relative performance increase of over 92% versus training with real data alone in real-world zero-shot visual settings (novel appearance/lighting), with a further +17% from AdaMix
claims.direction: strongly favors generative video-based visual augmentation (changing appearance, background, and lighting while preserving geometry) combined with adaptive hard-example weighting, over training on real demonstration data alone, specifically for generalizing to novel visual conditions
claims.conditions: real-world + simulated robot manipulation, 1800+ evaluation trials; zero-shot visual generalization setting

claims.claim: The framework specifically targets and substantially improves generalization to novel lighting and object/background appearance not seen in the original demonstrations
claims.direction: directly supports generative visual augmentation as a fix for exactly the lighting/appearance robustness failure mode we observe
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot visual settings

why_deep_read: Reports an exceptionally large (92%, +17% more with AdaMix) real-world relative improvement specifically for zero-shot generalization to novel lighting/appearance/background -- precisely our reported SmolVLA failure modes (new lighting, different-looking pumpkin) -- via generative augmentation of existing demos rather than collecting more; worth checking the compute cost of DreamTransfer and whether it's feasible to run once (offline data augmentation) rather than at inference time.

title: PEEK: Guiding and Minimal Image Representations for Zero-Shot Generalization of Robot Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Fine-tuning VLMs to predict a policy-agnostic point-based intermediate representation (end-effector paths for 'what actions to take' plus task-relevant masks for 'where to focus', overlaid directly on robot observations, trained via an automatic annotation pipeline across 20+ robot datasets spanning 9 embodiments) boosts zero-shot generalization by 41.4x in the real world for a 3D policy trained only in simulation, and by 2-3.5x for both large VLAs and SMALL manipulation policies
claims.direction: favors offloading 'where' and 'what' reasoning to a VLM-predicted intermediate point/mask representation (leaving the low-level policy to specialize purely in 'how'), over having the manipulation policy learn attention, action semantics, and execution jointly end-to-end
claims.conditions: real-world evaluations across 20+ robot datasets and 9 embodiments; explicitly validated with both large VLAs and small manipulation policies

claims.claim: The technique provides 2-3.5x zero-shot generalization gains specifically for SMALL manipulation policies (not just large VLAs)
claims.direction: supports that small policies particularly benefit from this offloaded semantic/visual complexity, since they cannot absorb it internally the way large models might
claims.conditions: real-world, small manipulation policy architectures

claims.claim: Task-relevant masks and end-effector paths are predicted from language+vision jointly and overlaid onto observations as the interface between high-level reasoning and low-level control
claims.direction: supports converting language/vision task specification into an explicit visual intermediate representation rather than conditioning the low-level policy on raw language tokens
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: Reports an exceptional zero-shot generalization gain (41.4x for a sim-trained 3D policy, 2-3.5x even for small manipulation policies matching our size constraint) from a policy-agnostic VLM-predicted point/mask intermediate representation; this is one of the largest and most directly relevant quantified improvements in the batch for our Q12/Q14 questions and is explicitly validated on small policies.

title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: CamVLA decouples manipulation control from camera geometry by predicting (i) an end-effector action expressed in the local camera frame and (ii) a 6-DoF hand-eye matrix relating camera to robot base, then deterministically composing these into a base-frame action; the resulting policy is calibration-free, depth-free, and single-view (only a monocular RGB image needed at deployment), and consistently improves success rates across diverse unseen viewpoints in both simulation and real-world robot data versus policies that require explicit camera extrinsics or tolerate view change only when told the camera pose
claims.direction: favors predicting actions in a camera-centric frame plus an explicitly predicted hand-eye transform (rather than a fixed/calibrated camera-to-robot mapping baked into training) for robustness to camera repositioning/remounting
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world robot data, evaluated across diverse unseen viewpoints

claims.claim: The method specifically targets robustness to cameras being 'repositioned or remounted' relative to their training-time setup, which is common in real-world deployment
claims.direction: directly supports this architecture as a fix for exactly our reported 'slightly moved camera' failure mode
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported failure mode (policy breaks when the camera is slightly moved) with a specific, principled architecture (camera-centric action + predicted hand-eye matrix, calibration-free) rather than just augmentation; worth checking whether it extends to a two-camera (scene+wrist) setup like ours and what real-world success-rate numbers look like.

title: OFlow: Injecting Object-Aware Temporal Flow Matching for Robust Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Forecasting future latents via temporal flow matching, then factorizing them into object-aware representations that emphasize physically relevant cues while filtering task-irrelevant variation, and conditioning continuous action generation on these predictions, consistently enhances robustness and success across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, MetaWorld, and SimplerEnv benchmarks plus real-world tasks, versus VLAs that act only on the current frame without unified temporal/object-aware reasoning
claims.direction: favors unifying future-latent forecasting with object-aware factorization (filtering irrelevant background/appearance variation) as an auxiliary conditioning signal for the action head, over acting only on the current frame or reasoning about time and objects in separate latent spaces
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, MetaWorld, SimplerEnv) plus real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Object-aware foresight specifically enables 'more reliable control under distribution shifts'
claims.direction: supports this approach for robustness under distribution shift generally (matching our lighting/appearance/camera shift concerns)
claims.conditions: same benchmarks + real-world

title: External vs. Implicit Touch Sensing and Actor Recurrence in PPO for In-Hand Rotation: A Systematic Ablation

claims.claim: In a controlled ablation on a low-cost anthropomorphic hand (LEAP Hand), actor recurrence (GRU-MLP vs feedforward MLP) consistently improved proprioception-only control in the single-object regime, but adding binary external contact signals DEGRADED GRU-MLP performance in that same regime while IMPROVING feedforward-MLP performance -- naive combination of recurrence and extra sensing modalities did not necessarily yield better performance, and the right choice depended on the interaction between architecture and modality
claims.direction: cautions against assuming recurrent/memory architectures and additional sensing modalities combine additively; the effect of adding a modality can depend on and even reverse with actor architecture (recurrent vs feedforward)
claims.conditions: simulation-based ablation, low-cost anthropomorphic hand (LEAP Hand), in-hand rotation task, RL (PPO) not imitation learning

title: VR-DAgger: Immersive VR for Dexterous Data Collection and Uncertainty-Guided On-Policy Correction

claims.claim: Using Monte Carlo dropout to score policy uncertainty during autonomous rollouts of a diffusion policy, then selectively replaying only the highest-uncertainty failure segments in VR for expert correction (rather than monitoring/correcting full rollouts), consistently improves over standard behavior cloning across three dexterous manipulation tasks with gains of up to 23 percentage points, while reducing per-sample collection/review time by approximately 40% versus unguided human-in-the-loop inspection
claims.direction: favors uncertainty-guided selective correction (targeting only high-uncertainty segments) over both plain behavior cloning and unguided full-rollout human-in-the-loop correction, for both performance gains and reduced expert time cost
claims.conditions: real hardware, 10-DoF XHand, three dexterous manipulation tasks (Pan pick-and-place, Drawer opening, Valve turning), standard and challenging initial configurations

title: Dual Latent Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Reconstructing historical experience into short-term and long-term latent memory tokens (retrieved via a query mechanism and injected into the same continuous embedding sequence as current observation/instruction, entirely within the VLA's native latent space) demonstrates superiority over prior memory-augmented VLA approaches (that keep memory outside the native latent space) on SimplerEnv and LIBERO
claims.direction: favors representing and retrieving history entirely within the policy's native continuous latent embedding space (rather than as separate retrieved context) for long-horizon, temporally-dependent manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv + LIBERO sim benchmarks; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: ARSTAG: An Agentic Real2Sim2Real System for Task-Specific Robot Data Generation

claims.claim: A hierarchy of language agents converts a single RGB image plus a natural-language instruction into a task-scoped simulation scene, robot-feasible demonstrations, and a task-consistent-randomized training distribution, entirely without manual scene engineering or teleoperated data collection; across seven manipulation tasks (grasping, placement, stacking) this enables sim-to-real transfer of three visuomotor policy architectures to a dual-arm robot, with pi0.5 achieving an average real-world success rate of 74.6%, and policy performance increasing with generated dataset size
claims.direction: favors fully automated Real2Sim2Real data generation (from a single image + instruction) as a substitute for manual teleoperated data collection when adapting a policy to a new task/workspace
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm robot, 7 tasks, 3 policy architectures (including pi0.5)

claims.claim: Ablations show task-consistent randomization (not just naive randomization) substantially improves robustness of the resulting policy
claims.direction: favors task-consistent (rather than arbitrary) randomization strategies when generating synthetic training data
claims.conditions: same real-world dual-arm evaluation

title: Astra: Efficient Transformer Architecture and Contrastive Dynamics Learning for Embodied Instruction Following

claims.claim: A trajectory-attention Transformer architecture with learnable action queries (rather than causal attention) for processing segmented multimodal trajectories demonstrates substantial performance improvements over previous models across three large-scale robot manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors trajectory/segment-aware attention over standard causal attention for interleaved multimodal (vision+language+action) history in imitation learning
claims.conditions: three large-scale robot manipulation benchmarks; qualitative 'substantial improvement' claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: A contrastive dynamics learning objective, added as a complement to the primary behavior-cloning objective, enhances the model's understanding of environment dynamics and multimodal alignment
claims.direction: supports adding a contrastive dynamics auxiliary objective alongside standard behavior cloning
claims.conditions: same benchmarks

title: 3D Equivariant Visuomotor Policy Learning via Spherical Projection

claims.claim: Projecting features from a single monocular RGB (eye-in-hand, e.g. GoPro-style) camera image onto a sphere enables reasoning about SO(3) symmetries without explicitly reconstructing a point cloud, making this the first SO(3)-equivariant policy learning framework for manipulation that works from monocular RGB alone (rather than requiring multi-camera point-cloud input as prior equivariant methods did)
claims.direction: favors achieving equivariance benefits via spherical projection of monocular RGB features over requiring an explicit multi-camera point-cloud input
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, single eye-in-hand RGB camera

claims.claim: Incorporating this spherical-projection equivariance into a diffusion policy consistently outperforms strong baselines in both performance and sample efficiency
claims.direction: favors equivariant diffusion policy architectures over standard (non-equivariant) diffusion policies
claims.conditions: sim + real-world

claims.claim: Equivariant models have previously been shown to improve data efficiency of diffusion policy by a significant margin; this method extends that benefit to the monocular-RGB (wrist-camera) setting
claims.direction: supports equivariant architectures for improving sample efficiency specifically when only a wrist/eye-in-hand camera is available
claims.conditions: sim + real-world

title: M3A Policy: Mutable Material Manipulation Augmentation Policy through Photometric Re-rendering

claims.claim: Given a single real-world demonstration, photometrically re-rendering the scene (using computational photography / light-transport modeling of material properties) to generate a diverse set of realistic demonstrations with different material properties, decoupling task-specific manipulation skill from surface appearance, improves the average success rate across three real-world tasks by 58.03% and shows robust performance on previously unseen materials
claims.direction: favors physically-grounded photometric re-rendering augmentation (varying material/appearance from a single real demo) over relying on additional real demonstrations or simulated-material sim-to-real transfer for appearance/material generalization
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, three tasks, evaluated on a new multi-material benchmark spanning sim and real

claims.claim: The augmented policy generalizes robustly to previously unseen materials (e.g., glass, metal, transparent/reflective surfaces) not present in the original single demonstration
claims.direction: supports this augmentation approach for robustness to novel object appearance/material, relevant to our different-looking-object failure mode
claims.conditions: real-world, unseen materials

title: Precise and dexterous robotic manipulation via human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning

claims.claim: A vision-based, human-in-the-loop RL system integrating demonstrations, human corrections, and sample-efficient RL algorithms, trained directly in the real world, achieved near-perfect success rates on precise assembly, dynamic manipulation, and dual-arm coordination tasks reflecting realistic industrial tolerances, within only 1 to 2.5 hours of real-world training -- outperforming other baselines by improving task success 2x
claims.direction: favors real-world human-in-the-loop RL (demonstrations + corrections + sample-efficient RL) over pure offline imitation learning for reaching near-perfect success on precision tasks, achievable within a few hours of real-world interaction rather than large offline demo collection
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, industrial tolerances, small critical variations in initial object placement; published in Science Robotics

claims.claim: The learned policies executed 1.8x faster on average than baseline approaches
claims.direction: favors RL-refined policies for both higher success rate and faster execution speed versus imitation-learning-only baselines
claims.conditions: real-world, same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: A high-profile (Science Robotics), influential real-world result showing that a few hours of human-in-the-loop RL (built on top of demonstrations) achieves near-perfect success and 2x better performance than baselines on precision manipulation with realistic tolerances; directly relevant to whether we should add a short real-world RL refinement phase on top of our teleop demos rather than relying purely on offline BC/diffusion training, and to how much real-world time such refinement would plausibly take.

title: Qwen-VLA: Unifying Vision-Language-Action Modeling across Tasks, Environments, and Robot Embodiments

claims.claim: Qwen-VLA, trained with large-scale joint pretraining over diverse data sources (robot manipulation, human egocentric demos, synthetic sim data, navigation data), shows consistent multi-task performance and out-of-distribution generalization under variations in scene layout, background, lighting, object configuration, and robot embodiment, achieving 97.9% on LIBERO, 86.1%/87.2% on RoboTwin-Easy/Hard, and 76.9% average OOD success in real-world ALOHA experiments
claims.direction: demonstrates that large-scale, diverse joint pretraining (across embodiments/tasks/data sources) yields robustness to lighting/background/object-configuration shift, though at large foundation-model scale rather than the small-model regime we target
claims.conditions: large-scale foundation VLA model; multiple sim benchmarks + real-world ALOHA OOD evaluation

title: Invertible Neural Network Adapter for One-Step Flow Matching in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: An invertible neural network adapter that constrains the flow-matching action-generation trajectory within an invertible latent space enables high-quality action synthesis with a single inference step (vs conventional iterative flow-matching policies), reducing real-world VLA average inference latency from 110ms to 61ms while maintaining strong task performance
claims.direction: favors an invertible-adapter one-step flow-matching action head over standard multi-step iterative flow-matching/diffusion, for latency reduction with maintained accuracy
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks + real-world robotic platforms

claims.claim: The adapter consistently demonstrates superior or near-state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of manipulation tasks despite using only one inference step
claims.direction: supports one-step flow-matching (via an invertible adapter) as competitive with iterative diffusion/flow policies
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real-world platforms

title: FELT: Generating Tactile Signals from Vision for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation

claims.claim: A frozen large visual encoder plus a lightweight query decoder synthesizes per-finger pseudo-tactile signals (images or latent features) directly from RGB observations in a single feed-forward pass; both generated tactile images and latent tactile features improve policy success over vision-only baselines on four contact-rich tasks, with the latent-feature variant requiring NO real tactile sensor during either training or deployment
claims.direction: favors deriving a pseudo-tactile auxiliary signal purely from vision (no physical tactile sensor needed at all) over either ignoring touch entirely or requiring real tactile hardware
claims.conditions: four contact-rich manipulation tasks; compatible with vision-only hardware setups like ours since no physical tactile sensor is required

title: End-to-end integration of a Vision-Language-Action Model for a custom Bimanual Manipulator

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained pi0.5 VLA via LoRA on a novel 14-DoF bimanual embodiment using ONLY synthetic demonstrations (generated by a high-fidelity MuJoCo digital twin via differential inverse kinematics and motion planning, with no real teleoperated data) failed to complete generalized pick-and-place tasks in closed-loop deployment, suffering from trajectory drift and premature grasping, despite the offline synthetic data generation and simulated baseline being highly reliable
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS/cautions against the assumption that purely synthetic (sim-generated) demonstrations are sufficient to adapt a large generalist VLA to new custom hardware -- real, human-driven demonstrations were found to be critical and their absence caused closed-loop failure despite good open-loop/offline metrics
claims.conditions: real custom bimanual Fairino FR5 manipulator, 14-DoF, synthetic-only training data via digital twin + LoRA adaptation of pi0.5

title: LieSpline-DP: Lie-Group B-Spline Diffusion Policy for Smooth Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Generating end-effector trajectories directly on SE(3) as Lie-group B-splines and coupling consecutive action-chunk plans by sharing their boundary control poses (guaranteeing C^2 continuity across the entire trajectory, not just within a chunk) produces lower trajectory jerk and higher task success than a standard Diffusion Policy baseline across three real-robot tasks; for tasks involving liquids and flexible objects, LieSpline-DP achieved 100% success on both pouring and bucket hooking, versus only 10% and 30% respectively for the Diffusion Policy baseline
claims.direction: strongly favors explicit cross-chunk continuity constraints (shared boundary control poses on SE(3) splines) over standard per-chunk diffusion action generation, for eliminating jerky motion specifically AT chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: three real-robot tasks (including pouring liquid and bucket hooking with flexible/dynamic objects)

claims.claim: Existing spline-based action representations promote smoothness within individual chunks but neither guarantee cross-chunk C^2 continuity nor respect the SE(3) group structure of end-effector poses; LieSpline-DP addresses both gaps
claims.direction: favors Lie-group-aware spline action representations over both naive Euclidean spline fits and standard discrete diffusion action chunking
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks

why_deep_read: Directly and dramatically addresses our stated 'jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries' failure mode with an explicit real-robot before/after comparison (10pp/30pp baseline success jumping to 100%) -- one of the most concrete, large-magnitude, directly-applicable results in the entire batch for our Q06 decision; worth reading in full for implementation details and whether it needs anything beyond a standard diffusion-policy training pipeline.

title: Multimodal Diffusion Transformer: Learning Versatile Behavior from Multimodal Goals

claims.claim: MDT establishes a new record on the CALVIN manipulation challenge with an absolute performance improvement of 15% over prior state-of-the-art methods that require large-scale pretraining and contain 10x more learnable parameters
claims.direction: favors a smaller diffusion-transformer policy with well-designed self-supervised auxiliary objectives over a much larger (10x parameters) pretrained model, for long-horizon multimodal-goal manipulation
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark (164 tasks combined with LIBERO), simulated and real-world environments

claims.claim: MDT masters long-horizon manipulation from multimodal (language + goal-image) specifications using a LIBERO variant containing less than 2% language annotations, via a latent goal-conditioned state representation that aligns image- and language-based goal embeddings
claims.direction: favors learning a shared latent representation that aligns sparse language annotations with goal-image embeddings, over requiring densely language-annotated demonstrations for language conditioning
claims.conditions: LIBERO (sparse language annotations) + CALVIN, sim + real-world

claims.claim: Two self-supervised auxiliary objectives (aligning image/language goal embeddings and predicting sufficient information for future states) trained alongside the primary diffusion objective substantially enhance the transformer backbone's performance
claims.direction: favors adding self-supervised future-state-prediction and cross-modal-alignment auxiliary objectives to a diffusion policy backbone
claims.conditions: CALVIN + LIBERO, sim + real-world

why_deep_read: A highly-cited (180), influential result showing a smaller diffusion-transformer policy with the right self-supervised auxiliary objectives beats a 10x-larger pretrained model, and works with under 2% language annotation coverage -- directly relevant to our Q08 (sparse language labels are enough), Q09 (which auxiliary objectives matter), and especially Q12 (small models can beat much larger ones with the right training objectives, exactly our stated goal).

title: Look, Focus, Act: Efficient and Robust Robot Learning via Human Gaze and Foveated Vision Transformers

claims.claim: Integrating human gaze data into Vision Transformers via a foveated patch tokenization scheme (processing more patches near the gaze point, fewer elsewhere, instead of uniform patch tokenization) significantly reduces the number of visual tokens and thus computation, while on certain high-precision tasks also improving task success rate
claims.direction: favors gaze-guided foveated (non-uniform) visual tokenization over uniform ViT patch tokenization, for simultaneously reducing compute and improving precision-task performance
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark and framework built on the AV-ALOHA platform; requires collecting human eye-tracking/gaze data alongside demonstrations

claims.claim: Foveated visual processing enhances robustness to background distractors
claims.direction: supports foveated/attention-guided visual processing for robustness to irrelevant background variation
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: Chain-of-Action: Trajectory Autoregressive Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Chain-of-Action generates an entire trajectory via explicit BACKWARD reasoning: the first predicted token is a stable keyframe action encoding the task goal, and subsequent action tokens are generated autoregressively conditioned on that keyframe and previous actions (global-to-local structure), achieving state-of-the-art performance across 60 RLBench tasks and 8 real-world manipulation tasks with strong spatial generalization
claims.direction: favors goal-conditioned backward trajectory reasoning (predict a stable goal keyframe first, then fill in local actions constrained by it) over standard forward-only next-action(s) prediction
claims.conditions: 60 RLBench sim tasks + 8 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The framework incorporates dynamic stopping for variable-length trajectory generation, a reverse temporal ensemble, and multi-token prediction to balance action-chunk modeling with global trajectory structure
claims.direction: favors variable-length chunking plus reverse temporal ensembling over fixed-length action chunks with standard forward temporal ensembling, for combining chunk efficiency with smooth global structure
claims.conditions: same RLBench + real-world evaluation

title: Making Foresight Actionable: Repurposing Representation Alignment in World Action Models

claims.claim: Diagnostic analysis (action-head attention analysis and causal interventions) reveals that world-action models generating plausible future video do NOT thereby guarantee accurate action extraction: the action decoder often fails to focus on task-relevant interaction regions and remains sensitive to perturbations in task-irrelevant areas, because hidden states optimized for visual reconstruction are not inherently organized in a form useful for low-level action control; aligning intermediate video-diffusion features with spatially coherent semantic representations from a foundation visual encoder (AGRA) fixes this and consistently improves both in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization on real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: CAUTIONS that naive video-prediction/world-model auxiliary objectives do not automatically produce action-useful representations, and shows that explicitly aligning world-model features with a foundation-model semantic representation is necessary to make the foresight 'actionable'
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks; diagnostic analysis plus a proposed fix (AGRA) evaluated against baseline world-action model

claims.claim: By grounding the action decoder's attention to correct interaction regions, AGRA makes the policy more robust to perturbations in task-irrelevant regions and improves OOD generalization
claims.direction: supports representation-alignment as a way to improve robustness to irrelevant visual perturbations (e.g., background changes) specifically for world-model-augmented policies
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation

title: Abstracting Robot Manipulation Skills via Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Skill Mixture-of-Experts Policy (SMP) learns a compact orthogonal skill basis and uses sticky routing to compose actions from only a small, task-relevant subset of experts at each step, achieving higher success rates and markedly lower inference cost than large diffusion baselines on a real dual-arm platform across multi-task and transfer-learning settings
claims.direction: favors a compact mixture-of-reusable-skill-experts diffusion architecture (activate only what's needed) over a single oversized diffusion backbone, for both performance and inference cost in multi-task settings
claims.conditions: simulation + real dual-arm platform, multi-task and transfer learning

claims.claim: Adaptive expert activation at inference yields fast sampling without oversized backbones
claims.direction: supports sparse expert activation for reduced inference cost/latency
claims.conditions: real dual-arm platform

title: Notes-to-Self: Scratchpad Augmented VLAs for Memory Dependent Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Incorporating a language scratchpad into a VLA -- allowing the model to memorize task-specific information (e.g., object positions) and track plan/subgoal progress in natural language, rather than only via architectural recurrence or observation-window expansion -- significantly improves generalization on memory-dependent tasks for BOTH non-recurrent and recurrent models, evaluated on ClevrSkills, MemoryBench, and a real-world pick-and-place task
claims.direction: favors a lightweight, interpretable language-based scratchpad for imparting spatial/temporal memory to an otherwise stateless VLA, over relying solely on architectural memory/recurrence
claims.conditions: ClevrSkills sim environment, MemoryBench, and a real-world pick-and-place task

title: Recover, Discover, Plan: Learning Skills and Concepts from Robot Failures

claims.claim: Jointly learning recovery skills (via RL on observed failures) and relational-predicate concepts (that explain/generalize those recoveries) converts local failure recoveries seen during training into global failure avoidance at test time, outperforming strong baselines by over 50% on long-horizon, previously unseen problems across four simulated domains, with demonstrated sim-to-real transfer for real-world non-prehensile manipulation
claims.direction: favors extracting generalizable abstract concepts from failure-recovery experience (not just reactive per-failure-mode recovery policies) for scalable failure-aware planning
claims.conditions: four simulated domains plus sim-to-real transfer for non-prehensile manipulation

title: TacO: Benchmarking Tactile Sensors for Object Manipulation

claims.claim: A systematic, task-driven evaluation training separate manipulation policies for four tactile sensor modalities (visual, acoustic, magnetic, resistive) across three tasks (pick-and-place with unknown mass, object reorientation, plug insertion) finds that tactile sensing is NOT universally beneficial in the same way -- its usefulness depends strongly on sensor modality, material properties, and the specific manipulation task
claims.direction: cautions against assuming any given tactile sensor modality is generically useful for manipulation; sensor choice should be matched to task and material properties rather than assumed beneficial by default
claims.conditions: real hardware setup across four tactile sensor modalities and three tasks; not directly applicable since our setup has no tactile sensing, but the general lesson (sensor benefit is task/modality-dependent, not universal) generalizes

title: DREAM-Chunk: Reactive Action Chunking with Latent World Model

claims.claim: A test-time-only method (no policy fine-tuning) that samples multiple candidate action chunks, rolls out their predicted latent futures via a lightweight latent world model, and selects actions from the chunk whose predicted state best matches the observed rollout, improves the robustness of action-chunking policies under stochastic dynamics on the Kinetix benchmark and on four manipulation tasks across two robot platforms and two VLA policies (simulation and hardware), especially when demonstrations contain corrective behaviors
claims.direction: favors test-time resampling/selection among multiple candidate action chunks (guided by a lightweight world model) over committing to a single open-loop chunk, to make chunked execution more reactive to stochastic dynamics and hardware execution errors
claims.conditions: sim (Kinetix) + hardware, two robot platforms, two VLA policies; test-time only, no additional policy fine-tuning required

claims.claim: DREAM-Chunk trades additional test-time computation for improved reactivity during long-horizon open-loop chunk execution
claims.direction: supports spending extra inference-time compute on chunk selection/verification as an alternative or complement to shortening the chunk/execution horizon
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: GuidedAttention: Interpretable and Correctable Visual Attention for OOD-Robust Robot Manipulation via Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Predicting task-relevant attention keypoints from camera images as an explicit intermediate representation (conditioning a diffusion-based action policy), which users can inspect and optionally correct once at rollout initialization (then auto-propagated by a tracking module throughout execution), consistently improves robot manipulation performance in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors an explicit, human-correctable visual-attention-keypoint intermediate representation over an uninterpretable end-to-end visual encoding for the action policy
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation

claims.claim: Improvements are particularly pronounced under positional and appearance out-of-distribution conditions
claims.direction: directly supports this attention-keypoint approach for robustness to both object/scene appearance shift and positional shift, matching our stated failure modes
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world

title: IntervenGen: Interventional Data Generation for Robust and Data-Efficient Robot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: IntervenGen autonomously generates a large set of corrective interventions with rich coverage of the state space starting from only a SMALL number of human interventions, increasing policy robustness by up to 39x with only 10 human interventions, evaluated across 4 simulated environments and 1 physical environment with object pose estimation error
claims.direction: strongly favors autonomously augmenting a small set of human corrective interventions (rather than collecting many more human interventions or demonstrations) as a highly data-efficient way to close distribution-shift-induced robustness gaps
claims.conditions: 4 simulated environments + 1 physical environment (object pose estimation error), interactive imitation learning (DAgger-style) setting, only 10 human interventions needed

claims.claim: The augmented interventions are specifically shown to increase robustness to distribution shift (e.g., object pose estimation error) at evaluation time
claims.direction: supports intervention-augmentation as a fix for distribution-shift robustness with very little human correction effort
claims.conditions: physical environment with object pose estimation error

why_deep_read: Reports an exceptional (39x) robustness improvement from autonomously augmenting just 10 human corrective interventions, validated on both simulated and a physical environment with realistic perception error -- this is one of the most extreme, concrete, and directly actionable data-efficiency findings in the whole batch for closing the gap between our brittle SmolVLA fine-tune and a robust policy without collecting many more demonstrations.

title: OSMO: Open-Source Tactile Glove for Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer

claims.claim: A robot policy trained EXCLUSIVELY on human demonstrations collected with a matching tactile glove (no real robot data at all) executes a challenging contact-rich wiping task requiring sustained contact pressure with 72% success, outperforming vision-only baselines by eliminating contact-related failure modes
claims.direction: favors human-only demonstration data (with matched sensing modality between human and robot) as sufficient for training a contact-rich policy, when embodiment gap in sensing is minimized
claims.conditions: real-world wiping task; requires a specialized tactile glove/sensor not present in our target setup

title: StaMo: Unsupervised Learning of Generalizable Robot Motion from Compact State Representation

claims.claim: An unsupervised, highly compressed two-token state representation (learned via a lightweight encoder plus a pretrained Diffusion Transformer decoder, encoded from static images alone, no video or complex architecture needed) integrates into existing VLA-based models with minimal inference overhead, improving performance by 14.3% on LIBERO and 30% in real-world task success; the difference between the two tokens (via latent interpolation) emerges as an effective latent action usable for policy co-training, outperforming prior latent-action methods by 10.4% with improved interpretability
claims.direction: favors a compact, unsupervised, image-only (not video-based) state/latent-action representation over more complex video-based or explicitly-supervised latent action learning methods, for both performance gains and minimal added inference cost
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark + real-world task success; scales across real robot data, simulation, and human egocentric video; minimal inference overhead

claims.claim: The representation is encoded from STATIC IMAGES alone (not video), challenging the assumption that video data is necessary for learning useful latent actions/dynamics
claims.direction: favors simpler image-only representation learning over video-based approaches for latent state/action discovery
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: Augmented Reality for RObots (ARRO): Pointing Visuomotor Policies Towards Visual Robustness

claims.claim: ARRO uses zero-shot open-vocabulary segmentation and object detection models to mask out task-irrelevant regions of the scene in real time, requiring NO additional training, setup modeling, or camera calibration, and applied during both training and inference; across Diffusion Policy and generalist policies (Octo, OpenVLA, pi0) on tabletop manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world, ARRO yields consistent performance gains and reduces the need for additional data collection
claims.direction: favors a training-free, calibration-free visual-distractor-masking preprocessing step (applied uniformly at train and test time) over collecting additional data or retraining the policy to become robust to background/scene variation
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world tabletop manipulation, compatible with multiple existing policy architectures (Diffusion Policy, Octo, OpenVLA, pi0) without modification

claims.claim: ARRO improves robustness to background/scene variations specifically, and remains effective even under challenging segmentation conditions
claims.direction: directly supports this technique for our background/scene-variation robustness concerns
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: A training-free, calibration-free, drop-in visual preprocessing technique (built on off-the-shelf zero-shot segmentation) that is explicitly shown to improve robustness to scene/background variation and reduce the need for additional data collection, and is compatible with essentially any existing policy architecture including small ones -- directly and cheaply actionable for our setup without needing to retrain or redesign our action head.

title: Knowledge Insulating Vision-Language-Action Models: Train Fast, Run Fast, Generalize Better
