claims.claim: Naively adding a continuous diffusion or flow-matching action expert module to a pretrained VLM backbone (the common recipe for building a VLA) significantly harms both training speed and the transfer of the VLM's pretrained semantic knowledge; the authors provide an extensive analysis of design choices affecting this and propose a technique for 'insulating' the VLM backbone during VLA training that mitigates the degradation
claims.direction: cautions that naively attaching a diffusion/flow-matching action-expert module to a pretrained VLM (as in many current VLA architectures) can degrade the VLM's semantic knowledge and slow training, unless the backbone is explicitly insulated during joint training -- directly relevant to how to properly combine a pretrained vision-language backbone with a continuous action head
claims.conditions: VLA models with continuous diffusion or flow-matching action experts attached to pretrained VLM backbones

claims.claim: The degree of degradation to pretrained VLM knowledge, and to training speed, depends heavily on specific architectural design choices for how the action expert interfaces with the frozen/finetuned VLM backbone
claims.direction: supports careful design of the interface between a pretrained vision-language encoder and an added action-generation module, rather than naive concatenation/joint fine-tuning
claims.conditions: same VLA architectures

why_deep_read: A high-profile, influential paper (152 citations, appears to be from a leading VLA research group) that directly diagnoses a failure mode in the exact architecture pattern we are considering (VLM backbone + diffusion/flow action expert, as in SmolVLA-style models): naive integration can quietly destroy the pretrained semantic knowledge and slow training. Given we are fine-tuning a similar architecture, understanding their proposed 'insulation' technique could directly affect our robustness-to-novel-object/lighting problems, which may partly stem from this exact failure mode.

title: StereoPolicy: Improving Robotic Manipulation Policies via Stereo Perception

claims.claim: Processing synchronized stereo image pairs with pretrained 2D vision encoders and fusing left-right features via a cross-attention Stereo Transformer (capturing spatial correspondence/disparity implicitly, without constructing explicit depth maps or point clouds) delivers consistent improvements over RGB, RGB-D, point-cloud, and multi-view baselines across three simulation benchmarks and seven real-robot tabletop and bimanual mobile manipulation tasks, when integrated with diffusion-based and pretrained VLA policies
claims.direction: favors implicit stereo-based geometric fusion over explicit depth-map/point-cloud representations (which the authors note are often noisy and fragile in real-world manipulation) or plain RGB, for geometric reasoning in manipulation policies
claims.conditions: 3 sim benchmarks + 7 real-robot tasks (tabletop + bimanual mobile manipulation); requires a stereo (two closely-spaced, synchronized) camera pair, not directly the same as our separate scene+wrist camera configuration

title: DynamicManip: Enabling Dynamic Manipulation from a Single Static Demonstration

claims.claim: A static-to-dynamic augmentation pipeline synthesizes diverse dynamic manipulation demonstrations from a SINGLE static demonstration, and combined with a dynamic-aware adaptive policy that adjusts inference frequency according to task dynamics, achieves a mean success rate 18.4 percentage points higher and policy-query latency 32.9% lower than baselines, in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors synthesizing diverse training data from a single demonstration (for dynamic tasks) plus adapting inference frequency to task dynamics, over fixed-frequency inference trained on more collected demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world dynamic manipulation tasks, custom benchmark with automatic evaluation

claims.claim: An adaptive inference-frequency policy (adjusting query rate based on task dynamics) reduces policy-query latency by 32.9% versus a fixed-frequency baseline
claims.direction: supports adapting inference/query frequency to task phase/dynamics rather than a fixed control rate
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: Memory Retrieval in Visuomotor Policies for Long-Horizon Robot Control

claims.claim: HALO, an attention-based memory retrieval mechanism for long-horizon visuomotor control, uses VLM priors (via training on memory-dependent question-answer pairs generated from demonstration trajectories) to steer retrieval toward task-relevant information and suppress spurious correlations between past information and predicted actions, and uses sparse attention restricted to the most relevant history to limit compounding memory errors, enabling reliable retrieval from up to eight minutes of past experience
claims.direction: favors VLM-prior-guided, sparsely-attended memory retrieval over naive long-context attention over full history, specifically to avoid spurious correlations (causal confusion) and error accumulation in long-horizon memory-dependent control
claims.conditions: long-horizon visuomotor control setting; specific benchmark/quantitative results not detailed in abstract excerpt

title: PonderPounce: A Pretrained MLLM as an Episode Context Engine for Robot Control

claims.claim: A jointly-trained fast-slow architecture (PONDER, a System-2 pretrained MLLM producing continuous cognition from episode history; POUNCE, a System-1 action model that asynchronously conditions control on the newest cognition and its age) achieves p50 latencies of 78ms for cognition-only refresh and 25ms for action-model invocation on an H100, and real-world experiments on four tasks under asynchronous execution show 60.98% mean success versus 40.67% for a frame-sampling baseline
claims.direction: favors an asynchronous System1/System2 split (with the fast policy explicitly conditioning on the age of the last high-level 'cognition') over synchronous execution or simpler frame-sampling context methods
claims.conditions: real-world (4 tasks) + RoboMME/RoboCasa-DC sim benchmarks; H100 GPU for latency measurement (more powerful than our target laptop GPU)

claims.claim: Reusing a pretrained MLLM's native causal context as episode memory (rather than a purpose-built memory module) achieves 60.83% success at base data scale and 75.54% with 9x data on RoboMME, versus 44.51%/57.88% for a frame-sampling baseline; a separately trained 9B model WITHOUT execution history achieves only 26.21% under matched supervision
claims.direction: strongly favors conditioning on execution/episode history (via native MLLM context) over a history-free model, and favors reusing pretrained MLLM context over ad hoc frame-sampling for memory
claims.conditions: RoboMME benchmark, varying data scale and model size

title: TAO-Force: Unifying Force-Aware Perception and Fast-Slow Control for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A contact-gated fast-slow control architecture -- a slow position-control branch tracking nominal trajectories during non-contact phases, and a fast admittance-control branch regulating physical interaction during contact phases, with force feedback injected into a frozen pretrained vision-language backbone via Force-conditioned FiLM -- is validated as effective and robust across four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors switching control mode (position vs admittance/compliance) based on detected contact phase, rather than using one control mode throughout, for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation; requires force/torque sensing not present in our target setup

title: Generalizable Humanoid Manipulation with 3D Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Using data collected in only ONE single scene, a full-sized humanoid robot with an improved 3D Diffusion Policy learning algorithm (designed to learn from noisy human teleoperation data) can autonomously perform skills in diverse real-world scenarios, validated over more than 2000 real-robot policy rollouts, using only onboard computing
claims.direction: favors 3D-representation-based diffusion policies as more robust to being trained in a single scene yet generalizing to diverse real deployment scenes, even with noisy human demonstration data and only onboard (not offloaded) compute
claims.conditions: real-world 25-DoF humanoid, whole-upper-body teleoperation data, onboard-only computing; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate percentages given in abstract

claims.claim: The system relies on a 3D LiDAR sensor and 3D Diffusion Policy learning rather than 2D-only observation
claims.direction: supports 3D spatial input for generalization across scenes
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid platform

title: Generalizable Motion Policies Through Keypoint Parameterization and Transportation Maps

claims.claim: Tracking only a small set of task keypoints (e.g., a sparse point cloud of a surface) during demonstration and execution, then fitting a nonlinear transformation (via Gaussian Process function approximators) that deforms the space and transports the original policy (position, velocity, orientation, stiffness) to novel situations, generalizes learned-from-demonstration policies to novel surfaces/postures while estimating uncertainty from limited demonstrations, outperforming state-of-the-art task-parameterization alternatives on real robot dressing, reshelving, and surface-cleaning tasks
claims.direction: favors sparse keypoint-based task parameterization plus a learned nonlinear transport map over standard task-parameterized GMM/DMP alternatives, for generalizing from a small number of kinesthetic demonstrations to novel object/surface configurations
claims.conditions: real robot manipulation tasks (arm dressing, product reshelving, surface cleaning); qualitative comparison to SOTA alternatives

title: DEMONSTRATE: Zero-shot Language to Robotic Control via Multi-task Demonstration Learning

claims.claim: Replacing LLM in-context prompt examples (which require hand-designed mathematical task examples) with task demonstrations plus embedding representations of task descriptions, structured via multitask learning to ensure target/example task similarity by construction, enables formulating control problems from language without requiring engineering expertise, and allows assessment of hallucination risk prior to task execution
claims.direction: favors grounding language-to-control via demonstration embeddings and multitask structure rather than hand-crafted in-context prompt examples with explicit mathematical task descriptions
claims.conditions: simulation + hardware experiments, robotic arm tabletop manipulation

claims.claim: The enforced multitask structure enables learning from few demonstrations
claims.direction: supports this approach for a low-demo-count regime
claims.conditions: simulation + hardware

title: Drift-Based Policy Optimization: Native One-Step Policy Learning for Online Robot Control

claims.claim: Drift-Based Policy (DBP) uses a fixed-point drifting objective to internalize corrective denoising dynamics into model parameters DURING TRAINING (rather than at inference), producing multimodal action chunks with a single network evaluation by design; on the 12-task Diffusion Policy suite it improves average success rate from 0.79 to 0.83 while reducing inference from 100 network-function-evaluations to 1, and on a physical dual-arm UR5 platform achieves 123/150 successes (82%) with average end-to-end latency of 9.5ms, compared with the MP1 one-step baseline's 89/150 successes (59%) under the same setup
claims.direction: favors training-time internalization of iterative refinement (native 1-NFE generation) over both standard multi-step diffusion and prior 1-NFE baselines (e.g., MP1), for simultaneously higher success rate and much lower latency
claims.conditions: 12-task Diffusion Policy suite (sim), 37 point-cloud manipulation tasks (88.4% avg success beating 1-NFE baseline OMP's 82.3%), and a real physical dual-arm UR5 platform

claims.claim: Drift-Based Policy Optimization (DBPO) augments the pretrained one-step backbone with a stochastic interface providing exact conditional rollout likelihoods for PPO-style on-policy RL fine-tuning, while preserving 1-NFE deployment, and further improves pretrained one-step policies via stable online fine-tuning on RoboMimic and D4RL
claims.direction: favors a one-step generative action head that remains compatible with subsequent on-policy RL fine-tuning, rather than requiring a separate architecture for RL refinement
claims.conditions: RoboMimic + D4RL

title: SARM2: Multi-Task Stage Aware Reward Modeling for Self Improving Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A multi-task stage-aware reward model (combining an action-primitive-based stage estimator with a multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts value head to produce dense per-step rewards without per-task annotations) reduces value-estimation MSE by 80% over the strongest baselines; used within an on-policy reward-guided framework (SPIRAL) that improves VLA policies from cheap autonomous rollouts, it raises task success from around 50% to near-perfect on two tasks (Folding Shorts: 58% to 100%; Cleaning Whiteboard: 50% to 90%)
claims.direction: favors using a general (not per-task-annotated), dense, stage-aware reward model to guide on-robot RL refinement of a BC-pretrained VLA policy from autonomous rollouts, over relying solely on more costly high-quality demonstrations
claims.conditions: 10-task benchmark; appears to be real-robot manipulation (task names like folding shorts, cleaning whiteboard suggest real-world evaluation)

title: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A linear-probe analysis on a tactile-enhanced VLA finds that future tactile states are most predictable from INTERMEDIATE action-expert features, not from vision-language features or final action outputs; a lightweight Latent Tactile Predictor applied at this intermediate representation (rather than at other points in the architecture, and predicting compact latent embeddings rather than raw noisy tactile signals) outperforms less-aligned or multi-interface tactile-prediction placements on real-world contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: provides a generalizable methodological finding about WHERE in a VLA architecture to attach an auxiliary future-prediction objective (at intermediate action-expert features, not at the vision-language encoder or the final action head) for it to be most effective -- relevant beyond just tactile prediction to any auxiliary future-state objective
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks; requires tactile sensing for this specific instantiation, but the architectural placement finding may generalize to other auxiliary signals

title: Privileged Sensing Scaffolds Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Scaffolder, an RL approach that exploits privileged sensing (e.g., motion capture, tactile) only in training-time-only auxiliary components (critics, world models, reward estimators) while the deployed policy uses only a cheap general-purpose sensor (e.g., camera), easily outperforms relevant prior baselines and frequently performs comparably even to policies with test-time access to the privileged sensors, across a new 10-task 'S3' benchmark
claims.direction: favors using expensive/extra sensors only during training (never at deployment) to improve a cheap-sensor-only deployed policy, over either training and deploying with the same cheap sensors throughout, or requiring the expensive sensors at deployment
claims.conditions: simulated benchmark (S3 suite, 10 tasks); reinforcement learning setting, not imitation learning

claims.claim: This training-time-only privileged information strategy improves the target policy without changing its deployment-time sensor requirements
claims.direction: supports using richer information sources only for data/training augmentation rather than requiring new deployment hardware
claims.conditions: same benchmark

title: CLAP: A Closed-Loop Diffusion Transformer Action Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Componentizing the VLA architecture with a specialized diffusion-transformer action module plus a critic module applied during inference (forming a closed-loop model), rather than repurposing a VLM for action prediction via simple action quantization, significantly outperforms existing methods on real robots, handling complex high-precision tasks
claims.direction: favors a dedicated diffusion-transformer action module with an inference-time critic (closed-loop) over simple action-token quantization repurposed from a VLM
claims.conditions: real robots; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: The closed-loop model generalizes to unseen objects and backgrounds
claims.direction: supports the closed-loop critic-guided design for improving generalization to novel objects/backgrounds
claims.conditions: real robots

title: Symskill: Symbol and Skill Co-Invention for Data-Efficient and Real-Time Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Jointly learning predicates, operators, and skills from unlabeled, unsegmented demonstrations (combining IL's reactivity with TAMP's compositionality and real-time symbolic+motion-level failure recovery) achieves 85% success on 12 single-step RoboCasa tasks and composes them into multi-step plans WITHOUT additional data; on a real Franka robot, it learns from only 5 MINUTES of play data and performs 12-step long-horizon tasks from goal specifications
claims.direction: favors jointly discovering symbolic abstractions and skills from a small amount of unsegmented play data (rather than large labeled/segmented demonstration sets) for compositional, data-efficient long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: RoboCasa simulation (12 tasks, 85% success) + real Franka robot (5 minutes of play data, 12-step tasks)

title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Steering a frozen pretrained flow-matching policy via RL-learned residual perturbations on a compact, task-relevant bottleneck latent (extracted by a variational information bottleneck module, rather than applying RL residuals directly in action space) improves both sample efficiency and final performance over strong post-training baselines; in the real world, it improves average success rate on four tasks by 33.7% over imitation base policies while producing smoother exploration behaviors than an action-residual counterpart
claims.direction: favors steering a frozen pretrained policy through a compact latent bottleneck (rather than through action-space residuals or full policy-weight fine-tuning) for online RL adaptation after offline imitation pretraining
claims.conditions: 8 simulation tasks + 4 real-world tasks, flow-matching policy backbone

claims.claim: The technique is instantiated on flow-matching policies specifically, exploiting their structure for latent-space steering
claims.direction: supports flow-matching action heads as amenable to this kind of cheap post-hoc RL adaptation
claims.conditions: real-world + sim manipulation

title: PAIWorld: A 3D-Consistent World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Current multi-view world models that simply concatenate view tokens (from egocentric, eye-to-hand, and wrist-mounted cameras) without explicit geometric reasoning suffer from cross-view object drift, depth inconsistency, and texture misalignment; adding Geometry-Aware Cross-View Attention, Geometric Rotary Position Embedding (encoding camera ray directions/extrinsics), and 3D-aware feature distillation from frozen 3D foundation models resolves these issues and achieves state-of-the-art multi-view 3D consistency (1st on WorldArena leaderboard)
claims.direction: cautions that naive multi-camera token concatenation (e.g., combining scene camera + wrist camera features) can cause cross-view inconsistency, and favors explicit geometric cross-view attention mechanisms when fusing multiple camera views
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation benchmarks (world-model evaluation, e.g. WorldArena, AgiBot-Challenge2026)

claims.claim: The resulting 3D-consistent world model enables downstream applications such as model-based planning and multi-view policy post-training
claims.direction: supports investing in explicit 3D consistency for world-model-based auxiliary objectives when using multiple cameras
claims.conditions: same benchmarks

title: Masked Visual Actions for Unified World Modeling

claims.claim: Expressing robot action as a partially-revealed pixel-space trajectory of an arbitrary entity in video (revealing robot motion for forward dynamics prediction, or revealing desired object motion for inverse robot-behavior recovery) lets a video model fine-tuned with only 15 hours of masked examples achieve strong visual fidelity and controllability across diverse scenes and embodiments, with imagined rollouts correlating with real-world execution outcomes for policy evaluation and ranking candidate futures in model-based planning
claims.direction: favors a pixel-space (visually-aligned) action interface for world models, requiring only a small amount (15 hours) of fine-tuning data, over action interfaces requiring dedicated architectural bridges
claims.conditions: real videos + simulation, multiple embodiments; qualitative correlational claims, no specific task success numbers given in abstract

title: A Principled Approach for Creating High-fidelity Synthetic Demonstrations for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Treating the expert trajectory as a strong prior (modeling it with Dynamic Movement Primitives and retargeting it to new goals/object configurations/viewpoints within a reconstructed 3D-Gaussian-Splatting scene, yielding phase-consistent, shape-preserving motion by construction, with an analytic obstacle-aware DMP formulation for collision avoidance) produces synthetic demonstrations with lower deviation and collision rates and yields HIGHER task success when training diffusion-based visuomotor policies, compared to planner- or optimization-based synthetic demonstration generation that lets new motions deviate substantially from the expert path
claims.direction: favors expert-motion-preserving synthetic demonstration generation (DMP retargeting in a reconstructed scene) over sampling-based-planner or trajectory-optimization synthetic data generation, especially for contact-rich/shape-sensitive tasks where increased 'diversity' from planner-based synthesis can actually HURT downstream policy learning
claims.conditions: real Spot mobile manipulator, three manipulation tasks with increasing sensitivity to trajectory fidelity

title: FabriVLA: A Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Model with Conformal Action Chunk Uncertainty

claims.claim: FabriVLA, a lightweight VLA that fuses shallow and intermediate VLM layers (preserving fine-grained visual features) and gates self-attention among action tokens so its flow-matching head only admits inter-step structure as far as training warrants, trained end-to-end in a single stage, reaches a state-of-the-art 90.0% average success on Meta-World MT50 with only 0.88B PARAMETERS
claims.direction: favors a small (sub-1B parameter) VLA with careful shallow+intermediate feature fusion and gated action-token attention over larger VLA backbones, showing strong performance is achievable at very small model size
claims.conditions: Meta-World MT50 benchmark (sim); very small parameter count close to our target model-size regime

claims.claim: Joint Conformal Action Chunk Calibration (JCAC), a post-training method adding a lightweight residual scale head to a frozen policy, turns a learned elementwise error scale into a calibrated confidence set covering the whole executed action-chunk prefix, 3.3x tighter in mean radius than an unconditional conformal set, enabling risk-ranked review of rollouts before execution on LIBERO-Safety
claims.direction: favors calibrated, chunk-level uncertainty quantification (conformal prediction over the executed action prefix) as a lightweight add-on for safety/risk-ranking of action chunks
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Safety benchmark; post-training addition, requires only a single policy query

title: Aligning robotic manipulation with human cognitive modalities: studies in perception, language, imitation, and foresight

claims.claim: CROG, an end-to-end model for 'referring grasp synthesis' (identifying an object described by a natural-language expression in a cluttered scene and generating a valid grasp for it), connects grasp prediction with human intent expressed through object names, attributes, spatial relations, and locations, introduced alongside the first benchmark (OCID-VLG) combining referring expressions, object masks, and 4-DoF grasp annotations
claims.direction: favors explicitly grounding language-specified object references into grasp synthesis (rather than treating grasp detection and language understanding as separate stages) for cluttered, ambiguous scenes
claims.conditions: benchmark introduced by the thesis (OCID-VLG); qualitative description, no specific numbers given in this abstract excerpt

claims.claim: DemoBot, a framework for acquiring bimanual dexterous manipulation skills from third-person human videos, extracts hand-object motion priors from a single visual demonstration
claims.direction: supports extracting motion priors from third-person (not first-person/egocentric) human video for bimanual skill acquisition
claims.conditions: not fully detailed in this abstract excerpt

title: Visible-Reachable Workspace for Perception-Aware Humanoid Design

claims.claim: On a 31-DoF humanoid with independently actuated RGB-D cameras, camera articulation increases visible-reachable workspace coverage from 38% to 97%; in a controlled two-target reach-and-grasp benchmark, a dual-actuated camera design reduces mean completion time by 17% and mechanical energy by 19% relative to the same robot with fixed cameras
claims.direction: favors actively repositionable/articulated cameras (that can redirect sensing to keep a reach target visible) over fixed camera placements, for both task efficiency and success in visually-guided manipulation
claims.conditions: real 31-DoF humanoid hardware with actuated RGB-D cameras; different context from our fixed scene+wrist camera setup, but suggests camera positioning/visibility of the target matters substantially for task efficiency

title: ALOHA Unleashed: A Simple Recipe for Robot Dexterity

claims.claim: A simple recipe of large-scale data collection combined with expressive generative models such as Diffusion Policies is effective for learning challenging bimanual manipulation tasks involving deformable objects and complex contact-rich dynamics, demonstrated on 5 real-world and 3 simulated tasks with improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines
claims.direction: favors diffusion-policy action heads for complex contact-rich bimanual tasks, though the demonstrated recipe explicitly relies on LARGE-SCALE data collection rather than our small (~50-100 demo) regime
claims.conditions: real + sim bimanual manipulation tasks, large-scale data collection on ALOHA 2 platform; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given in abstract

title: Unified Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: UniVLA autoregressively models vision, language, and action signals as discrete token sequences within a single unified multimodal model, enabling flexible learning from large-scale video data, and achieves 95.5% average success rate on LIBERO, surpassing pi0-FAST's 85.5%, with SOTA results on CALVIN and Simplenv-Bridge and real-world ALOHA validation
claims.direction: favors a fully unified discrete-token autoregressive formulation for vision+language+action over separate continuous action-expert modules, at large model/data scale
claims.conditions: LIBERO/CALVIN/Simplenv-Bridge sim benchmarks + real ALOHA; large-scale foundation-model regime, not our small-model/low-data setting

claims.claim: Incorporating world modeling during post-training (capturing causal dynamics from videos) facilitates effective transfer to downstream policy learning, especially for long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: supports video-based world-modeling post-training as beneficial specifically for long-horizon task transfer
claims.conditions: same benchmarks

title: TReF-6: Inferring Task-Relevant Frames from a Single Demonstration for One-Shot Skill Generalization

claims.claim: Inferring a simplified, abstracted 6DoF Task-Relevant Frame purely from a single trajectory's geometry (identifying an 'influence point' to define a local reference frame for a Dynamic Movement Primitive), then semantically grounding it via a vision-language model and localizing it in novel scenes with Grounded-SAM, supports one-shot imitation learning that preserves task intent across diverse object configurations, validated in simulation (robust to trajectory noise) and deployed end-to-end on real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors inferring a task-relevant reference frame from trajectory geometry (grounded via VLM + open-vocabulary segmentation) as the mechanism for one-shot generalization, rather than relying on many demonstrations to cover object-configuration variation
claims.conditions: simulation (noise robustness) + real-world manipulation, one demonstration

title: Fast Visuomotor Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Energy Policy natively predicts multimodal actions in a SINGLE forward pass (using an energy-score learning objective plus a simple, efficient 'energy MLP', rather than iterative denoising), enabling high-precision manipulation at high speed for resource-constrained systems; on the MimicGen benchmark it matches or surpasses state-of-the-art manipulation methods while significantly reducing computational overhead and achieving faster inference
claims.direction: favors an energy-score-based single-forward-pass multimodal action architecture over iterative diffusion/flow-matching action heads, specifically for high-frequency, resource-constrained (e.g., low-power/edge) robotic systems
claims.conditions: simulated (MimicGen) and real-world robotic manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The framework is explicitly designed for high-frequency robotic tasks and resource-constrained systems, prioritizing low computational overhead
claims.direction: supports single-forward-pass energy-based action heads as an alternative to diffusion/flow when compute/latency is tightly constrained (matching our laptop-GPU situation)
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Simultaneous Tactile-Visual Perception for Learning Multimodal Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A see-through-skin tactile-visual sensor (TacThru) combined with a Transformer-based Diffusion Policy (TacThru-UMI) achieves an average success rate of 85.5% on five real-world contact-rich tasks, significantly outperforming a tactile-only policy (66.3%) and a vision-only policy (55.4%)
claims.direction: favors simultaneous tactile+visual sensing over either modality alone for contact-rich tasks, when a sensor enabling truly simultaneous sensing (rather than separate/unreliable tactile tracking) is available
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation, five tasks; requires specialized STS tactile-visual sensor hardware not present in our target setup

title: Augmented Reality-Enhanced Robot Teleoperation for Collecting User Demonstrations

claims.claim: An AR-enhanced teleoperation system with spatial point-cloud rendering (vs without point-cloud rendering) improves demonstration-collection task performance (accuracy/efficiency) by 28% and increases operator usability (System Usability Scale) by 12%, on industrial ABB robot platforms
claims.direction: favors providing real-time environmental point-cloud perception feedback to the human operator during teleoperation/demonstration collection, for improving demonstration quality and collection efficiency
claims.conditions: industrial ABB robots (IRB 1200, GoFa 5), user study; teleoperation/data-collection interface, not the policy itself

title: AffordSim: A Scalable Data Generator and Benchmark for Affordance-Aware Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Integrating open-vocabulary 3D affordance prediction into simulation-based trajectory generation (grounding language-specified affordance queries on object surfaces, sampling region-conditioned grasps, and randomizing pose/texture/lighting/noise/backgrounds) achieves 93% of the trajectory-collection success rate of manual per-object contact annotations on affordance-critical tasks and 89% on hard composite tasks, across a 50-task benchmark with 500+ objects and 5 embodiments
claims.direction: favors affordance-grounded automated synthetic data generation over both generic (task-agnostic) grasp estimators and manual per-object contact annotation, as a scalable middle ground nearly matching manual-annotation quality
claims.conditions: simulation-based data generation, 50 tasks, 5 robot embodiments, 500+ objects

claims.claim: VLA policies trained purely on AffordSim-generated data transfer zero-shot to a real Franka FR3, reaching 24% average real-world success rate across the evaluated tasks
claims.direction: shows automated affordance-grounded synthetic data alone enables non-trivial (though still modest) zero-shot real-world transfer without any real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real Franka FR3, zero-shot from synthetic-only training data

title: SERF: Spatiotemporal Environment and Robot Feature Map for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning a mobile-manipulation VLA policy on a spatiotemporal feature map (representing environment and articulated robot body as neural points in a shared latent space, updated online via object-level rigid tracking and forward kinematics, with map tokens extracted from multiple reference frames/scales) outperforms image-only baselines on BEHAVIOR-1K, reaching subgoals faster via more direct trajectories and recovering from object-drop failures
claims.direction: favors an explicit persistent spatial/environment memory representation (beyond just image observation history) for long-horizon reasoning about localization, environment changes, and task progress
claims.conditions: BEHAVIOR-1K simulation benchmark, long-horizon mobile manipulation (different from our fixed-base tabletop setup, but the persistent-memory concept is relevant)

claims.claim: The map-conditioned policy improves robustness to scene-configuration shifts
claims.direction: supports persistent spatial memory for robustness to scene/configuration changes
claims.conditions: same benchmark

title: Training and Evaluating Diffusion Policies with Long Context Lengths

claims.claim: Systematically benchmarking Diffusion Policy performance as observation-history context length is scaled from short to long, across tasks with varying local stability/memory requirements and multiple data regimes, the results CHALLENGE PRIOR CLAIMS that naively scaling context length is brittle: with an appropriate conditioning method and denoising backbone (UNet + Cross-Attention), single-task policies achieve high success rates on many tasks in the usual data regime even with naive (unmodified) long-context scaling
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the commonly cited claim/lore that long observation-history context is brittle or harmful for diffusion-policy imitation learning; the right architecture (UNet+Cross-Attention conditioning) makes naive long-context scaling viable, and a proposed multi-context-length joint training algorithm further reduces the sample complexity of long-context learning
claims.conditions: systematic benchmark across a spectrum of tasks (varying local stability and memory requirements) and multiple data regimes; appears to be simulation-based imitation learning with Diffusion Policies

why_deep_read: This is a rare systematic, controlled ablation study directly on our Q07 question (observation history length for a diffusion policy) across multiple data regimes and tasks, and it explicitly contradicts prior claims of brittleness -- exactly the kind of evidence-vs-lore finding our review is meant to surface; worth reading in full to see which conditioning/backbone choices matter and whether the 'usual data regime' includes something close to our ~50-100 demo budget.

title: Transferring Policy of Offline Reinforcement Learning From Hybrid Dataset to Real World via Progressive Neural Network

claims.claim: Training offline RL on a hybrid dataset combining a small amount of high-quality real-world data with high-diversity simulation data (assuming mismatched dynamics but shared state space), then transferring via progressive neural networks, facilitates faster offline learning and better real-world adaptation than using either data source alone, on two manipulation tasks with a 6-DoF Ned robotic arm
claims.direction: favors combining a small real dataset with a larger, dynamics-mismatched simulation dataset (bridged via progressive neural network transfer) over using only one data source, for offline-to-real-world policy transfer
claims.conditions: real 6-DoF Ned robotic arm, two manipulation tasks; offline RL setting, not imitation learning

title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models

claims.claim: Despite strong zero-shot perception and language capabilities, state-of-the-art VLA methods (including Action Chunking Transformers and Pi0.5) show overall task performance that often degrades substantially under distribution shifts, revealing a gap between high-level understanding and robust low-level behavior; the benchmark's simulation metrics correlate strongly with real-world metrics
claims.direction: cautions that strong zero-shot perception/language ability in a VLA does not guarantee robust task performance under distribution shift -- an important caveat against assuming large pretrained VLA generality alone solves our robustness problem
claims.conditions: 28 tasks, 13 categories, 2 robot morphologies, ManiSkill-based simulation with demonstrated sim-to-real metric correlation

title: UniFS: Unified Fast-to-Slow Hierarchical Architecture for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Resolving the 'frequency dilemma' of fast-slow dual-system VLAs (large update gaps cause semantic drift from stale context; small gaps erode computational savings) by stratifying VLM layers into groups with progressively decreasing update frequencies, re-routing multi-scale VLM features to align fast-varying representations with fine-grained action decoding and slow-varying ones with coarse planning, and using multi-level supervision across temporal scales, UniFS achieves state-of-the-art 98.3% average success on LIBERO (a 2.5% gain over the VLA-Adapter baseline) while reducing average inference latency from 36.5ms to 17.8ms (2.1x speedup)
claims.direction: favors a graduated multi-frequency layer-stratified fast-slow architecture (rather than a simple two-frequency split) for simultaneously improving both accuracy and latency in VLA inference
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark plus real-robot experiments on a Franka platform

title: Object-grounded embodied picking for e-commerce warehouse fulfillment: a foveated diffusion policy for operational robustness

claims.claim: A panorama-fovea dual-stream visual encoder (a low-resolution global panorama stream plus a detection-guided high-resolution fovea stream using ROI Align on object regions), with object-guided cross-attention injecting the fovea tokens into each diffusion denoising step, grounds action generation in target-specific visual evidence rather than undifferentiated global scene representations; foveated conditioning improves average success rate by 11.3 percentage points over a non-foveated variant on a diagnostic subset
claims.direction: favors explicit object-centric foveated visual conditioning (high-res object crop + low-res global context, fused via cross-attention at each denoising step) over a single undifferentiated global visual encoding, to avoid the policy exploiting spurious contextual/background cues
claims.conditions: 10 benchmark datasets, six simulated manipulation tasks (proficient-human and multi-human demonstrations)

claims.claim: FDP achieves average success rates of 81.0% and 76.8% (proficient-human vs multi-human demos respectively), outperforming diffusion-based baselines, with particularly strong performance on object-centric tasks (Push-T 86.7%, Lift 100.0%), and maintains 84.0% success even under severe object-localization perturbations (sigma=10 pixels), demonstrating resilience to detection/perception noise
claims.direction: supports foveated object-grounded conditioning for robustness specifically to clutter, reflective packaging, background variation, and detection noise -- closely matching our warehouse-adjacent pick-and-place setting and appearance-robustness concerns
claims.conditions: six simulated manipulation tasks, diagnostic noise-perturbation subset

claims.claim: Accelerated DDIM sampling reduces policy-inference latency to approximately 55ms with 10 denoising steps, supporting closed-loop control feasibility
claims.direction: shows this object-grounded diffusion policy design is compatible with fairly low (55ms) inference latency using fewer denoising steps
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: Eq.Bot: Enhance Robotic Manipulation Learning via Group Equivariant Canonicalization

claims.claim: A model-agnostic SE(2)-equivariant canonicalization wrapper (transform observation to canonical frame, apply existing policy, map actions back) improves manipulation performance over baselines, with the most significant improvement reaching 50.0%, when applied on top of both CNN-based (CLIPort) and Transformer-based (OpenVLA-OFT) policies
claims.direction: favors adding an equivariance/canonicalization wrapper for robustness to spatial transformations (rotation/translation) without changing the underlying policy architecture
claims.conditions: sim and real manipulation tasks; applied on top of existing policies (CLIPort, OpenVLA-OFT), no architecture modification required

title: Fourier Features Let Agents Learn High Precision Policies with Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Mapping point-cloud coordinates from Cartesian into high-dimensional Fourier space before encoding significantly improves precision of point-cloud-based imitation-learning policies vs. plain Cartesian features, attributed to neural networks' spectral bias toward low-frequency functions; the benefit is consistent across diverse point-cloud encoder architectures and robust across hyperparameters. Abstract also notes RGB-only policies suffer depth ambiguity and perspective-scale issues that 3D/point-cloud priors help address
claims.direction: favors 3D/point-cloud representations (with Fourier positional encoding) over plain RGB or raw-Cartesian point clouds for high-precision manipulation
claims.conditions: RoboCasa and ManiSkill3 sim benchmarks plus a real robot setup; imitation learning (demo count not given in abstract)

why_deep_read: Directly bears on Q04 (RGB vs point-cloud/depth) for our RealSense-equipped setup; the full ablation tables would show which point-cloud encoders and how much data are needed, and whether the Fourier trick is cheap enough for an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: EDIL: An End-to-End Decoupled Imitation Learning Method for Stable Long-Horizon Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Decoupling bimanual manipulation into a Transformer encoder-decoder 'arm policy' for multimodal global trajectories plus a separate cross-attention 'gripper policy' for fine end-effector actions significantly outperforms end-to-end SOTA baselines on long-horizon bimanual tasks, particularly reducing spurious gripper activations
claims.direction: favors decoupling coarse arm-trajectory prediction from fine gripper/contact control rather than a single monolithic action head
claims.conditions: bimanual robot, 3 long-horizon manipulation tasks, imitation learning from expert demonstrations; no specific demo counts or success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: The gripper sub-policy integrates sequential state history via cross-attention with the arm stream to maintain cooperative stability in long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors incorporating observation/state history for contact-critical sub-policies
claims.conditions: bimanual long-horizon manipulation

title: Counterfactual Behavior Cloning: Offline Imitation Learning from Imperfect Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Expanding the demonstration dataset with 'counterfactual' nearby actions the human could have intended (rather than only the exact actions shown), and training BC to recover a simplified underlying policy from this expanded region, outperforms state-of-the-art offline-IL alternatives when demonstrations are noisy or suboptimal (e.g., noisy actions, overshooting)
claims.direction: favors data-augmentation/extrapolation methods over naive action-matching BC when human demos contain noise or suboptimality
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world settings; standardized datasets plus real human teachers of varying skill levels; noisy demonstrations

why_deep_read: Our teleop data has Feetech servo jitter/backlash noise; full text would show whether Counter-BC's noise-correction method and reported gains generalize to low-cost-arm-scale noise, and how much it helps at our 50-100 demo scale.

title: Few-shot SOP-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Policy for Proactive Human-Robot Collaborative Construction Assembly via Structured Semantic Prompts

claims.claim: Few-shot, parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a flow-based VLA foundation policy using 50 teleoperated demonstrations achieved 65% success (13/20) on a real 7-piece window-frame assembly task with 102s average completion time for successful trials, vs 5% (1/20) for a hand-engineered visual-servoing baseline (no VLA) and 0% (0/20) for the VLA baseline without parameter-efficient fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors few-shot (~50-demo) parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a flow-matching VLA over both classical visual servoing and a zero-shot/unfine-tuned VLA
claims.conditions: real robot, 7-piece window-frame assembly, human-robot collaborative construction task, 50 teleoperated demonstrations, flow-based VLA backbone

claims.claim: Structured semantic SOP prompts (precedence constraints, role allocation, proactive-trigger semantics) are necessary for reliability: a prompt-free ablation without the structured semantic SOP prompt achieved 0/5 successes
claims.direction: favors structured/explicit semantic language conditioning over generic language conditioning for multi-step collaborative tasks
claims.conditions: same real-robot assembly setup, ablation removing only the structured prompt

why_deep_read: Closely matches our setup: real robot, ~50 teleop demos, few-shot parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a flow-matching VLA, with concrete success-rate numbers and ablations (with/without fine-tuning, with/without structured prompt) directly informing Q01, Q08, and Q13.

title: GenDOM: Generalizable One-shot Deformable Object Manipulation with Parameter-Aware Policy

claims.claim: A policy conditioned on estimated deformable-object parameters, trained on diverse simulated objects and calibrated from a single real-world demonstration via differentiable-physics parameter estimation, outperformed baselines by 26% (ropes) and 50% (cloths) in real-world manipulation, and 62%/15% in-domain/OOD improvements in simulation
claims.direction: favors parameter-conditioned sim-trained policies plus single-demo real-world calibration over policies requiring many real demos per object
claims.conditions: real-world rope and cloth manipulation; single real-world demonstration used only for parameter estimation, not full imitation-learning training; simulated training diversity

title: Dreamitate: Real-World Visuomotor Policy Learning via Video Generation

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained internet-scale video diffusion model on human task demonstrations, then at test time generating a synthesized execution video conditioned on images of a novel scene and using it directly to control the robot, is proposed as an alternative to standard behavior-cloning action heads
claims.direction: favors a video-generation-based control paradigm over standard behavior cloning for bridging human-robot embodiment gap and improving generalization
claims.conditions: real-world, 4 tasks of increasing complexity, fine-tuned from internet-scale pretrained video diffusion model on human demonstrations

claims.claim: The video-generation-based policy achieves a significantly higher degree of generalization to diverse visual environments than existing behavior cloning approaches
claims.direction: favors leveraging internet-scale generative video pretraining for visual generalization
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, novel scenes at test time

title: RVT-2: Learning Precise Manipulation from Few Demonstrations

claims.claim: RVT-2 learns high-precision multi-task 3D manipulation (e.g., inserting a peg or plug into a socket at millimeter-level tolerance) from about 10 real-world demonstrations per task
claims.direction: favors that ~10 demonstrations per task can suffice for precise real-world manipulation when paired with a strong 3D-aware multitask architecture
claims.conditions: real world, single third-person RGB-D camera, ~10 demos/task, single model handles multiple language-conditioned tasks

claims.claim: RVT-2 uses only a single third-person RGB-D camera and a 3D manipulation representation to achieve millimeter-level precision (e.g., peg/plug insertion)
claims.direction: favors RGB-D/3D-aware representations over RGB-only for high-precision insertion-style tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, single RGB-D camera

claims.claim: Architectural and system-level improvements make RVT-2 6x faster in training and 2x faster in inference than its predecessor RVT, while also improving RLBench success rate from 65% to 82%
claims.direction: favors optimizing model architecture/system for speed, showing speed and accuracy are not necessarily in tension
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation benchmark

why_deep_read: Closely matches our few-demo (~10-100), single-depth-camera, real-robot regime and directly targets precision; full ablations would clarify which architectural choices are transferable to a smaller model on an 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Object-Centric Residual RL for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real VLA Enhancement

claims.claim: An object-centric residual RL policy, trained purely in simulation using object poses (with pose noise injection and dropout) as a compact observation space, and used to correct the actions of a frozen VLA, improves real-world zero-shot success rate from 42% to 76% averaged across five manipulation tasks on a real Franka Research 3 robot
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight residual correction policy on top of a frozen imitation-learning VLA rather than relying on the VLA's raw predictions, to counter compounding execution errors
claims.conditions: real Franka Research 3 robot, five manipulation tasks, residual policy trained only in simulation then deployed zero-shot; base VLA replayed with same teleop demos in sim to align domains

claims.claim: An object-centric (pose-based) observation space transfers consistently between simulation and reality, avoiding the visual domain gap that affects image-based residual approaches
claims.direction: favors compact object-pose state representations over raw images for sim-to-real transfer of corrective/residual policies
claims.conditions: sim-trained, zero-shot real-world transfer

title: SA-VLA: State-aware tokenizer for improving Vision-Language-Action Models' performance

claims.claim: Conditioning discrete (VQ-based) action-token decoding on the robot's current proprioceptive state (via cross-attention, or a lightweight state adapter predicting action-wise modulation factors) improves average success rate from 0.29 to 0.56 over the strongest tokenizer baseline on 12 RoboTwin manipulation tasks, and from 0.15 to 0.33 over the strongest baseline in zero-shot sim-to-real on three real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors state-conditioned discrete action tokenization over fixed action-token-to-continuous-action mappings for VQ/discrete-token action heads
claims.conditions: LLM-based VLA policy; 12 simulated RoboTwin tasks plus 3 real-world zero-shot sim-to-real tasks

title: Robot Few-Shot Manipulation Skills Learning Based on Meta Imitation Learning and Mixture of Experts Model

claims.claim: A coarse-to-fine framework combining Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (fast adaptation from limited demonstrations) with an attention-based mixture-of-experts gating mechanism consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in few-shot learning and multi-task generalization (e.g., stacking, pouring) on a real Franka Emika Panda
claims.direction: favors meta-learning combined with mixture-of-experts for rapid adaptation with limited demonstrations over standard single-model imitation learning
claims.conditions: real Franka Panda robot, few-shot demonstrations (exact count not given in abstract), simulation and real-world experiments

title: Tube Diffusion Policy: Reactive Visual-Tactile Policy Learning for Contact-rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Standard action-chunking imitation-learning policies fundamentally limit reactivity to unforeseen observations during chunk execution; Tube Diffusion Policy instead learns an observation-conditioned feedback flow around nominal action chunks (an 'action tube') enabling fast, adaptive step-wise correction during execution, and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imitation-learning baselines on Push-T plus three visual-tactile dexterous manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors adding step-wise reactive correction within/around action chunks rather than pure open-loop chunk execution
claims.conditions: Push-T sim benchmark plus real-world visual-tactile manipulation tasks with contact uncertainty and external disturbances

claims.claim: The step-wise correction mechanism enabled by the action tube significantly reduces the number of denoising steps required, making the policy better suited for real-time, high-frequency feedback control in contact-rich manipulation
claims.direction: favors architectures that reduce denoising steps for lower-latency, smoother real-time control, which would help reduce jerkiness at execution boundaries
claims.conditions: same real-world contact-rich tasks

why_deep_read: Directly targets our two hardest problems -- jerky motion at chunk boundaries and ~2s inference latency -- via a concrete tube/feedback mechanism; full text would clarify compute cost and how much latency reduction is achievable on comparable hardware.

title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Autoregressive normalizing flow (AR-NF) action policies provide exact likelihoods (enabling likelihood-based offline RL post-training) unlike diffusion/flow-matching policies which lack tractable likelihoods, but suffer sampling overhead; RoMAN-Flow addresses this with a sampling-free advantage-weighted likelihood objective plus distillation of the optimized AR-NF policy into a one-step action generator
claims.direction: favors distilling expressive-but-slow generative action heads (AR-NF, by extension relevant to diffusion/flow policies) into one-step generators for practical deployment
claims.conditions: multiple simulated manipulation benchmarks and real-world robotic platforms

claims.claim: The distilled one-step action generator substantially reduces inference latency while achieving competitive policy performance relative to the un-distilled autoregressive policy
claims.direction: favors one-step distillation of generative action heads for low-latency deployment
claims.conditions: real-world robotic platforms

title: Mantis: A Versatile Vision-Language-Action Model with Disentangled Visual Foresight

claims.claim: Disentangling visual-foresight (future-state) prediction from the VLA backbone via meta-queries and a diffusion-Transformer head (with the current visual state fed in via a residual connection) lets a simple next-state prediction objective implicitly capture latent actions and boost explicit action learning, without burdening the backbone and while preserving its language comprehension/reasoning via language supervision
claims.direction: favors a decoupled auxiliary future-frame-prediction objective over either directly predicting high-dimensional visual states in the main backbone or omitting such auxiliary objectives entirely
claims.conditions: pretrained on human manipulation videos, robot demonstrations, and image-text pairs; 96.7% success on LIBERO after fine-tuning; also evaluated in the real world

claims.claim: In real-world evaluations, Mantis outperforms pi_0.5 (a leading open-source VLA model), particularly in instruction-following, generalization to unseen instructions, and reasoning ability, while exhibiting high convergence speed
claims.direction: favors this disentangled-foresight VLA architecture over a standard leading VLA baseline
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, direct comparison against pi_0.5

why_deep_read: Directly addresses Q09 (auxiliary/world-model objectives), one of our explicit open questions, with a concrete real-world comparison to a leading VLA (pi_0.5) in the same lineage as our SmolVLA baseline; worth checking whether the disentangled-foresight trick is lightweight enough for an 8GB GPU.

title: Adaptive Diffusion Policy Optimization for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: An Adam-based adaptive-gradient fine-tuning framework (ADPO) for diffusion-based RL policies acquires better or comparable performance versus six popular diffusion-based RL baseline methods on standard robotic control tasks
claims.direction: favors adaptive-gradient optimization methods when fine-tuning diffusion action-head policies with RL
claims.conditions: standard robotic control benchmark tasks; RL fine-tuning setting rather than plain imitation learning; real-world status not stated in abstract

title: IMLE Policy: Fast and Sample Efficient Visuomotor Policy Learning via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation

claims.claim: IMLE Policy, a behavior-cloning approach based on Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation with a simple generator-based architecture, captures complex multi-modal action distributions using single-step action generation, outperforming single-step Flow Matching and matching/exceeding multi-step Diffusion Policy
claims.direction: favors IMLE-based single-step generative action heads over multi-step Diffusion Policy and over single-step Flow Matching for multi-modal human-demo distributions
claims.conditions: diverse manipulation tasks, both simulated and real-world

claims.claim: IMLE Policy requires 38% less data on average to match baseline performance on complex multi-modal behaviours, excelling specifically in low-data regimes with minimal demonstrations
claims.direction: favors IMLE Policy for sample efficiency under demonstration-count constraints
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation, low-data regime

claims.claim: IMLE Policy improves inference speed by 97.3% compared to Diffusion Policy due to single-step action generation
claims.direction: favors single-step generative action heads for low-latency inference
claims.conditions: same simulated/real-world tasks

why_deep_read: Extremely close match to our constraints: fewer demos needed, single-step generation addressing our ~2s inference latency, real-world validated, and direct comparison against Diffusion Policy and Flow Matching, two of the Q01 action-head options. Full paper would give exact demo counts, model size, and per-task success rates.

title: Dynamic Rank Adjustment in Diffusion Policies for Efficient and Flexible Training

claims.claim: DRIFT uses Singular Value Decomposition to dynamically adjust the trainable rank/parameter count of a diffusion policy during training, letting DRIFT-DAgger slide between an offline bootstrapping phase and an online interactive-imitation-learning phase; this achieves improved sample efficiency and faster training with minimal impact on model performance
claims.direction: favors dynamically-sized/parameter-efficient diffusion action heads over fixed large overparameterized diffusion policies, especially when online interactive training is needed
claims.conditions: diffusion-policy behavioral-cloning framework; real-world status not stated in abstract

title: DeFM: Learning Foundation Representations from Depth for Robotics

claims.claim: DeFM is a self-supervised depth-only foundation model trained with a DINO-style self-distillation objective on 60M depth images; it can be distilled into compact models suitable for resource-constrained robotic systems and adopted off-the-shelf without task-specific fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors a dedicated pretrained depth encoder (DINO-style self-distillation on depth) as an alternative/complement to RGB-pretrained encoders (DINOv2, SigLIP/CLIP, MAE, R3M, VC-1)
claims.conditions: self-supervised pretraining on 60M depth images; evaluated on depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks; sim-to-real generalization

claims.claim: A novel input normalization strategy retains metric awareness of depth across multiple scales, and the resulting representation achieves state-of-the-art performance and strong sim-to-real generalization on manipulation (among other) benchmarks
claims.direction: favors using depth as a first-class modality with dedicated representation learning rather than RGB-only, when depth sensing is available
claims.conditions: depth-only input; multiple robotic benchmark domains including manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly informs Q03/Q04 for our RealSense setup: a depth-specific pretrained encoder explicitly distilled for resource-constrained systems could be a drop-in replacement/complement to our vision encoder given our 8GB GPU limit; want to check compact-model sizes and whether real low-cost-arm manipulation results are reported.

title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Q2RL extracts a Q-function from a BC policy using only a few interaction steps, then gates between BC and RL actions by Q-value for online sample collection; on-robot it learns robust policies for contact-rich, high-precision tasks (pipe assembly, kitting) in 1-2 hours of online interaction, achieving success rates up to 100% and up to 3.75x improvement over the original BC policy
claims.direction: favors augmenting a BC policy trained from demonstrations with a small amount of on-robot online RL refinement, rather than relying on BC alone
claims.conditions: real on-robot RL setting, D4RL/robomimic benchmarks plus real contact-rich precision tasks, only a few hours of online interaction needed

title: Embodied.cpp: A Portable Inference Runtime of Embodied AI Models on Heterogeneous Robots

claims.claim: A portable C++ inference runtime (batch-1, latency-first, multi-rate execution designed for closed-loop control) achieves 1.05x-2.70x inference speedups and 7%-77% lower VRAM usage relative to Python baselines across three VLA models and two world-action models, while maintaining near-baseline task success/control quality
claims.direction: favors runtime-level engineering (C++ inference stack, batch-1 latency-first execution, quantization) as a way to cut inference latency and VRAM footprint for real-time closed-loop control on constrained hardware, independent of model architecture changes
claims.conditions: evaluated across 3 VLA models and 2 world-action models on heterogeneous edge devices; normalized Python vs C++ quantization comparisons

title: SynthDemo-RL: Breaking the Zero-Reward Barrier in VLA Adaptation with LLM-Guided Synthetic Demonstrations

claims.claim: An automated teacher converts simulator-privileged state into successful manipulation trajectories (synthetic demonstrations); a VLA student distilled from these via SFT then refined with PPO reaches 96.0% success on standard LIBERO with NO human demonstrations, within 1.7 points of pi_0.5 trained on 50 human demonstrations per task; with 50 synthesized trajectories per task (no new human demos) it rescues all 27 LIBERO-PRO tasks that scored 0% for a pi_0.5 policy fine-tuned on original LIBERO tasks, reaching 97.8%/97.1% average success
claims.direction: favors LLM/simulator-guided synthetic demonstrations as a substitute or supplement for costly human teleoperation demonstrations
claims.conditions: LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO (perturbed) benchmarks, RoboTwin 2.0; trajectories from a MuJoCo-twin-trained policy verified to execute open-loop on a physical robot

claims.claim: Direct PPO fine-tuning from a pi_0.5 policy under the same RL compute as SynthDemo-RL's refinement stage only rescues 10 of 27 zero-success tasks (leaving 17 at 0%), whereas adding 50 synthesized demonstrations per task rescues all 27
claims.direction: favors combining synthetic demonstration distillation with RL over RL-with-sparse-reward alone when real demonstrations/rewards are scarce or a policy scores 0% on some tasks
claims.conditions: same LIBERO-PRO benchmark and compute budget

why_deep_read: Directly bears on Q05/Q13: whether synthetic/simulator-generated demonstrations can substitute for additional costly human teleop demos, with concrete success-rate numbers nearly matching a policy trained on 50 real human demos, and physical-robot open-loop validation from a MuJoCo twin.

title: Universal Manipulation Interface: In-The-Wild Robot Teaching Without In-The-Wild Robots

claims.claim: UMI's policy interface uses a relative-trajectory action representation (rather than absolute), which the authors identify as a key design choice enabling hardware-agnostic, deployable policies
claims.direction: favors relative/delta trajectory action representations over absolute-pose action spaces for cross-embodiment, deployable manipulation policies
claims.conditions: hand-held gripper data collection, deployed across multiple real robot platforms

claims.claim: UMI incorporates inference-time latency matching in its policy interface as part of achieving deployable, smooth real-world execution
claims.direction: favors explicitly matching/compensating for inference latency at deployment time rather than ignoring it
claims.conditions: real-world deployment across robot platforms

claims.claim: Policies learned via UMI from diverse in-the-wild human demonstrations (collected with hand-held grippers) zero-shot generalize to novel environments and objects, and unlock dynamic, bimanual, precise, and long-horizon behaviors by only changing training data per task
claims.direction: favors diverse, portable, in-the-wild human demonstration collection (rather than only in-lab robot teleop) for improving generalization to novel objects/environments
claims.conditions: comprehensive real-world experiments across multiple tasks and robot platforms

why_deep_read: Foundational, highly-cited paper directly covering three of our decisions (action space, latency handling, generalization from diverse demo collection); full text would give concrete data-collection and action-representation details transferable to our SO-101 teleop setup.

title: SPIN: distilling Skill-RRT for long-horizon prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation

claims.claim: Distilling a computationally-intensive skill-chaining planner (Skill-RRT plus goal-conditioned 'connector' policies) into a single imitation-learned policy, trained entirely in simulation, transfers zero-shot to the real world and achieves over 80% success across three challenging long-horizon manipulation tasks, outperforming SOTA hierarchical RL and planning methods
claims.direction: favors distilling planner-generated demonstrations into an imitation-learning policy over training hierarchical RL/planning methods directly
claims.conditions: trained entirely in simulation, zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, long-horizon prehensile+non-prehensile tasks

claims.claim: High-quality demonstrations are generated by the planner (Skill-RRT) and distilled through noise-based replay to reduce online computation time, rather than relying on human teleoperation demonstrations
claims.direction: favors planner-generated synthetic demonstrations as a data source over human teleoperation for long-horizon skill chaining
claims.conditions: simulation-generated demonstrations, zero-shot real-world transfer

title: RoboScape-R: Unified Reward-Observation World Models for Generalizable Robotics Training via RL

claims.claim: A world model can serve as a general-purpose environment/reward proxy by generating 'endogenous' rewards derived from its intrinsic understanding of state-transition dynamics, rather than relying on task-specific handcrafted reward functions
claims.direction: favors using a learned world model as an auxiliary/reward-generation objective to improve policy generalization, versus pure imitation learning (which overfits to expert trajectories) or RL with handcrafted rewards
claims.conditions: RL training paradigm; evaluated for generalization to out-of-domain scenarios

claims.claim: RoboScape-R achieves an average 37.5% performance improvement over baselines under out-of-domain scenarios
claims.direction: favors world-model-based training for improving out-of-domain generalization
claims.conditions: out-of-domain evaluation scenarios; real-world status not stated in abstract

title: Physical Reasoning VLA Models for Enhancing Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding an auxiliary physics-reasoning objective -- predicting pixel-level contact points and contact forces via learnable physics queries before generating actions, combined with a hybrid attention scheme (full attention over image/language/proprioception, causal attention over physics-query/action tokens) -- improves average success rate over a vanilla pi0 baseline from 36.2% to 43.6%
claims.direction: favors adding explicit physics/contact-prediction auxiliary objectives to a VLA policy over mapping observations directly to actions
claims.conditions: RoboCasa simulation benchmark, compared against vanilla pi0 baseline

title: SymVD: Symmetric Vision Language Action Distillation for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Distilling a large VLA teacher into a compact student policy while explicitly exploiting geometric symmetries (rotational/reflectional invariance) via an equivariant actor-critic architecture and symmetry-aware objective improves sample efficiency during distillation over standard distillation
claims.direction: favors symmetry-aware distillation to a compact student model over standard (non-equivariant) distillation for reducing model size while preserving performance
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation tasks; simulation (real-world status not stated in abstract)

claims.claim: SymVD outperforms standard distillation and SAC in generalization to previously unseen symmetric transformations of the environment (e.g., rotations/reflections)
claims.direction: favors building in geometric symmetry awareness for robustness to spatial transformations
claims.conditions: same manipulation tasks

title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning

claims.claim: Given only a language instruction and a short demonstration video (no target-task action labels, no test-time optimization/fine-tuning), WIZARD predicts task-specific LoRA adaptation weights for a frozen VLA in a single forward pass, improving performance by up to ~2x on unseen dataset collections and up to ~14x on unseen tasks on LIBERO
claims.direction: favors weight-space meta-learning (generating LoRA adapters from a demo video) over per-task fine-tuning with action-labeled demonstrations, for fast adaptation to new tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark; also tested on a real Franka Emika Panda where it consistently improves over a real-domain adapted baseline

claims.claim: WIZARD sidesteps task-specific fine-tuning by generating compact LoRA parameters rather than updating the full frozen VLA backbone
claims.direction: favors small, generated parameter-efficient adapters over full-model fine-tuning for new-task specialization
claims.conditions: frozen VLA policy, LoRA-based adaptation

title: Steering Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Policies via Action Token Intervention

claims.claim: Token Steering injects low-dimensional user inputs directly into an autoregressive VLA's native action-token representation at inference time (no retraining/fine-tuning), improving success rates on two household manipulation tasks from 10.0% to 72.5% and from 16.7% to 93.8% respectively, while preserving the dexterity/smoothness/task priors of the pretrained policy
claims.direction: favors discrete/autoregressive action-token representations that support direct inference-time intervention as a lightweight mechanism for correcting or steering behavior, over continuous action heads that lack such an interface
claims.conditions: real household manipulation tasks (drawer closing after object placement; state-aware object swapping), autoregressive VLA backbone

title: Reinforced Planning with Latent World Models

claims.claim: A learned neural planner (RP1) that is trained fully offline from imagined world-model rollouts to both evaluate (critic) and iteratively improve multi-step plans substantially outperforms hand-designed search algorithms across visual navigation, arm reaching, and robotic manipulation, reaching near-perfect success in several settings while using 1,000x fewer world-model rollouts and up to 67x faster inference than the strongest alternative
claims.direction: favors learning the planning/search procedure itself on top of a pretrained latent world model, rather than using hand-designed search, when a world model is available as an auxiliary component
claims.conditions: two different world-model backbones; visual navigation, arm reaching, and manipulation tasks (sim, based on description)

title: StereoPatch: Patch-Aligned RGB-Depth Fusion for Spatial Perception in Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Binding registered metric depth directly to RGB patches (via asymmetric cross-attention producing 'StereoPatch Tokens') before action decoding achieves higher closed-loop success than appearance-only (RGB-only), geometry-only (depth-only), raw RGB-D concatenation, and late-fusion baselines across six real-robot tasks
claims.direction: favors patch-aligned early fusion of depth with RGB features over RGB-only, depth-only, raw RGB-D stacking, or late fusion, for resolving control-relevant geometric ambiguity (e.g., object height, contact geometry) that pretrained RGB features alone cannot disambiguate from limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: six real-robot manipulation tasks; additional simulation experiments testing compatibility across different visuomotor policy architectures and spatial generalization

why_deep_read: Directly answers Q04 for our exact sensor setup (fixed RealSense with RGB+depth): a controlled real-robot ablation comparing RGB-only, depth-only, raw RGB-D, late-fusion, and their patch-aligned fusion. Full text would give the actual success-rate numbers and whether the fusion module is cheap enough to add to a small backbone on our GPU.

title: Learning Efficient and Robust Language-Conditioned Manipulation Using Textual-Visual Relevancy and Equivariant Language Mapping

claims.claim: GEM (Grounded Equivariant Manipulation), which combines pretrained vision-language models with equivariant language mapping, achieves similar or higher performance with orders of magnitude fewer robot demonstrations compared with major data-efficient baselines such as CLIPort and VIMA
claims.direction: favors equivariant language-grounded architectures for large gains in demonstration/data efficiency over standard language-conditioned imitation baselines
claims.conditions: diverse tasks in both simulation and the real world

claims.claim: GEM demonstrates greater robustness than a large VLA model (OpenVLA) at correctly interpreting natural language commands on unseen objects and unseen poses
claims.direction: favors this equivariant, data-efficient architecture over large pretrained VLA models for robustness to novel objects/poses given limited data
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, unseen objects and poses

claims.claim: Textual-visual relevancy combined with equivariant language mapping is proposed as a way to make pretrained VLM-based language conditioning both efficient and robust, addressing the fragility of large pretrained methods to unseen scenarios
claims.direction: favors structured/equivariant language-vision grounding over naive language conditioning for robustness and efficiency
claims.conditions: language-conditioned manipulation, sim and real

why_deep_read: Directly matches our failure modes: robustness to a 'different-looking' object and needing far fewer demonstrations for language-conditioned tasks; worth checking if the equivariant-mapping technique is lightweight enough to retrofit onto a small policy for our second-object/language extension.

title: ARCADE: Scalable Demonstration Collection and Generation via Augmented Reality for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: ARCADE automatically generates additional synthetic demonstrations from a single human-derived demonstration (via AR-based collection), significantly reducing user effort and time needed to reach a sufficient number of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors augmenting/generating synthetic demonstrations from a small set of real demonstrations rather than collecting all data manually via teleoperation
claims.conditions: real Fetch robot, three tasks (3-Waypoints-Reach, Push, Pick-And-Place) plus a household Pouring-Water task

claims.claim: A policy trained using vanilla Behavioral Cloning on ARCADE-collected/generated data excelled across three robotics tasks and achieved an 80% success rate on a real household pouring-water task
claims.direction: favors AR-based, user-friendly demonstration collection combined with synthetic demonstration generation as a practical way to reach sufficient data quantity for BC
claims.conditions: real Fetch robot, vanilla BC training

title: DSPv2: Improved Dense Policy for Effective and Generalizable Whole-body Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: An encoding scheme that aligns 3D spatial features with multi-view 2D semantic features (rather than using either alone) enables a policy to achieve broad generalization while retaining fine-grained perception for precise control, significantly outperforming existing approaches in both task performance and generalization
claims.direction: favors fusing 3D spatial representations with 2D semantic (RGB) features over using either 3D-only or 2D-only representations
claims.conditions: whole-body mobile manipulation, real-world/sim not specified explicitly in abstract

title: Masked Generative Policy for Robotic Control
