claims.claim: Representing actions as discrete tokens and training a conditional masked transformer that generates tokens in parallel then refines only low-confidence tokens (MGP) achieves both faster inference and higher success rates than state-of-the-art diffusion and autoregressive policies across 150 manipulation tasks (Meta-World and LIBERO), increasing average success rate by 9% while cutting per-sequence inference time by up to 35x
claims.direction: favors masked-generative discrete-token action heads over diffusion and autoregressive action heads for both accuracy and speed
claims.conditions: 150 tasks across Meta-World and LIBERO benchmarks (sim)

claims.claim: MGP-Long predicts full trajectories in a single pass and dynamically refines low-confidence action tokens based on new observations, enabling reliable control on complex non-Markovian tasks (where temporal consistency/history matters) that prior methods struggle with, and improves average success rate by 60% in dynamic and missing-observation environments
claims.direction: favors globally-coherent, observation-history-aware trajectory prediction with adaptive refinement over purely reactive or fixed-chunk policies for non-Markovian/partially-observed settings
claims.conditions: dynamic and missing-observation simulation environments, two non-Markovian scenarios where other SOTA methods fail entirely

claims.claim: MGP cuts per-sequence inference time by up to 35x compared to state-of-the-art diffusion and autoregressive policies while improving success rate
claims.direction: favors parallel masked-token generation with selective refinement for drastically reducing inference latency without sacrificing (in fact improving) accuracy
claims.conditions: same 150-task benchmark suite

why_deep_read: Directly and simultaneously addresses our three hardest problems -- action-head choice, ~2s latency, and missing-observation/history robustness -- with large quantified gains (9% success, 35x speedup, 60% success in degraded conditions) across 150 tasks; worth checking model size and whether it is trainable on an 8GB GPU.

title: A Skill-based Hierarchical Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Pre-training a generalizable skill repository from heterogeneous datasets via a conditional generative model, then refining skill selection with only a small number of task-specific demonstrations, significantly improves learning efficiency, task-complexity handling, and generalization to unseen tasks compared to existing baselines
claims.direction: favors pretraining a shared skill repository plus a small number of task-specific demos over training long-horizon policies from task-specific demos alone
claims.conditions: two long-horizon tasks (standard and distribution-mismatch); simulation (real-world status not stated)

title: DASIP: Dynamic Test-Time Compute Scaling for Robot Control with Stochastic Interpolant Policies

claims.claim: A difficulty classifier that dynamically selects the integration-step budget, solver variant, and ODE/SDE mode at each control cycle (rather than using a fixed inference budget for every step regardless of task complexity) achieves a 2.6-4.4x reduction in total computation time while maintaining task success rates comparable to fixed maximum-computation baselines
claims.direction: favors adaptive, difficulty-aware test-time compute allocation over a fixed per-step inference budget for diffusion/flow-based action policies, to cut latency on easy subtasks without sacrificing performance on hard ones
claims.conditions: comprehensive benchmarks across diverse manipulation tasks; diffusion- and flow-based (stochastic interpolant) policies

claims.claim: The stochastic interpolant formulation provides a unified framework spanning diffusion- and flow-matching policies, allowing diverse training/inference configurations to be compared under one framework
claims.direction: treats diffusion and flow-matching as points on a shared interpolant spectrum rather than separate action-head choices
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Standard per-dimension, per-timestep binning schemes for discrete action tokenization typically perform poorly (fail completely) when learning dexterous skills from high-frequency robot data; a compression-based tokenization using the discrete cosine transform (FAST) enables autoregressive VLAs to be trained successfully on such highly dexterous, high-frequency tasks where standard discretization fails
claims.direction: favors frequency-domain (DCT-based) compression tokenization over naive per-timestep binning for discrete/autoregressive action heads, especially at high control frequencies
claims.conditions: released as FAST+, a universal tokenizer trained on 1M real robot action trajectories, usable as a black-box across diverse action spaces/control frequencies

claims.claim: When combined with the pi0 VLA and trained on 10k hours of robot data, FAST-based tokenization matches the performance of diffusion VLAs while reducing training time by up to 5x
claims.direction: favors discrete autoregressive tokenization (with proper compression) as a training-efficient alternative that can match diffusion-based action heads
claims.conditions: large-scale multi-embodiment training (10k hours)

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to Q01 and to our plan to possibly increase control frequency to 30fps: naive per-timestep discretization is reported to fail at high frequency, which is a concrete warning for our setup; full text would clarify at what frequency/precision this failure occurs and whether FAST is practical for a small model.

title: SimWeaver: Zero-Shot RGB Sim-to-Real for Deformable Manipulation

claims.claim: SimWeaver trains zero-shot RGB VLA policies purely on 200 simulated demonstrations per task (single-image asset generation, deterministic topology-aware trajectory synthesis, and ISP-aware photometric augmentation for sim-to-real), with no teleoperation and no per-task calibration, reaching above 80% per-task and 91% average real-world success across 5 diverse deformable-object tasks
claims.direction: favors synthetic/simulated demonstrations plus photometric augmentation as a full substitute for real teleoperated demonstrations, at roughly two orders of magnitude lower per-trajectory cost
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation across 5 deformable manipulation tasks including plastic-bag manipulation; zero-shot, no real-world fine-tuning

claims.claim: On silk grasping, the sim-trained policy reaches 100% success under visual distribution shifts where real-data-trained baselines drop to 9-70%
claims.direction: favors sim-trained policies with strong photometric/domain augmentation for robustness to visual distribution shift over policies trained on limited real data
claims.conditions: real-world visual distribution shift evaluation on silk grasping

why_deep_read: Directly targets our most painful failure mode (breaking under new lighting/appearance changes) with a concrete, large real-world robustness gap (100% vs 9-70% under visual shift) and a synthetic-data recipe; worth checking whether the sim/asset pipeline and augmentation recipe could be adapted cheaply to our pumpkin/tray task.

title: Reactive Motion Generation via Phase-Varying Neural Potential Functions

claims.claim: A dynamical-systems LfD framework (PNPF) that conditions a potential function on a phase variable estimated from state progression (rather than open-loop time) outperforms existing dynamical-system baselines on trajectories with self-intersections and demonstrates robust real-time performance under external disturbances
claims.direction: favors phase-conditioned dynamical-systems policies as an alternative action-generation paradigm to chunk-based neural-network action heads, particularly for reactive stability under disturbance
claims.conditions: point-to-point, periodic, and full 6D motion tasks; real-time robotic manipulation with external disturbances

claims.claim: Dynamical-systems methods for LfD provide stable, continuous policies from few demonstrations
claims.direction: favors dynamical-systems approaches for low-data regimes
claims.conditions: general LfD framing, not tied to a specific demo count in this abstract

title: ROG-Grasp: Root-Oriented Geometry for Robotic Grasping and Placement

claims.claim: A geometry-based grasping and placement framework using RGB-D root-orientation estimation (YOLO-based root detector plus point-cloud plane fitting) achieves more reliable and accurate grasp completion with faster execution than compared vision-language-action (VLA) policies on orientation-aware produce grasping
claims.direction: favors classical geometry-driven perception/control pipelines over learned VLA policies for orientation-constrained, well-structured grasp-and-place tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, tomatoes and onions, isolated and cluttered scenarios

claims.claim: RGB-D perception (root normal estimation from point-cloud plane fitting) is used to infer object orientation for stable grasp pose generation
claims.direction: favors using depth/point-cloud geometry for orientation estimation over RGB-only appearance-based methods
claims.conditions: real robot, agricultural produce

title: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robot Learning: A Dexterous Manipulation Study on Reactive Catching

claims.claim: Domain-Randomized Instance Set (DRIS), which represents and propagates a set of randomized dynamics instances simultaneously (rather than one randomized instance per episode as in conventional domain randomization), yields more robust policies and reduces the need for real-world fine-tuning even with a modest number of instances (e.g., 10), enabling reliable zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a highly disturbance-sensitive reactive catching task
claims.direction: favors richer, multi-instance domain randomization over conventional single-instance-per-episode domain randomization for sim-to-real robustness
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, dexterous reactive catching with a flat (non-stabilizing) end-effector plate, highly sensitive to noise

title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Converting discrete temporal observations into a coherent textual memory sequence with temporal logic, recursively updated by a high-level VLM using the previous memory as a contextual anchor, improves the success rate and robustness of VLA models on complex long-horizon tasks compared to policies conditioned only on current observations, which the authors note otherwise struggle to maintain temporal consistency and accumulate closed-loop errors
claims.direction: favors explicit, language-based memory/history representations over observation-only (memoryless) conditioning for long-horizon temporal consistency and error correction
claims.conditions: multiple simulation environments plus sim-to-real experiments on a real robotic platform; hierarchical high-level VLM + low-level VLA architecture

claims.claim: Decoupling a high-level VLM (semantic reasoning via a VQA-style training paradigm, updating language memory/subtask instructions) from a low-level VLA (precise continuous control conditioned on subtask instructions and visual observations) avoids weakening the VLM backbone's semantic representations through end-to-end action fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors hierarchical decoupling of high-level language reasoning from low-level continuous control rather than a single end-to-end language-conditioned action model
claims.conditions: same long-horizon sim/real setup

title: Temporal Consistency-Constrained Vision–Action Latent Space Alignment and Policy Optimization

claims.claim: TCVA-PO couples cross-modal latent increments from paired demonstrations with a policy-induced next-latent transition penalty (plus pointwise alignment, reconstruction, critic regression, advantage weighting, and a smoothness term), consistently improving task performance, latent consistency, and action smoothness over representative imitation and generative visuomotor baselines on six public robot manipulation datasets
claims.direction: favors explicitly aligning visual-state latent dynamics with action-induced latent transitions (and penalizing inconsistency) to improve action smoothness and reduce long-horizon error accumulation, versus policies that only optimize action generation without this alignment
claims.conditions: six public robot manipulation datasets, heterogeneous visual-control conditions

claims.claim: The framework's gains hold under noisy demonstration settings, improving long-horizon robustness compared to baselines
claims.direction: favors temporal-consistency-constrained training for robustness to noisy demonstrations
claims.conditions: same six-dataset evaluation, noisy-demonstration condition

title: Learning from Demonstration with Implicit Nonlinear Dynamics Models

claims.claim: A recurrent neural network layer incorporating a fixed nonlinear dynamical system (inspired by reservoir computing) for modelling temporal dynamics addresses compounding-error/drift in LfD and yields greater policy precision and robustness than a temporal ensemble of policy predictions and an Echo State Network baseline, on a handwriting-motion reproduction task
claims.direction: favors an internal recurrent-dynamics layer as an alternative to temporal ensembling for combating compounding execution errors/drift
claims.conditions: LASA Human Handwriting Dataset (2D trajectory reproduction, not robot manipulation); compared directly against temporal-ensemble and ESN baselines

claims.claim: The proposed layer generalizes to multiple dynamics regimes while maintaining competitive latency scores
claims.direction: favors recurrent/history-aware dynamics modelling that stays real-time competitive
claims.conditions: same handwriting task

claims.claim: The approach maintains competitive latency compared to baseline methods for combating compounding error
claims.direction: favors internal-dynamics-layer approaches that do not add significant inference latency
claims.conditions: same handwriting task

title: VFP: Variational Flow-Matching Policy for Multi-Modal Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Conventional flow-matching policies struggle with multi-modality, often collapsing to averaged/ambiguous behaviors; adding a variational latent prior for mode-aware generation, Kantorovich Optimal Transport for distribution alignment, and a Mixture-of-Experts decoder for mode specialization (VFP) achieves a 49% relative improvement in task success rate over standard flow-based baselines in simulation (41 tasks) and further outperforms them on 3 real-robot tasks
claims.direction: favors variational/mode-aware extensions to flow-matching action heads over standard (unimodal-collapsing) flow matching for capturing multi-modal human-demo behavior
claims.conditions: 41 simulated tasks plus 3 real-robot tasks

claims.claim: VFP maintains fast inference and a compact model size while achieving these gains, via a Mixture-of-Experts decoder for efficient inference
claims.direction: favors MoE-based mode specialization for keeping model size/inference cost low despite added multi-modality handling
claims.conditions: same sim+real evaluation

title: Precise Mobile Manipulation of Small Everyday Objects

claims.claim: A closed-loop visual-servoing framework (VSVM) that uses vision foundation models to generate 3D targets (with out-painting to handle end-effector occlusion, open-vocabulary detectors for semantic targets, and point-tracking for user-clicked targets) obtains a 71% zero-shot success rate manipulating unseen small objects in novel real-world environments, outperforming an open-loop control method by 42 absolute percentage points AND outperforming an imitation-learning baseline trained on 1000+ demonstrations by 50 absolute percentage points
claims.direction: favors a classical closed-loop visual-servoing pipeline built on pretrained vision foundation models over a large-demonstration imitation-learning baseline, for precise small-object manipulation with strong zero-shot generalization
claims.conditions: large-scale real-world evaluation: 10 novel environments across 6 buildings, 72 different object instances

claims.claim: The vision-foundation-model-based servoing approach generalizes zero-shot to unseen objects and novel environments far better than an imitation-learning baseline that saw 1000+ demonstrations
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained vision foundation models plus classical closed-loop control for generalization over scaling up demonstration count for an end-to-end learned policy
claims.conditions: same large-scale real-world evaluation

title: Efficient On-policy Visual-RL via Stochastic Decoupled Policy Gradient

claims.claim: Stochastic Decoupled Policy Gradient (SDPG) estimates policy gradients via random perturbations of trajectory rollouts, requiring orders of magnitude fewer batch-rendered environments and training diverse visuomotor control policies end-to-end within a few hours on a single consumer GPU (RTX 4080), consistently outperforming baselines in training time, memory usage, and rewards on visual MuJoCo benchmarks
claims.direction: favors lightweight, low-compute visual-RL training methods that fit on a single consumer GPU over compute-heavy batch-rendered RL, when compute is constrained
claims.conditions: visual MuJoCo benchmarks (dexterous manipulation, locomotion); sim-to-real transfer demonstrated on physical hardware

title: Generalizable Geometric Prior and Recurrent Spiking Feature Learning for Humanoid Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A Recursive Adaptive Spiking Network that parameterizes robot-object interactions via recursive spiking for spatiotemporal consistency mitigates overfitting in sparse-demonstration scenarios, and a lightweight 2D geometric-inductive-bias module grounds high-level VLM reasoning for robust generalization to unseen environments; the combined method outperforms SOTA baselines across ManiSkill simulation and three heterogeneous real-world robotic systems (a custom humanoid, a desktop manipulator, and a commercial platform)
claims.direction: favors combining geometric inductive biases with recurrent/spiking temporal feature learning to improve data efficiency and generalization under sparse demonstrations
claims.conditions: ManiSkill sim plus 3 real-world platforms including a desktop-scale manipulator

title: VILAS: A VLA-Integrated Low-cost Architecture with Soft Grasping for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Three state-of-the-art VLA models (pi_0, pi_0.5, and GR00T N1.6), all fine-tuned from publicly released pretrained checkpoints on an identical demonstration dataset collected on the same low-cost platform, were deployed and evaluated on a real grape-grasping task, providing a direct comparison of deployment characteristics of current VLA models on low-cost hardware
claims.direction: provides a controlled, same-data, same-hardware comparison across multiple leading VLA architectures rather than a single-model result, useful for choosing among Q01 action-head/backbone options
claims.conditions: fully low-cost modular platform (Fairino FR5 arm, electric gripper, dual-camera perception), real-world grape-grasping task

claims.claim: A fully low-cost, modular manipulation platform with dual-camera perception and a kirigami-based soft compliant gripper (for safe fragile-object grasping without force sensing) is shown to be sufficient hardware for training and deploying capable VLA-based manipulation policies
claims.direction: favors that low-cost hardware (comparable in spirit to our SO-101 setup) is adequate for deploying modern VLA policies, provided appropriate gripper/compliance design
claims.conditions: low-cost arm + gripper + dual camera, real-world grape grasping

title: GPU-Parallel Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning with Demonstration Guided Policy Optimization

claims.claim: DGPO, an on-policy method combining importance-weighted PPO with adaptive behavior cloning on matched demonstration actions, outperforms both prior-free RL and existing demonstration-based methods under sparse success signals and limited prior data, while preserving on-policy PPO's stability and online-improvement benefits
claims.direction: favors combining a small set of demonstrations with on-policy RL (rather than pure demonstration-only BC or pure RL) when success signals are sparse and demo count is limited
claims.conditions: GPU-parallel multi-task RL benchmark (MT-LIBERO, Isaac Lab simulation); state-input or visual-input policies

title: Action Map Policy: Learning 3D Closed-loop Manipulation via Pixel Classification

claims.claim: Action Map Policy (AMP) casts 3D closed-loop manipulation as pixel-space classification by projecting 3D actions onto the camera image plane and treating each pixel location as a discrete class, controlling dimensionality while retaining multi-modality and supporting millimeter-level precision without a prohibitively large token vocabulary; AMP outperforms strong baselines in success rate, inference speed, and spatial reasoning
claims.direction: favors a pixel-classification action representation as an alternative discretization scheme to per-dimension binning or diffusion, for combining precision with tractable vocabulary size
claims.conditions: various manipulation tasks (sim/real not fully specified in abstract)

claims.claim: AMP predicts the entire action chunk in a single forward pass, avoiding complex noise scheduling and iterative denoising, achieving substantially faster inference than diffusion policies
claims.direction: favors single-forward-pass discrete action prediction over iterative-denoising diffusion policies for reducing inference latency
claims.conditions: same evaluation

claims.claim: Actions are represented by projecting 3D targets onto the camera image plane, tying the action representation directly to camera-frame pixel coordinates
claims.direction: favors camera-projected/pixel-anchored 3D action representations that keep visual and action spaces tightly coupled
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Geometry Conditioning in an Embodied SLM: Training Controls and Robustness Diagnostics in a 0.8B Hybrid Model

claims.claim: In robustness tests, a state-only relative-coordinate policy retained 7/10 success under frame relabeling, whereas all four tested visual policies fell to at most 3/20 success after only a 5 cm object displacement
claims.direction: favors relative-coordinate/state-based action conditioning over vision-only policies for robustness to small camera/object-position shifts, a specific and severe visual-policy fragility to spatial displacement
claims.conditions: 0.8B hybrid embodied small language model, 6.2M trainable parameters, three LIBERO-Spatial tasks, three seeds, 540 held-out rollouts

claims.claim: Conditioning recurrent decay gates on geometric increments yielded 28.9% success, versus 36.7% when those same increments were shuffled during training (i.e. training-time geometric alignment provided no reliable benefit and was in fact outperformed by the shuffled/uninformative control), versus 24.4% without explicit object/goal geometry; a token adapter using the same increments scored 27.8% (inconclusive across seeds), and token-clock conditioning scored only 11.1%
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that training-time geometric/positional conditioning reliably helps; the paper explicitly reports no reliable advantage from this geometric-alignment recipe
claims.conditions: same small hybrid SLM, LIBERO-Spatial, controlled ablation with matched evaluation-time correct geometry across conditions

claims.claim: These controlled comparisons were run on a very small model (0.8B total / 6.2M trainable parameters), showing that fine-grained architecture ablations are tractable and informative even at small scale
claims.direction: supports that meaningful conditioning ablations can be run cheaply at small model scale rather than only on large VLAs
claims.conditions: same 0.8B/6.2M-parameter model

claims.claim: The reported failure under a 5 cm object displacement is a direct analogue of camera/scene-shift sensitivity relevant to camera placement and viewpoint robustness
claims.direction: highlights that visual (image-conditioned) policies are highly sensitive to small spatial perturbations regardless of geometric conditioning tricks tried here
claims.conditions: same evaluation

why_deep_read: This is a rare small-scale (0.8B/6.2M param), tightly controlled ablation that directly reproduces our worst failure mode -- breaking after the camera/object moves slightly -- and reports a CONTRADICTS-common-practice finding that training-time geometric conditioning did not reliably help and was beaten by a shuffled control. Given our exact concern about camera-shift robustness and small model size, the full paper's training controls and diagnostics would be unusually directly transferable.

title: Learning Interactive Real-World Simulators

claims.claim: A universal simulator (UniSim) learned via generative modeling on diverse orchestrated datasets (rich in objects, actions, and movements) can be used to train both high-level vision-language policies and low-level RL policies purely in simulation, both deployable in the real world zero-shot after training purely in simulation
claims.direction: favors training an auxiliary/general world model as a training environment substitute, enabling zero-shot real-world deployment of policies trained purely on generated experience
claims.conditions: trained on diverse orchestrated internet/robotics/navigation datasets; zero-shot real-world deployment reported for resulting policies

title: Autoregressive Action Sequence Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Chunking Causal Transformer (CCT) extends causal transformers' single-token prediction to predict a variable number of tokens per step, supporting heterogeneous, high-frequency continuous action types (joint positions, 2D pixel coordinates, end-effector poses) in one hybrid action-sequence design; the resulting Autoregressive Policy (ARP) matches or outperforms environment-specific state-of-the-art on Push-T, ALOHA, and RLBench as a single universal architecture, while being more efficient in computation and parameter size
claims.direction: favors a chunked autoregressive action representation capable of mixing heterogeneous action types and chunk sizes, over architecture-specific/task-specific action heads
claims.conditions: evaluated across Push-T, ALOHA, and RLBench benchmarks

claims.claim: Predicting a variable number of tokens per step (rather than one token at a time as in standard language-style autoregression) enables robust performance across diverse control frequencies and fewer autoregression steps
claims.direction: favors variable-size chunked token prediction over single-token-per-step autoregression for handling different control frequencies efficiently
claims.conditions: same three benchmarks

claims.claim: ARP is more efficient in computation and parameter size than the environment-specific SOTA baselines it matches or beats
claims.direction: favors this universal, chunked-autoregressive architecture for parameter/compute efficiency
claims.conditions: same three benchmarks

title: Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization

claims.claim: DPPO, a policy-gradient RL fine-tuning framework for diffusion-based policies, achieves the strongest overall performance and efficiency for fine-tuning compared to other RL methods for diffusion policies and to policy-gradient fine-tuning of other (non-diffusion) policy parameterizations, exploiting synergies between RL fine-tuning and the diffusion parameterization for structured on-manifold exploration, stable training, and strong policy robustness; it is demonstrated via zero-shot deployment of simulation-trained policies on real robot hardware in a long-horizon, multi-stage manipulation task
claims.direction: favors diffusion-parameterized policies as especially amenable to RL post-training/fine-tuning (contrary to prior conjecture that they would be less efficient for policy-gradient RL), for improving robustness beyond pure behavior cloning
claims.conditions: common benchmarks, simulated robotic tasks with pixel observations, real hardware zero-shot deployment for a long-horizon multi-stage task

title: Multi-Task Policy Learning with Key Region Extraction for Visual Understanding

claims.claim: Incorporating image keypoint extraction and segmentation of critical/key regions within high-dimensional multimodal observations (on top of a transformer-based offline-IL architecture) facilitates faster and more efficient processing, achieving 82% success across 30 MetaWorld multi-task scenarios in simulation
claims.direction: favors key-region/keypoint-focused visual attention mechanisms over processing full raw high-dimensional observations uniformly
claims.conditions: simulation, 30 multi-task scenarios (MetaWorld)

claims.claim: With approximately 20 expert demonstrations collected per real-world scenario (across 8 distinct real scenarios), the method achieved real-world success rates of 50%-70%, notable improvements over other algorithms
claims.direction: favors that ~20 demonstrations per task/scenario can yield workable (though not high) real-world success rates with an efficient key-region visual architecture
claims.conditions: real-world robotic arm, 8 distinct scenarios, ~20 demos/scenario

title: FOCA: Future-Oriented Conditioning for Data-Efficient Vision-Language-Action Adaptation

claims.claim: A systematic stress test shows state-of-the-art VLA models' performance degrades sharply as the number of demonstrations is reduced, revealing a key weakness of existing few-shot adaptation strategies; FOCA achieves 95.7% success with only 20 demonstrations on LIBERO, improves 7-12% on RoboCasa, and delivers up to 26% absolute success-rate gains on real robots
claims.direction: favors future-oriented conditioning methods specifically designed for data-efficient adaptation over standard VLA fine-tuning when demonstration counts are low (e.g., ~20)
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboCasa sim benchmarks plus real-robot evaluation; few-shot regime (as low as 20 demonstrations)

claims.claim: FOCA combines explicit prediction of task-grounded future interaction embeddings with implicit alignment to future goal observations, enabling long-horizon reasoning in latent space without pixel-level prediction, interpretable as learning a future-conditioned value-like representation
claims.direction: favors latent (non-pixel) future-prediction auxiliary objectives over either no auxiliary objective or full pixel-level future-frame prediction
claims.conditions: same LIBERO/RoboCasa/real-robot evaluation

claims.claim: The future-oriented conditioning formulation naturally supports action-free co-training with synthetic videos generated by video world models
claims.direction: favors co-training with generated/synthetic video data (not requiring paired actions) to supplement limited real demonstrations
claims.conditions: same evaluation setup

why_deep_read: Directly documents and addresses our central problem -- a SmolVLA-style fine-tune that is brittle and data-hungry -- with a systematic few-shot stress test and concrete real-robot gains (up to 26% absolute) at a demo count (20) close to ours; worth checking exact model size/compute and whether the future-conditioning module is cheap enough for our 8GB GPU.

title: SABER: A Scalable Action-Based Embodied Dataset for Real-World VLA Adaptation

claims.claim: A large corpus of natural (non-teleoperated) egocentric and exocentric human activity footage from a novel domain, retargeted into robot-relevant action representations (latent actions, dexterous hand-pose trajectories, whole-body motion), can be used for multi-task post-training of a VLA (GR00T N1.6), yielding a mean success rate of 29.3% across ten domain tasks vs. 13.4% for fine-tuning baselines (a 2.19x improvement)
claims.direction: favors sourcing large-scale non-teleoperated human demonstration data (retargeted to robot action spaces) to fill domain gaps, over relying solely on scarce in-domain teleoperated data
claims.conditions: real-world retail manipulation domain, 44.8K training samples, applied via shared-backbone multi-task post-training

title: Behavior Cloning for Active Perception with Low-Resolution Egocentric Vision

claims.claim: On a low-cost robot arm with a wrist-mounted egocentric RGB camera performing a structured object-finding/repositioning task, predicting relative joint deltas substantially outperforms predicting absolute joint positions under closed-loop control from low-resolution RGB images
claims.direction: favors delta/relative joint-position action representations over absolute joint-position prediction
claims.conditions: real low-cost robot arm, wrist-mounted egocentric camera, low-resolution RGB, closed-loop control, behavior cloning

claims.claim: Low-resolution egocentric (wrist-camera) vision is sufficient for reliable completion of an active-perception task requiring the robot to reposition to center a partially visible object before grasping
claims.direction: favors that a wrist camera alone, even at low resolution, can support active perception/repositioning behavior via behavior cloning, without necessarily requiring high-resolution or additional views
claims.conditions: same low-cost arm setup

why_deep_read: About as close to our exact hardware and decision as evidence gets: a low-cost arm, wrist camera, behavior cloning, and a direct head-to-head of delta vs. absolute joint actions (our Q02) plus a resolution-sufficiency finding relevant to our 640x480 wrist camera. Full text would give the resolution/action-space numbers directly transferable to SO-101.

title: AtomEgo: Exploring Ego-Robot Integration for Embodied Foundation Model Pretraining

claims.claim: Across VLA and world-action-model architectures and three co-training paradigms (joint co-training with domain-specific action heads, progressive ego-to-robot embodiment-alignment transfer, and joint video-action modeling), evaluated via multi-task real-robot experiments, the authors find that egocentric human data can improve generalization, but its value depends on how well it is aligned and utilized ('Data Scale x Alignment Quality -> Capability Gain')
claims.direction: favors incorporating large-scale egocentric human video into pretraining/co-training, but only when embodiment/action alignment quality is high; naive scale alone is insufficient
claims.conditions: ~2,659 hours curated ego-robot corpus, multi-task real-robot evaluation

title: Restoring Noisy Demonstration for Imitation Learning With Diffusion Models

claims.claim: A filter-and-restore framework that first filters clean samples from expert demonstrations and then learns conditional diffusion models to recover/denoise the noisy ones consistently outperforms existing methods across robot arm manipulation, dexterous manipulation, and locomotion tasks, with ablations confirming robustness to different noise types and levels
claims.direction: favors explicitly detecting and diffusion-restoring noisy portions of a demonstration dataset, rather than training directly on raw (possibly noisy) demonstrations or discarding noisy demonstrations outright
claims.conditions: multiple domains (robot arm manipulation, dexterous manipulation, locomotion); imperfect demonstrations from human error or sensor/control inaccuracies, similar in spirit to teleoperation noise

title: Robust Robotic Grasping via Teacher-Student Learning and Informed Point Cloud Sampling

claims.claim: An informed point-cloud sampling method (inspired by selective gaze) using a Teacher-Student framework with an auxiliary distance-estimation head identifies object-centric regions and prioritizes task-relevant point-cloud regions, achieving performance comparable to baseline methods while using significantly reduced point-cloud density, improving computational efficiency and sim-to-real transfer robustness
claims.direction: favors object-centric, selectively-sampled point-cloud representations over uniformly-processed dense point clouds, for compute efficiency and reduced overfitting to scene-specific features
claims.conditions: real-world robotic grasping, sim-to-real transfer

title: Robotic Visual Instruction

claims.claim: Robotic Visual Instruction (RoVI) replaces or supplements natural-language conditioning with object-centric, hand-drawn 2D symbolic sketches (arrows, circles, colors, numbers) that a VLM interprets and converts (via keypoint extraction) into executable 3D action sequences, achieving an 87.5% success rate in real-world scenarios with unseen multi-step tasks, disturbances, and trajectory-following requirements
claims.direction: favors visual/sketch-based instruction conditioning over purely natural-language conditioning for precise spatial-temporal task specification
claims.conditions: 11 novel tasks in real and simulated environments; small VLMs fine-tuned on a curated 15K-instance dataset for edge deployment

claims.claim: Small VLMs can be fine-tuned specifically for edge deployment to effectively learn RoVI (sketch-instruction) capabilities
claims.direction: favors that this instruction-following capability does not require a very large VLM and can run on edge-class compute
claims.conditions: same evaluation, edge-deployment-targeted small VLMs

claims.claim: VIEW (the RoVI-conditioned policy pipeline) demonstrates significant generalization capability to unseen tasks, including under physical disturbances
claims.direction: favors sketch/visual-instruction-conditioned policies for robustness to disturbances and generalization to novel task variations
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation with disturbances

title: CommitFlow: Semantic Commitment Verification and Local Correction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation VLA Execution

claims.claim: CommitFlow adds a closed-loop layer on top of a frozen base VLA policy: a Semantic Commitment Monitor holds back dependent actions when a required physical condition is unmet, a local correction module (BoundaryFlow) generates state/action-conditioned corrections, and a calibration module selects the smallest sufficient correction; on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark (10 tasks) this improves the base policy pi0.5's mean success rate by 22.7 percentage points (to 75.9%), with consistent gains when applied to other base policies
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight, frozen-base-policy correction/monitoring layer to catch and fix local execution deviations, rather than relying on the base policy alone for long-horizon reliability
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, 10 common long-horizon tasks, applied across multiple base VLA policies including pi0.5

claims.claim: Correction strength is calibrated to the smallest value satisfying task constraints, aiming to avoid unnecessary intervention/jerkiness while still correcting mismatches between semantic commitments and physical state
claims.direction: favors minimal, calibrated local corrections over larger uncontrolled interventions for maintaining smooth, reliable closed-loop execution
claims.conditions: same RoboTwin 2.0 evaluation

title: Non-Markovian Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Keyframe Chaining

claims.claim: Standard VLA models rely heavily on immediate observations and struggle to capture Non-Markovian dependencies (where optimal actions depend on specific past states rather than the current observation); Keyframe-Chaining VLA addresses this with an automatic keyframe selector plus a progress-aware query mechanism that retrieves historically-relevant frames and integrates them as interleaved visual tokens, achieving superior performance on a purpose-built suite of four Non-Markovian manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit, selectively-retrieved historical-frame conditioning (rather than only current observation or naive extended context windows) for tasks with non-Markovian/long-horizon temporal dependencies
claims.conditions: ManiSkill-simulator-based benchmark, four purpose-built Non-Markovian tasks; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: DSSP: Diffusion State Space Policy with Full-History Encoding

claims.claim: A history encoder based on State Space Models (SSMs) compresses the entire observation stream (not just current/recent observations) into a compact context representation, optimized with a dynamics-aware auxiliary objective, and fused with recent observations for hierarchical conditioning; this achieves state-of-the-art performance on simulation and real-world manipulation, with superior efficiency in capturing crucial information as history length increases
claims.direction: favors full-history (SSM-compressed) conditioning over short-window or current-observation-only conditioning for resolving history-dependent ambiguities in long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Instantiating the diffusion backbone itself as an SSM (rather than a Transformer/U-Net) maintains architectural consistency and minimizes GPU memory overhead while achieving SOTA performance
claims.direction: favors SSM-based diffusion backbones over standard diffusion architectures for memory-efficient long-context action generation
claims.conditions: same evaluation

claims.claim: DSSP achieves SOTA performance with a significantly smaller model size than compared baselines
claims.direction: favors this SSM-based history-conditioned architecture for achieving strong performance at reduced parameter count
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: HiMe: Hierarchical Embodied Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Control

claims.claim: Decoupling embodied intelligence into a high-frequency Executor, a working-memory Sentry, and a long-term-strategy Planner, with a dynamic knowledge system supporting Add/Update/Delete memory operations, significantly improves success rates on long-horizon non-Markovian tasks versus flat memory baselines
claims.direction: favors hierarchical, actively-managed memory architectures over flat/undifferentiated memory for long-horizon reasoning
claims.conditions: described as addressing a 'frequency-competence paradox'; specific benchmark/real-world details not given in abstract

claims.claim: The hierarchical decoupling is explicitly designed to balance real-time execution speed against slower deliberate planning/reasoning, resolving a tradeoff where fast models lack reasoning and reasoning models are too slow for real-time control
claims.direction: favors separating a fast low-latency executor from a slower reasoning/planning component rather than using one monolithic model for both
claims.conditions: same framework

title: Cross-View Action Consistency for Camera-Robust Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: For flow-based VLAs, regularizing the action-flow velocity field with a cross-view consistency loss (supervising action-equivalent nominal/perturbed scene-camera view pairs reset to the same simulator state, flow-matched, and encouraged to agree at matched flow coordinates) improves camera-perturbation robustness on LIBERO-Plus from 79.8+/-0.8% (flow-matching-only, same paired data) to 87.2+/-0.4% (+7.4pp), and +12.5pp over naive mixed-camera supervised fine-tuning, while maintaining nominal-camera in-distribution performance (95.0%); a shuffled-pair control collapses to 25.8%, confirming the gain specifically depends on action-equivalent pairing rather than just more camera diversity
claims.direction: favors explicit cross-view action-consistency regularization (using action-equivalent view pairs) over naive mixed-camera fine-tuning or flow-matching alone, for robustness to scene-camera viewpoint changes
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus camera-perturbation benchmark, flow-based VLA, only scene RGB+language+proprioception used (wrist stream masked, no camera labels/extrinsics/depth/point-cloud)

claims.claim: On a REAL ROBOT, evaluating three tabletop tasks with 10 rollouts per task and camera placement, held-out-camera (moved scene camera) success improved from 53.3% to 74.4% using this method, under the same single-scene-RGB inference interface
claims.direction: favors this camera-shift-robustness training technique specifically for scenarios with a single fixed scene camera whose position may shift between training and deployment
claims.conditions: real robot, 3 tabletop tasks, held-out (moved) camera placements

why_deep_read: This is a near-exact match to one of our two stated core failure modes -- the policy breaking when the scene camera is slightly moved -- with a rigorous ablation (shuffled-pair control) and REAL ROBOT numbers (53.3% to 74.4%) using only scene RGB + language + proprioception, exactly our sensor setup. Full text would give the training recipe and whether it is feasible to retrofit onto a SmolVLA-style fine-tune.

title: A Sim-to-Real Integration Pipeline for Training and Deployment of Chunk-Based VLA Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: An open-source protocol replays simulation-generated expert trajectories open-loop on a real Franka FR3 to record paired real visual/proprioceptive observations for VLA training, using the identical hardware configuration for both data collection and closed-loop evaluation, which the authors note directly measures and can reduce reliance on costly human-teleoperated data collection
claims.direction: favors sim-generated trajectories replayed on real hardware (rather than pure human teleoperation) as a demonstration source for chunk-based VLA training
claims.conditions: real Franka FR3 setup; end-effector-pose action-chunk VLA models

title: Learning Manipulation by Predicting Interaction

claims.claim: A pre-training objective (MPI) that, given a pair of initial/final keyframes and language instructions, predicts the transition frame and detects the interaction object achieves superior 'how-to-interact' and 'where-to-interact' representations, improving downstream manipulation performance by 10% to 64% compared with previous state-of-the-art on real-world robot platforms and simulation
claims.direction: favors auxiliary pretraining objectives centered on predicting interaction dynamics and interaction-object localization (not just static representation learning) for visual representations used in manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world robot platforms and simulation, multiple challenging manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Standard representation-learning approaches that leverage large-scale human video datasets but ignore interactive dynamics (behavior patterns, physical interaction) yield an inadequate understanding of object-environment relationships; incorporating interaction-prediction into pretraining substantially improves the resulting visual representation for manipulation
claims.direction: favors interaction-aware pretraining objectives over standard (non-interactive) visual representation pretraining from human video
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: L2D2: Robot Learning from 2D drawings

claims.claim: A sketching interface where humans draw and label trajectories on images (with vision-language segmentation autonomously varying object locations to generate synthetic images to draw upon, removing the need to physically reset the workspace) enables collecting more demonstrations with less time/effort than physical guidance; a user study found users preferred drawings and L2D2 learned more performant policies with a smaller dataset than other drawing-based approaches and generalized to longer-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors sketch-based demonstration interfaces combined with synthetic scene generation over physical kinesthetic teaching for collecting larger, more diverse demonstration sets with less human effort
claims.conditions: real robot arm and workspace, user study comparing to physical guidance and other drawing-based baselines

title: DexFlyWheel: A Scalable and Self-improving Data Generation Framework for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A closed-loop data flywheel combining imitation learning (extracting human-like behavior from seed demonstrations), residual reinforcement learning (enhancing generalization), rollout collection, and data augmentation across diverse simulated environments/spatial configurations iteratively self-improves and generates over 2,000 diverse demonstrations across four challenging tasks from a small seed set
claims.direction: favors an iterative IL+residual-RL+augmentation data-generation cycle over a fixed, manually-collected demonstration set, for scaling data diversity from limited real seed demonstrations
claims.conditions: seed demonstrations warmup, simulation-based iterative expansion

claims.claim: Policies trained on the flywheel-generated dataset achieve an average success rate of 81.9% on challenge test sets and, transferred to the real world via digital twin, 78.3% success on dual-arm lift tasks
claims.direction: favors this scalable synthetic-data-generation approach for reaching workable real-world success rates from a small number of seed demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world transfer via digital twin, dual-arm manipulation

title: Few-shot Sim2Real Based on High Fidelity Rendering with Force Feedback Teleoperation

claims.claim: Enhancing visual rendering realism in a simulation-based teleoperation data-collection pipeline substantially boosts downstream task performance while reducing the amount of real-world data needed for a few-shot sim-to-real visual-motor policy
claims.direction: favors investing in higher-fidelity simulation rendering for sim-collected demonstrations as a way to reduce real-world data requirements
claims.conditions: simulation-based teleoperation data collection, few-shot sim-to-real transfer, various manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Integrating force feedback into the teleoperation system (providing end-effector gripping force feedback during simulated data collection) significantly improves both success rates and execution efficiency of the resulting policy, particularly in simulation
claims.direction: favors adding force/haptic feedback to teleoperation interfaces to improve demonstration quality for contact-related tasks
claims.conditions: simulation-based teleoperation data collection

title: Point Cloud Decomposition for Task-Oriented Grasping

claims.claim: ITSI, a geometry-based (non-learned) iterative point-cloud slicing method for segmenting graspable regions, dramatically increases the number of discoverable robot grasps by up to 44% compared to state-of-the-art (including deep-learning-based) task-oriented grasp synthesis methods, without requiring object-specific knowledge or annotated training data
claims.direction: favors classical geometric point-cloud decomposition over deep-learning-based or bounding-box-based grasp region segmentation, at least for discovering graspable regions without training data
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation experiments across diverse object datasets

title: Robot Learning from a Physical World Model

claims.claim: PhysWorld couples a video generation model (synthesizing task-conditioned videos from a single image and language command) with physical world reconstruction, then grounds the generated visual motions into physically accurate robot trajectories via object-centric residual reinforcement learning against the reconstructed physical world model, substantially improving manipulation accuracy compared to previous approaches that directly retarget pixel motions from generated video (which neglects physics)
claims.direction: favors grounding video-generation-based policies in an explicit reconstructed physical world model (via residual RL) rather than naively retargeting pixel motion, when using generative video as a training/guidance signal
claims.conditions: diverse real-world manipulation tasks, single image + language command input

claims.claim: This synergy eliminates the need for real robot data collection, enabling zero-shot generalizable robotic manipulation from generated video demonstrations alone
claims.direction: favors generated-video-driven training pipelines as a substitute for real teleoperated demonstration collection when paired with physics grounding
claims.conditions: zero-shot real-world deployment

title: APEX: Adaptive Policy Execution for Precise Manipulation

claims.claim: APEX, a plug-and-play framework inserted between an already-trained policy and its low-level controller (treating both as black boxes), reconstructs a dynamically feasible reference from policy outputs and adapts it at test-time using low-level state feedback (with a provable convergence guarantee); this reduces controller-induced tracking error by 41.2% on demonstration replay and improves manipulation success by 4.8-25.8 percentage points across four different visuomotor and VLA policy classes
claims.direction: favors adding a black-box, plug-and-play execution-adaptation layer to correct the mismatch between policy-commanded and controller-realized actions, rather than modifying the policy architecture or the low-level controller directly
claims.conditions: four visuomotor/VLA policy classes; does not require access to internals of the policy or controller

claims.claim: The execution gap between policy-commanded high-level action references and controller-realized actions is identified as a systematic source of error that is independent of the choice of action-head architecture, since it arises purely from the policy/controller interface
claims.direction: treats execution-gap correction as an orthogonal fix applicable regardless of the underlying action-head choice (diffusion, regression, etc.)
claims.conditions: same four-policy-class evaluation

title: Trace-Focused Diffusion Policy for Multi-Modal Action Disambiguation in Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning diffusion-based action generation on the robot's execution history, represented as an explicit execution trace projected into the visual observation space (rather than conditioning only on instantaneous observations), resolves multi-modal action ambiguity (MA2) where visually similar observations recur across execution stages but require distinct actions; TF-DP outperforms a vanilla diffusion policy by 80.56% on tasks exhibiting MA2
claims.direction: favors explicit execution-history/trace conditioning over instantaneous-observation-only conditioning for disambiguating actions in long-horizon tasks with recurring visual states
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation tasks with pronounced multi-modal action ambiguity

claims.claim: The trace-focused field emphasizes task-relevant regions associated with historical motion, improving robustness to background visual disturbances; TF-DP outperforms vanilla diffusion policy by 86.11% under visual disturbances/visually cluttered conditions
claims.direction: favors history-trace-guided attention to task-relevant regions for robustness to background clutter/visual disturbance
claims.conditions: real-world visually cluttered conditions

claims.claim: TF-DP maintains inference efficiency with only a 6.4% runtime increase over vanilla diffusion policy despite adding history-trace conditioning
claims.direction: favors execution-trace conditioning as a low-overhead way to improve temporal consistency without materially increasing inference latency
claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation

title: ReactVLA: Fast and Lightweight Reactive Robot Manipulation via Improved Mean Flow Action Generation

claims.claim: ReactVLA combines an improved Mean Flow (iMF) action generator, which reduces expensive multi-step diffusion sampling to one-to-few-step action generation, with Attention Residuals (AttnRes), a dynamic depth-wise feature-routing mechanism replacing uniform residual accumulation; it consistently outperforms similarly-sized VLA baselines INCLUDING SmolVLA and pi0 on LIBERO, RoboIMI, and real-world manipulation, achieving up to 1.65x task performance improvement on precision manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors one-to-few-step mean-flow action generation plus attention-residual feature routing over standard multi-step diffusion action heads, directly outperforming SmolVLA and pi0 as an alternative architecture at similar model size
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboIMI sim benchmarks plus real-world robotic manipulation tasks; compared directly against SmolVLA and pi0 baselines

claims.claim: ReactVLA provides more than a 4x increase in inference speed compared with leading VLA models and reduces real-world policy latency to below 38.6 ms, enabling fast reactive closed-loop control on physical robot platforms
claims.direction: favors few-step mean-flow action generation specifically to eliminate the inference-latency bottleneck of iterative diffusion sampling for reactive real-time control
claims.conditions: real-world robot platforms, direct latency measurement

why_deep_read: Directly benchmarks against our current baseline architecture family (SmolVLA and pi0) and reports both a performance win and a latency reduction to under 40ms -- essentially a drop-in answer to our two stated pain points (2s inference latency and precision). Full text would give the exact model size, training data requirements, and whether iMF is implementable/trainable on our 8GB laptop GPU.

title: Hierarchical Policy Learning via Spectral Decomposition

claims.claim: Analyzing action sequences via discrete cosine transform reveals that low-frequency components capture global motion trajectories while high-frequency components encode precise timing, alignment, and contact behaviors; the Causal Spectral Policy (CSP) models action generation as a causal coarse-to-fine process (coarse motion predicted from observation+language, then fine corrections conditioned on the realized trajectory), consistently outperforming strong baselines on precision-sensitive manipulation tasks in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors explicit coarse-to-fine spectral decomposition of the action generation process over generating actions at a single resolution/scale, for precision-sensitive tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world evaluations

claims.claim: Human-inspired teleoperation noise injection is proposed as a data augmentation method, under which CSP demonstrates strong robustness to noisy demonstrations
claims.direction: favors deliberately injecting teleoperation-realistic noise as an augmentation strategy to improve robustness to naturally noisy human demonstrations
claims.conditions: same evaluation, noisy-demonstration condition

claims.claim: CSP's robustness to noisy demonstrations is demonstrated via this augmentation approach, directly targeting demonstration-quality issues characteristic of human teleoperation
claims.direction: favors augmentation-based robustness to demonstration noise over assuming clean demonstrations
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Transferring Foundation Models for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning an end-to-end two-stream 2D imitation-learning policy on language-reasoning segmentation masks generated by internet-scale vision foundation models (in addition to raw images), incorporating semantic/geometric/temporal priors, enables sample-efficient generalization
claims.direction: favors conditioning policies on foundation-model-derived object masks (semantic segmentation priors) rather than raw RGB features alone
claims.conditions: real-world experiments on a Franka Emika robot AND a low-cost dual-arm robot

claims.claim: The mask-conditioned policy robustly perceives object pose and generalizes to new object instances, new semantic categories, and unseen backgrounds
claims.direction: favors mask/segmentation-based conditioning for robustness to novel objects and backgrounds, directly targeting the generalization failure modes of raw-pixel policies
claims.conditions: real-world experiments including a low-cost dual-arm robot platform

title: Diffusion policy: Visuomotor policy learning via action diffusion

claims.claim: Representing a visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process (Diffusion Policy) consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art robot learning methods across 15 tasks from 4 different manipulation benchmarks, with an average improvement of 46.9%, gracefully handling multimodal action distributions and high-dimensional action spaces while exhibiting strong training stability
claims.direction: favors diffusion-based action heads over prior (non-diffusion) SOTA methods for handling multimodal human-demonstration distributions and high-dimensional action spaces
claims.conditions: 4 manipulation benchmarks, 15 tasks total

claims.claim: Key technical contributions unlocking diffusion policies on physical robots include receding-horizon control, visual conditioning, and a time-series diffusion transformer
claims.direction: establishes receding-horizon action-chunk execution as a core enabling component for diffusion-based visuomotor policies
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: Bootstrapping Imitation Learning for Long-horizon Manipulation via Hierarchical Data Collection Space

claims.claim: Segmenting a fine manipulation task into multiple key atomic tasks and designing atomic state/action spaces for human demonstrations (Hierarchical Data Collection Space, HD-Space) -- rather than collecting more raw demonstrations or adding complex human-in-the-loop correction systems -- significantly enhances policy performance across two simulated and five real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks, allowing a small amount of demonstration data to train a more powerful policy
claims.direction: favors restructuring the data-collection state/action space around atomic subtasks over simply scaling up raw demonstration count, for long-horizon manipulation data quality
claims.conditions: 2 simulated + 5 real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks

title: AirExo-2: Scaling up Generalizable Robotic Imitation Learning with Low-Cost Exoskeletons

claims.claim: A policy (RISE-2) trained solely on adapted in-the-wild demonstrations collected with a low-cost exoskeleton (AirExo-2, converted to pseudo-robot demonstrations) achieves comparable performance to the same policy trained with teleoperated robot data
claims.direction: favors low-cost, in-the-wild exoskeleton demonstration collection as a viable substitute for costly robot teleoperation, at least for the tested policy/tasks
claims.conditions: in-domain and generalization evaluations; RISE-2 policy

claims.claim: RISE-2 fuses 3D spatial and 2D semantic perception for robust manipulation, outperforming prior SOTA methods on both in-domain and generalization evaluations
claims.direction: favors combining 3D spatial representations with 2D semantic features over either alone
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Fast ECoT: Efficient Embodied Chain-of-Thought via Thoughts Reuse

claims.claim: Caching/reusing high-level chain-of-thought reasoning across timesteps, parallelizing modular reasoning-step generation, and adding an asynchronous scheduler that decouples reasoning from action decoding, reduces VLA inference latency by up to 7.5% with comparable or improved task success rate and reasoning faithfulness, requiring no model changes or additional training and integrating easily into existing VLA pipelines
claims.direction: favors inference-time engineering (caching, parallelization, async reasoning/action decoupling) to reduce chain-of-thought-induced latency, as a drop-in addition rather than a new architecture or retraining
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation and real-world robot tasks; applies specifically to VLA models that use embodied chain-of-thought reasoning

title: CDF-Glove: A Cable-Driven Force Feedback Glove for Dexterous Teleoperation

claims.claim: Adding real-time haptic/force feedback to a low-cost (~US30) teleoperation glove yields a 4x improvement in task success rate relative to no-feedback teleoperation (200ms force-feedback latency, 0.4-degree distal joint repeatability); Diffusion Policy baselines trained on CDF-Glove teleoperated demonstrations increase average success rate by 55% and reduce mean completion time by about 47.2% relative to policies trained on kinesthetic-teaching demonstrations
claims.direction: favors incorporating force/haptic feedback into low-cost teleoperation interfaces to improve demonstration quality, and favors teleoperated demonstrations over kinesthetic teaching for downstream policy performance
claims.conditions: bimanual teleoperation datasets, Diffusion Policy training and evaluation, multiple robotic hands

title: Scalable Multi-Task Data Generation via Reinforcement Learning for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: An RL-based synthetic data-generation pipeline integrating generalizable reward design, domain randomization, and language-conditioned task annotations synthesizes diverse high-quality datasets that significantly improve generalization across three representative bimanual manipulation tasks, compared to human-teleoperation-based data generation which offers limited task diversity
claims.direction: favors RL-based synthetic data generation with domain randomization over teleoperation-based synthetic trajectory generation, for task diversity and downstream generalization
claims.conditions: simulation-based data generation for training language-conditioned multi-task policies

title: Visuomotor Robotic Pruning in Planar Orchards Using Hybrid Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A closed-loop visuomotor controller using optical-flow inputs from a single wrist-mounted camera (avoiding full 3D reconstruction) is sufficient to continuously guide a cutter through cluttered environments to a specified point with correct orientation, trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot in real orchards across 38 physical trials
claims.direction: favors optical-flow-based wrist-camera-only visual input as a lightweight alternative to full 3D reconstruction for close-range, contact-precision guidance tasks
claims.conditions: zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, real-world field and lab trials

claims.claim: The pipeline avoids the need for full 3D reconstruction by using optical flow, and the learned policy outperforms a classical RRT-Connect motion-planning baseline on physical hardware
claims.direction: favors 2D optical-flow representations over full 3D reconstruction for reactive close-range visuomotor guidance
claims.conditions: same real-world trials

title: RotVLA: Rotational Latent Action for Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Modeling latent actions as continuous elements of SO(n) (rather than via discrete quantization encode/decode pipelines used by prior Latent Action Models, which can lead to trivial frame reconstruction and limited representational capacity) provides continuity, compositionality, and structure aligned with real-world action dynamics; combined with a flow-matching action head that jointly denoises latent and robot actions, RotVLA (1.7B parameters, 1700+ hours of pretraining) achieves 98.2% on LIBERO and 89.6%/88.5% on RoboTwin2.0 (clean/randomized settings), consistently outperforming existing VLA models including in real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors continuous rotational (SO(n)) latent action representations over discrete VQ-style latent action tokens for cross-embodiment VLA pretraining
claims.conditions: large-scale cross-embodiment pretraining (1.7B params, 1700+ hours); LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0, and real-world manipulation

title: Design and Implementation of a Dual Arm Imitation Learning System for Fine Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: FCE-ACT extends the Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) with automatic way-point compression, kernel-based latent modeling, and channel-spatial visual attention, consistently outperforming standard ACT with higher success rates and more stable execution across five dual-arm manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors augmenting a chunking-transformer action head with way-point compression and visual attention over the base ACT architecture, for long-horizon stability and reduced error accumulation
claims.conditions: five dual-arm fine-manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Automatic way-point compression is used to improve long-horizon stability of the chunked action-generation process
claims.direction: favors compressing/selecting way-points within action chunks over using uncompressed dense chunks
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: PearlVLA: Progressive Embodied Action-Plan Refinement in Latent Space

claims.claim: Moving explicit deliberation into the latent space of a VLM (rather than through textual chains, pixel-level subgoals, or action search) and decoding a refined plan in parallel into an action chunk after K refinement rounds achieves state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO while avoiding the substantial latency/computational cost that explicit reasoning methods incur
claims.direction: favors latent-space iterative plan refinement over explicit (textual/pixel-level) reasoning chains, for combining deliberation quality with low-latency parallel action decoding
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark

claims.claim: A plan-conditioned world query probes a lightweight frozen latent world model for an action-free future-observation latent, which is fed back to guide iterative plan refinement, and the refinement process is optimized with rewards derived from longer-horizon imagined futures
claims.direction: favors using a frozen latent world model as an auxiliary future-prediction signal to guide action-plan refinement, rather than training a full future-observation predictor end-to-end
claims.conditions: same LIBERO evaluation

title: What Matters for Latent Actions in Robot Learning

claims.claim: The first comprehensive empirical study unifying representative Latent Action Model (LAM) methods within a common autoencoding framework, systematically investigating 41 design choices across three dimensions (latent action modeling paradigm, learning objectives/regularization, and integration strategy) and four proxy quality metrics, finds that fine-tuning VLM backbones with latent actions provides a stronger initialization for downstream policy learning than alternative integration strategies, validated on three benchmarks plus real-world robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors VLM-backbone fine-tuning with latent-action supervision as the strongest identified initialization strategy among 41 systematically compared latent-action design choices
claims.conditions: three widely-used benchmarks, with further validation on real-world robot manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: This is a rare systematic, large-scale ablation (41 design choices across three axes) specifically on latent/discrete action representation design for VLAs, directly informing our Q01 decision. Given how fragmented and inconsistent prior latent-action work is (per the abstract itself), the full paper's proxy-metric and design-choice tables would be unusually decision-relevant and hard to reconstruct from any single other paper in this batch.

title: Task-Oriented Reinforcement Learning with Interest State Representation

claims.claim: Replacing pixel-dependent state representations with an object-centric 'interest state' -- Mask R-CNN-detected bounding boxes of task-relevant objects across four camera views, used to define state and reward -- improves goal transferability and anti-interference performance in visual RL for manipulation, while maintaining learning efficiency and stability, compared to standard pixel-based state representations
claims.direction: favors object-centric (detected bounding-box) state representations over raw pixel-based state representations for goal transfer and robustness to interference
claims.conditions: four experiments with multi-view (4-camera) observations

claims.claim: The object-centric interest-state representation directly improves 'anti-interference performance,' i.e., robustness to changes not tied to the original observation data
claims.direction: favors object-centric state abstraction for robustness over pixel-dependent policies that are highly correlated with original observation data
claims.conditions: same 4-camera experimental setup

title: THE COLOSSEUM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Generalization for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Across 20 manipulation tasks and 14 axes of environmental perturbation (color, texture, size of objects/table-tops/backgrounds, lighting, distractors, physical-property perturbations, and camera pose), 5 state-of-the-art manipulation models degrade in success rate by 30-50% under single perturbation axes, and by >=75% when multiple perturbations are applied together; changing the number of distractor objects, target-object color, or lighting conditions are identified as the perturbations that reduce performance the most; simulation results correlate with real-world experiments (R^2=0.614)
claims.direction: quantifies and confirms that current manipulation policies are highly fragile to exactly the kinds of shifts we are worried about (lighting, object appearance/color, distractors, camera pose), and identifies lighting/object-color/distractor-count as the single most damaging factors, ahead of many other perturbation types
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark (20 tasks, 14 perturbation axes) with real-world correlation validation; 5 SOTA models evaluated

why_deep_read: A rigorous, real-world-correlated benchmark that directly quantifies our exact stated failure modes (new lighting, different-looking object, camera shift) and ranks which perturbation types hurt most (distractors, object color, lighting are worst) -- this could materially reprioritize which robustness axis (Q14) matters most for our pumpkin/tray task and which specific perturbation to test/augment against first.

title: VLA-RL: Towards Masterful and General Robotic Manipulation with Scalable Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A trajectory-level online RL formulation for autoregressive VLA training (modeling manipulation trajectories as multi-modal multi-turn conversation), using a fine-tuned VLM as a robotic process reward model trained on automatically-annotated pseudo reward labels, enables OpenVLA-7B to surpass the strongest fine-tuned baseline by 4.5% on 40 challenging LIBERO manipulation tasks and match performance of pi0-FAST
claims.direction: favors online RL fine-tuning of a pretrained autoregressive VLA (using an automatically-trained reward model, not hand-crafted rewards) over pure imitation-learning fine-tuning, to correct for offline-data distribution limitations
claims.conditions: OpenVLA-7B, 40 tasks in LIBERO simulation benchmark

claims.claim: Offline imitation learning on limited-coverage demonstration data causes execution failure in out-of-distribution scenarios; online RL test-time optimization (increased inference-time compute) further improves performance, suggesting an early inference-scaling effect in robotics
claims.direction: favors supplementing offline demonstration-based training with online RL exploration to address distribution-shift failures when demo coverage is limited
claims.conditions: same LIBERO evaluation

title: FlowRAM: Grounding Flow Matching Policy with Region-Aware Mamba Framework for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining conditional flow matching (regressing deterministic vector fields instead of full diffusion denoising) with a region-aware perception module and state-space models for multimodal fusion achieves state-of-the-art performance on RLBench, outperforming previous (diffusion-based) methods by 12.0% average success rate, particularly on high-precision tasks
claims.direction: favors flow matching combined with region-aware, linear-complexity (SSM) multimodal fusion over standard iterative-denoising diffusion policies for precision tasks
claims.conditions: RLBench manipulation benchmark

claims.claim: FlowRAM generates physically plausible actions for real-world tasks in fewer than 4 time steps, significantly increasing inference speed compared to iterative diffusion-based policies
claims.direction: favors flow-matching-based action generation with very few inference steps for reducing the latency bottleneck of diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real-world task deployment

claims.claim: A Dynamic Radius Schedule enables adaptive region-aware perception, transitioning from global scene comprehension to fine-grained geometric detail as needed for 3D manipulation precision
claims.direction: favors adaptive, scale-varying 3D scene perception over fixed-resolution processing
claims.conditions: same RLBench evaluation

title: Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guidance for Vision-Language-Action Models via Constrained Flow Matching

claims.claim: For flow-matching-based VLAs that predict a full action-chunk trajectory via iterative denoising, applying a minimum-norm constrained-optimization correction during the denoising process (using predicted intermediate trajectories) enables predictive collision avoidance rather than purely reactive intervention, achieving 82.8% collision avoidance and 81.6% task success on SafeLIBERO -- 6.3 and 19.8 percentage-point improvements over single-step correction methods, with the largest gains on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors interleaving symbolic constraint correction within the iterative flow-matching denoising process (rather than single-step post-hoc correction) for flow/diffusion-based action chunks
claims.conditions: SafeLIBERO benchmark; flow-matching VLA architecture

title: GAP: Geometric Anchor Pre-training for Data-Efficient Visuomotor Learning of Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Under severe data scarcity (15-50 demonstrations), a lightweight spatial adapter on top of a frozen pretrained Vision Foundation Model, pre-regularized via an action-free 'Geometric Anchor Pre-training' warm-up (using free object masks in a lightweight simulated proxy task) to produce sharp, repeatable, object-covering keypoints, consistently outperforms stronger attention-based poolers and full end-to-end fine-tuning: 62% success on RoboMimic Can with 15 demonstrations (+16% over the AFA baseline), 63% on the long-horizon high-precision Tool Hang task with 50 demonstrations, and 61% on ManiSkill StackCube with 30 demonstrations (+11% over full fine-tuning)
claims.direction: favors a cheap, action-free geometric pretraining stage for the spatial adapter atop a frozen VFM, over both attention-based pooling and full fine-tuning, specifically for few-shot (15-50 demo) visuomotor policy learning
claims.conditions: RoboMimic and ManiSkill benchmarks, 15-50 demonstrations, frozen VFM kept fixed throughout

claims.claim: Using frozen pretrained Vision Foundation Models improves data efficiency but shifts most task adaptation onto a small spatial pooling module, which can latch onto task-irrelevant shortcuts and lose geometric grounding when fine-tuned with few samples; pre-trained visual representations for policy learning have been observed to struggle under even minor scene perturbations
