claims.claim: Grasp Pose variation is the most significant generalization challenge among tested out-of-distribution factors; force-torque sensing is the most informative modality for the contact-rich task while vision is the least informative
claims.direction: favors force/tactile signal over vision for contact-rich robustness
claims.conditions: peg-in-hole assembly task, Perceiver IO multisensory policy

title: Rethinking 3D Robotic Perception: Elastic Voxel Representation with Splatting Distillation

claims.claim: Elastic voxel encoder with depth-constrained Gaussian-Splatting feature distillation (2D pretrained features to 3D) achieves 6.8% average improvement over SOTA across 10 manipulation tasks with 166 variations
claims.direction: favors 3D voxel/point representation with distilled 2D semantic features over plain 3D or plain 2D
claims.conditions: sim benchmark, 10 tasks / 166 variations, VLA-style framework

title: Canonical Policy: Learning Canonical 3D Representation for Equivariant Policy

claims.claim: Canonicalizing 3D point-cloud observations under an equivariant representation before generative policy learning improves average performance by 18.0% in simulation and 39.7% in real-world experiments vs SOTA imitation-learning policies
claims.direction: favors 3D point-cloud + equivariant canonicalization over standard (non-canonical / 2D) policies
claims.conditions: 12 sim tasks + 4 real-world tasks across 16 configs, variations in object color/shape, camera viewpoint, and robot platform

claims.claim: Canonical representation gives superior generalization capability and sample efficiency under camera-viewpoint and object-appearance shifts compared to state-of-the-art baselines
claims.direction: favors canonical/equivariant 3D representation for viewpoint & appearance robustness
claims.conditions: real-world, 4 tasks, 16 configurations varying viewpoint/object/robot

title: ViSA-Flow: Accelerating Robot Skill Learning via Large-Scale Video Semantic Action Flow

claims.claim: Pretraining a generative prior on semantic action flow extracted self-supervised from large-scale human video, then fine-tuning on a small set of robot demonstrations, outperforms prior methods particularly in low-data regimes on CALVIN and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors video-pretraining + small robot demo fine-tuning to reduce demo count needed
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark + real-world tasks, small robot demo fine-tuning set

title: Continuous Vision-Language-Action Co-Learning with Semantic-Physical Alignment for Behavioral Cloning

claims.claim: Continuous co-learning across vision, language, and proprioception with bidirectional cross-attention alignment produces smoother, temporally consistent action execution and mitigates physical discontinuities/intermittent execution seen in standard behavioral cloning
claims.direction: favors continuous cross-modal alignment over standard chunked BC for smooth execution
claims.conditions: 3 simulation suites + real-world 7-DoF robot

claims.claim: CCoL achieves average 8.0% relative improvement across three simulation suites, with up to 19.2% relative gain on human-demonstrated bimanual insertion tasks, attributed to overcoming compounding errors from temporal abstraction/chunking discontinuities
claims.direction: favors semantic-physical alignment mechanism added on top of temporal abstraction
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real 7-DoF robot, bimanual insertion

claims.claim: Real-world tests confirm generalization under unseen and noisy object states
claims.direction: favors the co-learning approach for robustness to noisy/unseen states
claims.conditions: real 7-DoF robot

title: Structure-Aware Diffusion Policy for Bimanual Cooperative Manipulation

claims.claim: A diffusion policy conditioned on explicit structured cooperative representations (kinematic descriptors + force-difference cue) plus hierarchical cross-attention fusion raises success rate from 58% to 89% versus a vision-dominant diffusion baseline on real dual-arm cooperative carrying
claims.direction: favors structured/explicit state conditioning over vision-only conditioning for diffusion policies
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, cooperative carrying task, varying object size/appearance

title: CosmoH2G: A Hand-to-Gripper Transfer Dataset and Baseline Method for Object Manipulation with Complex Spatial Movements

claims.claim: Naive end-to-end generation of full gripper pose sequences is insufficient for complex spatial trajectories because minor deviations compound rapidly; a two-stage approach predicting sparse keyframes first, then the full sequence conditioned on keyframes, significantly outperforms traditional (single-stage) baselines in sim and real-robot experiments
claims.direction: favors keyframe/coarse-to-fine decomposition over direct full-trajectory regression
claims.conditions: large-scale hand-to-gripper dataset (6189 episodes, 1254 objects), sim + real-robot

title: Mimic Intent, Not Just Trajectories

claims.claim: Disentangling behavior intent from execution details via multi-scale frequency-space action tokenization (coarsest token = low-frequency global structure, finer tokens = high-frequency detail), with next-scale autoregressive generation, achieves state-of-the-art success rates, superior inference efficiency, robust generalization against disturbances, and effective one-shot skill transfer, versus standard action-chunk regression
claims.direction: favors hierarchical multi-scale discrete/frequency tokenization over flat regression or single-scale tokenization
claims.conditions: several manipulation benchmarks + real robot

title: Keypose Exploration: Efficient Automatic Trajectory Labelling and Cross-Embodiment Policy Transfer

claims.claim: A keypose-guided Diffusion Policy using automatically-labelled keyposes (VLM semantic detection + trajectory analysis) matches a standard Diffusion Policy baseline on robomimic tasks, and reachability-filtered keypose conditioning may benefit zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer on a multimodal insertion task
claims.direction: favors keypose-conditioned diffusion policy as at-least-comparable to standard diffusion, with added transfer benefit
claims.conditions: preliminary feasibility study, 2 robomimic sim tasks, cross-embodiment

title: ChainVLA: Chaining Vision-Language-Action Queries through a Unified Execution State for Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Feeding the preceding action-chunk prediction's unexecuted continuation ('Motion Tail') into the next query's state construction is critical for smooth/continuous chunk-to-chunk handoff in action-chunked VLA policies; removing this component drops RMBench success from 62.8% to 11.2%
claims.direction: favors carrying unexecuted motion continuation across chunk boundaries instead of independent re-planning each query
claims.conditions: 1.2B-parameter VLA policy, RMBench benchmark + LIBERO (98.8% average across 4 suites)

claims.claim: Removing the recurrent 'Progress Context' (working state + sparse event memory carrying observation-derived task progress) drops RMBench success from 62.8% to 3.0%, showing long-horizon task-progress memory across queries is essential
claims.direction: favors recurrent memory/progress-tracking across re-planning queries over memoryless re-planning
claims.conditions: 1.2B-parameter VLA, RMBench long-horizon benchmark

why_deep_read: Directly attacks our exact 'jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries with async inference' problem, with a strong ablation quantifying the effect of carrying motion continuation vs replanning from scratch; worth checking if the mechanism is applicable to a much smaller model than 1.2B.

title: Manipulate by Seeing: Creating Manipulation Controllers from Pre-Trained Representations

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pre-trained visual representation on human video to derive a distance function and dynamics predictor for planning substantially outperforms traditional behavior-cloning baselines (e.g. 70% vs 50% success on real-world pick-place) without using robot demonstrations at train time, and generalizes to novel objects
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained visual representations directly for action inference over pure BC from robot demos alone
claims.conditions: real-world diverse manipulation tasks, zero robot demos at train time, novel-object generalization test

title: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation

claims.claim: Casting policy learning as text-conditioned video generation (predict future frames from text goal, then extract actions) enables combinatorial generalization to novel language-specified goals and knowledge transfer from internet videos to real robots
claims.direction: favors language-conditioned video-generation-as-planner over direct language-conditioned action regression
claims.conditions: qualitative claims, real robot manipulation tasks, pretrained language embeddings + internet video pretraining

title: Learning future representation with synthetic observations for sample-efficient reinforcement learning

claims.claim: A self-supervised auxiliary task (future representation learning from synthetic/frame-masked observations, clustering-based temporal association) improves RL sample efficiency, achieving SOTA on 12/13 continuous control tasks (locomotion+manipulation) and outperforming the next-best video-pretraining method by 1.51x on action-free video demonstrations
claims.direction: favors future-prediction style auxiliary objectives, including from action-free video, for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: sim RL, robot locomotion and manipulation, action-free video pretraining variant

title: CoT-VLA: Visual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Incorporating explicit visual chain-of-thought reasoning (autoregressively predicting future image frames as visual subgoals before generating a short action sequence) outperforms the SOTA VLA baseline by 17% in real-world manipulation tasks and 6% in simulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors future-frame-prediction auxiliary/planning objective over direct input-output VLA mapping
claims.conditions: 7B-parameter VLA model, real-world + simulation manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Not selected: gains are clear from abstract but the 7B model size is far outside our 8GB-GPU laptop budget, limiting direct applicability.

title: Contrastive Action-Image Pre-training for Visuomotor Control

claims.claim: CAIP, a vision encoder contrastively pretrained on egocentric human video using 3D hand keypoints as an action proxy (32,041 hours human video + only 88 hours robot data), outperforms state-of-the-art vision encoders including DINOv2, SigLIP, MVP, and R3M by more than 30% on real-world dexterous manipulation tasks (folding, pouring, fine-grained manipulation)
claims.direction: favors action-centric contrastive pretraining over DINOv2/SigLIP/MVP/R3M for the vision encoder
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous hand manipulation (Dexmate Vega, Sharpa Wave), large-scale egocentric video pretraining + small robot dataset

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q03 vision-encoder-pretraining question with a head-to-head comparison against the exact encoder families we are weighing (DINOv2, SigLIP, R3M); worth checking if the encoder/checkpoint is available for a small model like ours.

title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Treating wrist-view and main-view observations asymmetrically (wrist camera used to anticipate future wrist-local interactions under global task context via a future-wrist predictor) improves fine-grained and contact-sensitive manipulation over treating both views as parallel/equal inputs, across single-arm and bimanual settings
claims.direction: favors task-conditioned, asymmetric wrist-camera modeling over simple multi-view concatenation
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The proposed architecture maintains action-generation rates above 80 Hz despite the added future-wrist-prediction module
claims.direction: shows added auxiliary prediction can be kept cheap enough for high-frequency control
claims.conditions: real-world + sim, VLA with latent future-wrist modeling tokens

title: DreamAvoid: Critical-Phase Test-Time Dreaming to Avoid Failures in VLA Policies

claims.claim: A test-time mechanism that detects critical phases, samples multiple candidate action chunks, and 'dreams' short-horizon futures to select the best one raises real-world manipulation success from 48.8% (base policy) to 72.5%, versus 54.4% for a competing ranking method (GPC-RANK)
claims.direction: favors test-time failure-avoidance/re-ranking over relying on the base action-chunk policy alone
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks + simulation benchmarks; adds test-time compute (multiple candidate rollouts + evaluator) per query

title: EquiVLA: A General Framework for Rotationally Equivariant Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Adding exact SO(2) equivariance to a flow-matching Diffusion Transformer action head (EquiActor), paired with approximately-equivariant visual features from a frozen ViT (EquiPerceptor), raises average LIBERO success from 78.1% (baseline) to 92.6%, CALVIN ABCD-to-D average sequence length from 3.45 to 4.03, and real-robot (Mobile ALOHA) success from 54% to 72%
claims.direction: favors adding rotational-equivariance inductive bias to flow-matching action heads over standard (non-equivariant) flow-matching baselines
claims.conditions: instantiated on GR00T N1.5, 4 LIBERO suites + CALVIN + 5 real-robot tasks on Mobile ALOHA

claims.claim: Policies trained at specific orientations normally require substantially more data to generalize across rotational configurations; the equivariant framework reduces this data burden and improves rotational generalization, evidenced by the real-robot success jump
claims.direction: favors geometric (rotational) inductive biases for generalization under viewpoint/orientation shift
claims.conditions: real-robot Mobile ALOHA tasks

why_deep_read: Real-robot success jump (54%->72%) from adding equivariance to a flow-matching head is a large, directly quantified effect relevant to our camera-shift/lighting robustness problem; want to see cost/complexity of retrofitting onto a small flow-matching policy on our compute budget.

title: Visual Feature Trajectory Prediction: A 3D-Aware Auxiliary Objective for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Adding an auxiliary objective (predicting 3D vision-foundation-model features at the end-effector's future location, over the same horizon as BC action chunks, no inference overhead since training-only) improves average success rate over BC-only baselines across all evaluated configurations: SmolVLA and E2VLA backbones, full fine-tuning at two model scales, LoRA adaptation, and a smaller VLA without pretrained LM; gains are +2.5 to +3.4 pp on LIBERO and +5.5pp (to 59.1% average) on MetaWorld, with up to +9.0pp on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight 3D-aware future-feature-prediction auxiliary loss on top of standard BC, including for SmolVLA specifically
claims.conditions: LIBERO + MetaWorld sim benchmarks; tested directly on SmolVLA (our current backbone) and on a smaller VLA without pretrained LM, plus LoRA adaptation

why_deep_read: This is evaluated directly on SmolVLA (our exact fine-tuning backbone) including a LoRA/small-model configuration, with quantified gains and no added inference cost -- very likely directly transferable to our low-compute setup; want the ablation details on which design choices (3D-VFM choice, horizon length) mattered.

title: PredTac: Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation with Predicted Touch

claims.claim: A tactile predictor trained with tactile supervision, then used to supply predicted (not measured) touch as an auxiliary input for policy training/execution, brings a vision-only ACT policy from 21.1% to 70.0% mean success on real-robot contact-rich tasks, approaching measured-touch ACT (72.2%)
claims.direction: favors predicted-touch auxiliary signal over vision-only input when no physical tactile sensor is available, for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot (USB insertion, barbed-spike extraction, valve rotation), ACT policy, requires a separately-trained tactile predictor with tactile supervision at training time only

title: Learning an Actionable Discrete Diffusion Policy via Large-Scale Actionless Video Pre-Training

claims.claim: Pre-training a unified discrete diffusion model on actionless human+robot video (tokenized), then fine-tuning low-level action prediction on a limited set of action-labeled robot data, generates higher-fidelity future videos for planning and enhances fine-tuned policies compared to prior SOTA approaches
claims.direction: favors actionless video pretraining + discrete diffusion to reduce action-labeled robot data requirements
claims.conditions: limited action-labeled robot demos for fine-tuning; discrete/token-based diffusion action representation

title: RLVR-World: Training World Models with Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Optimizing world models directly for transition-prediction metrics (accuracy/perceptual quality) via RL with verifiable rewards, rather than maximum-likelihood training, yields substantial performance gains for world models across domains including robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors RL-based fine-tuning of world models over standard MLE training when world models are used as auxiliary/planning components
claims.conditions: qualitative 'substantial gains' claim; domains include text games, web navigation, and robot manipulation

title: GraphCoT-VLA: A 3D Spatial-Aware Reasoning Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation with Ambiguous Instructions

claims.claim: Augmenting a VLA with a real-time updatable 3D Pose-Object graph (capturing spatial configuration of robot joints and object topological relationships) plus a chain-of-thought reasoning module significantly outperforms existing (largely 2D-observation) VLA methods in task success rate and response speed on real-world robotic tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D spatial graph representation over static 2D-only observation for ambiguous-instruction manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation tasks, qualitative 'significantly outperforms' claim (no exact numbers given)

title: Beyond Viewpoint Generalization: What Multi-View Demonstrations Offer and How to Synthesize Them for Robot Manipulation?

claims.claim: Controlled experiments (fixed and randomized backgrounds) show multi-view demonstrations consistently improve single-view policy success and generalization, but performance varies non-monotonically with view coverage (more views is not simply better; there are effective regimes), and multi-view data breaks the scaling limitation of single-view datasets, continuing to raise the performance ceiling after single-view saturation
claims.direction: favors adding multi-view demonstrations over single-view, but with a non-monotonic optimal number of views rather than maximizing views
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation, controlled ablation over number/coverage of views

claims.claim: Mechanistic analysis shows multi-view learning promotes manipulation-relevant visual representations, better aligns the action head with the learned feature distribution, and reduces overfitting; a geometry-aware self-supervised framework (RoboNVS) that synthesizes novel-view videos from monocular input consistently improves downstream policies when additional real views are unavailable
claims.direction: favors synthesizing extra views (novel-view synthesis) when multi-view data collection is impractical
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, monocular-to-novel-view synthesis pipeline

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled study of exactly our Q11 question (we have 2 fixed cameras) — quantifies how many/which views help and whether synthesizing extra views from our existing RealSense+wrist feed could substitute for physically adding cameras; the non-monotonic finding on view count is also a specific, actionable, possibly counter-to-naive-intuition result worth verifying in the full paper.

title: CDP: Composable Diffusion Policy for Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing demonstrations into phase-consistent skill segments and training a separate diffusion policy per segment (composed at execution via a VLM-based planner) gives better data efficiency and stronger generalization than Implicit Behavior Cloning and (monolithic) Diffusion Policy baselines, evaluated at two training-data scales on Robomimic
claims.direction: favors composable/segmented diffusion skills over a single end-to-end diffusion policy for data efficiency
claims.conditions: Robomimic sim benchmark (3 difficulty levels) + real-robot JAKA S5 with global+wrist cameras

title: ZETA: A Controlled Study of Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment VLA Transfer for Tabletop Manipulation

claims.claim: In a controlled benchmark across 14 held-out target embodiments (sim + real, two-finger grippers), local end-effector (EEF) state-action representations improve cross-embodiment transfer by about 15 percentage points versus alternative state-action representations
claims.direction: favors local end-effector-relative action representation over other (e.g. joint-based/global) representations for embodiment/setup generalization
claims.conditions: stationary tabletop manipulation, two-finger grippers, controlled benchmark isolating embodiment change

claims.claim: Auxiliary co-training objectives improve cross-embodiment transfer by about 7 percentage points; source embodiment diversity during pretraining improves it by about 18 percentage points
claims.direction: favors auxiliary co-training and diverse pretraining embodiments for transfer/generalization
claims.conditions: same controlled 14-embodiment benchmark

claims.claim: Adding only 5% target-embodiment data during pretraining improves average target-embodiment progress by 13.4 percentage points, showing pretrain-exposed and strict zero-shot transfer are meaningfully different regimes
claims.direction: favors including even a small fraction of target-setup data during pretraining/fine-tuning
claims.conditions: tabletop manipulation, two-finger grippers, controlled benchmark

title: Unifying Object-Centric World Models and Diffusion Policy: A Hierarchical Framework for Multi-Stage Robotic Tasks

claims.claim: A hierarchical framework (WorldDP) where a high-level object-centric world model proposes feasible subgoals and a low-level Diffusion Policy executes them consistently outperforms existing baselines on multi-stage robotic manipulation benchmarks, whereas single-stage world-model+MPC approaches struggle with multi-stage sequential planning
claims.direction: favors hierarchical world-model-subgoal + diffusion-policy-execution over flat world-model-MPC or flat diffusion policy for multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: multiple robotics benchmarks, qualitative 'consistently outperforms' claim (no exact numbers given)

title: Towards Long-horizon Embodied Agents with Tool-Aligned Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Distributing long-horizon manipulation between a high-level VLM planner and specialized VLA 'tool' policies for bounded subtasks, with an interface exposing in-execution progress feedback for event-triggered replanning (rather than continuous polling), improves success rate of a base policy (pi_0.5) by 4.8 points on LIBERO-Long and 23.1 points on RoboTwin, and improves invocation fidelity by 15.0 points
claims.direction: favors hierarchical tool-decomposition with event-triggered replanning over a monolithic long-horizon policy with continuous replanning
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin benchmarks, built on pi_0.5 backbone

title: Adaptive Video-Conditioned Imitation Learning via Bidirectional Cross-Domain Skill Transfer

claims.claim: A hierarchical imitation learning method (AdaMimic) that infers local intentions from a single human demonstration video (rather than following it step-by-step) and retrieves matching robot skill memories from prior experience generalizes better to unseen long-horizon tasks than prior video-conditioned imitation learning methods, evaluated in simulated and real-world kitchen domains
claims.direction: favors intention-based skill retrieval over direct step-by-step video imitation for generalizing from very few (single) demonstration videos
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world kitchen manipulation, single human prompt video per novel task, qualitative 'superiority' claim

title: Free Your Hands: Human-Demonstration-Free Diffusion Policy Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A well-trained diffusion policy struggles to adapt to new environments with lighting variation, object appearance change, different background, and unseen distractors; simply aligning domains at the visual level alone is insufficient because even subtle visual changes cause severe action failures, motivating a combined visual-level (adversarial) and policy-level (noise-aware adversarial) alignment for cross-environment adaptation without any additional teleoperated demonstrations
claims.direction: favors two-level (visual+policy) domain adaptation over visual-only alignment or collecting more teleop demos, for lighting/appearance/background/distractor shifts
claims.conditions: Sim2Sim (PushT, CALVIN, RoboTwin), Real2Sim (SimplerEnv), and Real2Real real-world robotic deployment; minimal added parameter overhead

title: Gaze-Regularized Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Regularizing a VLA's internal transformer attention toward human gaze heatmaps (via KL divergence on patch-level distributions) as an auxiliary training signal, with no architectural modification or inference-time overhead, yields 4-12% improvements across manipulation benchmarks and reaches equivalent performance with fewer training steps when integrated into existing VLA architectures
claims.direction: favors gaze-based attention regularization as a free (no-inference-cost) auxiliary objective added to existing VLA training
claims.conditions: integrated into existing VLA architectures across manipulation benchmarks; requires gaze-heatmap labels for training only

claims.claim: Gaze-regularized models maintain robustness under lighting variations and sensor noise
claims.direction: favors gaze-regularization for lighting/noise robustness
claims.conditions: same VLA benchmarks

title: Co-VLA: Coordination-Aware Structured Action Modeling for Dual-Arm Vision-Language-Action Systems

claims.claim: Replacing a monolithic continuous action head with a Structured Action Expert that splits a shared (task-coordination) latent from per-arm residual (execution) latents, interpreted at deployment by a Latent-Aware Controller, significantly outperforms monolithic action-head baselines: 27% success-rate gain in tight-coordination tasks, more than doubling OOD real-world success (13% to 27%), and up to 25% faster task completion
claims.direction: favors structured/decomposed (shared+residual) action latents over a single monolithic action head, at least for coordination-heavy bimanual tasks
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation dual-arm benchmarks; bimanual coordination setting

title: One Hand Watches The Other: Dynamic Multi-Agent Cooperation for Sample-Efficient Bimanual Manipulation in Dynamic Environments

claims.claim: DynaMAC, which treats the other arm (or a moving object) as a dynamic task parameter rather than assuming an exogenous reference frame, outperforms leading probabilistic and generative baselines by over 35 percentage points while requiring 20x fewer samples, and generalizes zero-shot from static demonstrations to dynamic environments
claims.direction: favors modeling action reference frames as dynamic/relative task parameters over assuming fixed exogenous frames, for sample efficiency and zero-shot dynamic generalization
claims.conditions: bimanual and single-arm dynamic-object manipulation, new DynaBench benchmark, policy-agnostic framework

title: ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations

claims.claim: Explicitly estimating object physical properties (mass, friction, stiffness) from human visual-tactile demonstrations and conditioning grasping policy on them achieves 95.0% success on in-distribution objects and 83.4% on out-of-distribution objects, with more human-like force profiles than a baseline (ACT) on OOD objects grasped by both
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit physical-property-conditioning auxiliary signal over standard vision-only ACT-style policies for adaptive grasping
claims.conditions: real robot, transfer from human demonstrations + limited robot teleoperation data + video augmentation, 60 rigid/deformable training objects

title: CLAW: A Vision-Language-Action Framework for Weight-Aware Robotic Grasping

claims.claim: Decoupling symbolic condition evaluation (a fine-tuned CLIP model monitoring a scale readout, producing discrete directives) from continuous action generation (fed into a flow-based VLA, pi_0) reliably executes weight-aware behaviors and outperforms both raw-pi_0 and fine-tuned-pi_0 baselines across single-object and dual-arm mixed-object grasping tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit decoupled symbolic-condition-monitoring architecture over end-to-end language/vision conditioning alone for precise numeric-threshold task constraints
claims.conditions: real robot, single- and dual-arm setups, pi_0 flow-based VLA backbone

title: On the Importance of Tactile Sensing for Imitation Learning: A Case Study on Robotic Match Lighting

claims.claim: A multimodal visuotactile imitation-learning framework (modular transformer + flow-based generative model) that adds tactile information improves policy performance over vision-only, on a dynamic, contact-rich, few-demonstration manipulation task (robotic match lighting)
claims.direction: favors adding tactile modality/auxiliary signal over vision-only for dynamic contact-rich tasks learned from few demonstrations
claims.conditions: real robot, dynamic contact-rich task, learned from few demonstrations; requires tactile sensor hardware

title: VolumeDP: Modeling Volumetric Representation for Manipulation Policy Learning

claims.claim: Explicitly lifting 2D image features into a volumetric (3D) representation via cross-attention, selecting task-relevant voxels, and decoding actions from a compact multi-token spatial set (rather than mapping 2D observations directly to actions or collapsing to a single descriptor) achieves a state-of-the-art 88.8% average success on LIBERO, beating the strongest baseline by 14.8 percentage points, with further large gains on ManiSkill and LIBERO-Plus
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D/volumetric lifting of 2D features over direct 2D-to-action mapping or single-vector 3D aggregation
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, ManiSkill, LIBERO-Plus) + real-world experiments

claims.claim: Real-world experiments show higher success rates and robust generalization to novel spatial layouts, camera viewpoints, and environment backgrounds compared to prior methods
claims.direction: favors volumetric/3D policy architecture for camera-viewpoint and background robustness
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, novel layouts/viewpoints/backgrounds

title: Posterior Optimization with Clipped Objective for Bridging Efficiency and Stability in Generative Policy Learning

claims.claim: POCO, an RL fine-tuning framework formulating policy improvement as posterior inference over temporal action chunks (via EM, reward-weighted implicit posterior, offline-to-online anchoring to pretrained priors), prevents catastrophic policy collapse during RL fine-tuning of generative (diffusion/flow) policies and outperforms SOTA baselines, reaching 96.7% success on real-world contact-rich tasks; the approach is model-agnostic and scales to large VLA models without architectural changes
claims.direction: favors RL fine-tuning of chunked generative policies via posterior-inference/EM rather than naive RL fine-tuning (which risks collapse)
claims.conditions: 7 simulation benchmarks + 4 real-world contact-rich tasks

title: Kitchen robotic manipulation utilizing foundation models

claims.claim: A modular perception pipeline enabling systematic substitution of visual/geometric foundation models found that the best-performing configuration for 6D pose estimation and grasp planning under clutter/occlusion is LLMDet + SAMv2 + DINOv2 + GeoTransformer (89.12% ADI on a 20-scene kitchen benchmark), and this configuration deploys on physical robots without environment-specific retraining
claims.direction: favors DINOv2 as the vision-feature component in a modular open-vocabulary perception stack, among the substitutable foundation models tested
claims.conditions: real-world kitchen manipulation (dishware handling), modular ablation across detector/segmenter/encoder/registration choices

title: Mix diffusion policy: hierarchical robotic manipulation via diffusion-flow matching fusion

claims.claim: A hierarchical policy combining a 3D Diffusion Policy (DP3) as a high-level task-guidance 'Guider' with a one-step Consistency-Flow-Matching 'FlowPolicy' as the low-level action 'Actor' retains high manipulation accuracy while improving inference speed by 56.6%-66.9% over a Hierarchical Diffusion Policy baseline
claims.direction: favors combining diffusion (for guidance/multimodality) with one-step flow-matching (for fast execution) over pure multi-step diffusion, to cut inference latency without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation, hierarchical high-level/low-level split, one-step flow-matching low-level actor

title: Realtime-VLA FLASH: Speculative Inference Framework for Diffusion-based VLAs

claims.claim: A speculative-inference framework (lightweight draft model + parallel verification via the main model's Action Expert + phase-aware fallback to full inference) replaces many full-inference replanning rounds (58.0 ms each) with much cheaper speculative rounds (as fast as 7.8 ms), lowering task-level average inference latency to 19.1 ms (a 3.04x speedup) on LIBERO while largely preserving task performance, and is demonstrated on real-world conveyor-belt sorting
claims.direction: favors speculative/draft-and-verify inference over always running full diffusion-VLA inference at every replanning step, to cut latency
claims.conditions: diffusion-based VLA (dVLA), LIBERO benchmark + real-world conveyor sorting task

why_deep_read: This is a direct, quantified solution (3.04x speedup, 19.1ms average latency) to precisely our stated ~2s inference latency and async-execution smoothness problem; want full details on draft-model size/training cost and whether it is compatible with a small backbone like ours rather than requiring a separate large 'main model' Action Expert.

title: WSA$_1$: a 3D-Centric World-Spatial-Action Model for Generalizable Robot Control

claims.claim: WSA1, pretrained with joint 3D world-state-transition and action modeling, achieves data-efficient pretraining using 6k hours of expert demonstration data of which only 1k hours come from real robots, while delivering 93% success on RoboTwin2.0 simulation and +20% average performance over SOTA robot foundation models on real-world robot control tasks
claims.direction: favors 3D-centric world-action joint modeling pretraining to reduce reliance on large-scale real robot data, versus 2D-centric imitation-only pretraining
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2.0 sim benchmark + real-world robot control tasks; large robot-foundation-model scale pretraining

why_deep_read: Not selected for deep read: the gains appear tied to large-scale foundation-model pretraining (6k demo-hours), which may not transfer directly to our small-model, ~50-100-demo regime, though the underlying 3D-world-action idea (Q04) is noted.

title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models

claims.claim: Grounding a JEPA world model's latents in robot proprioceptive state and grounding latent-pair differences in multi-horizon joint-angle changes (both training-only auxiliary objectives, leaving inference architecture and compute unchanged) consistently outperforms SOTA latent world-model baselines at all three evaluated levels: latent identifiability probing, goal-conditioned planning on frozen latents, and policy learning in simulation and on a real robot
claims.direction: favors adding explicit proprioceptive/state-grounding losses to forward-prediction (JEPA-style) world models over forward-prediction alone
claims.conditions: real robot + simulation policy learning, training-only auxiliary objectives with zero added inference cost

title: SkelWAM: A Skeleton-Guided World-Action Model for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing state/action via a shared 25-D geometric representation (arm centerline geometry, tool-center-point pose, parallel-jaw command) that is embodiment-agnostic (no one-to-one joint correspondence needed) lets a Franka-trained model transfer zero-shot (no target-task demonstrations or policy updates) to 10 unseen target embodiments, achieving 43.3% success vs the best baseline's lower performance (36.2 percentage-point gap) on a 10-task cross-embodiment benchmark
claims.direction: favors a shared geometric/TCP-based action representation over embodiment-specific joint-space representations for cross-embodiment/zero-shot transfer
claims.conditions: source-only cross-embodiment benchmark (LIBERO-Cross10), Franka source policy, includes deployment to a continuum robot

title: Reconciling Reality through Simulation: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach for Robust Manipulation

claims.claim: RialTo, which quickly scans/constructs a 'digital twin' simulation from small amounts of real-world data and fine-tunes an imitation-learning policy via RL in that twin (using an 'inverse distillation' procedure to bring real demonstrations into sim), increases policy robustness by over 67% (to object poses, physical disturbances, and visual distractors) without requiring extensive additional human data collection or unsafe real-world RL
claims.direction: favors real-to-sim-to-real RL robustification over pure imitation learning (which needs heavy human supervision) or pure real-world RL (impractical data needs)
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, 8 tasks (e.g. dish stacking, book shelving), small amount of real data used to build the sim twin

title: Experiments on Taking Loss Methods in Imitation Learning With Bilateral Control

claims.claim: In bilateral-control imitation learning using low-resolution images to grasp an autonomously moving object, using a loss based on end-effector (hand) coordinates (rather than joint-angle loss) caused a bias in learning joint-angle responses; learning joint angle responses with equal weights was found to be important
claims.direction: favors joint-angle-space loss with equal weighting over end-effector-coordinate-transformed loss for this bilateral-control imitation setup
claims.conditions: real robot, bilateral (leader-follower) teleoperation control, low-resolution image input, moving-object grasping task

title: OC-VLA++: Monocular Geometry-Guided Cross-View Consistency for Viewpoint-Robust Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Grounding robot actions in the camera coordinate system (as in OC-VLA) still overfits to the few viewpoints seen during training; adding geometry-guided paired-view supervision plus an explicit cross-view action-equivariance objective (training the model so camera-space predictions from geometrically related viewpoints correspond to the same robot-frame action) yields substantial improvements in unseen-view generalization under limited camera coverage, with performance degrading more gracefully as camera displacement increases
claims.direction: favors explicit cross-view action-equivariance supervision over camera-space action grounding alone or image-level augmentation, for viewpoint robustness with few training cameras
claims.conditions: limited camera coverage (few training viewpoints), paired-view training data required, no exact success-rate numbers given

title: Scalable Behavior Cloning with Open Data, Training, and Evaluation

claims.claim: An open-source BC stack (ABC-130K: 3,500 hours / 130K episodes / 195 tasks, plus 400 hours sim-teleop data) is used to compare common architectural choices for Diffusion Transformers (DiT) vs Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, with findings grounded in real-world evaluation and a co-training recipe that makes simulation a reliable proxy for ablating model-design/training decisions before costly real-world testing
claims.direction: provides an open, real-world-grounded comparison methodology for action-head/architecture choices (DiT vs VLA) rather than sim-only or anecdotal comparisons
claims.conditions: large-scale open teleoperation dataset, real-world + sim-teleop co-training, dexterous tasks (box folding, credit-card extraction from wallet)

title: ProbeAct: Probe-Guided Training-Free Failure Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Pretrained VLA policies lack robustness to lighting changes, altered camera viewpoints, or small initial-state variations; a training-free runtime intervention (hidden-state probe predicting 3D object positions + a kinematic failure-detection state machine + a Control Barrier Function filter that minimally corrects actions near known repeated-failure locations) improves OpenVLA-OFT success rate from 69.6% to 74.1% on the LIBERO-plus benchmark, without modifying model weights or requiring additional demonstrations
claims.direction: favors a training-free, plug-and-play runtime safety-net/failure-recovery layer over relying on the base VLA policy's own robustness, for lighting/viewpoint/initial-state perturbations
claims.conditions: LIBERO-plus benchmark, OpenVLA-OFT base and fine-tuned VLA policies, no additional training or demonstrations required

title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations

claims.claim: Fine-tuning VLA models on limited robot demonstrations erodes the semantic structure inherited from pretrained vision-language encoders, and this erosion correlates with both task success and OOD generalization; a plug-and-play method that anchors action representations to a semantic manifold (decomposing into a shared semantic channel and a private channel, both discarded at inference so the deployed model is unchanged) yields up to +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization
claims.direction: favors explicitly preserving/anchoring pretrained semantic structure in action representations during fine-tuning, over standard fine-tuning that lets this structure erode, especially for OOD generalization
claims.conditions: validated across different VLA backbones, simulation and real-world benchmarks; training-time-only cost, zero inference-time overhead

why_deep_read: Large, zero-inference-cost OOD generalization gains (+21.5%) from a plug-and-play fine-tuning regularizer directly relevant to our low-data fine-tuning regime and generalization failures; want backbone-size requirements and whether it applies to a small model like SmolVLA.

title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory

claims.claim: Making the subtask (rather than the whole long-horizon task) the unit of exploration, with a transition-aware memory tracking entry/exit conditions between subtasks (verified via wrist-camera confirmation before invoking the manipulation policy, plus handoff/lookahead transitions), improves task success by 11.6% and cumulative success by 14.9% over the SOTA on the RoboMemArena long-horizon benchmark, versus an LLM-agent-plus-frozen-VLA baseline with no transition representation
claims.direction: favors explicit subtask-transition memory/verification over treating a chained VLA-skill pipeline as memoryless
claims.conditions: long-horizon multi-stage manipulation, LLM planner + frozen VLA primitives, RoboMemArena benchmark, no parameter updates

title: Few-Shot Learning of Force-Based Motions From Demonstration Through Pre-training of Haptic Representation

claims.claim: Decoupling the model into a haptic-representation encoder (pre-trained on large amounts of easily-accessible unsupervised data) and a motion-generation decoder (trained via few-shot LfD) significantly improves the model's ability to recognise physical properties and generate desired motions for unseen objects, outperforming the same LfD approach without pre-training, validated on real robot hardware (KUKA iiwa)
claims.direction: favors self-supervised pretraining of a modality-specific encoder (here haptic) followed by few-shot LfD fine-tuning over training the full model from few demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: real robot (KUKA iiwa), wiping task with sponges of varying stiffness/friction, few-shot fine-tuning after pretraining

title: DiffGen: Robot Demonstration Generation via Differentiable Physics Simulation, Differentiable Rendering, and Vision-Language Model

claims.claim: Generating robot demonstrations by minimizing, via differentiable physics simulation and differentiable rendering, the distance between a VLM embedding of a language instruction and the VLM embedding of the resulting simulated observation (rather than training an RL agent or hand-designing rewards) efficiently and effectively generates robot data with minimal human effort or training time
claims.direction: favors differentiable-simulation+VLM-guided synthetic demonstration generation over RL-based demo generation or manual reward design, to reduce human-collected demo requirements
claims.conditions: simulated robot manipulation scenarios, qualitative 'efficient and effective' claim (no exact numbers given)

title: Real2Edit2Real: Generating Robotic Demonstrations via a 3D Control Interface

claims.claim: Policies trained on synthetic demonstrations generated from only 1-5 real source demonstrations (via 3D point-cloud editing of reconstructed scene geometry + multi-conditional video generation guided by depth/action/edge/ray maps) can match or outperform policies trained on 50 real-world demonstrations, improving data efficiency by up to 10-50x, across four real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors 3D-geometry-based synthetic demonstration augmentation (depth-guided video generation from edited point clouds) over collecting many more real teleoperated demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, metric-scale multi-view 3D reconstruction, depth as primary generation control signal; also validated for height/texture editing (appearance/spatial generalization)

title: RoboCopilot: Human-in-the-loop Interactive Imitation Learning for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A compliant bilateral teleoperation system enabling seamless control switching between a human and the autonomous policy during data collection (interactive human teaching, akin to DAgger-style correction) enables more efficient learning of complex bi-manual manipulation skills than passive demonstration collection alone, shown in simulation and hardware experiments
claims.direction: favors interactive/corrective human-in-the-loop demonstration collection over purely passive teleoperated demonstrations
claims.conditions: bimanual manipulation, simulation + real hardware, compliant bilateral teleoperation interface

title: IVRA: Improving Visual-Token Relations for Robot Action Policy with Training-Free Hint-Based Guidance

claims.claim: A training-free method that injects affinity hints already present in a VLA's own vision-encoder features into a language-model layer (realigning visual-token interactions without any external encoder or retraining) improves average success by +4.2% over baseline LLaRA on 2D VIMA in a low-data regime, and yields consistent gains on 3D LIBERO for OpenVLA and FLOWER baselines, including gains even when baseline accuracy is near saturation (96.3% to 97.1%)
claims.direction: favors exploiting/realigning existing vision-encoder token relations at inference time over flattening image patches into an unstructured 1D token sequence
claims.conditions: applied to diverse VLA architectures (LLaRA, OpenVLA, FLOWER), 2D (VIMA) and 3D (LIBERO) sim benchmarks + real-robot tasks; training-free, zero retraining cost, low-data regime tested

title: S-VAM: Shortcut Video-Action Model by Self-Distilling Geometric and Semantic Foresight

claims.claim: Video action models normally cannot simultaneously achieve real-time inference and high-fidelity visual foresight (slow multi-step generation vs noisy one-step extraction); a self-distillation strategy that condenses multi-step diffusion-generated video-foundation-model representations into a one-step 'shortcut' predictor lets S-VAM foresee coherent geometric/semantic representations in a single forward pass, outperforming SOTA methods in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors one-step self-distilled visual-foresight prediction over multi-step video generation or noisy one-step feature extraction, to get both speed and quality
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation; requires a teacher multi-step diffusion video model during training (student is one-step at inference)

title: GEAR-VLA: Learning Geometry-Aware Action Representations for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A coarse-to-fine action-learning framework that aligns a trainable 3D spatial backbone with the VLA representation (while freezing the original VLM-aligned visual pathway), combined with embodiment canonicalization (embodiment-aware states, embodiment-invariant actions confined to a low-level interface), achieves SOTA on LIBERO, zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, 85.9% success on AgileX, 81.0% on a pretraining-unseen embodiment, and 90.1% on a 6,360-trial universal grasping benchmark spanning 212 unseen objects
claims.direction: favors adding a semantically-aligned 3D spatial backbone plus explicit embodiment canonicalization over 2D-only VLA representations for generalization to unseen objects/embodiments/backgrounds
claims.conditions: extensive simulation + real-world experiments across multiple embodiments and a large unseen-object grasping benchmark

title: Multi-Objective Learning for Diffusion Models: A Statistical Theory under Semi-Supervised Learning

claims.claim: When paired (labeled) demonstration data is scarce but unlabeled condition/task data is abundant, a two-stage procedure (train lightweight specialist diffusion models on the limited paired data per task, then distill them into one generalist model via pseudo-samples) achieves Pareto trade-offs with a required paired-sample count that depends only on the specialist model's complexity, not the larger generalist model's; theory is extended to diffusion policies for sequential decision-making under on-policy distribution shift and validated on robotic control experiments
claims.direction: favors specialist-then-distill multi-task training over training one large generalist diffusion policy directly on scarce paired demonstration data across multiple tasks/environments
claims.conditions: theoretical framework + robotic control and image-restoration experiments; semi-supervised regime (scarce paired robot demos, abundant unlabeled/condition data)

title: ComVLA: Communication-Aware Split Inference for VLA Models in 6G-Connected Robotics

claims.claim: Using language guidance to select which visual tokens matter (adapting the VLA visual-token budget rather than transmitting/processing all image tokens), transmitting 32 tokens instead of 512 on LIBERO cuts inference compute by 74% and inference latency by 22% versus the OpenVLA-OFT baseline, at a cost of only 1.5 percentage points of average task success (95.4% vs 96.9%)
claims.direction: favors language-guided visual-token pruning/reduction over processing the full dense visual token set, to cut inference compute and latency at small accuracy cost
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, OpenVLA-OFT backbone; originally motivated by wireless/cloud-offload bandwidth constraints but the token-reduction technique itself is architecture-level

title: Imagine-RL: Residual-Confidence-Guided Cross-Attention for World-Model-Augmented VLA Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Augmenting noise-space RL post-training of a frozen VLA with an action-conditioned frozen visual-torque latent world model that imagines future consequences for each candidate action chunk (with confidence priors suppressing unreliable predicted tokens) improves average real-robot success rate by 23.6% over a noise-space-RL baseline (DSRL) and by 60% over VLA baselines, using only 100 RL trajectories across four real-robot tasks (50 trials/task)
claims.direction: favors critic-side future-consequence imagination (a world model evaluating candidate actions) over noise-space RL that only steers actions without modeling consequences, for post-training a frozen VLA
claims.conditions: real robot, 4 tasks, only 100 RL trajectories for post-training, both VLA and world model kept frozen (only actor/critic heads trained); requires a pretrained visual-torque world model (implies torque sensing)

why_deep_read: Not selected for deep read: relies on a pretrained visual-torque world model implying torque/force sensing our SO-101 setup lacks, limiting direct applicability despite strong real-robot numbers.

title: ViViDex: Learning Vision-Based Dexterous Manipulation from Human Videos

claims.claim: Comparing behavior cloning and diffusion policy for training a unified visual policy (after rolling out successful trajectories from per-video state-based policies), ViViDex outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on three dexterous manipulation tasks in both simulation and on a real robot, without using privileged object-state information at deployment
claims.direction: reports a head-to-head BC vs diffusion-policy comparison for the final visual policy stage (specific winner not stated in abstract)
claims.conditions: real robot + sim, dexterous multi-fingered hand, point-cloud visual representation with proposed coordinate transformation

title: Action-Free Reasoning for Policy Generalization

claims.claim: Training a reasoning-based policy (RAD) jointly on robot demonstration data (with reasoning+action labels) and action-free human video data (with only reasoning labels) enables effective transfer across the human-robot embodiment gap, letting robots perform tasks seen only in the action-free human data; scaling up the amount of action-free reasoning data significantly improves policy performance and generalization to novel tasks
claims.direction: favors language/reasoning-based transfer from action-free human video over grounded action-representation extraction (e.g. hand poses) for bridging the embodiment gap, and shows action-free data scaling helps generalization
claims.conditions: robot demos + action-free human video (new 3,377-demo reasoning-annotated dataset compatible with Bridge V2), qualitative/scaling claims

title: H2R: A Human-to-Robot Data Augmentation for Robot Pre-training from Videos

claims.claim: A human-to-robot data augmentation pipeline (retargeting estimated hand pose to a simulated robot arm, removing human limbs via segmentation/inpainting, compositing a rendered robot embodiment with camera-aligned geometry into original human-video frames) applied to large-scale egocentric human video pre-training data (Ego4D, SSv2) consistently improves downstream manipulation success rates in simulation by 1.3%-10.2% across four benchmark suites and different visual encoders/policy methods, and by 3.3%-23.3% in real-world experiments across gripper-based, dexterous, and bimanual tasks on UR5 and dual-arm Franka/UR5 platforms
claims.direction: favors explicitly rendering robot embodiments into human video data (closing the visual human-robot gap) over using raw human videos directly for pre-training, across multiple encoders and policy learning methods
claims.conditions: large-scale egocentric human video pretraining, evaluated across Robomimic/RLBench/PushT/CortexBench (sim) and UR5/dual-arm Franka-UR5 (real); compatible with VLA models

title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

claims.claim: Performance consistently improves with increased data scale and model size during pre-training, and this scaling behavior directly transfers to post-training, where a stronger pre-trained model yields better out-of-the-box real-robot performance in unseen environments; the resulting foundation policy can then be efficiently fine-tuned on complex, dexterous downstream tasks with high data efficiency, achieving new SOTA (57.4% vs prior 46.6% on RoboCasa365; 20.07 vs prior 13.07 on RoboDojo)
claims.direction: contradicts a 'small model is enough' assumption for the pre-training stage: larger models/data scale directly improve both zero-shot and fine-tuned downstream performance, though downstream fine-tuning itself can be data-efficient
claims.conditions: foundation-model-scale pretraining (100k+ hours real-world trajectories via UMI devices), auto-labeled scene-transition language annotations; downstream fine-tuning evaluated on multiple sim benchmarks

title: ZeroBot: Learning From Scratch in Minutes With Generative Real2Sim

claims.claim: ZeroBot learns a real-world manipulation task (grasping, pushing, articulated interaction, multi-stage manipulation) from a single image view and a goal pose, with zero human demonstrations, zero policy pre-training, and zero known object models, by generating a 3D object mesh via image-to-3D generative models and running large-scale parallel RL in simulation on that mesh; it achieves an 87% real-world success rate with an average training time of only 119 seconds per task
claims.direction: favors zero-demonstration real2sim generative-mesh-plus-RL bootstrapping over collecting any human teleoperation demonstrations, at least for simple single-object tasks with a known goal pose
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation, single-image object input, no known object CAD model, large-scale parallel sim RL for training (compute-heavy at train time, but reported total time is short)

why_deep_read: An 87% success rate with literally zero teleoperation demonstrations and ~2-minute training directly challenges our assumption that we need 50-100 demos per task; highly relevant to bootstrapping the second-object/language-conditioned task in our roadmap, if the simulation/RL infrastructure and image-to-3D pipeline can be replicated on our compute.

title: SPARR: Simulation-based Policies with Asymmetric Real-world Residuals for Assembly

claims.claim: A hybrid policy combining a simulation-trained base policy (low-level state observations, dense rewards) with a real-world residual policy (visual observations, sparse rewards, learned to compensate dynamics/sensor-noise discrepancies) achieves near-perfect success rates on real-world two-part assembly tasks, improving success rate by 38.4% and reducing cycle time by 29.7% versus SOTA zero-shot sim-to-real methods, without requiring human expertise (unlike real-world RL baselines)
claims.direction: favors sim-base-policy plus real-world visual residual-policy over pure zero-shot sim-to-real transfer or pure real-world RL, for adapting to real-world variation
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich two-part assembly tasks; requires an accurate low-level-state simulation of the specific parts for the base policy

title: FOCI Policy: Focus on Object-Centric Interactions for Relational Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: Representing skills as relative SE(3) motion between task-relevant objects (rather than predicting robot actions directly or using dense/simplistic object-centric representations), combined with automatically extracted compact interaction segments from demonstrations, yields invariance to scene configuration and robot embodiment
claims.direction: favors object-relative SE(3) action representation over robot-centric or overly dense/simplistic object-centric representations
claims.conditions: RLBench, COLOSSEUM sim benchmarks + real-world tasks; rigid relational manipulation

claims.claim: FOCI Policy achieves strong performance with substantially less training data than prior object-centric and action-centric manipulation policies
claims.direction: favors the interaction-centric inductive bias for reducing required training-demonstration count
claims.conditions: same benchmarks; qualitative 'substantially less' claim (no exact numbers given)

title: SmoLSTM: A Compact Vision-Language-Action Model with Recurrent Memory that Persists

claims.claim: A compact VLA (frozen 256M-parameter SmolVLM backbone + matrix-memory LSTM control layer, O(1) recurrent state in episode length, never reset during an episode) reaches 85.1% subgoal coverage and 77.5% full-task success on LIBERO-Mem with only 0.04B trainable parameters, surpassing the benchmark's own object-centric baseline and recent memory-based approaches; resetting the recurrent state at every control step collapses full-task success to 7.0%, showing the policy critically relies on context carried across decisions rather than only the current observation
claims.direction: strongly favors persistent recurrent memory over per-step/no-memory (or wide-observation-window) approaches for occlusion/ambiguity-prone tasks, especially in a small, compute-cheap model
claims.conditions: trained jointly on 7,461 demonstrations across 140 tasks, evaluated on held-out initial states on LIBERO-Mem and standard LIBERO (79.6% avg success), flow-matching action head predicting 10-step end-effector pose-delta+gripper chunks

why_deep_read: This uses a frozen SmolVLM backbone (closely related to our SmolVLA baseline) at only 0.04B trainable parameters -- squarely in our compute budget -- with a dramatic (77.5% vs 7.0%) ablation showing memory is critical; extremely actionable for our Q07/Q12 decisions and possibly adoptable almost directly given the backbone similarity.

title: Scaling Up and Distilling Down: Language-Guided Robot Skill Acquisition

claims.claim: Using an LLM for high-level planning plus sampling-based motion/grasp planners to auto-generate and auto-label (success/failure, with retry) large amounts of language-labelled robot demonstration data, then distilling this into a single multi-task language-conditioned diffusion-policy behavior-cloning model, improves absolute success rates by 33.2% on average across five task domains versus baselines, and the distilled policy learns the retry/recovery behavior present in its noisy data-collection procedure
claims.direction: favors auto-generated, auto-labelled (including failure/retry) demonstration data distilled into a single multi-task diffusion policy over training directly on smaller or unfiltered demonstration sets
claims.conditions: new 18-task, 5-domain benchmark testing long-horizon behavior, common-sense reasoning, tool-use, intuitive physics; sim-generated data via LLM+motion/grasp planners

title: CoinRobot: Generalized End-to-end Robotic Learning for Physical Intelligence

claims.claim: Diffusion-based models trained within a unified cross-platform framework (supporting varying sensor configurations and action spaces without task-specific modification) demonstrated superior performance and generalizability compared to the LeRobot framework, with improvements across diverse robotic platforms and environmental conditions, evaluated on seven manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors diffusion-based action modeling within a cross-platform/multi-task architecture over the (LeRobot-framework) baseline it was compared to
claims.conditions: seven manipulation tasks across multiple robotic platforms (industrial arms, collaborative arms, novel embodiments); qualitative superiority claim, no exact numbers given

title: Saliency-Aware Quantized Imitation Learning for Efficient Robotic Control

claims.claim: Saliency-Aware Quantized Imitation Learning (SQIL), which applies quantization-aware training with selective loss-weighting on mission-critical states (identified via saliency scores) to preserve decision fidelity under low-bit precision, achieves a 4-bit weight-quantized VLA model for robotic manipulation with up to 2.5x inference speedup and 2.5x energy savings on an edge GPU, with minimal accuracy loss, consistently recovering full-precision performance across simulation benchmarks, real-world tasks, and cross-domain tasks
claims.direction: favors saliency-weighted quantization-aware training over naive quantization or full-precision-only deployment, to shrink VLA policies for resource-constrained edge/laptop GPUs
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world + cross-domain (self-driving, physics sim) tasks; edge GPU deployment, 4-bit weight quantization

title: UpViTaL: Unpaired Visual-Tactile Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing unpaired (not simultaneously collected) visual and tactile self-supervised representations via an RL reward mechanism (removing the need for tactile sensors at deployment time) significantly improves manipulation success rate by more than 30% compared to existing visual-pretraining-only approaches
claims.direction: favors adding a tactile-informed auxiliary/reward signal (even from unpaired, low-cost tactile data) over visual-only pretraining, while keeping tactile sensors out of the deployed system
claims.conditions: RL-based dexterous manipulation, three tasks, low-cost unpaired visual+tactile data collected via camera + tactile gloves for training only

title: Object-centric diffusion policies for real-world robotic-arm imitation learning

claims.claim: A controlled comparison within a unified framework of CNN-MLP, transformer-patch (ViT), latent-variable (DETR+CVAE), and detector-based object-query-conditioned diffusion (DINO+CDP) policies shows that DINO-object-query-conditioned diffusion significantly improves task success rate, produces smoother trajectories, and is more robust to high-entropy (visually cluttered/organic) scenes than the other three variants, evaluated on a fully real-world manipulation dataset (no simulation or synthetic pretraining)
claims.direction: favors detector/object-query-grounded diffusion policy conditioning over pixel-level CNN-MLP, plain ViT, or CVAE-based latent-variable policies
claims.conditions: real-world robotic-arm biocell manipulation setup, comparing rigid-object baselines vs complex organic (plant) scenes measured by image entropy

claims.claim: Scene complexity (measured via image entropy) degrades standard pixel-centric models, but grounding action generation in stable DINO object-level features mitigates this degradation, giving superior robustness to high-entropy visual inputs (e.g. cluttered/organic backgrounds)
claims.direction: favors object-level (DINO-grounded) feature conditioning over raw pixel-level conditioning for background/clutter robustness
claims.conditions: real-world, comparison of rigid vs organic/complex scenes

why_deep_read: This is a direct, controlled, real-world-only comparison of exactly our Q01 action-head candidates (CNN-MLP/ViT/CVAE/diffusion) plus a Q03 vision-conditioning choice (DINO object-query), with a robustness-to-scene-complexity result relevant to our background/lighting brittleness; want the actual success-rate numbers and demo counts used per variant.

title: From Passive Observer to Active Critic: Reinforcement Learning Elicits Process Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Training a video-MLLM 'critic' via outcome-based RL (with chain-of-thought progress estimation, anchored between initial and current-state images) to evaluate task progress relative to the goal, rather than only passively recognizing events (SFT-style), achieves a 50% reduction in mean absolute error versus specialized reasoning baselines and outperforms much larger (72B-scale) general MLLMs, with strong zero-shot generalization to out-of-domain real-world humanoid failure-detection scenarios (67.0% accuracy on RoboFail, beating a closed-source model by 6.0 points)
claims.direction: favors RL-trained active process-monitoring/critic models over passive SFT-trained observers for progress/failure estimation, and shows a smaller specialized model can beat much larger general MLLMs at this specific task
claims.conditions: 7B model size (still large relative to our compute budget), evaluated on in-domain sim + out-of-domain real-world humanoid scenarios; used as an external progress/failure monitor, not the acting policy itself

title: Can Explicit Physical Feasibility Benefit VLA Learning? An Empirical Study

claims.claim: Integrating a geometry-grounded physical-feasibility objective (e.g. obstacle avoidance/kinematic feasibility) into the training stage of a diffusion-based VLA policy improves both physical reliability and overall task performance versus training without explicit feasibility supervision, using obstacle-aware manipulation as a controlled probe
claims.direction: favors adding explicit geometric feasibility supervision as an auxiliary training signal for diffusion-based VLA policies over relying on demonstrations alone to implicitly convey feasibility
claims.conditions: controlled empirical study, diffusion-based VLA policy, obstacle-aware manipulation task

claims.claim: The feasibility-supervision benefit is more pronounced in the low-data regime, enhancing learning efficiency when demonstrations are scarce
claims.direction: favors adding feasibility supervision especially when training data (demonstrations) is limited
claims.conditions: same controlled study, low-data regime explicitly tested

title: Human-Centric Transferable Tactile Pre-Training for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Pre-training on a large-scale (160-hour, 300+ task, 135k-episode) egocentric human tactile-action dataset with unified tactile/action spaces preserved through human-to-robot transfer, plus a tactile-expert-based future-tactile-prediction auxiliary objective, achieves superior performance with robust generalization and fine-grained manipulation on downstream robot tasks in simulation and real robots
claims.direction: favors large-scale human-video tactile pre-training plus future-tactile-prediction auxiliary objective over training tactile-conditioned policies from robot data alone
claims.conditions: simulation + real robot, requires tactile sensing hardware on the robot; human-to-robot transfer via unified tactile/action space

title: IMPACT: Attention Is the Interaction Map for Scalable Interaction-Aware World Model Training

claims.claim: Standard globally-averaged MSE denoising objectives for action-conditioned video/world models suffer a supervision-allocation mismatch (static background content dominates the loss, under-supervising sparse dynamic-object regions critical to interaction); reweighting denoising supervision using an attention-derived interaction map (from manipulated-object cross-attention, requiring no external representations or inference-time changes) consistently outperforms MSE-trained baselines in interaction fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality
claims.direction: favors attention-guided reweighting of the training loss toward interacted/dynamic regions over uniform MSE loss, for training world models used as auxiliary/planning components
claims.conditions: robot-arm and human-hand manipulation, multiple control modalities and DiT backbones; training-time-only change

title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces

claims.claim: A test-time guidance field derived from retrieved successful and failed rollout traces (using only a single terminal outcome bit per rollout, no other labels) can correct a frozen flow-matching action expert's velocity field without any weight update; on an ordered real-robot packing task this raises success from 21/50 (base policy) to 39/50 (TraceFlow) and to 47/50 with an additional stacking round, eliminating wrong-sequence episodes (20 down to 0); in simulation it raises RoboMemArena Sequence success from 78.92% to 91.50% and Transferring from 54.41% to 62.00%, though gains are selective (unchanged or slightly negative on some sub-metrics) and diminish with more rounds
claims.direction: favors retrieval-based test-time guidance using coarse success/failure signal over relying solely on a frozen flow-matching policy's own generation, especially for tasks with strict ordering/sequencing requirements
claims.conditions: real-robot ordered packing/stacking task + simulation (RoboMemArena); frozen flow-matching VLA, zero weight updates, requires storing a bank of past rollout traces

title: Efficient Tactile Sensing-based Learning from Limited Real-world Demonstrations for Dual-arm Fine Pinch-Grasp Skills

claims.claim: A convolutional-autoencoder-encoded tactile fusion framework enables data-efficient learning from demonstration, achieving robust bimanual fine pinch-grasping directly from few-shot demonstrations, generalizing to ten unseen new objects and remaining robust to external pushes and dropping-object perturbations; ablations on encoded tactile features confirmed the effectiveness of incorporating rich contact information
claims.direction: favors adding rich encoded tactile/contact information as an auxiliary modality over vision/proprioception alone for data-efficient (few-shot) contact-rich skill learning
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, few-shot demonstrations, requires tactile sensor hardware

title: TTF-VLA: Temporal Token Fusion via Pixel-Attention Integration for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A training-free method that selectively fuses historical and current visual tokens (via grayscale pixel-difference detection + attention-based semantic relevance, with hard fusion and keyframe anchoring to prevent error accumulation) improves VLA inference: +4.0 percentage points average on LIBERO (72.4% vs 68.4% baseline), +4.8% relative on SimplerEnv, and +8.7% relative on real robot tasks; the method is model-agnostic, working across OpenVLA and VLA-Cache architectures, and reveals that selective attention Query-matrix reuse enhances rather than compromises performance
claims.direction: favors selective temporal token fusion (using observation history) over frame-by-frame independent processing, as a zero-training-cost addition
claims.conditions: LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and real robot tasks; training-free, model-agnostic across VLA architectures

title: Data Augmentation for Instruction Following Policies via Trajectory Segmentation

claims.claim: Play Segmentation (PS), a probabilistic model that extracts labelled instruction-trajectory segments (of varying length) from large unannotated 'play' trajectory datasets, augments a small annotated instruction-trajectory dataset such that a downstream imitation-learning policy trained with PS-labelled segments matches the performance of a policy trained on twice the amount of manually labelled data; randomly sampled (unsegmented) segments instead diminish performance
claims.direction: favors semi-supervised segmentation of abundant unlabeled play data over collecting more manually-labelled instruction-trajectory pairs, and over naive random segmentation
claims.conditions: a game environment and a simulated robotic gripper setting; semi-supervised setup with small labelled + large unlabelled trajectory sets

title: Instrumentation for Better Demonstrations: A Case Study

claims.claim: Instrumenting a task object (a squeeze bottle) with a pressure sensor to enable automated, PI-controller-driven data collection produces demonstrations on which Transformer-based policies outperform policies trained on human-teleoperated demonstrations in 78% of cases
claims.direction: favors automated, sensor-instrumented demonstration collection over human teleoperation for demonstration quality, at least for this task
claims.conditions: real robot, liquid-dispensing task with an instrumented squeeze bottle (pressure sensor) enabling closed-loop automated data collection

title: ReconVLA: An Uncertainty-Guided and Failure-Aware Vision-Language-Action Framework for Robotic Control

claims.claim: Applying conformal prediction directly to a pretrained VLA's action-token outputs (and extending it to the robot state space to flag outlier/unsafe states) yields calibrated uncertainty estimates that correlate with execution quality and task success, consistently improving failure anticipation and reducing catastrophic errors across simulation and real-robot manipulation tasks, without retraining or modifying the underlying VLA
claims.direction: favors adding a post-hoc, training-free conformal-prediction uncertainty/failure-detection layer over relying on the base VLA's own (uncalibrated) confidence
claims.conditions: sim + real robot, diverse manipulation tasks; wraps around any pretrained VLA with no retraining

title: Overcoming Visual Clutter in Vision Language Action Models via Concept-Gated Visual Distillation

claims.claim: A training-free, model-agnostic inference-time framework (Concept-Gated Visual Distillation) that parses instructions into safe/distractor sets, refines the true target via cross-validation and spatial disambiguation, and applies Fourier-based inpainting to suppress background/distractor semantic noise while preserving spatial geometry, prevents performance collapse in highly cluttered manipulation scenes, achieving 77.5% success versus 43.0% for the state-of-the-art baseline in environments with dense semantic distractors
claims.direction: favors training-free, inference-time visual-clutter suppression (targeted inpainting of distractors) over relying on the base VLA's learned robustness to background clutter
claims.conditions: highly cluttered manipulation tasks with dense semantic distractors; no retraining/fine-tuning required, model-agnostic

why_deep_read: A large (77.5% vs 43.0%), training-free improvement targeting exactly our background/distractor and lighting robustness failure mode is extremely attractive given our compute constraints; want implementation detail on the Fourier-inpainting step's runtime cost relative to our tight inference budget.

title: V-Dreamer: Automating Robotic Simulation and Trajectory Synthesis via Video Generation Priors

claims.claim: A fully automated pipeline that generates physically-grounded 3D scenes (via LLMs + 3D generative models with geometric validation) and executable expert trajectories (via video-generation motion priors mapped to robot trajectories through a Sim-to-Gen visual-kinematic alignment module) from natural-language instructions alone, with no manual asset creation or heuristics, produces training data on which imitation-learning policies robustly generalize to unseen objects in simulation and achieve effective sim-to-real transfer to novel real-world objects
claims.direction: favors fully automated language-to-scene-to-trajectory synthetic data generation over manual simulation asset creation or real-world teleoperated data collection, for object generalization
