claims.conditions: tabletop manipulation, Piper robotic arm, sim-to-real transfer evaluated on real novel objects

title: GeoAlign: Beyond Semantics with State-Guided Spatial Alignment in VLA Models

claims.claim: Post-training an RGB geometry branch with robot-domain RGB-D supervision (producing RGB-derived Geometry-Enhanced Post-Trained features), then querying this feature grid with the robot's proprioceptive state to produce compact phase-dependent geometry tokens for action prediction, achieves 99.0% success on LIBERO, 85.3% across three SimplerEnv-Fractal tasks, and 78.8% on eight geometry-critical real-world ALOHA tasks, with ablations confirming both the geometry post-training and the proprioceptive-state-guided querying each contribute to these gains
claims.direction: favors RGB-D-supervised geometry-feature post-training plus state-guided geometry querying over semantics-only VLA grounding, for geometry-critical manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world ALOHA platform (8 geometry-critical tasks) + LIBERO + SimplerEnv-Fractal sim benchmarks; requires RGB-D supervision during post-training (matches our RealSense depth availability)

title: One Demo is Worth a Thousand Trajectories: Action-View Augmentation for Visuomotor Policies

claims.claim: From real-world eye-in-hand (wrist-camera) demonstrations captured with a single fisheye camera on a portable gripper, a Gaussian-Splatting formulation adapted to wide-FoV fisheye cameras reconstructs and edits the 3D scene (inserting unseen objects/obstacles), and trajectory optimization generates smooth, collision-free, view-rendering-friendly action trajectories with rendered novel-view visual observations; this augmentation improves success rate for manipulation tasks both in the original scene and in augmented scenes with new obstacles requiring collision avoidance
claims.direction: favors synthesizing new wrist-camera (eye-in-hand)視 views and trajectories from very few real demonstrations over collecting many additional real teleoperated demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world + simulation, portable parallel gripper with single fisheye wrist camera; requires 3D scene reconstruction/editing pipeline at training time (not inference)

title: FutureRTC: Real-Time Robot Execution with Anticipatory-Conditioned Action Chunking

claims.claim: Asynchronous execution of action-chunked VLA policies (computing the next chunk while executing the current one) causes prediction-execution misalignment and inter-chunk discontinuities; a plug-and-play framework (FutureRTC) that predicts execution-time proprioceptive states (via a state-correction module) and execution-time visual observations (via motion-aware feature transport using robot motion as a physical prior), combined with a policy-consistency loss aligning chunks generated from predicted vs actual execution-time inputs, achieves superior robustness to inference delays, smoother trajectories, faster execution, and consistently higher task success rates, without modifying the underlying policy
claims.direction: favors explicitly forecasting execution-time observations/states to condition the next action chunk over naively re-planning from stale (pre-execution) observations or only smoothing chunk boundaries post-hoc
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world environments; plug-and-play, does not require retraining/modifying the base VLA policy

why_deep_read: This is close to a direct match for our stated problem ('jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries with async inference'); a plug-and-play, no-retraining fix would be immediately testable on our SmolVLA setup, so the full paper's quantitative smoothness/latency numbers are high priority to review.

title: CounterAlign: Counterfactual Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Successful expert demonstrations alone (without any additional rollouts, curated non-expert data, or external reward annotation) can be transformed into dense corrective supervision by pairing expert actions with mismatched alternative language instructions to synthesize counterfactual instruction-observation-action tuples, then training an instruction-grounded reward model via adversarial discriminator training for offline RL
claims.direction: favors extracting denser (positive+negative) supervision from the same existing demonstrations over collecting additional demonstrations or curated non-expert data, in data-constrained VLA training
claims.conditions: offline RL applied on top of standard BC-trained VLA, no additional rollouts/annotations collected

claims.claim: On the robustness-focused LIBERO-PRO benchmark, this method improves robustness to object-position and task perturbations over a strong SOTA baseline, and outperforms competitive baselines in real-robot experiments on the TX-G2 platform
claims.direction: favors counterfactual-instruction-based corrective training for robustness to object-position/task perturbations over standard BC alone
claims.conditions: LIBERO-PRO (robustness benchmark) + real robot (TX-G2 / AGIBot G2 compatible)

title: Learning Sparse Control Tasks from Pixels by Latent Nearest-Neighbor-Guided Explorations

claims.claim: Learning an embedded neural dynamics model from a few demonstrations, then rewarding an RL agent for staying close (in embedding space) to demonstrated trajectories, achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency for sparse-reward, vision-based manipulation in simulation and enables efficient training on a real Franka Emika Panda manipulator using only a few demonstrations
claims.direction: favors combining a few demonstrations with embedding-space-guided exploration/reward over pure RL exploration or pure BC, for sample-efficient learning from very few demos
claims.conditions: real Franka Emika Panda + simulation, sparse-reward manipulation tasks, few demonstrations used to shape exploration rather than direct BC training

title: Admittance Visuomotor Policy Learning for General-Purpose Contact-Rich Manipulations

claims.claim: A diffusion-based policy that jointly plans action trajectories and desired contact forces from multimodal observations (contact force + vision + proprioception), executed via an admittance controller, achieves the highest success rate versus two SOTA methods across five contact-rich manipulation tasks, reducing required contact force by 48.8% on average and increasing success rate by 15.3% on average
claims.direction: favors adding force as an explicit auxiliary modality/prediction target (with compliant admittance execution) over vision+proprioception-only diffusion policies for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real robot, low-cost teleoperation system with contact interaction for demonstration collection, 5 tasks with different action primitives; requires force sensing and an admittance controller

title: Cross-Platform Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models from Edge to Cloud GPUs

claims.claim: Evaluating five representative VLA models (SOTA baselines + two new architectures) on LIBERO across edge and datacenter GPU platforms shows architectural choices such as action tokenization scheme and model backbone size strongly influence throughput and memory footprint, that power-constrained edge devices exhibit non-linear performance degradation (some edge configurations match or exceed older datacenter GPUs), and that high-throughput model variants can be achieved without significant accuracy loss
claims.direction: challenges the assumption that datacenter-class hardware is required for good VLA throughput/accuracy; favors carefully chosen architecture/tokenization over simply reaching for bigger hardware
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, measured latency/throughput/peak memory under varying edge power constraints vs datacenter GPU configurations

title: PolicyTrim: Boosting Intrinsic Policy Efficiency of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Current VLA policies suffer from planning unreliability (severe prediction degradation at the tail of action chunks) and action redundancy (unnecessarily redundant physical steps); an RL-based post-training framework (PolicyTrim) that rewards successful completion of longer executable chunk lengths and penalizes redundant steps improves action-chunk utilization by 3x and reduces physical execution steps by 51.4% across three benchmarks and three VLA models, delivering up to a 5.83x end-to-end deployment speedup without compromising task success rates
claims.direction: favors RL post-training to extend reliable action-chunk execution length and eliminate redundant steps over using a fixed, conservatively-short executable chunk length
claims.conditions: three benchmarks, three different VLA models, post-training-only (no architecture change)

title: JEPA-WAM: Connecting Generated Visual Instructions to World Action Models through JEPA Latent Representations

claims.claim: Augmenting sparse text-instruction conditioning with a bank of stochastically generated visual-goal images (from an off-the-shelf, untrained text-to-image generator, encoded via a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder into compact goal tokens that cross-attend into both video and action experts) improves instruction-grounding, achieving 87.3%/74.5%/80.9% success on a real-robot benchmark across in-distribution, out-of-distribution-scene, and out-of-distribution-instruction settings respectively, outperforming pi0 and Fast-WAM by at least 10.0/27.3/14.5 percentage points
claims.direction: favors grounding language instructions via generated visual-goal references (even if imperfectly matched to the true scene) over relying on sparse text-only conditioning or matching visual context alone
claims.conditions: real-robot instruction-following benchmark with explicit in-distribution / OOD-scene / OOD-instruction splits; goal-image generator is frozen/off-the-shelf, not trained

title: OmniGuide: Universal Guidance Fields for Enhancing Generalist Robot Policies

claims.claim: Arbitrary external guidance sources (3D foundation models, semantic-reasoning VLMs, human pose models) can be expressed as differentiable energy functions with task-specific attractors/repellers in 3D space that steer VLA action sampling at inference time; this significantly improves success and safety rates of state-of-the-art generalist policies (pi_0.5, GR00T N1.6) across diverse guidance sources in both simulation and real-world experiments, matching or surpassing prior methods designed for one specific guidance source
claims.direction: favors a unified, flexible test-time guidance-field framework (compatible with diffusion/flow-matching sampling) over training task-specific guidance mechanisms individually, for improving complex spatial/semantic manipulation performance
claims.conditions: sim + real-world, applied on top of existing large generalist VLA policies (pi_0.5, GR00T N1.6), inference-time only (frozen base policy)

title: Physical AI: The Convergence of Foundation Models, Sim-to-Real Transfer, and Embodied Intelligence

claims.claim: This survey's mathematical comparison of Diffusion Policy versus Flow Matching states that Flow Matching achieves roughly 10x faster inference (100+ Hz) than diffusion policies, through the use of deterministic ODE solvers
claims.direction: favors flow matching over diffusion-based action heads for inference speed
claims.conditions: survey-level claim (secondary source), not an original controlled experiment; no task-success-rate comparison given

title: TCAM for Autonomous Deformable Manipulation: The RMC2 Champion System for WBCD 2026 Track 4

claims.claim: Combining portable UMI-style demonstrations (broad manipulation priors) with real-robot demonstrations (deployment-specific dynamics), plus a closed-loop process that analyzes each trajectory's outcome to drive targeted data recollection and policy fine-tuning, enabled a fully autonomous champion-winning system (25 T-shirts loaded, ~23s/attempt, 22 meeting surface-smoothness criteria) on a real deformable-manipulation competition task
claims.direction: favors mixing portable/handheld demonstration devices with real-robot demonstrations and closed-loop targeted data recollection over a single static demonstration source
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot (ARX X5), wrist-centric four-camera setup (fisheye + close-range RGB), contact-rich deformable-object task, competition setting

claims.claim: A wrist-centric four-camera setup (upper fisheye cameras for task-level context, lower RGB cameras for close-range gripper-object contact observation) was used to provide both broad context and fine-grained contact observation for a multi-view VLA backbone predicting 30-step end-effector delta-pose action chunks
claims.direction: favors combining a wide-context wrist/task view with a close-range contact-observation view over a single wrist camera
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, deformable fabric manipulation

title: Localized Visual Feature Aggregation via Focus Pooling for Visuomotor Policies

claims.claim: FocusPool, an attention pooling module that selectively aggregates intermediate CNN-encoded visual features according to their relevance to the robot's current proprioceptive context (rather than cropping control/object-centric regions as input preprocessing, or using standard pooling), improves policy success rates over standard pooling and explicit local-focus-cropping methods by 36.2% and 41.2% respectively, across simulation and real-world experiments, while training only 5.8% of the encoder's parameters
claims.direction: favors proprioception-conditioned attention pooling over intermediate CNN features over either standard global pooling or explicit input-cropping for control-relevant visual focus
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world visuomotor policy experiments; CNN-based vision encoder, very parameter-efficient (5.8% of encoder trained)

title: MILES: Making Imitation Learning Easy with Self-Supervision

claims.claim: MILES, a fully autonomous self-supervised data collection paradigm that autonomously learns to return to and then follow a single human demonstration (with only a single environment reset, no further human intervention), significantly outperforms state-of-the-art imitation-learning-plus-reinforcement-learning alternatives on several real-world tasks, including precise contact-rich manipulation (e.g. locking a lock with a key), under the constraint of a single demonstration and no repeated environment resetting
claims.direction: favors autonomous self-supervised practice/data-collection from a single demonstration over collecting many additional human demonstrations or requiring repeated manual environment resets
claims.conditions: real-world tasks, single demonstration, single environment reset, no further human supervision during data collection/policy improvement

title: OPG-Policy: Occluded Push-Grasp Policy Learning with Amodal Segmentation

claims.claim: Predicting occluded portions of a target object via a dedicated amodal-segmentation module, and using the resulting amodal masks plus scene observations to learn a push-grasp motion critic via deep Q-learning, outperforms baseline methods in success rate and motion efficiency for retrieving partially-observed (occluded) targets in dense clutter, in both simulation and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors explicit amodal (occlusion-aware) segmentation as an intermediate representation over policies that only use partially-observed/visible segments directly
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, dense clutter with occluded targets, push-grasp motion primitives via deep Q-learning (not end-to-end BC)

title: VADiff: Velocity Aware Diffusion Policy for Grasping Moving Objects with Humanoid Robots

claims.claim: Explicitly incorporating robot joint velocities and target-object speed into the diffusion policy's conditioning (joint position-velocity modeling), instead of relying only on static observations as prior methods (e.g. RDT) do, yields superior task success rate, faster response, and smoother trajectory generation for time-sensitive dynamic manipulation (conveyor-based object picking)
claims.direction: favors explicit velocity-aware conditioning (position+velocity) over static-observation-only (position-only) diffusion policy conditioning for dynamic/moving-object tasks
claims.conditions: humanoid robot, conveyor-based object picking, hybrid teleoperation + MuJoCo simulation data collection

title: EgoDemoGen: Egocentric Demonstration Generation for Viewpoint Generalization in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: EgoDemoGen synthesizes paired observation-action demonstrations under novel egocentric (camera-mounted) viewpoints by jointly transferring the robot action trajectory into the new coordinate frame (geometry-aware transformation + IK filtering) and generating a matching photorealistic observation video (conditional video generation fusing a reprojected scene video and a rendered robot-motion video, trained self-supervised without needing multi-viewpoint data)
claims.direction: favors synthesizing new paired egocentric viewpoint+action demonstrations from existing single-viewpoint data over collecting additional multi-viewpoint real demonstrations
claims.conditions: self-supervised training (no multi-viewpoint data required); evaluated in both simulation and real-world

claims.claim: Policies trained with EgoDemoGen-augmented data show consistently improved success rates under both standard and novel egocentric viewpoints: absolute gains of +24.6% and +16.9% in simulation, and +16.0% and +23.0% on the real robot
claims.direction: favors egocentric viewpoint-augmentation over training only on the original fixed-viewpoint demonstrations, for camera-viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation, evaluated separately on standard vs novel egocentric viewpoints

title: Grounding Actions in Camera Space: Observation-Centric Vision-Language-Action Policy

claims.claim: Predicting end-effector poses in the camera coordinate frame (via the camera's extrinsic calibration matrix transforming robot-base-frame poses into camera space), rather than the conventional robot-base-frame prediction target, is a lightweight, plug-and-play strategy fully compatible with existing VLA architectures (no substantial modification needed) that unifies prediction targets across heterogeneous training viewpoints
claims.direction: favors camera-space (observation-centric) action grounding over robot-base-frame action grounding, to align perception and action space
claims.conditions: comprehensive sim + real-world manipulation evaluations, plug-and-play addition to existing VLA architectures

claims.claim: OC-VLA accelerates convergence, enhances task success rates, and improves cross-view (camera viewpoint) generalization compared to standard robot-base-frame action prediction
claims.direction: favors camera-space action grounding for camera-viewpoint robustness/generalization
claims.conditions: sim + real-world manipulation tasks with viewpoint variation

title: AugVLA-3D: Depth-Driven Feature Augmentation for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Extracting geometry-aware 3D cues from standard RGB inputs via a depth-estimation model (VGGT), constrained by an 'action assistant' module that enforces consistency with downstream control tasks, then fusing these enhanced 3D features with conventional 2D visual tokens, significantly improves the generalization ability, robustness, and action-prediction accuracy of VLA models, especially in geometrically ambiguous scenarios
claims.direction: favors fusing depth/3D-derived features (estimated or measured) alongside 2D visual tokens over 2D-only VLA conditioning
claims.conditions: depth features derived from RGB via monocular depth estimation (VGGT), not necessarily requiring a physical depth sensor; qualitative 'significantly improves' claim without exact numbers

title: AdaWorldPolicy: World-Model-Driven Diffusion Policy with Online Adaptive Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A unified framework interconnecting a world model, an action expert, and a force predictor (all Flow Matching Diffusion Transformers, exchanging features via multi-modal self-attention) with an Online Adaptive Learning strategy that dynamically switches between Action Generation and Future Imagination modes achieves state-of-the-art performance on simulated and real-robot benchmarks, with dynamic adaptive capacity to out-of-distribution scenarios and minimal-human-involvement online adaptation to visual and physical domain shifts
claims.direction: favors an online-adaptive, world-model-coupled flow-matching policy over a static (train-once) flow-matching or diffusion policy, for adapting to visual/physical domain shift at deployment time
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot benchmarks; includes a force-torque predictor module (implies force sensing) alongside the visual world model and action expert

title: TrAct: Bridging Robot Control and Visual Prediction with Visual Tracks

claims.claim: Using embodiment-agnostic visual tracks (dense image-space point trajectories) as an intermediate interface between a joint action-and-track prediction model (VLAT), a track-conditioned world model (TWM) that rolls out visual consequences, and a vision-language reward model (VLAC) that selects the best candidate action-track pair, improves task success from 27% to 55% in simulation (LIBERO-INTEGRAL) and from 49% to 76% on real-world Franka manipulation, compared with the strong VLA baseline pi_0.5; the track-conditioned world model also consistently improves video-prediction quality over an action-conditioned world model
claims.direction: favors visual-track-conditioned world modeling plus test-time candidate selection (predict multiple action-track pairs, roll out, select by predicted-outcome reward) over directly executing a single VLA-predicted action, for grounding control in accurate future-outcome prediction
claims.conditions: real-world Franka manipulation + LIBERO-INTEGRAL sim benchmark; adds test-time compute for candidate rollout and selection

title: Visual-Haptic Fusion for Contact-Rich Robot Skill Transfer via Diffusion Models

claims.claim: A controlled comparison on 387 real-world contact-rich assembly demonstrations shows a vision-force diffusion-based policy achieves 87.3% success, versus Diffusion Policy 78.6%, Action Chunking Transformer 73.9%, and Behavior Cloning 62.3% (a 25-percentage-point improvement over the BC baseline); ablations show vision-only reaches 67.8% and force-only 59.1%, and attention-based multimodal fusion outperforms linear-weight fusion by 8.2 percentage points; the approach maintains 78.4% success under added force-sensor noise and 75.8% under vision impairment, with 3.09s inference time
claims.direction: favors diffusion-based action generation with attention-based multimodal (vision+haptic) fusion over Diffusion-Policy-vision-only, ACT, or plain BC, and shows graceful degradation under single-modality sensor impairment
claims.conditions: 387 real-world demonstrations, collaborative robot with RGB-D cameras + force sensors, industrial contact-rich assembly tasks; requires force-sensing hardware we do not have

claims.claim: Cross-task generalization experiments show consistent performance above 86% across geometric variations of the assembly task
claims.direction: favors the multimodal (vision+force) diffusion approach for geometric-variation generalization
claims.conditions: same real-world assembly setup, geometric task variants

title: Task-Mix Entropy and the Economics of Robotic Generality: A Case Against Vision-Language-Action Models as the Default for Narrow Industrial Manipulation

claims.claim: On six industrial tasks, small task-specialist policies achieve 96.4% success versus 88.6% for a fine-tuned 7B VLA, at 24% lower cost per successful cycle and one-tenth the adaptation compute; the paper derives a break-even point (~2.4 bits of task-mix instruction entropy) above which a large generalist VLA outperforms specialists (83.0% vs 61.4% in a 40-variant regime)
claims.direction: favors small task-specialist policies over large (7B) generalist VLA models specifically for low task-mix-entropy (narrow, few-variant) industrial tasks like ours, with generalists only winning once task diversity/entropy is high
claims.conditions: working paper, NOT peer-reviewed, six industrial tasks; the source venue (a 'Technische Universitat Eisenfeld' working-paper series) could not be verified as an established academic institution, so this claim should be treated with caution despite being directly on-topic

why_deep_read: Not selected for deep read primarily due to unverified/unclear source credibility (apparently unreviewed working paper from an unfamiliar institution); flagged here because the claim (specialist beats 7B VLA on narrow low-entropy tasks like ours) is directly on-topic and would be worth corroborating from a more established source before relying on it.

title: Efficient Imitation Learning with Conservative World Models

claims.claim: Reframing imitation learning as a fine-tuning problem (rather than pure RL or adversarial IL, which need extra on-policy samples) with a principled conservative optimization bound over a learned world model sets a new state-of-the-art on the Franka Kitchen environment from raw pixel observations using only 10 demonstrations and no reward labels, and also solves a complex dexterity manipulation task
claims.direction: favors conservative world-model-based fine-tuning over adversarial imitation learning or naive online world-model RL, especially for extremely low demonstration counts
claims.conditions: high-dimensional raw pixel observations, only 10 demonstrations, no reward function; Franka Kitchen environment plus a separate complex dexterity task

title: Visuomotor Policy Learning for Task Automation of Surgical Robot

claims.claim: A hybrid model (ACMT) integrating state-space models (Mamba), transformer attention, and conditional variational autoencoders for sequential action modeling achieves 75-100% success rate with just 100 demonstrations for most surgical automation tasks
claims.direction: favors a Mamba+transformer+CVAE hybrid sequential-modeling architecture for achieving high success with a demonstration count in the same order of magnitude as ours (~100)
claims.conditions: real-world surgical robot tasks, end-to-end visual imitation learning, ~100 demonstrations per task

title: 3DFlowAction: Learning Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from 3D Flow World Model

claims.claim: Learning a 3D optical-flow world model (predicting future 3D movement of interacting objects, trained on a large synthesized 3D-flow dataset, ManiFlow-110k, from both human and robot manipulation videos via a video-diffusion-based model) provides an embodiment-agnostic action-planning signal; using predicted 3D flow as optimization constraints for a chunk of robot actions, plus a flow-guided rendering + GPT-4o closed-loop check, demonstrates strong generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks and reliable cross-embodiment adaptation without any hardware-specific training
claims.direction: favors a 3D-flow (object-motion-in-3D-space) world-model representation, learned jointly from human and robot video, as an embodiment-agnostic intermediate action-planning signal over directly regressing embodiment-specific actions
claims.conditions: synthesized large-scale 3D optical flow dataset (human+robot video), cross-embodiment evaluation without hardware-specific fine-tuning; qualitative 'strong generalization' claim

title: Mobi-π: Mobilizing Your Robot Learning Policy

claims.claim: Manipulation policies trained on data from a limited set of robot base positions/camera viewpoints generalize poorly to novel robot/camera positions; rather than retraining the policy to be robust to unseen viewpoints (which needs additional demonstrations), optimizing the robot's base pose (via 3D Gaussian Splatting novel-view synthesis, a pose-suitability score function, and sampling-based optimization) to align with an in-distribution viewpoint for the existing policy outperforms baselines in both a simulated benchmark and the real world, without requiring additional demonstrations
claims.direction: favors repositioning the camera/robot to an in-distribution viewpoint (decoupling navigation from manipulation) over retraining the manipulation policy itself to handle novel viewpoints
claims.conditions: mobile manipulation, simulated RoboCasa-based task suite + real-world experiments; requires a mobile base (not directly applicable to a fixed-base arm, but relevant context on viewpoint sensitivity)

title: Endogenous Spatial Perception for Vision-Language-Action Models via Monocular 3D Reconstruction

claims.claim: A pluggable spatial encoder that leverages 3D-reconstruction priors learned from multi-view RGB (no deployment-time depth sensor needed), fused with semantic visual/language representations through a Diffusion Transformer for action generation, achieves 93.4% average success on BridgeData V2 and 87.4% on GM-100 (best average across multiple benchmarks), with the largest gains on tasks requiring precise spatial understanding (versus SpatialVLA, PI0, and GROOT-N1); real-world evaluations were conducted on SO-101, WidowX, and AgileX Cobot Magic
claims.direction: favors a monocular-RGB-derived, world-grounded 3D spatial representation (avoiding egocentric-coordinate drift and not requiring a physical depth sensor at deployment) over depth-camera-based or purely egocentric-coordinate VLA spatial reasoning
claims.conditions: LIBERO, BridgeData V2, GM-100 sim benchmarks PLUS real-world evaluation directly on SO-101 (our exact robot platform), WidowX, and AgileX Cobot Magic

why_deep_read: This paper evaluates directly on the SO-101 robot (our exact platform) and claims the best average performance across benchmarks with the largest gains on spatially-demanding tasks, using only monocular RGB reconstruction (no depth sensor required at deployment, though we do have a RealSense); this is one of the most directly transferable papers in the batch and should be read in full for implementation details and SO-101-specific numbers.

title: Industrial Dexterity Benchmark: A Hardware-Software Benchmarking Platform for Industrial Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: On a cable-cleaning manipulation task (48 trials per configuration), a multimodal Diffusion Policy using a multi-view RGB image source passed through an R3M encoder (fused with point clouds, joint positions, and wrist-frame wrench data) reaches a 78% grasp-and-insert combined success rate, a significant improvement over the 36% observed from a single-camera RGB Diffusion Policy baseline
claims.direction: favors multi-view camera input (over single-camera) for a diffusion policy on precision industrial manipulation, and validates R3M as a usable vision encoder in this multimodal setup
claims.conditions: real-world industrial dexterity benchmark (datacenter cable management task), diffusion policy with R3M encoder, point cloud, and wrench inputs; approximately 100 teleoperated demonstrations per task phase (matching our data budget)

title: A1: A Fully Transparent Open-Source, Adaptive and Efficient Truncated Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: A budget-aware adaptive inference scheme that monitors action consistency across intermediate VLM layers to trigger early termination of the backbone, combined with Inter-Layer Truncated Flow Matching that warm-starts the denoising process across layers (enabling accurate actions with substantially fewer effective denoising iterations), achieves up to 72% lower per-episode latency for flow-matching inference and up to 76.6% backbone computation reduction, with only minor performance degradation; A1 achieves state-of-the-art success on RoboChallenge (29.00% average) outperforming pi0 (28.33%), X-VLA (21.33%), and RDT-1B (15.00%)
claims.direction: favors adaptive early-termination plus warm-started (truncated) flow-matching denoising over running the full VLM backbone and full multi-step denoising at every inference step, to cut latency with minimal accuracy cost
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, VLABench) + real robots (Franka, AgiBot); fully open-source training stack (code, data pipeline, checkpoints) released for reproducibility

why_deep_read: This is one of the most directly actionable papers for our stated ~2s inference latency problem: a 72% per-episode latency reduction with minor degradation, fully open-sourced (code, data pipeline, checkpoints), tested on real robots including Franka; extremely high priority to read the implementation details for adapting to our SmolVLA/flow-matching setup on an 8GB GPU.

title: CAST: Counterfactual Labels Improve Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Augmenting existing robot datasets with counterfactual language labels (generated by vision-language models, without any additional data collection) increases the diversity and granularity of language grounding, significantly improving instruction-following in VLA policies and doubling the success rate compared to VLAs trained on unaugmented data on vision-language navigation experiments across 3 environments; a similar performance gain is found for manipulation VLAs on tasks with distractors
claims.direction: favors VLM-generated counterfactual instruction relabeling of existing demonstrations over collecting additional demonstrations, for improving fine-grained language-following
claims.conditions: vision-language navigation (3 indoor/outdoor environments) + manipulation VLA evaluation with distractors; no additional data collection required, only relabeling

title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A generalist robotic value model built on a world-model backbone (rather than a VLM backbone, which lacks temporal modeling) achieves state-of-the-art Value-Order Correlation on standard (expert-only) benchmarks and remains robust on a new Suboptimal-Value-Bench (800 human-labeled suboptimal trajectories across multiple embodiments), and improves manipulation performance across various policy-extraction approaches in both simulated and real-world deployment when used to assess/guide learning from mixed-quality data
claims.direction: favors world-model-based value estimation (versus VLM-backbone value models) for assessing and leveraging mixed-quality (including suboptimal) demonstration data
claims.conditions: sim + real-world deployment, multiple policy-extraction approaches, evaluated on both expert-only and suboptimal-trajectory benchmarks

title: Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via Flow-Matching World Modeling

claims.claim: An action-conditioned flow-matching world model that scores inverse-transport nonconformity of observed short-horizon visual dynamics (with conformal calibration on successful executions only, no failure demonstrations needed) detects visual-action inconsistencies indicating failure; across four manipulation tasks with twenty failure modes, the wrist-camera view achieved the strongest failure-detection performance, including a 96.6% detection rate at a 1.3% false-alarm rate
claims.direction: favors the wrist camera view (over other camera views) as the most informative signal for detecting execution failures via world-model-based nonconformity scoring
claims.conditions: surgical robot (da Vinci Research Kit), simulation + real-world, no failure demonstrations required for training, only successful executions for calibration

title: UMI-Bridge: Action-Anchored Latent Alignment across Human and Robot Manipulation Data

claims.claim: Using handheld UMI demonstrations as an intermediate domain to align human and robot manipulation representations by action equivalence (end-effector motion/gripper behavior, via a frozen wrist-teacher dual-view latent action model) rather than pixel similarity achieves 91.7% mean success across three real-robot tasks versus 73.3% for naive co-training with matched UMI+robot data; on two data-efficiency tasks it matches a full-data robot-only baseline while using only 25% of the robot demonstrations (plus UMI data); it also reaches 85% and 90% success on two further tasks learned entirely from UMI demonstrations with zero task-specific robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors action-anchored (motion-equivalence-based) latent alignment between human/UMI and robot data over naive co-training or pixel-level alignment, to cut required robot demonstration count
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks, requires collecting UMI (handheld gripper) demonstrations in addition to/instead of robot teleoperation; wrist-camera/dual-view setup

why_deep_read: A 4x reduction in required robot demonstrations (25% of full data matching full-data performance) directly targets our Q13 constraint, and the fact that 2 tasks reached 85-90% success from UMI-only data (zero task-specific robot demos) suggests this could let us bootstrap our second object/task far more cheaply; want to check UMI hardware requirements and compatibility with our SO-101 gripper geometry.

title: RwoR: Generating Robot Demonstrations from Human Hand Collection for Policy Learning without Robot

claims.claim: A hand-to-gripper generative model, trained on a self-collected paired human-hand/UMI-gripper dataset, translates human-hand demonstrations (captured with a wrist-mounted GoPro fisheye camera, no robot needed) into synthesized robot gripper demonstrations with automatically extracted SE(3) actions, and the resulting robot policy shows robust manipulation performance, demonstrating both the quality of generated demonstrations and the practicality of this robot-free data collection method
claims.direction: favors collecting only human-hand video (no robot/teleoperation hardware) plus a generative hand-to-gripper translation model over standard teleoperation for demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-robot deployment evaluated after training only on generated (human-video-derived) demonstrations; requires training a separate hand-to-gripper generative model on paired data first

title: D2E: Scaling Vision-Action Pretraining on Desktop Data for Transfer to Embodied AI

claims.claim: A 1B-parameter model pretrained on desktop/gaming interaction data (1.3K+ hours: 259 hours human demonstrations + 1K+ hours pseudo-labeled gameplay) achieves 96.6% success on LIBERO manipulation and 83.3% on CANVAS navigation, matching or surpassing models up to 7x larger such as pi0 (3.3B) and OpenVLA (7B)
claims.direction: favors a smaller model with abundant, cheap desktop-interaction pretraining data over a larger model trained mainly on scarcer physical robot trajectories, for matching downstream manipulation performance
claims.conditions: desktop/gaming pretraining data (unified via an OWA toolkit + Generalist-IDM for zero-shot cross-game pseudo-labeling) transferred via VAPT to physical manipulation and navigation; evaluated on LIBERO and CANVAS

title: Failure-Aware RL: Reliable Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Self-Recovery for Real-World Manipulation

claims.claim: Integrating a world-model-based safety critic with an offline-trained recovery policy into offline-to-online RL post-training reduces Intervention-requiring Failures by 73.1% while improving task performance by 11.3% on average during real-world RL post-training
claims.direction: favors combining a world-model safety critic with a dedicated recovery policy over standard offline-to-online RL post-training without explicit failure-awareness, for reducing costly real-world failures
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, RL-based post-training (not pure BC); requires a benchmark of failure scenarios (FailureBench) for evaluation

title: GaussianWAM: Distilling Geometry and Semantics from 3D Gaussian Fields into World-Action Models

claims.claim: Organizing depth, camera geometry, and dense semantic features (from frozen geometry and vision foundation models, given synchronized multi-view observations) through a shared 3D Gaussian field, and distilling the resulting spatially-aligned semantic/depth/coverage targets into a World-Action Model's current-observation representations at training time only (all teacher models and Gaussian components removed after training, leaving the original inference path unchanged), improves FastWAM on LIBERO-Plus from 52.05% to 71.29% and Cosmos Policy from 71.52% to 77.30%, with the Gaussian-field unification adding further improvement (69.37% to 71.29%) over direct CLIP/VGGT distillation alone
claims.direction: favors training-time-only, geometry-and-semantics-unified 3D Gaussian-field distillation into WAM representations over either no geometric supervision or unstructured (non-unified) multi-teacher distillation, with zero added inference-time cost or architecture change
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus + standard LIBERO + positive transfer trends on RoboTwin and real-world manipulation; requires synchronized multi-view observations during training only

title: Tactile Modality Fusion for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: TacFiLM, a lightweight post-training finetuning approach that conditions intermediate visual features on pretrained tactile representations via feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), shows consistent improvements in success rate, task performance, completion time, and force stability across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution insertion and drawer-opening tasks, without the complexity of token concatenation or large-scale tactile pretraining
claims.direction: favors lightweight FiLM-based tactile-conditioning of visual features over token-concatenation-based tactile fusion or large-scale tactile pretraining, for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot insertion and drawer-opening tasks; requires tactile sensor hardware; post-training/finetuning stage only

title: ELASTIC: Efficiently Learning to Adaptively Scale Test-Time Compute for Generative Control Policies

claims.claim: A learned meta-policy that adaptively allocates test-time compute between sequential scaling (more denoising steps) and parallel scaling (more candidate action samples) at each denoising iteration, state-dependently, Pareto-dominates fixed and single-axis test-time-compute-scaling baselines at matched compute budgets across simulated diffusion-policy manipulation benchmarks; on real-world manipulation with the pi_0.5 VLA model, it matches best-of-10 sampling success while reducing wall-clock latency by 34%
claims.direction: favors learned, state-dependent test-time compute allocation (mixing sequential denoising depth and parallel sampling) over fixed schedules or naive best-of-N sampling, for generative (diffusion/flow-matching) action policies
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation benchmarks with diffusion policies + real-world pi_0.5 VLA; requires training a separate meta-policy on top of a frozen pretrained generative policy

title: UniVTAC: A Unified Simulation Platform for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation Data Generation, Learning, and Benchmarking

claims.claim: A visuo-tactile encoder trained on large-scale simulation-synthesized tactile data (from a platform supporting three common tactile sensor types) with designed supervisory signals improves average success rates by 17.1% on a new 8-task visuo-tactile benchmark, and real-world robotic experiments show a further 25% improvement in task success when integrating this encoder
claims.direction: favors simulation-synthesized tactile pretraining (to avoid costly real tactile data collection) as an auxiliary encoder for contact-rich tasks, over vision-only policies
claims.conditions: sim-generated tactile data (three sensor types) + real-world validation; requires tactile sensor hardware on the deployed robot

title: Revisiting Open-Loop Execution in Robotics: Toward Reactive, Higher-Performing Policies

claims.claim: Across four simulation and two real-world tasks, expert demonstration non-Markovianity (not compounding-error mitigation, the commonly cited explanation) is shown to be the primary factor determining how much long open-loop action-chunk execution helps a short-context policy; compounding errors matter but have a much weaker effect than non-Markovianity in this experimental setting
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that long open-loop chunk execution mainly helps by mitigating compounding errors; instead attributes the benefit to compensating for short policy context on non-Markovian demonstrations
claims.conditions: 4 simulation tasks + 2 real-world tasks, controlled study varying open-loop execution horizon and measuring interaction with expert non-Markovianity

claims.claim: When policies are given sufficiently long observation/action context, open-loop execution is no longer beneficial, and the most reactive, closed-loop (short open-loop horizon) policies perform best; this motivates long-context, reactive policies as a more principled paradigm than long open-loop chunking
claims.direction: favors increasing policy context length (memory) and using short open-loop/closed-loop execution over relying on long open-loop chunk execution to paper over short context
claims.conditions: same controlled study, real-world + simulation

why_deep_read: This directly contradicts common practice/explanation for action chunking (compounding-error mitigation) with controlled real-world+sim evidence, and offers a concrete alternative fix (longer context, more reactive/shorter open-loop execution) for our jerky-motion-at-chunk-boundary problem; central to our Q06/Q07/Q10 design decisions and worth reading in full before committing to a chunking strategy.

title: ObstaDiff: Generalizable Diffusion Policy Learning via Obstacle-aware Representations

claims.claim: A decomposed diffusion-policy framework with a lightweight obstacle-aware visual encoder, extracting a structured target-obstacle-background representation (rather than an unstructured/entangled visual encoding), achieves 75.41% average task success and 8.20% average obstacle collision rate across 61 real-robot trials per method (366 executions total) in cluttered real-world (greenhouse) scenes, outperforming representative imitation-learning baselines and improving generalization to unstructured obstacles/backgrounds
claims.direction: favors an explicit structured target-obstacle-background decomposition over an unstructured/entangled visual representation for generalizing diffusion policies to cluttered backgrounds
claims.conditions: real-robot cluttered agricultural (greenhouse) manipulation, 61 trials/method

title: Prioritized Rollouts for Efficient World Model-based Vision-Language-Action Policy Optimization

claims.claim: Policy uncertainty helps identify a small subset of states (often decision-sensitive stages where small action differences alter task outcomes) with greater potential for policy improvement; a lightweight, plug-and-play sampling layer (U-GROW) that directs more model-based-RL rollouts to these informative states improves the efficiency and effectiveness of world-model-based VLA policy optimization in simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, without changing the policy optimization objective
claims.direction: favors uncertainty-guided, non-uniform allocation of world-model rollouts across states over treating all states equally during model-based RL fine-tuning of VLA policies
claims.conditions: model-based RL fine-tuning of VLA policies, sim + real-world manipulation; integrates into existing MBRL pipelines by modifying only the rollout branch-start distribution

title: Refinery: Active Fine-tuning and Deployment-time Optimization for Contact-Rich Policies

claims.claim: Bayesian-Optimization-guided fine-tuning of individual policies plus Gaussian-Mixture-Model-based initialization sampling at deployment time (choosing starts that maximize expected execution success) reduces high variance in policy performance across diverse initial conditions, improving mean success rates by 10.98% over SOTA simulation-based-learning methods for robotic assembly (reaching 91.51% in simulation, comparable in the real world)
claims.direction: favors active fine-tuning plus deployment-time initialization selection over simply training one policy and deploying it as-is, to reduce brittleness/variance across initial conditions
claims.conditions: simulation-based learning for contact-rich robotic assembly, comparable real-world results

claims.claim: Fine-tuned policies produced by Refinery can be chained to accomplish long-horizon, multi-part assembly, successfully assembling up to 8 parts, without requiring explicit multi-step training
claims.direction: favors chaining robustified single-step policies for long-horizon tasks over training one long-horizon policy end-to-end
claims.conditions: same assembly domain, up to 8-part chained assembly

title: Fast-in-Slow: A Dual-System Foundation Model Unifying Fast Manipulation within Slow Reasoning

claims.claim: Embedding a fast System-1 execution module directly within a VLM-based System-2 reasoning model (via partial parameter sharing, heterogeneous modality inputs, and asynchronous operating frequencies for the two systems, trained with a dual-aware co-training strategy) rather than keeping the two systems as fully separate models, outperforms previous SOTA dual-system methods by 8% in simulation and 11% in real-world tasks in average success rate, while achieving a 117.7 Hz control frequency with an action chunk size of eight
claims.direction: favors partially-shared-parameter dual-system architectures (fast execution embedded within slow reasoning) over fully separate System-1/System-2 models, for simultaneously improving success rate and execution frequency
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks; action chunk size of 8 used to reach 117.7 Hz

why_deep_read: A 117.7 Hz control frequency (far above our current ~2s-latency SmolVLA) combined with success-rate gains over separate dual-system baselines is one of the strongest latency results in this batch; want architectural details on the partial parameter-sharing scheme to see if it is adaptable to a much smaller backbone than typical foundation-scale System-2 models.

title: DemoBridge: A Simulation-in-the-Loop Toolkit for Single-View Human Demonstration Retargeting

claims.claim: A single collision-aware whole-joint-trajectory planner, run with a physics simulator in the loop that validates and re-plans (rather than discards) infeasible phases, can convert a single-view RGB(-stereo) recording of a human hand demonstration into an executable, physics-validated, dynamically-stable robot-arm trajectory that also serves as a ready-to-use simulation rollout for policy learning
claims.direction: favors single-view human-demonstration retargeting (with in-the-loop physics validation/re-planning) over requiring multi-view capture or discarding infeasible demonstrations, for generating usable robot training trajectories from cheap human video
claims.conditions: evaluated on three real-demonstration tasks + a controlled synthetic planner benchmark; no downstream policy success-rate numbers given, evaluation is on retargeting fidelity/feasibility

title: Single-Demonstration Imitation with Residual Reinforcement Learning for Dual-Arm Robotic Bottle Opening

claims.claim: A base policy trained via behavioral cloning from a single kinesthetic demonstration performs reliably under nominal conditions but degrades under distribution shift; adding a residual policy learned via PPO in simulation (producing bounded corrective actions on top of the BC base policy) preserves nominal performance while significantly improving robustness and generalization to bottle-geometry variations, with the final controller deployed successfully via one-shot sim-to-real transfer across different bottle types
claims.direction: favors augmenting single-demonstration BC with a simulation-trained residual RL correction policy over relying on single-demonstration BC alone, to recover robustness lost to distribution shift
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, long-horizon bottle-unscrewing task, single kinesthetic demonstration for BC base policy, residual policy trained in simulation then transferred one-shot

title: PAKT: Physically-Aligned Kinesthetic Teaching for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A kinesthetic-teaching interface (admittance control mapping human-applied forces to motion, constrained by the same kinematic limits used during policy execution so collected trajectories stay reproducible) combined with a high-performance control stack (reference generator + impedance controller) reduces cycle time by 23%-48% and cumulative intervention count by 62%-86% relative to the HIL-SERL baseline across four insertion/assembly benchmarks
claims.direction: favors kinematically-constrained kinesthetic teaching (matched to policy execution limits) over unconstrained teleoperation/kinesthetic guidance, for collecting demonstrations/interventions usable by an RL policy
claims.conditions: real-world industrial insertion/assembly tasks (including a data-center compute tray), RL-based (not pure BC) policy improvement via demonstrations+interventions

title: Learning Bilevel Policies over Symbolic World Models for Long-Horizon Planning

claims.claim: Combining a neural low-level policy learned from low-level demonstrations with a high-level symbolic policy constructed from symbolic abstractions of those same demonstrations (bilevel policies) generalizes to longer horizons and greater numbers of objects than VLA and end-to-end imitation-learning methods, and is more time- and memory-efficient in both training and inference; when ignoring low-level execution, the high-level symbolic policies alone can solve high-level problems with 10,000 relevant objects in under a minute
claims.direction: favors combining a small neural low-level controller with an explicit symbolic high-level planner over a single end-to-end (VLA-style) policy for long-horizon, many-object generalization and compute efficiency
claims.conditions: extended MetaWorld benchmarks; requires constructing symbolic abstractions from demonstrations

title: Overcoming Imperfect Kinematics in Surgical Robotics Through Sim-to-Real Visuomotor Learning

claims.claim: A learned policy, trained via a teacher-student framework, can actively compensate for hardware kinematic inaccuracies (unreliable internal position sensors/actuation) in real time by fusing unreliable internal readings with precise external closed-loop visual feedback, without needing a perfect physical/kinematic model; this was successfully deployed on the da Vinci Research Kit, validating the feasibility of using external vision to overcome internal sensor/actuation deficits
claims.direction: favors closed-loop visual correction of imprecise internal kinematics/actuation over model-based calibration or trusting internal (noisy) proprioceptive readings alone
claims.conditions: real surgical robot (da Vinci Research Kit), teacher-student sim-to-real training; qualitative feasibility demonstration rather than a quantified success-rate comparison

title: A Causality-aware Infer-diagnose-refine Framework for Test-time Modality Adaptation in VLA Models

claims.claim: The importance of visual observations for action prediction varies over time across dynamic manipulation phases (e.g. long-distance movement vs. close-range interaction); a model-agnostic, training-free framework (infer actions under factual/counterfactual visual-observation scenarios via zero-padding interventions, diagnose the causal effect of vision via norm-based quantification, then refine actions via gated residual fusion) improves overall performance across multiple VLA backbones on both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks by dynamically reweighting visual importance at test time
claims.direction: favors training-free, test-time causal reweighting of visual-observation importance over static/fixed visual conditioning throughout a manipulation episode
claims.conditions: multiple VLA backbones, simulation + real-world tasks; test-time-only intervention, no retraining required

title: Learning to Act While Waiting: RL Finetuning of Generalist Robot Policies Under Inference Latency

claims.claim: Severe VLA inference latency alters effective environment dynamics and, if not accounted for, breaks the Markov assumption RL relies on, causing standard RL algorithms to fail completely during deployment-time policy improvement; a latency-aware framework (ARLI) that augments state with committed (in-flight) actions and a mid-inference observation restores near-Markovian structure within an asynchronous inference scheme, enabling effective RL fine-tuning under inference delays where standard RL fails entirely, and matching or exceeding standard RL's performance in idealized no-latency settings
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling/compensating for inference latency (via state augmentation with committed actions + mid-inference observations) over ignoring latency or only masking it with naive asynchronous execution, when RL-finetuning a policy under inference delay
claims.conditions: simulated + real-world manipulation tasks; RL-based post-training/finetuning, not the initial BC training itself

title: Emma-X: An Embodied Multimodal Action Model with Grounded Chain of Thought and Look-ahead Spatial Reasoning

claims.claim: A trajectory segmentation strategy based on gripper states and motion trajectories (rather than purely learned/predicted segmentation) helps mitigate hallucination when auto-generating grounded subtask reasoning labels for a large hierarchical embodiment dataset (60,000 trajectories); combined with grounded chain-of-thought and look-ahead spatial reasoning, this achieves superior performance over competitive baselines, particularly on real-world tasks requiring spatial reasoning
claims.direction: favors gripper-state-based trajectory segmentation (a simple, reliable signal) over purely learned segmentation for generating reliable subtask/reasoning labels, and favors grounded CoT + look-ahead spatial reasoning over standard VLA planning
claims.conditions: BridgeV2-based hierarchical dataset, real-world robotic tasks requiring spatial reasoning

title: Efficient Alignment of Unconditioned Action Prior for Language-Conditioned Pick and Place in Clutter

claims.claim: Aligning unconditioned action priors with 3D vision-language priors by learning just one attention layer (A2), rather than training an end-to-end policy from scratch on large datasets or chaining foundation models zero-shot (which suffers cascading errors), enables a policy for language-conditioned pick-and-place in clutter to train with less data while preserving zero-shot generalization; a single shared policy for both pick and place actions enhances performance on each task versus separate policies
claims.direction: favors lightweight alignment (one attention layer) of pretrained action/vision-language priors over full end-to-end training or zero-shot foundation-model chaining, for language-conditioned manipulation, and favors a shared pick+place policy over separate ones
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world pick-and-place-in-clutter, generalizes to unseen objects and language instructions, fewer execution steps required

claims.claim: The alignment formulation requires less training data than typical end-to-end approaches while achieving higher task success rates with fewer steps, for both pick and place tasks, generalizing to unseen objects and instructions
claims.direction: favors prior-alignment approaches for data efficiency over end-to-end training on large task-specific datasets
claims.conditions: same setup

title: VO-DP: Semantic-Geometric Adaptive Diffusion Policy for Vision-Only Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A vision-only, single-view diffusion policy (VO-DP) that fuses intermediate features from VGGT (geometric, via Alternating Attention blocks) and DINOv2 (semantic) through cross-attention and CNN spatial compression achieves simulation success on par with the point-cloud-based method DP3 (64.6% vs 64.0%) and far higher than the vision-only baseline Diffusion Policy (34.8%); in real-world tasks VO-DP reaches 87.9%, outperforming both DP3 (67.5%) and DP (11.2%)
claims.direction: favors fusing pretrained geometric+semantic 2D visual features (VGGT+DINOv2) over either plain vision-only diffusion policy conditioning or requiring an explicit point-cloud/depth-sensor pipeline (DP3), at least matching 3D methods without needing point clouds
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world manipulation tasks, single RGB view, no point cloud/depth input required

claims.claim: Further robustness evaluations confirm that VO-DP remains highly stable under varying conditions including color, size, background, and lighting
claims.direction: favors the VGGT+DINOv2 feature-fusion vision-only approach for robustness to appearance/lighting/background variation
claims.conditions: real-world robustness evaluation across color/size/background/lighting variations

why_deep_read: This is one of the most directly actionable results in the batch: a vision-only (no depth/point-cloud needed) diffusion policy matching point-cloud-based DP3 performance while being explicitly robust to lighting/background/appearance changes -- precisely our failure modes -- with a large real-world gap over plain vision-only DP (87.9% vs 11.2%); the authors also open-sourced a training library, making this very actionable for our SmolVLA-based setup even without needing to fully exploit our RealSense depth stream.

title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A frozen VLM writing and periodically (every K steps) re-observing/re-writing a short Python control function from multi-view RGB, proprioceptive state, and a state delta (rather than being fine-tuned on demonstrations) reaches 35.1% pooled success on a 57-task MuJoCo/RoboVerse sweep, versus 3.5% for the identical system queried only once per episode (open-loop), driven by a 27.3% within-episode recovery rate on failed grasps that would otherwise be carried to episode end
claims.direction: favors training-free, frequently-replanned code-as-policy (closing the loop at the control-code level) over both open-loop code generation and fine-tuned demonstration-based policies, when no demonstrations are available
claims.conditions: 57-task MuJoCo/RoboVerse benchmark, training-free (zero demonstrations), frozen VLM; a fundamentally different paradigm from standard BC/diffusion policies

title: CNN Vision Multi-Modal Perception for Robo-Arm Manipulation in Automotive Repair Tasks

claims.claim: A multi-stream CNN with attention fusing visual, depth, and touch sensory data for object recognition and pose estimation achieves 94.7% task completion accuracy on a 15,000-scene automotive-repair dataset, significantly higher than single-modal and other multi-modal baseline methods, with inference latency suitable for real-time industrial deployment
claims.direction: favors multi-modal (vision+depth+touch) sensor fusion over single-modality perception for precise industrial manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world automotive-repair workshop setting, 15,000-scene dataset; requires depth and touch sensors alongside vision

title: DySL-VLA: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference via Dynamic-Static Layer-Skipping for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Categorizing VLA layers into 'informative' (always executed) and 'incremental' (selectively skippable based on each action's importance, using a prior-post skipping guidance mechanism), combined with a skip-aware two-stage knowledge-distillation training procedure, achieves a 2.1% improvement in success length over Deer-VLA on the Calvin dataset while reducing trainable parameters by a factor of 85.7 and providing a 3.75x speedup relative to the RoboFlamingo baseline at iso-accuracy
claims.direction: favors action-importance-aware dynamic layer-skipping (skip more compute on low-precision-demand steps) over uniformly executing all VLA layers at every timestep, to cut inference cost with minimal or no accuracy loss
claims.conditions: Calvin benchmark; requires a skip-aware distillation training procedure to convert a standard VLA into the layer-skipping variant

why_deep_read: An 85.7x reduction in trainable parameters and 3.75x inference speedup at matched accuracy is one of the largest efficiency gains in this batch and directly targets our latency/compute constraints (Q10/Q12); want to check if the distillation procedure requires a large teacher model or can start from a small backbone like SmolVLA.

title: dVLA-RL: Reinforcement Learning over Denoising Trajectories for Discrete Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Reframing RL for discrete-diffusion VLAs (dVLAs, which unify vision/language/action into a single discrete token space via masked generative modeling) around the joint probability of the sampled denoising path (modeled as an MDP), rather than the intractable marginal action probability, plus a unified step-scheduling approach tailoring denoising steps to task complexity, achieves 99.7% success on LIBERO and a 30.6% improvement over the SFT baseline on RoboTwin 2.0, remaining competitive with strong World-Action-Model baselines
claims.direction: favors RL-based refinement of discrete-diffusion (masked generative) action heads, with per-task-adaptive denoising step scheduling, over SFT-only training of discrete-diffusion VLAs
claims.conditions: LIBERO (99.7% success) + RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmarks; discrete-diffusion (masked generative) action representation specifically

title: RoboTwin: Dual-Arm Robot Benchmark with Generative Digital Twins (early version)

claims.claim: Generating diverse expert demonstration datasets via digital twins (3D generative foundation models creating varied object twins from single 2D images, plus LLM-based spatial-relation-aware code generation for robot movement), then pre-training policies on this generated data and fine-tuning with limited real-world samples, improves success rate by over 70% for single-arm tasks and over 40% for dual-arm tasks compared to models trained solely on real-world data
claims.direction: favors generative-digital-twin data pretraining plus limited real-world fine-tuning over training solely on (scarce) real-world demonstrations
claims.conditions: validated on the open-source COBOT Magic Robot platform, single-arm and dual-arm tasks, comprehensive sim+real benchmark

title: Solving Challenging Tasks with Manipulation Policy with Limited Demonstrations

claims.claim: RL agents in manipulation tasks are acutely sensitive to demonstration quality in both online and offline settings; TD3+Smooth BC, which dynamically adjusts the balance between imitation and Q-value maximization to ensure a smooth transition from demonstration-based learning to experience-based learning, demonstrates marked improvements over baseline offline-RL-plus-BC methods on Adroit and MuJoCo tasks even with limited demonstrations of varying quality
claims.direction: favors dynamically-balanced imitation-to-RL transition methods over fixed-weight combinations of BC and RL objectives, when demonstrations are limited and/or of variable quality
claims.conditions: Adroit manipulator + MuJoCo sim tasks; combines RL with demonstrations rather than pure BC

title: You Only Teach Once: Learn One-Shot Bimanual Robotic Manipulation from Video Demonstrations

claims.claim: YOTO extracts and injects patterns of bimanual actions from as few as a single binocular (video) observation of human hand movements, and, using keyframe-based motion trajectories, generates diverse training demonstrations with varied object types/locations to train a customized bimanual diffusion policy; it mimics 5 intricate long-horizon bimanual tasks, generalizes strongly across visual/spatial conditions, and outperforms existing visuomotor imitation-learning methods in accuracy and efficiency
claims.direction: favors extracting reusable action patterns from a single human video demonstration (plus keyframe-based synthetic demonstration expansion) over collecting many robot teleoperation demonstrations directly
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, single binocular human-video observation as the sole source demonstration per task, keyframe-based data augmentation for diverse object/location variation

title: Pre-trained Visual Representations Generalize Where it Matters in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Contrary to prior findings that pre-trained vision models (PVMs) are ineffective in model-based RL, this work shows that in scenarios with severe visual domain shifts, PVMs perform much better than a baseline model trained from scratch; varying levels of fine-tuning were investigated, and partial fine-tuning of the PVM maintained the highest average task performance under the most extreme distribution shifts
claims.direction: favors using pre-trained vision encoders with partial (not full, not zero) fine-tuning over training a vision encoder from scratch or freezing it completely, specifically for robustness under severe visual domain shift
claims.conditions: model-based RL, visuomotor policy learning, severe visual domain-shift evaluation; contradicts prior work's finding that PVMs are ineffective in MBRL

title: Do You Need Proprioceptive States in Visuomotor Policies?

claims.claim: The common practice of conditioning visuomotor policies on both visual observations and proprioceptive state causes overfitting to training trajectories (the policy becomes overly reliant on proprioceptive state) and results in poor spatial generalization; a 'State-free Policy' that removes proprioceptive state input entirely and predicts actions only from vision (in the relative end-effector action space, using dual wide-angle wrist cameras for full task-relevant visual coverage) achieves dramatically stronger spatial generalization: average success improves from 0% to 85% in height generalization and from 6% to 64% in horizontal generalization, across real-world tasks (pick-and-place, shirt-folding, whole-body manipulation) and multiple robot embodiments
claims.direction: directly contradicts the common practice of including proprioceptive state alongside vision for visuomotor policies; favors vision-only, relative-end-effector-action-space policies (with full visual coverage via multiple wrist cameras) for spatial generalization
claims.conditions: real-world, relative end-effector action space, requires dual wide-angle wrist cameras for full task-relevant visual coverage (to compensate for removing proprioception); tested across multiple robot embodiments

claims.claim: The State-free Policy's strong generalization depends on ensuring full task-relevant visual observation coverage, provided here by dual wide-angle wrist cameras
claims.direction: favors wide-angle/dual wrist-camera coverage as a substitute for proprioceptive feedback
claims.conditions: same real-world experiments

claims.claim: State-free policies also show advantages in data efficiency and cross-embodiment adaptation versus state-based policies
claims.direction: favors removing proprioceptive state for both spatial generalization and cross-embodiment/data-efficiency benefits
claims.conditions: same real-world experiments, multiple embodiments

why_deep_read: This is a striking, large-magnitude (0%->85%, 6%->64%) contradiction of the near-universal practice of feeding proprioception into visuomotor policies, directly relevant to our Q02 action-space and Q11 camera-coverage decisions and our camera-shift/generalization problem; given we currently condition on robot state, this could be a high-value, low-cost experiment to try, and is a standout 'contradicts common practice' finding for our summary.

title: Language-Conditioned Representations and Mixture-of-Experts Policy for Robust Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Grounding visual features with language instructions via a Language-Conditioned Visual Representation module resolves perceptual ambiguity between visually similar tasks, and a Language-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts Density Policy (sparse expert architecture specializing in distinct multimodal action distributions, stabilized by gradient modulation) mitigates task conflict in multi-task imitation learning, achieving 73.4% success on LIBERO and 79% on real-robot multi-task experiments, with ablations isolating the contribution of each component
claims.direction: favors combining language-grounded visual representations with a sparse mixture-of-experts multimodal action head over a single shared (non-language-grounded, non-expert-specialized) policy for multi-task manipulation
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO) + real robot, multi-task setting with ablations for each component

title: ShapeGen: Robotic Data Generation for Category-Level Manipulation

claims.claim: ShapeGen generates shape-varied manipulation demonstrations in a simulator-free, 3D manner (curating a plug-and-play Shape Library of functionally-corresponding spatial warpings between object shapes, then using this library with minimal human annotation to synthesize physically-plausible, functionally-correct novel demonstrations), and real-world experiments demonstrate this boosts policies' in-category shape generalizability (generalizing to novel object instances within the same category, not just the exact training instance)
claims.direction: favors simulator-free, shape-library-based synthetic demonstration generation over manually collecting demonstrations across many object instances, for in-category object-shape generalization
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation experiments, category-level generalization (novel shape instances within a trained category); requires curating a Shape Library with minimal human annotation

title: MARS Policy: Multimodality Only When It Matters

claims.claim: Adaptively invoking stochastic (generative, multimodal) sampling only during phases of a task that inherently require behavioral diversity, and reverting to efficient deterministic prediction during single-modal phases (Modality-Adaptive Robot Sampling), bridges the gap between generative policies' multimodal expressivity and deterministic models' training/inference efficiency; across 8 simulated and 4 real-world tasks this yields a 16.67% success-rate improvement and an 83.20% inference-latency reduction in real-world tests versus (implicitly) always-stochastic generative policies, and even outpaces deterministic policies in training efficiency on near-deterministic tasks
claims.direction: favors phase-adaptive switching between stochastic/generative and deterministic action prediction over always using a fully generative (diffusion/flow) action head or a purely deterministic one
claims.conditions: 8 simulated + 4 real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: An 83.2% real-world inference-latency reduction combined with a success-rate improvement (not a trade-off) directly targets our ~2s-latency problem while preserving the multimodal expressivity we may need for ambiguous grasp approaches; want implementation details of the phase-detection mechanism and whether it needs labeled multimodal/unimodal phase annotations.

title: Threading Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Model Inference in Low-Cost Smart Agricultural Manipulation

claims.claim: A complete system-level implementation of the Real-Time Action Chunking (RTAC) algorithm on a low-cost robotic manipulation system, with a custom-optimized threading implementation for the policy-inference and control pipeline (reducing end-to-end latency without modifying the underlying policy), significantly improves control stability and speed compared to the base pseudocode-level RTAC implementation, evaluated on agricultural produce manipulation (garlic bulbs, walnuts)
claims.direction: favors careful systems-level (threading/pipeline) engineering of asynchronous action-chunking inference over a naive implementation of the same algorithm, to reduce latency and improve control stability on low-cost hardware
claims.conditions: real low-cost robotic arm, agricultural produce manipulation tasks; implementation-level optimization, not a new algorithm

why_deep_read: This is one of the few papers explicitly targeting 'low-cost robotic arm' deployment of real-time action chunking (directly matching our SO-101 setup and our jerky-motion/latency problem); the systems-engineering details (threading implementation) could be directly reusable even though the underlying RTAC algorithm itself is not new.

title: VLAW: Iterative Co-Improvement of Vision-Language-Action Policy and World Model

claims.claim: An action-conditioned video-generation world model, used as a learned simulator to generate additional rollout data, initially lacks the physical fidelity for policy improvement (poor coverage of failure cases, inaccurate contact-rich physics); an iterative algorithm that uses real-world rollout data to improve the world model's fidelity, which is then used to generate supplemental synthetic training data for the VLA, achieves a 39.2% absolute success-rate improvement over the base policy on a real robot across multiple downstream tasks, with 11.6 percentage points of that improvement attributable specifically to training with the generated synthetic rollouts
claims.direction: favors iterative co-improvement of a world model and a VLA policy (using real data to fix the world model, then synthetic data from the improved world model to fix the policy) over training the VLA on real rollouts alone or using a static/unrefined world model for data augmentation
claims.conditions: real robot, multiple downstream tasks, iterative real-then-synthetic training loop

title: Task-DP3: Goal-Centric Perception-Driven Adaptive Trajectory Generation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Task-DP3, combining a goal-conditioned point-cloud sampler (extracting target-centric point clouds from segmentation masks) with a perception-driven skill scheduler (dynamically determining task states and planning skill sequences for adaptive trajectory generation), achieves a 92.5% success rate on real-robot multi-object manipulation tasks using only 30 demonstrations, outperforming SOTA methods, and demonstrates strong generalization to unseen clutter and backgrounds plus long-horizon tasks with strict ordering constraints
claims.direction: favors goal-centric, point-cloud-based, perception-driven trajectory generation over generic diffusion imitation learning, for achieving high success rate with very few (30) demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-robot multi-object manipulation, only 30 demonstrations, point-cloud input (requires depth sensing), long-horizon tasks with sequential constraints

why_deep_read: A 92.5% real-robot success rate from only 30 demonstrations (below our 50-100 demo budget) with strong generalization to unseen clutter/backgrounds is one of the most directly relevant data-efficiency results in the batch; since it uses point-cloud input, it directly leverages our available RealSense depth stream, making it worth reading in full for architecture/training details.

title: Task Parameter Extrapolation via Learning Inverse Tasks From Forward Demonstrations
