claims.claim: A joint learning approach constructing a common representation of forward and inverse tasks, using auxiliary forward demonstrations from novel configurations to execute corresponding inverse tasks without direct supervision, extrapolates to novel conditions outside the training region, outperforming diffusion-based and multimodal-VAE-based alternatives in simulated and real-world experiments requiring complex manipulation with diverse objects/tools
claims.direction: favors forward-inverse joint task representation learning over standard diffusion-policy or CVAE-based imitation learning, specifically for extrapolation beyond the training data distribution
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, diverse objects/tools; direct comparison against diffusion and multimodal VAE baselines

title: Harnessing human expertise for high-precision robotic assembly in industrialized construction: A sample-efficient installer-in-the-loop interactive reinforcement learning framework

claims.claim: An installer-in-the-loop interactive RL framework combining offline teleoperated demonstrations, sparse event-driven binary takeovers at contact-failure boundaries, and acceptance-aligned terminal rewards attains 100% autonomous seating success on a precision assembly task with only 12-15 minutes of cumulative human supervision over 3 hours of online training, reaching a 95% success milestone in about 0.5-1.5 hours
claims.direction: favors sparse, event-triggered human intervention (rather than continuous demonstration/supervision) combined with offline-to-online RL for sample-efficient acquisition of precision skills
claims.conditions: simulation (MuJoCo), precision assembly with 2mm per-side clearance tolerances; requires an RL framework (Q-chunking with Flow Q-Learning), not pure BC

claims.claim: A temporally-abstract action-sequence policy built on Q-chunking with Flow Q-Learning captures multimodal recovery maneuvers under sparse terminal rewards
claims.direction: favors temporally-abstracted (chunked) flow-based action policies for handling multimodal recovery behaviors
claims.conditions: same sim precision-assembly setup

title: FEWT: Frequency-Enhanced Wavelet-Based Transformer for Multimodal Wheeled Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: A lightweight frequency-aligned imitation-learning framework (FEWT) that explicitly extracts and aligns multiscale spatial-visual and temporal-frequency features (via frequency-enhanced efficient multiscale attention and time-series discrete wavelet transform) significantly improves success rate over the widely-used Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) baseline, particularly during the most challenging phases of simulated bimanual insertion tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit frequency/multiscale feature alignment over standard ACT-style temporal modeling, especially for fine-grained/high-frequency-dynamics phases of a task
claims.conditions: simulated bimanual insertion tasks + real-world mobile/desktop manipulation; extended with a custom tactile fabric sensor for the full real-world system

title: VABench: Measuring Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Visual Demonstrations, Active Perception, and Metric Control

claims.claim: Actively selecting camera viewpoints (rather than passively observing from fixed multi-view cameras) significantly improves task success for general-purpose MLLMs performing an observe-reason-act-revise loop under incomplete observation; in one matched comparison, success rose from 27.86% (passive multi-view) to 57.50% (active camera control)
claims.direction: favors active camera-viewpoint selection over passive fixed multi-view observation for spatially-ambiguous or incompletely-observed manipulation scenarios
claims.conditions: VA-Bench, 14 base task families (11 single-arm, 3 dual-arm), RGB-only demonstrations, model-agnostic controller executing metric Cartesian commands

claims.claim: Held-out geometric/layout transfer can reduce task success by over 30 percentage points relative to in-distribution geometry, and no model completes a strict long-horizon 5-object composition track despite substantial partial progress
claims.direction: highlights a large generalization gap under geometric/layout shift, even for capable general-purpose models
claims.conditions: VA-Bench held-out geometry/layout variants and long-horizon composition track

title: Efficient Skill Acquisition for Complex Manipulation Tasks in Obstructed Environments

claims.claim: Combining an object-centric generative model (enabling one-shot target-object identification/re-identification in new scenes) for goal specification with motion planning for obstacle avoidance and a skill-transition network bridging planner terminal states to RL start states, outperforms competitive baselines including a state-of-the-art RL algorithm by a significant margin on complex manipulation tasks in obstructed environments, using only a few simple demonstrations
claims.direction: favors combining one-shot object-centric goal identification with motion planning and RL over end-to-end RL or motion-planning-alone, for data-efficient skill acquisition with obstacles
claims.conditions: real-world small-batch assembly-like obstructed environments; requires object-centric generative model as goal specifier

title: Lift3D Foundation Policy: Lifting 2D Large-Scale Pretrained Models for Robust 3D Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Lift3D progressively enhances a 2D foundation model with implicit 3D representation (via a task-aware masked autoencoder that masks task-relevant affordance patches and reconstructs depth) and explicit 3D representation (via a 2D-model-lifting strategy mapping 3D point positions to the 2D model's positional embeddings, letting the 2D foundation model directly encode point clouds), consistently outperforming previous state-of-the-art methods across several simulation benchmarks and real-world scenarios, addressing both the scarcity of large-scale robotic 3D data and the potential loss of spatial geometry
claims.direction: favors lifting/adapting large-scale pretrained 2D foundation models into 3D point-cloud encoders (rather than training a separate 3D encoder from scratch, which lacks large-scale 3D pretraining data) for robotic manipulation representations
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks + real-world scenarios; leverages existing 2D large-scale pretrained knowledge without requiring large-scale robotic 3D datasets

title: Visuo-tactile feedback policies for terminal assembly facilitated by reinforcement learning

claims.claim: Decomposing a precision assembly task into three explicit phases (vision-guided grasp, tactile-based align, visuo-tactile insertion), each with its own specialized model/policy, achieves 100% successful insertions across 100 different initial end-effector/grasp poses, versus only 9% for a standard imitation-learning policy and 0% for an online-RL policy trained without this phase decomposition
claims.direction: strongly favors explicit task-phase decomposition (separate specialized models per phase) over a single monolithic end-to-end IL or RL policy for a precision, pose-sensitive manipulation task
claims.conditions: real-world PLC terminal assembly, requires tactile sensing for the align/insertion phases; human demonstrations and interventions used for safe training

why_deep_read: Not selected for deep read primarily because it requires tactile sensing hardware we do not have, but the underlying finding (phase decomposition vastly outperforming monolithic IL/RL, 100% vs 9% vs 0%) is a strong, notable result on task decomposition (Q06) worth flagging even without the tactile component.

title: Tenma: Robust Cross-Embodiment Robot Manipulation with Diffusion Transformer

claims.claim: Tenma, a lightweight diffusion-transformer policy integrating multiview RGB, proprioception, and language via a cross-embodiment normalizer (mapping disparate state/action spaces into a shared latent space), a Joint State-Time encoder (temporally aligned observation learning with inference-speed boosts), and a diffusion action decoder optimized for training stability, achieves an average in-distribution success rate of 88.95% under matched compute, substantially exceeding baseline policies whose best in-distribution average was only 18.12%, using only a moderate data scale
claims.direction: favors this specific combination of design choices (cross-embodiment state/action normalization, joint state-time temporal encoding, stability-optimized diffusion decoder) over baseline diffusion-transformer/imitation architectures, even under matched (moderate) compute and data scale
claims.conditions: heterogeneous, multimodal, cross-embodiment bi-manual robot data; matched compute across compared methods

claims.claim: Tenma maintains strong performance under object and scene shifts, not just in-distribution
claims.direction: favors the same lightweight cross-embodiment diffusion-transformer design for object/scene-shift robustness
claims.conditions: same setup, moderate data scale

why_deep_read: An 88.95% vs 18.12% in-distribution success gap under matched compute and moderate data scale is one of the largest architecture-driven gains in the batch, and it is explicitly framed as a lightweight, lower-data-regime design (matching our compute/data constraints); want the specific design-choice ablations (which of the three components mattered most) to see what is cheaply adoptable in our SmolVLA-based setup.

title: HiFi-UMI: Learning Deployable Manipulation Policies from High-Fidelity UMI Data Alone

claims.claim: A portable, high-fidelity UMI (handheld gripper) data-collection system (head-mounted stereo-inertial SLAM, native inter-gripper relative pose, microsecond synchronization, ~200-degree dual wide-angle cameras per hand, reaching 3mm workspace-local end-effector accuracy without external tracking) enables 'zero-robot post-training': a policy trained solely on this robot-free UMI data deploys directly on a real robot and matches in-domain teleoperation-trained policies across three different VLA/world-action-model backbones (success-rate differences of only -2.5, +3.1, and -0.6 percentage points), with the strongest reaching 85% on a precision insertion task even though the teleoperation baseline was collected in the exact evaluation scene and no HiFi-UMI trajectory was
claims.direction: favors raising the fidelity of robot-free (handheld UMI) demonstration data over relying on real-robot teleoperation data, potentially eliminating the need for a real-robot 'anchor' fraction of the training data entirely
claims.conditions: real-robot deployment, tested across StarVLA-QwenPI, OpenPI-pi_0.5, and LingBot-VA backbones; also shows pretraining on 4,000 hours from the same corpus lowers action error by 41% on ten unseen tasks and raises real-robot success by a further 18.1 percentage points for one backbone

why_deep_read: A demonstration that zero real-robot teleoperation data (only handheld UMI-collected demos) can match in-domain teleoperation performance across multiple backbone families is extremely relevant to our costly demo-collection process; want to know the hardware/cost of building a HiFi-UMI-grade handheld gripper rig and whether the open-sourced HiFi-UMI-2K corpus includes tasks transferable to our pick-and-place setup.

title: KeyGen: Unsupervised Keypoint based Object-Centric Representations for Category-Level Policy Generalization

claims.claim: Learning canonicalized semantic 3D keypoints from point clouds (unsupervised) and conditioning a visuomotor diffusion policy on these keypoints plus object-centric geometry, enabling consistent geometric correspondence across object instances, significantly outperforms prior methods on both seen and unseen objects under pose variation, scales effectively with additional demonstrations per object, and maintains robustness to object rescaling, in both simulation and real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors canonicalized 3D-keypoint object-centric representations over instance-specific geometry/appearance encodings (which conventional BC tends to overfit to) for category-level (unseen-instance) generalization
claims.conditions: photorealistic simulation benchmark (3 tasks) + real-world manipulation; requires point-cloud input and a planning-driven data-generation pipeline for training-time expert trajectories across diverse instances

claims.claim: KeyGen maintains strong performance under object rescaling and pose variation, directly targeting category-level (not just instance-level) generalization
claims.direction: favors keypoint-based canonicalization for generalizing to novel object instances within a category (e.g., differently-shaped/sized/posed objects of the same type)
claims.conditions: same sim + real-world setup

title: Uncertainty-Guided Sparse Refinement for Action Chunking Transformer Policies

claims.claim: Failures of action-chunking policies are often dominated by prediction errors at a small number of critical timesteps within a chunk, rather than uniformly poor predictions across the whole chunk; a coarse-to-refine framework (Uncertainty-Guided Refinement) that predicts a full action chunk, estimates per-step temporal uncertainty from coarse hidden states, and applies residual correction only to the most uncertain timesteps (via a binary mask, with the uncertainty branch decoupled from the coarse predictor) achieves the best success rate on 4 of 5 dual-arm RoboTwin benchmark tasks, improving over the ACT baseline by up to 13 percentage points absolute, and outperforms both full-chunk refinement and position-agnostic block refinement in ablations
claims.direction: favors sparse, uncertainty-targeted residual refinement of only the most error-prone timesteps within an action chunk over uniformly refining the entire chunk or not refining at all
claims.conditions: RoboTwin benchmark, 5 dual-arm manipulation tasks, ACT-style action-chunking baseline

why_deep_read: This directly targets which parts of an action chunk are unreliable (a likely contributor to our jerky-motion-at-chunk-boundary problem) and proposes a lightweight, targeted fix rather than uniform refinement; the 13-point absolute gain over ACT is substantial and the method seems adoptable on top of a small ACT-style policy like ours.

title: Flow Matching Imitation Learning for Multi-Support Manipulation

claims.claim: In simulation, Flow Matching is shown to be more appropriate for robotics than Diffusion and traditional behavior cloning for generating multi-modal trajectory distributions, combined with an optimization-based multi-contact whole-body controller; on a real full-size humanoid (Talos), this enables learning a whole-body non-prehensile box-pushing task and closing dishwasher drawers using contact for balance
claims.direction: favors flow matching over diffusion and traditional BC as the generative action-modeling backbone
claims.conditions: sim comparison of flow matching vs diffusion vs BC, real-robot validation on a full-size humanoid whole-body contact task (different embodiment/task from ours)

title: Learning Precise Robot Assembly Tasks from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A portable teaching interface (GoPro camera + HTC Vive trackers + gripper encoder) supporting demonstration via physical interaction, simulation, or teleoperation enables rapid/intuitive data acquisition; combining a learned motion model with a finite-horizon online optimization refinement step (incorporating motion constraints and goal-state accuracy) ensures robust performance and high precision on a precision pick-and-place power-relay-assembly task across various test scenarios, addressing the imprecision of purely learned models
claims.direction: favors combining a learned motion model with an explicit constraint-aware optimization refinement step over relying on the learned model alone, for precision tasks
claims.conditions: real-world precision pick-and-place (power relay assembly)

title: Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation with Multifingered Hands via Visuomotor Diffusion

claims.claim: A novel demonstration outlier-removal approach based on HDBSCAN clustering and the GLOSH (Global-Local Outlier Score from Hierarchies) algorithm effectively filters out low-quality demonstrations that could degrade policy learning performance, applied to AR-collected teleoperation demonstrations for a diffusion-policy dexterous manipulation system
claims.direction: favors automated statistical outlier-filtering of collected demonstrations over using all collected demonstrations as-is, for improving policy learning from imperfect demo sets
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous in-hand manipulation, AR-based teleoperation data collection; qualitative improvement claim (no exact numbers given for the filtering's effect)

title: Diffusion ReRoll: Revisable Denoising for Robotic Sequential Prediction

claims.claim: Instead of a single monotonic denoising process (standard in diffusion-based sequence predictors), Diffusion ReRoll selectively re-noises regions that have become locally stable while other regions continue denoising, enabling iterative cross-horizon revision (earlier and later segments revise one another) while maintaining local consistency; in diffusion-policy-style action prediction, this improves average success by 56.5% relative to Diffusion Policy across different prediction horizons and history lengths on LIBERO-10, and shows the best action-video consistency and improved OOD performance in unified video-action modeling
claims.direction: favors structured, revisable (cross-horizon) denoising over standard single-pass monotonic denoising for diffusion-based action-chunk prediction
claims.conditions: LIBERO-10 multi-task benchmark (action prediction), plus OGBench PointMaze/AntMaze (planning) and unified video-action modeling; evaluated across varying prediction horizons and history lengths

claims.claim: The framework is evaluated explicitly across different prediction horizons and history lengths, showing the revisable denoising mechanism's benefit is consistent across these settings
claims.direction: suggests horizon/history-length choice interacts with denoising structure, and revisable denoising is robust across horizon settings
claims.conditions: same LIBERO-10 evaluation

why_deep_read: A 56.5% relative success improvement over standard Diffusion Policy purely from changing the denoising/revision structure (no new data or bigger model) is one of the largest single-mechanism gains in this batch for exactly our Q01 action-head question; want to understand the added inference-time cost of the re-noising/revision process given our latency constraint.

title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds

claims.claim: A physics-aligned real-to-sim-to-real data engine (digitizing scenes into metric-consistent twins, calibrating deformable dynamics through elastic modeling, and expanding behaviors via diffusion-based trajectory generation with quality filtering) lets policies trained on purely synthetic data achieve parity with real-data baselines at a 1:15 synthetic-to-real equivalence ratio, delivering 90% zero-shot success and 50% generalization gains in real-world deployment, given only limited initial demonstrations
claims.direction: favors physics-grounded (calibrated) synthetic data generation over collecting proportionally more real demonstrations, achieving large real-data-equivalent savings, at least for deformable-object manipulation
claims.conditions: deformable-object (cloth-like) manipulation specifically; limited real demonstrations needed to ground/calibrate the simulator

title: StrataVLA: Hierarchical and Efficient 3D Geometric Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Rather than requiring explicit depth/point-cloud inputs or injecting geometry only at the model input or action expert, StrataVLA uses a frozen geometry foundation model to extract shared geometric features from RGB observations, and sparse, layer-specific Geometry Adapters let visual representations at selected backbone depths retrieve relevant geometric evidence via cross-attention, persistently making 3D spatial information available throughout the VLA backbone; this achieves 98.53% average success on LIBERO suites, with consistent gains over strong VLA baselines on LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors hierarchical, persistent (multi-layer) geometric grounding of a frozen geometry model into a VLA backbone over one-shot input-level or action-expert-level geometry injection
claims.conditions: LIBERO + SimplerEnv sim benchmarks + real-world manipulation; RGB input only for geometric feature extraction (no physical depth sensor required)

claims.claim: Combining task-aware routing with an LRU feature cache that exploits temporal redundancy during task manipulation reduces geometry-model invocations by up to 88% while maintaining the 98.53% average LIBERO success rate
claims.direction: favors caching/routing to avoid redundant expensive geometry-model calls over invoking the geometry model at every inference step, to cut compute
claims.conditions: same LIBERO evaluation

why_deep_read: An 88% reduction in expensive geometry-model invocations while maintaining top accuracy directly addresses both our Q04 (3D grounding) and Q10 (latency/compute) constraints simultaneously; want to see the actual per-step latency numbers and whether the caching scheme is compatible with a small backbone under our 8GB GPU budget.

title: RL Token: Bootstrapping Online RL with Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Adapting a pretrained VLA to expose a compact 'RL token' readout (preserving task-relevant pretrained knowledge as an efficient interface for online RL) and training only a small actor-critic head on this token (anchoring the learned policy to the base VLA) enables sample-efficient online RL fine-tuning using just a few hours of real-world practice; across four real-robot precision-insertion-style tasks, this improves speed on the hardest part of the task by up to 3x and raises success rates significantly, in some cases surpassing human teleoperation speed, within minutes to a few hours of practice
claims.direction: favors lightweight RL fine-tuning via a small actor-critic head anchored to a frozen/pretrained VLA's compact token interface over full-model RL fine-tuning or relying on the base VLA's out-of-the-box speed/precision
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks (screw installation, zip tie fastening, charger insertion, Ethernet insertion), minutes-to-hours of online practice, works even for large VLAs

title: Learning Multi-View Spatial Reasoning from Cross-View Relations

claims.claim: Fine-tuning VLMs on a large-scale dataset (XVR: 100K vision-question-answer samples from 18K 3D scenes + 70K robotic manipulation trajectories) explicitly teaching cross-view spatial reasoning (correspondence, verification, localization across multiple camera views) yields substantial improvements on multi-view and robotic spatial-reasoning benchmarks, and when the resulting representations are used as VLA backbones, they improve success rates on RoboCasa
claims.direction: favors explicit training on cross-view spatial relations (even from a general dataset, not robot-specific) over standard single-view-trained VLM backbones for multi-camera manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: VLM fine-tuning + downstream VLA integration; RoboCasa benchmark for the robotic-manipulation transfer result

title: Online World Modeling Enables Real-World Inverse Reinforcement Learning from Observation

claims.claim: MPAIL2, an Inverse-RL-from-Observation method requiring only task observations (e.g. video, no action labels or hand-designed rewards), learns real-world visual pick-and-place from scratch to 82% success in under 40 minutes, whereas standard RL and behavior cloning given equal interaction/demonstration budgets reach only 0% and 12% success respectively, despite having reward and action supervision that MPAIL2 lacks
claims.direction: favors online-world-modeling-based learning from observation-only data (no action labels) over standard RL or BC given an equally small budget, for very fast real-world skill acquisition from scratch
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place, under 40 minutes total, first real-world demonstration of positive online transfer across tasks from scratch for this paradigm

title: MO-VLA: Preference Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A two-stage framework -- large-scale behavior cloning for general operational skills, followed by multi-objective RL fine-tuning with a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism in the action head that explicitly injects user-preference signals (e.g. speed, smoothness, safety) -- achieves superior multi-objective performance while maintaining high task success rate on the Meta-World benchmark, compared to standard BC-only VLA training that ignores such preference/intent information
claims.direction: favors adding an explicit FiLM-based preference-conditioning stage on top of BC pretraining over BC alone, for controlling qualitative execution properties like smoothness and speed
claims.conditions: Meta-World simulation benchmark, two-stage BC-then-MORL training

title: $\tau_0$-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation

claims.claim: Formulating high-level subtask generation as a compute-scalable inference problem (the high-level policy uses execution memory to generate a subtask and, when needed, searches over alternatives via world-model-guided test-time computation before committing) rather than a single forward pass per decision substantially improves next-subtask prediction accuracy, and these gains translate into higher closed-loop success on long-horizon robot manipulation tasks, across in-domain and distribution-shifted settings
claims.direction: favors allocating additional test-time search/computation to difficult high-level subtask decisions over always using a single forward pass, for long-horizon hierarchical VLA policies
claims.conditions: trained on 40,115 hours of heterogeneous real-world data, multimodal co-training, multi-embodiment low-level execution; foundation-model scale

title: Robot Learning with Super-Linear Scaling

claims.claim: CASHER crowdsources digital twins of real-world scenes (via 3D reconstruction) and collects large-scale behavioral data in simulation (initially RL bootstrapped with human demonstrations, later increasingly using the generalizing policy itself to generate demonstrations, reducing human effort over time); this shows zero-shot and few-shot scaling laws on three real-world tasks, and crucially enables fine-tuning of a pre-trained policy to a new target scenario using only a video scan of that scenario, with no additional human demonstration effort
claims.direction: favors crowdsourced-digital-twin simulation data collection (with human effort superlinearly amortized as the generalist policy improves) over proportional real-world human demonstration collection for each new scenario
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation across three tasks/diverse scenarios; adapting to a new scenario requires only a video scan, no new demonstrations

title: CATCH-FORM-ACTer: Compliance-Aware Tactile Control and Hybrid Deformation Regulation-Based Action Transformer for Viscoelastic Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Enhancing an Action Chunking with Transformer (ACT) policy to dynamically adjust stiffness, damping, and diffusion parameters in real time during multi-phase manipulation (rather than only planning trajectories, as conventional ACT does) achieves better force-field patterns and 10%-20% higher success rates versus conventional ACT-based methods on viscoelastic object manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors extending ACT with real-time compliance-parameter modulation (informed by force/tactile feedback) over standard trajectory-only ACT, for tasks requiring dynamic force-deformation regulation
claims.conditions: single-arm and bimanual real robots, viscoelastic (soft, deformable) object manipulation; requires tactile/force sensing and admittance/PDE-based compliance control

title: Learning Human-Robot Interactions in Perturbed Teleoperations

claims.claim: An LSTM-based imitation-learning framework, trained on structured demonstration data of successful task executions, learns to condition/correct teleoperation signals and human-operator inputs to maintain stable, safe task execution when input signals (e.g. force feedback) are disrupted; this framework outperforms state-of-the-art teleoperation methods and achieves a zero failure ratio under uncertainty-perturbed, long-distance (Australia-USA) teleoperation scenarios
claims.direction: favors using recurrent (LSTM-based) temporal memory learned from successful demonstrations to compensate for corrupted/disrupted real-time control signals, over standard (memoryless) teleoperation control
claims.conditions: remote medical teleoperation robot, long-distance network-induced signal disruption; different application domain (perturbed communication channel rather than local sensor jitter)

title: Action-aware Dynamic Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: Visual token redundancy in VLA models is higher during coarse manipulation phases than fine-grained operations and is strongly correlated with action dynamics; Action-aware Dynamic Pruning (ADP), which conditions visual-token pruning on recent action-trajectory dynamics (adaptively adjusting token retention ratio via a gating mechanism, combined with text-driven token selection) rather than pruning uniformly across a task, achieves up to 1.35x inference speedup on OpenVLA-OFT and a 25.8% success-rate improvement with OpenVLA, while significantly reducing FLOPs and action-inference latency, evaluated on LIBERO and diverse real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors action-dynamics-conditioned, stage-adaptive visual-token pruning over uniform (stage-agnostic) visual-token reduction, for cutting VLA inference cost without sacrificing (and sometimes improving) success rate
claims.conditions: LIBERO suites + real-world scenarios; a simple plug-in method compatible with existing VLA architectures (tested on OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT)

why_deep_read: A plug-in method giving both a speedup (1.35x) and a success-rate improvement (25.8%) is a rare 'free lunch' directly targeting our latency problem; want to understand how the action-dynamics gating signal is computed (whether it needs extra sensors or just the policy's own recent outputs) for compatibility with our low-compute deployment.

title: MimicDroid: In-Context Learning for Humanoid Robot Manipulation from Human Play Videos

claims.claim: Using continuous, unlabeled human 'play' videos (people freely interacting with their environment, not teleoperated demonstrations) as the sole training data source, MimicDroid extracts trajectory pairs with similar manipulation behaviors and trains a policy to predict one trajectory's actions conditioned on the other, acquiring in-context-learning (test-time few-shot adaptation) capability for novel objects/environments; this outperforms SOTA methods and achieves nearly twofold higher success rates in the real world
claims.direction: favors training on unlabeled, freely-collected human play video (no teleoperation needed) plus in-context learning over labor-intensive teleoperated demonstration collection, for few-shot adaptation to novel objects
claims.conditions: humanoid robot, real-world evaluation, requires retargeting human wrist poses to the robot embodiment plus random patch masking to reduce overfitting to human-specific visual cues

title: Flow-Guided Policies: Overcoming Diffusion Limitations for Robust Robot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Conditional Flow (CoF) policy, which explicitly models a continuous flow transforming suboptimal actions toward expert-like behavior guided by a learned vector field (rather than the standard denoising process of Diffusion Policy), consistently outperforms Diffusion Policy in modeling diverse multimodal action distributions and executing high-quality behaviors on more complex, contact-rich tasks than DP has typically been applied to; to the authors' knowledge this is the first work to show Flow Matching can outperform diffusion-based policies in imitation learning
claims.direction: favors flow-matching-based (vector-field-guided) action policies over standard diffusion policies for complex, contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: simulation + real-robot case studies

claims.claim: CoF policy maintains strong performance even with significantly reduced sampling/denoising steps, making it well-suited for real-time robotic applications
claims.direction: favors flow matching over diffusion specifically for real-time (low-latency) deployment, since accuracy degrades less when steps are cut
claims.conditions: same sim + real-robot experiments

title: Reinforcement-Enhanced LLM-based Intelligent Robotics Programming for Autonomous Industrial Automation Systems

claims.claim: Edge deployment of the proposed framework using pruning and quantization achieves a 45% model-size reduction, a 47% inference-latency decrease, and a 36% reduction in power usage, with less than 2 percentage points of accuracy loss, compared to the unpruned/unquantized model
claims.direction: favors pruning plus quantization for edge deployment to substantially cut model size, latency, and power draw at minimal accuracy cost
claims.conditions: industrial robotic arms + mobile industrial robots, hybrid LLM+hierarchical-RL+CBF framework; edge-adaptive deployment setting

title: AtlasVA: Self-Evolving Visual Skill Memory for Teacher-Free VLM Agents

claims.claim: Organizing agent memory into visually-grounded layers (spatial heatmaps, visual exemplars, symbolic text skills) that self-evolve directly from trajectory statistics and lightweight grid heuristics (rather than storing memory as text summarized by a proprietary teacher LLM) and reusing these as potential-based shaping rewards for RL, consistently outperforms text-centric memory baselines and competitive VLM agents, with especially strong gains on spatially intensive tasks including 3D robotic manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors visually-grounded, self-evolving multi-layer memory over text-only memory summarized by an external teacher model, especially for spatially demanding tasks
claims.conditions: evaluated across Sokoban, FrozenLake, 3D embodied navigation, and 3D robotic manipulation benchmarks; no external LLM supervision required

title: Self-Supervised Bootstrapping of Action-Predictive Embodied Reasoning

claims.claim: Treating embodied chain-of-thought reasoning as a latent variable within importance-weighted variational inference (rather than using rigid, hand-specified reasoning templates that force policies to process irrelevant primitives) lets models self-supervised-ly bootstrap and distill a refined reasoning training dataset of embodiment-specific strategies, without external rewards, verifiers, or human annotation; across manipulation (Franka Panda sim, WidowX hardware), legged navigation, and driving embodiments with VLA architectures from 1B to 30B parameters, this achieves 28% gains in manipulation success, 101% improvement in navigation scores, and 21% reduction in collision rate versus models reasoning indiscriminately about all available primitives
claims.direction: favors self-supervised, importance-weighted refinement of which reasoning primitives to attend to (task-adaptive CoT) over rigid, fixed reasoning templates that process all primitives indiscriminately
claims.conditions: real-hardware validation (WidowX) plus simulation (Franka Panda), tested across VLA model scales from 1B to 30B parameters

title: Event-VLA: Action-Conditioned Event Fusion for Robust Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Standard RGB-centric VLA policies assume well-lit, stable indoor settings and degrade under illumination shifts; injecting an illumination-robust, motion-sensitive event-camera stream through an action-query routing pathway (learnable action queries extract task-relevant semantics, selectively aggregated via gated cross-attention into event-aware action representations, rather than naively merging event features into the global semantic token space) preserves pretrained RGB-language semantic priors while improving success rates under low-light and near-dark real-world conditions, maintaining strong performance under normal lighting too
claims.direction: favors action-query-routed event-camera fusion (rather than naive multimodal token merging) as a targeted fix for illumination-robustness, over RGB-only VLA policies
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world deployment across varying illumination levels; requires event-camera hardware in addition to standard RGB cameras

title: AcrossVAM1.0: Particle World Modeling for Text-Assisted Robot Video Prediction

claims.claim: A lightweight (0.28M-parameter) spatio-temporal Transformer that factorizes future video prediction into object-centric motion (semantic particles for robot/arm/gripper plus a background latent, from a frozen SAM3-DLP codec) and appearance (encoded only from the last observed frame, combined via a causal dual-stream decoder), reduces trajectory error by 21.0% over a simple persistence baseline on a real-robot video-prediction benchmark, though it does not yet beat persistence on perceptual similarity (LPIPS), and language-instruction correctness affects trajectory error by only 2.8-3.1%, indicating weak language grounding in the current design
claims.direction: favors factorized particle-based motion prediction over monolithic pixel-level video prediction for the motion-accuracy component specifically, but reports this alone is not yet sufficient for full video-prediction quality or strong language grounding
claims.conditions: real-robot trajectories (VRS benchmark); extremely small model size (0.28M parameters) matching low-compute settings; self-reported limitations included by the authors

title: AnyViewDex: View-Invariant Dexterous Manipulation from RGB Observations

claims.claim: Instead of relying on explicit 3D modalities (RGB-D or point clouds) at test time for viewpoint invariance, AnyViewDex encodes geometric knowledge into the visual representation during simulated training (via an asymmetric pipeline combining multi-view contrastive alignment with privileged 3D geometric supervision -- regressing absolute 3D object coordinates -- which mitigates spatial collapse of the globally pooled contrastive embedding); at deployment the policy operates zero-shot using only uncalibrated monocular RGB and proprioception, reaching 76.7% grasping success across eight unseen objects and six uncalibrated viewpoints (480 trials) on a real xArm7 with a 16-DoF LEAP Hand
claims.direction: favors training-time-only privileged 3D geometric supervision (regressing 3D coordinates during sim training) distilled into an RGB-only policy, over requiring depth sensors or point clouds at deployment, for viewpoint-invariant manipulation
claims.conditions: real-hardware evaluation (xArm7 + 16-DoF LEAP Hand), 8 unseen objects, 6 uncalibrated viewpoints, validated with both RL and student-teacher distillation training

claims.claim: The approach achieves view invariance without test-time 3D sensing or camera calibration, directly addressing sensitivity to camera viewpoint shifts that typically degrades visuomotor dexterous policies
claims.direction: favors training-time geometric grounding over hardware-based (multi-camera/depth-sensor) solutions for viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: same real-hardware evaluation, uncalibrated cameras

why_deep_read: Real-hardware validation (480 trials) of RGB-only, viewpoint-invariant manipulation via training-time-only privileged 3D supervision is highly relevant to our 'camera slightly moved' failure mode and could reduce reliance on precise camera calibration or depth at deployment; want details on how much simulated privileged-3D training data/effort is needed and whether it transfers to a simple parallel-gripper task like ours rather than a dexterous hand.

title: Efficient Robotic Policy Learning via Latent Space Backward Planning

claims.claim: Backward subgoal planning in latent space (grounding final goal first, then recursive intermediate subgoals) outperforms fine-grained pixel-prediction and forward-planning world models on long-horizon multi-stage tasks
claims.direction: favors latent backward subgoal planning over forward pixel-level world models
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot long-horizon experiments

title: FLARE: Robot Learning with Implicit World Modeling

claims.claim: Aligning diffusion transformer policy features with latent embeddings of future observations (implicit world modeling) improves performance by up to 26% over prior baselines, and enables generalization to novel objects with as few as a single demonstration when co-trained on human egocentric video without action labels
claims.direction: favors adding future-latent auxiliary objective to diffusion-transformer VLA policies
claims.conditions: two multitask simulation benchmarks (single-arm and humanoid tabletop); lightweight addition of a few tokens to standard VLA models

title: ROPA: Synthetic Robot Pose Generation for RGB-D Bimanual Data Augmentation

claims.claim: Fine-tuning Stable Diffusion to synthesize novel third-person RGB(-D) robot poses with paired joint-space action labels (physically constrained via gripper-object contact) outperforms baselines/ablations for imitation-learning data augmentation
claims.direction: favors generative/synthetic pose augmentation over standard augmentation baselines
claims.conditions: 5 simulated + 3 real-world bimanual tasks, 2625 sim trials and 300 real-world trials, eye-to-hand (third-person) camera

claims.claim: Augmentation method generates both RGB and RGB-D observations for eye-to-hand training, addressing a gap versus prior work that mostly targeted eye-in-hand RGB-only augmentation
claims.direction: supports including RGB-D (not just RGB) in augmentation pipelines
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation

why_deep_read: Real-robot ablation numbers (2625 sim + 300 real trials) on generative augmentation vs baselines could directly inform whether generative/synthetic-pose augmentation is worth the engineering cost for our small pumpkin dataset.

title: From a Single Demonstration to a General Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A constraint-based (non-neural-trajectory) LfD pipeline achieves one-shot generalization (single demonstration) across object poses, geometries and unmodeled contact dynamics, reaching over 90% success on seven real-world multi-stage contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors structured/constraint-based representations over pure trajectory imitation when demo count is extremely low (1 demo)
claims.conditions: real-world robot, 7 multi-stage contact-rich tasks, single demonstration + self-guided exploration + human corrections

title: Humanoid Manipulation Interface: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Robot-Free Demonstrations

claims.claim: Portable robot-free data collection hardware achieves 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation
claims.direction: favors robot-free/portable demo collection over direct teleoperation for data throughput
claims.conditions: real humanoid, 5 whole-body tasks

claims.claim: Policy trained via hierarchical pipeline from robot-free demos attains 70% success rate in unseen environments
claims.direction: reports generalization performance number for unseen environments
claims.conditions: real humanoid whole-body manipulation tasks

title: PI-VLA: Adaptive Symmetry-Aware Decision-Making for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: An uncertainty-resolving module dynamically adjusts the execution horizon via closed-loop replanning when action-consensus discrepancies or state-prediction errors (symmetry-breaking signals) are detected, and ablations confirm this is critical to robust execution
claims.direction: favors adaptive/dynamic execution horizon over fixed chunking
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark + real-world manipulation under visual distractions

claims.claim: Jointly generating discrete and continuous action chunks together with predictive world-model features in a single forward pass improves cross-modal action consistency
claims.direction: favors hybrid discrete+continuous action generation with joint world-model prediction
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation (73.2% avg success, strong on Long-Horizon suite) and real-world (88.3% success)

claims.claim: Reports 88.3% real-world success under visual distractions and unseen conditions
claims.direction: reports robustness number under distractors/unseen conditions
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Ablations isolating the contribution of dynamic execution-horizon replanning vs fixed chunking could directly inform our Q06/Q10 jerky chunk-boundary problem.

title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud

claims.claim: A unified inference runtime achieves 1.40x-4.65x speedups over official implementations of pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.7 and MiniCPM-Robot; on one config reduces latency from 2.46s to 1.18s (2.08x); profiling shows pi0.5's action expert is 8.8% of FLOPs but 57.2% of latency at batch size 1, dropping to 13.5%/higher throughput at batch 32
claims.direction: shows large latency reductions are achievable via runtime/serving engineering (not just model architecture) and that small action-expert modules can dominate latency at low batch size
claims.conditions: server GPUs (H20/Hopper), VLA and world-action models; batch-size dependent

title: TacSushi: Tactile-Grounded World-Action Modeling for Dexterous Sushi Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding a training-only decoder that predicts future visual observations, task progress, contact risk and tactile summaries from action chunks (removed at deployment) plus tactile gated fusion raises in-distribution success from 36.7% (no future-consequence supervision) to 68.3%, and out-of-distribution from 10.0% to 37.5%; direct tactile concatenation (no gating) only reaches 25.0%/17.5%
claims.direction: strongly favors auxiliary future-prediction/consequence supervision (training-only, removed at inference) plus gated multimodal fusion over no auxiliary objective or naive concatenation
claims.conditions: real robot, 340 successful + 50 failed demos, 3 in-distribution + 2 OOD food-manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Direct real-robot ablation with concrete success-rate deltas (36.7%->68.3%) for a training-only auxiliary future-prediction objective on a small demo count (~390) is highly relevant to whether we should add a similar cheap auxiliary head to our SmolVLA fine-tune.

title: Conditional variational auto encoder based dynamic motion for multitask imitation learning

claims.claim: Combining a cVAE (generating torque conditioned on task parameters) with a DMP dynamical system achieves 100% success in reaching and 93.33% in pushing/grasping with only one demonstration per task on a real UR10
claims.direction: favors cVAE+DMP hybrid over data-demanding deep-learning-only multitask methods in low-data regime
claims.conditions: real UR10 manipulator, 1 demonstration per task, pushing/reaching/grasping

claims.claim: Method reaches high success with only a single demonstration per task, contrasted with conventional deep-learning multitask methods that need large training data
claims.direction: favors structured motion-primitive priors to reduce demo count
claims.conditions: real robot, 1 demo/task

title: SutureBot: A Precision Framework & Benchmark For Autonomous End-to-End Suturing

claims.claim: Benchmarks state-of-the-art VLA models (pi0, GR00T N1, OpenVLA-OFT, multitask ACT), each augmented with a high-level task-prediction policy, on a real dexterous long-horizon suturing task on the da Vinci Research Kit; a goal-conditioned framework explicitly optimizing insertion-point precision improves targeting accuracy by 59%-74% over a task-only baseline
claims.direction: favors goal-conditioned/high-level task-prediction augmentation over task-only baseline for precision long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: real dVRK surgical robot, 1890 demonstrations, long-horizon dexterous task

claims.claim: Releases a high-fidelity dataset of 1,890 demonstrations to support reproducible benchmarking of precision-focused imitation learning policies
claims.direction: establishes a benchmark demo scale for comparison
claims.conditions: real robot dataset

why_deep_read: Direct head-to-head comparison of pi0, GR00T N1, OpenVLA-OFT and ACT on one real-robot benchmark would give us rare controlled cross-architecture evidence for Q01.

title: GeoVLA: Empowering 3D Representations in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Converting depth maps to point clouds and fusing 3D geometric embeddings (via a Point Embedding Network) with 2D vision-language embeddings, processed by a spatial-aware action expert, achieves SOTA results on LIBERO and ManiSkill2 versus 2D-only VLA baselines
claims.direction: favors adding depth/point-cloud 3D representation over 2D-only VLA input
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, ManiSkill2) and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: Shows improved robustness in real-world tasks requiring height adaptability, scale awareness, and viewpoint invariance versus 2D-only baselines
claims.direction: favors 3D-augmented representations for viewpoint/scale robustness
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Directly tests whether adding depth/point-cloud fusion (feasible with our RealSense depth) improves robustness to camera/viewpoint shift and scale — one of our key open questions (Q04 vs Q11 tradeoff).

title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization

claims.claim: Introduces 'Universal Async Chunking' to universalize chunked control across embodiments with different latency and control profiles, intended to stabilize cross-embodiment policies in the real world
claims.direction: favors an embodiment/latency-adaptive chunking scheme over a fixed chunk size
claims.conditions: real-world deployment across 5 robotic platforms; foundation-scale VLA (35,000+ hours pretraining)

claims.claim: Introduces 'Manifold-Preserving Gating' specifically for robustness under sensory shift, as part of achieving state-of-the-art LIBERO (98.9%) and RoboCasa (53.9%) results plus strong cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: favors gating mechanisms to preserve action-manifold structure under sensory/embodiment shift
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, RoboCasa) and real-world, 30 embodiments

claims.claim: Maps heterogeneous robot action spaces into a 'Unified Action Space' of semantically aligned slots to enable low-resource robots to bootstrap skills from human/high-resource robot data
claims.direction: favors a unified/aligned action-space representation over embodiment-specific raw action spaces for cross-embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: large-scale foundation model, 30 robot embodiments

why_deep_read: The Universal Async Chunking and Manifold-Preserving Gating techniques target exactly our jerky chunk-boundary and sensory/camera-shift problems; worth checking if the technique is describable/adoptable at small scale even though the base model is a large foundation model.

title: EgoScale: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation with Diverse Egocentric Human Data

claims.claim: Uncovers a log-linear scaling law between human video data scale and validation loss, and validation loss strongly correlates with downstream real-robot performance; a two-stage recipe (large-scale human pretraining + lightweight human-robot mid-training) improves average success rate by 54% over a no-pretraining baseline on a 22-DoF hand and transfers to lower-DoF hands
claims.direction: favors large-scale human-video pretraining plus small robot-data mid-training over training on robot demos alone
claims.conditions: real robot, 22-DoF dexterous hand, transfers to lower-DoF embodiments, 20,854 hours egocentric human video pretraining

title: Faster Visuomotor Policy Learning on Action Manifolds via Riemannian MeanFlow

claims.claim: A Riemannian MeanFlow policy learns a flow map (rather than integrating a vector field over many steps) achieving on-manifold action generation with as few as one network function evaluation, attaining performance competitive with diffusion/flow-matching baselines at lower sampling cost
claims.direction: favors consistency/mean-flow-style single-step action generation over multi-step diffusion/flow-matching sampling
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LASA, Push-T, Robomimic Tool Hang/Transport, Franka Kitchen) plus one real-world robotic manipulation task

claims.claim: Demonstrates fast action generation under imperfect sensor measurements on a real-world task, addressing the multi-step-integration latency bottleneck of diffusion/flow policies
claims.direction: favors reducing action-generation steps to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation task

why_deep_read: Directly targets our ~2s inference latency bottleneck by replacing multi-step diffusion/flow sampling with one-step generation; would help decide whether to keep flow matching for the action head under our 8GB GPU laptop constraint.

title: Temporal Logic Guidance for Action-Only Diffusion Policies with World Models

claims.claim: Using a separately learned world model to provide differentiable STL-robustness gradients for guiding an action-only diffusion policy at inference reduces constraint violations from over 80% (baseline) to 4% while maintaining 100% task success, without retraining
claims.direction: favors pairing a learned world model with diffusion-policy guidance over unguided action-only diffusion policies
claims.conditions: Robomimic Can Transport simulation task

title: Mitigating the Human-Robot Domain Discrepancy in Visual Pre-training for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A human-robot contrastive alignment loss adapts pretrained visual representations (bridging human video pretraining and robot domains) in a parameter-efficient manner, improving average success rate by over 7% across 20 simulated tasks (two benchmarks) and 5 real-world tasks, in both single-task and language-conditioned multi-task settings, using two different pretrained backbone models
claims.direction: favors adapting/aligning human-video-pretrained visual encoders to the robot domain over using such pretrained encoders unadapted
claims.conditions: real-world (5 tasks) and simulated (20 tasks, 2 benchmarks); tested with two different pretrained vision models

why_deep_read: Quantified, controlled evidence (+7% success) on adapting human-video-pretrained vision encoders is directly relevant to our Q03 choice of vision backbone and whether/how to fine-tune it for the SO-101 setup.

title: Imitation Learning Policy based on Multi-Step Consistent Integration Shortcut Model

claims.claim: A one-step shortcut model with multi-step consistency loss and adaptive gradient allocation narrows the performance gap to multi-step diffusion/flow-matching imitation-learning policies while requiring far fewer inference steps
claims.direction: favors distilled one-step/shortcut action generation over full multi-step diffusion or flow-matching for imitation learning
claims.conditions: 2 simulation benchmarks + 5 real-world environment tasks

claims.claim: Explicitly targets the high inference-time cost of flow-matching/diffusion imitation-learning policies as the problem to be solved
claims.direction: favors reducing sampling steps to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world tasks

why_deep_read: Directly addresses whether we can keep a flow-matching-style action head while cutting the ~2s inference latency via distillation to one/few-step sampling, evaluated on real-world tasks.

title: PRISM: Performer RS-IMLE for Single-pass Multisensory Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A single-pass IMLE-based policy (Performer linear-attention generator) outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion policies by 10-25% success rate on real-world hardware (Unitree Go2+D1 arm, UR5) while running closed-loop at 30-50 Hz, and on CALVIN with only 10% training data improves success by ~25% over diffusion and ~20% over flow matching
claims.direction: favors single-pass IMLE-style generation over multi-step diffusion/flow matching, especially in low-data settings
claims.conditions: real-world loco-manipulation and tabletop manipulation; also CALVIN/MetaWorld/Robomimic sim benchmarks; 10% data split

claims.claim: Reduces trajectory jerk by 20x-50x compared to diffusion/flow-matching baselines on CALVIN
claims.direction: favors single-pass generation for smoother, less jerky action sequences
claims.conditions: CALVIN benchmark, 10% data split

claims.claim: Improvement over diffusion/flow-matching baselines is especially pronounced in a reduced-data (10%) regime
claims.direction: favors this architecture when demonstration count is limited
claims.conditions: CALVIN 10% data split

why_deep_read: Directly reports large reductions in trajectory jerk (our chunk-boundary jerkiness problem) and better low-data performance than diffusion/flow matching on real hardware — could change our action-head decision (Q01) and chunking approach (Q06).

title: FAVLA: A Force-Adaptive Fast-Slow VLA model for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Decoupling a slow, low-frequency VLM (perception/planning) from a fast action-expert that runs at a variable high frequency conditioned on recent sensor data significantly outperforms single-frequency fused baselines in reactivity and success rate on contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors async fast-slow (dual-frequency) architecture over unified single-frequency VLM+action fusion for real-time reactive control
claims.conditions: real robot contact-rich manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Adaptively schedules the action-expert's execution frequency based on the VLM's predicted variation, rather than a fixed execution horizon
claims.direction: favors adaptive execution frequency/horizon over fixed chunking
claims.conditions: real robot contact-rich manipulation

title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Jointly predicting future RGB, scalar affordance fields, affordance heatmaps and continuous actions (via masked joint self-attention between separate world/action experts under a flow-matching objective) gives consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC->D, and real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors affordance-conditioned auxiliary world-modeling objectives over RGB-only or robot-action-only training
claims.conditions: simulation (RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC->D) and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: Under fixed robot supervision, performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video data scales, showing human video can substitute for scarce robot action-labeled data
claims.direction: favors incorporating scalable human video (via affordance supervision) to compensate for limited robot demonstration data
claims.conditions: RoboCasa simulation

title: Semantically Structured Mixture-of-Experts for Compositional Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A semantically-structured MoE diffusion policy, with a lightweight inference-time skill predictor supervised by VLM offline annotations routing action chunks to phase-specialized experts, outperforms representative diffusion and generic MoE baselines on multi-task benchmarks
claims.direction: favors semantically-grounded MoE routing over dense diffusion policies or noise/latent-based MoE routing
claims.conditions: multi-task manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Achieves significantly improved parameter efficiency (activating only a subset of parameters) versus dense diffusion baselines while maintaining/improving performance
claims.direction: favors sparse/MoE parameter-efficient architectures over dense models for compute-constrained multi-task settings
claims.conditions: multi-task benchmarks, parameter-efficient fine-tuning for novel task transfer

title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A fixed (not fine-tuned) VLA policy conditioned at test-time on retrieved, DTW-aligned micro-demonstrations reaches 97.7% on LIBERO, 60.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 (exceeding the best reported baseline by 19.3 percentage points), and 83.2% across four physical tasks, without additional gradient updates for new settings
claims.direction: favors retrieval-based in-context test-time adaptation over gradient-based fine-tuning when task/compute is scarce
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0) and 4 real physical tasks

claims.claim: Introduces 'Target Action Masking' to reduce direct action-copying from retrieved context and increase reliance on current observation, addressing a copycat-style failure mode
claims.direction: identifies and mitigates a copycat/over-reliance-on-retrieved-context failure
claims.conditions: real and simulated tasks

title: Stochastic Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Skill Acquisition From a Suboptimal Demonstration

claims.claim: Denoising jittery/suboptimal demonstrated trajectories in the frequency domain (via a proposed MSES metric) combined with a multi-policy stochastic trajectory optimizer (MSTOMP) improves optimization performance and stability over existing methods on both sim and real robots
claims.direction: favors post-hoc trajectory optimization/denoising of imperfect (jittery, slow) human demonstrations rather than using them as-is
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments; addresses demonstrations with jitter and suboptimal dynamics

why_deep_read: Directly targets denoising jittery/suboptimal demonstrations, matching our Feetech servo jitter/backlash problem during teleop data collection — worth checking if the frequency-domain denoising method is applicable to our ~50-100 demo pipeline.

title: Robotic Compliant Object Prying Using Diffusion Policy Guided by Vision and Force Observations

claims.claim: A diffusion policy fusing vision with force feedback (addressing dilution of low-dim force by high-dim images) achieves 96% success on a real battery-prying task, a 57% improvement over a vision-only diffusion-policy baseline, with zero-shot transfer to unseen objects
claims.direction: supports diffusion policies as a real-robot-viable action head, and shows fusing an additional low-dimensional modality substantially helps over vision-only
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich battery disassembly task

title: Blindfolded Experts Generalize Better: Insights from Robotic Manipulation and Videogames

claims.claim: Cloning a 'blindfolded' expert (demonstrator with deliberately hidden task information, forced to explore) generalizes better to unseen tasks than cloning a fully-informed expert, with generalization error theoretically scaling as sqrt(I/m) where I is task information available to the demonstrator and m is number of demonstrated tasks; validated on real-world robot peg-insertion with limited human demonstrations
claims.direction: favors limiting demonstrator information (encouraging exploratory demonstrations) over fully-informed near-optimal demonstrations, especially when task count/demos are limited
claims.conditions: real-world robot peg insertion with limited human demonstrations, plus Procgen videogames; theoretical analysis included

claims.claim: Improved generalization to unseen tasks/variations is the primary outcome measured
claims.direction: supports a specific demo-collection strategy for better generalization
claims.conditions: real-world robot and videogame domains

why_deep_read: Counterintuitive, theoretically-grounded finding that CONTRADICTS common practice (giving the demonstrator full task information) and could directly change how we collect our ~50-100 teleop demos for better generalization.

title: Taming VR Teleoperation and Learning from Demonstration for Multi-Task Bimanual Table Service Manipulation

claims.claim: An ACT-based policy trained from 100 in-person teleoperated demonstrations with randomized initial configurations, combined with VR teleoperation for other subtasks, won first place in the ICRA 2025 WBCD Table Service competition
claims.direction: demonstrates ACT with ~100 demos is sufficient for a competitive real bimanual pick-and-place subtask when combined with randomized initial configurations
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot competition, 100 demonstrations, randomized initial object configurations

title: MimicFunc: Imitating Tool Manipulation from a Single Human Video via Functional Correspondence

claims.claim: A function-centric local coordinate frame (keypoint-based abstraction) lets a robot generalize a tool-manipulation skill from a single RGB-D human video to novel tools performing functionally equivalent tasks, and the generated rollouts can train visuomotor policies without labor-intensive teleoperation for novel objects
claims.direction: favors one-shot human-video imitation plus rollout generation over teleoperation data collection for scaling to new objects
claims.conditions: real robot, single RGB-D human demonstration video

title: Prepare Before You Act: Learning From Humans to Rearrange Initial States

claims.claim: ReSET autonomously rearranges out-of-distribution initial object poses (using action-agnostic human videos + task-agnostic teleoperation data) before executing a given policy; comparisons with diffusion policies, VLAs, and other baselines show this two-step process enables more robust task execution with equal amounts of total training data
claims.direction: favors adding an environment-preparation/rearrangement step over relying solely on the policy to handle OOD initial states
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, compared against diffusion policies and VLAs with equal training data

claims.claim: Theoretically and empirically reduces the generalization gap without requiring additional demonstrations, i.e., more robust behavior at equal total data budget
claims.direction: favors this two-stage approach as more data-efficient than scaling demonstrations to cover OOD states
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation

title: See Selectively, Act Adaptively: Dual-Level Structural Decomposition for Bimanual Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A View-Selective Visual Router that dynamically adjusts wrist-camera vs other view contributions to emphasize task-relevant visual cues, combined with an Interaction-Aware Action Mixture-of-Experts, improves overall average success rate over a monolithic baseline by 27.7% in simulation (RoboTwin 2.0, six tasks) and 43.3% in real-world (three long-horizon tasks)
claims.direction: favors dynamic, task-stage-dependent weighting of camera views (e.g., wrist vs scene camera) over static/fixed multi-view fusion
claims.conditions: 6 simulated bimanual tasks (RoboTwin 2.0) + 3 real-world long-horizon bimanual tasks

claims.claim: Decomposing action generation into coordinated and arm-wise pathways (Mixture-of-Experts) outperforms a monolithic action-generation module, and both visual routing and action decomposition contribute independently (single-module variants underperform the full model)
claims.direction: favors structured/decomposed action generation over a single monolithic action head
claims.conditions: same bimanual benchmarks as above

why_deep_read: The View-Selective Visual Router (dynamically weighting wrist-camera vs scene-camera contributions by task stage) is directly applicable to our two-camera (scene+wrist) setup and could inform how we fuse/weight our cameras (Q11).

title: PRISM: Personalized Refinement of Imitation Skills for Manipulation via Human Instructions

claims.claim: Refining an imitation policy with RL (Eureka-style LLM-generated rewards) plus human feedback correction on intermediate rollouts outperforms policies without human feedback, improving robustness and reducing computational burden, enabling data-efficient adaptation to new goal configurations
claims.direction: favors adding lightweight human-feedback-guided RL refinement on top of an initial IL policy over IL alone
claims.conditions: simulated pick-and-place task

title: DeVA: Decoupled Video-Action Model with physical guidance for robot policy learning

claims.claim: A decoupled video-expert/action-expert architecture with multi-level feature transfer, supervising intermediate video features and the action stream with physically salient guidance (affordance/depth), shows clear performance gains from this physical guidance versus without it, and converges faster than a unified video+action backbone
claims.direction: favors decoupled video-prediction auxiliary objective (with affordance/depth supervision) over a single shared backbone for video and action, and over omitting this auxiliary supervision
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks and real-world deployment

claims.claim: Achieves strong performance with limited data
claims.direction: favors this architecture in low-demo-count regimes
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world, limited-data condition stated qualitatively

title: Decoupling the Declarative from the Procedural in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Instead of feeding all multimodal VLM tokens into a large opaque transformer action expert, modulating the robot-state sequence with visual, spatial, and skill information compositionally decouples declarative (concept/entity) knowledge from procedural (how-to) knowledge encoded in VLA parameters
claims.direction: favors a modular, compositional/interpretable action-conditioning architecture over a monolithic large action-expert transformer fed all tokens
claims.conditions: VLA models fine-tuned from pretrained billion-parameter VLMs on robot data

claims.claim: Shows 'unprecedented zero-shot skill transfer' to dissimilar, unseen objects, whereas standard state-of-the-art VLAs remain brittle to minor spatial, semantic and task variations despite large-scale pretraining plus scenario-specific fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors the modular architecture for generalizing to novel objects over standard monolithic VLA fine-tuning
claims.conditions: comparison against popular state-of-the-art VLAs; unseen/dissimilar objects

why_deep_read: Zero-shot transfer to unseen/dissimilar objects is precisely our observed failure mode (breaks on a different-looking pumpkin); the declarative/procedural decoupling architecture could directly inform how to restructure our SmolVLA fine-tune for better object generalization.

title: When Does Legacy Data Start to Help? Emergent Transfer in Cross-Configuration Robot Learning

claims.claim: Contrary to the assumption that more cross-configuration legacy data always helps, co-training with legacy demonstrations (different camera/gripper) shows a three-phase pattern: no benefit at low new-hardware competence (10.0%->10.0%), a sharp gain after crossing a competence threshold (23.3%->86.7% on flower insertion), and diminishing returns at high competence (85.0%->93.3% on pen insertion); a phase-aware rule is derived for when to collect new data vs reuse legacy demos
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that mixing in more legacy/cross-configuration demonstration data is always helpful; benefit is threshold-dependent
claims.conditions: real-robot wheeled humanoid, two hardware generations (camera+gripper changed), validated also on a mobile dual-arm watering task

title: ROS2SmolVLA: Enabling Small Vision-Language-Action Models for Integration into Industrial-Grade Lightweight Robots

claims.claim: Adapting Hugging Face's SmolVLA (a small VLA) to a Universal Robots UR10e via a released ROS2 interface, validated on a pick-and-place task, supports SmolVLA as well-suited for small-sized tasks computed on-premise (no cloud/large-model dependency)
claims.direction: supports using small, on-premise-computable VLA models (like SmolVLA) for lightweight industrial robots rather than large cloud-dependent models
claims.conditions: real Universal Robots UR10e, pick-and-place task

title: IRASim: A Fine-Grained World Model for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: A diffusion-transformer world model with frame-level action-conditioning generates video with fine-grained action-frame alignment; policy evaluations using this world model correlate strongly with ground-truth simulator evaluations, and model-based test-time planning with it improves Push-T IoU from 0.637 to 0.961
claims.direction: supports using learned world models both for offline policy evaluation and for test-time planning to boost performance
claims.conditions: simulation (Push-T benchmark); video quality scales with model size/compute

title: OKAMI: Teaching Humanoid Robots Manipulation Skills through Single Video Imitation

claims.claim: Object-aware retargeting from a single RGB-D human video, without teleoperation, produces rollout trajectories that train closed-loop visuomotor policies achieving an average 79.2% success rate
claims.direction: favors single-video human imitation as a substitute for labor-intensive teleoperation data collection
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot, single video demonstration, outperforms SOTA open-world imitation-from-observation baseline

title: RoboGrasp: A Universal Grasping Policy for Robust Robotic Control

claims.claim: Integrating pretrained grasp-detection/segmentation models as visual guidance into a diffusion-based imitation policy (rather than relying on raw RGB + arm state alone, which overfits to specific object shapes/positions) improves grasp precision and generalizability
claims.direction: favors augmenting diffusion action heads with external object-detection/segmentation guidance over relying on raw RGB+state
claims.conditions: few-shot learning and grasping box-prompt tasks

claims.claim: Achieves up to 34% higher success rates in few-shot learning settings versus baseline
claims.direction: favors this guided approach for improved few-shot data efficiency
claims.conditions: few-shot learning tasks

title: LoHoVLA: A Unified Vision-Language-Action Model for Long-Horizon Embodied Tasks

claims.claim: A unified VLA that jointly generates language sub-task tokens and robot action tokens from a shared pretrained VLM backbone, with hierarchical closed-loop control to correct planning/control errors, significantly surpasses both hierarchical and standard VLA baselines on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors a single shared-backbone model jointly producing language and action tokens over separate hierarchical planner+controller VLA architectures
claims.conditions: simulation only (Ravens simulator, custom 20-task LoHoSet dataset, 1000 demos/task)

title: Planning from Point Clouds over Continuous Actions for Multi-object Rearrangement

claims.claim: A hybrid search-and-learning planner (SPOT) operating on point clouds, with learned action suggesters sampling continuous transformations directly from partially-observed point clouds, outperforms a policy-learning approach on multi-object rearrangement, with ablations confirming the importance of search-based planning
claims.direction: favors point-cloud-based continuous-action planning combined with search over pure learned-policy baselines
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world multi-object rearrangement

title: Video-Enhanced Offline Reinforcement Learning: A Model-Based Approach

claims.claim: Constructing an interactive world model from diverse unlabeled online video (transferring commonsense control/dynamics knowledge) yields substantial performance gains (over 100% in some cases) on visual control tasks including robotic manipulation
claims.direction: favors leveraging large unlabeled video for an auxiliary/world-model objective to boost policy performance beyond what robot-only data supports
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation, autonomous driving, and video games; offline RL setting

title: D-CODA: Diffusion for Coordinated Dual-Arm Data Augmentation

claims.claim: A diffusion model trained to synthesize novel, viewpoint-consistent wrist-camera images (with constrained optimization for valid gripper-object contact) plus matching joint-space action labels outperforms baselines and ablations for eye-in-hand bimanual imitation-learning data augmentation, validated across 2250 simulation trials and 300 real-world trials on 5 sim + 3 real tasks
claims.direction: favors generative/diffusion-based wrist-camera-consistent data augmentation over standard augmentation baselines for eye-in-hand setups
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation, eye-in-hand (wrist camera) setting

claims.claim: Specifically targets wrist-mounted (eye-in-hand) camera augmentation, showing the augmentation must preserve viewpoint consistency between both arms' wrist cameras to remain valid
claims.direction: highlights that wrist-camera augmentation requires viewpoint-consistency constraints not needed for third-person augmentation
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual eye-in-hand manipulation

why_deep_read: This is an eye-in-hand (wrist-camera) augmentation method with real-robot ablation numbers — directly matches our wrist-camera setup, unlike the earlier eye-to-hand ROPA paper, so worth reading in full for concrete augmentation recipes we could adapt.

title: CodeGraphVLP: Code-as-Planner Meets Semantic-Graph State for Non-Markovian Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Maintaining a persistent semantic-graph state (task-relevant entities/relations under partial observability) plus a code-based planner that constructs clutter-suppressed observations improves task completion on non-Markovian long-horizon tasks over strong VLA baselines and history-enabled variants, while lowering planning latency versus VLM-in-the-loop planning
claims.direction: favors explicit persistent symbolic/graph memory over implicit observation-history conditioning for handling non-Markovian, occlusion-prone tasks
claims.conditions: real-world non-Markovian manipulation tasks; ablation studies confirm component contributions

title: Where Success Breaks: Failure-Boundary Learning for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: DLS discovers failure boundaries via on-policy digital-twin rollouts with progress-aware (not just binary) success signals from privileged simulator states, then shapes flow-matching denoising directions toward success; this improves robustness over SFT and online-RL baselines especially under randomized initial states and unseen visual conditions on real-robot tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit failure-boundary discovery/shaping (using sim co-training) over standard supervised fine-tuning or online RL for robustness to visual/state variation
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation, built from few real demonstrations plus simulated co-training

claims.claim: Uses only a few real demonstrations plus simulated co-training as the 'real-grounded behavioral prior', rather than requiring large real demo counts
