claims.direction: favors combining few real demos with simulation-based boundary discovery over collecting more real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation

why_deep_read: Directly targets robustness under randomized initial states and unseen visual conditions — our core failure mode — using only a few real demos plus sim co-training, which matches our low-demo-count situation.

title: Phone2Act: A Low-Cost, Hardware-Agnostic Teleoperation System for Scalable VLA Data Collection

claims.claim: A smartphone-based (ARCore) 6-DoF teleoperation system exporting directly to LeRobot format was used to fine-tune GR00T-N1.5 on 130 collected episodes, achieving 90% success on a real-world multi-stage pick-and-place task on a low-cost robot (Dobot CR5)
claims.direction: supports that ~130 low-cost-collected demonstrations can be sufficient for a real multi-stage pick-and-place task when fine-tuning a modern VLA
claims.conditions: real-world Dobot CR5, 130 demonstrations, LeRobot dataset format

title: Native Video-Action Pretraining for Generalizable Robot Control (LingBot-VA 2.0)

claims.claim: An enhanced asynchronous inference scheme predicts future latents in parallel with action execution while re-grounding each rollout on the latest observation via learned forward dynamics, enabling real-time closed-loop control
claims.direction: favors asynchronous execution with continuous re-grounding on latest observations over naive open-loop chunk execution, to reduce staleness/jerkiness at chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: real-world deployment; few-shot generalization across complex manipulation tasks

claims.claim: A semantic visual-action tokenizer (aligning visual representations with both semantics and actions, rather than a reconstruction-focused VAE) improves instruction following and action precision in downstream policy learning
claims.direction: favors semantically-aligned action tokenization over reconstruction-focused tokenizers
claims.conditions: video-action foundation model pretraining

claims.claim: A sparse Mixture-of-Experts backbone expands model capacity without compromising inference efficiency, and causal (not bidirectional) pretraining from scratch avoids catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: favors sparse MoE plus causal pretraining over bidirectional/dense architectures for high-frequency inference needs
claims.conditions: foundation-model-scale video-action pretraining

why_deep_read: The asynchronous inference scheme (parallel future-latent prediction with re-grounding on latest observation) directly targets our exact reported problem of jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries under async inference.

title: SAIL: Test-Time Scaling for In-Context Imitation Learning with VLM

claims.claim: Reframing one-shot imitation as iterative test-time refinement (MCTS over trajectory refinements, guided by VLM scoring) shows success rate consistently improves with more test-time compute, reaching up to 95% on complex tasks
claims.direction: favors spending test-time compute on trajectory refinement/retrieval over collecting more demonstrations
claims.conditions: six manipulation tasks in simulation and real-world

title: PriGo: Test-Time Primitive Guidance to Diffusion and Flow Policies for Adaptive Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A lightweight test-time primitive-prediction module plus differentiable primitive guidance, added to pretrained diffusion/flow policies without retraining, consistently improves robustness, long-horizon execution, and generalization across both diffusion and flow-based policies
claims.direction: favors adding test-time primitive guidance to existing diffusion/flow action heads over using them unguided
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN, SIMPLER simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks

claims.claim: Addresses the failure mode of imitating superficial action correlations rather than underlying intent, improving generalization across tasks and environments
claims.direction: supports primitive-level guidance as a generalization booster
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

title: WA-SpecDec: World-Aware Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Injecting world-model-derived scene awareness into speculative decoding for autoregressive VLA policies preserves higher task success under looser token-acceptance relaxation and enables longer accepted draft prefixes, achieving a 1.5x matched-success speedup over standard VLA speculative decoding and reducing near-contact failures by 18.6% on average
claims.direction: favors scene-aware (vs scene-agnostic) speculative decoding for cutting closed-loop VLA latency without sacrificing safety near contact
claims.conditions: three state-of-the-art relaxed-acceptance speculative decoding schemes as baselines

title: CASD: Chunk-Aligned Semantic Distillation for Multi-Stage Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Deriving weighted semantic (stage) targets for an entire action chunk (rather than labeling only its first step) and distilling this into a frozen generator whose predictions condition the policy improves success versus references without this chunk-level semantic supervision: IDM+CASD reaches 98.9% vs 98.0% on LIBERO, Joint+CASD reaches 93.0% vs 90.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, DreamZero+CASD reaches 47.9% vs 40.7% on MolmoSpaces
claims.direction: favors chunk-level (not just first-step) semantic stage labeling/distillation as an auxiliary signal for action chunks
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, MolmoSpaces); across multiple Fast-WAM/DreamZero backbone variants, with performance varying by backbone

claims.claim: An offline VLM-derived semantic-stage distillation target, computed once per policy query (no online VLM calls), acts as an effective auxiliary objective for the policy
claims.direction: favors cheap offline-distilled semantic auxiliary targets over online VLM reasoning during inference
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks

title: ActiveArena: Benchmarking and Understanding Active Perception in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Controlled studies of memory writing, memory capacity, proprioceptive state, and subtask supervision show uniform memory sampling, larger memory capacity (under reliable write policies), proprioceptive inputs, and subtask supervision all improve OOD generalization, while planner-guided memory management can match best-performing configurations using only sparse memory
claims.direction: identifies which observation-history/memory design choices help OOD generalization versus a substantial ID-OOD gap seen otherwise
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark (ActiveArena-Sim/Bench), 35 tasks, ID/OOD protocols with disjoint scenes, distractors, novel backgrounds

title: SPOT: SE(3) Pose Trajectory Diffusion for Object-Centric Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing a task via an object-centric SE(3) object-pose trajectory (relative to target), which decouples embodiment action from sensory input and conditions a diffusion policy, enables learning from both action-based and action-less human-hand demonstrations and cross-embodiment generalization, capturing planning constraints without hand-crafted rules
claims.direction: favors object-centric SE(3) pose-trajectory action representation over embodiment-specific joint/end-effector action spaces, especially for generalization and mixed demo types
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world tasks

claims.claim: Using only eight demonstrations shot on an iPhone, the real-world evaluation completed all tasks while fully complying with task constraints
claims.direction: reports very high data efficiency (8 demos) for this action representation
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, 8 iPhone-recorded demonstrations

why_deep_read: Only 8 real-world demonstrations achieving full task compliance is a striking data-efficiency result directly relevant to our ~50-100-demo budget, and the object-centric SE(3) action representation is a fundamentally different Q02 choice worth understanding in depth.

title: Discrete Policy: Learning Disentangled Action Space for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A vector-quantized discrete-latent action-space policy outperforms Diffusion Policy, ACT, Octo, and OpenVLA on real-world multi-task manipulation (single-arm and bimanual): in a 5-task real-world setting it beats Diffusion Policy by 26% and OpenVLA by 15% average success rate, and the gap widens to 32.5% (vs Diffusion Policy) as tasks scale to 12
claims.direction: favors VQ/discrete-token action representations over continuous diffusion-based or standard autoregressive (OpenVLA/ACT/Octo) action heads, especially as task count grows
claims.conditions: real-world single-arm and bimanual manipulation, multi-task (5 to 12 tasks), controlled comparison against Diffusion Policy, ACT, Octo, OpenVLA

why_deep_read: One of the few controlled real-world head-to-head comparisons across VQ/discrete, diffusion, ACT, Octo and OpenVLA action heads — directly and rigorously answers our top-priority Q01 decision.

title: Enhancing Generalization in Vision-Language-Action Models by Preserving Pretrained Representations

claims.claim: A dual-encoder design (one frozen vision encoder retaining pretrained features, one trainable encoder for task adaptation), a string-based action tokenizer casting actions into character sequences aligned with the VLM's pretraining domain, and co-training with vision-language data emphasizing spatial reasoning/affordances together improve robustness to visual perturbations and generalization versus baselines, in both simulation and on real robots
claims.direction: favors partially freezing the vision encoder (dual-encoder) plus pretraining-aligned action tokenization over fully fine-tuning the whole VLM on robot data alone
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot evaluation

claims.claim: Improves generalization to novel instructions and environments and overall task success compared to baselines that directly fine-tune all VLM weights on robot data
claims.direction: supports representation-preserving fine-tuning strategies for better generalization
claims.conditions: real-robot and simulation evaluation

claims.claim: Co-training with vision-language datasets emphasizing spatial reasoning and affordances (alongside robot demonstrations) contributes to the generalization gains
claims.direction: favors co-training with general VL data over training on robot demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: real-robot and simulation evaluation

why_deep_read: Directly tests whether freezing part of the vision encoder and preserving pretrained representations (vs standard full fine-tuning, which is what our SmolVLA fine-tune currently does) improves robustness to visual perturbations and generalization — precisely our Q03 decision and our lighting/object-shift failure mode.

title: Trajectory-Consistent Flow Matching for Robust Visuomotor Policy Learning

claims.claim: Standard flow-matching training (pointwise velocity objective) mismatches multi-step numerical-integration inference, causing compounding trajectory errors; adding auxiliary rectified-flow regression, multi-step trajectory-consistency training, velocity-field smoothness regularization, and RK4 (vs Euler) inference together are needed (ablations show each alone is insuffient) and achieve 70% and 60% success on two long-horizon real-robot tasks where both baselines (standard flow matching / diffusion) score 0%, and 100% on a precision tool-placement task
claims.direction: favors closing the train-inference gap in flow-matching action heads via these four combined remedies over standard flow-matching training/Euler inference
claims.conditions: real robots (Franka arm and Boston Dynamics Spot), 4 real-robot tasks; 3 MetaWorld sim tasks confirm consistent gains

claims.claim: Pairs the flow-matching policy with a dual-view 3D point-cloud encoder (two independent PointNet encoders) for complementary spatial perception
claims.direction: supports point-cloud-based (not RGB-only) perception for these long-horizon real-robot tasks
claims.conditions: same real-robot tasks

why_deep_read: Shows baselines (standard flow matching/diffusion) scoring literally 0% on real long-horizon tasks while the fixed version reaches 60-70%; if we adopt a flow-matching action head, these specific train-inference-gap fixes (RK4 inference, trajectory-consistency loss) could be critical and are cheap to implement.

title: AffordGen: Generating Diverse Demonstrations for Generalizable Object Manipulation with Afford Correspondence

claims.claim: Using 3D generative models and vision foundation models to find semantic correspondence of affordance keypoints across large-scale 3D meshes, new manipulation trajectories are synthesized to train a closed-loop visuomotor policy, significantly improving data efficiency versus training on collected demonstrations alone
claims.direction: favors affordance-correspondence-based synthetic trajectory generation as a data augmentation/generation strategy over relying solely on collected demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments

claims.claim: Policies trained with this synthetic data achieve zero-shot generalization to truly unseen objects with high success rates
claims.direction: supports synthetic affordance-driven demo generation for novel-object generalization
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, unseen objects

title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs

claims.claim: Storing progress-calibrated successful observation-action segments from prior deployment episodes and retrieving/steering the flow-matching action sampler with them (confidence-adaptive prior guidance) improves task success and closed-loop stability without any parameter updates, especially for long-horizon/multi-stage tasks
claims.direction: favors non-parametric, memory-based test-time adaptation using the robot's own successful experience over static frozen deployment or retraining
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, persistent-deployment (repeated/slowly-changing environment) setting

claims.claim: Uses a long-term memory of past successful observation-action segments retrieved at inference, filtered by trajectory-level consistency
claims.direction: supports an explicit external memory mechanism as an alternative to relying purely on short observation history
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Robust Bimanual Vision-Language-Action Models via Embarrassingly Simple Modality Masking

claims.claim: A training-only Modality Masking Mechanism (M3) that stochastically masks subsets of modality channels (e.g., camera views, language) during training, with no architectural changes or extra pretraining, improves average success by 21.7% in a Clean setting and 11.4% in Clean2Rand (train on clean demos, evaluate on randomized scenes) versus an Adapter baseline, and improves real-world full-task success by over 30%
claims.direction: favors simple stochastic modality/channel masking during training as a robustness-improving augmentation over standard multi-view/language fusion training
claims.conditions: 10 bimanual tasks in RoboTwin 2.0 simulation + 3 long-horizon real-world tasks

claims.claim: Improves robustness specifically when training on clean demonstrations and evaluating on randomized scenes (Clean2Rand), addressing attention spreading to distracting regions
claims.direction: supports modality masking as a lightweight way to reduce reliance on distracting/unstable cues and improve generalization to randomized scenes
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Identifies unstable multi-view (camera) and language fusion, with attention spreading to distracting regions, as a contributing factor to discontinuous actions/failures in low-latency query-based VLA models
claims.direction: identifies multi-view fusion instability as a failure mode to be mitigated
claims.conditions: bimanual query-based VLA models

why_deep_read: An architecture-free, training-only technique (random modality/channel masking) with real-world numbers (+30% full-task success, +11-22% in sim) directly targeting robustness to randomized/novel scenes — cheap to try on our small SmolVLA fine-tune and directly relevant to our lighting/background/camera-shift robustness problem.

title: Light-WAM: Efficient World Action Models with State-Fusion Action Decoding

claims.claim: Performing future-video supervision in a downsampled latent space with a compact video backbone retains the representation-learning benefits of future-prediction auxiliary objectives while reducing training cost versus large-scale generative World Action Models
claims.direction: favors lightweight/downsampled future-video auxiliary objectives over large generative WAM architectures
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks

claims.claim: Using only 0.44B trainable parameters and a StateFusionActionExpert that fuses adapted states from multiple backbone layers via learned-query pooling to predict action chunks in a single forward pass, Light-WAM maintains strong LIBERO performance and usable multi-task RoboTwin 2.0 performance
claims.direction: supports that small (~0.44B parameter) models with an efficient action-decoding head can match/approach much larger WAM architectures
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0

claims.claim: Achieves 72.03ms inference latency with 4.1GiB peak GPU memory and improved training throughput
claims.direction: demonstrates that a world-action model can run with sub-100ms latency and under 4.5GB memory footprint
claims.conditions: reported inference benchmarking, hardware not further specified in abstract

why_deep_read: A world-action model at 0.44B parameters, 72ms latency and 4.1GiB peak memory is close to feasible on our RTX 5060 8GB laptop GPU, directly informing our Q09/Q10/Q12 trade-off between adding an auxiliary future-prediction objective and staying within our compute budget.

title: AC-VLA: Robust Out-of-Distribution Action Execution via Compositional Learning

claims.claim: Identifies a 'perceptual shortcut' failure mode where VLA action tokens over-rely on wrist-view textures at the expense of global spatial grounding; a state-conditioned asymmetric masking strategy that suppresses wrist-view inputs during closed-gripper phases, combined with compositional sub-task supervision, achieves ~28% absolute improvement on compositional OOD tasks while maintaining near-perfect in-distribution performance
claims.direction: favors suppressing/masking wrist-camera input during specific task phases (closed-gripper) to prevent over-reliance on wrist-view texture shortcuts, over unrestricted always-on wrist-camera conditioning
claims.conditions: instantiated on pi_0.5 backbone, evaluated on LIBERO and LIBERO-OOD (simulation)

claims.claim: Identifies 'trajectory overfitting' (fitting holistic trajectory patterns rather than compositional sub-skill semantics) as a second failure mode; dense sub-task supervision from an LLM-driven instruction decomposer plus mixed training on complete and decomposed demonstrations improves compositional OOD generalization
claims.direction: favors decomposed/compositional sub-task supervision over training only on complete demonstration trajectories, for generalizing to novel recombinations of familiar sub-tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO / LIBERO-OOD simulation benchmarks, architecture-agnostic/plug-and-play components

why_deep_read: Directly names 'over-reliance on wrist-view textures' as a specific VLA failure mode with a simple architecture-agnostic fix (phase-conditioned wrist-view masking) — highly relevant to our two-camera (scene+wrist) setup and generalization failures, though only validated in simulation so far.

title: SAM-E: Leveraging Visual Foundation Model with Sequence Imitation for Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: Adopting Segment Anything (SAM), a visual foundation model pretrained on massive image/mask data, with parameter-efficient fine-tuning for task-relevant feature extraction improves generalization in few-shot adaptation to new tasks compared to baselines without such a foundation-model backbone
claims.direction: favors large pretrained visual-foundation-model backbones with PEFT over training vision encoders from scratch or without such pretraining
claims.conditions: various instruction-following manipulation tasks

claims.claim: A novel multi-channel heatmap enables predicting an entire action sequence in a single pass, notably enhancing execution efficiency for long-horizon reasoning versus per-step prediction
claims.direction: favors single-pass multi-step action-sequence prediction over autoregressive per-step prediction for long-horizon efficiency
claims.conditions: long-horizon instruction-following tasks

claims.claim: Significantly improves generalization in few-shot adaptation to new tasks while requiring less high-quality robot trajectory data than baselines
claims.direction: supports foundation-model backbones as improving data efficiency
claims.conditions: few-shot task adaptation

title: 3D Diffuser Actor: Policy Diffusion with 3D Scene Representations

claims.claim: A 3D denoising transformer fusing 3D visual scene features (aggregated from single or multiple camera views using sensed depth), language, and proprioception sets a new SOTA on RLBench with an 18.1% absolute gain over prior SOTA in multi-view and 13.1% in single-view setups, and a 9% relative improvement on CALVIN; ablations show 3D representations dramatically outperform 2D representations
claims.direction: strongly favors 3D scene representations (using sensed depth) over 2D-only representations for diffusion-policy manipulation, in both single- and multi-camera setups
claims.conditions: RLBench and CALVIN simulation benchmarks; also controls a real robot from a handful of demonstrations

claims.claim: Ablations show diffusion (denoising) objectives dramatically outperform regression and classification action-prediction objectives, and tokenized 3D scene embeddings with relative attentions outperform holistic non-tokenized embeddings and absolute attentions
claims.direction: favors diffusion-based action generation with tokenized 3D scene embeddings and relative attention over regression/classification objectives and holistic/absolute-attention alternatives
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above; thorough controlled ablation study

claims.claim: Learns to control a real robot manipulator from a handful of real-world demonstrations
claims.direction: supports feasibility of diffusion+3D representations in low-demo-count real-world settings
claims.conditions: real robot manipulator

why_deep_read: A heavily-cited, thoroughly-ablated paper directly comparing 3D vs 2D representations, diffusion vs regression/classification objectives, and attention/tokenization choices — this single paper could settle several of our open questions (Q01, Q04) with rigorous controlled evidence.

title: Traj2Action: A Co-Denoising Framework for Trajectory-Guided Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer

claims.claim: Using a shared 3D endpoint trajectory as an intermediate representation to transfer manipulation knowledge from human video plus robot data (via a co-denoising framework generating a coarse trajectory then robot-specific actions) boosts performance by up to 27% and 22.25% over a pi0 baseline on short- and long-horizon real-world tasks, with gains increasing as human demonstration data scales
claims.direction: favors incorporating scalable human video data via a trajectory-based intermediate representation over training on robot demonstrations (pi0 baseline) alone
claims.conditions: real-world Franka robot experiments

claims.claim: Decouples high-level 3D trajectory motion planning from low-level robot-specific action synthesis (orientation, gripper state) via a co-denoising framework
claims.direction: favors a trajectory-based intermediate action representation (decoupled from final low-level action space) over directly predicting robot actions end-to-end
claims.conditions: real-world Franka robot

title: Physically-based Lighting Generation for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Inverse rendering decomposes the first frame of real demonstrations into geometric (normal, depth) and material (albedo, roughness, metallic) properties, then relights/re-renders it under novel lighting; fine-tuning Stable Video Diffusion propagates the lighting change temporally through the whole demonstration sequence for consistency
claims.direction: favors physically-based (inverse-rendering) lighting augmentation over standard photometric augmentation for generating lighting-diverse training data from existing demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world human demonstrations of manipulation tasks; ablation studies on individual modules included

claims.claim: Improves imitation-learning policy performance by 38.75% under six unseen real-world lighting conditions
claims.direction: directly quantifies the robustness benefit of this lighting augmentation for generalizing to novel lighting
claims.conditions: six unseen real-world lighting conditions, real robot evaluation

why_deep_read: Directly and quantitatively addresses our #1 stated failure mode ('breaks under new lighting') with a concrete real-world success-rate improvement (38.75%) and ablations — extremely high priority for our project.

title: HumanoidExo: Scalable Whole-Body Humanoid Manipulation via Wearable Exoskeleton

claims.claim: Combining wearable-exoskeleton-collected human motion data with real-robot data enables a humanoid policy to generalize to novel environments and learn complex whole-body control from only five real-robot demonstrations, and even acquire an entirely new skill solely from exoskeleton (non-robot) data
claims.direction: favors supplementing very few real-robot demonstrations with cheaply-collected embodiment-matched human motion data over collecting more real-robot demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid, table-top manipulation plus whole-body tasks, 5 real-robot demonstrations

title: From Seeing to Doing: Bridging Reasoning and Decision for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Generating intermediate spatial-relationship-reasoning representations (aligning spatial coordinates with visual signals via a self-consistency mechanism) provides fine-grained guidance for action generation, improving zero-shot manipulation performance
claims.direction: favors adding explicit spatial-reasoning intermediate representations to VLA/VLM pipelines over direct end-to-end action prediction
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv simulation and real-robot settings

claims.claim: Achieves 40.6% success in SimplerEnv and 72% success across 8 real-world tasks in zero-shot manipulation, outperforming the strongest baseline by 30%
claims.direction: reports a large zero-shot generalization improvement from this approach
claims.conditions: real-world (8 tasks) and SimplerEnv simulation

title: ManiDreams: An Open-Source Library for Robust Object Manipulation via Uncertainty-aware Task-specific Intuitive Physics

claims.claim: Wrapping any base policy with a sample-predict-constrain loop over a learned/simulated dynamics model (representing perceptual, parametric, and structural uncertainty) adds robustness without retraining, maintaining performance under perturbations where an RL baseline degrades significantly
claims.direction: favors an uncertainty-aware planning wrapper around a base policy over relying on the base policy alone
claims.conditions: ManiSkill simulation tasks (pushing, picking, catching) plus real-world deployment examples

title: AHA-WAM: Asynchronous Horizon-Adaptive World-Action Modeling with Observation-Guided Context Routing

claims.claim: Decoupling a low-frequency world-prediction branch (rolling key-value memory, layerwise latent context) from a high-frequency action-execution branch that queries this context via joint attention, without rerunning the video model each step, achieves 24.17 Hz closed-loop control with a 4.59x speedup over Fast-WAM, while attaining 92.80% average success on RoboTwin and 78.3% on 4 real-world tasks without robot-data pretraining
claims.direction: favors asynchronous, horizon-adaptive decoupling of world-model prediction rate from action execution rate over binding both to the same temporal resolution
claims.conditions: RoboTwin simulation and 4 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Allowing the video/world branch to model long-horizon scene evolution at a different (lower) rate than short action chunks, rather than forcing world prediction to match near-term action-chunk timing, better exploits the world-model's potential for embodied control
claims.direction: favors temporally asymmetric world-action coupling over synchronized world-action modeling
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Rethinking Camera Choice: An Empirical Study on Fisheye Camera Properties in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Wrist-mounted fisheye cameras' wide FoV significantly enhances spatial localization, but the benefit is contingent on scene visual complexity; fisheye-trained policies are prone to overfitting in simple scenes but achieve superior scene generalization when trained with sufficient environmental diversity
claims.direction: favors wide-FoV (fisheye) wrist cameras over standard FoV, conditional on training-scene diversity
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world imitation learning experiments

claims.claim: Naive cross-camera (hardware) transfer fails due to scale overfitting; a simple Random Scale Augmentation (RSA) strategy improves hardware-generalization performance
claims.direction: identifies scale overfitting as the root cause of camera-hardware-transfer failure and shows a specific augmentation (RSA) fixes it
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation cross-camera-hardware transfer experiments

title: TVGDP: Target-Visually-Guided Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Using DINOv3 as the vision backbone to capture richer semantic/geometric structure, combined with an open-vocabulary-detector-generated target mask as a dual-stream visual input, improves single-view-RGB manipulation success versus ACT and Diffusion Policy baselines
claims.direction: favors stronger self-supervised pretrained vision backbones (DINOv3) plus object-centric mask conditioning over standard single-stream RGB encoders
claims.conditions: single-view RGB imitation learning, compared against ACT and Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: A lightweight subtask classifier that dynamically modulates the visual input by phase (zeroing out the target mask once the object-centric phase completes) eliminates obsolete positional inductive bias and specifically eliminates action stagnation during the placement phase
claims.direction: favors phase-dependent dynamic visual conditioning over static, always-on visual conditioning for multi-stage pick-and-place-like tasks
claims.conditions: multi-stage manipulation tasks, single-view RGB

title: Mitigating State Aliasing in Vision-Language-Action Models via Inverse Dynamics Learning

claims.claim: Adding inverse-dynamics prediction (predicting the action between current and future observations) as an auxiliary objective directly supervising the VLA vision encoder reduces 'state aliasing' (visually similar states requiring different actions) and yields consistent gains across diverse VLA baselines on CALVIN ABC-D and SimplerEnv; frozen-encoder probing confirms more state-discriminative visual representations result
claims.direction: favors an inverse-dynamics auxiliary objective (directly supervising the vision encoder, using only standard observation-action pairs, no extra annotations, unchanged test-time inference) over end-to-end-only training or other indirect auxiliary objectives (future frames, grounding points/traces, spatial reasoning)
claims.conditions: CALVIN ABC-D and SimplerEnv simulation; applies to diverse VLA baselines

claims.claim: Pseudo-reversed supervision exposes the encoder to a broader range of action directions, improving generalization under limited robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors this auxiliary objective specifically to improve data efficiency under limited demonstration counts
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks, limited-demonstration setting

title: ForceRFT: Refining VLA Actions through Force-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Using a frozen, demonstration-trained SmolVLA-based prior to generate force-conditioned action chunks, then training a lightweight residual actor (refining end-effector pose commands from wrist wrench feedback during chunk execution) via human corrections plus verified autonomous-outcome critics, achieves higher autonomous success on real-robot plug insertion, ring-on-peg assembly, and whiteboard wiping than demonstration-trained and residual-imitation baselines
claims.direction: favors adding a residual RL correction layer on top of a frozen SmolVLA imitation-learning prior over relying on the SmolVLA policy or residual imitation alone
claims.conditions: real-robot contact-rich tasks; ablations on plug insertion indicate benefit of direct execution-time wrist-force feedback

claims.claim: Bootstrapping/value updates are restricted to autonomous (non-human-intervention) segments to prevent bad credit assignment across correction boundaries, improving robustness of the learned corrections
claims.direction: supports careful credit-assignment boundaries when mixing human correction and autonomous RL signals
claims.conditions: real-robot contact-rich tasks

why_deep_read: This directly extends a frozen SmolVLA policy (our exact base model) with a lightweight residual correction layer and reports real-robot success-rate gains over the plain SmolVLA baseline — the closest match in our batch to our own model/architecture, worth reading in full for implementation details.

title: Adaptive Compliance Policy: Learning Approximate Compliance for Diffusion Guided Control

claims.claim: Learning to dynamically adjust spatial/temporal compliance (rather than pre-selected or uniform constant stiffness) from human demonstrations, as an addition to a diffusion-guided control policy, achieves over 50% performance improvement compared to state-of-the-art visuomotor policy methods on contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors augmenting diffusion-based action heads with a learned adaptive-compliance signal over position-only diffusion policies for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks

title: Learning Robotic Manipulation Policies from Point Clouds with Conditional Flow Matching

claims.claim: A systematic study of imitation-learning design choices (input modality, training objective, 6-DoF pose representation) finds Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) gives the best performance specifically when combined with point-cloud input observations, achieving a new SOTA average success rate of 67.8% over eight RLBench tasks -- double the next-best method
claims.direction: favors CFM/rectified-flow action generation over alternative training objectives, especially when paired with point-cloud (not RGB) inputs
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation benchmark, extensive controlled experiments over design choices

claims.claim: Point-cloud input observations combined with CFM outperform other input modalities studied; the paper also studies (and finds feasible) a CFM formulation directly on the SO(3) manifold for rotation representation
claims.direction: favors point-cloud input over RGB-only for this action-generation objective
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation, simplified SO(3) example

title: A Novel Task-Driven Diffusion-Based Policy With Affordance Learning for Generalizable Manipulation of Articulated Objects

claims.claim: Enhancing a diffusion-based policy with affordance learning (to identify optimal interaction points) and linear temporal logic representations (for task semantics), plus an interaction-data-based action-refinement optimization, outperforms most existing methods in manipulation ability, generalization, transfer reasoning, and robustness for articulated-object manipulation
claims.direction: favors combining diffusion policies with explicit affordance-learning and logic-based task semantics over diffusion policies trained purely from demonstrations/offline RL
claims.conditions: articulated-object manipulation, category generalization

title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies

claims.claim: Scaling visuomotor context to 8,000 timesteps (three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art short-history policies) via a Test-Time-Training mechanism (fast weights updated by gradient descent during both training and inference, compressing history into weight space) unlocks one-shot in-context imitation from human video, on-the-fly policy improvement, robustness to perturbations, and better multi-stage long-horizon performance; performance improves steadily as pretraining context length scales, with 8K-context training outperforming 1K-context training by 62%
claims.direction: strongly favors much longer observation history/context (via a fast-weight/TTT mechanism) over the single-step or short-history context used by most current robot policies
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation tasks; improves overall performance by 87% over a single-step-context baseline and is the only method to fully complete a five-minute, ten-stage assembly task

claims.claim: This 8K-timestep context scaling is achieved without growing inference latency, unlike naively extending a standard attention context window
claims.direction: shows that long observation history and low inference latency are not necessarily in tension, given the right mechanism (fast-weight TTT)
claims.conditions: real-robot manipulation, real-time closed-loop

why_deep_read: Claims dramatic real-robot gains (+87%, uniquely completing a 10-stage task) from massively longer observation history/context WITHOUT increased inference latency — if true and reproducible, this could directly change our approach to memory/history (Q07) and inference-time efficiency (Q10), both open problems for us.

title: Feedback World Model Enables Precise Guidance of Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Maintaining a lightweight feedback state, updated online using the true observed next state to correct a world model's future predictions at inference time (interpretable as a latent-space observer, with convergence guarantees under mild conditions), substantially improves both prediction accuracy and diffusion-policy performance under distribution shift, without additional training data or parameter updates
claims.direction: favors closing the loop between world-model prediction and real observations at inference time over treating the world model as a static open-loop predictor
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus, Robomimic, and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Reduces world-model prediction error by up to 76.4% and improves out-of-distribution success rate by 30%
claims.direction: quantifies OOD robustness gain from this online feedback-correction mechanism
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

title: ROAD-VLA: Robust Online Adaptation via Self-Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: An advantage-guided self-distillation framework that perturbs action-token logits with calibrated advantage estimates to build a proximal teacher directly in action space converts sparse rewards into dense token-level supervision and outperforms PPO in nearly all of seven robotic manipulation environments under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution shifts
claims.direction: favors action-space advantage-guided self-distillation over standard PPO for online VLA adaptation, including under OOD shift
claims.conditions: seven robotic manipulation environments (simulation implied), ID and OOD evaluation

title: LLM-Guided Future Hypotheses for Horizon-Aware Exploration in Multi-Step Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning closed-loop BC/BC+RL policies on a latent representation of an LLM+digital-twin+video-diffusion-generated short future clip improves performance over no-future conditioning, while mismatched ('WrongFuture') futures degrade performance to zero throughout training; BC+RL with generated futures gives the strongest overall results
claims.direction: favors conditioning policies on generated future-video representations over no future conditioning, but only when the generated future is accurate -- inaccurate future conditioning actively harms learning
claims.conditions: simulation only (RoboCasa, CALVIN)

title: AgenticFocus: Object-Preserving Mixed Reality Synthesis from Human FPV Video for Dexterous Humanoid Learning

claims.claim: A mixed-reality synthesis pipeline converting ordinary human first-person videos into robot-trainable demonstrations (restoring occluded object geometry, reconstructing full-hand motion, retargeting to humanoid) achieves lower trajectory error and smoother wrist motion (SPARC -5.18) than cross-embodiment baselines (-5.56, -6.05)
claims.direction: favors this MR-synthesis pipeline for generating training data from ordinary human video over existing cross-embodiment demonstration-generation baselines
claims.conditions: humanoid dexterous manipulation, human FPV video source

title: StellaVLA: In-Context Structured Demonstration for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Converting a single retrieved demonstration into a structured representation (task plan, sub-goal descriptions, verbalized 3D motion) at zero human-annotation cost, and using it as in-context guidance at test time (rather than fine-tuning), lets the policy reason about a task rather than mimic a pixel trajectory, and works across embodiments (real-robot, human-hand, XR demos)
claims.direction: favors test-time in-context conditioning on a single structured demonstration over collecting more data and fine-tuning for each new OOD situation
claims.conditions: real-robot benchmark plus VLA-Arena leaderboard; LIBERO 98.8%, LIBERO-Plus 85.1%

claims.claim: Ranks first on the VLA-Arena leaderboard (0.63 overall) versus 0.44 (pi0.5) and 0.22 (LingBot-VLA), specifically targeting performance collapse out-of-distribution when scene, viewpoint, or object differs from training
claims.direction: demonstrates substantially better OOD robustness than strong prior VLA baselines
claims.conditions: VLA-Arena leaderboard, LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus

claims.claim: A parallel dual-training design internalizes the structured reasoning during training via a joint action-and-language objective, but inference uses the action expert alone, preserving real-time high-frequency control with no added latency
claims.direction: shows that in-context reasoning benefits can be captured at training time without incurring extra inference-time latency
claims.conditions: real-time control setting

title: BEACON: Belief-Enabled Adaptive CONtrol for Imitation Learning under Uncertainty

claims.claim: Conditioning a diffusion policy on a structured Bayesian belief representation (current most-likely hidden state plus remaining uncertainty), instead of raw recent observation history, substantially outperforms an observation-only baseline and approaches privileged ground-truth performance in two partially-observable domains; the policy implicitly modulates exploration vs exploitation based on belief uncertainty without explicit mode switching
claims.direction: favors structured belief-state conditioning over raw observation-history conditioning to resolve state aliasing/copycat-style ambiguity in partially observable manipulation
claims.conditions: two domains: continuous belief for tactile-sensed gripper alignment, discrete belief for latched door opening

title: DISCO: Language-Guided Manipulation With Diffusion Policies and Constrained Inpainting

claims.claim: Using off-the-shelf VLMs to translate language instructions into actionable 3D keyframes, which then guide a diffusion policy via constrained inpainting (balanced against learned motion priors when keyframes are inaccurate), outperforms conventional fine-tuned language-conditioned diffusion policies
claims.direction: favors VLM-derived keyframe-guided inpainting over standard end-to-end language-conditioned fine-tuning for language grounding
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world settings

claims.claim: Achieves superior generalization in zero-shot, open-vocabulary manipulation tasks versus baselines
claims.direction: supports this approach for open-vocabulary language generalization
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Efficient Robot Manipulation via Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Movement Primitives-Based Policy

claims.claim: Integrating a DMP-based policy into an actor-critic (DDPG) framework, with an inverse controller adaptively learning state-to-DMP-parameter translation, demonstrates significant advantages in control performance, learning efficiency, and smoothness of robot actions compared to related baselines on five robot arm benchmark tasks
claims.direction: favors DMP-parameterized action generation (smooth, low-dimensional trajectory primitives) over direct low-level action learning for smoothness and efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation, five robot arm control benchmark tasks

title: Actor-Critic for Continuous Action Chunks: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Sparse Reward

claims.claim: Learning continuous, high-dimensional action chunks directly via RL (with asymmetric actor updates from successful trajectories only, and critic stabilization using intra-chunk n-step returns plus self-supervised intrinsic rewards at chunk anchor points) achieves superior success rates on most of 25 BiGym/RLBench tasks using only a few demonstrations and a simple architecture
claims.direction: favors chunk-level RL stabilization mechanisms (asymmetric updates, intra-chunk returns) for learning action chunks directly, over naive RL on action chunks
claims.conditions: simulation (BiGym, RLBench), few demonstrations, simple model architecture

claims.claim: Achieves strong results using only a few demonstrations
claims.direction: supports data efficiency of this RL-on-action-chunks approach
claims.conditions: simulation, 25 tasks

title: VLM-TDP: VLM-guided Trajectory-conditioned Diffusion Policy for Robust Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a VLM to decompose long-horizon tasks into sub-tasks and generate voxel-based trajectories per sub-task, which condition the diffusion policy, achieves an average 44% increase in success rate and over 100% improvement on long-horizon tasks versus classical diffusion policies
claims.direction: favors VLM-generated sub-task trajectory conditioning over standard (unconditioned) diffusion policies, especially for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments

claims.claim: Sub-task decomposition and trajectory generation are driven by a VLM interpreting the task/language instruction
claims.direction: favors VLM-based language/task decomposition as a conditioning signal for the action policy
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Achieves a 20% reduction in performance degradation under challenging conditions such as noisy images or altered environments compared to classical diffusion policies, with the performance gap becoming even more pronounced in real-world long-horizon experiments
claims.direction: supports this trajectory-conditioning approach for robustness to image noise and environment changes
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated experiments

title: FRMD: Fast Robot Motion Diffusion with Consistency-Distilled Movement Primitives for Smooth Action Generation

claims.claim: Integrating Movement Primitives (compact, time-continuous, low-dimensional trajectory representations) with Consistency Models (probability-flow-ODE-based consistency distillation) within an encoder-decoder architecture eliminates the slow multi-step denoising of conventional diffusion policies, enabling one-step inference
claims.direction: favors combining classic movement-primitive trajectory parameterization with consistency-distillation over standard multi-step diffusion policies for the action head
claims.conditions: Meta-World and ManiSkills simulation benchmarks, simple to complex manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Standard diffusion policies produce non-smooth, jerky motions because they fail to capture temporally consistent movement dynamics across a chunk/trajectory; FRMD's MP+consistency-model design directly targets and fixes this, generating significantly smoother trajectories than SOTA baselines
claims.direction: directly targets and reduces jerky, non-smooth motion generation, which the paper attributes to a lack of temporally-consistent dynamics modeling in standard diffusion policies
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

claims.claim: Single-step trajectory generation removes the prohibitive latency of iterative multi-step diffusion sampling while achieving higher success rates than SOTA baselines
claims.direction: favors single-step (vs multi-step) generation for reducing inference latency without sacrificing (in fact improving) success rate
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly targets and explains BOTH of our two stated core failure modes (jerky motion at chunk boundaries AND high inference latency) with one combined mechanism (movement primitives + consistency distillation), making it an unusually direct match for our project's problems.

title: PosA-VLA: Enhancing Action Generation via Pose-Conditioned Anchor Attention

claims.claim: A lightweight pose-conditioned anchor-attention mechanism that consistently guides visual perception toward task-relevant regions (rather than a spatially uniform perception field) reduces redundant/unstable motions along trajectories, without requiring auxiliary segmentation or grounding modules
claims.direction: favors pose-conditioned attention anchoring over spatially-uniform visual attention for precise, time-efficient action generation
claims.conditions: diverse robotic manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Shows robust generalization in a variety of challenging environments
claims.direction: supports this attention mechanism for generalization robustness
claims.conditions: diverse benchmarks, qualitative claim

title: HY-Embodied-0.5: Embodied Foundation Models for Real-World Agents

claims.claim: A Mixture-of-Transformers foundation model family offers a 2B-activated-parameter variant for edge deployment and a 32B variant for complex reasoning; on-policy distillation transfers capability from the large to the small variant, and the resulting VLM foundation is used to train a VLA achieving 'compelling results' in real-world physical evaluations
claims.direction: supports distilling a large foundation model down to a small (2B) edge-deployable model as a viable route to a capable, small VLA backbone
claims.conditions: real-world robot control evaluation; specific quantitative VLA numbers not given in abstract (qualitative claim only)

title: DynaForge: Planning-Guided Residual Learning for Dynamic Manipulation Demonstration Generation

claims.claim: A planning-guided residual-RL framework for generating demonstrations increases mean demonstration-generation success from 41.30% (planning prior) to 78.37% across nine simulation tasks; policies trained on 800 DynaForge demonstrations/task reach 49.11% mean success vs 7.07% for a prior (DOMINO) generation method, and real-world dynamic-task policies trained on DynaForge data reach 30-60% success vs 0-10% for DOMINO-trained policies
claims.direction: favors planning+residual-RL-generated demonstrations over simplified replay-based (DOMINO-style) demonstration generation for training downstream imitation-learning policies on dynamic manipulation
claims.conditions: 9 simulation tasks plus 3 real-world dynamic manipulation tasks; large real/sim-to-real success-rate gap between methods

title: Scalable Trajectory Generation for Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Even for a single articulated-object manipulation task, state-of-the-art imitation-learning methods require tens of thousands of demonstrations to reach approximately 80% success, indicating that data scarcity -- not algorithmic limitations -- is the binding constraint for such tasks
claims.direction: highlights (for whole-body mobile manipulation with combinatorially large state space) that demonstration count, not algorithm choice, is often the bottleneck for high success rates
claims.conditions: whole-body mobile manipulation, articulated objects, large-scale generated trajectory dataset (500k+ trajectories, 330 scenes)

title: One-Step Flow Policy: Self-Distillation for Fast Visuomotor Policies

claims.claim: A from-scratch self-distillation framework (no pretrained teacher needed), combining a self-consistency loss, self-guided regularization toward high-density expert modes, and a warm-start mechanism exploiting temporal action correlations, achieves single-step action generation that outperforms 100-step diffusion and flow-matching policies across 56 diverse simulated manipulation tasks, while accelerating generation by over 100x; integrated into the pi_0.5 model on RoboTwin 2.0, one-step OFP surpasses the original 10-step policy
claims.direction: favors self-distilled single-step flow/diffusion action generation over standard multi-step diffusion/flow-matching action heads, even without a separately pretrained multi-step teacher
claims.conditions: 56 simulated manipulation tasks; also integrated directly into pi_0.5 and tested on RoboTwin 2.0

claims.claim: Achieves over 100x acceleration in action generation versus 100-step diffusion/flow baselines while improving (not just preserving) success rate
claims.direction: strongly favors reducing action-generation steps to cut inference latency, showing this need not trade off against performance
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Data-Asymmetric Latent Imagination and Reranking for 3D Robotic Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Learning a latent world model over 3D point clouds for imagined rollouts, plus a Task Completion Scorer that reranks candidate action chunks, improves decision-making from mixed-quality (including suboptimal/failed) trajectories without requiring additional high-quality demonstrations, achieving an average 6.8% improvement in success rate with less than 0.7x additional inference overhead across both diffusion and flow-matching 3D policies
claims.direction: favors leveraging suboptimal/mixed-quality collected trajectories (via world-model reranking) rather than discarding them or requiring only high-quality demos
claims.conditions: Adroit and MetaWorld simulation benchmarks; evaluated with both diffusion and flow-matching base policies

claims.claim: An auxiliary latent world model used for imagined-rollout reranking at test time improves decision-making with modest added inference cost
claims.direction: supports test-time world-model-based reranking as a lightweight auxiliary use of world modeling
claims.conditions: same as above

title: XEWorld: Can Action-Conditioned World Models Generalize to Unseen Robot Embodiments?

claims.claim: Systematic analysis reveals current action-conditioned world models act primarily as 2D visual pattern matchers whose generalization is governed by visual similarity rather than physical/kinematic similarity; they struggle to translate abstract numeric joint actions into coherent visual trajectories for unseen embodiments, and few-shot adaptation to a new embodiment triggers catastrophic forgetting of previously-seen embodiments
claims.direction: identifies a fundamental limitation of current action-conditioned world models: they do not capture true physical dynamics, only visual pattern-matching, which should temper expectations for using such world models as a robust auxiliary objective across embodiment/appearance changes
claims.conditions: controlled cross-embodiment testbed (XEWorld) isolating embodiment from scene

title: FAN: Foresight Action Normalization for Continual Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A systematic evaluation of five action-normalization strategies across four real-world task streams (single-arm and bimanual) shows existing normalization protocols induce severe failure modes from inter-task coordinate drift, limited motion coverage, or train-test coordinate mismatches; estimating normalization statistics once from a small task-independent calibration set before continual learning and freezing them throughout (guided by consistency, coverage, causality principles) achieves the highest and most robust performance across all streams
claims.direction: favors a fixed, pre-calibrated action-normalization scheme over normalization statistics that are re-derived or drift across tasks/sessions
claims.conditions: real-world single-arm and bimanual manipulation, continual/lifelong adaptation setting

title: Reinforcement Learning with Decoupled State Representation for Robot Manipulations

claims.claim: Explicitly decoupling robot and object information within a learned low-dimensional visual state representation (rather than encoding the whole image into one coupled vector) yields faster learning speed and superior performance across manipulation tasks, and applies successfully to real-world robot pushing with only 3096 offline images
claims.direction: favors representations that explicitly decouple robot-state and object-state information over monolithic coupled visual embeddings
claims.conditions: real-world robot pushing task, 3096 offline images

title: Beyond Success: Quantifying Demonstration Quality in Learning from Demonstration

claims.claim: Motion-related quality features of individual demonstrations -- specifically manipulability and joint-space jerk -- strongly correlate with downstream LfD task-execution quality; the impact is especially significant when the provided demonstration set is diverse in quality
claims.direction: favors screening/ranking individual demonstrations by motion-quality features (e.g., low jerk, good manipulability) rather than treating all collected demonstrations as equally useful
claims.conditions: simulation study, cube lifting and pick-and-place-of-soda-can LfD tasks

title: FP3: A 3D Foundation Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A large-scale 3D foundation policy (scalable diffusion transformer pre-trained on 60k trajectories with point-cloud observations, rather than 2D-image-only observations as in most existing robot foundation models) significantly surpasses existing robot foundation models
claims.direction: favors point-cloud/3D-based foundation policies over 2D-image-only foundation models for downstream fine-tuning generalization
claims.conditions: real robots, pre-trained on 60k point-cloud trajectories

claims.claim: With only 80 demonstrations, FP3 learns a new task with over 90% success rate
claims.direction: demonstrates strong task learning from a small (80) real-world demonstration count when built on a 3D-pretrained foundation policy
claims.conditions: real-robot fine-tuning, 80 demonstrations

claims.claim: Achieves over 90% success in novel environments with unseen objects
claims.direction: supports 3D-pretrained foundation policies for generalization to novel environments/objects
claims.conditions: real robots, novel environments and unseen objects

why_deep_read: Reports concrete real-robot numbers (80 demonstrations, >90% success, unseen objects/novel environments) from a 3D point-cloud foundation policy — the demo count almost exactly matches our budget (50-100), and the 3D-vs-2D comparison is central to our Q04 decision.

title: Residual Off-Policy RL for Finetuning Behavior Cloning Policies

claims.claim: Using existing BC policies as black-box bases and learning lightweight per-step residual corrections via sample-efficient off-policy RL (requiring only sparse binary reward signals) effectively improves manipulation policies on high-DoF systems, demonstrating the first successful real-world RL training on a humanoid robot with dexterous hands and achieving SOTA on vision-based tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight residual RL correction layer on top of a frozen/pretrained BC policy over BC alone or full RL from scratch
claims.conditions: simulation and real world, high-DoF systems including a real humanoid with dexterous hands

title: DreamVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Dreamed with Comprehensive World Knowledge

claims.claim: Forecasting comprehensive world knowledge (dynamic-region-guided prediction integrated with spatial and semantic cues) rather than raw future images, with a block-wise structured attention mechanism that masks mutual attention between dynamic/spatial/semantic streams to prevent information leakage, achieves 76.7% success rate on real robot tasks and 4.44 average task length on CALVIN ABC-D
claims.direction: favors disentangled multi-stream world-knowledge auxiliary prediction (dynamic+spatial+semantic, block-wise separated) over redundant raw-image future forecasting for VLA auxiliary objectives
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation (CALVIN ABC-D) environments

claims.claim: Uses a diffusion-based transformer that disentangles action representations from shared latent (world-knowledge) features for the action head
claims.direction: favors separating action generation from the shared perception/prediction latent space rather than sharing all representations
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Vision-Guided Recovery: Enhancing Robotic Manipulation through Intelligent Failure Detection

claims.claim: Continuously analyzing visual data of robot task performance with a multimodal LLM to predict success/difficulty and automatically trigger a backtracking/re-approach procedure (without human intervention) increases task success rates by up to 2x compared to standard vision-language models
claims.direction: favors adding automatic failure detection and backtracking/recovery on top of a base VLM/policy over running the policy without failure monitoring
claims.conditions: ManiSkill3 simulation platform, manipulation benchmarks

title: AtomVLA: Scalable Post-Training for Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Latent World Models

claims.claim: Decomposing high-level demonstrations into fine-grained atomic subtasks (via an LLM) and using a pretrained predictive world model to score candidate action chunks against subtask goals in latent space mitigates compounding errors in long-horizon tasks; achieves 97.0% average success on LIBERO and 48.0% on LIBERO-PRO, and confirms broad applicability on a real robot (Galaxea R1 Lite)
claims.direction: favors subtask-level world-model scoring of candidate action chunks over coarse, high-level-instruction-only fine-tuning for long-horizon robustness
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO) and real-world (Galaxea R1 Lite)

claims.claim: This subtask/world-model scoring approach enables offline Group Relative Policy Optimization without the prohibitive expense of online rollouts on physical robots
claims.direction: favors offline post-training with world-model-based scoring over costly online RL rollouts for scalable post-training
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world

title: Target-conditioned flow-matching policy for citrus harvesting robot pre-grasp approach behavior learning

claims.claim: A target-conditioned flow-matching policy (image + robot-state history + explicit target geometric conditions, dual-branch global/local visual encoding, multi-step TCP trajectory prediction) achieves lower offline trajectory error and better online target-specified approach performance than a fairness-aligned target-conditioned diffusion-policy baseline under the same small-sample training setting
claims.direction: favors conditional flow matching with explicit target/dual-branch conditioning over a comparable diffusion-policy baseline for small-sample, cluttered-scene fruit picking
claims.conditions: real UR5-based citrus harvesting platform, 160 demonstration episodes, small-sample regime

claims.claim: A target-oriented visual augmentation strategy applied to the global scene branch during training (to reduce overfitting to global appearance under small-sample conditions) mainly improves target-selection consistency, per ablation results, while the local ROI branch mainly improves final alignment precision
claims.direction: favors target-oriented augmentation specifically to counter overfitting to background/global appearance in small-sample fruit-picking data
claims.conditions: same real-world platform, ablation study

claims.claim: Under small-sample conditions (160 real demonstrations), the full model achieves 76% success, 4% target-picking error rate, and 20% picking-point offset rate on 50 target-specified multi-fruit trials
claims.direction: reports concrete performance achievable at a demonstration count close to our own budget for a visually similar (fruit picking) task
claims.conditions: real-world VR-teleoperated data collection, 160 episodes, UR5 robot

why_deep_read: This is a near-identical task type to ours (picking a round fruit from a cluttered scene with a single arm, small-sample real-world demonstrations, flow-matching vs diffusion-policy comparison, and an augmentation strategy specifically to prevent overfitting to global scene appearance under small-sample conditions) -- directly transferable design guidance for our pumpkin pick-and-place task.

title: Grasp as You Dream: Imitating Functional Grasping from Generated Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Using video-generation models pre-trained on internet-scale human data to synthesize human demonstrations, combined with embodiment-specific action optimization, enables zero-shot functional grasping without labor-intensive real data collection, with superior data efficiency and generalization versus previous methods on public benchmarks and real robots
claims.direction: favors generative-model-synthesized human demonstrations (rather than only collected teleoperation data) as a scalable augmentation source for functional grasping
claims.conditions: public benchmarks with different robot hands, plus real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Demonstrates superior data efficiency compared to previous methods, and shows the generated data can support downstream visuomotor policy learning
claims.direction: supports synthetic human-demonstration generation as a way to reduce required real demonstration count
claims.conditions: real-world validation

title: CoTinyVLA: Chain-of-Thought Distillation for a Sub-Billion-Parameter Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: A 0.9B-parameter VLA (on a Qwen3.5-0.8B backbone) obtains LIBERO-Plus robustness matching/exceeding 3-7B-parameter baselines by structuring supervision (dual-view temporal input, hierarchical CoT distillation from a 35B teacher into an episode-level Plan and chunk-level Think span, paraphrase augmentation) rather than enlarging the model; leads the strongest 7B baseline by 4.7-15.9 points across four perturbation suites, with closed-loop inference peaking at only 2.25 GiB of allocated GPU memory
claims.direction: strongly favors a small (sub-billion parameter), low-memory model with structured supervision over scaling model size (3-7B) for robustness under perturbations
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus benchmark, 10,030 perturbed tasks across 7 perturbation dimensions

claims.claim: Dual-view temporal input of 16 history frames per step (with textual camera/time markers) is one of three components driving the robustness gains; how frames are divided between the two cameras and across time accounts for 8.6 points of performance at a matched image budget
claims.direction: favors explicit multi-frame temporal history (16 frames) with textual markers over single-frame/short-history conditioning
claims.conditions: same benchmark as above

claims.claim: The episode-level 'Plan' (high-level CoT distilled guidance) is load-bearing: replacing it with an empty or contradictory span costs 40-45 points of success; the model reaches 73.6% on the hardest 'Robot Initial States' axis of Goal suite versus 39.9% for the strongest baseline (none of 11 published baselines exceed 53.2% on this axis)
claims.direction: shows structured high-level plan supervision is critical for robustness to novel/perturbed robot initial states and other perturbation axes, far beyond what scaling alone achieves
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus, ablations removing the Plan

why_deep_read: A sub-billion-parameter model (matching our need for a SMALL policy) running under 2.25GiB GPU memory that beats 7B baselines on a large robustness benchmark, with detailed ablations on history length and structured supervision -- extremely directly applicable to our compute-constrained, robustness-focused design questions (Q12, Q07, Q14).

title: Sensorless damage-safe grasping

claims.claim: Estimating contact/compression strain purely from servo encoder position and motor-effort signal (no tactile or force-torque sensor) and stopping gripper closure at a certified strain limit holds >=98% grasp success at 0% damage across medium-to-firm fruit stiffness in simulation, and on real stiffness-graded TPU cubes matches baseline grasp success at roughly half the grip force while cutting soft-object damage from 100% to 40%
claims.direction: favors using only standard servo encoder/effort signals (already available on position-controlled servos like Feetech) to bound grasp force/damage, without adding tactile or force-torque hardware
claims.conditions: MuJoCo simulation with sensor-noise model calibrated to a real servo, plus real-world stiffness-graded 3D-printed TPU cube tests

title: Visually Robust Adversarial Imitation Learning from Videos with Contrastive Learning

claims.claim: Learning a visually robust latent space via contrastive learning and data augmentation (to handle visual mismatch between agent and expert video domains), then performing adversarial imitation entirely within this latent space, improves performance versus baseline methods on high-dimensional continuous robotic tasks, confirmed via ablation study
claims.direction: favors contrastive-learning-based robust latent representations over standard visual encoders when there is visual discrepancy between demonstration and deployment domains
claims.conditions: high-dimensional continuous robotic tasks; also combined with additional reward signals for sparse-reward hand-manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Improves imitation performance under visual mismatch between expert (video) domain and agent (deployment) domain
claims.direction: supports this technique for robustness to visual-domain shift between training and deployment observations
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Progressor: A Perceptually Guided Reward Estimator with Self-Supervised Online Refinement

claims.claim: A task-agnostic, self-supervised progress-prediction reward (estimated from current/initial/goal observations, refined adversarially online to push back on out-of-distribution predictions) enables goal-conditioned RL without manual reward engineering, outperforming contemporary dense visual-reward methods for robotic learning under noisy demonstrations
claims.direction: favors self-supervised, adversarially-refined progress-based reward estimation over hand-engineered or naive learned dense rewards
claims.conditions: pretrained on large-scale egocentric human video (EPIC-KITCHENS), generalizes to real-robot offline RL without in-domain fine-tuning

claims.claim: Requires no fine-tuning on in-domain task-specific data to generalize, leveraging large-scale out-of-domain human video instead
claims.direction: supports reducing in-domain data requirements via large out-of-domain pretraining for the reward/auxiliary signal
claims.conditions: real-robot offline RL, noisy demonstrations

title: Expanding Spatial and Temporal Context for Robotic Imitation Learning With Scene Graphs

claims.claim: Maintaining a dynamic scene graph (explicit, structured memory of object-centric relationships and their evolution) as the observation-history mechanism substantially improves policy performance versus implicit/raw-history conditioning, particularly for long-term reasoning and generalization under partial observability
claims.direction: favors explicit structured (scene-graph) memory over raw observation-history conditioning for long-horizon, partially-observed tasks
claims.conditions: simulated mobile manipulation and real-world tabletop manipulation

title: VISTA: Vision-Grounded and Physics-Validated Adaptation of UMI data for VLA Training

claims.claim: Wrist-mounted fisheye views from UMI-style data collection are out-of-distribution for pretrained VLMs (severe radial distortion, local gripper-centric perspective); a dedicated VQA dataset (UMI-VQA) aligning VLM representations to this distorted visual regime, plus two-stage co-training, consistently improves downstream policy performance and lets the model significantly outperform pi_0.5, LingBot-VLA, and Wall-X
claims.direction: favors explicit vision-language alignment for wrist-camera-specific visual distortions over training on wrist-camera data without such alignment
claims.conditions: diverse simulation and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: A systematic physical-validation pipeline that pre-checks data completeness and scores each collected trajectory for continuity, self-collision risk, and execution fidelity before training produces scores that are strongly predictive of deployment success
claims.direction: favors filtering/scoring collected (teleoperated or UMI-style) demonstrations for physical plausibility before training, rather than using all collected trajectories as-is
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Toward Visually Realistic Simulation: A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Manipulation in Simulation

claims.claim: A systematic analysis isolating lighting and material effects shows these factors play a critical role in geometric reasoning and spatial grounding for manipulation policies, yet are largely overlooked in existing simulation benchmarks; a visually realistic benchmark built with physically-based-rendering materials achieves a 0.92 average Pearson correlation between simulated and real-world policy performance
claims.direction: confirms lighting and material realism are critical (not cosmetic) factors for policy robustness/evaluation validity, supporting investment in lighting-diverse training/evaluation data
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark correlated against real-world VLA policy performance

title: PAC-ACT: Post-training Actor-Critic for Action Chunking Transformers

claims.claim: Reformulating RL policy optimization at the action-chunk level for a pretrained Action Chunking Transformer (ACT), with a hybrid behavior-prior constraint preserving the pretrained action distribution during online fine-tuning, improves task success, contact stability, and force safety on industrial precision-contact benchmarks; on the Contour task it reduces the proportion of force readings above 60N by 46 times
claims.direction: favors chunk-level RL post-training (with a behavior-prior constraint) on top of a pretrained ACT policy over behavior-cloning-only ACT, for contact-rich distribution-shift correction
claims.conditions: industrial precision-contact manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Retains low latency and low GPU-memory usage suitable for real-time industrial control, unlike VLA models which introduce high inference latency and GPU-memory cost
claims.direction: favors action-chunking-transformer-style policies over larger VLA models when real-time, low-memory control is required
claims.conditions: industrial control setting

title: Whole-Body UMI: Transferring UMI Manipulation Skills to Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation via Real-Time Motion Generation

claims.claim: An asynchronous hierarchy integrating a diffusion policy, a real-time motion generator, and a whole-body controller with latency compensation and measured-state feedback achieves real-time closed-loop transfer, reaching 90% success in drawer closing and 80% in shelf pick-and-place on a real humanoid
claims.direction: favors an asynchronous, latency-compensated hierarchical control architecture for combining a learned action policy with lower-level real-time control
claims.conditions: real G1 humanoid, four tasks

claims.claim: A task-agnostic, end-effector-conditioned motion generator trained from retargeted motion capture (not paired image-whole-body demonstrations) decouples whole-body coordination learning from task-specific data collection, reducing the demonstration burden for new tasks
claims.direction: favors decoupling embodiment-coordination learning from task-specific demonstration collection to reduce data requirements per new task
claims.conditions: real humanoid deployment

title: Language Reward Modulation for Pretraining Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Using a frozen, pretrained VLM to compute contrastive alignment between diverse language instructions and image observations, as a pretraining exploration reward (rather than a downstream task reward), warm-starts sample-efficient learning of a language-conditioned policy on RLBench manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors using VLM-derived language-image alignment as a pretraining signal rather than only as a final task reward for language-conditioned policy learning
claims.conditions: simulation (RLBench)

claims.claim: This pretraining approach can warmstart sample-efficient downstream learning
claims.direction: supports using cheap VLM-derived rewards to reduce downstream data/sample requirements
claims.conditions: simulation

title: RoboCrowd: Scaling Robot Data Collection Through Crowdsourcing

claims.claim: Crowdsourced demonstration collection (using material, intrinsic-interest, and social-comparison incentives) yielded over 800 interaction episodes from 200+ volunteers in a two-week public field deployment, and using this crowdsourced data as pre-training data (before fine-tuning on expert demonstrations) boosted performance by up to 20% compared to not using it
claims.direction: favors incorporating even lower-quality, crowdsourced demonstrations as pretraining data on top of a smaller set of expert demonstrations, over relying on expert demonstrations alone
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual ALOHA platform, public crowdsourced data collection

title: Maximizing Alignment with Minimal Feedback: Efficiently Learning Rewards for Visuomotor Robot Policy Alignment

claims.claim: Focusing human preference feedback on fine-tuning pre-trained vision encoders to align with the end-user's visual representation (rather than directly learning a reward function) and constructing a dense reward via feature matching in this aligned space enables effective policy alignment with far less feedback
claims.direction: favors targeted preference-based fine-tuning of the vision encoder's representation over standard RLHF-style reward learning for visuomotor policies
claims.conditions: simulation (X-Magical, Franka Panda) and real hardware (3 object-manipulation tasks with pre-trained Diffusion Policies)
