claims.claim: Fine-tunes pre-trained Diffusion Policies with 5x less real human preference data than standard approaches while still improving alignment with user preferences
claims.direction: supports this method as a highly feedback-efficient way to adapt/align a pretrained visuomotor policy
claims.conditions: real hardware, 3 manipulation tasks

title: Latent Action Pretraining Through World Modeling

claims.claim: A model-agnostic framework (LAWM) pretrains imitation-learning models self-supervised by learning latent action representations from unlabeled video (robot recordings or human-object-interaction videos) through world modeling, outperforming models pretrained with ground-truth robot actions and other latent-action pretraining methods (LAPA, villa-X) on LIBERO and a real-world setup
claims.direction: favors self-supervised latent-action-from-video pretraining over supervised ground-truth-action pretraining or prior latent-action pretraining approaches
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark and real-world setup

claims.claim: Transfers learned knowledge across tasks, environments, and embodiments using unlabeled video sourced from robot recordings or human videos, reducing the need for labeled teleoperation data
claims.direction: favors leveraging unlabeled (robot or human) video for pretraining to cut labeled-demonstration requirements
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Prior latent-action pretraining methods (LAPA, villa-X) have large model sizes that make real-world deployment challenging; LAWM is presented as more efficient and practical for real-world settings
claims.direction: favors a more compact/efficient latent-action pretraining approach over larger prior latent-action models for practical deployment
claims.conditions: real-world setup

title: Real-World Reinforcement Learning of Active Perception Behaviors

claims.claim: Asymmetric advantage weighted regression (AAWR), which exploits privileged extra sensors at training time only to train privileged value functions aiding advantage estimation, synthesizes reliable active-perception (information-gathering) behaviors that outperform all prior approaches across 8 manipulation tasks on 3 real robots under varying partial observability
claims.direction: favors privileged-information-guided training (available only at training time) for learning active-perception behaviors, over standard observation-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: real-world, 8 manipulation tasks, 3 robots

claims.claim: Bootstraps from a small number of potentially suboptimal demonstrations plus a coarse policy initialization to quickly acquire active-perception behaviors and boost task performance, including when initialized from a 'generalist' policy that struggles with active perception
claims.direction: supports this method as data-efficient (few, possibly suboptimal demos) for adding active-perception capability to an existing policy
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation

title: GigaBrain-0: A World Model-Powered Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Using world models to generate diverse training data at scale (video generation, real2real transfer, human transfer, view transfer, sim2real transfer) significantly reduces reliance on real robot data while improving cross-task generalization
claims.direction: favors world-model-generated synthetic/transferred training data as a substitute/supplement for costly real robot data collection
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous, long-horizon, and mobile manipulation tasks

claims.claim: RGBD input modeling (not RGB-only) combined with embodied Chain-of-Thought supervision improves policy robustness by enabling reasoning about spatial geometry, object states, and long-horizon dependencies
claims.direction: favors RGBD input plus explicit spatial/CoT reasoning over RGB-only input without such reasoning supervision
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Presents GigaBrain-0-Small, an optimized lightweight variant designed to run efficiently on edge devices such as the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin
claims.direction: demonstrates that a distilled/optimized small variant of a world-model-powered VLA can run on constrained edge hardware
claims.conditions: edge deployment (Jetson AGX Orin)

claims.claim: Achieves superior generalization across variations in appearances (textures, colors), object placements, and camera viewpoints compared to baselines
claims.direction: supports world-model-augmented training for robustness to appearance and viewpoint variation
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

title: Vision-Language-Action Models: Experimental Insights from a Real-World UR5 Platform

claims.claim: A reproducible real-robot deployment of OpenVLA/OpenVLA-OFT on a UR5e reveals a consistent gap between promising offline indicators and unstable closed-loop behavior, and this gap is strongly influenced by action semantics and coordinate-frame conventions, not solely by model capacity
claims.direction: highlights that action-space/coordinate-frame choices and their consistency between training and deployment are often a larger determinant of real-world success than the underlying model itself
claims.conditions: real-world UR5e platform, OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT fine-tuning and deployment

claims.claim: Temporal alignment between modalities, image preprocessing consistency, and dataset coverage/quality are identified as key factors strongly influencing the offline-to-closed-loop performance gap
claims.direction: supports that dataset/preprocessing pipeline quality is often more decisive for real-world VLA deployment than incremental model improvements
claims.conditions: same real-world UR5e platform

title: FocalPolicy: Frequency-Optimized Chunking and Locally Anchored Flow Matching for Coherent Visuomotor Policy

claims.claim: Existing chunked visuomotor policies typically optimize intra-chunk action distributions but neglect inter-chunk coherence, causing inter-chunk discontinuities that impede learning of coherent long-horizon actions; a foresight composite objective supervising time-domain alignment within proximal actions while regularizing frequency-domain structure across multiple future chunks improves cross-chunk coherence and outperforms existing approaches, generalizing to other baseline architectures
claims.direction: favors explicitly optimizing for inter-chunk (not just intra-chunk) coherence via a frequency-domain regularization objective, over standard chunk-wise training that only optimizes within-chunk accuracy
claims.conditions: visuomotor manipulation experiments; modules shown to generalize across baselines

claims.claim: Locally anchored sampling enhances target-signal propagation efficiency during consistency flow-matching training, improving the efficiency of learning complex action distributions
claims.direction: favors locally-anchored consistency flow-matching training over standard flow-matching training for balancing precision and foresight
claims.conditions: same experiments as above

title: Drift is a Sampling Error: SNR-Aware Power Distributions for Long-Horizon Robotic Planning

claims.claim: Instruction drift in long-horizon VLA tasks is reframed as a sampling error (collapse into 'Negative Pivotal Windows'); a training-free, inference-time Context-Aware Power Sampling framework with an SNR-based metacognitive trigger for adaptive MCMC search achieves substantial improvements over strong baselines (OpenVLA, TACO) without parameter updates
claims.direction: favors training-free, inference-time adaptive search (triggered only when drift risk is detected) over standard greedy/local sampling for long-horizon robustness
claims.conditions: RoboTwin, Simpler-WindowX, Libero-long benchmarks (simulation)

claims.claim: The adaptive search is only triggered when drift risk is detected via an SNR signal, allowing a dynamic transition between cheap 'fast' sampling and expensive 'slow' search
claims.direction: favors conditionally invoking expensive inference-time computation only when needed, rather than always running expensive search or always running cheap greedy sampling
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

title: Geometry-Aware Motion Latents for Learning Robust Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: GeoMoLa achieves state-of-the-art performance using only single-view RGB-D input, whereas existing comparable methods require multi-view reconstruction, succeeding across diverse manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors single-view RGB-D input (with the right geometric learning objective) over requiring multi-view camera setups for 3D-aware manipulation
claims.conditions: diverse manipulation benchmarks plus real-world experiments

claims.claim: Learning discrete motion latent codes by predicting how point clouds evolve over time (a 4D geometric objective), rather than reconstructing visual (appearance) observations, forces representations to encode actual physical motion; ablations confirm geometric prediction (not appearance reconstruction) is the key driver of performance
claims.direction: favors a geometric/point-cloud-evolution-prediction auxiliary objective over visual (pixel/appearance) reconstruction objectives for learning action-relevant motion latents
claims.conditions: ablation study across manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: The learned motion-latent codes transfer to novel scenes producing physically consistent transformations regardless of visual context, achieving robust manipulation with minimal demonstrations in cluttered environments where geometric reasoning determines success
claims.direction: supports that geometry-grounded motion abstractions enable robust performance from minimal demonstrations, especially in visually cluttered scenes
claims.conditions: real-world experiments in cluttered environments

title: SpaceVLA: Spatially Grounded VLA for Robotic Manipulation with User-Authored Grasp and Place Anchors

claims.claim: A VLA (OpenVLA-7B + LoRA) predicting tokenized 7-DoF incremental actions from marked RGB observations achieves 91.25% grasp success with mean grasp/placement errors of 0.5cm/0.7cm
claims.direction: reports a concrete success rate for a tokenized incremental (delta) 7-DoF action representation
claims.conditions: simulation only (Unity), 200 demonstrations, closed-loop trials

claims.claim: Explicit user-authored spatial intent anchors (grasp/place regions rendered as image-space overlays), rather than language alone, condition the VLA's action prediction
claims.direction: favors explicit spatial/visual intent conditioning (XR-authored anchors) as a complement/alternative to purely linguistic instruction conditioning
claims.conditions: simulation (Unity) evaluation

title: RoboTok: An Internet-Scale Data Engine for Human Demonstration Retrieval and Dexterous Manipulation Learning

claims.claim: A latent motion space learned from 3D hand trajectories in actor-centered reference frames enables retrieval of manipulation-relevant human demonstrations from web videos that is invariant to camera viewpoint, scene appearance, and occlusion; this retrieval improves downstream robot policy success versus existing retrieval approaches
claims.direction: favors viewpoint/appearance-invariant retrieval of internet human-video demonstrations as a scalable supervision source, over existing (less invariant) retrieval methods
claims.conditions: retrieval benchmarks and downstream robot policy evaluation

title: Contrastive Imitation Learning for Language-guided Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation (Sigma-Agent)

claims.claim: Contrastive imitation-learning modules that strengthen vision-language and current-future representations, combined with a multi-view querying Transformer for aggregating semantic information, surpass RVT (a state-of-the-art baseline) by an average of 5.2% and 5.9% in 10- and 100-demonstration training settings respectively across 18 RLBench tasks
claims.direction: favors contrastive vision-language and current-future representation alignment over standard (non-contrastive) representation learning for language-guided multi-task manipulation, with gains present at both very low (10) and moderate (100) demo counts
claims.conditions: 18 RLBench simulation tasks, 10-demo and 100-demo training regimes

claims.claim: An efficient multi-view querying Transformer (MVQ-Former) aggregates representative semantic information across multiple camera views
claims.direction: favors a dedicated multi-view aggregation module over naive concatenation/fusion of multiple camera views
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Achieves 62% success rate with a single policy across 5 real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: demonstrates real-world multi-task viability of this contrastive IL approach
claims.conditions: real-world, 5 tasks, single shared policy

title: A Telepresence Enhancing Method Based on Human Arm Dynamics

claims.claim: A lightweight teleoperation device providing force feedback via motor-vibration-induced muscle exertion sensation (rather than heavier haptic hardware) improves operator teleoperation performance and helps collect better human demonstration data for subsequent imitation learning
claims.direction: favors lightweight force-feedback teleoperation interfaces for improving demonstration quality/collection over teleoperation without such feedback
claims.conditions: real-world teleoperation experiments (force sensation, maze navigation, object manipulation)

title: ExoGS: A 4D Real-to-Sim-to-Real Framework for Scalable Manipulation Data Collection

claims.claim: A robot-free 4D real-to-sim-to-real framework using a passive exoskeleton to capture kinematically-consistent human demonstration trajectories with synchronized RGB, then reconstructing robot/objects/environment as editable 3D Gaussian Splatting assets, significantly improves data efficiency and policy generalization compared to teleoperation-based baselines
claims.direction: favors capturing real interactions via passive exoskeleton + 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction (for scalable replay/augmentation) over standard teleoperation-based data collection
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, contact-rich tasks

claims.claim: A lightweight Mask Adapter injecting instance-level semantics into the policy enhances robustness under visual domain shifts
claims.direction: supports adding instance-level semantic conditioning as a low-cost way to improve robustness to visual domain/appearance shifts
claims.conditions: real-world experiments

title: One Demonstration, Many Objects: Generalizing Manipulation via Local Contact Geometry

claims.claim: A policy focusing on object geometry local to contact points, with contact-centric rewards, learns from a single human demonstration per skill (via sim-to-real RL with demonstration priors) and transfers to novel object instances
claims.direction: favors local-contact-geometry-focused policies for generalizing from very few (one) demonstrations to varying object shapes/scales
claims.conditions: real-world, 16 objects, 4 tasks, 2 robot-hand embodiments

claims.claim: Achieves 71% success across varying object shape, scale, mass, and friction wherever local contact structure is preserved, with the smallest sim-to-real performance drop compared to baselines
claims.direction: supports local-contact-geometry focus (rather than global object identity) as a generalization strategy across novel object instances
claims.conditions: same as above

title: G6D: Geometric Learning-Free RGB-D 6D Pose Solver for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A purely geometry-driven (learning-free) RGB-D 6D pose solver, using template-based geometric matching refined via silhouette/depth consistency given an object CAD model, achieves advanced performance on LineMOD and five BOP19 datasets without requiring pretrained visual models or target-specific training
claims.direction: favors a learning-free, geometry-driven RGB-D pose-estimation approach over learned/pretrained-model-based pose estimation when a CAD model is available and interpretability/low compute matter
claims.conditions: LineMOD and BOP19 datasets, plus real-world pick-and-place experiments

claims.claim: Adjustable hypothesis counts provide flexible accuracy-computation trade-offs, and a CPU-only configuration supports deployment without any GPU resources
claims.direction: supports that some manipulation-relevant perception (object pose estimation) can run without any GPU/large model, freeing GPU budget for other policy components
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place demonstration

title: Supervised Mixture-of-Experts for Surgical Grasping and Retraction

claims.claim: Adding a supervised Mixture-of-Experts architecture on top of a lightweight Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) policy significantly boosts its in-distribution success rate compared to standard ACT alone, while generalist Vision-Language-Action models fail to acquire the task entirely under standard in-distribution conditions
claims.direction: favors a lightweight ACT+supervised-MoE architecture over both plain ACT and large generalist VLA models for a data-scarce, phase-structured manipulation task
claims.conditions: real robot-assisted surgical bowel grasping/retraction task, stereo endoscopic images only

claims.claim: Learns complex, long-horizon manipulation from fewer than 150 demonstrations using solely stereo images, without relying on multi-camera setups or thousands of demonstrations as in prior surgical robot learning
claims.direction: supports that a lightweight decoder + phase-structuring architecture can achieve strong performance from under 150 demonstrations and a single stereo camera pair
claims.conditions: real robot, <150 demonstrations

claims.claim: The MoE-augmented ACT policy demonstrates superior robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios, including novel grasp locations, reduced illumination, and partial occlusions, and generalizes to unseen viewpoints and zero-shot to a different (ex vivo porcine) tissue domain without additional training
claims.direction: favors the MoE-augmented lightweight architecture specifically for robustness to lighting changes, occlusion, and novel viewpoints/domains over standard ACT or generalist VLA baselines
claims.conditions: same real robot task, OOD evaluation including reduced illumination and zero-shot ex vivo transfer

title: Improving Vision-Language-Action Model Fine-Tuning with Structured Stage and Keyframe Supervision (StaKe)

claims.claim: Automatically deriving a stage classifier and a keyframe (next gripper-transition target) predictor from demonstration gripper states, with no manual annotation, as lightweight auxiliary heads that leave the base VLA architecture and inference loop unchanged, consistently improves success rates (14% relative gain on bimanual simulation, 56% on single-arm Franka real-robot tasks), with larger improvements on longer-horizon tasks with more gripper-event transitions
claims.direction: favors adding cheap, automatically-derived stage/keyframe auxiliary supervision (from existing gripper-state labels only) during fine-tuning over standard uniform per-timestep action supervision, with zero added inference cost
claims.conditions: bimanual simulation and real-world single-arm Franka tasks; ablation studies validate each design choice

claims.claim: Standard VLA fine-tuning applies action supervision equally across all timesteps without structure on which manipulation stage the robot is in, causing failures to concentrate around challenging gripper-event transitions (i.e., near chunk/action boundaries involving gripper open/close)
claims.direction: identifies gripper-event transitions as a specific locus of failure that structured stage-aware supervision directly targets
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Exploring Saliency for Learning Sensory-Motor Contingencies in Loco-Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: An attention-mechanism-based framework that memorizes discrete sensory phases and their corresponding motor actions from human demonstrations, then generalizes them via a perception-space metric to determine context-appropriate memory retrieval, successfully controls loco-manipulation tasks on a 7-DoF arm with gripper and a mobile manipulator
claims.direction: favors an explicit discrete sensory-motor-contingency memory (retrieved via an attention/similarity metric) over continuous end-to-end observation-history conditioning
claims.conditions: real-world 7-DoF collaborative arm with gripper, and mobile manipulator

title: MonoLift: Learning 3D Manipulation Policies from Monocular RGB via Distillation

claims.claim: A tri-level knowledge distillation framework transfers spatial (geometry-aware), temporal, and action-level knowledge from a depth-guided teacher to a monocular-RGB student policy; the resulting monocular-RGB-only student not only outperforms existing monocular approaches but even surpasses several methods that rely on explicit 3D (depth/point-cloud) input at deployment, on both simulated and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors distilling depth/3D knowledge into an RGB-only student at training time over either using RGB alone (no distillation) or requiring explicit depth/3D sensing at deployment
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: Directly answers whether we need to feed depth into the deployed policy at all: it shows a monocular-RGB student distilled from a depth-guided teacher can match or beat methods using explicit depth/point-cloud input, which could simplify our pipeline (we have depth available from the RealSense at training time but could deploy RGB-only) while retaining 3D-aware performance -- a concrete, actionable answer to our Q04 trade-off.

title: OmniVTA: Visuo-Tactile World Modeling for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A world-model-based framework combining a two-stream visuo-tactile world model (predicting short-horizon contact evolution) with a contact-aware fusion policy and a 60Hz reflexive controller that corrects deviations between predicted and observed tactile signals in closed loop outperforms existing methods and generalizes to unseen objects/configurations on real robots
claims.direction: favors predictive contact/world modeling combined with a high-frequency closed-loop reflexive correction layer over treating tactile signals as passive observations
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments across six visuo-tactile interaction categories; requires tactile sensing hardware not present in our own sensor suite

title: PhysisForcing: Physics Reinforced World Simulator for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Video-generation-based world models frequently produce physically implausible manipulations (discontinuous motion, inconsistent robot-object interactions) due to object deformation and implausible spatio-temporal correlations at contact; adding a pixel-level trajectory-alignment loss and a semantic-level relational-alignment loss (supervising physics-informative regions) improves physical consistency, raising closed-loop success rate from 16.0% to 24.0% under an action-planner protocol and improving downstream policy success
claims.direction: identifies specific failure sources of world-model-based auxiliary objectives (deformation, contact-region implausibility) and shows targeted physics-consistency losses substantially improve downstream policy performance when a world model is used
claims.conditions: R-Bench, PAI-Bench, EZS-Bench; WorldArena action-planner protocol for closed-loop evaluation

title: MotionVLA: Injecting Geometric Motion into Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: More spatiotemporal evidence (history, depth, or 4D features) is not necessarily better for resolving ambiguity in long-horizon manipulation: when injected evidence is not motion-consistent it introduces geometric drift and unstable action generation; converting a short past-only video window into compact, time-continuous trajectory-field tokens (motion-consistent evidence) rather than treating history as independently-lifted frames improves long-horizon manipulation
claims.direction: favors representing observation history as continuous motion/trajectory evidence over representing it as a set of independently-encoded past frames
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks and preliminary real-robot rollouts

claims.claim: Recoupling motion-history evidence into the VLA stream under trajectory-grounded supervision produces smoother and more direct action executions
claims.direction: supports motion-consistent history representation as a way to reduce jerky/fragmented action execution
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection (LIFT)

claims.claim: Grafting a reactive action expert beside a pretrained VLA's original action expert, injecting recent 6D end-effector force via causal force memory and zero-initialized cross-attention, and post-training with a mixture of offline data and human-corrected online rollouts (online DAgger) learns faster and reaches higher performance than vision-only post-training on contact-rich tasks (towel folding, book insertion, Hanoi ring placement); ablations show both reactive force memory and online corrective data are important
claims.direction: favors adding a force-aware reactive correction module plus online human-corrected fine-tuning to a pretrained vision-only VLA, over post-training with vision alone
claims.conditions: real-robot contact-rich manipulation tasks; requires force sensing not present in our current sensor suite

title: MatchingPolicy: Correspondence-Aware Policy Enables Cross-Object In-Context Learning

claims.claim: A correspondence-aware diffusion policy that conditions robotic actions directly on dense semantic correspondences (rather than raw pixel/object identity), with demonstration-to-scene matching architecturally decoupled from policy learning, achieves superior few-shot performance and generalizes reliably across unseen object instances and semantic categories on RLBench and real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors explicitly decoupling object correspondence-matching from action generation (via dense semantic correspondences) over end-to-end policies that implicitly couple object recognition and action, for generalizing to novel object appearances
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Achieves superior few-shot performance using in-context demonstrations
claims.direction: supports correspondence-based conditioning as a way to generalize from few demonstrations to novel objects
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Incorporating Task Progress Knowledge for Subgoal Generation in Robotic Manipulation through Image Edits (TaKSIE)

claims.claim: Jointly training a recurrent network with a latent diffusion model to generate the next visual subgoal (conditioned on current observation and language command), monitored at execution time via a visual progress representation that adaptively resamples subgoals, achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CALVIN manipulation benchmark
claims.direction: favors an explicit visual-subgoal-generation auxiliary mechanism, informed by task-progress monitoring, over policies without such progress-aware subgoal guidance
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world robotic tasks, CALVIN benchmark

claims.claim: Including task-progress knowledge improves the robustness of the trained policy to different initial robot poses and to various movement speeds during demonstrations
claims.direction: supports task-progress-aware subgoal conditioning specifically for robustness to initial-pose and demonstration-speed variation
claims.conditions: same as above

title: NORA: A Small Open-Sourced Generalist Vision Language Action Model for Embodied Tasks

claims.claim: A 3B-parameter VLA (NORA, built on Qwen-2.5-VL-3B backbone with a FAST+ tokenizer, trained on 970k real-world robot demonstrations) outperforms existing large-scale (>7B parameter) VLA models on task performance while significantly reducing computational overhead, making it more practical for real-time robotic autonomy
claims.direction: favors a smaller (3B) VLA backbone with strong visual-semantic pretraining and an efficient action tokenizer over larger (>7B) VLA models for real-time deployment
claims.conditions: real-world robot demonstrations (970k), zero-shot and task-execution evaluation

claims.claim: Leverages the Qwen-2.5-VL-3B multimodal backbone's superior visual-semantic understanding specifically to address visual-encoding limitations that cause failures such as object-grasping errors in prior VLA models
claims.direction: supports choosing a strong pretrained vision-language backbone to mitigate visual-encoding-related grasping failures, even at smaller overall model scale
claims.conditions: same as above

title: TraceGen: World Modeling in 3D Trace Space Enables Learning from Cross-Embodiment Videos

claims.claim: With just five target-robot demonstration videos, TraceGen attains 80% success across four tasks; with only five uncalibrated human demonstration videos captured on a handheld phone (no robot data at all), it still reaches 67.5% success on a real robot
claims.direction: favors pretraining a compact 3D-trace-space world model on large cross-embodiment/cross-environment video corpora, then adapting with only ~5 target demonstrations (robot or even handheld-phone human video) rather than collecting dozens-to-hundreds of robot-specific demonstrations
claims.conditions: real robot, 5 target demonstrations (robot or handheld-phone human video), pretrained on 123K videos / 1.8M observation-trace-language triplets

claims.claim: Predicting future motion in a compact, symbolic 3D 'trace-space' (scene-level trajectories abstracting away appearance while retaining geometric structure) rather than in pixel space enables an efficient, transferable 3D motion prior across embodiments, cameras, and environments
claims.direction: favors trace-space (structured, appearance-invariant) world modeling over pixel-space video world modeling for cross-embodiment transfer and small-data adaptation
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Offers 50-600x faster inference than state-of-the-art video-based world models
claims.direction: favors trace-space world models over pixel-space video world models for inference-time efficiency
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: An almost perfect match for our situation: adapting to a new task/robot from only ~5 demonstrations (even from an uncalibrated handheld-phone human video, not a robot at all) with a world-model approach that is 50-600x faster than pixel-space alternatives -- directly relevant to our extremely limited demo budget and laptop-GPU inference constraints.

title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning by Guiding World Models with Non-Curated Data

claims.claim: Naive fine-tuning of a world model on abundant non-curated (reward-free, mixed-quality, multi-embodiment) offline data fails to accelerate RL due to distributional shift between offline and online data; adding experience rehearsal and execution guidance fixes this, achieving nearly 2x the aggregate score of learning-from-scratch baselines across 72 visuomotor tasks spanning 6 embodiments
claims.direction: identifies distributional shift as the key failure mode when using non-curated multi-embodiment data to pretrain/fine-tune a world model, and shows two specific techniques (experience rehearsal, execution guidance) resolve it
claims.conditions: 72 visuomotor tasks, 6 embodiments, offline-to-online RL setting (locomotion and manipulation)

title: DexSim2Real: Foundation Model-Guided Sim-to-Real Transfer for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Using a vision-language model as a visual-realism critic to optimize simulation (domain-randomization) parameters via closed-loop CMA-ES, complementing text-based reward-design approaches with direct visual feedback, contributes to an average 78.2% real-world success rate across six manipulation tasks, outperforming DrEureka and DeXtreme and reducing the sim-to-real gap to 8.3%
claims.direction: favors VLM-critic-guided (visually-grounded) domain randomization over purely text-based or manually-designed domain randomization for closing the sim-to-real gap
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, six tasks, blinded evaluation

title: Learning-Based Robust Control: Unifying Exploration and Distributional Robustness for Reliable Robotics via Free Energy

claims.claim: A policy-computation model based on a distributionally robust free energy principle, jointly learning environment dynamics and rewards while explicitly ensuring robustness to epistemic uncertainty, narrows the sim-to-real gap and enables repeatable tabletop manipulation with a real Franka Research 3 arm without task-specific fine-tuning after zero-shot deployment
claims.direction: favors explicitly modeling and bounding epistemic uncertainty during joint dynamics/reward learning for robustness, over standard policy learning without such uncertainty guarantees
claims.conditions: real-world tabletop manipulation, Franka Research 3, zero-shot deployment

title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Pretraining the action module alone with motion priors (a lightweight flow-matching encoder-decoder learning temporal motion structure solely from unconditioned action trajectories, without visual/language tokens) before cross-modal VLA alignment, then transferring via decoder reuse and early-stage latent distillation, gives faster convergence and higher success rates than VLA training without such action priors, across 13 diverse cross-embodiment tasks (simulated and real)
claims.direction: favors a two-stage training scheme (action-only motion-prior pretraining, then VLA alignment) over standard joint end-to-end VLA training where the action module learns motion from scratch
claims.conditions: 13 cross-embodiment tasks, simulated and real-world platforms

claims.claim: The trained action-prior encoder doubles as a compact history compressor, summarizing state-action histories into a single temporal context token for history-aware modeling at negligible additional cost
claims.direction: favors compressing observation/action history into a single learned token (from an action-motion-prior encoder) over conditioning directly on raw multi-step history
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Achieves substantially stronger performance specifically on data-scarce real-world tasks, and scaling up the action-only pretraining data yields a more generalizable action prior that directly improves downstream VLA performance even without more paired vision-language-action data
claims.direction: favors scaling cheap action-only (no vision/language needed) pretraining data to improve downstream performance in data-scarce real-world settings
claims.conditions: real-world data-scarce tasks

title: LM-X: Explainable Vision-Language-Action Modeling via Progress, Event, and Uncertainty Prediction

claims.claim: Jointly (not post-hoc) supervising three auxiliary online signals during action pretraining -- return-to-go (progress/state quality), event-to-go (predicted action sequence to next semantic event), and heteroscedastic action-flow variance (local command reliability/uncertainty), with each conditioning the next -- outperforms GR00T N1.7 substantially: 74.1% vs 55.4% success on 50 randomized-hard RoboTwin2.0 tasks and 73.5% vs 50.7% on seven real-robot tasks; a controlled ablation confirms joint training beats adding these signals post-hoc
claims.direction: favors jointly pretraining progress/event/uncertainty auxiliary signals with the action expert (rather than adding them after action-only pretraining) for both performance and explainability
claims.conditions: pretrained on 20,000+ hours of real-robot trajectories including 1,000+ hours of failed rollouts; evaluated on RoboTwin2.0 and 7 real-robot tasks against GR00T N1.7

title: Surgical Task Automation Using Actor-Critic Frameworks and Self-Supervised Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A self-supervised imitation-learning method (retrieving nearest-neighbor demonstrated states and bootstrapping actor networks) enables an actor-critic RL framework to learn effectively from state-only demonstrations (no action labels, from an unknown expert policy), delivering remarkable improvements over an RL baseline and comparable performance to action-based IL methods
claims.direction: favors leveraging state-only demonstrations (without costly action-label annotation) via self-supervised retrieval-based imitation, when action labels are hard or expensive to obtain
claims.conditions: open-source surgical simulation platform

title: SLIM: Sim-to-Real Legged Instructive Manipulation via Long-Horizon Visuomotor Learning

claims.claim: Using only a single wrist-mounted RGB camera (no scene/third-person camera) on accessible, low-cost hardware (Unitree Go1 quadruped + WidowX-250S arm), a hierarchical teacher-student visuomotor policy solves long-horizon tasks (search, move-to, grasp, transport, drop) with nearly 80% real-world success
claims.direction: demonstrates that a single wrist camera (without any external/scene camera) can suffice for long-horizon manipulation on low-cost hardware, given the right hierarchical training pipeline
claims.conditions: real-world, low-cost hardware (Unitree Go1 + WidowX-250S + single wrist RGB camera)

claims.claim: The entire policy is trained purely in simulation with zero real-world demonstrations, using a teacher-student RL pipeline (privileged task decomposition for the teacher, RL-guided distillation for the student)
claims.direction: favors sim-only RL training with sim-to-real transfer techniques over collecting real teleoperation demonstrations, for long-horizon mobile manipulation on low-cost hardware
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, zero real demonstrations used

claims.claim: Demonstrates effective deployment across diverse indoor and outdoor scenes under various lighting conditions, achieving performance comparable to expert human teleoperation while operating about 1.5x faster
claims.direction: supports that careful sim-to-real technique design (rather than real lighting-diverse data collection) can achieve robustness to varied lighting/scenes
claims.conditions: real-world diverse indoor/outdoor scenes and lighting conditions

title: Exploring the Limits of Vision-Language-Action Manipulations in Cross-task Generalization

claims.claim: A systematic benchmark (AGNOSTOS, 23 unseen manipulation tasks with two generalization-difficulty levels) reveals that current VLA models, despite being trained on diverse datasets, struggle to generalize effectively to unseen tasks in a zero-shot cross-task setting
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that VLA models trained on diverse data generalize well to genuinely new (not just new objects/scenes but new task types) manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, 23 unseen tasks

claims.claim: Conditioning an LLM on in-context demonstrations from seen tasks (with a dynamics-guided sample-selection strategy identifying relevant demonstrations via cross-task dynamics) significantly improves cross-task zero-shot generalization over leading VLA models, without any fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors in-context, dynamics-guided demonstration retrieval over standard VLA fine-tuning for generalizing to genuinely new tasks
claims.conditions: same benchmark

title: OmniVTLA: Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Models With Semantic-Aligned Tactile Sensing

claims.claim: Adding semantically-aligned tactile sensing (via a dual-encoder tactile vision transformer trained on a 135K tri-modal object dataset) to a VLA baseline significantly reduces task completion time and generates smoother trajectories, alongside large real-world success-rate gains (e.g. +21.9pp with grippers, +33.3pp on peg-insertion) versus vision-language-only VLA baselines
claims.direction: favors adding aligned tactile sensing as an extra modality to reduce jerky/slow trajectories and improve contact-rich task success, versus vision-language-only VLA baselines (though this requires tactile hardware we do not have)
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place and peg-insertion tasks, grippers and dexterous hands

title: ActionCodec: What Makes for Good Action Tokenizers

claims.claim: Establishing action-tokenizer design principles from a VLA-optimization (not just reconstruction-fidelity) perspective -- maximized temporal token overlap, minimized vocabulary redundancy, enhanced multimodal mutual information, and token independence -- and building ActionCodec around them lets a SmolVLM2-2.2B model fine-tuned with it reach 95.5% success on LIBERO without any robotics pretraining (97.4% with further architectural enhancements), a new SOTA for VLA models without robotics pretraining
claims.direction: favors designing discrete action tokenizers around information-theoretic VLA-optimization principles (not reconstruction fidelity alone) for autoregressive VLA action heads
claims.conditions: LIBERO and other simulation/real-world benchmarks; small (~2.2B) VLM backbone, no robotics-specific pretraining

why_deep_read: Concrete, actionable design principles for discrete action tokenizers (directly relevant to our Q01 action-head choice) validated on a small (2.2B) VLM with no robotics pretraining reaching SOTA -- close to our own compute/model-size regime and a natural fit if we consider an autoregressive discrete-token action head.

title: AttenA+: Rectifying Action Inequality in Robotic Foundation Models

claims.claim: Standard VLA/WAM training treats all timesteps in an action chunk as equally informative (temporal homogeneity), but low-velocity segments often dictate task success (precision-demanding interactions) while high-velocity segments are error-tolerant transitions; reweighting the training loss by the inverse velocity field (prioritizing low-velocity, kinematically-critical segments) is architecture-agnostic, adds no parameters, and improves OpenVLA-OFT to 98.6% (+1.5%) on LIBERO and FastWAM to 92.4% (+0.6%) on RoboTwin 2.0, with real-world Franka validation
claims.direction: favors velocity-weighted (non-uniform) action-chunk loss weighting over uniform per-timestep loss weighting, as a free (no extra params) plug-in improvement
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, plus real-world Franka manipulator validation

claims.claim: Mining intrinsic structural priors of action sequences (physical criticality via velocity) is presented as an efficient, physics-aware complement to standard model/data scaling for improving VLA/WAM performance
claims.direction: supports physics-aware training objective modifications as an alternative/complement to scaling model size or data for improving action-generation quality
claims.conditions: same as above

title: HALO: A Unified Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

claims.claim: A Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that decouples textual task reasoning, visual subgoal prediction, and action prediction into specialized but cross-collaborating experts (embodied multimodal chain-of-thought), trained via an automated EM-CoT data synthesis pipeline, surpasses baseline policy pi0 by 34.1% on the RoboTwin benchmark
claims.direction: favors decoupled but jointly-trained textual-reasoning + visual-subgoal + action experts over a single monolithic reasoning-and-acting module
claims.conditions: simulated (RoboTwin) and real-world environments

claims.claim: Exhibits strong generalization capabilities under aggressive unseen environmental randomization, attributed to the EM-CoT reasoning design
claims.direction: supports multimodal chain-of-thought (textual+visual foresight) as a mechanism for robustness under environmental randomization
claims.conditions: real-world environments with aggressive randomization

title: Self-Evolving Learning for Embodied AI with Criticality Model

claims.claim: Random data collection during finetuning over-represents nominal scenarios and misses rare failure cases; learning a state-wise criticality model (predicting probability of future failure from the policy's own execution outcomes) to guide importance-sampling toward failure-prone scenarios, then resampling training data with importance weights, reduces failure rates by 51-67% relative to trained baselines and 8-25% relative to SOTA VLA models
claims.direction: favors actively curating/resampling training data toward failure-prone scenarios (via a learned criticality model) over collecting/using demonstration data uniformly at random
claims.conditions: quadrupedal locomotion, multi-task manipulation, VLA benchmarks, and a real-robot task

title: Grasping by Hanging: a Learning-Free Grasping Detection Method for Previously Unseen Objects

claims.claim: A learning-free, three-stage geometric method (identifying hangable structures, detecting 6D hook poses, ranking grasp candidates) achieves significantly higher grasping accuracy and stability than a state-of-the-art learning-based method on previously unseen objects, especially thin and flat objects, without requiring training data
claims.direction: favors a learning-free geometric grasp-detection approach over learned methods specifically for generalizing to previously unseen object shapes
claims.conditions: real robot experiments

title: DNAct: Diffusion Guided Multi-Task 3D Policy Learning

claims.claim: A neural-rendering pretraining phase distills 2D semantic features from foundation models (e.g., Stable Diffusion) into a 3D space, providing comprehensive scene semantic understanding before diffusion-based multi-task policy training
claims.direction: favors distilling 2D foundation-model semantic features into a 3D representation over training a 3D encoder from scratch or using 2D features directly
claims.conditions: multi-task manipulation with few demonstrations

claims.claim: DNAct significantly surpasses SOTA NeRF-based multi-task manipulation approaches with over 30% improvement in success rate by combining this 3D semantic distillation with diffusion training over action sequences
claims.direction: favors this 3D-semantic + diffusion combination over prior NeRF-based 3D multi-task manipulation methods
claims.conditions: multi-task manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Designed explicitly to learn a generalizable multi-task policy with few demonstrations
claims.direction: supports this pretraining approach as improving data efficiency
claims.conditions: few-demonstration multi-task setting

title: Efficient and Reliable Teleoperation through Real-to-Sim-to-Real Shared Autonomy

claims.claim: A real-to-sim-to-real shared-autonomy framework fits a simple kNN human-behavior surrogate from less than five minutes of real-world teleoperation data, then trains a residual 'copilot' policy with model-free RL in simulation to assist the human operator; in a 16-participant user study on fine-grained contact-rich tasks (nut threading, gear meshing, peg insertion), this copilot improves task success for novice operators and execution efficiency for experienced operators versus direct teleoperation and shared-autonomy baselines relying on expert priors or behavioral-cloning pilots, and produces higher-quality demonstrations for downstream imitation learning
claims.direction: favors augmenting human teleoperation with a lightweight, quickly-fit (under 5 minutes of data) residual RL copilot to improve both demonstration quality and collection efficiency, over raw/unassisted teleoperation
claims.conditions: real-world fine-grained manipulation tasks, 16-participant user study, both novice and experienced operators

why_deep_read: Directly targets improving the QUALITY and reliability of teleoperated demonstrations (fitting a corrective copilot from under 5 minutes of data) for fine-grained, contact-rich tasks -- highly relevant to our own teleop data-collection pipeline, which suffers from Feetech servo jitter/backlash that likely degrades demonstration quality.

title: DexForce: Extracting Force-Informed Actions From Kinesthetic Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Computing force-informed actions from contact forces measured during kinesthetic demonstrations (rather than using raw kinematic actions alone) yields policies with an average 76% success rate across six contact-rich tasks, versus near-zero success rates for policies trained directly on actions that ignore contact forces; force data helps most for tasks requiring advanced precision/coordination
claims.direction: strongly favors incorporating force information into the action representation/observation (not just kinematic pose) for contact-rich manipulation over kinematics-only actions
claims.conditions: real-world kinesthetic demonstrations, six contact-rich tasks; requires force sensing (or estimation) during demonstration collection

title: Rethinking Progression of Memory State in Robotic Manipulation: An Object-Centric Perspective

claims.claim: In non-Markovian tasks requiring sequenced interaction with visually similar objects, key decision cues live in object-specific interaction histories rather than the current frame; standard VLA models struggle here and token-scaling multi-frame history quickly becomes intractable even for tasks spanning only a few hundred frames; a slot-centric framework maintaining spatio-temporally consistent object 'slot' identities (via slot-state-space modeling for short-term history plus a relational encoder aligning tokens to action decoding) enables temporally grounded, scalable action prediction
claims.direction: favors object-centric persistent 'slot' memory over naive multi-frame token concatenation for non-Markovian, object-tracking-dependent manipulation
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Mem (new non-Markovian benchmark) and general LIBERO tasks, simulation

title: OXE-AugE: A Large-Scale Robot Augmentation of OXE for Scaling Cross-Embodiment Policy Learning

claims.claim: The Open X-Embodiment dataset is highly imbalanced (top 4 robot types = 85%+ of real data); augmenting it with 9 additional robot embodiments (OXE-AugE, 4.4M+ trajectories, 3x original size) improves policy performance not only on the augmented robots but also on unseen robots and even the original robots under distribution shift
claims.direction: favors deliberately balancing/augmenting large cross-embodiment pretraining datasets across diverse arm/gripper combinations, rather than relying on an imbalanced aggregate dataset
claims.conditions: large-scale cross-embodiment pretraining corpus, systematic scaling study

claims.claim: Fine-tuning state-of-the-art generalist policies (OpenVLA, pi0) on OXE-AugE improves success rates by 24-45% on previously unseen robot-gripper combinations across four real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: supports that starting from a checkpoint fine-tuned on an embodiment-balanced dataset substantially improves generalization to a new (e.g., low-cost) robot-gripper combination versus starting from a checkpoint trained on the original imbalanced OXE
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, four tasks, previously-unseen robot-gripper combinations

title: Towards Efficient and Robust Manipulation via Multi-Frame Vision-Language-Action Modeling (CronusVLA)

claims.claim: Directly feeding multiple frames into a VLM backbone incurs substantial computational overhead/latency; a two-stage approach (single-frame VLM pretraining, then multi-frame post-training that adapts predictions to learnable features and aggregates historical information via feature chunking, avoiding repeated full VLM passes per frame) extends single-frame VLA models to multi-frame history efficiently, improving success 26.8% over OpenVLA on LIBERO and reaching 70.9% on SimplerEnv
claims.direction: favors efficient feature-chunking-based multi-frame history aggregation (post-hoc adaptation of a single-frame-pretrained VLA) over naively feeding multiple raw frames into the VLM backbone
claims.conditions: simulated (LIBERO, SimplerEnv) and real-world, three embodiments

claims.claim: Introduces SimplerEnv-OR, a benchmark with 24 types of observational disturbances and 120 severity levels, on which this multi-frame approach achieves the highest robustness score among compared methods
claims.direction: supports multi-frame temporal aggregation (done efficiently) as improving robustness specifically to a wide range of observational disturbances
claims.conditions: SimplerEnv-OR benchmark

title: Sparse2Act: Learning Action-Aligned Sparse 3D Representations for Cross-Domain Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Pretraining sparse point-cloud encoders using task-space end-effector actions as geometric supervision (masked sparse 3D tokens trained to organize scene features around paired workspace motion), rather than tying the 3D representation to a specific downstream task objective/policy architecture/action parameterization, produces a reusable encoder: only the encoder initialization is reused downstream, so policies keep their own architectures and action spaces (including joint-space commands)
claims.direction: favors action-aligned (not task-specific) pretraining of sparse 3D point-cloud encoders, decoupled from the final action space/architecture, for reusability across downstream policies
claims.conditions: LIBERO-10 (86.9% success after only 500 fine-tuning steps), cross-domain transfer to Meta-World-5 (73.4%)

claims.claim: Simulation pretraining followed by limited real-data fine-tuning achieves an average 72.5% success rate across four real-world tasks, demonstrating effective sim-to-real transfer with minimal real demonstrations
claims.direction: supports sim-pretrained action-aligned 3D encoders as a way to reduce required real-world demonstration count
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, 4 tasks, limited real fine-tuning data

title: VLAFlow: A Unified Training Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models via Co-training and Future Latent Alignment

claims.claim: Under a controlled comparison (identical pi0-style architecture, shared VLM backbone, action expert, 14-dim action space, ~5000 hours of heterogeneous OXEMix data), four training paradigms are compared: action-only modeling, language-supervised co-training, future latent alignment, and their combination. Action-only pretraining is sensitive to heterogeneous data; future latent alignment specifically improves state-transition and action-outcome modeling; combining language supervision with future latent alignment (MindLWPI) achieves the most stable overall transfer performance across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv
claims.direction: favors combining language-supervised co-training with a future-latent-alignment auxiliary objective over action-only training, especially when pretraining on heterogeneous multi-source robot data
claims.conditions: controlled architecture-matched comparison, ~5000 hours heterogeneous data (DROID, OpenX-Embodiment, OpenX-Augmented, RoboCOIN), evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv

claims.claim: Language-supervised co-training specifically helps preserve vision-language generalization (versus action-only training, which does not benefit from this), even though it alone is less stable than combining it with future latent alignment
claims.direction: favors retaining a language-conditioning/co-training objective (not dropping it for a pure action-prediction loss) specifically to preserve generalization
claims.conditions: same controlled comparison as above

why_deep_read: A rare, architecture-matched controlled ablation isolating exactly which auxiliary training objectives (language co-training vs. future-latent alignment vs. both) help VLA transfer and generalization -- directly and cleanly informs our Q08/Q09 decisions on whether to add language co-training and/or a future-prediction auxiliary loss to our small SmolVLA fine-tune.

title: Mimir: A Neuro-Symbolic Memory System with Dynamic Grounding for Embodied Agents in Interactive Environments

claims.claim: Separating world memory (object locations/states/perceptual evidence) from task memory (goal agenda, progress, hand state, failures, constraints), with a dynamic grounding module binding the active goal to recalled world candidates before each action, consistently improves long-horizon embodied task success over flat/implicit-history baselines, with maximum gains of 42.5% and average gains of 23.0% across tested backbones, and 8.5% average improvement over the best prior agent/memory systems
claims.direction: favors explicitly separated, structured world/task memory with dynamic per-step grounding over flat observation-history or implicit policy-state memory for long-horizon, partially-observable tasks
claims.conditions: EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat embodied household task benchmarks (simulation)

title: GraspLDM: Generative 6-DoF Grasp Synthesis Using Latent Diffusion Models

claims.claim: Using diffusion models as priors in the latent space of a VAE for object-centric SE(3) grasp-pose generation (conditioned on point clouds) allows efficient task-specific re-training of only a small low-dimensional denoising network, rather than expensive full-model re-training; models trained purely on simulation data transfer to the real world without further fine-tuning, achieving an 80% success rate across 80 real-world grasp attempts on two robotic setups
claims.direction: favors latent-space diffusion (small denoising network operating on a compact latent) over full-space diffusion models for efficient task-specific grasp-pose generation with good sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: real-world grasping, two robotic setups, no real-world fine-tuning

title: RT-Affordance: Affordances are Versatile Intermediate Representations for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning policies on affordances (robot pose at key task stages) as an intermediate representation -- rather than language alone, goal images, or trajectory sketches, which either underspecify or overspecify context -- exceeds the performance of existing intermediate-representation methods by over 50% on novel tasks and is empirically robust to novel settings
claims.direction: favors affordance-based intermediate conditioning over language-only, goal-image, or trajectory-sketch conditioning for generalization to novel tasks/settings
claims.conditions: diverse novel manipulation tasks; hierarchical model proposing an affordance plan then conditioning the low-level policy on it

claims.claim: The model can learn new tasks by training on cheap-to-collect in-domain affordance images alone, without collecting any additional costly robot trajectories, while still flexibly combining large web datasets with robot trajectory data
claims.direction: favors substituting cheap affordance-image collection for costly additional robot-trajectory collection when adding new tasks
claims.conditions: combination of large web datasets and robot demonstration data

title: FlowPolicy: Enabling Fast and Robust 3D Flow-based Policy via Consistency Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Refining flow dynamics by normalizing the self-consistency of the velocity field (consistency flow matching), conditioned on observed 3D point clouds, lets the model derive task-execution policies in a single inference step instead of recursive multi-step sampling
claims.direction: favors consistency-flow-matching (single-step) action generation over recursive multi-step diffusion/flow policies
claims.conditions: Adroit and MetaWorld simulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Achieves a 7x increase in inference speed while maintaining competitive average success rates compared to state-of-the-art recursive diffusion/flow methods
claims.direction: favors this consistency-based single-step approach specifically to reduce inference latency without sacrificing much performance
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

claims.claim: Conditions the policy on 3D point-cloud observations rather than 2D RGB
claims.direction: supports 3D point-cloud conditioning as compatible with fast, single-step flow-based policies
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

title: E-GAIL: efficient GAIL through including negative corruption and long-term rewards for robotic manipulations

claims.claim: Combining short-term and long-term observation-based rewards with negative-action corruption of generated trajectories (within a GAIL framework) achieves a 25% improvement in success rates across multiple manipulation tasks while requiring 70% fewer training episodes for policy convergence, from a limited set of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors these two techniques (long-term reward augmentation, negative-trajectory corruption) for improving data efficiency of adversarial imitation learning from limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: multiple manipulation tasks (setting -- sim or real -- not specified in abstract)

title: Latent Reasoning VLA: Latent Thinking and Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Internalizing multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning into continuous latent representations (via curriculum training that progressively shifts from explicit textual/visual CoT supervision to latent reasoning, then conditions action generation on latent reasoning dynamics) eliminates explicit CoT generation at inference time while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art VLA methods
claims.direction: favors internalizing CoT-style reasoning into a continuous latent space (learned via curriculum distillation from explicit CoT) over generating explicit discrete CoT text/tokens at inference time
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks and long-horizon real-robot manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Reduces inference latency by up to 90% compared to explicit CoT-based approaches, enabling efficient, action-oriented real-time control
claims.direction: strongly favors latent (implicit) reasoning over explicit CoT token generation specifically to cut inference latency
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Human-Robot Copilot for Data-Efficient Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A Human-Robot Copilot framework using a scaling factor for dexterous teleoperation (compatible with a wide range of industrial/research manipulators, unlike prior HG-DAgger-style approaches that trade off dexterity for generality or vice versa) achieves higher policy performance with the same number of demonstration trajectories than existing interactive imitation-learning baselines, while requiring only intermittent corrective interventions, making data collection more efficient
claims.direction: favors a copilot-assisted teleoperation scheme (occasional human corrective intervention with a dexterity-preserving scaling factor) over standard teleoperation or existing HG-DAgger-style interactive imitation learning, for the same demonstration count
claims.conditions: experimental comparison across manipulator types, demonstration-count-matched evaluation

title: GASE: Gaussian Splatting-Based Automated System for Reconstructing Embodied-Simulation Environments

claims.claim: An automated 3D-Gaussian-Splatting-based pipeline (panoramic multi-view scanning, camera-pose-based object extraction, scene inpainting) for reconstructing high-fidelity simulation scenes from real environments outperforms existing 3D-Gaussian-based methods in segmentation accuracy by over 10% and achieves real-robot deployment (manipulation and navigation) within less than 10% performance gap versus policies trained purely on real-world data
claims.direction: favors automated photorealistic scene reconstruction (Gaussian Splatting) for generating simulation training data over manually-built simulation scenes, for closing the sim-to-real visual gap
claims.conditions: real-robot deployment across manipulation and navigation tasks

title: FrameSkip: Learning from Fewer but More Informative Frames in VLA Training

claims.claim: Dense demonstration trajectories create a temporal supervision imbalance where long low-change segments dominate training while manipulation-critical transitions (alignment, contact, grasping, release) appear only sparsely; a dataloader-only frame-selection framework (scoring frames by action variation, visual-action coherence, task-progress priors, and gripper-transition preservation, then retaining only high-importance frames) improves the success-retention trade-off over full-frame training, reaching a 76.15% macro-average success rate across RoboCasa-GR1, SimplerEnv, and LIBERO (vs 66.50% for full-frame training) while retaining only 20% of unique frames, leaving the VLA architecture, action head, training objective, and inference procedure completely unchanged
claims.direction: favors smart, importance-weighted frame subsampling at the data-loading stage over using every recorded demonstration frame as equally-weighted supervision, since it can improve performance while using far fewer frames from the same demonstrations
claims.conditions: RoboCasa-GR1, SimplerEnv, LIBERO simulation benchmarks; requires zero architecture/inference changes

claims.claim: Explicitly preserving gripper-transition frames (alignment, contact, grasping, release) during frame selection is one of the four scoring criteria, since these transitions are disproportionately important but sparse in raw demonstration streams
claims.direction: identifies gripper-event/chunk-boundary-adjacent frames as specifically under-represented and worth up-weighting in training data
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: An essentially free (dataloader-only, no architecture or inference change) technique that improves success 66.50%->76.15% while using only 20% of frames, and explicitly up-weights gripper-transition frames -- directly actionable for our SmolVLA fine-tuning pipeline with our existing ~50-100 demos, requiring no additional engineering risk.

title: Geometric Entropy: When Trajectory Diversity Helps and Hurts in Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A task-agnostic Geometric Entropy metric (H_G), quantifying intrinsic trajectory-shape diversity after normalizing away extrinsic variation (goal pose, workspace scale), reveals a consistent inverted-U relationship between imitation-learning success and H_G across architectures and both simulated and real-robot contact-rich tasks: increasing diversity helps in low-diversity regimes but hurts once it induces strategy ambiguity; the optimal entropy shifts toward lower values as task mastery increases (more data, easier tasks, stronger priors), and for a pretrained VLA model the trend becomes effectively monotonic decreasing
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that more demonstration trajectory-shape diversity is always better; for a pretrained VLA model specifically, LESS geometric diversity (more consistent trajectory shapes) tends to be better, while some diversity only helps when starting from little data/weak priors
claims.conditions: multiple IL architectures, simulated and real-robot contact-rich manipulation tasks, varying data scales

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q13 'diversity vs count' sub-question with a nuanced, somewhat counterintuitive finding (an inverted-U, with pretrained VLA models actually preferring LESS trajectory-shape diversity) that could directly change how we plan our ~50-100 demonstration collection for our SmolVLA fine-tune -- worth reading in full to get the calibration guidance (the H_G metric and its practical auditing procedure) for our own dataset.

title: PAC-DP: PAC-Bayesian Diffusion Policy Learning

claims.claim: Modeling a Diffusion Policy as a Bayesian neural network and adding a PAC-Bayes-derived KL-divergence regularizer (between posterior and prior parameter distributions) to the standard denoising loss improves denoising performance, lowers variational negative log-likelihood, and raises success rates across multiple robotic manipulation benchmarks, without significantly increasing training time
claims.direction: favors adding a principled PAC-Bayesian regularizer to standard diffusion-policy training over the standard denoising-only objective
claims.conditions: multiple robotic manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: The largest improvements from this regularizer are observed specifically in low-data training regimes and complex tasks
claims.direction: supports this regularization technique as particularly valuable when demonstration counts are limited
claims.conditions: low-data regimes, complex manipulation tasks

title: Pointing-VLA: Typed Spatial Grounding Interfaces for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

claims.claim: Replacing autoregressive text-coordinate or opaque-action-token spatial grounding with typed hidden-state heads that directly predict normalized points, object-functional-grounding heatmaps, and visual trajectories (without serializing geometry as text), with an explicit execution contract assigning PICK/PLACE stages to different readout types, achieves SOTA on Bridge/WidowX (72.9% avg across four tasks) without task-specific finetuning
claims.direction: favors typed, geometry-native spatial-grounding readouts (points/heatmaps/trajectories) over text-serialized coordinate outputs for VLA spatial grounding
claims.conditions: Bridge/WidowX simulation/physical pick-place benchmark

claims.claim: Typed heads are 6.68-6.90x faster than text-based (Embodied-R1) decoding on a shared benchmark, and when integrated as spatial guidance for a pi_0.5 action policy, raise autonomous real-robot success from 52.7% to 80.7% across three visual contexts while reducing recorded controller time by more than 20x
claims.direction: favors typed spatial readouts over text-based decoding both for speed (6.68-6.90x faster) and for downstream real-robot success when used as guidance for an existing action policy
claims.conditions: real-robot deployment, pi_0.5 base policy, three visual contexts

title: Dense to MoE Adaptation for Compact Vision Language Action Policies

claims.claim: Adapting selected dense feed-forward blocks of a VLA's LLM into Mixture-of-Experts layers, then dynamically deactivating experts (masks derived from router usage statistics during fine-tuning, with staged training and expert protection to avoid early collapse) allows deactivating 40% of the LLM parameters while retaining 95.7% average success on LIBERO and 42.0% average success across all 50 RoboTwin2.0 tasks
claims.direction: favors dynamic dense-to-MoE conversion with usage-guided expert deactivation over keeping the full dense LLM, for reducing deployed VLA parameter count with minimal performance loss
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 simulation benchmarks

title: A Comparison of Imitation Learning Algorithms for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: A carefully-designed controlled comparison of prominent imitation-learning algorithms on a complex, over-constrained bimanual manipulation task (multiple contacts between manipulated object and environment) finds that imitation learning overall is well suited to such tasks, but algorithms differ substantially in hyperparameter sensitivity, ease of training, data efficiency, and performance -- not all algorithms are equal despite similar reported benchmark numbers elsewhere
claims.direction: cautions against assuming imitation-learning algorithms are interchangeable; algorithm choice materially affects robustness to hyperparameter/environmental perturbations, training ease, and data efficiency on high-precision, contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: complex bimanual manipulation task, industry-inspired high-precision environment, controlled experimental procedure

claims.claim: Data efficiency is explicitly studied and found to vary substantially across algorithms
claims.direction: supports algorithm choice as a key lever for data efficiency, not just architecture size or demo count alone
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Learning in ImaginationLand: Omnidirectional Policies through 3D Generative Models (OP-Gen)

claims.claim: 3D generative models can augment a dataset from a single real-world demonstration, from which an 'omnidirectional' policy is learned within this imagined/augmented dataset, showing superior performance to recent baselines using alternative data-augmentation methods
claims.direction: favors 3D-generative-model-based augmentation from a single real demonstration over other (non-3D-generative) data augmentation approaches
claims.conditions: real-world experiments: grasping objects, opening a drawer, placing trash into a bin

claims.claim: Significantly reduces the number of demonstrations required for policy learning, since a single real-world demonstration is augmented into a full training dataset
claims.direction: favors this augmentation approach specifically to reduce required demonstration count toward the low end (as few as one)
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: The resulting omnidirectional policy performs the task when initialized from states very far from those observed during the demonstration, including starting from the opposite side of the object relative to the real-world demonstration
claims.direction: supports 3D-generative augmentation as a way to achieve robustness to extreme initial-state variation beyond the demonstrated distribution
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across multiple tasks

title: Wavelet Policy: Imitation Learning in the Scale Domain with World Prior Memory

claims.claim: Encoding persistent physical scene structure from static background images into compact 'world-prior' memory tokens, fused into the encoder during forward propagation (with a dedicated world-prior adaptation loss keeping the background encoder lightweight and stable), provides an effective and efficient memory mechanism that consistently outperforms strong baselines across four simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors compact, background-derived persistent world-prior memory tokens over standard raw observation-history conditioning
claims.conditions: 4 simulated + 6 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Performing wavelet-domain decomposition over horizon-aligned latent action tokens (via a Single-Encoder Multiple-Decoder architecture modeling different temporal scales, then reconstructing action chunks via inverse wavelet transform) is a lightweight scale-domain alternative to direct time-domain action-chunk prediction
claims.direction: favors multi-scale (wavelet/scale-domain) action-chunk modeling over direct single-scale time-domain prediction
claims.conditions: same tasks as above

title: CEI: A Unified Interface for Cross-Embodiment Visuomotor Policy Learning in 3D Space

claims.claim: Quantifying functional similarity between different robot-arm/end-effector morphologies via Directional Chamfer Distance, then aligning robot trajectories through gradient-based optimization to synthesize observations/actions for unseen embodiments, transfers demonstrations/policies from a Franka Panda to 16 different simulated embodiments across 3 tasks, and supports bidirectional real-world transfer between a UR5+AG95-gripper robot and a UR5+Xhand robot across 6 real-world tasks, achieving an 82.4% average transfer ratio
claims.direction: favors an explicit functional-similarity-based action/observation alignment interface for cross-embodiment (cross-gripper) transfer over embodiment-specific policies or naive action-space sharing
claims.conditions: simulation (16 embodiments) and real-world (bidirectional gripper transfer, 6 tasks)

title: Deep Imitation Learning for Efficient Path-Following of Hyper-Redundant Robots

claims.claim: A two-stage noise-injection curriculum (rather than requiring an interactive expert as in DAgger) mitigates behavior-cloning covariate shift entirely offline, enabling robust recovery policies, combined with a refined Soft-Maximum formulation for generating smooth, kinematically-consistent expert demonstrations from otherwise unstable non-differentiable expert-generation objectives
claims.direction: favors offline noise-injection curricula as a substitute for interactive-expert-based covariate-shift correction (e.g., DAgger) when an interactive expert is unavailable
claims.conditions: simulation, hyper-redundant robot path-following

title: JEPA-VLA: Video Predictive Embedding is Needed for VLA Models

claims.claim: An in-depth analysis finds that commonly used VLA visual representations -- whether pretrained via language-image contrastive learning (e.g., CLIP/SigLIP-style) or image-based self-supervised learning (e.g., DINOv2/MAE-style) -- remain inadequate at capturing task-relevant environment information and at inducing effective policy priors (anticipatory knowledge of how the environment evolves under successful execution); predictive embeddings pretrained on video (specifically V-JEPA 2) instead flexibly discard unpredictable environment factors and encode task-relevant temporal dynamics, and adaptively integrating these into existing VLAs yields substantial performance gains across LIBERO, LIBERO-plus, RoboTwin2.0, and real-robot tasks
claims.direction: favors video-predictive (JEPA-style) visual pretraining over standard contrastive-image-language or image-only self-supervised pretraining for VLA vision encoders
claims.conditions: LIBERO, LIBERO-plus, RoboTwin2.0 simulation benchmarks and real-robot tasks

why_deep_read: A direct, explicit comparison of visual-pretraining paradigms (contrastive image-language vs. image self-supervised vs. video-predictive/JEPA) for the VLA vision encoder -- exactly our Q03 decision -- with a clear directional finding (video-predictive wins) validated on real robots; worth reading for the specific mechanism and whether it is adoptable with a small/frozen encoder on our compute budget.

title: Dexterous Point Policy: Learning Point-based Dexterous Hand Policies from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Learning policies directly from human videos via a unified 3D keypoint representation (wrist and fingertips align closely between human and robot behavior, bridging embodiments) requires zero robot demonstrations; on real-robot pick-and-place and tool-use tasks it attains 75.0% success, whereas a state-of-the-art VLA baseline (presumably fine-tuned with some robot data) reaches only 1.0%
claims.direction: strongly favors keypoint-based human-video policy transfer with zero robot demonstrations over a standard VLA baseline, for this class of tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks spanning pick-and-place and tool use

claims.claim: Generalizes strongly to unseen scenarios, including multi-object environments and novel object categories
claims.direction: supports keypoint-based (rather than pixel-based) representations for generalizing to novel objects/scenes
claims.conditions: real-robot generalization tests

title: An Empirical Study on Stage-Information Interfaces for VLA Fine-Tuning
