claims.claim: Comparing full-task-instruction, current-stage-text, and normalized-ordinal-stage-index interfaces on GR00T N1.6/LIBERO-10: under direct fine-tuning, explicit stage information does NOT automatically improve the policy (full-task instruction 57.45% > ordinal-stage-state 54.36% > current-stage-text 50.24%); under continuation fine-tuning from a full-task-instruction baseline, ordinal-stage-state exceeds both alternatives in all three paired runs (53.75% vs 50.00%/49.07%)
claims.direction: contradicts the common assumption that adding explicit stage/subtask information to VLA conditioning reliably helps; benefit depends heavily on how the stage information is represented (text vs. ordinal index) and on the training regime (direct vs. continuation fine-tuning)
claims.conditions: GR00T N1.6 backbone, LIBERO-10 benchmark

title: ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning

claims.claim: A lightweight (0.7kg), low-cost (~$550) visual-haptic teleoperation system with vibrotactile finger feedback improves demonstration-collection success rates across all six tested contact-critical tasks (+2.2 to +15.6 percentage points) versus without haptic feedback, in a 9-participant user study, and downstream visual-tactile policies trained on the collected demonstrations show tactile cues benefit contact-critical subtasks (peg-in-hole: +17 percentage points over vision-only)
claims.direction: favors adding low-cost haptic/vibrotactile feedback to teleoperation hardware to improve demonstration quality/success rate, even without expensive haptic devices
claims.conditions: real and simulated environments, 9-participant matched with/without-haptic user study

title: MachEmbodied-U0: Unified Understanding and Generation Model for Embodied Intelligence

claims.claim: Jointly predicting future RGB, depth, surface normals, and optical flow (visual dynamics providing complementary supervision for appearance, geometry, and motion), guided by subtask prediction and affordance grounding, via flow matching within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture, achieves 99.0%/82.5% average success on LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus and demonstrates zero-shot subtask prediction, affordance grounding, and visual-dynamics prediction on tasks without corresponding downstream supervision
claims.direction: favors jointly predicting multiple complementary visual-dynamics modalities (depth, normals, optical flow, not just RGB) as an auxiliary objective, guided by subtask/affordance structure, over RGB-only future prediction
claims.conditions: simulation (LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboDojo) and real-world robotic manipulation; pretrained on ~4,200 hours of curated demonstrations

claims.claim: Multi-Rate Rotary Position Encoding (MRPE) aligns these visual-dynamics predictions (including depth and normals) with fine-grained control at the appropriate temporal rate
claims.direction: supports incorporating depth/geometric prediction targets (not just RGB) with rate-aware positional encoding for fine-grained action generation
claims.conditions: same as above

title: DeeR-VLA: Dynamic Inference of Multimodal Large Language Models for Efficient Robot Execution

claims.claim: A Dynamic Early-Exit framework that automatically adjusts the size of the activated MLLM per situation (via a multi-exit architecture, terminating processing once a sufficient model size has been activated), with early-termination criteria conditioned on predefined resource demands (average compute/power, peak compute/latency, GPU memory), reduces LLM computational cost by 5.2-6.5x and GPU memory by 2-6x on the CALVIN benchmark without compromising performance
claims.direction: strongly favors dynamic, situation-dependent model-size activation over always running the full (largest) MLLM for every inference step, when compute/memory/latency budgets are constrained
claims.conditions: CALVIN robot manipulation benchmark

claims.claim: The same underlying large MLLM can be run at effectively varying capacity per-step depending on situational difficulty, rather than requiring a single fixed (large) model size for all situations
claims.direction: supports adaptive/conditional model-size use as an alternative to committing to one fixed (small or large) model size throughout deployment
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Reports large, well-validated reductions (5.2-6.5x compute, 2-6x GPU memory) with no performance loss via dynamic early-exit -- directly and concretely actionable for our RTX 5060 8GB laptop GPU inference-latency problem, and a well-established (146-citation) result worth understanding in full for implementation details.

title: DEAR: Disentangled Environment and Agent Representations for Reinforcement Learning without Reconstruction

claims.claim: Using the agent's own segmentation mask as supervision to learn disentangled environment/agent visual representations (via feature-separation constraints, without any pixel reconstruction) as an auxiliary loss surpasses state-of-the-art visual-RL representation methods in sample efficiency, with comparable or superior performance at reduced parameter count
claims.direction: favors disentangling agent-self representation from environment representation (using cheap self-segmentation supervision, no reconstruction) over monolithic entangled visual representations, for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: Distracting DeepMind Control Suite and Franka Kitchen manipulation benchmarks (RL setting)

title: Graph-Fused Vision-Language-Action for Policy Reasoning in Multi-Arm Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Extracting task-relevant hand-object/object-object interaction cues from RGB-D human demonstrations into temporally-ordered scene graphs, then fusing these with a language-conditioned transformer to produce hierarchical behavior trees and interpretable motion primitives, achieves over 95% graph accuracy, 93% subtask segmentation accuracy, and on a real dual-arm robot 94% grasp reliability / 89% placement accuracy / 90% overall task success across assembly tasks
claims.direction: favors structured scene-graph-plus-language conditioning (interpretable intermediate representation) over direct low-level trajectory replication for generalizing from human video demonstrations
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, four block-assembly benchmark tasks

title: HiF-VLA: Hindsight, Insight and Foresight through Motion Representation for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Using motion (inter-state change, filtering static pixel-level noise) rather than raw pixels as the world-model representation, with hindsight priors encoding past dynamics and foresight reasoning anticipating future motion integrated via a hindsight-modulated joint expert (a 'think-while-acting' paradigm), surpasses strong baselines on LIBERO-Long and CALVIN ABC-D and achieves substantial improvements in real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors motion-centric (not pixel-centric) bidirectional (hindsight+foresight) world modeling over standard Markov-property VLA baselines that use only the current observation, for long-horizon coherence
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Long, CALVIN ABC-D simulation, plus real-world long-horizon manipulation

claims.claim: Achieves these long-horizon coherence gains while incurring negligible additional inference latency
claims.direction: supports that motion-centric bidirectional world modeling can improve long-horizon performance essentially 'for free' in terms of inference latency
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Dexterous Manipulation Policies from RGB Human Videos via 3D Hand-Object Trajectory Reconstruction (VIDEOMANIP)

claims.claim: A device-free framework reconstructs explicit 3D robot-object trajectories from monocular RGB human videos (no wearables or specialized capture hardware) and synthesizes diverse training trajectories from a single video via hand-object contact optimization, enabling generalizable policy learning without additional robot demonstrations; achieves 62.86% average real-world success across seven tasks, outperforming retargeting-based methods by 15.87 percentage points
claims.direction: favors device-free monocular-RGB human-video-based demonstration synthesis over specialized-hardware-based retargeting methods for reducing robot-demonstration collection burden
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, 7 tasks, plus simulation (20 objects)

title: WorkBenchMark: A LEGO-Based Assembly Benchmark with an Assembly-by-Disassembly Baseline for the Smart Manufacturing League

claims.claim: On a new 400-task LEGO-assembly benchmark combining low-level manipulation with task-level symbolic reasoning, a planning-based, open-vocabulary-perception 'Assembly-by-Disassembly' baseline outperforms a modern vision-language-action approach across all four complexity tiers
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that end-to-end VLA approaches are always superior to structured planning-based pipelines, at least for symbolic, constraint-heavy assembly tasks
claims.conditions: LEGO Duplo-based assembly benchmark, 400 tasks across 4 complexity tiers

title: RoboStereo: Dual-Tower 4D Embodied World Models for Unified Policy Optimization

claims.claim: A symmetric dual-tower 4D world model with bidirectional cross-modal enhancement (reducing geometric hallucinations/physics inconsistencies common in single-tower world models) underlies a unified policy-optimization framework combining test-time pre-execution verification, imitative-evolutionary learning from expert demonstrations with visual perceptual rewards, and autonomous open-exploration skill discovery; this delivers over 97% average relative improvement on fine-grained manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors a higher-fidelity, hallucination-resistant (dual-tower, bidirectional) world model combined with a unified imitation+exploration+verification optimization framework, over single-tower world models or imitation learning alone
claims.conditions: fine-grained manipulation tasks (benchmark/setting not further specified in abstract)

title: Libra-VLA: Achieving Learning Equilibrium via Asynchronous Coarse-to-Fine Dual-System

claims.claim: Explicitly decoupling action generation into a coarse discrete macro-directional 'Semantic Planner' and a continuous micro-pose-alignment 'Action Refiner' (Hybrid Action Space, asynchronously executed) reduces the semantic-actuation gap versus a monolithic flat mapping from visual-linguistic features directly to high-frequency motor commands
claims.direction: favors hierarchical, hybrid discrete-plus-continuous action decomposition (with asynchronous execution) over a single monolithic continuous action-generation module
claims.conditions: general open-world manipulation setting

claims.claim: Empirical analysis shows performance follows an inverted-U curve relative to action-decomposition granularity, peaking exactly when learning difficulty is balanced between the coarse and fine sub-systems -- i.e., more decomposition is not always better
claims.direction: identifies an optimal, intermediate level of macro/micro action-space decomposition granularity, cautioning against both too little and too much decomposition
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Multisensory Continual Learning: Adapting Pretrained Visuomotor Policies to Force

claims.claim: A MultiSensory World Model (MuSe) incorporates a limited amount of new-modality (force-torque) data into an already-pretrained vision-only policy via multi-stage fusion, multisensory future prediction, and experience replay over original pretraining data, performing strongly on new contact-rich finetuning tasks while preserving (and sometimes improving) performance on the original vision-only pretraining tasks
claims.direction: favors continual multisensory adaptation (adding a new sensor modality post-hoc via replay + future-prediction fusion) over pretraining with every possible sensor modality from scratch, when only limited multisensory data is available
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, force-torque sensing added to a pretrained vision-only policy

title: SelfWAM: A Self-Grounded Unified World Action Model for Fast Robot Control

claims.claim: Jointly predicting actions, action-conditioned future RGB frames, and robot self-masks (grounding future prediction specifically in the robot's own visible body and action-induced motion, rather than generic task progression) via a modality-specialized Mixture-of-Transformers, with future visual queries attending to a clean copy of the demonstrated action, produces more action-sensitive future predictions and improves policy performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors grounding future-prediction auxiliary objectives explicitly in the robot's own action-induced visual changes (via self-mask supervision) over generic future-frame prediction that may capture task progression unrelated to the specific action taken
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Leaves the fast action-only inference path unchanged, so the auxiliary future/self-mask prediction does not add inference-time latency
claims.direction: supports that this style of grounded auxiliary future-prediction objective can be added without inference-time latency cost
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Learning Foresight without Explicit Trajectories for 3D Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Movement Trend Guidance learns a compact latent representation of interaction evolution from a short observation history, supervised during training by sparse future gripper states (no explicit trajectory/plan), retaining only this latent as future-oriented conditioning at inference (via global conditioning plus a gated FiLM branch at the UNet bottleneck); added to DP3 with only 3.52% more parameters, it consistently improves performance: 62.8% vs 56.1% on 50-task RoboTwin2.0 mixed training, 71.93% vs 37.08% on LIBERO-40, and 72.0% vs 49.0% on five real-robot tasks
claims.direction: strongly favors adding a minimal-parameter, sparse-future-state-supervised foresight/auxiliary latent to a 3D diffusion policy over the base diffusion policy without such foresight conditioning
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2.0 (50 tasks), LIBERO-40, and 5 real-robot tasks; built on the DP3 (3D diffusion policy) architecture, dense-action/receding-horizon formulation preserved

claims.claim: The foresight mechanism adds only 3.52% additional parameters to the base DP3 model
claims.direction: demonstrates a near-negligible parameter/compute cost for a substantial performance gain, relevant for compute-constrained deployments
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: An almost free (3.52% extra parameters) auxiliary foresight objective added to a small, common 3D diffusion policy (DP3) yields large real-robot gains (72.0% vs 49.0%, a 23-point jump) -- a very low-risk, high-reward candidate technique for our own compute-constrained SmolVLA/diffusion-style action head, directly matching Q09's 'future prediction' example.

title: Seg-CURL: Segmented Contrastive Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real in Visual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Segmentation-based canonical domain (U-Net) plus contrastive RL used as sim-to-real augmentation strategy; U-Nets fine-tuned with only 20 real images
claims.direction: favors semantic-segmentation/canonicalization as augmentation over raw RGB transfer
claims.conditions: sim RL trained, real Baxter robot, cube lifting, zero-shot transfer

claims.claim: Framework reported robust to texture, lighting, shadow, and camera position gap; 16/20 success rate zero-shot on real robot
claims.direction: favors segmentation-based domain canonicalization for robustness to lighting/camera shift
claims.conditions: real Baxter robot, single task, zero-shot sim-to-real

title: Sim-to-real via latent prediction: Transferring visual non-prehensile manipulation policies

claims.claim: Decoupled feature extractor (trained with latent-space dynamics model constraint) can be independently fine-tuned on real data without retraining the control policy
claims.direction: favors decoupling/fine-tuning vision encoder separately from policy for sim-to-real adaptation
claims.conditions: RL (SAC) sim-to-real, table-top pushing task

claims.claim: Method adapts to considerable variation in viewpoint, colors, and lighting using only real data to adapt the feature extractor (not the policy)
claims.direction: favors feature-extractor-only adaptation for robustness to lighting/viewpoint change
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, non-prehensile pushing

title: Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation with ControlNeXt-Conditioned Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Prior action sequences incorporated into diffusion policy via ControlNeXt-style lightweight conditioning to explicitly enforce temporal consistency between chunks, addressing temporal inconsistency in action generation
claims.direction: favors conditioning on prior action chunk to reduce chunk-boundary discontinuity
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks Adroit and MetaWorld, diffusion policy architecture

claims.claim: Lightweight convolutional modulation branch (vs deep/redundant conditioning networks) reduces computational overhead of diffusion policy while improving time efficiency
claims.direction: favors lightweight conditioning branch over heavier diffusion conditioning for latency
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks, 3D tasks noted as high-cost

claims.claim: Outperforms prior diffusion-based imitation learning approaches in task success rate and time efficiency on Adroit/MetaWorld
claims.direction: favors improved diffusion policy design over standard diffusion policy baselines
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks only

why_deep_read: Directly targets our observed jerky-motion-at-chunk-boundary failure via an architectural fix (ControlNeXt conditioning for temporal consistency); full ablations would clarify if this transfers to real low-cost-arm chunked diffusion policies.

title: Time-Unified Diffusion Policy with Action Discrimination for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Time-unified velocity field (single denoising process instead of time-varying) reduces policy-learning difficulty and speeds up action generation; larger success-rate gains appear specifically when using fewer denoising iterations
claims.direction: favors time-unified/simplified denoising schedule for faster, more accurate diffusion-policy inference
claims.conditions: RLBench sim benchmark, multi-view (82.6%) and single-view (83.8%) success rates; also tested on real-world tasks (unspecified numbers)

claims.claim: Action-wise training with an action-discrimination branch improves denoising accuracy relative to standard diffusion policies, achieving state-of-the-art RLBench results
claims.direction: favors adding action-discrimination auxiliary signal to diffusion policy training
claims.conditions: RLBench sim, real-world tasks mentioned qualitatively

title: Dense Policy: Bidirectional Autoregressive Learning of Actions

claims.claim: A bidirectionally-expanded, coarse-to-fine autoregressive action-prediction scheme (lightweight encoder-only) surpasses existing holistic generative (e.g., diffusion) policies
claims.direction: favors autoregressive coarse-to-fine action generation over holistic diffusion/generative action heads
claims.conditions: not specified in abstract (benchmark/robot details omitted); claims logarithmic-time inference

title: Coordinated Humanoid Manipulation with Choice Policies

claims.claim: Choice Policy (generate multiple candidate actions + score/select) significantly outperforms diffusion policies and standard behavior cloning on two real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors generate-and-score multimodal action head over diffusion policy and plain BC
claims.conditions: real humanoid robot, dishwasher loading and whole-body whiteboard wiping tasks

claims.claim: Hand-eye coordination (submodule of teleop/architecture) reported critical for success in long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit hand-eye/camera coordination modeling
claims.conditions: real humanoid, long-horizon loco-manipulation

title: Mem-World: Memory-Augmented Action-Conditioned World Models for Persistent Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Surfel-indexed geometry-aware memory retrieval of history frames improves persistence of world-model rollouts under occlusion/rapid wrist-camera motion versus baseline (Ctrl-World)
claims.direction: favors explicit geometry-anchored memory of observation history for wrist-camera manipulation
claims.conditions: sim/world-model rollouts, wrist-camera occlusion scenario

claims.claim: Action-conditioned world model used for policy evaluation (14.5% better Pearson correlation with real-world performance than Ctrl-World) and synthetic data generation raising success from 58% to 72% on long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors world-model auxiliary objective/synthetic-data generation for long-horizon policy improvement
claims.conditions: long-horizon manipulation, synthetic data augmentation via world model

title: HeRO: Hierarchical 3D Semantic Representation for Pose-aware Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing DINOv2 geometry-sensitive features with Stable Diffusion semantic correspondences yields dense features that improve pose-aware manipulation performance
claims.direction: favors combining DINOv2 with diffusion-model features over either alone for fine-grained pose tasks
claims.conditions: sim/real not specified explicitly; diffusion-based policy

claims.claim: Hierarchical-conditioning diffusion policy improves success on 'Place Dual Shoes' by 12.3% and averages 6.5% gains across six pose-aware tasks vs baseline
claims.direction: favors hierarchical semantic conditioning added to diffusion policy
claims.conditions: six pose-aware manipulation tasks

title: MicroHookACT: Monocular Microscopic Vision Guided Visuomotor Policy for Flexible Microelectrode Hooking

claims.claim: Visuomotor policy trained on only 60 human demonstrations achieved 96.7% success rate across five varying-difficulty setups on real hardware
claims.direction: supports that ~60 demos can suffice for a narrow real-robot task with a well-designed policy
claims.conditions: real robot, single-camera (monocular microscopic), ACT-based policy, contact-rich precision task

claims.claim: A frozen ViT backbone with an action-supervised attention module learns to focus on task-relevant regions (needle tip/loop) directly from demonstrations without manual visual annotation
claims.direction: favors frozen pretrained ViT + learned attention over trainable/annotated visual features
claims.conditions: real robot, single monocular camera, 60 demos

claims.claim: Single ACT (action-chunking transformer) policy with dynamically weighted coarse/fine attention adapts to changing visual conditions (defocus blur) throughout the task
claims.direction: favors ACT-style chunked policy with attention reweighting for varying visual conditions
claims.conditions: real robot, monocular vision, precision manipulation

title: Zero-Shot Transfer of Haptics-Based Object Insertion Policies

claims.claim: Investigated memory representation and time-delay modeling as necessary factors for successful zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of a contact-rich policy
claims.direction: favors explicit memory/history and delay modeling for contact-rich policies
claims.conditions: sim-trained, real robot zero-shot, plate-loading task

claims.claim: Domain randomization identified as a necessary factor (alongside memory and delay modeling) for zero-shot transfer without any real-world fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors domain randomization for zero-shot sim-to-real generalization
claims.conditions: sim-to-real, real robot, no fine-tuning

claims.claim: Policy generalizes zero-shot to objects of different sizes/weights (cups, plates) and significantly outperforms heuristic and learned baselines
claims.direction: favors the combined recipe (memory+delay+domain randomization) for object-generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-rich insertion task

title: Language-Driven Representation Learning for Robotics

claims.claim: Controlled comparison across five robot-learning problems shows masked-autoencoding representations capture low-level spatial features but lose high-level semantics, while contrastive learning captures the opposite; existing representations give inconsistent results across tasks
claims.direction: neither pure MAE nor pure contrastive pretraining is uniformly best; trade-off exists
claims.conditions: controlled experiments across grasp affordance, language-conditioned IL, intent scoring, and other robot-learning problems (video+caption pretraining)

claims.claim: Voltron (language-conditioned visual reconstruction + visually-grounded language generation) outperforms prior state-of-the-art visual representations, especially on tasks requiring higher-level (language-related) features
claims.direction: favors language-conditioned pretraining objective for representations used in language-conditioned imitation learning
claims.conditions: controlled evaluation suite, five distinct robot-learning problems

why_deep_read: Controlled, multi-task comparison of visual pretraining objectives (MAE vs contrastive vs language-driven) directly informs Q03 vision-encoder choice and Q08 language conditioning; full paper's evaluation suite/tables would clarify which pretraining best suits a small language-conditioned policy.

title: DiffClone: Enhanced Behaviour Cloning in Robotics with Diffusion-Driven Policy Learning

claims.claim: Among pretrained visual representations tested, MOCO fine-tuned ResNet50 performed best compared to other fine-tuned representations for offline-to-online BC transfer
claims.direction: favors contrastive (MOCO) pretraining fine-tuned on ResNet50 over alternatives tested
claims.conditions: TOTO benchmark, real online physical robot testing, offline demo dataset

claims.claim: Diffusion-based behavior cloning agent (DiffClone) with goal-state conditioning gave only a minute increase in success rate/mean reward over base BC
claims.direction: suggests diffusion policy + goal conditioning gives marginal gains in this benchmark
claims.conditions: TOTO benchmark, real robot test-time evaluation

title: Motion Tracks: A Unified Representation for Human-Robot Transfer in Few-Shot Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Representing actions as short-horizon 2D motion tracks (image-space trajectories) instead of standard action vectors achieves 86.5% average success across 4 real-world tasks, outperforming SOTA IL baselines that don't use this action space by 40%
claims.direction: favors motion-track (image-space trajectory) action representation over standard action-vector policies
claims.conditions: real robot, 4 real-world tasks, minutes of human video + limited robot demos

claims.claim: Policy trained with just minutes of human video plus limited additional robot demonstrations reaches high success, generalizing to scenarios seen only in human videos
claims.direction: favors leveraging human video data to reduce required robot teleop demo count
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment human-video + few robot demos

claims.claim: Two camera views used at test time to recover 6DoF trajectories via multi-view synthesis from predicted 2D motion tracks
claims.direction: favors multi-view camera setup to recover full 6DoF action from 2D track representation
claims.conditions: real-world multi-view test-time inference

why_deep_read: Directly tackles low-demo few-shot IL with an unconventional but simple action representation (2D motion tracks) that beats SOTA baselines by a large, quantified margin (40%) on real robots — worth reading full ablations to see if it applies to our single-camera low-cost SO-101 setup and whether 2-camera 6DoF recovery generalizes to 1 fixed+1 wrist camera.

title: Best of Sim and Real: Decoupled Visuomotor Manipulation via Learning Control in Simulation and Perception in Real

claims.claim: Achieves strong performance with only 10-20 real demonstrations by decoupling perception (learned/adapted in real) from control (trained in sim with privileged state)
claims.direction: favors decoupled sim-control/real-perception architecture to drastically cut required real demo count
claims.conditions: real robot tabletop manipulation tasks, 10-20 real demos

claims.claim: Perception module is adapted only at deployment/real data while control policy stays frozen (trained in sim); demonstrates superior data efficiency vs end-to-end baselines
claims.direction: favors decoupling perception adaptation from control policy training for sim-to-real
claims.conditions: tabletop manipulation, real robot

claims.claim: Learned policies handle object positions and scales beyond the training distribution, confirming decoupling improves out-of-distribution generalization vs end-to-end baselines
claims.direction: favors decoupled perception/control for OOD (position/scale) generalization
claims.conditions: real robot tabletop tasks

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our low-demo (50-100), single-fixed+wrist-camera setup: quantifies real-demo count (10-20) needed when perception and control are decoupled, and reports OOD generalization gains — worth checking full method/ablations to see if applicable to our SO-101 pipeline without privileged sim state.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Discrete-Time Gaussian Process Mixtures for Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: MiDiGaP enables learning from as few as five demonstrations using only camera observations and generalizes across long-horizon, highly-constrained, dynamic, and multimodal tasks
claims.direction: favors GP-mixture policy representation for extreme low-data (5-demo) regimes over deep-net action heads
claims.conditions: few-shot manipulation benchmarks, camera-only observations, CPU training <1 min

claims.claim: On constrained RLBench tasks improves policy success by 76 percentage points and reduces trajectory cost by 67%; on multimodal tasks improves success by 48 percentage points with 7x better sample efficiency; more than doubles success in cross-embodiment transfer, vs unspecified baselines
claims.direction: favors discrete-time GP mixture action representation over baseline policies for multimodal/few-shot manipulation
claims.conditions: RLBench and other few-shot benchmarks, evaluated against baseline imitation-learning methods (not necessarily against diffusion/VLA specifically)

why_deep_read: Reports SOTA few-shot (5-demo) performance and strong multimodal handling using camera-only observations and near-zero training cost (CPU, <1 min) — directly relevant to our extreme low-data regime (50-100 demos) and laptop-GPU compute constraint; worth checking whether GP-mixture action head is a viable, lightweight alternative to diffusion/VLA heads for our setup.

title: X-Distill: Cross-Architecture Vision Distillation for Visuomotor Learning

claims.claim: Distilling a frozen pretrained DINOv2 teacher into a compact ResNet-18 student (on ImageNet), then jointly fine-tuning with a diffusion policy head, consistently outperforms policies using from-scratch ResNet or fine-tuned DINOv2 encoders across 34 simulated tasks (3 benchmarks) and 5 real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors compact CNN distilled from a large ViT teacher over both from-scratch CNN and directly fine-tuned large ViT encoders
claims.conditions: 34 sim tasks/3 benchmarks + 5 real-world tasks, diffusion policy head, low-data setting emphasized

claims.claim: The distilled compact-CNN approach also surpasses 3D encoders that use privileged point-cloud observations
claims.direction: favors 2D RGB + distilled compact encoder over 3D point-cloud encoders
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

claims.claim: Approach surpasses much larger Vision-Language Models used as encoders, highlighting efficacy for low-data, data-efficient robotic manipulation with a small model
claims.direction: favors small distilled encoder over large VLM encoders for data-efficient manipulation
claims.conditions: low-data robotic manipulation setting

why_deep_read: Directly answers our Q03/Q04/Q12 questions simultaneously (which vision pretraining, RGB vs point cloud, small vs large models) under an explicitly low-data, compute-constrained framing that matches our laptop-GPU/8GB VRAM SO-101 setup; the ablation details (distillation recipe, benchmark breakdown) would materially inform our vision-encoder decision.

title: Imitation from Heterogeneous Demonstrations using Grounded Latent-Action World Models

claims.claim: GLAM-aligned BC policies significantly outperform BC baselines and prior latent-action methods, achieving an average of +48% improvement in task success rate in a data-scarce setting, across five manipulation tasks in sim and real
claims.direction: favors grounding heterogeneous (cross-source, some action-label-free) demonstrations in a shared predictive latent-action space to improve data efficiency
claims.conditions: 5 manipulation tasks, sim+real, data-scarce setting, heterogeneous demo sources with/without action labels

claims.claim: A generative world model with a latent action space grounded by predicting future observations is used as the mechanism enabling heterogeneous-data co-training
claims.direction: favors future-prediction/world-model auxiliary objective for aligning action representations across data sources
claims.conditions: paired generative models, shared latent action space

title: Temporally Centered SIGReg Improves LeWorldModel Representations for Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Standard (Raw) LeWorldModel objective biases variance allocation toward temporally-persistent latent components, suppressing residual variance needed to decode robot/gripper dynamics important for manipulation; applying the regularizer (SIGReg) to temporally-centered residuals instead fixes this
claims.direction: favors applying representation-learning regularization to temporal residuals rather than whole latent for world-model-based policy representations
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, pixel-based world model pretraining

claims.claim: On LIBERO, the fix improves downstream policy success on the Goal suite by 1.66x and raises average success across all suites from 63.6% to 83.8%, outperforming both Diffusion Policy trained from scratch and pretrained OpenVLA, without external pretraining
claims.direction: favors this self-supervised world-model representation over from-scratch diffusion policy and pretrained OpenVLA baseline
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark, no external pretraining used

title: VISTA: Visually Inferred Spatial ConTact Attention for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claims.claim: A Visual Deformation Field (3D displacement representation of a compliant gripper) used as visuo-physical feedback outperforms a strong pure-vision baseline (3D Diffusion Policy) and a tactile baseline on contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors vision-inferred 3D deformation/contact representation over both pure-vision 3D diffusion policy and dedicated tactile sensing
claims.conditions: real robot, Cross-Scale Object Grasping, Cap Unscrewing, Calligraphy Writing tasks; requires a compliant gripper

claims.claim: Deformation-Augmented Policy Network with incremental (delta) gripper actions enables precise closed-loop correction and substantial OOD generalization to unseen object scales
claims.direction: favors incremental/delta action correction conditioned on visual deformation feedback
claims.conditions: real robot, contact-rich fine manipulation, specialized compliant gripper hardware

title: Avi: Action from Volumetric Inference

claims.claim: Using 3D point clouds and language-grounded scene understanding with explicit geometric transforms (rather than training end-to-end on 2D-image action tokens) is proposed to enable action generation robust to occlusions, camera-pose variation, and viewpoint changes
claims.direction: favors 3D point-cloud-based reasoning over 2D end-to-end action-token policies for viewpoint/occlusion robustness
claims.conditions: preliminary results only (qualitative), no quantified benchmark numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Claims robustness to occlusions, camera pose variations, and viewpoint changes by construction (geometric reasoning rather than learned opaque policy)
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D geometric reasoning for camera/viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: preliminary, qualitative claim only

title: RoboAlign: Learning Test-Time Reasoning for Language-Action Alignment in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: RL-based alignment (sampling action tokens via zero-shot reasoning, refined with RL) applied after SFT to a diffusion action head on an MLLM backbone, using less than 1% of the data, improves performance by 17.5%, 18.9%, and 106.6% over SFT baselines on LIBERO, CALVIN, and real-world environments respectively
claims.direction: favors adding RL-based language-action alignment refinement on top of SFT diffusion-action-head VLA
claims.conditions: large MLLM backbone + diffusion action head, LIBERO/CALVIN sim benchmarks + real-world eval, <1% additional data for alignment stage

claims.claim: Prior VQA-style embodied-reasoning supervision for MLLM->VLA transfer was reported unstable, yielding only marginal or negative gains; RoboAlign's language-action alignment fixes this
claims.direction: cautions that naive language-conditioning/reasoning supervision can hurt VLA performance; targeted alignment needed
claims.conditions: MLLM-based VLA models

title: Cross-Embodiment Transfer Learning for Precise Robotic Manipulation via Abstract State Space

claims.claim: A world model (RSSM vs DreamerV3 variants compared) trained in a contrastively-learned abstract state space that removes platform-specific features enables 3-5x improvement in sample efficiency vs baseline methods, with strong zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: favors world-model auxiliary objective over an abstracted, platform-invariant state representation for sample-efficient policy learning
claims.conditions: Isaac Gym simulation, Franka/UR5/Baxter platforms, multi-step tasks (door opening, object stacking)

claims.claim: Systematic ablations of positive/negative sample ratio, encoder loss weight, and pre-training data configuration were used to identify what preserves task-relevant information while eliminating platform-specific features
claims.direction: provides ablation guidance on pretraining data/config choices for sample-efficient cross-embodiment transfer
claims.conditions: simulation only (Isaac Gym)

title: ProgVLA: Progress-Aware Robot Manipulation Skill Learning

claims.claim: A compact 0.1B-parameter VLA (ProgVLA) reaches success rates competitive with, and on long-horizon/harder task tiers exceeding, substantially larger pretrained baseline VLAs
claims.direction: favors small (0.1B) model with efficient context compression over larger pretrained VLA baselines, especially for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: two established multi-task manipulation benchmarks + real-world toy-kitchen validation

claims.claim: Auxiliary progress heads trained with offline-RL objectives (critics over normalized remaining-horizon targets) provide an internal task-progress estimate enabling advantage/success-weighted flow-matching IL; ablations show this gives a consistent additional gain concentrated on long-horizon and multi-object tasks
claims.direction: favors adding a progress-prediction auxiliary objective, especially for long-horizon/multi-object manipulation
claims.conditions: same benchmarks; ablation isolates progress-aware training contribution

claims.claim: A two-stage Perceiver resampling scheme compresses variable-length visual/language/proprioceptive streams into fixed-size context tokens; ablations indicate the context resampler and task-adaptive visual fine-tuning are the largest single contributors to performance
claims.direction: favors compressed fixed-size context-token representation of observation history for long multi-modal sequences under tight compute/memory budgets
claims.conditions: compute/memory-constrained VLA, real-world toy-kitchen environment

why_deep_read: A 0.1B-parameter VLA explicitly designed for tight compute/memory budgets that matches or beats larger baselines is directly on-point for our 8GB-laptop-GPU constraint; ablations isolate which components (context resampling vs progress-aware training) matter most, which would materially guide our own small-model architecture choice.

title: Adaptation of Generalist Robot Policies with Minimal Data

claims.claim: MiDAS recovers strong task performance starting from as little as ONE demonstration, by anchoring a pre-trained VLA via BC on single/few demos then improving with value-based online RL on a residual policy, substantially outperforming baselines on LIBERO and RoboCasa and generalizing beyond demonstrated conditions
claims.direction: favors single/few-demo BC anchoring + residual online RL over pure few-shot BC or pure RL from scratch
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboCasa sim benchmarks; also a real bimanual YAM platform

claims.claim: Improvement is achieved via a residual policy parameterization on top of a frozen pre-trained VLA (small additional residual head, not full model retraining); on the real YAM platform, a fragile low-success single-demo policy is made more robust after ~6 hours of online interaction
claims.direction: favors a lightweight residual policy head over full-model fine-tuning for adapting a generalist policy with minimal data
claims.conditions: real bimanual YAM robot, single demo starting point, ~6 hours online interaction

why_deep_read: Directly targets our core problem of adapting/improving a policy from very few demonstrations, including a real-robot case starting from a single demo; understanding the residual-RL recipe and how much online interaction/hardware setup it needs would materially inform whether a similar approach is feasible on our SO-101 with only teleop data and no autonomous RL infrastructure yet.

title: TaskAnchor: Grounding Task State in Reactive VLAs for Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Reactive VLAs suffer from 'task-state aliasing' (visually similar observations requiring different actions depending on stage/history); a lightweight adapter combining history-conditioned visual refinement with a milestone-supervised task-state coordinate achieves ~4.9-5.5x the average success rate of published pi_0.5 and X-VLA baselines on RMBench, with consistent gains on RoboMemArena and real robots
claims.direction: favors explicit task-state/history grounding (scalar execution-stage signal) over purely reactive VLA policies without memory of history
claims.conditions: RMBench, RoboMemArena, and real robots; added as adapter without modifying action-generation mechanism

claims.claim: The added latency of the task-state grounding adapter is only 2.08 ms per action chunk for pi_0.5
claims.direction: favors lightweight adapters for observation-history grounding since latency overhead is negligible
claims.conditions: pi_0.5 backbone, real-time chunk-based inference

why_deep_read: Directly addresses observation-history/causal-confusion (Q07) with a large, quantified real-robot success-rate improvement while adding negligible latency (Q10) — exactly the kind of low-overhead memory mechanism we'd want for our jerky, latency-constrained chunked policy; worth reading the adapter design in detail.

title: Object-centric 3D Motion Field for Robot Learning from Human Videos

claims.claim: An object-centric 3D motion field action representation (vs video frames, 2D pixelflow, or point-cloud flow) reduces 3D motion estimation error by over 50% compared to the latest prior method, and enables 55% average success in diverse real-world tasks where prior approaches achieve <=10%
claims.direction: favors 3D object-centric motion-field action representation over 2D pixelflow/point-cloud-flow representations for action extraction from video
claims.conditions: real-world robot evaluation, zero-shot control from human videos, noisy depth input

claims.claim: Extracting actions from human videos (rather than only robot teleop demos) with this representation supports cross-embodiment transfer and generalization to new backgrounds, even acquiring fine-grained skills like insertion
claims.direction: favors supplementing/replacing robot teleop demos with human video data using a 3D motion-field action representation
claims.conditions: real-world setups, zero-shot

why_deep_read: Reports a very large, quantified real-world success-rate gap (55% vs <=10%) tied specifically to the choice of 3D action representation extracted from video, directly relevant to Q04 (3D vs RGB representation) and to reducing teleop-demo burden (Q13); worth checking whether the depth/motion-field pipeline is feasible with our single RealSense + wrist camera setup.

title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity

claims.claim: A data-quality-aware training recipe (offline discriminator providing clip-level weights to down-weight low-quality/noisy teleoperated demonstrations during diffusion-transformer policy training) improves performance; ablations confirm the importance of real data and the discriminator for dexterity (average dexterous success 66.7% vs. 51.7% without)
claims.direction: favors weighting/filtering demonstration quality (vs. treating all teleop demos equally) during policy training
claims.conditions: high-DoF bimanual dual-hand real+sim teleoperated dataset (10K real episodes, 100K sim trajectories)

title: Route by Kinematics, Act by Observation: Kinematics-Supervised Expert Routing in MoE-Augmented VLA

claims.claim: Explicit kinematics-supervised expert routing (clustering action trajectories into kinematic archetypes to supervise a MoE router, using only visual-language observations at inference) outperforms both dense and MoE-featured VLA baselines by >23.26% on RoboTwin and >20.27% on an introduced low-cost DIYRobot platform
claims.direction: favors kinematics-supervised explicit MoE routing over dense or observation-only-routed MoE architectures
claims.conditions: RoboTwin sim benchmark and a real, sub-$2,000 3D-printed DIY robot platform (DIYRobot)

claims.claim: An economical (<$2,000) 3D-printed robot platform was built specifically to test cross-platform generalization of the policy architecture
claims.direction: supports evaluating architecture choices on genuinely low-cost hardware, not just expensive research arms
claims.conditions: real, low-cost custom-built robot

title: DexDiff: Towards Extrinsic Dexterity Manipulation of Ungraspable Objects in Unrestricted Environments

claims.claim: A goal-conditioned action diffusion (GCAD) model, conditioned on a VLM-generated high-level task plan as the goal, outperforms baselines by a 47% higher success rate in simulation and generalizes to unseen objects
claims.direction: favors diffusion action head conditioned on high-level VLM-derived goals over unconditioned diffusion/other baselines
claims.conditions: long-horizon extrinsic-dexterity tasks, simulation with real-world deployment demonstrated

claims.claim: High-level task planning from a VLM is used to condition low-level diffusion action generation (goal condition derived from language/vision reasoning)
claims.direction: favors hierarchical language/VLM-conditioned planning feeding a lower-level diffusion policy
claims.conditions: long-horizon manipulation with extrinsic dexterity

title: GEVRM: Goal-Expressive Video Generation Model For Robust Visual Manipulation

claims.claim: A closed-loop VLA integrating an internal-model-control (IMC) principle, using a text-guided video generation model for future visual planning goals plus contrastively-learned 'internal embeddings' to implicitly infer perturbations, achieves state-of-the-art performance on both standard and perturbed CALVIN benchmarks
claims.direction: favors adding a video-generation-based future-goal auxiliary objective plus explicit perturbation modeling for robustness
claims.conditions: CALVIN sim benchmark (standard + perturbed variants), also reports improvements on 'realistic robot tasks' (real-world, unspecified numbers)

claims.claim: Method explicitly targets robustness to external perturbations/unforeseen state information encountered during deployment, showing largest relative gains on the perturbed CALVIN benchmark
claims.direction: favors closed-loop, perturbation-aware VLA design for robustness under distribution shift
claims.conditions: CALVIN perturbed benchmark

title: Improving Generative Behavior Cloning via Self-Guidance and Adaptive Chunking

claims.claim: Standard open-loop diffusion-policy chunked execution (generate multi-step action chunks, execute without replanning) suffers from stochastic sampling errors and delayed responses; 'adaptive chunking' selectively updates action sequences only when reactivity benefits outweigh the need for temporal consistency, substantially improving performance across simulated and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors adaptive (variable) chunk re-planning over fixed open-loop chunk execution to reduce errors/discontinuities
claims.conditions: multiple simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, diffusion-policy-based generative BC

claims.claim: 'Self-guidance' improves action fidelity by leveraging past observations, implicitly promoting future-aware behavior on top of the diffusion policy
claims.direction: favors conditioning generation on past-observation history (self-guidance) to improve consistency
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

claims.claim: Open-loop chunked control is noted to suffer from delayed responses that degrade performance specifically in noisy or dynamic real-world environments; adaptive chunking is proposed as the fix
claims.direction: favors reactivity-aware chunk updating over fixed-horizon open-loop execution for latency/responsiveness in dynamic settings
claims.conditions: real-world dynamic/noisy manipulation tasks

why_deep_read: This is a near-exact match to our observed failure mode (jerky motion at chunk boundaries under async/open-loop chunked diffusion execution): it names the same open-loop delayed-response problem and proposes two concrete, real-world-validated fixes (self-guidance, adaptive chunking) directly applicable to our SmolVLA-style chunked policy.

title: Eye, Robot: Learning to Look to Act with a BC-RL Perception-Action Loop

claims.claim: A jointly-trained gaze (RL) + hand (BC) policy causes hand-eye coordination to emerge, with the active-gaze eye looking toward regions that let the hand complete the task, evaluated on five panoramic workspace manipulation tasks with a single (actuated, rotating) camera
claims.direction: favors active/movable camera viewpoint control jointly trained with the manipulation policy over a fixed camera, for large workspaces
claims.conditions: real robot, single actuated eyeball camera, five panoramic tasks

claims.claim: A foveal-inspired policy architecture (high resolution at small compute budget) leads to more stable fixation and improved ability to track objects and ignore distractors
claims.direction: favors foveal/high-resolution-at-low-compute visual processing for distractor robustness
claims.conditions: real robot, panoramic manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Foveal-inspired architecture achieves high resolution processing with a small compute budget
claims.direction: favors foveal sampling as a compute-efficient alternative to full-resolution processing for small models
claims.conditions: real robot

title: FailSafe: Reasoning and Recovery from Failures in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a VLM on auto-generated failure+recovery-action data (FailSafe-VLM) improves the performance of three state-of-the-art VLA models (Pi-0-FAST, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT) by up to 22.6% on average across several ManiSkill tasks by enabling failure detection and recovery
claims.direction: favors adding a failure-detection/recovery auxiliary module trained on synthetic failure data to improve robustness of existing VLA policies
claims.conditions: ManiSkill simulation, three different pretrained VLA backbones

claims.claim: FailSafe-VLM generalizes across different spatial configurations, camera viewpoints, objects, and robot embodiments
claims.direction: favors this failure-recovery approach for camera-viewpoint and object generalization
claims.conditions: simulation (ManiSkill), generalization claims

title: World-Env: Leveraging World Model as a Virtual Environment for VLA Post-Training

claims.claim: World-Env achieves notable performance gains with as few as five expert demonstrations per task by using a learned world model as a safe virtual simulator for RL post-training instead of requiring more real demonstrations or real-world RL interaction
claims.direction: favors RL post-training in a learned world-model simulator over collecting more real demonstrations, in extremely low-data (5-demo) regimes
claims.conditions: complex robotic manipulation tasks, RL post-training on top of IL-pretrained VLA

claims.claim: A physically-consistent world simulator (generating temporally consistent future visual observations) plus a VLM-guided reward/termination reflector enables safe policy exploration beyond the initial imitation-learning distribution without real-world interaction risk
claims.direction: favors world-model auxiliary/virtual-environment objective for post-training beyond the IL demo distribution
claims.conditions: resource-constrained, non-resettable real-world settings (e.g. industrial automation)

title: Resolving Ambiguous Language Instructions in Robotic Manipulation via Visually Grounded Vision-Languageaction Models

claims.claim: Fine-tuning a pretrained VLA on a real-world dataset of pointing-based manipulation demonstrations improves object-level grounding under linguistically ambiguous (deictic) instructions, with the manipulator more consistently approaching the intended target, while maintaining comparable behavior for explicit commands
claims.direction: favors fine-tuning with pointing-gesture demonstrations to resolve ambiguous language conditioning
claims.conditions: real-world dataset and evaluation, pretrained VLA fine-tuned

title: VQActFlow: Vector-Quantized Action Mode Steering for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Tokenizing continuous action chunks into a learned discrete VQ codebook, generated via Variational Flow Matching with an explicit, inference-time-steerable preference over action modes (classifier-free guidance + learned codebook critic), outperforms both continuous and discrete baselines on multi-task manipulation
claims.direction: favors VQ/discrete-token action representation with explicit mode-steering over standard continuous (e.g. diffusion) or naive discrete-token action heads, for multimodal multi-task demonstrations
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim, Unitree G1 humanoid whole-body pick-and-place, and ALOHA-style bimanual contact-rich real-world tasks

title: AffordVLA: Injecting Affordance Representations into Vision-Language-Action Models via Implicit Feature Alignment

claims.claim: Aligning intermediate VLA visual representations with a zero-shot affordance-teacher's task-conditioned affordance features (rather than relying on global object appearance) improves action accuracy and manipulation success while preserving inference efficiency
claims.direction: favors implicit affordance-feature alignment as an auxiliary visual-representation objective over relying on raw global visual features
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, ablations reported

claims.claim: Implicit representation alignment to an affordance teacher (rather than explicit mask injection or external perception modules) avoids added inference overhead while improving success rate and training efficiency
claims.direction: favors implicit auxiliary alignment objectives over explicit/external affordance modules for efficiency
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world

title: B-spline Policy: Accelerating Manipulation Policies via B-spline Action Representations

claims.claim: Parameterizing actions as continuous, time-continuous B-spline curves (knots + control points) instead of predicting discrete-time action chunks yields smooth trajectories that can be temporally scaled and executed at higher frequencies/speeds by low-level controllers
claims.direction: favors continuous B-spline action parameterization over discrete-time action-chunk prediction
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world manipulation tasks; integrates into standard policy-learning pipelines by predicting spline parameters directly

claims.claim: Standard discrete action-chunk prediction is contrasted with the smooth B-spline representation; BSP significantly reduces task completion time while maintaining strong success rates
claims.direction: favors smooth continuous trajectory representation over discrete chunking for both speed and success rate
claims.conditions: sim + real-world tasks

claims.claim: B-spline actions can be executed at higher frequencies and speeds by low-level controllers, directly reducing task completion time
claims.direction: favors continuous trajectory representations for faster, smoother real-time execution
claims.conditions: sim + real-world tasks

title: Foresight Without Seeing: Latent Futures for World Action Models

claims.claim: ForeWAM avoids iterative video denoising (the main inference-cost driver of 'explicit-future' world-action-models) by reusing key-value states from a single Video-DiT prefill pass, retaining predictive-dynamics benefits without decoding future videos at deployment time
claims.direction: favors a direct-policy world-action-model design (dynamics registers, no future video decoding) over explicit video-generation-based WAMs for lower inference latency
claims.conditions: LIBERO / LIBERO-Plus sim benchmarks, no embodied robot data pretraining

claims.claim: Dynamics registers supervised by a frozen latent-action teacher (during training only) let the model implicitly capture interaction-induced transitions (object motion, contact, task progress); standard and accelerated variants achieve 96.7%/96.9% success on LIBERO and 61.6% on LIBERO-Plus
claims.direction: favors latent (non-visual) future-dynamics auxiliary supervision during training, discarded at deployment, as an auxiliary objective
claims.conditions: LIBERO / LIBERO-Plus sim benchmarks

title: Fourier Controller Networks for Real-Time Decision-Making in Embodied Learning

claims.claim: FCNet uses Short-Time Fourier Transform to extract/encode time-varying trajectory features, enabling parallel training and efficient recurrent (sliding-DFT) inference for real-time decision-making, substantially more efficient than Transformer-based policies
claims.direction: favors frequency-domain (Fourier) sequence modeling over Transformer architectures for real-time, low-latency robot control
claims.conditions: simulated (D4RL) and real-world environments (e.g. robot locomotion)

claims.claim: Observation: energy density of a robot trajectory in the frequency domain is concentrated in the low-frequency part, motivating a compact frequency-domain model; FCNet outperforms Transformer across robotics datasets of all sizes tested (from 1.9M to 120M parameters)
claims.direction: favors compact frequency-domain architecture over Transformer across a wide range of model sizes, including small (~1.9M parameter) models
claims.conditions: multiple robotics datasets, varying dataset/model scale

claims.claim: FCNet models time-varying features (trajectory history) more data-efficiently than Transformer while retaining strong generalized low-level policy performance
claims.direction: favors Fourier-based temporal encoding over Transformer for representing observation/action history efficiently
claims.conditions: diverse robotics datasets

title: MResT: Multi-Resolution Sensing for Real-Time Control with Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Combining a large, off-the-shelf pretrained VLM operating on low-frequency global features with a small, non-pretrained model adapting to high-frequency local feedback (multi-temporal-resolution sensing) enables real-time control of precise and reactive tasks, improving over recent multi-task baselines by 2X on average across 3 domains (coarse, precise, dynamic manipulation)
claims.direction: favors a two-tier architecture (large slow pretrained model + small fast reactive model) over a single-resolution/single-network policy for real-time reactive control
claims.conditions: real experiments across 3 task domains (coarse, precise, dynamic manipulation)

claims.claim: Multi-spatial-resolution sensing (hierarchical information at different spatial scales) enables both coarse and precise motions within the same framework
claims.direction: favors combining multiple camera/sensing resolutions rather than a single fixed resolution
claims.conditions: real robot, language-conditioned multi-task policy

claims.claim: The approach generalizes well to visual and geometric variations in target objects and to varying interaction forces
claims.direction: favors the multi-resolution sensing architecture for robustness to visual/geometric variation
claims.conditions: real robot experiments

claims.claim: High-frequency reactive component uses a small, non-pretrained network (as opposed to relying entirely on the large pretrained VLM) to keep control frequency high
claims.direction: favors pairing a small dedicated reactive network with a large pretrained model rather than running the large model at high frequency
claims.conditions: real robot, laptop/edge-scale reactive component implied by 'small' network

why_deep_read: Directly proposes exactly the kind of architecture we may need: a small, fast, reactive component (feasible on our 8GB laptop GPU) paired with slower higher-level guidance, validated on real robots across coarse/precise/dynamic tasks with quantified 2x gains and demonstrated robustness to visual/geometric variation and force differences — highly actionable for our latency (Q10), camera (Q11), and robustness (Q14) concerns simultaneously.

title: Kinematics-Aware Diffusion Policy With Consistent 3D Observation and Action Space for Whole-Arm Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Representing both robot state and actions as 3D points on the arm body (rather than joint-space actions) naturally aligns with 3D point-cloud observations and avoids the non-linear joint-space/task-space misalignment that makes generalization hard to learn from limited demos
claims.direction: favors 3D/task-space-consistent action representation over raw joint-space action prediction, especially in low-demo settings
claims.conditions: whole-arm manipulation, diffusion-policy backbone, sim + real-world

claims.claim: Spatially consistent 3D representation (points aligned with point-cloud observations) improves sample efficiency and spatial generalizability compared to existing (presumably RGB/joint-space) methods
claims.direction: favors 3D point-based observation/action representation over 2D/RGB or pure joint-space approaches
claims.conditions: sim + real-world whole-arm manipulation experiments

claims.claim: Incorporating kinematics priors into the diffusion process guarantees kinematic feasibility of output actions, with joint commands computed via an optimization-based whole-arm IK solver at execution time
claims.direction: favors adding explicit kinematic-feasibility priors/constraints to a diffusion action head
claims.conditions: whole-arm manipulation with collision-avoidance/body-object interaction requirements

title: AVA-VLA: Improving Vision-Language-Action models with Active Visual Attention

claims.claim: Reformulating VLA policy learning from a POMDP perspective (conditioning action generation on a recurrent belief state over task history, rather than treating each timestep independently/history-agnostic) achieves state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO and CALVIN and transfers effectively to real-world dual-arm manipulation
claims.direction: favors explicit recurrent history/belief-state conditioning over history-agnostic (per-timestep) VLA policies
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN sim benchmarks, real-world dual-arm manipulation transfer

claims.claim: Active Visual Attention (AVA) dynamically reweights visual tokens in the current observation based on instruction and execution history to focus on task-relevant regions
claims.direction: favors dynamic, history-conditioned visual-token reweighting over static/uniform visual attention in the policy backbone
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: PRISM: Personalized Robotic Dataset Generation via Image-based Scene and Motion Synthesis

claims.claim: Generating personalized training data via 'digital cousin' scenes (semantically/geometrically aligned with the target user environment but instance-diverse), synthesized from a single image + language instruction without human teleoperation, outperforms baseline-generated datasets on LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus
claims.direction: favors image-conditioned synthetic scene/motion generation (digital-cousin augmentation) over generic simulation-based or teleoperated data for target-environment adaptation
claims.conditions: LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus sim + 3 real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Policies trained on this synthetically generated, personalized dataset achieve up to 100% success rate on three real-world manipulation tasks and maintain stronger performance when evaluated in environments differing from training, without requiring costly human teleoperation for the target environment
claims.direction: favors synthetic personalized data generation to reduce/replace real teleoperation demo collection for a specific target setup
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, evaluated in both matched and mismatched (novel) environments

title: MEM: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory for Vision Language Action Models

claims.claim: Combining video-based short-horizon memory (compressed via a video encoder, compensating for occlusions) with text-based long-horizon memory (abstracted semantic/stage concepts) enables robot policies to perform tasks spanning up to fifteen minutes and to intelligently adapt manipulation strategies in-context, outperforming policies that only feed a raw sequence of past observations
claims.direction: favors a mixed-modal (video + text), multi-granularity memory architecture over feeding a plain sequence of past observations into the policy
claims.conditions: long-horizon multi-stage real-world tasks (e.g., cooking, kitchen cleanup)

title: EmbodiedGen V2: An Agentic, Simulation-Ready 3D World Engine for Embodied AI

claims.claim: Online RL in generated simulation environments improved simulation success from 9.7% to 79.8%, and this transferred to real robots with task success increasing from 21.7% to 75.0%
claims.direction: favors generative, policy-ready simulated environments (as a form of synthetic-data/training augmentation) to boost both simulated and real-world task success
claims.conditions: generated 3D simulation environments, online RL training, sim-to-real transfer

title: VGFM: Expressive Robot Policies via Dense Value Guidance in Flow Matching

claims.claim: A flow-matching policy parameterized in action (x-prediction) space allows dense value-guided shaping (from a standard offline-RL critic) at randomly sampled flow times without backpropagation-through-time or auxiliary distillation, achieving strong performance across a wide range of locomotion and manipulation tasks in OGBench
claims.direction: favors flow-matching action heads that support lightweight value-guidance integration over diffusion/other generative heads that require BPTT or distillation for RL shaping
claims.conditions: OGBench sim tasks (locomotion + manipulation), offline RL, minimal hyperparameter tuning

title: Chain-of-Thought Predictive Control

claims.claim: Unsupervised discovery of multi-step subskill decomposition from demos, predicted as a chain-of-thought sequence of planning steps via a Transformer and coupled to action prediction via learnable prompt tokens, consistently surpasses existing strong baselines on challenging manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors explicit subskill/planning-step guidance (a form of structured task-history representation) over standard flat imitation learning
claims.conditions: challenging manipulation tasks using sub-optimal demonstrations

claims.claim: The method is designed to work with sub-optimal demonstrations, using an observation-space-agnostic approach to still extract useful subskill segmentation and improve generalizable policy learning
claims.direction: favors leveraging structure-discovery methods to make the most of imperfect/sub-optimal demo data
claims.conditions: sub-optimal demos

title: The Art of Imitation: Learning Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks From Few Demonstrations

claims.claim: The approach enables learning complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks from just FIVE demonstrations using only RGB-D observations, achieving state-of-the-art performance on RLBench with 20-fold improved sample efficiency compared to prior methods
claims.direction: favors sample-efficient, object-centric probabilistic (TP-GMM-based) methods over deep-network approaches when demonstrations are extremely scarce (as few as 5)
claims.conditions: RLBench benchmark, RGB-D observations only, 5 demonstrations per task

claims.claim: Riemannian GMMs are proposed to model end-effector velocity (factorized into direction and magnitude) instead of standard (non-Riemannian) GMMs, since raw velocities are non-Euclidean and hard to model with standard GMMs; this is combined with automatic per-skill task-parameter detection from vision
claims.direction: favors a probabilistic/Riemannian-GMM action head with explicit geometric structure over generic regression/deep generative heads for sample-efficient manipulation
claims.conditions: RLBench, few-shot (5-demo) regime

claims.claim: Factorizing end-effector velocity into direction and magnitude components (rather than raw Euclidean velocity vectors) and using time as an inductive bias for skill segmentation improves learning of complex, multi-skill trajectories
claims.direction: favors factorized (direction+magnitude) end-effector velocity action space over raw velocity/position vectors
claims.conditions: RLBench, TP-GMM framework

why_deep_read: Reports state-of-the-art RLBench performance with only 5 RGB-D demonstrations and 20x sample efficiency versus prior methods — this is an almost perfect match for our extreme low-data (50-100 demo, moving toward fewer) and RGB-D, laptop-compute setup; the Riemannian-GMM/factorized-velocity action representation is lightweight and could be a genuinely practical alternative to diffusion/VLA heads worth understanding in depth (Q01, Q02, Q13 simultaneously).

title: Hierarchical Autoregressive Modeling With Multi-Scale Refinement for Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: HAMR combines a hierarchical architecture (high-level long-horizon motion features guiding low-level fine-grained action generation), multi-scale action tokenization that actively corrects previous prediction errors during inference, and a lightweight diffusion-based decoder for multi-modality; it achieves 12% and 15% improvements over SOTA methods across 60+ tasks in simulation and real-world experiments respectively
claims.direction: favors hierarchical autoregressive-with-self-correction + lightweight diffusion decoder over standard (non-hierarchical, non-self-correcting) autoregressive or diffusion action heads
claims.conditions: 60+ tasks, both simulation and real-world

claims.claim: HAMR shows a 25% improvement over SOTA specifically in perturbed experiments, indicating better robustness to disturbance/perturbation than compared baselines
claims.direction: favors this hierarchical multi-scale-correction architecture for robustness under perturbation
claims.conditions: perturbed real-world/sim experiments (perturbation type unspecified in abstract)

title: Time as a Control Dimension in Robot Learning

claims.claim: Augmenting policies with two temporal signals (remaining time, and a time-ratio that modulates the policy's internal progression of time) allows a single policy to regulate execution pace/strategy, adapting continuously from fast dynamic execution under tight schedules to slow deliberate interaction when more time is available
claims.direction: favors giving the policy explicit control over its own execution timing/speed rather than a fixed inference/execution rate
claims.conditions: diverse manipulation tasks: long-horizon manipulation, granular-media pouring, articulated-object interaction, multi-agent coordination (RL framework)

claims.claim: Temporal awareness (time as a controllable variable) is reported to improve efficiency, robustness under sim-to-real mismatch and disturbances, and controllability through human input without retraining
claims.direction: favors explicit temporal control signals for robustness to sim-to-real mismatch/disturbance
claims.conditions: same task suite, RL-trained policies

title: RoboCasa365: A Large-Scale Simulation Framework for Training and Benchmarking Generalist Robots

claims.claim: Extensive experiments with SOTA methods across 365 tasks / 2,500 kitchen environments (600+ hrs human demo, 1600+ hrs synthetic demo) analyze the impacts of task diversity, dataset scale, and environment variation on generalization, providing insights into what factors most strongly affect generalist-robot performance
claims.direction: provides systematic (if not single-number) evidence on the relative importance of demo diversity vs. scale vs. environment variation for generalization
claims.conditions: large-scale simulation benchmark (RoboCasa), mixed human + synthetic demonstration data

title: Dex4D: Task-Agnostic Point Track Policy for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: A domain-agnostic 3D point-track conditioned 'Anypose-to-Anypose' policy, trained in simulation across thousands of objects, is zero-shot deployed to real-world tasks by prompting with object-centric point tracks extracted from generated videos, with online point tracking for closed-loop perception/control
claims.direction: favors 3D point-track-based action conditioning over end-to-end RGB policies for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer without finetuning
claims.conditions: sim training across many objects, real-robot zero-shot deployment

claims.claim: Demonstrates strong generalization to novel objects, scene layouts, backgrounds, and trajectories compared to prior baselines
claims.direction: favors point-track/3D representation for robustness to background, object, and layout variation
claims.conditions: real robot experiments

title: Design of a Lightweight Grasp Detection Network for Industrial Humanoid Robots Based on Dual-Modal Fusion Transformer

claims.claim: A dual-modal (RGB + depth) alignment Transformer (SATNet) enables high-precision grasping, addressing the limitation that single-modal data cannot capture complete information features
claims.direction: favors fusing RGB+depth over single-modality (RGB-only) input for grasp detection
claims.conditions: Cornell grasp dataset

claims.claim: The network achieves a very small model size (0.27M parameters) while achieving 97.8% grasp accuracy on the Cornell dataset
claims.direction: favors a very small, lightweight network for grasp detection rather than large complex architectures
claims.conditions: Cornell dataset, grasp-detection (not full manipulation) task

claims.claim: Inference time of 16.3ms is achieved with this lightweight dual-modal network, suitable for deployment on low-power devices
claims.direction: favors small dual-modal architectures for fast, low-power inference
claims.conditions: Cornell dataset benchmark

title: WALA Learning Executable Latent Actions from Action-Labeled Demonstrations and Action-Free Videos

claims.claim: Predicting future deltas in pretrained DINOv3 feature space and dense depth space (instead of reconstructing raw pixels) preserves task-relevant semantic/geometric structure while reducing sensitivity to appearance, used as latent-action pretraining targets
claims.direction: favors DINOv3-feature-space (and depth-space) prediction targets over raw-pixel reconstruction for latent action/world-model pretraining
claims.conditions: pretraining from mixed action-labeled + action-free video data

claims.claim: Latent actions are jointly supervised by robot action prediction, latent-action target matching, and future-dynamics prediction, achieving a new SOTA on RoboCasa (75.2% average success) and improving generalization in real-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors combining explicit action prediction with latent-action-matching and future-dynamics auxiliary objectives
claims.conditions: RoboTwin, RoboCasa sim benchmarks, real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Action-free videos (lacking robot action labels) contribute dynamics supervision, supplementing the more expensive action-labeled demonstrations
claims.direction: favors mixing cheap action-free video data with expensive action-labeled robot demos to reduce total labeled-demo requirements
claims.conditions: mixed video + robot-demo pretraining corpus

title: Reflex: Enabling Fast and Predictive Vision-Language-Action Models for Reaction-Critical Manipulation

claims.claim: ReflexVLA reduces deployment latency through batched visual encoding and CUDA Graph replay, while a companion benchmark (ReflexBench) explicitly supports configurable latency under both synchronous and asynchronous inference to evaluate reaction-critical manipulation
claims.direction: favors specific engineering techniques (batched encoding, CUDA graph replay) to cut VLA inference latency, and favors explicitly benchmarking sync vs async inference latency effects
claims.conditions: ReflexBench (6 dynamic tasks) + standard static benchmarks + real-world experiments

claims.claim: ReflexVLA maintains competitive accuracy on standard static manipulation benchmarks while consistently improving dynamic/reaction-critical manipulation performance, without large-scale robot-data pretraining
claims.direction: favors architectures explicitly designed for reaction-critical (fast-changing) scenarios over standard static-trained VLAs, relevant to async execution smoothness
claims.conditions: ReflexBench dynamic tasks + real-world validation

claims.claim: Temporal reasoning is enhanced through latent future prediction and multi-frame temporal fusion within the vision backbone
claims.direction: favors multi-frame fusion + latent future prediction for handling dynamic/reactive scenarios needing observation history
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

why_deep_read: Directly targets our two biggest stated pain points simultaneously — ~2s inference latency and jerky motion under async chunked execution — with concrete, real-world-validated engineering techniques (batched encoding, CUDA graph replay, configurable sync/async latency benchmarking) that could be directly adapted to our laptop-GPU deployment.

title: RoboDrop: Curating VLA Post-Training Data via Local Gradient Compatibility
