claims.claim: The approach specifically targets learning dexterous manipulation from few-shot demonstrations, integrating grasp primitives into demonstrations to generate stable, dexterous grasps with limited data
claims.direction: favors combining sparse distilled features with grasp primitives for few-shot (rather than large-scale) demonstration learning
claims.conditions: few-shot regime

title: Goal-VLA: Image-Generative VLMs as Object-Centric World Models Empowering Zero-shot Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Using an image-generative VLM as a world model to produce a goal-state image (from which target object pose is derived) separates a manipulation system into a highly-generalizable high-level policy and a training-free low-level controller, abstracting away the need for explicit action annotations at the high level
claims.direction: favors goal-image generation (rather than direct language-to-action mapping) as the interface between generalist VLM reasoning and low-level control
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world zero-shot manipulation experiments

claims.claim: A 'Reflection-through-Synthesis' process iteratively validates and refines the generated goal image before execution, improving robustness; both sim and real-world experiments show strong performance and generalizability in zero-shot manipulation
claims.direction: favors iterative self-validation/refinement of generated goals for robustness in zero-shot generalization settings
claims.conditions: sim + real-world

title: Two Bridges, One Pathway: From VLMs to Generalizable VLAs with Embodied Trajectory-Coupled Data

claims.claim: Mixing task-relevant, out-of-distribution 'embodied trajectory-coupled' (ETC) data — vision-language supervision derived from the same robot scenes/trajectories used for action learning, but retaining language-understanding objectives — with a small amount of action-labeled data enables the model to generalize to novel visual-language conditions WITHOUT requiring additional robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors supplementing a small action-labeled demo set with same-domain vision-language (non-action) supervision, rather than collecting more action-labeled demonstrations, to generalize to novel conditions
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot experiments

claims.claim: A three-stage recipe (Distribution Bridging: adapt VLM to embodied visual-language semantics; Objective Bridging: gradually shift toward action prediction while preserving representations; Retentive Adaptation: specialize to target domain) avoids the steep learning curve and representation degradation caused by directly fine-tuning a VLM on robot action data
claims.direction: favors a gradual, staged VLM-to-VLA adaptation recipe over direct one-shot fine-tuning on action data, to preserve pretrained generalization
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot experiments

title: LENS: LLM-guided Environment Simplification for Planning and Control in Clutter

claims.claim: A plug-and-play, LLM-guided scene-abstraction layer that merges (e.g., stacked objects) or prunes (e.g., distant objects) scene entities in closed loop, adaptively updating with task progress, improves classical planning, model-based control, AND a vision-language-action model across a diverse set of highly cluttered manipulation scenes, without requiring task-specific manual engineering of abstractions
claims.direction: favors an automatic, adaptive scene-simplification pre-processing layer (compatible with existing VLA policies) over manually-engineered scene abstractions for robustness to clutter/distractors
claims.conditions: diverse cluttered manipulation scenes, applied on top of classical planning, model-based control, and a VLA model

title: VAMPO: Policy Optimization for Improving Visual Dynamics in Video Action Models

claims.claim: Diffusion-based video predictors trained with standard likelihood-surrogate objectives produce globally plausible but precision-poor predictions (subtle errors in object pose, spatial relations, contact timing) that get amplified by downstream policies; reformulating multi-step denoising as a sequential decision process and optimizing it with rewards over expert visual dynamics in latent space (via policy optimization) improves task-relevant visual dynamics and downstream action generation across diverse sim and real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors post-training policy-optimization refinement of a video-action model's denoising process (targeting precision-critical visual dynamics) over training video predictors with likelihood-only objectives
claims.conditions: diverse simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, video-action-model-based policies

claims.claim: An 'Euler Hybrid' sampler injecting stochasticity only at the first denoising step enables tractable, low-variance policy-gradient estimation for refining diffusion-based video/action generation, while preserving trajectory coherence
claims.direction: favors this sampling scheme as a practical way to apply RL-style policy optimization to diffusion-based action/video generation without destabilizing the denoising trajectory
claims.conditions: same setting

title: LoopVLA: Learning Sufficiency in Recurrent Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: LoopVLA, a recurrent VLA that jointly learns representation refinement, action prediction, and a self-supervised 'sufficiency score' (estimating whether further refinement is needed) at each iteration, reduces parameters by 45% and improves inference throughput by up to 1.7x while matching or outperforming strong baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and VLA-Arena
claims.direction: favors adaptive, per-instance-sufficiency-gated recurrent computation over using a fixed, predefined number of transformer layers for every action prediction
claims.conditions: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, VLA-Arena sim benchmarks

claims.claim: By sharing parameters across refinement iterations (rather than using distinct layers per depth), LoopVLA decouples representation quality from a fixed layer-index budget, achieving a smaller overall parameter count than baseline VLAs
claims.direction: favors parameter-sharing recurrent refinement over deep feedforward stacks for reducing model size while retaining accuracy
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

claims.claim: Existing early-exit strategies (stopping at predefined layers or heuristic action-consistency rules) do not directly estimate whether a representation is sufficient for action; a self-supervised distribution-alignment objective (training intermediate confidence scores to match relative action quality across refinement steps) links sufficiency estimation directly to policy-optimization signals
claims.direction: favors learned, self-supervised sufficiency estimation over heuristic early-exit rules for adaptive-depth action prediction
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: When to Act, Ask, or Learn: Uncertainty-Aware Policy Steering

claims.claim: A framework (UPS) that jointly reasons about semantic task uncertainty and low-level action feasibility, calibrated via conformal prediction over the composition of a VLM verifier and a pretrained base (e.g., diffusion) policy, disentangles confident/ambiguous/incapable scenarios and minimizes expensive human interventions compared to uncalibrated baselines and prior continual-learning approaches, with residual learning used to improve the base policy from collected interventions
claims.direction: favors calibrated (conformal-prediction-based) uncertainty-aware steering plus targeted residual learning over uncalibrated VLM-verifier steering or standard continual learning for deployment-time policy improvement
claims.conditions: simulation and real hardware experiments

title: ULOHA: An Underwater Bimanual Robot System for Robot Learning

claims.claim: ULOHA evaluates ACT, Diffusion Policy, and SmolVLA on a real leader-follower bimanual platform, specifically examining how execution strategies developed for manipulation in air (action-execution horizons, real-time chunking) perform underwater under bubble disturbances and buoyancy-driven object motion
claims.direction: provides a direct comparative testbed for ACT/Diffusion-Policy/SmolVLA execution-horizon and chunking behavior under a different (underwater) physical disturbance regime, though specific quantitative results are not given in the abstract
claims.conditions: real underwater bimanual robot, LeRobot-based software stack

claims.claim: A separate single-arm study finds that demonstrations spanning both air and water media support execution in both, suggesting cross-domain demonstration mixing can support policy transfer between physical conditions
claims.direction: favors mixing demonstrations across differing physical conditions (rather than training only in one) to support transfer between conditions
claims.conditions: single-arm air/water transfer study on the same platform

title: LeTO: Learning Constrained Visuomotor Policy With Differentiable Trajectory Optimization

claims.claim: Integrating a differentiable trajectory-optimization layer directly into the policy network (a 'gray box' method) lets constraint information be introduced during training, balancing constraint satisfaction, trajectory smoothness, and demonstration-matching error in an end-to-end, constraint-controlled action-generation scheme
claims.direction: favors embedding differentiable trajectory optimization directly into the action-generation network over standard unconstrained neural action heads, when constraint satisfaction/safety matters
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot manipulation tasks

claims.claim: LeTO generates trajectories that are less uncertain, higher quality, and smoother compared to existing imitation learning methods
claims.direction: favors this constrained, optimization-embedded action generation for smoother output trajectories versus standard IL action heads
claims.conditions: same experiments

title: ExploRLLM: Guiding Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models

claims.claim: Combining foundation-model-generated policy code and efficient representations (to improve RL convergence) with a residual RL agent (to compensate for the FM's limited physical/spatial understanding) outperforms both pure FM-derived policies and RL baselines on table-top manipulation, with promising zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: favors combining FM-guided representations/code with residual RL over either FM-only zero-shot policies or RL-from-scratch alone
claims.conditions: table-top manipulation, sim training with real-world zero-shot transfer

title: GR-Dexter Technical Report

claims.claim: A training recipe combining teleoperated real-robot trajectories with large-scale vision-language data and carefully curated cross-embodiment datasets achieves strong in-domain performance for a bimanual dexterous-hand VLA system
claims.direction: favors mixing teleop data with large-scale VL and curated cross-embodiment data over teleop data alone for training generalist manipulation policies
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual dexterous-hand robot, long-horizon everyday manipulation + generalizable pick-and-place

claims.claim: This training recipe yields improved robustness to unseen objects and unseen instructions compared to (implied) baselines
claims.direction: favors this data mixing recipe for generalization to novel objects/instructions
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation

title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D Keyframe Transporter

claims.claim: Exploiting bi-equivariant symmetry within Keyframe Imitation Learning (evaluating actions via cross-correlation between grasped-object features and scene features, a Keyframe Transporter derived from Transporter Networks) with a coarse-to-fine SE(3) action-evaluation scheme outperforms strong Keyframe IL baselines by an average of >10% on a wide range of simulation tasks and by an average of 55% in 4 physical experiments
claims.direction: favors symmetry-exploiting (bi-equivariant), keyframe-based action representations with coarse-to-fine SE(3) reasoning over standard (non-equivariant) keyframe imitation learning baselines
claims.conditions: simulation (many tasks) + 4 real-world physical experiments

claims.claim: By exploiting workspace/object-transform symmetries, the method achieves large sample-efficiency gains (implied by the large physical-experiment improvement) over baselines that ignore these symmetries
claims.direction: favors symmetry-aware architectures as a route to sample efficiency (fewer demos needed) rather than scaling data alone
claims.conditions: same experiments

title: TesserAct: Learning 4D Embodied World Models

claims.claim: Training on RGB-DN (RGB, Depth, and Normal) video and converting generated RGB-DN predictions directly into a 4D scene provides more detailed shape/configuration/temporal information than traditional 2D video-based world models
claims.direction: favors incorporating depth+normal (not just RGB) into world-model training/prediction over RGB-only 2D video world models
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation video datasets extended with depth/normal via off-the-shelf models

claims.claim: Policy learning derived from this 4D world model significantly outperforms policy learning derived from prior (2D, video-only) world models, while also enabling accurate inverse dynamics and novel view synthesis for embodied environments
claims.direction: favors 4D (spatio-temporally coherent, depth-aware) world-model auxiliary representations over 2D video-only world models for downstream policy learning
claims.conditions: embodied manipulation scenarios

title: Sample from What You See: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Diffusion Bridge with Observation-Embedded Stochastic Differential Equation

claims.claim: BridgePolicy integrates observations directly into the stochastic dynamics of the diffusion process (via a diffusion-bridge formulation with a semantic aligner unifying heterogeneous visual/state inputs with action representations), allowing sampling to start from an observation-informed prior rather than random noise, and consistently outperforms SOTA generative policies across 52 simulation tasks (3 benchmarks) and 5 real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors observation-conditioned diffusion-bridge sampling (informative prior) over standard diffusion policies that always start denoising from random Gaussian noise
claims.conditions: 52 sim tasks across 3 benchmarks + 5 real-world tasks

title: StemVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model with Future 3D Spatial Geometry Knowledge and 4D Historical Representation

claims.claim: Explicitly forecasting structured 3D future spatial-geometric world knowledge (rather than relying solely on observed 2D images) enables the model to anticipate upcoming scene geometry and object configurations, contributing to 92.0% average accuracy across LIBERO subsets and 86.0% on long-horizon LIBERO-Long
claims.direction: favors explicit future 3D-geometry forecasting as an auxiliary signal over direct 2D-image-to-action mapping
claims.conditions: LIBERO sim benchmark suite only

claims.claim: Aggregating historical image frames through a pretrained video-geometry transformer backbone with temporal attention (forming a unified 4D historical spatiotemporal representation) is combined with the future 3D prediction for more comprehensive world understanding
claims.direction: favors combining explicit historical 4D spatiotemporal aggregation with future-geometry prediction over using only current-frame 2D observations
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: RoCo Challenge at AAAI 2026: Benchmarking Robotic Collaborative Manipulation for Assembly Towards Industrial Automation

claims.claim: Across 60+ teams and 170+ participants tackling a high-precision, long-horizon gearbox assembly task (sim + real dual-arm), the strategic utilization of recovery-from-failure curriculum data was identified as a critical insight for successful real-world deployment
claims.direction: favors deliberately including recovery-from-failure demonstrations in the training curriculum, over training only on successful/idealized demonstration trajectories, for high-precision long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: industrial gearbox assembly, simulation round + real-world round with teleoperated datasets, dual-arm robot

claims.claim: A dual-model framework for long-horizon multi-task learning was found to be highly effective by the top competition solutions (ARC-VLA, RoboCola)
claims.direction: favors dual-model (rather than single monolithic model) architectures for long-horizon, multi-phase task learning
claims.conditions: same competition, real + sim assembly rounds

title: Joint-Aligned Latent Action: Towards Scalable VLA Pretraining in the Wild

claims.claim: JALA learns a predictive action embedding aligned with both inverse dynamics and real actions (bypassing full visual-dynamics reconstruction), enabling effective pretraining from heterogeneous, large-scale in-the-wild human video (scaled to a 7.5M-video / 2,000+ hour corpus, UniHand-Mix, blending lab and in-the-wild footage) despite unreliable hand-tracking labels in the wild footage
claims.direction: favors action-alignment-based (rather than full visual-reconstruction-based) latent-action pretraining to make noisy, large-scale in-the-wild human video usable for VLA pretraining
claims.conditions: large-scale (7.5M video) human-video pretraining corpus, downstream sim + real-world manipulation evaluation

claims.claim: The jointly-aligned latent-action embedding significantly improves downstream robot manipulation performance in both simulation and real-world tasks compared to alternatives, and generates more realistic hand motions in both controlled and unconstrained scenarios
claims.direction: favors this inverse-dynamics-and-action-aligned latent pretraining objective as an auxiliary signal over standard visual-dynamics-only latent action learning
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: ADR-PNAS: A Novel Sim-to-Real Transfer Approach for Robotic Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Combining adaptive domain randomization with progressive neural architecture search (jointly optimizing simulation parameters AND network architecture) reduces the reality gap by up to 35% compared to state-of-the-art baselines including standard domain randomization, adaptive domain randomization alone, model-agnostic meta-learning, randomized-to-canonical adaptation networks, and ensemble policy learning
claims.direction: favors jointly optimizing domain-randomization parameters and network architecture together, over any single sim-to-real technique (DR, meta-learning, canonical adaptation, or ensembles) applied alone
claims.conditions: diverse manipulation tasks, comparison against 5 named SOTA sim-to-real baselines

title: Learning Versatile Humanoid Manipulation with Touch Dreaming

claims.claim: Augmenting behavioral cloning with 'touch dreaming' (predicting future hand-joint forces and future tactile latents, with targets from an EMA target encoder, requiring no separate tactile-pretraining stage) achieves a 90.9% relative improvement in average success rate over the strongest baseline across five real-world contact-rich tasks; predicting tactile targets in latent space (rather than raw tactile signal) gives an additional 30% relative gain
claims.direction: favors adding a future-latent-prediction auxiliary objective (for an additional sensing modality) trained jointly with action prediction, and specifically predicting in latent rather than raw sensor space, over action-prediction-only training
claims.conditions: real-world humanoid, contact-rich tasks, requires tactile sensing (not in our sensor set)

title: Efficient Real-World Online Reinforcement Learning for Robot Manipulation via Centralized Training and Critic Decomposition

claims.claim: Decomposing a centralized multi-head critic into task and grasp heads (matched to sparse task reward and a potential-based grasping reward respectively), combined with centralized-training-decentralized-execution, substantially improves both sample efficiency and policy performance for real-world online RL with human-in-the-loop interventions, raising success from 60% to 80-90% and from 25% to 95% across several pick-and-place/manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors decomposed, reward-component-specific critics over a single monolithic critic for real-world online RL fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real robotic arms + simulated humanoid, human-in-the-loop online RL

claims.claim: The approach is validated under dimension-wise domain randomization ranges approximately 5-25x larger than those considered in prior work, while still improving performance
claims.direction: suggests decomposed-critic online RL can tolerate much larger domain-randomization ranges than prior human-in-the-loop RL methods
claims.conditions: same experiments

title: Improving Robotic Generalist Policies via Flow Reversal Steering

claims.claim: Flow Reversal Steering (FRS) takes suboptimal-but-reasonable actions (e.g., from coarse human or VLM semantic guidance), finds their latent noise by passing them through a flow-matching generalist policy in reverse, and maps them to nearby generalist action modes, improving zero-shot control; these gains can be distilled via behavior cloning of an auxiliary noise-outputting policy, showing up to 95% absolute task-success-rate boosts in under a minute of training
claims.direction: favors reverse-flow-based steering/distillation of a pretrained flow-matching generalist policy toward coarse external guidance, over directly commanding the policy or retraining it from scratch, for very fast, large policy improvements
claims.conditions: many simulated and real-world manipulation settings, flow-matching generalist policies specifically

claims.claim: FRS also enables policy improvement by bootstrapping reinforcement learning with semantic knowledge, improving on tasks where standard RL alone fails to improve
claims.direction: favors combining flow-reversal-derived semantic guidance with RL bootstrapping over standard RL alone for hard tasks
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: Reports an unusually large (up to 95% absolute) task-success improvement achievable in under a minute of auxiliary training, specifically for flow-matching generalist policies — if our policy uses (or could use) a flow-matching action head, this offers an extremely cheap way to correct failures using only coarse human/VLM guidance rather than more demonstrations or expensive retraining, which is highly relevant given our compute constraints.

title: Asynchronous Multimodal Diffusion Policy Composition via Latency-Aware Guidance Fusion

claims.claim: LAG-Fusion allows modality-specific diffusion policies to run at their own native inference rates (rather than forcing synchronous fusion that either slows high-frequency feedback or limits extensibility), contributing denoising guidance whenever available, via a reference-frame rebasing rule for diffusion variables under relative action representations that lets delayed/asynchronous guidance be correctly aligned before fusion
claims.direction: favors explicit latency-aware, asynchronous multi-rate guidance fusion over standard synchronous multimodal diffusion-policy fusion or manually engineered fixed multi-frequency architectures
claims.conditions: contact-rich manipulation composing a low-frequency vision policy with a high-frequency force policy; heterogeneous modality latencies

claims.claim: Under heterogeneous modality latencies, LAG-Fusion improves policy responsiveness and task performance over synchronous fusion and specially designed force-aware baselines
claims.direction: favors asynchronous, latency-aware composition for responsiveness in the presence of mismatched sensing/inference rates, relevant to reducing jerkiness from rigid synchronous chunk execution
claims.conditions: same experiments

why_deep_read: Directly targets the mismatch between different components' inference rates in a chunked diffusion-policy pipeline — conceptually very close to our jerky-motion-under-async-inference problem — with a concrete mechanism (reference-frame rebasing for relative action representations) for combining asynchronous, differently-latent guidance signals without breaking action-chunk consistency; worth understanding even though their instantiation uses a force sensor we may lack, since the rebasing/fusion idea could generalize to our scene-camera vs. wrist-camera or vision-vs-proprioception rate mismatch.

title: RodForesight: A World Model Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Slender Rod Insertion

claims.claim: During insertion, a diffusion policy generates candidate action chunks while an action-conditioned world model predicts their effects on rod-hole alignment, enabling pre-execution evaluation that selects the best action chunk based on predicted tilt/radial error before execution, improving success rate from 88.9% to 96.7% compared to a baseline diffusion policy
claims.direction: favors world-model-based pre-execution scoring/selection among candidate diffusion action chunks over directly executing a single sampled chunk
claims.conditions: real precision slender-rod-insertion task, deformable/bending rod (non-rigid tip pose)

claims.claim: Factorizing the task into coarse visual-servoing approach + predictive (world-model-scored) fine insertion, wrapped into an end-to-end design, is shown to be more effective than either stage alone
claims.direction: favors a coarse-then-fine, world-model-scored chunk-selection pipeline over a single-stage diffusion policy for precision contact-rich insertion
claims.conditions: real robot, precision insertion task

title: Beyond Future Prediction: Denoising as Generative Adaptation for Robot Control

claims.claim: Under matched controlled settings, co-training with past vs. future visual targets perform comparably, while restricting training to the clean (non-noised) endpoint substantially reduces robustness — suggesting that a SEPARATE FUTURE-PREDICTION TARGET is not essential for adapting a pretrained generative DiT prior to control, contrary to the common practice of using future-frame prediction as the transfer mechanism; instead, the denoising trajectory itself (not necessarily anchored to a future target) is the effective interface for control
claims.direction: CONTRADICTS the common assumption that an explicit future-observation-prediction objective is necessary for transferring generative video/image priors to robot control; a future-target-free co-training formulation (denoise current observation + predict actions from the same stream) works as well or better
claims.conditions: matched controlled experiments, LIBERO-Plus benchmark, tested with both a video-generation backbone (FLUX2-Klein) and a pure text-to-image backbone (Z-Image)

claims.claim: NowWAM reaches 87.7% on LIBERO-Plus with FLUX2-Klein, improving 6.1 points over a future-target co-training baseline while halving training visual tokens (784->392) and reducing per-step time from 2.85s to 1.63s (a 1.8x speedup); a pure text-to-image backbone (Z-Image) reaches a comparable 87.8%, showing strong control adaptation is not tied to video-generation-specific backbones
claims.direction: favors a future-target-free denoising formulation for large latency/compute reductions (1.8x speedup, half the visual tokens) without sacrificing (and while improving) accuracy, and shows simpler (non-video) generative backbones suffice
claims.conditions: LIBERO-Plus sim benchmark

why_deep_read: This is a notable CONTRARIAN finding relative to the many world-model/future-prediction papers in this batch: it shows the common practice of explicit future-frame prediction is not necessary for good control performance, and that dropping it yields a large (1.8x) latency/compute reduction — directly relevant to our latency-constrained laptop-GPU deployment and worth flagging as a caution against investing in future-prediction auxiliary objectives without first checking whether they're actually earning their compute cost.

title: Learning to Manipulate Anywhere: A Visual Generalizable Framework For Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A multi-view representation-learning approach fused with a Spatial Transformer Network module captures shared semantic information and correspondences among different viewpoints, contributing to strong visual generalization
claims.direction: favors multi-view representation learning with explicit cross-view correspondence modeling over single-view or naively-fused multi-view encoders for viewpoint robustness
claims.conditions: 8 designed tasks (articulated objects, bimanual, dexterous-hand manipulation), sim training with sim2real transfer across 3 hardware platforms

claims.claim: Curriculum-based randomization and augmentation stabilizes RL training and strengthens visual generalization ability, and the combined framework (Maniwhere) significantly outperforms existing SOTA methods on generalization to multiple combined visual disturbance types
claims.direction: favors curriculum-scheduled (rather than fixed-intensity) domain randomization/augmentation for both training stability and generalization
claims.conditions: same task suite

claims.claim: Maniwhere demonstrates strong visual generalization and sim2real transfer across 3 different hardware platforms, generalizing across a combination of multiple visual disturbance types simultaneously (not just one at a time)
claims.direction: favors architectures explicitly designed to handle combined/compounded visual disturbances over those tested on single disturbance types in isolation
claims.conditions: sim2real across 3 hardware platforms

title: CARP: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Coarse-to-Fine Autoregressive Prediction

claims.claim: Redefining autoregressive action generation as a coarse-to-fine, next-scale process (an action autoencoder learns multi-scale action-sequence representations; a GPT-style transformer then refines predictions coarse-to-fine) produces highly accurate, smooth actions matching or surpassing diffusion-based policies, with up to a 10% success-rate improvement, across single-task, multi-task, state-based, image-based, and real-world settings
claims.direction: favors coarse-to-fine autoregressive action generation over both standard (single-scale) autoregressive and diffusion-based action heads for accuracy and smoothness simultaneously
claims.conditions: diverse sim benchmarks (single/multi-task, state/image-based) + real-world tasks

claims.claim: CARP delivers 10x faster inference compared to state-of-the-art (diffusion) policies while maintaining efficiency on par with standard autoregressive policies
claims.direction: favors this coarse-to-fine autoregressive paradigm for dramatically lower inference latency than diffusion-based action heads
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

title: villa-X: Enhancing Latent Action Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Improving both how latent actions (abstract motion representations between frames) are learned and how they are incorporated into VLA pretraining lets villa-X generate latent action plans in a zero-shot fashion, even for unseen embodiments and open-vocabulary symbolic understanding, achieving superior performance across diverse SIMPLER sim tasks and two real-world setups (gripper and dexterous hand)
claims.direction: favors an improved latent-action-modeling VLA pretraining paradigm over standard direct action-labeled pretraining, for cross-embodiment zero-shot generalization
claims.conditions: SIMPLER sim benchmark + 2 real-world robotic setups (gripper, dexterous hand)

claims.claim: Latent-action pretraining enables zero-shot latent action plans for unseen embodiments, reducing the need for embodiment-specific action-labeled data
claims.direction: favors latent-action-based pretraining as a scalable route to generalization across embodiments with less embodiment-specific labeled data
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Bi-LAT: Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning via Natural Language and Action Chunking with Transformers

claims.claim: Encoding human instructions specifying force nuance (e.g., 'softly grasp the cup', 'strongly twist the sponge') through a multimodal Transformer built on bilateral (leader-follower) control data lets the policy dynamically adjust applied force to match instructed levels, in both unimanual and coordinated bimanual real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors language-conditioned force modulation (leveraging bilateral leader-follower joint torque/position/velocity data) over language conditioning for task selection alone
claims.conditions: real-world leader-follower teleoperated bilateral control setup, unimanual + bimanual tasks

claims.claim: Among tested language encoders, SigLIP gave the best force-command distinction performance for this ACT-based, language-conditioned bilateral control policy
claims.direction: favors SigLIP as a language/vision-language encoder choice over other tested encoders for this force-modulation task
claims.conditions: real-world bilateral-control imitation learning

title: Generalizable Coarse-to-Fine Robot Manipulation via Language-Aligned 3D Keypoints

claims.claim: CLAP (task decomposition + VLM fine-tuning for 3D keypoint prediction + 3D-aware representation) achieves a 12% higher average success rate than the SOTA method on GemBench (a generalization benchmark) while using only 1/5 of the training trajectories; in real-world experiments, the policy trained on only 10 demonstrations successfully generalizes to novel instructions and environments
claims.direction: favors coarse-to-fine, language-aligned 3D-keypoint-based hierarchical policies over standard hierarchical or flat baselines for sample-efficient generalization from very few (10) demonstrations
claims.conditions: GemBench sim benchmark + real robot, 10 real-world demonstrations

claims.claim: A 3D-aware representation (VLM-predicted 3D keypoints) combined with a coarse-to-fine (region-of-interest then fine action) hierarchical policy structure improves generalization to novel instructions/environments over 2D-only or non-hierarchical 3D approaches
claims.direction: favors 3D-keypoint-based coarse-to-fine representations over 2D or flat 3D representations for generalization
claims.conditions: same evaluation

claims.claim: VLM fine-tuning for 3D keypoint prediction is used as the mechanism connecting task decomposition (language) to precise 3D action guidance
claims.direction: favors VLM-predicted 3D keypoints as the language-to-action interface over direct language-to-dense-action mapping
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: The Most Overestimated Q Value Regularization in High-Dimensional Discrete Action Spaces for Offline Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: In offline RL over high-dimensional discrete action spaces, penalizing only the single most-overestimated Q-value action (rather than applying uniform penalties across the whole action space) significantly outperforms baseline offline RL algorithms, achieving clearance rates of 96.94% (sim) and 99.04% (real-world dense configurations) on a robotic pushing-and-grasping task
claims.direction: favors targeted (most-overestimated-action) Q-value regularization over uniform action-space regularization for high-dimensional discrete-action offline RL in manipulation
claims.conditions: real and simulated robotic pushing/grasping with random, dense, and unknown object arrangements

title: Trajectory Conditioned Cross-embodiment Skill Transfer

claims.claim: Representing human demonstration-video motions as sparse optical-flow trajectories (embodiment-agnostic, removing morphological variation while preserving essential dynamics) and conditioning a joint video+action synthesis model on these trajectories improves cross-embodiment success rate by up to 16.7% versus SOTA, validated on real-robot kitchen manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors sparse optical-flow trajectory representations (rather than paired datasets or hand-crafted rewards) for transferring skills from human demonstration video to robot actions across embodiments
claims.conditions: MetaWorld sim + real-robot kitchen manipulation

claims.claim: Jointly synthesizing temporally consistent robot manipulation videos and translating them into executable actions (rather than predicting actions directly) reduces FVD by 39.6% and KVD by 36.6% compared to SOTA
claims.direction: favors joint video-and-action synthesis conditioned on embodiment-agnostic trajectories over direct action-only prediction, for temporal consistency
claims.conditions: MetaWorld sim benchmark

title: A Unified Multimodal Perception and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Autonomous Operation of Bionic Robotic Arms

claims.claim: A unified cross-modal (vision, depth, force, touch, EMG, language) representation network with safe-RL control achieves a perception-control closed-loop latency of 24.3 milliseconds and an 18.4-percentage-point average task-success improvement over baselines on a real 7-DOF hybrid bionic robotic arm across five complex tasks
claims.direction: favors tightly integrated multimodal perception + safe-RL control architectures for very low closed-loop latency alongside large success-rate gains, though on a much more complex/sensor-rich hardware platform than ours
claims.conditions: real-world 7-DOF hybrid rigid/continuum robotic arm, 72-hour continuous industrial operation test

claims.claim: A multimodal-physical coupled state-prediction model embeds dynamic priors into the policy-update process, contributing to a 93.6% success rate in continuous industrial operation
claims.direction: favors embedding physical/dynamics priors as an auxiliary predictive component in the policy-update loop
claims.conditions: same real-world system

title: HALOMI: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Active Perception from Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: Extending Universal Manipulation Interface with egocentric sensing (ego-view + wrist-view observations, head-hand trajectories) and a manifold-constrained controller (planning in a learned latent behavior manifold) enables precise, robust head-hand tracking in the world frame, achieving 85% average success across three quantitatively evaluated real-world tasks on a humanoid with an actuated neck
claims.direction: favors active, egocentric multi-view (head+wrist) sensing with a learned latent-manifold controller for robust world-frame tracking, over passive fixed-camera perception
claims.conditions: real Unitree G1 humanoid with actuated neck, 5 real-world task categories

claims.claim: Human demonstrations collected at scale (via UMI-style interface) naturally capture active hand-eye coordination usable for training, though a controller-aware reference-trajectory adaptation step is needed to bridge the human-to-humanoid embodiment gap in both observation and action execution
claims.direction: favors scalable human demonstration collection (with explicit embodiment-gap correction) over robot-only teleoperated data collection
claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation

title: Learning Sim-Grounded Policies for Bimanual Rope Manipulation from Human Teleoperation Data

claims.claim: Holding policy architecture (Action Chunking with Transformers) and teleoperation data scale fixed, a controlled comparison finds that a state-based policy (conditioned on the manipulated object's 3D particle state, obtained via multi-view fusion + physics simulation) reduces initial grasp-and-pull action L1 error by 30.8% compared to a vision-based policy (conditioned on two egocentric wrist-mounted RGB streams), on an unseen configuration
claims.direction: favors compact, physics-consistent state representations over raw egocentric RGB pixel observations for generalization from small teleoperated demonstration datasets, when such state can be estimated
claims.conditions: real bimanual teleoperation data, deformable rope knot-untangling task, open-loop evaluation on unseen configuration

claims.claim: The generalization failure of egocentric visual policies for this task is attributed to the observation space itself (an 'observability gap between pixels and physics-consistent state'), not to policy architecture or data scale, since both policies share the same architecture and training data
claims.direction: identifies observation-space choice (not just architecture/data scale) as a distinct, isolable factor in generalization failure, arguing for considering compact state/3D representations over raw RGB when few demonstrations are available
claims.conditions: same controlled comparison

title: CLAMP: Contrastive Learning for 3D Multi-View Action-Conditioned Robotic Manipulation Pretraining

claims.claim: Re-rendering multi-view four-channel (RGB + depth + 3D coordinate) image observations from a merged point cloud (computed from RGB-D + camera extrinsics), including dynamic wrist views, and contrastively pretraining encoders to associate 3D geometric/positional information with robot action patterns on large-scale simulated trajectories, substantially improves learning efficiency and policy performance on unseen tasks over standard 2D-image pretrained representations
claims.direction: favors 3D-aware (depth+coordinate-augmented), multi-view contrastive pretraining over standard 2D-image-only pretrained representations for behavior-cloning policies
claims.conditions: large-scale simulated robot trajectories for pretraining, fine-tuned on limited task demonstrations

claims.claim: Pretraining a Diffusion Policy during encoder pretraining to initialize policy weights (rather than only pretraining the encoder) is essential for improving fine-tuning sample efficiency and performance; CLAMP outperforms SOTA baselines across six simulated tasks and five real-world tasks after fine-tuning on a limited amount of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors jointly pretraining both encoder and policy weights (not just the encoder) before fine-tuning on limited demos
claims.conditions: 6 sim + 5 real-world tasks, limited fine-tuning demonstrations

claims.claim: Including dynamic wrist-view renderings (not just fixed scene views) in the multi-view 3D pretraining data provides clearer views of target objects for high-precision manipulation
claims.direction: favors incorporating wrist-camera viewpoints explicitly into 3D-aware pretraining rather than pretraining on fixed/scene-only views
claims.conditions: same setup

title: Stage-Aware and Roughness-Constrained Diffusion Policy for Multi-Stage Robotic Polishing

claims.claim: Inferring a process-stage posterior from multimodal observation histories and using it to condition a shared reverse-denoising process enables stage-consistent diffusion action generation WITHOUT requiring external stage labels during execution, improving stage-transition stability and process-parameter consistency versus baselines on real-robot multi-stage industrial tasks
claims.direction: favors internally-inferred stage-conditioning (rather than externally labeled stage/subtask signals) for diffusion-policy chunk generation on long-horizon, multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: real-robot multi-stage industrial polishing tasks (different domain from pick-place, but same class of long-horizon staged diffusion policy)

claims.claim: Conditioning generation on multimodal observation-history-derived stage posteriors (rather than raw history alone) improves consistency across uncertain stage transitions
claims.direction: favors explicit stage-posterior inference from observation history over raw history conditioning for staged long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: same real-robot experiments

title: Faster-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Deep Action Modules?

claims.claim: Faster-WAM docks a single-layer action head onto a 30-layer pretrained video Transformer backbone (via a 'Dock of Transformer' interface fusing keys/values from all backbone layers with RoPE realignment), rather than tying action-module depth to video-backbone depth; without additional embodied pretraining it achieves the lowest end-to-end latency in a controlled comparison (66.5 ms per inference, a 3.2x speedup over Fast-WAM) while matching competitive performance on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0
claims.direction: favors decoupling action-module depth from video-backbone depth (single lightweight action head docked onto a deep frozen/pretrained video backbone) over tying them together, for large latency reductions without sacrificing accuracy
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmarks, LIBERO-Plus OOD generalization, controlled latency comparison against Fast-WAM

claims.claim: A single-layer action head is sufficient when it can access (via docking) representations from all layers of a deep pretrained video backbone, avoiding the computational overhead of a deep, dedicated action module
claims.direction: favors a very shallow (single-layer), docked action head over deep dedicated action modules for world-action-model architectures
claims.conditions: same benchmark suite

title: GSP-3D: generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting with diffusion policy and world model for long-horizon bimanual manipulation

claims.claim: A Generalizable Gaussian Regressor predicts 3D Gaussian primitives from a single RGB-D frame in real time, and a 3DGS-conditioned diffusion policy aggregates these Gaussians into compact latent representations, replacing sparse point clouds (which limit structural completeness) as the 3D scene representation for a diffusion policy
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D Gaussian-splatting-based scene representation (from a single RGB-D frame) over sparse point clouds for structurally complete 3D-conditioned diffusion policies
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, bimanual manipulation tasks

claims.claim: A transformer-based world model forecasts future Gaussian sets and uses the prediction error as an auxiliary loss to enforce temporal consistency across actions, addressing the temporally inconsistent action generation that diffusion-based policies often suffer from
claims.direction: favors a future-Gaussian-prediction auxiliary loss specifically to improve temporal consistency of diffusion-generated action chunks
claims.conditions: same benchmark, long-horizon bimanual tasks

claims.claim: GSP-3D is evaluated under both clean and domain-randomized conditions explicitly including variations in LIGHTING, BACKGROUNDS, and TABLETOP DISTRACTORS, consistently outperforming baseline methods with minimal added computational overhead
claims.direction: favors this 3DGS+diffusion+world-model combination specifically for robustness to lighting/background/distractor variation, achieved with minimal extra compute
claims.conditions: RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, explicit lighting/background/distractor domain randomization

why_deep_read: This is one of the few papers in the batch that explicitly evaluates all three of our named environmental failure modes together (lighting, background, and tabletop distractors) while also addressing temporal-consistency of diffusion action-chunk generation, all with a real-time (single-frame), low-overhead 3D representation — a close match to our robustness (Q14) and chunk-smoothness (Q06) concerns simultaneously, worth checking whether the RGB-D-only Gaussian regressor could work with our RealSense camera.

title: ARCap: Collecting High-Quality Human Demonstrations for Robot Learning with Augmented Reality Feedback

claims.claim: A portable data-collection system providing real-time augmented-reality visual feedback and haptic collision warnings (rather than relying on user expertise alone, as with feedback-free portable devices) enables novice users to collect robot-executable, collision-free, kinematically-valid demonstrations, validated through extensive user studies
claims.direction: favors providing real-time AR/haptic feedback during demonstration collection over feedback-free portable data-collection devices, for demonstration data quality especially with non-expert operators
claims.conditions: user studies with novice operators, real-robot deployment on cluttered-environment and long-horizon cross-embodiment tasks

title: VLA-Reasoner: Empowering Vision-Language-Action Models with Reasoning via Online Monte Carlo Tree Search

claims.claim: A plug-in, test-time-scaling framework samples and rolls out possible action trajectories via a world model to foresee future states, using MCTS (seeded by step-wise VLA predictions) with KDE-based confidence sampling to search efficiently for optimal actions and correct incremental deviations in long-horizon trajectory tasks, without retraining the base VLA
claims.direction: favors test-time world-model rollout + tree search on top of an off-the-shelf VLA (rather than retraining for longer-horizon capability) to correct incremental deviation errors
claims.conditions: simulators and real-world experiments, applied to off-the-shelf VLAs

claims.claim: An offline value-estimation strategy scores predicted future states during MCTS to correct deviations with long-term feedback, achieving significant improvements over state-of-the-art VLAs
claims.direction: favors incorporating a learned value/scoring function over rolled-out future states as an auxiliary signal for long-horizon correction
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: UniBYD: A Unified Framework for Learning Robotic Manipulation Across Embodiments Beyond Imitation of Human Demonstrations

claims.claim: A unified morphological representation (UMR) enables consistent modeling of manipulation policies across diverse robotic hand morphologies, rather than requiring embodiment-specific action spaces
claims.direction: favors a unified, morphology-agnostic action/state representation over embodiment-specific representations for cross-embodiment policy learning
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment manipulation benchmark (UniManip), diverse robotic hand morphologies

claims.claim: A dynamic PPO with annealed reward schedule transitions from offline-informed imitation of human demonstrations to online-adaptive exploration, going beyond mere imitation and yielding a 44.08% average improvement in success rate over current SOTA on the new cross-embodiment benchmark
claims.direction: favors transitioning from pure imitation toward online-adaptive RL exploration (rather than staying purely imitative) to better adapt to a robot's own physical characteristics beyond human demonstration replication
claims.conditions: UniManip benchmark, diverse robotic hand morphologies

title: Generalizable Dense Reward for Long-Horizon Robotic Tasks

claims.claim: VLLR combines an LLM/VLM-derived extrinsic reward (task decomposed into verifiable subtasks, progress estimated by VLMs to initialize the value function during a brief warm-up, avoiding prohibitive full-training inference cost) with an intrinsic self-certainty reward for PPO finetuning; ablations show VLM-based value initialization mainly improves task-completion efficiency while self-certainty mainly enhances success rates, especially out-of-distribution
claims.direction: favors combining a cheap (warm-up-only) VLM-derived value initialization with a self-certainty intrinsic reward over either alone, and over manual reward engineering, for RL finetuning of long-horizon foundation policies
claims.conditions: CHORES benchmark (mobile manipulation + navigation)

claims.claim: VLLR achieves up to 56% absolute success-rate gains over the pretrained policy, up to 5% over SOTA RL finetuning on in-distribution tasks, and up to 10% on out-of-distribution tasks, without manual reward engineering
claims.direction: favors this dense-reward RL finetuning recipe specifically for improving OOD generalization over the base pretrained (IL) policy
claims.conditions: CHORES benchmark

title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments

claims.claim: Mainstream VLAs' reliance on single-frame observations restricts spatiotemporal reasoning, causing a performance gap on dynamic (moving-target) manipulation tasks; PUMA integrates scene-centric historical optical flow and specialized 'world queries' to implicitly forecast object-centric future states, coupling history-aware perception with short-horizon prediction, yielding a 6.3% absolute success-rate improvement over baselines on a new 35-task, 110K-trajectory dynamic-manipulation benchmark (DOMINO)
claims.direction: favors explicit historical-optical-flow-based observation history plus short-horizon future-state forecasting over single-frame observation VLAs, especially for tasks involving moving targets/dynamic scenes
claims.conditions: DOMINO benchmark (35 tasks, 110K+ expert trajectories)

claims.claim: Training on dynamic manipulation data fosters robust spatiotemporal representations that transfer to (improve performance on) static manipulation tasks as well
claims.direction: favors including dynamic-scene training data even when the deployment task itself is largely static, for improved robustness/representations
claims.conditions: same benchmark, cross-evaluation on static tasks

title: PACT: Self-Evolving Physical Safety Alignment for Diffusion Policies in Embodied Manipulation

claims.claim: A self-evolving post-training framework that distills constraint gradients into a pretrained diffusion policy (via a reverse-KL objective with dense per-timestep supervision, plus a curriculum that progressively tightens constraints) projects the policy onto constraint-feasible regions WITHOUT needing demonstration data or task rewards, reducing safety violations by 31.0% on average while IMPROVING task success by 30.7% on simulated and real-world benchmarks
claims.direction: favors post-hoc, demonstration-free/reward-free constraint-gradient distillation for diffusion policies over training-time constraint imposition or reactive test-time guardrails, achieving both safety and performance gains together
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world embodied manipulation benchmarks

title: simDP: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Shared Action Spaces

claims.claim: Reformulating the action space as end-effector pose + binary gripper state (rather than joint-space or robot-specific representations) allows it to be shared between simulated and physical robots, so a diffusion-policy action decoder trained purely in simulation can be reused in the real world with minimal modification
claims.direction: favors a compact, embodiment-shareable end-effector-pose + binary-gripper action space over joint-space/robot-specific action spaces, specifically to enable sim-trained decoder reuse in real-world deployment
claims.conditions: object manipulation tasks derived from MimicGen, evaluated across four real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Training a real-world observation encoder to align with the simulation-learned latent representation (while reusing the simulation-trained action decoder) achieves task performance similar to, and in some cases better than, diffusion policies trained only on limited real-world data
claims.direction: favors adapting only the observation encoder to real-world data (keeping a sim-trained action decoder fixed) over training the full policy from scratch on limited real-world demonstrations
claims.conditions: four real-world manipulation tasks, calibrated sim-to-real transfer setting

title: Learning Panorama-Aware VLA for Mobile Manipulation with Whole-Body Teleoperation

claims.claim: Existing VLA models predominantly rely on local camera observations, whose limited field of view hinders global spatial understanding; PanoVLA introduces dedicated panorama encoding and fusion modules (Mixture-of-Transformers) to integrate panoramic observations with language and robot state, achieving 91.3% average stage completion and 73.4% end-to-end success on real-world mobile manipulation tasks, substantially outperforming local-view baselines
claims.direction: favors incorporating wide/panoramic camera field-of-view over standard local/narrow-FOV camera observations for spatial understanding and closed-loop manipulation performance
claims.conditions: real-world mobile bimanual manipulation, four tasks, whole-body teleoperation dataset (5.5 hours)

title: Aligning Objects as Preprocessing Combined with Imitation Learning for Improved Generalization

claims.claim: Using an object-detection-based preprocessing step (YOLOv8) to automatically move the target object to a specific position and eliminate initial object-pose variation, BEFORE running an ACT imitation-learning policy, reduces the amount of demonstration data needed to cover pose variation — since ACT-style IL normally 'needs a lot of demonstration data that covers pose variation' to generalize — validated on a randomly-placed bag-opening task requiring both pose-variation generalization and dexterous bimanual manipulation
claims.direction: favors adding a simple, non-learned object-pose-alignment preprocessing step in front of an ACT policy over collecting substantially more demonstrations to cover object-position/pose variation
claims.conditions: real (or realistic) bimanual bag-opening task with randomly placed objects, ACT with vs. without preprocessing compared

claims.claim: The preprocessing step functions as a deterministic, non-learned alternative to data augmentation/scale for handling initial-pose variation, complementing (rather than replacing) the imitation-learning policy itself
claims.direction: favors combining classical object-alignment preprocessing with IL rather than relying purely on data augmentation or larger datasets to handle object-pose variation
claims.conditions: same experiment

why_deep_read: This is a very simple, cheap, and directly applicable idea for exactly our pick-and-place task (pumpkin placed at varying positions on the scene camera view): using an off-the-shelf detector to normalize/re-position the object before policy execution could substantially cut the number of demonstrations we need to cover position variation, complementing rather than requiring a larger or more complex policy — worth understanding exactly how the preprocessing controller works and how it composes with a chunked action-head policy like ours.

title: HyperVLA: Efficient Inference in Vision-Language-Action Models via Hypernetworks

claims.claim: Instead of activating the whole model at both training and inference time like monolithic VLAs, HyperVLA uses a hypernetwork-based architecture that activates only a small, task-specific policy during inference while retaining high model capacity (needed for diverse multi-task behaviors) during training; this requires specific design features (proper use of vision-foundation-model priors, hypernetwork normalization, and an action-generation strategy) to train successfully
claims.direction: favors hypernetwork-generated small task-specific sub-policies (large capacity only at training time) over monolithic 'always-fully-active' VLA architectures for efficient inference without sacrificing multi-task capacity
claims.conditions: comparison against monolithic VLAs including OpenVLA, both zero-shot generalization and few-shot adaptation settings

claims.claim: Compared to OpenVLA, HyperVLA reduces the number of activated parameters at test time by 90x and accelerates inference speed by 120x, while achieving similar or even higher success rate for both zero-shot generalization and few-shot adaptation
claims.direction: favors this hypernetwork architecture for enormous inference-latency and compute reductions with no success-rate penalty (and sometimes gains) versus a monolithic SOTA VLA
claims.conditions: same comparison, zero-shot and few-shot settings

why_deep_read: Reports a 120x inference speedup and 90x reduction in test-time activated parameters versus OpenVLA while matching or exceeding success rate — this is one of the largest, most directly quantified latency/compute wins in the entire batch and squarely targets our #1 stated problem (~2s inference latency on an 8GB laptop GPU); understanding whether the hypernetwork approach is compatible with a SmolVLA-scale backbone would be high-value.

title: GeoPredict: Leveraging Predictive Kinematics and 3D Gaussian Geometry for Precise VLA Manipulation

claims.claim: GeoPredict augments a continuous-action policy with predictive kinematic (multi-step 3D keypoint trajectory) and 3D-Gaussian-geometry priors, encoding motion history and forecasting workspace geometry with track-guided refinement, consistently outperforming strong VLA baselines especially in geometry-intensive and spatially-demanding scenarios (RoboCasa Human-50, LIBERO, real-world tasks)
claims.direction: favors adding explicit predictive 3D-geometric/kinematic reasoning to an otherwise 2D-centric, reactive VLA for precise spatial manipulation
claims.conditions: RoboCasa Human-50, LIBERO sim benchmarks + real-world manipulation

claims.claim: The predictive 3D modules (trajectory-level keypoint prediction + Gaussian geometry forecasting) serve EXCLUSIVELY as training-time supervision via depth-based rendering
claims.direction: favors using rich 3D/geometric auxiliary supervision only during training (not at inference) as a way to get 3D reasoning benefits without paying its usual cost
claims.conditions: same evaluation

claims.claim: At inference, GeoPredict requires only lightweight additional query tokens WITHOUT invoking any 3D decoding, avoiding the usual inference-time cost of 3D-aware policies
claims.direction: favors this training-only 3D supervision design specifically to avoid inference-time latency/compute overhead that explicit 3D processing (point clouds, Gaussians, depth) would normally add
claims.conditions: same evaluation

why_deep_read: Directly resolves the tension in our Q04 decision (3D/depth awareness vs. RGB-only for compute reasons) by using 3D/geometric supervision only at training time and paying almost no extra inference cost — if this holds up, it could let us get 3D-reasoning robustness benefits for the RealSense depth stream we already have, without adding to our already-tight ~2s inference latency budget.

title: Towards Safe Imitation Learning via Potential Field-Guided Flow Matching

claims.claim: PF2MP simultaneously learns a task policy and extracts an obstacle-related potential field from the same successful demonstrations, then modulates the flow-matching vector field via this learned potential field at inference time to enable safe motion generation
claims.direction: favors jointly learning an auxiliary potential-field representation from demonstrations and using it to modulate a flow-matching action head, over training a flow-matching policy on task success alone
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world settings, navigation and robotic manipulation, both task-space and joint-space control

claims.claim: PF2MP achieves a significant reduction of collisions compared to baseline policies without compromising task success, across diverse environments
claims.direction: favors potential-field-guided flow matching for robustness to obstacles/unstructured environments over standard flow-matching policies
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: HiPolicy: Hierarchical Multi-Frequency Action Chunking for Policy Learning

claims.claim: Fixed-frequency action chunking approaches cannot achieve both long-horizon dependency modeling AND fine-grained closed-loop control simultaneously; HiPolicy jointly predicts action sequences at DIFFERENT FREQUENCIES (extracting/fusing hierarchical features from history aligned to each frequency) to capture both coarse high-level plans and precise reactive motions, with an entropy-guided execution mechanism that adaptively balances long-horizon planning against fine-grained control based on action uncertainty
claims.direction: favors multi-frequency, hierarchical action chunking (with uncertainty-adaptive execution) over standard fixed single-frequency action chunking for jointly achieving long-horizon coherence and fine-grained reactivity
claims.conditions: diverse simulated benchmarks + real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: HiPolicy can be seamlessly integrated into existing 2D and 3D generative policies, delivering consistent performance improvements while significantly enhancing execution efficiency
claims.direction: favors this multi-frequency chunking mechanism as a plug-in enhancement to existing (e.g., diffusion-based) generative policies for both accuracy and efficiency gains, rather than requiring a new policy architecture from scratch
claims.conditions: same evaluation suite

why_deep_read: Directly targets our core Q06 tension (execution horizon vs. reactivity/smoothness at chunk boundaries) with a general mechanism explicitly designed to plug into existing generative (2D/3D) policies and reported to improve BOTH performance and execution efficiency on real-world tasks — a strong, generically-applicable candidate fix for our jerky-chunk-boundary problem that seems more directly retrofittable than some of the other chunking papers we've seen.

title: iFLYTEK-Embodied-Omni Technical Report

claims.claim: A unified 'brain-cerebellum' architecture combines vision-language and video-generation components (high-level 'brain': instruction understanding, task planning, progress tracking, future visual-state prediction) with an action-generation component (low-level 'cerebellum': converts planned subgoals and shared multimodal context into executable action chunks), communicating through shared multimodal self-attention rather than a cascaded pipeline
claims.direction: favors a jointly-trained, shared-attention multimodal architecture over cascaded pipelines (that first synthesize future observations then infer actions) to avoid interface bottlenecks and compounding prediction errors
claims.conditions: large-scale combined action-annotated and action-free embodied video + general image-text data, four-stage progressive training

claims.claim: The model combines action-annotated and action-free embodied videos from human demonstrations and robot interactions with embodied reasoning/perception data, using a four-stage strategy that progressively trains the VLM, video-generation model, and action-generation model before joint fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors staged pretraining across heterogeneous action-labeled and action-free data sources with a final joint fine-tuning stage, over training all components jointly from scratch
claims.conditions: large combined dataset

title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

claims.claim: Training the VLM with a future-prediction objective on cross-embodiment data drives a shared query representation to capture object motion, contact, and interaction-induced scene changes, forming shared dynamics priors usable across heterogeneous robots
claims.direction: favors a future-prediction auxiliary objective for learning cross-embodiment-transferable dynamics representations over embodiment-specific representation learning
claims.conditions: simulation + real-world, multiple embodiments

claims.claim: An embodiment-specific Mixture-of-Experts action head (shared attention layers for common temporal action structure + embodiment-specific feed-forward experts) translates shared dynamics priors into each embodiment's native action space, avoiding manual pre-alignment of heterogeneous action formats; achieves 98.0% on LIBERO, 59.25% on RoboCasa-GR1, 89.02% on RoboTwin 2.0

claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboCasa-GR1, RoboTwin 2.0 sim benchmarks + real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Leveraging diverse cross-embodiment visual and interaction data (rather than only single-embodiment data) via shared dynamics priors improves cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: favors mixing cross-embodiment data via a shared-dynamics-prior objective over training separately per embodiment
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies

claims.claim: Training VLA policies on limited, homogeneous demonstrations encourages 'modality entanglement' (spurious inter-sensor correlations rather than task-relevant signal), which under real-world occlusions/distractors manifests as nuisance sensitivity to corrupted uninformative sensors and single-modality insufficiency when only one informative sensor remains; Evidence-Gated Regularization (EGR) — a zero-inference-time-overhead training objective that gates invariance/sufficiency consistency losses by per-frame, per-sensor task-relevance — improves simulated success rates by +31% (full modalities), +75% (uninformative-sensor corruption), and +120% (single-sensor fallback)
claims.direction: favors an evidence-gated (task-relevance-conditioned) multimodal regularization objective, added at zero inference cost, over naive multimodal fusion trained on limited/homogeneous demonstrations, for robustness to sensor corruption/occlusion
claims.conditions: BEHAVIOR-1K-based benchmark (diagnostic suite + 47 rollout-based skills), plus two real-robot setups (bimanual Kinova+3 RGB cameras; single-arm MELFA with vision+GelSight tactile)

claims.claim: Under physical-object distractors, EGR boosts real-robot success rate from 30% to 85% on the bimanual camera setup (+183%) and from 55% to 70% on the tactile setup (+27%)
claims.direction: favors evidence-gated modality regularization specifically for robustness to physical distractors on real hardware
claims.conditions: real-robot bimanual and single-arm setups

why_deep_read: This directly names our situation (training on limited, homogeneous demonstrations causing brittle reliance on spurious sensor correlations) as the root cause of exactly the kind of camera/occlusion/distractor fragility we've observed, and proposes a training-time-only fix with ZERO inference overhead and very large real-robot gains under corruption/distractors — an unusually strong, low-cost, and directly relevant candidate for improving our SmolVLA fine-tune's robustness without collecting more data or adding inference latency.

title: Skel-WAM: A Hand-Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Human-to-Robot Manipulation Transfer

claims.claim: Aligning human and robot motion through a common hand-skeleton topology (skeleton overlays + structured 2.5D keypoints) lets Video and Keypoint Experts jointly learn visual/skeletal dynamics from BOTH human and robot demonstrations without requiring robot action labels for the human videos; human-robot cotraining more than doubles real-world success on task variations absent from robot training data, from 38.89% to 86.11%
claims.direction: favors a shared hand-skeleton interface for cotraining with unlabeled human video to expand task/variation coverage beyond what robot-only demonstrations provide
claims.conditions: four real-world bimanual tasks + seven simulated tasks

claims.claim: A separate robot-trained Action Expert maps shared video/keypoint dynamics predictions to executable controls, achieving average success rates of 79.86% (real) and 63.29% (sim), surpassing the strongest baseline by 22.22 and 8.28 percentage points respectively
claims.direction: favors separating shared dynamics-prediction experts from a dedicated robot action-decoding expert over a single monolithic policy
claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: NeRF in the Palm of Your Hand: Corrective Augmentation for Robotics via Novel-View Synthesis

claims.claim: SPARTN uses NeRFs to synthetically inject corrective viewpoint perturbations (and compute the corresponding corrective actions) into eye-in-hand (wrist-camera) visual demonstrations, fully offline with no additional expert supervision or environment interaction; in a simulated 6-DoF visual grasping benchmark this improves success rates by 2.8x over imitation learning without corrective augmentation, even outperforming some methods using online expert supervision

claims.claim: The technique is specifically designed for and validated on eye-in-hand (wrist) camera policies, distilling NeRF-derived geometric information into a real-time reactive RGB-only policy usable without depth sensors at deployment
claims.direction: favors this NeRF-based corrective augmentation as a wrist-camera-specific technique for building reactive closed-loop policies from limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: same setting

claims.conditions: real-world 6-DoF grasping from limited human demonstrations

claims.conditions: same evaluation

title: Predictive Preference Learning from Human Interventions

claims.claim: Bootstrapping each human intervention into L future time steps ('preference horizon', assuming the agent/human repeat their action/intervention) and applying preference optimization over these future states propagates expert corrections into safety-critical regions the agent is expected to explore, significantly improving learning efficiency and reducing the number of human demonstrations/interventions needed
claims.direction: favors propagating single-timestep human-intervention signals forward into a preference horizon over treating interventions purely as corrections at the intervened state alone, for more data-efficient interactive imitation learning
claims.conditions: autonomous driving + robotic manipulation benchmarks; theoretical analysis on choosing the preference horizon L

claims.conditions: same benchmarks

title: Parse-Augment-Distill: Learning Generalizable Bimanual Visuomotor Policies from Single Human Video

claims.claim: PAD learns generalizable bimanual manipulation policies from a SINGLE human demonstration video, by (a) parsing it into a robot-executable keypoint-action trajectory, (b) using bimanual task-and-motion-planning to augment the demonstration at scale WITHOUT simulators or image rollouts, and (c) distilling augmented trajectories into a keypoint-conditioned policy; this outperforms SOTA bimanual demonstration-augmentation methods (which rely on simulator rollouts + image policies) in both success rate and sample/cost efficiency

claims.claim: A keypoint-conditioned policy (distilled from the augmented trajectories) generalizes to unseen spatial arrangements, object instances, and background distractors, starting from just one human video
claims.direction: favors keypoint/state-based action representations over raw image-conditioned policies for category-level generalization from minimal demonstration data
claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation

claims.claim: The resulting one-shot policies generalize across unseen spatial arrangements, object instances, and background distractors
claims.direction: favors this single-video, keypoint-based pipeline for robustness to spatial/object/background variation from minimal data
claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation

title: PDFactor: Learning Tri-Perspective View Policy Diffusion Field for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Modeling the 6-DoF action distribution as a hybrid triplane (tri-perspective view) latent diffusion field — decomposing the 3D point cloud into three orthogonal feature planes, with a small denoising network acting both as a loss function and as an action-gradient decoder for sampling at inference — combines the spatial awareness of explicit representations with the arbitrary resolution of implicit representations, outperforming SOTA approaches across diverse manipulation tasks on RLBench
claims.direction: favors this hybrid explicit/implicit (triplane diffusion field) action-distribution representation over purely explicit (voxel/point) or purely implicit representations, for jointly achieving accuracy, inference efficiency, and scalability
claims.conditions: RLBench sim benchmark + real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: PDFactor can effectively learn multi-task policies from a limited number of human demonstrations, achieving promising accuracy on a variety of real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors this triplane-diffusion-field representation for sample-efficient multi-task learning from limited demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks

title: Advancing Omnimodal Embodied Agents from Isolated Skills to Everyday Physical Autonomy

claims.claim: An adaptive hierarchical memory with event-boundary-driven compression achieves sub-linear (near-flat) context/token growth over long-horizon operation (100k+ accumulated interaction tokens) while maintaining temporal coherence, unlike agent frameworks that accumulate unbounded context
claims.direction: favors event-boundary-driven hierarchical memory compression over naive unbounded context accumulation for long-horizon embodied task memory
claims.conditions: 40 real-world long-horizon tasks across two robotic platforms + IoT devices

claims.claim: This memory design keeps token consumption near-flat despite long accumulated interaction history, elevating mid-scale open-weight models to proprietary-level performance

claims.conditions: same real-world evaluation

title: Move-Then-Operate: Behavioral Phasing for Human-Like Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Explicitly decoupling manipulation into coarse-relocation ('move') and contact-critical-interaction ('operate') phases via a dual-expert policy routed by a learnable phase selector (with phase labels auto-generated via an MLLM pipeline conditioned on end-effector velocity and subtask decomposition) achieves 68.9% average success on RoboTwin2, outperforming a monolithic pi_0 baseline by 24 percentage points
claims.direction: favors an explicit dual-expert, phase-routed architecture (structural inductive bias separating transport-like motion from contact-rich manipulation) over a single monolithic policy that conflates both regimes
claims.conditions: RoboTwin2 benchmark

claims.claim: The phase-disentangled architecture matches or exceeds models trained on 10x more data and reaches peak performance in 40% fewer training steps
claims.direction: favors this architectural inductive bias (move/operate phase separation) as a way to achieve data efficiency equivalent to a 10x larger dataset, rather than scaling data alone
claims.conditions: same benchmark

claims.claim: Isolating phase-specific dynamics (transport vs. contact-critical interaction) via separate experts is presented as addressing the heterogeneous regimes that a monolithic action-chunking policy must otherwise conflate
claims.direction: favors phase-aware routing of chunked action generation over a single uniform chunking/action-generation scheme across qualitatively different motion phases
claims.conditions: same benchmark

title: Seeing Realism from Simulation: Efficient Video Transfer for Vision-Language-Action Data Augmentation

claims.claim: An efficient video-augmentation pipeline (extracting structured conditions via segmentation/captioning, rewriting captions to diversify environments, using a conditional video-transfer model with a diffusion feature-reuse mechanism for fast generation, plus coreset sampling to select a compact non-redundant subset) converts simulated VLA videos into realistic training videos while preserving task semantics/action trajectories, improving RDT-1B by 8% on RoboTwin 2.0 and pi_0 by 5.1% on LIBERO-Plus
