title: MaskHarness-WAM: Instance-Grounded Harnessing for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: For long-horizon tasks involving multiple visually-identical objects manipulated in order, connecting high-level task planning to a limited-horizon low-level policy through re-observed, re-verified target instance masks at each subtask boundary (rather than relying on the low-level policy alone to track which instance and when to transition) substantially outperforms limited-horizon policies on sequential multi-object manipulation on a real robot
claims.direction: favors explicit, re-verified instance-level target tracking/masking across subtask boundaries over relying on a limited-horizon policy's implicit memory for long-horizon, multi-identical-object task progress tracking
claims.conditions: real robot platform, sequential multi-object manipulation with identical-appearance objects

title: Equivariant Offline Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: For rotation-symmetric robotic manipulation tasks, SO(2)-equivariant versions of Conservative Q-Learning and Implicit Q-Learning outperform their non-equivariant counterparts specifically in the low-data (limited-demonstration) offline RL regime
claims.direction: favors incorporating SO(2)-equivariance as an inductive bias into offline RL value/policy learning over non-equivariant architectures, when the number of demonstrations is limited
claims.conditions: offline RL, rotation-symmetric manipulation tasks, limited number of demonstrations

claims.claim: Equivariant neural network architectures (SO(2)-equivariant CQL/IQL) empirically improve offline learning algorithms in the low-data regime
claims.direction: favors symmetry-aware (equivariant) action-value/policy architectures over standard architectures for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: limited demonstrations, rotation-symmetric tasks

title: CLIP-RT: Learning Language-Conditioned Robotic Policies from Natural Language Supervision

claims.claim: CLIP-RT, adapting the pretrained CLIP model to predict language-based motion primitives via contrastive imitation learning, outperforms OpenVLA (7B parameters) by 24% in average real-world success rate while using 7x fewer parameters (1B)
claims.direction: favors a small, CLIP-based contrastive imitation-learning VLA over a much larger (7B) autoregressive VLA, achieving both better performance and far greater parameter efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world evaluations, novel manipulation skills, trained on Open X-Embodiment plus in-domain fine-tuning data

claims.claim: Natural language supervision (e.g., 'move the arm to the right') collected from non-experts, further augmented, is sufficient to train language-conditioned visuomotor policies via contrastive learning of language-based motion primitives, without requiring specialized teleoperation hardware or expertise
claims.direction: favors natural-language-supervised data collection (accessible to non-experts) plus contrastive language-conditioned imitation learning over expert teleoperation-based data collection for language-conditioned policies
claims.conditions: real-world data collection framework, non-expert supervision

claims.claim: CLIP-RT achieves a 93.1% average success rate on the LIBERO benchmark with an inference throughput of 163 Hz
claims.direction: demonstrates that a small contrastive-learning-based VLA can achieve both high success rate and very high inference frequency (163Hz), relevant for real-time control
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation benchmark

title: 3D FlowMatch Actor: Unified 3D Policy for Single- and Dual-Arm Manipulation

claims.claim: 3D FlowMatch Actor (3DFA) combines flow matching for trajectory prediction with 3D pretrained visual scene representations, using 3D relative attention between action and visual tokens during denoising; it sets a new state of the art on 74 RLBench (unimanual) tasks by directly predicting dense end-effector trajectories, eliminating the need for motion planning, and on the bimanual PerAct2 benchmark outperforms the next-best method by an absolute margin of 41.4%
claims.direction: favors combining flow matching with 3D-relative-attention visual-action token interaction over prior 3D diffusion-based policies or motion-planning-dependent pipelines, for both single- and dual-arm manipulation
claims.conditions: 74 RLBench tasks (unimanual), bimanual PerAct2 benchmark, plus extensive real-world evaluations

claims.claim: 3D pretrained visual scene representations combined with flow matching enable strong performance without requiring motion planning, using 3D-aware perception for action generation
claims.direction: favors 3D-pretrained visual representations over 2D/RGB-only representations for precise trajectory-level action prediction
claims.conditions: sim (RLBench, PerAct2) and real-world evaluations

claims.claim: Through flow matching plus targeted system-level and architectural optimizations, 3DFA achieves over 30x faster training and inference than previous 3D diffusion-based policies without sacrificing performance, and in real-world evaluations surpasses strong baselines with up to 1000x more parameters and significantly more pretraining
claims.direction: favors a much smaller, flow-matching-based 3D policy architecture over far larger (up to 1000x more parameters) 3D diffusion-based baselines, achieving both better performance and dramatically lower compute cost
claims.conditions: real-world evaluations against baselines with up to 1000x more parameters and pretraining

why_deep_read: Reports an extreme efficiency result directly relevant to our small-model, low-compute constraint — beating baselines with up to 1000x more parameters while being >30x faster to train/run, using flow matching plus 3D representations and eliminating motion planning; this could be one of the most impactful architecture choices to evaluate for our SO-101 setup if it holds up outside RLBench/PerAct2.

title: Human-in-the-loop Online Rejection Sampling for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Hi-ORS, a post-training method combining rejection sampling (filtering negatively-rewarded samples for stable value estimation) with reward-weighted supervised training and asynchronous online human-in-the-loop corrections, fine-tunes a pi-base policy to master contact-rich manipulation in just 1.5 hours of real-world training, outperforming both RL and IL baselines substantially in effectiveness and efficiency across three real-world tasks and two embodiments
claims.direction: favors rejection-sampling-based, reward-weighted post-training with online human corrections over either pure RL fine-tuning (unstable) or pure offline imitation learning (underperforms), for fast, stable, data-efficient real-world policy improvement
claims.conditions: real-world, three tasks, two embodiments, pi-base (flow-matching-style) policy, 1.5 hours of real-world training

claims.claim: The fine-tuned policy exhibits strong test-time scalability by reliably executing complex error-recovery behaviors, learned explicitly from human-in-the-loop correction guidance during training
claims.direction: favors training explicitly on human-intervention/correction data to induce error-recovery behaviors, over training only on successful demonstration trajectories
claims.conditions: real-world, contact-rich manipulation

title: SemAnCorr: Semantic Anchored Correspondence for Zero-Shot Manipulation Skill Transfer

claims.claim: SemAnCorr, a training-free framework establishing dense correspondence via semantically-consistent anchor regions and functional-map propagation over the object surface, uses a single demonstration to enable substantially more reliable zero-shot manipulation-skill transfer to previously unseen, geometrically-diverse objects than existing correspondence methods, achieving 90.8% semantic accuracy on a PartNet-Mobility-based benchmark
claims.direction: favors semantically-anchored, training-free geometric correspondence over nearest-neighbor feature matching for transferring a skill learned from a single demonstration to novel object geometries sharing the same function
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, single demonstration, previously unseen objects, PartNet-Mobility-based benchmark

claims.claim: Preserving both semantic consistency and geometric coherence in correspondence translates directly into improved real-world zero-shot manipulation performance on unseen objects
claims.direction: favors correspondence methods that jointly optimize semantic and geometric coherence for generalizing manipulation skills to novel objects
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, unseen objects

title: LIDEA: Human-to-Robot Imitation Learning via Implicit Feature Distillation and Explicit Geometry Alignment

claims.claim: LIDEA aligns human and robot representations in a shared latent space via a dual-stage transitive distillation pipeline (2D visual domain) and an embodiment-agnostic explicit geometric alignment strategy (3D domain) that decouples embodiment from interaction geometry, avoiding the visual artifacts of prior visual-editing-based cross-embodiment transfer; results show human demonstration data can substitute up to 80% of costly robot demonstrations without loss of policy quality
claims.direction: favors implicit feature distillation plus explicit 3D geometric alignment (rather than visual editing) for using human video to reduce robot demonstration requirements, achieving up to 80% substitution of robot demos with human data
claims.conditions: human video demonstrations plus reduced robot demonstrations, cross-embodiment (human hand to robot arm) transfer

claims.claim: The framework successfully transfers unseen patterns from human videos for out-of-distribution generalization, validated from both data-efficiency and OOD-robustness perspectives
claims.direction: favors human-video-derived embodiment-agnostic geometric alignment for OOD generalization over robot-only training data
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment transfer, OOD evaluation

title: Learning Geometrically-Grounded 3D Visual Representations for View-Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A single-view 3D pretraining paradigm (point-cloud reconstruction plus feed-forward Gaussian splatting under multi-view supervision at pretraining time only, single-view at inference) combined with multi-step distillation into the policy shows strong zero-shot view generalization: success-rate drops of only 22.0% and 29.7% under moderate and large viewpoint shifts respectively, versus 41.6% and 51.5% drops for the prior state-of-the-art method
claims.direction: favors single-view-at-inference 3D-geometric pretraining (with multi-view supervision only during pretraining) over relying on multi-view observations at inference or standard 2D representations, specifically for robustness to camera-viewpoint shift
claims.conditions: 12 RLBench tasks for main comparison, 6 representative tasks for viewpoint-shift evaluation, single-view inference

claims.claim: The single-view 3D pretraining approach outperforms the previous state-of-the-art method by 12.7% in average success rate across 12 RLBench tasks by learning holistic and fine-grained geometric structure (versus incomplete/partial scene modeling in prior 3D-aware methods)
claims.direction: favors holistic single-view 3D geometric pretraining (point cloud + Gaussian splatting) over incomplete/partial 3D scene modeling approaches
claims.conditions: RLBench simulation, 12 tasks

title: HITL-D: Human In The Loop Diffusion Assisted Shared Control

claims.claim: A shared-control framework where a diffusion-based policy provides autonomous end-effector orientation updates (conditioned on scene point cloud and end-effector position) while a human controls fewer joystick axes reduced average task completion time by 40%, decreased perceived workload by 37%, and improved usability ratings versus traditional teleoperation, in a 12-participant study on multi-step, insertion, and fine manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors diffusion-assisted shared control (autonomy handling orientation while human controls fewer axes) over traditional full-manual teleoperation, for reducing operator workload and improving efficiency during demonstration/data collection
claims.conditions: user study with 12 participants, multi-step/insertion/fine manipulation tasks, real robot

title: FORGE: Towards Functional Tool-Use Generalization via Keypoint Trajectory Reasoning

claims.claim: Decoupling functional reasoning (predicting generalizable 2D keypoint trajectories from action-free data) from action execution (grounding trajectories into robot actions using limited demonstrations) achieves over 2x improvement in average success rate on unseen tools versus state-of-the-art methods, on a seven-tool hitting-function benchmark in both simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors 2D keypoint trajectories as an intermediate representation (over affordance images or human-video prompts) for functional generalization, and decoupling reasoning (from cheap action-free data) from execution (needing only limited demonstrations)
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation, seven-tool benchmark, functional generalization to unseen tools, limited demonstrations for grounding

claims.claim: Among intermediate representations tested (affordance images, human video prompts, 2D keypoint trajectories), keypoint trajectories best balance functional expressiveness and action groundability
claims.direction: favors keypoint-trajectory intermediate representations over affordance-image or human-video-prompt representations for grounding functional reasoning into robot actions
claims.conditions: real-world and simulation, tool-use generalization

title: OnEvoMemory: Evolving Memory through Online Robot Rollouts for Pretrained Robot Policies

claims.claim: A value-guided memory module that maintains recent context, high-value experiences, and salient transitions (initialized from offline demonstrations, then refined by both successful and unsuccessful online rollouts) helps a pretrained VLA policy recognize task-stage transitions and avoid repeating completed subtasks, improving performance on long-horizon manipulation benchmarks through both offline initialization and online memory evolution
claims.direction: favors learned, outcome-driven memory-retention policies (rather than external models or predefined update rules) for tracking completed subtasks in long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: long-horizon manipulation benchmarks, pretrained VLA base policy, real/sim unspecified

title: TACIT: Tactile Contact Supervision for Spatial Attention in Dexterous Manipulation

claims.claim: Using measured tactile contacts from teleoperated demonstrations (Gaussian targets over preceding camera point clouds) to supervise spatial attention during training only, TACIT achieves 66.7% and 73.3% real-robot success on ball placement and peg insertion respectively with only ten demonstrations per task, versus 10.0%/20.0% for input-matched 3D visuotactile fusion and 20.0%/43.3% for vision-only DP3
claims.direction: favors using tactile-derived spatial supervision (even if only during training, guiding what the policy attends to) over pure vision-only or naive visuotactile input fusion, for learning reliable approach/placement behavior from very few (ten) demonstrations
claims.conditions: real robot, ten demonstrations per task, requires tactile sensing during teleoperation for training supervision (tactile remains an input at inference too)

title: Pre-training Contextualized World Models with In-the-wild Videos for Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Explicitly separating context (background/appearance) modeling from dynamics modeling in a world model pretrained on abundant in-the-wild (non-robot) videos significantly improves the sample efficiency of downstream model-based RL across robotic manipulation, locomotion, and autonomous driving domains, compared to world models that entangle context and dynamics
claims.direction: favors context/dynamics-disentangled world-model pretraining on diverse in-the-wild video (not domain-specific/simulated data) over standard entangled world models, for sample-efficient downstream visual control
claims.conditions: in-the-wild video pretraining, downstream model-based RL across manipulation, locomotion, driving

claims.claim: In-the-wild videos contain complex contextual factors (backgrounds, textures) that can be explicitly factored out via a context encoder so the latent dynamics model concentrates on essential temporal variations, enabling knowledge transfer between distinct scenes
claims.direction: favors explicit context/appearance factoring (rather than treating background variation as pure augmentation noise) when pretraining on diverse visual data for cross-scene transfer
claims.conditions: in-the-wild video pretraining

title: Speeding up 6-DoF Grasp Sampling with Quality-Diversity

claims.claim: Quality-Diversity (QD) algorithms combined with priors substantially outperform standard 6-DoF grasp sampling schemes for generating diverse, high-performing grasp poses in simulation across grippers with 2-5 fingers, and QD-generated grasps maintain sim-to-real transferability when deployed on a 2-finger gripper and an Allegro hand
claims.direction: favors Quality-Diversity optimization (over standard grasp-sampling schemes) for efficiently generating large, diverse synthetic grasp datasets that transfer to real hardware
claims.conditions: simulation for generation, real-world validation of sim-to-real transfer, multiple gripper types

title: Haptic-ACT: Bridging Human Intuition with Compliant Robotic Manipulation via Immersive VR

claims.claim: An immersive VR teleoperation setup with haptic feedback significantly reduces demonstrator fingertip forces compared to systems without haptic feedback (enabling more delicate demonstrations), evaluated on a pick-and-place task with 50 demonstration episodes
claims.direction: favors haptic-feedback VR teleoperation over standard (non-haptic) teleoperation interfaces for collecting higher-quality, gentler demonstrations, at a similar demonstration count (50 episodes) to our target budget
claims.conditions: real-world pick-and-place task, 50 demonstration episodes, VR teleoperation with haptic feedback

claims.claim: Haptic Action Chunking with Transformers (Haptic-ACT), an ACT extension incorporating haptic/force information, teaches more compliant manipulation than the original ACT, validated in MuJoCo simulation and on a real robot
claims.direction: favors extending an ACT-style action-chunking architecture with haptic/force conditioning over the original (position-only) ACT for compliant manipulation
claims.conditions: MuJoCo simulation and real robot, pick-and-place task

title: H3DP: Triply-Hierarchical Diffusion Policy for Visuomotor Learning

claims.claim: Explicitly coupling visual perception and action generation through three hierarchy levels (depth-aware input layering, multi-scale visual representations, and a hierarchically-conditioned diffusion process aligning coarse-to-fine action generation with corresponding visual features) yields a +27.5% average relative improvement over baselines across 44 simulation tasks and superior performance on 4 challenging bimanual real-world manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors tightly coupling multi-scale, depth-aware visual features with a hierarchically-structured (coarse-to-fine) diffusion action generation process over standard diffusion policies that treat vision and action generation as loosely coupled
claims.conditions: 44 simulation tasks plus 4 bimanual real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Depth-aware input layering (organizing RGB-D observations by depth) combined with multi-scale visual representations (encoding semantic features at varying granularity) strengthens the vision-action coupling compared to standard single-scale visual encoders
claims.direction: favors depth-aware, multi-scale visual encoding over standard single-scale RGB(-D) encoding for diffusion-policy visuomotor learning
claims.conditions: 44 simulation tasks, 4 real-world bimanual tasks

title: Expertise need not monopolize: Action-Specialized Mixture of Experts for Vision-Language-Action Learning

claims.claim: AdaMoE inherits pretrained weights from a dense VLA model and scales up only the action expert by substituting feedforward layers with sparsely-activated Mixture-of-Experts layers (decoupling expert selection from expert weighting via an independent scale adapter), avoiding the need to train a new VLA from scratch while balancing model capacity with real-time computational efficiency
claims.direction: favors reusing pretrained dense VLA weights and sparsely scaling only the action expert (via decoupled MoE) over training a larger dense model from scratch, for efficient capacity scaling under data/compute scarcity
claims.conditions: builds on pretrained dense VLA weights, evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world experiments

claims.claim: AdaMoE consistently outperforms the baseline dense action-expert model, delivering 1.8% gains on LIBERO, 9.3% on RoboTwin, and a substantial 21.5% improvement in real-world experiments
claims.direction: favors a decoupled sparse-MoE action-expert architecture over a standard dense feedforward action expert
claims.conditions: LIBERO, RoboTwin sim benchmarks plus real-world robotic manipulation

title: DyWA: Dynamics-Adaptive World Action Model for Generalizable Non-Prehensile Manipulation

claims.claim: DyWA uses only single-view point cloud observations (rather than existing learning-based methods that heavily rely on multi-view cameras and precise pose tracking) and still improves success rate by 31.5% over baselines in simulation
claims.direction: favors single-view point-cloud input with dynamics-adaptive world-action modeling over requiring multi-view cameras and precise pose tracking
claims.conditions: simulation, single-view point cloud, non-prehensile manipulation

claims.claim: By jointly predicting future states while adapting to dynamics variations (object mass, table friction) based on historical trajectories, DyWA achieves 68% average success in real-world experiments, generalizing across diverse object geometries and varying physical conditions including slippery surfaces and half-filled water bottles
claims.direction: favors world-action models that explicitly adapt to physical/dynamics variation via historical-trajectory conditioning over policies assuming fixed physical conditions, for generalization to varying friction/mass/contents
claims.conditions: real-world, diverse object geometries, varying friction and mass, non-prehensile manipulation

claims.claim: Unifying the modeling of geometry, state, physics, and robot actions (jointly predicting future states while adapting to dynamics based on historical trajectories) enables more robust policy learning under partial observability than treating action learning and dynamics adaptation separately
claims.direction: favors a unified dynamics-adaptive world-action model (joint future-state prediction + dynamics adaptation) as an auxiliary/architectural design over standard action-only policy learning
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world, partial observability

title: EfficientFlow: Efficient Equivariant Flow Policy Learning for Embodied AI

claims.claim: Bringing equivariance into flow matching (theoretically proven: with an isotropic Gaussian prior and an equivariant velocity-prediction network, the resulting action distribution remains equivariant) leads to improved generalization and substantially reduced data demands compared to standard (non-equivariant) flow-matching policies
claims.direction: favors building equivariance directly into the flow-matching velocity network over standard flow matching, to reduce the amount of demonstration data needed
claims.conditions: a wide range of robotic manipulation benchmarks, theoretical proof plus empirical validation

claims.claim: A novel acceleration-regularization strategy (using a derived surrogate loss trainable from only conditional trajectories, since direct marginal-trajectory acceleration is intractable) enables dramatically faster inference/sampling for the flow-matching policy without sacrificing performance
claims.direction: favors adding an acceleration-regularization auxiliary loss during training to enable faster (fewer-step) sampling at inference, over standard flow-matching training that only optimizes for trajectory accuracy
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation benchmarks, limited-data regime

claims.claim: Across a wide range of robotic manipulation benchmarks, EfficientFlow achieves competitive or superior performance under limited data while offering dramatically faster inference than standard generative (flow-matching) policies
claims.direction: favors the equivariance-plus-acceleration-regularized flow-matching design over standard flow-matching or diffusion action heads, specifically for the combination of low-data and low-latency requirements
claims.conditions: robotic manipulation benchmarks, limited-data regime

title: GeoDiff: Geometry-Conditioned Diffusion Policy for Refined Robotic Trajectory Generation

claims.claim: Constructing object-centric geometric representations via clustering-based point-cloud segmentation and encoding relational spatial-dependency features between robot and surrounding objects (rather than conditioning only on raw point clouds or robot states) improves task success rate and motion smoothness by over 15% versus state-of-the-art diffusion and optimization-based baselines across three simulated manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors object-centric relational geometric conditioning over raw point-cloud/state conditioning for diffusion-policy trajectory generation
claims.conditions: three simulated manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: Generating multiple stochastic trajectory candidates from the diffusion policy and using a physics-aware evaluation module (scoring smoothness, goal accuracy, collision safety) to select the optimal candidate, combined with a differentiable physical-consistency loss during training, improves reliability over standard diffusion policies that output a single trajectory without physics-aware post-selection
claims.direction: favors multi-candidate diffusion sampling plus physics-aware candidate selection over single-sample diffusion decoding for reliable trajectory generation
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation benchmarks

claims.claim: The physics-aware evaluation/selection module explicitly scores and selects trajectories for smoothness, contributing to the reported motion-smoothness improvement
claims.direction: favors explicit post-hoc smoothness scoring/selection among diffusion-generated trajectory candidates over relying on the diffusion model alone to produce smooth motion
claims.conditions: simulated manipulation benchmarks

title: PLAN-MVP: Planning for Learning-Enabled Autonomous Navigation and Manipulation via Perception

claims.claim: A modular hybrid framework using a VLM only as a high-level, zero-shot task-planning 'brain' while delegating execution to lightweight classical modules (object detection, RGB-D pose estimation, inverse kinematics, joint-level control) avoids the substantial compute and large training datasets required by fully end-to-end VLA approaches, with the RGB-D pipeline achieving ~5% position error and the IK solver converging reliably with low end-effector error
claims.direction: favors a modular hybrid (VLM-for-planning plus classical control-for-execution) architecture over fully end-to-end VLA models, to avoid expensive end-to-end training while remaining practical for real-time deployment
claims.conditions: individual-component validation only (position error, IK convergence); no full task-success-rate results reported in the abstract

title: AR-VLA: True Autoregressive Action Expert for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Standard VLA models and diffusion policies reset temporal context with each new observation and predict actions reactively in chunks; a standalone autoregressive Action Expert instead generates actions as a continuous causal sequence, maintaining its own long-lived memory, and uses a re-anchoring mechanism that mathematically accounts for perception staleness during both training and inference to synchronize fast control with slow reasoning, exhibiting substantially smoother action trajectories than chunk-based action heads while maintaining or exceeding SOTA reactive VLA task success rates
claims.direction: favors a continuous, history-maintaining autoregressive action expert with explicit staleness re-anchoring over resetting, chunk-based reactive action generation, specifically for action-trajectory smoothness under asynchronous perception/control frequency mismatch
claims.conditions: simulated and real-robot manipulation tasks, comparison against chunk-based action heads for both specialist and generalist policies

claims.claim: The autoregressive Action Expert can effectively replace traditional chunk-based action heads while enabling independent pretraining of 'kinematic syntax' and modular integration with heavy perception backbones
claims.direction: favors a standalone autoregressive continuous action head (decoupled from and modularly integrated with the perception backbone) as an alternative to standard chunk-based diffusion/regression action heads
claims.conditions: simulated and real-robot manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The Action Expert maintains its own long-lived memory rather than resetting temporal context with each new observation, making it inherently history-aware
claims.direction: favors an action head with persistent internal memory over ones that reset context per observation, for spatio-temporally consistent action generation
claims.conditions: simulated and real-robot manipulation tasks

title: Learning Force-Regulated Manipulation with a Low-Cost Tactile-Force-Controlled Gripper

claims.claim: Compared to position control, direct force control (using a low-cost ~$150 tactile-force-controlled gripper) significantly improves grasp stability and task performance on five real-world tasks requiring precise force regulation; a framework (RETAF) decoupling high-frequency reactive force control (from wrist images and tactile feedback) from lower-frequency end-effector pose/gripper-state prediction outperforms baselines and integrates with various base policies
claims.direction: favors decoupling high-frequency force/grip control from lower-frequency pose prediction, and using direct force control over pure position control, for force-sensitive object manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world, five tasks requiring precise force regulation, requires custom low-cost tactile-force gripper hardware not present in a standard position-controlled parallel-jaw setup

title: DeformGen: Dynamics-Based Topology Augmentation for Deformable Manipulation Policy Learning

claims.claim: For deformable-object manipulation, augmenting demonstrations by applying localized physical disturbances and forward-simulating dynamics (to obtain topology-coherent, physically-plausible states) and transferring source trajectories via deformation-field warping (rather than low-dimensional pose perturbation or rigid-style trajectory transfer) generally improves policy learning compared to training on original demonstrations alone or with rigid-style augmentation baselines
claims.direction: favors dynamics-based, deformation-aware demonstration augmentation over rigid-pose-perturbation-style augmentation for deformable object manipulation
claims.conditions: high-fidelity simulated deformable manipulation benchmarks

title: MemoAct: Atkinson–Shiffrin-Inspired Hierarchical Memory-Augmented Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A hierarchical memory architecture inspired by the Atkinson-Shiffrin model (sensory memory filtering immediate perceptual input, lossless short-term memory for precise task-state tracking, compressed long-term memory for long-horizon retention), evaluated on a new benchmark (MemoryRTBench, built on RoboTwin 2.0) covering sequential, spatial, and episodic memory dimensions, achieves superior performance compared to both Markovian baselines and other history-aware policies in simulated and real-world scenarios
claims.direction: favors a multi-tiered (sensory/short-term/long-term) memory architecture, with each tier addressing a distinct memory bottleneck, over a single uniform memory mechanism or simply extending the observation window, for both precise task-state tracking and robust long-horizon retention
claims.conditions: simulated (RoboTwin 2.0-based MemoryRTBench) and real-world manipulation scenarios

title: The Treachery of Images: Bayesian Scene Keypoints for Deep Policy Learning in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Bayesian approach to tracking scale-invariant keypoints over time (BASK) resolves inherent ambiguities in camera images, enabling keypoint tracking on symmetrical objects and objects that are occluded or out of the current field of view, demonstrating superior utility for policy learning compared to other representation-learning techniques on challenging multi-object manipulation tasks from wrist-camera observations
claims.direction: favors probabilistic, temporally-tracked keypoint representations (that persist through occlusion/out-of-view periods) over representations assuming full scene observability, for policy learning from a single wrist camera
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world robotic experiments, multi-object manipulation, wrist camera observations only

claims.claim: The method shows outstanding robustness towards disturbances such as clutter, occlusions, and noisy depth measurements, and generalizes to unseen objects, using only wrist-camera input
claims.direction: favors robust temporal keypoint tracking from a single wrist camera over requiring additional fixed/multi-view cameras for robustness to clutter/occlusion/noisy depth
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world, wrist camera only, unseen objects

title: No, to the Right

claims.claim: LILAC (Language-Informed Latent Actions with Corrections) learns a low-dimensional, language-conditioned control space that a human can use to give real-time natural-language corrections (e.g., 'no, to the right') during shared-autonomy execution, requiring only a handful of demonstrations to learn (versus hundreds needed by other instruction-following approaches), validated in a user study with a Franka Emika Panda on complex manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors a shared-autonomy framework where online language corrections refine a learned low-dimensional control space over standard instruction-following imitation learning, for both data efficiency (few demos) and adaptivity
claims.conditions: real-world user study, Franka Emika Panda, complex manipulation tasks, shared autonomy (human-robot split agency)

claims.claim: Compared against learned baselines covering open-loop instruction following and single-turn shared autonomy, the corrections-aware approach achieves higher task completion rates and is subjectively preferred by users for reliability, precision, and ease of use
claims.direction: favors online, real-time language corrections (rather than one-shot upfront instructions) as the language-conditioning interface for precise, extended manipulation behaviors
claims.conditions: real-world user study

title: Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress

claims.claim: Sentinel splits failure detection into 'erratic' failures (detected via statistical measures of temporal action consistency, at negligible compute cost, well-suited to fast multimodal generative policies) and task-progression failures (detected via VLMs, used only for less time-sensitive checks); combining both complementary detectors detects 18% more failures than either alone, evaluated on diffusion policies for mobile manipulation in simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors combining a cheap statistical temporal-consistency monitor with a slower VLM-based progress monitor (rather than relying on either alone) for runtime failure detection of generative policies, since different failure modes require different, complementary detection signals
claims.conditions: diffusion policies, mobile manipulation, simulation and real-world

title: Re3Sim: Generating High-Fidelity Simulation Data via 3D-Photorealistic Real-to-Sim for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A 3D-photorealistic real-to-sim system using 3D reconstruction and neural rendering to faithfully recreate real scenes (enabling real-time rendering of simulated cross-view cameras within a physics simulator), combined with privileged-information-based expert demonstration collection in simulation, achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer with an average success rate exceeding 58% using ONLY simulated training data, and a large-scale generated simulation dataset yields policies that generalize across various objects
claims.direction: favors photorealistic 3D real-to-sim reconstruction (closing both geometric and visual sim-to-real gaps) plus privileged-information demo collection in simulation over collecting real-world demonstrations directly, for scalable, generalizable manipulation policy training
claims.conditions: zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, simulated training data only, various manipulation task scenarios and objects

title: EVOLVE-VLA: Test-Time Training from Environment Feedback for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: EVOLVE-VLA replaces unavailable oracle test-time rewards with a learned progress estimator (stabilized via accumulative progress estimation and a progressive horizon-extension strategy), enabling VLAs to continuously adapt through environment interaction with minimal or zero task-specific demonstrations; it achieves +8.6% on long-horizon tasks, +22.0% in 1-shot learning, and 20.8% success on unseen tasks with no task-specific demonstration training at all (versus 0% for pure SFT)
claims.direction: favors test-time training via a learned, noise-tamed progress estimator over standard SFT (which requires hundreds of demonstrations per task and rigidly memorizes trajectories) for adapting VLAs with minimal or zero task-specific demos
claims.conditions: comparison against pure SFT baseline, cross-task generalization to unseen tasks with zero task-specific demonstrations

claims.claim: Qualitative analysis reveals emergent capabilities absent from the training demonstrations, including error recovery and novel strategies, arising from continuous test-time environment interaction
claims.direction: favors continuous test-time adaptation (over static imitation) as a route to emergent robustness/error-recovery behaviors not present in the original demonstrations
claims.conditions: test-time training via environment feedback

title: Efficient Sampling Optimization for Robot Diffusion Policy

claims.claim: Integrating a fast diffusion sampler (DPM-Solver++) into the diffusion-policy framework, decoupling training and inference processes, reduces the number of sampling steps by 90% and increases inference speed by 10x compared to a standard DDPM-based diffusion policy, while guaranteeing control accuracy, evaluated in Robomimic and Push-T simulation environments
claims.direction: favors swapping in a faster ODE/SDE solver (DPM-Solver++) for diffusion-policy sampling over standard DDPM many-step denoising, as a training-compatible way to cut inference latency roughly 10x with no separate distillation needed
claims.conditions: Robomimic and Push-T simulation environments

title: CordViP: Correspondence-based Visuomotor Policy for Dexterous Manipulation in Real-World

claims.claim: Global point clouds from a single-view camera lack crucial contact information and spatial correspondences needed for fine-grained manipulation; constructing 'interaction-aware' point clouds (establishing object-hand correspondence via 6D pose estimation and proprioception, plus object-centric contact maps) achieves state-of-the-art performance across six real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, surpassing baselines by a large margin
claims.direction: favors interaction-aware, correspondence-enriched point-cloud representations (incorporating contact information) over raw global point clouds for fine-grained real-world manipulation
claims.conditions: real-world dexterous manipulation, six tasks, single-view camera input

claims.claim: The method demonstrates superior generalization and robustness to different objects, viewpoints, and scenarios compared to baselines
claims.direction: favors correspondence-based, contact-aware representations for viewpoint robustness over standard point-cloud representations
claims.conditions: real-world, varying viewpoints and objects

title: ExoStart: Efficient learning for dexterous manipulation with sensorized exoskeleton demonstrations

claims.claim: Collecting direct human demonstrations via a sensorized, low-cost wearable exoskeleton (no robot in the loop) captures rich human dexterous behaviors more scalably than robot teleoperation; combined with a simulation-based dynamics filter (converting collected demonstrations into dynamically feasible trajectories) that bootstraps auto-curriculum RL with only simple sparse rewards, this yields policies that transfer zero-shot to the real robot with success rates above 50% on complex dexterous tasks
claims.direction: favors robot-free, wearable-exoskeleton human demonstration collection (feasibility-filtered via simulation) over direct robot teleoperation as a scalable demonstration source for dexterous manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot, zero-shot transfer, complex dexterous tasks (e.g., opening an AirPods case, inserting/turning a key)

claims.claim: A simulation-based dynamics filter generates dynamically feasible trajectories from raw (robot-free) human demonstrations before using them to bootstrap policy learning
claims.direction: favors a feasibility-filtering simulation step between raw human demonstration collection and policy training, rather than using raw human motion data directly
claims.conditions: simulation-based filtering, real-world zero-shot deployment

title: G3VLA: Geometric inductive bias for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: VLA visual tokens are typically grounded only in 2D image coordinates rather than the calibrated geometry of the robot's cameras, a mismatch especially pronounced in multi-camera setups where views are coupled by known intrinsics/extrinsics yet processed as independent images; G3VLA injects calibrated camera structure (intrinsic-conditioned ray embeddings, projective positional encoding, bidirectional cross-view fusion) into the visual-token stream without altering the action space, requiring no depth sensors or manual annotations (geometric supervision from ground-truth or teacher-model point maps), yielding consistent gains across LIBERO, RoboCasa24, RoboTwin2.0, and real-robot settings when instantiated on pi_0, pi_0.5, and GR00T 1.5, with the largest improvements on spatially and object-sensitive tasks
claims.direction: favors explicitly injecting calibrated multi-camera geometric structure (intrinsics/extrinsics-aware) into a VLA's visual tokens over treating multiple camera views as independent 2D images, especially when cameras have a known fixed geometric relationship
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboCasa24, RoboTwin2.0) plus real-robot settings; multiple base VLA models (pi_0, pi_0.5, GR00T 1.5)

claims.claim: Geometric transfer is most effective when geometry-aware visual tokens have direct access to the action-generation pathway, using point-map supervision (from ground truth or a confidence-gated teacher model) rather than requiring depth sensors
claims.direction: favors point-map-based geometric supervision (no depth sensor needed) fed directly into the action pathway over standard depth-sensor-based 3D input or geometry-agnostic 2D tokens
claims.conditions: sim and real-robot settings, multiple VLA backbones

title: Equivariant diffusion policy for sample-efficient robotic manipulation

claims.claim: Equivariant Diffusion Policy, which theoretically characterizes when a diffusion policy is SO(2)-equivariant (for full 6-DoF control) and leverages this domain symmetry in the denoising function, obtains an average 34.5% higher success rate than baseline Diffusion Policy across 12 MimicGen simulation tasks, and on a real-world system, effective policies are learned with relatively few training samples where the baseline Diffusion Policy fails entirely
claims.direction: favors building SO(2) rotational equivariance directly into the diffusion denoising function over a standard (non-equivariant) diffusion policy, for markedly better sample efficiency and generalization, especially in low-data regimes
claims.conditions: 12 MimicGen simulation tasks plus a real-world system with few training samples

claims.claim: The paper theoretically characterizes the conditions under which a diffusion policy can be made equivariant and analyzes SO(2) symmetry for full 6-DoF control
claims.direction: favors symmetry-aware (equivariant) diffusion action heads over standard diffusion action heads for manipulation tasks with rotational symmetry
claims.conditions: 6-DoF control, theoretical plus empirical (sim + real) validation

title: ImageWAM: Do World Action Models Really Need Video Generation, or Just Image Editing?

claims.claim: Video-based World Action Models incur costly inference (dense multi-frame future tokens), waste capacity on action-irrelevant appearance/temporal details, and can accumulate long-horizon imagination errors; ImageWAM instead repurposes a pretrained image-editing model (modeling only a target-frame transformation, focused on action-relevant current-to-target visual differences) and does not decode the target frame at inference, instead conditioning a flow-matching action expert on KV caches from image-editing denoising as a compact world-action context
claims.direction: favors repurposing pretrained image-editing models (target-frame transformation only) over video-generation-based world models for world-action modeling, since editing provides a better-matched, cheaper prior for action-relevant visual change
claims.conditions: different simulator and real-world experiments, no additional policy pretraining

claims.claim: ImageWAM outperforms standard VLA baselines and matching competitive WAMs while reducing FLOPs to 1/6 and latency to 1/4 of video-based WAMs
claims.direction: favors image-editing-based world-action modeling over video-generation-based WAMs specifically for reducing inference compute/latency
claims.conditions: sim and real-world experiments, comparison against video-based WAM baselines

title: GRACE: Gradient-Free Robot Action Generation via Combined Diffusion-MPPI Posterior Mean Estimation

claims.claim: GRACE guides a pretrained diffusion policy toward deployment-time constraints (including nondifferentiable ones like binary collision checks) using Model Predictive Path Integral control with only forward cost evaluations, constructing a cost-conditioned guidance posterior at each reverse diffusion step; it attains higher success rates than diffusion-based and sampling-based baselines in simulation, and on a real 7-DoF manipulator avoids a deployment-time obstacle that the unguided prior collides with in every trial
claims.direction: favors gradient-free, forward-cost-evaluation-based guidance (combining diffusion score-ascent structure with MPPI) over requiring differentiable guidance costs, for steering a pretrained diffusion policy around nondifferentiable safety constraints at deployment
claims.conditions: simulation plus real 7-DoF manipulator, nondifferentiable deployment-time constraints

title: ForeTime-VLA: Causal Future-Token Distillation from a World Action Model for Conveyor-Belt Manipulation

claims.claim: Instead of running a video-scale world-model teacher or imagining future frames at deployment, ForeTime-VLA distills a future-aware representation offline (compressing current+future video latents into a whitened 64-D target) into an online causal encoder that predicts this target plus manipulation phase/time-to-transition to condition a pi0.5-based action expert; in real-robot evaluation on moving (conveyor-belt) objects it achieves 81.1% stationary and 58.9% slow-moving grasp success, exceeding the next-best reference by 12.2 and 22.2 percentage points respectively, at only a 2.46-2.93% latency cost
claims.direction: favors distilling a compact future-state representation from a frozen world-model teacher into a causal, deployment-time-cheap encoder (rather than running the full world model at inference) as an auxiliary objective for anticipating contact events in dynamic/moving-object manipulation
claims.conditions: real-robot conveyor-belt manipulation across multiple belt speeds, built on a dense pi0.5 policy, small added latency cost

title: KALM: Keypoint Abstraction Using Large Models for Object-Relative Imitation Learning

claims.claim: KALM uses large pretrained vision-language models to automatically generate task-relevant, cross-instance-consistent keypoints (verified against a small set of robot demonstrations, requiring no additional manual labels), then trains keypoint-conditioned policies that predict actions in keypoint-centric reference frames; this demonstrates strong real-world performance adapting to different tasks/environments from only a handful of demonstrations
claims.direction: favors automatically-generated (VLM-derived), object-relative keypoint representations over manually-designed keypoints or raw pixel/point-cloud representations, for data-efficient generalization from very few demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world, handful of demonstrations, no additional human labels beyond standard demonstrations

claims.claim: Keypoint-conditioned policies generalize effectively across varying object poses, camera views, and object instances with similar functional shapes
claims.direction: favors keypoint-centric action representations for robustness to camera-view variation over raw-pixel-frame action representations
claims.conditions: real-world, varying camera views and object poses

title: RL-100: Performant Robotic Manipulation with Real-World Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: A lightweight consistency-distillation step compresses a multistep diffusion visuomotor policy into a one-step controller for high-frequency control, meeting deployment latency requirements while the framework achieved 100% success across 1000 real-robot evaluation episodes on eight diverse tasks, including 250/250 consecutive trials on one task, and matched or surpassed expert teleoperators in time-to-completion
claims.direction: favors one-step consistency-distilled diffusion controllers over multistep diffusion sampling for meeting real-time deployment latency without sacrificing (and in this case achieving perfect) task success
claims.conditions: real-world, eight diverse manipulation tasks (pushing, bowling, pouring, cloth folding, unscrewing, juicing, box folding), 1000 total evaluation episodes

claims.claim: Without retraining, a single RL-100 policy attained ~90% zero-shot success under environmental and dynamics shifts, adapted in a few-shot regime to substantial task variations (86.7%), remained robust to human perturbations (~96%), and a juicing-robot deployment served customers continuously for about 7 hours without failure in a real shopping mall
claims.direction: favors a policy trained with RL-100's unified IL+RL framework for strong zero-shot and few-shot robustness to environmental/dynamics shifts and human perturbations, validated via extended real-world deployment rather than only short evaluation trials
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot and few-shot evaluation, extended real-deployment (7-hour continuous operation)

claims.claim: RL-100 unifies imitation learning and reinforcement learning under a single clipped proximal-policy-optimization surrogate objective applied within the diffusion denoising process, yielding conservative, stable improvements across offline and online training stages, and supports both single-action and action-chunking control in a task-, embodiment-, and representation-agnostic manner
claims.direction: favors unifying IL and RL objectives directly within the diffusion denoising process (rather than treating them as separate training stages/objectives) for stable, reliable real-world policy improvement
claims.conditions: real-world, eight diverse tasks, task/embodiment/representation-agnostic

claims.claim: Consistency distillation of the diffusion policy into a one-step controller is what enables meeting real-time control-frequency requirements for deployment
claims.direction: favors distilling large multistep diffusion action heads into a compact one-step model for deployment efficiency, rather than deploying the full multistep model
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, high-frequency control requirement

title: VLBiMan: Vision-Language Anchored One-Shot Demonstration Enables Generalizable Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Learns reusable skills from a single human demonstration via task-aware decomposition, claiming a drastic reduction in demonstration requirements compared to imitation-learning baselines
claims.direction: favors one-shot/very-low-demo skill learning over standard imitation-learning demo volumes
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, tool-use and multi-object tasks, one demo per skill

claims.claim: Reports robustness to background changes, object repositioning, visual clutter, and novel but semantically similar objects, without policy retraining
claims.direction: favors semantic/geometric-anchored skill adaptation for robustness over standard end-to-end IL
claims.conditions: real bimanual robot, tool-use/multi-object tasks

title: Latent evolving World Action Model

claims.claim: Predictive JEPA embeddings (I-JEPA best) support action generation better than compressed VAE latents in an encoder comparison for world-action models
claims.direction: favors JEPA-style pretrained visual encoders over VAE latents for action generation
claims.conditions: sim (RoboTwin 2.0) with some real-world manipulation validation; encoder ablation

claims.claim: Conditioning action generation on JEPA embeddings and predicting future embeddings directly (no video-diffusion backbone) reaches 92.28% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, comparable to state-of-the-art VLAs/world-action models
claims.direction: favors JEPA-based future-embedding prediction as the auxiliary/world-model objective over VAE-latent video-diffusion backbones
claims.conditions: sim benchmark RoboTwin 2.0, 0.4B trainable params, some real-world validation mentioned

claims.claim: Achieves this performance with only 0.4B trainable parameters
claims.direction: favors small model size
claims.conditions: sim benchmark; real-world manipulation mentioned but no numbers given

title: Tether: Autonomous Functional Play with Correspondence-Driven Trajectory Warping

claims.claim: An open-loop policy that warps actions from <=10 source demonstrations via semantic keypoint correspondences is described as extremely data-efficient; autonomous play bootstrapped from a handful of demos yields over 1000 expert-level trajectories, training closed-loop imitation policies competitive with those trained on human-collected demonstrations
claims.direction: favors bootstrapping large datasets from very few (<=10) demos via autonomous play, over collecting more human teleop demos directly
claims.conditions: real household-like multi-object robot setup

claims.claim: Policy reported robust even under significant spatial and semantic scene variations
claims.direction: favors correspondence/keypoint-anchored action warping for robustness
claims.conditions: real robot, multi-object household setup

title: Visuo-Tactile World Models

claims.claim: Multi-task visuo-tactile world model (VT-WM) improves physical fidelity of imagination by 33% on object permanence and 29% on compliance with laws of motion versus vision-only world models, and achieves up to 35% higher zero-shot real-robot success rates, with largest gains in multi-step contact-rich tasks
claims.direction: favors adding tactile sensing plus a world-model auxiliary objective over vision-only world models
claims.conditions: real-robot zero-shot experiments, contact-rich multi-step tasks; requires tactile sensing (not present in our RealSense+wrist-cam setup)

title: Learning Transferable Dynamics Priors from Action to World Modeling

claims.claim: Action-conditioned world-model pretraining (A2World) on large-scale robot manipulation data yields transferable dynamics priors that benefit both a simulator-based policy evaluator and a video-action joint-prediction policy, across sim benchmarks and real-robot settings
claims.direction: favors action-conditioned world-model pretraining as an auxiliary/pretraining objective
claims.conditions: large-scale pretraining data, sim + real-robot evaluation; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: MoE-ACT: Scaling Multi-Task Bimanual Manipulation with Sparse Task-Conditioned Mixture-of-Experts Transformers

claims.claim: Adding sparse Mixture-of-Experts layers to an ACT (action-chunking-transformer) encoder plus task-conditioned FiLM in the decoder achieves 62.0% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 (16 bimanual tasks), outperforming standard ACT by 17.4 percentage points
claims.direction: favors MoE-augmented action-chunking-transformer architecture over plain ACT
claims.conditions: sim benchmark RoboTwin 2.0, 16 bimanual tasks, also confirmed on real dual-arm robot

claims.claim: Uses task-conditioned FiLM in the action decoder plus multi-scale cross-attention for task grounding in a multi-task setting
claims.direction: favors FiLM-based task/language conditioning combined with cross-attention
claims.conditions: multi-task bimanual manipulation, sim + real robot

claims.claim: With only 195M activated parameters, MoE-ACT surpasses the 16x larger foundation model pi0 (3.24B params) by 5.1 percentage points on RoboTwin 2.0
claims.direction: favors small, parameter-efficient specialized architectures over large generalist foundation models
claims.conditions: sim benchmark RoboTwin 2.0; real dual-arm robot experiments also reported as confirming superiority

why_deep_read: Directly quantifies a small MoE-augmented ACT beating a much larger VLA foundation model (pi0) on success rate with real-robot confirmation; full-text ablations (MoE routing, FiLM contribution, parameter counts) would materially inform our Q01/Q12 model-size and architecture choice for an 8GB-GPU laptop setup.

title: PrimitiveVLA: Learning Reusable Motion Primitives for Efficient and Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Disassembling demonstrations into reusable motion primitives (rather than memorizing monolithic trajectories) is claimed to improve data efficiency for VLA fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors primitive-centric decomposition over direct instruction-to-control trajectory mapping for data efficiency
claims.conditions: VLA fine-tuning, unseen and long-horizon tasks; qualitative claim, no numbers given

claims.claim: Proposes a Primitive-Centric Disassemble & Assemble paradigm with a shared multimodal canonical representation as an alternative action-generation architecture to direct instruction-to-control mapping
claims.direction: favors primitive/skill-based action generation over monolithic trajectory regression
claims.conditions: VLA models, experiments across unseen/long-horizon tasks

claims.claim: Achieves superior zero-shot generalization across unseen and long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors primitive-based approach for generalization
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: FACT: Failure-Aware Causal Training for World-Action Models

claims.claim: A causal world-action model that predicts future video/task-progress conditioned on the executed action, trained with both successful and failure rollouts, outperforms baselines and improves further as more failure data is incorporated, reducing success-biased hallucination under bad actions
claims.direction: favors failure-aware, action-conditioned world-model auxiliary training over training only on successful demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world bimanual manipulation tasks; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: DISEIL: Demonstration Distillation for Sample-Efficient Imitation Learning

claims.claim: Deliberately choosing which failure mode to correct and where a corrective demonstration should start (rather than leaving this to whichever episode triggered interruption) gives the highest mean held-out success rate in 10 of 10 tested settings (tie in 1), with the largest margin at the smallest demonstration budget tested
claims.direction: favors targeted/deliberate selection of corrective (recovery) demonstrations over naive interactive-IL demo collection, especially in low-demo-budget regimes
claims.conditions: 5 simulated tasks, state and image observations, mostly scripted experts; authors note the scope is narrow (single round of practice, simulation only)

title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A training-free, inference-time recovery method (CoRe) that imagines continuation from a recent viable state and minimally realigns robot/scene improves success rates by up to 85.0 percentage points to near-nominal levels after task-goal changes or physical perturbations, while reducing physical restorations by 42.2%, without any policy fine-tuning or failure-specific training
claims.direction: favors training-free inference-time recovery/realignment over failure-data collection or policy retraining for robustness to online disruptions
claims.conditions: multiple simulators, multiple VLA backbones, and real-world settings tested

title: Video Language Planning

claims.claim: Tree-search video-language planning (VLM policies/value functions + text-to-video dynamics models) substantially improves long-horizon task success rates compared to prior methods on both simulated and real robots across 3 hardware platforms
claims.direction: favors video-generation-based world/dynamics models plus VLM planning for long-horizon tasks over standard flat policies
claims.conditions: real and simulated robots, 3 hardware platforms, multi-object rearrangement and bi-arm dexterous manipulation; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given; heavy compute (tree search + video generation) likely impractical for our 8GB laptop setup

title: Point Cloud Matters: Rethinking the Impact of Different Observation Spaces on Robot Learning

claims.claim: On OBSBench (2 simulators, 125 contact-rich manipulation tasks), point-cloud-based methods, even with the simplest designs, frequently outperform RGB and RGB-D counterparts, both when training from scratch and when using pretraining
claims.direction: favors point-cloud observation space over RGB or RGB-D
claims.conditions: sim benchmark, 125 tasks, contact-rich manipulation, tested across encoders/policy baselines

claims.claim: Point-cloud observations yield significantly stronger generalization across various geometric and visual conditions than RGB/RGB-D; combining appearance (color) with coordinate information further improves point-cloud method performance
claims.direction: favors point cloud (optionally + color) for robustness/generalization over RGB-only or RGB-D
claims.conditions: sim benchmark, 125 tasks

why_deep_read: A large controlled benchmark (125 tasks, 2 simulators) directly comparing RGB vs RGB-D vs point-cloud observation spaces is exactly the evidence needed for Q04 (we have a depth-capable RealSense but currently use RGB only); full text would give per-task numbers, encoder details, and whether gains hold in low-data/real-robot regimes relevant to our setup.

title: Single-Shot Learning of Stable Dynamical Systems for Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks

claims.claim: Segmenting long-horizon demonstrations into waypoint-defined steps and learning globally stable dynamical-system policies per subgoal improves task success rates while reducing the amount of training data needed, validated in sim and on real robots with sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: favors waypoint/subgoal-segmented stable dynamical-system policies over standard monolithic long-horizon imitation policies for data efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world and simulated experiments; qualitative claim, no specific demo counts or success numbers given

title: Sample-Efficient Motion Generalization via Task-Parameterized GMMs with Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization

claims.claim: Using only 5 demonstrations per subtask, TP-GMM plus Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters achieved a 95% task success rate on a real pick-and-place task with a Kinova Gen3 robot, outperforming both standard TP-GMM and a TP-GMM+EKF variant in accuracy and consistency
claims.direction: favors Bayesian-hyperparameter-tuned GMM action representations for very-low-demo-count regimes (as few as 5 demos)
claims.conditions: real robot (Kinova Gen3), 5 demos/subtask, pick-and-place with visual-marker-inferred task parameters

claims.claim: Task-Parameterized GMMs (a GMM-based action/motion representation) outperform non-parameterized models in accuracy and robustness while maintaining low computational cost
claims.direction: favors GMM-based action head over unspecified non-parameterized baselines in low-data, low-compute settings
claims.conditions: real robot pick-and-place, 5 demos/subtask

why_deep_read: A real low-cost-arm-relevant result (5 demos/subtask, 95% success, GMM-based action representation, low compute) is nearly a direct match to our 50-100-demo low-compute setup; full text would give the actual success-rate comparison table and hyperparameter-tuning method, materially informing Q01 (GMM viability) and Q13 (demo count needed).

title: DexFruit: Dexterous Manipulation and Gaussian Splatting Inspection of Fruit

claims.claim: Tactile-informed diffusion policies outperform baselines in both reduced bruising and pick-and-place success rate across three fruits (strawberries, tomatoes, blackberries), with a 92% overall grasping success rate, up to 15% reduction in visual bruising, and up to 31% improvement in grasp success on challenging fruit, evaluated over 630+ trials
claims.direction: favors a diffusion-policy action head (with tactile conditioning) over unspecified baseline policies for delicate real-object manipulation
claims.conditions: real robot, optical tactile sensing (not in our sensor set), 3 fruit types, 630+ trials; note fragile-produce grasping is directly relevant to our pumpkin task even though we lack tactile sensing

title: End-to-End Dexterous Arm-Hand VLA Policies via Shared Autonomy: VR Teleoperation Augmented by Autonomous Hand VLA Policy for Efficient Data Collection

claims.claim: A shared-autonomy scheme (human controls arm pose via VR, autonomous DexGrasp-VLA policy controls fine hand motion using tactile+visual feedback) reduces operator cognitive load and enables efficient collection of high-quality coordinated demonstrations; a Corrective Teleoperation system allows continuous policy improvement via human-in-the-loop failure recovery
claims.direction: favors shared-autonomy/human-in-the-loop data collection over full manual teleoperation for demonstration quality and efficiency
claims.conditions: real dexterous arm-hand robot

claims.claim: The resulting end-to-end VLA policy achieves a 90% success rate across diverse objects, including unseen instances
claims.direction: favors this data-collection + arm-hand feature enhancement approach for generalization to novel objects
claims.conditions: real robot, dexterous hand, diverse and unseen objects

title: Beyond Sight: Finetuning Generalist Robot Policies with Heterogeneous Sensors via Language Grounding

claims.claim: FuSe finetunes visuomotor generalist policies (both diffusion-based and large VLA models) on heterogeneous sensor modalities (touch, audio) using natural language as cross-modal grounding (multimodal contrastive loss + sensory-grounded language generation loss), increasing real-world success rates by over 20% compared to all considered baselines
claims.direction: favors language-grounded multimodal finetuning over vision/proprioception-only generalist policies when extra sensor modalities are available
claims.conditions: real-world robot manipulation; requires touch/audio sensors not present in our RealSense+wrist-camera setup, but the language-grounding recipe is reported applicable to diffusion and VLA policies generally

title: Learning Surgical Robotic Manipulation with 3D Spatial Priors

claims.claim: Notes that adding wrist-mounted cameras to supplement a fixed stereo view is rarely adopted in practice since wrist cameras can interfere with arm motion, and instead extracts 3D spatial cues directly from the fixed (stereo endoscopic) view via a finetuned geometric transformer
claims.direction: favors extracting 3D spatial awareness from a fixed/scene camera's images over adding a wrist camera, in settings where a wrist camera is impractical
claims.conditions: real surgical robot (different domain: endoscopic stereo camera, knot tying/organ dissection), end-to-end visuomotor policy

claims.claim: An end-to-end visuomotor policy (SST) that aligns learned 3D latent representations (from a geometric transformer finetuned on a 30K-pair stereo dataset) with the robot's action space achieves state-of-the-art performance and strong spatial generalization on complex manipulation tasks, without explicit scene reconstruction
claims.direction: favors learned 3D/geometric latent representations from images over either explicit 3D reconstruction pipelines or added multi-view RGB alone
claims.conditions: real surgical robot, stereo endoscope images, complex manipulation tasks; domain differs from tabletop pick-and-place

title: TiPToP: A Modular Open-Vocabulary Robot Manipulation System That Plans

claims.claim: A modular system combining pretrained foundation models with a GPU-accelerated Task-and-Motion Planner, requiring no robot training data, attains a higher average success rate and faster average completion time than pi0.5-DROID (a state-of-the-art VLA finetuned on 350 hours of demonstrations) across two real-world DROID setups and simulation
claims.direction: favors a modular perception+planning system (no learned action-regression policy, no robot training data) over an end-to-end VLA finetuned on hundreds of hours of demonstrations, at least on the tasks/setups tested
claims.conditions: real-world DROID robot setups (2, one external), plus simulation and the MolmoSpaces benchmark; qualitative comparison, no exact percentage-point numbers given in abstract

title: TAIL-Safe: Task-Agnostic Safety Monitoring for Imitation Learning Policies

claims.claim: Flow-matching and diffusion imitation-learning policies are reported to fail even within their training distribution due to extreme sensitivity to initial conditions and compounding approximation-error drift
claims.direction: flags a specific robustness weakness of flow-matching/diffusion action heads (relevant when choosing among diffusion, flow matching, regression, GMM, etc.)
claims.conditions: real Franka Emika robot experiments

claims.claim: A Lipschitz-continuous Q-value safety-set monitor (TAIL-Safe), with a gradient-ascent recovery mechanism, lets a flow-matching policy that fails under run-time perturbations instead achieve consistent task success when guided by the monitor
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight learned safety/recovery monitor on top of an imitation-learning policy to handle out-of-distribution perturbations, rather than relying on the base policy's own robustness
claims.conditions: real Franka Emika robot, run-time physical perturbations; safety-set learned via Gaussian-Splatting digital twin for safe failure-data collection

title: Bridge-WA: Predicting Where and How the World Changes for Robotic Action

claims.claim: Bridge-WA distills a frozen future-change teacher (world model) into three compact priors (future tokens, change maps, motion-flow maps) that condition the action transformer via attention/spatial-temporal biases at train time, with the teacher removed at inference, avoiding deployment-time dense future-image generation
claims.direction: favors distilling world-model/future-prediction knowledge into compact auxiliary priors used only at train time, over running a heavy generative world model at inference
claims.conditions: evaluated on VLABench, RoboTwin2.0, LIBERO-Plus, and real-robot settings

claims.claim: By focusing action generation on where/how the scene will change, Bridge-WA suppresses nuisance appearance factors such as background, lighting, and distractors, improving task success, progress, and robustness with particularly clear gains under out-of-distribution visual shifts
claims.direction: favors change-focused (future-change-prediction) auxiliary training for robustness to lighting/background/distractor shifts over standard appearance-based policies
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (VLABench, RoboTwin2.0, LIBERO-Plus) plus real-robot evaluation; qualitative claim, no specific percentage numbers given

title: Mind-VLA: Instruction-Aware Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Aligning a VLA's latent representation with instruction-specific target-object 3D features (canonical target views, VAE + VGGT features) instead of whole-scene 3D alignment reaches 94.4% on LIBERO and 4.47 on CALVIN, and on real-robot target-occlusion tasks achieves 54% average success, outperforming a matched whole-scene-VGGT control by 26 percentage points
claims.direction: favors instruction-aware, target-object-specific 3D representation alignment over uniform whole-scene 3D alignment
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks LIBERO/CALVIN plus real-robot occlusion tasks, compact 345M-parameter backbone

claims.claim: Uses VGGT (geometric) features aligned with VAE features as the visual representation basis for 3D understanding
claims.direction: favors geometry-pretrained visual features (VGGT) combined with VAE features over generic image encoders for spatial/occlusion-robust manipulation
claims.conditions: same setup as above

claims.claim: Achieves the above results with a compact 345M-parameter backbone
claims.direction: favors small/compact model size for this task class
claims.conditions: sim + real-robot

title: Robotic Multiphase Interaction: Manipulating Coupled Liquid and Solid Dynamics with a World Model

claims.claim: An action-conditioned world model predicting how manipulation changes a coupled liquid/solid state reduces retained-water prediction error by more than 60% compared to a baseline, and using the world model to select the best action sequence from policy proposals further roughly halves the predicted terminal error
claims.direction: favors adding an action-conditioned world model plus model-based action selection on top of a learned action policy
claims.conditions: simulated porous-material/liquid manipulation (sponge+water) using SPH dynamics; domain (liquid/porous dynamics) differs substantially from our rigid-object pick-and-place task

claims.claim: Uses a temporal UNet generating actions via either Diffusion Policy or rectified flow matching as the action decoder
claims.direction: treats diffusion policy and rectified flow matching as interchangeable action-head choices within a world-model-guided pipeline
claims.conditions: simulated liquid/solid manipulation; no direct comparison of the two action-head choices given in the abstract

title: DefGoalNet: Contextual Goal Learning from Demonstrations for Deformable Object Manipulation

claims.claim: Learning goal shapes directly from as few as 10 human demonstrations achieves a median success percentage of nearly 90% on a surgical retraction task
claims.direction: favors learning task goals/behavior from a small (~10) demonstration set
claims.conditions: simulation and physical robot, deformable object (surgical retraction) domain, differs from rigid-object pick-and-place

title: Gen2Act: Human Video Generation in Novel Scenarios enables Generalizable Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Conditioning a manipulation policy on a generated human video (from a pretrained web-scale video model, not finetuned) requires an order of magnitude less robot interaction data than the video prediction model was trained on
claims.direction: favors leveraging pretrained video-generation priors over scaling robot-specific demonstration collection
claims.conditions: real-world diverse scenarios; heavy video-generation model likely impractical for our 8GB-GPU / low-latency laptop setup

claims.claim: Enables manipulating unseen object types and performing novel motions for tasks not present in the robot training data
claims.direction: favors video-generation-conditioned policies for generalization to novel objects/motions
claims.conditions: real-world scenarios; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: World Models for Learning Dexterous Hand-Object Interactions from Human Videos

claims.claim: DexWM predicts future latent states conditioned on past states and actions (using finger keypoints as the action representation) trained on 900+ hours of human/non-dexterous-robot video, with an added auxiliary hand-consistency loss that enforces accurate hand configurations, outperforming prior world models conditioned on text/navigation/full-body actions in future-state prediction
claims.direction: favors action-conditioned world-model pretraining with an auxiliary consistency loss (matched to the action representation) over coarser action-conditioning schemes
claims.conditions: trained on large human video corpus; evaluated zero-shot on real Franka Panda + Allegro gripper (dexterous hand, differs from our simple 2-finger gripper)

claims.claim: Zero-shot transfer of the resulting policy to unseen skills surpasses Diffusion Policy by over 50% on average across grasping, placing, and reaching tasks
claims.direction: favors world-model-derived action generation over a standard Diffusion Policy baseline
claims.conditions: real robot (Franka Panda + Allegro hand), zero-shot on unseen skills

title: DexGarmentLab: Dexterous Garment Manipulation Environment with Generalizable Policy

claims.claim: Leveraging garment structural correspondence to automatically generate a dataset of diverse trajectories from a single expert demonstration significantly reduces the manual intervention otherwise needed (vs. teleoperation or RL-policy data collection)
claims.direction: favors automatic correspondence-based trajectory generation from a single demo over manual teleoperation/RL data collection
claims.conditions: simulation, deformable garment manipulation (15 task scenarios); domain differs from rigid-object pick-and-place
