claims.claim: A hierarchical affordance-based policy (HALO) consistently outperforms existing methods and generalizes to previously unseen garment instances with significant shape/deformation variation where other methods fail
claims.direction: favors affordance-point-based hierarchical policies for generalization to novel object instances/shapes
claims.conditions: simulation, deformable garments; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: MV-UMI: A Scalable Multi-View Interface for Cross-Embodiment Learning

claims.claim: Adding a third-person (scene) camera view to a first-person wrist-mounted camera improves performance on sub-tasks requiring broad scene understanding (shelf placement, rack insertion) by an average of approximately 47% over a single-view (wrist-only) UMI baseline, per an ablation study
claims.direction: favors combining a fixed/scene camera view with a wrist camera over a wrist-camera-only setup
claims.conditions: handheld-gripper (UMI) data collection, cross-embodiment; ablation study quantifying the multi-view benefit

title: EnerVerse-AC: Envisioning Embodied Environments with Action Condition

claims.claim: An action-conditional world model (EnerVerse-AC) that generates future visual observations from predicted actions is used both as a data engine and as an evaluator, eliminating the need for physical robots or complex simulations for policy testing, while maintaining high fidelity
claims.direction: favors action-conditioned world models as auxiliary tools for both training-data augmentation and low-cost policy evaluation
claims.conditions: trained with diverse (including failure) trajectories; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

claims.claim: Augments human-collected trajectories into diverse generated datasets, including diverse failure trajectories, to improve generalization
claims.direction: favors generative augmentation of demonstration data (including synthesized failures) over relying solely on collected human demonstrations
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: EgoZero: Robot Learning from Smart Glasses

claims.claim: Policies learned entirely from human demonstrations captured with smart glasses (zero robot data), using a morphology-agnostic state representation, achieve 70% success over 7 manipulation tasks on a real Franka Panda robot with only 20 minutes of data collection per task
claims.direction: favors learning from cheap, egocentric human demonstration data (no teleop, no robot data) as an extremely data-efficient alternative to robot teleoperation demonstrations
claims.conditions: real Franka Panda gripper robot, zero-shot transfer, 20 min human data collection per task, 7 tasks

claims.claim: Closed-loop policy learning generalizes morphologically, spatially, and semantically from human demonstrations to the robot
claims.direction: favors human-video-derived, morphology-agnostic representations for cross-embodiment generalization
claims.conditions: real robot, zero-shot transfer

title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision

claims.claim: A lightweight latent 'workspace token', distilled at train time from VLM-identified task-salient historical information via a set-reconstruction decoder loss, can be used as a drop-in replacement for raw observation history at deployment, solving memory-intensive tasks without needing VLM reasoning in-the-loop, and is reported to also improve policy performance over the alternatives compared, despite being more lightweight
claims.direction: favors a distilled, lightweight learned memory token over either full observation-history conditioning or in-the-loop VLM-based history compression
claims.conditions: both simulation and real hardware tested; qualitative comparative claim ('found that...leads to better policy performance'), no specific numbers given

claims.claim: Removes the need for expensive VLM queries in-the-loop at deployment time (only train-time cost), which is relevant to inference latency
claims.direction: favors moving expensive memory-compression computation to train time rather than incurring it at every inference step
claims.conditions: same setup as above

title: LatentVLA: Taming Latent Space for Generalizable and Long-Horizon Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: Inverse-dynamics-based latent action models (scalable but disconnected from physical reality) suffer from 'temporal entanglement', where the model cannot distinguish visually similar states requiring distinct actions (e.g. gripper approaching vs. receding from an object), compounded by discretization artifacts; LatentVLA's continuous, spatiotemporally-grounded latent action representation (temporal-attentive latent action model + latent diffusion transformer) resolves this and sets a new state-of-the-art across real-world bimanual tasks, outperforming prior methods
claims.direction: favors continuous, temporally-grounded latent diffusion action representations over discretized/tokenized (VQ-style) latent action models for avoiding temporal-ambiguity failures
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Demonstrates superior zero-shot generalization and few-shot efficiency compared to prior methods
claims.direction: favors this continuous latent-diffusion action representation for few-shot/low-demo efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual tasks; qualitative claim, no specific demo counts or numbers given

title: 3D-Mix for VLA: A Plug-and-Play Module for Integrating VGGT-based 3D Information into Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: A systematic pilot study comparing nine schemes for integrating a 3D vision model (VGGT) into VLAs finds that semantic-conditioned gated fusion (adaptively balancing 2D semantic and 3D geometric features based on task context) is the strongest of all nine fusion schemes tested
claims.direction: favors adaptive/gated fusion of 3D geometric features with 2D semantic features over naive concatenation or other fixed fusion schemes, and over 2D-only representations
claims.conditions: six MLLM series, nine model variants (2B-8B params), SIMPLER and LIBERO benchmarks

claims.claim: The resulting plug-and-play module (3D-Mix), added without modifying existing MLLM or action-expert components, delivers consistent gains, averaging +7.0% on the out-of-domain (OOD) SIMPLER benchmark across all nine GR00T-style variants tested
claims.direction: favors augmenting 2D vision-language backbones with a dedicated 3D geometric encoder (VGGT) for OOD robustness, over relying on the 2D MLLM's own (limited) spatial intelligence
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks SIMPLER/LIBERO, multiple VLA architectures (GR00T-style and pi-style)

why_deep_read: A systematic, controlled comparison of nine 3D-integration fusion schemes across nine model variants is exactly the kind of ablation needed to decide Q03/Q04 (how, if at all, to add depth/3D cues to our RGB pipeline); full text would give per-scheme numbers and whether gains hold at small model scale.

title: Multi-Resolution Tactile Imitation Learning for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: On five contact-rich manipulation tasks, a vision-only imitation-learning baseline achieves only 31% average success, a visual-tactile baseline achieves 54%, while fusing RGB with two heterogeneous tactile sensors at different temporal resolutions (MiTaS) conditioning a flow-matching policy achieves 80% average success
claims.direction: suggests vision-only (RGB) observation is a comparatively weak observation space for contact-rich tasks versus multimodal (here tactile) sensing; not a direct RGB-vs-depth comparison
claims.conditions: real contact-rich manipulation tasks; requires GelSight/Evetac tactile sensors not present in our RealSense+wrist-camera setup, so the specific 80% number is not directly transferable, but the low 31% vision-only figure is a useful reference point

title: World4RL: Diffusion World Models for Policy Refinement With Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Refining an imitation-learning-initialized policy entirely within a frozen, pre-trained diffusion world model (avoiding real or simulated online interaction) yields significantly higher success rates compared to imitation learning and other baselines
claims.direction: favors using a diffusion world model as a high-fidelity offline simulator for RL-based policy refinement after imitation-learning pretraining
claims.conditions: multi-task pretraining of the world model, extensive simulation and real-world experiments; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

claims.claim: Uses a two-hot action encoding scheme tailored for robotic manipulation together with a diffusion backbone for the world model
claims.direction: proposes two-hot action encoding as a design choice for action representation in this pipeline
claims.conditions: same setup as above

title: Reflective VLA: In-Context Action Consequences Make VLAs Generalize

claims.claim: Conditioning each decision on a context of observation-action-consequence triplets (not just raw observation history) improves average success rate by 5.4 and 4.2 percentage points over a matched reactive baseline under distribution shift (LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Plus-Hard); ablations against a matched history-only baseline show that action consequences specifically, rather than additional context length alone, are the key to cross-environment generalization
claims.direction: favors conditioning on observation-action-consequence triplets over either purely reactive (no-history) policies or naive observation-history-only conditioning
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks LIBERO, SimplerEnv-Bridge, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Plus-Hard

claims.claim: A block-causal attention mask enables parallel multi-frame training without leakage and supports KV-cached real-time inference
claims.direction: favors an architecture designed for KV-cache-compatible real-time inference when adding history/consequence conditioning
claims.conditions: same sim benchmarks; real-time inference claim not quantified with a specific latency number in the abstract

claims.claim: Preserves strong in-distribution performance while improving generalization under distribution shift, attributed specifically to embodiment-specific factors (camera-to-robot geometry, calibration, actuation bias) becoming disambiguated via observed action consequences
claims.direction: favors exposing action-consequence context to help a policy disambiguate embodiment/deployment-specific factors causing camera/calibration-related generalization failures
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks (LIBERO family)

title: RedFlow: Redirect Failure into Action-Level Corrections for Flow-matching VLA Policy

claims.claim: A fine-grained offline-RL framework that redirects failure rollouts into action-level corrective supervision for flow-matching VLA policies improves real-world success rate from 56.7% to 74.7%, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art offline RL baselines that use failure data only at the trajectory level or ignore it
claims.direction: favors action-level (not trajectory-level) use of failure/rollout data to correct flow-matching policies, addressing compounding errors from distribution shift
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark plus three real-world manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Matches strong on-policy RL methods (PPO, GRPO, DDPO) while requiring roughly an order of magnitude fewer training samples
claims.direction: favors this offline, failure-data-efficient correction approach over on-policy RL for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: same benchmarks; comparison is against on-policy RL fine-tuning, not against collecting more human demonstrations directly

title: GRAFT: Grounded and Efficient Online Reinforcement Adaptation for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Combining single-step action generation with cached visual-language prefix reuse accelerates online adaptation and reduces the computational overhead of online policy updates, improving success rates by 32.5 percentage points under matched adaptation budgets
claims.direction: favors caching visual-language prefixes and single-step action generation to reduce inference/update compute cost during online learning
claims.conditions: four biomedical manipulation tasks (different domain from tabletop pick-and-place); real-robot online adaptation

claims.claim: Uses region-level supervision to learn view-specific visual anchors that focus perception on task-relevant local cues, improving fine-grained visual grounding without needing region proposals at deployment
claims.direction: favors learned view-specific visual anchoring for fine-grained, view-dependent visual cues
claims.conditions: biomedical manipulation tasks; domain differs from our pumpkin pick-and-place task

title: Efficient Bi-manipulation using RGBD Multi-model Fusion based on Attention Mechanism

claims.claim: A mixed focal-attention module fuses RGB (color) and depth (3D shape/structure) images via cross-attention, highlighting prominent local features and their cross-modal relevance, addressing perception deficiencies from abnormal lighting, occlusion, and shadow
claims.direction: favors RGB-D cross-attention fusion over RGB-only observation for robustness to lighting/occlusion/shadow perception deficiencies
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm robot, four real-world tasks

claims.claim: Proposes a 'Focal CVAE' framework (a CVAE-based action head conditioned on the fused RGB-D features) with a saliency attention module for computational efficiency
claims.direction: uses a CVAE action head as the generative/multimodal action representation in this pipeline
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm robot, lower computational cost reported

claims.claim: Bi-manipulation performance is significantly improved across four real-world tasks, and robustness is validated specifically under different scenarios with perception-deficiency problems (abnormal lighting, occlusion, shadow)
claims.direction: favors RGB-D fusion for robustness under exactly the lighting/occlusion conditions in our failure list
claims.conditions: real-world dual-arm robot, four tasks, explicit lighting/occlusion/shadow robustness testing; qualitative claim ('significantly improved'), no exact numbers given

why_deep_read: Directly tests RGB-D (CVAE-based) fusion against exactly our reported failure mode (breaking under new lighting) on a real robot; full text would give the quantitative success-rate comparison against an RGB-only baseline and computational cost details relevant to our 8GB-GPU budget.

title: WristWorld: Generating Wrist-Views via 4D World Models for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Wrist-view observations are noted to capture fine-grained hand-object interactions that directly enhance manipulation performance, but large-scale datasets rarely include them, creating a substantial anchor-view/wrist-view data gap
claims.direction: reinforces the value of wrist-camera observations for manipulation performance, motivating ways to obtain more wrist-view data/coverage
claims.conditions: general observation about existing datasets (Droid, Calvin, Franka Panda)

claims.claim: A 4D world model (WristWorld) generates synthetic, geometrically consistent wrist-view videos solely from anchor (scene) views, using VGGT-based reconstruction plus a Spatial Projection Consistency loss and a video generation stage; this improves downstream VLA performance, raising average task completion length on Calvin by 3.81% and closing 42.4% of the anchor-wrist view gap
claims.direction: favors synthetically generating missing wrist-view data from existing scene-view demonstrations as an augmentation strategy, rather than only collecting more real wrist-camera demonstrations
claims.conditions: evaluated on Droid, Calvin (sim benchmark), and Franka Panda (real robot)

title: Active-Perceptive Language-Oriented Grasp Policy for Heavily Cluttered Scenes

claims.claim: An occlusion-aware, semantic-guided active-perception viewpoint-optimization strategy enables more efficient exploration of cluttered scenes than existing approaches with limited observational capability
claims.direction: favors active/optimized viewpoint selection over a fixed single viewpoint for occluded/cluttered scenes
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, heavily cluttered scenes; qualitative claim ('significant improvements'), no specific numbers given

claims.claim: Combines language-guided grasping with the active-perception scheme and a grasp-wise RL policy for robust grasp-pose selection
claims.direction: favors integrating language conditioning with active perception for cluttered-scene grasping
claims.conditions: real-world experiments

title: Phantom: Training Robots Without Robots Using Only Human Videos

claims.claim: Manipulation policies trained directly from human video demonstrations (hand-pose estimation + visual editing to inpaint the human arm and overlay a rendered robot), requiring zero robot data, achieve up to 92% success on a range of real-hardware tasks including deformable-object manipulation, multi-object sweeping, and insertion, deployed zero-shot without fine-tuning
claims.direction: favors training entirely from edited human-video demonstrations (no teleop/robot data at all) as a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation demonstrations
claims.conditions: real hardware, zero-shot deployment, multiple task types

claims.claim: The approach generalizes to novel environments and supports closed-loop execution
claims.direction: favors human-video-derived training for generalization to novel environments
claims.conditions: real hardware; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given beyond the up-to-92% figure

title: No Need for Real 3D: Fusing 2D Vision with Pseudo 3D Representations for Robotic Manipulation Learning

claims.claim: 3D point-cloud-based policy learning is noted (citing recent studies) to consistently outperform 2D image-based policy learning in both performance and generalization, but point-cloud acquisition is costly; the proposed NoReal3D framework instead learns a 3DStructureFormer that transforms monocular images into geometrically meaningful pseudo-point-cloud features fused with 2D encoder features, achieving performance comparable to real 3D point-cloud-based methods without needing actual point-cloud data, across various tasks
claims.direction: favors deriving pseudo-3D structural features from monocular RGB (fused with 2D features) as a lower-cost alternative to using a real depth/point-cloud sensor, while still capturing most of the 3D-vs-RGB performance gap
claims.conditions: extensive experiments across various manipulation tasks; comparison is against real point-cloud methods, not specified whether sim or real robot

title: Generate, Transfer, Adapt: Learning Functional Dexterous Grasping from a Single Human Demonstration

claims.claim: A correspondence-based data engine generates diverse synthetic training data (novel object instances, transferred and optimized expert grasps) in simulation from a single human demonstration
claims.direction: favors synthetic data generation/correspondence-based augmentation from one demo over collecting many real demonstrations
claims.conditions: simulation-generated data, dexterous hand, evaluated across various object categories

claims.claim: CorDex generalizes well to unseen object instances and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, starting from just a single human demonstration
claims.direction: favors single-demonstration-plus-synthetic-augmentation over larger real demonstration datasets for generalization to novel instances
claims.conditions: dexterous hand, various object categories; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: CofactVLA: Deconfounding Vision-Language-Action Models via Counterfactual Intervention

claims.claim: VLAs frequently exhibit a 'vision-override' phenomenon / causal confusion: due to modality imbalance between dense visual streams and sparse language instructions, policies overfit to spurious visual confounders (prominent objects, familiar layouts) instead of using language as the causal driver
claims.direction: identifies visual-confounder-driven causal confusion as a specific failure mode of standard VLA training, motivating explicit deconfounding mechanisms
claims.conditions: diverse simulation benchmarks plus real-world robot experiments

claims.claim: CofactVLA constructs a language-masked counterfactual branch and uses Action-Level Orthogonal Projection Guidance (projecting the factual flow-matching velocity field away from the counterfactual visual-bias direction) plus Feature-Level Counterfactual Covariance Reduction to suppress visual shortcuts while preserving causal language intent
claims.direction: favors explicit causal/counterfactual intervention mechanisms to strengthen language conditioning against visual shortcut confounds, over standard joint vision-language conditioning
claims.conditions: flow-matching-based VLA architecture, sim + real-robot

claims.claim: Yields a 52.3 percentage-point absolute success-rate gain under out-of-distribution scenarios in real-world robot experiments, beyond establishing new state-of-the-art results across diverse simulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors causal deconfounding methods for closing the generalization gap under OOD conditions
claims.conditions: real-world robot experiments, OOD scenarios

why_deep_read: A 52.3-percentage-point real-world OOD success-rate gain from explicitly countering visual-confounder overfitting (causal confusion) is one of the largest, most directly applicable numbers in this batch for our Q07 decision and for our observed failure under new lighting/objects/camera shift; full text would clarify implementation cost and compatibility with flow-matching action heads at small model scale.

title: UniHM: Unified Dexterous Hand Manipulation with Vision Language Model

claims.claim: A vision-language-action model trained solely on human-object interaction data (not robot teleoperation data) eliminates the need for massive real-world teleoperation datasets while still generalizing to seen and unseen objects/trajectories with state-of-the-art results
claims.direction: favors training on human-object interaction data instead of robot teleoperation data for data efficiency
claims.conditions: dexterous hand manipulation (different embodiment from our 2-finger gripper), multiple datasets and real-world evaluations

title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations

claims.claim: Task progress (normalized time remaining) is linearly readable from the residual-stream activations of a pretrained VLA (pi_0.5), including from the pretrained PaliGemma backbone prior to any robot-specific training; a linear probe trained on this signal generalizes to unseen tasks and, used as a label-free OOD detector for stalled task progress, is competitive with state-of-the-art OOD detection methods
claims.direction: favors using a lightweight linear probe on existing VLA activations as a runtime failure/OOD detector, rather than a separate learned monitor or additional sensors
claims.conditions: probing pi_0.5 / PaliGemma backbone; qualitative claim ('competitive with state-of-the-art'), no specific detection-accuracy numbers given

title: Time-Frequency Geometric Cross-Attention for Chunked Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Standard chunked VLA policies decode an action chunk as a sequence of generic per-timestep tokens, which entangles the chunk's smooth global trend with its fine corrective motion across time scales and fails to represent near-orthogonal cross-phase geometry (reach, contact, grasp adjustment, settling) well, since dot-product attention favors aligned tokens; a drop-in Time-Frequency Geometric Cross-Attention (TFGCA) module using a learnable per-dimension stationary wavelet decomposition plus a wedge-product-augmented attention fixes both issues
claims.direction: favors explicitly decomposing/reasoning over an action chunk's time-frequency and cross-phase-geometric structure, rather than treating chunk tokens as generic per-timestep vectors
claims.conditions: drop-in module added to a pretrained VLA and fine-tuned jointly (zero-initialized residual, base behavior preserved at init)

claims.claim: Relative to the same-source base model, TFGCA improves in-distribution LIBERO by +1.5 points on average, OOD LIBERO-Plus by +6.3 points, and randomized average success under RoboTwin domain randomization by +28.5 points, with larger gains further out of distribution
claims.direction: favors this time-frequency/geometric attention module for OOD and domain-randomization robustness specifically
claims.conditions: sim benchmarks LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin domain randomization

claims.claim: Improves the overall success rate on three real-robot AgiBot A2 tasks by +11.67 percentage points as a drop-in, fine-tunable addition to a pretrained chunked VLA
claims.direction: favors adding structured time-frequency/geometric attention within the action-chunk decoder to improve real-robot execution quality
claims.conditions: real-robot AgiBot A2, three tasks

title: ManipLVM-R1: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in Embodied Manipulation with Large Vision-Language Models

claims.claim: Replacing supervised imitation with rule-based Reinforcement Learning using Verifiable Rewards (an Affordance Perception Reward and a Trajectory Match Reward) achieves substantial performance gains across multiple manipulation tasks while using only 50% of the training data compared to standard supervised approaches
claims.direction: favors verifiable-reward RL over supervised imitation learning for data efficiency
claims.conditions: large vision-language model manipulation tasks; qualitative 'substantial gains' claim, no exact success-rate numbers given

claims.claim: Achieves strong generalization to out-of-domain (OOD) scenarios
claims.direction: favors this reward-based training approach for OOD generalization over standard human-annotated supervised training
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: χ0: Resource-Aware Robust Manipulation via Taming Distributional Inconsistencies

claims.claim: Identifies that the primary bottleneck to real-world robustness is not resource scale but a systematic distributional inconsistency among the human-demonstration distribution, the policy's learned inductive bias, and the test-time execution distribution, which causes compounding errors in multi-stage tasks
claims.direction: frames robustness failures (our observed lighting/object/camera-shift breakage) as a train/deploy distribution-mismatch problem rather than a pure data/model-scale problem
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robots, long-horizon garment manipulation (folding, flattening, hanging)

claims.claim: Uses 'Model Arithmetic' (weight-space merging) to efficiently absorb diverse demonstration distributions varying in object appearance and state, and 'Train-Deploy Alignment' via spatio-temporal augmentation and heuristic DAgger corrections to bridge the train/deploy distribution gap
claims.direction: favors weight-space merging across demo subsets plus spatio-temporal augmentation and DAgger-style corrections over training a single policy on pooled raw demonstrations
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, garment manipulation

claims.claim: Uses 'temporal chunk-wise smoothing' as part of Train-Deploy Alignment to address action-chunk-boundary issues, and a stage-aware advantage estimator ('Stage Advantage') for stable dense progress signals instead of numerically unstable non-stage approaches
claims.direction: favors explicit chunk-wise smoothing across chunk boundaries and stage-aware progress signals over standard fixed-chunk execution without smoothing
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robot, long-horizon multi-stage tasks

claims.claim: χ0 surpasses the state-of-the-art π_0.5 baseline in success rate by nearly 250%, using only 20 hours of data and 8 A100 GPUs, and runs autonomously from arbitrary initial states for 24 consecutive hours non-stop
claims.direction: favors this resource-efficient, distribution-alignment-focused framework over scaling data/compute alone (as in π_0.5) for high-reliability long-horizon manipulation
claims.conditions: real dual-arm robots, garment manipulation, 20-hour training data, 8 A100 GPUs (still substantially more compute than our single 8GB laptop GPU)

why_deep_read: This paper explicitly targets exactly our failure modes (distributional mismatch causing compounding errors under appearance/state variation, and chunk-boundary smoothness) with a large quantified real-robot gain (~250% over π_0.5); full text would clarify which of its three techniques (weight merging, stage advantage, chunk-wise smoothing) are lightweight enough to adapt to our much smaller compute/data budget.

title: Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation in Construction via Zero-Shot Learning: A Diffusion Policy-Guided Adaptive Control

claims.claim: A diffusion policy trained purely on simulation-generated pose and force/torque data, combined with an L1-inspired adaptive controller that corrects policy-predicted actions online, achieves 100% success on single-task contact-rich assembly and 90-100% success across sequential truss-assembly subtasks, with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
claims.direction: favors pairing a diffusion-policy action head with an online adaptive corrective controller over using the diffusion policy's raw predicted actions alone, for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: real-world timber joinery, pipe fitting, and truss assembly; zero real demonstration data used (simulation-only training)

claims.claim: Training entirely on simulation-generated data (no real-world demonstrations) and achieving zero-shot sim-to-real transfer reduces costly, labor-intensive real-world data collection
claims.direction: favors simulation-only data generation over real teleoperated demonstration collection for this task class
claims.conditions: real-world zero-shot deployment, construction assembly tasks

title: Acting in Meters: Learning Metric Interactions for Precise Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Adding object-level Interaction-Centric Tokens (end-effector pose trajectories relative to manipulated objects, jointly denoised with actions) and a scene-level Metric Action Interaction Field that attends to metric scene point-cloud features to produce geometry-conditioned action corrections improves diverse VLA and World-Action-Model baselines with only a small number of additional parameters and training steps
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight, explicit metric/point-cloud-grounded correction module on top of an existing VLA/WAM, over relying on the base model's implicit spatial reasoning alone
claims.conditions: two-stage adaptation on top of existing VLA/WAM baselines; evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks plus their OOD variants

claims.claim: Reports average success-rate gains of 0.80 and 3.59 percentage points on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 respectively, 6.80 percentage points on real-world tasks, and 7.45 percentage points on their out-of-distribution variants
claims.direction: favors this metric/geometry-grounded correction approach specifically for improving OOD robustness (larger gain OOD than in-distribution)
claims.conditions: real-world tasks and their OOD variants, small number of added parameters/training steps

title: Vision-Language Grounded Task-Context-Aware Imitation Learning for Robotic Disassembly

claims.claim: Combining hierarchical task selection with task-context-aware imitation learning that grounds language instructions in spatial visual representations improves end-to-end task success by 35 percentage points over a baseline diffusion policy and by 75 percentage points over a previous task-context-aware baseline, generalizing across diverse connector geometries and assembly configurations without explicit object annotations
claims.direction: favors explicit language-grounded, task-context-aware conditioning (hierarchical task selection + spatial grounding of language) over a plain diffusion-policy baseline lacking task-context language conditioning
claims.conditions: robotic disassembly domain (long-horizon, multi-part, multiple valid task goals); domain differs from single-object pick-and-place but the language-conditioning comparison against a diffusion-policy baseline is directly relevant

title: Simulation-Driven Imitation Learning for Biosignals-Free Shared-Autonomy Prosthetic Grasping

claims.claim: A scalable simulation framework automatically generates diverse reach-to-grasp demonstrations (physically feasible grasp synthesis, natural reaching-trajectory retargeting, procedurally generated indoor environments) recorded from a wrist-mounted virtual camera, producing a large-scale demonstration dataset without real-world data collection
claims.direction: favors large-scale simulated demonstration generation over collecting large real-world demonstration sets
claims.conditions: simulation benchmarks; wrist-view observations, proprioception, and actions recorded

claims.claim: Demonstrations and policies are built specifically around wrist-mounted camera observations
claims.direction: supports wrist-camera-centric observation design for reach-to-grasp tasks
claims.conditions: simulation-generated data, evaluated in simulation and via sim-to-real transfer

claims.claim: The learned sim-to-real policy achieves over 90% grasp success in three realistic real-world settings, surpassing baseline imitation-learning methods and exhibiting stronger object/scene generalization, despite using zero real teleoperated demonstrations
claims.direction: favors simulation-generated demonstrations as sufficient (and superior to some baselines) for real-world grasp policy learning, without any real teleoperated data
claims.conditions: real-world sim-to-real deployment, three settings, comparison against several SOTA imitation-learning methods; domain is prosthetic (different embodiment/task) reach-to-grasp

title: Decoupled Reactive World Model and Non-Anthropomorphic Echolocation for Hard Real-Time Robotics: Resolving the Embodiment Bottleneck via Acoustic Waveform ToF and Epistemic Externalization

claims.claim: Standard camera-based VLA pipelines (2D image capture at 30-60Hz through a vision transformer to autoregressive token generation) are reported to incur an irreducible closed-loop latency of 150-500ms, which the authors argue is incompatible with real-time dynamic stabilization or high-speed collision avoidance
claims.direction: identifies camera-plus-VLA-token-generation pipelines as an inherent latency bottleneck for real-time control (motivates non-camera-based fast sensing alternatives, in this paper's case active ultrasonic/radar echolocation)
claims.conditions: humanoid robotics context (Tesla Optimus/Figure/Atlas-style systems); claims are theoretical/architectural rather than tied to a specific benchmarked robot in the excerpt available

claims.claim: Passive camera-based depth estimation (monocular and stereoscopic) is reported to degrade catastrophically under specular reflections, strong backlighting, textureless surfaces, and darkness ('depth hallucination'), motivating replacing cameras with active 3D sensing (piezoelectric ultrasonic transducers and FMCW radar) for sub-millimeter, illumination-independent depth at high update rates and low power
claims.direction: flags a specific, named failure mode of camera-based (including RGB-D) depth sensing under lighting/reflectance conditions, as motivation for active (non-camera) depth sensing instead
claims.conditions: proposed architecture is for humanoid robots with a novel echolocation sensor suite, not evaluated on a standard manipulation benchmark or a RealSense-based setup; extraordinary claimed numbers (e.g., 28,000x efficiency gain) should be treated with caution given very limited independent validation evident from the abstract

title: ST-π: Structured SpatioTemporal VLA for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Rather than embedding spatiotemporal knowledge implicitly and directly mapping to step-level actions, ST-π has the VLM generate a sequence of causally-ordered, explicit chunk-level action prompts (sub-tasks, spatial grounding, temporal grounding), which an action expert then uses to jointly model spatial dependencies and temporal causality for step-level action parameters
claims.direction: favors explicit, structured chunk-level spatiotemporal planning (sub-task/spatial/temporal grounding per chunk) over implicit end-to-end spatiotemporal reasoning for handling multiple sequential behaviors with clear boundaries
claims.conditions: real-world robotic dataset with structured spatiotemporal annotations, used for fine-tuning; qualitative claim ('extensive experiments demonstrate effectiveness'), no specific success-rate numbers given in the abstract

claims.claim: Encodes 4D observations and task instructions jointly into latent spaces fed to an LLM to generate structured, causally-ordered action prompts
claims.direction: favors joint language-and-spatiotemporal conditioning at the chunk level over simple language-token conditioning
claims.conditions: same setup as above

title: Spline Policy: A Structured Representation for Robot Policies

claims.claim: Replacing fixed-resolution action chunks with spline parameters (while keeping the policy backbone unchanged) yields a compact continuous trajectory that can be queried at different temporal resolutions, constrained/edited in parameter space, and passed to downstream controllers; the representation is compatible with diffusion, flow-matching, transformer, and VLA backbones
claims.direction: favors a structured continuous (spline) action-chunk representation over standard fixed-resolution discrete action chunks, as a backbone-agnostic drop-in change
claims.conditions: tested in low-dimensional motion learning, simulated manipulation under matched backbones, dexterous manipulation, and real-robot case studies

claims.claim: For quadratic spline outputs, an analytical distance-field construction converts the spline into a state-dependent vector field whose induced dynamics do not increase distance to the generated spline, providing a principled local corrective mechanism around predicted motion; this also supports uncertainty propagation and combination with classical controllers (e.g., null-space collision avoidance) without retraining the backbone
claims.direction: favors a spline-based action representation with a built-in local-correction/vector-field mechanism for smoother, more correctable execution around predicted motion, relevant to reducing discontinuities at chunk boundaries
claims.conditions: same experimental settings as above; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given on smoothness or success-rate improvement

title: Reducing Temporal Redundancy for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference

claims.claim: Identifies two sources of temporal redundancy in VLA inference latency: repeated visual encoding of highly similar consecutive frames, and multi-step iterative sampling in diffusion-based policies; addressing both (incrementally updating only tokens for dynamic scene regions instead of re-encoding entire frames, and compressing diffusion sampling into a compact 2-step schedule via efficiency-oriented training) achieves over 2x speedup while maintaining high performance, up to 98% success rate on general manipulation benchmarks
claims.direction: favors incremental/partial visual re-encoding plus few-step diffusion sampling schedules over full frame re-encoding and many-step diffusion sampling, to reduce VLA inference latency without sacrificing success rate
claims.conditions: evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real robot platforms

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported ~2s inference-latency problem with a concrete, quantified (>2x speedup, up to 98% success retained) system-level acceleration strategy (incremental visual tokens + 2-step diffusion sampling); full text would give the real-robot latency numbers and clarify whether the technique is compatible with our smaller model and 8GB GPU.

title: An Unexpected Robot Policy: Early Evaluations of GPT-6 Astra on RoboDojo and Beyond

claims.claim: Using a large language model directly as the manipulation policy (no task-specific finetuning), GPT-6 Astra achieves 22.48% average success rate over 2,100 trials across all 42 RoboDojo tasks, ranking above 40 public trained policies, while two other LLMs (GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-Flash) reach only 0.88% and 1.92%; Astra generalizes well to tasks requiring semantic understanding but performs poorly on tasks requiring precision, dynamic control, or complex bimanual coordination, and shows no aggregate benefit from one-shot in-context demonstrations
claims.direction: suggests LLM-as-policy (no finetuning) can rival/exceed some trained policies on semantic-understanding-heavy tasks but remains weak specifically on high-precision/dynamic-control manipulation -- relevant caution for our precision pick-and-place task
claims.conditions: RoboDojo benchmark, 42 tasks, standard 50-episode-per-task protocol for Astra/GPT-5.5 (10 for DeepSeek-Flash); unclear if real robot or simulated benchmark

title: Benchmarking Vision, Language, & Action Models on Robotic Learning Tasks

claims.claim: Profiling GPT-4o, OpenVLA, and JAT across 20 diverse Open-X-Embodiment datasets finds that model performance is notably sensitive to action-space characteristics
claims.direction: flags action-space choice as a significant, empirically-observed source of performance variation across VLA models
claims.conditions: 20 datasets from Open-X-Embodiment, 3 models; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given per action-space type

claims.claim: All evaluated models show significant performance variation across different tasks/robot platforms and struggle with complex multi-step planning; performance is also notably sensitive to environmental factors
claims.direction: documents that current VLA models generalize inconsistently across platforms/environments, motivating explicit robustness evaluation
claims.conditions: same cross-dataset benchmark; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: SimLauncher: Launching Sample-Efficient Real-World Robotic Reinforcement Learning via Simulation Pre-Training

claims.claim: Pre-training a visuomotor policy in a digital-twin simulation, then using it to bootstrap target values and provide action proposals for real-world RL, significantly improves sample efficiency and achieves near-perfect success rates compared to prior real-world RL approaches, across multi-stage, contact-rich, and dexterous hand manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors simulation pre-training plus real-world RL fine-tuning over pure real-world RL for sample efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across multiple manipulation task types; this is an RL (not pure imitation-learning) data-efficiency result

title: GauDP: Reinventing Multi-Agent Collaboration through Gaussian-Image Synergy in Diffusion Policies

claims.claim: Constructing a globally consistent 3D Gaussian field from decentralized RGB observations (no additional sensing modality such as point clouds) and redistributing Gaussian attributes to each agent's local view achieves superior performance over existing image-based methods and approaches the effectiveness of point-cloud-driven methods
claims.direction: favors deriving an implicit 3D (Gaussian-splatting) representation from RGB-only observations, as a way to approach point-cloud-level performance without needing an actual depth/point-cloud sensor
claims.conditions: RoboFactory benchmark, multi-arm manipulation tasks (multi-agent setting differs from our single-arm setup)

title: AMPLIFY: Actionless Motion Priors for Robot Learning from Videos

claims.claim: Decoupling visual-motion prediction (a forward dynamics model trained on abundant action-free video, encoding visual dynamics into compact discrete motion tokens from keypoint trajectories) from action inference (an inverse dynamics model trained on a limited set of action-labeled examples) allows the two to be scaled independently, and the learned dynamics achieve up to 3.7x better MSE and over 2.5x better pixel-prediction accuracy than prior approaches
claims.direction: favors a decoupled forward-dynamics/motion-token auxiliary objective (learned mostly from action-free video) plus a separate, lightweight inverse-dynamics action decoder, over end-to-end action learning from scarce action-labeled data alone
claims.conditions: trained on large-scale action-free video plus a limited action-labeled set; evaluated on downstream policy learning benchmarks including LIBERO

claims.claim: Using these decoupled dynamics predictions gives a 1.2-2.2x improvement in low-data regimes, a 1.4x average improvement from learning with additional action-free human videos, and enables the first generalization to LIBERO tasks starting from zero in-distribution action-labeled data
claims.direction: favors leveraging abundant action-free video data (rather than scaling action-labeled robot demonstrations) to improve policy performance specifically in low-demo-count regimes
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark, various low-data regimes; some real-robot demonstrations may be involved but abstract emphasizes benchmark comparisons

title: Reinforcing Action Policies by Prophesying

claims.claim: Prophet, a unified action-to-video robot world model pretrained on large-scale heterogeneous robot data and few-shot adapted to new robots/objects/environments, provides a rollout-ready simulator used for RL-based post-training of VLA policies (avoiding expensive real-robot interaction and hard-to-engineer conventional simulators)
claims.direction: favors using a pretrained, few-shot-adaptable video world model as a substitute simulator for RL post-training over either real-robot RL or conventional simulators
claims.conditions: pretrained on large-scale heterogeneous robot data, few-shot adapted; evaluated across diverse VLA backbones

claims.claim: FlowScale, an RL procedure (Flow-GRPO plus intrinsic stepwise reweighting) tailored to flow-based action heads, together with the Prophet world model, gives 5-17% success-rate gains on public benchmarks and 24-30% gains on real robots across diverse VLA backbones, addressing imitation learning's overfitting-to-demonstrations brittleness under distribution shift
claims.direction: favors RL post-training specifically adapted to flow-matching action heads (via a world-model simulator) over pure imitation learning alone, to counter overfitting/distribution-shift brittleness
claims.conditions: real-robot experiments across diverse VLA backbones (flow-based action heads specifically)

title: Unified Noise Steering for Efficient Human-Guided VLA Adaptation

claims.claim: UniSteer inverts a frozen flow-matching decoder to convert human corrective actions (given in action space) into noise-space supervision targets, combining this with noise-space RL (which keeps the pretrained diffusion/flow VLA fixed and updates only a lightweight noise-predicting actor) to overcome the inefficient autonomous exploration of noise-space RL alone
claims.direction: favors combining human corrective action-space guidance with noise-space RL (via action-to-noise inversion) over either noise-space RL alone or action-space human-in-the-loop RL alone, for adapting a frozen flow-matching VLA
claims.conditions: real-world experiments, diverse manipulation tasks, four real-world adaptation tasks

claims.claim: UniSteer improves the real-world success rate from 20% to 90% in an average of 66 minutes across four real-world adaptation tasks, adapting more efficiently than both strong noise-space RL and action-space human-in-the-loop baselines
claims.direction: favors this lightweight, human-guided noise-space adaptation for extremely fast, low-interaction-budget post-deployment policy improvement, over either RL-only or naive human-in-the-loop correction
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation tasks, ~66 minutes of adaptation time per result

title: RoboDream: Compositional World Models for Scalable Robot Data Synthesis

claims.claim: An embodiment-centric world model anchors generation to rendered robot motion while conditioning on explicit scene/object priors, synthesizing photorealistic demonstrations with novel objects, novel scenes, and novel viewpoints (rather than superficial visual augmentation), enabling 'retrieval and rebirth' (repurposing existing trajectories into new contexts without new motion data) and 'prop-free teleoperation' (operators manipulate empty air and the model hallucinates target objects/scene afterward, eliminating reset time)
claims.direction: favors embodiment-anchored generative data synthesis (novel objects/scenes/viewpoints from existing trajectories) over either superficial visual augmentation or collecting entirely new teleoperated demonstrations for each new object/scene/viewpoint
claims.conditions: real-world experiments across diverse manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Generated data consistently improves downstream policy performance and significantly reduces real-world data requirements across diverse manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors this compositional world-model data-synthesis approach for reducing the amount of real teleoperated data needed
claims.conditions: real-world experiments; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: PokeVLA: Empowering Pocket-Sized Vision-Language-Action Model with Comprehensive World Knowledge Guidance

claims.claim: A lightweight, 'pocket-sized' VLA foundation model, pre-trained on a curated 2.4M-sample multimodal dataset (spatial grounding, affordance, embodied reasoning) and then injected with manipulation-relevant representations via multi-view goal-aware semantics learning, geometry alignment, and a novel action expert, achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO-Plus benchmark and in real-world deployment
claims.direction: favors a small/lightweight VLA design (with targeted pretraining and representation injection) over larger foundation models for achieving strong manipulation performance
claims.conditions: sim benchmark LIBERO-Plus plus real-world deployment

claims.claim: Outperforms comparable baselines in success rate and robustness under diverse perturbations
claims.direction: favors this lightweight, world-knowledge-guided design for robustness to perturbations, not just nominal success rate
claims.conditions: real-world deployment; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: AnoleVLA: Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Model with Deep State Space Models for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Replacing a standard transformer backbone with a deep state-space model (SSM) for processing multimodal (visual+textual) sequences enables efficient sequential state modeling for trajectory generation in a VLA
claims.direction: favors SSM-based sequence backbones over standard transformer backbones for lightweight, efficient VLA policies
claims.conditions: real-world physical experiments plus simulation

claims.claim: AnoleVLA outperformed a representative large-scale VLA by 21 percentage points on real-world task success rate
claims.direction: favors this lightweight SSM-based architecture over a large-scale VLA for real-world manipulation performance, not just efficiency
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation

claims.claim: Achieves an inference speed approximately three times faster than the representative large-scale VLA baseline
claims.direction: favors lightweight SSM-based VLA architectures for reducing inference latency
claims.conditions: real-world evaluation; specific baseline model and hardware not named in the abstract

why_deep_read: A lightweight state-space-model VLA that is both 21 points more accurate AND 3x faster than a large-scale VLA baseline on real-world tasks is an unusually strong, directly applicable result for our 8GB-GPU, ~2s-latency laptop setup; full text would give the exact parameter counts, baseline model identity, and hardware used, which are needed to judge transferability to our setup.

title: 3D HAMSTER: Bridging Planning and Control in Hierarchical Vision Language Action Models through 3D Trajectory Guidance

claims.claim: Feeding a point-cloud-based low-level policy with 2D end-effector trajectories (lacking depth) forces each waypoint to take the depth of whatever surface lies beneath it, producing geometrically distorted trajectories; augmenting the planning VLM with a dedicated depth encoder and a dense depth-reconstruction objective to directly output metrically reliable 3D waypoint sequences fixes this and consistently outperforms proprietary VLMs and 2D-guided baselines
claims.direction: favors giving the high-level planner explicit 3D/depth-aware trajectory prediction (rather than 2D trajectories fed into a 3D low-level policy) when the low-level policy operates on point clouds
claims.conditions: evaluated across 3D trajectory prediction, simulation, and real-world manipulation

claims.claim: The largest performance gains over baselines occur specifically under appearance-altering shifts and unseen language, spatial, and visual conditions
claims.direction: favors explicit 3D-aware planning for robustness specifically to appearance changes (e.g., a different-looking object) and novel conditions, more so than for in-distribution performance
claims.conditions: real-world manipulation, appearance-altering shift conditions

title: τ0-WM: A Unified Video-Action World Model for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A unified video-action world model, built on a shared video-diffusion backbone and trained on ~27,300 hours of real-robot teleoperation, UMI-style interaction, and egocentric human video, jointly predicts future visual latents and action chunks, and at inference time samples/ranks action candidates via re-denoising consistency plus simulator-based rectification for low-quality candidates, showing superior performance over other baselines on long-horizon and fine-grained tasks
claims.direction: favors combining action generation with an action-conditioned video-based future simulator for test-time candidate ranking/rectification, over action generation alone
claims.conditions: trained on ~27,300 hours of heterogeneous data (far larger than our data/compute budget); qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for Continuous and Consistent Robotic Action Generation

claims.claim: Standard flow-matching/diffusion policies rely on discretized action chunks, making them brittle to demonstrations collected at heterogeneous control frequencies and prone to temporally inconsistent actions that degrade control stability; Frequency-Aware Flow Matching (FAFM) instead transforms action sequences into the frequency domain via discrete cosine transform, performs flow matching over the DCT coefficients, and reconstructs continuous actions via cosine basis expansion
claims.direction: favors a frequency-domain, continuous action representation over standard discretized fixed-rate action chunks, particularly for robustness to mixed/heterogeneous control-frequency training data
claims.conditions: synthetic toy benchmark, obstacle avoidance, LapGym, LIBERO, and a real-world Franka robot

claims.claim: Regularizing the first-order temporal derivative of the reconstructed action (a Sobolev-type constraint) suppresses high-frequency errors and discourages abrupt action changes, improving motion smoothness; FAFM introduces no additional network parameters and applies to standalone flow-matching policies as well as VLA models, with consistent gains when deployed on a real-world Franka robot
claims.direction: favors adding a zero-extra-parameter smoothness regularization directly targeting abrupt/high-frequency action changes (i.e., jerkiness), rather than relying on chunk-level temporal ensembling alone
claims.conditions: real-world Franka robot deployment plus sim benchmarks

claims.claim: FAFM improves robustness specifically to mixed-frequency input and to mechanical bias, in addition to improving success rate, multimodal expressivity, and convergence speed
claims.direction: favors action representations that explicitly handle heterogeneous/mixed control frequencies, relevant when combining or transitioning between different demonstration-collection frequencies
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

why_deep_read: This is one of the most directly applicable findings in the batch: a zero-extra-parameter, frequency-domain smoothness regularization for flow-matching/VLA action chunks, validated on a real Franka robot, that explicitly targets action-chunk temporal inconsistency/jerkiness and robustness to mixed control frequencies -- both of which match our reported jerky-motion-at-chunk-boundaries problem and our planned 10fps-to-30fps transition.

title: Tra-MoE: Learning Trajectory Prediction Model from Multiple Domains for Adaptive Policy Conditioning

claims.claim: A trajectory-prediction model that predicts any-point 2D trajectories from an instruction, used to condition a downstream action policy via 2D mask representations explicitly aligned with image observations, guides action prediction more flexibly than direct instruction-to-action mapping
claims.direction: favors conditioning the action policy on an explicit predicted-trajectory/mask representation rather than mapping instructions directly to actions
claims.conditions: sim and real-world experiments

claims.claim: A sparsely-gated Mixture-of-Experts (Top-1 gating) trajectory-prediction architecture (Tra-MoE) consistently outperforms a dense baseline model even when the dense baseline is scaled to match Tra-MoE's parameter count, while maintaining constant FLOPs per token
claims.direction: favors sparse MoE architectures over dense architectures at matched parameter count, for learning from diverse (including out-of-domain) data
claims.conditions: sim and real-world experiments, multi-domain out-of-domain data

title: Few-Shot Vision-Language Action-Incremental Policy Learning

claims.claim: Learning Task-Specific Prompts through deep interaction of multi-modal information within few-shot demonstrations, combined with a Continuous Evolution Strategy that reuses skills learned from previous tasks via a task-relation graph, outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by over 26% in success rate on a proposed few-shot continual-learning benchmark, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting
claims.direction: favors task-specific prompt learning plus skill-reuse-based continual learning over standard few-shot fine-tuning for learning new tasks from only a few demonstrations without forgetting old ones
claims.conditions: transformer-based multi-view manipulation policies, few-shot per new task

claims.claim: Uses multi-view spatial representations combined with language instructions as the basis for extracting task-specific discriminative information
claims.direction: favors combining multi-view visual input with language conditioning for task discrimination in a few-shot/continual setting
claims.conditions: same setup as above

title: R2RDreamer: 3D-aware Data Augmentation for Spatially-generalized 2D Manipulation Policies

claims.claim: R2RDreamer performs lightweight 3D augmentation by editing incomplete object point clouds and end-effector trajectories in a shared 3D frame (from a few real source demonstrations), then projects the edited scene into masked image-space control videos with occlusion-aware reasoning and uses a dense-control image-to-video model to complete temporally coherent RGB observations -- avoiding the need for full simulation environment/object setup or reliance on a 3D-pointcloud-specific downstream policy
claims.direction: favors real-to-real, 3D-consistency-preserving data augmentation that outputs RGB (2D) observations, over either simulation-based augmentation (sim-to-real gap) or 3D-editing methods tailored only to point-cloud policies
claims.conditions: spatially shifted manipulation tasks (object pose, robot configuration, and camera-viewpoint variation), evaluated on both 2D diffusion-style policies and vision-language-action policies

claims.claim: Improves spatial generalization from limited source demonstrations on spatially-shifted manipulation tasks, with ablations validating the separate contributions of 3D editing, occlusion-aware projection, and video completion
claims.direction: favors this augmentation pipeline specifically for robustness to object pose, robot configuration, and camera-viewpoint shifts
claims.conditions: same setup as above; qualitative claim ('improves spatial generalization'), no specific success-rate numbers given

title: Monkey See, Can Monkey Do? A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Skill Learning by Observation

claims.claim: A unified benchmark (RoboReel) evaluating over seven state-of-the-art learning-from-observation (human-video) algorithms across ten manipulation tasks finds that long-horizon tasks and tasks with low tolerances remain challenging for current models, and specifically tests robustness to visual distractors
claims.direction: documents that current learning-from-human-video approaches still struggle with long-horizon, low-tolerance, and distractor-robustness settings, informing expectations for such methods
claims.conditions: bundled real human demonstration videos, simulated robot trajectories, and evaluation environments; qualitative claim, no specific success-rate numbers given

title: LAMP: Lift Image-Editing as General 3D Priors for Open-world Manipulation

claims.claim: LAMP lifts the implicit 2D spatial cues inherent in image-editing models into continuous, geometry-aware 3D inter-object transformations, providing fine-grained and accurate guidance for manipulation without relying on LLM/VLM 2D-annotation-based reasoning alone
claims.direction: favors deriving 3D geometric transformation priors from 2D image-editing models over relying on LLM/VLM semantic reasoning with limited 3D awareness
claims.conditions: extensive experiments, open-world manipulation; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

claims.claim: Achieves strong zero-shot generalization in open-world manipulation
claims.direction: favors this image-editing-derived 3D-prior approach for zero-shot generalization to novel objects/scenes
claims.conditions: qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: PointWorld: Scaling 3D World Models for In-The-Wild Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: PointWorld unifies state and action in a shared 3D space as 3D point flows, taking one or few RGB-D images plus a sequence of low-level robot action commands and forecasting per-pixel 3D displacements in response to actions
claims.direction: favors representing observations/dynamics as 3D point flows derived from RGB-D input over embodiment-specific 2D or joint-space-only representations
claims.conditions: trained on ~2M trajectories / 500 hours across a single-arm Franka and a bimanual humanoid, real and simulated data

claims.claim: Representing actions as 3D point flows instead of embodiment-specific action spaces (e.g., joint positions) directly conditions on the physical geometry of the robot while enabling learning across embodiments; the authors report 'rigorous, large-scale empirical studies of backbones, action representations, learning objectives, partial observability, data mixtures, domain transfers, and scaling' from which they distill design principles for 3D world modeling
claims.direction: favors a geometry-grounded (3D point-flow) action representation over standard embodiment-specific action spaces, based on a large empirical comparison of action-representation choices
claims.conditions: same large-scale training data as above; specific numerical results of the backbone/action-representation ablations are not given in the abstract

claims.claim: The pretrained 3D world model can be integrated into a model-predictive-control (MPC) framework at real-time (0.1s) inference speed
claims.direction: favors using a fast, pretrained 3D world model for MPC-style action selection at real-time speed, relevant to reducing overall inference latency when using a world model
claims.conditions: real-time inference benchmarked at 0.1s; hardware not fully specified in the abstract

claims.claim: A single pretrained checkpoint enables a real-world Franka robot to perform rigid-body pushing, deformable and articulated object manipulation, and tool use, without requiring any demonstrations or post-training, from a single in-the-wild image
claims.direction: favors a large-scale pretrained 3D world model as a zero-demonstration, zero-post-training solution for new manipulation tasks, as an alternative to task-specific imitation learning from teleop demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world Franka robot, zero-shot, single image, MPC-based execution

title: Adversarial Dual On-Policy Distillation from Expressive Teacher

claims.claim: Standard diffusion/flow-matching behavioral-cloning policies remain offline supervised learners with no corrective signal on states actually visited at deployment; FA-OPD instead learns a Flow-Matching teacher from demonstrations and co-trains a lightweight MLP student, where the teacher provides both a reward-channel expert-likeness signal (for online exploration) and an action-channel dense local target (for stabilized exploitation) on the student's own rollouts
claims.direction: favors augmenting a flow-matching-derived teacher with online on-policy distillation into a lightweight student, over pure offline behavioral cloning with a flow-matching/diffusion policy alone, to correct for the lack of feedback on visited states
claims.conditions: six robot navigation, manipulation, and locomotion benchmarks (mixed domains, not manipulation-only)

claims.claim: FA-OPD beats strong baselines and shows much stronger robustness under noisy or limited demonstrations
claims.direction: favors this teacher-student on-policy distillation approach for robustness specifically when demonstrations are noisy or limited in number
claims.conditions: same six mixed-domain benchmarks; qualitative claim, no specific numbers given

title: TFP: Temporally Conditioned Memory-Fusion Policies for Visuomotor Learning

claims.claim: In stage-dependent manipulation, visually similar states may require different actions depending on latent task progress and prior interaction outcomes; TFP maintains an episode-local task-progress belief updated with Liquid-Time-Constant dynamics (preserving progress during stable/occluded phases, revising it near contact/release/subgoal transitions) and injects this belief directly into the flow-matching action decoder via adaptive modulation, improving average success rate from 96.9% to 98.75% on LIBERO and from 91.4% to 93.77% on LIBERO-plus, with the memory-focused MIKASA ShellGameTouch diagnostic reaching up to 75.0% success; mechanistic analysis shows the belief's write-gain is about 6x larger near manipulation events than in non-event phases, and hidden-state interventions confirm the belief causally shapes generated action chunks
claims.direction: favors dynamics-aware, event-sensitive belief-state memory (revised at contact/release/subgoal transitions, held stable otherwise) injected into the action decoder, over either purely reactive policies or passive raw-history conditioning, for handling occlusion, visual perturbation, and stage-dependent task structure
claims.conditions: 3.3B-parameter model, sim benchmarks LIBERO/LIBERO-plus/MIKASA ShellGameTouch (large model size relative to our compute budget)

claims.claim: The updated task-progress belief is injected into the flow-matching action decoder through adaptive modulation, analogous to FiLM-style conditioning but based on internal task-progress state rather than external language
claims.direction: suggests adaptive-modulation-based conditioning (as used for language/FiLM) is also an effective mechanism for injecting internal memory/belief signals into an action decoder
claims.conditions: same setup as above

title: CompVLA: A Variable Compliance Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-rich Manipulation

claims.claim: Augmenting a conventional VLA architecture with a dedicated Compliance Expert that jointly predicts motion and a stiffness matrix (executed via geometric impedance control) achieves the highest average success rate across diverse contact-rich tasks, outperforming both vanilla VLA baselines (which output purely kinematic commands) and other compliance-aware VLA baselines, with ablations confirming each component is essential
claims.direction: favors jointly predicting stiffness/compliance alongside motion (not purely kinematic action output) for contact-rich manipulation tasks
claims.conditions: diverse contact-rich tasks; real vs. sim not specified in the abstract; may be relevant if placing the pumpkin in the tray involves contact-rich alignment

title: General Flow as Foundation Affordance for Scalable Robot Learning

claims.claim: A language-conditioned 3D flow prediction model, trained directly from large-scale RGBD human-video datasets, represents future trajectories of 3D points on objects of interest as the prediction target, providing actionable guidance for a closed-loop flow-prediction-based policy
claims.direction: favors 3D point-flow (derived from RGBD) as the prediction target/representation for scalable manipulation learning, over embodiment-specific action regression
claims.conditions: trained on large-scale RGBD human-video data (cross-embodiment), deployed on real robots

claims.claim: Without any in-domain (robot-specific) finetuning, the method achieves an 81% success rate in zero-shot human-to-robot skill transfer, covering 18 tasks across 6 scenes
claims.direction: favors leveraging large-scale human-video pretraining for zero-shot transfer over collecting robot-specific teleoperated demonstrations for each new task
claims.conditions: real-world robot deployment, 18 tasks, 6 scenes, zero in-domain finetuning

claims.claim: Provides stable skill transfer with a small inference domain-gap across multiple object categories including rigid, articulated, and soft bodies
claims.direction: favors this 3D-flow-based zero-shot transfer approach for generalization across diverse object types
claims.conditions: real-world deployment, 18 tasks

title: Geometry Meets Vision: Revisiting Pretrained Semantics in Distilled Fields

claims.claim: Comparing visual-only pretrained semantic features (e.g., DINO, CLIP) against geometry-grounded semantic features in distilled radiance fields: geometry-grounded backbones do produce higher-fidelity, finer structural detail in image features, but this does NOT improve semantic object localization (no significant difference found), and it actually DECREASES pose-estimation accuracy when used for radiance-field inversion; visual-only features are found to offer greater versatility across a broader range of downstream spatial tasks
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that adding geometry-grounding to pretrained visual features (e.g., replacing/augmenting DINO/CLIP with geometry-grounded encoders) necessarily helps spatial/pose-related manipulation tasks -- here it specifically hurt pose-estimation accuracy despite producing more geometric detail
claims.conditions: radiance-field/Gaussian-Splatting-based semantic distillation setting, evaluated on object localization and pose-estimation (via a proposed SPINE framework for radiance-field inversion); not evaluated as an end-to-end manipulation policy

title: SAM2Grasp: Resolve Multi-modal Grasping via Prompt-conditioned Temporal Action Prediction

claims.claim: When a scene contains multiple valid grasp targets, standard imitation-learning policies fail by averaging conflicting demonstrated actions into a single invalid action (the multimodality problem); SAM2Grasp instead reformulates the task as uni-modal by using a frozen SAM2 model's visual temporal-tracking capability plus a lightweight, separately-trained action head conditioned on an initial prompt (e.g., a bounding box), which disambiguates the target object and lets SAM2's built-in tracking maintain focus on it across subsequent frames without further guidance, achieving state-of-the-art performance in cluttered, multi-object grasping
claims.direction: favors resolving demonstration multimodality via external prompt-conditioning plus a frozen large-vision-model's temporal tracking (training only a small action head) over using a probabilistic multimodal action head (e.g., CVAE, diffusion, GMM) to directly model the multimodal action distribution
claims.conditions: cluttered, multi-object grasping tasks; only a lightweight action head is trained, using pre-computed features from a frozen SAM2 backbone

title: Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking

claims.claim: An empirical study reveals an inherent trade-off in action-chunk horizon length: longer horizons give stronger global foresight but degrade fine-grained accuracy, while shorter horizons sharpen local control but struggle on long-term tasks, implying any single fixed horizon choice is suboptimal; Mixture of Horizons (MoH) rearranges the action chunk into several segments with different horizons, processes them in parallel with a shared action transformer, and fuses outputs with a light linear gate, exploiting long-term foresight and short-term precision jointly within a single model
claims.direction: favors combining multiple prediction horizons within a single action-chunk decoder (via parallel segments + gating) over committing to one fixed chunk/horizon length
claims.conditions: tested across flow-based policies pi0 and pi0.5 and a one-step regression policy pi_reg, on both simulation and real-world tasks

claims.claim: MoH is plug-and-play for full-attention action modules with minimal training or inference overhead, and enables dynamic inference with adaptive horizons that selects stable actions via cross-horizon consensus, achieving 2.5x higher throughput than baselines while preserving superior performance; under a mixed-task setting, pi0.5 with MoH reaches a new state-of-the-art with 99% average success rate on LIBERO after only 30k training iterations
claims.direction: favors cross-horizon-consensus-based action selection at inference for both smoother/more stable actions and substantially higher throughput (lower latency) versus a single fixed-horizon baseline
claims.conditions: flow-based (pi0, pi0.5) and one-step regression (pi_reg) policies, sim (LIBERO) and real-world tasks; minimal added training/inference overhead reported

why_deep_read: This paper directly and comprehensively targets our Q06 decision (chunking/prediction horizon) with a plug-and-play, backbone-agnostic method validated across both flow-matching and regression action heads, real-world tasks, and a 2.5x throughput gain relevant to our latency problem; it is one of the most directly actionable findings in the whole batch and full text would give the per-horizon-length ablation numbers and guidance on choosing horizon segments for a 10-30fps, low-compute setup like ours.

title: Chronos: A Physics-Informed Full-History Framework for Non-Markovian Long-Horizon Manipulation

claims.claim: Treating observation history as the policy's latent state (via a selective state-space model) rather than a Markovian present-only observation strongly improves memory-dependent long-horizon manipulation: 73.6% avg success on RMBench vs Markovian VLA baseline pi0.5, a +62.4 percentage-point / 6.6x relative gain; in real-world dual-arm tasks with a single RGB camera, 78% avg success (72% on memory-dependent subset) vs pi0.5's 7% overall / 0% on memory-dependent subset.
claims.direction: favors explicit history/memory encoding over Markovian (single-frame/short-window) observation policies
claims.conditions: 16 simulated tasks + 4 real-world dual-arm tasks, single RGB camera, compared against pi0.5 and Mem-0

claims.claim: Chronos achieves its gains using 10x fewer parameters than pi0.5 and 30x fewer than Mem-0
claims.direction: favors smaller parameter-count models when paired with explicit history state
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Action head combines a multimodal coarse action prior (via IMLE) with a second-order Schrodinger-bridge style refinement predicting acceleration fields for smoother, more physically grounded motion
claims.direction: favors structured multimodal+refinement action generation over plain regression for smoothness
claims.conditions: same as above

title: SG-VLA: Learning Spatially-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Models for Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Co-training auxiliary decoders (robot position, joint configuration, grasp affordance, object relative pose, segmentation masks) from shared visual-language features substantially outperforms direct imitation learning on home rearrangement tasks
claims.direction: favors adding auxiliary reconstruction/prediction objectives over plain imitation learning
claims.conditions: home rearrangement tasks, 13-dim mobile manipulation action space, multi-view RGB+depth+short history; sim/real not specified in abstract

claims.claim: Depth cues combined with multi-view RGB and short temporal history enrich spatial understanding
claims.direction: favors adding depth alongside RGB
claims.conditions: same setup, qualitative claim only

claims.claim: Multi-view RGB observations provide global scene layout information that single view lacks
claims.direction: favors multi-view over single-view
claims.conditions: same setup, qualitative

title: Good in Bad (GiB): Sifting Through End-user Demonstrations for Learning a Better Policy

claims.claim: Automatically identifying and discarding only the erroneous subtasks/segments within mixed-quality non-expert demonstrations (rather than discarding whole demos or using them naively) yields more robust policies
claims.direction: favors segment-level data curation over naive use-all or discard-whole-demo approaches, especially in low-data settings
claims.conditions: real Franka robot + simulation, multi-step tasks, mixed-quality human demonstrations

title: HINT: Human-Intent Inception for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Invoking language/semantic reasoning only sparsely at manipulation-pattern transitions (rather than continuously per-step) and maintaining commitment via visual tracking improves intent understanding and task success while preserving low latency, on two foundation VLA policies
claims.direction: favors sparse/event-triggered language conditioning over dense per-step language conditioning for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: 3 long-horizon tasks + OOD variants, no added trainable parameters to base VLA

claims.claim: Maintaining a tracked intent/object-hand relationship across the episode acts as a form of memory that anchors continuous control between semantic re-evaluations
claims.direction: favors persistent intent-tracking memory over purely reactive per-frame policies
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Catch Me If You Can: Real-Time Feedback Denoising for Responsive VLAs
