claims.claim: A two-timescale architecture (low-frequency diffusion planning plus high-frequency visual feedback correction of the final denoising step) improves responsiveness during open-loop chunk execution when the scene changes: matched GR00T on static LIBERO, improved avg success on dynamic sim tasks from 27.5% to 85.0%, and improved real-robot avg success from 51% to 73%
claims.direction: favors adding a lightweight closed-loop correction step within action-chunk execution over fully open-loop diffusion chunk execution
claims.conditions: real-robot tasks and LIBERO simulation, dynamic vs static scenarios

claims.claim: Retaining only the final denoising step of a diffusion action head as a feedback interface preserves diffusion's expressiveness while enabling real-time correction without rerunning the full model
claims.direction: favors lightweight modification of diffusion action head over replacing it with a different head
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Correcting actions using latest observations before each action in a chunk is executed addresses limited responsiveness of open-loop chunked execution
claims.direction: relevant to reducing chunk-boundary staleness/jerkiness
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our reported jerky motion at chunk boundaries and 2s inference latency problem; full text ablations on the feedback mechanism's compute overhead would clarify feasibility on our RTX 5060 laptop.

title: HRP: Human affordances for Robotic Pre-training

claims.claim: Fine-tuning existing visual representations on hand/object/contact affordance labels automatically extracted from internet human videos boosts downstream real-robot manipulation performance by a minimum of 15% across 5 real-world tasks, validated with 3000+ robot trials
claims.direction: favors affordance-pretraining/fine-tuning of the vision encoder using human video data over representations without such fine-tuning
claims.conditions: real-world, 3000+ robot trials, 3 robot morphologies including a dexterous hand, 5 tasks

claims.claim: Performance improvements hold across 3 different camera views
claims.direction: favors representations that generalize across viewpoints
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Leveraging internet-scale human video instead of collecting more robot data improves generalization in out-of-distribution settings without requiring additional robot demonstrations
claims.direction: favors external human-video pretraining data to compensate for scarce robot demos
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Concrete quantitative real-world evidence (minimum +15%) on vision-encoder pretraining directly informs Q03 for our low-data setup; full text would clarify which affordance signals/backbone matter most and whether gains transfer to a simple scene+wrist camera setup like ours.

title: Responsive Noise-Relaying Diffusion Policy: Responsive and Efficient Visuomotor Control

claims.claim: Standard Diffusion Policy must execute multiple actions from the same inference step (open-loop chunk) to avoid mode bouncing, limiting responsiveness since actions aren't conditioned on latest observations; RNR-DP's noise-relaying buffer instead generates immediate noise-free actions from the latest observation while appending noisy actions at the tail, improving success rate by 18% over Diffusion Policy on response-sensitive tasks
claims.direction: favors a responsive/receding-horizon diffusion variant over standard fixed-chunk diffusion policy execution
claims.conditions: response-sensitive robot manipulation tasks; demo count/sim-vs-real not stated in abstract

claims.claim: Reusing denoising steps across the noise-relaying buffer accelerates action generation while maintaining motion consistency across the chunk
claims.direction: favors overlapping/receding chunk generation over independent per-chunk denoising
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: On regular (non-response-sensitive) tasks RNR-DP still exceeds the best acceleration baseline (DDIM) by 6.9% in success rate, showing a computational efficiency advantage
claims.direction: favors this responsive design even when responsiveness is less critical, due to latency/efficiency gains
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly tackles our exact reported problem (jerky motion at action-chunk boundaries under async inference); ablations would reveal buffer/noise-schedule parameters and latency numbers relevant to our RTX 5060 laptop budget.

title: Developing Vision-Language-Action Model from Egocentric Videos

claims.claim: Pre-training a pi0 architecture on a large-scale dataset of 6DoF manipulation trajectories automatically extracted from raw egocentric human videos (no auxiliary hand-pose annotations needed) improves task success rates by over 20% compared to training from scratch; performance is competitive with real-robot-dataset pretraining, and combining egocentric-video pretraining with real robot data yields further improvements
claims.direction: favors augmenting scarce real robot demonstrations with scalable egocentric human video pretraining data
claims.conditions: simulated and real-robot environments, pi0 architecture

title: Robust Industrial Manipulation Under Test-Time Perturbations in RLBench and Colosseum

claims.claim: Policies trained only in nominal simulation lose performance when lighting, background appearance, table appearance, or object appearance changes at deployment time, in a fixed-camera Franka Panda workcell
claims.direction: confirms lighting/appearance shift as a major robustness bottleneck
claims.conditions: sim benchmark (RLBench + Colosseum), fixed front/left-shoulder/right-shoulder cameras, Robotic View Transformer (RVT) backbone

claims.claim: Expanding targeted domain randomization (TDR) over deployment-relevant appearance/lighting perturbations improves overall mean robustness score from 32.4 (baseline RVT) to 50.0; adding adaptive hard-example sampling (AHS), which reweights replay toward persistently low-scoring perturbations, further improves it to 58.0; worst-perturbation-ID score rises from 0.0 to 28.0 and Tail-2 score from 9.8 to 42.0
claims.direction: favors broadened domain randomization combined with hard-example-focused replay weighting over standard/narrow randomization
claims.conditions: same sim benchmark as above, 4-task benchmark, largest gains on harder Close Box and Insert Onto Square Peg tasks

why_deep_read: Directly evidences our exact lighting/background/appearance-shift failure mode with a concrete two-stage augmentation + hard-example-mining recipe (Q05/Q14); worth checking whether these perturbation types and gains (measured on RVT) generalize to a small SmolVLA-style policy on real low-cost hardware.

title: Perfect Demo Makes Poor Teacher: Learning Robust Alignment from Critical Motion Segments

claims.claim: For fine-grained manipulation (insertion, stacking, alignment), fluent expert demonstrations compress decisive alignment/recovery moments into a brief window, starving the policy of supervision where precision matters; slowing down near alignment and resampling critical segments broadens coverage of recovery states and helps, but the gain comes from broadened state coverage rather than reweighting existing frames; a representation-level fix (STAIR) trained on fluent data alone recovers most of the deliberate-demonstration gain: success rises from 50.0% (fluent baseline) to 62.2% with STAIR, approaching 64.4% from deliberate/slowed demonstrations
claims.direction: favors deliberately-paced, recovery-rich demonstration collection (or a motion-aware representation that compensates for fluent data) over fast/fluent expert demos for precision tasks
claims.conditions: fine-grained manipulation tasks (insertion, stacking, alignment); sim/real not stated explicitly in abstract

claims.claim: STAIR distills short-horizon motion already present in each trajectory into a dense, motion-aware spatio-temporal feature interface between the vision-language model and the action expert, rather than mapping a single static image directly to an action
claims.direction: favors an explicit short-horizon temporal/motion feature over single-frame-to-action mapping
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Introducing a compact dynamic (spatio-temporal) feature as the interface fed to the action expert, distilled from recorded motion, is proposed as an alternative to static per-frame visual features
claims.direction: favors motion-aware representation over purely static per-frame representation
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly relevant to our low-demo-count teleop data collection strategy for a precision pick-and-place task; full text would clarify how much slower/recovery-focused demo collection is needed and whether STAIR's motion-feature interface is implementable in a small SmolVLA-scale model.

title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models

claims.claim: Making each VLA policy query elastic (adapting inference/replanning schedule to state difficulty via a lightweight latent-schedule adaptor and critic-ensemble disagreement) reduces amortized inference cost while preserving or improving task success, across simulation and real-robot manipulation
claims.direction: favors difficulty-adaptive inference/replanning schedules over fixed inference and replanning schedules
claims.conditions: simulation and real-robot manipulation, no fine-tuning of underlying VLA required

claims.claim: The adaptor jointly selects latent input, denoising budget, and action chunk length per query rather than using a fixed chunk length
claims.direction: favors variable/adaptive chunk length over fixed chunk length
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Denoising budget (number of function evaluations) is treated as an adaptive, state-dependent parameter rather than fixed
claims.direction: favors adaptive denoising budget for diffusion-style action heads
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Task-Prototype Guided Flow Matching for Few-Shot Generalization in Vision-Language Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: On the LEROBOT-ARM-SO101 platform (the same robot as our setup), TP-Flow achieves 66.8%, 79.6%, and 82.1% success under 1-, 4-, and 6-shot settings respectively (75.5% few-shot AUC), and at 1-shot improves over CFM, Pooled-Demo CFM, and In-Context Flow by 29.8, 14.5, and 9.9 percentage points
claims.direction: favors task-prototype-guided few-shot adaptation over plain conditional flow matching baselines when demonstrations are very scarce
claims.conditions: real SO-101 low-cost arm, 1/4/6-shot demonstrations, novel-object transfer, goal recombination, long-horizon composition, contact/correction task generalization tested

claims.claim: Uses flow matching as the action head, with task-prototype tokens (extracted via symmetric cross-attention from support demonstrations) guiding both the initial flow prior and the velocity field, plus prototype contrastive regularization
claims.direction: favors structured/conditioned flow matching over plain flow matching for few-shot adaptation
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Maintains real-time execution with six online prototype tokens at 54.3 ms latency, 3.9 GB peak memory, and a 10 Hz control rate
claims.direction: demonstrates flow-matching-based few-shot policy is feasible on modest compute/latency budgets
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Noisy-support success drop is reduced to 6.2% and the method operates within a 3.9 GB memory footprint
claims.direction: suggests small memory footprint achievable while retaining few-shot performance
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: This paper evaluates directly on our exact robot platform (SO-101) with 1/4/6-shot demonstrations matching our low-data regime, reporting latency and memory numbers comparable to our laptop GPU constraint; full text ablations on the action head and prototype mechanism would be highly transferable to our design choices.

title: Look Where It Matters: Adaptive Visual Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Vision encoders in VLAs exhibit attention artifacts where task-relevant spatial information (object location, depth ordering, local geometry) spills into low-information patch tokens due to limited global-token capacity; inserting learnable register tokens trained end-to-end on embodied data restores clean, spatially faithful attention in the remaining patch tokens
claims.direction: favors adding dedicated register tokens to the vision encoder over standard ViT token usage for spatial precision
claims.conditions: LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and a challenging single-view real-world benchmark

claims.claim: Sampling multiple action chunks and estimating uncertainty from their disagreement, then triggering high-resolution re-encoding and cropping only for uncertain predictions (~30% of replanning steps), improves precision while adding only 1.4-1.6x total compute over the base model
claims.direction: favors uncertainty-gated selective refinement over always using high-resolution or always using low-resolution observations
claims.conditions: same benchmarks as above

claims.claim: AtVLA improves average LIBERO success from 94.2% to 98.4% and real-world success from 46.5% to 69.0% on a single-view real-world benchmark
claims.direction: favors attention-rectification plus uncertainty-gated refinement for real-world generalization/precision
claims.conditions: single-view real-world benchmark (camera setup closer to low-cost single-camera setups)

title: PHR-VLA: Planning Horizon Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Adding a lightweight auxiliary future head that aligns internal VLA representations with latent dynamics extracted from future observations during training (not used at inference) improves success rate on LIBERO from 84.1% to 88.4% and on real-world disassembly tasks from 63.3% to 82.5%
claims.direction: favors auxiliary future-prediction/world-model-style objectives over training with only the action-prediction loss
claims.conditions: LIBERO simulation and real-world disassembly (contact-rich fine-grained manipulation)

claims.claim: Local, contact-centric, patch-level latent-dynamics supervision specifically from the wrist camera drives the largest gains, whereas patch-level supervision from a third-person camera gives a smaller improvement on Meta-World (56.70% to 57.8%)
claims.direction: favors wrist-camera-derived auxiliary supervision over third-person-camera-derived supervision for contact-rich tasks
claims.conditions: comparison across LIBERO, real-world disassembly, and Meta-World

title: LIFD: Anchored Diffusion for 3D-Aware Scene Memory in Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A persistent, 3D-aware scene memory (scene tokens learned via multi-view agreement during training, completed via recurrent memory and rectified flow at deployment) that integrates observation history improves performance under partial observability when the camera's field of view no longer covers previously seen regions
claims.direction: favors explicit scene memory/history integration over memoryless single-frame policies
claims.conditions: LIBERO, MetaWorld, and real UR5e task families

claims.claim: Multi-view and geometric supervision are used only during representation learning; at deployment the policy requires just one RGB camera, proprioception, and a task instruction (no depth or multi-view needed at runtime)
claims.direction: favors training-time 3D/multi-view supervision distilled into a deployment-time single-RGB-camera policy, rather than requiring 3D/depth sensing at runtime
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: After policy-head adaptation using only ten demonstrations per task family, LIFD achieves 56.0% mean success across four real UR5e task families compared with 40.5% for OpenVLA-7B
claims.direction: favors this architecture for low-demonstration-count adaptation over a large generalist VLA baseline
claims.conditions: real UR5e robot, 10 demos per family

claims.claim: LIFD outperforms the much larger OpenVLA-7B baseline in the low-data (10 demos/family) real-robot regime
claims.direction: favors a smaller specialized architecture over a large generalist model when demonstrations are scarce
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Language-Guided Object-Centric Diffusion Policy for Generalizable and Collision-Aware Manipulation

claims.claim: A diffusion policy conditioned on 3D point clouds of task-relevant objects (object-centric 3D representation) achieves 68.7% success vs 39.3% for a simple 2D representation and 43.6% for a full 3D scene representation, across 21 challenging RLBench tasks with only 40 demonstrations
claims.direction: favors object-centric 3D point-cloud representation over both 2D image representation and whole-3D-scene representation
claims.conditions: simulation (RLBench, 21 tasks), only 40 demonstrations; also evaluated in real-world for generalization to cluttered scenes, shifting camera views, and ambiguous similar objects

claims.claim: Diffusion model predicts end-effector trajectories, with cost-optimization incorporated into denoising steps at inference to guide the trajectory to be collision-free, using a time-independent cost function on estimated clean trajectories
claims.direction: favors diffusion action head augmented with inference-time cost guidance over vanilla diffusion policy
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: High success rate achieved with only 40 demonstrations across 21 tasks
claims.direction: supports diffusion+3D object-centric representation as sample-efficient in low-demo regime
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: A large language model interprets natural-language instructions to identify target objects and possible obstacles, guiding which point clouds to condition on
claims.direction: language used to select task-relevant object subsets rather than as a direct low-level conditioning signal
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Provides a controlled, quantitative ablation directly comparing 2D vs 3D-scene vs object-centric-3D-point-cloud representations (Q04) under a low-demo (40-demo) regime, which is central to our vision/3D design decision; full text would show whether the point-cloud pipeline is feasible with a single RealSense camera and modest compute.

title: Consistency Policy: Accelerated Visuomotor Policies via Consistency Distillation

claims.claim: Consistency Policy, distilled from a pretrained Diffusion Policy via self-consistency along learned diffusion trajectories, speeds up inference by an order of magnitude compared to the fastest alternative speed-up method while maintaining competitive success rates, demonstrated with inference on a laptop GPU
claims.direction: favors consistency distillation of a diffusion policy over standard diffusion policy or other acceleration methods, specifically for resource-constrained/low-power setups
claims.conditions: 6 simulation tasks and 3 real-world tasks, laptop-GPU inference explicitly demonstrated

claims.claim: Key design choices enabling this performance were the choice of consistency objective, reduced initial sample variance, and choice of preset chaining steps, distilled from a pretrained Diffusion Policy of any quality (robust to pretrained model quality)
claims.direction: favors consistency-distilled action head over full multi-step diffusion sampling when fast inference is required
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Designed explicitly for robotic systems (e.g., mobile manipulators, quadrotors) that cannot use high-end GPUs due to space/weight/power constraints
claims.direction: supports small/efficient models for resource-constrained real-time robot deployment
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly addresses our ~2s inference latency problem on a laptop GPU with an explicit laptop-GPU real-world demonstration; full text would give concrete latency numbers and success-rate trade-offs versus full diffusion policy, highly actionable for our RTX 5060 8GB constraint.

title: RoboTwin-Phys: Do WAMs and VLAs Understand the Physical World?

claims.claim: Evaluations of representative world/action models (WAMs) and VLAs across 13 continuously-varied physical attributes (mass, friction, joint dynamics) reveal a substantial robustness gap: models that remain effective under existing visual and layout randomization can degrade markedly under changes in physical conditions
claims.direction: shows that visual/appearance robustness (lighting, background) does not imply robustness to physical-parameter variation; both must be addressed separately
claims.conditions: simulation benchmark, 5,000+ expert demonstrations with ground-truth physical parameters

title: A VLM-Driven High-Fidelity Domain Randomization Framework for Imitation Learning

claims.claim: A VLM-inferred, semantic-aware domain randomization (assigning physically plausible friction/density values conditioned on VLM-predicted material category, instead of unconstrained random sampling) meaningfully improves average task success of a trained VLA policy over a position-only baseline
claims.direction: favors semantically-constrained domain randomization over unconstrained DR or position-only training
claims.conditions: simulation (Isaac Lab), UR5 manipulator + Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, closed-loop teleoperation data generation pipeline

title: mu_0: A Scalable 3D Interaction-Trace World Model

claims.claim: An action-free world model pretrained to forecast 3D trajectories of salient interaction points (objects, tools, hands, contact regions) from diverse video, then paired with action experts, yields trace-conditioned policies that achieve performance competitive with VLA models pretrained with action supervision (e.g. pi0)
claims.direction: favors action-free 3D-trace world-model pretraining as an auxiliary/alternative to action-labeled pretraining
claims.conditions: cross-embodiment; comparison against trace prediction models, tokenized VLM methods, and action-supervised pi0

claims.claim: Represents the action-relevant signal as compact, embodiment-agnostic 3D trace trajectories (via B-spline control points) rather than dense pixel prediction or direct low-level actions
claims.direction: favors a compact trajectory/trace representation as an intermediate action representation
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Behavior-Aligned Action Tokenization for Robot Policy Learning

claims.claim: Behavior-Aligned Action Tokenization (BAAT), which aligns quantized action-chunk codes across tasks with similar motions using soft-DTW, achieves mean simulation success ~45.2% exceeding a prior tokenizer (OAT) by ~7.2 percentage points; in a controlled LIBERO-All alignment ablation, downstream policy success rises from 70.2% to 79.0% with the alignment objective (while raw trajectory replay success decreases)
claims.direction: favors behavior-aligned discrete action tokenization over standard reconstruction-only tokenizers (e.g. OAT) for autoregressive discrete-token action heads
claims.conditions: three simulation benchmarks and two real robot tasks

title: A Robotic Skill Learning System Built Upon Diffusion Policies and Foundation Models

claims.claim: Diffusion-policy-based visuomotor behavioral cloning is used to acquire new skills from teleoperated demonstrations, combined with foundation models for language-driven skill selection and precondition checking
claims.direction: supports diffusion policy as a viable per-skill action head in a modular skill system
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world (food-serving scenario), comparison of different foundation models for skill selection, no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Foundation models perform skill selection from natural-language user prompts and a precondition check from workspace observation before executing a skill
claims.direction: favors using a separate high-level language-conditioned model for skill/task selection rather than conditioning the low-level policy directly on language
claims.conditions: same as above

title: STAR: Learning Diverse Robot Skill Abstractions through Rotation-Augmented Vector Quantization

claims.claim: Rotation-augmented residual skill quantization (encoding relative angles between encoder outputs via a rotation-based gradient mechanism) prevents codebook collapse in VQ-based skill abstraction and, combined with a causal skill transformer for skill composition, improves performance by around 12% over baselines on LIBERO and real-world tasks
claims.direction: favors rotation-augmented VQ discretization over standard VQ-VAE action/skill tokenization, which suffers codebook collapse
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark and real-world tasks

title: Support-Constrained RL Enables Real-World Policy Improvement without Real-World Experience

claims.claim: Constraining simulation-based RL policy improvement to the support of a generative policy pretrained on real demonstration data (via flow steering) improves average real-world success from 37.8% (base real-data policy) to 89.9%, versus 59.5% for the best baseline, across eight real-world dexterous multi-fingered manipulation tasks, without collecting additional real-world experience
claims.direction: favors simulation-based policy improvement constrained to the real-data policy's support over either unconstrained sim RL or collecting more real demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-to-sim-to-real, 8 real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, sparse rewards, no distillation

title: X-Tokenizer: A Multimodal Action Tokenizer for Vision-Language-Action Pretraining

claims.claim: An asymmetric residual vector-quantization action tokenizer (coarse level trained with Masked Action Modeling for semantic intent, deeper levels reconstruction-oriented) with contrastive alignment to a foundation model's representation space outperforms the FAST tokenizer by +13.5% in multimodal grounding and +8.25 points in long-horizon tasks
claims.direction: favors semantically-structured discrete action tokenization over standard reconstruction-focused tokenizers (e.g. FAST) for discrete-token VLA action heads
claims.conditions: pretrained on 2.4M trajectories (2.0B action frames); real-world aggregate and RoboTwin 2.0 simulation results; large-scale pretraining regime, likely not directly reproducible at our data/compute scale

title: SimFoundry: Modular and Automated Scene Generation for Policy Learning and Evaluation

claims.claim: Training on automatically generated 'digital cousins' (affordance-preserving variations of object, scene, and task from a real-to-sim reconstructed scene) improves zero-shot real-world task success by an average of 17% (object cousins), 21% (scene cousins), and 40% (task cousins) respectively, over training without such augmentation
claims.direction: favors generating diverse synthetic scene/object/task variations from real-to-sim reconstruction over training on a single reconstructed scene without such augmentation
claims.conditions: 7 manipulation tasks and 5 policy architectures; sim-trained policies evaluated zero-shot in the real world

claims.claim: Simulation evaluations on SimFoundry strongly predict real-world performance (mean Pearson correlation 0.911), supporting simulation-based augmentation/evaluation as a proxy for real-world generalization robustness
claims.direction: supports using this sim augmentation pipeline as a reliable proxy for assessing real-world generalization
claims.conditions: same as above

title: TempoVLA: Learning Speed-Controllable Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: VLAs otherwise inherit a single fixed execution speed from training demonstrations; TempoVLA conditions the policy on an explicit speed variable (via re-timed demonstration augmentation, VSTA) enabling flexible acceleration through low-risk transit phases and deceleration for high-risk contact phases, and boosts default 1x performance via better data utilization
claims.direction: favors explicit speed-conditioning/variable execution speed over a single fixed-speed policy, especially for contact-rich vs transit phase distinction
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world tasks; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract for the speed-control gains, though data-augmentation-driven 1x improvement is claimed

claims.claim: Re-timing demonstrations (merging or splitting actions) to any target speed while preserving motion semantics is used as a data augmentation and conditioning approach compatible with action-chunk execution
claims.direction: supports variable-rate re-timing of demonstrations as a training-time augmentation for chunked policies
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Implicit Drifting Policy: One-Step Action Generation via Conditional Expert Geometry

claims.claim: A one-step imitation learning generator (avoiding iterative diffusion/flow-matching sampling) that implicitly captures training-time trajectory-correction behavior via a conditional expert geometry improves adherence to valid action manifolds compared to explicit one-step 'drifting' methods, and is competitive with strong one-step baselines
claims.direction: favors one-step action generation with implicit geometric correction over iterative diffusion/flow-matching sampling or naive one-step distillation
claims.conditions: 2D, 3D, and real-world manipulation tasks; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: One-step action generation directly targets the latency problem of iterative diffusion/flow-matching sampling being prohibitive for high-frequency robot control
claims.direction: favors one-step generative action heads for reducing per-step inference latency
claims.conditions: same as above

title: CARE: Experience-Guided Atomic Corrective Execution for Vision-Language-Action Policies

claims.claim: Collecting failed rollouts, modeling stage-conditioned post-failure deviations, and synthesizing representative failure states and corrective demonstrations from these empirical distributions (rather than manually designed or random perturbations) improves recovery from execution deviations; average task-success gains of 14.5 points in simulation and 15.9 points in the real world across multiple VLA backbones
claims.direction: favors experience-derived synthetic failure/recovery demonstrations over manually-designed perturbation-based corrective data
claims.conditions: multiple VLA backbones, simulation benchmarks and real-world dual-arm tasks

claims.claim: Combining stage-wise planning with physically grounded 3D monitoring to trigger atomic adjustments improves recovery from intermediate failure states under local deviations and structural anomalies
claims.direction: favors explicit failure-state monitoring/recovery mechanisms for robustness
claims.conditions: same as above, using new Failure State Recovery Benchmark (FSR-Bench)

title: VLA-0: Building State-of-the-Art VLAs with Zero Modification

claims.claim: Representing actions directly as text (no action-token vocabulary modification, no special action head) outperforms more involved VLA designs: on LIBERO, VLA-0 outperforms all existing methods trained on the same robotic data, including pi0.5-KI, OpenVLA-OFT, and SmolVLA, and even outperforms methods trained on large-scale robotic data (pi0.5-KI, pi0, GR00T-N1, MolmoAct) without such large-scale training; in the real world, VLA-0 outperforms SmolVLA (a VLA pre-trained on large-scale real data)
claims.direction: favors the simplest action representation (text) over discretized action-token vocabularies or specialized action heads, contradicting the common assumption that specialized action heads/tokenizers are necessary
claims.conditions: LIBERO benchmark and real-world experiments; direct comparison against SmolVLA (our current baseline model)

claims.claim: Achieves SOTA performance without large-scale robotics-specific training and without added architectural complexity
claims.direction: favors simpler design achieving strong results without necessarily requiring larger/more complex models
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly benchmarks against SmolVLA (our current baseline) both in LIBERO and the real world, and claims a simpler action representation (plain text) beats it; this is a direct, actionable, contrarian finding for Q01 that could change our action-head choice, worth verifying against SmolVLA's specific failure modes in the full paper.

title: Unifying Latent Action and Latent State Pre-training for Policy Learning from Videos

claims.claim: Unifying latent-action tokenization (motion priors) and latent-state prediction (future-event anticipation) from video pre-training, then fine-tuning on action-labeled robot data, enhances performance by 19% on LIBERO and improves average consecutive tasks completed (of 5) on CALVIN from 2.50/2.35 to 3.89/3.73 baselines; real-world improvements exceed 36%
claims.direction: favors combining latent-action and latent-state (future-prediction) auxiliary pre-training objectives over using either alone or no video pre-training
claims.conditions: LIBERO, CALVIN, and real-world experiments; pre-training on video data before fine-tuning on action-labeled robot data

claims.claim: Leverages video data (not requiring action labels) as a rich pre-training source before fine-tuning on a smaller action-labeled robot dataset
claims.direction: favors using unlabeled video as a substitute/supplement for scarce action-labeled robot demonstrations
claims.conditions: same as above

title: DemoSpeedup: Accelerating Visuomotor Policies via Entropy-Guided Demonstration Acceleration

claims.claim: Segmenting demonstrations by per-frame action-entropy (estimated from a policy such as ACT or Diffusion Policy trained on normal-speed demos) and down-sampling low-entropy (precision-critical) segments less and high-entropy (casual) segments more, then retraining on these sped-up demonstrations, lets policies execute up to 3x faster while maintaining task completion performance, and sometimes achieves higher success rates than training on normal-speed demonstrations due to reduced decision-making horizons
claims.direction: favors self-supervised, entropy-guided non-uniform demonstration acceleration over using raw human teleoperation speed as-is
claims.conditions: generative policies (ACT, Diffusion Policy) as the entropy estimator; self-supervised, no manual labeling

claims.claim: Reducing the effective decision-making horizon (via demonstration acceleration) can itself improve success rate
claims.direction: supports shorter execution/decision horizons as beneficial, complementary to chunking/horizon choices
claims.conditions: same as above

title: ImaginationPolicy: Towards Generalizable, Precise and Reliable End-to-End Policy for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: A Chain of Moving Oriented Keypoints (CoMOK) action representation, extending standard end-effector pose representation, enables natural generalization to objects of different shapes/sizes with sub-centimeter accuracy and handles multi-stage tasks, multi-modal behaviors, and deformable objects in an end-to-end trained policy
claims.direction: favors an oriented-keypoint-based action representation over standard end-effector pose representation for precision and generalization
claims.conditions: extensive simulated and hardware experiments; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

title: Integrating Vision-Language-Action Models and RGB-D Sensing for Robotic Waste Sorting on KUKA LBR iiwa

claims.claim: Integrating RGB-D sensing with a pretrained VLA (Gemini) enhanced the model's ability to perceive object heights, resolve occlusions, and make informed grasping decisions in cluttered, three-dimensional settings, achieving 89.64% overall classification accuracy
claims.direction: favors adding depth sensing to RGB-only VLA perception for occlusion/height reasoning in cluttered scenes
claims.conditions: real-world, KUKA LBR iiwa collaborative robot, RGB-D camera, training-free (prompted) VLA, not fine-tuned imitation learning

claims.claim: System inference time is between 2 and 4 seconds, reported as suitable for collaborative robotic applications
claims.direction: provides a real-world reference point for acceptable inference latency in collaborative manipulation
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Depth Matters: Language-Guided Spatial Representation Learning for Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Injecting pseudo-depth (predicted from RGB via a patchified convolutional network) as spatial positional encoding into late transformer layers of an RGB-pretrained encoder (EVA-CLIP-based), combined with language-guided attention pooling, provides fine-grained perception and 3D spatial awareness without requiring an actual depth sensor at pretraining time
claims.direction: favors injecting pseudo-depth signals into an RGB-pretrained visual encoder over relying purely on RGB features when 3D spatial awareness is needed but large-scale RGB-D pretraining data is unavailable
claims.conditions: paired with a standard Diffusion Policy, evaluated on RLBench and ManiSkill simulation benchmarks

claims.claim: The resulting reusable, decoupled multimodal encoder matches or outperforms existing state-of-the-art visual encoders across diverse manipulation tasks when paired with a standard Diffusion Policy, addressing overfitting from parameter-data mismatch seen in end-to-end VLA visual encoders
claims.direction: favors a decoupled, reusable pretrained visual encoder over tightly-coupled task-specific VLA visual encoders
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Civil: causal and intuitive visual imitation learning

claims.claim: Standard visual imitation learning suffers causal confusion because the robot observes what the human does but not why (e.g., misattributing an action to background clutter color); having human teachers attach markers to task-relevant objects and describe their state representation via natural language, then using this to filter visual observations and extract an aligned causal feature representation for a transformer policy, avoids this confusion
claims.direction: favors explicitly-supervised causal/task-relevant feature extraction (marker+language annotated demos) over standard behavior-cloning from raw visual demonstrations alone, to reduce causal confusion
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments; user study also measured

claims.claim: CIVIL-trained policies are not confused by visual distractors or irrelevant items and show improved performance in previously unseen scenarios compared to state-of-the-art baselines
claims.direction: favors causal-feature-grounded imitation learning for robustness to distractors and novel scenarios
claims.conditions: same as above; user study also reports reduced total demonstration/training time needed

title: Imitation Learning for Construction Robot Timber Assembly using Demonstrations from Leader-Follower Teleoperation

claims.claim: A diffusion policy trained on demonstrations collected via a small-scale leader-follower teleoperation system (joint motions mapped from a small 3D-printed leader arm to a full-scale xArm 7 follower) achieves a 100% success rate on a timber truss assembly task when trained with the full collected dataset
claims.direction: supports leader-follower teleoperation as a viable low-cost data collection method sufficient for high task success when using the full dataset
claims.conditions: real xArm 7 robot, diffusion policy, single task (timber truss assembly)

claims.claim: Uses diffusion policy as the action-generation backbone for real-robot deployment
claims.direction: supports diffusion policy as viable for real-robot low-cost-teleop-collected data
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Behavior-Aligned Representations

claims.claim: Among behavior-aligned representations tested (object bounding boxes, language motions, end-effector traces of robot motion) for VLA cross-embodiment transfer, end-effector traces are identified as particularly beneficial for transfer to new embodiments, and this benefit improves sim-to-real cross-embodiment transfer, improving task completion progress of real robot policies pre-trained on simulation data by 28%
claims.direction: favors end-effector-trace representations as an embodiment-invariant interface over raw pixel/action representations for cross-embodiment and sim-to-real transfer
claims.conditions: simulation-based benchmark plus real robot evaluation; representations are more useful with larger prior datasets and can leverage action-free data

claims.claim: Behavior-aligned representations help unify large-scale cross-embodiment data (including action-free data) to compensate for limited same-embodiment demonstrations
claims.direction: supports leveraging cross-embodiment/action-free data via aligned representations when target-robot demonstrations are scarce
claims.conditions: same as above

title: TemporalFlow-VLA: Learning Physically Grounded Execution History for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Simply adding historical frames to a VLA does not reliably capture recent physical change, especially where visually similar states require different actions depending on prior execution; supervising two execution-aligned temporal queries with physically grounded temporal supervision (robot-surface temporal flow, training-only) achieves 97.63+/-0.26% avg success on LIBERO (96.60+/-0.87% on LIBERO-Long) and 85.5%/84.2% Clean/Randomized success on 12 RoboTwin tasks, with clearest advantage on longer-horizon, multi-stage manipulation; controlled history interventions show action prediction depends on both historical content and temporal order
claims.direction: favors structured, physically-grounded temporal/history supervision over naive frame-stacking history for long-horizon, multi-stage tasks
claims.conditions: LIBERO and RoboTwin simulation benchmarks; geometric supervision only used at training time, not at deployment

claims.claim: With asynchronous feature caching, this temporal conditioning maintains single-frame-level server-side sampling latency without additional historical-encoding overhead at deployment
claims.direction: shows that adding observation history for long-horizon reasoning need not increase inference latency if implemented with async caching
claims.conditions: same as above

title: CSWAM: Better Causal Semantic Representations for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in World Action Models

claims.claim: Augmenting a FastWAM-style world-action-model (efficient action-only inference) with a causal semantic expert built on V-JEPA 2.1 (providing temporally-grounded, appearance-independent representations of semantic state changes) raises Randomized success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean-to-Randomized visual distribution-shift transfer from 10.16% to 45.18% (+35.02 percentage points) over FastWAM; across two real-robot tasks and three OOD difficulty levels, average success improves from 27.5% to 70.0% (+42.5 points)
claims.direction: strongly favors causal/semantic (appearance-invariant) representations combined with sparse observation history over purely reconstruction-oriented (appearance-specific) world-action-model representations, for generalization under visual distribution shift (lighting/appearance/background changes)
claims.conditions: simulation (RoboTwin 2.0) and real-robot experiments across multiple OOD difficulty levels; retains efficient action-only inference at deployment

claims.claim: Without observation history, reconstruction-oriented world-action models lack temporal evidence to robustly identify task-relevant state changes in unfamiliar visual conditions; a sparse history of current and past observations shared via causal attention addresses this
claims.direction: favors adding sparse causal history specifically to improve robustness under distribution shift, not just task performance
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: A causal-semantic auxiliary expert (world-model-style future-state prediction grounded in V-JEPA features) is added alongside the action-only inference pathway during training/inference to improve generalization while retaining efficient deployment
claims.direction: favors auxiliary semantic world-model objectives for OOD robustness over pure reconstruction-based world models
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Any-point Trajectory Modeling for Policy Learning

claims.claim: Pre-training a trajectory model to predict future trajectories of arbitrary points within a video frame (from video demonstrations lacking action labels), then using these predicted trajectories as detailed control guidance, outperforms strong video pre-training baselines by 80% on average across 130+ language-conditioned tasks in simulation and the real world
claims.direction: favors arbitrary-point future-trajectory prediction as an auxiliary/pretraining signal over other video pre-training approaches, enabling robust visuomotor policies with minimal action-labeled data
claims.conditions: 130+ tasks, simulation and real world; also shows transfer from human videos and videos of a different robot morphology

claims.claim: Enables learning robust policies with minimal action-labeled data by extracting control-specific trajectory guidance from action-unlabeled video
claims.direction: favors leveraging action-free video pretraining to reduce required action-labeled demonstration count
claims.conditions: same as above

title: GraphMimic: Graph-to-Graphs Generative Modeling from Videos for Policy Learning

claims.claim: Pre-training via graph-to-graphs generative modeling on video (abstracting frames into object/visual-action vertex graphs and predicting future graphs) achieves superior performance using merely 20% action-labeled data, outperforming the state-of-the-art method by over 17% (simulation) and 23% (real-world), with over 33% improvement in cross-embodiment transfer
claims.direction: favors graph-structured video pre-training (capturing spatial relations) over prior video-pretraining methods for reducing action-labeled data requirements
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world experiments, cross-embodiment video transfer tested

claims.claim: Modeling internal object/visual-action graph structure and predicting future graphs (an auxiliary/generative prediction objective) conditions the control policy and enhances future-state generation accuracy
claims.direction: favors structured graph-based future-state prediction as an auxiliary objective over unstructured/pixel-based future prediction
claims.conditions: same as above

title: MobRT: A Digital Twin-Based Framework for Scalable Learning in Mobile Manipulation

claims.claim: Evaluating MobRT-generated synthetic demonstration data across multiple baseline algorithms establishes a strong correlation between task success and the number of generated trajectories, and combining simulated and real-world demonstrations markedly improves policy generalization and performance
claims.direction: supports the general finding that more (synthetically generated) demonstration trajectories improve policy generalization, and that mixing sim+real demos helps
claims.conditions: mobile manipulation whole-body tasks (articulated object interaction, mobile pick-and-place), simulated and real-world evaluation

title: ThinkingVLA: Interleaved Vision and Language Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Decomposing manipulation planning into a forward Chain-of-Thought that predicts the next visual subgoal state and an inverse CoT that reasons about actions to reach that predicted state, within a unified autoregressive Mixture-of-Transformers, consistently outperforms SOTA baselines, with particularly large gains on long-horizon manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors interleaved visual-forecasting-plus-inverse-dynamics reasoning (an auxiliary future-prediction objective coupled to action generation) over direct observation-to-action mapping, especially for long-horizon tasks
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world benchmarks; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Final action is generated conditioned on the full forward+inverse reasoning context rather than directly from raw observations
claims.direction: favors an action head that conditions on explicit intermediate visual/textual reasoning steps
claims.conditions: same as above

title: IntentVLA: Short-Horizon Intent Modeling for Aliased Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: Frame-conditioned VLA policies that infer each action chunk from only the current observation and instruction can, under partial observability, resample different short-horizon intents across adjacent replanning steps (observation aliasing), causing inter-chunk conflict and unstable execution; encoding recent visual observations into a compact short-horizon intent representation to condition chunk generation improves rollout stability and outperforms strong VLA baselines on AliasBench, SimplerEnv, LIBERO, and RoboCasa
claims.direction: favors conditioning chunk generation on a short-horizon history/intent representation over conditioning purely on the current-step observation and instruction, specifically to reduce chunk-to-chunk instability from observation aliasing
claims.conditions: 12-task ambiguity-aware AliasBench on RoboTwin2 plus SimplerEnv, LIBERO, RoboCasa; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Observation aliasing across adjacent replanning steps causes inter-chunk conflict, i.e., instability specifically at chunk boundaries under frame-conditioned (non-history) chunk generation
claims.direction: identifies short-horizon aliasing as a root cause of unstable/jerky execution at chunk boundaries, motivating history-conditioned chunk generation
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Dynamic Maclaurin-Series-Based Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: Replacing per-layer transformer weight tensors with a small set of shared Maclaurin-series templates plus layer-specific coefficients dramatically reduces memory footprint without degrading task performance, matching or slightly exceeding SOTA VLA baselines on LIBERO and SIMPLER
claims.direction: favors this parameter-sharing/compression approach over standard per-layer transformer weights when memory is constrained, without success-rate loss
claims.conditions: LIBERO, SIMPLER simulation benchmarks; real-robot trials on ALOHA and Emergen platforms

claims.claim: Dynamically adjusting the number of series terms per input (via target-action differencing) adapts computational effort to visual/language complexity, and deployment on NVIDIA H100, RTX4090 GPUs, and Jetson AGX Orin edge hardware yields 25%-55% inference speedups
claims.direction: favors adaptive-compute, compressed VLA architectures for resource-constrained (consumer GPU / edge) inference over standard fixed-compute transformer VLAs
claims.conditions: same as above; RTX4090 is a consumer-grade GPU comparable in class (though more powerful) to our RTX 5060 laptop

title: HCPG-Flow: Hierarchical Contact-Progress Guidance for Flow-Policy Robot Manipulation

claims.claim: An analytic rollout-time selector that scores multiple sampled flow-policy action proposals using hierarchical, object-centric contact-progress guidance (switching guidance from end-effector approach to task progress after contact) improves mean success over the base flow-policy method (SAC-Flow) on both simulated benchmarks tested, including a 9.5 percentage-point gain on Maniskill; four physical tasks show high success with a 17.4% reduction in successful completion steps
claims.direction: favors augmenting a multimodal flow-matching action head with contact-aware, rollout-time candidate selection over selecting actions via critic-based ranking alone
claims.conditions: ten simulated tasks (two benchmarks) and four physical/real-world tasks

claims.claim: Selecting among multiple sampled action proposals at rollout time (rather than committing to a single critic-ranked proposal) reduces completion steps needed
claims.direction: supports rollout-time multi-proposal selection as a way to improve execution efficiency
claims.conditions: same as above

title: The Gaussian Is Enough: Flow-Matching Priors Do Not Help When Fine-Tuning Large Behavior Models

claims.claim: While replacing the standard Gaussian prior with a non-Gaussian, closer-to-target prior substantially improves diffusion/flow-matching policy performance when TRAINING FROM SCRATCH, this benefit does NOT transfer to FINE-TUNING pretrained Large Behavior Models (LBM 1.0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.5): across 100K+ simulation rollouts (40+ tasks, two simulation platforms) and 1250 hardware rollouts (five bimanual manipulation tasks), non-Gaussian priors yield statistically indistinguishable or worse fine-tuning performance than a standard Gaussian prior, except possibly at very low fine-tuning data fractions
claims.direction: contradicts the assumption that a better-matched (non-Gaussian) diffusion/flow-matching prior improves performance in the fine-tuning regime specifically; favors the standard Gaussian prior as sufficient when fine-tuning a pretrained action model, with prior choice mattering mainly for from-scratch training
claims.conditions: fine-tuning of pretrained large behavior models on real hardware (5 bimanual tasks, 1250 rollouts) and simulation (40+ tasks); diagnostic analysis shows encoder training (not prior choice) is the dominant factor in fine-tuning performance

why_deep_read: Directly contradicts a common assumption (better priors help diffusion/flow-matching policies) specifically in the fine-tuning regime, which is exactly our setup (fine-tuning a pretrained SmolVLA); large-scale real-hardware validation (1250 rollouts) makes this highly actionable evidence to check before investing effort in a fancier action-head prior versus improving vision-encoder/fine-tuning strategy.

title: What matters in building vision-language-action models for generalist robots

claims.claim: Across a systematic study of over 8 VLM backbones, 4 policy architectures, and over 600 distinct experiments, the choice of VLM backbone significantly influences downstream VLA manipulation performance; the resulting RoboVLMs framework (requiring few manual designs) achieves new SOTA in three simulation tasks and real-world experiments
claims.direction: provides a controlled, large-scale comparison of backbone choices for VLA construction (directly informs which pretrained vision-language backbone to select)
claims.conditions: 3 simulation task suites and real-world experiments; framework and all experiment details open-sourced

claims.claim: The study explicitly compares different ways of formulating the VLA architecture (how to inject action components into a VLM) and identifies design choices that matter most for performance
claims.direction: provides controlled comparative evidence on action-head/architecture formulation choices
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: The study examines when to add cross-embodiment data during training and how this affects performance
claims.direction: provides controlled evidence on cross-embodiment data mixing strategy and timing
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: This is one of the largest controlled ablation studies of VLA design choices available (8 backbones x 4 architectures, 600+ experiments), directly covering backbone/vision-encoder choice (Q03), architecture/action-head formulation (Q01), and cross-embodiment data timing (Q13); the full paper's tables would likely give the most direct, load-bearing guidance for several of our 14 decisions at once.

title: Learning Generalizable Visuomotor Policy through Dynamics-Alignment

claims.claim: Integrating dynamics prediction directly into policy learning, with policy and dynamics models providing mutual corrective feedback during action generation (rather than using action-agnostic video-prediction dynamics learned separately), enables self-correction and improved generalization on real-world robotic manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors tightly-coupled, action-conditioned dynamics-alignment (mutual policy/dynamics feedback) over action-agnostic video-prediction-based auxiliary objectives, and over plain behavior cloning
claims.conditions: real-world robotic manipulation tasks

claims.claim: The Dynamics-Aligned Flow Matching Policy (DAP) shows particular robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios including visual distractions AND LIGHTING VARIATIONS compared to baseline methods
claims.direction: favors dynamics-alignment as a mechanism for improving robustness specifically to lighting-variation and visual-distraction shifts
claims.conditions: real-world OOD evaluation; no specific numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Uses flow matching as the action-generation mechanism, coupled with a dynamics-prediction model
claims.direction: supports flow matching combined with dynamics-alignment as a strong action head choice
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Learning Coordinated Bimanual Manipulation Policies Using State Diffusion and Inverse Dynamics Models

claims.claim: Training a diffusion model to predict future states given historical observations (disentangled from agent-specific inverse-dynamics action computation) consistently outperforms state-of-the-art state-to-action mapping policies across diverse simulation and real-world manipulation setups (multimodal goals, bimanual, deformable objects, multi-object)
claims.direction: favors decoupling future-state prediction (world-model-style) from action computation via a separate inverse dynamics model, over direct state-to-action mapping policies
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world, primarily bimanual manipulation tasks

claims.claim: Actions are computed via an inverse dynamics model conditioned on predicted future states rather than being directly regressed/diffused from observations
claims.direction: favors a two-stage (predict-state, then inverse-dynamics-to-action) action generation pipeline
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Unified World Models: Coupling Video and Action Diffusion for Pretraining on Large Robotic Datasets

claims.claim: Integrating an action diffusion process and a video diffusion process within one unified transformer (governed by independent per-modality diffusion timesteps, so the same model can act as policy, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, or video generator) enables pretraining on large-scale multitask robot datasets with both dynamics and action prediction, resulting in more generalizable and robust policies than imitation learning alone
claims.direction: favors unifying world-model (video) and policy (action) objectives in a single architecture over training an imitation-learning policy alone
claims.conditions: simulated and real-world experiments, large-scale multitask robot datasets

claims.claim: Independent control of modality-specific diffusion timesteps naturally facilitates learning from action-free video data, further improving performance of fine-tuned policies
claims.direction: favors leveraging action-free video data (not just action-labeled robot data) to improve policy fine-tuning performance
claims.conditions: same as above

title: A Lightweight Modular Vision-Language-Action Framework for Real-Time Closed-Loop Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: Fusing RealSense RGB/depth data via improved YOLOv8 for target detection and 3D pose estimation, combined with a modular (non-end-to-end-trained) perception-decision-control pipeline, achieves 98% recognition accuracy and +/-3mm coordinate error for grasping rigid/fragile/irregular objects in occluded scenes
claims.direction: favors RGB-D fusion with explicit detection/pose-estimation over end-to-end RGB-only learned perception for precise grasping, at the cost of using a modular non-learned pipeline instead of an end-to-end VLA
claims.conditions: real self-built 6-DOF platform with Ti5 dexterous hand, RealSense D455, no end-to-end training or VLA fine-tuning

claims.claim: The full perception-decision-control pipeline achieves more than 95% grasping success rate with less than 2 seconds end-to-end latency
claims.direction: provides a real-world reference point that sub-2s end-to-end latency with high success is achievable using a modular (not end-to-end fine-tuned) architecture
claims.conditions: same as above

title: Towards Efficient Embodied Reasoning: Mixture-of-Depth Compute Allocation for Vision-Language-Action Model

claims.claim: An action-aligned attribution analysis (Effective-Edge Flow) reveals depth asymmetry in VLA backbones (visual evidence dominates early layers, linguistic reasoning matters more in deeper layers); MoDeVLA allocates compute depth-wise accordingly (Mixture-of-Depth Conditioning, fusing shallow visual-spatial with deep textual-logical features), preserving task performance while reducing latency by about 38% and FLOPs by 86% on the edge device NVIDIA Jetson Orin
claims.direction: favors rate-distortion-driven, depth-wise adaptive compute allocation over uniform full-forward-pass backbone compression methods, for real-time inference on resource-constrained edge/consumer hardware
claims.conditions: real-robot evaluations across 20 tasks and multiple embodiments

claims.claim: Achieves large compute/latency reductions without the information loss of standard lightweight compression techniques (which degrade spatial representations for action generation)
claims.direction: favors this structured compute-reduction approach over naive backbone size reduction or pruning
claims.conditions: same as above

title: OGPO: Sample Efficient Full-Finetuning of Generative Control Policies

claims.claim: OGPO can fine-tune poorly-initialized behavior cloning policies to near full task-success with no expert data in the online replay buffer, drastically outperforming alternative policy-steering/residual-correction methods, across multi-task, high-precision insertion, and dexterous control tasks
claims.direction: favors off-policy RL fine-tuning (maintaining off-policy critics, propagating gradients through the full generative process) over standard behavior cloning alone when initial demonstration-only policies are poor, reducing reliance on more expert data
claims.conditions: manipulation tasks spanning multi-task settings, high-precision insertion, dexterous control; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Applies to diffusion- and flow-based generative control policies (GCPs), fine-tuning through the full generative process via a modified PPO objective
claims.direction: supports diffusion/flow-based action heads as amenable to this RL fine-tuning approach
claims.conditions: same as above

title: The Moving Eye: Enhancing VLA Spatial Generalization via Hybrid Dynamic Data Collection

claims.claim: Simply increasing the number of static camera viewpoints is insufficient for spatial generalization; models (evaluated: ACT, Diffusion Policy, Pi0, Gr00t) tend to fall into shortcut learning, latching onto spurious correlations such as fixed relative poses between objects or between camera and robot base; a hybrid data-collection strategy combining continuous camera motion (a moving arm-mounted camera) with diverse static viewpoints substantially reduces these spurious correlations while maintaining training stability, and all evaluated architectures benefit significantly
claims.direction: favors mixing continuous camera-motion data with diverse fixed viewpoints during data collection, over simply adding more fixed viewpoints, to achieve genuine spatial/viewpoint generalization
claims.conditions: dual-arm setup (one arm manipulates, one arm serves as a mobile environmental camera); tested across three data distribution patterns (Fixed, Multi-Fixed, Moving Views) and multiple policy architectures

claims.claim: The hybrid moving+static viewpoint strategy enables generalization to unseen camera poses and object configurations where adding more static viewpoints alone fails; susceptibility to shortcut learning and struggle with spatial generalization are shown to be universal across diverse VLA/imitation architectures
claims.direction: favors this data-centric fix specifically for camera-pose/viewpoint-shift robustness (directly matching a camera-shift failure mode) over architecture changes alone
claims.conditions: same as above

why_deep_read: Directly targets our reported failure mode of breaking under a slightly moved camera, with a controlled comparison of data-collection viewpoint strategies (Fixed vs Multi-Fixed vs Moving) across multiple architectures including ACT and Diffusion Policy relevant to our setup; full text would give the concrete data-collection recipe and quantitative viewpoint-shift robustness numbers.

title: Deltoris: Enabling Real-time VLA Inference in Embodied AI via Bit-level Sparsity and Speculative Inference

claims.claim: An algorithm-hardware co-design exploiting temporal similarity of consecutive diffusion-VLA inputs (computing only differences between consecutive control steps) plus speculative inference and a custom bit-serial accelerator achieves up to 34.2x speedup over mobile GPUs and 6.1x over prior accelerators for diffusion-based VLA inference, while maintaining comparable accuracy
claims.direction: favors exploiting temporal redundancy between consecutive control-step inputs to reduce diffusion-VLA inference latency, though requiring custom accelerator hardware rather than being usable on an off-the-shelf laptop GPU
claims.conditions: diffusion-based VLA models running at high control frequency (50-200 Hz); requires dedicated hardware co-design, not directly applicable without custom accelerator

title: ImitDiff: Transferring Foundation-Model Priors for Distraction-Robust Visuomotor Policy

claims.claim: Standard visuomotor imitation policies that perform well in simple settings experience substantial performance degradation as scene complexity and visual distractions increase; ImitDiff outperforms SOTA vision-language manipulation frameworks and visuomotor imitation policies particularly under increased scene complexity and visual distractions, and exhibits strong generalization in zero-shot settings involving novel objects and visual distractions
claims.direction: favors using pretrained vision-language foundation-model priors to generate pixel-level semantic masks that focus the policy on task-relevant regions, over standard visuomotor policies without such semantic guidance, for distraction/novel-object robustness
claims.conditions: real-world visuomotor manipulation; dual-resolution perception (global low-res + local high-res); no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Leverages pretrained vision-language foundation model priors, transformed into pixel-level visual semantic masks, to guide perception rather than relying on the raw visual encoder alone
claims.direction: favors incorporating foundation-model semantic priors into the visual pipeline over a standalone vision encoder
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: A consistency-driven diffusion transformer action head achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in inference speed while maintaining competitive success rates compared to standard diffusion action heads
claims.direction: favors consistency-distilled diffusion transformer action heads over standard multi-step diffusion for real-time inference
claims.conditions: same as above

claims.claim: Introduces a consistency-driven diffusion transformer action head that bridges visual semantic conditions and real-time action generation
claims.direction: supports consistency-distillation as a design choice for the action head
claims.conditions: same as above

title: MV-Actor: Aligning Multi-View Semantics and Spatial Awareness for Bimanual Manipulation

claims.claim: A Guided Metric Depth Repair module that refines degraded sensor depth provides more reliable metric anchors under consumer-grade depth noise; in real-world evaluations with unstable consumer-grade depth, MV-Actor outperforms both RGB and RGB-D baselines
claims.direction: favors explicit depth-repair/refinement when using noisy consumer-grade depth sensors, over using raw RGB-D or RGB-only input
claims.conditions: real-world bimanual manipulation with consumer-grade depth sensors (relevant to RealSense-class depth), plus PerAct2 simulation benchmark (87.8% avg success)

claims.claim: Sharing semantic perception across multiple camera views (rather than encoding each view independently or fusing shallowly) improves reliable spatial awareness, especially with frequent viewpoint changes
claims.direction: favors deep multi-view semantic interaction over independent per-view encoding or shallow fusion
claims.conditions: same as above

title: UniLACT: Depth-Aware RGB Latent Action Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

claims.claim: Latent action representations learned solely from RGB observations primarily encode appearance-driven dynamics and lack explicit 3D geometric structure needed for precise, contact-rich manipulation; incorporating depth-aware latent pretraining (learning a shared RGB+depth embedding space via inverse/forward dynamics objectives, used as pseudo-labels) consistently outperforms RGB-based latent action baselines under both in-domain and out-of-domain pretraining regimes, on seen and unseen manipulation tasks
claims.direction: favors depth-aware latent-action pretraining over RGB-only latent-action pretraining when depth is available at pretraining time (even if not required at deployment)
claims.conditions: simulation and real-world settings; no specific success-rate numbers given in abstract

claims.claim: Depth-aware pretraining produces stronger spatial priors inherited by the downstream VLA policy compared to RGB-only latent-action pretrained encoders
claims.direction: favors depth-augmented pretraining of the visual representation over RGB-only pretraining
claims.conditions: same as above

title: IG-RFT: An Interaction-Guided RL Framework for VLA Models in Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: For flow-based VLA models, an interaction-guided reinforced fine-tuning system (combining SFT, Offline RL, and Human-in-the-Loop RL stages, with interaction-status-modulated exploration and hybrid trajectory+subtask dense rewards) achieves 85.0% average success on four real-world long-horizon tasks, significantly outperforming supervised fine-tuning alone (18.8%) and standard Offline RL (40.0%)
claims.direction: favors RL-based reinforced fine-tuning of a flow-based VLA action head over supervised fine-tuning alone or standard offline RL, for long-horizon real-world tasks with scarce high-quality demonstrations
claims.conditions: real-world, four challenging long-horizon manipulation tasks

title: Genie Sim 3.0: A High-Fidelity Comprehensive Simulation Platform for Humanoid Robot

claims.claim: An LLM-powered simulation scene generator producing an open-source dataset of 10,000+ hours of synthetic data across 200+ tasks validates robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, demonstrating that synthetic data can serve as an effective substitute for real-world demonstration data under controlled conditions
claims.direction: favors large-scale LLM-generated synthetic simulation data as a substitute for costly real-world demonstration collection
claims.conditions: sim-to-real zero-shot transfer validation; no specific transfer-performance numbers given in abstract

title: Effects of SO(3) Action Representations on Observation-based Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation

claims.claim: In a controlled comparison holding the action interface fixed (7D robosuite-compatible) and varying only the internal 3D rotation representation, quaternion or 6D rotation representations achieve the highest mean success rate in 11 of 12 task-method combinations (MLP and RNN policies; robomimic Lift, Can, NutAssemblySquare tasks), outperforming axis-angle representation; on the harder Square task, 6D performs best for BC-RNN and ties with quaternion for BCO-RNN
claims.direction: favors quaternion or 6D rotation action representations over axis-angle representation for the orientation component of the action space in imitation learning
claims.conditions: simulation (robomimic benchmark), behavioral cloning (BC) and behavioral cloning from observation (BCO) with inverse-dynamics-model pseudo-actions, MLP and RNN policy architectures

why_deep_read: A clean, controlled ablation isolating exactly one sub-choice of Q02 (rotation representation: axis-angle vs quaternion vs 6D) while holding everything else fixed; small-scale and directly transferable methodology for us to sanity-check our own end-effector orientation representation choice on the SO-101.

title: GALA: Geometry-Aware Latent Action Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Model Pretraining across Embodiments

claims.claim: Augmenting image-based latent action models (which fail to capture fine-grained end-effector articulation) with 3D end-effector geometric motion via a Unified End-effector Motion Representation, combining visual latent actions (scene-level dynamics) with geometric latent actions (fine-grained articulation), achieves 68.3% success on RoboCasa-GR1 and 75.5% real-world success
claims.direction: favors combining geometric (3D end-effector motion) latent action representations with visual latent actions over purely image-based latent action pretraining
